Homer: No I don't. I hate to rhyme.
Snake: A singing family! it's worse than I feared. For hostage purposes, you're just too weird!
Snake: Because of you all, I got a tune in my head. And the only way to stop it is to make you all dead!
Homer: Ugh, I knew I should have shut that window.

title: Bart Carny (S9E12)
text: "Bart Carny" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F08), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by John Swartzwelder, originally airing January 11, 1998. The Simpsons visit a carnival, where Bart accidentally wrecks a car billed as Hitler's limousine, forcing him to work off the debt as a carny. Homer joins in, and the two are placed in charge of a rigged ring-toss booth run by carnies Cooder and Spud, who also secretly live inside the booth. When Chief Wiggum shows up looking for a bribe, Homer fails to understand the hint, leading Wiggum to shut down and confiscate the booth, leaving Cooder and Spud homeless. Feeling guilty, Homer invites the pair to stay at the Simpson house, but while the family is away on a boat tour Cooder gives them tickets for, the carnies board up the house and take it over as their own. Forced to live in their treehouse, the Simpsons scheme to reclaim their home. Homer challenges Cooder to a bet involving tossing a hula hoop over the chimney, wagering the deed to the house, but the wager is a ruse—while Cooder is distracted, the family rushes inside and locks the carnies out. With their home reclaimed, Homer settles back in and repairs the couch groove that Cooder had disturbed. Guest starring Jim Varney as Cooder. Notable quotes: Homer: The experts say that if you want an animal to do something, you should do it yourself first, to show 'em how. | Bart: Man, look at all this stuff... pull weeds, mow lawn, scoop and bag dog business. There's gotta be a way out of this. Lisa! Chop off my hands! | Cooder: In that case let me show you how I scammed you. | Chief Wiggum: Okay, let's try this again and watch as I wink each time. The man I'm really looking for, wink, is Mr. Bribe. Wink, wink. | Homer: I tried, but the opportunity never came up.
quotes: Homer: The experts say that if you want an animal to do something, you should do it yourself first, to show 'em how.
Bart: Man, look at all this stuff... pull weeds, mow lawn, scoop and bag dog business. There's gotta be a way out of this. Lisa! Chop off my hands!
Cooder: In that case let me show you how I scammed you.
Chief Wiggum: Okay, let's try this again and watch as I wink each time. The man I'm really looking for, wink, is Mr. Bribe. Wink, wink.
Homer: I tried, but the opportunity never came up.

title: The Joy of Sect (S9E13)
text: "The Joy of Sect" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F23), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Steve O'Donnell, originally airing February 8, 1998. Homer pulls Bart out of school to watch the local football team return from a championship loss, and at the airport they're approached by two cheerful strangers, Glen and Jane, who invite them to a free retreat run by the Movementarians. Despite Marge's suspicions, Homer visits the group's compound, where he initially resists their brainwashing techniques through sheer distractibility, only to finally succumb when Glen sings a catchy jingle about the mysterious Leader. Homer signs the whole family up, and they move to the compound, gradually losing their individuality to the cult's teachings about an imminent journey to the planet Blisstonia. Marge alone resists the indoctrination and flees, teaming up with Reverend Lovejoy and Groundskeeper Willie to kidnap her family and attempt to deprogram them at Ned Flanders' house. The cult's lawyers retrieve Homer just as a drop of beer starts to break his conditioning, and he returns to the compound still secretly clear-headed enough to expose the contents of the supposedly sacred Forbidden Barn. Inside is the Leader's ramshackle escape vehicle, which falls apart in flight, revealing the con man fleeing with all the money stolen from his followers before crashing into Cletus's farm. With the cult exposed as a fraud, the Simpsons return home and celebrate their freedom to think for themselves, though the episode ends with them mindlessly parroting a TV announcement, suggesting they're still susceptible to mass persuasion. Notable quotes: Reverend Lovejoy: This new so-called religion is nothing but a pack of weird rituals and chants designed to take away the money of fools. Now let's say the Lord's Prayer 40 times, but first let's pass the collection plate. | Groundskeeper Willie: I'll kidnap him for fifty. De-program him for a hundred. And I'll kill him for five hundred. | Homer: Homer no function beer well without. | Lisa: Watch yourself, Dad. You're the highly suggestible type. | Marge: When we got married, you promised me my harvesting days were over.
quotes: Reverend Lovejoy: This new so-called religion is nothing but a pack of weird rituals and chants designed to take away the money of fools. Now let's say the Lord's Prayer 40 times, but first let's pass the collection plate.
Groundskeeper Willie: I'll kidnap him for fifty. De-program him for a hundred. And I'll kill him for five hundred.
Homer: Homer no function beer well without.
Lisa: Watch yourself, Dad. You're the highly suggestible type.
Marge: When we got married, you promised me my harvesting days were over.

title: Das Bus (S9E14)
text: "Das Bus" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F11), directed by Pete Michels and written by David S. Cohen, originally airing February 15, 1998. After staying up all night watching a Troy McClure film about Noah's Ark, the Simpson kids head to school exhausted for a Model United Nations event, which quickly descends into chaos. On the way there, a bus full of squabbling students crashes off a bridge after a fruit-rolling contest gone wrong, leaving the kids stranded on a deserted island while Otto is picked up by fishermen and forced into servitude. On the island, the children attempt to build a society, but hunger, poisonous berries, and a shaky treehouse lead to infighting, with Milhouse wrongly blamed and put on trial for stealing food. Meanwhile, back home, Homer discovers Ned Flanders' secret internet business selling religious rugs and decides to start his own vague, undefined internet company called Compu-Global-Hyper-Mega-Net. Homer's clueless enterprise attracts the attention of Bill Gates, who buys him out and has his goons destroy Homer's home office rather than risk competition. On the island, Lisa uncovers the truth that no one actually saw Milhouse eat the food, clearing his name, and the group discovers a wild boar that leads them to a sustainable food source. The episode ends with the kids learning to cooperate as a society, and they are eventually rescued—by Moe. Guest starring Phil Hartman as Troy McClure, James Earl Jones as the narrator. Notable quotes: Bart: Whoa, cool! God is so in-your-face. | Homer: Yeah. He's my favorite fictional character. | Nelson: People, people. Let's not blame each other. We all know this is Milhouse's fault. | Ralph: They taste like burning. | Narrator: So, the children learned to function as a society. And eventually, they were rescued by, oh, let's say, Moe.

Homer: Yeah. He's my favorite fictional character.
Nelson: People, people. Let's not blame each other. We all know this is Milhouse's fault.
Ralph: They taste like burning.
Narrator: So, the children learned to function as a society. And eventually, they were rescued by, oh, let's say, Moe.

title: The Last Temptation of Krust (S9E15)
text: "The Last Temptation of Krust" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F10), directed by Mike B. Anderson and written by Donick Cary, originally airing February 22, 1998. Bart convinces Krusty the Clown to perform at a comedy festival organized by Jay Leno, hoping to revive his flagging career. Krusty's old-fashioned routines flop badly next to the edgier, trendier comedians also on the bill, leaving him humiliated. After a massive bender, Krusty holds a press conference intending to announce his retirement, but instead unleashes a scathing, honest rant against the new generation of comics, which unexpectedly delights the crowd. Reinventing himself as a brutally honest, anti-corporate truth-teller, Krusty starts performing low-key, credible shows that win him new respect, even if they pay far less than his old sellout gigs. Two marketing executives soon approach him to endorse the Canyonero SUV, and though he initially refuses on principle, the temptation of easy money proves too strong. In the end, Krusty caves and does the commercial, ultimately admitting to himself that selling out, not comedy, is truly what runs in his blood. Guest starring Bruce Baum, Janeane Garofalo, Bobcat Goldthwait, Jay Leno, Hank Williams, Jr., Steven Wright. Notable quotes: Krusty: Me, I learned something about myself today. It ain't comedy that's in my blood. It's selling out. | Homer: Heh heh heh, from now on, I'm gonna be just like Krusty and tell it like it is. Marge, you're getting a little fat around the old thighs! | Marge: Oh, knock it off, Homer; you're the fattest one in the car! | Agnes: Oh you're burning it all wrong Seymour. | Principal Skinner: It's my allowance mother; I'll burn it however I want.
quotes: Krusty: Me, I learned something about myself today. It ain't comedy that's in my blood. It's selling out.
Homer: Heh heh heh, from now on, I'm gonna be just like Krusty and tell it like it is. Marge, you're getting a little fat around the old thighs!
Marge: Oh, knock it off, Homer; you're the fattest one in the car!
Agnes: Oh you're burning it all wrong Seymour.
Principal Skinner: It's my allowance mother; I'll burn it however I want.

title: Dumbbell Indemnity (S9E16)
text: "Dumbbell Indemnity" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F12), directed by Dominic Polcino and written by Ron Hauge, originally airing March 1, 1998. Homer notices that Moe is lonely and depressed, so he takes him out to a nightclub to help him meet women. The outing seems to fail until a flower-stand worker named Renee approaches Moe and the two hit it off. As their relationship grows, Moe spends lavishly to impress Renee and quickly maxes out his credit, leaving him desperate for cash. He convinces Homer to help him fake the destruction of his car for an insurance payout by abandoning it on train tracks. Homer bungles the plan, missing the train and instead driving the car off a cliff into water in full view of the police, who arrest him. Moe promises to bail Homer out but instead spends the money on a Hawaiian vacation for Renee, prompting a guilty hallucination of Homer to confront him. After confessing his betrayal to Renee, Moe hatches a new scheme to burn down his bar for insurance money, but accidentally sets it ablaze prematurely. Meanwhile, Homer escapes jail seeking revenge, and the two end up fighting inside the burning bar until Barney rescues them both. With Moe's Tavern destroyed, Homer offers his own house as a temporary bar until Moe's is rebuilt. Guest starring Helen Hunt as Renee. Notable quotes: Moe: Well, that's it. It's over. Renee ain't gonna want to hang around with no Joe pinch-penny. | Moe: It's been four years since my last date with a whatchoo-call-it, uh, woman. | Homer: Aww, I could never stay mad at you, Moe. After all, you get me drunk! | Renee: Oh no. You're gay, aren't you? Oh boy, Renee, you sure can pick 'em! | Homer: To Marge, and all the blissful years I spent hiding from her in this bar.
quotes: Moe: Well, that's it. It's over. Renee ain't gonna want to hang around with no Joe pinch-penny.
Moe: It's been four years since my last date with a whatchoo-call-it, uh, woman.
Homer: Aww, I could never stay mad at you, Moe. After all, you get me drunk!
Renee: Oh no. You're gay, aren't you? Oh boy, Renee, you sure can pick 'em!
Homer: To Marge, and all the blissful years I spent hiding from her in this bar.

title: Lisa the Simpson (S9E17)
text: "Lisa the Simpson" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 4F24), directed by Susie Dietter and written by Ned Goldreyer, originally airing March 8, 1998. Lisa begins to doubt her own intelligence after a string of embarrassing failures, from forgetting her locker combination to bungling a school project and losing her sax skills. Grampa Simpson tells her that every Simpson starts out bright but inevitably grows dumber due to a hereditary trait he calls the Simpson Gene, and Lisa fears she is doomed to the same fate. As she spirals into despair and even embraces her supposed stupidity, Homer tries to disprove the family curse by gathering all the Simpson relatives to show they aren't complete failures, but the parade of men with absurd, low-achieving jobs only makes things worse. Marge suggests he ask the women instead, and Homer discovers that the female relatives all hold impressive, high-powered careers, revealing that the defective gene lies on the Y chromosome and only affects men. Relieved and reassured, Lisa regains her confidence and solves the brain teaser that had stumped her earlier. Meanwhile, Jasper sneaks into the Kwik-E-Mart's freezer to preserve himself for the future, and Apu turns the frozen old man into a profitable tourist attraction called "Frostilicus," rebranding the store as the Freak-E-Mart. When the freezer malfunctions and Jasper thaws out alive, Apu scrambles to keep business going by transforming the store yet again, this time into the risqué Nude-E-Mart. Guest starring Phil Hartman as Troy McClure. Notable quotes: Billy: Mr. McClure, what does DNA stand for?
quotes: Billy: Mr. McClure, what does DNA stand for?

title: This Little Wiggy (S9E18)
text: "This Little Wiggy" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F13), directed by Neil Affleck and written by Dan Greaney, originally airing March 22, 1998. After witnessing Ralph Wiggum get shoved into a museum exhibit by bullies, Marge feels sorry for him and pressures Bart into a forced friendship, despite his objections. Bart initially finds Ralph's clinginess unbearable, but things change when he discovers Chief Wiggum's closet full of police gear and, more importantly, the master key that opens every lock in Springfield. That night Bart convinces Ralph to sneak out with the key, and after ditching some bullies who want in on the fun, the two boys break into Morningwood Penitentiary. While exploring, they accidentally reactivate the prison's supposedly defunct electric chair and are nearly caught by a guard. The next day, Mayor Quimby plans to sit in the chair for a publicity stunt, unaware it's live, forcing Bart and Ralph to enlist Lisa's help to warn him before he's electrocuted. Their homemade rocket signal misfires and lands at the power plant instead, alerting Mr. Burns that the prison has been stealing electricity for decades, prompting him to cut its power just in time to save Quimby. The ordeal ends with the Simpsons celebrating Ralph's cleverness, while an ominous final gag reveals Ralph has been hallucinating a leprechaun urging him to commit arson. Guest starring Phil Hartman as Troy McClure. Notable quotes: Bart: Houston, we have a booger. | Ralph: Help! She's touching my special area! | Homer: Woo hoo! Beer, beer, beer! | Ralph: Smells like hot dogs. | Leprechaun: You've done grand, laddie. Now you know what you have to do. Burn the house down. Burn them all.
quotes: Bart: Houston, we have a booger.
Ralph: Help! She's touching my special area!
Homer: Woo hoo! Beer, beer, beer!
Ralph: Smells like hot dogs.
Leprechaun: You've done grand, laddie. Now you know what you have to do. Burn the house down. Burn them all.

title: Simpson Tide (S9E19)
text: "Simpson Tide" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 3G04), directed by Milton Gray and written by Joshua Sternin, Jennifer Ventimilia, originally airing March 29, 1998. After accidentally starting a fire at the power plant with an oversized donut, Homer gets fired again and impulsively joins the Navy Reserve after seeing a lax recruitment ad, with Barney, Moe, and Apu following suit out of loyalty. While Homer endures basic training and needles his drill instructor, Bart gets his ear pierced to seem cool, only to find the trend has already spread to the whole school by the time he shows it off. Homer is assigned to the nuclear submarine U.S.S. Jebediah under the eccentric Captain Tenille, and during a tense encounter with an enemy sub, Homer's panicked order to fire torpedoes accidentally launches the captain out of a torpedo tube, killing him. Now in command by default, Homer first orders the sub home but then impulsively steers it into Russian waters, sparking an international incident and accusations of treason. As an aircraft carrier attacks and the submarine begins flooding, Homer saves the crew by plugging the leak with the earring he'd confiscated from Bart. Brought before a military court, Homer avoids serious punishment when it's revealed the admirals judging him have their own scandals to hide, and he walks away with only a dishonorable discharge. Guest starring Bob Denver, Rod Steiger. Notable quotes: Abraham Simpson: My Homer is not a Communist. He may be a liar, a pig, an idiot, a Communist... but he is not a porn star. | Homer: You can't spell "dishonorable" without "honorable." | Captain Tenille: Ah Simpson, you're like the son I never had. | Apu: And although my religion strictly forbids military service—what the hey, I'm in too. | Milhouse: No, I think she's hot! Sorry, it just slipped out.
quotes: Abraham Simpson: My Homer is not a Communist. He may be a liar, a pig, an idiot, a Communist... but he is not a porn star.
Homer: You can't spell "dishonorable" without "honorable."
Captain Tenille: Ah Simpson, you're like the son I never had.
Apu: And although my religion strictly forbids military service—what the hey, I'm in too.
Milhouse: No, I think she's hot! Sorry, it just slipped out.

title: The Trouble with Trillions (S9E20)
text: "The Trouble with Trillions" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F14), directed by Swinton O. Scott III and written by Ian Maxtone-Graham, originally airing April 5, 1998. After procrastinating all year, Homer scrambles to file a fraudulent tax return at the last minute, and his stuffed envelope accidentally lands in the IRS's severe audit bin, leading to his arrest. Facing prison, Homer agrees to become an informant for the FBI, first exposing Charlie's plot to attack government officials, and then getting recruited for a bigger mission. Agent Johnson reveals that a trillion-dollar bill printed by President Truman in 1945 went missing and is believed to be hidden by Mr. Burns, so Homer is sent undercover to Burns's mansion to find it. Burns, mistaking Homer for a magazine reporter, reveals he has kept the bill on him the whole time, but before the FBI can fully arrest him, his impassioned rant about government overreach convinces Homer to help him escape. Homer, Burns, and Smithers flee the country by plane, hoping to buy an island and found their own nation, but mistakenly land in Cuba, believing Batista is still in charge. Fidel Castro asks to see the trillion-dollar bill as proof of Burns's wealth, then simply confiscates it, leaving the trio penniless. The episode ends with the three adrift on a raft, with Burns nonchalantly planning to bribe his way out of the legal trouble ahead. Guest starring Paul Winfield as Lucius Sweet. Notable quotes: Homer: Okay, Marge, if anybody asks, you require 24-hour nursing care, Lisa's a clergyman, Maggie is seven people and Bart was wounded in Vietnam. | Mr. Burns: I'm not the thief; the government is. Every year you make hardworking Joes like my reporter friend pay income taxes. | Mr. Burns: Sorry about the landing, boys. This fog is so thick I can't see my own cataracts. | Charlie: Why stop there, Homer? My militia has a secret plan to beat up all sorts of government officials. | Homer: Barney!? That was me! And I'd do it again.
quotes: Homer: Okay, Marge, if anybody asks, you require 24-hour nursing care, Lisa's a clergyman, Maggie is seven people and Bart was wounded in Vietnam.
Mr. Burns: I'm not the thief; the government is. Every year you make hardworking Joes like my reporter friend pay income taxes.
Mr. Burns: Sorry about the landing, boys. This fog is so thick I can't see my own cataracts.
Charlie: Why stop there, Homer? My militia has a secret plan to beat up all sorts of government officials.
Homer: Barney!? That was me! And I'd do it again.

title: Girly Edition (S9E21)
text: "Girly Edition" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F15), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Larry Doyle, originally airing April 19, 1998. Facing FCC pressure over Krusty's lack of educational content, Channel 6 launches a children's news program and recruits students from Springfield Elementary, naming Lisa head anchor. Marge pressures Lisa into giving Bart a spot on the show, and he quickly steals the spotlight with a flashy, over-the-top sports segment that catches the eye of network executive Lindsey Naegle, who promotes him to co-anchor. Meanwhile, at home Homer becomes fascinated by a helper monkey used at the Kwik-E-Mart while Apu recovers from an injury, and adopts one of his own named Mojo, only to watch the monkey spiral into gluttony and sloth just like himself, forcing Homer to return him. Back at the news show, an overheard insult from Lisa sends Bart to Kent Brockman for advice, resulting in a manipulative, saccharine human-interest segment called 'Bart's People' that moves viewers to tears. Lisa, disgusted by Bart's insincerity, sets him up with a fake feel-good story involving Groundskeeper Willie, who Bart had earlier made homeless by ruining his shack with creamed corn. When the segment airs live, an enraged Willie tries to attack Bart, and Lisa has to rescue her brother, prompting the siblings to reconcile and agree to improve the show together. Despite their efforts, the news program is ultimately canceled and replaced by a candy-and-toy-sponsored kids' hour, undercutting the whole educational premise that started the story. Notable quotes: Bart: I just think our veterans deserve a little recognition. | Lisa: That's what Veterans Day is for, Bart. | Bart: Well, maybe they should have three. I'm Bart Simpson. | Krusty: What about that [[Mattel and Mars Bar Quick Energy Chocobot Hour]]? | Channel 6 Executive: That's barely legal as it is.
quotes: Bart: I just think our veterans deserve a little recognition.
Lisa: That's what Veterans Day is for, Bart.
Bart: Well, maybe they should have three. I'm Bart Simpson.
Krusty: What about that [[Mattel and Mars Bar Quick Energy Chocobot Hour]]?
Channel 6 Executive: That's barely legal as it is.

title: Trash of the Titans (S9E22)
text: "Trash of the Titans" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F09), directed by Jim Reardon and written by Ian Maxtone-Graham, originally airing April 26, 1998. When Costingtons department store invents a new gift-giving holiday called Love Day to boost sales, the resulting mess causes the Simpsons' garbage to pile up until Homer finally takes it out, only to insult the sanitation workers and get their pickup service canceled. The trash accumulates into a mountain on the family's lawn, until Homer wakes to find it gone and gloats that he beat city hall, unaware that Marge secretly forged an apology letter in his name to get service restored. Furious at being humiliated, Homer confronts Sanitation Commissioner Ray Patterson to reclaim the letter, and their petty argument spirals into Homer deciding to run against him for the position. Adopting Moe's slogan "Can't Someone Else Do It?", Homer promises absurdly generous sanitation services and wins the election in a landslide. His extravagant campaign promises quickly bankrupt the department, so he starts accepting other cities' garbage for cash, secretly burying it under Springfield. The buried trash eventually erupts and floods the town, ruining Homer's reputation and getting him publicly disgraced and removed from office. Patterson refuses to return to his old job, leaving Springfield in ruins, so Mayor Quimby's only solution is to relocate the entire town five miles away. Guest starring Steve Martin as Ray Patterson, U2 as themselves. Notable quotes: Homer: You guys are the lousiest garbagemen ever! Yeah, I'm talkin' to you, you trash-eatin' stink bags! | Homer: I never apologize! I'm sorry, but that's just the way I am. | Homer: Well, this man does not crawl, he stands tall! That rhymes Marge, and you know it rhymes. Admit it! | Marge: You've have signed my name lots of times. | Bono: What the... bloody hell?
quotes: Homer: You guys are the lousiest garbagemen ever! Yeah, I'm talkin' to you, you trash-eatin' stink bags!
Homer: I never apologize! I'm sorry, but that's just the way I am.
Homer: Well, this man does not crawl, he stands tall! That rhymes Marge, and you know it rhymes. Admit it!
Marge: You've have signed my name lots of times.
Bono: What the... bloody hell?

title: King of the Hill (S9E23)
text: "King of the Hill" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F16), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by John Swartzwelder, originally airing May 3, 1998. After Homer embarrasses himself at a church picnic game of capture the flag, he realizes how disappointed Bart is in his poor physical condition. Determined to change, Homer begins secretly exercising at night, discovering a new energy bar called Power Sauce and eventually a 24-hour gym run by Rainier Wolfcastle, who trains him into peak physical shape. When representatives from Power Sauce look for a spokesman to climb Springfield's tallest peak, the Murderhorn, as a publicity stunt, Bart volunteers Homer for the dangerous task. Grandpa Abe warns Homer against the climb, revealing his own disastrous attempt years earlier that ended with the betrayal and death of his friend C.W. McAllister, but Homer presses on undeterred. During the ascent, Homer discovers his Sherpa guides have been secretly dragging him up the mountain while he sleeps and fires them, continuing solo. He eventually stumbles upon McAllister's frozen body and diary, learning the horrifying truth that it was actually Abe who betrayed and tried to eat McAllister. Despite his shame, Homer plants his flag, inadvertently breaking off the true summit and making his position the new peak, before sledding down the mountain on McAllister's corpse to a triumphant welcome and Bart's renewed pride in him. Guest starring Brendan Fraser as Brad, Steven Weber as Neil. Notable quotes: Homer: If God didn't want us to eat in church, he would have made gluttony a sin. | Homer: Look at you people! Bart's a tub, Lisa's weak as a little girl and Maggie doesn't seem to be growing at all! | Abraham Simpson: Son, don't go up that mountain! You'll die up there, just like I did! | Homer: The hell I won't! You're forgetting I've got my Powersauce bars! | Brad: Uh, I'm pretty sure he's dead, little girl. Here, have a Powersauce bar. It's on the house.
quotes: Homer: If God didn't want us to eat in church, he would have made gluttony a sin.
Homer: Look at you people! Bart's a tub, Lisa's weak as a little girl and Maggie doesn't seem to be growing at all!
Abraham Simpson: Son, don't go up that mountain! You'll die up there, just like I did!
Homer: The hell I won't! You're forgetting I've got my Powersauce bars!
Brad: Uh, I'm pretty sure he's dead, little girl. Here, have a Powersauce bar. It's on the house.

title: Lost Our Lisa (S9E24)
text: "Lost Our Lisa" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F17), directed by Pete Michels and written by Brian Scully, originally airing May 10, 1998. Marge plans to take Lisa to the Springsonian Museum to see the Orb of Isis before the exhibit closes, but she instead has to rush Bart to the doctor after he glues novelty items to his face. Desperate not to miss her last chance to see the exhibit, Lisa convinces a hesitant Homer to let her ride the bus alone. She boards the wrong bus, route 22A instead of 22, and ends up stranded near Area 51-A in an unfamiliar part of town. When Homer realizes his mistake after talking with Carl and Lenny, he frantically searches Springfield's Russian District for her, eventually commandeering a cherry picker to get a better view. The vehicle breaks loose and sends him on a wild, dangerous ride through the city and into the harbor, culminating in a terrifying near-miss with a closing drawbridge. Meanwhile, Bart has his face freed from the glue and unknowingly tries to apologize to an empty room, thinking Lisa is upset and silent. After Homer and Lisa reunite safely, he tells her it's okay to take risks sometimes, and the two sneak into the now-closed museum to see the Orb of Isis. They discover the orb is actually a hidden music box, validating Homer's advice, but their triumph is cut short when the alarm trips and guard dogs chase them out. Notable quotes: Homer: I'm not normally a praying man, but if you're up there, please save me Superman! | Homer: Naw, I'll just walk it off. | Marge: That's the kind of faucet I want for your bathroom. | Bart: That shut her up. | Chief Wiggum: Ah god, ah man, somebody stop that awful, awful man!
quotes: Homer: I'm not normally a praying man, but if you're up there, please save me Superman!
Homer: Naw, I'll just walk it off.
Marge: That's the kind of faucet I want for your bathroom.
Bart: That shut her up.
Chief Wiggum: Ah god, ah man, somebody stop that awful, awful man!

title: Natural Born Kissers (S9E25)
text: "Natural Born Kissers" is an episode of Season 9 (production code 5F18), directed by Klay Hall and written by Matt Selman, originally airing May 17, 1998. On their eleventh wedding anniversary, Homer and Marge's plans for a romantic dinner are derailed when Bart insists the family eat at a kitschy airplane-themed restaurant instead of a fancy establishment. Their attempt at intimacy that night fizzles, and the next day a burnt-out freezer motor forces the couple on an errand to a rural hardware store, during which their car gets stuck in the mud. Meanwhile, Bart and Lisa borrow Grampa's metal detector and unearth a long-buried alternate ending to Casablanca, learning from an elderly former studio executive that it was suppressed decades earlier. Seeking shelter from a storm, Homer and Marge hide in a farmer's barn, where the thrill of almost being caught reignites their passion, leading them to believe risky, semi-public trysts are the key to saving their marriage. They chase that thrill through a bed and breakfast, and finally back to the mini-golf windmill where Bart was conceived, but this attempt nearly gets them gassed by Moe and forces them to flee naked through Springfield in a stolen hot-air balloon. Their balloon crash-lands in the middle of a football game, leaving them exposed in front of a stadium crowd and later immortalized in the local newspaper. Despite the humiliating exposure, the ordeal seems to leave their marriage more revitalized than ever. Notable quotes: Homer: Take a picture. It'll last longer. | Moe: Who cares what it is? Let's monoxide it. | Bart: Priceless like a mother's love, or the good kind of priceless? | Homer: Now they did say bed and breakfast, right? | Farmer: If somebody's in here, you're in for some serious ass forkin'!
quotes: Homer: Take a picture. It'll last longer.
Moe: Who cares what it is? Let's monoxide it.
Bart: Priceless like a mother's love, or the good kind of priceless?
Homer: Now they did say bed and breakfast, right?
Farmer: If somebody's in here, you're in for some serious ass forkin'!

title: Lard of the Dance (S10E01)
text: "Lard of the Dance" is an episode of Season 10 (production code 5F20), directed by Dominic Polcino and written by Jane O'Brien, originally airing August 23, 1998. As the school year begins, Homer discovers from Apu that recycled grease can be sold for cash and drags a reluctant Bart out of class to help him start a grease-collecting business. Their venture proves far less profitable than expected, pushing Homer to resort to stealing grease from Krusty Burger and eventually raiding the school's kitchen during a dance. Meanwhile, Lisa is asked by Principal Skinner to welcome sophisticated new student Alex Whitney, who quickly charms Lisa's friends and convinces Skinner to hold a school dance instead of his planned event. Lisa feels pushed aside as Sherri, Terri, Janey and Allison abandon her for Alex, and a shopping trip for the dance turns into a makeover session that leaves Lisa uncomfortable in a gothic outfit. At the dance, boys and girls awkwardly stay separated, and Lisa explains to Alex that this is simply how children behave. Homer and Bart's late-night grease heist goes wrong when Groundskeeper Willie catches Homer in the air ducts, leading to a scuffle that causes the stolen grease to burst through the ventilation system and rain down on the dance floor. The resulting chaos turns into a spontaneous, greasy 'snowball fight' that unites the students, with Alex finally letting loose and acting her own age. Guest starring Lisa Kudrow as Alex Whitney. Notable quotes: Homer: Without the grease, all you can taste is the hog anus. | Homer: This is where all the hard work, sacrifice and painful scaldings pay off. | Homer: I've been muscled out of everything I've ever done, including my muscle-for-hire business. | Homer: Stop pummelling me! It's really painful! | Willie: Alright. I'll strangle you for a while!
quotes: Homer: Without the grease, all you can taste is the hog anus.
Homer: This is where all the hard work, sacrifice and painful scaldings pay off.
Homer: I've been muscled out of everything I've ever done, including my muscle-for-hire business.
Homer: Stop pummelling me! It's really painful!
Willie: Alright. I'll strangle you for a while!

title: The Wizard of Evergreen Terrace (S10E02)
text: "The Wizard of Evergreen Terrace" is an episode of Season 10 (production code 5F21), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by John Swartzwelder, originally airing September 20, 1998. After hearing that the average male life expectancy is 76.2 years, Homer panics upon realizing his life may already be half over, only to have Marge deflate his math by pointing out he's actually 39. Sinking into a depressive funk, he's inspired at a party in his honor when Lisa notes how many of Homer's everyday comforts trace back to Thomas Edison's inventions. Homer becomes obsessed with Edison, quits his job at the power plant, and sets up shop in the basement as an amateur inventor. His creations, including a constant safety beeper, a makeup-spraying shotgun, an unwieldy electric hammer, and a toilet built into a recliner, are all disasters. Just when he thinks he's finally created something original, an untippable chair with extra hinged legs, he discovers a photo showing Edison sitting in an identical chair, seemingly beating him to the invention. Determined to erase evidence of his own inadequacy, Homer drags Bart along on a trip to Edison's New Jersey museum to smash the chair with his electric hammer. Along the way he's confronted by Edison's ghost, who warns him against destroying it, but Homer literally runs him down and presses on. At the museum, though, Homer spots a poster revealing Edison himself idolized Leonardo da Vinci and never lived up to that idol either, which comforts Homer enough to leave the chair intact. He accidentally forgets his electric hammer at the museum, and it's soon reported that both the chair and hammer will earn a fortune for Edison's heirs, leaving Homer to console himself with his own toilet-recliner invention at home. Guest starring William Daniels as KITT. Notable quotes: Homer: I've wasted half my life, Marge. Do you know how many memories I have? Three! Standing in line for a movie, having a key made, and sitting here talking to you. 38 years and that's all I have to show for it! | Marge: You're 39. | Homer: They won't let me in the big people library downtown. There was some...unpleasantness. I can never go back. | Bart: Hey Dad, heard you swearin'. Mind if I join in? Crap, boobs, crap! | Man: Do us a favor. Invent yourself some underpants.
quotes: Homer: I've wasted half my life, Marge. Do you know how many memories I have? Three! Standing in line for a movie, having a key made, and sitting here talking to you. 38 years and that's all I have to show for it!
Marge: You're 39.
Homer: They won't let me in the big people library downtown. There was some...unpleasantness. I can never go back.
Bart: Hey Dad, heard you swearin'. Mind if I join in? Crap, boobs, crap!
Man: Do us a favor. Invent yourself some underpants.

title: Bart the Mother (S10E03)
text: "Bart the Mother" is an episode of Season 10 (production code 5F22), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by David S. Cohen, originally airing September 27, 1998. During a family outing to the Family Fun Center, Bart begins hanging out with the reckless Nelson Muntz, who has just won a BB gun. Despite Marge's disapproval, Bart borrows the gun and accidentally shoots and kills a mother bird, leaving behind two unhatched eggs. Wracked with guilt, Bart secretly nurtures the eggs back to warmth, earning Marge's unexpected approval once she discovers his efforts. The eggs eventually hatch into two lizards that Bart names Chirpy Boy and Bart Junior. A trip to the Springfield Birdwatching Society reveals the shocking truth: the animals are invasive Bolivian Tree Lizards that parasitize bird nests and have historically wiped out species like the dodo. Principal Skinner, acting on behalf of the Society, demands the lizards be destroyed, prompting Bart to flee with his pets. The lizards proceed to devastate Springfield's pigeon population, which the townspeople actually celebrate since they considered pigeons a nuisance. Bart is publicly honored by Mayor Quimby for the unintended pest control, even as Lisa worries about the ecological chain reaction Skinner describes involving snakes and gorillas. The episode ends with Bart keeping his two lizards while the government takes custody of the rest, and a final grim reminder of the lizards' predatory nature as one attacks a pigeon in the street.

title: Treehouse of Horror IX (S10E04)
text: "Treehouse of Horror IX" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF01), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by David S. Cohen, Larry Doyle, Donick Cary, originally airing October 25, 1998. This Halloween anthology episode opens with a gruesome twist on the family's usual intro before diving into three separate tales of terror. In 'Hell Toupée,' Snake is executed for his crimes, but his still-living hair is grafted onto Homer's bald head, possessing him and driving him to murder the witnesses to Snake's arrest, including Apu and Moe, before Bart manages to help his father tear the malevolent toupée off. In 'The Terror of Tiny Toon,' Bart rigs the family remote with stolen plutonium so he and Lisa can sneak a forbidden Itchy & Scratchy special, only to be sucked into the cartoon world itself, where the vengeful duo hunts them down until they narrowly escape back to reality, accidentally bringing Itchy and Scratchy along with them. The final segment, 'Starship Poopers,' reveals that Maggie is actually the half-alien offspring of Kang, forcing the Simpsons into a bizarre custody battle that plays out on The Jerry Springer Show, complete with Maggie murdering Jerry Springer himself. The episode resolves with Kang and Kodos threatening to eliminate American politicians instead, flying off while baby Maggie ominously reveals she shares her alien father's sinister ambitions and thirst for children's blood. Guest starring Robert Englund, Kathie Lee Gifford, Ed McMahon, Regis Philbin, Jerry Springer. I love it! This installment is made up of 3 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 9): "Hell Toupée", "The Terror of Tiny Toon", and "Starship Poopers".

title: When You Dish Upon a Star (S10E05)
keys: when you dish upon a star
text: "When You Dish Upon a Star" is an episode of Season 10 (production code 5F19), directed by Pete Michels and written by Richard Appel, originally airing November 8, 1998. The Simpsons spend a day boating on Lake Springfield, but a parasailing accident sends Homer crashing through the window of a lakeside vacation home belonging to celebrities Alec Baldwin and Kim Basinger. Rather than leaving, Homer talks his way into becoming their personal assistant, all while trying to keep their secret presence in Springfield under wraps. He grows close to the couple, unnerving their visiting friend Ron Howard with his eccentric behavior and pestering him with a bizarre movie pitch involving a time-traveling killer robot driving instructor and a talking pie. When Homer proves unable to keep their identities secret, Baldwin and Basinger cut ties with him, feeling betrayed. Furious, Homer retaliates by creating a traveling 'Hollywood Jerks' museum exhibit featuring their stolen personal items. The celebrities track down the exhibit intending to make amends, but the encounter turns into a wild car chase between Homer's mobile museum and their Hummer, ending only when Ron Howard is injured. Homer is legally barred from coming near any celebrity ever again, while Ron Howard salvages Homer's ridiculous script idea by successfully pitching it to producer Brian Grazer at 20th Century Fox. title: Lisa Gets an "A" (S10E07)
text: "Lisa Gets an "A"" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF03), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Ian Maxtone-Graham, originally airing November 22, 1998. After a tedious Sunday at church, the Simpsons stop for free samples at a grocery store, where Homer accidentally locks Lisa in a freezer, leaving her with a bad cold. While home sick, Lisa discovers Bart's video game Dash Dingo and becomes so obsessed with it that she fakes being ill for days to keep playing. When she finally returns to school, she's unprepared for a test on The Wind in the Willows and, in a moment of panic, buys cheat answers from Nelson in the boys' restroom. Her resulting perfect score turns out to boost the school's average enough to secure a financial grant, putting Principal Skinner and Superintendent Chalmers in an awkward position when Lisa confesses her guilt. Her honesty is seemingly rewarded at a public ceremony, though it's later revealed that scene was staged by Otto in disguise, and the real grant ceremony happens without her ever knowing the truth. Meanwhile, Homer buys a live lobster intending to fatten it up and eat it, but grows attached and adopts it as a pet named Mr. Pinchy. Tragedy strikes when Homer accidentally kills Mr. Pinchy while giving him a bath that's too hot, leading Homer to tearfully eat his former pet, insisting it's what Pinchy would have wanted. title: Homer Simpson in: "Kidney Trouble" (S10E08)
text: "Homer Simpson in: "Kidney Trouble"" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF04), directed by Mike B. Anderson and written by John Swartzwelder, originally airing December 6, 1998. The Simpsons set out on a road trip to the ghost town of Bloodbath Gulch, reluctantly bringing along Grampa on his birthday after their car breaks down near his retirement home. During the long drive home, Homer refuses to stop so Grampa can use the bathroom, and by the time they reach the hospital, Grampa's kidneys have literally exploded from holding it in. Homer impulsively volunteers to donate one of his own kidneys, and is treated like a hero by his family, but his resolve crumbles after Moe and his barflies scare him with tales of surgical risk and life with only one kidney. Marge tries to talk him through his fear by reminding him of his father's past kindnesses, but on the day of the operation Homer bolts out the hospital window in a panic. He winds up joining Captain McCallister's Ship of Lost Souls, a vessel of people trying to forget their pasts, only to be thrown overboard once his own sob story disturbs even them. Washing ashore and seeing a bonding father and son, Homer has a change of heart and returns to go through with the donation, but flees a second time and is knocked out in a freak accident involving a falling car. He wakes up in the hospital to find Grampa fully recovered and teasing him about the surgery that ultimately went ahead while Homer was unconscious, and the episode ends with the family reconciling as Homer jokingly checks Bart's kidneys. But if I die during the operation, will you do one thing for me? | Grampa: Am I dead yet? | Captain McCallister: Welcome aboard The Ship of Lost Souls.

title: Mayored to the Mob (S10E09)
text: "Mayored to the Mob" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF05), directed by Swinton O. Scott III and written by Ron Hauge, originally airing December 20, 1998. The Simpsons attend the Bi-Monthly Sci-Fi Convention, where Mark Hamill's promotional appearance for Sprint sparks a riot among the frenzied nerd attendees. Homer bravely shields Mayor Quimby and Hamill from the chaos, impressing the mayor enough that he fires his incompetent bodyguards and hires Homer on the spot. Thrilled with his new position, Homer embraces the perks of being a bodyguard, often to Marge's exasperation, using code names and knocking out his family with a newly learned pressure-point technique. During his duties, Homer uncovers that Fat Tony's crime family is secretly selling rat milk disguised as regular milk to Springfield's schools. Horrified, Homer pressures Quimby into shutting down the operation, despite the mayor's fear of retaliation from the mob. While dining at the Springfield Dinner Theater during a performance of Guys and Dolls, Fat Tony's men ambush the pair; Homer fends off several thugs, but Fat Tony still manages to beat Quimby, sending him to the hospital. The episode ends with the milk scandal exposed and Homer's chaotic tenure as bodyguard leaving lasting consequences for the mayor. Guest starring Mark Hamill, Joe Mantegna, Dick Tufeld. title: Viva Ned Flanders (S10E10)
text: "Viva Ned Flanders" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF06), directed by Neil Affleck and written by David M. Stern, originally airing January 10, 1999. After the long-forgotten Mr. Burns' Casino is demolished, Homer publicly exposes Ned Flanders for using a senior citizen discount, forcing Ned to admit he's actually 60 years old. Mocked by the congregation for having lived such a cautious, predictable life, Ned resolves to loosen up and asks Homer to teach him how to truly enjoy life. Homer enrolls Ned in his own makeshift self-improvement program and, after their intended destination turns out to be rubble, takes him to Las Vegas instead. There Homer gambles away Ned's money at roulette, and the two end up drinking heavily with two casino waitresses, Amber and Ginger. The next morning they wake up in a hotel hot tub with no memory of the night before, only to discover they've accidentally married the two women. Panicked about explaining this to their real wives, Homer and Ned attempt to flee the hotel but are chased down by casino security after the waitresses raise the alarm. Ultimately thrown out of Las Vegas, the pair trudge through the desert concocting an alien-abduction cover story, only to be set upon by circling vultures as the episode ends. title: Wild Barts Can't Be Broken (S10E11)
text: "Wild Barts Can't Be Broken" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF07), directed by Mark Ervin and written by Larry Doyle, originally airing January 17, 1999. After Cyndi Lauper sings the national anthem, the Springfield Isotopes pull off a surprise win, sending Homer and his drinking buddies Lenny, Carl, and Barney into a celebratory frenzy. Driving home drunk, the group ends up rampaging through Springfield Elementary, trashing the school and skinny-dipping in the locker room showers before Homer stumbles home with no memory of the night. When police find no leads, Chief Wiggum simply blames the town's children and imposes a strict sundown curfew, complete with a giant billboard warning kids they're being watched. Bored and resentful, Bart, Lisa, and their friends defy the curfew to sneak out to a horror movie called The Bloodening, only to be caught and sentenced to community service scrubbing Wiggum's billboard. Inspired by the film's premise of kids exposing adult secrets, the children set up a secret radio broadcast revealing embarrassing truths about their parents, throwing the whole town into chaos. The resulting confrontation between generations erupts into a musical showdown, but the conflict is hijacked by the town's senior citizens, who are furious about being kept awake. In a surprise twist, the elderly push through a new curfew banning anyone under 70 from being outside at night, and the seniors reclaim the streets for themselves, leaving both the adults and kids sidelined. title: Sunday, Cruddy Sunday (S10E12)
text: "Sunday, Cruddy Sunday" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF08), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Tom Martin, George Meyer, Brian Scully, Mike Scully, originally airing January 31, 1999. After a school field trip to the post office nets Bart some undelivered mail, he gives Homer a forgotten savings passbook as a birthday gift, and Homer eagerly spends the surprise windfall. While getting swindled into new tires at a garage, Homer meets travel agent Wally Kogen, who promises him a free trip to the Super Bowl if he can recruit enough men from Springfield to fill a charter bus. Homer succeeds, and he, Bart, and a busload of townsfolk head off to the big game, while Marge and Lisa pass the time at home dealing with a defective egg-decorating toy missing its plastic feet. At the stadium, the group discovers their tickets are counterfeit crackers, so they steal halftime-show costumes to sneak past security, only to be caught and thrown in a makeshift jail. Dolly Parton, an old client of Wally's, helps free them by melting the lock with her makeup remover, and the men wander the stadium raiding a skybox before being tossed out by Rupert Murdoch and swept into the winning team's locker room celebration. They head home victorious in spirit, with Homer sneaking off with the actual Super Bowl trophy. The episode closes with sports announcers John Madden and Pat Summerall wryly criticizing the very episode for lacking football and musical numbers, right before revealing Vincent Price is now driving their bus home. Guest starring Troy Aikman, Rosey Grier, John Madden, Dan Marino, Rupert Murdoch, Dolly Parton, Pat Summerall, Fred Willard. title: Homer to the Max (S10E13)
text: "Homer to the Max" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF09), directed by Pete Michels and written by John Swartzwelder, originally airing February 7, 1999. The Simpsons sift through disappointing new TV shows and settle on 'Police Cops,' where Homer is thrilled to discover the suave hero detective shares his exact name. He briefly enjoys minor celebrity status around town, adopting the character's scarf and catchphrase, until the show's producers retool the character into a bumbling, accident-prone buffoon. Homer becomes a laughingstock at Moe's, at work, and around Springfield as people mock him by referencing the show's humiliating gags. After his plea to the producers backfires and a lawsuit fails, Homer legally changes his name to 'Max Power,' adopting a bold new persona that catches Mr. Burns' attention. As Max, Homer befriends wealthy socialite Trent Steele and gets drawn into Springfield's elite social scene, culminating in a garden party that turns out to be a environmental protest to save a redwood forest. Max and Marge are chained to trees alongside other protesters, and chaos ensues when Chief Wiggum's police try to subdue them, resulting in a toppled tree and an accidentally injured eagle. Disgraced in front of the elite, Homer reverts to his old name that night, only to reveal to Marge that he's changed her name to 'Chesty La Rue' instead. Guest starring Ed Begley, Jr. as himself. title: I'm with Cupid (S10E14)
text: "I'm with Cupid" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF11), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Dan Greaney, originally airing February 14, 1999. When Bart's last-minute school project falls apart, Marge is forced to scramble to fix it, setting the stage for a Valentine's Day-themed chain of events. Apu and Manjula invite Homer and Marge to dinner, but the evening turns awkward when Apu's lies about American work culture spark an argument between the couple. Inspired by an offhand comment from Homer, Apu resolves to shower Manjula with extravagant romantic gestures, from poems and flower-strewn beds to a singing parrot and a chocolate-covered version of himself delivered by messenger. As Apu's gestures become the talk of Springfield, the other wives grow envious and their husbands feel increasingly inadequate, prompting Homer to rally the men of Springfield to sabotage Apu's grand Valentine's Day surprise. Their pursuit leads them to the airport, where they mistakenly believe Apu has hired Elton John, before realizing the real surprise involves a skywriter named Fantastic Dan. Homer's clumsy attempt to intervene ruins the skywritten message and sends him flying through a field of roses, which he presents to Marge in an unintentionally romantic finale. Meanwhile, Apu's true Valentine's surprise for Manjula turns out to be an intimate performance by Elton John, capping off the chaotic holiday with a happy ending for the Nahasapeemapetilons. Guest starring Jan Hooks as Manjula Nahasapeemapetilon, Elton John as himself. title: Marge Simpson in: "Screaming Yellow Honkers" (S10E15)
text: "Marge Simpson in: "Screaming Yellow Honkers"" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF10), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by David M. Stern, originally airing February 21, 1999. After a disastrous teachers' talent show, Homer becomes envious of Krusty the Clown's massive Canyonero SUV and rushes to buy one for himself, only to be humiliated when he discovers he bought the model marketed to women. He hands the vehicle off to Marge, who unexpectedly finds herself thrilled by its size and power, quickly descending into a spree of aggressive, reckless driving around Springfield. Her road rage lands her in legal trouble, and after accidentally smashing the SUV into the penitentiary fence and freeing a group of soon-to-be-rehabilitated convicts, she loses her driver's license entirely. Meanwhile, a family outing to the zoo turns chaotic when Homer inadvertently provokes a group of rhinos into a violent stampede that escapes into the city. Desperate, the police turn to Marge and her Canyonero to help corral the rampaging animals, and she agrees once she sees her own family endangered by the rhinos on a news broadcast. She successfully rounds up the herd, but discovers Homer is being dragged by the last loose rhino, so she chases it down and deliberately crashes the SUV to create a fire, instinctively prompting the rhino to try to stomp out the flames long enough for zookeepers to recapture it. Marge credits her clever strategy to a tip from newsman Stone Phillips, and the family publicly praises NBC for the informative programming, leading into a runner about Homer being forced at gunpoint to praise FOX during the credits. Guest starring John Kassir, Hank Williams Jr.. Notable quotes: Bart: I didn't think it was physically possible, but this both sucks and blows. | Bart: Kill me. | Homer: Marge, come in the house! title: Make Room for Lisa (S10E16)
text: "Make Room for Lisa" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF12), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Brian Scully, originally airing February 28, 1999. Homer takes the kids on a family outing that ends up destroying a replica of the Bill of Rights at a museum sponsored by OmniTouch, forcing him to pay off the debt by letting the company install a cell phone tower on the Simpsons' house. The installation requires demolishing Lisa's room, forcing her to share a bedroom with Bart, who deliberately torments her until she develops stress-induced stomach pains. When Homer dismisses her interests and insists on antacids instead of the herbal tea Dr. Hibbert suggests, Lisa finally confronts him about how he belittles everything she cares about, leading to a tense but honest conversation about their differences. Seeking to relieve their stress, they visit a New Age shop where a hippie lady offers them isolation containers for meditation, and Lisa has a vision that helps her appreciate Homer's efforts as a father. Meanwhile, Homer's container is mistakenly repossessed, buried by the Flanders family who think it's a coffin, and washed out to sea before Ralph Wiggum discovers it and it's returned to the shop, allowing Homer and Lisa to reunite and bond at a monster truck rally. In a parallel subplot, Marge discovers she can eavesdrop on neighbors' phone calls through Maggie's baby monitor (thanks to interference from the new tower) and becomes addicted to gossip. Bart and Milhouse decide to teach her a lesson by staging a fake robbery, but the prank backfires when Marge knocks Milhouse out with the monitor, and she and Bart cover it up by blaming Bart for the injury. I've got some class three gossip here. | Dr. Hibbert: Lisa, I'm afraid your tummy ache may be caused by stress. | Lisa: I'm really not the chuckling type. | Repo Man: Hey, channel somebody who gives a damn!

title: Maximum Homerdrive (S10E17)
text: "Maximum Homerdrive" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF13), directed by Swinton O. Scott III and written by John Swartzwelder, originally airing March 28, 1999. When Lisa protests a steakhouse that lets diners kill their own meat, Homer instead becomes enamored with the restaurant and challenges trucker Red Barclay to a steak-eating contest. Red wins but drops dead moments later, prompting Homer to take on the responsibility of completing Red's delivery, with Bart along for the ride. On the road, Homer pops both pep pills and sleeping pills to stay awake, eventually passing out and discovering his truck has a secret autopilot system that truckers rely on to nap through their routes. When Homer carelessly reveals this trucking industry secret to outsiders, a mob of furious truckers chases him down, and he must survive without the autodrive system's help. After finishing the delivery, Homer and Bart hitch a ride home on a train hauling napalm since no one else will drive it. Meanwhile, back home, Marge and Lisa buy an elaborate musical doorbell but struggle to get anyone to actually ring it, leading to a series of comic near-misses with visitors. When Lisa finally rings it herself, the doorbell malfunctions and blares uncontrollably, drawing an angry crowd until the doorbell store's whip-wielding mascot, Señor Ding-Dong, silences it and saves the day. title: Simpsons Bible Stories (S10E18)
text: "Simpsons Bible Stories" is an episode of Season 10 (production code AABF14), directed by Nancy Kruse and written by Tim Long, Larry Doyle, Matt Selman, originally airing April 4, 1999. During a sweltering Easter service, Reverend Lovejoy's long-winded sermon lulls the Simpson family into individual biblical daydreams. Marge imagines herself and Homer as Eve and Adam in the Garden of Eden, where Homer's gluttonous eating of forbidden apples gets them both cast out after a scheming attempt to sneak Eve back in fails. Lisa then dreams she and her classmates are enslaved Israelites in Egypt, with Milhouse as Moses leading a plague-filled rebellion against Principal Skinner's Pharaoh before parting a toilet-drained sea to escape. Homer's fantasy casts him as King Solomon, comically misapplying his wisdom by ordering a disputed pie split in two so he can eat both halves and execute the claimants. Bart's dream turns him into King David, who must avenge his slain friend Methuselah by defeating the monstrous Goliath II, ultimately succeeding only with help from a surprisingly resilient Ralph. When the family wakes up, they discover the church empty and the Rapture underway, with the Flanders ascending to Heaven while the Simpsons, after Homer refuses to give up Lisa, are sent down to Hell instead. The episode ends on this comedic apocalyptic note, explicitly marked as non-canon by the framing device. Notable quotes: Homer as Adam: No, you're too kind. And wise, and righteous... In the second story, a malfunctioning X-ray machine at Springfield Elementary bathes Bart and Lisa in radiation, giving Bart the power to stretch and Lisa super strength; as the superheroes Stretch Dude and Clobber Girl, they must rescue actress Lucy Lawless from Comic Book Guy's obsessive supervillain alter ego, The Collector, who has been kidnapping and preserving celebrities as collectibles. The trio defeats him by tricking him into unsealing a 'mint condition' lightsaber, destroying its collectible value and sending him to his doom in a vat of Lucite. In the final segment, Homer's incompetence as the power plant's Y2K compliance officer causes a global computer meltdown on New Year's Eve 1999, sending machines haywire and forcing humanity to evacuate via rocket ships to Mars. Lisa secures a spot for herself, Marge, and Maggie on the 'legitimate' rocket, while Homer and Bart sneak aboard a second ship that turns out to be filled with disgraced celebrities and is on a suicidal collision course with the sun, forcing them to eject into space rather than endure the trip. Guest starring Tom Arnold, Dick Clark, Lucy Lawless. Notable quotes: Homer: I'm caught on something! | Marge: I don't want you looting. | Homer: But I was going to loot you a present. | Homer: Uhh, Shiny McShine? | Homer: Good-bye, Lisa. Remember me as I am— filled with murderous rage! This installment is made up of 4 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 10): "I Know What You Diddily-Iddily-Did", "Desperately Xeeking Xena", "Life's a Glitch, Then You Die", and "Title Cards".

title: E-I-E-I-(Annoyed Grunt) (S11E05)
text: "E-I-E-I-(Annoyed Grunt)" is an episode of Season 11 (production code AABF19), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Ian Maxtone-Graham, originally airing November 7, 1999. After watching a swashbuckling movie at the Googolplex, Homer becomes obsessed with dueling and starts glove-slapping people around Springfield, until a stern southern colonel actually accepts his challenge to a pistol duel at dawn. Terrified, Homer fakes his own disposal as a Christmas tree to escape, and the family flees to the countryside, eventually settling at the old Simpson farm where Homer grew up. Struggling to make anything grow, Homer resorts to dumping plutonium from the power plant onto the fields, which unexpectedly produces a strange hybrid crop that turns out to be a cross between tomatoes and tobacco, dubbed Tomacco. The addictive plant draws the attention of both Springfield locals like Chief Wiggum and a cigarette company looking to buy the rights, but Homer's greedy demand for an absurd sum kills the deal. Farm animals go into a Tomacco-fueled frenzy, devouring the crop and forcing the family to barricade themselves before Homer manages to save the last plant. The Simpsons return home only to find the southern colonel still waiting to finish the duel, and after being distracted by Marge's pie, he shoots Homer in the shoulder, ending the ordeal with a comedic, low-stakes injury Homer waves off until after dessert.

title: Hello Gutter, Hello Fadder (S11E06)
text: "Hello Gutter, Hello Fadder" is an episode of Season 11 (production code BABF02), directed by Mike B. Anderson and written by Al Jean, originally airing November 14, 1999. Homer, running 26 hours late for work, is punished by Mr. Burns before sneaking off to go bowling with Lenny and Carl instead of keeping a promise to Maggie. He lies to Marge about the reason for his absence, but his deception is overshadowed when he unexpectedly bowls a perfect 300 game, turning him into a local celebrity. His newfound fame lands him a spot on a game show and a disastrous stunt during a Penn & Teller special, where he nearly gets shot with a crossbow. When the attention fades and he feels forgotten, Homer spirals into despair and attempts suicide, only to be saved by Otto, who happens to be bungee jumping nearby. Shaken by the experience, Homer resolves to live more meaningfully by bonding with his children, but Bart and Lisa rebuff his efforts, leaving him to focus on baby Maggie. His attempts to teach her to swim go poorly, and he nearly drowns at the beach, only to be saved by Maggie herself. Grateful, Homer takes her bowling as a reward, where she unknowingly rolls a perfect game of her own, which Homer disqualifies on a technicality, restoring his sense of ego and normalcy. Guest starring Ron Howard, Penn Jillette, Nancy O'Dell, Pat O'Brien, Teller. Notable quotes: Homer: Are "poo" and "ass" taken? | Homer: Damn, could my life get any worse? | Dr. Hibbert: Mr. Simpson, you're going to be fine... although you do seem to have swallowed a number of shark eggs. | Wiggum: All right, smart guy, where's the fire? | Homer: Waldo, where are you?

Homer: Waldo, where are you?

title: Eight Misbehavin' (S11E07)
text: "Eight Misbehavin'" is an episode of Season 11 (production code BABF03), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Matt Selman, originally airing November 21, 1999. While furniture shopping, the Simpsons run into Apu and Manjula, and Marge encourages the couple to consider having children. After struggling to conceive, and receiving some awkward encouragement from Homer, Manjula finally becomes pregnant. When she goes into labor, the family and friends gather at the hospital, only to discover that secret fertility drugs slipped to Manjula by multiple well-meaning friends have resulted in octuplets. The babies briefly become media sensations, showered with free gifts, until a Shelbyville family with nonuplets steals the spotlight and the freebies dry up. Overwhelmed, exhausted, and increasingly hostile, Apu and Manjula are approached by zoo promoter Larry Kidkill, who offers them free childcare in exchange for putting the octuplets on display as a zoo exhibit. They agree, but soon discover the babies are being exploited in a garish stage show called Octopia, prompting them to try to break the contract. When the zoo takes the babies away in response, Homer and Apu sneak in at night to reclaim them. Kidkill and his men confront the family, but Homer resolves the standoff by volunteering himself to take the octuplets' place in the dangerous, cobra-filled stage act alongside Butch Patrick. Guest starring Jan Hooks as Manjula Nahasapeemapetilon, Garry Marshall as Larry Kidkill, Butch Patrick as himself, Frank Welker as animals. Notable quotes: Homer: Kids are the best, Apu. You can teach them to hate the things you hate. And they practically raise themselves, what with the Internet and all. | Apu: By chilling my loins, I increase the chances of impregnating my wife. | Homer: Mine tasted like strawberry. Mmm... Ovulicious. | Homer: Free baby cola? Apu hits the jackpot, and I'm stuck with these useless one-tuplets. | Apu: I can't believe you don't shut up.

title: Take My Wife, Sleaze (S11E08)
text: "Take My Wife, Sleaze" is an episode of Season 11 (production code BABF05), directed by Neil Affleck and written by John Swartzwelder, originally airing November 28, 1999. The Simpsons visit a new 1950s-themed diner, Greaser's Cafe, where Homer and Marge enter a dance contest and win a vintage Harley-Davidson motorcycle. After Bart teaches him to ride, Homer forms his own biker gang with Moe, Lenny, Carl, and Ned, calling themselves the Hell's Satans and causing minor mayhem around Springfield that earns them a magazine photo spread. Unfortunately, a real, far more dangerous biker gang already uses that name, and its members, led by the fearsome Meathook, storm the Simpson home, trash it, and kidnap Marge in retaliation. Homer sets off to rescue her, getting beaten up repeatedly at a rough biker bar called Poppa Wheelie's while searching for clues to her whereabouts. Meanwhile, Marge charms her captors, teaching them manners and nonviolence, and discovers that the gentle Ramrod finds her attractive. After finally tracking down the gang's campsite, Homer challenges Meathook to a fight for Marge's freedom, wielding motorcycles like swords, and ultimately wins, bringing Marge safely home. Guest starring John Goodman, Jan Hooks, Jay North, NRBQ, Henry Winkler. Notable quotes: Homer: No! My wife is not a dooby... to be passed around! I took a sacred vow on my wedding day to bogart her forever. | Meathook: Mrs. Simpson, I killed my pencil. | Marge: Oh, I just swept the circle of death. | Bart: "PS: We've taken your old lady." | Father: He's a rebel, I tell ya – a rebel without a cause. Just like that boy in that boy in that popular movie we saw.

title: Grift of the Magi (S11E09)
text: "Grift of the Magi" is an episode of Season 11 (production code BABF07), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Tom Martin, originally airing December 19, 1999. When Bart breaks his tailbone after a prank goes wrong, Springfield Elementary is forced to build wheelchair ramps, but Fat Tony's shoddy construction bankrupts the school and forces Principal Skinner to close it. The school is saved when Jim Hope, head of Kid First Industries, buys and privatizes it, replacing lessons with toy-design workshops disguised as education. Lisa grows suspicious of the new curriculum and eventually uncovers that the 'school' is secretly using two-way blackboards and hidden cameras to spy on students for market research. No one believes her claims until she and Bart sneak into KFI headquarters, where an unhinged security guard, Gary Coleman, tries to stop them before they get a free sample of the company's new toy, Funzo. The siblings discover Funzo is programmed to violently destroy other toys, and they rally the town to boycott it. On Christmas Eve, Homer steals and burns all the Funzos in Springfield to stop the toy's rampage, clashing again with Gary Coleman until the two bond over the meaning of Christmas. The episode ends with the Simpsons inviting Gary Coleman to their holiday dinner, with everyone laughing together as Gary breaks the fourth wall. Guest starring Clarence Clemons, Gary Coleman, Joe Mantegna, Tim Robbins. Notable quotes: Bart: Lisa in trouble? The ironing is delicious. | Lisa: The word is irony! | Gary Coleman: Well, what do we have here? Looks like the biggest ripoff since Webster! | Homer: He releases the hounds on every charity that comes to the door. Feed The Children, Save The Whales, even Release The Hounds. | Bart: Not really, but if you're gonna throw a spaz, I'll come with.

title: Little Big Mom (S11E10)
text: "Little Big Mom" is an episode of Season 11 (production code BABF04), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing January 9, 2000. While cleaning out the attic, Marge realizes her family hoards useless junk and refuses to help her declutter, so Homer insists on using his neglected ski equipment, prompting a family ski trip. At the lodge, a falling clock breaks Marge's leg, forcing her into a hospital stay where she discovers she actually enjoys being pampered and waited on. Lisa takes over household duties, instituting a chore system for Homer and Bart, but the two treat their responsibilities with total apathy, letting the house fall into squalor. When Lisa calls Marge for help, Marge selfishly lies about still being too injured to return, leaving Lisa overwhelmed and resentful. Guided by the ghost of Lucy McGillicuddy Ricardo Carmichael, Lisa exacts revenge by faking a leprosy outbreak on Homer and Bart using paint and oatmeal while they sleep. Terrified, the two flee to Ned Flanders for help, who panics and sends them to a real leper colony in Hawaii. Once Marge is finally released and confronted by an exhausted, furious Lisa, the two travel to Hawaii, where they find Homer and Bart happily staying on as 'patients,' having decided the free vacation is worth the daily discomfort. Guest starring Elwood Edwards as the virtual doctor. Notable quotes: Homer: Electric needle room?! | Homer: And you're "interferon" with our good time! Hehehehe! | Bart: Stomp that pickle revert! | Ned: I guess we'll have an imagination Christmas this year.. | Homer: Aaaaaaaah! Stupid sexy Flanders.

title: Faith Off (S11E11)
text: "Faith Off" is an episode of Season 11 (production code BABF06), directed by Nancy Kruse and written by Frank Mula, originally airing January 16, 2000. Homer sneaks onto the campus of Springfield University with his old nerd friends to prank the dean, but ends up with a glue-filled bucket stuck on his own head. At a revival meeting led by the charismatic Brother Faith, Bart yanks the bucket free, and the preacher declares that Bart has been touched with a healing gift. Despite Lisa's rational explanation involving stage lights and metal expansion, Bart embraces his new status, performing showy 'miracles' and starting his own healing ministry for the townspeople. His fame collapses after he 'cures' Milhouse's poor eyesight by knocking off his glasses, leading to Milhouse being hit by a truck he mistook for a dog, and a guilt-ridden Bart quits faith healing for good. Meanwhile, Homer builds a flower float for SU's homecoming game using flowers stolen from Ned Flanders, but gets drunk during the festivities and forgets about it until it's too late. Crowd-surfing down to the field, Homer drives his float directly over the leg of star kicker Anton Lubchenko, badly injuring him, which draws a deadly threat from mob boss Fat Tony unless Lubchenko can still play. Desperate, Homer begs Bart to use his 'powers' one last time to heal the injured athlete before the game's outcome is decided. Lubchenko returns to the field, and though his kick initially seems to miss, his prosthetic leg detaches and knocks the ball through the goal anyway, winning the game and allowing Bart to finally admit he never had any real powers at all. Guest starring Don Cheadle as Brother Faith, Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony. title: The Mansion Family (S11E12)
text: "The Mansion Family" is an episode of Season 11 (production code BABF08), directed by Michael Polcino and written by John Swartzwelder, originally airing January 23, 2000. At the Springfield Pride Awards, hosted by Britney Spears and Kent Brockman, Mr. Burns learns he is being honored as the city's oldest citizen only after the previous title-holder drops dead onstage. Rattled by the reminder of his own mortality, Burns checks himself into the Mayo Clinic for a thorough examination, and puts Homer in charge of watching over his opulent mansion in the meantime. Homer quickly grows accustomed to a life of luxury, resenting any suggestion that his stay is temporary. He decides to throw a lavish party aboard Burns' yacht, the Gone Fission, sailing his friends out into international waters where no laws apply. Meanwhile, doctors at the clinic discover that Burns suffers from literally every known disease, including several exclusive to him, but since they all cancel each other out he is left oddly indestructible. Homer's yacht party is interrupted when Chinese pirates board the vessel, rob everyone, and toss them overboard, forcing the group to swim back to shore. With the yacht seized and the mansion no longer his to enjoy, Homer returns to his own modest home, grumbling about his relative poverty compared to Burns and other wealthy people, even complaining about the show's own voice actors during the credits. Guest starring Britney Spears as herself. Notable quotes: Kent Brockman: And I'm Kent Brockman. [no applause; Kent gestures to Britney Spears] With Britney Spears! [wild applause] | Doctor: You are the sickest man in the United States. You have everything. | Mr. Burns: Hysterical pregnancy? | Pirate Captain: Set a course for hidden pirate island, AKA Hong Kong! | Pirate: Looks like another homosexual party boat. They always have such nice things!

title: Saddlesore Galactica (S11E13)
text: "Saddlesore Galactica" is an episode of Season 11 (production code BABF09), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Tim Long, originally airing February 6, 2000. At the Springfield State Fair, Lisa's school band loses a competition to a rival band's flashy but rule-breaking glow-stick routine, sparking her ongoing letter-writing crusade to President Clinton. Meanwhile, the family discovers Duncan, an abused diving horse, and adopts him after Chief Wiggum shuts down his cruel act. To offset the cost of keeping Duncan, Homer and Bart try various money-making schemes before turning him into a racehorse. After an embarrassing first race, they rebrand Duncan as the aggressive 'Furious D,' and he begins winning consistently, much to the fury of the other jockeys. The rival jockeys kidnap Homer and threaten to eat his brain unless Duncan starts losing, but Bart refuses to throw the race. During the climactic final race, Duncan fights off the attacking jockeys and wins, after which Homer and Bart trap the vengeful jockeys in a bag. The episode ends with Homer helping Duncan find a mate to retire with, while President Clinton personally visits Lisa to address her complaints, offering dubious advice about persistence paying off. Guest starring Bachman-Turner Overdrive, Trevor Denman. Notable quotes: Homer: Vietnam Veteran. | Bart: Get bent. | Wiggum: I'd rather let a thousand guilty men go free, than chase after them. | Homer: Man, I got more trophies than Wayne Gretzky and the Pope combined. | Trevor Denman: Could it be? In a bizarre twist, a horse is abusing a jockey. Might this be the start of a terrifying Planet of the Horses?
