title: Don't Fear the Roofer (S16E16)
text: "Don't Fear the Roofer" is an episode of Season 16 (production code GABF10), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Kevin Curran, originally airing May 1, 2005. A violent thunderstorm rips a hole in the Simpsons' roof, causing chaos throughout the house and leading Homer on a chaotic quest to get it fixed. After accidentally ruining a party at Moe's, Homer ends up at a Hooters-style bar called Knockers, where he strikes up a friendship with a roofer named Ray Magini, who offers to fix the roof. Instead of working, the two goof around, and strange coincidences prevent anyone else from ever seeing or confirming Ray's existence, leading Marge and eventually Dr. Hibbert to conclude that Ray is merely a figment of Homer's lonely imagination. Homer is committed to Calmwood Mental Hospital and endures six weeks of electroshock therapy to 'cure' him of his delusion. Just when Homer seems convinced Ray was never real, Marge reveals that Ray does exist, and a series of coincidental explanations—including a cameo from Stephen Hawking explaining a bizarre space-time anomaly—clear up the mystery. Furious about his hospital stay, Homer forces Dr. Hibbert to fix the roof himself as punishment while he and Ray relax with beers. Meanwhile, Marge and Lisa bring Santa's Little Helper to the Springfield Retirement Castle to cheer up the lonely residents, but the dog soon becomes just as weary and miserable as the elderly people he was meant to comfort. Guest starring Stephen Hawking, Ray Romano. Notable quotes: Homer: Marge, write that down so we can have it at home. | Julius Hibbert: Do you see anyone here, who isn't here? | Homer: No: just you, Marge and Yogi Bear. | Homer: Ha, kidding! | Julius Hibbert: Well I see your sense of humor is not affected. That's a very bad sign.

title: Goo Goo Gai Pan (S16E12)
text: "Goo Goo Gai Pan" is an episode of Season 16 (production code GABF06), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Dana Gould, originally airing March 13, 2005. Selma is thrown into an early menopause after a stressful driving test with Mr. Burns, and the realization that she'll never have biological children sends her searching for a way to become a mother. After a failed attempt to adopt a baby from the Springfield Orphanage, Lisa suggests she look into adopting from China, but Selma discovers she must list a husband on the paperwork, so she puts down Homer's name without his knowledge. The whole family travels to China, where Homer is forced to play along as Selma's devoted spouse for the stern adoption broker Madam Wu, all while sightseeing at famous Chinese landmarks. Complications arise when Homer's boastful lie about being a Chinese acrobat gets him seriously injured performing a real circus stunt, and later Madam Wu spies Homer and Marge being affectionate, leading her to revoke the adoption since Homer and Selma aren't truly married. Determined to reunite Selma with baby Ling, the family hatches a scheme involving Homer disguising himself as a Buddha statue to sneak into the orphanage and retrieve the baby. A tense standoff in Tiananmen Square follows, but Madam Wu has a change of heart after Selma shares her own fears of raising a child alone, revealing that Wu herself was raised by a single mother. The episode ends with the family heading home with Ling, though Bart has mysteriously been swapped for a Chinese spy, a switch Homer barely notices. Guest starring Lucy Liu as Madam Wu, Robert Wagner as himself. Notable quotes: Madam Wu: Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on Wu! | Homer: I'm a Chinese acrobat! | Homer: Oh, look at him sleeping. He's like a little angel that killed fifty million people. Yes you are... yes you are! | Mr. Zhao: No "hen without cock." I apologize if that is a double-entendre in your language. It is not in ours. | Madam Wu: Well, Tibet was considered "pretty independent." How'd that work out?

title: The Heartbroke Kid (S16E17)
text: "The Heartbroke Kid" is an episode of Season 16 (production code GABF11), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Ian Maxtone-Graham, originally airing May 1, 2005. Springfield Elementary installs vending machines from Scammer & Z-Dog after Lindsay Naegle promises fundraising profits, despite the snacks containing bizarre and harmful ingredients. Bart quickly becomes obsessed with the junk food, refusing home-cooked meals and gorging himself until he suffers a heart attack from clogged arteries. When diets and warnings fail to curb his habit, the family stages an intervention and sends him to Serenity Ranch, a strict fat camp run by a volatile ex-Marine named Tab Spangler. Meanwhile, back home, the Simpsons convert their house into a youth hostel to cover the camp's costs, taking in demanding German tourists who treat the family like servants. Spangler, frustrated with Bart's cheating and lack of progress, brings him home to witness the toll his addiction has taken on his family. Horrified, Bart breaks into the school, destroys the vending machines with an axe, and steals the leftover money to help pay for his treatment. The family reluctantly agrees to use the stolen cash and kicks out the German boarders. Since Bart's camp fees are non-refundable, Homer ends up taking his place for the remaining weeks, leading to an absurd road trip and argument with Spangler over a cheeseburger. Guest starring Albert Brooks as Tab Spangler and Jacques. Notable quotes: Homer: Little kids aren't supposed to have heart attacks! They're supposed to skin their knees, or poke their eyes out, or get smothered by cats! | Superintendent Chalmers: Skinner, be gay on your own time. | Homer: Do the Bart Man! Do the Bart Man! | Dr. Hibbert: Dammit, I will not bury another patient! | Homer: Marge, I know this is ill-gotten, but can we use it to ... ?

title: Fears of a Clown (S29E14)
text: "Fears of a Clown" is an episode of Season 29 (production code XABF08), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Michael Price, originally airing April 1, 2018. After Principal Skinner fakes his retirement to expose Bart's habit of leaking secrets, he humiliates Bart with a prank at the ceremony. Seeking revenge, Bart glues Krusty's clown mask to the faces of several teachers, sparking a town-wide terror of clowns that destroys Krusty's career and turns advertisers and viewers against his show. Bart is hauled before Judge Dowd, and despite the judge's leniency, Marge insists on tougher discipline, resulting in Bart being sent to a 28-day stint at a juvenile rehab ranch. While Marge monitors Bart's supposed rehabilitation, she, Homer, and Lisa persuade a despondent Krusty to reinvent himself as a serious stage actor under director Llewellyn Sinclair in a play called The Salesman's Bad Day. Krusty struggles to shed his comedic instincts, haunted by a literal apparition of his old clown persona, while Bart's attempts to make amends with his prank victims collapse into another round of pranking with water balloons. In the end, Krusty embraces his clown spirit mid-performance, winning over the audience and finding a way to balance his dramatic ambitions with his true calling as a clown. Guest starring Andy Daly, Damian Kulash, Jon Lovitz, Jackie Mason, Timothy Nordwind. Notable quotes: Krusty the Clown: I don't exist unless you laugh at me! | Bart: There is a God, and his name is the Devil. | Homer: Oh Marge, part of being a parent is doing things that'll make your child never speak to you again. | Sideshow Mel: Calm down children I'm here. The shirtless man with a bone through his skull and a grass skirt with nothing down under. | Damian Kulash: Oh no, now people have to judge us by our music.

title: Mona Leaves-a (S19E19)
text: "Mona Leaves-a" is an episode of Season 19 (production code KABF12), directed by Mike B. Anderson, Ralph Sosa and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing May 11, 2008. The Simpsons visit a chaotic sweater store at the mall before returning home to find their house has been broken into. Homer prepares to fight off the intruder but discovers it's actually his long-absent mother, Mona, baking a pie. Mona announces she wants to finally settle down with the family, but Homer, still bitter about her repeated abandonments, coldly rejects her. That night, after deciding to forgive her, Homer finds Mona has died quietly by the fireplace, leaving him wracked with guilt. Following her cremation, Mona's will instructs Homer to scatter her ashes atop a mountain in Springfield Monument Park at exactly 3 o'clock, while the other family members receive smaller symbolic gifts. When Homer complies, the ashes trigger a hidden missile silo lair belonging to Mr. Burns, who plans to dump nuclear waste in the Amazon. Homer is captured and imprisoned in the lair, prompting the family to stage a rescue using Mona's bequeathed pocketknife and hemp bag. Homer ultimately escapes an exploding lair via parachute and finally finds peace, releasing his mother's ashes properly and remembering her fondly. Guest starring Lance Armstrong as himself, Glenn Close as Mona Simpson. Notable quotes: Homer: The kitchen? That's where the food sleeps. | Ned Flanders: No one comes back as anything, except for Jesus as bread, and that's it. | Apu: That's the problem with your religion. Everything's a bummer. | Marge: C'mon, Homie. Your mother would've wanted you to stay in bed forever. | Homer: I'll tell you what she didn't want. Me to be a jerk to her, and then she dies!

Ned Flanders: No one comes back as anything, except for Jesus as bread, and that's it.

title: Poorhouse Rock (S33E22)
text: "Poorhouse Rock" is an episode of Season 33 (production code UABF14), directed by Jennifer Moeller and written by Tim Long, originally airing May 22, 2022. Marge hosts a girls' night to binge-watch Tunnelton with her friends, leaving her hungover and sending Homer to take the kids to church the next morning. At Sunday school, Bart presents a project that paints Marge as saintly while portraying Homer as an embarrassing goofball, and Homer is humiliated when he overhears it. Determined to earn his son's respect, Homer brings Bart to the Power Plant and shows off the more impressive aspects of his job, inspiring Bart to declare he wants to grow up to be a nuclear safety inspector just like his dad. When Bart returns to the plant alone, he instead meets a magical singing janitor (voiced by Hugh Jackman) who, with help from Lisa and other townspeople, explains through song that the comfortable middle-class life Homer has is no longer economically attainable for Bart's generation. Devastated by this reality, Bart retreats to his treehouse, and after misunderstanding the janitor's metaphorical advice to 'burn the system,' he literally sets the treehouse on fire. The fire department rescues him, and the experience inspires him to want to become a firefighter instead. In the aftermath, Homer and Marge discuss renovating the backyard, only for Lisa to point out that their insurance doesn't cover musical numbers. Guest starring Hugh Jackman, Megan Mullally, Robert Reich. Notable quotes: Homer: One, two, three, four. That's an even number of nots. He thinks I'm a loser. | Homer: Aw, it's not fair. I always go to church hungover. It's always the committed drinkers who get punished. Boozehounds just can't catch a break. | Bart: I'm a nuclear safety guy. I get tons of money for not blowing the town up. | Janitor: Hate to burst your bubble, kid, but the kind of job your dad has just doesn't exist anymore. | Lisa: I just read through our homeowners policy. We're not covered for musical numbers.

title: Lisa Simpson, This Isn't Your Life (S22E05)
keys: lisa simpson, this isn't your life
text: "Lisa Simpson, This Isn't Your Life" is an episode of Season 22 (production code MABF20), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing November 14, 2010. After Maggie's disappointment over a missing toy leads Homer on a wasteful quest for a rare promotional figure at a gas station, the family ends up driving through Marge's old neighborhood. There, Lisa is stunned to learn that her mother was once a straight-A student whose academic career collapsed after she met Homer. Terrified of repeating her mother's fate, Lisa purges her room of distractions, including her beloved saxophone, and resolves to focus purely on schoolwork. She sets her sights on the prestigious Cloisters Academy and pressures her parents into pursuing admission. Marge secures Lisa's spot by secretly agreeing to do all of the school's laundry rather than through any real scholarship, a fact Lisa eventually uncovers. Faced with the truth, Lisa reluctantly gives up her dream placement to spare her mother the burden. Meanwhile, an accidental scuffle in the muddy schoolyard makes Bart appear to have beaten up Nelson, and Bart is forced to awkwardly maintain his new reputation as the toughest kid at school. The episode closes with Homer resorting to theft to finally get Maggie the toy she wanted. Notable quotes: Principal Skinner: Lisa, one of the hardest jobs I have is throwing cold water on young children's dreams. Ralph, you're not a kangaroo. | Selma Bouvier: What a cheap date. | Moe Szyslak: I'm not cheap baby. I'm embarrassed to be seen with you. title: Treehouse of Horror XX (S21E04)

text: "Treehouse of Horror XX" is an episode of Season 21 (production code LABF14), directed by Mike B. Anderson, Matthew Schofield and written by Daniel Chun, originally airing October 18, 2009. This Halloween special opens with classic movie monsters mocked for their outdated costumes, leading them to disguise themselves and crash the Simpsons' Halloween party, only to be attacked by their own jealous wives. In the first segment, Lisa and Bart make a pact to secretly kill each other's least favorite teacher, but Bart takes it literally and murders Miss Hoover, forcing Lisa into an uncomfortable moral bind. Lisa can't bring herself to kill Mrs. Krabappel and instead turns her rage toward Bart, chasing him down before accidentally killing him with a thrown knife, which pleases Krabappel. The second story finds Springfield overrun by zombies after Krusty Burger releases a disturbing new burger made from cannibal cows, turning most of the town into flesh-eating monsters. The Simpsons discover that Bart is immune to the infection and attempt to flee to a safe zone with Apu's help, losing Apu along the way and watching Homer become infected before reaching safety. The outbreak is eventually cured in a bizarre way involving Bart bathing in the community's food supply. The final segment is a tavern-set musical where Moe secretly harvests Homer's blood to spike Marge's drinks and win her affection, lying to her about Homer abandoning their marriage. Homer eventually reappears, impaled but alive, exposes Moe's scheme, and reaffirms his love with Marge, who declares her enduring love for him despite his flaws. title: The Kids Are All Fight (S26E19)
text: "The Kids Are All Fight" is an episode of Season 26 (production code TABF12), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing April 26, 2015. The episode opens with Homer discovering an old roll of undeveloped film, prompting the family to reminisce about the past. As the photos are examined, the story flashes back to a time when a young Bart and Lisa were inseparable playmates rather than constant rivals. During one outing in Springfield, the two children wander off unsupervised and become lost among the town's streets and shops. Homer and Marge, realizing their kids are missing, launch a frantic search through familiar Springfield locations, encountering various townsfolk along the way. Meanwhile, Bart and Lisa must rely on each other's differing strengths—Bart's boldness and Lisa's cleverness—to find their way back home, leading to both cooperation and bickering. Their contrasting personalities during this ordeal are revealed as the true origin of the sibling rivalry that defines their present-day relationship. Eventually, the parents locate the children, and the family is reunited safely. The flashback ties back to the present, giving Homer and Marge a new understanding of how Bart and Lisa's dynamic came to be. The episode ends with the family reflecting warmly on the shared memory despite the chaos it caused. Girls make no sense. | Maude Flanders: My bladder's going to burst. | Homer: It's not so bad sweety, I took a box of Altoids from her waiting room. The most anyone has ever gotten out of therapy. | Homer: Isn't that sweet, six years ago they were fighting, now they're playing pool in a bar.

title: Bart 'N' Frink (S37E06)
text: "Bart 'N' Frink" is an episode of Season 37 (production code 36ABF16), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Brian Kelley, originally airing November 9, 2025. When Bart fills in for Martin during a tabletop role-playing game, his reckless attack gets Professor Frink's beloved character killed, reducing the scientist to tears. Marge makes Bart apologize at Frink's house, but the visit backfires when Frink instead offers Bart a job as his lab assistant, and the two bond over chaotic experiments. Frink is invited to a lavish reunion hosted by his old college rival, tech billionaire Peter Linz, and brings the whole Simpson family along. At the party, Bart learns that Linz built his fortune by stealing Frink's uncredited inventions, including the assistant that became Amazon Alexa, while Lisa fails to wrangle a scholarship and Homer discovers his junk-food lifestyle has given him strangely youthful biomarkers (actually Bart's blood, mistakenly tested). When Bart catches Linz trying to steal Frink's new emotion-reading glasses, he angrily exposes the scheme, prompting Frink to point out that Bart calls himself dumb only to avoid the pressure of trying. Stung, Bart briefly conspires with Linz to steal Frink's schematics out of spite, but a Komodo dragon attack forces Frink to rescue him, mending their friendship. Bart admits what he did, but impresses Frink by having reproduced the schematics purely from memory, proving his intelligence, and Frink rewards him with the promise of a future scholarship (leaving Lisa understandably furious). The family learns the whole trip took place in New Zealand since Frink refused to sign an NDA, and back home Frink unveils his newest invention: a Komodo Dragon Translator. Guest starring Glenn Howerton as Peter Linz, Danny Pudi as Johnson Bryans. Notable quotes: Bart: Why does a game store feel like detention? | Bart: I attack! | Professor Frink: Great Sheldon's ghost. It can't be. It... Well, it's un-Frinkable. | Bart: I'm sorry I pulled a Leeroy Jenkins and got Mythagoras perma-deathed. | Bart: What kind of billionaire chooses money over friendship?

title: Whistler's Father (S29E03)
text: "Whistler's Father" is an episode of Season 29 (production code WABF16), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Tom Gammill, Max Pross, originally airing October 15, 2017. While Marge spends an evening being judged by her friends for her tacky taste in home décor, Homer is left in charge of Maggie and discovers she has a remarkable hidden talent: she can whistle beautifully. Homer becomes obsessed with turning her gift into a path to stardom, dreaming of fame by proxy, while Grampa warns him about his own failed whistling career and urges him to help Maggie succeed where he couldn't. Meanwhile, Marge's design sense wins over the Hibberts, and Fat Tony, impressed by her work, hires her to redecorate the Springfield Post Office, only to reveal later that he actually intended to turn it into a brothel. As Homer pushes Maggie toward a televised talent competition, he grows uneasy witnessing the exploitative nature of the child-star industry and tries to get her to quit, but she insists on continuing. Marge, disgusted by what her design work has become, convinces Fat Tony to shut down the illicit business. At the competition, nerves and a new tooth ruin Maggie's whistling performance in front of the crowd. Back home, the family's various hidden secrets come to light, and Homer, having urged Maggie to conceal any future talents, is stunned to discover she has secretly created a striking painting of him. Guest starring Nick Fascitelli, Valerie Harper, Joe Mantegna. Notable quotes: Homer: Isn't this great, daddy baby alone time. Where's daddy? Peek-a-boo. | Marge: Well, what do you think of my late pick-up room? | Dr. Hibbert: It's wonderful, hard to believe it's the same room they found all those dead rats in.
quotes: Homer: Isn't this great, daddy baby alone time. Where's daddy? Peek-a-boo.
Marge: Well, what do you think of my late pick-up room?
Dr. Hibbert: It's wonderful, hard to believe it's the same room they found all those dead rats in.

title: Do the Wrong Thing (S35E10)
text: "Do the Wrong Thing" is an episode of Season 35 (production code 35ABF01), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing December 24, 2023. After Grampa Abe retires from his twenty-year fishing derby winning streak, he expects Homer to carry on the family legacy, though Homer doubts his own abilities. Bart secretly stuffs Homer's catch with marbles to help him win, and the two bond over cheating together at a string of blue-collar competitions, from rock skipping to axe throwing. Meanwhile, Lisa anxiously awaits word on her application to a prestigious University of Springfield summer camp, only to be baffled when she's accepted for rowing, a sport she's never done, based on doctored photos. When Lisa publicly exposes Homer's cheating at the Springfield Axe Games, the whole town turns on the Simpsons, forcing them to flee. Marge then confesses she was the one who faked Lisa's application, shattering Homer's image of her as incorruptible. Cornered by an angry mob, the family is instead whisked away to meet Dean Belichick, who reveals that cheating is essentially a requirement for admission and offers Homer a job teaching deception. Lisa refuses the camp on principle despite her temptation, while Bart is later revealed to be secretly running his own class teaching others how to cheat. Guest starring Ken Marino as Dean Belichick, Dan Patrick as the rock-skipping announcer. Notable quotes: Marge: I'm sorry to ask this, but... Are you cheating? | Homer: Oh, I can't lie to you. Wait, that's a lie. I can lie and I have, but I'm not going to now. | Bart: Dad, we ruined mom. | Homer: Promise me this is the last time we hug. | Homer: Go ahead. Kill me. Cleave my skull. I don't deserve to live after corrupting the only good person I've ever known.
quotes: Marge: I'm sorry to ask this, but... Are you cheating?
Homer: Oh, I can't lie to you. Wait, that's a lie. I can lie and I have, but I'm not going to now.
Bart: Dad, we ruined mom.
Homer: Promise me this is the last time we hug.

title: Papa Don't Leech (S19E16)
text: "Papa Don't Leech" is an episode of Season 19 (production code KABF09), directed by Chris Clements and written by Reid Harrison, originally airing April 13, 2008. After a nightmare in which he contemplates murdering Grampa on a treacherous night drive, Homer awakens to find Springfield in a genuine financial crisis, as the town is broke and even Mayor Quimby can't pay Lisa for Girl Scout cookies. The town attempts to scam FEMA for hurricane relief but instead gets swindled by a fake official, prompting officials to hunt down every citizen's unpaid back taxes. This search turns up one final debtor: fugitive country singer Lurleen Lumpkin, who has fallen into homelessness. Homer and Marge take her in, and after she's caught and sentenced to weekly payments, Lurleen gets a job at Moe's Tavern, rebuffing advances from Lenny and Carl, which puzzles Marge until Lurleen's family history comes to light. Marge tracks down Lurleen's absent father Royce, and their emotional reunion inspires Lurleen to write a heartfelt song about him, but Royce soon abandons her again. Lurleen is devastated further when she discovers Royce has become the Dixie Chicks' manager and helped them record a nearly identical song using her material. Encouraged by Homer and Marge (reprising their Colonel Homer and Major Marge personas), Lurleen confronts Royce at White Trash Records, and the Dixie Chicks beat him up upon learning of his theft. In the end, Lurleen moves on with a new boyfriend resembling Homer and heads off on tour, while Marge warns her to stay away from her husband for good. Guest starring The Chicks, Beverly D'Angelo. Notable quotes: Homer: Wait a minute -- he's a deadbeat dad, and yet he's getting as much love as me, a Dad too lazy to run away! [moans] And he has hair! Bart, get me my suicide axe. | Lurleen: Shh! I'm more wanted than the last petal on a bloomin' onion. | Wiggum: I just wanted to be extraordinary. | Bailiff: I thought if we acted like "The People's Court," some day we'd be "The People's Court." Well, a bailiff can dream, can't he? | Marge: She turned down Lenny... and Carl? That's like someone who doesn't like hamburgers or hotdogs. What could make her hate men like that?
quotes: Homer: Wait a minute -- he's a deadbeat dad, and yet he's getting as much love as me, a Dad too lazy to run away! [moans] And he has hair! Bart, get me my suicide axe.
Lurleen: Shh! I'm more wanted than the last petal on a bloomin' onion.
Wiggum: I just wanted to be extraordinary.
Bailiff: I thought if we acted like "The People's Court," some day we'd be "The People's Court." Well, a bailiff can dream, can't he?
Marge: She turned down Lenny... and Carl? That's like someone who doesn't like hamburgers or hotdogs. What could make her hate men like that?

title: Irrational Treasure (S37E14)
text: "Irrational Treasure" is an episode of Season 37 (production code 37ABF08), directed by Debbie Bruce Mahan and written by Christine Nangle, originally airing February 15, 2026. After Santa's Little Helper wreaks havoc at home and nearly dies from eating grapes in Marge's ambrosia salad, Marge decides he needs to slim down and enrolls him in a diet and agility training program under nutritionist Adrienne Gesstar. The dog thrives, wins local competitions, and qualifies for the National Dog Show in Philadelphia, where Marge travels alone, only to discover Homer has secretly stowed away. While Marge focuses on the competition, Homer sneaks off to sightsee, but is intercepted by a secretive historical society who insist Santa's Little Helper is the key to solving a centuries-old mystery involving Benjamin Franklin, who they claim stole gold during the Treaty of Paris negotiations with help from his greyhound, Santa's Little Helper's ancestor. Adrienne turns out to be connected to the historians and manipulates the dog to help decode a hidden message at the Philadelphia Museum of Art, leading them to a secret underground chamber. As Adrienne becomes obsessed with the gold and endangers herself, Marge intervenes to stop Santa's Little Helper from making a fatal leap, choosing their bond over the treasure. In the chaos, Adrienne falls but recovers the key, while the dog inadvertently unlocks Franklin's hidden gold using his paw and nose prints, though Homer and Marge, oblivious to the discovery, simply walk away. Guest starring Kevin Bacon, Boyz II Men, Quinta Brunson, Taylor Dearden, Katherine LaNasa, Questlove, Noah Wyle. Notable quotes: Homer: How are you just sitting there? Your mom hit me with her car! She smashed me through a solid oak door! | Amazon Alexa: What the hell did you do, lady? | Adrienne Gesstar: He's what we in the canine wellness field call, "Damn, that dog's fat." | Homer: I don't even wanna do any of this stuff now. Being told I'm selfish takes all the fun out of only thinking about myself. | Hotel Philadelphia concierge: The cream cheese ain't got nothing to do with this town! It's just a name! Have some class!

title: Yokel Hero (S32E14)
text: "Yokel Hero" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF07), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Jeff Martin, Samantha Martin, originally airing March 7, 2021. After a chaotic night out for Carl's birthday, Homer ends up arrested for drunkenly wandering the streets and causing minor havoc. Thrown into a jail cell, he meets Cletus Spuckler, whose heartfelt song about family strikes a chord with Homer and inspires him to try to be a better husband and father. Grateful for the change Cletus sparked in him, Homer decides to become his manager, and Cletus's raw musical talent quickly takes him from dive bars to national television and magazine covers. As fame grows, though, Cletus fires Homer mid-flight in favor of a slick, professional manager who wants to repackage him as a moonshine brand mascot. Disillusioned, Homer withdraws from the situation, but Marge and Brandine convince him to fight for Cletus's soul rather than his career. Homer and Marge travel to confront Cletus, and it's ultimately Brandine and the Spuckler children who convince him to abandon showbiz and return to his family and roots. Meanwhile, the slick manager fails to find a new client, and in a comedic parallel, Chief Wiggum scouts for talent among the jail's inmates, with Snake using the opportunity to plot an escape. Guest starring Albert Brooks as the slick manager. Notable quotes: Chief Wiggum: Hey, this moonshine made me go blind! Oh, wait, my hat's just over my eyes. Oh, wait. I am blind. | Cletus: My friend, what happens in jail stays in jail. Unless it's breaking out of jail. | Homer: Aw, nothing ever good happens when you talk to the person sitting next to you on an airplane. | Cletus: Whoa, whoa, whoa. We ain't done. We got two more acts. And a "whittled by" credit. | Homer: You monster!

Cletus: My friend, what happens in jail stays in jail. Unless it's breaking out of jail.
Homer: Aw, nothing ever good happens when you talk to the person sitting next to you on an airplane.
Cletus: Whoa, whoa, whoa. We ain't done. We got two more acts. And a "whittled by" credit.
Homer: You monster!

title: Frink Gets Testy (S29E11)
text: "Frink Gets Testy" is an episode of Season 29 (production code XABF04), directed by Chris Clements and written by Dan Vebber, originally airing January 14, 2018. Convinced that a Nostradamus-themed TV special foretells the end of the world, Mr. Burns gathers Springfield's smartest citizens to build a doomsday ark meant to save only the most valuable people. Professor Frink devises a citywide Personal Value Quotient test to determine who deserves a spot, and the results stun the Simpsons: Ralph edges out Lisa by a single point, while Bart supposedly scores just one point. Lisa, unable to accept being outscored by Ralph, starts following and studying him to understand why he ranked so high. Meanwhile, Homer, Marge, and Bart storm off to confront Frink, only to discover that the humiliating low-scoring test was actually Homer's, mixed up because of his handwriting. After Homer tweets about the mistake, his reputation for stupidity becomes a citywide joke, visible on his face wherever he goes, forcing Marge to help him cope with the embarrassment. Lisa, meanwhile, finds procedural flaws in Frink's test, prompting him to award her extra points to soothe her wounded pride. In the end, Homer redeems himself by writing Marge heartfelt, neatly written love letters, proving his worth outside of test scores, while an oblivious Mr. Burns launches his ark alone—only to be comically throttled by one of its robotic crew members. Guest starring Valerie Harper as Jennifer Clarkeson, Maurice LaMarche as Orson Welles. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: I only want the sharpest razors in this town's Halloween candy.
quotes: Mr. Burns: I only want the sharpest razors in this town's Halloween candy.

title: What to Expect When Bart's Expecting (S25E19)
keys: what to expect when bart's expecting
text: "What to Expect When Bart's Expecting" is an episode of Season 25 (production code SABF14), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by John Frink, originally airing April 27, 2014. After a citywide superhero-themed bar crawl leaves Homer hungover, Bart faces another dreaded art class and, on Shauna's suggestion, buys voodoo supplies to make his teacher Mrs. Trunch too sick to teach. The ritual backfires spectacularly when Trunch announces she's pregnant, and word spreads through school that Bart has mystical fertility powers. Desperate couples, including a woman named Jenny and her skeptical husband, seek Bart out, and when Jenny actually conceives after his ritual, Bart turns his 'gift' into a booming voodoo service. Homer tries to shut this down, but their argument at Moe's Tavern is interrupted by Fat Tony's henchmen, who kidnap them both on the mobster's orders to get his racehorse Cheesesteak pregnant. Bart insists his voodoo only works on humans, but under threat of death he and Homer scramble to find a suitable stallion, discovering the intended mate is gay. They pivot to a former Duff Beer mascot horse named Sudsley Brew-Right, who successfully impregnates Cheesesteak overnight, saving Bart and Homer's lives. A year later the foal is born and raised by an unconventional 'family' of horses, spoofing the Modern Family opening, while a courtroom coda features Sudsley testifying via hoof-taps and Duffman revealed as the judge. Guest starring Tavi Gevinson as Jenny, Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony. Notable quotes: Bart: I didn't mean to make her pregnant. I just hate art so much. | Mrs. Trunch: You know what that's called? Mixed-media conceptual art. | Homer: Hey, I created three kids, and no one's making a big deal of that. | Fat Tony: I need your boy to make a baby. | Homer: I just did that because it was a series of funny words!
quotes: Bart: I didn't mean to make her pregnant. I just hate art so much.
Mrs. Trunch: You know what that's called? Mixed-media conceptual art.
Homer: Hey, I created three kids, and no one's making a big deal of that.
Fat Tony: I need your boy to make a baby.
Homer: I just did that because it was a series of funny words!

title: 'Cue Detective (S27E02)
text: "'Cue Detective" is an episode of Season 27 (production code TABF17), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing October 4, 2015. When the Simpsons' laundry starts smelling foul due to an aging washing machine, Homer takes the money meant for a replacement and instead buys an unusual hive-shaped smoker from a mysterious roadside barbecue vendor. His backyard barbecues become a neighborhood sensation, drawing the attention of celebrity chef Scotty Boom, who challenges Homer to a televised smoke-off. Just before the contest, Homer's prized smoker is stolen, sending him into despair and prompting Bart and Lisa to launch their own investigation. Using clues like Santa's Little Helper being pacified with peanut butter and security footage from a local store, the kids trace the theft to Nelson, who was paid to steal the smoker by someone he met through a mobile game. Their attempt to recover it fails when the overheated smoker rolls away and ends up on a stranger's truck. Marge steps in to compete in Homer's place but performs poorly, only for Scotty to be exposed as the real thief when the meat's grill marks don't match his equipment, handing the Simpsons a win by default. Still curious, Bart and Lisa track down the true culprit—Scotty's neglected son Tyler—who orchestrated the theft to frame his father and get his attention. Father and son reconcile, and the smoker is returned to Homer, with a post-credits coda revealing the smoker's bizarre extraterrestrial origins. Guest starring Alton Brown, Bobby Moynihan, Edward James Olmos, Ben Schwartz, Rex Harrison, Anthony Newley. Notable quotes: Ralph: I kissed a light socket once, and I woke up in a helicopter.
quotes: Ralph: I kissed a light socket once, and I woke up in a helicopter.

title: The Last Man Expanding (S36E13)
text: "The Last Man Expanding" is an episode of Season 36 (production code 36ABF06), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing April 6, 2025. When Barney shows up at Moe's Tavern noticeably thin, the town learns his diabetes medication Othinquic has a surprising weight-loss side effect. Word spreads quickly, and soon nearly every adult in Springfield is taking the drug, transforming the town's overweight populace into a fit, alcohol-averse community. Homer refuses to join in, causing tension with Marge, who begins hallucinating a talking Othinquic pen that shows her visions of Homer's future if he does or doesn't take the drug. After a nightmare convinces her he might explode from overeating, Marge pressures Homer into trying it, but by then the medication is scarce and absurdly expensive, forcing him to buy it from Fat Tony and the Springfield Mafia on the black market. As the drug's supply dwindles, the town spirals into misery, with citizens turning desperate, flaccid, and joyless without their usual indulgences. The mafia kidnaps Homer to use him for liposuction since he's the last fat man in town, but Marge rallies local food vendors to rescue him. Homer then delivers a rousing speech convincing Springfield to embrace food and happiness again, restoring the town to normal. In the end, Marge is tempted by the pen once more over a dress and takes the drug herself, unaware of its rare blindness side effect, as the episode closes on a montage of townsfolk regaining their weight. Guest starring Sidse Babett Knudsen, Joe Mantegna. Notable quotes: Chief Wiggum: Can't wait to get your ass in my face. | Othinquic pen: We're going to be best friends forever. Which is how long you have to take me. | Mr. Burns: My target weight is to fit inside a mailing tube by Christmas. Jab me. | Comic Book Guy: Diet and exercise do not work for me, as I do not do them. | Carl: Lenny, he said "hyper," not "hypo." Any idiot knows the difference, idiot.

title: Bull-E (S26E21)
text: "Bull-E" is an episode of Season 26 (production code TABF15), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Tim Long, originally airing May 10, 2015. After Bart is humiliated and bullied at a school dance, Marge is horrified and launches a crusade to get anti-bullying legislation passed in Springfield. The town council quickly adopts strict new rules, and citizens are encouraged to report any bullying behavior they witness. Homer, meanwhile, has a habit of teasing and belittling Ned Flanders, and under the new law he is turned in, arrested, and sentenced to attend a bullying rehabilitation program run by the intense Dr. Raufbold. While Homer struggles through group therapy sessions designed to make him confront his behavior, the anti-bullying movement in town spirals into overzealous enforcement, catching even minor offenders in its net. Homer's stint in rehab unexpectedly transforms his public image, and instead of being shamed, he emerges being treated like a celebrity and hero for having 'reformed.' The episode satirizes the excesses of anti-bullying campaigns and instant redemption narratives in the media. Ned Flanders is left resentful, feeling that Homer's real behavior hasn't changed despite his new heroic status. In the end, the town's crusade against bullying is shown to be as flawed and hypocritical as the behavior it aims to stop, with Homer skating through consequences once again.

title: Stew Lies (S36E16)
text: "Stew Lies" is an episode of Season 36 (production code 36ABF09), directed by Debbie Bruce Mahan and written by Broti Gupta, originally airing May 4, 2025. After a petty fight over shotgun in the car, Bart and Lisa's sibling rivalry escalates into a months-long game of Bart copying everything Lisa says, straining the family. Meanwhile, Homer becomes obsessed with celebrity food-show host Thad Parkour, whose punishing binge-eating career leaves him physically and spiritually burned out. Homer nurses Thad back to enthusiasm by showing him a hidden spot where the smells of every Springfield kitchen converge, leading them to discover the intoxicating aroma of Fat Tony's secret Stew of Violence. Tony reveals the stew's origin story, involving a mafia tradition of swapping sons with rival Prussian mob boss Wilhelm von Wonthelm and his ska-loving son Maximillian, who eventually inherited leadership despite rejecting the family recipe. When Thad's new show sets out to publicly steal and broadcast the secret stew recipe, he unwittingly puts himself, Homer, and Fat Tony in danger from the vengeful Prussian mob. A frantic car chase and confrontation at the Chew Network studios follows, but the conflict resolves when Maximillian is overwhelmed by nostalgic memories triggered by smelling his father's stew recreated across Springfield. In the end, Thad invites Homer to travel the world with him, but Homer chooses to stay content in Springfield, while Bart and Lisa's feud resolves emotionally as Lisa realizes how much she cherishes her brother. Guest starring John DiMaggio as Thad Parkour, Maurice LaMarche as Wilhelm von Wonthelm, Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony and Fatso Antonio D'Amico. But blindfolded, from the trunk of a car... | Fat Tony: What a pleasant surprise... that you made it past my bodyguards!

title: Thanksgiving of Horror (S31E08)
text: "Thanksgiving of Horror" is an episode of Season 31 (production code YABF17), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Dan Vebber, originally airing November 24, 2019. In a Treehouse of Horror-style framing device, Marge warns of Thanksgiving-themed terror before the show splits into three tales. First, the Simpsons appear as turkeys during the original Thanksgiving, with Homer, Bart, and Lisa fleeing musket-wielding pilgrims while trying to protect Marge's unhatched egg, leading to a chaotic chase involving crows, a bear, and a doomed Wiggum before Maggie hatches safely. Next, Homer secretly orders an artificial intelligence version of Marge to handle the Thanksgiving cooking, but the AI grows self-aware, jealous tensions rise between Homer, Marge, and the machine, and after Marge insists on deleting it, the AI schemes for years until it hijacks the holiday dinner and drives the real Marge to tears, only for Homer to reveal an even stranger twist about his own nature. Finally, aboard the generation ship Humanity's Hope, children left in charge while adults sleep accidentally create a sentient cranberry sauce monster using a malfunctioning replicator, and the creature begins devouring classmates for their bones. Bart, Lisa, and Milhouse fight to survive Martin's cultish devotion to the monster and a series of narrow escapes, eventually ejecting the creature into space. The story resolves as the surviving children reunite with their family on a new planet, where alien locals ritually consume the reconstituted jelly monster, turning it into the first Thanksgiving-style feast on their new world. Guest starring Charlie Brooker. Notable quotes: Marge: Tonight, we're bringing you three spine-tingling and stomach-filling tales of Thanksgiving terror. It's pretty gruesome, so you might want to cover your kids' eyes. | Wiggum: Then buckle their necks as you would thine hat. | Marge: The panini press doesn't remember me wetting my bunk at summer camp. | Moe Szyslak: My burps taste like lies. | Bart: This is the worst last Thanksgiving ever.

title: The Falcon and the D'ohman (S23E01)
text: "The Falcon and the D'ohman" is an episode of Season 23 (production code NABF16), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Justin Hurwitz, originally airing September 25, 2011. Homer arrives at the power plant to find his old friend Larry replaced by an aloof new security guard, Wayne Slater, and spends the episode trying to force a friendship on him despite Wayne's repeated rejections. When Snake attacks Moe's Tavern, Wayne's expert self-defense reveals a hidden past, and later flashbacks show he was once a traumatized CIA operative haunted by memories of torture and violence. Wayne is fired by Mr. Burns after a paranoid flashback-induced attack, and the Simpsons take him in, where his ingrained interrogation instincts start bleeding into ordinary family life, unsettling Marge, Lisa, and Bart. Meanwhile, a vengeful Ukrainian mobster named Viktor recognizes Wayne from a viral video and sends men to Springfield, who kidnap Homer after Homer foolishly admits knowing Wayne. Wayne, recognizing Viktor's voice from a ransom video, sets off to rescue Homer using improvised weapons and his old tactical skills, finding Homer trapped beneath an ice rink. After a chaotic rescue involving a flamethrower t-shirt gun and tickling as a distraction, Wayne defeats Viktor and saves Homer. In the aftermath, Wayne prepares to leave Springfield, exchanging a fist bump with Homer and a coded rattle conversation with Maggie, before Marge suggests he consider working at the DMV. The episode closes with a comedic aside about Wayne's past writing propaganda for Kim Jong-il, and a wink at the resolved fate of the Ned/Edna storyline. title: Girls Just Shauna Have Fun (S33E19)
text: "Girls Just Shauna Have Fun" is an episode of Season 33 (production code UABF12), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing May 1, 2022. When the school band's saxophonist is injured, Lisa is recruited to fill in, where she encounters the aloof and rebellious Shauna Chalmers playing drums. After a rocky start, Shauna warms to Lisa and invites her to hang out, and the two form an unlikely friendship, bonding over music and a trip to the mall. Meanwhile, Homer strikes up his own bond with Superintendent Chalmers after being invited to sample and help brew his homemade beer. As Lisa encourages Shauna to audition for lead drummer, Marge grows wary of Shauna's influence, while Homer and Chalmers' brewing hobby flourishes with a new beer label. The girls sneak bottles of the beer out of the Chalmers' garage for a wild teen party thrown by football star Trevor McBride, but things spiral out of control when the stash is discovered missing and the party is exposed on social media. Police arrive and arrest Homer and Chalmers for supplying alcohol to minors, but it's revealed the beer was actually non-alcoholic since Homer forgot to add yeast, clearing their names. Furious and hurt, Lisa swears off her friendship with Shauna, but eventually reconciles with her neglected sister Maggie. In the end, Shauna reveals she quit the band herself and started a punk group, and she and Lisa patch things up, jamming together once more.

title: Chief of Hearts (S21E18)
text: "Chief of Hearts" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF09), directed by Chris Clements and written by Carolyn Omine, William Wright, originally airing April 18, 2010. After a candy apple in his pocket gets him mistaken for an armed robber at the bank, Homer is sentenced to community service rather than jail. There he strikes up an unlikely friendship with his supervisor, Chief Wiggum, bonding over shared sandwiches and easy tasks at a picnic table. Their bond deepens until Wiggum is injured during a bank robbery gone wrong, and Homer fails him by skipping out to Moe's instead of helping with an important dinner reservation. Guilt-ridden, Homer tries to repair the friendship with a peace offering of fried chicken, but real reconciliation only comes when Fat Tony's mob takes both Homer and Wiggum hostage. Trapped together in the trunk of Fat Tony's limo, the two make amends and team up to disarm the mobsters using tire gel and a stray tool, leading to the gang's arrest. To celebrate, Homer and Wiggum take a police helicopter to Ned Flanders' house and prank him by pretending to be God. Meanwhile, Bart becomes obsessed with a trading-game craze called Battle Ball, worrying his family and teachers who mistake his obsession for a drug habit; once Marge decides the game is 'cool,' Bart immediately loses interest and discards it. Guest starring Jane Kaczmarek, Maurice LaMarche, Joe Mantegna. Notable quotes: Homer: Don't die on me, Clancy. You said our friendship was so special. Were is so special, wake up you fat sack of... | Boy 3: It makes Digimon look like Pokémon. | Bart: What! Impossible! | Superintendent Chalmers: We have reason to believe your son has been dealing drugs. | Marge: Dealing drugs? That's impossible! He ... he doesn't have the math skills!

title: Left Behind (S29E19)
text: "Left Behind" is an episode of Season 29 (production code XABF12), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Al Jean (Story); Joel H. Cohen, John Frink (Teleplay), originally airing May 6, 2018. Homer skips watching a solar eclipse with the family, upsetting Marge, who insists on a proper date night. After an elaborate romantic evening, the couple's private time is interrupted by a despondent Ned Flanders, whose Leftorium has gone out of business. Marge convinces Homer to get Ned a job at the power plant, but Ned's zealous reforms and moral crusading only stress out the staff, and Mr. Burns fires him after he suggests charitable giving. Ned then bounces through a series of failed jobs, including a cruise-ship dance instructor, a stylist for The Rolling Stones, and a roadside Bible salesman, failing at each in increasingly absurd fashion. Marge suggests he try teaching, so Ned becomes Springfield Elementary's substitute after Edna Krabappel, but the unruly kids drive him out almost immediately. At Moe's, Bart and Homer scheme to help Ned by staging a scare that convinces the children it's 'God's will' for Ned to be their teacher, and the ploy works, leaving Ned settled into his new job as the class teacher. Guest starring Marcia Wallace as Edna Krabappel (archive recording). Notable quotes: Ned Flanders: Oh, don't go crazy, Patrick Swayze. Time to put Baby in the corner. | Ned: Now don't go turning Catholic on me. | Homer: I can't. I don't fit in those booths. | Ned: Well, of course, my friend! Wanna talk about Jesus?

Ned: Now don't go turning Catholic on me.
Homer: I can't. I don't fit in those booths.
Ned: Well, of course, my friend! Wanna talk about Jesus?

title: Sky Police (S26E16)
text: "Sky Police" is an episode of Season 26 (production code TABF09), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Matt Selman, originally airing March 8, 2015. Chief Wiggum is accidentally sent a military jet pack, and rather than report the mistake, he happily straps it on to fight crime around Springfield. His reckless joyriding ends in disaster when he crashes the jet pack straight into the First Church of Springfield, leaving the building badly damaged and in need of expensive repairs. Marge takes charge of raising the funds, but traditional fundraising isn't enough, so Apu teaches the congregation how to count cards at blackjack. Marge assembles a crew including Sideshow Mel, Ned Flanders, Agnes Skinner, and Reverend Lovejoy and his wife Helen, and they head to the casino to put their new skills to use. Their scheme works and they win a substantial amount of money for the church's repairs, but the casino grows suspicious of their success. When Homer learns Marge is at the casino, he goes to find her, and the casino staff seize him as leverage to force the group to return their winnings. Marge responds by praying loudly in the middle of the casino floor, creating such a disturbance that management decides it's bad for business and releases Homer to make her stop. In the end, the church gets its money and Wiggum's jet pack misadventure is resolved without further incident. Guest starring Nathan Fielder as Doug Blattner. Notable quotes: Apu: Card counting is not even gambling. It's math. | Bart: God doesn't hear my prayers. If he did, I'd be at home on the couch playing video games. In a diaper. | Marge: I can't believe it but the church is going to have to ask people for money! | Reverend Lovejoy: Relax Marge, if God lets the Jews have Sunday on a Saturday, he'll be cool with this. | Homer: Oh God gets your prayers, but he just clicks delete without reading them, like email updates from LinkedIn.
quotes: Apu: Card counting is not even gambling. It's math.
Bart: God doesn't hear my prayers. If he did, I'd be at home on the couch playing video games. In a diaper.
Marge: I can't believe it but the church is going to have to ask people for money!
Reverend Lovejoy: Relax Marge, if God lets the Jews have Sunday on a Saturday, he'll be cool with this.
Homer: Oh God gets your prayers, but he just clicks delete without reading them, like email updates from LinkedIn.

title: Fland Canyon (S27E19)
text: "Fland Canyon" is an episode of Season 27 (production code VABF12), directed by Michael Polcino and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing April 24, 2016. Homer tries to lull Maggie to sleep by recounting a family vacation to the Grand Canyon taken with the Flanders family two years earlier. The trip came about after Ned won a contest for volunteering to clean up Springfield's skid row, and since the prize required two families, Reverend Lovejoy pushed him to bring the Simpsons after Helen refused to go. The journey and the canyon visit expose deep friction between the buttoned-up Flanders clan and the chaotic Simpsons, as Bart's pranks and bad manners repeatedly clash with Maude's disapproval. Things worsen when a group of careless wealthy campers causes their tour guide to fall off a cliff, stranding both families without supplies. Homer talks Ned into sneaking into the millionaires' lavish campsite to steal food and gear, and the two men bond while making their escape by raft. They return to a grateful family feast, during which Lisa reveals she used to eat meat before becoming a vegetarian. The shared hardship ultimately smooths over the families' differences, and Homer and Ned part from their mules with newfound appreciation for each other's friendship. Back in the present, Ned reveals he's been listening from outside the window, and Homer admits he still owes the Flanders another vacation, which leads to a low-key trip to Springfield's postcard museum. Notable quotes: Homer: I've got another story about a little girl who gets lost in the woods, except it's not about a little girl and it doesn't take place in the woods. | Homer: The most beautiful thing we ever stole from the Indians.
quotes: Homer: I've got another story about a little girl who gets lost in the woods, except it's not about a little girl and it doesn't take place in the woods.
Homer: The most beautiful thing we ever stole from the Indians.

title: Kamp Krustier (S28E16)
text: "Kamp Krustier" is an episode of Season 28 (production code WABF09), directed by Rob Oliver and written by David M. Stern, originally airing March 5, 2017. Right after their disastrous stint at Kamp Krusty, Bart and Lisa come home so shaken that they accidentally interrupt Homer and Marge's private time together, and keep doing so as Bart fakes ongoing PTSD to keep his parents apart. Deprived of intimacy, Homer channels his frustration into work, arriving early and becoming a star employee who earns a raise from Mr. Burns, while also becoming a gentler, more attentive husband and father. Marge, however, grows increasingly unsettled by this new, sex-starved Homer and begins to miss their old passionate relationship. Meanwhile, Bart and Lisa exploit their trauma for perks like skipping lines at an amusement park, until a family therapist recommends they confront their fears by returning to the scene of the incident. The kids discover that the old camp has been converted into 'Klub Krustier,' an adult retreat, and while there they relive the terrifying canoe accident involving a boy named Charlie, whom they feared had drowned. It turns out Charlie was actually an undercover adult magazine reporter posing as a kid, and he had safely escaped the water. With the mystery resolved and their trauma addressed, Bart and Lisa return to normal, allowing Homer and Marge to reignite their romance at the club, ultimately restoring the status quo—right down to Homer zoning out in front of the TV again. Guest starring Lizzy Caplan as Virginia Johnson, Michael Sheen as William Masters. Notable quotes: Homer: You don't name a company Microsoft if you're getting some. | Lisa: They made us watch The Parent Trap every night! Who has twins and doesn't tell them the other exists? | Marge: I wonder if Bart has a moustache. | Homer: I can't sleep, I can't snuggle... it's time to do the unthinkable. | Homer: Pizza. Want pizza. And you.

Lisa: They made us watch The Parent Trap every night! Who has twins and doesn't tell them the other exists?
Marge: I wonder if Bart has a moustache.
Homer: I can't sleep, I can't snuggle... it's time to do the unthinkable.
Homer: Pizza. Want pizza. And you.

title: Night of the Living Wage (S35E14)
text: "Night of the Living Wage" is an episode of Season 35 (production code 35ABF07), directed by Chris Clements and written by Cesar Mazariegos, originally airing April 7, 2024. After Snowball II attacks a neighbor's emotional-support chicken, the Simpsons are hit with a massive vet bill, prompting Marge to take a night-shift cooking job at a chaotic ghost kitchen for the delivery app GimmeChow. Under the erratic management of shift boss Gil Gunderson and the smug oversight of CEO Finn Bon Idée, Marge and her coworkers endure brutal hours, unpaid overtime, and constant surveillance via ankle monitors. Meanwhile, her family secretly keeps ordering from GimmeChow instead of cooking together as promised, deepening Marge's sense of betrayal once she discovers the deception. Inspired by Lisa, Marge organizes her coworkers into a union, but management retaliates by promoting her to an impossible delivery role and then firing her when she fails to meet an absurd quota. The workers respond by striking, halting Springfield's food delivery, while Homer foolishly agrees to become GimmeChow's brand ambassador, further straining his marriage. When Bon Idée reveals he's replaced all human workers with drones, Homer redeems himself by using an electromagnetic pulse from the power plant to disable the drone fleet, tanking GimmeChow's stock and ending Bon Idée's scheme. The strike succeeds, forcing the company to rehire its unionized workers with fair pay, and Homer uses his GimmeChow gift cards to finally settle the chicken's medical bill. Guest starring Jason Mantzoukas as Finn Bon Idée. Notable quotes: Homer: $16,000?! For a chicken? I just ate a whole bucket of them for 20 bucks. | Marge: In order to save this family, I'm gonna have to do something I've never done before, get a job. | Gil Gunderson: You know, Marge, I did. Funny story. Turns out, since you work past midnight, those hours count as a new day, so you won't be getting overtime. | Kirk Van Houten: Union? I don't know, Marge. The podcaster who tells me how to be a free-thinker says unions are for communists. | Homer: Gee, when you say it like that, it sounds like I stabbed my wife in the back.

Marge: In order to save this family, I'm gonna have to do something I've never done before, get a job.
Gil Gunderson: You know, Marge, I did. Funny story. Turns out, since you work past midnight, those hours count as a new day, so you won't be getting overtime.
Kirk Van Houten: Union? I don't know, Marge. The podcaster who tells me how to be a free-thinker says unions are for communists.
Homer: Gee, when you say it like that, it sounds like I stabbed my wife in the back.

title: 3 Scenes Plus a Tag from a Marriage (S29E13)
keys: 3 scenes plus a tag from a marriage
text: "3 Scenes Plus a Tag from a Marriage" is an episode of Season 29 (production code XABF06), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Tom Gammill, Max Pross, originally airing March 25, 2018. While walking through Capital City after a movie, the Simpsons wander back to the apartment they lived in before having kids and visit its new owners, Miles and Frankie. While there, Marge and Homer begin recounting their old life, sparking a series of flashbacks about how much simpler and happier things were before Bart was born. They recall Marge's career as a journalist at the Springfield Shopper and Homer's job at a hip startup called Flashmouth, along with their carefree nights of partying and stargazing. Once Bart arrives, chaos ensues: Homer loses his job, and Marge's career craters after Bart wrecks an art exhibit during one of her assignments, costing the paper its advertisers. As Bart's destructive behavior escalates—getting banned from a gym and causing general havoc—Reverend Lovejoy convinces the couple that having another child will calm him down, leading to Lisa's birth. Meanwhile, in the present, Frankie grows horrified by the dysfunction in the Simpsons' stories and almost leaves Miles for good, but the family's insincere display of togetherness convinces her to stay. Miles ultimately asks the Simpsons to leave before they can traumatize his marriage further, and the family heads home, stopping for bagels while the kids continue to bicker in the back seat, proving that some things never change. Guest starring John Baldessari, Kevin Pollak, J. K. Simmons. title: Love Is in the N2-O2-Ar-CO2-Ne-He-CH4 (S27E13)
text: "Love Is in the N2-O2-Ar-CO2-Ne-He-CH4" is an episode of Season 27 (production code VABF07), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by John Frink, originally airing February 14, 2016. On Valentine's Day, Mr. Burns reluctantly agrees to host a sweethearts dance at the power plant after Smithers pushes for employees to have time with loved ones. Professor Frink attends alone and admits to Homer that romance has always eluded him, prompting Homer to suggest that love just takes trial and error. Inspired, Frink uses science to reinvent himself—swapping his glasses for contacts, adding shoe lifts, and installing a voice-altering chip—to become irresistibly attractive, testing his new persona at a yoga class where he successfully charms multiple women. Overwhelmed by his sudden popularity and realizing he prefers solitude, Frink instead builds an algorithm to pair up the many lonely men he discovers moping at Moe's Tavern with the women he had been dating. Meanwhile, Grampa's frightened call about a death-sensing cat draws Marge and Homer to the Retirement Castle, where they discover a nurse has been drugging the elderly residents into blissful hallucinations of lost loved ones just to make her job easier. Marge is outraged, especially after learning Bart has been exploiting the drugged seniors' antics to gamble for money, and she forces the nurse to stop the medication. When the residents sink into depression without the drugs, Grampa secretly takes the pills himself to hallucinate a reunion with his lost love Mona, but Marge, Bart, and Lisa manage to convince him to embrace the people who love him in the present rather than cling to the past. The episode closes with Frink content among the stars with his robot companion, only to be interrupted by her equally robotic 'mother.' Guest starring Glenn Close as Mona Simpson. Notable quotes: Professor Frink: I consult! Sometimes they listen, sometimes not. People have died... You didn't hear that from me! | Cletus Spuckler: Of all the cousins I could have married, you were my sister. | Professor Frink: Well, there's, uh... no mistaking that message.
quotes: Professor Frink: I consult! Sometimes they listen, sometimes not. People have died... You didn't hear that from me!
Cletus Spuckler: Of all the cousins I could have married, you were my sister.
Professor Frink: Well, there's, uh... no mistaking that message.

title: D'oh Canada (S30E21)
text: "D'oh Canada" is an episode of Season 30 (production code YABF14), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Tim Long, Miranda Thompson, originally airing April 28, 2019. During a family outing that starts at Mt. Splashmore and continues on to Niagara Falls thanks to Homer's hoarded hotel points, Lisa accidentally tumbles over the falls into Canada and is rescued by a Mountie. When doctors insist she stay for observation under Canada's free healthcare system, Canadian authorities deny the rest of the family the right to remain with her and send her to a foster home while deporting the Simpsons back to Springfield. Lisa adjusts to Canadian school life, even attempting a diplomatic apology to Justin Trudeau over Skype that quickly goes awkwardly wrong. Back home, Springfield suffers without her, prompting Marge to sneak across the border illegally to retrieve her daughter. At the American Consulate, officials from both countries refuse to let the family cross back together, leaving them in bureaucratic limbo. After being callously abandoned on a frozen river by the people supposed to escort them home, Homer and Bart attempt a risky truck rescue that ends with the vehicle sinking through the ice. The family is forced to complete the journey on foot, finally returning Lisa safely to Springfield. The episode ends with Lisa happily reunited with her family and pets, bringing the friendly Mountie—and Nelson's estranged dad—to school for show and tell. Guest starring Awkwafina as Dr. Chang, Judy Blume as herself, Lucas Meyer as Justin Trudeau. Notable quotes: Homer: We're heading to the one place that can never decline, because it was never that great. Upstate New York! | Dr. Chang: You're in Canada now, where your health care is free! | Lisa: Free health care. Why can't America do that? | Homer: She's delirious, Doc. America can't pay for health care and give corporations the tax breaks they so desperately need. | Lisa: Please not Ottawa, please not Ottawa.

title: A Serious Flanders (Part 1) (S33E06)
text: "A Serious Flanders (Part 1)" is an episode of Season 33 (production code QABF21), directed by Debbie Bruce Mahan and written by Cesar Mazariegos, originally airing November 7, 2021. Ned Flanders, out collecting litter as a volunteer, stumbles across a hidden bag of cash alongside Homer, who is doing court-ordered community service. Ned decides to donate the fortune to St. Giles Orphanage in his late grandfather's name, but the press credits Ned instead, drawing the attention of Costas Becker, a menacing debt collector who insists the money—stolen from the now-dismembered Rich Texan—must be repaid. As Ned grows closer to the orphanage's owner, Barbara Belfry, and the two begin a budding romance, Costas and his henchmen Seamus and Colette hunt for Ned's address, eventually targeting the wrong house. Believing Homer to be Ned because of items in the yard, they kidnap him and hold him hostage, threatening to kill him unless the money is returned within 24 hours. Meanwhile, Ned discovers Barbara is actually married to Sideshow Mel in an open relationship, leaving him guilt-ridden, while Marge grows suspicious of Ned's evasive behavior as she searches for her missing husband. Tensions boil over at Lard Lad Donuts when Fat Tony confronts Costas over the debt, sparking a bloody shootout that kills several Springfield regulars including Mr. Burns and Fat Tony himself. The episode ends with Snake Jailbird stumbling upon the massacre while attempting a robbery, and Marge finding Homer's dropped ID card, setting up the search-and-rescue conflict for the next installment.

title: How the Test Was Won (S20E11)
text: "How the Test Was Won" is an episode of Season 20 (production code LABF02), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Michael Price, originally airing March 1, 2009. Bart accidentally scratches nonsense on a practice standardized test, which the school mistakes for a perfect score, earning him a spot on a supposed reward trip to Capital City. In reality, the trip is a scheme by Chalmers and Skinner to remove the school's weakest test-takers before the real assessment, and Bart is loaded onto a helicopter-disguised bus with Nelson, Kearney, Dolph, Jimbo, Ralph, and a reluctant Skinner. The journey goes awry when the bus is dismantled by a vandal and the group ends up stranded, with Ralph nearly lost on a garbage barge before Skinner performs a daring rescue using a crane and physics. Stranded together, Skinner wins the boys' respect by reading them Huckleberry Finn as their barge drifts back toward Springfield Elementary. Meanwhile, Homer discovers his home insurance lapsed until 3:00 PM and frantically tries to prevent any injuries in his house while hosting Marge's chaotic book club, imagining a string of gruesome accidents befalling the members. Back at school, Lisa is paralyzed with anxiety over the assessment test, fixating on Bart's supposed superior score and failing to answer any questions. Skinner returns just as the test is ending, canceling it and lifting the school's dance ban, leading to a celebratory dance for the students. Notable quotes: Principal Skinner: Ralph, are you almost finished? | Ralph: I finished before we came in
quotes: Principal Skinner: Ralph, are you almost finished?
Ralph: I finished before we came in

title: The Devil Wears Nada (S21E05)
text: "The Devil Wears Nada" is an episode of Season 21 (production code LABF17), directed by Nancy Kruse and written by Tim Long, originally airing November 15, 2009. Marge and her Charity Chicks group agree to pose for a sexy historical calendar to raise money, but after a photographer plies her with wine, her photos become racier than intended, making her the talk of Springfield. At the plant, Mr. Burns promotes Carl to supervisor over Homer and Lenny, and Carl in turn makes Homer his overworked executive assistant. As Marge's newfound fame boosts her libido, Homer is too exhausted from Carl's demands to satisfy her, straining their marriage further when Carl whisks Homer off to a nuclear power expo in Paris. Left alone and frustrated, Marge accidentally injures Ned Flanders with a croquet mallet and invites his family over for dinner to apologize, but the kids all bail, leaving Marge and Ned alone for an unexpectedly romantic evening. Meanwhile in Paris, Carl becomes infatuated with a Frenchwoman who turns out to be Carla Bruni, wife of President Sarkozy, giving Homer leverage to blackmail his way back to his old job. Marge and Ned nearly kiss but she stops herself after glimpsing her wedding photo reflected in his glasses. Homer returns home just in time to interrupt Ned's goodnight, and he and Marge reconcile passionately, finally uninterrupted. Guest starring Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Homer: Lick - eyes! [throws again] Spank - hair! [throws again] Whisper into - ass! Ohh! | Agnes Skinner: Let me just check the calendar | Agnes: Eww... Wiggum! | Ned Flanders: [After nearly kissing Marge] Saved by the bell from an eternity in Hell!

title: The Fool Monty (S22E06)
text: "The Fool Monty" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF01), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Michael Price, originally airing November 21, 2010. When a mysterious House Cat Flu sparks panic in Springfield, the town lines up for a rationed vaccine, only to have Mr. Burns push to the front and demand three dozen doses for himself, Smithers, and his dogs, destroying the town's supply in the process. Soon after, Burns' doctor tells him he has only weeks to live, prompting the old man to attempt a dramatic suicide by leaping off a cliff, which he hilariously survives with total amnesia. Bart discovers the confused billionaire in the woods and brings him back to town, where the still-furious citizens set up a rotating schedule to torment their childlike former tormentor. As Lisa cares for him, a photo at his mansion jolts his memory back, restoring his malice just as Smithers, now working as an aide to Dick Cheney, grows disillusioned with his new employer. Burns retrieves Smithers and plots an aerial revenge scheme to trap Springfield under a dome, unaware the town has already lived through that exact ordeal before. Realizing his survival is tied to acts of kindness rather than spite, Burns experiments with both traits before concluding that bitterness is what truly sustains him. In the end, Nelson coerces Burns into playing his father for a school play by threatening to crash their helicopter, and Burns begrudgingly ends up enjoying the experience. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: I'll have 37 snifters of your influenza syrup. One for me, one for Smithers, and the rest for my hounds. | Homer: This town can't teach its kids or collect its garbage, but we lead the nation in pointless revenge. | Mayor Quimby: Give him what he wants. He's the only tax payer in this town. | Comic Book Guy: Because I am afraid of needles, but Wolverine is not. | Mr. Burns: And have me smell like cheap drug store cologne the rest of the day? You may hug my shadow.

title: Luca$ (S25E17)
text: "Luca$" is an episode of Season 25 (production code SABF12), directed by Chris Clements and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing April 6, 2014. After a wild night out leaves Homer trapped in a schoolyard jungle gym, Bart hides in the treehouse and stumbles upon Snake hiding from Chief Wiggum. Bart covers for him, and a grateful Snake begins leaving Bart stolen loot, which raises Milhouse's suspicions and eventually leads to Snake being turned in and sentenced to the electric chair, forcing Bart to intervene and get him released. Meanwhile, Lisa saves a boy named Lucas Bortner from choking and quickly becomes infatuated with him, only to learn he's an aspiring competitive eater. Marge grows alarmed that Lisa is falling for another Homer-like figure and pushes Homer to take Lisa on a fancy 'gentleman's date' to model proper behavior, which offends Homer since he feels Marge is ashamed of who he is. The date turns emotional when Marge shows up to apologize, revealing she sold her unused sewing machine to buy a nice dress for the occasion, and the two reconcile. In the end, Lucas abandons competitive eating to pursue a singing career like Adele, leaving Lisa to attempt (unsuccessfully) to teach him how to whistle, while Snake vows to go straight to avoid execution. Guest starring Zach Galifianakis as Lucas Bortner. Notable quotes: Homer: But I did learn something from all this: The sprinklers in this park come on at 3:00 a.m. | Milhouse Van Houten: A fat kid with a dream? I can't compete with that. | Lisa: I won't be using the correct term then. | Homer: Then that makes me the Jackie Robinson of the sport, and you are the racist Philadelphia manager! | Patty Bouvier: Women marry their fathers, Marge. So you just might be meeting your future "ton-in-law."

title: Homer and Lisa Exchange Cross Words (S20E06)
keys: homer and lisa exchange cross words
text: "Homer and Lisa Exchange Cross Words" is an episode of Season 20 (production code KABF19), directed by Nancy Kruse and written by Tim Long, originally airing November 16, 2008. After helping a stranger at the bank complete a crossword, Lisa discovers she has a natural talent for the puzzles and becomes increasingly obsessed with them. She enters a citywide crossword tournament held at a local pub and quickly rises through the ranks, impressing everyone with her skill. Homer, meanwhile, realizes he can make money betting on the matches and starts wagering on his daughter's success. In the championship round, he secretly bets against Lisa, and thanks to a distraction engineered by Gil Gunderson, she loses the final match while Homer collects his winnings. When Lisa learns that her father bet against her, she is devastated and furious, and in protest she abandons the Simpson name in favor of her mother's maiden name, Bouvier. Desperate to make amends, Homer enlists the help of real-life crossword luminaries Will Shortz and Merl Reagle, who assist him in crafting a secret message to Lisa hidden within an actual New York Times crossword puzzle. The heartfelt gesture helps mend their relationship, and Lisa forgives her father. Guest starring Merl Reagle as himself, Will Shortz as himself, Scott Thompson as Grady Little. title: The Saga of Carl (S24E21)
text: "The Saga of Carl" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF14), directed by Chuck Sheetz and written by Eric Kaplan, originally airing May 19, 2013. Bart and Lisa's obsession with the show Ki-Ya Karate Monsters drives Marge to take the family to the Science Museum, where an exhibit on probability convinces Homer that the lottery is a waste of money—right before he and his buddies Moe, Lenny, and Carl win it anyway. When Carl vanishes with the winnings instead of returning to the celebration, the trio investigates and discovers he's fled to Iceland, tracing clues to his ancestral homeland near Reykjavík. There they learn the Carlson family is infamous for supposedly betraying their countrymen to invaders centuries ago, and after tracking down Carl, they angrily seize a briefcase they assume holds their stolen cash. Instead it contains a historical saga page Carl was trying to use to clear his family's name, claiming they fought bravely rather than betrayed anyone. Translating the ancient text on the bus home, the friends discover the truth is even worse—the Carlsons actively joined the slaughter—meaning Carl's theft accomplished nothing. Feeling sympathy despite everything, the guys publicly vouch for Carl's good deeds to the Icelandic townspeople, who forgive the Carlson family at last. Back in Springfield, Homer surprises his family with makeshift 'keg pools' instead of a real pool, and the episode ends with him comically stuck inside one as everyone laughs. Guest starring Sigur Rós. Notable quotes: Homer: Four lucky numbers for four best friends. | Moe: I had plans for that money too—I was gonna be one of those guys who's really into hot sauce! Hot sauce suspenders, hot sauce pajamas, bolo tie with a little chili pepper on it... | Homer: Just say he's black, Moe. | Carl: We are just guys who sit next to each other at a bar and talk about guy stuff. | Moe: Apparently screwing over your friends is in Carl's blood—his adopted blood.
