title: Walking Big & Tall (S26E13)
text: "Walking Big & Tall" is an episode of Season 26 (production code TABF06), directed by Chris Clements and written by Michael Price, originally airing February 8, 2015. Lisa discovers that Springfield's beloved town anthem was actually plagiarized from another city, prompting her to feel a civic duty to fix the wrong. She sets out to write a brand-new anthem for Springfield, navigating the town's skepticism and pride in its old, stolen song. Meanwhile, Marge grows concerned about Homer's weight and health, urging him to attend a weight-loss support group to slim down. Homer attends, but instead of joining the group dedicated to losing weight, he mistakenly falls in with a different group that celebrates and embraces obesity rather than fighting it. Homer quickly becomes enamored with this community's philosophy of self-acceptance, abandoning any real effort to get healthier. As Lisa works to gain the town's acceptance of her new anthem, Homer's involvement with his new group leads to some eye-opening and comedic realizations about health and self-image. Eventually, both storylines reach a resolution as Springfield begins to embrace change—Lisa's replacement anthem gains traction, and Homer confronts the consequences of his choices regarding his health and identity within the group.

title: Homer the Whopper (S21E01)
text: "Homer the Whopper" is an episode of Season 21 (production code LABF13), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Seth Rogen, Evan Goldberg, originally airing September 27, 2009. Comic Book Guy secretly writes his own comic, Everyman, which Bart and Milhouse discover and convince him to publish. The comic becomes a massive hit across Springfield, catching the attention of two rival movie studios who both want to adapt it into a summer blockbuster. Ginormous Pictures secures the rights and lets Comic Book Guy cast the lead, and after rejecting every Hollywood hunk, he chooses an overweight Homer, who happened to wander into his shop. Homer is thrilled to star but is told he must slim down, so the studio hires trainer Lyle McCarthy to whip him into shape, which reinvigorates his marriage to Marge. However, once Lyle leaves for another client, Homer relapses into binge eating, causing his weight to fluctuate wildly during filming and creating continuity nightmares. Meanwhile, Comic Book Guy is gradually pushed out of creative control over his own creation as Hollywood reshapes his life and family. When the finished film is finally test-screened, it's a disastrous flop due to Homer's inconsistent appearance and story problems. Studio executives offer Comic Book Guy the chance to direct a sequel if he publicly lies about liking the film, but he refuses and instead declares it the worst movie ever. Guest starring Matt Groening as himself, Kevin Michael Richardson as the Ginormous Pictures security guard, Seth Rogen as Lyle McCarthy. Notable quotes: Comic Book Guy: Shut up! No one is interested in the critical judgment of a worthless child... | Comic Book Guy: I played hardball with Hollywood! The closest I will ever come to playing a sport in my life! | Lyle McCarthy: Take my hand, Homer. And wave goodbye to fat you. | Homer: Because I'm swallowing my frustrations and disappointments? | Comic Book Guy: You... Are... Acceptable!

title: Go Big or Go Homer (S31E02)
text: "Go Big or Go Homer" is an episode of Season 31 (production code YABF21), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by John Frink, originally airing October 6, 2019. After Mr. Burns steals the spotlight at Lenny's surprise birthday party, an already irritable Homer confronts him, only to learn that Burns' new medication has made him incapable of being cruel. As punishment for questioning him, Homer is demoted to supervising the plant's interns, where he's mocked until 35-year-old intern Mike Wegman, an obsessive fan, defends him and begs Homer to be his mentor. Flattered, Homer embraces the role, buying a new wardrobe and bringing Mike home for dinner, where Mike's violent devotion to defending Homer's honor terrifies the family. Marge urges Homer to help Mike mature, so Homer encourages him to pursue his pizza-truck business idea, Mike's Slices, and pitches it to Burns, whose insult sets off another of Mike's rages, resulting in Burns shooting him. Guilt-ridden, Homer admits he isn't the wise mentor Mike believes him to be, but this confession only spurs Mike to chase his dream harder, and he secures a food truck using money borrowed from mob boss Fat Tony. When Mike can't repay the loan after a bad bet, he and Homer flee to a truck graveyard, where Fat Tony catches up but is won over by the quality of the pizza and Mike's business instincts. The episode ends with the food truck permanently stationed outside the plant serving multiple purposes, and Fat Tony praising Homer for mentoring Mike so well. Guest starring Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony, Michael Rapaport as Mike Wegman. Notable quotes: Homer: Stupid unpaid signature. This is the worst thing that ever happened at a nuclear power plant. | Mike Wegman: This man is a god and his clangers are unbustable. You're looking at the Michael Jordan of Sector 7G. | Homer: Well, now that I'm a mentor, everything's changed. For the first time, another human being is dependent on me to guide them through life. | Bart: Oh, I get it. He's super dumb. | Mr. Burns: Then it's my pleasure to tell you... that that is the stupidest idea I've ever heard. Get this intern out of my office, you nincompoop!

title: Super Franchise Me (S26E03)
text: "Super Franchise Me" is an episode of Season 26 (production code SABF19), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Bill Odenkirk, originally airing October 12, 2014. After Marge's homemade sandwiches become a lunchtime sensation at Springfield Elementary, she decides to turn her hobby into a business by opening a sandwich shop called Mother Hubbard's Sandwich Cupboard. At home, Lisa and Bart request massive batches of sandwiches, revealing that the kids at school have started using them as a bartering currency in place of contraband like cigarettes. Marge's freezer space runs short, forcing her to borrow Ned Flanders' freezer to store the overflow, which leads to some awkward but comedic interactions between Homer and Ned. As Marge's shop grows in popularity, the strain of managing daily operations begins to wear on her, showing that running a business is far more complicated than she anticipated. Just as she starts to find her footing, a corporate rival opens an identical sandwich franchise directly across the street, undercutting her customer base. Marge is forced to compete against this copycat business while trying to maintain quality and her own sanity. The family pitches in various ways, and even quirky Springfield residents like Professor Frink get roped into promotional efforts for the shop. Ultimately, Marge must decide how to balance her entrepreneurial ambitions with the toll it's taking on her family life, resolving the conflict with the rival franchise in a way that reasserts the value of her original, personal touch. Notable quotes: Homer: Seriously, I am getting so tired of those stupid Flandersisms. | Bart: They replaced cigarettes as our currency. | Homer: Woo Hoo! Flanders isn't perfect! | Lisa: No, whenever anything bothers me, I harmlessly vent it to Maggie. | Marge: Professor, could you say, "Welcome to Mother Hubbard's Sandwich Cupboard" without making any other noises?

title: Angry Dad: The Movie (S22E14)
text: "Angry Dad: The Movie" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF07), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by John Frink, originally airing February 20, 2011. Left home alone while the family gets frozen yogurt, Bart wrecks the house with a skateboard-and-ceiling-fan contraption, only for chaos to escalate when Herman Millwood arrives wanting to turn Bart's web cartoon Angry Dad into a movie. With original voice actor Dan Castellaneta unable to perform after losing his voice, Homer steps in as Angry Dad, though his laziness nearly sinks the project until it's trimmed into a short film. The short becomes an unexpected awards-season sensation, but at each ceremony—from the Golden Globes to the Children's Choice Awards to the Kennedy Center Honors—Homer rushes onstage and steals the recognition that should go to Bart. Furious, Bart deliberately withholds the news of an Oscar nomination and instead sends Homer on a bogus sightseeing trip to the Watts Towers, hoping to sabotage him. Homer's antics there accidentally connect him with DJ Kwanzaa and the Rolling 80s gang, who end up giving the Simpsons a ride to the Academy Awards just in time. Angry Dad wins the Oscar, and this time Bart takes the stage, generously crediting the whole crew and breaking the trophy into pieces to share with everyone who worked on the film. In a closing gag, an emotional Ricky Gervais realizes the man he's been bonding with is not Ridley Scott but merely a seat filler. Guest starring Halle Berry, Russell Brand, Ricky Gervais, Maurice LaMarche, Nick Park, J. B. Smoove. Notable quotes: Bart: That's "Angry Dad"! The semi-autobiographical web cartoon I created! | Homer: I legally forced him to say "semi". | DJ Kwanzaa: Damn, Home-Simp—you've been Oscar-blocked! What do you think about that, Nasty J? | Homer: I was born a Rollin' Eighty, and I'll die a Rollin' Eighty. | Halle Berry: When most people think of animated movies, they think of forty minutes or more. But there is another type of animated film—forty minutes or less!

title: The Man from G.R.A.M.P.A. (S32E21)
text: "The Man from G.R.A.M.P.A." is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF13), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing May 16, 2021. In 1970 London, a young MI5 agent named Terrance begins a decades-long hunt for an American double agent code-named the Grey Fox, finally tracing him to Springfield fifty years later. Terrance moves into the Retirement Castle, sparking a squabble among the residents over a vacated room, and becomes convinced that Grampa is the elusive spy. He recruits a skeptical Homer to help investigate, plying him and his friends with drinks at Moe's before revealing his suspicions. Together they stake out Abe, with Terrance disguising himself as an old woman, and witness Abe swapping canes and receiving a mysterious package from two men they assume are Russian agents. Their surveillance escalates into a chaotic car chase and an attempt to smuggle Abe away from the Retirement Castle before Terrance can act on his suspicions. Abe eventually explains the innocent truth—the men were Canadians delivering his blood pressure medication, and the cane swap was just senior confusion. When police intervene and arrest Terrance for kidnapping, Abe selflessly claims to be the real Grey Fox to protect him, and the misunderstanding is resolved as Homer and Terrance return home. Meanwhile, a subplot about Lisa suspecting Maggie of speaking Russian is revealed to be nothing more than a Russian-made toy's animal sounds. Guest starring Stephen Fry as Terrance, Terrance's father, Hazel, and the head of MI5. Notable quotes: Grampa: What's my greatest fear? | Homer: Cocktail olives and fascism. | Terrance: And I know who you are. You work at the nuclear plant, are married to Marge and have three children. | Homer: No, I only have tw... Wait a minute, you're right. | Moe Szyslak: Every time you sing a song, it's $5,000 in damage.

title: Iron Marge (S35E06)
text: "Iron Marge" is an episode of Season 35 (production code OABF22), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Mike Scully, originally airing November 12, 2023. After a middle-of-the-night car crash wakes the neighborhood, Marge is embarrassed when the other mothers mock her ragged robe, revealing she's never received a proper birthday gift from Bart and Lisa. Determined to do better this year, the kids instead get sidetracked at a store, trading a nice robe for a free ironing board cover so they can also snag a Junior Operative Spy Kit. When Marge opens two ironing board covers on her birthday, she hides her disappointment, but Bart and Lisa overhear her tearfully confessing to Ned Flanders that she feels invisible to her family. Guilt-stricken, they use their new spy gadgets to dig into Marge's forgotten past and learn she once owned a beloved childhood parrot named Petey. Their search leads them to North Townsburg, where they track the bird through a series of former owners before finally luring him down from a tree using a recording of Marge's voice. Meanwhile, Homer becomes obsessed with topping the leaderboard on a neighborhood-watch app called Alarmist, exaggerating and inventing dangers until he clashes with rival alarmist Agnes Skinner, and the two end up trapped together in a sinkhole, where Homer's rescue of a choking Agnes teaches him that real satisfaction comes from helping people, not chasing rankings. Back home, Petey turns out to be aggressive and messy, but his return still touches Marge once she realizes how hard her kids worked to make her feel special. The family sends Petey back to North Townsburg, and the episode ends with Bart, Lisa, and Marge staging a harmless late-night 'mission' with their spy gear, finally bonding as a team. Guest starring Megan Mullally as Sarah Wiggum. Notable quotes: Bart: What do you get for the woman who has only one ironing board cover? | Bart: She's in my phone contacts three times—Under "mom," "mommy" and "sandwich." | Homer: I smell like a lot of things. | Homer: No, I'm asking. I don't know what ironic means. | Bart: We did not make friends on the bus ride home. Petey is kind of racist.

title: Waiting for Duffman (S26E17)
text: "Waiting for Duffman" is an episode of Season 26 (production code TABF10), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by John Frink, originally airing March 15, 2015. When Duffman requires hip replacement surgery, he decides to retire, leaving the Duff company without its beloved mascot. To find a successor, Duff launches a televised competition called 'So You Think You Can Duff?' drawing in a wide range of eccentric contestants. Homer, eager for fame and free beer, enters the contest and surprises everyone by winning the coveted mascot role. His victory is complicated by a major catch: Duffman is contractually required to remain completely sober, forcing Homer to give up drinking entirely. Struggling to adjust, Homer fears he won't be able to have fun without alcohol, leading to tension at home as Marge and the kids worry about the toll his new lifestyle and public duties take on him. Meanwhile, Lisa grows increasingly anxious about the family's repeated public humiliations, prompting sessions with a family therapist who is rarely actually present. As Homer settles into his new identity, he discovers that he can indeed enjoy life and entertain crowds without needing beer, finding unexpected confidence and purpose in his sober persona. By the episode's end, Homer embraces his new role as Duffman, having grown both personally and as a father despite the unusual circumstances of his job. Guest starring Cat Deeley, R. Lee Ermey, Stacy Keach. Notable quotes: Homer: I will do something no one has ever done, be fun sober! | Marge: These reality shows really leave you no privacy. | Homer: You wouldn't tell Batman he can't eat bats! | Lisa: I'm not sure how many more times we can watch dad chased down by an angry crowd before it affects us psychologically. | Marge: Why is Lisa talking to an empty seat?

Marge: These reality shows really leave you no privacy.

title: My Way or the Highway to Heaven (S30E03)
keys: my way or the highway to heaven
text: "My Way or the Highway to Heaven" is an episode of Season 30 (production code XABF17), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Deb Lacusta, Dan Castellaneta, Vince Waldron, originally airing October 14, 2018. In Heaven, God and St. Peter fret over declining admissions and decide to review three test cases to loosen the entry rules. Ned Flanders recounts his irreligious Beatnik upbringing and his brief, lucrative career selling trampolines, which turns disastrous when the devices prove deadly; he sacrifices himself to save young Homer from electrocution and is sent to meet Jesus, who offers him a path to redemption and a second chance at life devoted to God. Marge then tells the tale of her freethinking grandmother Genevieve, who runs a French café with her Nazi-collaborator husband Meaux during World War II, and who cleverly disguises trapped American paratroopers, including a young Abraham Simpson, as waiters to protect them from German soldiers, ultimately helping them fight back and survive. Marge's point is that atheists can be heroic too, persuading God to open Heaven's doors to nonbelievers. Lisa's contribution reimagines the story of Buddha through Princess Siddmartha, a bored royal who sneaks out disguised as a poor boy to discover the hardships and joys of ordinary life, eventually attaining enlightenment after a long spiritual journey. Moved by all three stories, God decides to admit all good souls into Heaven, not just the traditionally faithful. Back on Earth, the Flanders family experiences what they think is divine thunder, actually a bowling pin dropped by clumsy angels, which St. Peter apologizes for while the family cheerfully accepts it as a blessing. Guest starring H. Jon Benjamin as Bob Belcher, Jon Lovitz as himself, Dan Mintz as Tina Belcher, Eugene Mirman as Gene Belcher, Tracy Morgan as himself, John Roberts as Linda Belcher, Kristen Schaal as Louise Belcher. Notable quotes: Lisa: Let me share the Buddhist path to heaven with an enlightened tale I call 'The Princess Not Affiliated with Disney'... unless we are now owned by Disney.
quotes: Lisa: Let me share the Buddhist path to heaven with an enlightened tale I call 'The Princess Not Affiliated with Disney'... unless we are now owned by Disney.

title: Halloween of Horror (S27E04)
text: "Halloween of Horror" is an episode of Season 27 (production code TABF22), directed by Mike B. Anderson and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing October 18, 2015. The day before Halloween, Homer finishes his elaborate 'Everscream Terrors' yard display, then heads to a Halloween pop-up store where he unwittingly gets three lazy employees fired after mentioning a shady discount deal to the store's manager, Apu. The furious ex-workers vow revenge on Homer. Meanwhile, Homer takes Lisa and Bart to Krustyland's Halloween Horror Night, where Lisa becomes so terrified that she gets lost and the event is shut down, leaving her traumatized by even mild Halloween imagery afterward. Marge insists Homer dismantle his home haunt to help Lisa cope, upsetting both Homer and Bart, so Marge tries to make it up to Bart by taking him and Maggie to an exclusive neighborhood block party while Homer stays home with Lisa. That night, the vengeful ex-employees break into the Simpson house to torment Homer, forcing him and Lisa to hide in the attic while Marge and the kids are turned away from the party and head home too late to help. Lisa's comfort object, a plush tail called Tailee, ends up being sacrificed as kindling to light emergency fireworks that signal for help. The homeowners are rescued, the invaders are arrested, and Homer rebuilds his Halloween decorations for the whole town to enjoy. Guest starring Blake Anderson as Dickie, Nick Kroll as Lem. I've lied to you more times than there are stars in the sky but I gotta be straight — this is real. But you can't let fear shut down your brain because between the two of us you've got the only good one. | Robbers: Sooner or later, you're going to have to buy Thanksgiving decorations, and we'll be waiting for you by the Indian corn! | Homer: How can you reject a holiday where you can serve candy from a salad bowl? | Homer: I'm the Mozart of Halloween decorations and tonight is the Super Bowl!

title: Million Dollar Maybe (S21E11)
text: "Million Dollar Maybe" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF03), directed by Chris Clements and written by Bill Odenkirk, originally airing January 31, 2010. Homer skips a promised singing toast at his cousin Valerie's wedding to buy a lottery ticket after a fortune cookie convinces him it's his lucky day, leaving Marge humiliated. On his way home he narrowly causes a car crash and wakes up in the hospital to learn his ticket won a million dollars. Terrified of admitting he ditched the wedding for the lottery, Homer has Barney pretend to be the winner and secretly showers his family with gifts, hiding cash in odd places like a tree. Bart discovers the money and blackmails Homer into servitude, threatening to expose his lie to Marge. Exhausted by being Bart's slave, Homer decides to come clean, taking Marge on a hot-air balloon ride where he confesses everything, including that he's already spent all the winnings. Marge is upset only briefly, then reassures Homer that having each other matters more than money, and the two finally perform their wedding toast song together. Meanwhile, Lisa notices the seniors at the Springfield Retirement Castle are bored and buys them a motion-sensing video game system after seeing it rejuvenate Mr. Burns; the residents become lively and youthful again until overworked nurses ruin the console by washing it, returning everyone to their dull routine. Guest starring Chris Martin as himself. Notable quotes: Bart: Can I just ask, who the hell says po-tah-to? | Homer: Songwriters who are stuck. | Mr. Burns: Oh, I feel like I'm mashing the tufty on the links at St. Andrew's! | Homer: Son, if I was interested in fun, I would've run away the day you were born. | Homer: You're right. I have been acting like telethon Jerry Lewis when I should've been acting like rest-of-the-year Jerry Lewis.

title: Elementary School Musical (S22E01)
text: "Elementary School Musical" is an episode of Season 22 (production code MABF21), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Tim Long, originally airing September 26, 2010. When Krusty the Clown unexpectedly wins the Nobel Peace Prize, he invites Homer, his most loyal laugher, and Bart to accompany him to Europe to collect it. Meanwhile, Marge takes a bored Lisa to Expressions, a performing arts camp led by quirky counselors Kurt Hardwick and Ethan Ballantyne, where she bonds with fellow young artists Aiesha, Sarah, and Flynn through music and creativity. Krusty's trip takes a turn when he's detained in The Hague and put on trial before the International Court of Justice for corrupting Western culture, forcing Homer and Bart to dig up evidence of any good he's done. They discover that one of Krusty's tantrums indirectly contributed to Nelson Mandela's release, which is enough to get him acquitted. Back home, Lisa's camp experience ends, but she becomes convinced that her counselors' promises of a glamorous artistic life in Sprooklyn are real, so she runs away to find them. Instead of glamour, she finds a decaying, crime-ridden neighborhood where Kurt and Ethan are barely scraping by working at a sandwich shop. Disillusioned, Lisa calls Marge to take her home, but not before the counselors leave her with one final magical, whimsical surprise as she departs. Guest starring Jemaine Clement, Ira Glass, Stephen Hawking, Lea Michele, Bret McKenzie, Cory Monteith, Amber Riley. Notable quotes: Sarah: Goodbye, Lisa! I'll miss you a lot, then a little, then not too much! | Lisa: Quiet! It's time for the noblest Nobel Prize of all: the Peace Prize. | Homer: I'd kill for that.
quotes: Sarah: Goodbye, Lisa! I'll miss you a lot, then a little, then not too much!
Lisa: Quiet! It's time for the noblest Nobel Prize of all: the Peace Prize.

title: Treehouse of Horror XXIII (S24E02)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXIII" is an episode of Season 24 (production code PABF17), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by David Mandel, Brian Kelley, originally airing October 7, 2012. This Treehouse of Horror opens with ancient Mayan priests miscalculating a human sacrifice, leading to a comic reveal that the world truly will end in 2012, followed by an alien apocalypse in the present day. In 'The Greatest Story Ever Holed,' Springfield's new supercollider spawns a growing black hole that the Simpsons foolishly use as a garbage disposal, eventually swallowing much of the town before Maggie's pacifier tames it, and the sucked-in townspeople find themselves worshipped as gift-givers by strange alien beings. In 'UNnormal Activity,' the Simpsons are tormented by a demonic presence that turns out to be tied to a childhood pact Marge made with the devil to save her sisters, promising him her favorite child; the family exposes the demon, and a chaotic renegotiation ends with Homer proposing an ill-fated three-way. In 'Bart & Homer's Excellent Adventure,' Bart travels back to 1974 to buy a comic at cover price, but his interference causes teenage Marge to reject teenage Homer, altering the timeline so Bart becomes 'Barty Ziff,' son of Artie Ziff and Marge. Multiple versions of Homer from different eras team up to fight Artie for Marge's affection, but they are easily defeated, prompting Marge to realize her mistake and reunite with all the Homers, who still can't manage to take out the trash. Guest starring Jon Lovitz as Artie Ziff. Notable quotes: Homer: Oh, sweetie, sometimes a mysterious, invisible being from hell waits for a family to go to sleep then kills them. Now go to bed. | Homer: Okay, it's possible that someone may have started a business called "Magic Craphole Waste Removal," but it wasn't me. | Bart: I'm your unwanted son from the future, who killed all your fun! | Homer: Now, before we start what's the safe word? | Marge Ziff: Lemme get this straight. None of you had time to take out the garbage? This installment is made up of 3 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 23): "The Greatest Story Ever Holed", "UNnormal Activity", and "Bart & Homer's Excellent Adventure".
quotes: Homer: Oh, sweetie, sometimes a mysterious, invisible being from hell waits for a family to go to sleep then kills them. Now go to bed.

title: Blazed and Confused (S26E07)
text: "Blazed and Confused" is an episode of Season 26 (production code TABF01), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Carolyn Omine, William Wright, originally airing November 16, 2014. Springfield Elementary hires a strict new teacher, Jack Lassen, who is assigned to Bart's class and quickly reveals himself to be a harsh bully toward the students. Bart, tired of being humiliated, decides he needs to find a way to expose Lassen's weaknesses and get him removed. He discovers that Lassen is deeply invested in the secretive fraternal order known as the Blazing Guys, a local men's lodge with elaborate rituals. Seeing an opportunity, Bart convinces his family to help him infiltrate the group's activities in order to publicly embarrass Lassen during an event that means a great deal to him. Meanwhile, Marge grapples with her own tendency to hope for good things despite repeated disappointments, including a mishandled camping trip that Homer forgot to cancel. As the Simpsons work their way into the Blazing Guys' world, tensions rise between Bart's scheme and the adult politics of the secretive club. In the end, Bart's plan culminates in a public confrontation that strips away Lassen's authority and reputation among his peers, giving Bart the upper hand and forcing the teacher to back down from his bullying ways. Guest starring Willem Dafoe as Jack Lassen, Kelsey Grammer as Sideshow Bob. Notable quotes: Mr. Lassen: I'm Mr. Lassen. | Nelson Muntz: You mean Mr. Less-than? | Marge: My biggest sin is that I dare to hope. | Homer: You're right. No one can be expected to remember something from a year ago. Certainly not me. | Blazing Guy member: Have him be stripped of his nudity!

title: Much Apu About Something (S27E12)
text: "Much Apu About Something" is an episode of Season 27 (production code VABF05), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Michael Price, originally airing January 17, 2016. During Springfield's parade honoring Jebediah Springfield, Bart sets off a fire engine's water cannon, sparking a chaotic turf war between the police and fire departments that ends with a SWAT tank crashing into the Kwik-E-Mart, injuring Apu and Sanjay. Recovering in the hospital, Sanjay decides to retire and hands over his ownership stake to his son Jamshed, now going by 'Jay.' Shaken by the destruction his prank caused, Homer forces Bart to swear off pranking forever, and Bart's newfound maturity improves his grades and his relationship with Lisa. Weeks later, Apu discovers the Kwik-E-Mart has been replaced by Jay's trendy health-food store, Quick & Fresh, and learns he's been reduced to a minority stakeholder due to his scratch-ticket addiction. After Jay mocks Apu as an ethnic stereotype and fires him, a devastated Apu turns to Moe, who convinces Homer to let Bart return to pranking one last time to help reclaim the store. Bart plans a harmless-seeming stunt of cutting the power for thirty seconds to spoil the preservative-free food, but Lisa's talk about unconditional love gets misinterpreted by Bart as permission to do whatever he wants. The blackout ruins the store's stock and causes a fire that the depleted fire department can't extinguish, burning Quick & Fresh to the ground. In the aftermath, Apu finds an intact scratch ticket in the wreckage that wins him a million dollars, giving him enough money to buy back his beloved Kwik-E-Mart. Guest starring Utkarsh Ambudkar as Jay Nahasapeemapetilon. Notable quotes: Jay: I'm Indian, I do yoga. title: The Ten-Per-Cent Solution (S23E08)
text: "The Ten-Per-Cent Solution" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF02), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Deb Lacusta, Dan Castellaneta, originally airing December 4, 2011. After his TV show is cancelled and his agent drops him, Krusty the Clown hits rock bottom and ends up living in the ball pit at Krusty Burger, where the Simpson kids find him. They connect him with Annie Dubinsky, his former agent and old flame, whom he abandoned decades earlier after she discovered and transformed him into a star. Despite her lingering resentment, Annie agrees to represent Krusty again and engineers a comeback with a new show, 'The Krusty the Clown Show Retro Reboot!', which becomes a massive hit. The success leads to a lucrative offer from network HBOWTIME, and Krusty and Annie rekindle their romance while working together as producer and star. However, Annie's abrasive, demanding personality quickly clashes with network executives, especially after she disrupts guest appearances by Kevin Dillon and Janeane Garofalo. When the executives pressure Krusty to fire her, he refuses out of loyalty and love, and the two walk away from the show together. They ultimately find new success starring in their own series, 'Sex Over Sixty', proving their partnership can thrive outside the corporate system. Guest starring Kevin Dillon, Janeane Garofalo, Jackie Mason, Joan Rivers. Notable quotes: Krusty the Clown: Why is my show all cartoons?! And all the movies they're making fun of are over a year old. | Homer: Oh, my pants are splitting wide open. And people will see my tattoo of Donald Duck smoking a doob! | Annie Dubinsky: I will never forgive you for what you did to me. | Krusty: This morning I was a star, with a top agent. Now I'm strung out in a ball pit! | Lisa: Well, you're not exactly my hero. I see you more as a cautionary tale.

title: Undercover Burns (S32E01)
text: "Undercover Burns" is an episode of Season 32 (production code ZABF19), directed by Bob Anderson and written by David Cryan, originally airing September 27, 2020. On Take Your Kids to Work Day at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, Mr. Burns callously forces the children into labor, prompting Lisa to confront him before he flees into the men's room, where he discovers graffiti and an effigy revealing just how despised he is by his employees. Shaken, Burns has Smithers and a team build him a robotic disguise so he can walk among the workers as the friendly Fred Kranepool and learn what they really think of him. Fred quickly bonds with Homer, Lenny, and Carl over beers at Moe's and outings around town, and genuinely starts improving conditions at the plant out of newfound affection for his employees. Smithers grows increasingly jealous and alarmed as Burns seems ready to abandon his old identity permanently, especially after Fred delivers a convincing in-character scene arguing for treating the workers better. Tensions boil over when Lenny insults Mr. Burns in front of Fred, causing the robotic persona to violently snap and attack Lenny, exposing the danger of the disguise. Homer breaks the suit's arm to stop the assault, and the true Burns inside briefly regains control, leading to a physical and philosophical struggle between Burns and the Fred persona. After both sides make their case, things settle back into the normal cynical status quo of boss versus employees, revealing the man in the fight was actually one of Fred's creators. The plant returns to its old grim self, though a rebuilt Fred suit is later reintroduced as a new coworker, allowing Burns to continue quietly enjoying karaoke nights with Homer and friends. Guest starring David Harbour as Fred Kranepool, Phil Rosenthal as himself. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: This plant has over 17,000 contaminated crevices that only your tiny hands can reach. Get to work, slackers. | Lenny Leonard: I heard the craziest thing. Some nuclear plants don't have hounds chasing you. | Lenny: Mr. Burns is a withered old corn husk with a rotten apple for a head, and I'm getting special clogs made up so I can riverdance on his grave. | Fred: Because I'm the last spark of goodness in you. It can't be extinguished! | Mr. Burns: I'm glad I went to the bathroom in you.

title: Desperately Seeking Lisa (S36E03)
text: "Desperately Seeking Lisa" is an episode of Season 36 (production code 35ABF18), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Tim Long, originally airing October 20, 2024. Lisa is sent to Capital City for the weekend with her aunts Patty and Selma so Marge can get a break from their constant arguing. After a big meal leaves the aunts sick and asleep, Lisa sneaks out to join Julian, a charming artist, and his bohemian friends at a wild loft party. Dazzled by their world, she helps them move art to a museum and is invited to a late-night event, where she inadvertently improves a play by interrupting it, catching the attention of celebrated playwright Tracy Letts. Encouraged by the artists, Lisa seeks funding from the eccentric heiress Lacey Van Aster to attend the prestigious Horace Frick Academy, only to discover that Julian and his friends are running a con to scam wealthy admirers like Lacey and past victim Martin Prince. Fleeing with the check, Lisa becomes the target of the whole artist community, who brand her a thief through mocking artwork, and she spends a chaotic night dodging them while crossing paths with Superintendent Chalmers' secret romantic escapades. Exhausted and hallucinating from sleep deprivation, she narrowly escapes by cutting herself free during a parade balloon mishap after Julian insults Katya. Lisa eventually makes her way home to Springfield, returning to the ordinary comfort of her classroom and family life, having learned a hard lesson about being seduced by glamorous strangers. Guest starring Griffin Dunne, Richard E. Grant, Tracy Letts, Molly Shannon. Notable quotes: Homer: I'm glad I don't have a daughter. | Julian: Yes, it is. Poor, dear Sylvia. The world's loss was that oven's gain. | Patty Bouvier: Out of our way, kid. We got to either sleep or die, and we don't care which one. | Lacey Van Aster: Teddy Roosevelt, Franklin Roosevelt, Eleanor Roosevelt. Every one of them I seduced. And destroyed. | Superintendent Chalmers: Sweet vermouth in a snifter. Lisa Simpson.

title: He Loves to Fly and He D'ohs (S19E01)
keys: he loves to fly and he d'ohs
text: "He Loves to Fly and He D'ohs" is an episode of Season 19 (production code JABF20), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing September 23, 2007. After Mr. Burns nearly drowns reaching for a penny in a mall fountain, Homer saves his life and is rewarded with a lavish trip to Chicago aboard Burns's private jet, complete with gourmet food and a personal serenade from Lionel Richie. The taste of luxury leaves Homer dissatisfied with his ordinary life, so Marge hires quirky life coach Colby Krause to help him chase his dream of a high-flying career. Colby discovers that bowling is the key to unlocking Homer's confidence, and armed with his bowling shoes everywhere he goes, Homer suddenly becomes a magnet for job offers, settling on an interview at a copper tubing company purely because it comes with access to a corporate jet. When the interview goes disastrously wrong, Homer is too embarrassed to tell Marge and instead spends his days hiding out at Krusty Burger, a secret Bart stumbles upon and eventually convinces him to come clean about. Unable to bear disappointing Marge over the phone, Homer instead hires a small plane to take her up in the air so he can break the news in style. Before he can confess, the plane hits turbulence and the pilot passes out, forcing Homer to take the controls himself while Marge frantically calls Colby for guidance. With Colby's motivational coaching over the phone, Homer manages to land the plane safely, after which he decides that private jets are far too dangerous and happily returns to his old job at the power plant.

title: Warrin' Priests: Part Two (S31E20)
text: "Warrin' Priests: Part Two" is an episode of Season 31 (production code ZABF13), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Pete Holmes, originally airing May 3, 2020. As attendance dwindles at the First Church of Springfield, new pastor Bode Wright tries to modernize services by embracing multiple faiths, frustrating traditionalists like Ned Flanders. Lisa is intrigued by Bode's inclusive views on God, while Marge warns her that Springfield never truly accepts change. Reverend Lovejoy and Helen travel to Michigan to investigate why Bode really left his old megachurch, enduring the bizarre practices of Preacher Mac before obtaining proof of a scandal. Meanwhile, Homer helps broker peace between Bode and the town by taking him to Moe's, and Bode wins a scripture debate at the Flanders house. When Lovejoy returns and reveals that Bode was fired for burning a Bible, the congregation turns on him despite his explanation that faith lives in the heart rather than in objects or buildings. Lisa moderates a public debate, but the townspeople reject Bode's plea for understanding, forcing him to leave Springfield. After a farewell dinner with the Simpsons, Bode departs following an act of vandalism, leaving Chief Wiggum disillusioned and the church's future uncertain. Guest starring Pete Holmes as Bode Wright, Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony. Notable quotes: Lisa: Why would you burn a Bible? Why couldn't you burn Bill O'Reilly's books? There are so many. | Ned: This church has gone from a place of warm, awkward silence into a gooey lovefest run by a narcissistic kum-bah-yo-yo, and I will not stand for it. | Fat Tony: This is the first time I've come to church when it's not part of a big montage of my enemies being whacked. | Dr. Nick: Well, I learn from my mistakes. Malpractice makes malperfect. | Chief Wiggum: Just when I understood that guy, when I believed again, when I believed in people, they took him away. I've lost my faith, Lou.

title: It's a Blunderful Life (S35E07)
text: "It's a Blunderful Life" is an episode of Season 35 (production code OABF19), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Elisabeth Kiernan Averick, originally airing November 19, 2023. Sixty years in the future, Lisa tells her family the story of the great Springfield blackout as they mourn the late Homer on Thanksgiving. The tale begins with Marge reminding Homer to install storm windows before a big storm, but he gets distracted by Hawaiian Day festivities at the Power Plant, where Mr. Burns is quietly replacing union workers with non-union hires. A plug overload caused by Burns' phone sparks a fire that triggers a meltdown, and the panicked employees blame Homer for the disaster. As Springfield descends into darkness and chaos, including a debated 'death game' targeting Milhouse, Marge grows suspicious of Homer's innocence when she can't find missing fridge food, accusing him of eating it. Homer proves he actually buried the food in the snow to preserve it, restoring some of Marge's trust and prompting the family to suspect Burns is the true culprit behind the blackout. Fed up townspeople drag the Simpsons' house out of town, stranding it on a rocky outcrop, but the family presses on to confront Burns at his manor. After a failed attempt to dispose of them via a broken trap door, the family exposes Burns' guilt, leading to his arrest and a token fine. Marge then invites the whole town to dinner in exchange for having their house returned, closing out the framed story as future Bart's holographic self and Homer bicker over a turkey leg. Notable quotes: Homer: This isn't Hawaii. It's never Hawaii. It's just stupid America. | Mr. Burns: Welcome, nonunion workers. In an older era, they'd call you scabs. Now you're just friends without benefits. | Power Plant notification: Plant meltdown imminent. Please take this time to get right with your god. Now please put your name tag inside your mouth for the easy identification of your skull. | Mayor Quimby: To take your minds off your troubles, I propose some kind of games. Either "hunger" or "squid." With that in mind, tomorrow we will begin with everyone attempting to kill Milhouse. | Mayor Quimby: Montgomery Burns, we will give you the stiffest punishment any billionaire ever gets. A fine you can easily pay.

title: The Great Phatsby: Part Two (S28E13)
text: "The Great Phatsby: Part Two" is an episode of Season 28 (production code WABF05), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Dan Greaney, Matt Selman, originally airing January 15, 2017. After Mr. Burns is left penniless by Jay G's con, Homer initially stays loyal to Jay G, taking a job at the newly renamed power plant while Marge struggles to keep her whimsical boutique afloat and Bart, seemingly dead, turns out to be fine. Guilt-ridden over abandoning Burns, Homer visits the Burns family mausoleum and reconciles with the old man, and together with Bart they hatch a scheme to publicly humiliate Jay G and destroy his reputation. With help from Milhouse, they recruit rapper Jazzy James, and Burns's ex-wife Praline brings in Snoop Dogg, RZA, and Common to record a diss track aimed at Jay G. The plan collapses when Jay G reveals he simply bought off the rappers with cash, forcing Burns to improvise a new scheme to steal Jay G's prized golden goose and ruin him financially. The theft goes awry when Homer produces the real goose, leading to a frantic chase that ends with Burns and Jay G dangling from a chandelier, where Jay G confesses his ruthless ambition was inspired by Burns's own writings. Meanwhile, Smithers' bizarre trek to fetch ice for Burns finally pays off when he and a group of Canadians arrive just in time to save the two men as the chandelier breaks. Back in Springfield, the family wonders if the ordeal has softened Burns, but when he considers embracing hip-hop culture at the plant, the workers' unenthusiastic reaction makes him quickly abandon the idea. Guest starring Common, Snoop Dogg, Taraji P. Henson, Keegan-Michael Key, RZA. Notable quotes: Homer: F. Scott Fitzgerald once wrote: "There are no second acts in American lives." But he never said anything about second parts in American TV shows. | Mr. Burns: I should've seen it all coming. My eyes were clouded by the cataracts of excess. And by an excess of cataracts. | Bart: If you want to take down a rapper, you got to destroy the thing that's most important to him: his rep. | Homer: Rep means reputation. | Mr. Burns: I swear on the squid beak of Lord Cthulhu and all his briny shoggoths, I will get revenge on you, Jay G.

title: Lisa the Boy Scout (S34E03)
text: "Lisa the Boy Scout" is an episode of Season 34 (production code UABF21), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Dan Greaney, originally airing October 9, 2022. Bart and Lisa's usual rivalry escalates when the Boy Explorers scouting troop becomes co-ed, prompting both siblings to try to out-scout each other at the annual jamboree, only for their antics to end with them getting lost and giving up on the outdoors entirely. Meanwhile, Homer and Marge nearly divorce over something trivial but reconcile through a simple gesture of eye contact. The main storyline is interrupted when a hacker duo calling themselves Pseudo-nonymous seizes control of the broadcast, threatening to release hundreds of hours of unaired, embarrassing Simpsons footage unless Disney pays a $20 million Bitcoin ransom. As the ransom goes unpaid, the hackers release a series of increasingly absurd anthology segments, including revelations that Lenny never existed, that future Bart delivers uncannily real predictions, and that several beloved side characters have shocking secret identities and family ties. Throughout the ordeal, the two hackers, both named Ashley, start bickering and eventually fall in love despite technical mishaps with their voice-changing app. The FBI surrounds their hideout to stop the leaks, but the hackers threaten to expose Disney's new secret intellectual property, Baby Jeff Goldblum, forcing the agents to back down. In the end, the two Ashleys escape together on a scooter, having bonded over their shared name and shared chaos, while the Simpsons family returns to normalcy after their bizarre coma-dream revelations. Guest starring Anna Faris, Matthew Friend, Megan Mullally. Notable quotes: Homer: It is true, Carl. There never was a Lenny. | Homer: Less yelling, more foretelling. | Future Bart: No, they're both absorbed by Panda Express. Pretty much everything now is Panda Express. | Reggie: Look at me, Didi. I'm the only 36-year-old who can pass for ten! | Ned Flanders: That's it. Boys, we're Jewish now.

title: The Food Wife (S23E05)
text: "The Food Wife" is an episode of Season 23 (production code NABF20), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Matt Selman, originally airing November 13, 2011. When Marge feels left out of being the 'Fun Mom,' Homer promises she'll get a chance to take the kids somewhere exciting, but she accidentally brings Bart and Lisa to a Christian sports expo instead of the X Games, leaving everyone disappointed. On the drive home, their car breaks down in Little Ethiopia, and the kids talk a reluctant Marge into trying food at an Ethiopian restaurant, where she discovers she loves it. Inspired by the experience, Marge, Bart, and Lisa start a food blog called the Three Mouthketeers, bonding over restaurant reviews while Homer feels increasingly excluded and jealous of their new hobby. When the family's blog earns them a reservation at the exclusive El Chemistri, Marge invites Homer along despite her own doubts, fueled by a nightmare in which celebrity chefs mock her for letting him intrude on their fun. Trying to keep Homer away, Marge gives him the wrong address, which turns out to be a meth lab instead of the restaurant, and Homer is taken hostage during a police raid. Realizing what happened, Marge and the kids abandon their fancy dinner to rescue Homer, with Marge using a stolen dessert to distract the meth lab owner and free him. The family reconciles, and by the end, Homer and Marge decide to spend a special day together while the kids enjoy Krustyland on their own. Guest starring Mario Batali, Anthony Bourdain, Tim Heidecker, Gordon Ramsay, Eric Wareheim. Blow off "Fun Dad," go eat your walrus mustaches and deep-fried pixie wangs. | Homer: When I'm happy, I make birdhouses!

title: Brick Like Me (S25E20)
text: "Brick Like Me" is an episode of Season 25 (production code RABF21), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Brian Kelley, originally airing May 4, 2014. Lego Homer lives an idyllic brick-built life in Springfield until he begins having flickering visions of a fleshy, non-Lego version of himself, leaving him shaken and confused. As his hallucinations intensify, even causing his hands to turn to real flesh in front of the congregation, he seeks answers from the Lego Comic Book Guy at the Android's Dungeon. There he glimpses a memory of his real self building a Lego Springfield model with Lisa for a contest, only to be abandoned when Lisa chooses to see a Hunger Games parody movie with friends instead. Overwhelmed by hurt, Homer wishes for a world where everything fits together perfectly, and a falling Lego statue knocks him out, trapping him in the fantasy Lego world permanently. Meanwhile, in the Lego world, Bart is forced by Principal Skinner to single-handedly rebuild the school he destroyed while chasing a skunk, and his creative redesigns keep getting rejected. When Homer realizes he wants to return to reality to actually experience his family's lives, the sinister side of his psyche—embodied by Lego Comic Book Guy—unleashes Lego pirates and ninjas to stop him from escaping. Bart saves the day by building a giant robot to fight them off, letting Homer reach the toy box and transform back into his real self. Homer reconciles with Lisa, who feels guilty for leaving him, and he lets her grow up and go see her movie, while still grumbling about it beside Marge in the theater. Notable quotes: LEGO Skinner: Age guidelines are conservative, and everyone knows it. | LEGO Homer: Aw, they're so cute when they're Duplo. | Homer: Nope, not even one. Just look at the things you kids like: Tea parties with pretend food; Hide-and-seek with flagrant peeking; And the most inhumane torture ever devised by man... Candy Land. | LEGO Bart: You are going back where you came from, Denmark. | Homer: But I'm letting you in on a secret. When parents play with their kids, they don't like it.

title: Puffless (S27E03)
text: "Puffless" is an episode of Season 27 (production code TABF19), directed by Rob Oliver and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing October 11, 2015. During a visit to celebrate Jacqueline Bouvier's 80th birthday, the family learns that Clancy Bouvier died of lung cancer, prompting Patty and Selma to vow to quit smoking together. Patty struggles intensely with withdrawal after her stroke and years of addiction, while Selma seems suspiciously unaffected. When Patty discovers Selma secretly relapsed just minutes after quitting, she feels betrayed and moves in with Marge and Homer. Homer's patience is tested by Patty's loud snoring and awkward household intrusions, including an incident where he accidentally gets bleach in his and Bart's eyes. Meanwhile, Selma wrestles with the choice between smoking and keeping her sister's trust, ultimately deciding to quit for real, which allows the sisters to reconcile. In a twist ending, both sisters end up smoking again anyway, reasoning it's easier to mask their apartment's bad odor with cigarette smoke than to actually clean. In a parallel subplot, Maggie climbs onto the roof and befriends a group of animals, including a squirrel, owl, and a parrot revealed to belong to Duffman. When Cletus Spuckler captures a possum from the group for dinner, Maggie recruits Plopper the Spider-Pig to help stage a daring rescue mission against the Spucklers. Guest starring Jon Lovitz as Selma's cigarette, Yo-Yo Ma as himself. Notable quotes: Patty Bouvier: Is anyone here to get an ambulance licence? | Comic Book Guy: That'll be me! | Comic Book Guy: I lied!

title: Barthood (S27E09)
text: "Barthood" is an episode of Season 27 (production code VABF02), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Dan Greaney, originally airing December 13, 2015. The episode traces Bart's life from childhood to young adulthood, alternating between real memories and an imagined non-canon future. As a six-year-old, Bart is neglected by an inattentive Homer and sent to stay with Grampa, who lets him drive an old Studebaker. As he grows, Bart struggles academically and emotionally while Lisa effortlessly outshines him, becoming Springfield Elementary's repeat student of the month and gaining the family's admiration. Attempts by Homer to bond with Bart, including a botched camping trip and a stoned heart-to-heart with Chief Wiggum, only deepen Bart's resentment and sense of being the family's overlooked child. In the speculative future segments, Bart rebels through skateboarding, BMX stunts, and delinquency, all while feeling perpetually eclipsed by Lisa, even after she saves his life following a bad accident. Tensions boil over at Milhouse's graduation party when Lisa calls out Bart for blaming her for his own lack of ambition, prompting him to finally start using his artistic talent. Years later, Bart owns a successful bike customization shop, reconciles with former bully Nelson (who is now dating Lisa), and reveals a mural celebrating his life's journey, including a hidden tribute to Lisa. The episode closes with the reveal that Bart has secretly been the elusive graffiti artist El Barto all along. title: Marge the Meanie (S33E20)
text: "Marge the Meanie" is an episode of Season 33 (production code UABF15), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Megan Amram, originally airing May 8, 2022. During a shuffleboard rivalry match at the YMCA, Marge is recognized and branded 'Marge the Meanie' by a terrified woman who turns out to be her old middle-school principal, Ms. York. Bart is delighted to learn his mother was once a notorious troublemaker, and the two bond as she recalls her rebellious youth and begins pulling pranks again, targeting Comic Book Guy, Helen Lovejoy, and eventually Mr. Burns. When a prank on Burns nearly gets him killed, Marge grows uneasy about the influence she's having on Bart and tries to quit, but relents to do one final prank so as not to disappoint him. Meanwhile, in a lighter subplot, Lisa tries to get Homer excited about vegetarian and vegan cooking, and despite his initial reluctance, the two discover they share food allergies and a similar gentle nature. The main plot culminates when Marge and Ms. York stage a fake heart attack during a prank to teach Bart a real lesson about the consequences of pranking, terrifying him into swearing off pranks forever. The episode ends with Marge and Bart sharing one last harmless prank together, and Marge writing apology letters to everyone she wronged. Notable quotes: Bart: You were a bad kid in school! High five. And now you're trying to lie about it! | Comic Book Guy: How can someone with such a big head be so stupid? | Carl Carlson: You look exactly like her if she was a big, fat, bald guy, which she's not. title: Treehouse of Horror Presents: Simpsons Wicked This Way Comes (S36E07)

text: "Treehouse of Horror Presents: Simpsons Wicked This Way Comes" is an episode of Season 36 (production code 35ABF14), directed by Debbie Bruce Mahan and written by Jessica Conrad, originally airing November 24, 2024. At a mysterious traveling night circus, Lisa reluctantly meets a tattooed sideshow performer called the Illustrated Man, who is being fired by the ringmaster for being out of fashion. He shows Lisa three visions through his tattoos. In the first, Bart hears a woman's ghostly singing coming from underground in the woods, but his parents refuse to believe him until Homer recognizes the tune as one sung by Kirk Van Houten, leading them to dig up his 'grave' and discover Luann buried him alive for a petty betrayal, with Chief Wiggum letting her off since 1950s morality favors murder over divorce. In the second story, set in the future, Superintendent Chalmers and Principal Skinner both secretly buy lifelike robotic duplicates of themselves to avoid dealing with each other, but the robots become sentient, bond with students, and spark a violent showdown that ends with Skinner accidentally killing the real Chalmers. In the final tale, a dystopian society has outlawed 'lowbrow' entertainment, and Homer, working for a firehouse that burns forbidden VHS tapes, secretly keeps one and gets caught enjoying it by Bart, triggering a manhunt by the sinister Burn-Master General Siegfried Blaze. Homer discovers an underground library of banned media run by Krusty, but his own smuggled tape betrays its location, forcing Homer to help the group escape to a refugee camp before the library is destroyed. Back at the circus, having listened to all three tales, Lisa is trapped and turned into a tattoo herself as a twisted reward. Guest starring Andy Serkis. Notable quotes: Homer: Yeah, like that time you said there was a boy in the woods crying wolf, and when we got there, there was no boy at all. Just a fat wolf. | Chief Wiggum: Uh, she's got a point. Here in the 1950s, murder is much more socially acceptable than, uh, you know, divorce. You're free to go. | Superintendent Chalmers: You know you're a tragic figure? Like Hamlet if he was boring and a principal and a-- and an idiot. | Superintendent Chalmers: What? You don't Robot-Skinner me, I Robot-Chalmers you. | Homer: Do you guys ever wish TV could be dumb and fun? So when you watch it, you just laugh? This installment is made up of 3 segments: "The Screaming Woman", "Marionettes, Inc.", and "Fahrenheit 451".

title: Treehouse of Horror XXII (S23E03)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXII" is an episode of Season 23 (production code NABF19), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing October 30, 2011. This Halloween special unfolds in four separate segments bookended by a gag involving Homer, a candy heist, and self-inflicted limb loss. In the opening, Homer defies Marge's attempt to swap the kids' candy for vegetables and ends up trapped under a boulder, gnawing off his own arms and a leg to escape, only to discover the bag he saved contains vegetables after all. In 'The Diving Bell and Butterball,' a spider bite leaves Homer paralyzed, and Lisa discovers he can communicate through farts, until a second spider bite grants him web-slinging superpowers he uses to fight crime with Marge. 'Dial D for Diddily' finds Ned Flanders transformed into a serial killer after Homer tricks him into believing he's receiving murderous commands from God, leading to a string of deaths including Mr. Burns, Sideshow Bob, and the Bouvier sisters before the real God intervenes and kills Homer, blaming Ned for the chaos. Finally, in 'In the Na'vi,' Bart and Milhouse are sent in avatar bodies to Rigel 7 to secure a laughter-inducing substance called hillarium from the native Rigellians, and Bart falls in love with a native named Kamala and impregnates her before a war erupts over the resource, which ends with the humans' defeat and the revelation that the Rigellians would have shared the hillarium if only they had asked. This installment is made up of 3 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 22): "The Diving Bell and Butterball", "Dial D for Diddily", and "In the Na'vi".

title: Holidays of Future Passed (S23E09)
text: "Holidays of Future Passed" is an episode of Season 23 (production code NABF18), directed by Rob Oliver and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing December 11, 2011. Thirty years after a rapid-fire montage of aging Christmas photos, the Simpson family has scattered, and Bart and Lisa decide to reunite everyone at Homer and Marge's house for the holidays. Bart, now a divorced deadbeat dad living in a converted Springfield Elementary loft, struggles to connect with his telepathic sons, while Lisa frets over her tech-obsessed daughter Zia, who spends her time plugged into the virtual Ultranet. Meanwhile, a very pregnant Maggie, touring with her band in London, is barred from teleporting home and must make a frantic, obstacle-filled journey back to Springfield as she goes into labor. Homer, having given up drinking, tries to bond with his grandkids by taking them on a chaotic tour of futuristic Springfield, encountering a cyborg Snake, an ancient and hostile Mr. Burns, and a cloned, self-destructing Chief Wiggum. Bart and Lisa share a heartfelt, tipsy conversation in the treehouse about the guilt and frustration of parenthood, eventually finding perspective through Homer's advice at the cryogenic facility where Grampa has been needlessly frozen. Elsewhere, Patty and Selma's Lovebots reject their owners for each other, and Apu and Manjula cope with their growing brood of grandchildren. By the episode's end, Maggie safely delivers her baby, Bart reconciles with his sons, and the whole extended family gathers for a joyful, if bizarre, future Christmas photo taken by their now-sentient pets. Guest starring Matt Groening as a soccer announcer. Notable quotes: Bart: Don't worry. I've got some buyers coming over to look at my good kidney. They grow back, right? | Skippy Simpson: You know, we can hear thoughts now! | Milhouse Van Houten: I can't believe we put a man on the sun, but we can't stop my sneezing! | Maude's ghost: There is no God, Neddy. It's just an empty, meaningless void. | Homer: See you next Christmas.

Skippy Simpson: You know, we can hear thoughts now!
Milhouse Van Houten: I can't believe we put a man on the sun, but we can't stop my sneezing!
Maude's ghost: There is no God, Neddy. It's just an empty, meaningless void.
Homer: See you next Christmas.

title: What Animated Women Want (S24E17)
text: "What Animated Women Want" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF08), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing April 14, 2013. After watching a screening of A Streetcar Named Desire, Milhouse becomes obsessed with Marlon Brando's brooding, tough-guy image and tries to reinvent himself as a rebellious bad boy to win Lisa's affection. Unsure how to pull off the act convincingly, he turns to the school counselor for guidance on channeling raw, moody masculinity. Meanwhile, Marge grows increasingly frustrated with Homer's laziness and broken promises, pushing their marriage to a breaking point. Determined to prove he can change, Homer sets out to become a more attentive husband and finally follow through on things he's long neglected. Struggling with how to win Marge back, he seeks wisdom from his neighborhood sushi chef, who offers him unconventional advice about patience and effort. Through a series of comic missteps and small gestures, Homer slowly rebuilds trust with Marge, culminating in a romantic reconciliation. Meanwhile, Milhouse's brooding persona has mixed results with Lisa, who finds his awkward attempts at intensity more endearing than intimidating. Both subplots end with the couples finding renewed affection, though not without a few absurd detours along the way. Guest starring Bryan Cranston as Walter White, Maurice LaMarche as Karl Malden, Aaron Paul as Jesse Pinkman, Wanda Sykes as the Springfield Elementary School therapist, George Takei as the sushi chef. Notable quotes: Homer: Once again, by eating alone, I have saved my marriage. | Marge: It's a snuggle dungeon. | Lisa: Hush, sweet boy. Let me get lost in the blue of your eyebrows. | Milhouse: Whichever you picked, you picked wrong. | Homer: Give up? It's Marge. I'm having a lunch date with my wife.

Marge: It's a snuggle dungeon.
Lisa: Hush, sweet boy. Let me get lost in the blue of your eyebrows.
Milhouse: Whichever you picked, you picked wrong.
Homer: Give up? It's Marge. I'm having a lunch date with my wife.

title: Clan of the Cave Mom (S35E13)
text: "Clan of the Cave Mom" is an episode of Season 35 (production code 35ABF06), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Brian Kelley, originally airing March 24, 2024. While chaperoning a school museum trip, Marge is distracted by homeowners' association complaints, and during a chaotic moment Bart and Milhouse break an exhibit, with Bart fleeing so Milhouse takes the blame. As Bart pesters Marge to let him attend a concert, a parallel story unfolds in prehistoric times where a caveman version of the Simpson family struggles to survive against hunger, harsh weather, and a menacing wolf. When Luann publicly declares Bart a lost cause and cuts him out of the concert plans, Marge's protective fury boils over, mirroring her ancient counterpart's fierce defense of her cubs. Marge and Homer's confrontation with the Van Houtens escalates into a full-blown feud, culminating in a PTA showdown where Luann tries to have Marge removed from the board. Meanwhile, Homer battles ticket apps and scalpers to get Bart into the concert's Front Row Club, echoing his prehistoric self's grueling hunt for food. As both timelines reach a climax—present-day Marge sneaking into the arena and ancient Marge fighting off the wolf—Marge realizes her rage has clouded her judgment when Bart calls her out. She apologizes to Bart, mends fences with Luann, and allows Milhouse to rejoin him at the concert, while in the past, Marge shows mercy to the wolf, adopting it as part of the family instead of killing it. Guest starring Kerry Washington as Rayshelle Peyton. He's all I got. | Bart: I can handle bad. I can't handle losing the one good parent I've got. | Nelson Muntz: Milhouse, don't feel bad about the bailing. Just feel happy that for a few days, I pretended to like you for your tickets. | Luann Van Houten: Bart, you're a bad friend, and you're beyond hope. Be well.

title: Labor Pains (S25E05)
text: "Labor Pains" is an episode of Season 25 (production code RABF19), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Don Payne, Mitchell H. Glazer, originally airing November 17, 2013. Homer lies to Marge about working overtime so he can attend a poker night at Carl's apartment, but on his way home he gets stuck in an elevator with a pregnant stranger named Gretchen and ends up helping deliver her baby. Gretchen names the boy Homer Jr., and Homer quickly becomes emotionally attached to the child, secretly babysitting and buying him supplies under the guise of shopping for Maggie. Meanwhile, Lisa is drawn into the world of the Springfield Atoms cheerleaders after being pulled into their halftime routine, and she discovers the cheerleaders are underpaid and exploited by their boss, the Rich Texan. Lisa organizes the cheerleaders into a protest, eventually forcing the boss to give them a raise after briefly replacing them with the likes of Patty, Selma, and Mrs. Muntz. Marge grows suspicious of Homer's late nights and discovers the truth about Homer Jr., reacting with shock but ultimately allowing Homer to remain involved with the baby after learning he's stayed sober. Tensions boil over during a family zoo trip when Maggie and Homer Jr. clash and a stroller mishap nearly ends in disaster, prompting Marge to forbid further contact. Homer tearfully says goodbye to Homer Jr. as the boy's biological father returns from military service, and Homer returns home to a comforting reconciliation with Maggie. Guest starring Elisabeth Moss. Notable quotes: Homer: Wow, so now there's two things named after me... a baby, and a law banning air horns after 3:00 a.m. | Marge: I'm a Schwarzenegger wife. | Homer: But you're also the housekeeper, so it's all good. | Grampa: If this is heaven, why don't my shoes match? | The Rich Texan: Okay, I give up. I'm gonna do what we secretly did at the Alamo—surrender.

title: Sorry Not Sorry (S32E09)
text: "Sorry Not Sorry" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF01), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Nell Scovell, originally airing December 6, 2020. While stargazing with Homer on the roof, Lisa recalls the classroom clash that has been bothering her. For a class project on inspirational figures, she creates an elaborate tribute to mathematician Gladys West, but the overworked and apathetic Miss Hoover gives the whole class a flat B- grade rather than evaluating each project individually. Furious, Lisa calls her teacher an "uninspiring hack" and refuses to apologize, landing herself in escalating rounds of detention despite pressure from Marge, Homer, and even Bart's suggestion to fake an apology by saying "I'm soggy." Seeking real guidance, Lisa visits the Springfield Education Annex, where a consultant advises her to walk in Miss Hoover's shoes to understand her perspective. Trailing her teacher, Lisa learns that chronic back pain and a grueling commute have worn Miss Hoover down, prompting Lisa to spend her Yale fund on a reclining chair as a peace offering. Miss Hoover initially rejects the gift as a hollow, belated gesture, but after discovering its massage feature she finally accepts Lisa's apology and bumps her project grade up to a B+. Back in the present, the family remains huddled on the roof to dodge Grampa, and a flash-forward shows an older Lisa thriving at Yale, while Homer wakes from a Red Baron fantasy crying like Charlie Brown. Notable quotes: Lisa: In other words, you're an uninspiring hack! | Miss Hoover: The truth has no place in this classroom. Lisa, go to detention. | Ralph: My hero is my thumb. It has its own room in my mittens. Thank you. | Shauna: I guess. You learn a lot of sad things when you sell weed to teachers. | Bart: Guilty as Marged.

title: The Fabulous Faker Boy (S24E20)
text: "The Fabulous Faker Boy" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF12), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Brian McConnachie, originally airing May 12, 2013. Marge encourages Bart to develop his creative side, leading him to take piano lessons from a beautiful young teacher named Zhenya, on whom he quickly develops a crush. To afford the lessons, Marge strikes a deal with Zhenya's father Slava, a Russian immigrant, agreeing to teach him how to drive in exchange for the discounted lessons. Bart, more interested in impressing Zhenya than actually learning piano, secretly cheats his way through his lessons rather than practicing honestly. Eventually his deception comes to light, forcing him to admit the truth and apologize to Marge, though Slava reassures her that cheating for love is practically a Russian tradition. Meanwhile, Homer is devastated when he loses the final two hairs on his head, pushing him into a crisis about his identity and appearance. Patrick Stewart, playing himself, steps in to mentor Homer, teaching him to embrace and take pride in his baldness. By the episode's end, Bart comes clean about his musical shortcomings while still salvaging his bond with Zhenya's family, and Homer gains newfound confidence in his hairless head thanks to Stewart's guidance. Guest starring Justin Bieber, Bill Hader, Jane Krakowski, Patrick Stewart. Notable quotes: Slava: I give you something you want... you give me something I want. I'm sorry, did my voice go all evil? It is common with Russian accent. | Slava: Marge, in Russia, everyone succeeds by cheating. Even Russian dressing is just Thousand Island. | Bart: Every good booger deserves flicking. | Zhenya: Your tongue is nimble, unlike sausage fingers. | Milhouse Van Houten: Did you ever wonder if hippopotamuses think that rhinos are unicorns?

title: Panic on the Streets of Springfield (S32E19)
keys: panic on the streets of springfield
text: "Panic on the Streets of Springfield" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF12), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Tim Long, originally airing April 18, 2021. After a discouraging physical exam, Homer ignores his doctor's advice and instead buys a massive off-road truck, becoming obsessed with being a 'truck guy' despite having no real interest in the outdoors. Meanwhile, Lisa discovers the music of Quilloughby, a reclusive 1980s British vegetarian singer, through a music-streaming app, and becomes so enamored with his ideals that she starts an unpopular Mushroom Monday campaign at school. After being humiliated when the lunch lady sneaks bacon into supposedly vegan tacos, Lisa begins hallucinating an imaginary version of Quilloughby who follows her around, encouraging her rebellious streak and alienating her from her friends and family. Her behavior worsens, culminating in her secretly using Homer's credit card to buy tickets to a music festival where the real Quilloughby is performing. When she and her imaginary friend arrive, they discover the real Quilloughby has become an overweight, bitter sellout who has abandoned his vegetarian ideals, sparking a riot from the disillusioned crowd. Homer imagines heroically crashing through the festival to save her, but in reality Marge calmly walks in and rescues Lisa herself. The episode ends with Marge sharing her own teenage rebellion story with Lisa, mending their relationship as the family drives home together. Guest starring Benedict Cumberbatch. title: Eeny Teeny Maya, Moe (S20E16)
text: "Eeny Teeny Maya, Moe" is an episode of Season 20 (production code LABF06), directed by Nancy Kruse and written by John Frink, originally airing April 5, 2009. After Homer neglects Maggie during a hockey game, Marge insists he spend more quality time with her, so he takes her to Moe's Tavern, discovering a play area just outside the bar's window where he can drink while keeping an eye on her. Meanwhile, Moe strikes up an online romance with a woman named Maya, who turns out to be a little person when they finally meet in person, though the two quickly fall for each other despite Moe's insecurity about what his friends will think. As their relationship deepens, Moe hides Maya from his social circle, straining their bond, while at home Maggie becomes traumatized by a bullying incident in the play area that Homer fails to notice, prompting a worried Marge to secretly spy on them using a hidden camera. When Moe finally introduces Maya to Homer and Marge on a double date, things go well until his insensitive height jokes ruin a marriage proposal, causing Maya to storm off. Devastated, Moe considers dangerous height-reduction surgery from Dr. Nick to win her back, but Maya intervenes, telling him she can't be with someone so uncomfortable with her identity, and ends things for good. Simultaneously, Marge discovers via the hidden camera that Homer truly does love and protect Maggie, easing her fears, and the episode closes with Homer comforting a heartbroken Moe with reassurance that love will find him again. Notable quotes: Moe Szyslak: It was a typical Friday night: me surfing the net at the public library, with occasional drinking fountain breaks. | Moe: All right, before I send this, I'd better, uh, un-beady the eyes... de-Neanderthal the brow... smooth out my hate lines... lighten up the ear hair... switch my lips... Then, black tie the whole deal. Aw, I can't build a relationship on a lie. The lies come later. | Carl Carlson: How'd your date go, Moe? | Moe: Incredible. I've never felt like this before. It's like my heart wants to do her. | Homer: Moe, this was a great thing for you. You went from sitting on the sidelines to getting in the game.

title: Bart's Birthday (S36E01)
text: "Bart's Birthday" is an episode of Season 36 (production code 35ABF15), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Jessica Conrad, originally airing September 29, 2024. Conan O'Brien hosts a live special billing itself as the true series finale of The Simpsons, revealing that an AI program called Hack-GPT has been tasked with writing the perfect ending after decades of FOX's failed attempts to cancel the show. The 'episode' it generates centers on Bart's eleventh birthday, where Homer forgets to mail invitations, forcing Bart to race around Springfield delivering them himself. As Bart travels through town, he notices unsettling signs that everything is wrapping up for good: Skinner quits as principal, Mr. Burns dies and leaves his fortune to the plant workers, Moe closes the tavern, Comic Book Guy shuts down his store after John Cena delivers his baby, and various couples suddenly marry or reunite with lost family. Growing increasingly anxious, Bart tries to warn his family that something is wrong, but no one will listen as they celebrate his birthday and their own supposed personal growth. When Bart confronts Homer about never truly changing, Homer snaps and strangles him in a callback to the show's classic dynamic, causing the AI-generated 'finale' to glitch and collapse. The simulation resets, revealing that nothing has actually changed and the whole scenario was Hack-GPT's failed attempt at a series finale. Back at the live special, Hack-GPT declares that the show hasn't ended but simply reset itself, and after literally exploding under the pressure of continuing indefinitely, Conan gladly exits the theater, unbothered by its destruction. Guest starring John Cena, Danny DeVito, Tom Hanks, Joel McHale, Conan O'Brien, Mark Proksch, Seth Rogen, Amy Sedaris. Notable quotes: Homer: Marge, I could lie and tell you what you want to hear, but I won't. I mailed the invitations. And the reason no one is coming is... because everybody hates Bart. | Conan O'Brien: You ran billions of computations and that's what you come up with? Homer screws up Bart's birthday party? | Comic Book Guy: I don't need toys anymore. I've got the ultimate limited edition collectible right here. I think I'm going to miss this place. | Comic Book Guy: Help me, OB-GYN Kenobi. You are my only hope. | Bart: No more Skinner? Oh, man. This is the best birthday present ever.

title: Aunt Misbehavin' (S37E09)
text: "Aunt Misbehavin'" is an episode of Season 37 (production code 37ABF02), directed by Gabriel DeFrancesco and written by Juliet Kaufman, originally airing November 30, 2025. After their supervisor Ken retires, Selma is promoted over Patty, and the resulting rivalry spills into the Simpson household. When Homer punishes Bart by destroying his Xbox for a dentist-office prank, Bart teams up with Patty to get revenge by exploiting her identical resemblance to Selma and faking Homer's death in the state DMV records. The prank backfires spectacularly when Homer discovers that being 'legally dead' frees him from taxes, dues, and other annoyances, leaving him delighted rather than distressed. Selma uncovers the scheme and fires Patty, sparking an explosive sisterly feud that drives Patty out of the house and into her own apartment in Palm Springfield. As the sisters try to reinvent themselves—Patty with a new look and Selma with a new boyfriend, Merle—Bart and Lisa realize both aunts are secretly miserable without each other. The kids scheme to reunite them by getting them to unknowingly attend the same golf tournament, but Homer's fake-death status nearly ruins their VIP access until Marge convinces him to finally end the charade. At the tournament, Patty and Selma's argument boils over, but Marge's intervention forces them to confront how much they need each other, leading to a heartfelt reconciliation. The episode ends with the twins deciding to live in neighboring apartments, maintaining independence while staying close. Guest starring Stephen Tobolowsky as Merle. Notable quotes: Homer: Dead? Can I still rent a U-Haul? | Homer: I should have died years ago. | Homer: Honey, life is so short. Certainly mine was. So, take it from your late husband, ghost those hags. | Patty: I should've done this years ago. I feel so free. This is a queer paradise. We have slurs for straight people here and the obscene amount of water wasted keeping this place green... I love it. | Homer: As someone who's already dead, it kills me to say this. There is one way into the Amex VIP lounge.
