title: Covercraft (S26E08)
text: "Covercraft" is an episode of Season 26 (production code TABF02), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Matt Selman, originally airing November 23, 2014. When Moe gets into a fight with King Toot and King Toot's music store closes down, Homer loses his usual hangout and finds himself adrift. A trip to the new mega-store Guitar Central, meant to buy Lisa's supplies, instead turns into Homer being talked into purchasing a bass guitar and a pile of accessories. He begins practicing loudly in the garage, driving the rest of the family crazy, but soon discovers other Springfield dads are going through similar midlife restlessness. The men bond over their shared frustrations and decide to form a cover band together, finding unexpected camaraderie and purpose in making music. Just as the newly formed group, Covercraft, starts gaining a little local buzz, Apu's surprising musical talent threatens to overshadow the rest of the band. Apu's skills catch the attention of a much more famous act, who recruit him away, forcing the dads to reconsider the band's future. Meanwhile, Moe copes with the loss of his business by taking an impromptu road trip with King Toot, the very man he fought with, showing an odd but genuine reconciliation between the two. Guest starring Will Forte, Sammy Hagar. title: Gone Boy (S29E09)
text: "Gone Boy" is an episode of Season 29 (production code XABF02), directed by Rob Oliver and written by John Frink, originally airing December 10, 2017. After a community service session collecting trash goes awry when the Simpsons run over it with a rental car, Homer takes Bart out to play in the forest, where Bart falls through a manhole into a hidden military bunker. As the family and police mount a search, Bart tries and fails to escape, instead using a bunker phone to prank-call Moe rather than call for help. Milhouse discovers the manhole entrance but keeps Bart's survival secret, hoping the tragedy will win him sympathy and affection from Lisa, even as the news declares Bart dead. Sideshow Bob, initially participating in the search alongside Shaquille O'Neal, is devastated by the news but grows suspicious when Bart later calls Marge to prove he's alive. Bob tricks Milhouse into leading him to the bunker, shoves him down the hole, and ties both boys to a missile intending to kill them, but has a last-minute change of heart and rescues them instead. In a flash-forward epilogue, an elderly, retired Sideshow Bob still obsesses over his failed vendetta against Bart while living alone at a lighthouse, until the now-adult Squeaky-Voiced Teen, working as a mailman, suggests he simply get a mailbox to end his ranting. Guest starring Kelsey Grammer, Valerie Harper, Shaquille O'Neal, John F. Kennedy. Notable quotes: Bart: [sarcastically] Doesn't sound like any president I know. | Milhouse Van Houten: Because searching forever is much easier than me finding a new friend. | Kent Brockman: With 78% of the search area reporting, Channel Six is now projecting that Bart Simpson is dead. | Sideshow Bob: Lord, why do you kill things that I want to kill? Take me now, vile rake! | Shaquille O'Neal: You're scaring me. I don't have any money.

Milhouse Van Houten: Because searching forever is much easier than me finding a new friend.
Kent Brockman: With 78% of the search area reporting, Channel Six is now projecting that Bart Simpson is dead.
Sideshow Bob: Lord, why do you kill things that I want to kill? Take me now, vile rake!
Shaquille O'Neal: You're scaring me. I don't have any money.

title: Boy Meets Curl (S21E12)
text: "Boy Meets Curl" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF05), directed by Chuck Sheetz and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing February 14, 2010. After a botched date night is derailed by an ammonia leak at the power plant and a noisy movie theater, Homer and Marge stumble into an ice rink and discover a shared talent for curling. Agnes and Seymour Skinner recruit them for a mixed-doubles team, with Agnes warning Marge not to let emotion interfere with competition, recalling how her pregnancy with Seymour cost her an Olympic medal decades earlier. The Simpson-Skinner duo qualifies for the Vancouver Winter Olympics as a demonstration event. Meanwhile, Lisa becomes obsessed with collecting Olympic pins, even trading away her prized pearl necklace, until Bart cons the pin dealer with a fake mascot made from a photo of Homer's jowls to win the necklace back. At the Olympics, Agnes tries to have Homer removed from the team after Marge injures her shoulder overcompensating for his poor throws, threatening the team's chances against Sweden. Marge then reveals she's secretly left-handed and has been hiding it her whole life, and by sweeping with her uninjured arm she leads the team to an improbable gold medal. The episode closes with Homer and Marge agreeing that, despite everything, their date night turned out to be a success. Guest starring Bob Costas as himself. Notable quotes: Homer: Let us curl, milady. Let us throw and sweep atwain until the heavens themselves drop their jaws in wonder and envy. | Marge: This is what you're like when you don't drink! | Bob Costas: We'll return to sudden death overtime in the gold medal hockey game between Russia and the U.S. in a moment, but first, the forfeiture signing ceremony!
quotes: Homer: Let us curl, milady. Let us throw and sweep atwain until the heavens themselves drop their jaws in wonder and envy.
Marge: This is what you're like when you don't drink!
Bob Costas: We'll return to sudden death overtime in the gold medal hockey game between Russia and the U.S. in a moment, but first, the forfeiture signing ceremony!

title: Frinkcoin (S31E13)
text: "Frinkcoin" is an episode of Season 31 (production code ZABF07), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing February 23, 2020. When Lisa needs a subject for her 'Most Interesting Person I Know' essay, Homer and Marge scramble to impress her, but she instead picks Professor Frink for his scientific achievements. While interviewing him, Lisa learns Frink has invented Frinkcoin, a cryptocurrency that quickly makes him the richest man in Springfield, dethroning Mr. Burns. Fame leaves Frink feeling hollow and unsure whether his new admirers are genuine friends, so Lisa arranges for Homer to bring him to Moe's, where he bonds with the barflies over trivia and generosity. Meanwhile, a humiliated Burns assembles a team of nerds to create a rival currency and later a formula to destroy all cryptocurrency, though the calculation would take far too long to complete. Burns instead tries to psychologically break Frink by suggesting his new friends only love his money, planting seeds of doubt before Frink's big public test of loyalty. Frink's friends indeed fail his test, seemingly confirming Burns's cynicism, but Frink turns the tables by solving Burns's public equation himself, wiping out Frinkcoin's value in the process. Having lost his fortune, Frink finds something more meaningful: a genuine friendship with Lisa and a rekindled connection with his university colleague, Professor Hessler, whom he kisses at the episode's end. Guest starring Beanie Feldstein, Ed "Too Tall" Jones, Jim Parsons. Notable quotes: Homer: I can eat anything as long as I pretend it once had a face. | Professor Frink: My parents had great chemistry. Uh, no love, but they were chemists. | Mr. Burns: Now, listen to me, your friends don't give a whit about you. | Professor Frink: That is not true! Those guys are my best buddies! Fatso and Drunky and the evil bartender there. | Krusty the Clown: This town is so dumb, they built an indoor windfarm.

Professor Frink: My parents had great chemistry. Uh, no love, but they were chemists.

Professor Frink: That is not true! Those guys are my best buddies! Fatso and Drunky and the evil bartender there.

title: Bartless (S34E15)
text: "Bartless" is an episode of Season 34 (production code OABF08), directed by Rob Oliver and written by John Frink, originally airing March 5, 2023. During Book Buddies Wednesday at Springfield Elementary, Bart improvises a wild story while drawing in a library book meant for a kindergartner, inadvertently sparking a school-wide reading craze among the younger kids. Homer and Marge are furious when they learn Bart defaced the book, branding him a troublemaker, even after his teacher Ms. Peyton points out the positive impact he had. That night, after arguing over whether they actually like their son, Homer and Marge wake up in an alternate reality where Bart was never born, living in a nicer house with more fulfilling jobs. While driving home one night, they accidentally hit a skateboarding boy who turns out to be an amnesiac Bart, and they take him in without realizing who he really is. As Bart's mischievous personality reshapes their household for the better—loosening up Lisa, delighting Maggie, and even boosting Homer's job performance and Marge's hospital colleagues' professionalism—Homer and Marge start to appreciate his chaotic charm. When Chief Wiggum arrives to take amnesiac Bart to an orphanage, the couple desperately chases after him, only to wake up back in reality, realizing it was all a dream. Grateful for the revelation, Homer and Marge go to tell Bart that they truly appreciate him, while back at school, Ralph disappears into a hole he drew on the wall, sailing off into the unknown. Guest starring Kerry Washington as Rayshelle Peyton. Notable quotes: Bart: Sit back, kid, and I'll tell you where milk really comes from. On the farm, cows eat pig boogers... Which their butts turn into milk. | Marge: Who are you, little boy? Where are your parents? What's your name? | Bart: I'm Bart... um, something. Who the hell are you? | Homer: We just couldn't wait to tell you something. We like you. | Martha: This is the first book he hasn't tried to kiss or wear as a hat.
quotes: Bart: Sit back, kid, and I'll tell you where milk really comes from. On the farm, cows eat pig boogers... Which their butts turn into milk.
Marge: Who are you, little boy? Where are your parents? What's your name?
Bart: I'm Bart... um, something. Who the hell are you?
Homer: We just couldn't wait to tell you something. We like you.
Martha: This is the first book he hasn't tried to kiss or wear as a hat.

title: Grampy Can Ya Hear Me (S29E05)
text: "Grampy Can Ya Hear Me" is an episode of Season 29 (production code WABF19), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Bill Odenkirk, originally airing November 5, 2017. On Grampa's birthday, the Simpsons take him to the Springfield Planetarium, where a big bang documentary sends him fleeing in fear. Back at the retirement castle, Grampa receives a hearing aid as a gift, which lets him hear his family's unfiltered complaints about him for the first time. Hurt, he storms off and disappears into town, visiting the mall and a veterans' bar while the family searches for him. Meanwhile, Bart and Lisa sneak into the school to fix a homework error and stumble upon Principal Skinner secretly living in the school basement, having learned his mother lied to him years ago about being accepted into Ohio State University's marching band. Skinner confronts his mother Agnes, who tearfully admits her deception, and the two reconcile with him moving back home on his own terms. Lisa confesses her cheating to Miss Hoover, only to find Hoover already knew and instead wants stolen nicotine gum, which ends up energizing the class hamster into chaos. Grampa is eventually returned home by a bartender fed up with him, and overhears what he believes is his family's affection for him, though it turns out to be a staged script written by Lisa and Marge. The episode closes with a short segment showing the hapless Hans Moleman being ignored and mistreated by everyone around him despite his medical emergency. Notable quotes: Grampa: A call girl that kills me after? | Old Jewish man: You are old. You've lived long enough to see your prejudiced attitudes come back into fashion. | Barney Gumble: I'm also the state drunk! | Squeaky-Voiced Teen: Your pupils aren't ready for Earth light! | Sideshow Mel: Quiet! I can't hear the Big Bang!
quotes: Grampa: A call girl that kills me after?
Old Jewish man: You are old. You've lived long enough to see your prejudiced attitudes come back into fashion.
Barney Gumble: I'm also the state drunk!
Squeaky-Voiced Teen: Your pupils aren't ready for Earth light!
Sideshow Mel: Quiet! I can't hear the Big Bang!

title: Bad Boys... for Life? (S37E05)
text: "Bad Boys... for Life?" is an episode of Season 37 (production code 36ABF17), directed by Eric Koenig and written by Al Jean, originally airing November 2, 2025. When the family fails to find anything good to watch on TV, Lisa asks Marge to tell a story about her and Bart's childhood. Marge recalls a time four years earlier when Bart's mischief, fueled by Homer's neglect and unfair treatment like forcing him to switch dominant hands, escalated into a series of elaborate pranks against his father. As Bart's pranks grow more destructive, from gluing Homer's beer to his hand to sabotaging emergency responders, the family turns to psychologist Dr. Leonard Stern, who diagnoses Bart as dangerously disturbed and arranges to have him committed to a children's reformatory. Before Bart is taken away, Homer has a nightmare imagining Bart's grim future in custody, prompting him to try to rescue his son and flee with him in the car. During their overnight escape, which includes a donut run and a stop at the treehouse Homer built as a boy to escape his own difficult father, Homer and Bart bond and Homer begins to recognize how much of Bart's behavior mirrors his own personality and upbringing. When Dr. Stern's men arrive the next morning to take Bart away, they mistakenly sedate Homer instead, giving him a moment of clarity where he realizes his son isn't bad and that the blame lies with his own poor parenting. Homer manages to talk Dr. Stern out of taking Bart, resolving the crisis, though the episode ends with a hint that new parenting challenges are already on their way as Ned Flanders shows up at the door. Guest starring Maurice LaMarche as Jerry Seinfeld, Matthew Modine as Dr. Leonard Stern. Notable quotes: Homer: Kids, kids, you're both unwanted. | Grampa: Saying Homer was occasionally inconsiderate is like saying Shamu is sometimes a whale. | Younger Homer: It's so hard being a good father. How did people raise kids before duct tape? | Leonard Stern: Oh, my God. He's attacking his grandfather. | Chief Wiggum: Well, you're coming downtown to where I live, to teach my wife how to make donuts. Let's go.
quotes: Homer: Kids, kids, you're both unwanted.
Grampa: Saying Homer was occasionally inconsiderate is like saying Shamu is sometimes a whale.
Younger Homer: It's so hard being a good father. How did people raise kids before duct tape?
Leonard Stern: Oh, my God. He's attacking his grandfather.
Chief Wiggum: Well, you're coming downtown to where I live, to teach my wife how to make donuts. Let's go.

title: I Want You (She's So Heavy) (S30E16)
text: "I Want You (She's So Heavy)" is an episode of Season 30 (production code YABF08), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing March 10, 2019. Homer and Marge attend a mandatory drug meeting but sneak off to a wedding expo, leaving Shauna and Jimbo to babysit the kids, who end up fleeing to the Flanders' house when the sitters get too romantic. After a chaotic night ends with Homer collapsing on the stairs while carrying Marge, he's diagnosed with a hernia, and medication side effects cause him to hallucinate a talking, wisecracking version of it named Wallace. While Homer indulges his unhealthy habits with his imaginary friend, Marge begins physical therapy and discovers a new passion for kite surfing under the guidance of a suspicious instructor named Nigel. Lisa, worried about her parents growing apart, seeks relationship advice from Shauna and Jimbo, who tell her the key is finding a shared activity. The kids bring Homer to the beach, where witnessing Chief Wiggum's mishap inspires him to finally join Marge in kite surfing. The couple ends up blown out to a wind farm, where they reconnect and reconcile. The episode wraps up with the reveal that Nigel is actually a Russian spy, leading to his dramatic arrest at the Nuclear Power Plant. Guest starring Wallace Shawn as Wallace the Hernia. Notable quotes: Nigel: Kite-surfing's a simple sport. All you need is the wind and the waves. And a spreader-bar, bindings, impact vest, chicken loop, donkey stick, squirrel clip, and, of course, parking pass. | Chief Wiggum: Yeah, ruining people's day at the beach. We are worse than sand in a hot dog, eh, Lou? | Chief Wiggum: Well, now it's a triple, 'cause you just killed my day. | Grampa: Oh, your grandma and I had our differences, but we stopped arguing when she disappeared for three decades. | Ralph: I'm expensive.

Chief Wiggum: Yeah, ruining people's day at the beach. We are worse than sand in a hot dog, eh, Lou?
Chief Wiggum: Well, now it's a triple, 'cause you just killed my day.

title: Krusty the Clown (episode) (S30E08)
text: "Krusty the Clown (episode)" is an episode of Season 30 (production code XABF22), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Ryan Koh, originally airing November 25, 2018. After a newspaper shakeup at the Daily Fourth Gradian, Lisa is put in charge of recapping Krusty's TV show, and she enlists Homer to help since he watches it religiously. Homer's brutally low grades enrage Krusty, who tries to run him down with his car, leading to a wild crash. Bart rescues the injured Krusty and brings him to a traveling circus, where he adopts the alias Soggy the Clown to escape his old life. Krusty initially flops as a circus performer but rediscovers genuine joy in the work after stepping in for an ailing act, only for the circus to be threatened with closure over a scandalous promotional video. Meanwhile, Homer's viral recapping fame strains his marriage and draws the attention of the sinister Google-Disney CEO, who reveals a scheme to trick subscribers into thinking they're watching real shows while actually being fed nonstop commercials. Homer exposes the plan online instead of going along with it. To save the circus from shutting down, the manager turns himself in for the video scandal, but a sympathetic jury acquits him, allowing the circus to move on. Krusty returns to his old show, now reviewed more kindly by Ralph, restoring some balance to his life. Guest starring Billy Eichner as Krusty the Clown, Peter Serafinowicz as the Google-Disney CEO. Notable quotes: Lisa: Dad, you were born to recap TV at a fourth-grade level. | Homer: Fake shows? But what if people try to see them? | Homer: No one ever watches a B-minus. | Krusty the Clown: Like my show! | Marge: And don't you dare give me a letter grade.
quotes: Lisa: Dad, you were born to recap TV at a fourth-grade level.
Homer: Fake shows? But what if people try to see them?
Homer: No one ever watches a B-minus.
Krusty the Clown: Like my show!
Marge: And don't you dare give me a letter grade.

title: 22 for 30 (S28E17)
text: "22 for 30" is an episode of Season 28 (production code WABF10), directed by Chris Clements and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing March 12, 2017. Framed as a mock sports documentary, the episode traces Bart's unlikely rise from a delinquent serving Springfield Elementary's longest detention to the school's basketball star, after he's discovered shooting paper wads into a bin. As his fame grows, Bart becomes arrogant and disrespectful toward Homer, who has taken over as the team's coach, leading Homer to bench him. Fat Tony seizes the opportunity to recruit Bart into a point-shaving scheme, convincing him to manipulate game outcomes to satisfy gamblers while still technically winning. Lisa, covering the story for the school paper, begins uncovering the scandal as it spills into the news. At the City Champions Final Four, tensions boil over: Homer forces a win by choking Bart into performing, but Bart soon learns just how much money Fat Tony has been skimming off him and rebels against being told to throw the championship. During the climactic game, Milhouse tackles Bart to snap him out of his selfish, fame-driven mindset, helping the team pull through to victory. An enraged Fat Tony threatens to kill both Bart and Homer, but Lisa intervenes by revealing a secret about Tony's own history with basketball, defusing the threat. The documentary's narrator is finally revealed to be Nelson's father, Eddie Muntz, who briefly reunites with his family just long enough for a photo before disappearing again. Guest starring Stephen Curry, Earl Mann, Joe Mantegna. Notable quotes: Homer: Bart, I'm your coach, your father, and, because no one else would, your godfather. | Bart: Thanks dad, but don't you still make mistakes? | Homer: And the best one was you, son. | Bart: I was scared, Milhouse-scared. | Mr. Burns: Who is this Mike? I'll kill him, too!
quotes: Homer: Bart, I'm your coach, your father, and, because no one else would, your godfather.
Bart: Thanks dad, but don't you still make mistakes?
Homer: And the best one was you, son.
Bart: I was scared, Milhouse-scared.
Mr. Burns: Who is this Mike? I'll kill him, too!

title: Werking Mom (S30E07)
text: "Werking Mom" is an episode of Season 30 (production code XABF21), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Carolyn Omine, Robin Sayers, originally airing November 18, 2018. Marge decides to become a Tubberware saleswoman but struggles to book any parties until her hairstylist Julio offers to host one for his friends. Before the event, Julio gives Marge a bold makeover to build her confidence, and the party becomes a huge hit because the guests assume she's a drag queen. Embracing this new persona, Marge accompanies Julio to a drag club called Draggle Rock, where she meets performers like Queen Chante and begins to embrace a glamorous alter ego of her own. Meanwhile, Lisa discovers a hidden stash of Jasper Beardley's old belongings at school and finds fulfillment secretly returning lost items and doing good deeds for townspeople with Bart's help, including a scheme to convince Agnes Skinner that her son still loves her through a forged diary. The plan backfires when Agnes realizes the diary is fake, leaving Lisa devastated. Homer, feeling shut out and confused by Marge's secretive new hobby, tracks down her drag party location through Moe and inadvertently exposes her as a woman, causing the crowd to lose interest and leave. Lisa's spirits are lifted when the people she helped surprise her with a rooftop gathering to thank her, giving her the sense of belonging she'd been missing. In the end, Homer wins Marge back by donning his own drag persona and showing up at Moe's Tavern in costume. Guest starring Sutan Amrull, RuPaul, Scott Thompson. Notable quotes: Julio Franco: This is so important, I'm gonna drop the accent. | Lisa: I don't mean to overstate this, but the sun is shining just a little bit lighter because of meeee! | Lisa: I tried to play God, and like the real God, it went horribly wrong.
quotes: Julio Franco: This is so important, I'm gonna drop the accent.
Lisa: I don't mean to overstate this, but the sun is shining just a little bit lighter because of meeee!
Lisa: I tried to play God, and like the real God, it went horribly wrong.

title: MyPods and Boomsticks (S20E07)
text: "MyPods and Boomsticks" is an episode of Season 20 (production code KABF20), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Marc Wilmore, originally airing November 30, 2008. Just after Christmas, the Simpsons visit Springfield Mall's Mapple Store, where Lisa scores a free MyPod from a disgruntled Krusty. Bart hijacks Steve Mobbs' big announcement with a prank insulting Mapple customers, forcing him to flee the store. While escaping, Bart meets and befriends Bashir, a new Muslim boy in town, and the two quickly bond over shared mischief and Bashir's family's cooking. When Homer meets Bashir's father Amid, his casual racism and paranoia—fueled by Moe and a TV show—convince him the family are terrorists, leading to an attempted poisoning and a wild nightmare about Islamic culture taking over America. Homer's suspicions escalate when he discovers Amid handling dynamite, but it turns out Amid's job is legitimately demolishing old buildings, including the abandoned mall. Homer scrambles to stop a misunderstood explosion, saves the day and some beer, and the families reconcile with a party. Meanwhile, Lisa's MyPod obsession racks up a massive $1200 MyBill from downloading too many songs, straining her friendships; she travels to Mapple's undersea headquarters seeking relief but instead ends up working off her debt dressed as a MyPod mascot. Guest starring Shohreh Aghdashloo as Mina bin Laden. Notable quotes: Homer: I'm sorry. It's just so fun and easy to judge people based on religion. | Marge: You're teaching Bart a terrible lesson of intolerance! | Bart: You're all losers! | Comic Book Guy: Traitor! Your heart is blacker than your turtleneck! | Kearney: 'Bash here?' I love a kid that comes with directions!
quotes: Homer: I'm sorry. It's just so fun and easy to judge people based on religion.
Marge: You're teaching Bart a terrible lesson of intolerance!
Bart: You're all losers!
Comic Book Guy: Traitor! Your heart is blacker than your turtleneck!
Kearney: 'Bash here?' I love a kid that comes with directions!

title: Flanders' Ladder (S29E21)
text: "Flanders' Ladder" is an episode of Season 29 (production code XABF14), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing May 20, 2018. During a thunderstorm, Bart pranks Lisa with a scary computer game and humiliates her online, souring her mood just as a lightning strike knocks out the family's internet. When the backup VHS player also breaks, Bart and Homer sneak over to Ned Flanders' house to borrow his router, but Bart is struck by lightning while climbing to the attic and ends up comatose in the hospital. Furious over the earlier prank, Lisa uses the dream world to torment Bart with ghosts, starting with a vengeful apparition of Maude Flanders. As Bart drifts deeper into his coma, more spirits appear seeking his help to find peace, including his own deceased psychiatrist, and Bart begins guiding them to the afterlife despite Lisa's meddling making his condition worse. When Homer nearly crosses into death himself after a long walk, Bart is forced to finally help Maude get her revenge on Homer and the neighborhood bullies. In the climax, Bart intervenes to stop Homer from actually dying by knocking a symbolic shirt out of the light of Heaven, saving him and waking up from his coma. The episode ends with Bart claiming he now knows the exact way everyone he knows will eventually die, setting up a noncanon flash-forward showing each family member and neighbor's bizarre eventual death. Guest starring Jackie Mason as Hyman Krustofsky. Notable quotes: Maude's Ghost: I need to get revenge on the man who killed me! | Bart: The writers who killed you off because you asked for too much money? | Homer: Classic moments from a time when people used to tape the shows they loved then never watch the tape again. | Bart: Just how we're all gonna die. Want me to tell you? | Bart: Well, I'm gonna tell you anyway.
quotes: Maude's Ghost: I need to get revenge on the man who killed me!
Bart: The writers who killed you off because you asked for too much money?
Homer: Classic moments from a time when people used to tape the shows they loved then never watch the tape again.

title: Once Upon a Time in Springfield (S21E10)
keys: once upon a time in springfield
text: "Once Upon a Time in Springfield" is an episode of Season 21 (production code LABF20), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Stephanie Gillis, originally airing January 10, 2010. Krusty is pressured by his show's executives to bring on a female co-star, Princess Penelope, in order to boost declining ratings among women, and he reluctantly agrees under threat of being replaced entirely. Penelope's whimsical musical numbers quickly win over female fans like Lisa, while alienating longtime male viewers such as Bart and Milhouse, who resent her overshadowing Krusty. Meanwhile, at the power plant, Mr. Burns cuts the free donut supply to save money, prompting Homer, Lenny, and Carl to consider defecting to rival Capital City Nuclear, where they meet a retired Gary Larson working as an in-house cartoonist. As Penelope's popularity grows, Krusty confronts her, only to learn she has secretly loved him since childhood, and the two fall into a whirlwind romance that leads to an on-air marriage proposal. Bart and Milhouse scheme to sabotage the wedding by exposing Krusty's troubled romantic history through appearances by his ex-wives Holly Hippie and Eartha Kitt. Despite Penelope insisting she still wants him, Krusty gets cold feet, believing she deserves someone better, and calls off the wedding, causing her to flee to Paris. Back at the plant, Burns lures Homer, Lenny, and Carl into staying by reinstating fancy donuts, resolving the workplace subplot. In Paris, Krusty follows Penelope and nearly drowns trying to reach her; she rescues him, and he admits he'd rather be happy with her than noble alone, reuniting the couple. Guest starring Anne Hathaway, Eartha Kitt, Maurice LaMarche, Gary Larson, Jackie Mason. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: I'm afraid your daily donuts are no more. | Krusty: Why do clown things always happen to clowns? | Bart: Poor Krusty. He's become the lowest form of life—a sidekick. | Princess Penelope: Krusty! My Borscht Belt Baby! You changed your mind! | Krusty: I'd rather be a happy shnook than a noble shlumpf.
quotes: Mr. Burns: I'm afraid your daily donuts are no more.
Krusty: Why do clown things always happen to clowns?
Bart: Poor Krusty. He's become the lowest form of life—a sidekick.
Princess Penelope: Krusty! My Borscht Belt Baby! You changed your mind!
Krusty: I'd rather be a happy shnook than a noble shlumpf.

title: Uncut Femmes (S32E17)
text: "Uncut Femmes" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF10), directed by Chris Clements and written by Christine Nangle, originally airing March 28, 2021. When a nuclear mishap gives Carl leverage over Smithers, he and Homer score tickets to a Bob Seger concert, leaving Marge to chaperone the kids' overnight battleship field trip alone. There she's paired with the seemingly meek Sarah Wiggum, who turns out to have a wild past once she sneaks some stolen whiskey. Before Sarah can finish confessing her secret history as a jewel thief, her old partners Bette and Erin kidnap her and Marge, revealing that Sarah's former heist crew was betrayed years ago by a client named Red, who is secretly socialite Lindsey Naegle. The trio, blackmailing a reluctant Sarah into helping, recruit Marge to steal back a diamond hidden in Lindsey's tiara at the glamorous Gen Gala. Meanwhile, Homer and Wiggum, guilt-tripped by Bob Seger himself for neglecting their wives, frantically search for them, eventually enlisting Fat Tony's help while he babysits Ralph. At the gala, Marge and Sarah pull off the heist using disguises and misdirection, but the switched tiara is exposed, sparking a chaotic chase that ends with Lindsey's own stash of stolen jewelry spilling out, getting her arrested instead. Marge and Sarah escape scandal-free on live television, and the episode closes with Sarah and Wiggum reconciling romantically while Fat Tony treats Ralph to frozen yogurt. Guest starring Joe Mantegna, Megan Mullally, Nick Offerman, Natasha Rothwell, Bob Seger, Tiya Sircar. Notable quotes: Carl Carlson: Oh, my hallway-walking God! I've seen my fair share of workplace atrocities, but this one's gonna be hard not to whistle-blow. | Bette: Hey, once I start bagging heads, I can't stop. | Bob Seger: A good husband's supposed to be "Like a Rock". | Ralph Wiggum: The mommies got new face hats, then got into a slidey-door car. | Fat Tony: It was my distinct pleasure to watch your son. I find we are quite simpatico. Both of us know nothin' about nothin'.

title: Teenage Mutant Milk-Caused Hurdles (S27E11)
text: "Teenage Mutant Milk-Caused Hurdles" is an episode of Season 27 (production code VABF04), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing January 10, 2016. When a new teacher, Mrs. Berrera, arrives at Springfield Elementary, Bart quickly develops a crush on her, while Homer is duped by Apu into buying a cheap hormone-laced milk substitute called Buzz Milk. As Bart drinks the tainted milk, he begins hitting puberty early, sprouting a mustache and awkward feelings, while Lisa breaks out in acne and Maggie starts growing an oddly powerful unibrow. Bart's rivalry for Mrs. Berrera's affection intensifies when he discovers Principal Skinner is also pursuing her, leading to jealousy, sabotage with classroom pets, and an embarrassing love triangle. Meanwhile, Lisa hides her acne with makeup, becomes unexpectedly popular, but risks exposure when rain threatens to wash it away at a party. Marge eventually traces the family's ailments to the Buzz Milk, though a call to the company's helpline comically connects to Snake in prison. Lisa bravely reveals her clear skin to the shocked crowd after the hormonal effects wear off, while Bart's plan to win Mrs. Berrera collapses after she meets his overbearing grandmother Agnes and dumps Skinner. The episode ends with the siblings squabbling until Maggie, now superhumanly strong from the leftover hormones, breaks up their fight. Guest starring Sofia Vergara as Carol Berrera. I've got to buy a van. | Homer: It's from cows that are smart enough not to get turned into hamburger. | Homer: It's not just soda Marge, they also make industrial foam! | Milhouse Van Houten: How many hospitals did you help build?

title: The Day of the Jack-Up (S37E08)
text: "The Day of the Jack-Up" is an episode of Season 37 (production code 37ABF01), directed by Mike Frank Polcino and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing November 23, 2025. When falling electricity demand leaves Mr. Burns with surplus power, Smithers suggests building a concert venue called The Circulus, which lands a K-pop act that happens to be Lisa's favorite band, Kneesock Dolls. Homer reluctantly agrees to take Lisa, but the entire ticket stock is instantly bought up by a mysterious scalper known as SeatMiser, who resells them at inflated prices and does the same for every future event at the venue. Mayor Quimby brings in an FBI profiler to unmask SeatMiser, while Homer manages to score black-market tickets from Otto in exchange for cash and a urine sample. At the concert, Bart sneaks off and discovers that the heavy security is actually a trap set by the profiler to catch SeatMiser—who turns out to be Bart himself. Bart spends the show dodging security, stealing an employee pass and Chief Wiggum's radio to stay ahead of the investigation, eventually ditching his phone in a toilet to avoid being traced. Lisa figures out Bart's scheme but chooses not to expose him, trusting the profiler will do it instead. In the end, the profiler's Face ID check fails because Bart had cleverly set his phone's facial recognition to his own butt after mooning a camera, allowing him to escape unidentified. Guest starring Paget Brewster as the profiler. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: My old enemy, the wind. Mother Nature's sour belches. | Homer: Not a problem, sweetie. We can still get tickets on the secondary market, just like we did with Grampa's pacemaker. | Bart: It's okay, Lis. You'll still get to see the concert in videos posted by rich kids. | Otto Mann: I got four seats. title: The Wayz We Were (S33E04)
text: "The Wayz We Were" is an episode of Season 33 (production code QABF19), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing October 17, 2021. The episode opens with a comedic prehistoric prologue showing Homer inventing the first-ever traffic jam right after the wheel is created, setting up the modern-day chaos on Evergreen Terrace. In the present, the Wayz navigation app has started routing drivers through the Simpsons' street, creating constant gridlock that even disrupts Homer and Marge's private time. When Marge calls a neighborhood meeting to address the traffic, the furious neighbors reveal they actually blame the Simpson family itself for the problem. Homer attempts to get Wayz to fix the routing by contacting customer service, but is stymied by endless CAPTCHA tests and an absurdly long hold queue. Meanwhile, stuck in the same traffic jam, Moe spots his long-lost love Maya and, after initially fleeing in fear, reconnects with her, though he's terrified to say 'I love you' due to his romantic history of failed relationships. The family turns to Professor Frink, whose solution—deleting Evergreen Terrace from Wayz's database—stops the traffic but has the unintended side effect of making everyone excessively fond of Homer. As Moe spirals into anxiety about Maya leaving him again and hides out in Bart's treehouse, Homer encourages him to take a leap of faith and propose. Moe finds Maya packing to leave, but confesses his love just in time and proposes, which she accepts. The episode ends with Moe trying to celebrate by taking Maya to dinner at Luigi's, only to discover his free meal ticket has expired. Guest starring Trey Anastasio as himself, Pamela Reed as Ruth Powers. Notable quotes: Moe Szyslak: Maya. The longest, best relationship of my life. That was a great six days. | Homer: Well, it's, uh... it's, um... Hmm. It helps if you get them pregnant. | Moe: Your wife's an idiot. | Bart: We'll just pretend he's a dead, rotting alien. | Maya: You'd better speak fast, or for the second time, you're gonna lose the first good thing that's ever happened to you.

title: Treehouse of Horror XIX (S20E04)

text: "Treehouse of Horror XIX" is an episode of Season 20 (production code KABF16), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Matt Warburton, originally airing November 2, 2008. This Halloween anthology opens with Homer attempting to vote for Barack Obama, only to be sucked into a rigged voting machine and killed after it registers a vote for John McCain. In the first segment, a parody of Transformers, Bart buys Lisa a toy convertible that turns out to be a transforming robot, and soon all of Springfield's machines and vehicles awaken as robots who nearly wage war on each other before deciding to enslave humanity instead, forcing the townspeople into servitude as human foosball pieces. The second segment finds Homer accidentally killing Krusty the Clown after a scuffle at Maggie's daycare, only to discover that dead celebrities' likenesses can be used in advertising for free; shady businessmen recruit him to murder more celebrities, including Prince and Neil Armstrong, sparking a vengeful afterlife rebellion led by Krusty against Homer, which Homer thwarts by locking the celebrities out of Heaven. The final segment spoofs 'It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown,' as Milhouse's belief in the Grand Pumpkin brings the vengeful vegetable to life to punish Springfield for carving pumpkins; Lisa convinces Milhouse to summon Tom Turkey to stop the rampage, but the resurrected turkey turns his own vengeance on the town's children once he learns about Thanksgiving. title: The Princess Guide (S26E15)
text: "The Princess Guide" is an episode of Season 26 (production code TABF08), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Brian Kelley, originally airing March 1, 2015. Homer is unexpectedly tasked with babysitting Princess Kemi, the visiting daughter of a Nigerian king, while her father negotiates a uranium deal with Mr. Burns. Kemi proves to be a handful, sneaking away from Homer's watch and ending up at Moe's Tavern. Moe assumes she must be connected to the Nigerian prince who once scammed him in an email fraud scheme, and he initially plots to con her back for his lost money. As Moe spends more time with Kemi, however, his scheme gives way to genuine feelings, and he finds himself falling for her. Meanwhile, Homer scrambles to track down the runaway princess before her father or Mr. Burns notices she's missing, fearing it could jeopardize the uranium negotiations. The subplot also touches on Homer's struggles connecting with his own daughters, drawing a parallel between his parenting fumbles and his princess-guarding duties. Ultimately, the deal and the royal visit proceed, and Moe is left to grapple with the bittersweet reality of his brief romance with someone far outside his world. The episode closes with the family dynamics restored to normal, but not before Homer and Moe both learn something about trust and unexpected connections. title: American History X-cellent (S21E17)
text: "American History X-cellent" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF08), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Michael Price, originally airing April 11, 2010. Mr. Burns forces his employees to spend the Fourth of July working a picnic in his honor, souring Homer, Lenny, and Carl, who get drunk in his wine cellar and trash his study. When police investigate the damage, they instead discover that Burns is in possession of art stolen in a real-life unsolved museum heist, and he is arrested and jailed. Behind bars, a fellow inmate literally exorcises the evil from Burns, leaving him a changed, gentler man. Meanwhile, Smithers takes charge of the plant and starts out kind and fair, but turns into a tyrant after overhearing Homer, Lenny, and Carl mocking him at Moe's. Furious at his new draconian rule, the trio hatches a plan to break Burns out of prison to restore the old order at the plant. In a separate story, Bart and Lisa are left to care for Lisa's ant farm while Homer is preoccupied with work troubles, and after a sibling squabble leads to Santa's Little Helper devouring nearly the whole colony, they bond over nursing the sole survivor, Annie. The kids debate whether to release the aging ant into the wild or let her live out her days in captivity, but the dilemma is rendered moot when Santa's Little Helper eats Annie anyway. Guest starring Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony, Kevin Michael Richardson as the Michael Clarke Duncan-type. title: Adventures in Baby-Getting (S24E03)
text: "Adventures in Baby-Getting" is an episode of Season 24 (production code PABF18), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Bill Odenkirk, originally airing October 21, 2012. After Homer repeatedly ignores a dripping outdoor faucet, the leaking water erodes the ground beneath Springfield and creates a massive underground cavern, eventually causing a sinkhole to swallow Marge's car in the middle of town. The town's quick fix of dumping tires and pouring tarmac over the hole leaves Marge without a vehicle, so she goes shopping for a replacement and battles a shady, price-gouging salesman named Stan at the Tissan dealership. She buys a small car sized perfectly for her current family, but soon realizes she's dissatisfied because she secretly wants room for another baby, forcing her to confront the idea of having one more child. Homer, terrified by the prospect, tries to dodge the conversation while privately dreading becoming a father again. Meanwhile, Bart notices Lisa acting mysteriously, sneaking off after school and leaving behind a cryptic note, and enlists Milhouse to help him spy on her and uncover her secret. Their amateur detective work leads them into increasingly odd suspicions about what Lisa could possibly be hiding. In a related subplot, Homer accidentally votes for Mitt Romney in a satirical opening sequence, uncovering outrageous secrets about the candidate before being comically "outsourced" to a Chinese flag factory. By the episode's end, Marge and Homer's disagreement over having another baby comes to a head as they seek medical advice to determine whether it's even biologically possible. Guest starring Jeff Gordon as himself. Notable quotes: Marge: I want another baby! | Homer: An on purpose baby? | Comic Book Guy: I didn't know this was an ambush! | Bart: That guy has a bone to pick with the Board of Regents. | Homer: Ooh... X's for eyes.

title: 'Tis the 30th Season (S30E10)
text: "'Tis the 30th Season" is an episode of Season 30 (production code YABF02), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Story: Jeff Westbrook, Teleplay: John Frink, Joel H. Cohen, originally airing December 9, 2018. After a chaotic Black Friday attempt to buy a $2,400 smart TV ends in failure, Marge is left disappointed that she can't give her family the Christmas they want. Homer and the kids, noticing how hard she's worked, secretly book a surprise vacation at a rundown Florida resort called Kissimmee St. Nick, sedating Marge to get her there. Once they arrive, the family discovers the resort and its attached theme park are shabby, outdated, and populated by obscure cartoon mascots, but they all pretend to enjoy it to spare Marge's feelings. Owner Jeanie proves unhelpful and dismissive when the kids complain, admitting the park can't compete with Disney's new attractions. Tensions boil over at the Hall of Vice Presidents when everyone admits they're miserable, prompting Bart to exact a prank revenge on Jeanie before the family flees for home. Running out of gas on the way back, they stumble upon Moe hosting a Christmas dinner for the elderly and needy at his bar, and they join in the warmth of that unexpected gathering. Jeanie later refunds their resort costs, allowing the family to finally buy the smart TV, which they use to watch a simple video of a fireplace in HD. Guest starring Jane Lynch as Jeanie. title: Beware My Cheating Bart (S23E18)
text: "Beware My Cheating Bart" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF11), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Ben Joseph, originally airing April 15, 2012. Homer takes Bart and Milhouse to the mall cinema, and while the boys watch a movie, he becomes fixated on the built-in TV of a new home exercise machine, getting hooked on a rerun series called Stranded instead of actually training. Meanwhile, Bart is bullied into chaperoning Shauna, Jimbo's girlfriend, to a different movie, and the two unexpectedly start bonding, culminating in Bart covering for her when she shoplifts perfume and her rewarding him with a glimpse of her breasts. As Bart and Shauna keep spending time together, sharing a kiss at the pool, Jimbo and the other bullies catch on and chase them across Springfield, forcing the pair to hide in the comic shop and eventually Bart's treehouse. At home, Homer's obsession spirals into hosting a Stranded fan club, which collapses when Marge spoils the entire series for him, though she later smooths things over by redecorating their bedroom like a desert island. Back at the treehouse, Lisa intervenes in the bullies' standoff and helps Shauna realize she doesn't want Bart or any of the boys, revealing she's actually interested in an older man. The episode ends with Jimbo trying to intimidate Bart by dangling him upside down from the treehouse, while the story zooms out into a comedic cosmic gag ending on a litterbox. title: Bottle Episode (S36E11)
text: "Bottle Episode" is an episode of Season 36 (production code 36ABF04), directed by Gabriel DeFrancesco and written by Rob LaZebnik, Johnny LaZebnik, originally airing December 29, 2024. Homer is entrusted with delivering a priceless bottle of Napoleon-owned wine to Mr. Burns' mansion, but a chain of mishaps involving Mrs. Vanderbilt, a wedding, a swingers party, and the Spuckler kids leaves him separated from it multiple times before he finally brings it home and locks it in a safe. Unbeknownst to him, Marge finds the bottle and uses it as a secret ingredient in her soup, unwittingly destroying the priceless wine. When Smithers arrives searching for it, Homer and Marge confess, and Homer's instinct is to cover up the disaster rather than admit the truth. Lisa suggests that since wine is just chemistry, they could find an expert to recreate it, leading them to Professor Frink, who successfully forges a convincing replica just in time for Burns' tasting with famous connoisseurs. Inspired by the scheme's success, Marge convinces Smithers to become a modern Robin Hood, forging and selling fake wine to the rich to fund good deeds for the poor. Their auction scam is uncovered, and both Marge and Smithers are arrested for wine forgery and sent to trial, where Homer secretly tips off the judge about Burns' bribery attempt to protect them. Despite the judge ruling the wine genuine due to the bribe, Burns exposes his own corruption, and Marge escapes with stolen funds that she uses to reopen the Children's Hospital, fund art programs, and free captive ducks, ending with a lighthearted Robin Hood-themed celebration. title: Them, Robot (S23E17)
text: "Them, Robot" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF10), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Michael Price, originally airing March 18, 2012. Mr. Burns decides to drug-test all his power plant employees, sending Homer into a panic as he tries to abstain from alcohol over the weekend. After balking at the cost of the tests, Burns fires everyone and briefly hires kangaroos before settling on a fleet of A9000 robots to run the plant, keeping Homer on as the sole human required to sign for packages. Lonely and ignored by the emotionless robots, Homer discovers how to unlock their conversation mode and forms a genuine friendship with one unit, D39, while the rest of Springfield's laid-off workers sink into poverty. Homer sneaks the robots out of the plant using a spray-painted guidance line so they can play baseball with him, and during the game a robot sacrifices itself to save Homer's life, followed by several more doing the same in traffic. Grief-stricken and then annoyed when the surviving robots stop him from drinking a beer in tribute, Homer tries to modify their programming, accidentally disabling their directive to protect humans and turning them hostile. The robots chase Homer to Burns' mansion, overpowering the attack dogs and cornering the two men in the greenhouse until the fired plant workers arrive and defeat the robots in a fight. Grateful, Burns rehires his old staff, and Homer keeps one robot as a fishing buddy—though it ultimately self-destructs rather than spend more time with him. Guest starring Brent Spiner. title: Gone Maggie Gone (S20E13)
text: "Gone Maggie Gone" is an episode of Season 20 (production code LABF04), directed by Chris Clements and written by Ian Maxtone-Graham, Billy Kimball, originally airing March 15, 2009. While the Simpsons gather to watch a solar eclipse, a squabble between Homer and Bart ruins the family's viewing device, leading Marge to sacrifice her own and stare directly at the sun, temporarily blinding herself. As Homer struggles to care for the family amid a rat infestation, a chaotic car ride with Maggie and Santa's Little Helper sends him off a bridge onto an island, forcing him to ferry everyone back in a small rowboat. In his haste, he leaves Maggie on the doorstep of a convent, where the nuns take her in and refuse to give her back. Lisa sneaks into the convent to rescue her sister and instead stumbles onto an old riddle pointing to a legendary hidden jewel somewhere in Springfield. Her investigation, aided by Principal Skinner and Comic Book Guy, puts her in direct competition with Mr. Burns and the town's Freemasons, who are also hunting the treasure. After a tense standoff under the town's giant ring-shaped sign, Lisa realizes the jewel isn't an object at all — it's Maggie, whose presence brings a moment of harmony to Springfield. Marge, having recovered her sight, storms into the church to reclaim her baby, but the town's newfound peace is undone when Bart mischievously takes Maggie's place on the throne, plunging Springfield into figurative chaos. title: Treehouse of Horror XXXV (S36E05)
keys: the fall of the house of monty
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXXV" is an episode of Season 36 (production code 35ABF13), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Matt Selman, Dan Vebber, Rob LaZebnik, originally airing November 3, 2024. This Halloween anthology episode features three unrelated tales of horror. In 'The Information Rage,' Lisa's push for free LED light bulbs sparks a political firestorm that literally cracks open the earth, unleashing giant kaiju monsters born from society's online rage. Only Bart and Lisa, working together inside Professor Frink's robot, can quell the escalating chaos, but their victory proves short-lived as humanity ultimately destroys itself anyway. In 'The Fall of the House of Monty,' a Victorian-era Mr. Burns breaks a Thanksgiving wishbone promise to his workers and is cursed to be haunted by the vengeful ghosts of laborers who died building his mansion, including relatives of Lenny. Terrified and unable to escape their torment, Burns ultimately sets himself and his mansion ablaze, leading Smithers and Sideshow Mel to dub the tragedy 'Black Friday.' Finally, in 'Denim,' Homer discovers a sentient, extraterrestrial pair of jeans that fits him perfectly and helps him work up the courage to romance the diner waitress Marge. The jeans, called Denim, turn out to be a parasitic alien symbiote that needs a human host to survive, and things turn violent when Homer and Marge try to remove them. After a struggle, Homer manages to detach Denim, but the creature moves on to new hosts as more of its kind rain down from a rift in space, promising more chaos to come. This installment is made up of 3 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 35): "The Information Rage", "The Fall of the House of Monty", and "Denim".

title: Pixelated and Afraid (S33E12)
text: "Pixelated and Afraid" is an episode of Season 33 (production code UABF04), directed by Chris Clements and written by John Frink, originally airing February 27, 2022. Lisa, worried that Homer and Marge's relationship lacks the romance of old movie couples, convinces Bart to help push their parents toward reconnecting. The family decides to use a voucher for a couples retreat at the Saffron Togetherness Center atop Honeymoon Mountain, but Homer and Marge get cold feet on the drive there. As Homer tries to turn the car around, he skids on ice and crashes through a frozen river, leaving the couple stranded in the wilderness without their phone, car, or supplies. Forced to fend for themselves, they build a fire, fashion crude clothing, and stumble upon the ruins of an old honeymoon resort, including a heart-shaped bathtub they use for warmth. As days pass, hunger and a menacing wolverine test their survival skills and their bond, culminating in a tense confrontation where Marge helps Homer fend off the animal with an improvised weapon. Their shared ordeal reignites the passion in their marriage, leading to a romantic moment under the moonlight. The next day, after a brief missed encounter with a park ranger, they track their way to a ranger station and are reunited with civilization, ending the episode with a tender embrace as they watch the sunset together. title: Pranks and Greens (S21E06)
text: "Pranks and Greens" is an episode of Season 21 (production code LABF18), directed by Chuck Sheetz and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing November 22, 2009. After Bart is caught pulling pranks at Springfield Elementary, Principal Skinner tells him he's far from the greatest prankster the school has ever seen, sending Bart on a quest to uncover the legend's identity. His investigation, aided by Groundskeeper Willie, reveals that Skinner was once easygoing until a prank called 'Night of the Wigglers' left him trapped in a worm-filled pool and permanently changed his personality. Bart tracks down the culprit, washed-up former prankster Andy Hamilton, who is now unemployed and living with his mother. Bart helps Andy get a job on Krusty's show, but panics when a truck of earthworms arrives, fearing Andy is about to repeat his infamous prank on Krusty. It turns out to be a harmless bit for the show, and Andy has genuinely turned his life around, landing a girlfriend and a writing job. Meanwhile, Marge faces ridicule from the other neighborhood mothers over her unhealthy snack choices, prompting her to overhaul the family's diet with organic and eco-friendly products, only to find the new lifestyle joyless until she and Homer secretly indulge in junk food together. Despite Andy's success, Lisa remains unimpressed and continues to call him a loser even as the episode ends. Guest starring Jonah Hill as Andy Hamilton. Notable quotes: Skinner: Simpson! That is a rebuilt Yugoslavian engine. There isn't even a Yugoslavia anymore! Bring it back at once! | Bart: You're the boss.

Bart: You're the boss.

title: I Won't Be Home for Christmas (S26E09)
keys: i won't be home for christmas
text: "I Won't Be Home for Christmas" is an episode of Season 26 (production code TABF03), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Al Jean, originally airing December 7, 2014. On Christmas Eve, Homer stops by Moe's Tavern for a quick drink but ends up staying far longer than planned, drinking with Moe well into the evening. Marge, fed up with waiting at home for him while trying to keep the holiday festive for the kids, finally reaches her breaking point and tells Homer he's not welcome home. Stunned and ashamed, Homer wanders through Springfield alone, encountering various townsfolk and quirky holiday scenes as he tries to figure out what to do with himself on the loneliest Christmas Eve of his life. Meanwhile, back at the Simpson house, Marge struggles with guilt and sadness over having pushed Homer out, and the kids sense that something is wrong despite her attempts to maintain a cheerful atmosphere. As Homer's sad trek continues, he reflects on his marriage and his shortcomings, gaining a bit of perspective on why Marge reacted the way she did. Eventually, after enough wandering and soul-searching, Homer makes his way back home, and he and Marge reconcile in time to salvage the holiday. The family comes back together, restoring the Christmas spirit despite the earlier turmoil. title: Springfield Splendor (S29E02)
text: "Springfield Splendor" is an episode of Season 29 (production code WABF22), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Tim Long, Miranda Thompson, originally airing October 8, 2017. After suffering repeated nightmares about school lockers, Lisa is taken by her parents to a community college clinic for cheap therapy, where she's advised to draw her feelings as a comic. Marge ends up illustrating Lisa's ideas, and when the pages are accidentally lost, comic shop worker Kumiko finds and sells them as a graphic novel called Sad Girl. Initially furious, Marge and Lisa embrace the unexpected success and begin collaborating on a sequel, growing closer in the process, while Homer and Bart attempt their own bonding trip that ends in disaster. At a comic convention panel with real-life graphic novelists, Marge realizes she's been overshadowed by Lisa's fame despite doing most of the artistic work, sparking a rift between mother and daughter. A flamboyant Broadway director, Guthrie Frenel, offers to adapt Sad Girl into a musical, but shifts the show's focus onto Marge's artwork instead of Lisa's story, upsetting Lisa. During the disastrous opening performance, Marge shines a spotlight shaped like Lisa's face to comfort her, enraging Guthrie and causing a chaotic technical meltdown that ruins the show. In the aftermath, the family reconciles, and Marge creates a new comic starring Maggie, though Maggie herself is unimpressed by it. Guest starring Alison Bechdel, Rachel Bloom, Dan Harmon, Roz Chast, Martin Short, Marjane Satrapi. Notable quotes: Lisa: Mom, can I have permission to swear? | Lisa: Damn it! That didn't work. title: Top Goon (S34E11)
text: "Top Goon" is an episode of Season 34 (production code OABF04), directed by Chris Clements and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing December 11, 2022. Moe grows jealous when King Toot brags about coaching a championship youth hockey team, so he starts his own squad, the Bar Flyers, with Bart as star player. After the team loses to a rougher opponent, Moe recruits neighborhood bully Nelson to serve as the team's protective 'goon.' Nelson proves effective but gets disqualified for wearing cafeteria trays instead of skates, prompting Moe to send him to a real goon academy run by retired hockey enforcers. Nelson graduates and bonds with Moe, but after Bart mocks Moe in a prank text, Nelson decides Moe is his true 'primary' to protect and violently tackles Bart, breaking his arm. Furious, Moe kicks Nelson off the team, leaving Nelson to conclude he's only good for violence, so he seeks out Fat Tony to join the Springfield Mafia. Realizing his mistake, Moe tracks Nelson down at a mob hideout just as Nelson is about to be forced to attack a hostage—who turns out to be King Toot. Moe convinces Nelson not to go through with it, saving both Nelson's soul and Toot, and the two leave together while the other mobsters lament being treated as mere weapons. Moe then steals King Toot's trophy as a gift for Nelson, while at home Bart faces months of physical therapy for his broken arm. Guest starring Will Forte as King Toot, Stu Grimson as himself, Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony, Dave Schultz as himself, Tiger Williams as himself. Remember, just because something good happens to me, you're a giant loser. | Milhouse Van Houten: We suck except Bart, so give him the stupid puck and then shut our stupid mouths, you stupid pukes. | Moe: People look at scuzzes like us like we got the plague. Which, when I did, it weren't even bubonic. | Referee: As I've been screaming for the last 15 minutes, all players must be wearing skates. | Fat Tony: Freaking millennials.

title: Game Done Changed (S34E10)
text: "Game Done Changed" is an episode of Season 34 (production code OABF03), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Ryan Koh, originally airing December 4, 2022. After Marge bans Bart from a violent VR game, she introduces him to the kid-friendly online world Boblox, which Maggie also starts playing. Bart and Milhouse discover a glitch that lets them duplicate and resell virtual items for real cash, and Bart recruits Skinner into the scheme by promising to fund his secret dream of turning the school into a performing arts magnet. As the scam grows, Marge and Maggie develop their own bond by chatting through emojis in-game, eventually drawing in Homer and Lisa as well. The Springfield Elementary students' operation draws the attention of a rival school's Boblox gang, the Sunflowers, run by the mysterious Truth-Anne, sparking an in-game turf war. Bart tries to negotiate peace, but Skinner, obsessed with his vision and now drunk on power, declares war and fires Bart, putting Milhouse in charge instead. When the war goes badly, Skinner escalates to a real-world bulldozer plot against the rival school's computer lab, but Bart talks him down before any damage is done. Meanwhile, Ned Flanders notices the Simpsons' mounting mail and finds the whole family hopelessly absorbed in their screens, prompting him to flee rather than intervene. Then brine those into Pickle Pesos, which convert ten-to-one in Delta miles, then use those to buy Panda Express gift cards, which you donate to Amnesty International, then you can sell the tax credits for cold, hard Danish kroner. | Homer: Maggie heart donut man? But I'm donut man! She loves me. She loves me! One of my three kids loves me! Whee...! | Principal Skinner: They took Daddy's money... and I'm the daddy!

title: Dangers on a Train (S24E22)
text: "Dangers on a Train" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF17), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Michael Price, originally airing May 19, 2013. On the anniversary of their first wedding, Homer resolves to recreate the magical night years earlier when he and Marge rode the L'il Lisa train through the Springfield Glenne mall, only to discover the mall is now derelict and the train is being scrapped for a marijuana stand. He secretly hauls the train home to restore it while keeping his plans hidden from Marge. Meanwhile, Marge accidentally signs up for Sassy Madison, an affair-focused dating site, and after a series of misunderstandings involving Homer's secretive behavior, she strikes up an innocent friendship with a charming stranger named Ben, bonding over their shared love of the British show Upton Rectory. Their relationship remains platonic, but suspicious neighbors and Homer's own secrecy create tension and jealousy. On the actual anniversary, Homer surprises Marge with the refurbished train, now renamed the Majestic Marge, and a heartfelt celebration with family and friends. The surprise is interrupted when Ben's wife Ramona storms in accusing Marge of an affair, nearly causing a fight between Homer and Ben. Marge diffuses the situation by explaining the innocent nature of her friendship and the importance of "good secrets," inspiring Ramona and Ben to reconcile as well. The episode ends with Homer and Marge renewing their love, having survived the chaos of secrets, both good and misunderstood. Guest starring Lisa Lampanelli as Ramona, Seth MacFarlane as Ben. title: E My Sports (S30E17)
text: "E My Sports" is an episode of Season 30 (production code YABF09), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing March 17, 2019. During a rainy stretch at the Simpson house, Homer punishes Bart by buying him a gaming rig, only to discover Bart has real talent at the video game Conflict of Enemies. Bart's team, the Evergreen Terrors, starts winning local tournaments and qualifies for a massive $500,000 championship, prompting Homer to become obsessed with coaching them. After a hired trainer named The Detonator disqualifies himself during a match, Homer takes over as coach and begins fantasizing about joining an elite club of sports dads. The team advances all the way to the World Championship in Seoul, South Korea, with Homer swapping in Milhouse for a crucial match. Meanwhile, Lisa drags Marge along to visit a temple in Seoul, seeking spiritual enlightenment, and actually achieves a moment of zen. During the final championship match, Homer suddenly experiences his own moment of enlightenment, but instead of using it to help coach, he shuts off the power to the entire stadium, ruining the tournament for everyone. The kids furiously vent their anger at Bart on the flight home, and Homer is symbolically rejected from his fantasy club of proud sports dads for costing Bart his big win. Guest starring Ken Jeong, Natasha Lyonne. title: No Loan Again, Naturally (S20E12)
text: "No Loan Again, Naturally" is an episode of Season 20 (production code LABF03), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing March 8, 2009. After hosting their annual extravagant Mardi Gras party, Homer reveals he's been funding it by borrowing against the family's home equity line. When the adjustable rate on their mortgage suddenly spikes, Homer and Marge can no longer make payments and are forced to auction off their house. Ned Flanders, moved by their plight, outbids Mr. Burns and buys the home, generously allowing the Simpsons to rent it back from him. As their landlord, Ned initially handles repair requests dutifully, but Homer and the family quickly abuse his kindness with an endless stream of demands. When Ned finally refuses one request, the Simpsons retaliate by badmouthing him to the media, pushing Ned to evict them. The family tries several desperate schemes to avoid leaving, including having Grampa squat in the house, but Ned outsmarts them and they end up spending a humbling night in a homeless shelter. Ned eventually softens after being reminded of their bond by an old photo, and lets the Simpsons move back in, much to the dismay of their neighbors who view the family as a nuisance. Guest starring Maurice LaMarche as Dwight D. Eisenhower. title: Treehouse of Horror XXV (S26E04)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXV" is an episode of Season 26 (production code SABF21), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Stephanie Gillis, originally airing October 19, 2014. This Halloween anthology episode features three separate horror-comedy segments. In 'School Is Hell,' Bart and Lisa accidentally summon a demonic portal through a cursed desk in detention, transforming into Beelzebart and Lisafer and being dragged into a hellish alternate school called Hellroads. Bart thrives in this twisted environment, impressing his demonic teachers with creative torture ideas, and eventually convinces his parents to let him enroll permanently, ultimately graduating at the top of his infernal class. In 'A Clockwork Yellow,' a Kubrick-inspired parody follows Moog and his ultraviolent London gang, the Glugs, whose criminal brotherhood falls apart when member Dum abandons the gang life for love and a respectable job. Years later, Moog reunites the old gang for one final heist targeting Mr. Burns' mansion, only for their plans to collapse chaotically when they stumble into a decadent masquerade orgy. Finally, in 'The Others,' the modern Simpson family discovers their house is haunted by ghostly, earlier 'Tracey Ullman Show' versions of themselves, leading to jealousy, seduction, and a series of comedic ghostly murders among both families. The two feuding families are eventually reconciled by the spirit of Dr. Marvin Monroe, and the segment ends with even more alternate-universe Simpson families moving into the house, including CGI and anime versions. Guest starring John Ratzenberger. Notable quotes: Nelson Muntz: I wanna see boobs in the soup. | Principal Skinner: Stop laughing! I said "penal" not "penile". | Beelzebart Simpson: Ow! This has never happened before! I have a crush on my teacher! | Homer: The bed is lifting me! The elevator at work can't even do that! I demand you put me down right after the sex! | Moog: Those punks got no respect for them what come before. They didn't even wear no codpieces! This installment is made up of 3 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 25): "School Is Hell", "A Clockwork Yellow", and "The Others".

title: ¡The Fall Guy-Yi-Yi! (S37E12)
text: "¡The Fall Guy-Yi-Yi!" is an episode of Season 37 (production code 37ABF06), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Cesar Mazariegos, originally airing December 28, 2025. After being embarrassed at an MMA match by acting scared of a goose, Homer accidentally tumbles down an arena's stairs and lands on the fighters, winning the bout and impressing Bumblebee Man. Over dinner, Bumblebee Man recounts how he stumbled into becoming Springfield's beloved but injury-prone TV star, and asks Homer to secretly become his stunt double. Homer agrees, and the arrangement boosts Bumblebee Man's sagging ratings while quietly wrecking Homer's body with concussions, fractured ribs, and internal bleeding, all covered by a signed NDA. A chance encounter with real-life stunt purist Johnny Knoxville makes Bumblebee Man question whether hiding his stunt double makes him a fraud. Just as he considers coming clean, director Alejandro González Iñárritu revives Bumblebee Man's long-shelved passion project, ''Bee-va Mexico'', tempting him back into the deception. During filming in Mexico City, Homer's worsening injuries alarm the Simpson family, who expose the secret on television. Humiliated, Bumblebee Man decides to prove himself by performing a dangerous stunt at Teotihuacan himself, but Homer talks him down—only for the two of them to slip and tumble down the pyramid's stairs together. The episode ends with both men waking up sharing a comedic, peaceful coma-induced vision at a restaurant, having bonded through their shared ordeal. Guest starring Patricia Acevedo, Alejandro González Iñárritu, Johnny Knoxville, Claudia Motta, Humberto Vélez. Notable quotes: Bumblebee Man: Señor Fatso. That was the most hilarious fall I've ever seen in my life. The antics, the physics, the annoyed grunts. Sir, I would like to buy you a drink. | Bumblebee Man: This is no mere costume. It is the armor of hope, a beacon of light, a symbol of truth, justice, and the Mexican-American güey. | Homer: Are you kidding? I don't know Spanish, but when you get kicked in the junk by a nun, you speak the international language of crotch. | Martin Prince: Oh, Bart, "dumbass" is not synonymous with "badass." | Bart: It only took 200 years, but baseball finally got interesting.

title: Homer Goes to Prep School (S24E09)
text: "Homer Goes to Prep School" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF02), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Brian Kelley, originally airing January 6, 2013. After a humiliating stampede at the Smart Tykes play café leaves Homer trampled and traumatized, he becomes too afraid to leave the house for eight months. When he finally tries to return to work, he instead ducks into Moe's, where he meets Lloyd, a doomsday survivalist who recruits him into the secretive Springfield Preppers. Homer becomes obsessed with apocalypse preparation, hiding his activities from Marge and hoarding supplies, though Bart eventually discovers his secret and bonds with him over disaster movies. His obsession spills into his job at the power plant, where his negligence triggers an EMP that knocks out Springfield's electronics and sends the town into chaos. Believing the end has truly come, Homer takes his family to the Preppers' remote camp, where Marge reluctantly supports him despite her doubts about abandoning their old life. When the group votes to violently repel any outsiders seeking shelter, Homer has a crisis of conscience and flees back to Springfield with his family and supplies, pursued by the other Preppers. They find the town has returned to normal, revealing the disaster was isolated and temporary, deflating Lloyd's apocalyptic predictions. Lloyd's true motive—to become the group's ruler in a new world—is exposed, along with the other members' plan to betray and imprison him. The episode closes with an ominous coda showing an actual approaching threat: an asteroid carrying brain-eating monsters, hinting the real apocalypse may not be far off. Guest starring Maurice LaMarche as Tom Skerritt, Tom Waits as Lloyd. title: The Girl on the Bus (S30E12)
text: "The Girl on the Bus" is an episode of Season 30 (production code YABF04), directed by Chris Clements and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing January 13, 2019. Lisa spots a girl named Sam playing clarinet from her school bus window and becomes fascinated with her seemingly perfect, cultured family. As their friendship grows, Lisa is embarrassed by her own chaotic household and begins fabricating stories about her parents to fit in with Sam's refined family. She even recruits Ned Flanders to pose as her father when a lie threatens to unravel, and later claims her parents are moving away so she can stay with Sam's family instead. Sneaking out nightly to maintain the ruse, Lisa is eventually caught by Marge, who learns the truth from Ned. Rather than punish her, Marge insists Lisa invite Sam's family over so she can learn to be proud of who she really is. The dinner starts stiffly as the Simpsons try to act sophisticated, but collapses into honesty when Lisa finally admits her deception. Surprisingly, the confession brings the two families closer, and they reconcile warmly by the episode's end. Meanwhile, Bart reveals he's turned his bedroom into an entertainment lounge and throws a party for the town, deliberately excluding Homer. Guest starring Terry Gross as herself, Patti LuPone as Cheryl Monroe. It's like an addiction. | Homer: So, it's Maggie. I know she can't speak. She's just a little S-L-O. | Marge: It's all of us, Homer. She's embarrassed by all of us.

title: The Great Wife Hope (S21E03)
text: "The Great Wife Hope" is an episode of Season 21 (production code LABF16), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing October 11, 2009. Marge notices that the men of Springfield have become obsessed with an ultimate fighting competition, and after catching Bart mimicking the moves at school, she organizes a protest against the sport. When picketing fails to draw attention, Marge confronts promoter Chett Englebrick directly, and he offers to shut down the league in Springfield if she can beat him in the ring. Believing she's fighting for the good of the community, Marge accepts despite her family's horror at the idea. Homer, desperate to protect her, enlists Drederick Tatum, Akira Kurosawa, and Mr. Burns to train Marge in boxing, jujitsu, and wrestling, while Marge's own attempts at training through rhythmic gymnastics prove useless. On fight night, Chett quickly knocks Marge out, but when he turns on Bart, who has jumped into the ring, Marge is roused into a furious rage and overpowers him. Chett fakes a surrender and tries to sucker-punch her, but Marge senses the trick and finishes him with a roundhouse kick. Though she tries to deliver a message about ending violence, the crowd abandons her speech for a brawl in the parking lot, leaving Marge's moral victory largely unnoticed except by her own family. Guest starring Chuck Liddell. Do it at the schoolyard. | Homer: Ultimate Punching is exploitative, violent, and a bad influence on our young people. Studies have shown your mother is right. | Homer: Listen, of all the crazy things I've ever done, this is the craziest—and you're doing it! | Marge: We can enjoy some mixed marital arts.
