title: 101 Mitigations (S30E15)
text: "101 Mitigations" is an episode of Season 30 (production code YABF07), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Rob LaZebnik, Brian Kelley, Dan Vebber, originally airing March 3, 2019. Homer wins a 100%-off dinner at The Gilded Truffle, while Marge treats herself to a massage with the money they saved. A valet mix-up leaves Homer with the keys to a valuable Cadillac Eldorado belonging to Comic Book Guy, and Homer and the kids take it for a joyride. When they return the car, they discover a rare comic book inside was destroyed, prompting Comic Book Guy to sue Homer for grand theft auto. Judge Snyder finds Homer guilty despite Lisa's touching apology letter, leaving the family scrambling to avoid Homer going to jail. Marge tries to personally reconcile with Comic Book Guy without success, so Lisa proposes making a mitigation video, inspired by a tactic once used by Mr. Burns, with unexpected assistance from filmmaker Guillermo del Toro. After rejecting shaky-camera-prone Gil, the family produces and edits their own heartfelt testimonial video, but Comic Book Guy remains unconvinced even after they replace his destroyed comic with a pristine copy. The situation only turns when Comic Book Guy notices Homer's cherished Welcome Back, Kotter keychain and smashes it with Thor's hammer to make Homer feel his own loss, finally releasing his anger and dropping the charges. The two become unlikely best friends and bond over Comic-Con, while in a side story, Bart cleverly submits a mockingly insincere mitigation video to torment Skinner and dodge detention. Guest starring Guillermo del Toro as himself. Notable quotes: Homer: Your Honor, I'm not the one on trial here. | Judge Snyder: Yes, you are. | Lisa: "Hire a lawyer," I said. "Waste of money," he said. | Sideshow Mel: This is what I spend my time in courtroom audiences for. This is my Starbucks. | Homer: Careful, Marge. He's a lazy, overweight slob. Don't fall in love with him.
quotes: Homer: Your Honor, I'm not the one on trial here.
Judge Snyder: Yes, you are.
Lisa: "Hire a lawyer," I said. "Waste of money," he said.
Sideshow Mel: This is what I spend my time in courtroom audiences for. This is my Starbucks.
Homer: Careful, Marge. He's a lazy, overweight slob. Don't fall in love with him.

title: Treehouse of Horror XXI (S22E04)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXI" is an episode of Season 22 (production code MABF16), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing November 7, 2010. This Halloween special unfolds in three separate segments. In 'War and Pieces,' Marge pushes Bart and Milhouse away from violent video games toward old-fashioned board games, but the boys unwittingly unleash a cursed game called Satan's Path that literally transforms their world into a series of deadly board-game challenges they must survive. In 'Master and Cadaver,' Homer and Marge take a romantic second honeymoon on a sailboat, only to rescue a mysterious castaway named Roger who claims his ship's passengers were poisoned; convinced Roger is the real killer, Homer and Marge murder him and dump his body, then discover evidence suggesting he was innocent all along. Roger returns, prompting Homer to kill him again along with the surviving bankers, horrifying Marge, who then eats a poisoned pie herself—before it's revealed the entire story was just Maggie's imagination. In 'Tweenlight,' a parody of vampire romance stories, Lisa falls for a teenage vampire named Edmund, and after an awkward family dinner, the young couple flees to escape Homer's embarrassing behavior. Homer and Count Dracula track them down, and when Dracula and Edmund try to force Lisa into vampirism, Homer's cholesterol-laden blood proves fatally toxic to the vampires. Homer then transforms into an overweight bat and attempts to fly off, but plummets to his death due to his excessive weight. Guest starring Hugh Laurie, Daniel Radcliffe. Notable quotes: Homer: They should call this one recipe for murder. | Marge: What do you mean "this one?" | Homer: Nevermind. | Rich Uncle Pennybags: There was a bank error in my favor and I'm spending it all on Oriental Avenue prostitutes. | Sideshow Mel: At least the cup is lined with felt. This installment is made up of 3 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 21): "War and Pieces", "Master and Cadaver", and "Tweenlight".
quotes: Homer: They should call this one recipe for murder.
Marge: What do you mean "this one?"
Homer: Nevermind.
Rich Uncle Pennybags: There was a bank error in my favor and I'm spending it all on Oriental Avenue prostitutes.
Sideshow Mel: At least the cup is lined with felt.

title: The Color Yellow (S21E13)
text: "The Color Yellow" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF06), directed by Raymond S. Persi and written by Billy Kimball, Ian Maxtone-Graham, originally airing February 21, 2010. When Miss Hoover assigns a family tree project, Lisa struggles to find any decent Simpson ancestor until she discovers the diary of Eliza Simpson, a 19th-century relative involved in the Underground Railroad. As Lisa pieces together fragments of the story from the crumbling diary, a library cookbook footnote, and an old film reel, she learns that Eliza helped a slave named Virgil escape from Colonel Burns, fleeing with him through a traveling circus before reaching the Simpson farm. Just as Lisa prepares a proud Black History Month presentation, Milhouse produces a rival diary revealing that Eliza's father Hiram betrayed Virgil's hiding place to Colonel Burns for a pair of shoes, and that Eliza did nothing to stop it. Devastated, Lisa digs deeper and finds a filmed interview with elderly Eliza expressing regret over her inaction. Grampa Simpson, prompted by Homer, reveals the story's true ending: Eliza's mother Mabel bravely held off Colonel Burns and fled with Virgil to Canada, aided along the way by Abraham Lincoln, eventually marrying him and starting a family. Lisa realizes this makes her part African-American, delighting the family, while Grampa admits he hid the story out of old-fashioned prejudice. Guest starring Wren T. Brown as Virgil Simpson. Notable quotes: Lisa: I can't believe we're descended from slave owners! | Homer: Me neither. For once, the Simpsons were in management! | Bart: Then they should've called it the "Above-Ground Normal-Road." | Virgil: You defied your husband for me? Man, this is the sixties. | Grampa: Well, it's hard to explain this to a young person, but people of my generation are... you know...
quotes: Lisa: I can't believe we're descended from slave owners!
Homer: Me neither. For once, the Simpsons were in management!
Bart: Then they should've called it the "Above-Ground Normal-Road."
Virgil: You defied your husband for me? Man, this is the sixties.
Grampa: Well, it's hard to explain this to a young person, but people of my generation are... you know...

title: Lisa Gets an F1 (S35E12)
text: "Lisa Gets an F1" is an episode of Season 35 (production code 35ABF05), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Ryan Koh, originally airing February 25, 2024. Lisa develops severe car anxiety after enduring one too many of Homer's reckless driving episodes, prompting her parents to bring her to a therapist named Annette. When Annette reveals that Homer's driving is the root cause of Lisa's anxiety, Homer storms off and promptly crashes his car, landing him in community service. As part of her therapy, Annette encourages Lisa to confront her fear head-on by trying go-karting, and Lisa unexpectedly discovers a talent and passion for racing, soon competing professionally. A televised go-kart circuit brings wealthy young racer Paolo Paoletti to Springfield Elementary, where Bart cynically befriends him for his money and lavish lifestyle, hiding the fact that Paolo's rival Lisa is his sister. When Paolo eventually learns the truth, he sabotages Lisa's kart out of spite before a big race. Homer, having overcome enough of his own anxiety to attend, notices the sabotage and races onto the track to protect Lisa, guiding her safely to a first-place finish. Paolo, disillusioned, quits racing altogether, while Homer and Lisa share a triumphant embrace, having both grown more confident and connected through the ordeal. Guest starring Matt Berry as Chester Arborday, Rachel Bloom as Annette. Notable quotes: Homer: Lenny thinks I drive cool. Everything is always my fault. Well, two can play at that game. I say you're a terrible driver. I'm much faster than you. | Chester Arborday: The truth is she's from an obscure racing backwater called—and I hope I'm pronouncing this correctly—America. | Paolo Paoletti: America is such a wonderfully disgusting country. All the guns and the billhillies, And all of the television shows about Chicago. | Homer: It's-a me, Wario! It's all my fault! Wah! | Lisa: Okay, missing a wheel, no brakes, still in control. Okay, now I'm not in control, but still calm. Wow, I have a great therapist.
quotes: Homer: Lenny thinks I drive cool. Everything is always my fault. Well, two can play at that game. I say you're a terrible driver. I'm much faster than you.
Chester Arborday: The truth is she's from an obscure racing backwater called—and I hope I'm pronouncing this correctly—America.
Paolo Paoletti: America is such a wonderfully disgusting country. All the guns and the billhillies, And all of the television shows about Chicago.
Homer: It's-a me, Wario! It's all my fault! Wah!
Lisa: Okay, missing a wheel, no brakes, still in control. Okay, now I'm not in control, but still calm. Wow, I have a great therapist.

title: To Courier with Love (S27E20)
text: "To Courier with Love" is an episode of Season 27 (production code VABF14), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Bill Odenkirk, originally airing May 8, 2016. After Marge admits she's unhappy with her humdrum life, Homer sells a valuable antique Morgan car he found in the garage to Jay Leno to fund a surprise trip to Paris. When Leno demands his money back over ownership issues, Homer refuses, determined to keep Marge happy, and instead books a cut-rate flight by agreeing to secretly courier a mysterious package. On the plane, he and Lisa discover the package is actually a rare, endangered Amazon Blue Constrictor destined to be turned into a fashion belt. Horrified, father and daughter vow to protect the snake and flee from the smugglers, Ugolín and Cesar, through the streets and jazz clubs of Paris. Meanwhile, Marge, Bart, and Maggie explore the city's dining scene, leading to a comic subplot where Bart pranks a group of starving Paris Fashion Week models. The smugglers eventually catch up with Homer and Lisa, leading to a tense confrontation and a police search of their hotel room, but the hidden snake goes undetected. With the ordeal behind them, Homer confesses the truth to Marge, and the couple reconnects romantically in Paris. Back home in Springfield, Homer distributes souvenirs to his friends at Moe's Tavern, including a suspiciously snake-like belt he claims is fake. Guest starring Jay Leno as himself. Notable quotes: Homer: For the first time a snake has ruined paradise! | Homer: Boy, either show me a writ of replevin or pipe down! | Marge: I'm sorry, Homie. Your life is full of fun surprises. My life sucks! | Homer: It's time for me to do what I do best: prolong this marriage! | Homer: Fortune favors the bald.
quotes: Homer: For the first time a snake has ruined paradise!
Homer: Boy, either show me a writ of replevin or pipe down!
Marge: I'm sorry, Homie. Your life is full of fun surprises. My life sucks!
Homer: It's time for me to do what I do best: prolong this marriage!
Homer: Fortune favors the bald.

title: Politically Inept, with Homer Simpson (S23E10)
text: "Politically Inept, with Homer Simpson" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF03), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by John Frink, originally airing January 8, 2012. The Simpsons head to Springfield Airport to fly to Bozeman, Montana for a cousin's wedding, but their flight is delayed on the tarmac for seven hours due to an unrelated prison break in Australia. Fed up, Homer erupts in an on-board rant that Bart films and uploads online, turning Homer into an overnight viral sensation. His newfound fame lands him a combative TV debut against pundit Nash Castor, which impresses network executives enough to give Homer his own political talk show. The local Republican Party then recruits Homer to help pick their presidential nominee, and he impulsively throws his support behind rocker Ted Nugent, horrifying Lisa and unsettling Marge. Nugent moves into the Simpson house and causes chaos, while Homer's on-air crusade against a bland family dinner spirals into a nationwide 'Gravy Boat Movement' of protest. Worried about his growing influence, the family schemes to use a James Madison lookalike to talk Homer out of endorsing Nugent, but Homer sees through the ruse. In the end, Homer decides on his own, without any trick, that he doesn't actually believe Nugent should be president, and he publicly withdraws his endorsement on live television. Guest starring Dana Gould, Ted Nugent. Notable quotes: Homer: Ted Nugent. I made love on my honeymoon to your sweet music. You're my man! | Ted Nugent: No one's voting Democrat while I can still draw a bow. | Homer: Oh, Marge, don't worry. People know I'm doing a character, like Stephen Colbert or Newt Gingrich. | Lenny Leonard: No way. When a guy who loves America cries, it makes him super straight. | Air Springfield flight attendant: You should have thought of that before you drank the fluids you need to live.
quotes: Homer: Ted Nugent. I made love on my honeymoon to your sweet music. You're my man!
Ted Nugent: No one's voting Democrat while I can still draw a bow.
Homer: Oh, Marge, don't worry. People know I'm doing a character, like Stephen Colbert or Newt Gingrich.
Lenny Leonard: No way. When a guy who loves America cries, it makes him super straight.
Air Springfield flight attendant: You should have thought of that before you drank the fluids you need to live.

title: Mother and Child Reunion (S32E20)
text: "Mother and Child Reunion" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF14), directed by Jennifer Moeller and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing May 9, 2021. The Simpson family visits Werner Herzog's Magic Shop to buy Lisa a birthday magic set, and after Bart's antics with Homer, Herzog offers to reveal the family's future using tarot cards. The vision shows Lisa becoming president, Homer quitting drinking, Bart becoming a decent person, and years of tension between Marge and Lisa over college. When the day arrives for Lisa to announce her decision, she shocks Marge by declaring she won't attend college at all, sparking a bitter rift between mother and daughter. Lisa takes a miserable retail job at the mall before pivoting to education, eventually founding the nationwide Lisa Simpson Academy chain and rising through politics from school superintendent to the presidency. Meanwhile Bart, having mastered Fruit Ninja instead of pursuing school, becomes a wealthy marijuana-business CEO and NBA team owner. As Lisa's inauguration approaches, she and Marge are nearly estranged, until Bart reminds Lisa how much Marge quietly sacrificed for her, prompting a rooftop reconciliation aided by a translator. Back in the present, Nate Silver crunches the real statistical odds of Lisa's future, undercutting Herzog's dramatic predictions, while Homer just wants to know if the fortune-telling ball plays video games. Guest starring Werner Herzog as Werner Herzog, Nate Silver as Nate Silver, George Stephanopoulos as George Stephanopoulos. Notable quotes: Homer: Well, you know, Marge, I didn't go to college, and I'm wealthy in the most important way: lack of student loans. | Bart: Why should I go to college? I've become a master of Fruit Ninja. | Marge: No college? No kids? How dare you lead the life I wish I'd led. | Lisa: God, that job sucks. | Werner Herzog: Welcome. Good to see you. If you're here to use the bathroom, try the Burger King next door.
quotes: Homer: Well, you know, Marge, I didn't go to college, and I'm wealthy in the most important way: lack of student loans.
Bart: Why should I go to college? I've become a master of Fruit Ninja.
Marge: No college? No kids? How dare you lead the life I wish I'd led.
Lisa: God, that job sucks.
Werner Herzog: Welcome. Good to see you. If you're here to use the bathroom, try the Burger King next door.

title: Apocalypse Cow (S19E17)
text: "Apocalypse Cow" is an episode of Season 19 (production code KABF10), directed by Nancy Kruse and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing April 27, 2008. Homer signs Bart up for the 4-H Club in Shelbyville after learning it requires no parental involvement, and Bart is assigned a runty calf to raise for a summer contest. With help from Cletus's daughter Mary, Bart names the calf Lou and nurtures him into a prize-winning bull, not realizing that winning means the animal will be sent to slaughter. When Lou is taken to the slaughterhouse, Bart's grief reveals a deep bond with the animal, and Lisa's attempt to turn him vegetarian with mooing sound effects fails, so she instead helps him rescue Lou. Unable to keep the cow himself, Bart gives Lou to Mary, but her father Cletus interprets the gift as a traditional token of marriage proposal, setting up a wedding between Bart and Mary that Homer and Marge scramble to stop. After breaking up the ceremony, Marge devises a clever swap, sending Homer disguised in a cow suit to the slaughterhouse instead of Lou. Lou is flown safely to India with Apu, who promises he'll live like a sacred animal, while Homer's cow disguise nearly gets him killed at the slaughterhouse before Marge rescues him in time. The episode ends with Bart contentedly reflecting on his unusual bond with Lou. Guest starring Zooey Deschanel as Mary Spuckler. Notable quotes: Bart: I don't care how much of a pumped-up freak you are. I still love you. The way Barry Bonds' kids probably still love him. | Bart: Oh, I thought she was peein' out of her nipple. | Homer: Hey, that sounds like Tress MacNeille! | Bart: Sorry, Lise. I can't be a vegetarian. I love the taste of death. | Bart: Mom, they're gonna kill Lou and make him into food and fringe vests for gay cowboys!
quotes: Bart: I don't care how much of a pumped-up freak you are. I still love you. The way Barry Bonds' kids probably still love him.
Bart: Oh, I thought she was peein' out of her nipple.
Homer: Hey, that sounds like Tress MacNeille!
Bart: Sorry, Lise. I can't be a vegetarian. I love the taste of death.
Bart: Mom, they're gonna kill Lou and make him into food and fringe vests for gay cowboys!

title: Homer? A Cracker Bro? (S37E15)
text: "Homer? A Cracker Bro?" is an episode of Season 37 (production code 37ABF05), directed by Chris Clements and written by Ryan Koh, originally airing February 15, 2026. After Lisa convinces Mayor Quimby to build a wildlife crossing over the freeway, the local animals end up raiding a pharmaceutical factory and rampaging through Springfield in a drugged frenzy. While sheltering from the chaos at the Van Houten house, Homer bonds with Kirk over their shared domestic struggles, particularly Homer's habit of leaving cracker crumbs in bed. Inspired by his own crack-resistant windshield, Kirk pitches Homer on a new business: a crumbless cracker, and the two quit their jobs to launch Kirkers Crackers together. The product becomes a nationwide sensation, but Kirk's behavior grows increasingly erratic, and Dr. Hibbert reveals that Kirk has stopped taking medication for his bipolar disorder. As Kirk's mania spirals into delusions of grandeur and reckless spending on an aquatic rocket, federal investigators close in on the company for fraud. Homer decides to take the fall for Kirk's crimes in hopes of protecting their fortune, defying Marge's objections and landing himself in jail. Ultimately Marge convinces Kirk to get back on his medication and confess the truth to the FBI, and after a dramatic rescue involving the actual rocket he built, Kirk turns himself in, restoring both his sanity and Homer's freedom. Guest starring Michael Stipe as himself. Notable quotes: Homer: Homer? A cracker bro? | Kirk Van Houten: Get in here, or you'll be trampled. | Homer: I do like faith. It's the best way to get out of thinking about stuff. | Kirk: Oh, come on, baby. Shake your Milhouse maker. | Kirk: We don't have a plan for expansion. We have a plan for domination. I eat skyscrapers.
quotes: Homer: Homer? A cracker bro?
Kirk Van Houten: Get in here, or you'll be trampled.
Homer: I do like faith. It's the best way to get out of thinking about stuff.
Kirk: Oh, come on, baby. Shake your Milhouse maker.
Kirk: We don't have a plan for expansion. We have a plan for domination. I eat skyscrapers.

title: Ae Bonny Romance (S35E08)
text: "Ae Bonny Romance" is an episode of Season 35 (production code 35ABF02), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Michael Price, originally airing December 3, 2023. After accidentally handing out nicotine patches instead of band-aids during a school dance unit, Bart lands in detention working with Groundskeeper Willie, and the two bond over their shared disdain for girls after Willie tells him about a lost love named Maisie. When Willie mysteriously disappears and calls Bart for help, the Simpsons travel to Edinburgh and discover Willie is reuniting with Maisie to get married at her family's distillery, having reconnected after she saw him in one of Bart's TikTok videos. Bart feels betrayed that his 'anti-girl' friendship with Willie is ending, while Lisa wanders off to enjoy the Fringe Festival on her own. Meanwhile, Homer's resentment toward destination weddings causes a rift with Marge, who drunkenly airs her frustrations about his unromantic nature at the rehearsal dinner. Bart overhears the MacWeldon family plotting to exploit Willie's peat-sniffing talent before discarding him, and after being locked away for exposing them, he escapes using a makeshift rope of sleeping masks to stop the wedding. Maisie proves her genuine love by breaking Willie's nose so he can never be used for his sense of smell again, and the wedding proceeds happily. Meanwhile, Homer and Marge reconcile after a sentimental video reminds them of their own bond, leading to a romantic reunion on the golf course. Guest starring Karen Gillan as Maisie MacWeldon, Paul Higgins as Hamish MacWeldon and the Ticket Booth actor, David Tennant as Pa MacWeldon. Notable quotes: Homer: What the hell, boy? A destination wedding? You promised me a kidnapping, or murder. | Principal Skinner: Well, Bart, you've really wet the mogwai this time. | Nelson Muntz: My mom says only sheeple wear masks, but I don't care. Cooties aren't a hoax. They're real. | Homer: This is the worst thing that's ever happened in the beheading room of this castle. | Homer: I'm sorry I was such a downer about this destination wedding. I should have just pretended to go along with it, like I do with everything else in our marriage.
quotes: Homer: What the hell, boy? A destination wedding? You promised me a kidnapping, or murder.
Principal Skinner: Well, Bart, you've really wet the mogwai this time.
Nelson Muntz: My mom says only sheeple wear masks, but I don't care. Cooties aren't a hoax. They're real.
Homer: This is the worst thing that's ever happened in the beheading room of this castle.
Homer: I'm sorry I was such a downer about this destination wedding. I should have just pretended to go along with it, like I do with everything else in our marriage.

title: Clown V. Board of Education (S34E21)
text: "Clown V. Board of Education" is an episode of Season 34 (production code OABF15), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing May 14, 2023. Krusty's TV show is failing because kids no longer find him funny, forcing the network to fill his audience with confused senior citizens. Desperate for a new income stream, he takes fellow clown Little Debbie Dimples' suggestion and opens a clown school, charging hefty tuition to eager parents like Homer, who enrolls Bart. To Bart's surprise, he excels academically at the school, even helping it triumph over Springfield Elementary in a Science Bowl. Krusty's pride is short-lived when Fat Tony and the Springfield Mafia muscle in, forcing him into a corrupt partnership that quickly turns the school into a mismanaged racket full of extortion and neglect. Fed up, Krusty agrees to work with the police, wearing a hidden wire in his squirting flower to gather evidence against the mob. The scheme nearly gets him killed when the flower malfunctions and exposes the wire, but Bart and his classmates intervene, filming the confrontation and scaring off the gangsters. Though the school is burned down, Bart and Homer reassure Krusty that his teaching genuinely mattered, and a mispronounced word about nachos gives Krusty a sentimental connection to his late father, restoring his happiness. In a coda, Fat Tony is shown delivering ominous, comedic 'morning announcements' from before the mob's downfall, hinting at the chaos brewing during his takeover. Guest starring Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony. Notable quotes: Krusty: Clowning is now the most despised profession in America after Supreme Court justice. But that will change. We will lift our clown horns high and tell the world, "Agagabawoogakazowie!" Now, let's pull together as only clowns can. | Homer: Teachers. They have it so easy. They get to buy their own classroom equipment, and people tell them what they can and can't teach. What a racket. | Fat Tony: Running a school is a dangerous business. I foresee possible boiler explosions, Taco Tuesday trichinosis, a mysterious increase in owies and boo-boos. But I can prevent these things. | Chief Wiggum: Yeah, sorry, Krusty, but the police have no jurisdiction in private schools, private clubs, private homes. Basically any place outside the police station. | Superintendent Chalmers: Now, about the curriculum. Will you teach STEM?
quotes: Krusty: Clowning is now the most despised profession in America after Supreme Court justice. But that will change. We will lift our clown horns high and tell the world, "Agagabawoogakazowie!" Now, let's pull together as only clowns can.
Homer: Teachers. They have it so easy. They get to buy their own classroom equipment, and people tell them what they can and can't teach. What a racket.
Fat Tony: Running a school is a dangerous business. I foresee possible boiler explosions, Taco Tuesday trichinosis, a mysterious increase in owies and boo-boos. But I can prevent these things.
Chief Wiggum: Yeah, sorry, Krusty, but the police have no jurisdiction in private schools, private clubs, private homes. Basically any place outside the police station.
Superintendent Chalmers: Now, about the curriculum. Will you teach STEM?

title: Specs and the City (S25E11)
text: "Specs and the City" is an episode of Season 25 (production code SABF06), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Brian Kelley, originally airing January 26, 2014. Mr. Burns distributes high-tech, internet-connected eyeglasses called Oogle Goggles to every employee at the power plant, secretly intending to use them to monitor his workers. Homer is thrilled with the gadget's augmented-reality features, using it to browse videos and enhance his everyday life, including moments with Marge. His enthusiasm turns to shock when Marge borrows the glasses and he discovers, through her recent activity, that she has secretly been visiting a marriage counselor. This revelation forces Homer to confront hidden tensions in his relationship with Marge that he hadn't realized existed. Meanwhile, at school, Bart is required to give Valentine's Day cards to every classmate, but he refuses to give one to his tormentor Nelson, arguing that he shouldn't have to show affection to a bully. Marge and Lisa debate the pointlessness of mandatory valentines, while Bart wrestles with the moral question of loving one's enemies. As the Homer-Marge storyline unfolds, the surveillance nature of the glasses becomes a growing problem for Burns' employees. By the end, Homer and Marge address the issues the glasses exposed, while Bart's Valentine's Day standoff with Nelson reaches its own resolution. Guest starring Maurice LaMarche as the Super Bowl XLVIII announcer, Will Lyman as himself. Notable quotes: Bart: Well, no way I'm giving a valentine to Nelson. He's a bully, and I do not love him. | Bart: That's because Jesus knows one day, he gets to look his enemies in the eye and say "It was me who sent you to Hell." | Marge: I don't understand what's so great about these state of the art, solar-powered, computo-glasses. | Marge: I'm afraid wives don't make passes at husbands in those glasses. | Homer: Glasses, find me a great gift for my wife. (whispers) Under five dollars.

Bart: That's because Jesus knows one day, he gets to look his enemies in the eye and say "It was me who sent you to Hell."
Marge: I don't understand what's so great about these state of the art, solar-powered, computo-glasses.
Marge: I'm afraid wives don't make passes at husbands in those glasses.
Homer: Glasses, find me a great gift for my wife. (whispers) Under five dollars.

title: Trust but Clarify (S28E05)
text: "Trust but Clarify" is an episode of Season 28 (production code VABF21), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Harry Shearer, originally airing October 23, 2016. Bart and Lisa grow suspicious of Krusty's new candy, Krustaceans, after noticing odd behavior in kids who eat it, and sneak into the factory to discover the treats are chemically manufactured by robots. Meanwhile, Homer is passed over for a promotion at the power plant in favor of a barely-English-speaking coworker, and with encouragement from a newly freed personification of his Ambition, he enlists Marge's help to overhaul his wardrobe and image. At the same time, aging newsman Kent Brockman is publicly humiliated after fabricating war stories on a talk show, leading to his firing from Channel 6 and a humbling search for new work. Homer's stylish makeover impresses his coworkers but backfires when Mr. Burns rejects the new look and denies him the promotion, sending a demoralized Homer to Moe's. Lisa and Bart's investigation reveals formaldehyde in the candy, but Channel 6 refuses to air the story to protect its ties to Krusty and the sponsor. Down on his luck, Kent is eventually persuaded by the kids to help expose Krusty, and together they confront him on camera at Krustylu Studios. The successful exposé restores Kent's reputation and job, and he thanks Lisa while vowing to stop lying. Guest starring Dan Rather. Notable quotes: Krusty the Clown: Presenting: Krustaceans! They look like shrimp, they taste like candy, and they're organic! | Bart: I'm a Krusty Prime member. $75.00 a month, but it's worth it. | Homer: I was in line for that job and I lost it to someone who barely speaks English! It's humidifying. | Homer's Ambition: I've been locked up for 30 years by Apathy and Alcoholism! | Ralph: I made the doctor cry.
quotes: Krusty the Clown: Presenting: Krustaceans! They look like shrimp, they taste like candy, and they're organic!
Bart: I'm a Krusty Prime member. $75.00 a month, but it's worth it.
Homer: I was in line for that job and I lost it to someone who barely speaks English! It's humidifying.
Homer's Ambition: I've been locked up for 30 years by Apathy and Alcoholism!
Ralph: I made the doctor cry.

title: When Nelson Met Lisa (S34E09)
text: "When Nelson Met Lisa" is an episode of Season 34 (production code OABF02), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Ryan Koh, originally airing November 27, 2022. Set years in the future, the episode follows Lisa and Nelson as their lives repeatedly intersect after high school. As a young adult about to graduate, Lisa reconnects with Nelson, now living in a church bell tower, and the two spend a night talking and bonding, but Lisa ultimately leaves town without saying goodbye after imagining a life with him. Five years later she is married to tech mogul Hubert Wong, while Nelson has become a bounty hunter dating a woman named Rott; a chance train encounter reveals lingering tension between Nelson and Hubert, culminating in Nelson humiliating him. Another five years on, both couples have split, and Lisa and Nelson almost pursue a relationship until Hubert dramatically wins Lisa back with a sky-written apology. Nelson, regretting his choice to encourage her, wedgies himself in frustration. Months later, at Jimbo and Sophie's wedding, Nelson and Lisa are forced together again as best man and maid of honor, and watching the happy couple makes Nelson realize what he's missing. Lisa, seeing Hubert already looking into divorce, finally chooses Nelson, and the two share a kiss, resolving their long, on-again-off-again connection. That's about it. | Nelson: She's leaning in, and I'm not looking down her shirt. I must really respect her. | Homer: The police horses will not share their oats. I repeat: not share their oats. | Nelson: No, mattress-cide. He ripped the tag off his mattress. | Sophie: People ask me, "Why Jimbo?" And I say, "Screw you, mind your own business, Mom."

title: The Bob Next Door (S21E22)
text: "The Bob Next Door" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF11), directed by Nancy Kruse and written by John Frink, originally airing May 16, 2010. As Springfield faces a budget crisis, Mayor Quimby releases minor offenders from prison, prompting many families to move, including the Powers next door to the Simpsons. A mysterious new neighbor, Walt Warren, moves in, and Bart is instantly convinced that his voice belongs to Sideshow Bob in disguise. Despite Bart's attempts to expose Walt—through operetta traps and sneaking into his house—Marge takes him to the penitentiary to prove Bob is still locked up, seemingly disproving his theory. In reality, Bob had swapped faces with his cellmate Walt via plastic surgery and escaped, using Walt's identity and money to buy the house next door for revenge. While the real Walt is held captive by Homer and Marge, Bob lures Bart on a road trip to Five Corners, a spot where he plans to commit an untraceable murder across five states. The real Walt escapes and races to stop him, and after a chaotic showdown involving a bee, gunplay, and a mistaken detour to Mexico, police from all five states arrive just in time to arrest Bob. The episode closes with a new, equally eccentric Flanders relative, Ted, moving into the vacated house, much to Homer's exasperation. Guest starring Kelsey Grammer as Sideshow Bob. title: Mathlete's Feat (S26E22)
text: "Mathlete's Feat" is an episode of Season 26 (production code TABF16), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Michael Price, originally airing May 17, 2015. Springfield Elementary's math team loses badly to the wealthy Waverly Hills Elementary, embarrassing Lisa. Taking pity on the school, the visiting nerds decide to modernize it with tablets, a networked digital blackboard, and a 3D printing lab, while Principal Skinner burns all the now-obsolete paper textbooks. When students discover the network password and cause a server meltdown, every digital device in the school breaks down, leaving teachers with no way to teach. Watching Groundskeeper Willie measure grass with a knotted rope outside her window, Lisa is inspired to convert the school into a Waldorf-style institution focused on hands-on learning. The change proves popular, and Willie is unexpectedly made coach of the math team. After Bart accidentally demonstrates a knack for calculating angles while helping Willie chase down Superintendent Chalmers, Willie names him team captain. In the rematch against Waverly Hills, Bart initially struggles, not realizing the competition is all math, but the score ends up close. When the final problem stumps everyone, Bart recalls the M-shaped pattern of his father Homer's hair and uses it to solve the puzzle, winning the Mathlympics for Springfield Elementary. Guest starring Justin Roiland as Rick Sanchez and Morty Smith. Notable quotes: Ralph Wiggum: If mommy's purse didn't belong in the microwave, why did it fit? | Principal Skinner: It was the name of the street I grew up on, Password Drive. | Bart: Math? No one told me there would be math! | Homer: Woo-hoo! I'm part of the solution! | Mr. Burns: I love it when it's not us.

title: The Real Housewives of Fat Tony (S22E19)
keys: the real housewives of fat tony
text: "The Real Housewives of Fat Tony" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF12), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Dick Blasucci, originally airing May 1, 2011. While waiting at the DMV, Homer abandons Bart and Lisa, prompting them to give up their spot to Fat Tony, whose mobsters later kidnap Selma after she refuses to help him. Fat Tony and Selma unexpectedly fall for each other, and after Selma demands liposuction as a condition of her release, their whirlwind romance leads to marriage. Marge struggles to accept her sister's new life with a mob boss, especially after a disastrous wedding seating arrangement, and tensions escalate when the two families vacation together at Fat Tony's Jersey Shore mansion. There, Homer and Marge discover Fat Tony is keeping a mistress, or 'goomar,' leading to a chaotic confrontation when his actual wife crashes into the party. Meanwhile, Bart discovers he has a bizarre talent for smelling out truffles in the woods, which Lisa exploits for personal gain and secret vegetarian indulgence. Their scheme spirals out of control when Bart's truffles end up making Spider-Pig go on a food-eating rampage through Luigi's restaurant. In the end, Fat Tony's tangled love life implodes publicly, while Homer and Marge retreat from the drama by hiding together in a tanning bed. Guest starring Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony. title: The Wreck of the Relationship (S26E02)
text: "The Wreck of the Relationship" is an episode of Season 26 (production code SABF17), directed by Chuck Sheetz and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing October 5, 2014. After Bart repeatedly mouths off to Homer, the two clash so badly that Marge enrolls them in the Relation Ship, a floating father-son therapy program run by the gruff Captain Bowditch. At sea, Bart thrives under the nautical discipline and is quickly promoted to mid-shipman, while Homer struggles, contracts scurvy, and turns to a hidden flask of beer for comfort, accidentally revealing the captain's own past struggles with alcoholism. Back home, Marge is stuck managing Homer's fantasy football team, and despite knowing nothing about the sport, she enlists Lisa's help to study stats and strategy. Their unlikely partnership pays off as the team starts winning games and climbing toward a championship. Meanwhile, a violent storm strikes the Relation Ship and knocks Captain Bowditch out of commission, forcing Bart to take command and prove his new skills under pressure. Homer initially resists deferring to his son's authority, but a small act of defiance-turned-acceptance (eating broccoli) softens his stance. Realizing he's been too controlling and unfairly harsh, Homer finally embraces Bart's competence and their bond is repaired. The family reunites as Bart safely guides the ship home and Marge's football triumph adds to the happy ending. Guest starring Nick Offerman as Captain Bowditch. Angled parking, lemons, Kickstarters by famous guys who already have lots of money, and this boat! | Homer: Marge, I want you—my wife—to draft my fantasy football team. | Homer: My team name is "Somewhere Over the Dwayne Bowe" and my password is "Annoyed Grunt." Draft with God, honey. | Bart: Hey, lame ass, Thanks to you, we're stuck on a stupid therapy boat. | Homer: Brief Nudityyyy!!

title: Opposites A-Frack (S26E05)
text: "Opposites A-Frack" is an episode of Season 26 (production code SABF22), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Valentina L. Garza, originally airing November 2, 2014. Lisa becomes politically active after learning that Mr. Burns plans to begin fracking operations near Springfield, and she recruits Democratic Assemblywoman Maxine Lombard to intervene. Lombard arrives determined to shut down Burns' environmentally destructive scheme, but the two ideological opposites unexpectedly develop a passionate, secretive romance despite publicly clashing over the issue. Meanwhile, Homer becomes an enthusiastic advocate for fracking, convincing the townspeople that the jobs it creates will boost everyone's business, from Moe's bar to Apu's Kwik-E-Mart. As the affair between Burns and Lombard deepens, their private tenderness contrasts sharply with their fierce public political battle, complicating Lisa's crusade against the fracking project. Eventually the consequences of fracking become impossible to ignore, symbolized by the town's water catching fire, forcing a reckoning between environmental harm and economic gain. Lombard and Burns' relationship ultimately collapses under the weight of their opposing values, with each blaming the other for the destruction they've caused. In the end, the fracking operation's damage to Springfield underscores the episode's environmental message, while Lisa's activism highlights the ongoing struggle between progress and preservation. Guest starring Jane Fonda as Maxine Lombard, Robert Siegel as himself. You got my e-mails!

title: Highway to Well (S31E17)
text: "Highway to Well" is an episode of Season 31 (production code ZABF10), directed by Chris Clements and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing March 22, 2020. With Maggie starting pre-school, Marge finds herself with empty days and, after failing at several hobbies, lands a job at Well + Good, a trendy new dispensary, without realizing at first that it sells marijuana. She grows to enjoy helping customers like Agnes, even as her boss Drederick Tatum pushes her to become the public face of his lavish new cannabis resort, The Drederick. Meanwhile, Homer, inspired by Otto's nostalgia for old-fashioned drug deals, sets up a rival low-key weed operation at Moe's Tavern with Moe and Lenny. When Tatum demands Marge shut down Homer's competing business to keep her job, she reluctantly reports him to the Health Department by exploiting a food-service loophole, forcing his operation to close and straining their marriage. At the glitzy launch of The Drederick, Homer crashes the event and reveals Marge has never actually smoked marijuana herself, so she tries it to save face and ends up delightfully high. Chaos erupts when Homer's attempt to light a joint instead ignites an e-cigarette, setting off a chain explosion that levels the entire resort. In the aftermath, Mayor Quimby re-criminalizes marijuana in Springfield, while Homer walks away with a new addiction—not to weed, but to the cheese balls from his failed dispensary. Guest starring Chelsea Peretti as Lauren, Billy Porter as Desmond, Kevin Smith as himself. Notable quotes: Marge: I feel like I'm on an elevator that's going up and down at the same time. title: Throw Grampa from the Dane (S29E20)
text: "Throw Grampa from the Dane" is an episode of Season 29 (production code XABF13), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing May 13, 2018. After Homer accidentally punctures a water pipe while moving a painting, the Simpsons' house is flooded and they must file an insurance claim with Gil. While repairs are underway, Grampa shows up needing medical attention, but Dr. Nick is unable to help him. Lisa suggests they travel to Denmark, where healthcare is free for anyone injured on Danish soil, so the family flies overseas hoping to get Grampa treated. In Denmark, their host Søren shows them around, and Lisa becomes infatuated with a real-life Danish prince, imagining herself as royalty. Homer, meanwhile, tries various schemes to get Grampa hurt so the family can cash in on free healthcare, even taking him to a historic castle for the purpose. As the family grows to love Denmark and its lifestyle, they pressure Homer to stay permanently, creating tension between him and Marge after he's caught dancing with a seductive Danish woman at a bar. Homer nearly leaves for home alone, feeling replaced by the household's cat, but Grampa talks him into reconciling with Marge. In the end, the family agrees to return to America, and Grampa accidentally injures himself by overeating, allowing him to finally get the free Danish medical care needed to remove an old tattoo of Mona's name from his arm. title: Yellow Subterfuge (S25E07)
text: "Yellow Subterfuge" is an episode of Season 25 (production code SABF04), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing December 8, 2013. Principal Skinner announces that the best-behaved students at Springfield Elementary will earn a special trip aboard a submarine, prompting Bart to believe that a clean disciplinary slate means his past misdeeds are officially forgiven. Determined to keep his record spotless, Bart struggles mightily to resist his pranking urges, but when Skinner ultimately reneges on the promised reward, Bart feels betrayed and enlists Homer's help to plot an elaborate revenge scheme against the principal. Their plan escalates into faking the death of Skinner's mother, Agnes, to torment him emotionally before revealing the ruse. Meanwhile, Lisa notices that Krusty the Clown is in dire financial straits and encourages him to capitalize on his fame by selling the international broadcasting rights to his show, leading to humorous glimpses of foreign versions of his program, including a Jamaican adaptation. As Krusty's fortunes improve, Bart's prank against Skinner reaches its climax, exposing both the absurdity of the school's reward system and the lengths Homer and Bart will go to for payback. In the end, Skinner is left humiliated but essentially unharmed, and the status quo of Springfield Elementary resumes. Guest starring Kevin Michael Richardson as Jamaican Krusty. title: The Changing of the Guardian (S24E11)
text: "The Changing of the Guardian" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF04), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing January 27, 2013. During a family game night, a sudden tornado sweeps through Springfield, endangering Santa's Little Helper and forcing Homer and Marge to chase after him with Carl and Lenny in tow. After getting trapped under a fallen bank door during the storm, the couple survives but realizes they have never designated a guardian for Bart and Lisa. Determined to fix this, they search among relatives and Springfield locals, only to find each candidate unsuitable or unwilling. Discouraged, they head to the beach for a break and instead stumble upon Mav, a laid-back pro surfer, and his wife Portia, a sharp environmental lawyer, who seem like the perfect fit. After a pleasant dinner, Homer and Marge ask the couple to be legal guardians, and Mav and Portia agree on the condition they get to know the kids. As Homer and Marge enjoy newfound free time, Mav and Portia grow overly attached to Bart and Lisa, treating them as if they were their own children. Realizing the arrangement has gone too far, Homer and Marge decide to end it, and the kids affirm that they only want their real parents. The story closes with the Simpsons reunited and appreciating their family bond once again. Guest starring Danny DeVito as Herb Powell, Rashida Jones as Portia. I can barely remember what he looks like. | Homer: He was a black guy, but his voice sounded like a white guy. | Grampa: Oh, you'd let me have another chance after the way I screwed things up with you?

title: The Homer of Seville (S19E02)
text: "The Homer of Seville" is an episode of Season 19 (production code JABF18), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing September 30, 2007. After a chaotic Sunday, the Simpsons end up eating at a stranger's funeral, where Homer agrees to be a pallbearer, mistakenly thinking he's being asked to be a polar bear, and ends up falling into an open grave and injuring his back. At the hospital, Dr. Hibbert discovers that Homer's injury has rearranged his internal organs in a way that gives him a stunning operatic singing voice whenever he lies flat. Mr. Burns quickly capitalizes on this by casting Homer in operas performed while lying down, and Homer becomes an overnight sensation, even bonding with real-life tenor Plácido Domingo. Homer's fame attracts a devoted fanbase, including Julia, a leather-clad female biker who rescues Homer and Marge from a mob of admirers and worms her way into becoming Homer's manager. Julia's obsession turns dangerous when she tries to seduce Homer and later attempts to murder him after he rejects her, first with a cobra and then during a live opera performance using poisoned blow darts while disguised as the conductor. Marge intervenes heroically, deflecting the dart back at Julia with a French horn, and police snipers and a falling chandelier finally subdue her. With Julia arrested and hospitalized, Homer decides to quit opera due to the dangers of stardom, instead finding a new lying-down hobby: painting a ceiling mural inspired by Michelangelo's famous work. Guest starring Plácido Domingo, Maya Rudolph. Notable quotes: Homer: If anyone asks, tell them we're plumbers... and then start plumbing until they go away. | Homer: Mmmm, au jus! Not quite gravy, not quite blood... | Dr. Hibbert: Not dirt—vegetables! | Mr. Burns: Well, young people are my future. | Marge: I'm sorry you got hurt, but you learned an important lesson. No one comes between me and my Homie.

title: Father Knows Worst (S20E18)
text: "Father Knows Worst" is an episode of Season 20 (production code LABF08), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing April 26, 2009. After accidentally eating a flaming stick at a carnival, Homer destroys his taste buds and becomes a hypersensitive 'super-taster' who can only stomach bland cafeteria food, forcing him to eat lunch at Springfield Elementary. While there, he watches Bart's foolish behavior and Lisa's social struggles, and after meeting an overbearing helicopter mom, he decides to micromanage his kids' lives. He pushes Bart into building an overly ambitious plywood model of Westminster Abbey and coaches Lisa on climbing the social ladder using a popularity guide and a cellphone-cover party. When Homer tries to secretly finish Bart's project himself, a dream visit from ghostly advisors warns him to let his son learn through his own failures, but he accidentally wrecks the model in his sleep anyway. At the school competition, Bart's now-imperfect project wins for being genuinely his own work, prompting him to expose Homer's meddling and demand he back off; Lisa echoes the sentiment, rejecting the forced popularity. Meanwhile, Marge discovers a hidden sauna in the basement and selfishly keeps it to herself, using it to unwind while ignoring the family's chaos, until she finally reveals it to Homer and gets some payback by using his beer on the sauna rocks. title: How I Wet Your Mother (S23E16)
text: "How I Wet Your Mother" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF08), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Billy Kimball, Ian Maxtone-Graham, originally airing March 11, 2012. After a chaotic incident at the power plant involving Smithers and a stray portal gun, Homer inadvertently gets away scot-free while his coworkers take the blame, earning him a day off. He spends that day fishing with Bart, but that night begins wetting the bed, a shameful problem that recurs despite his attempts to make amends with his coworkers. Desperate, Homer buys an alarm device and later resorts to adult diapers, which puts a strain on his relationship with Marge. When Marge confides in Professor Frink during a nighttime walk, she learns he has built a machine capable of entering people's dreams, and the family decides to use it to investigate the root of Homer's problem. Their dream-hopping adventure takes them through surreal versions of Bart's and Lisa's psyches before landing back in Homer's fantastical dreamscape, where a giant flood of Duff Beer threatens them all. They are saved by a mysterious figure who turns out to be Homer's late mother, Mona, who guides the family to a memory of a childhood fishing trip gone wrong that Homer believes caused her to abandon the family. Mona reassures Homer that her departure had nothing to do with that incident, easing his guilt and, seemingly, curing his bed-wetting. The family wakes up believing everything is resolved, only for an ambiguous final twist to suggest they might still be dreaming after all. Guest starring David Byrne as the "Dream Operator" singer, Glenn Close as Mona Simpson. Moist?! I wet the bed! The one embarrassing thing I've never done! | Homer: Oh Death, you're a life saver. | Mona: No. But I live on in Homer's dreams. | Bart: Not me, when I hit the dance floor.

title: My Fare Lady (S26E14)
text: "My Fare Lady" is an episode of Season 26 (production code TABF07), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Marc Wilmore, originally airing February 15, 2015. Tired of constantly chauffeuring the kids to their endless activities, Marge signs up to drive for a social media-based ride-hailing app, hoping to save enough to buy a new ice maker. She quickly grows disillusioned ferrying oddball Springfield residents around and earns the wrath of the town's taxi drivers. Meanwhile, Homer volunteers to run Moe's Tavern for a night so Moe can attend a Laney Fontaine show, but his ladies' night scheme backfires when a mob of women trash the bar instead of buying drinks. To make amends, Homer, Lenny, and Carl get Moe a janitorial job at the power plant, where Mr. Burns quickly promotes him to supervisor after he impresses during an NRC inspection. Moe's newfound authority makes him insufferable to his old drinking buddies, who cut him off. The two plots converge when Marge, now driving Moe home, urges him to quit his job as she quits hers, and the vengeful taxi drivers corner them outside the bar. Moe saves the day by pulling out his shotgun and scaring off the cabbies, restoring peace and reuniting with his friends. Guest starring Christopher Lloyd as Jim Ignatowski, Rich Sommer as the young man. title: Smoke on the Daughter (S19E15)
text: "Smoke on the Daughter" is an episode of Season 19 (production code KABF08), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Billy Kimball, originally airing March 30, 2008. After a family outing to grab the latest Angelica Button novel, Marge is inspired by a TV ad for the Chazz Busby Ballet Academy and decides to revive her dormant dream of becoming a dancer. Her audition ends in embarrassing failure when her leg locks up mid-stretch, but the caustic Busby is struck by Lisa's naturally perfect posture and invites her to join instead. Lisa struggles until she discovers, quite by accident, that inhaling secondhand smoke from her fellow ballerinas' breaks dramatically improves her performance, and she begins relying on it to dance well. Meanwhile, Homer initiates Bart into his secret jerky stash, the 'jerkytorium,' only to find it raided by a family of raccoons; when he tracks them to their den, he finds them so charmingly similar to his own family that he can't bring himself to harm them and befriends them instead. As Lisa's smoke dependency deepens and Marge grows increasingly wrapped up in living vicariously through her daughter's ballet success, Homer intervenes to stop Lisa from actually lighting a cigarette herself. Using one of his new raccoon friends, Homer sabotages the ballerinas' cigarette supply on the night of the big recital, causing the smoke-deprived dancers to fall apart on stage. Lisa seizes the chaotic moment to denounce the pressures of ballet and quit, inspiring Busby to quit as well, while Marge realizes she has been projecting her own unfulfilled dreams onto Lisa and resolves to let her daughter live her own life. title: Three Dreams Denied (S32E07)
text: "Three Dreams Denied" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF02), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Danielle Weisberg, originally airing November 22, 2020. Comic Book Guy sells one of Skinner's toys for a huge sum on MeBay, using the money to attend Comicalooza in San Diego, where he hopes to ask a perfect question at a big panel and impress Marvel. Meanwhile, at Springfield Elementary, Lisa befriends a charming new saxophone player named Blake, who is competing with her for first chair in the school band. Bart discovers a talent for voice acting after meeting professional voice artist Phil Muhlstock, and lands a role on the show Cookie Castle, only to learn he'll be voicing a female character. Lisa's growing crush on Blake sours when she learns his good looks are partly fake and he manipulates her out of her band position through trickery. Bart faces ridicule from classmates for playing a girl, while Comic Book Guy loses his carefully prepared question card just before his big moment at the panel, crushing his dream of impressing Marvel. Despite these setbacks, each character finds redemption: Ralph's odd affection restores Comic Book Guy's confidence, Bart's over-the-top voice performance turns him into an unlikely hit and boosts his popularity, and Lisa wins over a crowd at the mall with a spirited jazz performance despite losing her chair. In the end, all three main characters, having faced disappointment, find a way to reclaim happiness and pride in their own way.

title: Bart's Brain (S35E18)
text: "Bart's Brain" is an episode of Season 35 (production code 35ABF12), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Dan Vebber, originally airing May 19, 2024. After moving Grampa into a smaller, cheaper room at the Retirement Castle, the family sorts through his old war belongings, and Bart sells them at Herman's Military Antiques for store credit, which he uses to buy a preserved human brain as a prank prop. After the brain causes chaos at school, Mrs. Peyton punishes Bart by making him care for it as a homework project for two weeks. Bart initially resents the responsibility, but after leaving it with Homer, who abandons it at Moe's and nearly loses it to bullies, Bart rescues it, names it Buddy, and grows genuinely attached to it. His devotion earns him ridicule as "Brain Boy," embarrassing the whole family, especially when he brings Buddy to church and declares their friendship publicly. The moment is undercut when a hidden label reveals the brain actually belonged to Corbin Everly, an ordinary tax accountant who donated his body to science. Disillusioned that his "best friend" was just an average guy, Bart releases the brain, which ends up with Professor Frink at Springfield University. Marge tries to get Bart into a support group for kids with odd attachments, but he decides he'd rather just get ice cream instead. Guest starring Megan Mullally as Sarah Wiggum, Kerry Washington as Rayshelle Peyton. Notable quotes: Grampa: No! They're dumb as dirt. | Bart: Shut up, stupid, or I'll go back to sniffing permanent markers! | Kearney Zzyzwicz: I wonder if anyone will ever love me the way he loves that brain. | Homer: Ah, wifeless shopping, where all the meat is nuggets and the produce section doesn't exist. Ooh, the candy aisle. Formerly known as cereal. | Bart: So Buddy's nothing like me? He's not some rude, crude, prankin' dude with the freaky fresh 'tude? He was just some guy named Corbin?

title: Lisa the Veterinarian (S27E15)
text: "Lisa the Veterinarian" is an episode of Season 27 (production code VABF08), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Dan Vebber, originally airing March 6, 2016. During a family outing to an indoor water park, Bart sparks mass panic with a prank about wiener-invading fish, giving Lisa an unexpected opportunity to save a tased raccoon with CPR. The heroics inspire Lisa to pursue veterinary medicine, and she is soon entrusted with the class hamster Nibbles and takes an internship with the eccentric Dr. Budgie. As Lisa immerses herself in helping other people's animals, she becomes distracted and neglects Nibbles, whose declining health goes unnoticed until it's too late. Meanwhile, Marge stumbles into a side job cleaning grisly crime and accident scenes for Chief Wiggum, initially motivated by the thrill and the extra cash to replace a dangerous ceiling fan. The gruesome nature of the work, especially a horrific 'suicide-murder' scene, leaves Marge emotionally numb and detached. When emergency surgery fails to save Nibbles, a devastated Lisa blames herself for his death. Homer cleverly brings Marge in to comfort Lisa, realizing the act of consoling her daughter might also help Marge process her own trauma, and the plan works for both of them. The episode closes with a heartfelt funeral and video memorial for Nibbles. Guest starring Michael York as Lionel Budgie. Notable quotes: Homer: Wow, an indoor water park! Hopefully, this will put the final nail in the coffin of lakes and rivers. | Ralph: I saw heaven! | Lisa: Bart got my hair wet and I wasn't ready to get it wet! | Ralph: Your breath smells like don't drink that!

title: Dad Behavior (S28E08)
text: "Dad Behavior" is an episode of Season 28 (production code WABF01), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Ryan Koh, originally airing November 20, 2016. Homer discovers ChoreMonkey, an app that lets him pay strangers to handle his household chores and responsibilities, and quickly becomes dependent on it. When Marge grows frustrated with his laziness, she tries the app herself with a former hostage negotiator named Blake and becomes a convert. Homer takes things further by hiring former football star Matt Leinart to bond with Bart, but Matt ends up usurping Homer's role as father entirely. Meanwhile, Grampa is stunned to learn his girlfriend at the Retirement Castle is pregnant, a result of the seniors' newfound access to the internet and dating apps. Bart, hurt that Homer only shows him affection professionally, tries to reconnect, but Homer instead starts spending his time with Milhouse, prompting Bart to seek fatherly attention from Kirk. A wild car chase erupts between the two mismatched father-son pairs at Itchy & Scratchy Land, ending when Bart is thrown from a car and Homer rushes to his side, finally earning back Bart's trust and the word 'dad.' Grampa's story resolves happily when an ultrasound reveals the baby is actually Jasper's, delighting him. The episode closes with the Simpson men reconciled, watching baseball together on the couch. Guest starring Matt Leinart. title: The Incredible Lightness of Being a Baby (S31E18)

text: "The Incredible Lightness of Being a Baby" is an episode of Season 31 (production code YABF13), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Tom Gammill, Max Pross, originally airing April 19, 2020. Marge takes Maggie to a nicer park where Maggie develops a crush on a baby named Hudson, but Marge grows to dislike Hudson's eccentric, pretentious mother Courtney. Determined to avoid Courtney, Marge cuts off the budding friendship, sending Maggie into a deep sadness that worries the family. Meanwhile, Homer's secret pizza habit causes a car crash that leads him to meet Cletus, from whom he buys balloons, inadvertently discovering Cletus's helium-rich land. Mr. Burns becomes obsessed with acquiring Cletus's helium fortune and enlists Homer to swindle him out of it. As Homer spends time with Cletus fishing and sharing family meals, he bonds with him and starts to feel guilty about the planned con. When the moment comes to force Cletus into a lopsided deal, Homer refuses to go through with it, and the Spuckler family holds Burns at gunpoint until he agrees to a fair price. Meanwhile, Marge relents and reunites Maggie with a heartbroken Hudson, patching things up with Courtney as well, while Homer and Cletus celebrate their newfound friendship with a song. title: Diary Queen (S32E12)
text: "Diary Queen" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF05), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing February 21, 2021. During a garage sale hosted by Ned Flanders, Bart and Milhouse buy a stack of old books to burn for fun, and among the ashes Bart finds a barely-singed diary belonging to his old teacher, Edna Krabappel. Reading it in his treehouse, Bart becomes convinced that Edna secretly believed he had great potential, and he's inspired to start behaving better, helping around the school and earning top grades. Lisa, suspicious of his sudden success, secretly reads the diary herself and discovers the loving passages Bart cherished were actually written about Edna's cat, not about him. Torn between protecting her brother's newfound confidence and telling the truth, Lisa keeps the secret, though the stress gives her anxiety severe enough that Dr. Hibbert prescribes her children's Xanax. Bart's good deeds earn him recognition at an Improvement Day assembly and a spot in the school Spelling Bee, but Lisa finally confesses the truth before he can embarrass himself publicly. Devastated, Bart is comforted that night by Ned Flanders, who shares a story about how Edna once nearly left Springfield but chose to stay to help troubled boys like Bart find the good inside themselves. Touched, Bart returns the diary to Ned, who reads aloud a passage where Edna reflects fondly on their years together, closing the episode with a nostalgic montage of memories from her diary. title: Moe Letter Blues (S21E21)
text: "Moe Letter Blues" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF13), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Stephanie Gillis, originally airing May 9, 2010. On Mother's Day, Marge, Manjula, and Helen Lovejoy send their husbands off with the kids for a day trip so they can have time to themselves. As the ferry departs, Homer, Apu, and Reverend Lovejoy each receive a letter from Moe declaring that he's running off with one of their wives, but not specifying which. Stranded on Weasel Island with their children, the three men anxiously relive past marital troubles, each convincing himself his own wife might be the one who left. Homer recalls a disastrous birthday party where he clashed with Marge and her sisters, Apu remembers accidentally leaving his son at Moe's Tavern while his wife Manjula spent an odd amount of time with Moe, and Reverend Lovejoy realizes he has long neglected Helen's emotional needs, especially after Apu reveals Moe once confided his love for a married woman to her. When they return home, Homer discovers Marge has simply been painting a portrait of her late mother, and the Reverend finds Helen thrilled with tickets for a romantic trip. By elimination, Apu fears the worst, but finds Moe at his house helping to repair his marriage with Manjula rather than stealing her away. Moe reveals that his cryptic letter was a scheme to make the three husbands appreciate their wives more, having secretly arranged gestures of reconciliation for all three families. When did you realize Marge was checked out like a Harry Potter book at the public library? | Manjula: What a great father, I say sarcastically! | Apu: If only that mark on your forehead was an off button! | Otto: Even I've hooked up with your old lady.

title: Judge Me Tender (S21E23)
text: "Judge Me Tender" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF15), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Dan Greaney, Allen Glazier, originally airing May 23, 2010. At the Springfield Pet Fair's Ugly Dog Contest, Moe unexpectedly wins over the crowd with his biting insults after Krusty's judging falls flat, and he ends up taking over as judge. Word spreads about his talent for cruel critique, and Moe starts getting hired to judge everything from beard contests to other local competitions, closing his bar in the process and leaving Homer without his usual hangout. A talent agent discovers Moe and lands him a judging seat on American Idol, sending him to Los Angeles where Simon Cowell takes him under his wing. Back home, Marge struggles to keep Homer occupied now that he's stuck at home, eventually nearly pushing him toward taking up golf before deciding it will consume their family life. In LA, Simon secretly manipulates Moe into confronting how much everyone in Springfield actually despises him, encouraging him to soften up. When Moe tries to be kind to a contestant on air, Simon publicly humiliates him instead, revealing he only wanted Moe gone as unwanted competition. Furious, Moe attacks Simon and gets banned from both the show and the state of California. Moe returns to Springfield banned from broadcasting Fox in his bar, resuming his old life just as Rupert Murdoch shows up with a new demand. Guest starring Simon Cowell, Ellen DeGeneres, Kara DioGuardi, Randy Jackson, Rupert Murdoch, Ryan Seacrest. title: Guess Who's Coming to Skinner (S37E10)
text: "Guess Who's Coming to Skinner" is an episode of Season 37 (production code 37ABF04), directed by Rob Oliver and written by John Frink, originally airing December 7, 2025. During a field trip to a Victorian textile museum, a snow globe fight breaks out and Bart accidentally injures Principal Skinner's eye, leading to a painful hospital recovery. Bitter and newly convinced all parents are failures, Skinner returns to work only to discover a mysterious presence hiding in the school over spring break. With Groundskeeper Willie's help, he finds Hub, a snarky runaway boy who has secretly been living in the school library posing as a student. Superintendent Chalmers forces Skinner to care for the boy himself rather than involve Child Services, thrusting the lifelong bachelor into unwanted parenthood. Skinner clumsily bonds with Hub through shopping trips, pizza parlor mishaps, and eventually casting him in the school's Peter Rabbit musical, even rewriting the show to make him the star. As Skinner grows attached and starts adoption paperwork, Hub discovers the papers and panics, then his wealthy, negligent biological parents suddenly show up looking for him. Rather than leave with his family, Hub chooses to go on with the reimagined play, telling his and Skinner's story on stage instead of running away again. The episode ends with the emotional bond between Skinner and Hub solidified, while Lisa is left struggling to finish rewriting the musical's script with little help from Milhouse and the other kids. Guest starring Kieran Culkin, Karen Gillan, Kurtwood Smith, Barry Sonnenfeld, Kerry Washington. title: Burger Kings (S32E18)
text: "Burger Kings" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF11), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing April 11, 2021. After a near-fatal heart attack from eating too many hamburgers, Mr. Burns discovers that the entire town is celebrating his impending death, forcing him to confront how universally hated he is. Determined to change his image, he uses Professor Frink's plant-based burger-making robot to launch a new vegetarian restaurant chain, X-Cell-Ent Burger, and enlists Homer as its TV spokesman. The chain becomes wildly popular, driving rival Krusty Burger toward bankruptcy and even causing Marge to accidentally invest in and profit from its stock through a mishap with Amazon Alexa. Suspicious of the burgers' success, Bart, Lisa, and Milhouse investigate and discover that Burns is illegally harvesting endangered plants from the Amazon Rainforest to make the patties. Lisa tries to expose him, but Burns, Marge, and even Homer initially refuse to listen, each having their own reasons to keep supporting the venture. After a change of heart prompted by a dream, Homer joins Lisa in publicly denouncing Burns during the chain's national rollout, using the very approved catchphrases meant to promote it. The exposure destroys X-Cell-Ent Burger's reputation, reviving Krusty Burger's fortunes and allowing Marge to sell her stock before losing money. In the end, Burns admits he's relieved to abandon his brief attempt at being good, reverting to his cheerfully villainous ways. But in the end, evil always wins. | Sideshow Mel: Your product is inferior. Your marketing is offensive. And you have more ex-wives than franchise locations.

title: E Pluribus Wiggum (S19E10)
text: "E Pluribus Wiggum" is an episode of Season 19 (production code KABF03), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Michael Price, originally airing January 6, 2008. Homer's junk-food binge before his diet leads him to carelessly toss a leaky battery and lit match into a trash can outside Krusty Burger, sparking an explosion that levels Fast-Food Boulevard. To fund rebuilding, Mayor Quimby moves up Springfield's presidential primary, making it the nation's first, and the town is instantly swarmed by candidates, reporters, and camera crews desperate for votes. Lisa grows disillusioned as she realizes none of the actual candidates offer anything meaningful, while the Simpson household becomes ground zero for campaigning politicians. Fed up with the pandering, Homer and the regulars at Moe's Tavern decide to protest by writing in the most absurd candidate they can think of, settling on young Ralph Wiggum. To everyone's shock, Ralph wins the primary outright, sending the media into a frenzy and horrifying Lisa, who knows firsthand how unfit he is. Both the Republican and Democratic parties scramble to claim Ralph as their own, seeing him as a guaranteed path to victory, while Lisa tries in vain to talk him out of running. Ralph, in his own naive way, explains he just wants to bring peace to warring nations, winning over both parties completely. The episode closes with a joint political ad for Ralph, uniting Republicans and Democrats behind his candidacy. Guest starring Dan Rather, Jon Stewart. title: The Last Barfighter (S32E22)
text: "The Last Barfighter" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF15), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Dan Vebber, originally airing May 23, 2021. Moe accidentally reveals to Homer and the other barflies that bartenders belong to a secret society called The Confidential, where they trade the private secrets of their patrons. Meanwhile, Bart wins a mystical tequila-filled crystal skull at a game show hosted by Bumblebee Man, and Homer swipes it from him, only to be tempted into a drunken night at Moe's that leads Moe to blab all the secrets he's sworn to protect. Summoned before the society's enigmatic leader Artemis, Moe learns he broke the group's only rule, and as punishment his barfly friends are marked to be injected with Antibooze, a drug that permanently kills the ability to enjoy alcohol. Homer, Moe, Lenny, and Carl attempt to flee Springfield, but the town's bartenders—including the previously unsuspected Dr. Hibbert—track them down one by one. Barney, Lenny, and Carl are all dosed, and eventually so is Homer, who becomes an unnervingly wholesome, sober family man. Months later, the friends reunite over coffee and visit a humbled Moe working at an omelet bar, reaffirming their loyalty to him despite no longer being able to drink together. When Artemis offers an antidote, the others accept it, but Homer refuses, prompting the bartenders' guild to pursue him once more. In a final twist, the shattered crystal skull reassembles itself and warns Bart, Lisa, and Maggie that their family is genetically prone to addiction, sending the kids running in fear. Guest starring Ian McShane as Artemis. Game, set, skull. | Homer: Marge, pack what you need and choose one kid. We're leaving Springfield forever.

title: The Tell-Tale Pants (S35E16)
text: "The Tell-Tale Pants" is an episode of Season 35 (production code 35ABF10), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Al Jean, originally airing May 5, 2024. After a dream in which the Simpsons attend the Springie Awards and Marge finally receives recognition, she wakes up feeling unappreciated in real life. Throughout the day she juggles emergencies with Santa's Little Helper and Bart while failing to reach Homer, whose phone messages are being blocked by Moe's illegal signal jammer. When Homer accidentally rips his pants, Marge sews them, but soon discovers on a TV pawn show that an identical pair of Homer's rare Leevi's jeans could fetch thousands of dollars. She secretly sells his pants for $2,595 to a collectible clothing dealer, leaving Homer to wear sweatpants, which he ends up loving. Meanwhile, at the power plant, Mr. Burns' reckless experiment with a small nuclear reactor nearly causes a meltdown, which Homer heroically stops, earning him baseball tickets instead of any real reward. Guilt-ridden over selling Homer's pants, Marge splurges on an expensive ring but immediately regrets the purchase and struggles to hide it. After Moe scolds Homer for taking Marge for granted, Homer returns home, discovers the ring, and instead of being angry, realizes how much Marge sacrifices for the family and gives her the ring as a token of his love. The episode ends with Marge deciding to only wear the ring at home after learning the diamond was unethically sourced. Guest starring Kipp Lennon as "Leevi's" singer. title: I'm Dancing as Fat as I Can (S30E13)

text: "I'm Dancing as Fat as I Can" is an episode of Season 30 (production code YABF06), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Jane Becker, originally airing February 10, 2019. When Marge is called away to Florida to be with her dying aunt Eunice, she leaves Homer strict instructions not to watch new episodes of their favorite show, Odder Stuff, without her. Homer initially resists, but after seeing Bart and Lisa watching it and even his co-workers binging it at the plant, Netflix CEO Ted Sarandos personally convinces him to give in. Meanwhile, Patty and Selma's premature squabbling over Eunice's belongings upsets the dying woman, and Krusty launches a toy-store contest to boost his show's flagging ratings, pitting Bart against Milhouse and Ralph. When Marge returns and discovers Homer broke his promise, she freezes him out, prompting a guilt-ridden nightmare in which Reverend Lovejoy sends him to a vine-filled hell for spoiling The Crown. Dream-Ted Sarandos reveals that Marge secretly loves dance shows, so Homer secretly enrolls at a dance studio, lying to Marge about nightly trips to Moe's. His clumsy attempts frustrate instructor Julia until tougher trainer Sweet Sal takes over, while Marge grows suspicious and banishes him to the couch. At the toy contest, Ralph wins by grabbing both Bart and Milhouse's carts, and it's later revealed Lisa ghostwrote his winning essay, earning her a toy pony. Homer finally reveals his secret dance training by taking Marge to the Snow Ballroom, and their romantic dance reconciles them. Guest starring Ted Sarandos.
