title: Ned 'n Edna's Blend Agenda (S23E21)
text: "Ned 'n Edna's Blend Agenda" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF15), directed by Chuck Sheetz and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing May 13, 2012. The Springfield Playhouse stages a passion play, and Ned Flanders is devastated when the role of Jesus goes to Homer instead. Disaster strikes during the premiere when a falling cross gives Ned a concussion, and as he's rushed to the hospital he accidentally reveals that he has secretly married Edna Krabappel. Word spreads fast, and the whole town descends on the newlyweds' hospital room to celebrate, only to be thrown out by an annoyed Ned and Edna, who wanted to keep things quiet. Marge insists on throwing them a proper wedding reception anyway, while Edna, frustrated that Ned is too busy to attend a parent-teacher meeting, decides on her own to pull Rod and Todd out of their Christian school and enroll them at Springfield Elementary. Ned is upset by this unilateral decision and by the changes he sees in his suddenly more worldly sons, leading to tension between the newlyweds. As the reception unfolds, other couples' own marital imperfections come to light, showing Ned and Edna that no relationship is flawless. After a heartfelt public reconciliation at the school, Ned and Edna reaffirm their love and agree to compromise on raising the boys. The episode closes with Homer, still riding his Jesus role, getting comically struck by lightning while inaugurating a payday loan store. title: Flaming Moe (S22E11)
text: "Flaming Moe" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF04), directed by Chuck Sheetz and written by Matt Selman, originally airing January 16, 2011. After a brawl between the plant's day and night shifts, Smithers discovers he's been left out of Mr. Burns' will, prompting Burns to explain he only respects self-made men. Stung, Smithers tries to console himself at a snobby gay club but is turned away for not being attractive enough, so he ends up at Moe's Tavern instead. There he hatches a plan with Moe to transform the rundown bar into 'Mo's,' a welcoming gay hangout for average-looking men, hoping the business success will win Burns' approval. The makeover is a hit, drawing in Springfield's gay community while alienating regulars like Homer, Lenny, and Carl. As Mo's popularity soars, patrons assume Moe himself is gay, and he lets the assumption stand since it's fueling the bar's success, eventually being pushed to run for city council as an 'openly gay' candidate. Meanwhile, Principal Skinner uses Bart to get closer to new substitute teacher Ms. Juniper by having him date her daughter Melody, though Bart isn't interested and the ruse falls apart. Skinner nonetheless wins Juniper over and runs off with her, leaving Groundskeeper Willie as interim principal. At a town hall event, Smithers forces the issue by demanding Moe prove his sexuality with a kiss; Moe ultimately admits he was never gay, disillusioning the crowd and ending his political ambitions, while the bar reverts to plain old Moe's Tavern. Guest starring Alyson Hannigan as Melody Juniper, Scott Thompson as Grady Little, Kristen Wiig as Calliope Juniper. title: Livin La Pura Vida (S31E07)
text: "Livin La Pura Vida" is an episode of Season 31 (production code ZABF03), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Brian Kelley, originally airing November 17, 2019. The Simpsons are invited by Luann Van Houten to join several Springfield families on the Van Houtens' annual trip to Costa Rica, and despite their financial troubles, Marge and Homer eagerly accept over Lisa's objections. Once there, Lisa grows suspicious about how the perpetually broke Van Houtens can afford this lavish yearly vacation, while Homer strikes up an unexpectedly close friendship with Patty's new girlfriend Evelyn, much to Patty's annoyance. Kirk Van Houten obsessively tracks every group expense in a notebook, planning to split the bill evenly, all while nursing a stomach illness from drinking river water. Bart and Lisa sneak into the Van Houtens' room and discover a stash of strange gemstones, which turn out to be homemade salt and pepper shakers Kirk had hidden as a surprise gift. When Homer's drunken antics with Evelyn ruin Marge's dream vacation photo, tensions boil over between the couples, but a bigger scandal emerges: Kirk has been secretly overcharging everyone because his family actually owns the vacation house, inherited from an ancestor named Kirkedemious Van Houten. The group confronts Kirk, who flees down a zipline, and ultimately the families reclaim their money and salvage the trip, while Patty and Evelyn reconcile and Marge reassures Patty of her love despite Homer's disdain. The episode closes with lighter fallout, including Jimbo and Shauna's short-lived engagement and a chaotic monkey attack back at the Van Houten vacation home. title: A Mid-Childhood Night's Dream (S35E02)
text: "A Mid-Childhood Night's Dream" is an episode of Season 35 (production code OABF16), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing October 8, 2023. After accidentally getting food poisoning from a night of drinking and street-vendor hot dogs, Marge falls into a series of vivid dreams about Bart growing up. Each dream forces her to confront a memory or fear about her children leaving childhood behind, from a young Bart begging her to watch him play to a teenage Bart ignoring her in favor of his phone. Guided by dream versions of Homer (as an otter, then a dog) and a young Lisa who explains lucid dreaming, Marge starts to realize she can shape and understand these nightmares. Weaving through the dreams, she recalls a real conversation with Bart's teacher, Ms. Peyton, who warned that fifth grade would mark the end of his childhood, a thought that terrifies Marge. Meanwhile, in the waking world, Homer accidentally worsens Marge's illness by feeding her burnt rice covered in eggnog, all while trying to prepare for the school's Bounce-A-Thon. Despite her sickness, Marge insists on attending the event to see Bart and Lisa finish their race, collapsing from the smells before she can get a clear photo. Waking in the medical tent, she realizes Ms. Peyton's ominous words were just part of her fevered dream, and rushes to see Bart's real race. Bart good-naturedly makes the moment funny by faking a big butt with balloons, delighting the family, and the episode ends with Bart dunking his teacher, Coach Krupt, in a dunk tank alongside Marge. title: No Good Read Goes Unpunished (S29E15)
text: "No Good Read Goes Unpunished" is an episode of Season 29 (production code XABF07), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing April 8, 2018. Tired of her family's obsession with a marathon of Itchy & Scratchy episodes, Marge confiscates everyone's electronics and insists on a family outing to encourage real bonding. After the library closes early and a coffee shop turns out to sell no books, the Simpsons end up at a small used bookstore, where Bart discovers Sun Tzu's The Art of War. Bart begins applying Sun Tzu's strategies to real life, first using them to outsmart and neutralize Nelson's bullying at school, then manipulating Homer into taking him and Milhouse to a video game convention called TunnelCraft-Con, where they get a starstruck encounter with Daniel Radcliffe. Meanwhile, Marge revisits her childhood favorite book, The Princess in the Garden, only to find its content troubling by modern standards, and after a whimsical dream conversation with the book's author, she resolves to rewrite it in a way that will resonate with Lisa. Milhouse, feeling used and betrayed after learning that Bart has been manipulating him with Sun Tzu's tactics, decides to turn the tables by mimicking Ned Flanders' persona to unsettle Bart. The two friends' rivalry escalates until a fire breaking out at the Aztec Theater forces them to set aside their scheming and reconcile. The episode ends with the family's various side plots resolved, blending themes of media influence, manipulation, and reconnecting through shared experiences. title: Bart the Bad Guy (S31E14)
text: "Bart the Bad Guy" is an episode of Season 31 (production code ZABF08), directed by Jennifer Moeller and written by Dan Vebber, originally airing March 1, 2020. After witnessing the cliffhanger ending of a superhero blockbuster, Bart later gets an unexpected chance to see its sequel before anyone else when a visiting actor mistakes him for the injured Milhouse in the hospital. Realizing he holds knowledge no one else has, Bart transforms into 'Spoiler Boy,' blackmailing Comic Book Guy and other townspeople with threats of revealing plot details unless they meet his demands. His scheme escalates from petty extortion to genuine cruelty, such as deliberately ruining the film for Homer, straining his relationships with Marge, Lisa, and Milhouse, who accuses him of acting like a supervillain. As the sequel's theatrical release nears, Bart is suddenly yanked into what appears to be an alternate 'Marble Universe,' where he learns that his spoilers have real-world consequences, including the apparent death of the actor Airshot's heroic alter ego. This turns out to be an elaborate virtual reality scare tactic staged by the film's real producers to frighten Bart into silence, complete with a villain named Chinnos offering him fake superpowers in exchange for more spoilers. Bart refuses the offer and destroys his phone, ending the simulation and prompting him to sincerely abandon his spoiler-based tyranny. He returns everyone's stolen goods and calls off a treehouse project he'd coerced the town into building, but the episode closes with the irony of theater patrons casually spoiling the movie for each other via their phones anyway. Guest starring Kevin Feige, Tal Fishman, Taran Killam, Joe Mantegna, Anthony Russo, Joe Russo, Cobie Smulders. title: Moe Goes from Rags to Riches (S23E12)
keys: moe goes from rags to riches
text: "Moe Goes from Rags to Riches" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF05), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Tim Long, originally airing January 29, 2012. During a town meeting held at Moe's Tavern while the actual town hall is being fumigated, the regulars mock Moe for having no real friends other than his grimy old bar rag. Stung by their laughter, Moe listens as the rag itself narrates its incredible journey through history, beginning with its creation as a demon-wool tapestry woven by a cursed seamstress for a cruel duke in medieval France. The tapestry passes through a series of increasingly grim and absurd owners, including looting Vikings, a murderous sultan, Spanish executioners, and eventually Michelangelo, who uses it while painting the Sistine Chapel ceiling. It later becomes part of a Confederate flag, rag soup for a starving family, and a flag left on Mount Everest, before a yeti retrieves it and passes it down to his son, who turns out to be Moe. Meanwhile, in a parallel subplot, Bart and Milhouse's friendship falls apart after Bart repeatedly insults Milhouse, and Bart spends the episode trying various clumsy ways to apologize. The boys only reconcile after Milhouse has Drederick Tatum punch Bart as a form of twisted penance. Back in the present, Marge secretly washes Moe's beloved rag to surprise him, but when she points out that the whole Simpson family (and Milhouse) truly consider him a friend, Moe realizes he doesn't need the rag anymore and tosses it out the window. The rag ends up with Santa's Little Helper, who happily adopts it as a toy, giving the well-traveled object a peaceful new home despite occasional squabbles with Maggie. Guest starring Jeremy Irons as Moe Szyslak's bar rag. Notable quotes: Lisa: Even a boy with a Finding Nemo back brace has a little pride.
quotes: Lisa: Even a boy with a Finding Nemo back brace has a little pride.

title: A Tree Grows in Springfield (S24E06)
text: "A Tree Grows in Springfield" is an episode of Season 24 (production code PABF22), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Stephanie Gillis, originally airing November 25, 2012. After a storm floods the Simpsons' house, Homer sinks into a funk that even Moe and Duffman can't cure. His luck seems to turn when Lisa buys him a raffle ticket at a school fundraiser and he unexpectedly wins a myPad tablet. Homer becomes obsessed with the device, using it for everything from flirting with Marge to entertaining himself at the IRS, while a deceased Steve Mobbs speaks to him from the afterlife through the gadget. His fixation alienates his family, and disaster strikes when he falls down an open manhole while distracted by a game, shattering the myPad and landing him in the hospital. Devastated, Homer is lifted out of his despair when Ned Flanders shows him a tree in the Simpsons' yard that mysteriously reads 'Hope,' which Homer takes as a genuine miracle and spreads across Springfield. Kent Brockman's news team exposes the message as a hoax, painted in syrup, sending the town—and Homer—into disillusionment. Marge consoles Homer by pointing out that the hope he felt was real regardless of who wrote the message, leading them to wonder who could have known he needed it most. The episode ends with the reveal that Homer himself, sleepwalking, repainted the message, all while God watches from his own myPad and gets a visit from Steve Mobbs urging a software update. Guest starring Kelsey Grammer as Sideshow Bob. Notable quotes: Homer: Aw, that's Tooth Fairy money down the drain, sweetie. I never win anything. It's always some stupid jerk you've never heard of. | Steve Mobbs: Greetings, I am Steve Mobbs, welcoming you from beyond the grave. | Homer: I left a half-eaten apple outside your store the greatest tribute of all. | Homer: What would you have me do? One basket for each egg? | Dr. Hibbert: This is the part of the job I hate most. Talking to crazy people.

title: Lisa with an "S" (S27E07)
text: "Lisa with an "S"" is an episode of Season 27 (production code TABF20), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Stephanie Gillis, originally airing November 22, 2015. Homer joins his buddies for poker night at Moe's, promising Lisa he'll pay for elite band camp if he wins. Instead he loses $5,000 to Broadway legend Laney Fontaine, who is now dating Moe for his liquor license. Desperate to get his money back, Homer invites Laney to dinner, but the plan backfires when Lisa's singing and saxophone playing convince Laney that the girl has real star potential. Laney proposes borrowing Lisa for a month to perform in her Broadway shows, and despite Marge's objections, Lisa talks her way into going with Grampa's encouragement. In New York, Lisa quickly impresses old ballet teacher Chazz Busby and lands a spot in a Broadway production, but a Skype call reveals to Marge that something feels off about her daughter's new life. The Simpsons travel to New York to bring Lisa home, only to find she's genuinely thriving and decide to leave without her. However, Laney grows jealous, fearing Lisa will outshine her, and pushes her away, prompting a hurt Lisa to choose her family after all. A side plot involves Ned Flanders' estranged cousin Jacob, whose visit exposes Ned's secret shame, and the two reconcile in a hug at the Simpsons' house. Notable quotes: Lisa: I'd like two things, a hug and a favor. To save time I'll start describing the favor while we hug. | Bart: We have Disco Stu in this town, Mom. He's a resource, use him. | Homer: You can't take a daughter from her mother. Unless you're a bigger star and this is a third-world country.
quotes: Lisa: I'd like two things, a hug and a favor. To save time I'll start describing the favor while we hug.
Bart: We have Disco Stu in this town, Mom. He's a resource, use him.
Homer: You can't take a daughter from her mother. Unless you're a bigger star and this is a third-world country.

title: The Greatest Story Ever D'ohed (S21E16)
text: "The Greatest Story Ever D'ohed" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF10), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Kevin Curran, originally airing March 28, 2010. After Homer's antics disrupt Ned Flanders' Bible study, Ned decides to invite the Simpsons on his church group's tour of Jerusalem, hoping the trip will finally redeem Homer's soul. In the Holy Land, eccentric guide Jakob and his niece Dorit, who turns out to be a security agent, lead the group through famous religious sites, but Homer keeps prioritizing hotel buffets and silly souvenirs over spiritual reflection. His irreverence—falling asleep on the tomb of Christ and destroying Ned's camera—finally pushes Flanders past his limit, leading him to storm off and get banned from the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. Fearing Ned is in danger, Homer steals a camel and rides into the desert, where he becomes dangerously dehydrated after drinking from the Dead Sea. Suffering from a hallucinatory case of Jerusalem Syndrome, Homer becomes convinced he is the Messiah destined to unite the world's religions, and gathers a crowd at the Dome of the Rock to preach unity. His makeshift ministry collapses when Agnes Skinner, suffering the same delusion, shoves him aside, and Dr. Hibbert, also afflicted, refuses to intervene. As the family heads home, Ned reveals he has forgiven Homer, admitting that despite the chaos, Homer's message came closest to real faith. The episode closes with Bart and Lisa's petty sibling squabble over an airplane window seat, underscoring that not much has changed back to normal Simpsons dynamics. Guest starring Sacha Baron Cohen as Jakob, Yael Naim as Dorit. Notable quotes: Ned Flanders: Let's start with the words you love to hear: "Welcome to Bible study!" | Agnes Skinner: Stop making this relatable. | Bart: Great. More hell for me. | Homer: Porky pig?! | Homer: Dome of the Rock? Messiah away!

Agnes Skinner: Stop making this relatable.
Bart: Great. More hell for me.
Homer: Porky pig?!
Homer: Dome of the Rock? Messiah away!

title: The Clown Stays in the Picture (S30E14)
keys: the clown stays in the picture
text: "The Clown Stays in the Picture" is an episode of Season 30 (production code YABF05), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Matt Selman, originally airing February 17, 2019. While riding in the car, Bart's phone dies and he ends up listening to Lisa's podcast, which features an interview with Krusty. When the host, Marc Maron, brings up the long-buried film 'The Sands of Space,' Krusty is forced to recount its disastrous history. The story reveals that Krusty, fresh off his 'Good Cop, Dog Cop' fame, pushed to produce a serious sci-fi epic instead of a lucrative sequel. Homer and Marge are hired as production assistants and travel with the crew to Mexico, where the shoot quickly spirals out of control after the original director quits. Krusty takes over directing but proves incompetent, leading Marge to step up as his de facto assistant director, a role that boosts her confidence but strains her marriage. Jealous and insecure, Krusty secretly sabotages Homer by giving him increasingly dangerous assignments, including a solo trek into a sandstorm that leaves Homer stranded in a ravine, hallucinating visions of his children as cacti. Local captors seize Homer, and when Krusty refuses to help, the cast and crew improvise a rescue using prop weapons, though it's ultimately Marge who saves him by trading away the film itself. The production collapses, ending Krusty's dreams of movie stardom and sending him back to children's TV. Years later, Bart and Lisa learn that the film eventually screened in Mexico, where, to Krusty's bewilderment, the audience finds its tragic ending hilarious. Guest starring Marc Maron. Notable quotes: Krusty: I have a phobia... of pies. | Krusty: No, no, no, those are cakes decorated as pies. | Krusty: It's not the crust, it's the fillings. | Krusty: So? We got plenty of them. That's why they're called "extras," right? | Homer: Oh, I'm trapped in a ravine. Only one thing to do: wait patiently for death.

title: Oh Brother, Where Bart Thou? (S21E08)
text: "Oh Brother, Where Bart Thou?" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF01), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Matt Selman, originally airing December 13, 2009. Stuck indoors during a huge snowstorm with the power out, Bart watches Lisa and Maggie share a close sisterly bond during a makeshift fashion show and becomes jealous, deciding he desperately wants a baby brother of his own. After a dream showing off famous brothers like the Manning siblings and the Smothers Brothers, Bart tries everything to convince Homer and Marge to have another child, from setting up a romantic dinner to sabotaging Marge's birth control, but nothing works and Marge shoots down the idea entirely. Determined, Bart sneaks off to the Springfield Orphanage, only to be turned away for being underage, but a mischievous orphan boy named Charlie secretly follows him home. Delighted to finally have a 'little brother,' Bart spends a wild day with Charlie, skipping responsibilities and getting into trouble, until Lisa discovers the runaway orphan and insists he be returned. Bart refuses and the two boys go on the run, hiding out in a snow cave after evading Chief Wiggum, but they eventually get trapped by a snowplow. Forced to choose, Bart ultimately loses Charlie back to the orphanage, and by the time he and Homer go to visit, Charlie has already been adopted by a family of six daughters, leaving Bart's dream of brotherhood unfulfilled as Charlie is driven away pleading for help. Guest starring Kim Cattrall, Huell Howser, Cooper Manning, Eli Manning, Peyton Manning, Jordan Nagai, Smothers Brothers. Notable quotes: Bart: Dad... I want a baby brother. | Homer: Son, I love you kids. But I'm only going to the hospital one more time in my life and I ain't comin' out. | Bart: I don't need a brother... and no dream will convince me I do. | Lisa: You can have mine, but he's kind of an idiot. | Homer: Point and shoot.

title: The Dad-Feelings Limited (S32E11)
text: "The Dad-Feelings Limited" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF04), directed by Chris Clements and written by Ryan Koh, originally airing January 3, 2021. Comic Book Guy and Kumiko spend a lazy Sunday together while the Simpson kids clamor for birthday presents at the Android's Dungeon. Meanwhile, Homer and Marge, exhausted from parenting, accidentally bring home a lookalike stranger instead of Bart and dump their kids on Ned Flanders so they can sneak off to trivia night at Moe's. There they team up with Comic Book Guy and Kumiko, and afterward Marge bonds with Kumiko, helping her discover a natural gift for soothing baby Maggie, which sparks Kumiko's desire to have a child of her own. When Comic Book Guy flatly refuses, citing his overexposure to kids at the shop, Marge and Homer scheme to change his mind through a family outing to a cemetery movie night. The plan backfires when Bart and Lisa scare Comic Book Guy by resembling zombies, causing him to flee back to his childhood home and the father who neglected him, Postage Stamp Fellow. Marge and Homer track him down, and through flashbacks we learn his father missed his one shot at pitching in a baseball game, leading him to comics instead of sports. Marge forces a confrontation that reveals Postage Stamp Fellow's true motive—he bought a signed Sandy Koufax ball instead of showing up, fearing he wouldn't know how to comfort his son if he failed. Father and son reconcile by playing catch with the ball, and Comic Book Guy returns home emotionally ready to start a family with Kumiko. Guest starring Dan Aykroyd, Bob Balaban. No money. | Kumiko: Impregnate me at once! | Comic Book Guy: It's selfish to bring a new life into a world with diminishing resources. The planet is running out of watchable IP! title: Postcards from the Wedge (S21E14)
text: "Postcards from the Wedge" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF04), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Brian Kelley, originally airing March 14, 2010. Bart is discovered to be a month behind on his homework, prompting Homer to demand he complete an even heavier workload while Marge worries the pressure will crush his love of learning. Bart exploits his parents' disagreement to dodge schoolwork entirely, and their bickering escalates into a full-blown marital rift that spreads to unrelated arguments. Ned Flanders' story about a trivial fight with Maude before her death spooks Marge into wanting to make peace, while Homer has a nightmare in which winning the argument leads to Marge's death, scaring him into the same conclusion. The two reconcile in the middle of traffic and agree to stop letting Bart manipulate them, choosing to ignore him instead. Left without attention, Bart and Milhouse revive the condemned old subway system for kicks, but Bart finds pranking hollow now that no one reacts with anger. He escalates by planning to ram a train into the already-damaged Springfield Elementary, and a note supposedly from Lisa warns Homer and Marge just in time for them to stop him by pulling the emergency switch. Bart is grounded, but secretly pleased that his parents are paying attention to him again, and Lisa later reveals to the audience that Bart forged the warning note himself to be caught. Notable quotes: Lisa: Congratulations. You're officially a sociopath. | Bart: Hey, at least I'm on a path. | Bart: I tried really hard to stop you from finding out. That help?

title: Treehouse of Horror XXXIV (S35E05)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXXIV" is an episode of Season 35 (production code OABF17), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Jeff Westbrook, Jessica Conrad, Dan Vebber, originally airing November 5, 2023. This Halloween anthology offers three separate horror tales. In 'Wild Barts Can't Be Token,' Springfield's art museum is shut down so its collection can be turned into NFTs, and when Bart is accidentally digitized and his body destroyed, Marge must enter the blockchain herself, fighting and absorbing worthless NFTs to increase her value and reach the train car where Bart is being kept in luxury; she rescues him just as Homer, trying to sell Bart, ends up selling himself into the crashing NFT market instead. In 'Ei8ht,' a dark parody of 'Cape Feare' and serial-killer thrillers, Bob murders Bart on the boat, and decades later Professor Lisa Simpson is called in to help solve a string of murders targeting firstborn children, teaming with officer Nelson Muntz and eventually consulting imprisoned Sideshow Bob for clues. The investigation twists into horror when Lisa is framed for Nelson's murder, only to reveal in the finale that she has a split personality and is the true killer, using her 'accomplice' persona to gain access to Bob's cell and finally kill him. In 'Lout Break,' Homer eats a radioactive, mutated donut that alters his DNA, and after burping on Ned, he unwittingly spreads a plague that turns Springfield's citizens into lazy, beer-loving Homer clones. Professor Frink and Homer's uninfected children try to stop the outbreak and reverse the effects, but the virus proves unstoppable, spreading worldwide and transforming the entire planet into a Homer-esque utopia visible even from space. Guest starring Matthew Friend, Kelsey Grammer, Kylie Jenner. Notable quotes: Marge: My baby is an app! | Sideshow Bob: Really, Professor Simpson, am I meant to spoon-feed you all the answers? | Lisa: You're gonna die in that cell, Bob. And when that happens, wherever I am, I'll be dancing. | Homer: Pfft. The nanny state wins again. | Ned-Homer: I've been neighborino'd into Home-diddly-omer. title: A Springfield Summer Christmas for Christmas (S32E10)

text: "A Springfield Summer Christmas for Christmas" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF03), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Jessica Conrad, originally airing December 13, 2020. Television producer Mary Tannenbaum is sent to Springfield to salvage the troubled production of a Christmas movie, staying at the Simpsons' home, which has been converted into an Airbnb. While clashing with the locals over her big-city tastes, she meets Principal Skinner, who reluctantly helps with the film's carpentry in exchange for her promoting the town's Lettuce and Tomato Festival. As the two spend more time together, Mary begins to fall for Skinner even as her surgeon fiancé checks in from afar, and Bart grows increasingly displaced from his own bedroom by the film crew. When Mary suggests merging the festival with the movie's Christmas theme, Skinner is furious, but the plan wins over the town until Bart sabotages the fake snow machine, trapping Mary and Skinner together and sparking a romantic night between them. Their happiness is short-lived when her fiancé arrives and Bart broadcasts her private complaints about the townspeople, causing the set to be abandoned and later catch fire. After tearfully revealing to Marge the tragic reason she hates Christmas movies, Mary's admission is filmed by Lisa and Bart and shown to the town, prompting them to forgive her and rebuild the set together. Forced to choose between her fiancé and Skinner, Mary picks Skinner, though he initially rejects her for deciding too quickly before they reconcile. The episode ends with the family watching the finished film, though only Marge truly enjoys it. Guest starring Ellie Kemper, Richard Kind, Chris Parnell. title: Frinkenstein's Monster (S35E11)
text: "Frinkenstein's Monster" is an episode of Season 35 (production code 35ABF03), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing February 18, 2024. Homer, bored and unfulfilled at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, is unexpectedly offered a job at a cutting-edge nuclear facility in Shelbyville. Knowing he can't pass the interview on his own, he enlists Professor Frink, who secretly feeds him answers, helping him land the position over the far more qualified Dr. Lori Spivak. To keep up the ruse on the job, Frink outfits Homer with hidden glasses and an earpiece so he can continue coaching him in real time, while Marge revels in the family's newfound wealth and Lisa grows suspicious of how Homer is suddenly succeeding. Dr. Spivak, forced to work as Homer's assistant, becomes convinced he's faking his competence and gets Lenny and Carl drunk to confirm that Homer was actually terrible at his old job. She then discovers Frink's earpiece, exposing the scheme to him and causing a guilty Frink to cut off his help. Stripped of his secret assistance, Homer struggles during a company ski trip, where Spivak hijacks the earpiece herself and manipulates Marge into pressuring Homer to confess. At the mountain summit, Homer publicly admits he's a fraud, prompting a chain reaction of confessions from other employees, before he quits and injures himself sliding off a cliff. After recovering in the hospital, Homer returns to his old job at the Springfield plant, having learned little from the entire ordeal. Guest starring Amanda Seyfried as Lori Spivak. I never knew smart people could be unhappy. | Professor Frink: My quid was woefully un-pro quo'd. | Dr. Spivak: You're like an idiot that ate a genius. | Homer: Um, is there a box for "preposterous scheme that blew up in my face"?

title: Lisa Goes Gaga (S23E22)
text: "Lisa Goes Gaga" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF14), directed by Matthew Schofield and written by Tim Long, originally airing May 20, 2012. After winning the humiliating 'Least Popular Student' award, Lisa secretly begins posting glowing anonymous comments about herself on her school's message board under the alias 'Truth Teller.' Her scheme briefly boosts her social standing until Bart discovers her notebook of drafted posts and exposes her, causing her classmates to mock her as a 'Lie Smeller' and sending her into deep despair. Meanwhile, Lady Gaga, touring aboard her own train, senses Springfield's record-low self-esteem and Lisa's personal crisis through a psychic vision, prompting her to visit the town. Gaga tries various methods to lift Lisa's spirits, from performing for her to having a heartfelt talk in her bedroom, while also inadvertently seducing Marge during a late-night kitchen conversation about parenting struggles. When Lisa lashes out and rejects her help, Gaga leaves in tears, but a rambling pep talk from Homer helps Lisa realize her own ingratitude. Lisa chases down the departing Gaga Express and reconciles with the singer, admitting that unloading her anger on Gaga was oddly cathartic. The episode ends with Lisa and Gaga performing an empowering duet about self-acceptance for the town, before Gaga's train departs, leaving a self-esteem-starved Moe behind. Guest starring Lady Gaga as herself, Kevin Michael Richardson as Lady Gaga Express conductor. Notable quotes: Lady Gaga: I just can't ignore a billboard in pain. Hurts like Hell.

title: Bart Stops to Smell the Roosevelts (S23E02)

text: "Bart Stops to Smell the Roosevelts" is an episode of Season 23 (production code NABF17), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Tim Long, originally airing October 2, 2011. After Bart pulls an elaborate prank on Principal Skinner during a school fundraising auction, pretending to be a wealthy English widow placing fake bids, Skinner is humiliated and lashes out at Superintendent Chalmers. Chalmers, tired of Skinner's incompetence, takes personal charge of Bart's education to prove he could do better. While teaching Bart American history, Chalmers discovers that Bart becomes genuinely fascinated by Theodore Roosevelt, especially his toughness and adventurous spirit. This sparks a study group among Bart's friends, leading to an overnight expedition into Springfield Forest to find Roosevelt's legendary lost spectacles. When Nelson is injured during the search, the school is sued and Chalmers is fired for organizing an unauthorized trip. Frustrated by his return to boring textbook lessons, Bart rallies his friends into the 'Brotherhood of the Spectacles' to force the school to reinstate Chalmers. The group stages a lockdown of Springfield Elementary, holding the school hostage until their demand is met, resulting in a tense standoff with police and media. The situation resolves comically when Chief Wiggum's gun accidentally discharges and wounds State Comptroller Atkins, who then not only reinstates Chalmers but promotes him to 'Super-duper-intendent,' prompting the students to end their occupation. title: The Sound of Bleeding Gums (S33E17)
text: "The Sound of Bleeding Gums" is an episode of Season 33 (production code UABF10), directed by Chris Clements and written by Loni Steele Sosthand, originally airing April 10, 2022. Lisa is outraged when the Springfield Lottery uses a reworked version of a Bleeding Gums Murphy song in its ad campaign, and her frustration grows when she learns the local jazz musicians have all bought into the lottery. After a failed on-air debate about the lottery's harms, she's blindsided by the revelation that Bleeding Gums Murphy had a son, Monk, who was born deaf and has never heard his father's music. Lisa tracks Monk down and, despite his reluctance, decides to make helping him her new personal crusade, discovering along the way that Bleeding Gums was swindled out of the rights to his own songs by a shady publisher. When Monk asks her to back off and let him live his life on his own terms, a dejected Lisa seeks guidance from her father's ghost at his memorial bridge, gaining a deeper understanding of the blues and of respecting others' choices. She apologizes to Monk, who reveals he's since gotten a cochlear implant using lottery winnings, allowing him to hear his father's music for the first time. After Bart accidentally ruins the original vinyl, Lisa instead plays a different Bleeding Gums recording for Monk's first listening experience, and the episode closes with Lisa dreaming of jamming alongside her father's ghost and the Jazz Hole musicians. Guest starring John Autry II, Kathy Buckley. title: Dangerous Curves (S20E05)
text: "Dangerous Curves" is an episode of Season 20 (production code KABF18), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Ian Maxtone-Graham, Billy Kimball, originally airing November 9, 2008. On the Fourth of July, the Simpsons drive to a remote cabin, picking up two young hitchhikers along the way, which sparks a series of memories for Homer and Marge. Flashbacks reveal their early dating days in 1988, when a bike crash left them stranded and they were picked up by newlyweds Ned and Maude Flanders, who insisted on keeping them apart. A second set of flashbacks jumps to 2003, showing a more strained Homer and Marge whose car troubles land them at a stranger's party, where Marge grows jealous of a woman named Sylvia and Homer grows resentful of a man named Alberto. Back in the present, the family reaches the same cabin from Homer and Marge's past, and further flashbacks reveal that both parents had secret flirtations with Alberto and Sylvia during that earlier trip, hiding each other's would-be lovers from one another. The present-day reveal that Alberto and Sylvia later married each other devastates Homer and Marge, since their reconciliation years earlier was built on a lie. Wandering into the woods, Homer rediscovers a tree where he once carved a message of eternal love to Marge, prompting a dramatic tumble down a ravine when the weakened tree gives way. Clinging to the peeling bark as they fall, Homer and Marge are reminded that their love isn't tied to a physical token, and they are ultimately rescued from the river by Bart and Lisa, who arrive in a runaway pedal car. Guest starring Maurice LaMarche as Toucan Sam. Notable quotes: Homer: Hey! Everybody pees in the pool! | Patty: Not from the diving board! | Ned Flanders: It's separate accommodations for you not-lyweds. | Homer: That's just your trouser devil talking? title: The Scorpion's Tale (S22E15)
text: "The Scorpion's Tale" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF08), directed by Matthew Schofield and written by Billy Kimball, Ian Maxtone-Graham, originally airing March 6, 2011. During a school field trip to Springfield Desert State Park, Lisa discovers a rare flower, Springfield Silvertongue, that calms aggressive scorpions, and she brings samples home to study. Around the same time, Grampa is kicked out of the retirement home for being too cranky and moves in with the Simpsons, quickly wearing out his welcome. Homer secretly slips Lisa's flower-derived compound into Grampa's coffee, instantly turning him cheerful, but Lisa is troubled by the idea of manufactured happiness and eventually flushes the drug away. When pharmaceutical mogul Walther Hotenhoffer overhears the family discussing Grampa's mood swings, he isolates the compound and mass-produces it as the drug MusBeNys, intending it only for Grampa. Bart, however, steals the supply and sells it around town, causing nearly every elderly resident to become blissfully happy. The celebration turns alarming when Grampa's eyes pop out of his skull, a side effect mirrored in the drugged scorpions, revealing the drug's dangerous flaw. The family confronts Hotenhoffer as a mob of drugged, eyeball-popped seniors demands more of the substance, but he agrees to destroy the remaining stock rather than exploit them. The crowd is redirected when Grampa shames them into helping Homer fix his car the old-fashioned way, proving they don't need artificial happiness after all, and everyone learns a lighthearted lesson about staying with the group on field trips. Guest starring Werner Herzog as Walther Hotenhoffer, Kevin Michael Richardson as Clark. Notable quotes: Bart: Better—the prospectors left naughty French postcards! | Milhouse: Never get off the bus! Never get off the bus! | Grampa: You're a fish tank! | Carl Carlson: I was wonderin' when that guy was gonna state his name and occupation. | Grampa: Funny how many Germans say that these days.

title: Penny-Wiseguys (S24E05)
text: "Penny-Wiseguys" is an episode of Season 24 (production code PABF19), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Michael Price, originally airing November 18, 2012. Homer is stunned to learn that his mild-mannered bowling buddy Dan Gillick moonlights as an accountant for Fat Tony's crime syndicate. When Fat Tony is summoned for jury duty and can't oversee his operations, he puts Dan in charge as acting boss. Dan initially enjoys the perks of power, but quickly grows uneasy as the responsibilities escalate, especially when Fat Tony orders him to eliminate several unnecessary mob associates. Desperate and scared, Dan turns to Homer for help avoiding the hit, but their scheme unravels and Dan flees, intent on carrying out the killings himself. Homer chases him down and manages to talk him out of it before real harm is done. With his jury service finished, Fat Tony resumes control of the mob, while Dan happily moves on to a much safer profession piercing ears at the mall. In a parallel storyline, Lisa faints during a school concert due to an iron deficiency and decides to start eating insects to supplement her vegetarian diet. She begins breeding grasshoppers, but they escape their enclosure, inadvertently aiding Dan's attempted getaway and later swarming to devour a corn maze. Disturbed by nightmares about the bugs, Lisa abandons her insect-eating experiment for good. Guest starring Steve Carell, Joe Mantegna, Alex Trebek. Notable quotes: Homer: Bart! This is America. Anyone can eat what they want as long as they eat too much. | Bart: But I will not be sharing my mini-fridge with Homer. | Homer: You really should tweet less. | Dan Gillick: But everyone deserves to know what I'm thinking all the time. | Moe Szyslak: Just granny-throw it!

title: Dogtown (S28E22)
text: "Dogtown" is an episode of Season 28 (production code WABF15), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing May 21, 2017. Driving home from the Power Plant, Homer's brakes fail while using the EZcape app, forcing him to choose between hitting Santa's Little Helper or Gil Gunderson, and he hits Gil. Gil decides to sue the Simpsons, threatening to take everything they own, but at trial the jury is swayed by heartwarming stories about dogs and Homer wins the case. In the aftermath, Springfield becomes obsessed with dogs, with Mayor Quimby declaring it the 'dog loving capital of the world' and canines taking over local businesses. As predicted by visiting expert Lionel Budgie, the dogs soon turn savage and violent, attacking citizens including Homer, and Santa's Little Helper runs away from home. Bart and Lisa enlist the Crazy Cat Lady to help search for their missing dog in the Springfield Dog Park, where they're surrounded by a pack led by Milhouse's vicious chihuahua Taquito. Marge arrives just in time to fend off the alpha dog and restore order, reuniting pets with their owners including Santa's Little Helper, while Gil, who had tried but failed to help resolve the crisis, ends up adopting Taquito for himself. Guest starring Michael York as Lionel Budgie. Notable quotes: Kent Brockman: It's now official: a Springfield jury has decided that the life of this greyhound is more valuable than the life of this Greyhound station inhabitant. | Gil Gunderson: That's why I'm doin' it! To show everyone I'm not the town failure. | Barney Gumble: I thought I was the town failure! | Moe Szyslak: You're not even that! | Homer: If you were a dog these days, would you come home? It's like doggy heaven out there, only real.

title: The Squirt and the Whale (S21E19)
text: "The Squirt and the Whale" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF14), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Matt Warburton, originally airing April 25, 2010. After deciding to cut costs, Homer installs a backyard windmill but then rejects it once he learns excess power flows back to the electric company, prompting him to disconnect the house from the grid entirely. This leaves the family at the mercy of unpredictable wind for electricity, causing constant household chaos until Bart climbs the windmill and prays for wind, inadvertently summoning a massive storm that destroys the turbine. The storm also washes a giant blue whale, which Lisa names Bluella, onto Springfield Beach, and the town rallies to push it back into the ocean without success. Lisa grows emotionally attached to the dying whale, singing and reading poetry to it, and dreams of a triumphant military rescue that turns strangely cosmic. When the whale actually dies, the police detonate it with dynamite, scattering it across the beach and leading to its parts being turned into food and consumer products. Grieving, Lisa later spots the whale's two orphaned calves being threatened by sharks and, with Homer's help in a borrowed boat, tries to save them, only to be interrupted by rival environmentalists and nearly get Homer eaten before the calves' father whale arrives to rescue everyone. The episode ends on a whimsical note with the family imagining the father whale finding new romance with an octopus, illustrated in drawings shown during the credits. Notable quotes: Homer: The wind may have stopped working, but my brain nev [stops] er does.
quotes: Homer: The wind may have stopped working, but my brain nev [stops] er does.

title: Women in Shorts (S36E06)
text: "Women in Shorts" is an episode of Season 36 (production code 35ABF17), directed by Eric Koenig and written by Christine Nangle, originally airing November 10, 2024. This anthology-style episode weaves together a series of vignettes centered on Springfield's women. Luann's book club friends stage an intervention over her obsession with wine-branded merchandise, while Malibu Stacy abandons her toy kingdom to find a girl who truly loves her, only to be violently rejected by Shauna. Mrs. Muntz spins a bawdy bedtime fairy tale for Nelson about a dancing princess and her rival, and Marge sends an embarrassed Homer to buy her tampons, leading to a humiliating musical number at the pharmacy. Patty and Selma descend into chaos when a Panama Canal shipping snag threatens their cigarette supply, and Dr. Hibbert's attempt to spice up his marriage with role-play is derailed by a real medical emergency. Elsewhere, Luigi's mother proves herself both his mom and his lawyer in a wild courtroom win, and Lunchlady Dora reveals the surprisingly poetic philosophy behind her cafeteria cooking. Lisa dreams of ruling a fantasy kingdom but finds governing joyless, while Agnes searches online for a new nemesis after her longtime rival's death. The episode closes with Helen Lovejoy briefly believing the world is ending due to a misheard commercial, and Springfield Elementary's teachers betting on playground injuries until Mrs. Peyton and Lisa turn the tables on them. Guest starring Ruth Reichl, Kerry Washington. Notable quotes: Marge: Luann, you have an addiction to wine merch. | Miss Hoover: How about "proud slut"? | Shauna Chalmers: Um. Who are you, freak? Besides a freaky freak, you freak. | Dr. Hibbert: No. Uh, my name is also Lavern McCray. | Kirk Van Houten: You said if I stayed in character, we could have sex.

title: To Surveil with Love (S21E20)
text: "To Surveil with Love" is an episode of Season 21 (production code MABF12), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Michael Nobori, originally airing May 2, 2010. After Duffman showers Moe's Tavern with free merchandise, Homer accidentally leaves a Duff gym bag containing plutonium that Smithers hid at a train station, triggering a bomb scare and citywide terrorism fears. To calm the town, Springfield hires British consultant Nigel Bakerbutcher to install surveillance cameras everywhere, a move Lisa opposes even as she battles her own problem: being dismissed as a 'dumb blonde' by the school debate team's judges. Fed up, Lisa dyes her hair brown, while the police recruit ordinary citizens, including Marge and Ned Flanders, to monitor the new camera feeds. Marge quits after growing uncomfortable spying on neighbors, leaving Ned in charge, and he becomes an overzealous moral watchdog nagging everyone through the cameras' speakers. When the townsfolk discover the Simpsons' backyard is a blind spot, Homer and Ned turn it into a paid hideaway for people to misbehave freely. Confronted by Homer, Ned realizes he's been acting like an overreaching deity and, remorseful, joins Homer in destroying all the cameras. Lisa cleverly exposes the judges' hair-based bias at her next debate, though her triumphant point is undercut when Grampa crashes his car into the venue. In a final twist, it's revealed the entire ordeal was secretly broadcast in England as a hit reality show, amusing Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Charles. Guest starring Eddie Izzard as Queen Elizabeth II, Nigel Bakerbutcher, and Prince Charles. And one way to remember that is ABC, Always Be Considering PB&J, but the single most important rule is the four 'A's, Always Act According to ABC. | Marge: That's not Sesame Street, that's a gay bar. | Homer: God create the devil? Finally he did something cool! | Queen Elizabeth II: I'll miss that Ralph Wiggum. He reminds me of my boy. | Mr. Burns: Just find the biggest idiot on our payroll and slip it in his bag.

title: Gorgeous Grampa (S24E14)
text: "Gorgeous Grampa" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF06), directed by Chuck Sheetz and written by Matt Selman, originally airing March 3, 2013. Homer becomes obsessed with the reality show Storage Battles and drags the family to a real storage locker auction, where he wins a locker that turns out to belong to Grampa. Inside they find flamboyant clothing and fitness magazines, leading them to wrongly assume Grampa is secretly gay, and Homer and Marge set out to 'support' him by finding him a boyfriend. When their well-meaning meddling backfires, Mr. Burns arrives and reveals the truth: Grampa was once a famous masked wrestler named Glamorous Godfrey. Burns, a lifelong fan, convinces a reluctant Grampa to return to wrestling, and Bart becomes enthralled with his grandfather's villainous wrestling persona, adopting cruel 'heel' behavior in his own life. As Bart's attitude alienates his family and friends, Grampa realizes the damage his old act is causing and decides to change his approach before a big match. During the bout, Grampa switches from villain to hero, transforming himself and Bart into patriotic good guys instead, angering Burns. The episode ends with Burns packing away all his Godfrey memorabilia in defeat, mirroring Homer's storage-locker obsession from the start. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: Fake? Ridiculous! If professional wrestling were fake...that would make every fan in the history of the sport a complete and utter moron. | Grampa: I ain't a heel no more—I'm a good guy... and you're a baby-face. | Homer: My gay dad is gay for gays. | Marge: I so wanted him to be gay. | Grampa: What?! title: Thirst Trap: A Corporate Love Story (S35E04)
keys: thirst trap: a corporate love story
text: "Thirst Trap: A Corporate Love Story" is an episode of Season 35 (production code OABF21), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing October 29, 2023. Mr. Burns is interviewed for a documentary about his late business partner and wife, Persephone Odair, and the rise and fall of her company LifeBoat, which claimed it could turn seawater into clean drinking water. After Lisa introduces Persephone to Burns, the two form an unlikely partnership, take over Sector 7-G at the power plant, and eventually marry, becoming Springfield's new power couple. As LifeBoat grows, secrecy tightens with strict NDAs, employees are mysteriously fired, and Carl disappears after raising concerns about the technology. An anonymous whistleblower, later revealed to be Homer, exposes that the machine doesn't actually purify water but instead masks its salty taste with a soda additive called Jab-a-tose. Homer and Lisa track down Carl, who confirms he was blackmailed into silence and that Persephone's whole company is a fraud built on a fabricated story about her grandfather. As a public demonstration at Springfield Elementary threatens to poison children with the fake purified water, Burns finally realizes the truth and shuts off the machine just in time. Persephone is arrested and imprisoned while still denying any wrongdoing, and Burns and Persephone divorce, leaving Burns alone once again to muse that he'll always bounce back. Guest starring Christiane Amanpour, Elizabeth Banks, Ken Burns, Peter Coyote, Peter Jackson, Andrew Ross Sorkin, Kara Swisher. title: Homer Scissorhands (S22E20)
text: "Homer Scissorhands" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF13), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Peter Gaffney, Steve Viksten, originally airing May 8, 2011. When Lisa's messy squabble with Bart ends with paint in Patty's hair, Homer steps in with scissors and discovers he has a real gift for styling. Word spreads quickly, and after wowing Lindsey Naegle he opens his own salon, Are We Hair Yet?, becoming the most sought-after stylist in Springfield. The catch is that his female clients bombard him with endless gossip and personal drama, which wears him down until he snaps and tries to quit, only to be forced back into the chair by Chief Wiggum and Sarah ahead of the Policeman's Ball. Meanwhile, Milhouse, shaken by the emotional trauma of watching Finding Nemo, resolves to seize the day and confesses his love to Lisa again, but she turns him down. His romantic song is instead misheard as a serenade by classmate Taffy, and the two start dating, which stirs unexpected jealousy in Lisa. Lisa secretly follows the couple on a date to Holding Hands Point, interrupting both their outing and an unrelated tryst between Hans Moleman and Lunchlady Dora. Confronted, Taffy breaks up with Milhouse because she realizes he's still hung up on Lisa, and Lisa kisses him but admits she's still confused about her feelings. At the ball, Marge publicly credits a stylist named Julio instead of Homer, causing Springfield's women to abandon Homer's salon for Julio, but Homer ultimately finds contentment styling only Marge's hair at home, happy to please just her. Guest starring Kristen Schaal as Taffy. Notable quotes: Selma: I can't believe I'm saying this... Homer Simpson, do me. | Homer: Lady, I'm not a hairdresser—I just put a new lid on a couple of trashcans. | Homer: Just call me "Homer Fingerhands." | Milhouse: Not after Chapter One he doesn't. If death can happen to a fish, it can happen to anyone. | Lunchlady Dora: In the sack he's Salisbury steak, everywhere else creamed corn.

title: White Christmas Blues (S25E08)
text: "White Christmas Blues" is an episode of Season 25 (production code SABF01), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Don Payne, originally airing December 15, 2013. After a news report predicts a snowless Christmas due to global warming, Springfield is surprised by a freak snowfall that Professor Frink reveals is actually caused by radioactive steam from the power plant combined with tire fire particulates. Word spreads that Springfield is the only snowy town in America, triggering a massive influx of holiday tourists who drive up prices and drain local supplies. Struggling to afford Christmas, Marge reluctantly agrees to rent out the family's rec room to a Midwestern family for $300 a night, forcing the Simpsons to share their home with strangers. As Homer and Marge cater to their demanding boarders and Bart minds the visiting kids, the strain of hosting begins to wear on Marge's patience. Meanwhile, Lisa shops for meaningful, inexpensive gifts, but her family—especially Bart, who receives a copy of Treasure Island—finds them underwhelming, leading Bart to burn the book in protest and confront Lisa about her selfish motives. Lisa takes the criticism to heart and gets Bart a tablet instead, while Marge, feeling guilty over her short temper, apologizes to the boarders as they prepare to leave. The boarders forgive her and serenade the family with Christmas carols, though Marge ultimately flees to the kitchen and drowns out their singing with a blender rather than endure another verse. Notable quotes: Bart: Ah geez, when did everything turn to crap? | Professor Frink: So you see, the "snow" is a micro-climate aberration caused by radioactive steam from the nuclear plant and of course tire fire particulate. So, we're the only place in America with snow, if you can call it that. I guess you can. | Homer: Oh good. Marge remarried after I died. Wait a minute, I'm not dead. What's goin' on? | Marge: For your information, Gloria, my "wassail" is just Gatorade I put in the microwave! | Marge: My uncle died in your bed. Merry Christmas.

title: Portrait of a Lackey on Fire (S33E08)
keys: portrait of a lackey on fire
text: "Portrait of a Lackey on Fire" is an episode of Season 33 (production code UABF01), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Rob and Johnny LaZebnik, originally airing November 21, 2021. After one of Mr. Burns' hounds gives birth, Homer is enlisted to help train the resulting litter of puppies for Burns' wealthy friends. When Homer discovers a lonely Smithers longing for companionship, he sets out to find him a boyfriend, eventually pairing him with the last unclaimed puppy's would-be owner, dashing fashion designer Michael de Graaf. Smithers and Michael quickly fall in love, and Marge, a fan of Michael's work, throws them a celebratory party after learning of the romance. Trouble brews when Michael announces plans to open a factory in Springfield, and the Simpsons discover his operation is dangerously polluting and unethical, even by Mr. Burns' low standards. Smithers is torn, but Burns dismissively encourages him to overlook the flaws and marry Michael anyway. Matters come to a head when the factory suffers a serious accident and Michael cruelly kicks the puppy he once seemed to love, leading Smithers to finally end the relationship and take custody of the dog himself. The episode closes with Smithers finding comfort in his new pet while cleverly keeping Mr. Burns distracted with another puzzle.

title: Meat Is Murder (S33E21)
text: "Meat Is Murder" is an episode of Season 33 (production code UABF13), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Michael Price, originally airing May 15, 2022. During Krusty Burger's 50th anniversary celebration, the Simpsons attend Krusty Fest while Grampa stubbornly refuses to eat the food due to an old grudge. It's revealed that Krusty's fortune was built decades earlier by stealing the recipe and idea from a humble burger stand run by young Gus, now the fabulously wealthy Augustus Redfield. Augustus arrives to publicly ruin Krusty's career and reveals that his real revenge target all along was his former partner, Grampa Simpson, whom he lures onto the board of his massive company RedStar with promises of wealth and importance. Lisa tags along and befriends Augustus's idealistic daughter Sheila, who is plotting to oust her father and transform the company into the eco-friendly GreenStar. At a dramatic board vote, Grampa unexpectedly sides with Augustus, foiling Sheila's coup, only for it to be revealed that Augustus intended to use the vote to purge his own children from the company entirely. Grampa outsmarts him by claiming the vote was based on a misunderstanding about Japanese Noh theater, invalidating the decision and creating a tie that thwarts Augustus's scheme. Lisa and Grampa leave feeling triumphant for stopping both Redfields' selfish plans. Meanwhile, Krusty, exiled to a kibbutz in Israel, is thrilled to learn his show and persona have been reinstated. title: Love, Springfieldian Style (S19E12)
text: "Love, Springfieldian Style" is an episode of Season 19 (production code KABF05), directed by Raymond S. Persi and written by Don Payne, originally airing February 17, 2008. On Valentine's Day, Homer takes Marge to a carnival and they get stranded in the Tunnel of Love after Bart sabotages the ride with jello. To pass the time, Homer and Marge each tell romantic anthology stories to their kids. The first depicts Bonnie and Clyde as a Depression-era crime couple whose passionate but doomed relationship ends in a police ambush. The second follows two dogs, Shady and the Vamp, whose romance produces a litter of puppies and is tested when Shady must rescue his pups from the dog catcher before reuniting with his family. The third recasts the tragic real-life romance of Sid Vicious and Nancy Spungen as a punk-rock tale of addiction and self-destruction, ending with the couple bombing at CBGB. The episode closes by returning to the Tunnel of Love, where Homer humorously breaks the fourth wall with a Valentine's message as trash covers the screen, tying back to Bart's parody ending of the Sid and Nancy story. title: The Day the Earth Stood Cool (S24E07)
keys: the day the earth stood cool
text: "The Day the Earth Stood Cool" is an episode of Season 24 (production code PABF20), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Matt Selman, originally airing December 9, 2012. A hip young family from Portland, led by donut artisan Terrence and his wife Emily, moves in next door to the Simpsons, and Homer quickly becomes infatuated with their effortlessly cool lifestyle. Homer tries to reinvent himself to fit in with Terrence, even letting his beard be shaved and adopting hipster fashions, while Lisa enjoys the family's earthy charm and Bart clashes with their son T-Rex. Marge feels increasingly alienated, especially when Emily's open breastfeeding makes her self-conscious about having used formula for Maggie, and she fakes nursing at T-Rex's birthday party to avoid judgment. When T-Rex mocks Homer's birthday gift, Bart and T-Rex get into a fight, causing a rift between the two families that spreads as more Portland transplants flood into Springfield and take over the town's culture. Homer and Marge, unhappy with how their family and city have changed, attempt to reconcile with Terrence and Emily at a local festival, but the reunion is interrupted when T-Rex accidentally starts a fire at the Simpson house after neglecting the compost. With the fire department out of water, Marge saves the day using baby formula to douse the flames, earning Emily's gratitude and easing Marge's guilt about not breastfeeding her other children. Ironically, once Springfield is publicly declared the coolest city in America by The New York Times, all the hipster families abandon town, leaving Lisa sad to see her new friends go. Guest starring Fred Armisen as Terrence, Carrie Brownstein as Emily, Colin Meloy as himself, Patton Oswalt as T-Rex. Notable quotes: Clancy Wiggum: Make more or I shoot! I'm not bluffing. Come on. What have I become? | Marge: Hmm, that's not applesauce. | Emily: I'm sorry we judged you, Marge. Your formula saved us all. | Homer: Honey, I'm not cool. I was never cool. title: Moonshine River (S24E01)
text: "Moonshine River" is an episode of Season 24 (production code PABF21), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Tim Long, originally airing September 30, 2012. After the chaotic Springfield Grand Prix and Tour de Springfield leave the town in ruins, Bart is teased by Lisa for never keeping a girlfriend, prompting him to visit his exes to prove they still like him. Each encounter ends in rejection until he learns from Cletus that his old flame Mary Spuckler has run away from home to New York City. Determined to find her, Bart convinces his family to make the trip, and they arrange a house swap with a New York family to afford it. While Homer and Bart search the city for Mary, Marge and Lisa try to experience Broadway culture on a shoestring budget, first getting cheated at a ticket booth and then facing a canceled performance of Shakespeare in the Park. Bart eventually reunites with Mary disguised as an old 'duchess,' and the two share a tender walk through the city, culminating in Mary singing him a heartfelt song. Just as they're about to kiss, Cletus arrives to bring Mary home because her mother Brandine misses her. Meanwhile, Lisa takes charge of the botched Shakespeare performance, rallying the crowd to stage their own impromptu version of the play. Guest starring Ken Burns, Zooey Deschanel, Sarah Michelle Gellar, Anne Hathaway, Maurice LaMarche, Don Pardo, Natalie Portman, Kevin Michael Richardson, Al Roker, Sarah Silverman. Which is that love doesn't exist, except briefly between a man and a woman before marriage. | Nikki McKenna: You've got a lot of nerve showing up here. And not giving me a kiss.

title: Sex, Pies and Idiot Scrapes (S20E01)
text: "Sex, Pies and Idiot Scrapes" is an episode of Season 20 (production code KABF17), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Kevin Curran, originally airing September 28, 2008. Springfield bans alcohol for St. Patrick's Day, leading to a violent brawl between Irish and Northern Irish tourists. While chasing down bail-skippers involved in the riot, Homer discovers a passion for bounty hunting and partners with Ned Flanders after Ned accidentally saves him from being shot by Snake. Meanwhile, Marge's cupcakes catch the eye of a baker named Patrick Farrelly, who hires her without revealing that his bakery specializes in erotic cakes, a fact she only discovers when Patty and Selma come in to order one. Homer and Ned's partnership sours after a chaotic chase to capture Fat Tony, and Ned quits the business in frustration with Homer. When bondsman Lucky Jim assigns Ned one final bounty—Homer himself—Ned reluctantly agrees so no other hunter can hurt his friend. The two end up trapped together in hardening wet cement atop a construction site after a wild chase, bonding as Ned recites scripture to pass the time. Homer is eventually arrested for his earlier mayhem, but Marge visits him in jail with a cake to remind him of her love, having come to terms with her unusual new job. Guest starring Robert Forster as Lucky Jim, Julia Louis-Dreyfus as Gloria, Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony. Notable quotes: Marge: This was such a pleasant St. Patrick's day until the Irish people showed up. | Mayor Quimby: Greetings, fellow Irishmen and lady-Irishmen! | Judge Snyder: Bail is set at $25,000. | Chief Wiggum: Well, Simpson looks like for you and you little friend's mayhem, you're going to jail for six weeks! | Superintendent Chalmers: Quick! We'll have to eat from each end. We'll know we're safe when our lips meet in the middle.

title: Moms I'd Like to Forget (S22E10)
text: "Moms I'd Like to Forget" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF03), directed by Chris Clements and written by Brian Kelley, originally airing January 9, 2011. During a heated dodgeball rematch between Springfield Elementary's fourth and fifth graders, Bart notices that his rival Erik has an identical tiny sword-shaped scar on his hand. Curious about its origin, Bart asks Marge, who explains that when he was a toddler she belonged to a clique of mothers called the Cool Moms who met at a daycare center for playdates. Eager to relive those days, Marge reunites the group, but while the mothers happily reminisce, Bart is worn out and picked on by the other kids, and the fathers can't stand each other's company. Determined to solve the scar mystery, Bart and Lisa track down Comic Book Guy, who reveals that a chaotic fireworks mishap years earlier—caused by the toddlers, including Bart—sent flaming sandwich forks flying into their hands, branding them all with matching marks. Frustrated by the group's return, Bart and Milhouse scheme to break up the Cool Moms by rigging fireworks in the garage to frame them, but Marge catches Bart in the act before he can pull it off. After Bart storms out and Homer gets blasted by an accidental explosion, Marge confronts the other moms, only to learn they always saw Bart as the troublesome one, prompting her to angrily quit the group. As the mothers' friendships dissolve amid petty drama, the long-suffering fathers finally reach their breaking point, with Homer impulsively hugging Ned Flanders out of sheer relief that the forced socializing is over. Notable quotes: Bart: Ew, your sitting on the toilet! | Marge: When its closed its a chair. | Marge: We called ourselves the cool moms. | Bart: There's nothing cooler than calling yourselves cool. | Marge: We called ourselves The Cool Moms!

title: Pay Pal (S25E21)
text: "Pay Pal" is an episode of Season 25 (production code SABF15), directed by Michael Polcino and written by David H. Steinberg, originally airing May 11, 2014. After a store-bought cake mishap at a block party, Marge befriends a charming British couple who moves into the neighborhood, but Homer's clumsiness at their game night gets the Simpsons banned from their circle. Discouraged by her own lack of friends, Marge becomes obsessed with ensuring Lisa isn't similarly isolated, especially after Lisa insists she doesn't need friends either. A pity party for Lisa flops when only one obnoxious boy shows up, and Marge learns from Miss Hoover that Lisa's classmates avoid her because she's overbearing and dismissive of their interests. Desperate, Marge secretly pays a girl named Tumi to befriend Lisa, and the plan seems to work until Bart catches Marge handing over cash and exposes the scheme with photos. Lisa is devastated and refuses to forgive her mother, while Homer learns from Grampa that he himself only became friends with Lenny and Carl because Grampa paid them off as kids. Marge's tearful attempts to apologize eventually soften Lisa's heart, and the two reconcile on Mother's Day, much to Homer and Bart's guilty realization that they'd forgotten the holiday. The next day, Tumi confesses she took the bribe for a new belt but genuinely likes Lisa, and the girls reconcile—until Lisa discovers Tumi eats horse meat and ditches her for good. Guest starring Carl Kasell, John Oliver, Peter Sagal. Notable quotes: Marge: Don't you dare say "ostrich eyes"! | Homer: Well, Lisa's gonna be here in five minutes, and the only kid who showed up is Gus freakin' Huebner. | Gus Huebner: Oh, no. I was the only chump who showed up at this train wreck. Well, I'm not leaving till I get a party. | Shauna: If I make out with you, will you shut up? | Gil Gunderson: Roger dodger, boss.

title: Gorillas on the Mast (S31E05)
text: "Gorillas on the Mast" is an episode of Season 31 (production code YABF20), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Max Cohn, originally airing November 3, 2019. During a family outing at Aquatraz Water Park, Lisa is disturbed by the misery of the captive animals, while Homer is captivated by the lifestyle of boat owners and recalls his childhood dream of owning one. A boat salesman talks Homer into buying a boat he names the Something's Fishy, and after an enjoyable first outing with the family, the excitement quickly turns sour when the boat springs a leak and begins sinking. To cover the mounting repair costs, Homer starts selling shares of ownership to Lenny, Carl, and eventually a growing crowd of co-owners. Meanwhile, having discovered the joy of freeing animals, Bart enlists Milhouse to release more creatures from captivity, leading them to break a gorilla named Lolo out of the zoo. The gorilla rampages through Springfield, eventually terrorizing Springfield Elementary, until Lisa manages to calm it using a clip of Seinfeld. Lisa then brings Lolo to real-life primatologist Jane Goodall, who takes the gorilla to a proper sanctuary where she can live freely. In the end, Homer's boat scheme collapses under its own weight from too many owners, but he manages to convince his disgruntled partners at Moe's Tavern that briefly owning a boat was worth it anyway. Guest starring Jane Goodall as herself. Notable quotes: Bart: Look how happy that thing is. Lis, this is a new feeling. We helped a whale be free and now I feel wonderful. | Homer: I thought you sold boats. Make up your mind, liar. | Homer: No. We bought this boat. You just weren't aware. | Lou: Uh, yeah, I think that's a balloon, Chief. | Bart: Altruism rocks! Like when you let something go and it smashes everything. Next, I want to altruism a rhino.

title: The Star of the Backstage (S33E01)
text: "The Star of the Backstage" is an episode of Season 33 (production code QABF17), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Elisabeth Kiernan Averick, originally airing September 26, 2021. At a memorial for Franklin Chase, Marge is reminded of a high school-era musical, Y2K: The Millennium Bug, which she stage-managed years earlier, and Mrs. Chase's gift of the old prompt book inspires her to organize a reunion performance. Homer steps in to replace an injured Lenny, and the original cast, including Broadway actress Sasha Reed, reassembles for the show. As rehearsals proceed, Marge discovers that the cast has been socializing and reminiscing without her, since she was only ever the stage manager and not a true member of their group. Hurt and feeling excluded, she digs into Sasha's background using her mother's computer and uncovers information that could expose Sasha as a fraud. Rather than turning the group against Sasha, however, Marge's revelation causes the cast to turn against Marge herself, deepening her sense of isolation. Struggling with anger and sleeplessness, Marge is comforted by Homer, who helps her see her own mistake through song. She then apologizes at Moe's and reunites the cast to successfully stage the musical. Though she still feels overlooked, two admirers invite her to dinner to honor her contributions, and Homer throws a celebratory party for the cast at their house. Guest starring Kristen Bell as Marge's singing voice, Sara Chase as Sasha Reed. Notable quotes: Homer: Wow, honey, those dorks are so excited to be in your show again. And I will do everything I can to support you... while I'm at Moe's. | Homer: From this day forward, we are enemies. Forever and ever. Forever. | Marge: We were such a tight-knit group. Remember the tightness of the knitting? | Jacqueline Bouvier: I never liked that Sasha Reed. Taking pop out of the fridge without asking... getting us sued... | Sasha: Why would Marge do that to me? title: The Tipping Point (S35E17)
text: "The Tipping Point" is an episode of Season 35 (production code 35ABF11), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing May 12, 2024. The Simpsons head out expecting a fun surprise but instead spend the day at the medical plaza for a marathon of checkups. Afterward, a trip for treats introduces Homer to Springfield's aggressive new tipping culture, which wears him down at every register. At a pub, a scribbled note meant to limit his tip to one dollar is misread by server Sandee as a staggering $10,000 gratuity, and the resulting viral praise gives Homer an addictive rush. He spirals into a reckless tipping spree, overpaying strangers and workers all over town while ignoring the family's mounting debt, straining his marriage with Marge. After a failed, awkward attempt to flirt his way out of the bill with Sandee ends in pepper spray, Homer flees into the water and is rescued into the hidden tip-free enclave of Little Europe. Bart and Lisa track him down there via his Amazon purchases, and the tranquil, gratuity-free community inspires Lisa to suggest Homer bring reform back home. Homer tries to pitch a living-wage solution at a public awards event, but his dream of universal acceptance collapses into a real beatdown. In the end, Marge devises a practical fix: Homer will work as a server himself to understand and address the tipping problem from both sides. Guest starring Kyle Gordon as DJ Crazy Times, Chrissi Poland as Ms. Biljana Electronica, Audrey Trullinger as Inga. Notable quotes: Homer: You want a tip? It's self-serve. We did all the work. | Marge: We don't have $10,000. We don't have 10,000 of anything. | Homer: For once, people aren't judging me by the content of my character but by the content of my wallet. | Homer: Marge, for once you're right. I have a serious problem. But, like any addiction, it can easily be stopped by just deciding to stop. | Homer: No one service worker can satisfy my needs. God help me, I'm a tip-phomaniac.

title: Seperance (S37E13)
text: "Seperance" is an episode of Season 37 (production code 37ABF07), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing January 4, 2026. Ten years after Homer was made safety inspector at the plant, he's grown lazy and apathetic, even about a family field trip to a state park with Marge, Bart, and Lisa. When Marge urges him to fake enthusiasm at a gift shop for the kids' sake, his convincing performance catches the attention of a mysterious stranger who turns out to be a retired Duffman, now recruiting for EOD (Enthusiasm on Demand), a covert marketing firm run by the enigmatic Consonance. Homer thrives at first, using his newfound fake enthusiasm to sell products, but when he can't bring himself to pitch non-alcoholic beer to his bowling buddies, Consonance subjects him to the 'seperance' procedure, a brain operation that strips away his personal tastes and turns him into an emotionless salesman. Marge, worried about Homer's zombie-like behavior, confronts Consonance and ends up undergoing the same procedure so they can work together, alarming Bart and Lisa. With help from Duffman, who has 'de-seperanced' himself, the kids sneak into EOD's headquarters to rescue their parents. There, Consonance reveals the company's talking founder statue is a hoax and that the 'procedure' was only cosmetic surgery — the real cause of the parents' burnout is simply overwork. Confronted by their children, Marge decides to quit and find balance, while Homer returns to normal, though the episode ends with both parents still emotionally drained from the demands of ordinary parenting. Guest starring Zach Cherry as Farley Lewis, Julianne Moore as Consonance. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: Simpson, you're brand-new here, but I have a nose for men, and you stink of reliability. I'm putting you in charge of the big red button. | Homer: I worked all week at the world's most boring job, and now I have to spend time in the natural world that I devoted my life to destroy. | Marge: Can't you fake a little enthusiasm for five minutes? | Mr. Burns: I should be furious that you're leaving with no notice, but your sincere enthusiasm for taking this job and shoving it has won me over. Consider it shoved. | Duffman: Then what did I drill out of my skull?
