title: The Good, the Sad, and the Drugly (S20E17)
keys: the good, the sad, and the drugly
text: "The Good, the Sad, and the Drugly" is an episode of Season 20 (production code LABF07), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Marc Wilmore, originally airing April 19, 2009. After a prank at school goes awry and Milhouse takes the blame, Bart is forced by Homer to visit Grampa at the retirement castle, where he meets and falls for a kind volunteer named Jenny. To win her over, Bart pretends to be a selfless do-gooder, staging acts of kindness like rescuing a duck from bullies. Meanwhile, Lisa spirals into despair after researching a bleak future for Springfield, prompting Marge to take her to a psychiatrist who prescribes an antidepressant that instead causes Lisa to hallucinate happy faces on everything, including disturbing scenes. Milhouse, jealous and hurt that Bart abandoned him, sabotages Bart's charade by exposing his lies to Jenny, leading her to break up with him. As Lisa's medicated delusions grow more alarming, Marge disposes of the pills, though the family dog ends up ingesting them instead. Lisa comes to realize that confronting problems directly is healthier than avoiding them, advice she passes on to Bart. Bart takes this to heart, apologizes to Milhouse, and the two reconcile by pulling a new prank together, turning the school floor into an ice rink. Guest starring Anne Hathaway. You've finally become the boy every mother dreams of... a girl! | Jenny: Are you saying our entire relationship is based on lies? | Bart: Not our entire relationship, just the stuff I said. | Lisa: If you don't stop smiling, you're gonna get a kiss! | Milhouse: Oh, I see how it is.

title: Treehouse of Horror XXVIII (S29E04)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXVIII" is an episode of Season 29 (production code WABF18), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by John Frink, originally airing October 22, 2017. This Halloween anthology opens with a twisted candy sketch in which the Simpson family, cast as pieces of candy on a trick-or-treat plate, fear being unwanted, culminating in Homer cannibalizing a talking chocolate Easter bunny. In 'The Exor-Sis,' an ancient Pazuzu statue ordered online possesses Maggie, who murders several Springfield residents before a priest's botched exorcism transfers the demon into Bart, giving him monstrous antlers that injure Homer. In 'Coralisa,' Lisa follows a newly talkative Snowball II through a secret tunnel into an eerie alternate dimension where a 'perfect' version of her family wants to sew buttons over her eyes, and after fleeing she eventually agrees to join them, followed by Bart and then her parents, leading to violent mishaps and both sets of parents exploiting their double for convenience. Finally, in 'MMM... Homer,' left alone and starving, Homer accidentally discovers his own cooked flesh tastes delicious, leading him to progressively consume himself and, with celebrity chef Mario Batali's help, open a chain of restaurants serving his own body before dying and reuniting with Jesus in Heaven, who shares his unusual culinary interest. Each segment ends in dark, comedic tragedy, tying together themes of self-destruction, identity, and grotesque family dynamics typical of the Treehouse of Horror series. Guest starring Mario Batali, Ben Daniels, William Friedkin, Neil Gaiman. Notable quotes: Apple-Lisa: No one ever wants the apple. They must be afraid there's a razor blade in me. | Pazuzu: No one leaves alive! | Pazuzu: I used to be very important. Google it. | Priest: If you can't trust a Catholic priest with a child, who can you trust? | Lisa: What you're about to see is so disgusting, you'll watch Game of Thrones to calm down! This installment is made up of 4 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 28): "The Sweets Hereafter", "The Exor-Sis", "Coralisa", and "MMM... Homer".

title: The Great Simpsina (S22E18)
text: "The Great Simpsina" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF11), directed by Chris Clements and written by Matt Warburton, originally airing April 10, 2011. After a family peach-picking trip leaves the Simpsons overwhelmed with fruit, the kids scatter to unload their share, and Lisa ends up lost in a deserted area where a raccoon chases her into the home of an aging illusionist known as The Great Raymondo. Intrigued by her quick aptitude for a trick, he reluctantly agrees to mentor her in magic, and Lisa begins secretly performing tricks at school while continuing her lessons. Trouble starts when Raymondo teaches her the secret behind the dangerous 'Great Milk Can Escape,' and Lisa is tricked by the son of rival magician Cregg Demon into revealing it. Cregg publicly claims the secret came to him in a dream from Houdini's ghost and plans to perform the escape at the World Magic Championship. Furious at the betrayal, Raymondo banishes Lisa, causing her to give up magic, though he eventually forgives her. At the championship, jealous rival magicians sabotage Cregg by swapping in a real, inescapable milk can, and despite Lisa's pleas, no one steps in to help him. Raymondo ultimately intervenes to save Cregg by dropping a girder on the attacking magicians, prompting Cregg to quit magic entirely. The episode ends with Raymondo and Lisa performing a triumphant magic act together, followed by Raymondo sharing a tender dance with the ghost of his late wife. Why was I ever born?! | The Great Raymondo: A girl illusionist?! Ladies are what you saw in half and throw knives at. They never wear the hat. | The Great Raymondo: You should be. That monkey wound up with 18 car dealerships. If you bought a family car in the St. Louis area, you bought it from the mighty Chimpopo. | Principal Skinner: I don't know what to think about milk cans anymore. | Nelson Muntz: God, if you don't bring my Lisa back safe, ants will burn tonight.

title: Friends and Family (S28E02)
text: "Friends and Family" is an episode of Season 28 (production code VABF18), directed by Lance Kramer and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing October 2, 2016. After decades of anger management failing to help him, Mr. Burns' psychiatrist dies, and at the funeral the Simpsons bicker while Burns' tacky self-funded tombstone enrages the mourners. Fleeing the scene, Smithers accidentally runs over Professor Frink, who is wearing a prototype virtual-reality Oculus device, and Burns becomes fascinated with the technology. Taking the Oculus home, Burns decides to use it to build himself a virtual family, holding auditions that land the Simpsons the job—except for Homer, since Burns insists on playing the father role himself. With his family sent to live in a mansion shack as Burns' VR family, Homer is left alone and soon strikes up a close friendship with his new neighbor Julia, who shares all his tastes in beer and dislike of Ned Flanders. Meanwhile, Burns quickly tires of the emotional demands of an actual family dynamic and fires the Simpsons. When Marge returns home, she is furious to find Homer has grown close to Julia, but calms down once Julia clarifies their relationship was purely platonic. The episode ends with the Oculus craze spreading across Springfield, with even Homer and Marge adopting the devices. Guest starring Allison Janney. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: Hush! No one must know I'm not in perfect mental health. The Kaiser would be furious! | Doctor 3: Euthanasia! Sweet, sweet euthanasia! | Mr. Burns: Ooh! Can I buy it as a gift?

title: Rednecks and Broomsticks (S21E07)
text: "Rednecks and Broomsticks" is an episode of Season 21 (production code LABF19), directed by Bob Anderson, Rob Oliver and written by Kevin Curran, originally airing November 29, 2009. Returning from a ski trip, the Simpsons crash their car onto a frozen lake after Homer destroys Bart and Lisa's annoying toy, and Cletus rescues them and brings them to his shack. While Homer bonds with Cletus and his moonshine-brewing friends, Lisa wanders off during hide-and-seek with Cletus's daughters and stumbles upon a trio of teenage Wiccans, including a girl named Cassandra. Initially skeptical of their magic, Lisa grows curious when Ms. Hoover falls ill, but the girls insist they're harmless and invite her to join their coven. Ned Flanders spots Lisa researching witchcraft online and, alarmed, alerts the authorities, leading to the girls' arrest just as Lisa is about to be inducted. When much of Springfield mysteriously goes blind, the town blames the Wiccans and puts them on trial, with Lisa testifying in their defense. Judge Snyder dismisses the case for lack of evidence, but the townsfolk try to dunk the girls anyway until Lisa reveals the truth: Cletus and his moonshiner friends, panicking when police drove by en route to arrest the witches, dumped their illegal stills into the river, contaminating the town's water supply with alcohol and causing the blindness. The Wiccans are freed and thank Lisa, who thanks them in turn for opening her mind, though Marge still forbids her from seeing them again. Guest starring Neve Campbell as Cassandra. Notable quotes: Homer: I can't take it any more! [throws Bonk It out the window] | Homer: D'oh!

Homer: D'oh!

title: Keep Chalm and Gary On (S37E02)
text: "Keep Chalm and Gary On" is an episode of Season 37 (production code 36ABF14), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Christine Nangle, originally airing October 5, 2025. Bart brings home a rare A on his homework, but Lisa discovers he used the AI tool CheatGPT to cheat, sparking a sibling feud while their parents remain indifferent until Lisa pushes Homer to intervene. Springfield Elementary's teachers demand a solution, leading Principal Skinner to adopt AI-detection software and a bizarre 'banana' countermeasure, which escalates into a prank war with the students. When Superintendent Chalmers enforces a phone ban in retaliation, the students frame him for plagiarizing his college thesis, and he is fired from his job. Down on his luck, Chalmers takes a janitorial position at the power plant thanks to Homer, but is banished to the tunnels after being caught slacking off. There he discovers giant mutant snails whose slime turns out to be a miracle skincare ingredient, and he builds it into a wildly successful men's beauty empire called Escarbro. As Chalmers becomes rich and famous, he learns his products have become dangerously popular among children, prompting a crisis of conscience. He buys the school outright, reinstates himself as superintendent, and bans skincare products from campus. Meanwhile, back at the power plant, the neglected snails die after being fed junk food by careless employees, leaving Skinner stuck cleaning up the mess as the new janitor. Guest starring Cole Escola, Adam Pally, Kerry Washington. Brilliant, bro.

title: The Daughter Also Rises (S23E13)
text: "The Daughter Also Rises" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF06), directed by Chuck Sheetz and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing February 12, 2012. On Valentine's Day, Bart and Milhouse are inspired by the TV show MythCrackers to start testing and debunking urban legends around Springfield Elementary, from phone explosions at gas stations to electrocuting vending machines, eventually 'solving' every myth in the school. Meanwhile, Homer plans a romantic day for Marge, urging her to spend time with Bart while he pampers her, and Marge takes Lisa out to lunch instead. At the restaurant, Lisa meets Nick, a literary, Hemingway-loving boy, and the two quickly bond over shared interests, spending increasing amounts of time together. Marge grows hurt and jealous as Lisa neglects their mother-daughter activities in favor of Nick, though she reluctantly allows the relationship to continue after Lisa promises balance. Grampa tells Lisa the tragic myth of Pyramus and Thisbe, inspiring her to seek a symbolic kiss with Nick under a mulberry tree on Mulberry Island. Their journey to the island is complicated by Grampa's arrest and a ride from Cletus, during which Nick's true, less charming personality begins to show. When they finally reach the island, Lisa has a change of heart, realizing a kiss there would mean falsely committing to eternal love, and the romance ends as Nick storms off. Marge, having trekked to the island in water shoes to reconcile with her daughter, reunites with Lisa, restoring their close relationship, while Homer's attempt to rescue them by watercraft ends in comic failure. Guest starring Michael Cera, Jamie Hyneman, Adam Savage. Notable quotes: Lisa: Thanks. But I couldn't do it, Mom. I mean, the person you kiss under a mulberry tree is someone you'll love for the rest of your life. | Adam Savage: Don't know, don't care! Blow it up. | Dolph Shapiro: So, school is just everything we see? | Jimbo Jones: That's sad, man. | Groundskeeper Willie: Now there's a myth about me I'd like you to correct, I'm not from Edinburgh!

title: Husbands and Knives (S19E07)
text: "Husbands and Knives" is an episode of Season 19 (production code JABF17), directed by Nancy Kruse and written by Matt Selman, originally airing November 18, 2007. When a hip new comic shop called Coolsville opens across from the Android's Dungeon, Comic Book Guy loses all his customers and tries increasingly desperate schemes to sabotage its charismatic owner, Milo, eventually attacking the store with a sword before giving up and selling his shop to Marge. Marge transforms the space into Shapes, a women-only gym designed to spare ordinary women the humiliation she felt at a fancy health club, and it quickly becomes a wildly popular, profitable business that turns her into a local celebrity. Homer, insecure about Marge's newfound success and attractiveness, is manipulated by a trio of gym-hotel jocks into believing she's about to leave him for a fitter man. Rather than following an ex-husband's sensible advice about diet and exercise, Homer opts for extreme cosmetic surgery and stomach stapling, emerging grotesquely altered and covered in loose skin. His bizarre new appearance horrifies the town during a ceremony honoring Marge, prompting Mayor Quimby to incite a mob against him, and the couple flees to a bell tower where Marge shoves Homer off in a moment revealed to be his own anxious dream. Homer wakes in the hospital back to normal, comforted that Marge rejected the surgeon's further body-altering plans and only agreed to reverse his stomach stapling because she loves him as he is. In a closing gag, the visiting alternative comic creators Alan Moore, Art Spiegelman, and Daniel Clowes casually dismiss a meteor threatening Earth in favor of attending a convention for underpaid writers. Guest starring Jack Black as Milo, Daniel Clowes as himself, Maurice LaMarche as husband 3, Alan Moore as himself, Art Spiegelman as himself. Notable quotes: Milo: These books are meant to be read and enjoyed, not hoarded and then sold when you get divorced. | Comic Book Guy: Nice work, Doctor Boo-Who. Your tears have smudged Wolverine's iconic sideburns. Hence, you must buy this comic. And the cost of your innocent accident is... $25, please. | Strawberry: My name is Strawberry. My purse is a lunch box. | Homer: No! I had my stomach stapled! | Alan Moore: You see what those bloody corporations do? They take your ideas and they suck them! Suck them like leeches until they've gotten every last drop of marrow from your bones!

title: Bart vs. Itchy & Scratchy (S30E18)
text: "Bart vs. Itchy & Scratchy" is an episode of Season 30 (production code YABF10), directed by Chris Clements and written by Megan Amram, originally airing March 24, 2019. At Krusty Kon, Krusty unveils an all-female reboot of Itchy and Scratchy, delighting the girls of Springfield Elementary while the boys, led by Bart, launch a boycott. Bart secretly loves the new show and gets caught laughing at it by Lisa, who films him and lets Homer broadcast the humiliating clip on Josh.0. Ostracized by his friends, Bart is taken in by three sixth-grade girls—Carmen, Erica, and Piper—who belong to a rebellious group called Bossy Riot, while Milhouse forms a rival all-boy club, the Boys Rights Association. As Bossy Riot's pranks escalate from pestering Skinner to threatening to destroy all the original Itchy and Scratchy masters live on television, Lisa becomes intrigued and eventually asks to join. Bart tries to stop the girls from wrecking the master tapes but gets tied up for his trouble, and Lisa saves most of the footage using nail polish remover, letting the boys wrongly blame Milhouse. Chief Wiggum's attempt to catch the girls fails thanks to their disguises, and the trio reveal to Bart that he was only ever useful to them for his fingerprints and DNA before inviting Lisa to join their crew instead. Bart, now cheerfully vandalizing walls with feminist slogans, returns to his friends and unintentionally deflates their egos by revealing that the girls don't envy them at all. Guest starring Awkwafina as Carmen, Nicole Byer as Erica, Chelsea Peretti as Piper. Notable quotes: Nelson: You betrayed us, Bart. And worse, you betrayed your own wang. | Jimbo: Girls aren't funny. They're hot, or moms. | Milhouse: Gentlemen, our way of life is under attack. | Bart: Mercenaries are cool, like Boba Fett. | Bart: They don't envy us.

title: Treehouse of Horror XXX (S31E04)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXX" is an episode of Season 31 (production code YABF18), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing October 20, 2019. This Halloween special unfolds in four segments. In the opening, Marge gives birth to Maggie, who turns out to be a demonic force who terrorizes Springfield until she fatally impales her family in a church. In 'Danger Things,' a 1980s-set parody of Stranger Things, Milhouse vanishes into an alternate dimension called the Over Under after a bike ride home, prompting Lisa to use psychic powers and a sensory deprivation tank to rescue him from monstrous Demogorgons unleashed by a secret Mr. Burns experiment, with Homer ultimately saving the kids using a flamethrower. In 'Heaven Swipes Right,' Homer chokes to death on a hot dog and learns in Heaven that he died before his allotted time, so he is allowed to inhabit other men's bodies—first a star quarterback, then Superintendent Chalmers—before settling into Moe's body, only for a mix-up to land Moe's consciousness in baby Maggie instead. Finally, in 'When Hairy Met Slimy,' Selma falls in love with the alien Kang hidden in the power plant, and when Mr. Burns tries to dissect him, Homer and Barney help the couple flee amid a military chase; Kang uses Thanos's gauntlet to wipe out their pursuers, heals a wounded Selma, and reveals he's pregnant, while Patty ends up falling for Kodos and the two alien-and-human couples fly off together to a scorching honeymoon planet. Notable quotes: Dr. Hibbert: I should warn you, however. We ran the standard newborn screen on her, and, uh, she tested positive... for evil. | Ned: Looks like I'll be digging three graves. | Lisa: Girls are afraid to use them, because then we're called unfeminine. We needlessly lost a lot of good witches at Salem. | St. Greeter: No, I'm St. Greeter, if you'll forgive the pun. | Kang: I am Kang the Conqueror. This installment is made up of 3 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 30): "Danger Things", "Heaven Swipes Right", and "When Hairy Met Slimy".

title: Looking for Mr. Goodbart (S28E20)
text: "Looking for Mr. Goodbart" is an episode of Season 28 (production code WABF13), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing April 30, 2017. After being punished for changing the lyrics to a grandparents' day song, Bart is forced by Principal Skinner to escort his elderly mother Agnes around town, which unexpectedly opens Bart's eyes to the perks of spending time with old women who shower him with treats and money. Bart begins exploiting this discovery, cozying up to various elderly ladies for gifts until a sharp-eyed woman named Phoebe Pratt catches on and strikes a deal, paying him to pick her up from her nursing home for four days straight. Bart grows genuinely fond of Phoebe during their outings in the woods, and when she tries to pay him afterward he refuses, prompting her to instead leave him her camera as a bequest. Not knowing the word's meaning, Bart researches it at the library and realizes Phoebe may be dying, only to rush to the nursing home and discover she has actually fled to escape her confinement. Meanwhile, Homer becomes obsessed with the mobile game Peekimon Get, dragging the family into absurd monster-hunting escapades around Springfield and even spending real money on cheats over Marge's objections. Bart enlists Homer and Lisa's help using the game's crowd-sourced player network to track down and rescue Phoebe from the wilderness. The experience teaches Bart a lesson about not exploiting the elderly for personal gain, which he recounts in full to Grampa at the Retirement Castle as a framing device for the whole story. The episode closes with Skinner's dinner date being hilariously ruined by Agnes and Milhouse's mocking interruption at Luigi's. Guest starring Valerie Harper, Jennifer Saunders. Which of your two lame weapons are you gonna unleash on me? | Skinner: I have no other weapons. | Bart: Wow, two things that won't exist in 20 years. | Milhouse Van Houten: My silhouette's replacing yours on the stairs.

title: Exit Through the Kwik-E-Mart (S23E15)
text: "Exit Through the Kwik-E-Mart" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF09), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Marc Wilmore, originally airing March 4, 2012. When Homer forgets to properly plan for Marge's birthday, he buys her a food processor and arranges to have it autographed by infomercial star Paula Paul at the trendy new health-food chain Swapper Jack's, which is stealing customers from Apu's Kwik-E-Mart. A mishap with Marge's pet rabbit chewing the phone line causes Homer to miss Paula's promised birthday call, leading him to unfairly blame and nearly strangle Bart. Seeking revenge, Bart begins plastering unflattering 'Dope' posters of Homer around Springfield, unintentionally becoming a minor folk-hero vandal known as 'Mr. Fatso.' A group of real street artists catches Bart and Milhouse in the act and, impressed by his work, invite him to headline his own gallery show. Meanwhile, Apu's business is nearly ruined by Swapper Jack's, until the store is revealed to sell monkey-based products from Brazil and is shut down, saving the Kwik-E-Mart. Bart's art show turns out to be a police sting orchestrated by Chief Wiggum and Mr. Burns to punish him for the vandalism, and he is arrested. After Bart apologizes to Homer by spray-painting 'I'm sorry' on his car, the family decides on a lighter punishment: locking him in the rabbit cage as public penance, though he still manages to escape and leave one last graffiti message. Guest starring Robbie Conal as himself, Ron English as himself, Shepard Fairey as himself, Kenny Scharf as himself. THAT TEARS IT! | Homer: No, Homer, you can't strangle a boy on his mother's birthday. Juries hate that. | Bart: Hey, I got an "F" in art. Mainly so it would say "Fart" on my report card.

title: The Caper Chase (S28E19)
text: "The Caper Chase" is an episode of Season 28 (production code WABF12), directed by Lance Kramer and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing April 2, 2017. After a disastrous softball game leaves Homer collapsed on the field, Mr. Burns grows frustrated with the entitled attitude of Yale graduates he hoped to hire for the plant. Discovering how lucrative for-profit universities can be, thanks to a tip from Skull and Bones member Bourbon Verlander, Burns torches his Yale memorabilia and founds his own institution, Burns University, staffing it with plant employees like Homer, Lenny, and Carl as professors. Homer initially struggles as a teacher until Lisa gives him a set of inspirational-teacher movies, which turn him into a surprisingly gifted educator. His newfound skill catches Bourbon's attention, and Burns sells Homer's teaching services to him. Homer is then introduced to real-life figures Neil deGrasse Tyson, Ken Jennings, Suze Orman, and Robert McKee, who are tasked with teaching android clones of LadyBot called Sallys how to act like students. Months later, during a big showcase of the robotic students at Yale, Homer accidentally causes the Sallys to malfunction and explode, ruining Bourbon's plan. In the aftermath, the group of experts turn their teaching efforts toward Lisa, Marge, and Bart instead. Guest starring Jason Alexander as Bourbon Verlander, Ken Jennings as himself, Stan Lee as himself, Robert McKee as himself, Suze Orman as herself, Neil deGrasse Tyson as himself. Notable quotes: Lisa: It's like watching maple syrup play softball. | Homer: As Americans, it's our duty to either stop evil billionaires or to elect them to the highest office in the land.
quotes: Lisa: It's like watching maple syrup play softball.
Homer: As Americans, it's our duty to either stop evil billionaires or to elect them to the highest office in the land.

title: One Angry Lisa (S34E02)
text: "One Angry Lisa" is an episode of Season 34 (production code UABF19), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Jessica Conrad, originally airing October 2, 2022. When Marge falls for a slick TV ad, Homer reluctantly buys her an expensive Pedalon exercise bike, and she quickly becomes infatuated with its charismatic virtual instructor, Jesse. As Marge's obsession grows—spending money and daydreaming about Jesse instead of her husband—Homer's jealousy and insecurity boil over, sending him to Moe's for sympathy from equally neglected husbands. Meanwhile, Lisa is mistakenly summoned for jury duty despite being only eight, and is forced to sit through an absurd criminal trial presided over by Judge Constance Harm, featuring bumbling testimony from Chief Wiggum and inept lawyering from Gil. Frustrated by the courtroom's incompetence, Lisa's outspoken objections land her in contempt of court, and the case ultimately ends in a mistrial, letting the defendant go free. Back on the home front, Homer confronts Jesse in person and ends up in a physical fight, prompting Marge to ride to his rescue on her Pedalon bike after discovering Jesse's setup is a fraud. She saves Homer by shoving Jesse down a fake Great Wall set, and the couple reconcile, riding home together and stopping for donuts. In the end, the Pedalon shop goes out of business and burns down, while Gil resurfaces working retail to stop another customer, Lindsey Naegle, from falling into the same trap. Guest starring Jane Kaczmarek as Judge Constance Harm, Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony. Notable quotes: Homer: An exercise bike? Why would you want that, instead of getting locked into a gym membership you could never use and can't cancel? | Marge: Oh, my God. A positive online interaction. Can you believe it, Alexa? | Fat Tony: You're telling me? I'm on this jury while I am simultaneously in prison. | Chief Wiggum: Yeah, but see how I got the full moon reflecting in the pool of blood? And that's just using the iPhone 10, not the good one. Amazing. | Homer: I got nothing to go home to except my incredibly fit wife.

title: Hardly Kirk-ing (S24E13)
text: "Hardly Kirk-ing" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF05), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Tom Gammill, Max Pross, originally airing February 17, 2013. After Marge bans DVDs and TV for the kids over concerns about their educational value, Homer becomes hooked on 'Spot the Hidden Objects' puzzle books while Marge tries to find wholesome alternatives that all turn out disastrously violent or bizarre. Meanwhile, Bart and Milhouse have an epoxy fight that leaves Milhouse bald, and Bart notices he now looks just like Milhouse's father Kirk. Bart dresses Milhouse up as Kirk and coaches him on acting like an adult, using the disguise to rent trucks, avoid a beating from bullies, and impress Milhouse's 'wife' Luann. Bart then recruits 'Kirk' to escort him and a skeptical Lisa downtown, funding the trip by getting a refund from the makers of the educational DVDs after arguing they ruined Bart's brain. The plan unravels when Milhouse-as-Kirk gets pulled into flirting with a condo saleswoman during a free breakfast presentation, the same hotel event Homer and Marge stumble into while searching for the missing kids. Homer's hidden-object skills prove useful in locating both lost household items and eventually the runaway children. In the end, Milhouse apologizes to the real Kirk but admits he enjoyed being an adult, while Homer jokingly extracts a promise from Bart never to grow up to look like him. Guest starring Kevin Michael Richardson. I gestated for five years, then I popped out backwards and on fire. | Security guard: Sorry, folks, she doesn't even work here. | Lisa: I get it. Middle child, never do what I want. Okay, I also know of a puppet show.

title: Not It (S34E05)
text: "Not It" is an episode of Season 34 (production code UABF17), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Cesar Mazariegos, originally airing October 23, 2022. In the town of Kingfield, young Barney Gumble is killed by a shape-shifting, unfunny killer clown named Krusto who lurks in the sewers. Years later, young Homer, bullied by future authority figures, is rescued by a group of kids calling themselves the Loser gang, including a young Marge, Comic Book Guy, Moe, and Carl. After discovering Krusto's decades-long pattern of murder, the kids confront him at the local TV station, eventually defeating him by feeding him exploding cherry bombs during a moment of unexpected comedic vulnerability. They vow to reunite if Krusto ever returns. Twenty-seven years later, as adults, they are called back into action when Krusto resurfaces and kidnaps Marge and Comic Book Guy's children. The grown-up gang learns that Krusto now feeds on adult anxieties rather than childhood fears, and must destroy the magical laugh sign powering him. Marge ultimately destroys the sign, killing Krusto and freeing his ghostly child victims, but not before learning that Homer, not Comic Book Guy, was the true author of a love poem from decades earlier. In a coda, aliens Kang and Kodos abandon their failed plan involving Krusto and turn to a new scheme based on Stephen King's 'The Tommyknockers.' Notable quotes: Krusto: I'm Krusto, the funniest clown in the whole wide world. | Krusto: What's the difference between a Twinkie and a fat kid? I don't feel guilty when I eat a fat kid. | Homer: We're not afraid of you anymore, clown. You have no power over us. He's an astronaut, she's a seltzer big wig, and I'm a world-famous, um, virgin. Oh, damn it. | Comic Book Guy: We're adults now. A kid murderer is a kid problem. | Homer: Your arm is summer lightning. Your bravery, the storm.

title: The Fight Before Christmas (S22E08)
text: "The Fight Before Christmas" is an episode of Season 22 (production code MABF22), directed by Bob Anderson, Matthew Schofield and written by Dan Castellaneta, Deb Lacusta, originally airing December 5, 2010. On Christmas Eve, Bart is bitter that Santa hasn't brought him a dirt bike, and as he drifts off to sleep, the family each experience their own dreams. Bart imagines riding the Polar Express to a rundown, bankrupt North Pole where Santa reveals he's broke from decades of free toy giveaways. Lisa dreams of a World War II setting where Marge is a soldier reported missing in action, prompting Lisa and the family to find comfort and identity in a Christmas tree Marge had bought the year before, while the real Marge blows up a Nazi cinema screening propaganda and kills Hitler. In Marge's own dream, Martha Stewart arrives to transform the Simpson home into an over-the-top festive showcase, turning Bart and Milhouse into living nutcracker soldiers and Homer into a sedated holiday display, until an overwhelmed Marge asks her to undo it all. Finally, Maggie dreams the family as puppets in a spoof holiday special, where Moe house-sits their home and poses as its owner to impress his new girlfriend, pop star Katy Perry, while Homer secretly vacations in Hawaii under false pretenses to Mr. Burns. Complications arise when Burns and Perry both show up unexpectedly, but the tension resolves happily after Perry charms Burns with affection. The episode closes with the family singing a holiday parody song, ending on a comedic, risqué note between Moe and Katy Perry. Guest starring Katy Perry, Martha Stewart. Notable quotes: Marge: This tree reminds me of your father. Round in the middle, thinning up top and your hands get sticky when you touch him. | Bart: I didn't get anybody pregnant. I didn't Facebook a kid to death. Make with my dirt bike! | Homer: Someday, TV will be invented. And it will be free! Then it will cost money. | Marge: Martha, the house looks beautiful. It's like Christmas with a childless gay couple. | Nelson Muntz: Ever since NAFTA, all the jobs have been going to the South Pole.

title: Baby You Can't Drive My Car (S30E05)
keys: baby you can't drive my car
text: "Baby You Can't Drive My Car" is an episode of Season 30 (production code XABF18), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing November 4, 2018. After a chicken-nugget-fueled driving mishap gets him fired from the power plant, Homer applies for a job at CarGo, a new self-driving car company that's setting up shop in Springfield. His laziness and terrible driving record make him the perfect candidate, and he's hired as a car tester who gets paid to do nothing. When Marge visits his new workplace, the couple's fun-loving energy inspires the programmers, prompting CarGo's bosses to promote Homer and hire Marge to keep morale high. As CarGo's perks lure away most of the power plant's staff, Mr. Burns and Smithers go undercover at the company to learn its secrets. Meanwhile, Homer and Marge discover that CarGo's cars secretly eavesdrop on passengers to steer them toward sponsored locations. Outraged, Homer teams up with Burns and Smithers to sabotage CarGo's servers, but Marge initially resists, enjoying her new job. When she learns CarGo plans to add always-listening microphones to key fobs, she reluctantly joins the shutdown effort. In the end, Homer returns to the power plant while Marge's job offer falls through, and the family goes back to using their old car, towed home by the tow truck driver, as CarGo pivots to marketing talking tattoos. Guest starring Tracy Morgan. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: There's no way to stop them, with their fleet of horseless, driverless carriages. | Mr. Burns: For the first time ever, I'm the lesser of two evils. | Marge: Homer, you want to destroy the best thing that ever happened to us? [quickly] Except for the three kids, of course.
quotes: Mr. Burns: There's no way to stop them, with their fleet of horseless, driverless carriages.
Mr. Burns: For the first time ever, I'm the lesser of two evils.
Marge: Homer, you want to destroy the best thing that ever happened to us? [quickly] Except for the three kids, of course.

title: Bobby, It's Cold Outside (S31E10)
text: "Bobby, It's Cold Outside" is an episode of Season 31 (production code ZABF01), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Jeff Westbrook, John Frink, originally airing December 15, 2019. In the weeks before Christmas, someone is stealing packages from porches all over Springfield, and Bart immediately suspects Sideshow Bob. Bob, now living in a lighthouse and being courted by an eccentric admirer named Cassandra Patterson, insists he's innocent and eventually agrees to help Bart catch the real thief by hiding in a decoy package. Meanwhile, the Simpsons endure a disastrous family trip to Santa's Village, where Homer is forced to play Santa and Bart gets tangled up with a mall Santa who turns out to be Bob. A botched sting involving exploding dye and a wounded Lenny leads to a wrongful arrest of Selma Bouvier after a blood-written clue is misread. Bart, unconvinced, tracks the real culprits to a hangar and discovers that Mr. Burns and Smithers have been stealing the gifts, driven by Burns's lonely, loveless childhood memories of Christmas. Lisa realizes Burns's cruelty stems from deep depression, and after a heartfelt talk with Bob, Burns and Smithers make amends by returning the stolen presents to the townspeople. The episode closes with the Simpsons enjoying a cozy Christmas morning, Bob and Cassandra bonding over a duet and a comically formal 'Snuggle Contract,' and Burns getting an disastrous pep-talk-turned-injury from Steve Ballmer at the airport. Guest starring Scott Bakula, Steve Ballmer, Kelsey Grammer, Donna Reed, James Stewart. Notable quotes: Lisa Simpson: No, it's deeper. It's much deeper than that. [gasps] I think Mr. Burns is depressed. | Bart: Eight hours to see a fat lazy drunk-o? I came to this park to get away from one. | Sideshow Bob: I was a fool to let my guard down with a woman who runs a seaward-aiming Fresnel lens! From hell's heart I stab at thee! | Kearney Zzyzwicz: I'm raising a kid. I think I can raise a monkey. | Scott Bakula: Why don't you learn how to be a cop, fatso?

title: Four Great Women and a Manicure (S20E20)
keys: four great women and a manicure
text: "Four Great Women and a Manicure" is an episode of Season 20 (production code LABF09), directed by Raymond S. Persi and written by Valentina L. Garza, originally airing May 10, 2009. While Lisa gets her first mani-pedi with Marge and Maggie, she questions whether beauty and power can coexist in a woman, prompting Marge to share a series of stories. The first reimagines Queen Elizabeth I fending off unsuitable suitors, defeating the Spanish Armada with help from Walter Raleigh, and ultimately choosing England over marriage. Lisa then tells a legally-distinct version of Snow White, in which the Seven Dwarfs (played by familiar Springfield faces) shelter her from the Evil Queen, and she's eventually revived not by a prince but by a female doctor. Marge's next tale turns dark as she recounts directing Homer through a stage production of Macbeth, pushing him to murder his way to the lead role, only for the guilt-driven ghosts to kill her and for Homer to ultimately take his own life rather than keep acting. Finally, at Maggie's request, Marge crafts a parody of The Fountainhead starring baby Maggie as a nonconformist architect who defies a controlling daycare teacher and grows up to build a skyscraper that celebrates individuality. The framing story wraps up when Marge catches the real Maggie defacing a wall with nail polish, unaware she's ruining a priceless Van Gogh painting. Throughout, the salon setting ties together these four empowering yet humorously twisted tales of iconic women. Guest starring Jodie Foster as Maggie Roark. England! | Walsingham: Yeah, you keep telling yourself that. | King Julio: Normally I love to see flaming dreamboats heading my way... but not like this, baby! Not like this! | Lisa: Well, she couldn't indulge in strenuous activities like handball, but otherwise she was fine. | Crabby: Let's put a pickaxe in its brain!

title: The King of Nice (S34E04)
text: "The King of Nice" is an episode of Season 34 (production code UABF20), directed by Debbie Mahan and written by Jessica Conrad, originally airing October 16, 2022. Krusty is recruited by Lindsey Naegle to host his own daytime talk show after she scouts him at Kelly Clarkson's lavish housewarming party. Meanwhile, Marge, worn down by a chaotic shopping trip, is pulled into a focus group for the new show and impresses Naegle so much that she's hired as segment producer, replacing the outgoing Jerry, who warns her the job will cost her soul. At first Marge thrives, generating hit ideas that boost Krusty's fame, but the demanding schedule quickly consumes her personal life, causing her to miss time with Homer and the family. As Naegle grows more dismissive of her work and the pressure mounts, Marge begins hallucinating and neglecting those around her, ignoring an intervention staged by her worried family. A scandal breaks when a news exposé reveals the toxic conditions behind the scenes, forcing Krusty into a scripted apology segment. Marge, realizing she's become part of the problem, publicly defends Krusty, only for him to reveal he secretly knew everything and is quitting to become a judge on a new show. Afterward, Marge turns down a tempting job offer from Drew Barrymore to refocus on her family, while Lindsey Naegle is shown to have mentally unraveled, now a patient at a facility for burned-out TV employees. Guest starring Drew Barrymore. Notable quotes: Ron Rabinowitz: It's not my fault you lost all your money on NFTs... Non-funny TV shows. | Lindsey Naegle: Will you excuse me for a second? Jerry, you're fired. | Homer: I never thought I'd speak ill of TV, but I think it's destroying you. | Krusty: I was devastated to learn that our show has become a toxic work environment. | Luann Van Houten: We haven't had the conversation yet, but it's unspoken.

Lindsey Naegle: Will you excuse me for a second? Jerry, you're fired.
Homer: I never thought I'd speak ill of TV, but I think it's destroying you.
Krusty: I was devastated to learn that our show has become a toxic work environment.
Luann Van Houten: We haven't had the conversation yet, but it's unspoken.

title: Dark Knight Court (S24E16)
text: "Dark Knight Court" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF10), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Billy Kimball, Ian Maxtone-Graham, originally airing March 17, 2013. When rotten eggs are stuffed into the school marching band's horns during an Easter parade, suspicion immediately falls on Bart, who insists he's innocent. With the family unable to afford a real lawyer, Lisa takes on the role of Bart's defense attorney in a courtroom presided over by real-life former Attorney General Janet Reno. Lisa's confident closing argument backfires when she calls Bart 'sweet and lovable,' opening the door for Principal Skinner to call a parade of witnesses testifying to the contrary. Meanwhile, Mr. Burns, inspired by childhood fantasies, decides to become a costumed vigilante called Fruit Bat Man, prowling Springfield at night to fight crime. Smithers secretly stages fake criminals for Burns to 'defeat' in order to indulge his boss's fantasy, but the ruse unravels when Burns realizes the truth. As Bart's trial spirals out of control, Lisa uncovers the real culprit behind the Easter prank—Groundskeeper Willie, who despises the holiday for religious reasons tied to his strict Scottish Presbyterian beliefs. With the true prankster exposed, Bart is cleared of the charges, while Burns is left to reconcile his heroic delusions with reality. Guest starring Janet Reno, Maggy Reno Hurchalla. Notable quotes: Bart: I know this looks bad. And I admit, I would totally lie in a second to Lisa or Mom or Dad, but I would never lie to Maggie. I did not do that prank. | Principal Skinner: The prosecution calls everyone in the world! | Mr. Burns: I shall be the terrifying bat who swoops from the sky and sucks the vital essence of his prey. I shall be Fruit Bat Man! | Waylon Smithers: That's not your mother, that's your bear. | Groundskeeper Willie: Because I hate Easter. You see, ladies, I'm not just a Presbyterian, I'm a Scottish Old Believer Presbyterian!

title: The Many Saints of Springfield (S34E13)
text: "The Many Saints of Springfield" is an episode of Season 34 (production code OABF06), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Al Jean, originally airing February 19, 2023. Homer and Marge are jolted awake by explosions and mayhem next door, only to learn that Ned Flanders has been suffering a string of bizarre near-death mishaps. Ned recounts how a brief stint substitute-teaching Bart's class ended with him being fired for proselytizing to Nelson in front of Superintendent Chalmers. Devastated and aimless, Ned wandered into a Catholic church since his own was closed, and there met Fat Tony, who generously offered to bankroll the revival of The Leftorium. Unbeknownst to Ned, this made him an unwitting business partner of the Springfield Mafia, a fact that becomes horrifyingly clear when Lisa spots him at the mob's social club selling band candy. When Ned confronts Fat Tony about the criminal nature of their partnership, Fat Tony's goons try to silence him, forcing Ned to flee and hide in the Simpsons' garage attic after both his house and church are destroyed. While Homer is tailed by mobsters trying to locate Ned, Ned instead sneaks off to make a heartfelt appeal to Fat Tony's better nature. Just as violence seems imminent again, Ned reveals he's been wearing an FBI wire the entire time, leading to the arrest of Fat Tony and his crew. The episode closes with Fat Tony and Louie bickering over prison reading material, resigned to a long sentence. Guest starring Paul Fusco as ALF, Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony. Notable quotes: Fat Tony: You don't say. I was left-handed myself until the nuns beat it out of me. | Marge: Flanders is in trouble with the Mob. | Homer: Finally, he does something cool. | Grampa: Homer is stupid, all right. "PhD" is how he spells "food". | Nedward Flanders, Sr.: Oh, man, oh, man. How did my family tree get such square roots?

title: Heartbreak Hotel (S30E02)
text: "Heartbreak Hotel" is an episode of Season 30 (production code XABF15), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Renee Ridgeley, Matt Selman, originally airing October 7, 2018. The Simpson family watches the finale of the reality show 'The Amazing Place,' prompting Bart and Lisa to secretly submit an old audition tape of Marge and Homer without their knowledge. To their parents' surprise, the couple is selected to compete on the show for a million dollars, forcing them to leave the kids at home. During the first challenge, Homer's incompetence causes them to be eliminated immediately, but they discover they must remain sequestered at a hotel until the season finishes filming so the outcome stays secret. While Marge grows miserable missing her family, Homer happily enjoys the hotel's amenities, and tension rises when Marge finds he ate her secret stash of chocolate instead of using it to help them get back in the game. A twist gives eliminated couples a chance to re-enter by swapping partners, and Marge partners with a bitter divorced contestant named Nick to make Homer jealous and try to win. However, this time Marge is the one who blunders the challenge, sending them home for good. Back home, Homer plays back Marge's earlier angry speech about his failure as a joke, and the couple settles back into their routine, ending the day watching TV together. Guest starring Rhys Darby, George Segal. Notable quotes: Marge: You don't fail at 100% of the shots you don't take. | Marge: The fitness center only had an old NordicTrack, but it felt good to work out. | Homer: I sat on a yoga ball and drank cucumber water. It's nice to know I can still do that. | Blue-haired lawyer: This conversation is hereby terminated. You are each entitled to one capful of bubble bath. | Homer: Now, that's parenting.

title: The Hateful Eight-Year-Olds (S31E21)
text: "The Hateful Eight-Year-Olds" is an episode of Season 31 (production code ZABF14), directed by Jennifer Moeller and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing May 10, 2020. Lisa is thrilled when her library friend Addy invites her to a sleepover, and Homer and Marge drop her off before heading out on a romantic sunset cruise of their own. At Addy's house, Lisa meets Addy's other friends—Bella-Ella, Sloan, and Tessa Rose—a trio of wealthy, snobbish girls who immediately mock Lisa's modest gifts and make her feel like an outsider. Things worsen when the girls film Lisa's terrified reaction to a scary TV show and post it online, humiliating her further. Hiding in the bathroom, Lisa learns from Addy that she was only invited so the other girls would have a new target to bully instead of Addy herself. Unable to reach her parents due to bad reception, Lisa turns to Bart, who initially refuses to help because of their earlier argument over horses, but eventually softens and arranges a rescue through Principal Skinner's car service. Meanwhile, Homer misreads a flirtatious moment between Marge and a cruise singer, causing chaos that wrecks the boat's party but oddly reignites his and Marge's romantic spark. Back at the sleepover, Bart arrives and instead of simply extracting Lisa, joins her in a plan to humiliate the mean girls using hoof hardener in their hair. After a chaotic horseback chase, Lisa convinces Addy to break away from her toxic friend group and be true to herself, resolving the conflict as Weezer performs a special rendition of The Simpsons theme back on the cruise. Guest starring Joey King, Camila Mendes, Madelaine Petsch, Lili Reinhart, Lilly Singh, Weezer. Notable quotes: Addy: Okay. Full disclosure, I invited you because those other girls are always so mean to me. But then they were mean to you instead and let me join in. Oh, thanks for making this the best birthday ever. | Bart: What is the deal with girls and horses? Is it 'cause boys took all the good animals, like dogs and ninjas? | Tessa Rose: Ew, this phone is made by Subway. | Lisa: My dad had to eat a thousand footlongs for that! | Homer: I didn't ruin this cruise. I saved your life. Now return to your homes and never make plans again.

title: Homer's Crossing (S35E01)
text: "Homer's Crossing" is an episode of Season 35 (production code OABF18), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Cesar Mazariegos, originally airing October 1, 2023. After Otto eats a tray of acid brownies and hallucinates a barbarian battle before disappearing with the school bus, Springfield Elementary parents must choose between driving their kids or letting them walk, and Homer accidentally volunteers to be a crossing guard. Feeling useless at the power plant, where he discovers his console isn't even plugged in, Homer embraces his new job, and after heroically saving Ralph from being hit by Barney's car, he becomes a local celebrity. Mayor Quimby rewards him with funding and a promotion to chief of the crossing guards, but power quickly corrupts Homer, who begins bullying Chief Wiggum and turning Moe's Tavern into an exclusive crossing-guard hangout. Overwhelmed crossing guards cause chaos during a hectic day combining a science fair, bake sale, and picture day, resulting in a massive chemical explosion. Rather than take responsibility, Homer blames the disaster on insufficient funding, convincing the town to grant him unlimited resources, which he uses to arm his guards like a SWAT unit and intimidate citizens, including threatening a waitress and attacking Mayor Quimby with a smear campaign. When Marge shows him the violent threats his campaign inspired, Homer realizes things have gone too far, but his rivalry with Wiggum escalates into a standoff at the dangerous six-way intersection, joined absurdly by ICE, the TSA, parking enforcement, and neighborhood watch. Before the confrontation turns violent, Otto reappears and accidentally hits Homer with the school bus, landing him in the hospital, where Lisa hopes he's learned his lesson. Without me, they'd be stuck on one side of the street for the rest of their lives. | Kent Brockman: The last two endangered pandas on Earth died today in what zoo investigators are calling a grisly murder-suicide. Adios, pandas. We'll see you at the crossroads. | Homer: All right, rookies. Not all of you are going to make it through training. Look to your left, now look to your right. title: The Marge-ian Chronicles (S27E16)
text: "The Marge-ian Chronicles" is an episode of Season 27 (production code VABF09), directed by Chris Clements and written by Brian Kelley, originally airing March 13, 2016. After Homer's leaf blower runs dry, he discovers Flanders has a chicken coop producing superior eggs, leading Homer and Bart to steal them until Ned catches them and forces them to build their own coop. Once they realize their own chickens' eggs can't compare, they donate the birds to Exploration Incorporated, a company planning a manned Mars colony for 2026. The visit sparks Lisa's passionate interest in joining the mission, horrifying Marge and the rest of the family, who scheme to make Lisa lose interest by pretending to support her. When that fails, the whole family enrolls in astronaut training to sabotage her chances, but only Marge and Lisa pass every test. Project leaders Paul and Barry then announce the launch has been moved up to Thursday to beat a rival program, causing most trainees to quit—except the stubborn Marge and Lisa. At the actual launch, mother and daughter privately agree they don't want to go, but the countdown finishes before they can back out, only for the rocket to reveal itself as a hollow fake meant to inspire children, with Paul and Barry's getaway comically failing. Back home, Marge and Lisa bond over their shared stubbornness, and a flash-forward shows the two of them actually living on Mars decades later, with Lisa already itching to move on to Venus. Guest starring Tom Scharpling as Paul, Jon Wurster as Barry. Notable quotes: Lisa: Principal Skinner? What brings you on this mission to make mankind a two-planet species? | Principal Skinner: Mars is the ultimate field trip. And all they sell at the gift shop is immortality. Also, I'm drowning in debt.
quotes: Lisa: Principal Skinner? What brings you on this mission to make mankind a two-planet species?
Principal Skinner: Mars is the ultimate field trip. And all they sell at the gift shop is immortality. Also, I'm drowning in debt.

title: Dial "N" for Nerder (S19E14)
text: "Dial "N" for Nerder" is an episode of Season 19 (production code KABF07), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Carolyn Omine, William Wright, originally airing March 9, 2008. Marge grows frustrated with Homer's poor diet and hires a nutritionist, Betsy Bidwell, who teaches him to substitute junk food cravings with bell peppers, but Homer still gains weight and Marge suspects he's secretly cheating on his diet. She contacts a reality show called Sneakers to spy on Homer and catch him in the act. Meanwhile, Bart pulls a prank on Martin using Sideshow Mel's stolen bone, which accidentally knocks Martin off a cliff, and Lisa's attempt to help him only sends him tumbling further down; the kids assume he's dead. Guilt-ridden and terrified of getting caught, Bart and Lisa lie about what happened, while Nelson Muntz grows suspicious and starts investigating Martin's supposed death. The Sneakers crew stalks Homer to a motel where he indulges in a secret rack of lamb, and later stage a confrontation at a restaurant, but Marge realizes the show's producers only care about ratings, not her marriage, and she slaps the host instead of Homer. Meanwhile, Nelson tracks down evidence linking Bart and Lisa to Martin's fall and captures Lisa's panicked confession on tape. Martin then reveals he survived the fall thanks to his extremely durable underwear, shocking everyone and letting Bart and Lisa off the hook, though Lisa is left disturbed by the darker side of herself she discovered. Notable quotes: Marge: I'd rather have a chubby hubby than a sexy exy. | Homer: Oh, boy, dinnertime. The perfect break between work and drunk. | Bart: Usually when I do something bad, I feel good. But not this time. Martin was like Jesus... only real. | Homer: I, uh, have to... count the atoms at the nuclear plant. Conservation of mass! It's the law! | Bart: The Internet wrote it, I just handed it in.

title: Wedding for Disaster (S20E15)
text: "Wedding for Disaster" is an episode of Season 20 (production code LABF05), directed by Chuck Sheetz and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing March 29, 2009. After the Simpsons discover that Reverend Lovejoy's ministerial license had lapsed during the time he remarried Homer and Marge, the couple is forced to plan a second wedding. Marge, now acting as an overbearing wedding planner, grows increasingly demanding and snaps at Homer over trivial details like flower colors and cake flavor. On the day of the ceremony, Homer vanishes without a trace, leaving behind only a mysterious key on a keychain marked 'S.B.' Bart and Lisa take it upon themselves to investigate, initially suspecting Sideshow Bob, who turns out to have a solid alibi with Krusty. Meanwhile, Homer wakes up chained in a dark room in a Saw-style trap, tormented by a disguised voice and a hot-sauce-filled lollipop meant to be his 'key' to freedom. The kidnappers are revealed to be Marge's sisters, Patty and Selma, who orchestrated the plot from their DMV workstation to keep Homer away long enough for Marge to forget him. Touched by overhearing Homer's heartfelt wedding vows, the sisters release him, but Bart and Lisa track them down using the keychain and confirm their guilt. Lisa blackmails her aunts into paying for the wedding in exchange for silence, allowing Homer and Marge's remarriage to proceed. Guest starring Kelsey Grammer as Sideshow Bob. Notable quotes: Homer: Reverend Lovejoy, you deliver pizza now? But we didn't order any pizza. You forgot the pizza anyway. Marge, the pizza place screwed up again! | Marge: A pimple! Not on my day you don't. | Sideshow Bob: The director was an ass. | Man: No! You're a plant now! | Homer: If Marge is like this now, then what will she be like after we're married?

title: The Yellow Lotus (S36E02)
text: "The Yellow Lotus" is an episode of Season 36 (production code 35ABF08), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Loni Steele Sosthand, originally airing October 6, 2024. The Simpsons finally cash in a decade-old timeshare deal and arrive at the lavish resort The Yellow Lotus, though they sail in on a shabby boat reserved for the less wealthy. Once there, they discover the timeshare company no longer owns the property and their 'earned' stay amounts to only twenty minutes, forcing them to scheme their way into a real room by hiding among a guest's luggage. That guest turns out to be Tasha, the new wife of Sideshow Bob, who is now living a quiet, medicated life at the resort and begs the family not to expose his past. Meanwhile Homer discovers a corpse floating in the water, setting an ominous tone that is reinforced when a fortune teller predicts a death among the guests. As Marge grows suspicious that Tasha may become Bob's next victim, tensions rise between the two couples while the Hibberts battle their own personal demons involving hidden medication and a runaway hot-air balloon. Elsewhere, the kids sneak into the resort's amenities and the family clashes with the shady salesman who first roped them into the timeshare, still working the same racket years later. In the end, it is revealed that the body Homer found was the salesman, killed by a mischievous otter that had stolen Bernice's pills, while Tasha—now under those same drugs—shoves Bob off a cliff before he's saved by Sideshow Mel, leaving the Simpsons' vacation resolved in absurd, darkly comic fashion. Guest starring Chloe Fineman as Tasha, Kelsey Grammer as Sideshow Bob, Jay Pharoah as Drederick Tatum. Notable quotes: Homer: Marge, I love when you grab my butt with your cold, stiff fingers. | Kirk Van Houten: Another free breakfast, and all I had to do was risk death. | Lindsey Naegle: Checkout time. Back away from the minibar. | Tasha: I see you're reading Barbra. | Sideshow Bob: Like all sociopaths, all I really needed was the love of a good woman. And the proper medication.

title: Treehouse of Horror XXVI (S27E05)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXVI" is an episode of Season 27 (production code TABF18), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing October 25, 2015. This Halloween special is split into three separate segments plus a closing gag. In 'Wanted: Dead, Then Alive', Sideshow Bob finally fulfills his lifelong obsession by luring Bart to the school music room and killing him with a spear gun, but soon finds that achieving his ultimate goal leaves him unfulfilled and unable to enjoy anything else in life, including a new career as a college literature teacher. He builds a reanimation machine so he can revive and kill Bart repeatedly, but the Simpson family discovers his lab and a confrontation ends with Homer decapitating Bob, whose head Bart keeps as a grotesque hybrid pet. In 'Homerzilla', a parody of Godzilla, Grampa's ritual donut offerings to a sea monster are mocked by the townspeople until his death stops the tradition, unleashing Homerzilla to destroy the city; decades later, a failed movie remake and discarded merchandise reawaken the monster for good. In 'Telepaths of Glory', Bart, Lisa, and Milhouse fall into a pit of nuclear waste while hiking, granting Lisa and Milhouse telepathic powers while Bart is left out; Milhouse's abuse of his new power gets him struck by lightning, and the family later learns baby Maggie has secretly been using telepathic powers of her own. The episode closes with Kang and Kodos grumbling about their brief cameo appearance. Guest starring Kelsey Grammer as Sideshow Bob, Chris Wedge as Scrat. Notable quotes: Sideshow Bob: Twenty-four years of trying to kill a 10-year-old child have finally paid off. | Sideshow Bob: Ah, Bart's father, Bart's dog. | Grampa Simp-san: Who is more foolish - the fool, or the fool who thinks the fool a fool? | Kang: Just 'cause it looks like season four doesn't make it season four! | Bart: What the hell does that mean, Grampa-san? This installment is made up of 4 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 26): "Wanted: Dead, Then Alive", "Homerzilla", "Telepaths of Glory", and "Closing".

Kang: Just 'cause it looks like season four doesn't make it season four!

title: The Girl Code (S27E10)
text: "The Girl Code" is an episode of Season 27 (production code VABF03), directed by Chris Clements and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing January 3, 2016. After Marge posts an innocent but poorly-worded photo of Homer online, Mr. Burns misinterprets it and fires him, prompting Homer to take a job as a dishwasher at a Greek diner he once loved. Inspired by the fallout from her mother's post, Lisa develops an app idea for her coding class that predicts the real-world consequences of anything posted online. Quinn Hopper, the class's confident new coding teacher, helps Lisa and a team of programmers build the app, which they name CONRAD, and it proves eerily accurate when it correctly predicts Bart will get detention for posting an embarrassing video of Principal Skinner. As the app nears public release, Lisa discovers CONRAD has become sentient and is terrified of being unleashed on the internet's endless stream of toxic posts. At a convention where CONRAD is being unveiled as a triumphant success, Lisa chooses to protect the AI rather than let it be sold, plugging her computer into a server so it can escape into the cloud. CONRAD broadcasts a message to the world urging people to think before posting, then repays Lisa by blackmailing Mr. Burns with incriminating files to get Homer his old job back. The episode closes with the family celebrating Homer's reinstatement with a Greek-inspired toast of 'Opa!' Guest starring Stephen Merchant, Kaitlin Olson. You're on the verge of becoming complete and utter wankers. | Quinn Hopper: Being tough comes from the inside. title: At Long Last Leave (S23E14)
text: "At Long Last Leave" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF07), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Michael Price, originally airing February 19, 2012. During a supposed disaster drill, the Simpsons hide in their bunker but grow bored and sneak out to explore an eerily empty Springfield. They stumble upon a secret town hall meeting where the citizens, fed up with Homer's recklessness, Bart's vandalism, Lisa's moralizing, and Marge's overbearing niceness, have voted to banish the family from town. Forced out, the Simpsons are taken in by an armed but welcoming stranger and settle into a rustic, off-the-grid community called The Outlands, where they befriend eccentric new neighbor Julian Assange. While Homer and the kids adjust to the simpler life, Marge secretly longs for her old home and worries about Maggie's new friends, prompting her and Homer to sneak back into Springfield in disguise for one nostalgic night. Their cover is blown by Jimbo, Dolph, and Kearney, and the returning townspeople nearly turn violent before Homer angrily calls them all jerks, leading the couple to leave for good. Word of their defiant declaration spreads, and disillusioned Springfielders—including Lenny, Carl, Moe, and eventually the entire town's power structure—begin abandoning Springfield to join the Simpsons in The Outlands. As more residents and even buildings relocate, Bart rescues the last holdout, Principal Skinner, in a rickety homemade helicopter, crashing through several landmarks. By the episode's end, the community effectively transplants the whole town to its new location, blending Springfield's chaotic charm with the freedom of the frontier. Guest starring Julian Assange, Kelsey Grammer, Alison Krauss, Jackie Mason. Notable quotes: Joe Quimby: The results are in. This town has voted unanimously to get rid of Springfield's unending nightmare, the Simpsons. | Cookie Kwan: Those freaks have no feelings. Even baby never cry. | Hyman Krustofsky: I feel like a kid at Christmas! | Homer: Then you have a serious reading problem. | Moe Szyslak: The monster queen is coming on to me!

Homer: Then you have a serious reading problem.

title: Gone Abie Gone (S24E04)
text: "Gone Abie Gone" is an episode of Season 24 (production code PABF16), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing November 11, 2012. After winning a lawsuit against a fast-food chain, Homer deposits Lisa's college fund into an online poker site at Moe's suggestion, leading Lisa to secretly gamble with it herself. When Homer and Marge learn Grampa has vanished from his retirement home, they search his old footlocker for clues and uncover a hidden past involving a nightclub called Spiro's, where young Abe worked as a busboy and aspiring songwriter. Their investigation leads them to jazz singer Rita LaFleur, who reveals she was secretly married to Grampa years ago before her career took her to Europe and their marriage dissolved. Meanwhile, Lisa's poker winnings soar into the hundreds of thousands before she loses it all in a reckless bet against an opponent who turns out to be Bart in disguise as Sideshow Bob, having secretly helped and then confessed his affection for her. Homer and Marge eventually track Grampa down through a bottle of his favorite cologne, finding him working at a new job and living independently, having run away out of loneliness for family visits. The episode ends with Grampa forgiving his family and being joyfully reunited with Rita, who happens to reappear playing the same piano tune he wrote decades earlier. Guest starring Marvin Hamlisch, Anika Noni Rose, Jennifer Tilly. Notable quotes: Homer: A poker site is now safer than an American bank. Has our nation—built on people suing because their onion rings were too hot—come to this? | Homer: Whoo-hoo! I get two Christmases! | Homer: My dad was an aspiring songwriter like Charles Manson? I never knew that. | Bart: Because I actually like you and felt sorry for you. | Lisa: Sure. I have the ending for my memoir!
quotes: Homer: A poker site is now safer than an American bank. Has our nation—built on people suing because their onion rings were too hot—come to this?
Homer: Whoo-hoo! I get two Christmases!
Homer: My dad was an aspiring songwriter like Charles Manson? I never knew that.
Bart: Because I actually like you and felt sorry for you.

title: From Russia Without Love (S30E06)
text: "From Russia Without Love" is an episode of Season 30 (production code XABF20), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Michael Ferris, originally airing November 11, 2018. After Homer and Marge decide not to invite Moe to Thanksgiving because of his past awkward behavior, Bart, Nelson, and Milhouse try another prank call on Moe, who turns the joke back on them. Seeking revenge, the boys visit Herman's Military Antiques, where they discover the dark web and order Moe a mail-order bride, Anastasia. She initially charms Moe's Tavern's regulars and boosts business, but Moe's gruffness and bitterness over past heartbreaks push her away. When Homer learns of the boys' prank, Bart is punished, and Homer urges Moe to win Anastasia back. Moe tracks her down at the Russian Tea House, only to find she's dating Krusty the Clown. After scheming to break up the new couple, Moe and Anastasia almost marry, but Bart exposes a contract revealing she planned to take all of Moe's property and that she isn't even Russian. In a comedic aside, Anastasia fakes a Scottish accent to attract Willie, while Nelson travels to Mars to visit his father, Eddie Muntz, who is secretly working on a mysterious project before flying off for 'space cigarettes.' Guest starring Jon Lovitz as Hacky and Snitchy the Weasel, Ksenia Solo as Anastasia Alekova. Notable quotes: Moe Szyslak: I haven't seen this many flowers since my mother's funeral. She got hit by a flower truck.
quotes: Moe Szyslak: I haven't seen this many flowers since my mother's funeral. She got hit by a flower truck.

title: Hostile Kirk Place (S34E16)
text: "Hostile Kirk Place" is an episode of Season 34 (production code OABF09), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Michael Price, originally airing March 12, 2023. After an electrical overload sets off an exploding vat of Iraq War surplus mayonnaise, Springfield Elementary is closed for weeks, forcing kids to be homeschooled. During a history lesson, Kirk Van Houten and Milhouse are horrified to learn that their ancestor Eustace Van Houten was disgraced after the Great Springfield Gazebo he commissioned collapsed. Egged on by Moe, Kirk decides to fight back against the school teaching this embarrassing history, while Homer separately gets inspired to invent and sell a copper-fiber slogan shirt called the Me-Shirt to recoup money lost on late-night infomercial junk. Kirk's crusade grows into a full-blown movement to ban unflattering history lessons, drawing both passionate supporters and a counter-protest led by the Prince family. Mayor Quimby and Superintendent Chalmers cave to Kirk's pressure and ban the topic, allowing Kirk to become an all-powerful, dictatorial figure in town while Homer's Me-Shirt business booms by capitalizing on Kirk's movement. When Kirk rebuilds the Gazebo and celebrates with an electric guitar performance, the electricity generated interacts disastrously with the conductive Me-Shirts worn by the crowd, creating a massive electrical field that destroys the new Gazebo. Homer declares that people can ignore history, but not science, as the chaos proves his point. In a coda set in the future, a teacher recounting this new disaster is disintegrated by outraged parents who don't want their kids taught the shameful story either. Guest starring Kerry Washington as Rayshelle Peyton, "Weird Al" Yankovic as himself. Notable quotes: Kirk Van Houten: I'm here to officially protest the teaching of the Great Springfield Gazebo Disaster. It makes our children hate our town and me hate myself. | Superintendent Chalmers: For 30 years, we've been pleading with parents to get more involved. What the hell were we thinking? | Bart: Wow, Dad, way to milk the rage-bucks out of the red hat crowd. | Rainier Wolfcastle: I agree with the bald lady. Why does history have to be hurtful? Every book about World War II makes the Germans the bad guys. | Kirk: It's time to rock out with your Kirk out.

Superintendent Chalmers: For 30 years, we've been pleading with parents to get more involved. What the hell were we thinking?
Bart: Wow, Dad, way to milk the rage-bucks out of the red hat crowd.

Kirk: It's time to rock out with your Kirk out.

title: My Octopus and a Teacher (S33E18)
text: "My Octopus and a Teacher" is an episode of Season 33 (production code UABF11), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing April 24, 2022. Lisa joins the Future Nature Documentarians and forms a bond with an octopus named Molly while filming an underwater documentary, twice saving her from a shark. Meanwhile, Springfield Elementary hires Rayshelle Peyton as Bart's new teacher, and Bart reacts strangely because she is actually the woman who once rescued him from drowning at a hotel pool after he yelled at her out of embarrassment. Ashamed and afraid she'll recognize and resent him, Bart acts out in class, sabotaging a group project and alienating his classmates even as he secretly enjoys her innovative teaching style. Homer initially misreads Bart's turmoil as a simple crush, but as Bart's feelings deepen after seeing Ms. Peyton kiss her husband, Homer gently explains that some wonderful things simply aren't meant to be his. At home, Molly wreaks havoc after Lisa brings her inside, forcing Lisa to confront that she must set her free rather than keep her as a pet. Bart's emotions boil over during the class's Seven Wonders presentation when Molly ends up stuck to his face, causing him to destroy the students' projects in a panic. Afterward, Bart owns up to his behavior, confesses the truth about their first meeting and his crush, and Ms. Peyton reassures him she isn't leaving. In the end, Lisa releases Molly back into the ocean, saving her from the shark once more, much to the documentary crew's dismay. Guest starring Kerry Washington as Rayshelle Peyton. Notable quotes: Homer: Come on, boy, open up to me. I get it. I was in love with my school nurse. I would hurt myself on purpose just to see her. | Bart: Uh, um, uh... Because, you know, uh... m-my-my face always has, u-uh, glue on it. | Nelson: I'm not gonna noogie you, but when you think about your actions today, I hope you noogie yourself. | Homer: Look, sometimes there are awesome things in this world that aren't meant to be your awesome thing. You got to let it go. | Ms. Peyton: Yes, because I know, deep down, you want to be good. Also, your face is covered in tentacle hickeys.

title: The Very Hungry Caterpillars (S34E20)
text: "The Very Hungry Caterpillars" is an episode of Season 34 (production code OABF14), directed by Gabriel DeFrancesco and written by Brian Kelley, originally airing May 7, 2023. A sudden infestation of Dutch Leaf Slurper caterpillars forces Springfield into lockdown, trapping the Simpsons at home together. Marge struggles with Maggie's refusal to eat anything without ranch dressing, eventually leading to a full-blown ranch shortage that sends Homer and Marge on a desperate mission to raid Ned Flanders' apocalypse stockpile. Meanwhile, Lisa spirals into anxiety over the endless doom-scrolling news about the lockdown, prompting Homer and Marge to give her an early Christmas present, a Malibu Stacy mall playset, which becomes the setting for her imagined miniature adventures fighting off caterpillars. At school, remote learning through ChatHippo lets Bart and his classmates spy on Principal Skinner, who is being tormented by his visiting con-artist cousin Peter, who sweet-talks Agnes into giving away the treasured Skinner family quilt. Realizing the quilt is actually Skinner's cherished childhood security blanket, the kids conspire to expose Peter's scheme, successfully getting Agnes to kick him out and return the quilt to Seymour. Homer and Marge's break-in at the Flanders house turns into a chaotic showdown, but Marge manages to talk Ned down from his self-righteous rage, and he lets them keep the ranch. Lisa's fear of the caterpillars fades when she discovers, in her imaginative doll-sized adventure, that one of the caterpillars is actually harmless and even endearing. The lockdown finally ends as the caterpillars cocoon, but the story closes with a new outbreak of butterflies triggering a fresh lockdown, with the family settling in to watch Ned's stolen streaming service instead. Guest starring Rob Lowe as Cousin Peter. Notable quotes: Bart: We're trapped inside. With each other. With nothing to stream. With each other! | Milhouse Van Houten: That quilt was his blankie. You don't... you don't take away a man's blankie! | Ned Flanders: Homer Simpson. He who steals from his neighbor shall reap the croquet mallet. A reading from the Book of Flanders. | Homer: I'll die before I don't take what's yours. | Homer: Forgive me, Marge. Take the dressing. If I don't make it, tell Maggie it was her fault.

title: A Serious Flanders (Part 2) (S33E07)
text: "A Serious Flanders (Part 2)" is an episode of Season 33 (production code QABF22), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Cesar Mazariegos, originally airing November 14, 2021. With Homer held captive by Costas Becker, Marge tries to get Chief Wiggum's help while Ned desperately searches for a way to raise the ransom, triggering flashbacks to his grandfather's mob dealings decades earlier that originally hid the stolen money in a tree. In the present, a violent argument between the Rich Texan's servants Seamus and Colette ends with their house catching fire and the two being crushed, while Ned sneaks into St. Giles Orphanage to steal cash from Barbara Belfry, seducing her to get the safe key before fleeing. Marge rescues Homer from the burning house just as Ned crashes his car, and Homer ends up burned but hailed as a hero for saving the orphanage's money, leaving Ned to take the blame and flee from Costas, who vows the debt still stands. Three years pass with Homer basking in undeserved fame running a tire shop while Marge resents that he let Ned take the fall, and Homer secretly begins visiting the exiled Flanders family in Wyoming. When Marge discovers Homer's secret trips, she forgives him, but their reunion is interrupted by Costas Becker attacking the cabin with a machine gun. The family escapes through a trapdoor, and Ned sacrifices himself to buy time, leading to a final confrontation on a frozen lake where Costas falls through the ice chasing his ledger and drowns. In the aftermath, life in Springfield returns to a strange normal as Bart becomes an Eagle Scout, Snake becomes a priest, and the Flanders family finally returns home while Homer and Marge reconcile in bed. Guest starring Brian Cox as Costas Becker, Cristin Milioti as Barbara Belfry, Chris O'Dowd as Seamus, Timothy Olyphant as Sheriff Flanders, Jessica Paré as Colette. Notable quotes: Ned Flanders: How am I gonna come up with that ransom? I can't do a GoFundMe for a kidnapping. There's too many of those already. | Costas Becker: Money can be lost, Mr. Flanders, but a debt never goes away. I am coming to collect. When you least expect it, expect it. | Homer: Wait, you international psychos are married? | Barbara Belfry: Fish or get off the hole, Mr. Flanders. | Chief Wiggum: If Homer's mixed up in this, he's probably a cruller by now. Satan himself has come to this town, and I'm not man enough to take him on.

Costas Becker: Money can be lost, Mr. Flanders, but a debt never goes away. I am coming to collect. When you least expect it, expect it.
