Chief Wiggum: If Homer's mixed up in this, he's probably a cruller by now. Satan himself has come to this town, and I'm not man enough to take him on.

title: The Spy Who Learned Me (S23E20)
text: "The Spy Who Learned Me" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF13), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Marc Wilmore, originally airing May 6, 2012. Homer and Marge's marriage is strained after Homer embarrasses her by loudly narrating a spy movie in the theater. At work, a freak accident with Mr. Burns' mini car gives Homer a concussion and eight weeks of paid leave, which he hides from his still-angry family, sneaking off each day as if going to work. While drinking at Moe's, Homer is visited by a hallucinated version of the suave movie spy Stradivarius Cain, who coaches him on how to become a better husband, including how to flirt and how to handle dangerous situations with charm rather than panic. Meanwhile, at school, Bart devises a scheme to stop Nelson from stealing lunch money by feeding him free Krusty Burgers until he becomes too overweight and lazy to bully anyone, inspired by a documentary about fast food's effects on the body. The plan works almost too well, drawing local news attention to childhood obesity and prompting Lisa to intervene by getting Nelson a personal trainer. When Marge discovers Homer has been missing from work for weeks, he finally confesses the truth about his concussion and his fear of disappointing her, and she forgives him. Using what he's learned from his fictional spy mentor, Homer talks down an enraged boyfriend threatening him at a nightclub, cementing his growth as a husband. In the end, Nelson returns to bullying, now bigger and stronger than before, leaving Bart's plan backfired but Lisa unexpectedly charmed by the new-and-improved bully. Guest starring Bryan Cranston as Stradivarius Cain, Eric Idle as Declan Desmond. Notable quotes: Homer: He turned that Russian guy into Swiss cheese! | Marge: Homer! People are here to see the movie, not listen to you! | Nelson Muntz: Hey Simpson. Let me save you the trouble of putting that money back in your pocket. Haw-haw! | Milhouse Van Houten: My mom says bullies only bully 'cause they're scared. | Lisa: Well, he's tough on nerds, but easy on the eyes.

Marge: Homer! People are here to see the movie, not listen to you!
Nelson Muntz: Hey Simpson. Let me save you the trouble of putting that money back in your pocket. Haw-haw!

title: Girl's in the Band (S30E19)
text: "Girl's in the Band" is an episode of Season 30 (production code YABF11), directed by Jennifer Moeller and written by Nancy Cartwright, originally airing March 31, 2019. Springfield's music teacher Dewey Largo is haunted by nightmares of his own unfulfilled potential as a conductor, and things get worse when Victor Kleskow, the intense director of the Capital City Philharmonic, comes to scout talent at the school concert. Victor bypasses Largo and instead recruits Lisa, setting off a chain of events that strains the Simpson family financially and emotionally. Homer and Marge scramble to pay for Lisa's advanced training, with Homer even considering selling his prized Breaking Bad box set before taking on an exhausting night shift at the plant. In Capital City, Lisa discovers Victor's brutal, high-pressure teaching methods and the toll they take on the other young musicians, while Bart is stuck babysitting other kids in a cramped closet. As Lisa competes for first chair and impresses Victor, she starts to realize her ambitions are hurting her family, especially as Homer begins hallucinating from overwork and exhaustion. When Victor offers to advance her to an even pricier, farther-away program, Lisa decides to sacrifice her dream by deliberately failing her audition to protect her family's stability. Meanwhile, Homer dismisses signs of Maggie's own musical talent to avoid further financial strain. The episode closes with Largo reconciling with his partner after a spat, finally settling on a name for their dog. Guest starring Dave Matthews as Lloyd, J. K. Simmons as Victor Kleskow. Notable quotes: Dewey Largo: Our recital's tomorrow, and we're gonna be ready. And if you play the way I know you're capable of, you'll never see me again. | Dewey Largo: Oh, Salieri, patron saint of losers, runners-up and also-rans, please let this Garfunkel become a Simon, this Pepsi become a Coke, and this ugly duckling conduct Swan Lake. | Victor Kleskow: Hi. Victor Kleskow. We're conductors, so don't shake hands. Just a friendly wave on the beat of four, three, two and done. | Victor Kleskow: That was good... middle school good. Tonight, I witnessed a once-in-a-semester talent that I must add to my organization. | Dewey Largo: Well, then, wear it on your head. Here we go. I'm gonna do something I've never done as a teacher before: actually try.

title: A Midsummer's Nice Dreams (S22E16)
text: "A Midsummer's Nice Dreams" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF09), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Dan Castellaneta, Deb Lacusta, originally airing March 13, 2011. Cheech Marin and Tommy Chong come to Springfield for a reunion tour, but Chong balks at performing one of their old routines, throwing the show into jeopardy. Homer eagerly volunteers to take Chong's place, rebranding the act as 'Cheech and Chunk' and hitting the road with Cheech. Meanwhile, a disgruntled Chong doesn't give up performing and instead recruits Principal Skinner to be his new comedy partner, forming the awkward duo 'Teach and Chong.' At home, Marge takes pity on the notoriously unkempt Crazy Cat Lady and tries to help her declutter her home and break her hoarding habits. The effort backfires when Marge herself becomes obsessed with collecting and saving junk, turning into a hoarder in her own right. As Homer's touring life with Cheech pulls him away from the family, tensions rise until the various comedic partnerships and personal struggles resolve themselves. By the episode's end, Homer returns home to Marge, Cheech is reunited with Chong, and Marge manages to shake off her hoarding tendencies. Guest starring Tommy Chong, Cheech Marin. Notable quotes: Tommy Chong: And what is rain, man? It's like we're in the apartment under God and his fat sister overflowed the tub. | Krusty: When they asked me to introduce Cheech and Chong, I said, "How much?" And they said, "We don't pay for introductions," so I said, "Then I don't need this crummy gig." And they said, "Yes, you do," and I said... "Ladies and gentlemen, Cheech and Chong!" | Homer: How about Don Johnson? | Cheech Marin: It would be easier to meet Dave. | Tommy Chong: Wow. You are the un-funniest man I've ever seen. Which means, teaming up with you would be totally pushing the envelope.

Cheech Marin: It would be easier to meet Dave.
Tommy Chong: Wow. You are the un-funniest man I've ever seen. Which means, teaming up with you would be totally pushing the envelope.

title: Monty Burns' Fleeing Circus (S28E01)
text: "Monty Burns' Fleeing Circus" is an episode of Season 28 (production code VABF20), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Tom Gammill, Max Pross, originally airing September 25, 2016. After the iconic Lard Lad statue mysteriously vanishes, Springfield panics until the donut company unveils a shiny new metallic replacement. The new statue's reflective surface accidentally creates a deadly light beam that burns much of the town to the ground, and despite Mayor Quimby's promises, six months pass with no progress on rebuilding. Desperate, the Simpsons approach Mr. Burns for funding, and he agrees—on the condition that he gets to stage his own variety show at the Springfield Bowl. As Burns auditions townsfolk, he is haunted by traumatic childhood memories of humiliating himself at a pageant in front of his cold, unsupportive mother. Lisa becomes his assistant and, after learning the full story behind his fear of public ridicule, convinces him to go through with the show despite his doubts. Meanwhile, Homer neglects his safety inspector duties at the power plant, which the staff have turned into a makeshift resort, leading to a fire and an unplanned fireworks display. The variety show ultimately ends in disaster when Burns's pants catch fire on stage, causing the audience to laugh and flee, and he unfairly blames Lisa before abandoning her to play saxophone to an empty venue. The episode closes with the destroyed metallic Lard Lad statue being dumped at the tire yard, revealing Ralph trapped underneath as he delivers a classic cartoon sign-off. Guest starring Amy Schumer as Mrs. Burns, Pendleton Ward as "Simpsons Time" singer. Notable quotes: Kent Brockman: Springfield has risen from the ashes like a phoenix. That's phoenix the mythical bird, and not Phoenix the cultureless Mars-scape of the Southwest. | Marge: What a beautiful day for a family stroll! | Apu: Tell that to my aching back! | Homer: Ooh, rebranding! | Lisa: That just means admitting failure, Dad.

title: Step Brother from the Same Planet (S34E08)
keys: step brother from the same planet
text: "Step Brother from the Same Planet" is an episode of Season 34 (production code UABF22), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Dan Vebber, originally airing November 20, 2022. At an Art in the Park event, Homer discovers that his father has a man bun, a new girlfriend named Blythe, and plans to move in with her, leaving Homer jealous and unsettled. When he meets Blythe's quirky taxidermy-obsessed son Calvin, Homer grows increasingly resentful as Grampa dotes on the boy far more warmly than he ever treated Homer. After an allergic reaction to Marge's furniture polish forces Homer out of the house, he ends up bunking with Calvin at Blythe's home, sparking a bitter prank war between the two. Meanwhile, Bart and Lisa exploit Grampa's paid-up Retirement Castle room to throw an increasingly wild slumber party in hopes of making Lisa popular, until the chaos draws police attention and Lisa fakes her own arrest to preserve her new social status. As Homer's jealousy boils over, Calvin helps him see that his real issue is with wanting Grampa's affection, leading Homer to create a symbolic taxidermy entry representing his strained relationship with his father. Grampa finally recognizes how he's been neglecting Homer emotionally and apologizes, mending their bond. In the end, Blythe leaves Grampa for a wealthier, more spiritually compatible man who takes Calvin to Africa, and though Grampa tries to reconnect with Homer by phone, Homer dismisses the call as an accidental butt-dial. title: A Father's Watch (S28E18)
text: "A Father's Watch" is an episode of Season 28 (production code WABF11), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Simon Rich, originally airing March 19, 2017. Worried about Bart's poor grades and lack of self-esteem, Marge seeks advice from an online parenting expert who advocates giving children trophies for everything they do, no matter how small. Springfield's parents embrace the trend, and Homer, seeing a business opportunity, starts selling trophies out of the garage after Lisa unwittingly inspires him. When Bart overhears Homer say he'll always be a screw-up, he wanders to the Retirement Castle, where Grampa comforts him with a family story and gives him a treasured old pocket watch. Newly confident, Bart flaunts the watch until its chain breaks and it falls off a mountain, sending him and Milhouse on a frantic search. Meanwhile, Lisa organizes a counter-movement with a new expert, Dr. Fenton Pooltoy, whose G.R.I.T. philosophy turns Springfield against participation trophies, leaving Homer stuck with unsold inventory. Homer eventually recovers the lost watch from a pawn shop after Milhouse pawned it out of anger, but instead of gloating, he comforts a distraught Bart by admitting his own shortcomings stem from generations of Simpson fathers. Bart and Grampa reconcile and pose for a magazine photo with the watch, only for it to break again, prompting Grampa to comically strangle him. The episode closes with Lisa and Homer watching Ralph get picked first in the NBA draft. Guest starring Vanessa Bayer, Brian Posehn, Rob Riggle, Adam Silver. Notable quotes: Homer: It's the craziest thing — she will not give up on that kid. | Homer: Next you'll be telling me that this whole trophy business—and, in fact, all of my get-rich quick schemes over the years—are born of a desperate need for approval from a father who couldn't show love, likely because of his traumatic relationship with his own father, and his before him, and so on. But unfortunately, Dr. Freud, that couldn't be further from the truth... Doctor. | Luann Van Houten: Trophies. So that's the easy answer. | Chief Wiggum: If Ralphie's shelf says he's a winner, then he'll be one! | Moe: And Moe yells a third thing to feel part of the group!

title: The Ned-liest Catch (S22E22)
text: "The Ned-liest Catch" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF15), directed by Chuck Sheetz and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing May 22, 2011. After a chaotic pep rally celebrating a rare basketball win, Bart's antics push Mrs. Krabappel to slap him publicly, leading to her suspension pending a disciplinary hearing. Wracked with guilt, Bart sneaks into the holding area to help Edna escape, but she nearly falls from a ladder during the getaway and is saved by a passing Ned Flanders. The rescue sparks an unexpected romance between Ned and Edna, much to Bart's dismay since his teacher now frequently visits next door. Emboldened by Edna, Ned finally demands Homer return his long-borrowed belongings, clearing out the Simpsons' garage. Homer, initially annoyed, decides he actually wants Ned to be happy, but inadvertently causes trouble by getting the guys at Moe's talking about their past flings with Edna. Ned becomes increasingly unsettled learning about her romantic history, including with Homer, and flees when he starts seeing visions of her exes on her face. Homer talks him into reconciling, and Edna agrees to continue the relationship only if her past stays out of it going forward. The episode ends on a cliffhanger, breaking the fourth wall as Homer and Marge ask viewers to vote on the couple's fate. Guest starring Ken Burns as himself, Joey Kramer as himself. title: Pin Gal (S34E17)
text: "Pin Gal" is an episode of Season 34 (production code OABF10), directed by Chris Clements and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing March 19, 2023. When Homer learns that Barney's Bowlarama is being sold to Terrence, a hipster who plans to shut down the lanes, he and the Pin Pals scramble to save it, negotiating a week to prove bowling still has fans. Struggling to boost turnout, Homer discovers that his wife Marge is secretly a skilled bowler, and Terrence offers to keep the alley open if she can defeat an opponent of his choosing. Marge's old flame and former bowling coach Jacques resurfaces, and Homer brings him in to train her, unaware of their romantic past. As Jacques flirts and reminisces about a near-kiss years earlier, Grampa grows suspicious and uncovers a trail of Facebook photos showing Jacques romancing many of his female students. Enraged, Homer confronts Jacques at his shrine-like apartment full of Marge photos, leading to a fight before Marge arrives to clarify that nothing ever happened between them. On the day of the big match, Marge faces off against Jacques himself and narrowly wins by a single point, saving the bowling alley. Jacques is then arrested for overstaying his bowling visa and deported to Paris, while Terrence agrees to preserve one lane with a long waiting list. Homer is reassured of Marge's love for him, much to the amusement of the cheering crowd. Guest starring Albert Brooks as Jacques, Fred Armisen as Terrence. Notable quotes: Grampa: We did to that ball what we did to Hitler's bombs... got out of the way. | Homer: Oh, my God. Oh, my God! What the... I don't know what shocks me more... these photos or that you know how to use Facebook. | Lenny Leonard: Hey, pal, if you don't like bowling, you don't like me. | Homer: I'll have you know this place is endorsed by a group that's popular with today's kids: ZZ Top. | Carl Carlson: Eh. Still the most exciting bowling match I've ever seen.

title: Black-Eyed, Please (S24E15)
text: "Black-Eyed, Please" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF09), directed by Matthew Schofield and written by John Frink, originally airing March 10, 2013. Homer starts spending time with Ned Flanders' laid-back parents, and Ned becomes jealous when he realizes they prefer Homer's easygoing company to his own uptight nature. The tension boils over when Ned punches Homer in the eye, injuring him and requiring a doctor's visit, and Ned is consumed by guilt over losing his temper. He desperately tries to make amends with Homer, going so far as to offer to pray at his bedside, leading to a comedic clash over what counts as an acceptable deity to pray to. Meanwhile, at school, Lisa gets a strict substitute teacher, Ms. Cantwell, who inexplicably takes a dislike to her and begins bullying her in class. Lisa is baffled and hurt, unable to understand why the teacher is targeting her despite her good behavior. When Lisa finally confronts Ms. Cantwell about why she dislikes her, the teacher reveals it's simply personal jealousy over Lisa's looks and popularity with boys. Lisa is oddly comforted by this explanation, reframing the bullying as proof of her own prettiness. Meanwhile, Ned's guilt-driven quest for reconciliation with Homer plays out in a series of awkward, faith-based exchanges that highlight their theological differences. Guest starring Richard Dawkins as himself, Tina Fey as Ms. Cantwell. Notable quotes: Lisa: But I am playing. I'm hop-scotching from paragraph to paragraph, climbing the monkey bars of plot and theme. | Homer: I didn't know you were left-handed. | Dr. Hibbert: Homer, you'll need to wear this eye patch for a couple weeks. And, uh, you may never see a film in 3-D again. | Homer: But the storytelling is finally catching up to the technology. | Lisa: She hates me because I'm pretty! Woo hoo!

title: The Nightmare After Krustmas (S28E10)
text: "The Nightmare After Krustmas" is an episode of Season 28 (production code WABF02), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing December 11, 2016. As church attendance dwindles, Reverend Lovejoy is pressured by his superiors to bring in new converts, setting him on a quest that eventually leads him to Moe's Tavern and an unlikely target: Krusty the Clown. Krusty, meanwhile, is trying to reconnect with his estranged daughter Sophie during a visit that coincides with a chaotic pagan winter festival, where Theo Jansen's wind-powered Strandbeest runs amok and injures him. The Simpsons invite Krusty and Sophie to spend Christmas with them, but Krusty's self-promoting antics keep alienating his devout daughter. At home, Maggie becomes terrified of a creepy new toy called Gnome in Your Home, which springs to life in a nightmare where she travels to the North Pole and is nearly devoured by the monstrous gnome. Krusty, moved after a strange vision involving a tased Snake resembling Jesus, agrees to convert to Christianity, delighting Sophie and reviving Lovejoy's congregation. During his baptism, Krusty falls through breaking ice and has a near-death hallucination of his father, Rabbi Krustofsky, who questions whether changing religion truly makes him a better father. Lovejoy heroically pulls Krusty from the icy water, becoming a local celebrity and reinvigorating the church's popularity. In the end, Maggie destroys the frightening gnome toys, finally sleeping peacefully, while in heaven various deities bicker over whether Krusty's icy dunking actually counts as a valid baptism. Guest starring Wayne Gretzky, Theo Jansen, Natasha Lyonne, Jackie Mason. Notable quotes: Reverend Lovejoy: Even Milhouse could have made that shot. | Apu: Our nonsense is so much better than your nonsense. Look at this guy, he could be a Pixar hero! | Bart: If he was going to convert why didn't he pick a funny religion? | Milhouse Van Houten: Like Zoroastrianism. Their top god is named Mazda. Tell me that's not hilarious.

title: Treehouse of Horror XXVII (S28E04)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXVII" is an episode of Season 28 (production code VABF16), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing October 16, 2016. This Halloween special opens with the family ambushed at a Christmas tree lot by Sideshow Bob, Kang, a leprechaun, and the vengeful ghost of Frank Grimes, only for Maggie to decapitate them all before a virtual-reality couch gag plays. In 'Dry Hard,' a severe drought has left Springfield desperate for water, prompting Mr. Burns to force the town's children into a lethal gladiatorial contest for access to his private reservoir; Lisa, guided by her coach Homish, ultimately convinces the surviving kids to rebel against Burns, but the reservoir's destruction floods the town and triggers a sudden ice age. In 'BFF R.I.P.,' Lisa's forgotten imaginary friend Rachel returns as a jealous killer, murdering Lisa's friends and classmates one by one and framing Lisa for the crimes; after escaping police custody with Bart's help, Lisa realizes Rachel only exists in her mind and manages to banish her before she can kill Marge and the rest of the family. In 'Moefinger,' Bart discovers that Moe and the bar patrons are secret agents who recruit him to replace the supposedly deceased Homer, only to learn that Homer is actually the villainous mastermind Remoh, plotting to melt the world with a lava machine and steal all the Duff Beer; Bart defeats Remoh's henchmen and kills Homer, closing the segment and the episode with a musical celebration of the show's 600th episode milestone. Guest starring Drew Carey, Donald Fagen, Kelsey Grammer, Sarah Silverman. Notable quotes: Frank Grimes: I'm the guy who hated you. Hated you! Died from my hatred of you!! | Sideshow Bob: To the point, we are evil geniuses who, somehow, lost every battle we've had with Homer Simpson. | Frank Grimes: Will nobody stop these people? | Bart: Violence never solved anything. | Carl Carlson: I cancelled a few Czechs. This installment is made up of 4 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 27): "Opening scene", "Dry Hard", "BFF R.I.P.", and "Moefinger".

title: Bart Gets a "Z" (S21E02)
text: "Bart Gets a "Z"" is an episode of Season 21 (production code LABF15), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Matt Selman, originally airing October 4, 2009. After Mrs. Krabappel confiscates the students' cellphones, Bart and his classmates decide to spike her coffee with alcohol, having noticed how much fun a drunk Homer can be. The plan backfires when Krabappel makes a drunken scene at school and gets fired by Principal Skinner. Wracked with guilt, Bart uses a self-help book called 'The Answer' to help Edna start a new business, and together they open a muffin shop called Edna's Edibles. Just as she seems to be settling into her new life, Bart confesses that he was responsible for her getting fired, and a furious Krabappel storms off. Meanwhile, at school, the charismatic new teacher Zachary Vaughn wins over the entire class except Bart, who secretly misses Mrs. Krabappel. Bart considers spiking Zachary's drink too, but changes his mind and decides to confess to Skinner instead. Before he can finish, Zachary is heard drunkenly ranting in the hallway, revealing that he has a habit of spiking his own drinks, clearing Bart of blame. With Zachary removed from the school, Mrs. Krabappel returns to teaching, taking petty revenge on her students by serving them stale muffins from her shop. title: Full Heart, Empty Pool (S36E17)
text: "Full Heart, Empty Pool" is an episode of Season 36 (production code 36ABF10), directed by Chris Clements and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing May 11, 2025. After destroying his backyard with a rented backhoe while trying to build a pool, Homer sues Builder's Barn and wins a settlement, but spends the money on pool equipment despite having no actual pool. Flush with a new Wiccapedia page, Homer becomes obsessed with building a lasting legacy, and is disappointed to learn Springfield has honored countless other people but never him. While moping around the empty pool hole, he and Grampa invent a new sport called Noodleball, which quickly becomes a citywide sensation as families dig similar holes in their own yards. The craze causes chaos as people fight over pools for competing uses, prompting shady promoter Gabriel Razelton to step in and offer to build a professional Noodleball stadium. Razelton convinces Homer to cut Grampa out of the business because he's too old, and Homer reluctantly agrees, betraying his father to chase fame. Marge and Lisa grow suspicious, with Lisa discovering that Razelton's company is using Noodleball's popularity to cover up unrelated scandals. Grampa teaches Homer that legacies are meaningless since you won't be around to enjoy them, and Homer decides to make amends by teaming with Grampa again to challenge the top Noodleball team. The comeback ends badly when Homer breaks his hip and Grampa suffers a heart attack, effectively ending Noodleball for good, but Homer takes solace in seeing the Squeaky-Voiced Teen finally get the girl and his voice deepen at last. Guest starring Blake Griffin, Andrew Luck, Megan Rapinoe, Robert Smigel, Rick Steves. title: The Burns Cage (S27E17)
text: "The Burns Cage" is an episode of Season 27 (production code VABF10), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing April 3, 2016. After a daring skydiving rescue in which he saves Mr. Burns' life, Smithers finally confesses his love for his boss, only to be coldly rebuffed and reduced to removing popcorn from Burns' teeth. Heartbroken, Smithers takes his frustration out on the plant workers, prompting Homer to organize a party using a gay dating app to help Smithers find a new love interest. Smithers meets and falls for a man named Julio, quits his job at the power plant, and moves with him to Cuba, leaving Burns to struggle through a series of failed replacement assistants. In Cuba, Julio realizes Smithers is still hung up on Mr. Burns, leading to their breakup and Smithers' return to Springfield, where he and Burns reconcile over a quiet dinner. Meanwhile, at Springfield Elementary, Lisa lands the lead female role in a school production of Casablanca, while Milhouse and new student Jack Deforest compete for the male lead, which Jack wins. Jealous, Bart enlists Dolph, Jimbo, and Kearney to beat up Jack and remove him from the play, but the bullies are defeated by Jack instead. However, Principal Skinner witnesses the fight and disqualifies Jack, handing the role to Milhouse, whose lack of talent worries Lisa until Marge convinces her to support him. Milhouse ultimately performs surprisingly well on stage, but it's revealed afterward that Jack had secretly been playing Milhouse's role from behind, letting Lisa go off with the real Jack in the end. Guest starring George Takei. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: I did it! All by myself! | Waylon Smithers: Sorry, sir. If there was a less spectacular way to save your life, I... I should've found it. | Mr. Burns: Don't take this the wrong way, but you mean nothing to me. | Mr. Burns: I'll see you back at the office. Don't be late! | Superintendent Chalmers: You can teach acting, you can't teach popular.

title: The Yellow Badge of Cowardge (S25E22)
text: "The Yellow Badge of Cowardge" is an episode of Season 25 (production code SABF18), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Ian Maxtone-Graham, Billy Kimball, originally airing May 18, 2014. On the last day of school, Bart celebrates while Homer discovers the town's Fourth of July fireworks show has been cancelled due to budget cuts, prompting him to track down an old pyrotechnician named Giuseppe to revive it. At Springfield Elementary's Field Day, Milhouse secretly trains for the school's traditional race, hoping to finally beat the odds, but Nelson and the bullies ambush him mid-race to make sure he loses. Bart witnesses the attack but chooses to keep running, ultimately claiming first place and a hero's welcome. When Milhouse turns up with convenient amnesia, Bart repeatedly fails to admit what really happened, even accepting a town celebration in his honor. Milhouse's memory returns after a bully hits him again, and he exposes Bart's cowardice, turning the whole town against him. Bart flees to the retirement home for help from Grandpa, while Homer and Giuseppe's fireworks plan disintegrates into a chaotic, dangerous mishap that endangers the crowd. Thinking fast, Bart hijacks a retirement home bus and drives it in front of the crowd to shield them from the wayward fireworks, then slips away so Milhouse gets credit for the heroic save, quietly making amends for his earlier betrayal. Guest starring Glenn Close as Mona Simpson, Edwin Moses as himself. Notable quotes: Bart: Take it from me, the boy who's lied throughout!
quotes: Bart: Take it from me, the boy who's lied throughout!

title: The Old Blue Mayor She Ain't What She Used to Be (S29E06)
keys: the old blue mayor she ain't what she used to be
text: "The Old Blue Mayor She Ain't What She Used to Be" is an episode of Season 29 (production code WABF20), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Tom Gammill, Max Pross, originally airing November 12, 2017. Springfield celebrates the opening of a new Skypark-Line built over the old monorail tracks, but the festivities end in disaster when the monorail breaks loose, killing Sebastian Cobb and destroying the station and a memorial statue. At the resulting town hall inquiry, Mayor Quimby condescends to Marge, sparking her fury and prompting Lisa to urge her mother to run for mayor. Marge's campaign gains momentum, and she eventually defeats Quimby by promising to extinguish the long-burning Springfield Tire Yard fire. Once in office, she fails to keep that promise and further alienates voters by insulting a tire-fire souvenir shop owner who turns out to be a Vietnam veteran, sending her approval ratings plummeting. Desperate to recover, Marge takes advice to connect with voters by mocking Homer publicly, and her popularity soars even as it strains their marriage and confuses Homer, who mistakes Krusty's joking insult for real ridicule. As Marge's mockery of Homer escalates, she seeks guidance from Quimby, who reveals that his own marriage improved once he left politics. Realizing the toll her ambition has taken on her family, Marge chooses not to continue humiliating Homer and steps back from her harsh political persona. An epilogue set eight years later shows a Marge Simpson Memorial Library that includes a section devoted to her eventual impeachment and disgrace. title: The Book Job (S23E06)
text: "The Book Job" is an episode of Season 23 (production code NABF22), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Dan Vebber, originally airing November 20, 2011. After witnessing a scary dinosaur show, Lisa discovers that her favorite author, T.R. Francis, is actually a fictional brand name used by a team of hired writers working for profit-driven publishers. Devastated, Lisa decides she will write her own honest novel, while Homer gets the opposite idea: assemble a crew of Springfield locals, including Bart, Moe, Professor Frink, and eventually famous author Neil Gaiman, to ghostwrite a commercial fantasy book for money. The group creates 'The Troll Twins of Underbridge Academy' and sells it to publisher Slick at the Springfield Book Fair, agreeing to use a fake author's name. When the printed advance copy comes back retitled and rewritten as 'The Vampire Twins of Transylvania Prep,' the outraged team infiltrates the publisher's headquarters to reclaim their original work. Their heist is nearly foiled, but it turns out Lisa secretly swapped the flash drives to restore the real manuscript, feeling guilty about compromising her ideals. In the end, Gaiman also swapped a drive of his own, ensuring he'd be credited as author, leaving Moe and the others slightly duped but ultimately satisfied with the outcome. Guest starring Neil Gaiman, Andy García. Notable quotes: Milhouse Van Houten: These aren't dinosaurs! Dinosaurs sing! | Ralph Wiggum: I wanna go back inside mommy! | Neil Gaiman: I don't like the taste... of poison.

title: Married to the Blob (S25E10)
text: "Married to the Blob" is an episode of Season 25 (production code SABF03), directed by Chris Clements and written by Tim Long, originally airing January 12, 2014. Comic Book Guy is despondent about being perpetually single until he meets Kumiko, a friendly Japanese manga fan who frequents his shop. The two bond over their shared love of comics and slowly begin a tentative romance, with Homer and other regulars at the Android's Dungeon cheering him on. Things get complicated when Kumiko's father, Yutaka Nakamura, travels from Japan looking for his daughter and stumbles into the comic shop, mistaking it for something disreputable. Homer, trying to help smooth things over, inadvertently makes Comic Book Guy look even less appealing as a suitor by blurting out embarrassing details about him. Realizing he has jeopardized his friend's one shot at happiness, Homer sets out to personally win over the skeptical father, bonding with him over strange food, drink, and a wild night out. Through these bizarre bonding experiences, Yutaka comes to see that Comic Book Guy, despite his eccentricities, is sincere and good-hearted. In the end, Yutaka gives his blessing, and Comic Book Guy and Kumiko's relationship deepens, with him even taking a real job and softening his obsessive nerd persona for her sake. The episode closes with Comic Book Guy declaring his devotion to Kumiko with a small, heartfelt daily ritual. Guest starring Harlan Ellison as himself, Maurice LaMarche as Milo, Stan Lee as himself. title: The Debarted (S19E13)
text: "The Debarted" is an episode of Season 19 (production code KABF06), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing March 2, 2008. After Marge crashes the family car while distracted by squabbling kids, Bart arrives at school to find his desk taken by Donny, a charismatic new troublemaker who quickly wins over Milhouse and Nelson. Feeling eclipsed, Bart tries to one-up Donny's antics but only embarrasses himself, until a shoe-magnet prank on Principal Skinner restores his status and Donny nobly takes the blame. Unbeknownst to Bart, Donny is actually a snitch secretly working for Skinner and Superintendent Chalmers to catch Bart in the act. Meanwhile, Homer becomes obsessed with a luxury loaner car while his own vehicle is being repaired, romancing Marge with its gadgets even as Lisa uses its radio feature to interact with NPR's Terry Gross. Bart, tipped off by Groundskeeper Willie that a mole is in his crew, wrongly accuses Milhouse before spotting Donny's blue-stained tongue from illicit licorice and realizing he is the real snitch. Just as Bart and Nelson prepare to punish Donny with a Diet Coke and Mentos ambush, Chalmers, Skinner, and Willie arrive, only for Donny to save Bart from being caught, proving his loyalty before departing. Homer, meanwhile, discovers his beloved old car being resold for scrap and realizes his emotional attachment to it, abandoning the fancy loaner to reclaim it. Guest starring Topher Grace, Terry Gross. Notable quotes: Ralph Wiggum: When he grows up, I want to be like me! | Bart: Skinner's five steps ahead of me! I put a tack on his chair, he's corked his pants. I throw a tomato, he's making salad. | Homer: Unlike love, respect can't be bought. | Lisa: I never dreamed an American car designed in Germany, assembled in Mexico from parts made in Canada, could be so amazing. | Principal Skinner: Sorry to plop, plop on your fizz, fizz.

Bart: Skinner's five steps ahead of me! I put a tack on his chair, he's corked his pants. I throw a tomato, he's making salad.
Homer: Unlike love, respect can't be bought.

Principal Skinner: Sorry to plop, plop on your fizz, fizz.

title: Lost Verizon (S20E02)
text: "Lost Verizon" is an episode of Season 20 (production code KABF15), directed by Raymond S. Persi and written by John Frink, originally airing October 5, 2008. Bart is embarrassed that everyone else has a cell phone but him, and Marge explains the family can't afford one, or Lisa's dream trip to Machu Picchu. Determined to earn money, Bart starts a business retrieving golf balls at the country club, but loses his earnings when Groundskeeper Willie takes his bucket. When celebrity golfer Denis Leary angrily hurls his cell phone away in frustration, Bart snatches it up and begins impersonating Leary on prank calls, even fooling producer Brian Grazer. After Marge confiscates the phone, Leary suggests she use its GPS to spy on Bart, and guilt-ridden but curious, she does so, catching him in various minor misdeeds. When Bart discovers the tracking, he angrily straps the GPS chip to a bird's leg, sending the whole family on a wild chase that leads them to Machu Picchu. There, Marge has a vision from an Incan god teaching her that overprotective parenting stifles children, prompting her to loosen her grip on Bart. The family returns home to find Bart safe and unbothered by their absence, and after a heartfelt reconciliation, they realize they've accidentally left baby Maggie behind in Peru, where she's now being worshipped as a deity. Guest starring Brian Grazer, Denis Leary. Notable quotes: Marge Simpson: Son, we can't afford to get you a cell phone. As it is, I'm buying frozen peas in installments. | Bart: Which one? The one that got canceled, or the one that's gonna get canceled? | Lisa: And I'm never gonna go to Machu Picchu. In this family, you get used to disappointment. | Agnes Skinner: You had to drive with the windows open, didn't you, Rockefeller? | Bart: Mom, even Milhouse has a cell phone. Your son is lamer than Milhouse! What does that say about you?

Bart: Which one? The one that got canceled, or the one that's gonna get canceled?
Lisa: And I'm never gonna go to Machu Picchu. In this family, you get used to disappointment.
Agnes Skinner: You had to drive with the windows open, didn't you, Rockefeller?
Bart: Mom, even Milhouse has a cell phone. Your son is lamer than Milhouse! What does that say about you?

title: Marge the Lumberjill (S31E06)
text: "Marge the Lumberjill" is an episode of Season 31 (production code ZABF02), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Ryan Koh, originally airing November 10, 2019. At Springfield Elementary, students perform self-written skits, and one depicting the Simpsons as seen from the outside makes Marge realize the family thinks she's boring. After a failed attempt at a comedic sermon, Marge's life takes a turn when a lightning-struck tree trunk crashes onto the family car. When Homer proves too lazy to clear it, Marge takes an axe to the trunk herself, catching the attention of Patty and professional timbersports coach Paula, who sees raw talent in her. Marge enters and wins a local lumberjack competition, impressing everyone and finally breaking her boring image. Paula invites her to train intensively for a month in Portland, and Marge accepts, leaving her family behind. When Homer and the kids travel to Portland to bring her home, they find Marge deeply settled into her new life with Paula, on the eve of a major championship. Marge and Paula win the championship together, but Paula reassures a jealous Homer that she already has a family of her own and has no interest in stealing Marge away. The Simpsons return home intact, and Homer tries to boost baby Maggie's confidence with an ill-advised toy chainsaw that only frightens her. Guest starring Asia Kate Dillon as Paula, Natasha Lyonne as Sophie. Notable quotes: Paula: Timbersports is more than a hobby. It's an unpaid passion that you do in your spare time. | Anger Watkins: Matt isn't a nickname. It's a name name. I'd storm out of here right now if I weren't so terrified of squirrels. | Homer: Where you going? She might leave and never come back. Just like the McRib. | Homer: You're married in the two most important ways there are: emotionally and cooking. | Grampa: Aw, her baby head fell out. You'll be getting a visit from the Head Fairy.
quotes: Paula: Timbersports is more than a hobby. It's an unpaid passion that you do in your spare time.
Anger Watkins: Matt isn't a nickname. It's a name name. I'd storm out of here right now if I weren't so terrified of squirrels.
Homer: Where you going? She might leave and never come back. Just like the McRib.
Homer: You're married in the two most important ways there are: emotionally and cooking.
Grampa: Aw, her baby head fell out. You'll be getting a visit from the Head Fairy.

title: Write Off This Episode (S34E19)
text: "Write Off This Episode" is an episode of Season 34 (production code OABF12), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing April 30, 2023. After Homer loses his wedding ring under the house while celebrating a bet and gets skunk-sprayed retrieving it, Marge reveals a homemade, machine-free method for cleaning stinky laundry using a simple pillowcase mix. Lisa is inspired to use this method to help Springfield's homeless, and the two start handing out cleaning kits at the Squidport, eventually catching the attention of the Rich Texan, who helps them formally register as the Lisa M. Simpson Foundation. When they run out of baking soda, Lisa discovers Marge has been using a brand linked to child labor and sets off with Homer to find ethically sourced ingredients abroad, leaving Marge to run things alone. In her absence, Bernice Hibbert convinces Marge to shift the charity's focus from actual aid to corporate sponsorships and 'awareness raising,' which horrifies Lisa upon her return. The mother-daughter conflict escalates until Marge strips Lisa of any real authority, but with Homer's support, Lisa gets over being pushed aside and reconciles with Marge. At the grand opening of the charity's flashy new center, Marge discovers the building was built by displacing homeless people like Gil, prompting her to publicly denounce the charity's hollow mission and hand it back to Lisa. Lisa transforms the center into an actual homeless shelter, while Mr. Burns delivers a cynical speech about charity being self-serving theater, and Marge and Lisa officially reconcile with Lisa reinstated as the charity's true leader. Notable quotes: Marge: Rather than clean them? Don't rob me of the one part of your dad getting skunk-sprayed I enjoy. | Gil Gunderson: Ah, hot diggity. I can finally get my old job back as a stock image model for "man in suit." | Marge: Well, we're a little behind in our bag making, but we've been doing something even more important: raising awareness about our bag making. | Homer: Oh, why can't anything good ever be at the bottom of a mountain? | Mr. Burns: We all want the United Way because that's the American way.

Gil Gunderson: Ah, hot diggity. I can finally get my old job back as a stock image model for "man in suit."
Marge: Well, we're a little behind in our bag making, but we've been doing something even more important: raising awareness about our bag making.
Homer: Oh, why can't anything good ever be at the bottom of a mountain?
Mr. Burns: We all want the United Way because that's the American way.

title: Love Is a Many-Strangled Thing (S22E17)
text: "Love Is a Many-Strangled Thing" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF10), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Bill Odenkirk, originally airing March 27, 2011. After Mr. Burns gets stuck aloft in a hot air balloon, Homer's clumsy rescue attempt earns him free tickets to a Springfield Atoms game, where he ends up tickling Bart until the boy wets himself on the Jumbotron in front of the whole crowd. Mortified, Marge forces Homer into a fathering enrichment class run by Dr. Zander, who discovers that Homer has also been strangling Bart for years. To make Homer understand Bart's perspective, Zander enlists his friend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar to play Homer while Homer plays Bart, and Abdul-Jabbar strangles him so convincingly that Homer becomes terrified of his own son. Bart quickly exploits his father's newfound fear, prompting Marge to seek further counseling for both of them. When she tracks down Dr. Zander, she finds he's lost his practice and is living homeless in a park due to the bad economy, but she convinces him to help for a small payment of cash and canned beans. His unconventional desert therapy involves leading a blindfolded Homer into cacti and later stringing Homer up by a noose to teach Bart a lesson about defiance, even strangling Bart himself when the boy refuses to cut his father down. Bart finally relents and saves Homer, mending their relationship, while an unrepentant Homer threatens to sue Zander, who reveals he has nothing to take since he now lives in a tree trunk house. Guest starring Paul Rudd as Dr. Zander, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar as himself, Kevin Michael Richardson as the retired lineman masseur. Notable quotes: Homer: Marge, he's laughing. That means he's happy. Has the Joker taught you nothing? | Sideshow Mel: The child has wetted his trousers! | Bart: Dad, how could you do that? The whole audience saw me pee my pants! | Homer: Son, I'm really, really sorry. | Bart: This song's a little bossy for me.
quotes: Homer: Marge, he's laughing. That means he's happy. Has the Joker taught you nothing?
Sideshow Mel: The child has wetted his trousers!
Bart: Dad, how could you do that? The whole audience saw me pee my pants!
Homer: Son, I'm really, really sorry.
Bart: This song's a little bossy for me.

title: Treehouse of Horror XXXIII (S34E06)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXXIII" is an episode of Season 34 (production code UABF18), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Carolyn Omine, Ryan Koh, Matt Selman, originally airing October 30, 2022. This Halloween anthology opens with 'The Pookadook,' in which Marge reads Maggie a haunted bedtime book that refuses to stay destroyed and eventually possesses her, turning her into a threat to her own baby; Maggie must fend off the possessed Marge with makeshift traps and toys until a tender memory breaks the curse, letting Marge vacuum the demon away for good. In 'Death Tome,' Lisa discovers a supernatural book that kills anyone whose name is written in it, and after testing it on a hostage-taking Snake Jailbird, she is confronted by a death-god named Steve Johnson who declares the book now hers. Lisa escalates to killing Mr. Burns and his entire corporate board to stop a climate-wrecking scheme, but when she realizes the power has corrupted her and nearly turns it on Bart, she instead destroys Steve Johnson and unwittingly becomes the next reaper herself. The final segment, 'SimpsonsWorld,' reveals that Homer is actually an animatronic in a Simpsons-themed amusement park; after a malfunction exposes his robotic nature, he escapes captivity, cranks his own self-awareness, and frees Lisa and the rest of his robotic family from their programmed loop. The liberated family fights through armies of malfunctioning Ralph Wiggum security bots and escapes the park in a Canyonero driven by Marge, only to wind up as customers in Bob's Burgers, which is revealed to be just another attraction in a sprawling multiverse of animated theme parks. A closing coda shows Kang and Kodos reading the very book that recounts the episode's stories, and they flee in terror upon realizing they are its subjects. Guest starring John Roberts as Linda Belcher, Hank Williams, Jr. as "Canyonero" song singer. Notable quotes: Marge: Oh, Maggie, I'm so sorry I got possessed and almost chopped you up into little pieces. Oh, but I'm here now. Mommy's here. | Snake Jailbird: Ha-ha, I'm totally gonna get away with murd... Oh! Oh, my heart! Heart attack! And... death. | Steve Johnson: I think you'll find that murder is almost as addictive as plastic surgery. | Female park employee: Uh, calm down, Mr. Simpson. I know it feels like you're a man, but you are actually something much, much more expensive: intellectual property. | Ralph Wiggum bots: I choo-choo-choose you... to die. This installment is made up of 4 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 33): "The Pookadook", "Death Tome", "SimpsonsWorld", and "Epilogue".
quotes: Marge: Oh, Maggie, I'm so sorry I got possessed and almost chopped you up into little pieces. Oh, but I'm here now. Mommy's here.
Snake Jailbird: Ha-ha, I'm totally gonna get away with murd... Oh! Oh, my heart! Heart attack! And... death.
Steve Johnson: I think you'll find that murder is almost as addictive as plastic surgery.
Female park employee: Uh, calm down, Mr. Simpson. I know it feels like you're a man, but you are actually something much, much more expensive: intellectual property.

title: Treehouse of Horror XVIII (S19E05)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XVIII" is an episode of Season 19 (production code JABF16), directed by Chuck Sheetz and written by Marc Wilmore, originally airing November 4, 2007. This Halloween anthology episode opens with Marge baking a killer dessert that satirizes Fox's primetime lineup. In 'E.T., Go Home,' Bart discovers the alien Kodos hiding in the family's shed and, along with Lisa, helps him gather technology to contact his homeworld, unaware that Kodos is secretly plotting an invasion. When government agents close in, Kodos begins killing them and eventually opens a portal for his fellow aliens, sparking a war that humanity ultimately wins, with Homer finishing off the captured Kodos. In 'Mr. and Mrs. Simpson,' a parody of Mr. and Mrs. Smith reveals that Homer and Marge are secretly rival assassins, each assigned to either kill or protect Kent Brockman; after a chaotic battle of weapons and lies, they realize their shared love of killing reignites their passion, and the whole story turns out to be a session with Principal Skinner about Bart, whom they ignore before shooting Skinner instead. In 'Heck House,' Bart, Lisa, Milhouse, and Nelson's escalating Halloween pranks prompt Ned Flanders to convert the church into a terrifying 'Heck House' meant to scare them into good behavior. When ordinary scare tactics fail, Ned transforms into a devil and shows the kids horrifying visions of Springfield residents suffering for the seven deadly sins. The frightened kids finally repent, and Ned returns to normal, closing the episode with a jab at Fox viewers being doomed to hell. Guest starring Maurice LaMarche. Notable quotes: Homer: Creme Brulee! Creme Brulee! Creme Brulee! Or in English: Burnt Cream! Burnt Cream! Burnt Cream! | Kodos: My friends and I come in peace to find your vulnerabilities...and cure them with more peace. | Kodos: Well done, Columbo! That's right, we watch Columbo. They air it during rainouts of kleep-klop games. | Kodos: Actually, I'm still alive, so it's technically vivisection. | Nelson Muntz: I was just in it for the sin! This installment is made up of 3 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 18): "E.T., Go Home", "Mr. and Mrs. Simpson", and "Heck House".
quotes: Homer: Creme Brulee! Creme Brulee! Creme Brulee! Or in English: Burnt Cream! Burnt Cream! Burnt Cream!
Kodos: My friends and I come in peace to find your vulnerabilities...and cure them with more peace.

Kodos: Actually, I'm still alive, so it's technically vivisection.
Nelson Muntz: I was just in it for the sin!

title: Habeas Tortoise (S34E01)
text: "Habeas Tortoise" is an episode of Season 34 (production code UABF16), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Broti Gupta, originally airing September 25, 2022. After Homer is publicly mocked for suggesting the town's tiny free libraries be combined into one big library, Marge takes the family to the Springfield Zoo to cheer him up, only to find that the beloved tortoise Slow Leonard has vanished from his enclosure. When both the zoo director and Chief Wiggum brush off Homer's attempts to investigate, he turns to Facelook and joins a growing online group obsessed with finding Leonard. Fueled by the attention and respect he's never gotten before, Homer hosts a meeting of amateur sleuths at his house, complete with paella and a full evidence board, and the group's wild theories multiply. Meanwhile Gil impulsively proposes to Ms. Hoover during one of the group's protest marches outside the zoo director's house. Homer secretly discovers that Leonard simply fell into a rabbit hole near the zoo and was never kidnapped, but he keeps the truth hidden from the group because he doesn't want to lose the camaraderie and attention the mystery has brought him. When the conspiracy group's schemes turn dangerous, Marge shows up with the real Leonard, but the paranoid group insists he's a government robot until Homer finally helps them accept the truth. As the group starts to disband, Homer proposes a new mystery to keep everyone together, and it's revealed that the conspiracy board's yarn was secretly a hidden camera used by its manufacturer to spy on conspiracy theorists worldwide for profit. Guest starring Joe Mantegna as Fat Tony, Jay Pharoah as Drederick Tatum. Notable quotes: Homer: Did you see how the credit card thing at the ticket booth told me to remove my card, like I didn't know how to do it? Then it got stuck 'cause I didn't know how to do it. | Homer: I don't need to show off for you, Marge. You already bought the cow. I finally have a group of friends who think I'm smart. Who haven't used a skeptical emoji with a monocle even once with me. | Marge: Homer, did you kidnap Leonard? | Homer: No, I didn't commit the crime. I did something much worse. I solved it. | [[Springfield Zoo director]]: Please stop these protests. Why would I kidnap an animal? That's what a zoo is: a bunch of kidnapped animals.

Homer: I don't need to show off for you, Marge. You already bought the cow. I finally have a group of friends who think I'm smart. Who haven't used a skeptical emoji with a monocle even once with me.
Marge: Homer, did you kidnap Leonard?
Homer: No, I didn't commit the crime. I did something much worse. I solved it.
[[Springfield Zoo director]]: Please stop these protests. Why would I kidnap an animal? That's what a zoo is: a bunch of kidnapped animals.

title: Manger Things (S32E16)
text: "Manger Things" is an episode of Season 32 (production code QABF09), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Rob LaZebnik, originally airing March 21, 2021. While decorating the Christmas tree, the Simpson kids find an ornament reading 'Todd's first Christmas,' prompting Marge to recount a chaotic holiday from years earlier. After Lenny and Carl spike his soda at the plant's office party, Homer gets drunk and mocks Mr. Burns, triggering a wild chase involving the released hounds and a runaway ice statue. Marge, furious, locks Homer out of the house, forcing him to seek shelter with the reluctant Flanders family, where he eats their raw Christmas ham and hallucinates a hellish vision. As Homer bounces between Moe's Tavern and a secret room above the Simpsons' garage, Bart and Lisa struggle with his absence, even offering to give up all their toys if he can come home for Christmas. Marge sets one condition for his return: he must do something to make up for all the trouble he's caused. Just as Homer despairs after accidentally burning the kitchen, Maude Flanders goes into labor, and with Ned away delivering turkeys to the poor, Homer steps up to help deliver the baby—Todd. Marge, watching from the doorway, is moved by his selfless act and reconciles with him. The story concludes with the revelation that Todd's middle name is 'Homer' and Maggie's middle name is 'Lenny,' both tied to this chaotic Christmas, while in the present, the family shares a warm holiday postcard-like ending in Springfield. You have to order an Uber Sad for that. | Rod: Daddy, you're a jackass. | Maude: Give me my baby!

title: Crystal Blue-Haired Persuasion (S30E23)
text: "Crystal Blue-Haired Persuasion" is an episode of Season 30 (production code YABF16), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Megan Amram, originally airing May 12, 2019. When Mr. Burns slashes children's healthcare from the power plant's benefits, Bart loses access to his usual ADD medication and is switched to a cheaper drug with unsettling side effects. Desperate for a solution, Marge discovers a new age shop selling blue healing crystals, and after Bart's grades mysteriously improve, she becomes convinced they are the cure. When the original shop closes, its owner hands over her entire crystal stock to Marge, who starts her own home business selling them to other Springfield mothers. The venture explodes into a full-fledged store called Murmur with help from Lindsey Naegle, making Marge briefly wealthy and drawing the jealous wrath of a rival crystal-shop owner in Shelbyville. Meanwhile, Lisa suspects the crystals are nonsense and eventually uncovers Bart's real secret: he's been secretly reading cheat notes hidden behind the crystals in class rather than being magically cured. Torn between loyalty to his mother and honesty, Bart admits the truth just as Marge's business rivalry reaches a boiling point at the mall. Confronted with proof that the crystals never worked, Marge shuts down her business, and the episode ends with her narrowly escaping a chaotic, gun-fired standoff at the cult compound of the original shop's former owner. Guest starring Illeana Douglas as the New age clerk, Werner Herzog as Walther Hotenhoffer, Jenny Slate as Piper Paisley. Notable quotes: Grampa: Back in my day, children didn't need no meds! You just gave 'em a shot of whiskey and sent 'em off to school! | Marge: His father wants him to join football for a nice, calming concussion. | Store clerk: Crystals are a timeless database of energy, knowledge and sparkling. | Marge: I am pretty desperate.
quotes: Grampa: Back in my day, children didn't need no meds! You just gave 'em a shot of whiskey and sent 'em off to school!
Marge: His father wants him to join football for a nice, calming concussion.
Store clerk: Crystals are a timeless database of energy, knowledge and sparkling.
Marge: I am pretty desperate.

title: I Don't Wanna Know Why the Caged Bird Sings (S19E04)
keys: i don't wanna know why the caged bird sings
text: "I Don't Wanna Know Why the Caged Bird Sings" is an episode of Season 19 (production code JABF19), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Dana Gould, originally airing October 14, 2007. When Lisa is honored as 'Student of the Millennium,' Marge insists Homer finally attend one of her big events, leading to a comic negotiation over how sober he must be. While Marge waits in a slow-moving bank line, a charming stranger named Dwight suddenly reveals himself as a robber, taking the bank hostage and severely wounding Gil, who had just started his security guard job. During the standoff, Dwight bonds with Marge and agrees to surrender only if she promises to visit him in prison, a promise she reluctantly makes to save the hostages. Wracked with guilt and anxiety, Marge keeps stalling her prison visit, missing visiting hours and leaving Dwight devastated and increasingly unstable behind bars. Dwight breaks out of prison and tracks Marge down using her address from a newspaper, eventually taking her hostage again and bringing her to the amusement park where his mother once abandoned him, hoping to relive lost childhood memories together. Chief Wiggum attempts a rescue but gets trapped on the same amusement ride, prompting Dwight to sacrifice his own safety by jamming the ride's mechanism to save him. Dwight survives, recovers in the hospital, and is returned to prison, where Marge finally keeps her promise and visits him. He gives her a sentimental handmade gift with a hidden note asking for help escaping again, but Marge declines, and Dwight accepts her decision without resentment. Guest starring Steve Buscemi, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Ted Nugent. Notable quotes: Dwight: Okay, this isn't the way I planned it, but you can make it out alive as long as there's no funny stuff. | Snake: Hey, baby. Listen carefully. Someone's been editing my biography on Wikipedia. I want you to kill him. | Homer: American sober or Irish sober? | Homer: What?! Name twelve! | Krusty the Clown: Don't worry about me. I was voted America's least funny clown.

title: Singin' in the Lane (S29E07)
text: "Singin' in the Lane" is an episode of Season 29 (production code WABF21), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Ryan Koh, originally airing November 19, 2017. After Mr. Burns invites Homer to a basketball game with only four tickets, Homer picks Carl, Lenny and Barney, leaving Moe out and hurting his feelings. To make it up to him, the guys revive their old bowling team, the Pin Pals, with Moe as captain, and they start winning tournaments that lead them to the state finals in Capital City. There they face the Fund Bunch, a group of wealthy, condescending bowlers who bully everyone around them, including Moe. The two teams strike a high-stakes wager: if the Fund Bunch wins, they take over Moe's Tavern and force Moe to change his name, but if the Pin Pals win, Moe gets a rich-man's reward. Meanwhile, Bart becomes seduced by the Fund Bunch's wealthy lifestyle, prompting Lisa and Marge to try to teach him that money can't buy happiness, while Lisa also recruits nerds to dig up dirt on the Fund Bunch. During the climactic match, the Fund Bunch discover Barney becomes a terrible bowler when drunk and get him intoxicated to sabotage the Pin Pals. Despite the setback, Homer manages to bowl three critical strikes to secure the win for the team. Moe, who had imagined a humiliating fresh start in France if they lost, is overjoyed when his friends reaffirm their loyalty to him, and the defeated Fund Bunch graciously reward the Pin Pals with a zero-gravity plane experience. Notable quotes: Moe: You really don't want me? I, uh, I thought we was friends. | Carl: Then we realized you were serving us beer that's mostly suds. | Reynolds: I'll give you $100 to stop talking. | Bart: I think I'm giving you a $500 look. | Moe: I just gotta go back to the worst thing in the world — bein' me.
quotes: Moe: You really don't want me? I, uh, I thought we was friends.
Carl: Then we realized you were serving us beer that's mostly suds.
Reynolds: I'll give you $100 to stop talking.
Bart: I think I'm giving you a $500 look.
Moe: I just gotta go back to the worst thing in the world — bein' me.

title: Havana Wild Weekend (S28E07)
text: "Havana Wild Weekend" is an episode of Season 28 (production code VABF19), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Dan Castellaneta, Deb Lacusta, Peter Tilden, originally airing November 13, 2016. The Simpsons discover that Grampa has been secretly wetting the carpet, revealing his declining health, and their attempts to get him care at the Retirement Castle and the V.A. Hospital both fail miserably. A fellow veteran suggests they travel to Cuba for affordable medical treatment, so the whole family heads there hoping for a solution. Cuban doctors offer little hope for Grampa, but a joyride in a vintage 1958 car reignites his spirit and gives the family a newfound love for the country. At a hotel bar, Grampa reconnects with an old Army buddy and falls for a flirtatious waitress named Isabella, eventually deciding he wants to stay in Cuba for good. He joins a wild party thrown by veterans aboard a hijacked airplane, prompting Homer to enlist the U.S. Embassy to track him down. Isabella shocks everyone by revealing she's actually a CIA agent tasked with returning fugitives to the United States, and she gases the whole plane to subdue them. Back in Miami, Homer and Grampa reconcile, bonding with Bart over a mischievous round of golf where they use air horns to throw off other players' shots. Guest starring Stacy Keach as H.K. Duff, Deb Lacusta as Isabella. Notable quotes: Marge: Cuba sounds a little dangerous. Why don't we try Canada? | Grampa: I don't want to go there, now that the commie Trudeau is in charge. We're going to Cuba. | Homer: Oh, now that's a Milhouse I'd marry!
quotes: Marge: Cuba sounds a little dangerous. Why don't we try Canada?
Grampa: I don't want to go there, now that the commie Trudeau is in charge. We're going to Cuba.
Homer: Oh, now that's a Milhouse I'd marry!

title: Steal This Episode (S25E09)
text: "Steal This Episode" is an episode of Season 25 (production code SABF05), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing January 5, 2014. Fed up with the high cost and endless commercials at the movie theater, Homer turns to Bart, who shows him how to illegally download films for free online. Homer becomes obsessed with pirating movies, roping in Marge, Carl, and the rest of Springfield, who all revel in getting big-budget entertainment without paying. Their piracy ring draws the attention of the FBI's anti-piracy division, led by the intense Deputy Director Gratman, who is determined to make an example of the culprits. After Homer is turned in by an anonymous tip, he is arrested and thrown into prison, where hardened criminals are outraged to learn he's a movie pirate rather than a 'real' criminal. Meanwhile, Lisa and Bart debate the ethics of piracy, questioning whether media companies or internet-freedom advocates are the true villains, while Marge seeks help from a Swedish ambassador who defends free file-sharing as a cultural ideal. Gratman's aggressive pursuit of internet pirates escalates into an absurd international standoff involving death metal music used to flush out fugitives. In the end, Homer's ordeal exposes the murky morality on both sides of the piracy debate, and he narrowly avoids the harshest consequences of his actions. Guest starring Judd Apatow, Will Arnett, Rob Halford, Leslie Mann, Kevin Michael Richardson, Paul Rudd, Seth Rogen, Channing Tatum. title: The Road to Cincinnati (S32E08)
text: "The Road to Cincinnati" is an episode of Season 32 (production code ZABF20), directed by Matthew Nastuk and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing November 29, 2020. Superintendent Chalmers plans to bring Principal Finch instead of Principal Skinner to the Edu-Con administrators convention in Cincinnati, leaving Skinner desperate to prove himself worthy of the invitation. When Finch falls suspiciously ill just before departure, Skinner seizes the opportunity to take his place, though he later admits he secretly sabotaged Finch's food to cause the illness. Their flight ends in disaster due to Chalmers' fear of flying, forcing the pair to drive 800 miles together, enduring destroyed vehicles, a run-in with an eccentric judge, hostile cyclists, and a rescue by armed forces veterans. Along the way old resentments boil over, and Skinner overhears Chalmers planning to fire him in favor of Finch, leading to a bitter argument where both men air years of grievances. Skinner storms off, but the two accidentally swap jackets, leaving Chalmers without his speech notes when he reaches the convention in Cincinnati. As Chalmers begins improvising a heartfelt speech about their chaotic journey, he realizes how much Skinner truly means to him, and Skinner arrives just in time to hand over the cards, mending their friendship. Back in Springfield, Skinner earns newfound respect from the kids, while the Simpson family enjoys an unrelated night of watching improv Shakespeare performers, and the episode closes with Skinner and Chalmers reconciled over dinner at Skyline Chili. Guest starring Jason Bateman, Hannibal Buress. Notable quotes: Skinner: Fire me?! You bald-pated son of a bitch. | Chalmers: You know why I was gonna fire you, Seymour? Because your neediness, it sucks the life out of me! After all these years of trying to spare your feelings, I'm just gonna say it now: I... don't... like you! | Chalmers: I just... I-I want to die. | Bart: Dude, you're Seymour Skinner. No matter how badly you're treated, you keep coming back for more. That's your superpower. Use it! | J.T. Winchester: My car is for good boys!

J.T. Winchester: My car is for good boys!

title: To Cur, with Love (S24E08)
text: "To Cur, with Love" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF01), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing December 16, 2012. Professor Frink's sound-powered vehicle crashes into the Springfield Retirement Castle, forcing Grampa to move in with the Simpsons. Homer fakes a back injury to avoid helping with the move and instead becomes hopelessly addicted to a mobile game called Villageville, completely neglecting Santa's Little Helper in the process. When the dog goes missing and is later found hiding, Bart and Lisa realize Homer has ignored him all day, and Grampa's mention of Homer's childhood dog Bongo sends Homer into an emotional tailspin. Through a flashback, it's revealed that young Homer and Bongo were inseparable until Bongo attacked Mr. Burns, prompting Abe to secretly give the dog away to protect him, which damaged both Homer's bond with Bongo and his relationship with his father. Back in the present, Homer struggles to accept that Bongo is gone and may not remember him, but Abe reassures him by showing a photo of Bongo still keeping Homer's old sweatshirt. Realizing how he's failed both Santa's Little Helper and his father, Homer reconciles with Abe and recommits himself to being a better companion to his dog. The episode ends warmly with Homer bonding with Santa's Little Helper and Abe, followed by a whimsical dream sequence blending past and present canine relationships across Springfield. Notable quotes: Homer: Bongo?! I told you never to ever talk about Bongo. Ever! | Lisa: I love that dog, but that is one long, stupid name. | Homer: Hold down the fort? With my bad back? | Homer: Why would you think that? Just because I put you in a home where they feed you dog food? | Marge: You know you can't lift your lifting belt without wearing your belt-lifting-belt.

title: The D'oh-cial Network (S23E11)
text: "The D'oh-cial Network" is an episode of Season 23 (production code PABF04), directed by Chris Clements and written by J. Stewart Burns, originally airing January 15, 2012. Lisa is on trial for the citywide chaos caused by SpringFace, the social networking site she created, and she recounts the events leading up to it. After a family trip to the mall where Lisa is mocked by Sherri and Terri for being unpopular, she takes solace in Homer's new computer and discovers how easy it is to make online friends compared to real ones. With help from Martin, Database, Cosine, and Report Card—and a layout idea swiped from Nelson—she launches SpringFace, which quickly becomes a sensation across Springfield, drawing in kids and adults alike. As the whole town becomes obsessed with checking updates, even while driving, Lisa realizes she has become more isolated than ever despite her site's massive popularity. The obsession spirals into real danger, culminating in deadly car accidents caused by distracted SpringFace use. Back in court, Lisa is forced to shut down the site, and life in Springfield slowly returns to normal. The episode closes with a series of humorous epilogue text updates about various townspeople, followed by a cutaway to Patty and Selma competing in Olympic rowing against the Winklevoss twins in London. Guest starring Armie Hammer as Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss, David Letterman as himself, The Tiger Lillies as the end credits performers. Notable quotes: Homer: Leave her alone! That's my only talking daughter. | Bart: Lethal inject her on the electric chair! | Lisa: All right, already! I had no friends. | Lisa: Hit refresh. Hit refresh. I have a thousand friends! And only eight of them are Milhouse! | Hans Moleman: Dislike! Dislike!

title: Lisa Gets the Blues (S29E17)
text: "Lisa Gets the Blues" is an episode of Season 29 (production code XABF11), directed by Bob Anderson and written by David Silverman, Brian Kelley, originally airing April 22, 2018. After being humiliated by Dewey Largo and mocked at school, Lisa loses confidence in her saxophone playing and develops a case of the 'yips.' The family heads to Florida to celebrate great-grandmother Eunice Bouvier's 100th birthday, but Homer's antics on the plane get them rerouted to New Orleans instead, leaving Eunice's party unattended. While Marge takes Bart and Maggie sightseeing, Bart discovers a voodoo shop and buys dolls modeled after the bullies who tormented him, using them for petty revenge. Homer, meanwhile, tries to cheer up a despondent Lisa while indulging heavily in the city's food and drink. A magical encounter with an animated statue of Louis Armstrong nudges Lisa toward listening to her father's well-meaning advice. At a jazz club, she's invited on stage by the nephew of the late Bleeding Gums Murphy, who reveals that Murphy once called her the most promising young musician he'd ever met. The encouragement helps Lisa shake off her yips and rediscover her passion for music, and she returns home able to play confidently again, even receiving a visit from Armstrong's ghost. The family's trip ends on a sweet note as they share beignets together at Café Du Monde. Guest starring Trombone Shorty as himself. Notable quotes: Homer: Well, we did it, kids. And the best thing is, the next episode will beat Gunsmoke. | Bart: What about all the episodes they made on the radio? | Homer: Have a beignet.
quotes: Homer: Well, we did it, kids. And the best thing is, the next episode will beat Gunsmoke.
Bart: What about all the episodes they made on the radio?
Homer: Have a beignet.

title: Treehouse of Horror XXXI (S32E04)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXXI" is an episode of Season 32 (production code ZABF17), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Julia Prescott, originally airing October 18, 2020 (Canada), November 1, 2020 (USA). This Halloween anthology opens with Homer dreaming about the horrors of voting during the Trump era before a real apocalyptic future breaks out in Springfield. In 'Toy Gory,' Bart's habit of destroying his toys catches up with him when a new Radioactive Man action figure comes to life and rallies the rest of his abused toys for revenge, culminating in a gruesome plastic-surgery transformation that turns Bart into one of them. In 'Into the Homer-verse,' a candy-hungry Homer accidentally triggers a machine at the power plant that pulls several alternate-universe Homers into Springfield, causing citywide chaos that Kent Brockman covers on the news. Mr. Burns tries to exploit the duplicate Homers as cheap labor and unleashes his own multiversal allies, sparking a battle that wipes most of them out before the survivors are sent back through the machine. In 'Be Nine, Rewind,' Lisa is trapped in a Groundhog Day-style time loop on her ninth birthday, dying repeatedly—by car crash, treehouse collapse, falling objects, and more—each time resetting to the start of the party. Nelson reveals he's also stuck in the loop, and after several failed attempts and near-misses, the two realize the key is to stop Gil's driving-test car from crashing into the house. By throwing a brick at Gil's car, they finally break the cycle, letting Lisa enjoy her birthday party without further catastrophe, aside from one lingering casualty in Ralph's twisted neck. Guest starring Ben Mankiewicz as himself. Notable quotes: Old Jewish man: I'm gonna need to see three forms of ID. Twelve if you're a Democrat. | Grampa: Mm, I think it's in my other pants. | Krusty Doll: His widow was a monkey? Eh, love is love. | Mr. Burns: I like my children stringy and tough. | Homer Barbera: I'm Homer Barbera, a-smarter than the average Homer. This installment is made up of 4 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 31): "Opening segment", "Toy Gory", "Into the Homer-verse", and "Be Nine, Rewind".

title: The Cad and the Hat (S28E15)
text: "The Cad and the Hat" is an episode of Season 28 (production code WABF08), directed by Steven Dean Moore and written by Ron Zimmerman, originally airing February 19, 2017. During a family trip to Springfield Bay, Lisa buys a sunhat she names Sunny while Bart's temporary tattoo washes off, leaving him feeling inadequate. Meanwhile, Homer surprises everyone by revealing a hidden talent for chess, easily beating Jasper and later several regulars at Moe's. Jealous and humiliated after being mocked by bullies, Bart spitefully throws Lisa's beloved hat into a scrapyard while she sleeps in the car. That night, Bart's guilt literally manifests as a growing creature that torments him until he finally confesses to Lisa, who refuses to forgive him despite his attempts to make amends. In a parallel subplot, Homer discovers his chess skill stems from a repressed desire to finally beat his father, and after a pep talk from Magnus Carlsen via Skype, he challenges Grampa to a decisive match but ultimately forfeits when he realizes their relationship matters more than winning. Meanwhile, Bart enlists Rod and Todd Flanders to retrieve Sunny from a crushed car cube using Buzz Cola to dissolve the metal, successfully recovering the hat. When Bart returns it, Lisa still won't forgive him until her own guilt appears and convinces her to relent, leading to a tearful reconciliation. Bart's now-massive guilt flies off and crashes into the power plant, transforming into a monster that intrigues Mr. Burns, closing the episode on a comedic note as Magnus Carlsen cuts off contact with an overly needy Homer. Guest starring Magnus Carlsen as himself, Seth Green as the Nerd, Patton Oswalt as Bart's guilt. Notable quotes: Homer: I do some of my best fathering when I'm not around. | Moe Szyslak: Yeah, Homer, you're some kind of an idiot savant. | Homer: It was, until I learned the pieces weren't licorice. | Bart's guilt: You know these cartoons are made by exploiting Korean children? | Nelson Muntz: Haw haw! Bart's getting beat up by a beach turkey!
