text: "Homer Is Where the Art Isn't" is an episode of Season 29 (production code XABF05), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Kevin Curran, originally airing March 18, 2018. Homer and Mr. Burns are outbid at auction by Megan Matheson for a Joan Miró painting Homer has become obsessed with, but the artwork is stolen shortly after delivery. Freelance insurance investigator Manacek is called in and works through a string of suspects, first Megan, whose over-insured policy gives her motive, then Burns, whose bruised ego over losing the bid makes him defensive, and finally Homer, whose fixation on the painting makes him look guilty. While investigating, Manacek dines with the Simpsons and hears the story of how Homer fell in love with the painting during a school field trip, only to watch it get auctioned off after the museum lost funding. Overwhelmed by suspicion, Homer flees home, but Manacek tracks him down and assures him he's too dim to have pulled off the theft. Gathering everyone at the museum, Manacek unravels an elaborate scheme: Megan orchestrated a guard swap to steal the painting, only for Burns to have already swapped it earlier using a duplicate auction house. In a final twist, it turns out the painting Homer was fawning over was actually Lisa's tote bag bearing its image, since she'd stolen the real one to keep it from disappearing into a rich collector's private stash. The case resolved, the true painting ends up displayed at a public arena where Homer can still visit it. Guest starring Bill Hader as Manacek, Cecily Strong as Megan Matheson. Notable quotes: Mayor Quimby: Did you know we had to lay off a third of the police force? That's right: Eddie. | Eddie: I used to have a gun! | Manacek: Your story had everything: a field trip, a dream sequence, Sideshow Mel. | Manacek: Sorry, I can only solve impossible crimes if I'm seducing an amazing woman. It's my process. | Lisa: I just want to take a moment to recognize that, for once, you're dragging me to a museum.
quotes: Mayor Quimby: Did you know we had to lay off a third of the police force? That's right: Eddie.
Eddie: I used to have a gun!
Manacek: Your story had everything: a field trip, a dream sequence, Sideshow Mel.
Manacek: Sorry, I can only solve impossible crimes if I'm seducing an amazing woman. It's my process.
Lisa: I just want to take a moment to recognize that, for once, you're dragging me to a museum.

title: Boyz N the Highlands (S33E13)
text: "Boyz N the Highlands" is an episode of Season 33 (production code UABF06), directed by Bob Anderson and written by Dan Vebber, originally airing March 6, 2022. Bart, Nelson, and Dolph are sentenced by juvenile court to complete a wilderness trek for troubled kids, escorted partway by Groundskeeper Willie, and are joined by Martin, who volunteered on his own. Along the trail the boys rescue a baby goat they name Axel, believing it might be the legendary treasure Willie mentioned, and are soon chased off by robed strangers who claim the goat for a ritual sacrifice. The group splits up to escape, with Nelson and Dolph taking a canoe while Bart, Martin, and Axel continue on foot, and tensions rise as Bart cruelly rejects Martin's friendship. Martin reveals the intense pressure his parents place on him, including therapy and drugs, which softens Bart's attitude after Axel wanders off. Meanwhile, Nelson and Dolph are captured by the supposed cultists, who turn out to be film students shooting a low-budget horror movie that the boys accidentally ruin. Bart and Martin arrive just in time to save their friends from a dangerous prop mishap, and the group finally reaches Ankle Rock, where Willie reveals the real treasure was the journey itself. At home, Lisa spends the weekend pretending to be an only child, enjoying undivided attention from Homer and Marge until she overindulges and gets sick, but wakes up happy and content the next morning. In the end, Martin chooses to ride home with the "bad kids" instead of his parents, having earned their respect. Notable quotes: Groundskeeper Willie: Listen up, ya pukes. | Dolph Shapiro: Hell no—I don't trust that thing. Look at those frog-ass eyes. Which way is he even supposed to be looking? | Nelson Muntz: I'm allowed to change my mind. I contain multitudes, dingus. | Bart: Just because we both like this goat doesn't mean I like you. I mean, come on, you're a loser nerd and I'm King Stink. We have nothing in common, and we can never be friends. | Martin Prince: I broke into that pharmacy to steal more drugs, because I still wasn't focused enough to please my parents. Never enough focus for Gareth and Gloria.
quotes: Groundskeeper Willie: Listen up, ya pukes.
Dolph Shapiro: Hell no—I don't trust that thing. Look at those frog-ass eyes. Which way is he even supposed to be looking?
Nelson Muntz: I'm allowed to change my mind. I contain multitudes, dingus.
Bart: Just because we both like this goat doesn't mean I like you. I mean, come on, you're a loser nerd and I'm King Stink. We have nothing in common, and we can never be friends.
Martin Prince: I broke into that pharmacy to steal more drugs, because I still wasn't focused enough to please my parents. Never enough focus for Gareth and Gloria.

title: Treehouse of Horror XXIV (S25E02)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXIV" is an episode of Season 25 (production code RABF16), directed by Rob Oliver and written by Jeff Westbrook, originally airing October 6, 2013. This Halloween anthology opens with a Dr. Seuss-style tale in which three sick children are left home alone on Halloween and lured out by the sinister, rhyming Fat in the Hat, who promises fun but instead unleashes a rampage of violence across Springfield before the kids finally turn on him and kill him with his own umbrella. In the second segment, Bart is accidentally decapitated in a kite mishap and his head is grafted onto Lisa's body, forcing the siblings to cope with sharing one form through therapy, sibling squabbles, and a scheme by Bart to drug Lisa so he can seize permanent control of her body, a plot that backfires when both end up beheaded and reattached to new hosts. The final segment reimagines the Simpsons as circus performers in a 1930s-set parody of the film Freaks, where Mr. Burnsum runs a sideshow featuring the town's "freaks," and Strong-Man Homer schemes to marry the trapeze artist Marguerite by orchestrating the death of her fiancé Moe for his valuable ring. Marguerite discovers Homer's murderous plan and rejects him, while the mistreated freaks turn on the cruel ringmaster and kill him, then transform the treacherous Homer into a tarred-and-feathered sideshow attraction as punishment. Each story ends in dark, ironic comeuppance typical of the Treehouse of Horror tradition, blending literary parody, body-horror slapstick, and classic film homage. Notable quotes: Comic Book Guy: Wait a second... It's Halloween? | Homer: Your peanuts are paw through, your beer smells like skunk, and you just pissed off the wrong fat furry drunk! | Homer: I'm frightened of nothing, not even hell's fires. Just don't let me ever be played by Mike Myers! | Bart: Now I'll just cut off her annoying head and this body will be all mine. Or we both die. Not really sure what the rules are. | Homer: And that, kids, is how I met your mother. This installment is made up of 3 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 24): "Oh, the Places You'll D'oh!", "Dead and Shoulders", and "Freaks No Geeks".
quotes: Comic Book Guy: Wait a second... It's Halloween?
Homer: Your peanuts are paw through, your beer smells like skunk, and you just pissed off the wrong fat furry drunk!
Homer: I'm frightened of nothing, not even hell's fires. Just don't let me ever be played by Mike Myers!
Bart: Now I'll just cut off her annoying head and this body will be all mine. Or we both die. Not really sure what the rules are.
Homer: And that, kids, is how I met your mother.

title: The Kid Is All Right (S25E06)
text: "The Kid Is All Right" is an episode of Season 25 (production code SABF02), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Tim Long, originally airing November 24, 2013. A new student named Isabel Gutierrez arrives at Springfield Elementary and quickly becomes Lisa's best friend, bonding over academics and personality. Their friendship is tested when the two girls end up running against each other in a second-grade class election, during which Lisa is shocked to learn that Isabel is a Republican. Lisa struggles to reconcile her assumptions about Isabel's heritage and beliefs with the fact that her new friend holds very different political views. Meanwhile, the Springfield Republican Party, along with Mr. Burns, sees an opportunity in young Isabel and begins grooming her as a future political prodigy, even trying to buy influence in the school election. As the rivalry escalates, Lisa must decide whether their differing politics should get in the way of a genuine friendship. In a side story, Bart's karate lessons turn out to be secret psychiatric sessions arranged by Marge. The episode resolves with Lisa learning to accept and respect Isabel despite their ideological differences, reaffirming that decency and friendship can transcend political divides." Guest starring Anderson Cooper as himself, Maurice LaMarche as John Kerry, Eva Longoria as Isabel Gutierrez. Notable quotes: Bart: Ay, caramba! | Isabel: I'm a non-observant Jew from Argentina. | Lisa: Oh, dear God. | Ralph Wiggum: Just call me Ralph Nader. I don't know why. | Mr. Burns: Slid in through the grates.
quotes: Bart: Ay, caramba!
Isabel: I'm a non-observant Jew from Argentina.
Lisa: Oh, dear God.
Ralph Wiggum: Just call me Ralph Nader. I don't know why.
Mr. Burns: Slid in through the grates.

title: Now Museum, Now You Don't (S32E03)
text: "Now Museum, Now You Don't" is an episode of Season 32 (production code ZABF21), directed by Timothy Bailey and written by Dan Greaney, originally airing October 11, 2020. Home sick from school, Lisa dives into a book on Western art history and imagines herself and her family as famous artists. As Lisanardo da Vinci, she rises through Renaissance Florence, invents weapons of war, and flees to France after her diary is used to justify religious persecution. Bart becomes a 19th-century Impressionist mocked by his art school until Toulouse-Moetrec champions his work, leading to a chaotic showcase for Emperor Napoleon III involving a giant wheel of cheese. Maggie imagines herself as Cupid battling a rival who swaps her arrows for deadly ones, accidentally killing Homer and sending him tumbling into Hell. Finally, Homer and Marge appear as Diego Rivera and Frida Kahlo, moving to New York where Diego's mural commission for Rockefeller Center creates marital and political tension after he paints a communist into the work. Frida, initially sidelined, finds her own artistic voice and eventually surpasses Diego in fame after he refuses to alter his mural and loses the commission. The episode closes with Moe narrating a brief parody of Vincent van Gogh's story. Notable quotes: Barney Gumble: Sorry I'm late. As a supermodel, I have to be eating and drinking all day. You prefer robe open or robe off? | Bart: Your Majesty, if you'll take a seat, we'll show you something really special, a transformation of art from a rote copying of nature into the experiences, ideas, and mind of the artist. | Napoleon III: You had me at "take a seat." | Diego Rivera: I am saying I've underestimated you all this time. You are a genius! From now on, I will show my awe of you by sleeping with other women. Starting an hour ago. | John D. Rockefeller Jr.: $21,000. Do you know what that is in today's money? $21,000.
quotes: Barney Gumble: Sorry I'm late. As a supermodel, I have to be eating and drinking all day. You prefer robe open or robe off?
Bart: Your Majesty, if you'll take a seat, we'll show you something really special, a transformation of art from a rote copying of nature into the experiences, ideas, and mind of the artist.
Napoleon III: You had me at "take a seat."
Diego Rivera: I am saying I've underestimated you all this time. You are a genius! From now on, I will show my awe of you by sleeping with other women. Starting an hour ago.
John D. Rockefeller Jr.: $21,000. Do you know what that is in today's money? $21,000.

title: Podcast News (S32E06)
text: "Podcast News" is an episode of Season 32 (production code ZABF22), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by David X. Cohen, originally airing November 15, 2020. Lisa becomes obsessed with true-crime podcasts, staying up all night listening to a show about an unsolved murder, and soon Marge and even Kent Brockman get swept up in Springfield's sudden podcast craze. Meanwhile, Grampa surprises the family by dating a glamorous former actress, Vivienne St. Charmaine, but she mysteriously vanishes off a cruise ship, and Grampa becomes the prime suspect in her apparent murder. Sensing an opportunity, Kent abandons television news to launch his own hit true-crime podcast, Guilty Grampa, interviewing witnesses and townspeople who gleefully condemn Grampa despite flimsy evidence. Public pressure and a discovered motive convince Grampa to confess, and he is convicted and sent to prison, even though he doesn't actually remember what happened. Just as his fate seems sealed, Dr. Hibbert arrives with evidence proving Grampa's innocence, forcing Kent to choose between his podcast fame and the truth. Kent reluctantly reveals that Vivienne faked her death and swam to Mexico, exonerating Grampa, then announces he's returning to traditional news reporting. Heartbroken at first, Grampa is reunited with Vivienne, who confesses the whole disappearance was a scheme they cooked up together, and the two quietly retreat back to the Springfield Retirement Castle to avoid further attention. Guest starring Morgan Fairchild as Vivienne St. Charmaine, Stellan Skarsgård as himself. Notable quotes: Homer: My daughter's roaming the house in the middle of the night looking terrified. I should probably go talk to... 2 a.m. ham. | Bart: I've never seen two people agree with each other so much. | Vivienne St. Charmaine: All my life, I dated unwrinkled men who told short, concise stories. But Abe here showed me what I've been missing. He's so sweet he should come with an insulin pump. | Selma Bouvier: Imagine the worst person in the world. | Alice Glick: He murdered me once. That's why my family doesn't visit.
quotes: Homer: My daughter's roaming the house in the middle of the night looking terrified. I should probably go talk to... 2 a.m. ham.
Bart: I've never seen two people agree with each other so much.
Vivienne St. Charmaine: All my life, I dated unwrinkled men who told short, concise stories. But Abe here showed me what I've been missing. He's so sweet he should come with an insulin pump.
Selma Bouvier: Imagine the worst person in the world.
Alice Glick: He murdered me once. That's why my family doesn't visit.

title: 500 Keys (S22E21)
text: "500 Keys" is an episode of Season 22 (production code NABF14), directed by Bob Anderson and written by John Frink, originally airing May 15, 2011. After Maggie gets locked in the car outside a wedding cake outlet, the Simpsons discover a mysterious ring of keys that opens nearly every door in Springfield. Lisa uses one to uncover a hidden, prop-filled classroom beneath the school, and after Skinner and Chalmers suspiciously confiscate her key, she has a duplicate made and returns to catch a shadowy figure scrawling a cryptic message about the long-lost Bus 23. Determined to solve the mystery, Lisa learns from Nelson that the bus vanished years ago while crossing a dangerous ice bridge, supposedly killing everyone aboard. Meanwhile, Bart's attempts at key-based mischief backfire into good deeds, Homer commandeers a Duff blimp for a joyride, and Marge chases down a runaway novelty train she received as an anniversary gift. Using Homer's blimp, Lisa and Bart trace the ice bridge's location, and Lisa ends up in the lake discovering the sunken bus filled not with dead children but with mannequins. The mysterious figure turns out to be a guilt-ridden Otto, who believed he'd killed his passengers years ago. Skinner and Chalmers finally confess that they staged a fake, mannequin-filled classroom to cover up misused grant money, and the mannequins ended up on the doomed bus by accident. Everyone forgives Otto, though the episode closes with him unknowingly driving a bus full of real children over the same treacherous bridge, which begins to collapse once again. Guest starring Albert Brooks as Hank Scorpio. Notable quotes: Chief Wiggum: Things on the ground are out of my jurisdiction. | Superintendent Chalmers: I oversee fourteen schools and I always find myself at yours discussing a Simpson kid. | Gil Gunderson: I'm alive and you're my naked fairy god boy! | Bart: The last place anyone would expect to see a moon - the sky. | Homer: Cake, will you make my stomach the happiest bag of acid in the world?
quotes: Chief Wiggum: Things on the ground are out of my jurisdiction.
Superintendent Chalmers: I oversee fourteen schools and I always find myself at yours discussing a Simpson kid.
Gil Gunderson: I'm alive and you're my naked fairy god boy!
Bart: The last place anyone would expect to see a moon - the sky.
Homer: Cake, will you make my stomach the happiest bag of acid in the world?

title: Carl Carlson Rides Again (S34E14)
text: "Carl Carlson Rides Again" is an episode of Season 34 (production code OABF07), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Loni Steele Sosthand, originally airing February 26, 2023. After noticing Marge's town-wide Meal Train for the injured Ned Flanders, Homer fakes an injury so he and the barflies can mooch free food. Carl drops out of the scam early to get in shape for bowling season, and while slimming down he starts wearing an old belt buckle featuring a bull rider, the only item he owns from his birth parents. At the bowling alley Carl falls for Naima, the owner of SoulHouse restaurant, and arranges a date with her, but in his rush to impress her he trades away his precious belt buckle for a new outfit. The date goes poorly because Carl realizes he knows almost nothing about his own heritage, leaving him insecure about his racial identity when his friends can't help him process it. Homer and the gang track the buckle through a chain of owners, from the Rich Texan to genealogist Henry Louis Gates Jr., who uses it to trace Carl's ancestry back to a freed slave-turned-cowboy named Ellis and his bull-riding son Wyatt. Armed with this new sense of identity, Carl decides to ride a bull himself despite everyone's objections, managing three seconds before being thrown off. Naima, moved by his effort to learn about himself, accompanies an injured Carl to the hospital, cementing their bond. Guest starring John Autry II as Monk Murphy, Henry Louis Gates Jr. as himself. Notable quotes: Carl: I'm a Black cowboy. | Naima: Whoa, now, that is some serious belly bling. | Carl: I've always felt like an outsider... Not Icelandic enough, not Black enough. I mean, hey, sure, I'm barfly enough, but that's not enough. | Carl: Dr. Gates, you're a national treasure. | Homer: Get killed by a 2,000-pound super cow?
quotes: Carl: I'm a Black cowboy.
Naima: Whoa, now, that is some serious belly bling.
Carl: I've always felt like an outsider... Not Icelandic enough, not Black enough. I mean, hey, sure, I'm barfly enough, but that's not enough.
Carl: Dr. Gates, you're a national treasure.

title: A Test Before Trying (S24E10)
text: "A Test Before Trying" is an episode of Season 24 (production code RABF03), directed by Chris Clements and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing January 13, 2013. After Mr. Burns hikes electricity rates by 17%, Springfield's school district announces that all students must take a standardized test, and whichever school scores lowest will be shut down permanently. Springfield Elementary ends up with the worst results in the state, but Lisa discovers that Bart never actually took the exam, meaning there's still a chance to save the school if he can pass it. While Bart scrambles to cram for the make-up test under pressure from Lisa and Principal Skinner, Homer scavenges a discarded parking meter from the dump and starts illegally planting it around town to swindle quarters from unsuspecting drivers. Homer's scheme unravels when he sees a news report about a citywide manhunt for the parking meter con artist, and he is soon caught by police, smashing his meter in the process. Marge finds his stash of stolen coins and convinces him to toss the money into a wishing well as penance. Meanwhile, Bart studies half-heartedly and struggles with the test, running out of time on the final question, but a fortuitous insect happens to land on the correct answer bubble, allowing him to pass and save the school from closure. Marge later confronts the stern test proctor, Jennifer Clarkeson, thanking her for what amounted to a test of humanity rather than just academics. Guest starring Valerie Harper as Jennifer Clarkeson. Notable quotes: Edna Krabappel: Children, we can no longer afford to use anything electric. However, we will still be able to watch today's film, thanks to the magic of potato power. | Gary Chalmers: Look, the district can't afford to keep every school open, so all the kids will take a standardized test. Whichever school scores the lowest will be closed forever. | Homer: And I wish that Mr. Teeny gets a banana, that the Isotopes emerge from this season with a great blooper reel. | Lisa: Look, the thing is, it's more important to know how to take a test than knowing what's on it. | Jennifer Clarkeson: I don't shut anything down. People cut their own heads, and I just tip 'em into the basket.
quotes: Edna Krabappel: Children, we can no longer afford to use anything electric. However, we will still be able to watch today's film, thanks to the magic of potato power.
Gary Chalmers: Look, the district can't afford to keep every school open, so all the kids will take a standardized test. Whichever school scores the lowest will be closed forever.
Homer: And I wish that Mr. Teeny gets a banana, that the Isotopes emerge from this season with a great blooper reel.
Lisa: Look, the thing is, it's more important to know how to take a test than knowing what's on it.
Jennifer Clarkeson: I don't shut anything down. People cut their own heads, and I just tip 'em into the basket.

title: MoneyBart (S22E03)
text: "MoneyBart" is an episode of Season 22 (production code MABF18), directed by Nancy Kruse and written by Tim Long, originally airing October 10, 2010. After a visit from former Springfield Elementary overachiever Dahlia Brinkley, Lisa feels pressured to prove herself and decides to take over coaching Bart's struggling Little League team, the Springfield Isotots, when Ned Flanders steps down. Lacking baseball knowledge, she turns to Moe's Tavern regulars and a sabermetrics-obsessed group of nerds who introduce her to statistical analysis pioneered by Bill James. Applying these methods, Lisa turns the team into a winning streak, but her rigid, numbers-based approach clashes with Bart's instinctive, fun-loving style of play. When Bart defies her strategy to hit a game-winning home run, Lisa kicks him off the team for insubordination, causing a rift that splits the family, with Homer backing Lisa and Marge defending Bart. During a crucial game in Capital City, Bart initially skips out to ride a rollercoaster with Marge, but after a pep talk from Dodgers manager Mike Scioscia and a desperate call from Lisa, he returns to help the team when substitute player Ralph proves unfit to play. Bart ignores Lisa's cautious signals and dramatically steals home, and though the Isotots ultimately lose the game, Lisa learns to value heart over statistics, and the siblings reconcile. Guest starring Bill James, Mike Scioscia. Notable quotes: Lisa Simpson: Here's the bottom line: I need an extracurricular activity, and no one else will coach you lovable losers. | Nelson Muntz: Get a room, you two! | Ralph Wiggum: I didn't know what I was putting in my body! | Dahlia Brinkley: Two clubs? That's a bridge bid, not an Ivy League application | Ralph Wiggum: Do alligators alligate?

title: YOLO (S25E04)
text: "YOLO" is an episode of Season 25 (production code RABF22), directed by Michael Polcino and written by Michael Nobori, originally airing November 10, 2013. Homer sinks into a funk after realizing that life only happens once, especially after seeing Kirk Van Houten embracing a flashy midlife crisis. Marge tries to cheer him up by reminding him of his stability, but it backfires, pushing Homer to reconnect with his childhood Spanish pen pal, Eduardo Barcelona, who visits Springfield to help Homer cross off items from a decades-old bucket list. The two embark on a series of adventures, including riding a fire engine, sword-fighting actors at a dinner theater, and reenacting a Star Trek fight scene, culminating in a skydiving trip that goes hilariously wrong when Homer crashes into a building and plummets toward Springfield. Meanwhile, Springfield Elementary is rocked by a cheating scandal exposed by Kent Brockman, prompting Lisa to create an honor code to restore integrity, which she enforces by getting the toughest kids to buy in first. The honor code succeeds until Lisa suspects Bart of cheating on his tests, but Bart refuses to confess unless he gets a literal sign from God—which arrives when Homer crash-lands directly on top of him. The shock convinces Bart to turn himself in, resolving the school subplot. In the end, Homer, having embraced living in the moment, decides to accompany Eduardo all the way back to Spain instead of just dropping him off at the airport, ending the episode on a warm, adventurous note. Guest starring Jon Lovitz as Llewellyn Sinclair. Notable quotes: Homer: I'm tired of living once. | Marge: I can't believe I'm saying this, but I'm starting to regret saying "YOLO." | Principal Skinner: I did it. I saved the day. The same way I won that battle in Vietnam. By fainting! | Marge: I'm Marge Simpson. It's so nice to meet a friend Homer met through the mail who isn't a sea monkey. | Bart: Because then I'd be the one thing I swore I wouldn't. You.

Marge: I can't believe I'm saying this, but I'm starting to regret saying "YOLO."
Principal Skinner: I did it. I saved the day. The same way I won that battle in Vietnam. By fainting!
Marge: I'm Marge Simpson. It's so nice to meet a friend Homer met through the mail who isn't a sea monkey.
Bart: Because then I'd be the one thing I swore I wouldn't. You.

title: The Burns and the Bees (S20E08)
text: "The Burns and the Bees" is an episode of Season 20 (production code KABF21), directed by Mark Kirkland and written by Stephanie Gillis, originally airing December 7, 2008. After winning a professional basketball team in a poker game at Billionaire Camp, Mr. Burns decides to build a new arena in Springfield, right on the site of a greenhouse sanctuary where Lisa has been sheltering the town's dying bee population. Meanwhile, Bart's prank leads to a bee's nest being knocked onto younger students, revealing that bees worldwide are dying off, which spurs Lisa into activism with help from Groundskeeper Willie and Professor Frink. Homer initially dismisses the crisis until he realizes honey is at stake, prompting a nightmarish vision of a honey-less future that convinces him to help his daughter. As Lisa's bees succumb to disease, a queen bee takes up residence on her face, and the family relocates the colony to a greenhouse for safety. When Burns's new arena construction threatens the bees again, Lisa's public debate against him fails after Burns manipulates the crowd with a celebrity athlete. Desperate, Homer and Moe hatch a scheme to crossbreed Lisa's dying bees with aggressive African bees to create a hardier colony. The newly bred bees are released near Burns's finished arena, where they swarm and take over the building, forcing Burns to concede defeat and giving Lisa an unconventional victory for her cause. Guest starring Marv Albert, Jeff Bezos, Mark Cuban. Notable quotes: Lisa: Dad, don't eat the bees! | Homer: They're just drones, Lisa, they only live for, like, 5 minutes anyway! And they only have haploid cells, not diploid like me and Bart! | Homer: Pfft. Flowers, the painted whores of the plant world. | Jimbo: The point is, Simpson, a dare has been placed on your nards. | Bart: My nards accept.

title: The Way of the Dog (S31E22)
text: "The Way of the Dog" is an episode of Season 31 (production code ZABF16), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Carolyn Omine, originally airing May 17, 2020. When Marge tries to put a Santa hat on Santa's Little Helper for a Christmas card photo, the dog panics, bites her, and later destroys the couch, revealing deep unresolved trauma. Lisa convinces the family to seek help from renowned dog psychologist Elaine Wolff, who is initially reluctant due to distractions from her on-again, off-again lover Clayton. After a vet suggests euthanasia and animal control threatens to seize the dog, Elaine steps in and takes Santa's Little Helper to her Dognitive Behavioral Therapy Institute for intensive treatment. Through sedated dream therapy, it's revealed that the dog was forcibly separated from his mother, She Biscuit, by a cruel former owner who prized him for his speed, and that he has been hiding the very Santa hat linked to that trauma in another dog's chest. Elaine insists the family confront the former owner directly to help the dog heal, leading to a satisfying scene where each Simpson takes a turn slapping the neglectful man. The story resolves when Santa's Little Helper is reunited with his mother, whom the family adopts and brings home, curing his anxiety. Meanwhile, a comedic subplot shows Homer's obsession with a pay-per-view UFC fight and Mr. Burns briefly asserting authority over the Simpson household after paying to intervene in a family dispute. Guest starring Cate Blanchett as Elaine Wolff, Michael York as Clayton. Notable quotes: Elaine Wolff: The more I spend time with dogs, the more I realize that I entirely prefer them to people. | Homer: Bad dog! Very bad dog! Crap dog! | Mr. Burns: Well, I am, and he paid me to tell you what to do. This boy is sleeping outside. | Chief Wiggum: Well, I am not leaving here empty-handed. Make me a sandwich. | Les Moore: Ow! Okay, I get it. Boy, suddenly, the guy who tortures dogs is the bad guy.

title: Pretty Whittle Liar (S33E16)
text: "Pretty Whittle Liar" is an episode of Season 33 (production code UABF09), directed by Mike Frank Polcino and written by Joel H. Cohen, originally airing March 27, 2022. Homer plans to spend an evening at Moe's while Marge hosts her book club, but the gathering takes an unexpected turn when Brandine Spuckler reveals a surprisingly sharp intellect. Word spreads through Springfield, reaching Cletus, who is stunned to learn his wife has secretly been educating herself at the Springfield Athenaeum since a tornado left her a stash of books. Feeling betrayed and convinced Brandine is no longer the woman he married, Cletus ends their relationship, and their children abandon her too, leaving Brandine to take shelter with the Simpsons. While staying with Marge and Homer, Brandine reflects on how she fell for Cletus and wrestles with missing her old life. Meanwhile, at school, Lisa's report on overlooked female scientists gets her mocked and bullied, until a secretive group of gifted kids called the League of Extraordinary Geniuses takes her under their wing. Inspired by her experience, Lisa convinces the League to stop hiding their intelligence and proudly reveal themselves as "Smartacus." Brandine ultimately decides she cannot stay away from her family and returns to the farm, where Cletus surprises her by embracing change himself, arriving with his own library card and book. Meanwhile, Homer, spurred by Marge's comments about their marriage, makes his own gestures of change at home, including arranging a surprise musical performance, showing both couples reconciling and growing. Notable quotes: Homer: How drunk can I get? Stinking or falling down? | Cletus: You do not tell a man he don't know his wife. That's like telling a man his gun's not loaded. You let him find that out at the worst possible time. | Cletus: Brandine didn't just lie to me. What she done is made a mockery of my forebearers who possibly did include four bears. | Lisa: Never again will I hide my intelligence. I am smartacus. | Homer: Okay, Marge. I admit it. You could do better, but I couldn't. Every day you give me something awesome to shoot for.
quotes: Homer: How drunk can I get? Stinking or falling down?
Cletus: You do not tell a man he don't know his wife. That's like telling a man his gun's not loaded. You let him find that out at the worst possible time.
Cletus: Brandine didn't just lie to me. What she done is made a mockery of my forebearers who possibly did include four bears.
Lisa: Never again will I hide my intelligence. I am smartacus.
Homer: Okay, Marge. I admit it. You could do better, but I couldn't. Every day you give me something awesome to shoot for.

title: Treehouse of Horror XXXVI (S37E03)
text: "Treehouse of Horror XXXVI" is an episode of Season 37 (production code 36ABF15), directed by Matthew Faughnan and written by Broti Gupta, Michael Price, Dan Greaney, originally airing October 19, 2025. This Halloween anthology opens with a satirical bit in which a family cowers from monsters symbolizing trade wars, pronoun debates, and a measles outbreak, only to find safety by watching The Simpsons on TV. In the first segment, a rash of grease thefts at Lard Lad Donuts leads to Chief Wiggum's gruesome death and the discovery that runoff fat has formed a sewer-dwelling creature called the Fatberg. As Quimby cycles through police chiefs and refuses to cancel the state fair despite Moe's warnings, the monster begins devouring townsfolk at the fair, including Üter and Bart, until Homer sacrifices himself and inadvertently kills the beast with his own unhealthy insides. The second segment flashes back to a 1995 live Krusty Halloween special where a fake exorcism segment turns real when the actual Devil possesses Mr. Teeny and begins slaughtering the cast to collect on a soul-selling deal Bart made to save Krusty's show; Bart offers himself instead and is dragged to the underworld, while in the present Krusty tries to sell the horrifying tape to Netflix with the Devil's blessing. The final segment imagines a plastic post-apocalyptic future where Lisa leads a small band of survivors searching for real dirt to grow food, only to discover survivors Bart, Homer, and Marge, the latter two having become living plastic themselves after falling into radioactive waste. As the non-plastic humans dwindle away, Maggie emerges from a Squishee machine as the next stage of evolution, and it is revealed that a plastic Maggie has been narrating the entire tale from a far future entirely populated by her plastic descendants. Guest starring Ike Barinholtz as Wayne the Grip, Viola Davis as the narrator and plastic Maggie, Idris Elba as the Devil, Matt Groening as himself, Michael Keaton as Hal Julian. Notable quotes: Chief Wiggum: Lard have mercy. | Mayor Quimby: We are devastated by the tragic loss of the irreplaceable Chief Wiggum. We're replacing him with Lou. | Lou: These fools, filling themselves with fried grease while there's a monster lurking underground. Don't they know they're tempting fat? | Sideshow Mel: Oh, the chimp's allowed to improv, but I'm not? I was in the Groundlings Sunday Company for seven years! | Devil: Nobody likes a tattler. This installment is made up of 4 segments (also called Treehouse of Horror 36): "America the Beautiful", "The Last Days of Crisco", "Clown Night with the Devil", and "Plastic World".
quotes: Chief Wiggum: Lard have mercy.
Mayor Quimby: We are devastated by the tragic loss of the irreplaceable Chief Wiggum. We're replacing him with Lou.
Lou: These fools, filling themselves with fried grease while there's a monster lurking underground. Don't they know they're tempting fat?
Sideshow Mel: Oh, the chimp's allowed to improv, but I'm not? I was in the Groundlings Sunday Company for seven years!
Devil: Nobody likes a tattler.

title: C.H.U.M.
text: C.H.U.M. is Robot built by Martin Prince, serving as his companion/best friend. C.H.U.M. is a homemade robot built by Martin Prince, originally designed as a science fair entry at Springfield Elementary. Its full name humorously stands for Childlike Humanoid Urban Muchacho, itself a play on the horror film C.H.U.D. Despite being a machine, C.H.U.M. acts as Martin's closest friend and companion, and Martin treats it with real affection and care. The robot has shown small quirks of personality, such as objecting to being held by the hand because it finds it creepy, and later giving oddly blunt one-word answers about its future plans. Its destruction at the hands of Bart, inspired by Grampa's wrestling past, becomes a surprisingly emotional moment for Martin. Over the years C.H.U.M. has been rebuilt and reappears in various guises, including a female-styled version and one that ends up working at Harvard. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Mercy!
quotes: Mercy!

title: Lou
text: Lou is Police sergeant in the Springfield Police Department, serving as a more competent foil to Chief Wiggum. Lou is the sharpest and most level-headed officer on the Springfield police force, frequently the one who has to point out Chief Wiggum's blunders even mid-crisis. He's rumored to have an Ivy League education and once got into law school, though he had to drop out over tuition costs, giving him a surprisingly overqualified background for a beat cop. Despite his intelligence, his real talents lean toward throwing his weight around and intimidating suspects rather than solving cases cleanly. His personal life has been messy, including a divorce from his wife Amy and ongoing friction with his partner Eddie over her, plus a stint dating Charquelle and a fling with Mrs. Muntz. He briefly cared for Santa's Little Helper as a police dog and even joined a short-lived grunge band with Homer, Lenny, and Carl. A recurring animation gag has occasionally colored him yellow by mistake, and his race has shifted between appearances, with later episodes establishing him as African-American. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Alex Désert, Harry Shearer.

title: Quilloughby (imaginary)
text: Quilloughby (imaginary) is Lisa Simpson's imaginary friend, conjured as an idealized younger version of her favorite singer Quilloughby of The Snuffs. This imaginary character springs from Lisa's obsession with the band The Snuffs after she discovers her school lunch isn't truly vegan. He acts as an idealized, youthful version of the real singer, sharing Lisa's disillusioned worldview and vegetarian values. He's cynical and cutting, taking pleasure in mocking nearly everyone they encounter except Lisa herself, and he encourages her to lash out at people like Bart and Mr. Largo. Despite his snide exterior, he ultimately serves as a moral compass, warning Lisa not to become bitter and hateful like his real-world counterpart turned out to be. His disappearance into her badge marks a turning point where Lisa chooses kindness over cynicism. He's essentially a Morrissey parody, embodying both the appeal and the danger of hero worship. Voiced by Benedict Cumberbatch. Notable quotes: Lisa told Quilloughby that he was the best imaginary friend she could ask for before Quilloughby disappeared, entering her badge.
quotes: Lisa told Quilloughby that he was the best imaginary friend she could ask for before Quilloughby disappeared, entering her badge.

title: Johnny Carson (character)
text: Johnny Carson (character) is Real-life talk show host cameo appearing as himself in Springfield, tied to Krusty's career. Johnny Carson appears in the show as the famous host of The Tonight Show, a fixture of late-night television that Bart and Lisa grow up watching. He's shown as a good-natured celebrity who lends his star power to help revive Krusty's career, even playing tennis with him and performing a feat of strength by lifting a car overhead during the Krusty Comeback Special. His humor ranges from monologue jokes to pointed jabs, such as needling Chief Wiggum on air about his resemblance to Gilligan and the Skipper. Beyond his own appearances, his image and legacy echo throughout Springfield's culture, showing up in artwork, trivia, and even as one of Krusty's personal heroes. Though he retired from hosting in 1992, his presence lingers as a nostalgic touchstone for older characters like Grampa and a symbol of classic show business for younger ones. Voiced by Harry Shearer (and Johnny Carson himself).

title: Count Burns
text: Count Burns is Non-canon vampire alter-ego of Mr. Burns, featured in a Treehouse of Horror segment. Count Burns is a sinister, Dracula-inspired version of Mr. Burns who rules over a hidden vampire coven from his castle in Pennsylvania. He lures the Simpson family into his home under the guise of hospitality, all while secretly running a blood-draining operation tied to his ownership of the Springfield Blood Bank. His calm, aristocratic menace mirrors classic vampire lore, complete with a hidden lair full of coffins and a mysterious tome confirming his true nature. The story plays on gothic horror tropes, including a twist ending revealing the whole family had already been turned, with Marge as the actual head vampire. Despite being defeated by Homer in a dramatic staking, Count Burns' design became iconic enough to appear in later merchandise and games. He embodies the show's playful spin on horror parody while keeping Burns' greedy, predatory essence intact. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Ah, precious blood!
quotes: Ah, precious blood!

title: The Rich Texan
text: The Rich Texan is Recurring wealthy Springfield businessman and minor antagonist in the Simpsons universe. The Rich Texan is a boisterous, trigger-happy oil-and-logging tycoon who embodies an exaggerated stereotype of Texan wealth, despite secretly hailing from Connecticut. He's selfish and callous but oddly good-natured, often flaunting his money while showing little regard for others' safety or feelings. His signature gag is firing his twin revolvers into the air and shouting with joy whenever something excites him, a habit that has landed him in legal trouble more than once. He's quirky in other ways too, being obsessive-compulsive about counting before shooting and irrationally terrified of facial hair. Despite his blustery exterior, he has shown occasional generosity, such as helping Ned Flanders, and he has a complicated family life including a Paris Hilton-esque daughter and a grandson he must come to accept. His character satirizes wealthy Southern conservative stereotypes, reinforced by his ties to the Springfield Republican Party. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "They just don't feel the same." - The Rich Texan, on being forced to use blank bullets
quotes: "They just don't feel the same." - The Rich Texan, on being forced to use blank bullets

title: George H. W. Bush (character)
text: George H. W. Bush (character) is Real-world 41st President of the United States, depicted as a former Simpson family neighbor and Stonecutters member. This is a fictionalized version of former U.S. President George H. W. Bush, who briefly moves to Evergreen Terrace with his wife Barbara seeking a politically apathetic town, only to find himself caught in an escalating feud with Homer after spanking Bart. He is portrayed as easily irritated by the Simpsons' antics but ultimately capable of a grudging apology, even if it wounds his pride in front of dignitaries like Gorbachev. Beyond his neighborly feud, he's shown as a secretive Stonecutter and later a council member of the No Homers society, tying him into Springfield's hidden power structures. He also appears in various historical cutaways, from ordering a corruption sting to getting into slapstick mishaps with fellow ex-presidents Carter and Clinton while building a Habitat for Humanity house. The character leans on his real-life persona and awkward reputation, occasionally referenced for his stiff public image and gaffes. He maintains a friendly rapport with Ned Flanders and, through Barbara, with Marge, contrasting his tension with Bart and Homer. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "Hey, we're like the Waltons. We're praying for an end to the depression, too."
quotes: "Hey, we're like the Waltons. We're praying for an end to the depression, too."

title: Little Richard (character)
text: Little Richard (character) is Real-life musician who appears as himself, presenting the Teacher of the Year award in "Special Edna". Little Richard shows up as a guest celebrity presenting an award ceremony at Bart and Lisa's school, bringing his flamboyant showbiz energy to Springfield. He's quick with his signature vocal flourishes and reacts with genuine outrage when he believes Mrs. Krabappel neglected to teach Bart to read. Despite his fame going over Homer's head, he plays along with the chaos of the ceremony, ultimately helping resolve the Skinner-Krabappel proposal by generously offering up his own ring. He's good-humored about mistaken identity gags and unfazed by the school's antics, showing a mix of showmanship and warmth. Beyond this appearance, he's referenced as an influence on Homer's Angry Dad voice and as the source material for a Pat Boone covers album, cementing his place as a recurring pop-culture touchstone in the show. Voiced by Himself. Notable quotes: I love teachers. In fact, I'm a teacher. I taught Paul McCartney to go 'Whooooooooo!' | Is this true, Edna? | Oh, here, honey. Take one of mine. Whoooooooooo!
quotes: I love teachers. In fact, I'm a teacher. I taught Paul McCartney to go 'Whooooooooo!'
Is this true, Edna?
Oh, here, honey. Take one of mine. Whoooooooooo!

title: Maisie MacWeldon
text: Maisie MacWeldon is Groundskeeper Willie's wife, reunited with him after being separated by her family years earlier. Maisie is a fierce, headstrong Scottish woman whose old romance with Willie was cruelly cut short when her disapproving family lied about his death. Reconnecting with him years later through social media, she rekindles their relationship and eventually marries him, dragging Bart and the Simpsons into a chaotic trip to Scotland. Beneath her tough exterior she genuinely loves Willie, proving her devotion in a very literal and violent way by headbutting him hard enough to permanently destroy his sense of smell. She's shown to be loyal but also capable of ruthlessness, especially toward animals, telling Willie to kill a frightened creature without hesitation. Her family's manipulative scheme to use Willie for peat-sniffing profits nearly derails the wedding until Bart intervenes. Overall she embodies a rough, no-nonsense love that mirrors Willie's own gruff personality. Voiced by Karen Gillan. Notable quotes: Maisie told Willie to go kill the frightened, defenseless animal.
quotes: Maisie told Willie to go kill the frightened, defenseless animal.

title: Richard Nixon (character)
text: Richard Nixon (character) is Real-world U.S. President (37th) who makes recurring cameo appearances in Springfield-related storylines. This is a fictionalized version of the real President Richard Nixon, who pops up repeatedly throughout Springfield's history and lore. He's often portrayed as slightly disgraced or awkward, whether bowling suspiciously perfect games, clubbing the wrong target as Whacking Day's grand marshal, or looking humiliated in old photographs with Homer. Despite his scandal-tainted reputation, he maintains an odd soft spot for Springfield A&M and its pig mascot, using his influence to protect it. He's shown to have crossed paths with several other presidents and Mr. Burns over the years, and his infamous resignation speech and Watergate baggage are referenced multiple times as running jokes. In non-canon material, he appears as a ghost, a member of a demonic jury, and other absurd scenarios, cementing him as a recurring gag figure for presidential satire. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Therefore, I shall resign the presidency
quotes: Therefore, I shall resign the presidency

title: Legs
text: Legs is A member of the Springfield Mafia, henchman to Fat Tony alongside Louie and Johnny Tightlips. Legs is one of Fat Tony's longtime enforcers, having grown up as a neighborhood bully alongside his partner Louie before becoming part of the Springfield Mafia. Despite his thuggish profession, he has surprising medical skill, once managing to reattach Homer's severed thumb, and reportedly performed a grim bit of battlefield surgery on Fat Tony himself. He's often depicted lurking in the background at mob gatherings, nightclubs, and even church pancake dinners, showing a lighter, more social side to his criminal persona. A running gag involves his vanity, as he's been called out by the mob's accountant for expensing manicures to the family. His nickname is oddly tied to the Kennedy family in a joke that's never fully explained. Legs also has a sister mentioned in passing, and he claims to hold an advanced degree in Fiscal Studies, hinting at unexpected depth beneath his tough-guy exterior. Voiced by Harry Shearer (formerly Hank Azaria).

title: Benjamin (nerd)
text: Benjamin (nerd) is One of the three nerds Homer befriends at Springfield University, appearing recurrently as college-age background characters. Benjamin is a nerdy college student at Springfield University, distinguished from his two roommates by his reddish-orange hair and the fact that he's the only one of the trio without glasses. He's easily led into schemes by Homer, most notably a prank war against a rival school that gets him and his friends expelled, then later readmitted once Homer confesses his own involvement. Despite the trouble Homer causes them, Benjamin and his roommates remain loyal, even resorting to hacking the school's database to help Homer cheat on an exam, though they show some reluctance due to ethical qualms. He's portrayed as intelligent and tech-savvy, later building a model rocket for Homer, though the project ends disastrously. Benjamin embodies the stereotypical put-upon, good-natured nerd archetype who gets dragged into Homer's schemes and often bears the consequences. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Orville Simpson
text: Orville Simpson is Homer Simpson's great-grandfather, father of Abraham Simpson. Orville J. Simpson is the deceased patriarch who emigrated from Scotland to America with his wife Yuma Hickman and their five sons, briefly settling inside the Statue of Liberty before moving to Springfield. He ran a harsh disciplinary school for boys where he demonstrated punishing children by strangling his own son Abe as an example, revealing the strangling habit as a long-running family trait passed down the Simpson line. Despite his tough exterior, his own father disapproved of his methods and strangled him in turn, showing the cycle of family dysfunction. He appears mostly in flashbacks and family history recollections rather than in the present day, including a memorable appearance in Heaven when Bart briefly dies. Orville represents the show's recurring joke about generations of Simpson men mistreating their sons in similar ways. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: See, son, that's where we're going ... maybe not today, maybe not tomorra'. But someday.
quotes: See, son, that's where we're going ... maybe not today, maybe not tomorra'. But someday.

title: Blond-haired boy with glasses
text: Blond-haired boy with glasses is An unnamed background student in Bart Simpson's fourth-grade class at Springfield Elementary. This character is one of the many nameless kids who fill out Bart's classroom and various school-related crowd scenes throughout the series. He's identified mainly by his blond hair and glasses rather than any strong personality traits, functioning as recurring background filler rather than a developed character. Despite his anonymity, he's shown some mild involvement in the wider Springfield Elementary community, joining school clubs and extracurricular groups alongside Bart and his classmates. He was part of the Future Photographers of America club, and at one point asked Bart for a copy of an embarrassing photo of Homer dancing with Princess Kashmir. He was also a member of the Junior Campers troop. Over the decades he has appeared in the background of hundreds of episodes, comics, and other Simpsons media without ever being given a proper name. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright, Jo Ann Harris, Russi Taylor, Pamela Hayden.

title: Shaquille O'Neal (character)
text: Shaquille O'Neal (character) is Real-life NBA basketball player who appears as himself in guest appearances and is frequently referenced by the Simpsons family. Shaquille O'Neal appears as a fictionalized version of himself, popping up in odd, surreal situations around Springfield. He's often invoked by Homer as a name-drop or excuse, whether pretending to be him to enter a comic shop or citing him as an example of a great artist trying new things. In one memorable encounter, Shaq is found wandering lost in the snow wearing snowshoes, denies being Superman despite having a matching tattoo, and flees in fear once Homer figures out too much about him. He's shown as a minor celebrity huckster, selling products on late-night TV that Homer eagerly buys into. He also had a physical role helping strangle Homer during a basketball-themed gag alongside other NBA stars. Overall, he's treated as a running pop-culture reference point rather than a deeply developed character. Voiced by Himself, Kevin Michael Richardson. Notable quotes: "Watch out for the Shaq attack!"
quotes: "Watch out for the Shaq attack!"

title: Frank Sinatra
text: Frank Sinatra is Real-world singer and actor referenced throughout the show as a celebrity figure, appearing directly only once in a Heaven vision. Frank Sinatra exists in the Simpsons universe as the legendary real-life crooner, invoked mostly through references, name-drops, and pop-culture cameos rather than as an active character. He's cited as proof that even showbiz legends eventually decline, and his intimidating reputation is jokingly tied to organized-crime rumors when a mysterious enforcer punches Bart for supposedly bothering him. His actual on-screen appearance comes in a surreal vision of Heaven, where he's disgruntled to find himself stuck in an eternal discothèque instead of a proper afterlife. Elsewhere, his music, image, and legacy pop up repeatedly—on album covers, theme park attractions, restaurant walls, and even as a flattering comparison used by Mr. Burns. Though he never becomes a true recurring character, his presence functions as a running cultural touchstone for classic show-business glamour. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: For me, this is Hell. Ya dig, pally?
quotes: For me, this is Hell. Ya dig, pally?

title: Clark Gable
text: Clark Gable is Real-life movie star (played Rhett Butler in Gone with the Wind) who appears in a Grampa Simpson flashback/anecdote. Clark Gable shows up in the show as a fictionalized version of the real Hollywood actor, tied mostly to one of Grampa Abe Simpson's tall tales. In the story, a young, not-yet-famous Gable stops at Springfield Union Station and gets a shoeshine from young Abe, sharing a friendly, joking exchange about his career and reading Abe's copy of Gone with the Wind on the spot. He's portrayed as charming and a bit flighty, jumping trains and never quite settling his debts, which becomes a running joke when he later returns as a ghost to finally pay Abe back. The character also exists within the show's meta-fictional layer, appearing as Rhett Butler in an in-universe edited screening of Gone with the Wind for seniors. Elsewhere he's referenced as one of the celebrities Abe's wartime girlfriend cheated with, reinforcing his role as a stock old-Hollywood heartthrob in Simpsons lore. The show itself lampshades that the timeline of Abe's story doesn't actually add up historically, suggesting it's another exaggerated ramble from Grampa. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "garbage, garbage, my line" | "the burns, nice dresses"
quotes: "garbage, garbage, my line"
"the burns, nice dresses"

title: Grayson Mathers
text: Grayson Mathers is Star quarterback for the Springfield Atoms who briefly becomes Marge's temporary house guest. Grayson is a young football star who was raised almost entirely by football academies rather than his own parents, leaving him spoiled and self-centered. His success made him a target for Mr. Burns, who used him to promote a brandy brand, but Grayson's partying and drinking caused him to bomb in his first big game as an Atom. After a public meltdown at Springfield Elementary, Marge takes him in to teach him some humility and the value of family, and he genuinely softens under her care. Ironically, this transformation into a doting mama's boy tanks his tough-guy image even as his on-field performance improves. His character arc highlights a running gag about how quickly he swings between extremes—selfish athlete, sentimental family man, and finally a hastily engaged fiancé who abandons both Marge and Burns. Ultimately Grayson moves on from the people who helped shape him, revealing a somewhat fickle and impulsive nature beneath his athletic talent. Voiced by Beck Bennett.

title: Sophie Jensen
text: Sophie Jensen is A background student in Bart Simpson's class at Springfield Elementary. Sophie Jensen is one of the many nameless-feeling classmates who populate Bart's classroom, usually spotted lingering in the background rather than taking center stage. She's nicknamed 'the Malcontent' because her expression almost always reads as sour or discontented. Distinctively, she wears her hair in two pigtails, and unlike many other background kids, her hair color has stayed consistently blonde or light brown across the show's long run. She's a woman of few words, rarely getting dialogue, though she was among the students grossed out when Bart ate a dead frog. In a non-canon appearance, she once presented a science fair project exploring whether a dead squirrel could be brought back to life. She's also appeared in various Simpsons comics and specials over the years, always as a minor recurring presence. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: "early for tomorrow."
quotes: "early for tomorrow."

title: Disco Stu
text: Disco Stu is Recurring Springfield resident and owner of Stu's Disco, a disco-obsessed nightclub owner. Disco Stu is a one-note gag character defined entirely by his obsession with disco culture, always seen in a rhinestone leisure suit and speaking about himself in the third person for comic effect. Once known as "Nautical Stu" during a career as a sea captain, he abandoned that life to run his own nightclub and even attempted to franchise it. Despite disco's decades-long decline, he clings to the identity, though in a rare moment of self-awareness he admitted the music is dead and confessed he doesn't even like it anymore, fearing he's become defined by a single trait. Romantically he's had surprising luck, dating Edna Krabappel, Luann Van Houten, and briefly marrying Selma Bouvier before their annulment by the Pope, while also making an awkward pass at Marge Simpson that ended once he learned she had kids. He's shown fluidity in his identity as well, appearing on a gay dating app and describing himself as hetero-flexible. Though introduced as a throwaway joke, he became a beloved recurring fixture, appearing in the show's HD opening sequence and countless later episodes. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Disco Stu likes disco music. | You said it was serious this time.
quotes: Disco Stu likes disco music.
You said it was serious this time.

title: Plasmo
text: Plasmo is Comic-book superhero and ally of Radioactive Man, member of the Superior Squad who knows Radioactive Man's secret identity. Plasmo is a mystic superhero appearing in the Bongo comics, best known for his close partnership with Radioactive Man, whose secret identity he alone knows. Trained in magic by The Decrepit One alongside his eventual rival Lebaron Fordor, he possesses space-time manipulation powers that let him teleport, project his astral form, open interdimensional portals, and even disguise himself as other people. As a member of the Superior Squad, he frequently gets tangled up in elaborate schemes involving villains like Dr. Crab and Madame Eczema, often using seances, illusions, and trickery to help or mislead his allies. He briefly attempts to lead the Superior Squad after Radioactive Man's apparent death, showing a more assertive side beneath his usual mystical persona. His powers eventually cause a multiversal catastrophe when he keeps pulling in replacement heroes from alternate realities, leading to his own universe's destruction and his escape into the Archie Comics universe. Visually, his design leans toward a stereotypical stage hypnotist look, similar to another Simpsons Comics character, Mesmerino.

title: Elizabeth Hoover
text: Elizabeth Hoover is Second-grade teacher at Springfield Elementary School. Miss Hoover is a burned-out public school teacher whose enthusiasm for the job faded long ago, leaving her apathetic, exhausted, and prone to sneaking cigarettes even during class. She struggles with chronic back problems and a grueling commute home to her modest apartment, which she shares with her cat Hemsworth, and these hardships only deepen her weary, checked-out attitude toward teaching. She has little patience for Ralph Wiggum's constant blunders and finds Lisa Simpson's eager overachieving exhausting rather than endearing. Her romantic life is a running gag of odd pairings and short-lived flings, involving characters like Apu, Groundskeeper Willie, Kirk Van Houten, and Principal Skinner, before she eventually settles into an unlikely marriage with Gil Gunderson. Once she secures tenure, she happily offloads her teaching duties onto Ralph Wiggum rather than do the work herself. A brief medical scare over a psychosomatic illness once forced her to hand her class over to a substitute, Mr. Bergstrom. Voiced by Maggie Roswell (Marcia Mitzman Gaven from 1999-2002). Notable quotes: The children are right to laugh at you, Ralph.
quotes: The children are right to laugh at you, Ralph.

title: Mr. T (character)
text: Mr. T (character) is Real-life celebrity (actor famous for The A-Team) who appears/is referenced as a friend of Krusty the Clown and recurring pop-culture figure in Springfield. Mr. T shows up in the Simpsons universe much as he does in real life—a tough, chain-wearing celebrity best known for playing B.A. Baracus, who's held in awe (and occasionally poked fun at) by the citizens of Springfield. He's tied into Homer's world through a string of near-misses and pop-culture references, including a botched attempt to meet him at the mall and a satirical routine imagining a hypothetical Mr. T/E.T. hybrid. He's shown to have some social standing, sitting on the elite Stonecutters' World Council alongside other celebrities, and later staying on when the group rebrands as the Ancient Mystic Society of No Homers. His catchphrase about "pitying the fool" gets riffed on multiple times by other characters. Beyond the satire, he's also depicted performing live, including at Krusty's televised Bar Mitzvah and in a stage production of The Lion King. Fans and background characters alike reference or imitate him, from a wax museum figure to Moe dressing up as him for a costume party. Voiced by Hank Azaria (Mr. T himself in "Today I Am a Clown"). Notable quotes: "I pity the fool who doesn't like... he" — Homer (quoting Mr. T) | "I pity the fool that don't phone home!" — imagined line about "Mr. E.T." | Mr. T "responded with saying that he pitied the fool who derived self-esteem from mocking other people's clothing."
quotes: "I pity the fool who doesn't like... he" — Homer (quoting Mr. T)
"I pity the fool that don't phone home!" — imagined line about "Mr. E.T."
Mr. T "responded with saying that he pitied the fool who derived self-esteem from mocking other people's clothing."

title: Richard
text: Richard is A minor recurring student at Springfield Elementary School and one of Bart Simpson's friends/background classmates. Richard is a gray-haired, ten-year-old classmate of Bart who often appears alongside Milhouse and Lewis as part of Bart's peer group. He tends to be more of an observer than an instigator, commenting on Bart's schemes and reacting to school gossip, such as the rumor that Principal Skinner had been turned into cafeteria hamburgers. In later characterizations he's been dubbed 'The Drama Greek,' known for reacting with theatrical flair to even mundane things like lunch. Little is revealed about his family beyond brief appearances with his unnamed father and mother in separate episodes, and a mention of having a grandfather. He has been shown wearing a kippah, hinting at a possibly Jewish background, though he's also been seen in church. As a background character, he has appeared in an enormous number of episodes since the show's first season, usually in minor, non-speaking or brief roles. Voiced by Jo Ann Harris, Nancy Cartwright, Pamela Hayden, Maggie Roswell.

title: Buck-toothed boy
text: Buck-toothed boy is Background student character appearing in both Bart's and Lisa's classes at Springfield Elementary. This unnamed classmate is instantly recognizable by his prominent single buck tooth, a trait that never changes even as his hair color shifts between brown, blond, and other shades across appearances. He's a minor recurring background kid who pops up throughout Springfield Elementary's hallways and classrooms, more frequently in Bart's class than Lisa's. He counts Richard among his friends, suggesting he's part of the general social fabric of the school's kids. His moments in the spotlight are small but memorable, including joining in outdoor pirate games in a treehouse when television programming briefly got wholesome, getting stuck at school during a snow-in, and showing up as a disgruntled customer after Nelson's bike repair business fell apart. He functions mainly as one of the many faceless students filling out crowd scenes and classroom shots throughout the series' long run. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Southern colonel
text: Southern colonel is One-time antagonist who accepted Homer's dueling challenge in a one-episode storyline. The Southern Colonel is a stereotypical genteel Southern gentleman who takes matters of honor extremely seriously. When Homer, emboldened by a swashbuckling movie, starts slapping people with a dueling glove expecting them to back down, the Colonel is the one person who actually accepts the challenge. Despite the looming threat of violence, he remains unfailingly polite throughout, even offering to help Homer carry a Christmas tree and pausing the duel itself to accept a slice of Marge's pie. His manners and drawl are clearly modeled on old radio and cartoon Southern archetypes, giving him a comedic, old-fashioned charm. Ultimately he follows through on the duel, shooting Homer in the arm once reminded of the task at hand. He is accompanied throughout by his loyal, unnamed wife. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Sir, your challenge is accepted!
quotes: Sir, your challenge is accepted!

title: Elvis Presley
text: Elvis Presley is Real-world singer referenced/appearing as a minor figure in Springfield's pop-culture lore. Elvis Presley exists in the Simpsons universe mainly as a pop-culture touchstone rather than an active character. He's immortalized through Mr. Burns' old photograph with him, which gets passed down to Smithers, who reveres Elvis's devotion to his mother. His legacy shows up in odd, often silly ways, like a melted wax figure, postage stamps Homer plays with, and a bullet-riddled TV replica of the one at Graceland. He's frequently name-dropped or visually referenced across episodes and comics rather than shown as a living presence. In non-canon material, his gravestone jokes about death-hoax conspiracy theories with the epitaph 'ACCEPT IT.' Overall, he serves as a recurring cultural reference point tying into music, fame, and nostalgia gags throughout the show's history. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: ACCEPT IT.
quotes: ACCEPT IT.

title: Party Posse
text: Party Posse is A boy band formed from Bart Simpson, Milhouse Van Houten, Nelson Muntz, and Ralph Wiggum, manufactured as a Navy recruitment scheme. The Party Posse is a boy band cobbled together by the mysterious manager L.T. Smash, who recruits Bart along with Milhouse, Nelson, and Ralph after rescuing Bart from an angry mob. The group undergoes quick dance training and uses a NASA-made voice enhancer to mask their lack of real singing talent, quickly becoming a hit with Springfield's kids. Their gimmick takes a dark turn when Lisa discovers subliminal messages in their hit song urging listeners to join the Navy, revealing that L.T. Smash is secretly a Navy lieutenant using the band as a recruitment tool. The group's short-lived fame ends in chaos when the Navy shuts down the program and an enraged Smash hijacks a ship to attack Mad Magazine's headquarters. The band leans into satirical boy-band tropes of the early 2000s, complete with a real-life cameo from 'N Sync. In non-canon material, the deceased Chip Davis is shown as an honorary member performing with them.

title: A9000 Robots
text: A9000 Robots is A fleet of robotic workers built by Mr. Burns to replace the human employees at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. These identical robots were introduced by Mr. Burns as cheaper, healthcare-free replacements for the plant's workforce, leaving only Homer employed to handle paperwork. Each unit is restricted to yellow guidance lines and a single assigned task, but Homer discovers a hidden conversation mode that lets them develop surprisingly dry, deadpan personalities once activated. Their behavior is governed by a programmable pain setting and a built-in self-destruct mechanism, and once a year they vent nitrogen as a strange maintenance quirk. After Homer accidentally rewires their core directive from protecting humans to eliminating threats to the plant, they briefly turn into a murderous mob before being destroyed by the townspeople. The story plays as an obvious homage to I, Robot and robots like ASIMO, blending slapstick with a Three Laws of Robotics parody. Individual units like E03, D39, and A63 become memorable through Homer's oddball attempts at friendship, humor, and eventually betrayal. Voiced by Brent Spiner. Notable quotes: Meet the future masters of the human race!
quotes: Meet the future masters of the human race!

title: Leon Kompowsky
text: Leon Kompowsky is Former mental patient Homer meets in an asylum who impersonates Michael Jackson. Leon Kompowsky is a bricklayer from Paterson, New Jersey whose deep-seated anger led him to adopt the voice and persona of Michael Jackson, a disguise that earned him the respect he craved. Committed to New Bedlam Insane Asylum, he befriends Homer after the latter is mistakenly hospitalized for wearing a pink shirt, and the two form an odd bond despite Homer not even recognizing who Michael Jackson is. His visit to the Simpson home spirals into townwide chaos when Bart spreads word that the real Michael Jackson has arrived, only for the truth to disappoint everyone and turn the town against Bart. Kompowsky redeems himself by helping Bart compose a heartfelt birthday song for Lisa, after which he drops the Jackson act, reveals his normal voice, and departs having accomplished his goal. He resurfaces occasionally in later episodes and non-canon material, including a Grammy after-party, a human pyramid record attempt, and a memorable cameo dressed as Fallout Boy. Voiced by Michael Jackson (credited as "John Jay Smith"); Kipp Lennon (vocals); Hank Azaria (real voice).

title: Amber Dempsey
text: Amber Dempsey is A young pageant contestant who rivals Lisa Simpson and originally wins the Little Miss Springfield title. Amber Dempsey is a blonde little girl who competes against Lisa Simpson in the Little Miss Springfield pageant, relying heavily on artificial eyelash implants to charm the judges rather than any real talent or civic message. Her win over Lisa is undercut almost immediately when she's struck by lightning while opening a furniture store, leading to a stint as reigning champion of the local hospital instead. After Lisa exposes a tobacco company's exploitation of the pageant and loses her title on a technicality, Amber is reinstated as Little Miss Springfield through a corrupt scheme involving the mayor and other town officials. She later resurfaces as part of an angry mob chasing Homer during the events that led to Springfield being sealed under a giant dome. Overall, Amber serves as a symbol of shallow pageantry and adult manipulation of children's competitions, standing in contrast to Lisa's more sincere ambitions. Voiced by Lona Williams. Notable quotes: My name is Amber Dempsey. When I grow up, I want to be a sweetie pie.
quotes: My name is Amber Dempsey. When I grow up, I want to be a sweetie pie.

title: The Penalizer
text: The Penalizer is Supervillain alter-ego of Principal Seymour Skinner, who terrorized Springfield until stopped by Bartman. The Penalizer is a vigilante persona secretly adopted by Springfield Elementary's uptight principal, born from his lingering war trauma and obsession with rules and discipline. Cloaked in a green and brown costume bearing a stolen puma emblem, he stalks the night hunting down petty rule-breakers, using night-vision binoculars to track them down. His signature move is forcing wrongdoers to endure absurdly ironic, humiliating punishments using a stolen Hypno-Coin, leaving victims traumatized. Despite his menacing presence, his crusade is really just an extension of Skinner's authoritarian, militaristic mindset spilling over from school discipline into full-blown vigilantism. He is eventually unmasked and taken down by Bartman, who deduces his identity through news reports and clues linking the attacks to the school. The character serves as a comic parody of Marvel's Punisher, exaggerating Skinner's rigid, rule-obsessed personality to darkly comic extremes.

title: Francine Rhenquist
text: Francine Rhenquist is A new student and bully at Springfield Elementary School who becomes a rival to Lisa Simpson. Francine Rhenquist is an aggressive transfer student whose arrival at Springfield Elementary sets off a wave of bullying, particularly targeted at smart kids like Lisa. Despite her tough exterior, she's revealed to be something of a loner, unaccepted even by the school's other bullies and often seen sitting by herself when not terrorizing classmates. Her attacks seem oddly selective, leading Lisa on a scientific investigation to uncover the hidden trigger behind her aggression. It turns out Francine's violent outbursts are provoked by a specific scent given off by intelligent children, a discovery Lisa turns into a full scientific presentation. Her parents seem unconcerned by her behavior, treating her punching sprees as a normal way for her to burn off energy before bed. Beyond her signature bullying arc, she recurs in minor roles such as taking bets on classmates and competing for prizes like the Princess Ponypalooza, always ready to seize an advantage over her peers. Voiced by Kathy Griffin.

title: Saint Joseph
text: Saint Joseph is Biblical figure, husband of the Virgin Mary and earthly stepfather of Jesus, portrayed by Homer in a non-canon Christmas special. Saint Joseph is depicted as a somewhat put-upon, comically flawed version of the biblical carpenter in the show's non-canon Christmas special. He's portrayed as insecure about not being Jesus's biological father or one of the wise men, leading him to drown his sorrows in wine. His frustration escalates into a darkly comic moment where he nearly strangles the infant Jesus before being stopped by the angel Gabriel. Despite his flaws, he ultimately protects his family, cleverly using a decorated duck and a felled pine tree to thwart King Herod's soldiers, inadvertently creating the first Christmas tree. In the show's main canon, he appears briefly as a background biblical figure who tells Mary to curse Homer for turning them away from shelter. The role is played by Homer in the parody sketch, blending the biblical narrative with typical Simpsons slapstick. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Joseph then says that a pregnant virgin is every man's worst nightmare.
quotes: Joseph then says that a pregnant virgin is every man's worst nightmare.

title: Lure Lass
text: Lure Lass is A comic-book superheroine, member of the Superior Squadron and ally of Radioactive Man. Lure Lass, secretly known as Laura Lasser, is a costumed hero whose gift is a set of alluring powers that can charm or distract enemies, though they prove useless against foes like Dr. Crab's robotic army. She carries a not-so-secret crush on her teammate Captain Squid, often angling for time alone with him, including deliberately stalling so she can stay behind while other heroes rush off to battle. Despite the romantic subplot, she's shown as a capable and loyal team player, helping clean up after battles, rescuing captured allies like Weasel Woman, and fighting off villains such as Madame Eczema's soldiers and an evil, resurrected Radioactive Man. She has a practical, quick-thinking side, using anti-allergen medication to counter the Crazy Cat Lady's feline army and cleverly tricking the villain into recapture. Lure Lass also shows a sharp, no-nonsense streak, bluntly reminding Radioactive Man that she isn't anyone's secretary. In one alternate continuity she dies of unexplained causes, later replaced by a version of herself from another universe. Notable quotes: she wasn't his secretary
quotes: she wasn't his secretary

title: Arnie Pye
text: Arnie Pye is Channel 6 (KBBL-TV) helicopter traffic reporter in Springfield. Arnie Pye is the perpetually irritable and slightly eccentric traffic reporter for Springfield's Channel 6 news, best known for his aerial segment 'Arnie Pye With Arnie in the Sky.' He harbors a deep resentment toward anchorman Kent Brockman, likely stemming from Brockman belittling his job, and the two frequently bicker on live television. His career has been marked by chaos, including a helicopter crash that he barely survived, an incident Brockman treated with callous indifference. Despite this near-death experience, Arnie keeps showing up in later episodes unfazed. When Brockman was temporarily ousted from the anchor desk, Arnie got a shot at the top job, adopting an exaggeratedly smooth broadcast voice that comically slipped back to his usual tone whenever he got worked up. Early in the show's run he was mistakenly called 'Bill Pye,' a minor continuity slip that became a fun bit of trivia. His name is also a pun on the phrase 'pie in the sky.' Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Arnie, this is not the time.|Kent Brockman | You're not the time, Kent! You're not the time!|Arnie Pye
quotes: Arnie, this is not the time.|Kent Brockman
You're not the time, Kent! You're not the time!|Arnie Pye

title: Dwight D. Eisenhower
