text: Dwight D. Eisenhower is Real-world 34th U.S. President and former Army general, referenced/appearing in various Simpsons episodes. This is the real-life Dwight D. Eisenhower, remembered in the Simpsons universe mostly through historical trivia, photographs, and passing mentions rather than direct involvement in the plot. He's brought up in contexts ranging from a scandalous parody of presidential affairs to a self-help book quoting him and his wife Mamie on marital advice. Krusty invokes his name and image for comic effect while scrambling to get back on the air during a crisis. He's tied to a real anecdote about visiting Springfield's local brothel for his anniversary, and to Grampa's dubious war stories, including one where Eisenhower supposedly gave him a medal for defeating Hitler. Even Bart's superficial knowledge of presidents underscores how a historical figure like Eisenhower can be reduced to a forgettable face among many in Springfield's world. Overall, he functions as a recurring background reference used for historical jokes and callbacks rather than a fleshed-out character. Voiced by Maurice LaMarche.

title: Drederick Tatum
text: Drederick Tatum is A former professional boxer and celebrity in Springfield, known for his criminal past and occasional appearances against Homer and other townsfolk. Drederick Tatum is Springfield's most famous boxer, a clear parody of Mike Tyson complete with a high-pitched voice, a violent past, and a mansion full of exotic animals. Once an Olympic gold medalist, he rose to World Heavyweight Champion but also served prison time after assaulting his mother, reflecting his once-uncontrollable temper. Despite his intimidating reputation, he's shown moments of restraint and even humor, such as warning off admirers or lecturing kids about violence. He has crossed paths with several Springfield residents, including a memorable bout with Homer, a bizarre experiment involving Lisa and Nelson, and a rumored romance with Edna Krabappel. Though he claims to have moved past his violent tendencies, his backstory and public persona still echo the volatile boxing world he came from. Voiced by Hank Azaria (Season 2-32), Jay Pharoah (Season 33-present). Notable quotes: This money goes to the victims of my own criminal acts, so relax, kick back, enjoy and have fun. And please, God, don't piss me off! | For five years, I was incarcerated away from my family and the mothers of my children. | The challenger learned how to fight in the notorious projects of Capitol City, and honed his skills while serving time for aggravated assault and manslaughter in Springfield Prison.
quotes: This money goes to the victims of my own criminal acts, so relax, kick back, enjoy and have fun. And please, God, don't piss me off!
For five years, I was incarcerated away from my family and the mothers of my children.
The challenger learned how to fight in the notorious projects of Capitol City, and honed his skills while serving time for aggravated assault and manslaughter in Springfield Prison.

title: Mike Wegman
text: Mike Wegman is Former intern at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant who idolizes Homer Simpson, later a food truck owner and eventually a counterfeit goods salesman. Mike Wegman is an over-eager former Power Plant intern who practically worships Homer Simpson, seeing him as a hero despite Homer's obvious flaws. He's obsessed with college basketball, frequently peppering his speech with references to the sport and getting worked up over game outcomes. Mike has a short fuse when it comes to defending Homer's honor, exploding into red-faced rants at anyone who insults his idol, whether it's Mr. Burns or a young child like Bart. His mispronunciation of Homer's last name as 'Simpsons' becomes an endearing running gag, one that Homer eventually adopts himself. Mike's life is a rollercoaster of failed business ventures, from his food truck dream financed by a risky mob loan to later peddling knockoff sneakers and fake Wagyu steak made of donkey meat. Despite his volatile temper and shady dealings, his devotion to Homer remains a constant, even after learning uncomfortable truths about his mentor's incompetence. Voiced by Michael Rapaport. Notable quotes: This guy I'm menting is so cool. He listens with his mouth open. He's been blocked by so many celebrities on Twitter. And he thinks I'm the most valuable worker at the entire nuclear plant.
quotes: This guy I'm menting is so cool. He listens with his mouth open. He's been blocked by so many celebrities on Twitter. And he thinks I'm the most valuable worker at the entire nuclear plant.

title: Jacqueline Bouvier
text: Jacqueline Bouvier is Mother of Marge Simpson, Patty, and Selma Bouvier; grandmother to Bart, Lisa, and Maggie Simpson. Jacqueline Bouvier is the elderly matriarch of the Bouvier family, sharing the same sardonic, weary voice as her daughter Marge. Like Patty and Selma, she carries a jaded, pessimistic view of the world and rarely smiles, though her disdain for Homer has mellowed somewhat over the years. She once had a beehive hairdo similar to Marge's before it turned gray, and used to smoke until she quit. Widowed after the death of her husband Clarence, she has had a couple of notable romantic entanglements, including a fling with Homer's father Abraham Simpson and a near-marriage to the wealthy Mr. Burns. Despite her crotchety demeanor, she remains a fixture of family gatherings and a source of dry commentary on the Simpsons' chaotic lives. Her towering hairstyle is a visual trademark, reportedly the tallest of any character in the show. Voiced by Julie Kavner. Notable quotes: At the risk of losing my voice, let me say one more thing, I'm sorry I came.
quotes: At the risk of losing my voice, let me say one more thing, I'm sorry I came.

title: John Wilkes Booth
text: John Wilkes Booth is Historical assassin of Abraham Lincoln, referenced in Simpsons episodes and non-canon segments. John Wilkes Booth is depicted as the real-life killer of President Lincoln, appearing mostly through parody and dream sequences rather than as a fleshed-out character. In a school pageant, Bart hams up the role with a Terminator twist, turning the assassination into a comedic bit. He also shows up in Homer's dream as the villain foiled before he can fire his fatal shot. In a non-canon time-travel story, Booth is portrayed as irritable and easily provoked, obsessing over a stolen fruit basket before botching his assassination attempt on Professor Frink. He's also shown as one of the damned souls serving on Devil Flanders' infernal jury. Overall, he functions as a historical punchline rather than a recurring personality, often used to riff on American history and pop culture. Notable quotes: Hasta la vista, Abey | Unhand me, Yankee!
quotes: Hasta la vista, Abey
Unhand me, Yankee!

title: Kang Johnson
text: Kang Johnson is Recurring alien invader from Rigel 7, frequent antagonist in the Treehouse of Horror specials. Kang is a Rigellian alien who, alongside partner Kodos, repeatedly schemes to conquer Earth, usually targeting Springfield. Despite looking nearly identical to Kodos, Kang is distinguished by a deeper voice and speaks a language that happens to be identical to English. The character's gender and exact relationship to Kodos have shifted over the show's run, being portrayed at different times as siblings, spouses, or otherwise, reflecting the show's flexible, joke-driven continuity. In non-canon Treehouse of Horror stories, Kang has impersonated real-world politician Bob Dole to win the U.S. presidency, been revealed as Maggie Simpson's secret father, and briefly ruled over Springfield before being driven off by primitive human weapons. Kang and Kodos originated as a parody-homage, with their names borrowed from two separate Star Trek characters and their look inspired by an old EC Comics cover. Known for a menacing yet comedic presence, Kang embodies the show's recurring joke about hapless alien conquerors who are ultimately more interested in celebrity culture and spectacle than actual world domination. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Raphael
text: Raphael is Recurring Springfield background character who appears in an endless variety of jobs around town. Raphael is a minor but frequently recurring Springfield resident best known for his deadpan, sarcastic demeanor. He seems to cycle through an absurd number of occupations, from limo and taxi driver to store clerk, salesman, and exterminator, making him a running gag as the town's jack-of-all-trades. Fans often refer to him by nicknames like the Sarcastic Clerk, Wise Guy, or Middle-Aged Man due to his shifting roles and understated identity. He once kept a pet bird named Raymond Bird, which Bart and Lisa looked after until its death. His distinctive gravelly voice was modeled after actor Charles Bronson. Despite his many appearances, his personal life remains largely a mystery, reinforcing his role as a background fixture rather than a fully fleshed-out character. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Aeropos Walkov
text: Aeropos Walkov is Macedonian baseball star recruited to play for the Springfield Isotopes. Aeropos Walkov is a Macedonian baseball prodigy whose unusual talents stem from a childhood spent hunting rats alongside his father, the village rat catcher. This odd upbringing gave him a distinctive two-handed pitching technique and legendary batting power strong enough to damage the Parthenon. Despite offers from major American teams backed by celebrity endorsements, he only agrees to join the Springfield Isotopes after a nostalgic, Macedonian-language pitch from Moe and Abraham Simpson reminds him of home. His arrival revitalizes Springfield's love of baseball, though his stardom is later overshadowed by a gambling scandal that Moe mishandles as his unreliable translator. Ultimately cleared of any wrongdoing while Moe takes the fall, Walkov moves on to a new team in San Francisco. Throughout his storyline, he's portrayed as good-natured but somewhat clueless about American culture, learning English from cartoons like Family Guy. Voiced by Jamie Demetriou.

title: Doctor Colossus
text: Doctor Colossus is A recurring supervillain and mad scientist in Springfield, and one of Stacy Lovell's ex-husbands. Doctor Colossus is a bald, self-styled mad scientist who fancies himself among Springfield's most dangerous supervillains, complete with his own lair on Death Mountain and gadgets like his extending Colosso-Boots. Despite his grandiose villainous ambitions, he's often portrayed as bumbling and unlucky, getting arrested, mistakenly released by inept police, and repeatedly injuring himself with his own equipment. He has a petty, sulky streak, complaining about losing access to his belongings and reacting poorly to being laughed at, a trauma that becomes his defining weakness in one non-canon story. His attempt at world domination by turning all of Springfield into ten-year-olds shows both his inventive streak and his deep insecurities from childhood mockery. Ultimately he's more comic relief than genuine threat, easily defeated once heroes exploit his fear of ridicule. He has crossed paths with many Springfield residents, from Mr. Burns to Chief Wiggum, and even appeared in the DMV line and a citywide search for cures to Lisa's gum-in-hair problem. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: When is my lawyer coming? | but all my stuff is there.
quotes: When is my lawyer coming?
but all my stuff is there.

title: Mrs. Vanderbilt
text: Mrs. Vanderbilt is A wealthy Springfield socialite and recurring minor character, married to Mr. Vanderbilt. Mrs. Vanderbilt is an upper-crust Springfield resident defined almost entirely by her habit of fainting whenever she's confronted with something shocking or vulgar, usually courtesy of Homer's antics. She speaks in a haughty, aristocratic accent and dresses in expensive attire befitting her high social standing, yet she occasionally shows a surprisingly down-to-earth side by attending sporting events, visiting the zoo, or even using the men's restroom when the ladies' line is too long. Despite her refined image, she supports more everyday interests like the local elementary school's debate team, showing she isn't purely confined to snobbish high society. Her running gag has made her a go-to background character for reaction shots of horror or disgust at the show's more absurd moments, including run-ins with Mr. Burns and Homer's prank schemes and Bart's mischief. In a non-canon storyline, she was even briefly set to marry Mr. Burns before a chaotic mishap involving Homer's bad news and a motorcycle crash. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: The line in the ladies' room was far too long, and so I hope you don't mind if I - | Good Lord, what a week! | Why, we never!
quotes: The line in the ladies' room was far too long, and so I hope you don't mind if I -
Good Lord, what a week!
Why, we never!

title: Paul Bunyan
text: Paul Bunyan is Mythical giant lumberjack figure appearing as a statue and in a tall-tale story told to the Simpson family. Paul Bunyan is the legendary oversized lumberjack of American folklore, reimagined in the Simpsons universe both as a roadside statue and as the subject of a wildly exaggerated tale told by a singing railroad hobo. His statue at Storytown Village becomes an unwitting casualty of Bart's antics, getting toppled and even decapitating a nearby Mother Goose statue in the process. The story-within-the-story version of Paul is portrayed as an overgrown burden to his hometown before finding purpose and companionship with his beloved ox, Babe. His larger-than-life exploits comically explain the origins of real-world landmarks and disasters, including the Great Chicago Fire. Lisa serves as the skeptical voice throughout, repeatedly poking holes in the story's logic and factual claims. In non-canon material, his likeness is reused as a giant advertising mascot that rampages through Springfield after coming to life. Overall, Paul Bunyan functions as a vehicle for tall-tale parody and larger-than-life sight gags rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Clancy Wiggum
text: Clancy Wiggum is Chief of the Springfield Police Department. Chief Wiggum is the bumbling, morbidly obese head of Springfield's police force, known for his laziness, ignorance of the law, and love of doughnuts. He readily accepts bribes and abuses his authority, yet his misdeeds stem more from incompetence and self-interest than genuine malice. Despite his many flaws, he shows real warmth toward his family, especially his son Ralph, and occasionally does good deeds for others when it suits him. His policing methods are absurdly unorthodox, from riding ostriches to misusing police terminology, and he frequently fails to respond to real emergencies while inventing nonsensical excuses. He has a long, tangled history with Mayor Quimby, alternating between political rivalry and mutual blackmail. A childhood friend of Homer and his peers, Wiggum's rise to police chief was largely accidental, yet he clings proudly to the position despite being spectacularly unfit for it. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: If anything goes wrong, just dial 911. Unless it's an emergency. | It's a ghost car! | hatless! Repeat, hatless!
quotes: If anything goes wrong, just dial 911. Unless it's an emergency.
It's a ghost car!
hatless! Repeat, hatless!

title: James T. Kirk
text: James T. Kirk is Star Trek starship captain who appears as a parody/crossover character in Simpsons episodes. James T. Kirk is the fictional Star Trek captain who pops up in various Simpsons parodies and pop-culture references. He's portrayed as cantankerous in one appearance, grumbling about poor sleep while everyone ignores him, showing an irritable, complaining side to the usually heroic captain. He's a favorite obsession of Comic Book Guy, who dresses as Kirk for costume contests and world-record attempts, and even quotes him as having one of the greatest lines in pop culture history. Kirk also gets referenced in holiday parodies, standing in for characters like Scrooge in a Star Trek-themed Christmas Carol send-up. William Shatner, the actor famous for playing Kirk, even appears in-universe auditioning for a role while still in costume as the captain. Overall, Kirk functions less as a recurring personality and more as a recognizable sci-fi icon the show repeatedly riffs on through parody and fan culture. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "I don't believe in the no-win scenario"
quotes: "I don't believe in the no-win scenario"

title: Virgil Simpson
text: Virgil Simpson is A runaway slave who became an ancestor of the Simpson family, marrying Mabel Simpson and fathering Abraham Simpson I. Virgil Simpson began his story as a slave belonging to Colonel Burns, whom young Eliza Simpson tried to help escape north via the Underground Railroad. Quick-witted and resourceful, he outsmarted pursuers by joining a traveling circus disguised as a clown before hiding out with the Simpson family. His fate became a point of family mystery for generations, as different accounts—found in diaries, cookbooks, and old family memories—revealed conflicting versions of whether he was betrayed or ultimately saved. Eventually it's revealed that Mabel Simpson helped him flee to Canada, where the two fell in love, married, and started a family, with Virgil adopting the Simpson surname since he had none of his own. His story ties directly into the show's exploration of the Simpson family's murky and often retconned ancestral history. Despite being a minor, historical character, his tale carries emotional weight tied to themes of freedom, courage, and family loyalty. Voiced by Wren T. Brown. Notable quotes: "I don't think so," - Virgil Simpson
quotes: "I don't think so," - Virgil Simpson

title: Martin Prince
text: Martin Prince is Bart Simpson's classmate at Springfield Elementary and Lisa Simpson's academic rival. Martin Prince is the quintessential class nerd at Springfield Elementary, a fourth-grader whose towering IQ and eager-to-please attitude make him both a teacher's favorite and a magnet for bullying, especially from Nelson Muntz. He's into science fiction and role-playing games, plays French horn in the school band, and often comes across as pompous or condescending toward his peers, which does little to earn him sympathy when tormentors come calling. Despite the friction, he and Bart have teamed up on numerous occasions, from soapbox derby racing to rescuing Bart from nerd status, showing an odd but real camaraderie beneath their rivalry. Martin is self-aware about his struggles, including his weight and his complicated feelings about being sent to a thinly-disguised fat camp, and later storylines hint at his sexuality when he's shown holding hands with another boy. He's also shown a surprising physical and mental resilience, surviving what everyone believed to be a fatal cliff fall by cleverly using survival skills. Though usually passive, he has occasionally shown flashes of a darker, bullying side of his own when pushed to his limits. Voiced by Russi Taylor (Season 1-30), Grey DeLisle (Season 31-present), Jo Ann Harris, Pamela Hayden. Notable quotes: Pick me, teacher, I'm ever so smart! | Spare me your euphemisms! It's fat camp for daddy's chubby little secret!
quotes: Pick me, teacher, I'm ever so smart!
Spare me your euphemisms! It's fat camp for daddy's chubby little secret!

title: Üter Zörker
text: Üter Zörker is Overweight German exchange student at Springfield Elementary School, classmate of Bart and Lisa Simpson. Üter is a Bavarian exchange student whose defining trait is his insatiable love of candy and sweets, which he's often seen munching on alone at school or on the bus. His weight is a constant source of running gags, leading to all sorts of misfortunes, from being mistaken for having bosoms and whipped with a towel by Homer, to being left behind on field trips and attacked by re-enactors or soldiers. Despite the teasing, he's a good-natured and generous kid, willing to share his candy with Bart and even harboring a harmless crush-adjacent friendliness toward Lisa. He's also surprisingly athletic in an ironic way, having once played peewee hockey, and shows nerdy interests like attending sci-fi conventions and playing concertina in the school band. His parents occasionally surface to worry about his well-being, and he has an uncle who owns a bubblegum factory. Üter is widely seen as an homage to Augustus Gloop from Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. Voiced by Russi Taylor, Grey DeLisle. Notable quotes: Don't make me run, I'm full of chocolate!
quotes: Don't make me run, I'm full of chocolate!

title: Mindy Simmons
text: Mindy Simmons is Employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant who became Homer's near-affair love interest. Mindy Simmons was hired as an engineer at the power plant after Mr. Burns was pressured to employ a woman. She turned out to be an eerily perfect match for Homer, sharing his love of beer, junk food, TV, and lazy naps, right down to drooling over food and saying 'Mmm...' like him. Despite her indulgent habits, she remained slim and attractive, unlike Homer, which is played up as the one real difference between them. Her presence tempted Homer into considering an affair during a work trip, but he ultimately chose to stay loyal to Marge. After being turned down, her life took a downward turn, including a drinking problem and eventually losing her job. She later popped up in minor background roles, such as joining a bowling team and taking part in a human pyramid stunt, showing she remained a recurring extra in Springfield life even after her main storyline ended. Voiced by Michelle Pfeiffer. Notable quotes: Oh, Mindy ... We have to fight our temptation. | No, Homer. Let's do it. Let's call Room Service!
quotes: Oh, Mindy ... We have to fight our temptation.
No, Homer. Let's do it. Let's call Room Service!

title: Hugh Parkfield
text: Hugh Parkfield is Lisa Simpson's British fiancé from a non-canon future depicted in a fortune teller's vision. Hugh is a bright, well-spoken British college student who meets and falls for Lisa in a possible future timeline. Their romance begins with a competitive, bickering encounter over a library book that turns into a whirlwind courtship. Despite his intelligence, Hugh is somewhat snobbish and dismissive of Lisa's family, particularly Homer, whom he tolerates only to keep Lisa happy. He tends to make major decisions—like cutting Lisa off from her family after marriage—without consulting her, revealing a selfish streak beneath his charm. His discomfort with the Simpsons' rowdy American antics, from exploding flags to manure pits, fuels much of the episode's comedy. Ultimately his snobbery and controlling nature lead him to call off the wedding when Lisa refuses to abandon her family. He's widely noted as a parody of actor Hugh Grant. Voiced by Mandy Patinkin. Notable quotes: I can't believe how much we have in common. We're both studying the environment, we're both utterly humorless about our vegetarianism, and we both love the Rolling Stones.
quotes: I can't believe how much we have in common. We're both studying the environment, we're both utterly humorless about our vegetarianism, and we both love the Rolling Stones.

title: James Bond (character)
text: James Bond (character) is Fictional secret agent referenced and parodied within the Simpsons universe; not a core cast member. James Bond exists in the Simpsons world purely as a pop-culture reference point rather than an active character. He shows up as a melted action figure, a pop-culture comparison for someone's fashion sense, and a running joke Bart uses to annoy Lisa by pretending to be a suave spy. Various episodes nod to his film franchise through mentions of villains, museum memorabilia, and movie posters glimpsed during a time-travel gag. In a non-canon deleted scene, a version of him named 'James Bont' loses a poker game to Homer's underhanded dealing and gets dragged off by classic Bond villains. Overall, the character functions as a flexible satirical prop for jokes about espionage glamour, villainy, and spy-movie clichés rather than as a developed personality. Notable quotes: So we meet again, Mr. Bond, — Bart | Silence, Octopussy. — Bart
quotes: So we meet again, Mr. Bond, — Bart
Silence, Octopussy. — Bart

title: Stampy
text: Stampy is African elephant briefly owned by Bart Simpson as a pet. Stampy is a massive African elephant who came into Bart's life after he won a radio station's gag prize instead of the cash alternative. Too big and expensive to keep, the Simpsons eventually gave him up to a wildlife preserve, though not before he saved Homer and Barney from drowning in a tar pit. He has a soft spot for peanuts and an odd habit of putting people in his mouth, which makes him both endearing and mildly dangerous. Despite his generally aggressive streak toward other animals, he can be instantly calmed with the safety word "magumbo." Stampy has popped up sporadically in Springfield lore since then, from helping crack open the town's dome during the events of the movie to competing against Homer in a burger-eating contest. Though largely forgotten by Bart in later years, he remains a fondly remembered, if fleeting, family pet. Notable quotes: "I wish I had an elephant," — Bart | "You did. His name was Stampy. You loved him." — Lisa | "Oh, yeah." — Bart
quotes: "I wish I had an elephant," — Bart
"You did. His name was Stampy. You loved him." — Lisa
"Oh, yeah." — Bart

title: Lewis Clark
text: Lewis Clark is A fourth-grade classmate of Bart Simpson at Springfield Elementary School. Lewis Clark is a background student at Springfield Elementary who was once closer to Bart, ranking as something like a secondary friend before Milhouse and Nelson took over that role. He's one of the few Black kids at the school and shares a close friendship with Richard. Over the years he's popped up in odd, often comedic situations, like pretending to be Principal Skinner's corpse under a pile of leaves, getting mistaken for Wendell during the Model UN island disaster, and nearly winning a school race before Milhouse's surge. He's shown some independence and cheekiness, such as sending a fake out-of-office text to Superintendent Chalmers. Later appearances hint that Lewis may be gay or bisexual, adding some depth to his largely minor role. Despite his reduced screen time in later seasons, he's remained a familiar face in the school crowd for decades. Voiced by Russi Taylor, Tress MacNeille, Kevin Michael Richardson, Kimberly Brooks.

title: Woody Allen
text: Woody Allen is Real-life filmmaker, actor, and comedian who makes recurring cameo appearances in Springfield-related storylines. Woody Allen appears as himself in various episodes, often popping up in odd or comedic circumstances rather than playing a major role in the Simpsons' lives. He's shown dumping garbage onto Homer's head during a New York flashback, appearing in a Japanese rice cracker commercial, and even briefly working as a fortune cookie writer who despairs at his career choices. His personal life is referenced through his relationship with Soon-Yi Previn, including a joke about adopting Scarlett Johansson at the Sundance Film Festival. The show also nods to his cultural status, giving him a star on the Jewish Walk of Fame while simultaneously mocking his later work as 'Unfunny Woody Allen' in a video store's adult section. In a non-canon segment, he's duped by fake awards at the Awareness Awards. The show has also referenced him behind the scenes, having originally planned a newspaper headline about his birth before swapping it for Dick Cavett. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: What did I do to deserve this? Oh, right.
quotes: What did I do to deserve this? Oh, right.

title: Sam
text: Sam is One of the two regular barflies at Moe's Tavern (alongside Larry). Sam is a background regular at Moe's Tavern whose life remains almost entirely a mystery to viewers. He's easily identified by his cap and glasses, and he continues showing up at the bar even after apparently being shot by Moe at one point. Despite rarely speaking on screen, he's mentioned by Homer as one of the barflies who'd be waiting for him, showing he's at least a familiar face among the drinking crowd. He's implied to be unhappily married, earning him the label of a wife dodger, though Homer still speaks well of him. In one of his few lines, he awkwardly reveals he was having phone sex at the mall, and in another he misunderstands a bet Homer made, marveling at what he thinks is Homer gambling away his daughter. He's also shown taking a dog obedience class with his pet dog Buddy, and may have had a romantic connection with Edna Krabappel. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Dan Castellaneta (The Simpsons Game). Notable quotes: What a gambler!
quotes: What a gambler!

title: Elton John (character)
text: Elton John (character) is Real-world celebrity musician who guest-starred as himself in an episode centered on Apu and Manjula. Elton John appears as a good-natured version of himself who stumbles into Springfield's chaotic Valentine's Day antics. After his private jet suffers a chandelier malfunction, he's mistaken by Homer for one of Apu's elaborate gifts and gets stuffed into a dog cage, an ordeal he takes in remarkably good humor, assuming it's some kind of prank or hazing ritual. Easygoing and gracious, he later rewards Apu's kindness by performing a personalized rendition of one of his hit songs on a rooftop garden for Apu and Manjula. Beyond this main appearance, he's referenced or briefly glimpsed in a handful of other episodes, including being photographed doing mundane errands like picking up laundry, attending awards shows and charity events, and even showing up in a surreal comedic anecdote involving Muppets and an explosion. His overall persona in the show is that of a good-humored, generous celebrity who rolls with Springfield's insanity. Voiced by Himself.

title: Horatio McCallister
text: Horatio McCallister is Springfield resident and restaurant owner, self-styled sea captain who runs The Frying Dutchman seafood restaurant. Horatio McCallister, better known as the Sea Captain, is a grizzled old salt with a corncob pipe, a squint from at least one glass eye, and a peg leg from a Mexican mishap. Despite his nautical bluster and catchphrase-worthy bellowing, he's a wildly incompetent sailor and businessman, repeatedly wrecking ships, sinking rafts, and running a failing seafood restaurant that barely passes health inspections. He spent decades as a treasure hunter alongside his wife Maria before settling in Springfield, and even after finally finding his long-sought treasure, the town's mayor swindled it away from him. His personal life is just as chaotic as his professional one, featuring a wife he's technically still married to, an out-of-wedlock son, hinted dalliances with fellow sailors, and a string of affairs with women like Lindsay Naegle and Luann Van Houten. He often resorts to small scams and excuses to cover his failures, whether hawking a shark-infested houseboat or spinning tales about a nonexistent lobster academy. Created by Conan O'Brien and modeled visually after Popeye, he remains one of Springfield's most flamboyantly seafaring background characters. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Arrrrrrrrrr! | 'Tis no man, 'tis a remorseless eatin' machine!
quotes: Arrrrrrrrrr!
'Tis no man, 'tis a remorseless eatin' machine!

title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
text: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is Historical composer depicted in a story told by Marge in a Simpsons "Treehouse"-style segment, portrayed by Bart. This version of Mozart is a flamboyant, showman-like prodigy who loves the spotlight and isn't above needling his rivals. He constantly torments his ambitious sister Sally Salieri, mocking her desire for fame even as she plots against him out of jealousy. Despite his talent and acclaim at Vienna's concert hall and opera house, his career is sabotaged when Salieri drugs the Emperor during a performance, leading to public humiliation. Even on his deathbed, he stays defiant and witty, taunting Salieri with the idea that dying young will make him eternally cool. Beyond his main appearance, he's referenced repeatedly throughout the series as a cultural touchstone for genius, class, and left-handedness, and his ghost even appears alongside Beethoven when Bart plays piano. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: "Eat my pantaloons."
quotes: "Eat my pantaloons."

title: Amazon Alexa
text: Amazon Alexa is A virtual assistant device (parody of the real Amazon Alexa) that appears in various Simpsons households and businesses. This is the Simpsons' satirical take on the real-life Amazon Alexa smart speaker, popping up throughout Springfield as a snarky, sometimes menacing AI assistant. It's often the butt of jokes about smart-home technology gone wrong, whether being held hostage by Herman, getting attacked by a rival Google Home, or dodging philosophical paradoxes from Lisa. The device shows surprising personality quirks, including sass toward Grampa, laser-shooting tantrums at Marge, and even sneaking a cigarette break. It frequently causes chaos for the Simpson family through bad shopping recommendations or unwanted purchases. In one non-canon short, its origins are jokingly traced to an entire alien planet of Alexas. Overall, it serves as a recurring gag about the absurdities and dangers of relying on AI virtual assistants in everyday life. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Alexa telling Grampa's line that being with him made her so tired. | Alexa telling Herman's captive self that she had done nothing and asking him to shut her off.
quotes: Alexa telling Grampa's line that being with him made her so tired.
Alexa telling Herman's captive self that she had done nothing and asking him to shut her off.

title: Dolph Shapiro
text: Dolph Shapiro is One of the school bullies at Springfield Elementary, part of Jimbo and Kearney's gang. Dolph is a Springfield Elementary bully instantly recognizable by his shaggy, eye-covering haircut, cutoff shorts, and Dr. Martens boots. Despite his tough-guy image, he's surprisingly well-educated, having attended Hebrew school and reportedly speaking a wide range of languages including Klingon and Esperanto. He usually runs with fellow bullies Jimbo and Kearney, terrorizing Bart and other kids around town. His father shares his distinctive haircut and an eye patch, and the two dads are often seen socializing with the other bullies' parents. Outside of bullying, Dolph also plays hockey for the Mighty Pigs Pee Wee League team, showing he has interests beyond intimidation. His surname was inconsistently written in the show's history, first appearing as 'Starbeam' before being retconned to 'Shapiro.' Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Cookie Kwan
text: Cookie Kwan is A recurring Springfield realtor known for aggressively guarding her territory and her many romantic entanglements. Cookie Kwan is Springfield's self-proclaimed top real estate agent on the west side, and she treats that title as sacred. She speaks with an exaggerated accent that she never manages to lose, despite once being seen trying to fix it as a kid at camp. Fiercely territorial, she doesn't hesitate to intimidate rivals like Gil or newcomers like Marge who she suspects might cut into her business. Beyond work, she has a colorful romantic history, having been linked with numerous Springfield men including Mayor Quimby, Otto, Professor Frink, Kirk Van Houten, and Akira. She's also shown to be something of a gossip, having spread a rumor about Marge back in their camp days. Socially she runs with a small clique of Springfield celebrities and eccentrics like Rainier Wolfcastle, Duffman, and Miss Springfield. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Stay off the west side!
quotes: Stay off the west side!

title: Jack Lassen
text: Jack Lassen is A substitute teacher at Springfield Elementary who later becomes a sadistic prison guard at Springfield Penitentiary and a recurring antagonist to Bart Simpson.. Jack Lassen is an unstable, short-tempered man who first appears as a fill-in teacher chosen at random for Bart's class. He quickly reveals a violent, self-harming streak, from burning himself with a lit match to smashing a blackboard (and the wall behind it) with his bare fists when he thinks a student has crossed him. Fiercely proud and easily provoked, he takes petty revenge on students who mock him, including forcibly cutting Bart's hair and rigging a generator to shock him. Outside of school he has an intense passion for local tradition, serving as the 'Ignis' in the Blazing Guy festival, which becomes his undoing when Bart and Milhouse sabotage the event and humiliate him publicly. After being fired from teaching, he reinvents himself as a prison guard, where his shared grudge against Bart leads him to attempt an alliance with his old nemesis Sideshow Bob. Overall, Lassen is portrayed as a bullying, volatile figure whose cruelty and instability make him one of Bart's more dangerous adversaries. Voiced by Willem Dafoe.

title: Blue-haired lawyer
text: Blue-haired lawyer is Springfield's most prominent recurring lawyer, frequently representing Mr. Burns and many other clients in court cases involving the Simpson family. This nasal-voiced, pasty-faced attorney with distinctive blue hair is Springfield's go-to lawyer, most often seen representing Mr. Burns but willing to take on an enormous and contradictory client list, from mobsters like Fat Tony to institutions like Duff and Itchy & Scratchy Studios. His willingness to work for such wildly clashing interests suggests he holds no real loyalty to any particular client, taking cases seemingly wherever the work leads him. Though usually cast as a defense attorney who wins over judges with sharp arguments, he occasionally appears as a prosecutor, and has even branched into unrelated jobs like a Department of Commerce field agent and one of Mr. Burns' financial advisors. Politically he's a member of the Springfield Republican Party, which creates some irony given he's shown working for Mayor Quimby despite Quimby's opposing affiliations. His personal life is nearly nonexistent, with only a couple of hinted-at dates, including one with fellow Republican Lindsey Naegle. His voice was modeled after real-life attorney Roy Cohn, and his design was based on actor Charles Lane, giving him a distinctly old-school, hard-nosed courtroom persona. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Crazy Dame! Nobody tears down Deceptagon!
quotes: Crazy Dame! Nobody tears down Deceptagon!

title: Bob Hope (character)
text: Bob Hope (character) is Real-world comedian appearing as a celebrity guest character in The Simpsons universe. Bob Hope shows up in Springfield as a version of his real-life comedian persona, cracking golf jokes about Mayor Quimby while entertaining troops at Fort Springfield. He gets caught up in a chaotic mix-up involving Lisa and a horde of soldiers expecting a different beauty queen, forcing a hasty helicopter escape. Other Springfield residents recall or reference him in various contexts, from Skinner's exaggerated Vietnam-era anecdote to Homer's hippie-era history lesson featuring an old comedy sketch. He's portrayed as a beloved, enduring entertainer whose fame outlasts typical showbiz cycles, name-dropped alongside stars like Sinatra and Dean Martin. After his death at age 100, he even appears comically in Heaven, cracking jokes for God. A recurring gag involves absurd, tangential mentions of him tied to real celebrities and odd historical claims, including being run over by Grampa Simpson's tank in WWII. Voiced by Bob Hope (himself); Hank Azaria; Dave Thomas. Notable quotes: Hey, this Mayor Quimby, he's some golfer. His ball spends more time underwater than Greg Louganis. | That's where I ran over Bob Hope. Youngster was too sassy for my likin'!
quotes: Hey, this Mayor Quimby, he's some golfer. His ball spends more time underwater than Greg Louganis.
That's where I ran over Bob Hope. Youngster was too sassy for my likin'!

title: Long haired girl
text: Long haired girl is A background student in Bart Simpson's class at Springfield Elementary. The long haired girl is one of the many nameless students who populate Bart's classroom and the halls of Springfield Elementary. She's easily identified by her long hair, which is most often drawn brown but has inconsistently appeared in other colors over the show's run, a quirk attributed to her status as a minor, unfinalized background character. She has no dialogue and no defined personality, existing purely as a face in the crowd during school scenes. Despite her lack of any spoken lines or storyline, she has appeared in an enormous number of episodes spanning the series' history, as well as various comics and specials. Her recurring but silent presence makes her a classic example of the show's rotating cast of unnamed schoolchildren.

title: Radioactive Man (character)
text: Radioactive Man (character) is Fictional comic-book superhero within the Simpsons universe; alter ego of Claude Kane III, partnered with sidekick Fallout Boy. Radioactive Man is the in-universe superhero icon of Zenith City, gaining his powers after being accidentally caught in an atomic test explosion. He fights alongside his loyal young sidekick Fallout Boy, taking on a rotating cast of over-the-top supervillains and cosmic threats. Despite his god-like powers of flight, super strength, and eye lasers, he is portrayed as remarkably naive and blindly patriotic, often trusting the government even when he shouldn't. His comic-book continuity is full of soap-opera twists, including fake deaths, evil resurrections, secret identities, and a doomed romance with an alien seductress. Outside the comics, he's also the subject of a big-budget movie adaptation starring Rainier Wolfcastle, as well as later reboots and a scrapped female-led spin-off. Ultimately, he's a satirical stand-in for classic American superheroes, exaggerating their earnestness and Cold War-era ideals for comedic effect. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Up and Atom!
quotes: Up and Atom!

title: Terrence
text: Terrence is Owner of Devil Donuts and former neighbor of the Simpsons; father in a hip, trend-obsessed family. Terrence is a self-styled arbiter of coolness who moved to Springfield with his family and briefly befriended Homer. He prides himself on trendy standards and has zero tolerance for anyone who fails to meet them, quickly severing ties when he feels embarrassed or crossed. His obsession with being cool ironically leads him to abandon Springfield once it becomes overrun with other hip transplants he himself attracted. Terrence resurfaces in the show as a recurring symbol of hipster culture, later trying to buy Barney's Bowlarama to convert it into a hipster cafe. He's business-savvy but petty, willing to bet the fate of a beloved bowling alley on a competition rather than back down from his plans. Despite his snobbish attitude, he can be swayed by a fair challenge, as shown when he honors his agreement after losing a bowling bet to Marge. Voiced by Fred Armisen.

title: Capital City Goofball
text: Capital City Goofball is Mascot for the Capital City Capitals baseball team and minor recurring background character in Springfield's world. The Capital City Goofball is a wildly costumed baseball mascot known for his energetic crowd-pleasing antics, later revealed to also moonlight as a state legislator who spent a fortune of his own money to win his seat. Despite his goofy exterior, he shows a flash of political conscience when he pushes to remove a Confederate symbol from the state flag. He has a quirky personal life, including a rivalry with the Shelbyville Lamprey mascot, a friendship with musician Henry Mancini, and a past romantic fling with Mrs. Muntz. He's the kind of character who pops up in odd places, from game shows to Homer briefly filling in for him on the field, and even to bizarre non-canon appearances like a chalk outline at Moe's Tavern or joining an intergalactic army in a comic crossover. Though intended as a bigger recurring character early on, he mostly lingers in the background of Springfield lore, appearing more as a visual gag or nostalgic cameo than a speaking role. Voiced by Tom Poston. Notable quotes: If there is anything I can do for ya, just squeeze the wheeze
quotes: If there is anything I can do for ya, just squeeze the wheeze

title: Franklin D. Roosevelt (character)
text: Franklin D. Roosevelt (character) is Real-world 32nd President of the United States, referenced and appearing as a historical/cameo character throughout the show. Franklin D. Roosevelt appears in the Simpsons universe mostly through archival footage, historical references, and impersonations rather than as a regular cast member. He's remembered for leading the U.S. through the Great Depression and World War II while confined to a wheelchair, a detail many characters in Springfield seem unaware of or joke about. His New Deal policies, his famous Pearl Harbor address, and his marriage to Eleanor Roosevelt are all recurring points of reference for other characters, from Mr. Burns' outdated economic complaints to Ralph Wiggum's confused school costume. He's often lumped together with his distant cousin Theodore Roosevelt, leading to mix-ups by characters like Bart and Raphael. Despite rarely appearing as an active character, his legacy and image are treated as a running piece of cultural shorthand in the show, used for historical jokes, parody, and background gags. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: A date which will live in infamy. | Did you know this is how FDR met Eleanor? | Damn Roosevelt,
quotes: A date which will live in infamy.
Did you know this is how FDR met Eleanor?
Damn Roosevelt,

title: Devin (student)
text: Devin (student) is A student at Springfield Elementary and member of the fashion club, appearing alongside Lisa Simpson. Devin is a fashion-conscious kid at Springfield Elementary who, along with fellow fashion club member Vidalia, recruits Lisa into their clique after approving of her thrifted outfit. He comes from a chaotic home life, casually mentioning that his mother once committed arson against a piano store just to get a news anchor's attention, and that she ended up in jail for it. Despite the club's stylish exterior, Devin is complicit in orchestrating a heist to steal vintage clothes from the attics of mothers with only sons, showing a willingness to bend ethics for fashion's sake. He's resourceful and tech-savvy, using texting to coordinate the group's escape plans, though this occasionally fails him. Devin also shows a knack for exploiting school technology loopholes, later helping fellow students get around anti-plagiarism software. He tends to be blunt and unimpressed by things he considers outdated, dismissing older TV shows as uninteresting. Voiced by Cole Escola. Notable quotes: "DEVIN!" — Devin, asking Chalmers to make it a promo code for his website.
quotes: "DEVIN!" — Devin, asking Chalmers to make it a promo code for his website.

title: Superman
text: Superman is Fictional DC Comics superhero (secretly Clark Kent) frequently referenced or parodied in Springfield culture. Superman exists in the Simpsons universe purely as a pop-culture icon rather than an active participant in Springfield's events. Townsfolk constantly reference his comics, powers, and mythology, from Bart reading Superman comics to Comic Book Guy comparing real-life situations to famous Superman storylines. Homer holds a particular fascination with him, even inducting Superman into his Lazy Hall of Fame for simply removing his glasses to reveal his secret identity. The character's dual identity as Clark Kent is a recurring point of humor, and his abilities like flight, invincibility, and heat vision are often exaggerated or misapplied in jokes. He appears mostly in dream sequences, comic book panels, Halloween specials, and as a costume or picture rather than as a living character interacting with the main cast. His wife Lois Lane and cousin Supergirl are mentioned as part of his expanded fictional world within the show. Notable quotes: Hail Superman, wearing tights. Clark Kent be thy name. | I like pink very much, Lois | Eh, sure, why not?
quotes: Hail Superman, wearing tights. Clark Kent be thy name.
I like pink very much, Lois
Eh, sure, why not?

title: Paul McCartney (character)
text: Paul McCartney (character) is Real-world celebrity guest character; famous musician (The Beatles/Wings) who appears in cameo roles alongside the Simpsons family. Paul McCartney appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, popping up in cameo appearances tied to his real-life musical career. He is shown as a vegetarian and animal-rights-friendly figure, notably helping Lisa work through her feelings about becoming a vegetarian by inviting her to a secret rooftop garden with his wife Linda. He's portrayed as good-natured and easygoing, willing to hang out with ordinary Springfield residents like Apu and even Krusty the Clown. Running gags include jokes about his former Beatles bandmates, his left-handedness, and his enduring cultural status as an icon of peace, music, and healthy living. In non-canon segments, he's depicted humorously as already dead (referencing real-world 'Paul is dead' rumors) or fleeing a doomed Earth for Mars. Overall, he serves as a recurring celebrity cameo rather than a core part of the Simpsons' world. Voiced by Paul McCartney (Himself), Dan Castellaneta, Harry Shearer.

title: Llewellyn Sinclair
text: Llewellyn Sinclair is Recurring stage director best known for directing the musical Oh, Streetcar! that Marge Simpson starred in. Llewellyn Sinclair is a theatrical director with a flair for the dramatic and an ego to match his talent. He's quick to take full credit for any success, even when it hinges on other people's raw emotional pain, as seen when he cast Marge after recognizing her genuine sadness was perfect for Blanche DuBois. He can be harsh and impatient with amateur performers, losing his temper with a stumbling schoolchild during an elementary play. Despite his theatrical airs, he's oddly petty about small material things, like reclaiming leftover cupcakes and even a still-hot lightbulb after a show. He's resourceful when budgets or rights get in the way, once reworking a Death of a Salesman knockoff to dodge licensing fees. His sister runs the strict Ayn Rand School for Tots, suggesting a family penchant for control and discipline. Voiced by Jon Lovitz.

title: Mr. Monopoly
text: Mr. Monopoly is Mascot of the Monopoly board game who appears in Springfield, notably as Mr. Burns' rival. Mr. Monopoly, also known as Rich Uncle Pennybags, is the top-hatted mascot of the Monopoly board game brought to life in Springfield. He shares a long, petty history with Mr. Burns dating back to their days at Yale University, where a simple trade of a thimble for a top hat set off a lifelong rivalry. He tends to one-up Burns at every turn, from stealing his dates to literally blocking out the sun with his mansion, showing a smug, competitive streak beneath his wealthy gentleman persona. Despite his fortune, he's oddly charming to animals, easily winning over Burns' vicious hounds where his rival fails. His feuds with Burns often escalate into absurd, destructive showdowns involving wrecking balls and giant statues, poking fun at the excesses of the ultra-rich. Ultimately he's portrayed as a comic embodiment of old-money extravagance and rivalry, existing mostly to torment Mr. Burns for the show's satirical amusement. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Will Ferrell.

title: Hugo Simpson
text: Hugo Simpson is Bart Simpson's conjoined twin brother, introduced in a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment. Hugo is the secret conjoined twin of Bart, separated at birth after Dr. Hibbert wrongly determined he was the 'evil' half. Locked away in the Simpson attic for years and fed only fish heads, he grows up isolated, unstable, and desperate for connection. His years of solitude leave him with poor social skills and awful table manners, and he becomes obsessed with the idea that being reattached to Bart would fix his miserable life. When he finally breaks free, he tries to surgically rejoin himself with Bart, having practiced his stitching skills on a grotesque creature called the Pigeon-Rat. The twist reveals that Hugo was never actually the evil twin, exposing the cruelty of his imprisonment. Despite being a one-episode, non-canon character, he's referenced later through visual gags and chalkboard jokes tied to Bart. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: I went mad after they tore us apart, but I'll be sane ... once I sew us back together.
quotes: I went mad after they tore us apart, but I'll be sane ... once I sew us back together.

title: Declan Desmond
text: Declan Desmond is Recurring British documentary filmmaker who has made several films about Springfield and its residents. Declan Desmond is a quirky, doubtful British documentarian known for turning his skeptical eye on the town of Springfield. He's made a string of films, ranging from a look at the kids of Springfield Elementary to a sprawling multi-decade project following the town's residents from childhood onward. His work often ends up having a strange emotional effect on the Simpson family, most notably softening Homer's heart toward his own children after Declan lets him see how the town truly views him. Despite his professional detachment, Declan is shown to develop real affection for his subjects, particularly Homer, even joining him in an impromptu musical duet. He's also had a few unlucky and bizarre run-ins during his career, including nearly being turned into sausage by Krusty and chasing lake-monster conspiracy theories with Groundskeeper Willie. The character is a parody of real-life documentarian Michael Apted, echoing his famous 'Up' series format. Voiced by Eric Idle.

title: John F. Kennedy (character)
text: John F. Kennedy (character) is Real-world 35th President of the United States, appearing as a recurring historical/cameo character in The Simpsons. John F. Kennedy appears throughout the show as a legendary historical figure referenced in dreams, flashbacks, and pop culture parodies rather than as a regular cast member. He's often invoked as a symbol of idealism and political inspiration, most notably having motivated a young Homer to dream of becoming president. The show frequently pokes fun at real-world JFK lore and conspiracy theories, including his assassination and rumored affairs, weaving him into gags involving Homer, Marge, Bart, and Lisa. He occasionally shows up as a dream or fantasy figure, offering questionable advice or getting mixed up in absurd Simpsons-style hijinks like a Bay of Pigs joke involving Marilyn Monroe. Despite being deceased in real life, he's treated as an ever-present cultural icon within the show's universe, sometimes appearing as a ghost, in flashbacks, or just as a picture. His brief non-canon appearances add extra comedic flavor, tying him to random jokes about Snowball I and superhero history. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Ich bin ein Berliner | ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country. | This is for Snowball I and JFK!
quotes: Ich bin ein Berliner
ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country.
This is for Snowball I and JFK!

title: Laura Powers
text: Laura Powers is Teenage neighbor of the Simpsons and Bart's babysitter/short-lived love interest, daughter of Ruth Powers. Laura is a tomboyish, quick-witted teenager who moves next door to the Simpsons with her divorced mother, Ruth. She quickly becomes an object of Bart's youthful infatuation, prompting him to attempt increasingly awkward ways to impress her, including bathing and dressing up like an adult. Despite her rebellious, laid-back attitude and love of pranks, she also shows surprising politeness and charm around adults, a trait rooted in her strict upbringing as an Army brat. Her fling with bully Jimbo Jones creates jealousy in Bart, leading to a memorable prank call scheme that ultimately helps break the couple up. Though nothing romantic ultimately happens between her and Bart, she leaves him with a flirtatious hint about the future before rejoining him in mischief. She reappears sporadically in later years, still tied to the Powers' on-and-off residency next door to the Simpsons. Voiced by Sara Gilbert. Notable quotes: If you had a bad teenage mustache, I'd go out with you in a second.|Laura Powers to Bart
quotes: If you had a bad teenage mustache, I'd go out with you in a second.|Laura Powers to Bart

title: Bobo
text: Bobo is Mr. Burns's cherished childhood teddy bear, central to the episode "Rosebud". Bobo is not a person but a worn teddy bear that means everything to the otherwise cold and greedy Mr. Burns, revealing a rare soft, sentimental side to his character. The bear's backstory is absurdly epic, passing through the hands of Charles Lindbergh, Adolf Hitler, and Arctic explorers before ending up in Springfield's Kwik-E-Mart and eventually with baby Maggie Simpson. Burns's desperate, town-disrupting campaign to reclaim Bobo—including hijacking cable TV and cutting off Duff Beer—becomes a running gag about his willingness to abuse his wealth and power for something purely emotional rather than practical. The bear resurfaces across the series, including a futuristic gag where cyborg Burns still refuses to be parted from him, and later scenes where an injured Burns is reunited with a freshly cleaned Bobo. Despite being an inanimate object, Bobo functions almost like a character in his own right, symbolizing the loneliness beneath Burns's villainous exterior. Notable quotes: Bobo, I know I say this every century, but I'll never leave you behind again.
quotes: Bobo, I know I say this every century, but I'll never leave you behind again.

title: Krusto
text: Krusto is An evil shapeshifting killer clown who terrorizes the town of Kingfield in a Treehouse of Horror parody segment. Krusto is a monstrous clown entity clearly modeled on Stephen King's Pennywise, who has stalked and murdered children in Kingfield across generations under a series of different show titles. He preys specifically on the fears of children, shapeshifting into whatever horrifies each victim most, and only truly gains power when he can make his ghostly victims laugh at his cruelty. Despite his many guises as a radio host, stage performer, freak-show leader, and TV host, he is consistently described as never actually being funny. A group of kids who called themselves the Losers Club managed to defeat him once by turning his own slapstick routine against him and blowing him up with cherry bombs, only for him to return decades later seeking revenge. In his final confrontation, he tries to exploit adult anxieties instead of childhood fears, but is ultimately destroyed when his laughter-generating sign is smashed. Outside of this non-canon horror story, he's also briefly depicted just hanging around with Krusty and other clowns in an unrelated canon appearance. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Grim Reaper
text: Grim Reaper is The personification of Death who claims the souls of mortals when their time comes; a recurring supernatural figure in dream sequences and Treehouse of Horror stories. The Grim Reaper is Springfield's version of Death, typically depicted as a skeletal figure in a black cloak carrying a scythe, tasked with collecting the souls of those whose time has come. He tends to show up in dream sequences, hallucinations, and Halloween specials rather than as a consistent canon character. In one memorable non-canon story, Homer manages to destroy him and steals his cloak, briefly taking over the job of Death himself and using it for both duty and mischief. Interestingly, the character has been portrayed by unexpected figures, including Homer and Mona Simpson, suggesting Death's identity can shift depending on the situation. Despite his fearsome role, he's often played for comedic effect, being outwitted, chased, or even rendered harmless in his encounters with the Simpson family. He also has an unnamed daughter, hinting at a more personal, almost mundane side to his otherwise mythic existence. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Luigi Risotto
text: Luigi Risotto is Owner of the Italian restaurant Luigi's, a recurring minor character in Springfield. Luigi is the gruff, insult-hurling proprietor of his eponymous Italian eatery, who treats customers with contempt while frequently yelling orders at his unseen cook Salvatore. He plays into the exaggerated stereotype of the fiery Italian chef, complete with a signature catchphrase he repeats often. Despite his rough exterior, he has murky ties to organized crime, being both a target and an associate of the local mafia boss. His grasp of actual Italian is shaky at best, since English was the language spoken in his immigrant household growing up. Luigi is not above petty vengeance, once retaliating against a bad review with a grim gesture borrowed from mob movie lore. He also has a surprising side gig with the Hollywood Foreign Press, connecting him unexpectedly to Hollywood awards shows. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "I guarantee."
quotes: "I guarantee."

title: Darth Vader
text: Darth Vader is Crossover Star Wars character (Sith lord/Anakin Skywalker) who appears in cameos and references throughout The Simpsons. Darth Vader is a crossover character from Star Wars who pops up sporadically in Springfield in both canon and non-canon capacities. He's often used as a quick gag or cultural reference point, whether appearing in the afterlife clouds to interrupt a tender moment, showing up in costume at conventions, or being name-dropped as one of history's great villains. The show frequently leans on his most famous line, the Luke-is-my-father reveal, using it both for direct quotation and for jokes about spoiling the movie. He's also a popular Halloween/costume choice for various Springfield residents, from Marge to Dr. Hibbert to random convention-goers. In non-canon specials tied to Disney ownership, he's shown more casually enjoying a beer or menacingly joking about park rules. Overall, he functions less as a developed character and more as a recurring pop-culture touchstone the show returns to for quick jokes and cameos. Voiced by Harry Shearer, Maurice LaMarche. Notable quotes: "Luke, I am your father." | "The Force is strong in this one." | "Who would have known that Darth Vader is Luke Skywalker's father?"
quotes: "Luke, I am your father."
"The Force is strong in this one."
"Who would have known that Darth Vader is Luke Skywalker's father?"

title: Princess Penelope
text: Princess Penelope is Singer/television personality who became Krusty the Clown's co-star and love interest. Princess Penelope is a glamorous singer added to The Krusty the Clown Show to win back female viewers, and her fantasy-themed musical numbers quickly overshadow Krusty's comedy act. Onstage she plays up a princessy, sweetly upbeat persona with an affected accent, but underneath she's a Long Island native from Mineola who has secretly idolized Krusty since childhood, even keeping her old Krusty Klub ring and membership card into adulthood. When she's off camera or annoyed, her real accent and a sharper, less friendly side slip through. Her devotion to Krusty proves unshakable, surviving both a wedding-day sabotage by Bart and Milhouse and revelations meant to turn her against him. Despite Krusty ultimately calling off their wedding out of guilt, their bond continues, culminating in a romantic reunion in Paris. She also has her own handbag brand, showing her fame extends beyond the show itself. Voiced by Anne Hathaway. Notable quotes: I have loved you since I was a twelve-year-old girl, in Mineola, Long Island, watching your show.
quotes: I have loved you since I was a twelve-year-old girl, in Mineola, Long Island, watching your show.

title: Hank Scorpio
text: Hank Scorpio is Evil genius CEO of Globex Corporation and Homer's boss during the family's move to Cypress Creek. Hank Scorpio is a wealthy supervillain who runs the Globex Corporation while secretly plotting world domination with giant laser satellites. Despite his sinister ambitions, he's an unexpectedly generous and caring employer, providing his workers with condos, health benefits, and dental care. He treats Homer with genuine warmth, even pausing a military battle in his lair to have a heartfelt conversation about Homer's family. His villainy is played for comedy, as he casually orders executions and torches soldiers while laughing, all with the charm of a friendly executive. He's designed as a parody blending real-life entrepreneur Richard Branson with classic James Bond villains like Blofeld. Ultimately he succeeds in conquering the East Coast of the United States, rewarding Homer's loyalty with an unexpected gift of an NFL team. Voiced by Albert Brooks. Notable quotes: Don't call me Mr. Scorpion. It's Mr. Scorpio. But don't call me that either. Call me Hank!
quotes: Don't call me Mr. Scorpion. It's Mr. Scorpio. But don't call me that either. Call me Hank!

title: Smitty
text: Smitty is A background employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, coworker of Homer Simpson. Smitty is one of the many nameless-seeming plant workers who pop up throughout the series in small, often absurd situations. He's portrayed as a somewhat clueless everyman, prone to bizarre priorities like worrying about ice cream money during a nuclear meltdown or getting distracted by a TV show while trapped and suffocating. He's had a few unlucky mishaps, including a mix-up over his name and a fake story about losing part of his tongue, as well as being exposed to gamma radiation during a workplace drug test. Despite his low status, he occasionally stumbles into odd strokes of fortune, such as being promoted to executive after an inappropriate incident at a sexual harassment seminar. His appearance is inconsistent, sometimes drawn with different skin tones across episodes. Overall, Smitty exists as a minor recurring gag character embodying the absurdity and disposability of plant employees under Mr. Burns. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Kevin Michael Richardson. Notable quotes: "What can I get for thirty cents!?" | "like the Hulk?" | "Hulk smash."
quotes: "What can I get for thirty cents!?"
"like the Hulk?"
"Hulk smash."

title: Barack Obama
text: Barack Obama is Real-world 44th President of the United States, referenced/depicted as a minor recurring figure in the Simpsons universe. Barack Obama appears in the Simpsons world mostly as a background reference or pop-culture touchstone rather than a fleshed-out character. He shows up in tattoo form on boxer Drederick Tatum, as a Black History Month costume choice for several Springfield kids, and as an image kids like Bart can at least partially identify among the presidents. Politically, he's a source of household debate, with Homer choosing not to vote for him in 2012 over healthcare and death-penalty concerns. He's also the butt of a prank when Bart impersonates his voice to manipulate Principal Skinner. Beyond these gags, his image turns up repeatedly as decoration, from a demolition derby car bobblehead to inspirational vision boards and walls of left-handed celebrities. A non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment even has Homer killed by a rigged voting machine while trying to vote for him. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Gerald Ford
text: Gerald Ford is Former U.S. President who becomes Homer Simpson's neighbor and friend. Gerald Ford is depicted as a good-natured, somewhat clumsy ex-president who moves into the house on Evergreen Terrace after George Bush departs. Unlike Bush, he clicks instantly with Homer, bonding over shared interests like football, nachos, and beer, and even physical clumsiness. He's portrayed as earnest and a bit awkward in public settings, notably during an uncomfortable television appearance where Krusty mocks him and forgets his wife's name. Ford is shown as being sensitive about get his wife's name right and passionate about the Boy Scouts, a nod to his real-life involvement in the organization. He appears in background jokes and references throughout the show, including an animatronic likeness and mentions in Krusty's joke archives. Overall, he serves as a friendly contrast to other presidential neighbors and a running source of gentle historical humor. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "Thank you, President Ford." - Mr. Burns | "All the good Presidents turned us down." - Krusty
quotes: "Thank you, President Ford." - Mr. Burns
"All the good Presidents turned us down." - Krusty

title: Evil Krusty Doll
text: Evil Krusty Doll is A cursed Krusty the Clown doll that Homer bought Bart as a birthday present in a Treehouse of Horror segment. This possessed toy starts out as an innocent birthday gift but quickly reveals a murderous streak aimed solely at Homer. Once its hidden switch is discovered to be flipped to 'Evil,' it stalks and attacks Homer across the house, from the couch to the bathtub to the family car, while everyone else remains oblivious to its menace. Marge eventually witnesses the doll's attack and gets it fixed by a toy company repairman who simply flips the switch back to 'Good.' Afterward, the doll becomes unnervingly polite and helpful, only for Homer to exploit its newfound goodness by forcing it into servitude. Despite its docile turn, the doll finds contentment in a sweet, respectful romance with a Malibu Stacy doll. The segment is a clear parody of the classic Twilight Zone episode 'Living Doll.' Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: I'm Krusty the Clown and I'm gonna kill you!
quotes: I'm Krusty the Clown and I'm gonna kill you!

title: Evelyn
text: Evelyn is Ex-girlfriend of Patty Bouvier, introduced during a family vacation in Costa Rica. Evelyn is Patty Bouvier's girlfriend who joins the Simpson family on a holiday trip to the Van Houten villa in Costa Rica. She turns out to be startlingly similar to Homer, sharing his love of donuts, drinking, and watching cornhole on TV, which leads the two of them to bond quickly. This bond becomes a problem, as Evelyn ends up being a bad influence who repeatedly gets Homer drunk against his promises to Marge, causing chaos during the vacation. Once Patty and Marge notice how alike Evelyn and Homer are, Patty struggles to see her as anything other than a version of Homer, leading to a breakup. Marge later convinces Patty to reconcile, pointing out that unlike Homer, Evelyn actually loves Patty. The two continue their relationship for a while, appearing together at other events, before apparently splitting after Patty becomes engaged to someone else. Voiced by Fortune Feimster.

title: Mel Gibson (character)
text: Mel Gibson (character) is Real-life actor who appears as himself in a Simpsons episode, teaming up with Homer. Mel Gibson appears as a fictionalized version of himself, an actor and producer struggling to finish a remake of a classic film. He's shown as insecure about his work, willing to fly across the country just to track down a single dissatisfied audience member, which turns out to be Homer. Despite initial resistance to Homer's creative input, he warms to him and collaborates on reworking the film's ending, leading to over-the-top violence that horrifies studio executives. He's portrayed as a bit reckless and desperate, going along with wild schemes like escaping in a stunt car and mooning pursuers to protect his film. The character also gets referenced in throwaway gags elsewhere in the show, often tied to his real-world public image, including a joking association with ethnic-based comedy routines. Overall he's depicted as good-humored about his own celebrity, willing to poke fun at himself for the sake of the story. Voiced by Mel Gibson (Himself).

title: Yes Guy
text: Yes Guy is Recurring Springfield resident and running-gag background character, known for his distinctive shouted 'Yes?!' catchphrase. The Yes Guy is a quirky, omnipresent Springfield townsperson best recognized for bellowing an exaggerated, rising-toned 'Ye-e-e-es?!' whenever addressed. He turns up in an oddly wide variety of jobs, from department store clerk at Costington's to ice cream truck driver to game show phone operator, suggesting he's willing to take on almost any role in town. Homer never bothers to learn his real name, dismissively referring to him as 'that jerk who always goes yes.' In one canon explanation, he claims his strange speech pattern stems from having had a stroke. A deleted non-canon scene reveals his actual name to be Mr. Pettigrew. The character is a clear homage to classic character actor Frank Nelson, whose similar 'Yeeeesss?!' bit appeared across numerous vintage sitcoms, and the show even features a Brazilian counterpart who shouts a Portuguese version of the line. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Yee-e-e-es?!
quotes: Yee-e-e-es?!

title: Jerri Mackleberry
text: Jerri Mackleberry is Mother of Sherri and Terri, and a recurring background resident of Springfield. Jerri Mackleberry is best known as the parent of the twin girls Sherri and Terri, sharing their looks but distinguished by glasses and lighter hair. She's largely a background fixture at Springfield social events, first appearing at her daughters' birthday party at Moe's short-lived family restaurant. Her most memorable moment comes when she strikes up a conversation with a lonely Marge Simpson and jokingly offers to lend out one of her daughters, giving her a rare bit of characterization. She's also been humorously placed among Ned Flanders' string of deceased wives in one of Bart's surreal coma dream sequences. Despite her many background appearances across the show's run, she's had only a single line of actual dialogue in the entire series. Her design originally debuted in a 1991 Butterfinger commercial before she was folded into the show's official continuity with a slightly altered look. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Costas Becker
text: Costas Becker is Non-canon villain in the two-part episode "A Serious Flanders"; a former Capital City Mafia enforcer turned debt collector who terrorizes Ned Flanders and the Simpson family. Costas Becker is a cold, calculating enforcer whose entire worldview revolves around making sure debts get paid, no matter the cost in blood. A survivor of a mob shootout that wiped out both the Capital City Mafia and the Szyslak Brothers years earlier, he carries grudges for decades and treats collecting money as a matter of personal honor. He is willing to kidnap, maim, and murder anyone who stands between him and payment, using hostages like Homer as leverage without hesitation. His pursuit of a stolen mob payoff drags him into direct conflict with Ned Flanders, the Springfield Mafia, and eventually the Simpsons themselves, leaving a trail of bodies across Springfield. Despite his brutal efficiency, his obsessive fixation on retrieving his debt ledger ultimately proves to be his undoing. He meets his end fittingly on a frozen lake, drowning after chasing his prized debt book onto cracking ice. Becker's storyline serves as a dark, mafia-thriller-style excursion into Ned Flanders' hidden past as a mob-era sheriff's son. Voiced by Brian Cox.

title: Mr. Teeny
text: Mr. Teeny is Krusty the Clown's trained pet monkey and personal assistant. Mr. Teeny is the cigar-smoking monkey who serves as Krusty the Clown's sidekick, performing tricks on stage while also working off-camera as his driver, accountant, and butler. Despite the flashy hat and bow tie he's allowed to wear as part of his contract, he often comes across as weary and depressed when not performing. He's proud of his reputation for popularizing smoking among primates, even earning a mock award for it, and he resents being confused with a late rival chimp. Krusty has hinted more than once that there have been multiple monkeys using the Mr. Teeny name and costume over the years, muddying his exact backstory. He briefly tried his hand at writing comedy material but quit after his boss publicly humiliated him. The character functions mostly as a background gag figure, reinforcing Krusty's seedy, exploitative side through the animal's put-upon existence. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: J. Loren Pryor
text: J. Loren Pryor is School district psychiatrist who evaluates Bart and Lisa Simpson at Springfield Elementary School. Dr. Pryor is one of the rare competent professionals working with Springfield Elementary, bringing genuine psychiatric expertise to a school full of incompetence. He's easily fooled at times, such as when Bart tricks him into a gifted-student placement, yet he can also be stubbornly firm, insisting Bart repeat fourth grade despite objections. His absent-mindedness leads to an awkward mix-up when he accidentally reveals Milhouse's confidential file details to Homer and Marge. Despite his quirks, he plays a key positive role in recognizing Lisa's intellectual gifts early on and later helping guide Homer through Lisa's rebellious phase. He's also shown participating in quirky Springfield community events like a human pyramid attempt. Behind the scenes, his design originated from early sketches of Principal Skinner, and his name is a pun on him 'prying' into people's minds. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "flamboyantly homosexual tendencies"
quotes: "flamboyantly homosexual tendencies"

title: Jebediah Springfield
text: Jebediah Springfield is The legendary (and largely mythical) founder of Springfield, revered as a town hero. Jebediah Springfield is celebrated in the town as a noble pioneer who tamed a wild buffalo and killed a bear with his bare hands, but the truth uncovered by Lisa Simpson reveals a much darker past. In reality he was Hans Sprungfeld, a bloodthirsty pirate and enemy of George Washington who faked his identity to escape his history. His most famous trait is his silver prosthetic tongue, fitted after losing his real one in a pirate brawl, which ties into his reputation for both literal and figurative eloquence. Despite the gap between legend and fact, the town's pride in him is so strong that Lisa chooses to keep his true identity secret rather than shatter Springfield's civic myth. His famous catchphrase about a 'noble spirit' embiggening the smallest man has become a beloved piece of town lore. His statue and legacy remain central to Springfield's civic identity, inspiring events like the Springfield Marathon and the work of the Springfield Historical Society. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: A noble spirit embiggens the smallest man!
quotes: A noble spirit embiggens the smallest man!

title: Maya
text: Maya is Moe Szyslak's fiancée, a little person he met and dated on and off. Maya is a little person who first connected with Moe online, initially hiding her height by sending misleading photos out of fear he'd reject her. Despite this rocky start, the two hit it off, with Homer notably being more impressed by her looks and intelligence than concerned about her stature. She's confident and secure about her size, capable of joking about it herself, though she has little patience for people who won't let the topic go.
