Their relationship fell apart when Moe's joking became hurtful and he absurdly offered to undergo height-reduction surgery, which convinced her he wasn't ready to fully accept her as she was. Years later they reunited, broke up again briefly due to Moe's fear of commitment, and finally got engaged when he tracked her down and proposed. Throughout, she remains one of the rare people who genuinely appreciates Moe's sense of humor. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Persephone Odair
text: Persephone Odair is Entrepreneur and founder of LifeBoat, briefly the ex-wife of Charles Montgomery Burns. Persephone Odair is a charismatic but deeply dishonest businesswoman who built her career on a fraudulent scheme to purify saltwater. She's relentlessly persistent, refusing to give up until she manipulated Mr. Burns into funding and eventually marrying her. Despite the company's fraudulent practices, cover-ups, and even blackmail, she genuinely seems to believe she's a force for good in the world, showing a striking level of self-delusion. Her fabricated backstory about a heroic grandfather lost at sea reveals how willing she is to lie for sympathy and image. Even after being exposed and imprisoned, she remains convinced that LifeBoat is thriving and that her reputation is intact. She serves as a parody of real-life startup fraudsters, echoing scandals like Theranos. Voiced by Elizabeth Banks. Notable quotes: things had never looked better for LifeBoat
quotes: things had never looked better for LifeBoat

title: Kumiko Albertson
text: Kumiko Albertson is Comic Book Guy's wife, a Japanese manga artist who becomes part of the Springfield community. Kumiko is a manga artist from Osaka who arrives in Springfield while touring America's saddest towns, only to fall for Comic Book Guy after wandering into his shop. She's passionate about comics and drawing, working on an autobiographical manga about her own life. Rather than being put off by Comic Book Guy's cynical, insulting nature, she finds it endearing, which helps their unlikely romance blossom into dates, moving in together, and eventually marriage. Her father's initial disapproval adds a family conflict that Homer inadvertently worsens and then helps resolve. Later, her desire to start a family creates tension with her commitment-wary husband, showing her as more emotionally ready for domestic life than he is. Throughout, she's portrayed as warm, understanding, and quietly assertive when it comes to getting what she wants for her relationship. Voiced by Tress MacNeille (Season 25-Season 31); Jenny Yokobori (Season 32-present).

title: Walther Hotenhoffer
text: Walther Hotenhoffer is German pharmaceutical industrialist who created the drug MusBeNys, a minor recurring character connected to the Simpson family's schemes. Walther Hotenhoffer is a somber, German-accented pharma mogul who claims to secretly be Augustus Gloop from Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, having survived being sucked up a chocolate river tube as a child. That trauma left him deeply scarred, giving him recurring nightmares and a bleak, depressive outlook on life. Despite his gloomy demeanor and tendency to hold a gun to his head in moments of despair, he shows a surprisingly strong moral compass, refusing to exploit vulnerable elderly test subjects once he learns his drug is being misused. His storyline involves synthesizing a docility drug from Grampa Simpson's altered biology, only to have Bart illegally distribute it around Springfield. He eventually appears in an educational video about the side effects of another drug, ending with a darkly comic breakdown. Overall, he's portrayed as a tragicomic, world-weary businessman haunted by his bizarre past. Voiced by Werner Herzog. Notable quotes: life is heartless and brutal | if you are a fat little boy in a chocolate factory, never drink from the river
quotes: life is heartless and brutal
if you are a fat little boy in a chocolate factory, never drink from the river

title: William Shakespeare
text: William Shakespeare is Real-world historical figure (English playwright/poet) referenced, depicted, and parodied throughout the show, including as a zombie and ghost. William Shakespeare appears in the Simpsons universe mostly as a cultural touchstone, invoked whenever characters want to reference literary greatness or highbrow culture. He's the namesake and mascot of the fictional fast-food chain Shakespeare's Fried Chicken, showing how his legacy gets comically commercialized in Springfield. In canon he's typically just a name-drop, portrait, or brief spectral cameo, such as appearing as a ghost after a disastrous play performance where he trades barbed literary banter with Arthur Miller. In non-canon material he gets a much wilder treatment, returning as a shotgun-blasted zombie during a Treehouse of Horror segment, guarding the gates of Heaven, and even being booted down to Hell for having performed blackface in his lifetime. Across appearances he's treated with a mix of reverence and irreverent mockery typical of the show's approach to historical icons. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Maurice LaMarche, Chris Edgerly. Notable quotes: Is this the end of zombie Shakespeare? | exactly
quotes: Is this the end of zombie Shakespeare?
exactly

title: Itchy & Scratchy robots
text: Itchy & Scratchy robots is Animatronic robot attractions at Itchy & Scratchy Land theme park that went berserk and attacked the Simpson family. These are state-of-the-art animatronic robots built in the likeness of Itchy and Scratchy, designed to parade through the park's main street and battle each other with axes, chainsaws, mallets, and machine guns purely for visitor entertainment. Their programming supposedly guaranteed they would never harm guests, though camera flash photography was strictly prohibited because it caused them to short-circuit and malfunction. True to Professor Frink's chaos theory prediction, the robots eventually turned on the humans around them, going on a rampage through the park. The Simpson family, left behind due to Bart and Homer's earlier bad behavior, discovered that camera flashes could stun the robots and used disposable cameras to defeat them. Their heroics earned a reward of park passes from owner Roger Meyers, Jr., and Homer later kept several robot heads in his closet as trophies. The robots represent a classic sci-fi trope of technology turning against its creators, played for comic effect within the show's satire of theme parks and robotics.

title: Piper
text: Piper is Sixth-grade student at Springfield Elementary and member of the all-girl gang Bossy Riot. Piper is a rebellious sixth-grader who leads a mischievous streak within Bossy Riot, a girl gang dedicated to pranking Springfield Elementary and pushing a feminist agenda. She's resourceful and a bit sneaky, first crossing paths with Bart when he stumbled into the girls' restroom while hiding from bullies. Piper acts as something of a spokesperson for the group, explaining their hideout activities and their schemes to outsiders like Bart. She shows a flair for vandalism-as-protest, notably tagging Principal Skinner's office wall during their sandals campaign. Piper is also loyal to her gang's cause, willing to go to extremes like destroying Itchy & Scratchy tapes in retaliation for the female reboot's cancellation. Despite her troublemaking tendencies, she and her friends ultimately show a lighter, almost gleeful side when they successfully prank a room full of boys with glitter and fake tears. Voiced by Chelsea Peretti.

title: Michael de Graaf
text: Michael de Graaf is Fashion designer, reality TV judge, and former boyfriend of Waylon Smithers. Michael de Graaf is a wealthy Milan-based fashion designer and judge on the reality show America's Got Fabric, known for his biting critiques delivered with theatrical flair. He comes across as charming and affable, sweeping Smithers off his feet with romantic gestures and celebrity favors, and he's beloved by fans like Marge for his savage on-air zingers. Beneath the charismatic exterior, though, lies a ruthless businessman who built his fortune on fast fashion, turning a blind eye to the pollution and exploitative labor conditions at his own factory. His selfishness ultimately extends to his personal life, valuing his designer clothes over the well-being of his pets. This callousness, culminating in him kicking away an innocent puppy, is what finally drives Smithers to end their relationship. Voiced by Victor Garber. Notable quotes: Now, that is avant-gorgeous.
quotes: Now, that is avant-gorgeous.

title: Bill Gates
text: Bill Gates is Real-world celebrity guest character; founder of Microsoft who appears in various episodes interacting with the Simpsons. This version of Bill Gates is portrayed as a ruthless tech mogul willing to crush competition rather than negotiate fairly. His first major appearance has him buying out Homer's internet company only to have it destroyed out of spite, showing a cutthroat business mentality hidden behind a mild-mannered exterior. He's frequently referenced as a benchmark for extreme wealth, appearing among elite billionaire circles alongside figures like Warren Buffett and Mr. Burns. The show also plays with his real-life reputation, referencing his Harvard dropout status and pairing him humorously with his wife Melinda Gates. In non-canon segments, he's the subject of wilder gags, including escaping Earth via rocket and enduring a bizarre sweatshop ordeal with a fictionalized Steve Jobs. Overall, he functions as a recurring satirical stand-in for real-world tech wealth and power. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "I didn't get rich by writing a lot of checks." - Bill Gates
quotes: "I didn't get rich by writing a lot of checks." - Bill Gates

title: Claude Kane III
text: Claude Kane III is Fictional comic-book character within the Simpsons universe; secret identity of the superhero Radioactive Man. Claude Kane III is a wealthy, idle playboy who secretly transforms into the superhero Radioactive Man after being caught in a nuclear test explosion. He lives a life of luxury in Kane Manor but must constantly hide the electrical bolt-shaped shrapnel embedded in his head by wearing a hat. Despite his heroic alter ego, Claude is portrayed as somewhat gullible and not particularly intelligent, easily swayed by conspiracy theories and unaware of basic facts about radiation. He is romantically persistent, repeatedly asking his love interest Gloria Grand out despite constant rejection, showing a stubborn but devoted streak. Over the course of his comic history, he builds his secret lair, battles threats to his identity, and even experiences a strange split from his heroic persona before reconciling with it. In his later years, he retires from superheroics, passing the mantle to Rod Runtledge, and appears as an elderly man still looking out for those he loves.

title: Albert Einstein
text: Albert Einstein is Real-world physicist referenced throughout the show as a symbol of genius, appearing mostly in pictures, mentions, and cameos. Albert Einstein appears in the Simpsons universe not as an active character but as a recurring cultural reference point for intelligence and scientific achievement. He's most often seen as a photograph, poster, or passing mention used by characters to illustrate genius, from Principal Skinner's comparisons to Homer's pep talks to Bart. The show plays with his legacy in odd ways, such as claiming he didn't speak until age three and only in German, or imagining him dancing in light-up shoes in a non-canon dream sequence. He even shows up as a zombie in a Treehouse of Horror segment and as a spirit in Jewish Heaven chatting with Moshe Dayan. Einstein is honored on the Jewish Walk of Fame within the show's world and is treated with a mix of reverence and gentle mockery. He's a background cultural touchstone rather than a fleshed-out character with dialogue of his own. Notable quotes: "you've convinced me, Einstein"
quotes: "you've convinced me, Einstein"

title: Chuck Berger
text: Chuck Berger is A recurring background student in Lisa Simpson's class at Springfield Elementary School. Chuck Berger is a minor schoolboy character known primarily for two embarrassing moments that have stuck with him as running gags. He once tried to perform a censored version of Chuck Berry's suggestive song 'My Ding-a-Ling' at a school talent show, only to be yanked off stage by Principal Skinner before he could finish, earning him the nickname 'My Ding-a-Ling Kid.' He speaks with a noticeable lisp and has an odd party trick of being able to flip his eyelids inside out. His home life includes a strict father who doubted his ability to build his own volcano for the school science fair. Chuck's aptitude test humorously predicted he'd grow up to be an insurance salesman, a career path that seems to amuse him. He's also been on the receiving end of Nelson Muntz's bullying after criticizing one of his yo-yo tricks, showing he's not shy about giving his opinion even when it backfires. Voiced by Jo Ann Harris, Tress MacNeille, Pamela Hayden. Notable quotes: Ainksurance salesman. - Chuck Berger, reading his aptitude test result, Separate Vocations
quotes: Ainksurance salesman. - Chuck Berger, reading his aptitude test result, Separate Vocations

title: Marvin Monroe
text: Marvin Monroe is Local Springfield psychiatrist/radio host who treats the Simpson family and other townsfolk. Marvin Monroe is Springfield's go-to psychiatrist, best known for his unconventional and often disastrous therapy methods, such as his family shock-therapy chairs. He runs a media empire of sorts, hosting a call-in advice show on KBBL and appearing as a talk-show panelist, while also authoring several self-help books and even an autobiography. Despite his questionable techniques, like the cattle-prod-based "Monroebilizer," he became wealthy and well known throughout town. For years fans believed he had died, since his business quietly closed and buildings were named in his memory, though he later resurfaces alive, explaining he had simply been very sick. His recurring gag involves his supposed death versus sudden reappearances, and he's tied to Homer's family through their infamous disastrous therapy session that started it all. He also has a brother, Mervin Monroe, and is noted as a smoker. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "family bliss or double your money back"
quotes: "family bliss or double your money back"

title: Zeus
text: Zeus is King of the Greek gods, portrayed in various Simpsons parody segments by characters like Mayor Quimby, Homer, and Mr. Burns. Zeus is depicted as the powerful but often exasperated ruler of Olympus, quick to anger when mortals or fellow gods defy him. He is shown as a womanizer who spends much of his time chasing after mortal women, a trait that causes constant friction with his wife Hera. Despite his god-like status, he is portrayed with very human flaws—short-tempered, self-indulgent, and fond of simple pleasures like sports, drinking, and food once he discovers the Olympics. His relationships with his many divine and mortal children, including Hercules, Dionysus, and Perseus, add a comedic family dynamic to his mythological role. In various Simpsons parody segments, he's satirically played by recognizable characters such as Mayor Quimby, Homer, and Mr. Burns, each casting drawing humor from parallels to Zeus's philandering and authoritative nature. Overall, Zeus serves as a recurring figure in the show's send-ups of Greek mythology, used mainly for comedic effect rather than as a serious character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: He grew up (Zeus)
quotes: He grew up (Zeus)

title: "Just stamp the ticket" man
text: "Just stamp the ticket" man is A recurring, unnamed Springfield background character known for his blunt, irritable remarks; later works as a Naval Recruiter. This grumpy townsperson pops up again and again across Springfield, always ready with a curt, sarcastic, or hostile comment. He has little patience for pleasantries, small talk, or nonsense, whether it's Ned Flanders' cheerful wordplay, Barney's baby costume, or an overpriced gas purchase at the Kwik-E-Mart. His irritation sometimes escalates into physical outbursts, such as punching a singing hippie or slugging Homer after an insulting comment. Despite his sour disposition, he later reappears in a more official capacity as a Naval Recruiter, showing a flash of nervousness rather than anger when faced with an awkward paperwork situation. Fans have nicknamed him after his most famous line, and there's some indication his name may be Byron, though that detail comes from a cut scene rather than the aired show. He's become a recognizable, if nameless, fixture of the show's background cast. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "Just stamp the ticket." | "Don't touch me." | like a man who needs help satisfying his wife.

title: Crazy Cat Lady
text: Crazy Cat Lady is A recurring mentally-ill Springfield resident known for hoarding cats and erratic public behavior. Eleanor Abernathy was once a brilliant overachiever, earning both a medical degree from Harvard and a law degree from Yale by her mid-twenties. The pressure of her dual careers eventually led to burnout, alcoholism, and an unhealthy obsession with her cat, which spiraled into full-blown mental illness by the time she reached forty. Now known simply as the Crazy Cat Lady, she wanders Springfield surrounded by dozens of cats, shrieking nonsensical sounds and hurling felines at anyone nearby. Despite her disheveled state, flashes of her old intellect occasionally surface, most notably when she runs a surprisingly coherent mayoral campaign focused on real policy issues. Medication can temporarily restore her lucidity, though this effect vanishes once she realizes she's been tricked with candy instead of real pills. She has also shared brief, oddball romantic and social connections with other eccentric Springfield characters, including Moe and the Crazy Dog Man. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: "because a woman can do anything"
quotes: "because a woman can do anything"

title: Charlie
text: Charlie is Minor recurring character; Dangerous Emissions Supervisor at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant and a friend of Homer Simpson. Charlie is a background employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant who seems to be a magnet for misfortune. Whether it's being wrongly implicated in workplace pranks, getting sucked through an emergency escape tube to a foreign country, or catching fire due to Homer's carelessness, bad luck follows him wherever he goes. Despite this, he remains a steady presence among the plant's rank-and-file workers, occasionally joining in on their antics, such as playing for the plant's softball team. He's shown some questionable judgment of his own, including getting arrested over frustration with slow HDTV progress. Voice actor Dan Castellaneta has noted that Charlie's voice is essentially a variation of Lenny's, and the character shares a visual and thematic kinship with Turanga Leela's coworker Terry from Groening's other show, Futurama, both serving as background fillers with rotten luck. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Steve Mobbs
text: Steve Mobbs is Founder and CIO of Mapple Inc., a parody tech mogul who interacts with the Simpson family. Steve Mobbs is a satirical stand-in for Steve Jobs, presiding over the tech company Mapple Inc. as its eccentric, reclusive chief imaginative officer. He is defined by his obsessive vanity, constant use of the phrase 'insanely great,' and his signature black turtleneck look. Despite founding the company, he was once fired before returning to power, mirroring real-world tech industry lore. He shows little regard for customers, as seen when Bart's prank message reveals an underlying contempt Mobbs is easily made to seem to embody. Even after death, his influence lingers, appearing in hologram-like recordings and even bossing around God in Heaven. His story blends corporate satire with absurdist humor typical of the show's parody of real-world figures. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Greetings! It is I, your insanely great leader, Steve Mobbs. | speaking from beyond the grave
quotes: Greetings! It is I, your insanely great leader, Steve Mobbs.
speaking from beyond the grave

title: Allison Taylor
text: Allison Taylor is A Springfield Elementary student who briefly rivals and later befriends Lisa Simpson. Allison Taylor is an academically gifted second-grader who arrives at Springfield Elementary and quickly proves to be Lisa's intellectual equal, if not her superior. Despite being younger, she outshines Lisa in areas like saxophone playing and impresses both peers and teachers, sparking jealousy rather than instant friendship. Their rivalry peaks during a school diorama contest, leading to a moment of sabotage that Lisa later regrets and confesses to. The two eventually reconcile and settle into a genuine friendship, occasionally appearing together in later episodes such as dance class. Allison is characterized as poised, intelligent, and talented, embodying the kind of high-achieving peer who forces Lisa to confront her own insecurities. She has since become a minor recurring background character rather than a focal point of the show. Voiced by Winona Ryder, Pamela Hayden, Maggie Roswell.

title: George W. Bush
text: George W. Bush is Real-world 43rd President of the United States, referenced/appearing as a minor background character in Springfield. George W. Bush appears in the show mostly as a background or mentioned figure rather than a fully voiced character, reflecting his real-world status as U.S. President. He's the son of George H. W. Bush, who feuds with Homer as a neighbor, and Bart once pranked the elder Bush using cardboard cutouts referencing his sons, including George Jr. His presidency and identity become running points of confusion for the Simpsons kids, most notably when Bart mistakes his picture for actor Will Ferrell. He's tied into jokes about school budget cuts eliminating lessons on obscure or less notable presidents. Later appearances tie him to Springfield's wealthy elite, showing him mingling with Mr. Burns and joining a corporate board. Overall, he functions as a topical, non-speaking cultural reference rather than a developed character in the show's universe.

title: Mahatma Gandhi
text: Mahatma Gandhi is Real-world historical figure (Indian independence leader) referenced/appearing as a minor character in The Simpsons. This is the animated show's occasional nod to the real Mahatma Gandhi, the historic Indian leader famous for nonviolent resistance and helping win India's independence. He tends to pop up as a hallucination, hologram, or cultural reference rather than a fully developed character, appearing in Homer and Mr. Burns' avalanche-induced delirium and later as a dancing hologram in the Simpson home. Characters frequently cite him as a shorthand for peaceful protest or moral greatness, such as Bart's misguided comparison of himself to Gandhi or Marge invoking his fasting endurance. He's also treated as a benchmark of admired historical figures, listed alongside other Nobel Peace Prize winners and included on lists of famous progressive or 'lefty' icons. In non-canon material, his grave shows up in a spooky burial ground, and he's humorously ranked below Homer Simpson in importance by a tongue-in-cheek tour guide. Overall, Gandhi functions less as a personality in the show and more as a running cultural touchstone for peace, nonviolence, and historical greatness. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "good Gandhi." | "If Gandhi could go without eating for a whole three-hour movie, I can do this"

title: Male Golem
text: Male Golem is A clay Golem controlled by Bart Simpson, appearing in a Treehouse of Horror segment. The Male Golem is a centuries-old Jewish clay figure, originally the legendary Golem of Prague, brought to life through mystical scrolls placed in its mouth. Though built as a killing machine that once served a rabbi and later Krusty the Clown for violent purposes, the Golem shows a surprisingly gentle, guilt-ridden personality once given the ability to speak. Bart takes control of him for mischief, using him to exact revenge on bullies and Principal Skinner, treating him almost like a living toy. Despite his murderous history, the Golem is portrayed as anxious and remorseful about the harm he's caused. His arc culminates in a comedic romance with a homemade Female Golem, blending horror-movie tropes with sitcom domestic humor. The character serves as a one-off parody of classic golem folklore and old monster films, appearing primarily in a Halloween special. Voiced by Richard Lewis. Notable quotes: Finally! I can talk! This is the voice I've got? Sounds like I should be selling egg creams in Brighton Beach.
quotes: Finally! I can talk! This is the voice I've got? Sounds like I should be selling egg creams in Brighton Beach.

title: Hans Moleman
text: Hans Moleman is Minor recurring Springfield resident; a hapless, accident-prone townsperson and former mayor. Hans Moleman is a diminutive, mole-like elderly-looking man who claims to be only 31 despite his decrepit appearance, a discrepancy blamed on hard drinking and possibly a licensing error. Nearly blind from cataracts, he shuffles through life with a hidden-sword cane and an endless string of odd jobs, from radio DJ to truck driver to bank teller. He is the show's go-to punching bag for slapstick misfortune, surviving explosions, drillings, burials, and countless other near-fatal accidents with deadpan indifference. Despite his fragility, he once served as Springfield's mayor, only to be run out of town after a scandal involving a purchased town anthem. His romantic life is similarly disastrous, including short-lived dates with Selma Bouvier and Lunchlady Dora. Inspired by Droopy Dog's unassuming demeanor, Moleman has become a beloved background gag precisely because of his relentless bad luck and calm acceptance of it. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: My name is Hans. Drinking has ruined my life. I'm 31 years old! | This is Moleman in the Morning, Good Moleman to you | We paid for blood!!

title: Snow White
text: Snow White is Fairytale princess character who appears as a fan-fiction figure and in a Lisa Simpson-imagined story within the show. Snow White exists in the Simpsons universe both as a real-world collectible/fictional icon and as the heroine of a story Lisa imagines herself starring in. In the 'real' continuity, she's the subject of a picture owned by Nelson Muntz and later appears as a doll figure at Disneyland that Gina Vendetti pushes off a parapet. In Lisa's retelling of the classic fairy tale, Snow White is hunted by the Evil Queen, spared by a reluctant Huntsman Willie, and taken in by the seven dwarfs, echoing the traditional story but with a feminist twist where a female doctor—not a prince—revives her from her poisoned sleep. The character embodies innocence, kindness, and domestic patience, cooking and cleaning for the dwarfs while enduring the Queen's jealousy. She also appears in several non-canon holiday specials, mingling with other Disney princesses and characters. Overall, she serves as a vehicle for parody of Disney fairy tale tropes and light commentary on gender roles. Voiced by Yeardley Smith.

title: John Frink
text: John Frink is Real-life writer and executive producer for The Simpsons; the character Professor Frink was named after him. John Frink is a real-world television writer and producer, not a character within the show's fictional universe, though his surname was borrowed for the beloved mad scientist Professor Frink. Born in 1964, he joined the show's writing staff and has steadily climbed the production ranks over more than two decades, moving from producer to supervising producer, co-executive producer, and eventually executive producer. His long tenure has made him one of the more prolific contributors to the series, credited on dozens of episodes across many seasons as both writer and producer. A recurring in-joke among the credits is that his producer title cards are frequently given punny, Frink-themed alternate names referencing horror and pop-culture titles. His work has earned him numerous industry accolades, including multiple Primetime Emmy Award wins for Outstanding Animated Program and a Writers Guild of America Award. Though never appearing as an on-screen character, his behind-the-scenes influence has helped shape the show's comedic direction for many years.

title: Lance Murdock
text: Lance Murdock is Professional stunt daredevil who inspires Bart Simpson and occasionally crosses paths with Homer. Lance Murdock is a battered, accident-prone stunt performer who has broken every bone in his body over the course of his reckless career. He serves as a hero figure for Bart, personally encouraging him to attempt the famous skateboard jump over Springfield Gorge. Despite his constant hospital visits and injuries, ranging from cirrhosis of the liver to catastrophic stunt mishaps, he keeps returning to perform ever more dangerous feats. His most infamous appearance involves a Las Vegas stunt through rings of fire, ice, and dog feces, which goes horribly wrong when Homer, filling in for a reluctant Ned Flanders, stands up too early. A clear parody of real-life stuntman Evel Knievel, Murdock embodies the show's recurring gag of over-the-top, absurdly dangerous stunts performed with reckless disregard for personal safety. He's a minor but memorable recurring figure, popping up on TV screens throughout the series performing or recovering from his latest death-defying act. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Poochie
text: Poochie is A short-lived cartoon dog character added to the show-within-a-show, The Itchy & Scratchy Show. Poochie was a network-mandated addition to The Itchy & Scratchy Show, created by executives who wanted a hip, edgy mascot to boost sagging ratings. He was designed as a dog 'with an attitude,' and after a huge publicity push, Homer Simpson won the role of providing his voice. Audiences despised him almost immediately, seeing him as an unwelcome intrusion on the show's classic violent slapstick formula. When fan backlash escalated into demands for his removal, the studio killed him off in a famously abrupt and lazily animated segment, cementing him as a symbol of shameless corporate tie-in characters. Despite his in-universe death, he has continued to appear as a running joke and nostalgia reference in later episodes, comics, and video games. His legacy within the show is largely as satire of forced marketing gimmicks and shark-jumping character additions in entertainment. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Poochie's dead!
quotes: Poochie's dead!

title: Nibbles
text: Nibbles is Class hamster at Springfield Elementary School, later used as an unlikely rescuer and astronaut. Nibbles is the school's pet hamster, a small brown creature whose seemingly minor role belies a surprisingly eventful life. He becomes an accidental hero during a blizzard, rolling through the snow in his exercise ball to save both the school and Homer and Ned from disaster. Later, Homer repurposes him as a makeshift astronaut for a homemade rocket, though the mission ends in chaos when Nibbles bails out mid-flight. Despite his bravery, Nibbles' story ends sadly when neglect under Lisa's care leads to his death, prompting a school funeral. Throughout his appearances, Nibbles never speaks, instead reacting with simple animal expressions like quizzical stares, underscoring the absurdity of the human situations he gets swept into. He also has a wife and several hamster babies, adding a small domestic side to his brief but memorable existence. Notable quotes: You did it Nibbles! Now chew through my ball-sack!
quotes: You did it Nibbles! Now chew through my ball-sack!

title: Akira Kurosawa
text: Akira Kurosawa is Recurring Springfield background character who works as a waiter and karate instructor, occasionally interacting with the Simpson family. Akira Kurosawa is a hardworking Asian Springfield resident who has held a variety of jobs over the years, including waiter at The Happy Sumo and Swanky Fish, a salesman at Costington's department store, and sensei at the Springfield Martial Arts Academy. He has a complicated history with Homer, having both helped him uncover the secret of the Mr. Sparkle mascot and nearly poisoned him with improperly prepared blowfish. Despite occasional friction, he's shown to be a capable and patient teacher, training Marge for an MMA bout and attempting to instruct Bart, though the latter skipped classes to play video games. Akira's storylines often place him in the middle of Springfield's quirky civic and social happenings, from a citizenship test spurred by anti-immigrant legislation to joining a mass restaurant-owner plot against Homer. He's also been romantically linked to both Cookie Kwan and Mrs. Muntz, adding a touch of personal life to his otherwise service-industry-centric appearances. His name is a nod to the famous Japanese film director of the same name, reflecting the show's penchant for cultural references in naming background characters. Voiced by Hank Azaria, George Takei.

title: Addy
text: Addy is A rich classmate who briefly befriends Lisa Simpson after meeting her in the library. Addy is a wealthy young girl whose family made its fortune supplying ketchup to stadiums and megachurches. She initially bonds with Lisa over a shared love of the Gallop Girls book series, inviting her into her exclusive circle of friends. However, Addy proves to be a fickle and somewhat cruel figure, caving to peer pressure from her clique and joining in on mocking Lisa rather than defending her. Her friendship operates on a toxic, cliquish logic—she admits the other girls are mean, but frames that meanness as something to pass along rather than resist, encouraging Lisa to bring a new target next time. Despite this troubling social dynamic, Addy has a redeeming moment when her genuine connection with Lisa over their favorite book series resurfaces, prompting her to help Lisa escape her friends' wrath. In the end she chooses to stay behind with her lavish lifestyle rather than leave with Lisa and Bart, but sincerely calls Lisa her best gift. Voiced by Joey King. Notable quotes: Addy then called Lisa her best gift.
quotes: Addy then called Lisa her best gift.

title: Mary Tannenbaum
text: Mary Tannenbaum is A movie producer for The Heartmark Channel who visits Springfield to film a Christmas movie, staying with the Simpsons. Mary is a driven, no-nonsense city professional who is so focused on her career that she rarely pauses to appreciate her surroundings. Despite her tough exterior, she secretly harbors a deep aversion to Christmas movies rooted in a tragic personal loss involving her father. Her problem-solving skills and negotiation tactics make her effective at smoothing over production issues, even when the town's quirks threaten to derail her film. Throughout her stay, she develops an unexpected connection with Principal Skinner, revealing a more impulsive and romantic side to her personality. This impulsiveness becomes a running trait, as she admits to having fallen for other men while still engaged, showing a pattern of indecision beneath her composed professional image. Ultimately, her experience in Springfield softens her guarded nature and reconnects her with her fiancé. Voiced by Ellie Kemper. Notable quotes: Okay, Mary, you're a big city girl who never stops to enjoy the little things in life. And today, it all pays off.
quotes: Okay, Mary, you're a big city girl who never stops to enjoy the little things in life. And today, it all pays off.

title: Charles Montgomery Burns
text: Charles Montgomery Burns is Billionaire owner of the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant and the town's most powerful, wealthy citizen; Homer Simpson's boss. Mr. Burns is the ancient, frail-looking tycoon who rules Springfield through sheer wealth and ruthless self-interest. He treats his employees, especially Homer, as disposable and rarely bothers to learn their names despite their long, eventful history together. Cruel and greedy by nature, he shows no concern for worker safety, charity, or basic decency, often sending his dogs after unwanted visitors instead of helping them. His constant companion and devoted aide is Waylon Smithers, who secretly harbors unrequited feelings for him that Burns never notices. Burns's speech is peppered with archaic, outdated phrases and Victorian-era references, reinforcing how disconnected he is from the modern world. Over the course of the series he becomes portrayed as less purely evil and more comically senile and eccentric, though his lust for money and power never fades. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Excellent. | Release the hounds! | You're fired.
quotes: Excellent.
Release the hounds!

title: Nina Skalka
text: Nina Skalka is Background student in Bart Simpson's fourth-grade class at Springfield Elementary School. Nina Skalka, sometimes called Missy, is one of the many nameless-seeming faces that fill out Bart's classroom crowd, easily spotted thanks to her blond pigtails and pink outfit. She rarely gets to do anything memorable, spending most of her screen time simply existing in the background of school scenes across the series' long run. On one occasion she was caught trying to shoplift a pair of socks at the store Wee Monsieur, only for security guards to burst in after spotting her on camera. She was also lucky enough to be the sole kid who managed to snag a Lisa Lionheart doll during the toy's frenzied release. Her only real speaking moment came when Milhouse insulted Mrs. Krabappel on the school bus, giving Nancy Cartwright a rare chance to voice her directly. Fittingly for such a minor character, her name itself is an inside joke, borrowed from a real-life licensing coordinator at the company that published the Virtual Bart video game. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Elaine Wolff
text: Elaine Wolff is Dog psychologist who helps the Simpson family treat Santa's Little Helper's behavioral issues. Elaine Wolff is a dedicated dog psychologist who runs the Dognitive Behavioral Therapy Institute. She claims to prefer animals to people, yet this is complicated by her lingering feelings for an ex named Clayton, who repeatedly tries to win her back. Elaine is deeply committed to her work, even sleeping on the floor beside troubled dogs to comfort them, and she prioritizes her patients over her own romantic life. She's analytical and persistent, eventually diagnosing Santa's Little Helper's aggression as trauma from his past as a racing dog. Elaine also takes noticeable pride in being proven right, especially once her suspicions about the dog's behavior are confirmed. Her strong sense of justice comes through when she confronts and slaps Santa's Little Helper's former owner for his mistreatment of the dog. Voiced by Cate Blanchett.

title: Constance Harm
text: Constance Harm is A recurring judge in Springfield's courtroom, often presiding over cases involving the Simpson family. Constance Harm is a strict, merciless judge who seems to relish handing out harsh, over-the-top punishments to those who appear before her. Unlike the more relaxed Judge Snyder, she keeps a guillotine on her bench instead of a friendly ornament, signaling her severe approach to justice. Despite her intimidating demeanor, she is knowledgeable and precise about the law, often catching people trying to twist legal technicalities in their favor. She's easily provoked by personal jabs, especially about her private life, and reacts with disproportionate retaliation. It's revealed that she is transgender, having transitioned from male to female, a fact that shocks some Springfield residents when it comes up in court. Outside the courtroom, she has had brief personal entanglements, including a past relationship with Moe Szyslak. Her character serves as a comedic parody of real-life tough television judges, exaggerated for effect in her cruel sentencing style. Voiced by Jane Kaczmarek. Notable quotes: I'm going to lock you up 'till frogs do fractions! | I have a husband! | You remind me of me, when I was a little boy.
quotes: I'm going to lock you up 'till frogs do fractions!
I have a husband!

title: Monk Murphy
text: Monk Murphy is Deaf son of Bleeding Gums Murphy who mentors deaf children; briefly connects with Lisa Simpson. Monk is the previously unknown son of jazz musician Bleeding Gums Murphy, born deaf and unable to afford cochlear implants growing up. He gets by using lip-reading and sign language, and works as a mentor to deaf kids at a center called The Sky's the Limit. When Lisa tracks him down, he's initially open but grows bitter after a music publisher reveals his father's song rights were sold off long ago, causing him to shut Lisa out. His arc centers on reconciliation, as Lisa's apology mends their relationship, and he eventually gets cochlear implants after winning some lottery money. His storyline is notable for making him the show's first deaf character, fittingly voiced by an actor who is also deaf. Voiced by John Autry II. Notable quotes: screw you, Bart!
quotes: screw you, Bart!

title: Princess Kashmir
text: Princess Kashmir is Exotic dancer in Springfield first introduced at a bachelor party attended by Homer. Princess Kashmir, whose real name is Shawna Tifton, is a minor recurring figure in Springfield's seedier entertainment scene, performing under stage names like April Flowers at various strip clubs around town. Despite once being genuinely moved by Homer's clumsy speech about respecting women, she never actually changes careers and continues dancing for years afterward, which is treated as a running ironic joke. She has romantic or flirtatious ties to several Springfield men, both single and married, showing up in unexpected contexts across many episodes. Outside of dancing, she dabbles in minor celebrity culture, appearing on a local game show and joining a bowling team with other women connected to Homer's world. She also nurses ambitions of being taken seriously as an actress, landing small, campy film roles that never quite elevate her status. Her personality is often shown as easily annoyed by rudeness, yet she's also willing to indulge in some hypocrisy when it suits her. Voiced by Maggie Roswell.

title: Snowball II
text: Snowball II is The Simpson family's pet cat, owned primarily by Lisa Simpson. Snowball II is Lisa's black cat, adopted as a replacement after the death of the original white cat, Snowball I, making her name something of an ironic joke. Despite the tragic pattern of pets dying in the Simpson household, she has remained a fairly steady presence, generally shown lounging around the house and getting along peacefully with the family dog, Santa's Little Helper. She's shown occasional moments of heroism, such as helping save Homer from danger, and moments of neediness when craving affection. In one storyline she wanders off to live with another family who spoils her, leading her to become overweight before eventually returning home. In non-canon Treehouse of Horror material, she's portrayed as secretly capable of human speech, revealing a hidden double life and a whole secret family of button-eyed beings. Overall, she functions as a low-key background gag character rather than a driver of plots, appearing across countless episodes as part of the show's ongoing visual continuity. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Frank Welker, Neil Gaiman.

title: Everyman
text: Everyman is Comic-book superhero created by Comic Book Guy, later portrayed by Homer Simpson in a film adaptation. Everyman is a fictional superhero whose alter ego, mail carrier Avery Mann, is an unremarkable, out-of-shape everyday guy. His unique power lets him absorb the abilities of any superhero simply by touching their comic book, letting him borrow Iron Man's armor, Plastic Man's stretching, Batman's gadgets, and even more abstract traits like Captain America's patriotism or Wonder Woman's... assets. Created by Comic Book Guy as a hit indie comic, the character's popularity led to a botched Hollywood adaptation starring Homer Simpson, whose fluctuating weight during filming became an ongoing joke reflected in the finished movie. The story satirizes superhero movie productions, showing how studio interference and vanity (via a fickle personal trainer) can derail a passion project. Despite his silly gimmick, Everyman is portrayed as sincere and heroic within his own comic-book world, once teaming with Marmaduke and battling the villainous Dr. Reptilicus. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Everyman will stop every crime every time! And I... am... Everyman!
quotes: Everyman will stop every crime every time! And I... am... Everyman!

title: Pope
text: Pope is The leader of the Catholic Church and ruler of Vatican City, referenced sporadically as a background/real-world figure in Springfield's universe. The Pope appears in the show mostly as a distant, real-world authority figure rather than a fully developed character, popping up in mentions, news reports, and the occasional cameo. He's depicted attending the unveiling of a Homer statue and later dying, as reported by Kent Brockman. Various Springfield residents reference him in passing, comparing lenience, prestige, or fame to the Pope, showing how deeply his symbolic authority permeates their culture. He's also the target of a get-rich scheme by Mr. Burns, who mistakenly believes he can access Vatican riches through a Protestant church. In non-canon material, he's treated as background celebrity, appearing in parades and even getting a wedgie from Bart. Overall, the character functions as a running cultural reference point for religious authority and fame rather than a recurring personality. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Wonder Woman
text: Wonder Woman is DC Comics superhero referenced repeatedly as a pop-culture icon within the Simpsons universe. Wonder Woman isn't a true member of the Simpsons cast but a real-world comic book icon that pops up throughout the show as a running pop-culture reference. She's treated as an object of fascination for various characters, from Homer's leering comments to Lisa's admiration of her as an empowering, superpowered goddess. Her image appears in many forms across Springfield—cardboard cutouts, statues, magazine covers, and even inspiring Marge to open her clothing store, Shapes. Comic Book Guy has a notably awkward history with her, having once dressed as her for Halloween and calling it his worst holiday ever. She's also tied to actress Lynda Carter, who appears in-universe dressed as the character on multiple occasions. Overall, Wonder Woman functions as a flexible cultural touchstone the show uses for jokes about superhero fandom, gender, and nostalgia. Notable quotes: "Give me Wonder Woman," - Homer | "Wonder Woman showed that if you are a goddess with superpowers, there's no limit to what you can do." - Lisa
quotes: "Give me Wonder Woman," - Homer
"Wonder Woman showed that if you are a goddess with superpowers, there's no limit to what you can do." - Lisa

title: Warburton Parker
text: Warburton Parker is Hipster branding/marketing expert who sponsors Homer and Bart's viral online videos. Warburton Parker is a trend-obsessed branding consultant who thrives on YouTube and MyTube virality, always pushing aggressive, in-your-face product placement no matter the cost to his clients. He claims a colorful backstory as a former outcast turned pro-snowboarder and tech mogul, though how much of it is true is left ambiguous. Petty and vindictive, he even bought out and shut down the factories where his childhood bullies' parents worked. His hipster sensibilities make him embrace things others consider uncool, and he's more concerned with profit and image than the wellbeing of the people he represents, as seen when he happily lets Homer and Bart risk real harm for views. When his schemes collapse, he abandons his clients without much remorse, showing his loyalty is purely transactional. He later resurfaces trying to help rebrand Mr. Burns' failing brandy company before being unceremoniously dropped through a trap door. Voiced by John Mulaney. Notable quotes: My name is Warburton Parker. I'm a stranger to you. Why should you listen to me? You don't know my backstory. Well, here it is.
quotes: My name is Warburton Parker. I'm a stranger to you. Why should you listen to me? You don't know my backstory. Well, here it is.

title: Dewey Largo
text: Dewey Largo is Music teacher at Springfield Elementary School who leads Lisa's band class. Dewey Largo is the joyless, uptight music instructor at Springfield Elementary, infamous for draining any hint of passion or creativity out of the songs he teaches. He sticks to dull, unimaginative arrangements, which constantly frustrates Lisa and pushes her to break away with improvised saxophone solos. His own backstory suggests his bitterness stems from missing out on a chance at Juilliard as a kid, and from being force-fed 'fake dreams' at an arts camp called Expressions. Largo is gay and spent much of his life closeted, dodging questions about his sexuality until eventually being outed after running off with a boyfriend also named Dewey. He later marries Grady Little, though that doesn't last, and settles into a relationship with Geoffrey, with whom he shares a dog. Beyond music class, he's shown to be generally incompetent outside his specialty, such as when he briefly and disastrously filled in as school groundskeeper. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "it's just a place where they fill people with fake dreams." - Dewey Largo
quotes: "it's just a place where they fill people with fake dreams." - Dewey Largo

title: St. Peter
text: St. Peter is Gatekeeper of Heaven who appears in various dream sequences, flashbacks, and non-canon Treehouse of Horror episodes. St. Peter is depicted as the stern but occasionally whimsical doorman of Heaven, deciding who gets to enter based on their deeds in life. He's shown to be a stickler for the rules, famously denying Homer entry multiple times over his lack of good deeds, only to seemingly ignore Homer's one genuine good act out of spite or amusement. Despite his serious duty, he has a dry, almost mischievous sense of humor, particularly evident when he sends Homer to Hell with a casual joke. He also appears in a more solemn, inspirational role, guiding Father Sean toward the priesthood in a vision. In other appearances, he's portrayed as somewhat lazy or detached, reading a newspaper while judging souls, and even casually mentions Heaven being sold to Google. Despite the absurdity of his non-canon antics, he remains loosely tied to his real-world religious significance as the first Pope and keeper of Heaven's keys. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Yes, I'm afraid so, yes.
quotes: Yes, I'm afraid so, yes.

title: Gautama Buddha
text: Gautama Buddha is Historical/religious figure (founder of Buddhism) who occasionally appears in Springfield's fantasy/dream sequences and Heaven-set scenes. Gautama Buddha shows up in the Simpsons universe mostly as a spiritual figure referenced or imagined during the family's various religious explorations. He's portrayed as a calm, wise teacher of non-attachment, but the show often undercuts his serenity with absurd gags, like being pulled over by police while driving a sports car, or being genuinely stumped by Ralph Wiggum's nonsensical zen-like statements. He appears in Heaven alongside God, Jesus, and other religious/pop-culture figures, sometimes advocating for fairness, such as arguing that Buddhists deserve a place in Heaven too. Lisa is the character most drawn to his teachings, repeatedly turning to him during her spiritual searches and even attempting to convert others using his philosophy. Despite his importance as a historical religious founder, he's treated with light irreverence, becoming a punchline in Homer's misadventures as often as a source of genuine wisdom. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Kevin Michael Richardson. Notable quotes: Buddha told the police that he wasn't going to jail again and that he had their badge numbers. | Buddha asked Lisa what he was going to do with Ralph Wiggum when Ralph said "everything is nothing," which blew Buddha's mind.
quotes: Buddha told the police that he wasn't going to jail again and that he had their badge numbers.

title: Alice Glick
text: Alice Glick is Elderly Springfield resident and minor recurring character, occasionally the church organist, who briefly employed Bart for chores. Mrs. Glick is a cranky, dementia-addled old woman who lives in the Simpsons' neighborhood and pops up constantly in the background of Springfield life. She first drew attention when she hired Bart for underpaid chores, revealing macabre habits like dyeing her wedding dress black for her husband's funeral. Her grip on reality is shaky at best, leading to bizarre incidents such as mistaking Lisa for a pineapple and Ralph for a pumpkin during a hurricane panic, or unknowingly selling priceless historical artifacts for nickels at a swap meet. Despite her frailty, she shows flashes of civic pride and stubbornness, and she has a habit of hoarding oddly specific keepsakes and stories about her late brother Asa. She's died multiple times across the show's non-canon continuities, from being killed by a rogue robotic seal to collapsing again at the church organ, each time treated with dark comic absurdity. Overall, she's a background fixture of Springfield's elderly population, defined by senility, gallows humor, and unexpected cameos in nearly every era of the show. Voiced by Cloris Leachman (first appearance); Tress MacNeille (other appearances). Notable quotes: Well, I think what you're doing for Mrs. Glick is very nice. Poor old thing doesn't have anybody. | There's a reason.
quotes: Well, I think what you're doing for Mrs. Glick is very nice. Poor old thing doesn't have anybody.
There's a reason.

title: Matt Groening (character)
text: Matt Groening (character) is Fictionalized version of the real-life creator of The Simpsons and Futurama, appearing as a celebrity character within the show. This character is a cartoonish stand-in for the real Matt Groening, celebrated within Springfield as a legendary animator and cartoonist. He's often mobbed by adoring fans at conventions, generously offering pieces of his mustache for luck. Despite his fame, his artistic skill is sometimes mocked, as when Homer dismisses his Life in Hell drawings as amateurish. He has a habit of popping up in odd cameo situations, from serving as a courtroom caricature artist to wandering past Comic Book Guy at a comic expo. In non-canon material, he's portrayed in far more exaggerated and violent ways, including as a gun-toting war veteran or a mansion-dwelling supervillain who battles Homer and Bart with living cartoon monsters. Across appearances he embodies a mix of self-parody, geek-culture reverence, and absurd exaggeration typical of the show's meta humor. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Batman
text: Batman is DC Comics superhero who appears/is referenced in various Simpsons episodes, often as a pop-culture touchstone. Batman exists in the Simpsons universe as the famous crime-fighting superhero from DC Comics, appearing in cameos, hallucinations, comics, and countless references throughout the show. Homer famously misunderstands a rescue situation by assuming Batman himself has come to help stop a runaway monorail, showing his tendency to confuse fiction with reality. The character is frequently used as a punchline, cultural reference, or costume choice for other Simpsons characters like Krusty the Clown, Comic Book Guy, and even Homer and Ned during a hallucinogenic trip. Batman's ward Robin, his vehicle the Batmobile, and his rogue The Joker are also referenced in the show's world. Various real actors associated with playing Batman, such as Adam West, Michael Keaton, and Diedrich Bader, have guest-starred on the show, sometimes as themselves interacting with the Simpsons family. The character underscores the show's love of parodying pop culture and superhero tropes, most directly through Bart's own alter ego, Bartman. Voiced by Adam West, Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Batman?|[[Homer Simpson]] | Batman's a scientist.|Homer | It's not Batman.|Marge|Marge vs. the Monorail

Batman's a scientist.|Homer

title: Julius Hibbert
text: Julius Hibbert is Springfield's family doctor to the Simpsons and most of the town. Dr. Hibbert is Springfield's most respected physician, a Johns Hopkins graduate and Mensa member who serves as the Simpson family's doctor. His defining quirk is an odd habit of chuckling warmly at even the most serious or inappropriate moments, giving him an air of unshakable good humor. Despite his polished, upstanding image, the show repeatedly hints that he's mercenary and ethically flexible, casually raising his fees, joking about black-market babies, and hinting at a shady past that may include practicing without a proper license. He's also something of a Bill Cosby parody, right down to his ugly sweaters and wholesome family-man image that occasionally cracks to reveal marital tension or a surprisingly wild past as a stripper named 'Malcolm Sex.' A running gag involves his unacknowledged connection to jazz musician Bleeding Gums Murphy, who may actually be his long-lost brother, though neither ever puts it together. His hairstyle changes constantly in flashbacks, and he's shown to be both a committed Republican and an enthusiastic pitchman for pharmaceutical companies. Voiced by Harry Shearer (1990-2021); Kevin Michael Richardson (2021-Present). Notable quotes: It's very simple. When an adult's life is in danger, a child can summon superhuman strength! | I'm afraid it's now $40,000 | paying for it sure is!

title: Fred Flintstone
text: Fred Flintstone is Crossover character from The Flintstones who appears/is referenced in The Simpsons universe. Fred Flintstone is the famous stone-age patriarch from the classic Hanna-Barbera cartoon, imported into the Simpsons universe as a recurring pop-culture reference. He's most often invoked as a shorthand for a bumbling, loud everyman husband, frequently compared to or confused with Homer Simpson. His likeness turns up on merchandise like T-shirts and toy phones, and characters sometimes dress up as him for costume parties or Halloween. In one non-canon crossover appearance, he even takes on the unexpected role of a courtroom judge. True to his cartoon roots, his signature catchphrase gets triggered whenever someone presses his face on a toy phone. Despite never being a physical presence in Springfield, his cultural footprint pops up repeatedly through mentions, imagery, and Homer's own self-comparisons. Voiced by Henry Corden, Jeff Bergman. Notable quotes: Yabba dabba doo! I like talkin' to you!
quotes: Yabba dabba doo! I like talkin' to you!

title: Booberella
text: Booberella is Local Springfield TV personality who hosts late-night monster movies; minor recurring character connected to Mr. Burns, Kent Brockman, and Duffman. Booberella, real name Barbara Lelavinsky, is a busty, vampire-styled television host known for her late-night monster movie broadcasts in Springfield. Her defining trait is an exaggerated obsession with her own breasts, which she references constantly, often in a campy Dracula-esque cadence. She is the daughter of Bill, an accountant at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, and has been romantically linked to Duffman. She once briefly took over Marge Simpson's job at the Springfield Shopper and even runs her own line of handbags. Booberella also appeared on Homer's hypothetical remarriage list, showing she's seen as an eligible, if eccentric, local celebrity. She's a parody of Elvira, Mistress of the Dark, blending horror-host camp with self-aware sexual humor. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: He's got a heart as big as my booooooooobs! | I guess we'll have to agree to agree on this one. | (After long pause) Boooooobs!
quotes: He's got a heart as big as my booooooooobs!

title: Vicki Valentine
text: Vicki Valentine is A strict dance instructor and former child star who runs a Springfield dance studio attended by Lisa and Ralph. Vicki Valentine was once a famous child actress in the late 1930s and early 1940s, starring in dozens of movies before growing up and reinventing herself as a dance teacher. She proudly displays memorabilia from her acting days around her studio and clearly still enjoys being recognized for her past fame. As an instructor she's demanding and offers minimal real guidance, relying on repetitive chanting rather than teaching technique, which frustrates less talented students like Lisa. Her professional pride borders on vanity, and she reacts with visible irritation whenever she feels a student might outshine her, going so far as to insert herself into a recital to avoid being overshadowed. Despite her strict and somewhat self-centered nature, she is regarded as an effective teacher who has helped many people learn to dance. She's loosely modeled after real-life former child star Shirley Temple. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Tappa, tappa, tappa. Tappa, tappa, tappa.
quotes: Tappa, tappa, tappa. Tappa, tappa, tappa.

title: Buck Mitchell
text: Buck Mitchell is A professional baseball player for the Springfield Isotopes, married to singer Tabitha Vixx. Buck Mitchell is a star player for the Springfield Isotopes whose personal life spills over into his performance on the field. He's a self-described old-fashioned guy who expected his wife to abandon her own career to support his, which creates ongoing tension in their marriage. Easily embarrassed by his wife's provocative stage persona, his on-field performance fluctuates wildly with the state of his relationship, playing brilliantly when things are good and terribly when they're not. His marital troubles become public spectacle, drawing in Homer and Marge as unlikely and often disastrous marriage counselors. Despite jealous outbursts, including knocking Homer out after catching him giving Tabitha a neck massage, Buck's story ultimately centers on his desire to win his wife back through grand, sports-themed gestures. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Daphne Burns
text: Daphne Burns is Mother of Charles Montgomery Burns, matriarch of the wealthy Burns family. Daphne Burns is the elderly, rarely-seen mother of Springfield's tycoon Mr. Burns, whose exact fate—alive in a nursing home or long dead—is a running point of confusion in the show. Her marriage to Clifford Burns was overshadowed by a scandalous affair with President Taft, something her son never forgave her for, and he even hints he tried to have her disconnected from life support out of spite. She's depicted as having birthed numerous children, several of whose paternity remains murky despite all bearing the Burns surname. In her rare present-day appearance, she's reduced to feebly dialing phones and shouting from what seems to be a care facility, with Mr. Burns almost never bothering to call her. Various episodes contradict whether she's dead, deceased by neglect, or simply estranged, adding a dark comic uncertainty to her characterization. She also became briefly entangled in a subplot where an impersonator hired to play her ended up marrying Abraham Simpson, momentarily making Homer and Mr. Burns believe they were step-brothers. Voiced by Tress MacNeille, Amy Schumer, Pamela Hayden. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns has a mother? She must be a hundred million years old! - Homer Simpson
quotes: Mr. Burns has a mother? She must be a hundred million years old! - Homer Simpson

title: Leonard Nimoy (character)
text: Leonard Nimoy (character) is Real-world actor famous for playing Spock in Star Trek, who appears as himself in guest appearances throughout the show. Leonard Nimoy appears as a fictionalized version of himself, most memorably as the Grand Marshal at the disastrous opening of the Springfield Monorail. He plays up his Star Trek fame with constant sci-fi quips and references that annoy the other passengers, while also showing a surprisingly caring side by talking Krusty out of jumping from the moving train. His legacy in Springfield is later commemorated with a statue crediting him for saving the townspeople, though it meets a fittingly absurd end when destroyed by a runaway monorail. Beyond that episode, he pops up in cameo roles such as narrating an alien story and singing with the town, cementing his status as a recurring celebrity guest. The show also references his real-world career through jokes about his books and albums, often blurring the line between his actual persona and comedic exaggeration. Overall, he serves as a running gag about celebrity cameos and pop-culture nods to Star Trek lore. Voiced by Leonard Nimoy. Notable quotes: A solar eclipse. The cosmic ballet goes on. | I'd say this vessel could do at least Warp 5.
quotes: A solar eclipse. The cosmic ballet goes on.

title: The Be Sharps
text: The Be Sharps is A barbershop quartet formed by Homer Simpson, Apu Nahasapeemapetilon, Seymour Skinner, and (at various times) Chief Wiggum or Barney Gumble, parodying The Beatles' rise and fall. The Be Sharps started as a casual singing group performing at Moe's Tavern before being discovered and turned into a real recording act by a shady manager named Nigel. Their fame skyrocketed after a rooftop-style concert at the Statue of Liberty and a Grammy win, mirroring the real-life trajectory of famous rock bands. Success brought infighting, ego clashes, and personal drama, including Barney's romance with a Japanese conceptual artist, which ultimately tore the group apart. The band's rise-and-fall arc is played as a direct spoof of The Beatles, right down to an album title referencing John Lennon's infamous 'bigger than Jesus' remark. Even after breaking up, the Be Sharps left behind a legacy of merchandise, novelty songs, and pop-culture cameos, including a dangerous foam toy product that got recalled. The group has been referenced and revisited many times in flashbacks, tributes, and non-canon material long after their in-universe breakup. Notable quotes: "Can I rejoin now that Skinner's croaked?" - Chief Wiggum | "We'll call you!" - Homer Simpson | "Anyone who ate it deserved to die" - Homer Simpson

title: Lily (The 7 Beer Itch)
text: Lily (The 7 Beer Itch) is A British woman who moves to Springfield and becomes a romantic interest for Homer in "The 7 Beer Itch". Lily is an irresistibly charming British woman whose beauty causes men everywhere to fall for her, a trait that once drove her out of her home country to escape jealous conflicts. After a whimsical dart-throw sends her to Springfield, she settles in at Moe's Tavern, quickly becoming popular among the barflies for her lively singing and energy. She's drawn to Homer precisely because he initially resists her charm, and her infatuation grows into genuine feelings even as Mr. Burns clumsily competes for her affection. Despite the emotional pull between them, Lily respects Homer's devotion to Marge and ultimately lets him go. Her storyline plays with themes of temptation and fidelity, ending on a bittersweet note as she returns to London and finds solace with a man who resembles Homer. Throughout, she's portrayed as warm-hearted, alluring, and self-aware about the chaos her beauty causes. Voiced by Olivia Colman. Notable quotes: Lily told Homer that they would see each other in their dreams.
quotes: Lily told Homer that they would see each other in their dreams.

title: Snoopy
text: Snoopy is A crossover character from Peanuts—Charlie Brown's dog—who appears as a recurring background reference/image in The Simpsons rather than a true cast member. Snoopy is not an active character in The Simpsons universe but rather a recurring pop-culture reference borrowed from the Peanuts comic strip, always tied to his owner Charlie Brown. He shows up repeatedly as an image—on puzzles, stationery, wine bottles, flags, and paintings—rather than as a physical presence interacting with the Simpsons family. Occasionally the reference goes further, such as characters wearing Snoopy costumes or masks, including a memorable moment when Dolly Parton escapes in one. He's also used as a punchline or point of comparison, like Homer citing Snoopy's crying as inspiration for his Angry Dad voice, or Marge naming him her favorite Peanuts character. As a non-speaking character, Snoopy never has dialogue of his own within the show; his role is purely that of a running visual gag and nostalgic nod to another famous cartoon universe.

title: Karl
text: Karl is Homer Simpson's personal assistant during his brief stint as a junior executive at the power plant. Karl was the sharp, competent assistant assigned to help Homer navigate his unexpected promotion to junior executive. He boosted Homer's confidence, taught him how to dress and carry himself, and even smoothed over Homer's forgotten wedding anniversary with a clever save. When Homer's health insurance fraud was uncovered, Karl selflessly took the blame and lost his own job to protect him, then continued helping Homer prepare for a big speech even after being fired. His mannerisms and a notable kiss with Homer sparked long-running fan speculation about his sexuality, especially given that he was voiced by openly gay actor Harvey Fierstein. Despite his loyalty and effort, his final act of encouragement couldn't save Homer's executive career, which ended in demotion. Karl's fate after leaving the plant is never revealed. Voiced by Harvey Fierstein. Notable quotes: "My mother taught me never to kiss a fool." | "I deserve this! I am nature's greatest miracle!"
quotes: "My mother taught me never to kiss a fool."
"I deserve this! I am nature's greatest miracle!"

title: Kearney Zzyzwicz
text: Kearney Zzyzwicz is One of the school bullies at Springfield Elementary, alongside Jimbo and Dolph. Kearney is the roughest-looking and most intimidating of Springfield Elementary's trio of bullies, sporting a shaved head and a gruff demeanor that makes him seem far older than his classmates. Despite his tough exterior, he's easily sidetracked and not particularly bright, remaining stuck in school for years while his peers move on. His backstory is full of odd contradictions, having a teenage son, a father who looks just like him, and a troubled home life with an absent, medicated mother. He tends to drift between petty crime, casual violence, and strange domestic moments, blurring the line between menacing bully and pathetic man-child. In various non-canon glimpses of the future, he's imagined as everything from a mellowed-out vice principal to a trigger-happy presidential bodyguard. Kearney's exaggerated toughness and constant confusion about his own age and life stage make him a running joke throughout the series. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: Kearney says that he is speaking "as a teenager and parent of a teenager"
quotes: Kearney says that he is speaking "as a teenager and parent of a teenager"

title: Jimmy Carter
text: Jimmy Carter is Former U.S. President who makes recurring cameo appearances in Springfield, often tied to Habitat for Humanity. Jimmy Carter appears in the show as a real-world figure best remembered for his post-presidency charity work building homes for the needy. He's portrayed as good-natured but occasionally short-tempered, notably challenging Homer to a duel after being insulted. He gets mixed up in slapstick mishaps with fellow ex-presidents George H. W. Bush and Bill Clinton during a joint building project. The show also mocks him as a one-term president, having him tossed out of Mr. Burns' birthday party for that reason. A statue of him briefly stood in Springfield's park after a bake sale failed to raise enough money for a Lincoln statue instead, leading to public backlash. He's frequently referenced in Homer's jokes and comparisons to other political figures. Voiced by Karl Wiedergott, Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: C'mon, Carter, build us a house, you lazy bum. | Scooby-Doo can doo-doo, but Jimmy Carter is smarter.
quotes: C'mon, Carter, build us a house, you lazy bum.
Scooby-Doo can doo-doo, but Jimmy Carter is smarter.

title: Grady Little
text: Grady Little is One of two gay men (with his boyfriend Julio Franco) whom Homer temporarily moves in with; recurring member of Springfield's gay community.. Grady Little is a laid-back, self-absorbed gay man living in Springfield's Gay Village with his on-and-off boyfriend Julio Franco. When Homer briefly moves out of the Simpson house, he ends up as their roommate, and Grady develops unrequited feelings for him, even sharing a kiss before Homer returns to Marge. His romantic life is notably chaotic, cycling through breakups and reunions with Julio, a stint being pushed by Homer into dating Duffman, and eventually a marriage to Dewey Largo that later seems to end in divorce. Despite his tangled love life, Grady remains a good-humored, easygoing presence at Springfield social gatherings, from parties at the Simpson house to Tupperware get-togethers. He's characterized as somewhat oblivious to things outside his own concerns, admitting he's usually too self-involved to notice what's going on around him. Over the years he's appeared as a recurring background character representing Springfield's LGBT community. Voiced by Scott Thompson.

title: Plopper
text: Plopper is Homer Simpson's pet pig, first introduced in The Simpsons Movie. Plopper is the pig Homer rescues from being slaughtered after appearing in a Krusty Burger commercial, and he quickly becomes one of Homer's most cherished companions. Homer dotes on him obsessively, even singing a goofy superhero-style song while walking him along the ceiling like Spider-Man, which gives the pig his nickname Spider-Pig. Over time Homer renames him multiple times, from Spider-Pig to Harry Plopper, before settling on simply Plopper, and the pig's droppings inadvertently trigger a major environmental disaster in Springfield. His close bond with Homer causes friction with Bart, who resents being treated as less important than a farm animal. Plopper later becomes a recurring presence in the Simpsons' lives, at one point being used as a fake therapy animal excuse and even getting caught in a bizarre custody-style dispute involving Mr. Burns and Smithers. Despite his simple nature, Plopper's ceiling walk and theme song became one of the most iconic and memorable gags associated with the movie. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Gary Chalmers
text: Gary Chalmers is Superintendent of Springfield's school district and Principal Skinner's ever-exasperated boss. Gary Chalmers is the perpetually stern, humorless superintendent overseeing Springfield Elementary, whose military-like bearing and low tolerance for chaos make him a source of constant dread for Principal Skinner. He's best known for storming into rooms and bellowing Skinner's name whenever something has gone wrong at the school, a habit so ingrained that he sometimes does it even when nothing is amiss, or applies the same booming inflection to unrelated rhyming words. Despite his authoritative image, Chalmers is shown to be surprisingly unprincipled and inconsistent, making decisions based on personal grudges or bias rather than merit, and he's had a messy string of romantic entanglements despite being a widower. His backstory includes a failed teaching career cut short by an assault from students, a stint as a power plant janitor, and an unlikely rise to wealth through a beauty product made from snail slime. Underneath the blustery exterior, he's portrayed as cynical and detached about the true state of the school system, often reacting to its decline with dark humor rather than real concern. Chalmers stands out as one of the few characters in Springfield who seems genuinely aware of how absurd everything around him is. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Skinnerrrrr!!! | Skinner really bugged me. | the way America's public schools are sliding, they'll all be like this in a matter of months. I say enjoy it — it's a hell of a toboggan ride!
quotes: Skinnerrrrr!!!
Skinner really bugged me.
