title: Database
text: Database is A nerdy student at Springfield Elementary and leader of "The Superfriends" club. Database, real name Kyle, is a bespectacled science-minded kid who leads a clique of fellow nerds called the Superfriends. He's almost always found alongside his fellow outcast Martin Prince, and like other geeky kids at school, he's a frequent target of bullies such as Nelson, Dolph, Jimbo, and Kearney. His defining trait is his sharp scientific reasoning, shown when he quickly deduced that a supposed comet was actually on a collision course with Springfield. He's welcoming to new members, having formally inducted Bart Simpson into the Superfriends and given him a science-themed nickname. Database has also taken part in bigger group adventures, including helping retrieve the town's stolen lemon tree and joining the Pre-Teen Braves. Despite his intelligence, he's not particularly athletic or lucky, having lost a school race after getting distracted testing wind speed. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Rod Runtledge
text: Rod Runtledge is Comic-book character from the Radioactive Man comics; a teenage sidekick who becomes Fallout Boy. Rod Runtledge is a fictional character within the Simpsons universe's in-universe comic series about Radioactive Man. Orphaned after his parents and twin brother died in a plane crash, he was raised by his troubled Aunt June and briefly turned to petty crime before being set straight by his hero, Radioactive Man. An accident involving a malfunctioning Xeno-Ray grants him superpowers, leading him to discover that his neighbor Claude is secretly Radioactive Man, and he becomes his sidekick, Fallout Boy. His story includes losing and regaining his powers, being kidnapped by villains, and eventually being revealed in a possible future to have taken over the mantle of Radioactive Man himself. The character also appears in a fictional Radioactive Man film adaptation, where he's portrayed by Milhouse Van Houten, tying him into the show's meta-fictional layers of media parody. Recurring themes around him involve identity, mentorship, and the ties between ordinary teenage life and superheroics.

title: Jimbo Jones
text: Jimbo Jones is One of the bullies at Springfield Elementary who torments Bart and his friends. Jimbo is the de facto ringleader of Springfield Elementary's bully quartet, usually seen alongside Nelson, Kearney, and Dolph. He dresses the part of a rebellious tough guy with a skull T-shirt and purple knit cap, and enjoys shoplifting, smoking, drinking, and generally intimidating other kids. Despite his delinquent image, he's shown occasional flashes of conscience and even claims strong religious conviction, creating a contradiction between his bully persona and hinted-at morals. His home life is murky and a bit chaotic, with an absent or lowlife father figure and a mother whose reputation is a running joke among the gang. Jimbo's relationship with Bart fluctuates between grudging respect and casual bullying, and he even briefly dated Bart's babysitter before being humiliated by one of Bart's prank calls. Ultimately he's a comic archetype of the not-too-bright, image-obsessed schoolyard tough guy whose real name isn't even settled among the show's own continuity. Voiced by Pamela Hayden (Mo Collins, Tress MacNeille in "The Telltale Head"). Notable quotes: It's a lucky coincidence, you happen to be your sister's brother. | Jesus is our only king | His name's "Gunnar," and he's dating my mom. Sometimes, he buys us beer.
quotes: It's a lucky coincidence, you happen to be your sister's brother.
Jesus is our only king
His name's "Gunnar," and he's dating my mom. Sometimes, he buys us beer.

title: Lady Gaga (character)
text: Lady Gaga (character) is Real-world pop singer who appears as a celebrity guest character in Springfield. Lady Gaga appears as herself, popping up in Springfield in various celebrity cameos and mentions rather than as a regular cast member. She's shown as glamorous and famous, attracting paparazzi and being namedropped by star-struck locals like Apu. In one notable visit she rides into town on the Lady Gaga Express and takes it upon herself to boost the low self-esteem of Springfield's citizens, focusing especially on cheering up a gloomy Lisa. She's good-natured and determined, though she admits defeat when it comes to fixing Moe's outlook. The show also plays on her real-life fame and eccentric fashion, referencing her elaborate dresses and even a rumored stint in rehab. Occasionally she's treated as a minor annoyance or disaster in Springfield lore, and non-canon material has her attending a Simpsons premiere and being petitioned as an authority on detention rules. Voiced by Herself.

title: L.T. Smash
text: L.T. Smash is A Navy recruiter who poses as a record producer and forms the boy band Party Posse, recruiting Bart. L.T. Smash is a Navy lieutenant who moonlights as the founder and manager of the boy band Party Posse, using it as a front to secretly recruit young listeners into the Navy through subliminal messages. He presents himself as a cool, hip record producer, but his military bravado constantly threatens to break through his civilian disguise, especially when he barks orders and insults at people like a drill sergeant. Fiercely loyal to the Navy's mission, he refuses to accept authority when told to shut the program down, instead taking drastic and illegal action against Mad magazine for mocking the band. Outside of this scheme, he's shown to be resourceful and community-minded, rescuing Bart from an angry mob and later playing an active role in Homer's doomsday survival club. His personality is a blend of manufactured charm and unfiltered military intensity, with the mask slipping more as the story progresses. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Do you maggots want to see a show or not?! I, uh... I mean, uh, uh, here they are, the Party Posse!
quotes: Do you maggots want to see a show or not?! I, uh... I mean, uh, uh, here they are, the Party Posse!

title: Radioactive Ape
text: Radioactive Ape is A comic-book superhero ape from the Radioactive Man comics, allied with (and sometimes rescued by) Radioactive Man. Radioactive Ape, whose true identity is Grrk-Grrk, is a member of a once-peaceful, intelligent ape tribe empowered by radioactive ore. He gained his powers when Radioactive Man shielded him from a Xeno Ray blast meant to harm his tribe, fusing radiation with his own tribal biology. Using his abilities, he helped uplift his people's civilization, building Simian City and founding the Secret Society of Super-Simians. He's prone to bizarre, comic transformations—turning into a giant ape-baby, a mermaid-tailed creature, a hand puppet, and even a super-intelligent future ape—providing much of the story's comedic tension. Despite the chaos, he remains a loyal ally to Radioactive Man, fighting alongside him against villains like Brain-O the Magnificent and Nega-Pneumatica. He also has a romantic partner, Grrla-G'rrl, and enjoys a close, almost brotherly bond with his human superhero counterpart.

title: Old Jewish man
text: Old Jewish man is An elderly recurring resident of Springfield Retirement Castle, friend to Grampa Simpson and Jasper Beardley. This eccentric elderly gentleman is best known as one of Grampa Simpson's cronies at the Springfield Retirement Castle, often seen alongside Jasper Beardley. He's a bit senile and prone to outbursts, having earned nicknames like 'Crazy Guy' and 'Crazy Old Man' for his erratic behavior. Despite his frailty, he claims a colorful past, including a stint as a Warner Bros. executive during the filming of Casablanca, where he take credit for tampering with the film's ending. He also enjoyed a fleeting moment of internet-before-its-time fame for a bizarre pantsless street performance. His Jewish heritage occasionally connects him to other Jewish characters in Springfield, such as Krusty the Clown and Rabbi Krustofsky, with whom he shares a comic holiday tradition. He mostly exists as background comic relief, popping up across hundreds of episodes over the show's history. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "was just dopes in suits. Not like today!"
quotes: "was just dopes in suits. Not like today!"

title: Augustus Redfield
text: Augustus Redfield is Businessman, CEO of RedStar, and Abraham Simpson's former business partner. Gus Redfield is a wealthy tycoon who once ran a struggling burger joint, Worth-A-Try Burger, with a young Abraham Simpson before Krusty the Clown stole their signature spatula trick and put them out of business. Decades later, he resurfaces as a ruthless corporate mogul, buying out Krusty Burger just to fire Krusty and reclaim a measure of revenge. Beneath his sentimental reunion with Grampa lies a calculating mind, as he manipulates Abe into unknowingly helping him thwart his own children's boardroom coup. His three kids, Colby, Mav, and Sheila, are shown to be just as scheming as he is, revealing a family dynamic built on corporate ambition rather than warmth. Gus's arc blends nostalgia for his working-class past with the cutthroat instincts of a modern billionaire. He continues to appear in high-society settings, sitting on corporate boards and attending exclusive auctions. Voiced by John Lithgow.

title: Virgin Mary
text: Virgin Mary is Biblical figure, mother of Jesus Christ, who appears in Simpsons folklore, statues, and non-canon holiday specials. The Virgin Mary exists mostly at the edges of Simpsons canon, referenced through religious statues, family history, and one holiday-themed special. She's depicted as a powerful, almost supernatural figure, as seen when her statue springs to life and violently intervenes in a soccer riot. She also has a vengeful streak, cursing Homer after he refused to shelter her and Joseph. In the non-canon Christmas special, she plays a more traditional maternal role, giving birth to Jesus in a barn, fending off Herod's soldiers, and cleverly disguising her son to protect him. The gag of Marge portraying her in dream sequences and games ties Mary thematically to the show's own matriarch. Overall she functions as a recurring bit of religious iconography and holiday parody rather than a fleshed-out character with her own arc. Voiced by Julie Kavner, Tress MacNeille.

title: Carmen (Bart vs. Itchy & Scratchy)
text: Carmen (Bart vs. Itchy & Scratchy) is Sixth grade student at Springfield Elementary School and member of the girl gang Bossy Riot. Carmen is a tough, secretive sixth-grader who leads a clique of rebellious girls calling themselves Bossy Riot. She's guarded about her group's activities, often shutting down other members when they reveal too much to outsiders like Bart. Carmen and her friends use vandalism and pranks as a form of feminist protest against perceived unfairness at school and beyond. She's willing to manipulate others for her cause, as shown when she reveals Bart was only ever used for his fingerprints and DNA rather than genuine friendship. Despite her tough exterior, she and her gang eventually recruit Lisa Simpson, showing a willingness to expand their ranks to those who prove themselves 'hardcore' enough. Her recurring presence highlights themes of mischief, group loyalty, and rebellious spirit among Springfield's youth. Voiced by Awkwafina.

title: Mr. Sparkle
text: Mr. Sparkle is Japanese dishwashing detergent mascot who coincidentally looks exactly like Homer Simpson. Mr. Sparkle is the cartoonish face of a Japanese cleaning product that bears an uncanny resemblance to Homer, sparking confusion when Bart, Homer, and Lisa discover his image on a detergent box at the dump. His over-the-top promotional commercial features aggressive catchphrases, dancers turned into sumo wrestlers, and a shattered two-headed cow, showcasing the character's surreal, hyper-intense marketing persona. The mystery of his Homer-like appearance is eventually explained as pure coincidence, since his logo was formed by merging a fish company and a lightbulb company's symbols. Beyond the show itself, Mr. Sparkle has appeared in a wild manga-style comic battling anime parody villains, as a toy, and in various video games and merchandise. He's a recurring pop-culture in-joke about doppelgängers and bizarre foreign advertising tropes. In non-canon material, he even takes on a tragic note, committing ritual suicide in a video game after failing to meet expectations. Voiced by Sab Shimono. Notable quotes: I'm disrespectful to dirt!! Can you see that I am serious?
quotes: I'm disrespectful to dirt!! Can you see that I am serious?

title: Snake Jailbird
text: Snake Jailbird is Recurring career criminal in Springfield, frequently in and out of jail and often clashing with Chief Wiggum and the Simpson family. Snake is Springfield's perpetual repeat offender, forever getting arrested but never staying locked up for long. He talks with an exaggerated laid-back 'Valley dude' drawl, keeps a lighter tucked in his sleeve, and drives a beloved muscle car nicknamed Lil' Bandit. Despite his criminal lifestyle of car theft, robbery, and general mayhem, he shows surprising softness as a devoted father to his son Jeremy and maintains an on-and-off romance with his girlfriend Gloria. His backstory reveals he was once an idealistic archaeology professor whose stolen discovery pushed him toward a life of crime, adding an unexpected tragic layer to his rebellious persona. He frequently locks horns with Chief Wiggum, who has known him since childhood, and pops up across nearly every era of the show in small comedic crime-related bits. His many aliases and conflicting backstories are themselves a running joke about how unreliable his personal history is. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: totally self-defense
quotes: totally self-defense

title: McBain
text: McBain is Fictional movie action hero character played by actor Rainier Wolfcastle within the Simpsons universe. McBain is the over-the-top hero of a long-running fictional action movie franchise within the show, portrayed by the vain actor Rainier Wolfcastle. He's a hyper-violent parody of 1980s-90s action stars like Arnold Schwarzenegger and Bruce Willis, complete with implausible stunts, one-liners, and a relentless drive for revenge. His signature storyline involves avenging his partner Scoey's murder by taking down the drug lord Senator Mendoza through escalating violence, culminating in throwing Mendoza off a skyscraper. McBain frequently disregards rules and authority, punching out his own captain and blowing up a police manual rather than follow regulations. Beyond his crime-fighting movies, the character has been stretched into other genres, including a comedy film and a war-themed picture as a transport pilot. He recurs throughout the series mainly as clips or posters from his in-universe films, functioning as a running gag about excessive Hollywood machismo. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Roofi
text: Roofi is A children's singer-songwriter whose music Marge loves but Bart and Lisa despise. Roofi is a musician who writes simple, nonsensical songs aimed at toddlers, delighting Maggie and Marge while driving Bart and Lisa up the wall. Despite his gentle, kid-friendly image, he behaves like a temperamental rock star behind the scenes—short-tempered with fans and quick to abandon a performance if things go wrong. His concerts can spiral into chaos, as seen when an oversold, rain-soaked show full of unattended babies ends with him getting hit by a bottle and storming off stage. He's a clear parody of real-life children's entertainer Raffi, right down to referencing the actual performer in a news headline gag. Even after disastrous public appearances, his popularity in Springfield doesn't waver, and Marge keeps buying his albums for Maggie. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Show's over. Five, six, so long hicks.
quotes: Show's over. Five, six, so long hicks.

title: Brandine Spuckler
text: Brandine Spuckler is Wife of Cletus Spuckler and matriarch of the redneck Spuckler family. Brandine is Cletus Spuckler's wife and the mother of the numerous Spuckler children, embodying the show's exaggerated hillbilly stereotype. Her family tree is famously tangled, with hints that she and Cletus are cousins or even siblings, something she shrugs off with backwoods nonchalance. She's held a bizarre string of jobs, from a brief stripper audition to working at Dairy Queen to serving as a soldier in the Iraq War. Despite her rough exterior, she secretly taught herself to read after a tornado left books near her, hiding her literacy from Cletus out of fear of how he'd react. She's depicted as the stricter of the two parents, enforcing basic hygiene rules on the kids, and she plays the hambone in the Spuckler Family Band. Her devotion to Cletus is genuine, if oddly expressed, often blurring the line between spouse and family member in her affectionate remarks. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: "We's all kinda things!" | "the most wonderful husband, and son, I ever had." | "the shirt what Dairy Queen gave me"
quotes: "We's all kinda things!"
"the most wonderful husband, and son, I ever had."
"the shirt what Dairy Queen gave me"

title: Mrs. Muntz
text: Mrs. Muntz is Mother of school bully Nelson Muntz. Mrs. Muntz is depicted as a neglectful, alcoholic single mother whose chaotic personal life often overshadows her role as a parent. She has cycled through numerous jobs, most notably as a stripper, and has had an extensive string of romantic and sexual relationships with a wide variety of Springfield residents. Her love life is a running gag, with a literal 'wall of exes' in her home showcasing just how many partners she's had, including several unexpected figures like Krusty and Hank Scorpio. Despite her often careless behavior, she occasionally shows flashes of maternal concern, such as hiring a lawyer after Nelson was injured on a school trip. Her marriage history is turbulent, having been left by Nelson's father early on and later marrying a clown. She's also shown to dye her hair, hinting at a bit of vanity beneath her rough exterior. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Al Gore
text: Al Gore is Real-world former U.S. Vice President who appears as a recurring caricature in Springfield, often tied to environmental jokes. This version of Al Gore is a fictionalized take on the real politician, appearing occasionally to poke fun at his public image as stiff, monotone, and obsessively focused on the environment. He's the author of dull, self-important books like 'Sane Planning, Sensible Tomorrow,' which nobody seems to buy until the Pentagon itself has to be notified. Running gags include his flat, emotionless delivery even during celebrations, his fixation on global warming and carbon footprints, and other characters casually invoking his name as shorthand for environmentalism or political irrelevance. He's shown as someone who can laugh off his own stolen election by comparing notes with his Nobel Peace Prize, literalizing his post-political life as an environmental icon. Gore also shows up in merchandise form, dream sequences, and even monstrous fantasy versions where he embodies humanity's guilt over climate change. Despite the mockery, the show acknowledges his real achievements, including his Nobel Prize win for climate activism. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "Well, this calls for a celebration." - Al Gore | "I will." - Al Gore | "You are hearing me talk." - Al Gore doll
quotes: "Well, this calls for a celebration." - Al Gore
"I will." - Al Gore
"You are hearing me talk." - Al Gore doll

title: Kodos Johnson
text: Kodos Johnson is Recurring alien invader from Rigel 7, married to Kang, frequently seen attacking Springfield in Treehouse of Horror episodes. Kodos is one half of the infamous alien duo who repeatedly try to conquer Earth, always paired with their spouse Kang. Visually almost indistinguishable from Kang, Kodos is set apart mainly by a slightly higher-pitched voice, since the two otherwise share the same green, tentacled, one-eyed design. Despite hailing from another galaxy, Kodos speaks flawless English, a running joke attributed to a coincidental shared language with Rigellians. Kodos and Kang's gender has shifted between installments, being called both male and female across various episodes and comics, making their identity a point of ongoing ambiguity within the show's canon. Most of their appearances occur in the non-canon Treehouse of Horror specials, where they scheme to destroy or take over Earth, only to be foiled by human ingenuity or distracted by pop culture. Their partnership and campy sci-fi menace have made them a beloved annual fixture of the show's Halloween tradition. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Harry Potter (character)
text: Harry Potter (character) is Crossover character from the Harry Potter book/film series who makes cameo appearances and references throughout The Simpsons. Harry Potter appears in the Simpsons universe purely as a pop-culture reference rather than a fully developed character. He shows up as a poster boy on book covers, in a parody film screened at Moe's Tavern, and in various background gags referencing the wizarding world. Homer even nicknames Plopper the pig 'Harry Plopper' after him, showing how deeply the character has seeped into the show's cultural shorthand. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he's reimagined as a classmate of Bart and Lisa at a magic school, cleverly talking his way out of trouble with a teacher over contraband gum. The character is treated as an in-universe celebrity, name-dropped and depicted enough times to become a recurring meta-joke rather than a plot-driving figure. Notably, the actual film actor Daniel Radcliffe has guest-starred on The Simpsons multiple times, blurring the line between the fictional wizard and his real-world portrayer. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: Principal Skinner told Lisa she would be like Harry Potter "without all the magic and wonder".
quotes: Principal Skinner told Lisa she would be like Harry Potter "without all the magic and wonder".

title: Waylon Smithers, Jr.
text: Waylon Smithers, Jr. is Mr. Burns' devoted personal assistant and executive at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. Smithers is the loyal, obsequious right-hand man of Mr. Burns, handling the countless minor duties of running the power plant while nursing a not-so-secret crush on his boss. Despite being openly gay in practice, he rarely acknowledges it outright, and his affection for Burns goes largely unnoticed by the oblivious old tycoon. He's a devoted collector of Malibu Stacy dolls and even wrote a stage musical about them, showing a nerdy, fannish side beneath his buttoned-up professionalism. Though usually a yes-man, Smithers occasionally reaches a breaking point and pushes back against Burns' worst schemes, sometimes getting fired as a result. His identity is deeply tied to serving Burns, to the point that losing the job sends him spiraling into depression and drinking. Comedic subplots often explore his repressed longing, jealousy over Burns' romantic pursuits of women, and his fantasies about a relationship that will likely never be reciprocated. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: That's Homer Simpson, one of your (nickname) from sector 7G. | I've never seen someone taken to a Turkish prison so quickly. | Hello Smithers. You're quite good at turning me on

title: Gloria Grand
text: Gloria Grand is A journalist for WZEN News in the Radioactive Man comic-book universe, and love interest of superhero Radioactive Man/Claude Kane III. Gloria Grand is a dedicated, career-focused reporter who is far more interested in chasing big stories than romance, repeatedly rebuffing the wealthy socialite Claude Kane III's advances. Her investigative work keeps pulling her into the orbit of superheroics, and over time she develops genuine feelings for Radioactive Man without realizing he and Claude are the same person. In a memorable twist, an accident during a monster attack temporarily grants her Radioactive Man's own powers, transforming her into the short-lived heroine Radioactive Girl and nearly leading to a superhero wedding before a villain's scheme strips her abilities away. She's brave enough to fight back against villains herself, whether using improvised objects to deflect death rays or knocking out enemies during a rescue. Emotionally, she cycles through admiration, heartbreak, and renewed affection as Radioactive Man dies, returns, turns evil, and redeems himself. Despite the chaos surrounding her, she remains a consummate professional who struggles to keep her personal feelings separate from her reporting duties.

title: Conan O'Brien (character)
text: Conan O'Brien (character) is Real-life talk show host who appears as himself in cameo roles throughout the series. Conan O'Brien appears as a fictionalized version of himself, tied to his real career as a former Simpsons writer turned late-night host. He's referenced or shown hosting his various talk shows, with Bart, Snake, and other Springfield residents appearing on or mentioning his programs. His image turns up as decor in Springfield hangouts like The Pimento Grove and Springfield Sardi's, a running gag nodding to his celebrity status. In non-canon material, he's shown to be self-deprecating about his appearance, revealing he wears a wig over hair similar to Homer's. He also plays a meta role hosting a faux series finale premiere, reacting with dry skepticism to an AI-generated episode before sarcastically dismissing the whole endeavor. Overall, his character serves as a wink to his real behind-the-scenes history with the show and his broader fame as a comedian and TV personality. Voiced by Conan O'Brien (Himself).

title: Sanjay Nahasapeemapetilon
text: Sanjay Nahasapeemapetilon is Apu Nahasapeemapetilon's brother and occasional Kwik-E-Mart co-worker. Sanjay is a member of the sprawling Nahasapeemapetilon family who periodically pitches in at the Kwik-E-Mart alongside his brother Apu. He's not the most reliable employee, often skipping shifts and leaving Apu frustrated and shorthanded. As a family man, he dotes on his daughter Pahasatira and son Jamshed, even cheering enthusiastically at his daughter's beauty pageant performance when almost no one else appreciates it. He shares some of Apu's quirks, including a hinted tendency toward nudism. Sanjay mostly appears in the background of Springfield life, popping up for small moments involving the Kwik-E-Mart or family gatherings rather than driving major plots himself. His recurring presence reinforces the show's running joke of Apu's enormous extended family. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Julio Franco
text: Julio Franco is A gay Cuban-American resident of Springfield, member of Grady's circle, and Marge Simpson's photographer and hairdresser. Julio is a flamboyant, warm-hearted member of Springfield's gay community who has gone through several relationships, including a marriage to a woman before coming out, a long partnership with Grady, and a brief marriage to Thad. He works two jobs, as a photographer and as a hairdresser at Hairy Shearers, and both professions tend to draw him into Marge Simpson's personal dramas. He's shown to be mischievous but caring, whether it's spiking Marge's wine to loosen her up for a pin-up calendar or secretly dyeing her hair for years to spare her feelings about going gray. Julio also has a secret drag persona, Penelope Cruising, and enjoys introducing friends to Springfield's vibrant nightlife and drag scene. Despite occasional chaos he causes, he consistently acts as a supportive friend, boosting Marge's confidence and guiding her through new experiences. His on-again, off-again romance with Grady is a recurring thread in his personal history. Voiced by Hank Azaria (seasons 1-30), Mario Jose ("Diary Queen"), Tony Rodríguez (season 32-present).

title: Wendell Borton
text: Wendell Borton is A fourth-grade classmate of Bart Simpson at Springfield Elementary School. Wendell Borton is one of the many background students at Springfield Elementary, best known for his perpetually pale, sickly appearance and his tendency to vomit at the slightest provocation, especially on the school bus. Despite being lumped in with the school's nerds alongside Martin Prince and Database, he has shown a mischievous streak, occasionally landing in detention or getting caught misbehaving in the halls. He counts Martin Prince as a friend, even helping him win a classroom election against Bart, and he's also been part of the Model U.N. Club, the Springfield Wildcats football team, and the school basketball team. His weak stomach has led to some memorable mishaps, from throwing up right after surviving a bus ride to getting sick following a bus crash. Lisa Simpson once singled him out as embodying 'The Feeb' archetype among the various personality types found at the school. Voiced by Pamela Hayden, Tress MacNeille, Grey DeLisle, Russi Taylor.

title: Jasper Beardley
text: Jasper Beardley is Elderly resident of the Springfield Retirement Castle and longtime friend (and occasional rival) of Abe Simpson. Jasper Beardley is a cranky, accident-prone old-timer who spends most of his time at the Springfield Retirement Castle, bickering with and occasionally comforting his friend Abe Simpson. A World War II veteran who once dodged the draft by dressing as a woman, he has held odd jobs over the years including substitute teacher and even minister before Reverend Lovejoy took over. He's famously unlucky, suffering through a wooden leg, gunshot wounds, frozen suspended animation as a Kwik-E-Mart sideshow, and failing eyesight, all while remaining stubbornly good-humored about his misfortunes. His romantic history includes a deceased wife, a brief and awkward fling with Edna Krabappel, and an unfinished adult film with fellow retiree Alice Glick. Despite his frailty, he's shown to be surprisingly sharp and combative when provoked, such as foiling Abe's attempt to steal his dentures. He's best remembered online for a single deadpan catchphrase that became an internet meme. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: That's a paddlin'. | Oh well. Easy come, easy go. | Hey little girl, is this seat taken?
quotes: That's a paddlin'.
Oh well. Easy come, easy go.
Hey little girl, is this seat taken?

title: Ugolín
text: Ugolín is One of two hostile French wine makers (with his uncle César) who enslave Bart during a foreign exchange trip. Ugolín is a cruel French vintner who, alongside his uncle César, exploits the foreign exchange program to bring Bart to their vineyard as unpaid, mistreated labor, essentially replacing their donkey Maurice. He shows a flicker of conscience when he worries that spiking their wine with antifreeze could actually kill someone, though this doesn't stop him from going through with the scheme. His plans unravel when Bart, having unconsciously absorbed fluent French, exposes their antifreeze wine scam to the police. Despite being arrested, Ugolín and César keep resurfacing over the years in various criminal or shady ventures, from robbing the nuclear plant to running a wine jail scheme back in Springfield. He's a recurring background villain whose partnership with César ties him to a running gag of French stereotypes and petty criminal misadventures. The characters are a nod to figures from Marcel Pagnol's novels. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Agnes Skinner
text: Agnes Skinner is Mother of Principal Seymour Skinner; elderly Springfield resident. Agnes is a domineering, sharp-tongued elderly woman whose entire life revolves around micromanaging her adult son Seymour, treating him more like a helpless child than a grown man running a school. She's prone to petty tyranny, like covering half the TV with cardboard or hiding car keys to punish him for talking to another woman, and openly despises his girlfriend Edna Krabappel. Her signature move is barking his name in exasperation whenever she needs him, a habit that's become one of the show's recurring bits. Beneath the harsh exterior lies a surprisingly colorful past, including a stint as a 1920s wing walker and a controversial pole-vaulting career that ended when a pregnant-belly kick from baby Seymour cost her an Olympic medal. Despite her age, she has an active and often scandalous love life, having married four times and carried on flings with numerous Springfield men. The show occasionally hints that her bitterness stems from a specific humiliating incident from Bart, contrasting with her original, gentler characterization when Seymour was introduced. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Seymour!
quotes: Seymour!

title: Troy McClure
text: Troy McClure is Recurring minor character; a washed-up B-movie actor and TV presenter who briefly married Selma Bouvier. Troy McClure is a fading Hollywood star reduced to hosting cheap infomercials, educational videos, and low-budget films. He's instantly recognizable by his slick, self-promoting introductions where he lists a pair of obscure past projects to establish his credibility, even though his career has clearly seen better days. Beneath his charming showbiz veneer lies a troubled personal life, including a rumored unusual fetish involving fish that nearly derailed his career entirely. In a rare moment of depth for the show's side characters, his sham marriage to Selma Bouvier reveals a more vulnerable, calculating side as he tries to salvage his fading fame. Despite being a minor character, he became beloved for embodying the washed-up celebrity archetype with both humor and an odd touch of pathos. His catchphrase became one of the show's most quoted running gags, and the character was retired permanently after voice actor Phil Hartman's death in 1998. Voiced by Phil Hartman (also Dan Castellaneta in "Bart's Dog Gets an "F""). Notable quotes: Hi! I'm Troy McClure! You might remember me from such [films, TV shows, dates] as...
quotes: Hi! I'm Troy McClure! You might remember me from such [films, TV shows, dates] as...

title: Lyle Lanley
text: Lyle Lanley is Con artist salesman who swindled Springfield and other towns into buying faulty monorails. Lyle Lanley is a smooth-talking swindler who travels from town to town selling shoddy monorail systems to gullible communities with surplus cash. He wins people over with a catchy, persuasive musical pitch, then quickly sets up a sham conductor training school before skipping town with the profits just as the rickety monorail is unveiled. His get-rich scheme is driven by a dream of retiring comfortably in Tahiti, funded entirely through repeated fraud. In Springfield, he convinces the town to blow its windfall on a monorail instead of fixing Main Street, and arbitrarily appoints Homer Simpson as conductor. When the monorail nearly causes disaster, only Homer's quick thinking prevents catastrophe, while Lanley makes his getaway. His comeuppance seems to catch up with him when angry victims from a previous scam recognize him on his escape flight, leaving his ultimate fate ambiguous. He serves as a satirical stand-in for slick, opportunistic salesmen who exploit civic pride and gullibility for personal gain. Voiced by Phil Hartman. Notable quotes: You know, a town with money's a little like the mule with a spinning wheel. No one knows how he got it, and danged if he knows how to use it! | I've sold monorails to Brockway, Ogdenville and North Haverbrook!
quotes: You know, a town with money's a little like the mule with a spinning wheel. No one knows how he got it, and danged if he knows how to use it!
I've sold monorails to Brockway, Ogdenville and North Haverbrook!

title: Ronald Reagan
text: Ronald Reagan is Real-world 40th U.S. President who appears as a recurring background/reference character in The Simpsons. This version of Ronald Reagan is depicted as a former actor turned president, married to Nancy Reagan, who pops up in various odd contexts throughout Springfield's history. He's shown as a bit out of touch and impatient, complaining about wasting time watching a barbershop quartet perform. His famous verbal habit of saying 'well' becomes the butt of a joke when Homer owns a bootleg tape of him repeating it. He's often invoked as a cultural touchstone, referenced in comparisons, encyclopedias, and even a wax museum exhibit where his severed head appears on a pike. Mr. Burns holds him in particularly high regard, keeping his photo displayed and wanting the Republican Party to name everything after him. In non-canon material, he's imagined as a vice president serving under a cloned Abraham Lincoln, adding to his legacy as a recurring pop-culture reference rather than a fully fleshed-out character. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "well"
quotes: "well"

title: Timothy Lovejoy, Jr.
text: Timothy Lovejoy, Jr. is The local reverend of the First Church of Springfield, married to Helen Lovejoy and father of Jessica. Reverend Lovejoy is Springfield's weary, jaded clergyman who long ago lost his enthusiasm for ministry, preferring his beloved model trains to actually helping his flock. He's especially burned out on Ned Flanders' constant, trivial moral dilemmas, and tends to dispense advice as quickly as possible so he can get back to his hobbies. Despite occasional flashes of tolerance—performing a Hindu wedding, co-hosting a radio show with a rabbi—he has grown increasingly rigid and intolerant over the years, clashing with Catholics, Buddhists, and anyone who challenges his authority. He's hypocritical and morally compromised himself, secretly struggling with alcoholism, exploiting his congregation for money, and even burning down his own church for insurance payouts. As a father he's largely absent and in denial about his troubled daughter Jessica, while his marriage to the gossipy Helen seems to be the most stable part of his life. Running gags include his love of toy trains, his button of pre-recorded noises to wake sleeping churchgoers, and his open contempt for Homer Simpson. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: I just stopped caring. Fortunately by that time it was the eighties, and no one noticed. | Have you ever really read this thing? Technically, we're not allowed to go to the bathroom. | Well, if that's the worst thing to happen to you today, consider yourself lucky.
quotes: I just stopped caring. Fortunately by that time it was the eighties, and no one noticed.
Have you ever really read this thing? Technically, we're not allowed to go to the bathroom.
Well, if that's the worst thing to happen to you today, consider yourself lucky.

title: Lenny Leonard
text: Lenny Leonard is Coworker of Homer Simpson at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant; one of his closest friends alongside Carl Carlson and Barney Gumble. Lenny is a good-natured, somewhat dim blue-collar guy despite holding a master's degree in nuclear physics, working alongside Homer and his inseparable best friend Carl Carlson at the power plant. He drifts through a string of odd side jobs and backstories—Stonecutter, novelist, NRA member, even a fill-in plant boss—without ever settling into a consistent identity, reflecting the show's loose approach to his character history. A running gag involves Homer constantly mixing him up with Carl despite their obvious differences, and another long-running joke plays on the ambiguous, borderline romantic devotion Lenny shows toward Carl. He's portrayed as easygoing to the point of apathy about his own safety and well-being, and his love life is a parade of failures and fabrications. Lenny is generally liked by the Simpson family and is a regular fixture among the barflies at Moe's Tavern. Despite his simple nature, he's shown occasional flashes of depth, like war-hero status and unexpected talents such as guitar playing. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "Quick and pointless, that's the death for me" | "I don't know where Carl ends and I begin!" | "Remember when we used to kiss like that, Carl...with our respective girlfriends?"
quotes: "Quick and pointless, that's the death for me"
"I don't know where Carl ends and I begin!"
"Remember when we used to kiss like that, Carl...with our respective girlfriends?"

title: Weasel Woman
text: Weasel Woman is Fictional superhero and member of the Superior Squad in the Radioactive Man comic-within-a-show universe. Weasel Woman is a comic-book superheroine who fights alongside Radioactive Man and the rest of the Superior Squad against various villains in Zenith City. She wields claws and super strength, drawing an obvious parody resemblance to Marvel's Wolverine. Through her adventures she battles foes like Hypno Head, Madame Eczema, The Scarlet Floozy, and Dr. Crab, often getting captured or incapacitated before rejoining the fight. She briefly attempts to take leadership of the Superior Squad after Radioactive Man's apparent death, showing a mix of ambition and loyalty to her team. Her claws prove ineffective against certain enemies, like Dr. Crab's robots, highlighting a recurring vulnerability despite her fierce reputation. In one continuity she is killed by a giant metal foot, only to be replaced by an alternate-reality version of herself, poking fun at comic book multiverse tropes. She also shares camaraderie with fellow heroine Lure Lass during a mission against the Crazy Cat Lady.

title: Gloria Prince
text: Gloria Prince is Martin Prince's mother, a recurring resident of Springfield. Gloria Prince is the mother of Martin and Montaigne, married to Gareth Prince. She's depicted as somewhat neglectful and morally questionable, at one point attempting to sell off her son's cherished Star Wars collectibles for next to nothing until other kids talked her out of it. Martin's own remarks suggest she has a habit of shoplifting items she doesn't even need, hinting at a casual dishonesty beneath her suburban-mom exterior. Her most infamous moment came when she served spoiled oysters at Martin's birthday party, sickening nearly every child in attendance and turning an already awkward gathering into a minor disaster. Despite these flaws, she remains a steady background presence throughout the series' long history. Her full name wasn't revealed until decades into the show's run, in a much later season episode. Voiced by Russi Taylor / Pamela Hayden / Grey DeLisle.

title: Girl with glasses
text: Girl with glasses is A minor background student in Bart Simpson's class at Springfield Elementary. This character is one of the many nameless kids populating Bart's classroom and the halls of Springfield Elementary. She's easily identified by her thin glasses, though her design isn't very consistent since her hair color shifts frequently between episodes, often blue but sometimes red or other shades. As a background filler character, she has no defined personality traits and has never been given a single line of dialogue in the show's history. Despite her silence, she's proven to be a remarkably persistent presence, appearing in the opening sequence as well as in hundreds of episodes across decades of the series. She also shows up occasionally in Simpsons comic books and other tie-in media, cementing her status as a recognizable, if anonymous, fixture of the show's world.

title: Mickey Mouse
text: Mickey Mouse is Disney's iconic cartoon mouse, appearing as a crossover character in various Simpsons episodes and specials. Mickey Mouse pops up in the Simpsons universe as a nod to his real-world Disney ownership, often appearing in photos, costumes, or brief cameos rather than as a fully developed character. He's shown as a mascot figure tied to Disneyland and Disney+ promotions, sometimes with a darker, sarcastic edge—such as mocking the Simpsons as "suckers" or a jaded suit-wearer bluntly stating the character is essentially dead when off-duty. In several non-canon segments he interacts playfully with Minnie Mouse and other Disney figures, reinforcing the crossover gag. Bart has even impersonated him to clear out a party, showing how the show uses Mickey as a flexible cultural reference point rather than a consistent personality. Overall, his appearances lean on recognizability and meta-humor about Disney's corporate ownership of Fox/Simpsons properties. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: "Suckers" — Loki disguised as Mickey Mouse, Bart's in Jail! | "When he was on his break, the mouse was dead." — Man in Mickey Mouse suit, A Tree Grows in Springfield
quotes: "Suckers" — Loki disguised as Mickey Mouse, Bart's in Jail!
"When he was on his break, the mouse was dead." — Man in Mickey Mouse suit, A Tree Grows in Springfield

title: Russ Cargill
text: Russ Cargill is EPA administrator and main antagonist of The Simpsons Movie. Russ Cargill is a self-important, power-hungry bureaucrat who heads the Environmental Protection Agency and takes drastic action against Springfield after it becomes the most polluted town on Earth. He is arrogant and manipulative, easily talking President Schwarzenegger into approving the destruction of the town, and shows a gleeful, almost theatrical villainy in his dealings with underlings. Despite his polished, successful exterior, he becomes increasingly unhinged and violent as his plans unravel, eventually chasing down the Simpson family with a shotgun. His downfall is fittingly undignified, being knocked out by a boulder pushed by baby Maggie. After his defeat, he loses his job and is arrested, marking the end of his reign of environmental terror over Springfield. Voiced by Albert Brooks. Notable quotes: Sir I'm afraid you've gone mad with power! | Of course I have. Have you ever tried going mad without power? It's boring; no one listens to you.
quotes: Sir I'm afraid you've gone mad with power!
Of course I have. Have you ever tried going mad without power? It's boring; no one listens to you.

title: Joe Quimby
text: Joe Quimby is The corrupt, long-serving Mayor of Springfield. Joe Quimby is Springfield's perpetually re-elected mayor, a smooth-talking politician whose main concerns are staying in power, chasing women, and lining his own pockets. He's openly corrupt, taking bribes from the mob and paying off the police chief, and his office seal literally translates to 'extremely corrupt.' Despite this, he occasionally makes half-hearted gestures toward genuine civic good, though these efforts are usually underfunded or ignored. He shows barely concealed contempt for the citizens he governs and frequently disappears on lavish vacations rather than doing his job. His tangled personal life includes a wife, a mistress, multiple affairs, and several illegitimate children, echoing the scandal-prone image of a Kennedy-style political dynasty. No matter the situation, he can't resist plugging his campaign slogan, often at wildly inappropriate moments. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Vote Quimby. | the system works: just ask Claus von Bülow
quotes: Vote Quimby.
the system works: just ask Claus von Bülow

title: Theodore Roosevelt (character)
text: Theodore Roosevelt (character) is Real-world 26th President of the United States, referenced and appearing in various Simpsons episodes and media as a historical/cultural touchstone. Teddy Roosevelt shows up in the Simpsons universe mostly as a piece of Americana rather than a fleshed-out character, popping up in hallucinations, product branding, and history lessons. He's gruesomely axed by Itchy in an old cartoon-within-the-show, appears as one of the 'political powers' Mr. Burns hallucinates, and lends his face to a salve bottle and a Mount Rushmore-themed sting operation. His legacy as a rugged, larger-than-life figure is used as inspiration for Bart Simpson, whose Roosevelt-themed study group eventually stages a small rebellion to save Superintendent Chalmers' job. Roosevelt is also linked to his real-life family tree within the show's canon, including his niece Eleanor and distant cousin Franklin. His archival voice recording is used for his one physical appearance, underscoring his role as a historical curiosity woven into Springfield lore rather than an active character. Voiced by Himself (voice archive).

title: Anger Watkins
text: Anger Watkins is A sports commentator for ESBN who frequently appears on Springfield's sports broadcasts. Anger Watkins is a fiery, opinionated sports commentator whose name matches his short temper. He hosts and appears on various sports shows, often clashing with hosts or callers who disagree with his takes, most notably berating Homer for wrong answers during a call-in segment. He's quick to anger over trivial sports debates, embodying an exaggerated parody of overly dramatic sports pundits. Despite his gruff exterior, he shows a softer side when he's demoted to timbersports commentary and unexpectedly grows to love the sport, bonding with his lumberjack son in the process. His storylines often highlight the absurdity of sports media culture, from petty rivalries with fellow commentators to overblown reactions to trivial disputes. He also narrated a documentary about Bart's rise and fall in basketball, showing he covers a range of local sports stories. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Cecil Terwilliger
text: Cecil Terwilliger is Younger brother of Sideshow Bob and recurring criminal antagonist in the Terwilliger family. Cecil is the perpetually overlooked younger sibling of Sideshow Bob, forever living in his brother's shadow and consumed by resentment over it. His lifelong dream of becoming Krusty's sidekick was crushed when Krusty chose Bob instead, fueling a deep jealousy that drives much of his villainy. Posing as a legitimate engineer, he schemes to defraud Springfield through a shoddy dam project while trying to frame Bob for the fallout, revealing a cunning and vindictive personality beneath his polished exterior. Despite his intelligence and ambition, his plans are consistently foiled by Bart and Lisa Simpson, often with unintentional help from Bob himself. His refined, fussy mannerisms and rivalry with his brother are clearly modeled on the Niles and Frasier Crane dynamic from the actors' other famous roles. Even in non-canon stories, he continues plotting petty, elaborate revenge schemes against the Simpson children, cementing his role as a scheming, bitter foil to his more famous brother. Voiced by David Hyde Pierce. Notable quotes: And now to kill you. There may be a slight ringing in your ears. Fortunately, you'll be nowhere near them. | I'd thank you not to refer to Princeton that way
quotes: And now to kill you. There may be a slight ringing in your ears. Fortunately, you'll be nowhere near them.
I'd thank you not to refer to Princeton that way

title: Johnny Tightlips
text: Johnny Tightlips is A caporegime in the Springfield Mafia who works for Fat Tony. Johnny Tightlips is a low-level mobster in Fat Tony's crew, usually seen alongside Legs and Louie. True to his nickname, he almost never speaks, sticking rigidly to the mafia code of silence even when it works against his own interests, such as refusing to say where he was shot during a mansion shootout. This extreme reticence is his defining trait and the source of most of his humor, since his silence is often unhelpful or absurd rather than useful. Despite his tough, tight-lipped mobster persona, he's hinted to have a softer, more altruistic side, reportedly spending vacations digging wells in Darfur. He's also said to suffer from a bad back, adding a touch of very human frailty to his hardened criminal image. His name and character are a nod to a real gangster killed in the St. Valentine's Day Massacre who likewise refused to name his killer. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: I ain't sayin' nothin'! | Tell 'em to suck a lemon.
quotes: I ain't sayin' nothin'!
Tell 'em to suck a lemon.

title: Mary Spuckler
text: Mary Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's children, a recurring love interest of Bart Simpson. Mary is the most articulate and educated of the Spuckler brood, having gained proper English skills through her time in the 4-H club rather than the dubious upbringing of her siblings. She's warm-hearted and animal-loving, which first draws her to Bart when she sees how devoted he is to his cow, Lou. Despite her hillbilly roots, she dreams of a life beyond Springfield as a singer-songwriter, even running away to New York City at one point to chase that ambition. Her on-and-off romance with Bart is a recurring thread, marked by a near-marriage, a heartfelt reunion, a breakup driven by Bart's video-game distractions, and eventually a brief rekindling after she becomes a widow. Musically inclined, she plays the saw in the Spuckler Family Band and channels her heartbreak into original songs. Ultimately she returns to accept the hillbilly lifestyle she once tried to escape. Voiced by Zooey Deschanel.

title: Jonathan Frink, Sr.
text: Jonathan Frink, Sr. is Father of Professor Frink, a deceased scientist who appeared as a resurrected 'Frinkenstein' in a Treehouse of Horror episode. Jonathan Frink, Sr. was a brilliant but cold scientist who never had a warm relationship with his son, Professor Frink, viewing him as an embarrassment because of his seasickness and reluctance to join dangerous research trips. He and his wife were chemists who conceived their son as a test-tube baby, showing more interest in science than in parenting. He died after being attacked by a shark while testing suntan lotion, but was later brought back to life by his son using mechanical organs, sparking a gruesome non-canon storyline. Reanimated, he became obsessed with stealing organs and brains from other characters to improve himself, going on a murderous rampage until his son and Lisa Simpson convinced him to stop. Despite his monstrous behavior, he ultimately showed genuine affection for his son, even sacrificing his stolen body parts to reconcile with him. He is notable as one of the more macabre and darkly comic 'Treehouse of Horror' guest characters, and his design and voice were tied to Jerry Lewis, who also inspired his son's character. Voiced by Jerry Lewis. Notable quotes: What a great crowd. You all have such big hearts and such... big brains. With large juicy dripping with knowledge heads... that's it, I'm going smorgasbord on these Poindexters.
quotes: What a great crowd. You all have such big hearts and such... big brains. With large juicy dripping with knowledge heads... that's it, I'm going smorgasbord on these Poindexters.

title: Gabbo
text: Gabbo is Ventriloquist dummy and rival children's TV personality who briefly eclipsed Krusty the Clown's popularity. Gabbo is a garish, brightly colored puppet who bursts onto Springfield's airwaves as a rival to Krusty the Clown, quickly stealing away his young audience. Operated by the stern, buttoned-up ventriloquist Arthur Crandall, Gabbo's manic energy contrasts sharply with his handler's rigid demeanor, making for an oddly effective double act. Despite his cheerful public persona, he privately shows contempt for the children who idolize him, a hypocrisy that gets exposed on live television thanks to Bart Simpson. Even after this scandal, his popularity proves nearly unshakeable, only fading naturally over time as fads do. In later appearances he's reduced to a washed-up casino act, visibly worn down, and is eventually depicted as nothing more than an inert dummy when not being performed—raising questions about whether Gabbo ever had a personality independent of Crandall at all. His look is a clear homage to classic puppet icons, and he remains a running symbol of fickle celebrity and fleeting fame in Springfield. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: I'm a bad widdle boy! | All the kids in Springfield are S.O.B.s.
quotes: I'm a bad widdle boy!
All the kids in Springfield are S.O.B.s.

title: Bloody Heart
text: Bloody Heart is A comic-book superhero and former member of the Superior Squadron, appearing in Radioactive Man comics within the Simpsons universe. Bloody Heart is a fictional superhero whose secret identity, Miles Mando, he guards closely, even from his own teammates. Over the years he has cycled through a string of aliases—Purple Heart, Purple Badge of Courage, Brave Heart, Heart of Darkness, and Bleeding Heart—reflecting shifting personas and eras of his heroics. He's shown as a loyal ally to Radioactive Man, fighting alongside him against villains like Hypno Head, Dr. Crab, and Madame Eczema, and even stepping up to lead the Superior Squad after Radioactive Man's apparent death. Despite his heroics, he's not immune to controversy, holding conspiracy-minded suspicions about the government's motives for banning superheroes and coming across as somewhat callous or clueless in social situations, such as when he's viewed as a jerk by Black Partridge. His financial fortunes swing wildly, from bankruptcy after losing defense contracts to rebuilding wealth through a chain of disco Kung Fu schools. In one continuity he is killed, bisected by Samaroo's sword, and is later replaced by an alternate-reality counterpart named Black Brave Heart.

title: Naima
text: Naima is Owner of the restaurant SoulHouse and a romantic interest of Carl Carlson. Naima is a business-savvy restaurateur who runs SoulHouse, a restaurant founded by her great-grandparents 75 years ago from a gumbo cart. She's practical and perceptive, quickly picking up on Carl Carlson's insecurities and identity crisis when he tries too hard to impress her with a makeover. Despite the romance not working out, she remains a supportive presence in Carl's life, later helping him through his genealogy-driven bull-riding stunt and giving him blood after he's injured. She has an interesting personal history, including a past relationship with Kool from Kool & the Gang. Naima is well-educated, holding a business degree from Howard University, and takes pride in her family's restaurant legacy, which her nephew even promotes through music. Voiced by Dawnn Lewis.

title: The Seven Duffs
text: The Seven Duffs is Costumed mascot characters representing Duff Beer at Duff Gardens theme park. The Seven Duffs are a group of theme-park mascots for Duff Beer, clearly modeled as a parody of Disney's Seven Dwarfs. Each has a distinct name and personality trait reflected in their name, such as Tipsy, Queasy, Sleazy, Edgy, Dizzy, and Remorseful, but only Surly is ever heard speaking. True to his name, Surly is grumpy and cynical, brushing off fans and even sarcastically promoting responsible drinking. The joke of the group is that, unlike the silent, short Dwarfs (where only Dopey doesn't talk), the Duffs are tall and only one of them talks. Over the years other similar costumed characters have appeared, including Duff Jr., Mrs. Surly, Snoozy, and Bossy, expanding the mascot family. The Duffs have made appearances across various episodes, video games, and even mobile game content as topiaries. Notable quotes: Hey, Surly only looks out for one guy ... Surly! | Take a picture, it'll last longer. Get outta here! | Drink Duff! ... Responsibly
quotes: Hey, Surly only looks out for one guy ... Surly!
Take a picture, it'll last longer. Get outta here!
Drink Duff! ... Responsibly

title: Mr. Bergstrom
text: Mr. Bergstrom is A substitute teacher who briefly taught Lisa Simpson's class and became a cherished role model to her. Mr. Bergstrom is a warm, artistic, and liberal substitute teacher who fills in for Ms. Hoover at Springfield Elementary. He quickly becomes an important male role model for Lisa, encouraging her intellectual curiosity and creativity, including urging his students to visit the Springfield Museum of Natural History. He's good-natured even when students mock him, taking a joke about him being a 'Singing Dork' in stride and laughing it off. Though his time as a teacher is short-lived, his impact on Lisa is lasting, as she continues to reference his words and lessons long after he's gone. He later makes a brief return to Springfield to reconnect with Lisa, though the reunion doesn't go as planned. Notably, both he and his voice actor share a Jewish background, which is subtly acknowledged in the show's humor. Voiced by Dustin Hoffman. Notable quotes: You are Lisa Simpson. | I already have one of those.
quotes: You are Lisa Simpson.
I already have one of those.

title: Barbara Belfry
text: Barbara Belfry is Manager of St. Giles Orphanage and wife of Sideshow Mel. Barbara Belfry runs St. Giles Orphanage and is married to Sideshow Mel, though the two maintain an open relationship that she prefers to keep hidden. A former javelin thrower whose athletic career ended due to her figure, she still shows off her throwing arm when provoked, notably hurling a flagpole like a javelin at a fleeing car. Despite her secret swinger lifestyle, she publicly presents herself as a devout Christian to maintain a respectable image. She becomes romantically entangled with Ned Flanders after he makes a large anonymous donation to her orphanage, leading to a brief affair that ends badly when Ned steals the donated money back. Quick to protect her reputation, she later spins the story to the public, casting herself as an innocent victim of seduction rather than an unfaithful wife. Voiced by Cristin Milioti. Notable quotes: In all my years of orphanagereal management, I've never seen a donation this generous.|Barb Belfry
quotes: In all my years of orphanagereal management, I've never seen a donation this generous.|Barb Belfry

title: Sara Sloane
text: Sara Sloane is A famous film star who briefly dated Ned Flanders. Sara Sloane is a glamorous Hollywood actress who stumbles into Ned Flanders' life while shopping for left-handed beauty supplies. Despite her celebrity status and tabloid-heavy love life, she's drawn to Ned's kindness and sensitivity, finding it refreshing compared to her jealous ex, Rainier Wolfcastle. She has a flirtatious, daring side, unafraid to show off in public or push boundaries, but ultimately she resists commitment, valuing her independence over marriage. Her whirlwind romance with Ned exposes him to the chaos of celebrity culture, including paparazzi invasions and public scrutiny. After their breakup, she briefly marries and divorces Bob Balaban in the span of a few hours, underscoring her flighty approach to relationships. She later reappears among Springfield's celebrities scheming against Homer. Voiced by Marisa Tomei. Notable quotes: Ned, I've never met a man like you. You're sensitive, you're in great shape, you have a mustache, and yet you're not gay.
quotes: Ned, I've never met a man like you. You're sensitive, you're in great shape, you have a mustache, and yet you're not gay.

title: George Washington
text: George Washington is Historical figure (first U.S. President) who appears in various forms—portraits, dreams, flashbacks, and non-canon segments—throughout the show. This version of George Washington leans into the historical reverence Americans hold for him while poking fun at how his legacy gets distorted in pop culture. He's shown as a somewhat combative figure, getting into a fistfight with Jebediah Springfield that only ends when his wife intervenes. He also pops up as a ghostly financial advisor of sorts, egging Homer on to spend Marge's savings alongside Benjamin Franklin and Andrew Jackson. In Mr. Burns' dream, Washington is eager to bond over shared wartime service, only to be brushed off and replaced by Richard Nixon as a dance partner. Beyond these appearances, he mostly exists as an image—on currency, in captchas, on calendars, and in a memorable non-canon appearance as a Treehouse of Horror zombie shot down by Homer. Overall, he's treated as a recognizable historical icon used for quick jokes and cameos rather than a deeply characterized figure. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "the guy who chopped up George Washington"
quotes: "the guy who chopped up George Washington"

title: Neil Armstrong (character)
text: Neil Armstrong (character) is Real-world astronaut, first man on the Moon, appearing as a character/celebrity in Springfield. This version of Neil Armstrong is a caricature of the real astronaut, famous for his lunar landing but treated with surprising indifference by Springfield's citizens. At a sci-fi convention, he's dismayed to find that fans don't care about his historic Moon walk, nearly driving him to fire his agent out of frustration. His legendary achievement is referenced repeatedly throughout the show, from Grampa's emotional reaction watching the landing live to Krusty's jealousy over his ex-wife's fascination with him. In one absurd side story, Barney claims to have won ownership of the Moon from Armstrong in a dice game, which Homer then buys for Maggie. He also shows up in non-canon material, including being killed for his celebrity likeness in a Treehouse of Horror segment. Overall, Armstrong serves as a pop-culture touchstone whose iconic status is often undercut for comedic effect by the citizens of Springfield. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Lurleen Lumpkin
text: Lurleen Lumpkin is An aspiring country-western singer briefly managed by Homer Simpson, who develops an unrequited romantic obsession with him. Lurleen is a talented, sultry country singer discovered by Homer in a rowdy bar, whose career he tries to launch despite Marge's jealousy. Though grateful for his help, she quickly falls for Homer, expressing her feelings through increasingly flirtatious and seductive song lyrics rather than direct confessions. Her storyline plays on classic country-music tropes of heartbreak and longing, turning her act into a running gag about thinly veiled romantic yearning. After Homer ends their professional relationship to save his marriage, her career enjoys a brief high point before spiraling into alcoholism, financial trouble, and a string of failed marriages—ironically, always to men who resemble Homer. She resurfaces periodically in Springfield's orbit, from bowling with other women linked to Homer to battling back taxes, never quite escaping her fixation on him. Despite her personal struggles, she remains a sympathetic, resilient figure who keeps trying to reclaim her career and dignity. Voiced by Beverly D'Angelo (Doris Grau in "Marge vs. the Monorail"). Notable quotes: I used to play the field, I used to be a roamer / But the season's turning 'round for me now, / I finally bagged me a Homer!
quotes: I used to play the field, I used to be a roamer / But the season's turning 'round for me now, / I finally bagged me a Homer!

title: Howard K. Duff VIII
text: Howard K. Duff VIII is Former CEO of Duff Beer and owner of Duff Stadium and the Springfield Isotopes. Howard K. Duff VIII is a wealthy, ruthless businessman who runs both Duff Beer and Springfield's beloved baseball team, the Isotopes. He's willing to deceive the public and exploit fans, as seen when he secretly plans to move the Isotopes to Albuquerque while hiding the truth from the city. His greed and dishonesty are exposed by Homer, leading to public outrage and his own security mascot, Duffman, turning against him. He later appears as a panelist on the show Vulture's Nest under the alias 'Malt Disney,' hinting at a mocking, self-important persona. Eventually he steps down as CEO of Duff Beer, replaced by Harriet K. Duff, showing his declining influence over time. Despite his corporate power, he's portrayed as petty and image-obsessed, even staging distractions like Kiss Cams to cover for the team's failures. Voiced by Stacy Keach. Notable quotes: making a mockery out of Amerisnack.com troll-doll night.
quotes: making a mockery out of Amerisnack.com troll-doll night.

title: Spock
text: Spock is A Star Trek character who appears in The Simpsons purely as a pop-culture reference, often via costumes, hallucinations, or Comic Book Guy's fandom rather than as an active character.. Spock exists in the Simpsons universe mainly as a beloved sci-fi icon rather than a fully developed character, showing up through references, costumes, and merchandise. Comic Book Guy is his biggest fan, owning multiple Leonard Nimoy books and even hallucinating that he himself is Spock, complete with romantic fantasies about Uhura. Other characters like Principal Skinner and various background extras dress up as Spock for costume parties and record attempts, reflecting his status as a nerd-culture touchstone in Springfield. He's been the subject of Simpsons-style mashups, such as being merged with Dr. Octopus into the fictional 'Dr. Spocktopus.' In one Halloween special, he even appears as one of the celebrities captured by the villain The Collector. Overall, Spock functions as a running gag representing geek fandom and Star Trek's enduring cultural footprint rather than a character with his own personality within the show.

title: Brendan Beiderbecke
text: Brendan Beiderbecke is A former student at Springfield Elementary and Lisa Simpson's brief love interest in "Haw-Haw Land". Brendan is a musically gifted boy who briefly attends Springfield Elementary after Lisa meets him at a STEM conference, drawn in by his piano skills, singing voice, and good looks. Despite his talent, he's insufferably arrogant, frequently criticizing Lisa's musical timing and belittling those around him, including his rival Nelson. His charm is a calculated tool—he smooths over his insults with flattery to keep Lisa interested, showcasing a manipulative streak beneath his polished exterior. He becomes entangled in a love triangle with Lisa and Nelson, using his singing (often bursting into original songs) as a weapon to win her affection and outshine his bullying rival. Ultimately his and Lisa's romance is undone not by personality flaws but by a technicality—his residence in West Springfield's school district disqualifies him from the talent show he wins, forcing the two to part ways. He represents a fleeting, bittersweet first crush for Lisa, embodying both her attraction to intelligence and talent and her frustration with condescension. Voiced by Ed Sheeran. Notable quotes: I've had my share of crazy flings, but they all end up leaving. And leaving, well it really stings.
quotes: I've had my share of crazy flings, but they all end up leaving. And leaving, well it really stings.

title: Sophie
text: Sophie is Daughter of Krusty the Clown, born from his wartime romance with a soldier named Erin. Sophie is the secret daughter Krusty the Clown never knew about until she introduced herself at an autograph signing. She's a talented musician who plays both violin and French horn, and she also enjoys soccer. Despite her father's fame, she craves genuine attention from him rather than being used as a prop for his television specials, which leads to real friction between them. She's Christian rather than Jewish, a fact that surprises Krusty and eventually inspires him to briefly explore Christianity himself just to connect with her. Sophie is forgiving and values effort and sincerity over grand gestures, reconciling with Krusty once she sees how hard he tries for her sake. In a non-canon future timeline, she grows up and marries Jimbo, with several Simpson-adjacent characters serving as her bridesmaids. Voiced by Drew Barrymore.

title: Stacy Lovell
text: Stacy Lovell is Creator of the Malibu Stacy doll; guest character who clashes with Lisa Simpson over feminist toy design. Stacy Lovell is the wealthy, cynical businesswoman behind the wildly popular Malibu Stacy doll line, living in a mansion modeled after her own creation's dream house. Despite once sharing Lisa's frustration with the doll's shallow, sexist phrases, she ultimately proves more interested in profit than principle, secretly working to undermine Lisa's rival doll, Lisa Lionheart. She has been married multiple times, to a string of oddly named or exaggerated husbands, which hints at a colorful and chaotic personal life. Lovell shows a dry, self-aware sense of humor about her own greed, muttering sarcastic asides about money even while pretending to support Lisa's idealistic project. She reappears sporadically in the show's universe, popping up on talk shows, at charity events, and in crowd scenes, suggesting she remains a recognizable public figure in Springfield. Her arc highlights the show's satire of consumerism and empty feminist marketing within toy culture. Voiced by Kathleen Turner. Notable quotes: Yes. Particularly if that little girl happens to pay $46,000 for that doll.
quotes: Yes. Particularly if that little girl happens to pay $46,000 for that doll.

title: Tab Spangler
text: Tab Spangler is Director of Serenity Ranch, a maximum-security fat camp attended by Bart (and later Homer). Tab Spangler is a former Marine who brings his military discipline into his job running a brutal weight-loss camp. He speaks in a commanding, order-barking tone and uses harsh tactics like clanging garbage cans to wake clients and cracking a whip to make them run. Despite his tough exterior, he's emotionally volatile, prone to sudden outbursts of yelling at people and even inanimate objects, though he calms down and apologizes just as quickly. He's sensitive about his age, reacting angrily when Marge guesses it. Several hints throughout his appearances suggest he may be gay or bisexual, including his choice of chariot name and a suggestive comment to Homer about sharing a motel room. His strained relationship with his own father adds a touch of unresolved personal history beneath his hardened persona. Voiced by Albert Brooks. Notable quotes: It hurts when people's guesses are over, or even when they are correct. | They could worry about that when they were "standing naked before the bed".
quotes: It hurts when people's guesses are over, or even when they are correct.
They could worry about that when they were "standing naked before the bed".

title: Lard Lad
text: Lard Lad is Advertising mascot statue for Lard Lad Donuts, a giant donut-holding figure seen around Springfield. Lard Lad is a towering promotional statue for the Lard Lad Donuts chain, typically shown standing atop or beside the shop holding an oversized donut. He doesn't speak and mostly exists as a piece of Springfield scenery, though he's taken on a life of his own in several non-canon stories. In one Halloween special, a freak lightning storm animates him and other advertisements, and he rampages through town seeking revenge on Homer for stealing his giant donut. In a video game adaptation, aliens Kang and Kodos bring him to life with their ship's laser, turning him into a colossal-donut-styled boss battle that Homer and Bart must stop. Fans have noted his design likely parodies the real-world Big Boy restaurant statue, and he's appeared inconsistently colored in at least one film appearance. Despite his lack of dialogue, he's become a recurring visual gag and merchandising icon across the show's history.

title: Santa Claus
text: Santa Claus is The legendary gift-giver of Christmas lore, who appears throughout the show in various forms—live, dreamed, or impersonated by other characters.. Santa Claus is the classic jolly, white-haired figure who delivers presents to good children at Christmas, and in the Simpsons universe he pops up constantly as both a real character and a recurring joke. He's often the subject of parody—reported dead by Kent Brockman, replaced in efficiency by Homer, or reduced to an action figure with steroids in a dream sequence. Various Simpsons family members impersonate him, most famously Homer working as a department-store Santa, which leads to Bart accidentally unmasking him. He also shows up in nightmares, commercials, and surreal fantasy sequences, sometimes teaming up with other holiday icons to fight monsters or getting knocked out and having his sleigh stolen in non-canon stories. Despite being mocked, exploited, and occasionally violent in these gags, the traditional image of Santa as a benevolent gift-giver remains intact, contrasted against the show's cynical humor. His wife, Mrs. Claus, is also referenced as part of his household. Overall, he serves as a flexible running gag and symbol of Christmas across countless episodes, comics, and games. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Dan Castellaneta, Chris Edgerly.

title: Maude Flanders
text: Maude Flanders is Ned Flanders' wife, mother of Rod and Todd Flanders, and neighbor of the Simpson family. Maude Flanders was a devoutly religious housewife whose life revolved around her faith, her family, and her efforts to keep Springfield morally upright. She often teamed up with Helen Lovejoy to crusade against perceived cultural evils like cartoon violence, frequently coming across as prim and judgmental despite her good intentions. Beneath her strict exterior, she had a softer, more sensual side that occasionally emerged around Ned and even drew unwanted lustful attention from Homer and Moe. She had quiet personal passions, including a love of drawing, ficus plants, and unflavored ice milk, that were largely hidden from those around her. Her sudden death in a freak T-shirt cannon accident, indirectly caused by Homer, became a defining tragedy for the Flanders family and inspired Ned's ill-fated Praiseland venture. Even after death, she remained a lingering presence in the show through flashbacks, hallucinations, and dream sequences. Voiced by Maggie Roswell. Notable quotes: In many ways, Maude Flanders was a supporting character in our lives. She didn't grab our attention with memorable catchphrases, or comical accents. But, whether you noticed her or not, Maude was always there ... and we thought she always would be.
quotes: In many ways, Maude Flanders was a supporting character in our lives. She didn't grab our attention with memorable catchphrases, or comical accents. But, whether you noticed her or not, Maude was always there ... and we thought she always would be.

title: Wainwright Montgomery Burns
text: Wainwright Montgomery Burns is Ancestor of Mr. Burns; his adoptive father/grandfather and a plantation-owning forebear of the Burns family. Colonel Wainwright Montgomery Burns was a cruel, racist plantation owner from the 1860s who later shaped the fate of the Burns family. He is believed to be the mysterious figure who took young Charles Montgomery Burns from his kind biological parents, adopting him and stripping away his cheerful nature to mold him into the cold, greedy man he later became. Wainwright's own personality mirrors that of his infamous descendant, marked by menace, power-hunger, and disdain for the working class. He owned a slave named Virgil, tying his legacy directly to Homer Simpson's ancestry. Though largely shown through flashbacks and family history rather than direct appearances, his influence looms large over the Burns family's dynasty of wealth and villainy. He appears mostly in historical or non-canon contexts like the Burns family tree and video game dialogue. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Becky Shorter
text: Becky Shorter is One of Lisa Simpson's friends and classmates at Springfield Elementary School. Becky Shorter is a minor recurring background student who runs in the same social circles as Lisa Simpson. She's shown participating in typical childhood activities like playing tag with Bart and Chuck Berger, and attending a sleepover where peer pressure leads her into an awkward first kiss with Bart. She occasionally wears braces, though not consistently across appearances. Becky seems easily delighted by small things, like getting excited over a simple yearbook signing from Bart. She also keeps up with modern trends, such as using a Facebook-style website and following online personalities.
