Overall, she represents one of the many background schoolkids who pop up repeatedly without ever taking center stage. Voiced by Pamela Hayden. Notable quotes: He writes the way people talk! — Becky Shorter
quotes: He writes the way people talk! — Becky Shorter

title: Moses
text: Moses is Biblical prophet and lawgiver who appears in various dream sequences, artwork, and references throughout the Simpsons universe. Moses is depicted in the Simpsons universe as the biblical figure who received the Ten Commandments from God, referenced across multiple episodes rather than being a consistent character. He appears in different forms including a child's drawing, a short film made by the Flanders family, and a dream sequence where Milhouse plays him opposite Lisa. In the afterlife, he's shown enjoying a comedic role parting a sea for Krusty and his father to relax on in Jewish Heaven. His character design in some appearances was modeled after Charlton Heston's famous film portrayal. The show often uses him for religious humor and parody, especially in dream and fantasy sequences, while also referencing his biblical story of leading the Israelites out of Egypt. He's a recurring but non-central figure used mostly for visual gags and religious references rather than deep characterization. Voiced by Phil Hartman (reality); Pamela Hayden (dream); Nancy Cartwright (played by Todd).

title: Sting (character)
text: Sting (character) is Real-life musician Sting appearing as himself, an old friend and former opening act of Krusty the Clown. Sting appears as a fictionalized version of himself, tied into Springfield through his history with Krusty the Clown, for whom he once opened before being fired in 1969. Despite lingering resentment, he's quick to help Krusty record a charity single for a boy he believes is trapped in a well, showing his generosity and dedication to his fans. His earnest, almost naive devotion to helping others is played for laughs when he exhausts himself digging to rescue Bart, insisting he must keep going for his fans even though Bart has likely never listened to his music. He resurfaces occasionally as a symbol of celebrity activism and aging rock stardom, writing protest letters to save the environment and being invoked as an example of a beloved, aging icon. The show also pokes fun at his environmental sensitivities and celebrity status, referencing his tears over rainforest destruction and his name appearing on lists of admired liberal celebrities. A recurring irony noted in the show's universe is that Sting worked as a ditch digger before fame, making his well-digging heroics fittingly appropriate. Voiced by Sting (Himself). Notable quotes: Sting worked to the point of near-exhaustion, saying that he couldn't stop as long as one of his fans needed him.
quotes: Sting worked to the point of near-exhaustion, saying that he couldn't stop as long as one of his fans needed him.

title: Helen Lovejoy
text: Helen Lovejoy is Wife of Reverend Timothy Lovejoy and mother of Jessica Lovejoy; a recurring Springfield townsperson and one of Marge's frenemies. Helen Lovejoy is the town's quintessential busybody, always ready to pry into her neighbors' business and spread whatever secrets she uncovers. Beneath her prim, pink-sweatered exterior lies a judgmental, small-minded moralist who wields gossip as a form of social currency and control. She's famous for erupting into hysterics during moments of civic panic, invoking her signature plea about protecting the town's children. Despite an openly conservative outlook and a habit of meddling in the Simpsons' marriage, she maintains a complicated, gossip-fueled frenemy dynamic with Marge that swings between camaraderie and rivalry. At home, she's surprisingly patient with her often troubled husband, even as their marriage faces its own quiet strains. Her backstory hints at a strict, punishing childhood that may explain her rigid, controlling adult personality. Voiced by Maggie Roswell (1990-1999; 2002-present), Marcia Mitzman Gaven (1999-2002). Notable quotes: Won't somebody please think of the children? | Do it, sweetie! Save our troubled marriage!
quotes: Won't somebody please think of the children?
Do it, sweetie! Save our troubled marriage!

title: Shauna Chalmers
text: Shauna Chalmers is Student at Springfield High School, daughter of Superintendent Chalmers, and one of Bart's on-again-off-again girlfriends. Shauna is a tough, streetwise teenager who runs with Jimbo, Dolph, and Kearney but frequently gets tangled up in romances and schemes involving Bart Simpson. She's manipulative and self-serving, often two-timing boyfriends, shoplifting, or blackmailing people like Marge for cash, yet she occasionally shows a softer or more vulnerable side, such as being hurt by Marge's private letter about her. Shauna cycles through an absurd number of part-time jobs, most of which end in her getting fired, quitting, or slacking off. She's also depicted as sexually casual and possibly bisexual, freely flirting with multiple boys and even Gil at one point. Despite her rough edges, she's shown moments of loyalty, like appreciating Bart taking the blame for her shoplifting. Her family ties to the strict Superintendent Chalmers add an ironic contrast to her rebellious lifestyle. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Either the duck suffers or the kid does, or none of you is getting nothing from Shauna. (Points on herself and looks at Bart.) I'm Shauna.
quotes: Either the duck suffers or the kid does, or none of you is getting nothing from Shauna. (Points on herself and looks at Bart.) I'm Shauna.

title: Roy Snyder
text: Roy Snyder is A recurring judge in Springfield who frequently presides over court cases involving the Simpsons and other townspeople. Judge Roy Snyder is Springfield's go-to courtroom authority, having mellowed from a strict disciplinarian into a more lenient figure over the years, especially compared to his stricter counterpart Judge Constance Harm. He holds a personal grudge against lawyer Lionel Hutz for repeatedly running over his son, and he's dealt with his own messy divorce, later being seen with Lindsey Naegle. Snyder tends to go easy on Bart Simpson, chalking up his mischief to boys just being boys. He's presided over some of Springfield's biggest legal moments, including banning (and later un-banning) sugar in the city and ruling in the landmark Itchy copyright case that cost Itchy & Scratchy Studios $800 billion. Despite his growing softness, he still delivers harsh fines when needed, such as slapping Mr. Burns with a multi-million dollar penalty for illegal nuclear dumping. His character design is based on real-life judge Robert Bork, and his skin tone has famously flip-flopped between yellow and black across the show's run. Voiced by Harry Shearer / Kevin Michael Richardson. Notable quotes: I'm a judge. But I'm also a father. A father whose ex-wife only lets him see the kids on summers and Christmas. I don't need you to rub it in.
quotes: I'm a judge. But I'm also a father. A father whose ex-wife only lets him see the kids on summers and Christmas. I don't need you to rub it in.

title: Rachel Cohen
text: Rachel Cohen is Lisa Simpson's imaginary childhood friend. Rachel Cohen was a figment of Lisa's imagination, created when Lisa was young and lacked real friends who could match her intellect. The two shared imaginary tea parties, and Lisa even attended Rachel's imaginary wedding to a unicorn. As Lisa grew older and made real friends with Marge's encouragement, she outgrew and forgot about Rachel. In a non-canon Halloween story, Rachel resurfaces as a jealous, murderous entity who kills off Lisa's new friends and allies to reclaim her place in Lisa's life. She proves dangerous and vengeful, attacking Milhouse, Marge, and even Homer's own imaginary friend, Sergeant Sausage, before Lisa ultimately defeats her by imagining her grown up and married off. Despite her sinister non-canon portrayal, in canon she remains simply a fond, quirky memory of Lisa's childhood loneliness. Voiced by Sarah Silverman.

title: Rainier Wolfcastle
text: Rainier Wolfcastle is Austrian-accented, musclebound Hollywood action star best known for the McBain film franchise; father of Greta and Dieter Wolfcastle. Rainier Wolfcastle is Springfield's larger-than-life answer to Arnold Schwarzenegger, a hulking action hero whose career runs the gamut from grim shoot-'em-up McBain sequels to bizarre passion projects like a Radioactive Man adaptation and a movie based on Marge's script. Despite his tough-guy image, he's constantly undermined by comic mishaps, weight gain he blames on 'research for a role,' and a filmography full of critically panned schlock. He dabbles in local politics as a staunch member of Springfield's Republican elite, even running for mayor, though he breaks from party lines on issues like stem cell research. His past includes childhood bratwurst commercials in Austria and, awkwardly, a stint in gay pornography tied to his early bodybuilding days. He's friendly with other Springfield celebrities like Duffman and Cookie Kwan, and his tough-guy persona occasionally slips into genuine violence, such as shooting James Lipton in character as McBain. Ultimately, Wolfcastle is a satirical send-up of macho celebrity culture, blending vanity, misplaced confidence, and unexpected charm. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: I used it to carry Rob Schneider in the movie My Baby is an Ugly Man.
quotes: I used it to carry Rob Schneider in the movie My Baby is an Ugly Man.

title: Ms. Albright
text: Ms. Albright is Sunday school teacher at the First Church of Springfield, close friend of Helen Lovejoy. Ms. Albright leads the children's Sunday school class in Springfield, dogmatically fielding kids' bizarre theological questions about who and what gets into Heaven. She's easily flustered by Bart's relentless, absurd hypotheticals about the afterlife, robots, and ventriloquist dummies, often losing patience with him. Her teaching style is rigid and literal, whether discussing the Ten Commandments or the horrors of Hell, which tends to invite more chaos from her students than clarity. She once banned Bart from her class for bad behavior before relenting when he wanted to impress Jessica Lovejoy. Outside the classroom, she's been linked romantically to the sleazy lawyer Lionel Hutz. Minor inconsistencies mark her design over the years, including changing hair color and the disappearance of her original eyeglasses after her debut. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: "Wouldn't you eventually get used to it, like in a hot tub?" | "Are there pirates in Hell?"
quotes: "Wouldn't you eventually get used to it, like in a hot tub?"
"Are there pirates in Hell?"

title: Chewbacca
text: Chewbacca is Star Wars character who appears as a crossover figure/cameo in various Simpsons episodes. Chewbacca is the famous Wookiee from Star Wars who pops up repeatedly in Springfield as a nod to the franchise's cultural presence. He first appeared as part of a police lineup of aliens when the FBI tried to help Homer identify the creature he'd seen, later joining the whole town in a lighthearted singalong while sporting a mocking t-shirt. Beyond that, his likeness turns up on merchandise like board games, cologne bottles, action figures, and a bust in Comic Book Guy's shop, underscoring the show's running gags about Star Wars fandom and merchandising excess. He's also been the subject of speculation about a romance with C-3PO, and has appeared in various hallucinations and non-canon specials, including as a doorman and party guest at Star Wars-themed events. Despite being a background/crossover character, he's iconic enough that Homer and Ned both fantasize about being him and Han Solo. Willie even claims he once got cut from a Star Wars version where he played Chewbacca himself. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Chris Edgerly.

title: God
text: God is The supreme, omnipotent creator and overseer of the universe, occasionally appearing to interact with the Simpsons family. God is depicted as the all-powerful, eternal being responsible for creation and the running of the universe, occasionally stepping in to influence events in Springfield. He is generally shown as reasonable and even good-humored, such as when he playfully shuts down Homer and Barney's boastful claim that nothing can stop them. Despite his immense power, he is portrayed with relatable emotional depth, expressing sorrow over the fate of his son who lived on Earth. He maintains a hands-off approach to most human affairs but will intervene when someone tries to invoke his authority carelessly. His appearances are often brief and his face is usually obscured, adding to his mysterious, iconic presence. He has been shown with unexpected traits, like having five fingers instead of four, distinguishing him from ordinary characters. In non-canon material, he takes on a more comedic role, even negotiating the sale of Heaven or acting as a video game final boss. Voiced by Phil Hartman, Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: He is a force bigger than mom and dad put together, and you owe Him big. | Oh no?
quotes: He is a force bigger than mom and dad put together, and you owe Him big.
Oh no?

title: Rod Flanders
text: Rod Flanders is Elder son of Ned and Maude Flanders, older brother of Todd Flanders, and classmate of Bart at Springfield Elementary School. Rod is one half of the devoutly religious Flanders brothers, raised under his father's strict, wholesome, sugar-free household rules. He prays constantly, loves religious-themed games and songs, and finds simple pleasures like quiet car rides genuinely enjoyable. He's squeamish about bugs, particularly moths and ladybugs, a fear likely inherited from Ned's own dramatic reactions to insects. Rod copes well with hardship, notably bouncing back cheerfully after his mother Maude's death, and has grown close to Marge as a comforting maternal figure since then. A long-running gag involves confusion among fans and even the show's own writers over whether Rod or Todd is actually the older brother, since conflicting evidence appears across different episodes. Despite the mix-up, Rod is generally depicted as the taller, bigger sibling, and he's shown occasional bursts of surprising competence, such as rescuing Bart from a gorilla using new climbing skills. Voiced by Pamela Hayden (Season 2–36); Chris Edgerly (Season 36); Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "It's less fun that way" | "I don't like this story!"
quotes: "It's less fun that way"
"I don't like this story!"

title: Terri Mackleberry
text: Terri Mackleberry is Fourth-grade classmate and occasional tormentor of Bart Simpson at Springfield Elementary, twin sister of Sherri. Terri is one half of an inseparable twin duo who are smart, odd, and prone to scheming, even communicating in a private language of their own. Though she and her sister are close enough to be terrified of separation and cling together when scared, they're also devious pranksters who delight in targeting Bart without ever getting caught. She appears to harbor a crush on Bart, though he seems more drawn to Sherri, leaving the feeling unreciprocated. Her relationship with Lisa swings between rare moments of kindness and frequent, oddly personal cruelty, suggesting their dislike of her isn't really about her intelligence or weirdness since the twins share those same traits. Despite often being grouped with Springfield Elementary's popular clique, Terri and Sherri are rarely treated as true equals to them, and Terri herself seems to feel overshadowed by her sister, once expressing a wish to step out from under Sherri's shadow. In non-canon material, she's been paired romantically with both Bart and Nelson Muntz, though these entanglements never last. Voiced by Russi Taylor (Season 1-30); Grey DeLisle (Season 31-present).

title: Donald Trump (character)
text: Donald Trump (character) is Real-world businessman and 45th President of the United States, referenced and appearing as a recurring background/parody figure in The Simpsons. Donald Trump appears in the show mostly as a real-world cultural touchstone rather than a fully developed character, cropping up in jokes, background cameos, and non-canon specials. He's referenced as a rich celebrity Homer daydreams about emulating, and multiple characters try (and fail) to do convincing impressions of him. In the show's flash-forward continuity, he's depicted as a past U.S. President whose administration left behind serious financial problems for his successor, Lisa Simpson. Several online-exclusive shorts lean into satire, showing him scheming, bribing, tweeting from bed, and eventually having a fleeting moment of self-reflection before reverting to old habits. He's also merchandised in-universe as toys and dolls, reinforcing his status as a pop-culture icon within the Simpsons world. Overall, his portrayal leans heavily on real-world political satire rather than original characterization. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta (also himself via archive footage).

title: Luann Van Houten
text: Luann Van Houten is Wife (on-and-off) of Kirk Van Houten and mother of Milhouse Van Houten. Luann is an Italian-American Springfield resident whose marriage to her cousin Kirk has been famously rocky, marked by divorce, reconciliation, and remarriage. After splitting from Kirk, she embraced a much more adventurous single life, dating a string of Springfield men including Pyro, Gyro, Disco Stu, Captain McCallister, Otto, and even having a fling with Dr. Hibbert during her marriage. Unlike Springfield's other exaggerated Italian-American characters, she's portrayed as relatively low-key and unassuming in demeanor. She and Kirk share an odd resemblance to their son Milhouse, leading to jokes about them looking like siblings. Their on-and-off relationship is a recurring source of chaos for Milhouse and Bart, who at one point schemed to keep them apart. Despite their turbulent history, Luann and Kirk eventually reconcile and remarry, even surviving a shipwrecked honeymoon together. Voiced by Maggie Roswell.

title: Jay G
text: Jay G is A wealthy rapper and business mogul who becomes entangled with Mr. Burns and Homer in a scheme of mutual betrayal. Jay G, born Jeremy Gilroy, is a flashy, ultra-rich rapper and entrepreneur who owns the Golden Goose brand and once performed with the group The Five Boyfriends. He idolizes Mr. Burns after reading his ruthless business philosophy in a book, and initially befriends Burns and Homer, only to bankrupt Burns through predatory spending and then repossess his belongings. His personality mirrors the very cruelty Burns preaches, showing he's willing to betray friends and business partners alike, as seen when he strong-armed his former bandmate Jazzy James out of song rights. Despite his cutthroat business tactics, he has a genuine soft spot for his golden goose mascot, Goosius, and reacts with horror and fury when Burns threatens or seemingly kills the bird. The feud between Jay G and Burns escalates into a chaotic showdown involving kidnapping, fake death, and a chandelier collapse, ultimately reinforcing Burns' own philosophy of ruthlessness living on through others. Outside of this main storyline, he also appears at other events, including a product launch and a bar trivia night at Moe's Tavern. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Stephen Hawking (character)
text: Stephen Hawking (character) is Real-world theoretical physicist who appears as a recurring guest character and occasional visitor to Springfield. Stephen Hawking is depicted much as he was in real life, confined to a motorized wheelchair, but his Springfield version comes equipped with absurd gadgets like a boxing glove, a toothbrush, and a helicopter propeller. He's portrayed as brilliant but also a bit vain and opportunistic, frequently threatening to 'steal' other people's ideas for his own use. Despite his genius, he enjoys simple pleasures like grabbing a beer with Homer and seems to genuinely appreciate Homer's oddball theories. He has a habit of popping up around Springfield for various reasons, from rescuing Lisa to attending parties to even buying a fast food franchise. His chair's punch feature becomes a recurring gag, often used on Principal Skinner or Homer when they annoy him. Over the years he's referenced or seen in cameos across many episodes, comics, and other Simpsons media, cementing his status as a beloved recurring celebrity guest character even after his real-world death. Voiced by Himself. Notable quotes: Your theory of a donut-shaped universe is intriguing, Homer. I may have to steal it. | Do I look like Steven Hawking to you?
quotes: Your theory of a donut-shaped universe is intriguing, Homer. I may have to steal it.
Do I look like Steven Hawking to you?

title: Kirk Van Houten
text: Kirk Van Houten is Milhouse's unemployed, divorced (and later remarried) father, and Luann's husband/cousin. Kirk is a hapless, perpetually unlucky middle-aged man best known for his string of dead-end jobs and his emotionally devastating divorce from Luann. Once a promising lacrosse star in college, his life took a downward turn after a freak injury cost him his shot at going pro, and things only got worse when he lost his position at his father-in-law's cracker factory. After Luann left him, Kirk became the show's go-to portrait of a sad-sack deadbeat dad, breaking down in tears at the drop of a hat and drifting through a series of humiliating gigs, from sign-holding to being a human scarecrow. Despite his misfortune, he's had a surprising number of romantic entanglements with various Springfield women. He was also wrongly arrested for kidnapping Bart, a mishap that ended in his release once the truth came out. Eventually he and Luann reconciled and remarried, only for the two to be presumed lost at sea before turning up safe on a deserted island. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Tress MacNeille.

title: Buck McCoy
text: Buck McCoy is Retired Western film star who becomes Bart Simpson's idol and later a family acquaintance in Springfield. Buck McCoy is a once-beloved cowboy movie star whose career faded when Westerns fell out of fashion in the 1970s, leaving him a reclusive alcoholic in his Springfield mansion. He is fiercely proud of his past fame, often boasting about being the world's most famous movie cowboy, yet his drinking undermines his attempts at a comeback. His friendship with Bart, who idolizes him, sparks a brief Western craze at school and a strained rivalry with a jealous Homer. A disastrous, drunken appearance on Krusty's show nearly ruins his reputation for good, but he redeems himself by heroically stopping a bank robbery using his old lasso skills. Despite his flaws, Buck remains stubborn about his right to drink, refusing rehab and quick to push people away once his pride is wounded. He later reappears among Springfield's citizens, notably joining the mob against Homer during the Lake Springfield pollution crisis. Voiced by Dennis Weaver. Notable quotes: Buck McCoy? He was the greatest of them all. He was bigger than opium! - Abraham Simpson
quotes: Buck McCoy? He was the greatest of them all. He was bigger than opium! - Abraham Simpson

title: Gnome in Your Home
text: Gnome in Your Home is A Christmas doll toy owned by Maggie Simpson, similar to Santa's watcher, that reports on children's behavior. Gnome in Your Home is a creepy Christmas-themed doll parodying 'The Elf on the Shelf', designed to spy on children and report their behavior to Santa Claus. Homer and Marge give one to Maggie to watch over her, but instead of comfort it becomes a source of terror, especially after Homer explains it never sleeps and might nibble her fingers if she misbehaves. The toy fuels a nightmarish dream sequence where it grows monstrous, chases Maggie through the North Pole, and even devours her before she wakes up on Christmas morning. Despite the horror, Maggie gets a strange form of revenge, eventually destroying the doll and its wife in her crib, and later mowing down a whole group of them with a lawnmower. The character recurs as a symbol of dread tied to the holidays, appearing again in later episodes as discarded junk or as part of a spooky amusement ride. Its unsettling nature and dark humor make it a memorable one-off holiday antagonist within the show's Christmas specials. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: The Gnome then asks Maggie if she's been a bad baby and when she shakes her head, the Gnome tells her not to lie or Christmas morning will never come.

title: Rigellians
text: Rigellians is A recurring alien species from the planet Rigel 7, best known through their members Kang and Kodos, who frequently appear as antagonists in the Treehouse of Horror specials. The Rigellians are a one-eyed, tentacled, drooling alien race hailing from the harsh, rocky world of Rigel 7, though in the distant future their home becomes a lush, peaceful jungle. Despite their menacing appearance, their language is oddly identical to English, save for quirky differences like using "beautiful" as a synonym for screaming. They practice a self-declared religion called Quantum Presbyterianism and claim to have witnessed the universe's creation. Their culture is defined by advanced technology such as ray guns and interstellar travel, yet they consider outdated human novelties like Pong to be cutting-edge entertainment. The species is primarily remembered through its two most famous representatives, Kang and Kodos, who serve as the show's go-to extraterrestrial invaders in the non-canon Halloween episodes. Their design and naming draw inspiration from classic EC Comics artwork and Star Trek lore, giving them a tongue-in-cheek sci-fi pedigree.

title: Space Mutants (characters)
text: Space Mutants (characters) is Fictional alien monsters from the in-universe 'Space Mutants' movie series referenced throughout the show. The Space Mutants are shape-shifting extraterrestrial creatures that exist within the Simpsons universe as villains of a long-running horror/sci-fi film franchise. Green-skinned with three eyes, four tentacle arms, and only two teeth, they disguise themselves as humans in order to prey on people, often striking couples right after intimate moments. Lacking feet, they move by slithering like slugs, and their monstrous design suggests they swallow victims whole rather than chew them. Their pop-culture presence in the show is mostly through merchandise and background references, such as the toy on Bart's nightstand, rather than direct appearances as characters. Notably, the Mutants served as an inspiration for the design of the recurring aliens Kang and Kodos. Their over-the-top gore and post-coital attack scenes are implied to be why their in-universe films carry an R rating.

title: James Woods (character)
text: James Woods (character) is Celebrity guest character who temporarily replaces Apu as Kwik-E-Mart clerk. James Woods appears as an exaggerated version of himself, taking a job at the Kwik-E-Mart purely to research a role for an upcoming movie about a convenience store clerk. True to his reputation as an intense method actor, he treats the mundane tasks of the job—like giving change or cleaning a microwave—as dramatic scenes to be perfected, often frustrating and confusing the people around him, especially Jimbo. His dedication crumbles comically when his film role is abruptly changed, prompting him to consider quitting on the spot before being reminded of workplace notice policies. When a robber threatens him, Apu selflessly takes the bullet meant for Woods, and out of gratitude, Woods arranges for Apu to get his old job back. He then exits just as dramatically as he arrived, hinting at another over-the-top acting gig involving aliens. Beyond his main appearance, his image shows up as background decor in a couple of other Springfield locations, and he even gets a non-canon crossover moment with his Family Guy counterpart. Voiced by James Woods (Himself). Notable quotes: What do you mean, I gotta give two weeks' notice? Why you frickin', no good, mother [beep] [beep] cheese! ...No, not you, I'm just talking to my oven. | I kind of like to research my roles and really get into it. | you're like the guy, you're a legend around here

title: Arthur Fonzarelli
text: Arthur Fonzarelli is Crossover character from Happy Days who occasionally appears/is referenced in The Simpsons; a former Springfield Elementary student. Fonzie is the iconic leather-jacketed cool guy from Happy Days who pops up in Springfield lore as a running pop-culture reference rather than a regular cast member. He's treated as a real historical figure in the Simpsons universe, complete with his famous jacket being displayed in the Smithsonian alongside The Bill of Rights. Homer is his biggest fan, frequently invoking Fonzie's name, mimicking his signature move of hitting a jukebox to fix it, and getting nostalgic about Happy Days episodes and characters. It's revealed he actually attended Springfield Elementary School, tying him more directly into the show's own history. He also shows up in odd background details like locket photos, old TV Guide covers, and even receives a stray vote in a school election. Overall, he functions as a nostalgic nod to classic TV culture that the show's characters reference and admire. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "This is not Happy Days and he is not The Fonz" | Fonzie freed the squares. | I don't always keep my cool like the Fonz but my love for my kids has given me plenty of happy days.

title: Madam Wu
text: Madam Wu is Chinese adoption center worker who oversees Selma's (and Homer's) adoption of baby Ling in China. Madam Wu is a stern, rule-following bureaucrat in charge of vetting prospective adoptive parents at a Chinese adoption center. She rigidly monitors Homer and Selma, who pose as a married couple, closely observing their behavior to confirm they're fit to raise a child. Despite her strict exterior, she shows a surprisingly flexible and even manipulative streak, goading Homer into a dangerous acrobatic stunt and later spying on the family in the hospital. When she discovers Homer and Selma aren't actually married, she initially punishes Selma by taking Ling away, but ultimately relents after hearing their heartfelt plea, showing unexpected compassion rooted in her own upbringing by a single mother. Her personality blends bureaucratic rigidity with situational leniency, making her both an obstacle and, eventually, an ally to the Simpson family's adoption plans. She's also given a darkly comic backstory involving her ping-pong champion father's freak death. Voiced by Lucy Liu. Notable quotes: Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on Wu!
quotes: Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on Wu!

title: The Grumple
text: The Grumple is A green, hairy monster who first appears as a Grinch-like villain menacing Springfield during the holidays, recurring as a background/parody character in later episodes. The Grumple is a strange, growling green creature who debuts as the villain of Krusty's Kristmas on Ice, threatening to steal everyone's holiday cheer. He fights Homer both at the ice show and later at Moe's Tavern, and a green ooze leaking from his eye reveals he's not just a guy in a costume but an actual monster. Despite his menacing catchphrases and violent tendencies, he eventually softens, bringing his own family to celebrate Christmas peacefully with the Simpsons and Gil. Beyond his main holiday storyline, he becomes a recurring background gag, popping up everywhere from ice-skating rinks and Lady Gaga concerts to bowling alleys and hallucinations. He's essentially Springfield's resident parody of the Grinch, blending genuine menace with absurd comic appearances across many later episodes. His running joke is his rhyming, sing-song threats that echo classic holiday-villain dialogue while feeling completely out of place in mundane settings. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Grumply Grumply Groo! Your blood will make my stew! | Grumpily Grumpily Groo! We would like to spend Christmas with you! | Grumple, Grumple Groo, Sometimes I feel sad too!

title: Lucille Botzcowski
text: Lucille Botzcowski is A criminal who posed as a babysitter for the Simpson children, also known as 'The Babysitter Bandit'. Lucille Botzcowski is a cunning fugitive who infiltrated the Simpson household under the guise of a babysitter while using an alias to hide her criminal past. She's resourceful and manipulative, disabling the house phones and attempting to loot the family's belongings before being outwitted by the kids. Despite getting captured and hog-tied by Bart, Lisa, and Maggie, she manages to con Homer into releasing her, proving her skill at deception even in a vulnerable position. She operates under multiple aliases, showing she's been dodging the law for some time under different identities. In later appearances, she's shown to have possibly gone mad, suggesting the psychological toll of her encounter with the Simpson children's revenge via a children's video tape. Her recurring presence in police-related backgrounds and mentions hints that she remains a minor but memorable figure in Springfield's criminal underworld. Voiced by Penny Marshall. Notable quotes: "never take your eyes off the boy"
quotes: "never take your eyes off the boy"

title: Dean Martin
text: Dean Martin is Real-world singer/actor referenced and appearing as a character in Heaven, connected to Krusty and various Simpsons pop-culture gags. This version of Dean Martin represents the legendary crooner and actor as he exists within the Simpsons universe, appearing mainly as a heavenly figure and a recurring pop-culture reference. He's portrayed as a laid-back entertainer, a friend of Krusty's from their Las Vegas days, and someone Krusty admired as the ultimate straight man in comedy. The show plays on his real reputation for being relaxed about work, which comes up when Homer criticizes him in Heaven for not making full use of his talent. His music and image pop up repeatedly throughout the series, from songs covered by Marge and Homer to his picture appearing in the background of scenes. He's also tied into an in-universe controversy where Krusty and Martin apparently borrowed a melody from one of Martin's own songs. Overall, he functions as a nostalgic nod to classic show business rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Clarence Bouvier
text: Clarence Bouvier is Marge Simpson's father, husband of Jacqueline Bouvier, and maternal grandfather of Bart, Lisa, and Maggie Simpson. Clarence Bouvier was a chain-smoking patriarch of the Bouvier family, sharing the same habit that plagued his daughters Patty and Selma. He served in the Navy, which left him with a swearing habit that his wife tried to curb with a swear jar, and later worked as a baby photographer and one of the first male flight attendants, a job he was embarrassed by and hid from his family. Though initially warm toward Homer when he mistook him for Marge's prom date Artie Ziff, he was privately relieved his daughter went with someone else, revealing a dismissive attitude toward Homer that lingered even after his death, as he left Marge a monthly stipend in his will in case she ever needed to escape her marriage. In his later years he kept up a sentimental tradition of singing the city anthem at Springfield Town Hall. He eventually died of lung cancer after losing a leg, though non-canon material offers a wildly different, comedic cause of death involving a rollercoaster. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: When that Simpson boy showed up, it took years off my life!
quotes: When that Simpson boy showed up, it took years off my life!

title: Don Brodka
text: Don Brodka is Store detective/security guard at Try-N-Save who catches Bart shoplifting. Don Brodka is the gruff, no-nonsense security guard at the Try-N-Save store who catches Bart trying to steal a copy of Bonestorm. A heavy smoker and Marine Corps veteran with a USMC tattoo, he runs his office like an interrogation room, complete with an educational shoplifting video he can't stand himself. He shows little patience for excuses, sticking rigidly to his own rules, and even calls Bart's parents to report the theft. Despite his intimidating demeanor, he has a quirky habit of snacking on cheese and crackers and enjoys cracking jokes, though he hates it when others laugh at his expense. His confrontation with Bart leaves a lasting impression, causing Bart to become paranoid and imagine Brodka lurking around every corner. He later appears in background crowd scenes, including among Springfield residents mocking Nelson and in the angry mob during The Simpsons Movie. Voiced by Lawrence Tierney. Notable quotes: If I wanted smoke blown up my ass, I'd be at home with a pack of cigarettes and a short length of hose.
quotes: If I wanted smoke blown up my ass, I'd be at home with a pack of cigarettes and a short length of hose.

title: Lord Montymort
text: Lord Montymort is Non-canon villain and Voldemort parody from the 'Treehouse of Horror XII' segment 'Wiz Kids'. Lord Montymort is a dark wizard obsessed with stealing magical essence from other wizards to bolster his own power, earning him grim nicknames like the 'absorber of souls.' His scheme to capture Lisa Simpson, the most talented student at Springwart's School of Magicry, drives the plot, and he manipulates Bart's sibling rivalry to get close to her. Cold and calculating, he shows little regard for the lives of those he drains, even when the process yields nothing useful, as with the hapless Ralph Wiggum. His immense power is tied to a single vulnerable point, his enchanted shin, which ultimately becomes his downfall. He keeps a devoted snake servant, Slithers, who remains loyal even in death, tearfully eating his master's body. Montymort's design and backstory serve as a direct spoof of Harry Potter's Lord Voldemort. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: How would you like to humiliate your sister?|Lord Montymort to Bart | I'm not getting squat from this yo-yo.

title: Jay Sherman
text: Jay Sherman is Guest film critic who judged the Springfield Film Festival, crossover character from The Critic. Jay Sherman is a New York-based film critic who hosts his own show, Coming Attractions, and is brought to Springfield to judge a local film festival. He shares many of Homer's tastes and slobbish habits, which makes Homer jealous when the rest of the family takes an instant liking to him. Despite this overlap with Homer, Jay is more thoughtful and cultured, able to appreciate genuine artistic merit in films rather than just cheap laughs. He's also socially sharp, capable of delivering subtle insults that go over people's heads, as seen with Rainier Wolfcastle. Jay proves easygoing and adaptable, fitting in with the Simpson family and even enduring an uncomfortable run-in with Patty and Selma. His stint in Springfield ties into a wider crossover meant to promote his own short-lived spinoff series. Voiced by Jon Lovitz. Notable quotes: No, Homer, I won't make fun of you. But I will suggest that there may be better things in life than seeing a man get hit in the groin with a football.|Jay Sherman|A Star Is Burns

title: Erica
text: Erica is Sixth-grade student at Springfield Elementary and member of the girl gang Bossy Riot. Erica is a strong-willed sixth grader who leads a small group of self-styled feminist pranksters called Bossy Riot. She prefers to call their mischief 'awareness bombs' rather than pranks, showing she sees their vandalism as activism rather than mere troublemaking. Erica is resourceful and a bit ruthless, testing newcomers like Bart with tasks before letting them join, and she isn't afraid to tie him up when he opposes the group's plans. Despite her rebellious antics, she has a softer, responsible side, admitting to Chief Wiggum that she babysits, which leads to her being tasked with watching Ralph. She's also socially savvy, recognizing Lisa's potential and recruiting her into Bossy Riot after witnessing her boldness during their scheme against the Itchy & Scratchy reboot's cancellation. Erica represents the show's exploration of youthful activism and gender dynamics among Springfield's kids. Voiced by Nicole Byer.

title: Bleeding Gums Murphy
text: Bleeding Gums Murphy is Jazz musician and mentor/idol to Lisa Simpson. Bleeding Gums Murphy is a soulful street-corner saxophonist who becomes Lisa Simpson's musical hero and closest artistic confidant. Despite recording one hit album, Sax on the Beach, he squanders his fortune on a bizarre Fabergé egg obsession and dies poor and largely unrecognized outside Lisa's family. His backstory is full of tragicomic misfortune, from learning music on what turned out to be an umbrella disguised as a saxophone, to failing to raise enough money for his deaf son's cochlear implants. He's warm, world-weary, and given to reminiscing about a colorful showbiz past that included brushes with real celebrities. After his quiet, under-attended death, his legacy is repeatedly exploited commercially through holograms and repurposed songs, which becomes a recurring sore point for Lisa. Even so, he remains a beloved fixture of the show's opening sequence and a symbol of overlooked artistic genius. Voiced by Ron Taylor (also Daryl L. Coley, Kevin Michael Richardson). Notable quotes: Well let me put it this way... you ever been to the dentist? Not me. I suppose I should go to one, but I got enough pain in my life as it is.
quotes: Well let me put it this way... you ever been to the dentist? Not me. I suppose I should go to one, but I got enough pain in my life as it is.

title: Luke Stetson
text: Luke Stetson is A teenage boy at the Lazy I Ranch who becomes Lisa Simpson's love interest during the Simpsons' ranch vacation. Luke is a nature-loving ranch boy whose passion for animals and the environment immediately connects him with Lisa when they meet. He shows Lisa around the ranch, shares her values about protecting wildlife, and even plays music with her at night, sparking a brief romance. Despite being only 13, he comes across as more mature and grounded than Lisa in some ways, comfortable in his rural surroundings. He deeply values trust and honesty, and reacts with real hurt and anger when he discovers Lisa lied about sending his sister Clara into the forest. This betrayal ends their budding relationship, with Luke lumping Lisa in with the arrogant city folk his family moved away from. His story is a bittersweet one-episode romance that ends in heartbreak rather than lasting friendship. Voiced by Jonathan Taylor Thomas.

title: Ruth Powers
text: Ruth Powers is The Simpsons' next-door neighbor and one of Marge's close friends. Ruth Powers is a divorced single mother who moves in beside the Simpsons with her daughter Laura. She's tough, independent, and not afraid of a little mischief, having once stolen her ex-husband's car in revenge for unpaid child support. Her friendship with Marge leads to some wild misadventures, including a night of line dancing, target shooting, and an accidental run from the law. Ruth later reappears as a bodybuilder who introduces Marge to steroids, showing her willingness to bend the rules for fun or friendship. She's a recurring presence in Springfield's social scene, known for hanging out at Moe's Tavern and attending Alcoholics Anonymous meetings. Over the years she's been linked romantically to several Springfield men, reflecting her free-spirited, no-nonsense personality. Voiced by Pamela Reed (3 episodes); Pamela Hayden (all other appearances). Notable quotes: "stopped by to say hello in 25 years, and I live next door"
quotes: "stopped by to say hello in 25 years, and I live next door"

title: Orson Welles
text: Orson Welles is Real-world film director and actor who appears as a character in various Simpsons episodes, including a heavenly encounter with Mr. Burns and a Treehouse of Horror segment. Orson Welles appears in the Simpsons universe as himself, the famed director, writer, actor and producer. He's portrayed as a larger-than-life, slightly whimsical figure who pops up in dreams, documentaries, and even amusement park rides. In one vision he appears in Heaven, delivering a quirky, philosophical explanation involving God, a rainbow, and budget woes to Mr. Burns. In another canonical appearance, he takes a leisurely trip on a Ferris wheel, complaining that everything looks like blurry dots after drinking wine beforehand. A non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment reimagines his famous 1938 'War of the Worlds' broadcast, with Springfield rioting in panic before growing cynical and refusing to believe a real alien invasion by Kang and Kodos. Despite his gravitas as a historical figure, the show often uses him for comedic effect, blending his real legacy with absurd, exaggerated scenarios. Voiced by Maurice LaMarche. Notable quotes: That young man had a lot of potential.
quotes: That young man had a lot of potential.

title: Jimi Hendrix
text: Jimi Hendrix is Real-world musician who appears in the Simpsons universe, notably in Homer's dream/flashback sequences. Jimi Hendrix appears in the show as a legendary guitarist tied to several surreal or nostalgic moments involving the Simpson family. He's depicted playing air hockey against Benjamin Franklin in a dream Homer has about Heaven, and later as the electrifying performer at Woodstock who inspires a young Homer to dance wildly in the mud while his father Abe disapproves. His image and legacy pop up repeatedly as a cultural touchstone, from a pudding painting made by a prison inmate to being featured on a list of famous left-handed people. Even in non-canon material, he's portrayed as easygoing, willing to give guitar lessons to Jesus in Heaven, and unbothered by his student's lack of practice as long as he still gets paid. Throughout his appearances, Hendrix serves less as a character with his own arc and more as a symbolic figure representing counterculture, music, and Homer's brief flirtation with the hippie lifestyle. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Frog Prince
text: Frog Prince is Non-canon magical creature created by Bart's failed spell in a Treehouse of Horror segment. The Frog Prince is a botched magical creation, born when Bart's toad-to-prince incantation went horribly wrong during a lesson at Springwart's School of Magicry. Unlike Lisa's successful, dashing Handsome Prince, this creature is a grotesque toad-man hybrid that spends nearly all its screen time vomiting uncontrollably. Its defining trait is a miserable, suicidal outlook, repeatedly begging to be killed because its existence is so agonizing. It later turns up as a minor celebrity figure at Fox Studios, awkwardly rubbing shoulders with the Leprechaun and Pierce Brosnan while still retching everywhere. The character functions mostly as a running gag about Bart's ineptitude at magic compared to Lisa, and as a piece of absurd background comedy in Treehouse of Horror episodes. Mr. Burns later cites it as an example of a particularly unpleasant interdimensional visitor. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "Well, Bart, did you study your spell book last night, or did your fairy godmother die again?" - Mrs. Krabappel | "Every moment I live is agony." - Frog Prince | "They used to give us champagne 'till somebody ruined it!" - Leprechaun

title: Arnold Schwarzenegger
text: Arnold Schwarzenegger is President of the United States in The Simpsons Movie, based on the real-life actor and politician. This character is a fictionalized version of the real Arnold Schwarzenegger, appearing as the sitting U.S. President during the events of The Simpsons Movie. He is depicted as somewhat indecisive, relying on advisors to make major policy choices rather than reviewing the details himself. This trait is exploited by the power-hungry Russ Cargill, who manipulates him into approving a disastrous plan for Springfield by appealing to his ego about leadership. Despite briefly showing hesitation and a desire to actually read his options, he ultimately caves to Cargill's flattery. Outside the film, he is referenced in passing as an example of a successful action star alongside Stallone and Van Damme, and is mentioned as having a romantic history with Chloe Talbot. The show's long-running character Rainier Wolfcastle is explicitly built as a parody of him, and in a twist, the animators ended up basing his movie design partly on Wolfcastle rather than drawing him from scratch. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "Anyone can make a decision if they know what they're picking. It takes real leadership to pick something you know nothing about."
quotes: "Anyone can make a decision if they know what they're picking. It takes real leadership to pick something you know nothing about."

title: El Barto
text: El Barto is Bart Simpson's secret graffiti-tagging alter-ego, notorious as an unidentified vandal in Springfield. El Barto is the mysterious tag Bart Simpson uses to sign the graffiti he scrawls across Springfield, turning him into a minor urban legend that the town's authorities can never quite pin down. Despite Chief Wiggum's efforts, sketches, and public appeals, El Barto's identity stays officially unsolved for most of Springfield's population, even though Bart has let it slip to a few people, including Skinner and apparently Homer. The joke recurs throughout the show as other characters misidentify or misattribute the tag—Milhouse, a girl named Eloise Barto, and various students all get suspected at different points. The gag has also spawned copycat and parody versions, with other characters adopting their own spray-painted aliases like El Homo, El Margo, El Barbo, and El Frinko. It highlights Bart's rebellious, mischievous streak while also underscoring the general incompetence of Springfield's law enforcement and school administration in ever catching him. The tag itself has become a recognizable piece of the show's visual background gags, appearing on walls, buildings, and even microscopic imagery. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: "Bart is the second most wanted student after the mysterious El Barto." | "If Bart can be El Barto..."

title: Gremlin (character)
text: Gremlin (character) is A creature that appears in a Treehouse of Horror segment, tormenting Bart on the school bus. The Gremlin is a mischievous, malevolent creature that only Bart can see, sabotaging the school bus by prying loose the wheel screws while flying alongside it. Its presence drives Bart into escalating fits of panic that no one else believes, echoing a classic paranoia-driven horror trope. The segment plays on the idea of an unreliable witness, as adults like Principal Skinner dismiss Bart's warnings as childish imagination, only reinforcing the creature's threat. Even after seemingly being defeated by a flare and struck by a car, the Gremlin proves persistent, resurfacing to terrify Bart one final time while holding a severed head. Beyond the show itself, the character was later reused as a collectible, non-canon creature in a mobile game tied to a Halloween-themed event. It stands as a direct parody of a famous creature from a classic anthology TV series. Voiced by Frank Welker.

title: Carl Carlson
text: Carl Carlson is Supervisor of Sector 7-G at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant and best friend of Lenny Leonard; part of Homer's circle of coworkers and drinking buddies at Moe's Tavern. Carl is a reserved, dry-witted power plant worker who often acts as the quiet, sensible counterpart to the more boisterous Homer and Lenny. Despite his low-key demeanor, he's noted as unusually intelligent and accomplished, holding a master's degree in nuclear physics and a very high IQ. He's a Buddhist of African-Icelandic-American heritage who enjoys bowling and hanging out at Moe's Tavern. A recurring gag involves the ambiguously close, almost romantic-seeming bond between Carl and Lenny, which other characters frequently misread as something more than friendship, much to Carl's mild annoyance. His backstory reveals he was adopted, and later episodes explore his search for his biological family, including a cowboy father and an ancestor who was a freed slave. He's also had on-and-off romances, notably with Lenny's sister Lainie and with a restaurant owner named Naima. Voiced by Hank Azaria (Season 1-31), Alex Désert (Season 32-Present); Harry Shearer voiced him in his debut appearance "Homer's Night Out". title: Nick Riviera
text: Nick Riviera is A shady, incompetent quack doctor in Springfield who occasionally treats the Simpson family when they can't afford Dr. Hibbert. Dr. Nick Riviera is Springfield's go-to bargain doctor, holding degrees from laughably fraudulent institutions and possessing almost no genuine medical competence. He gets by on sheer luck rather than skill, botching procedures, robbing graves for spare body parts, and giving dangerous advice without ever facing real consequences. A born huckster, he hawks his services through cheesy infomercials and treats surgeries like television spectacles, embodying a Ron Popeil-style showman more than a physician. Despite his incompetence, he's endearingly cheerful and unfailingly polite, greeting every room with his signature catchphrase. His shady nature is played for comedy rather than menace, and he's survived numerous disasters that should have ended his career or his life. Over the show's run he's popped up in countless bizarre contexts, from citizenship tests to game shows to nearly being killed in freak accidents, always bouncing back unscathed. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Hi, everybody! | Well if it isn't my old friend Mr. McGregg — with a leg for an arm and an arm for a leg | Inflammable means flammable? What a country?!
