Inflammable means flammable? What a country?!

title: Alexander Hubley
text: Alexander Hubley is A runaway boarding-school kid, nicknamed 'Hub,' who squats at Springfield Elementary and is temporarily taken in by Principal Skinner. Hub is a resourceful but troubled boy who ran away from his boarding school and ended up secretly living in the Springfield Elementary library, even convincing Groundskeeper Willie he was a ghost. He's cunning and manipulative early on, lying about his parents being dead to gain sympathy, but he's also just a scared, lonely kid underneath the bravado. Skinner's growing attachment to him brings out an unexpected paternal side in the principal, while Hub's fame from starring in the school play turns him briefly into an arrogant show-off. His storyline explores themes of found family and belonging, as he temporarily fills a void in Skinner's life before his real parents track him down. In the end, Hub shows genuine gratitude for Skinner's care by improvising a heartfelt farewell during the play. He mainly appears in a single major episode after a brief background cameo. Voiced by Kieran Culkin.

title: Cosine Tangent
text: Cosine Tangent is A member of The Superfriends nerd club at Springfield Elementary, classmate of Bart and Lisa Simpson. Cosine Tangent is a minor student character defined almost entirely by his math-themed name, which hints at a fondness for trigonometry. As part of the Superfriends, he's one of the school's brainy clique who welcomed Bart into their group after his comet discovery made him briefly famous. He tends to get swept up in the group's science-driven schemes, from biking to the observatory to warn of an incoming comet to helping build a homemade social network called SpringFace. His nerdiness sometimes works against him, such as when he and Database lose a school race because they stop to measure wind speed instead of running. Overall, he serves as background texture for Springfield Elementary's academic subculture rather than a character with deep individual development. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Vance Connor
text: Vance Connor is Successful local businessman and Springfield Wall of Fame honoree; former high school rival of Homer for senior-class president. Vance Connor is a friendly, well-liked entrepreneur who owns multiple businesses around Springfield and has even earned a spot on the town's Wall of Fame. Back in his Springfield High days, he was the composed, policy-minded vice president who beat out a floundering Homer in a class president election that the students had actually intended as a joke at Homer's expense. His victory only happened because Principal Dondelinger secretly had the real ballot box hidden away to protect Homer from public humiliation. Confident and approachable, Vance seems to genuinely enjoy interacting with the townspeople, greeting everyone warmly during his Wall of Fame ceremony. Despite unknowingly holding onto a stolen election win for years, he comes across as gracious rather than smug, even cheering for Homer in an imagined alternate timeline where the truth came out differently. His look in flashbacks pays homage to 1970s teen idol David Cassidy. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Local businessman, Frequent Flyer Silver Card-holder, and legendary twenty-percent tipper... Springfield's own Vance Connor!
quotes: Local businessman, Frequent Flyer Silver Card-holder, and legendary twenty-percent tipper... Springfield's own Vance Connor!

title: Blinky
text: Blinky is A three-eyed mutant fish from Springfield's radioactive waters, notable for a scandal involving Mr. Burns during his gubernatorial campaign. Blinky is one of the many three-eyed orange fish that live in Springfield's ponds and lakes, a visible symbol of the pollution caused by the town's nuclear power plant. Unable to speak, Blinky exists mostly as background wildlife and a recurring visual gag representing environmental contamination. Its most famous moment came when Bart caught it and it became a political football during Mr. Burns' run for governor, ultimately costing Burns the election after he was caught on camera spitting out a bite of the cooked fish. Over the years, variations of the Blinky species have appeared with different mutations, from extra eyes to alien tongues, reflecting the show's running joke about nuclear contamination. In one non-canon storyline, a monstrous, shark-sized version of Blinky terrorizes the Springfield coastline in a parody of 'Jaws.' Despite dying at least once in canon continuity, related three-eyed fish continue to appear across the show's run, and even show up as a nod in 'Futurama.'

title: Mona Simpson
text: Mona Simpson is Homer Simpson's long-lost mother and Abraham Simpson's ex-wife; grandmother to Bart, Lisa, and Maggie. Mona is a former hippie and political activist whose radical past as a fugitive kept her separated from her family for most of Homer's life. Once a free-spirited cocktail waitress known as Sunny, she fell into the 1960s counterculture movement, taking part in protests and activism that eventually forced her to abandon her husband and young son and go on the run under various aliases. Despite her absence, she cared deeply for Homer, secretly sending him care packages for years and leaving him affectionate notes on recipe cards. Her sporadic reappearances in Springfield are marked by tension with the bitter, resentful Abe and joyful reconnections with Homer, though she's constantly pursued by the authorities and Mr. Burns. Her ultimate death deeply affects Homer, and her final wishes—delivered through a will and later through a dream sequence—reveal her enduring love and the guilt-driven emotional baggage Homer carries throughout his life. She embodies themes of guilt, forgiveness, and unconditional maternal love despite her unconventional and rebellious nature. Voiced by Maggie Roswell, Glenn Close, Pamela Hayden, Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: You know, Moe, my Mom once said something that really stuck with me. She said, "Homer, you're a big disappointment." And God bless her soul, she was really on to something.
quotes: You know, Moe, my Mom once said something that really stuck with me. She said, "Homer, you're a big disappointment." And God bless her soul, she was really on to something.

title: Lewis look-alike
text: Lewis look-alike is A background student in Bart Simpson's class at Springfield Elementary who bears a strong resemblance to classmate Lewis Clark. This nameless kid is one of Springfield Elementary's many faceless extras, notable mainly for looking almost identical to Bart's classmate Lewis Clark. He turns up constantly in crowd scenes, the school band, and even as a member of the Mighty Pigs pee-wee hockey team, yet has never spoken a line in the actual TV series. Despite his low profile, he's shown a reckless streak, once sticking a lit firecracker into a pencil sharpener, and was brave (or unlucky) enough to be among the first to sample one of Edna Krabappel's infamous stale muffins. Animators distinguish him from Lewis through small details like his blue-and-green jacket, taller eyes, a more frequent smile, and slightly purplish hair. He briefly gets an actual voice and personality in The Simpsons Game, where he talks about hobbies and Robo-bots, and is caught up in a citywide crime wave triggered by a violent video game. He's essentially a visual inside joke for eagle-eyed fans who like spotting background characters. Voiced by Pamela Hayden (The Simpsons Game).

title: Dr. Crab
text: Dr. Crab is Comic-book supervillain and arch-nemesis of Radioactive Man, within the Simpsons universe's in-fiction comic mythology. Dr. Crab, originally the scientist Dr. Vladmir Krabokov, is the recurring archenemy of the superhero Radioactive Man in the Bongo comics-within-the-show. He began as a mastermind orchestrating heists and thefts, eventually mutating himself through nuclear research into the crab-like villain audiences know. Obsessed with defeating his nemesis, he cycles through elaborate schemes involving giant robots, ray guns, cloned dinosaurs, and even crab-themed robot henchmen. Despite his intelligence and persistence, he is a chronic loser, repeatedly foiled, defeated, or humiliated by Radioactive Man and his allies. His character arc sees him mutate further into a creature called Prawn, and later attempt to reverse his transformation entirely. In non-canon material, he appears as a major villain in mobile game storylines, ultimately becoming a bizarre permanent resident of Springfield after his defeats.

title: Captain Squid
text: Captain Squid is Comic-book superhero character within the Simpsons universe; member of the Superior Squadron. Captain Squid is a comic-within-a-comic superhero who fights alongside the Superior Squadron in the Radioactive Man comic series. His powers stem from deep-sea origins, giving him extending tentacles hidden beneath his gloves and super strength, which he's insecure about revealing to others. He harbors a quiet, mutual romance with fellow hero Lure Lass, though his self-consciousness about his squid-like tentacles keeps him hesitant. Loyal and dependable, he regularly helps his teammates in battles against villains like Dr. Crab, Hypno Head, and an evil version of Radioactive Man, using his stretchy tentacles resourcefully to rescue allies. He also has his own spin-off comic and a young sidekick named L'il Squiddie. In one alternate continuity, his story ends tragically when a version of Bug Boy from another reality—where Captain Squid is a villain—kills him, prompting Plasmo to bring in a replacement Captain Squid from a different universe.

title: Joan of Arc
text: Joan of Arc is Historical/legendary French figure depicted in a Simpsons parody segment, played by Lisa Simpson. Joan of Arc is portrayed in the show through a retelling of her legend in the 'Hot Child in the City' segment, with Lisa Simpson taking on her role. In this version, she is called by God to lead the French army against the English during the Hundred Years' War, achieving early triumphs before being captured and put on trial for witchcraft. The story adds a comedic twist by revealing that an enemy soldier also believed he was divinely chosen, leaving God to awkwardly admit the mix-up. Rather than a grim historical ending, the segment gives her a whimsical rescue by Sir Lancelot, followed by an absurd escape into space. Beyond this main appearance, she recurs as a background cultural reference—appearing in trivia about left-handed historical figures, on a wall of admired great women in Lisa's fantasy bedroom, and in jokes involving past-life photo booths. She symbolizes courage and faith, but the show treats her legacy with playful irreverence. Voiced by Yeardley Smith.

title: Manjula Nahasapeemapetilon
text: Manjula Nahasapeemapetilon is Apu's wife and mother of their octuplets; a recurring character in Springfield. Manjula is the devoted wife of Apu Nahasapeemapetilon, having entered an arranged marriage with him at the age of eight. Though primarily a homemaker, she occasionally pitches in at the Kwik-E-Mart and juggles the chaos of raising eight children. She's a skilled cook, famous for stretching just a few basic ingredients like chickpeas, lentils, and rice into varied meals. Her marriage to Apu is loving but frequently tested by his grueling work schedule and past infidelity, leading to periods of separation and eventual reconciliation through counseling. She maintains a close friendship with Marge Simpson, bonding over motherhood, and has a playful running joke about marrying Sanjay if Apu ever dies. Despite the strain in her marriage, she remains caring toward her family and willing to forgive Apu after he proves his devotion. Voiced by Jan Hooks / Tress MacNeille.

title: Coach Krupt
text: Coach Krupt is A sadistic gym teacher at Springfield Elementary School. Coach Krupt is a brutal, dodgeball-obsessed physical education teacher who took over for Ms. Pommelhorst at Springfield Elementary. His defining trait is an unhealthy fixation on a violent game called Bombardment, which he schedules relentlessly and even incorporates into non-gym activities like test prep and dining out. He shows little regard for student safety, ignoring medical excuses and forcing kids to participate even in absurd circumstances, such as making Milhouse mime climbing a missing rope. Despite his cruelty, he's physically fit and quick enough to dodge retaliation attempts from students like Bart. Outside of school, he has a family life with a wife and two children, though he's shown to have a temper that extends to physical altercations with other parents. His surname is a not-so-subtle pun on the word 'corrupt,' reflecting his abusive approach to teaching. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Jaffee Ziswhisky
text: Jaffee Ziswhisky is A background student in Bart Simpson's fourth-grade class at Springfield Elementary School. Jaffee Ziswhisky, also known by the nickname Dooley, is one of the many minor kids populating Bart's classroom under Ms. Krabappel. He's mostly a silent background presence, appearing in crowd scenes and group activities rather than getting his own storylines. He took part in the school's Christmas Pageant as a singer and later joined Bart's makeshift army when the boys squared off against Nelson and his gang of bullies. A running joke about him is that he almost never speaks on screen, with one of his only vocal moments being a yelp of pain after getting hit with a dodgeball. Adding to his quirky, inconsistent design, he has occasionally been drawn with blond hair instead of his usual brown. His first and last names weren't even given until many seasons after his debut, reflecting his status as one of the show's many nameless-turned-named extras. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Artie Ziff
text: Artie Ziff is Marge's obsessive high school admirer turned billionaire businessman, and a recurring rival for her affection against Homer. Artie Ziff is a wealthy, nerdy egomaniac whose entire personality revolves around his unshakable belief that he deserves the best of everything, especially Marge Bouvier. Ever since a disastrous prom night where his wandering hands got him slapped and dumped, he's carried a torch for her into adulthood, using his software fortune to repeatedly try to win her over from Homer. He's prone to self-flattering fantasies, plays the victim by blaming criticism on antisemitism, and can't seem to accept rejection gracefully. His financial empire is built on absurd luck and questionable ethics, leading to a spectacular bankruptcy, a stint hiding in the Simpsons' attic, and eventually prison time after his company collapses. Even behind bars his obliviousness persists, as he pesters fellow inmates about their smoking habits with little regard for his own safety. Despite cycling between staggering wealth and utter ruin, Artie's defining trait remains his inability to move past his teenage crush on Marge, culminating in increasingly desperate and bizarre schemes, including building robotic Marge duplicates. Voiced by Jon Lovitz (Dan Castellaneta in "The Front").

title: Tad Winslow
text: Tad Winslow is Fictional doctor character on the show-within-a-show "It Never Ends," briefly played by Moe Szyslak. Tad Winslow is a soap opera doctor character within the fictional series It Never Ends, originally portrayed by another actor before Moe Szyslak took over the part after getting plastic surgery. As a character, Tad is written as a suave womanizer who juggles romances with multiple women, including a resurrected mummy and a scheming contessa. Despite his charming exterior, he is fiercely devoted to his medical profession, often citing hospital regulations as a reason to end relationships. His most telling trait is a hidden vulnerability, expressed through a recurring line about having an unfixable hole in his soul, suggesting deep self-doubt beneath his womanizing confidence. Moe's tenure in the role ends dramatically when he leaks future plotlines to get revenge on the show's producer, resulting in his firing. The show itself seems prone to absurd, over-the-top storylines involving mummies, angels, and terrorist attacks at baby showers. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta / Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: I've dedicated my life to diseases of the head holes. But the one hole I've never been able to fix is the one in my soul.
quotes: I've dedicated my life to diseases of the head holes. But the one hole I've never been able to fix is the one in my soul.

title: Rayshelle Peyton
text: Rayshelle Peyton is Fourth grade teacher at Springfield Elementary School, married to orchestra musician Darryl Peyton. Rayshelle Peyton is a dedicated and compassionate teacher who moved to Springfield after her husband landed a job with the local orchestra. She first crosses paths with Bart when she rescues him from drowning at a resort pool, an act that inadvertently sparks his embarrassment and a lingering crush. As his new teacher, she goes out of her way to bring innovative project-based learning to the school, showing far more initiative than her colleagues. Despite Bart's disruptive behavior stemming from his feelings for her, she remains patient and continues to see the good in him. She's also a supportive spouse, standing by her husband's music career even though she's not particularly impressed by his talent. Her calm, understanding nature ultimately helps Bart work through his emotions rather than punishing him outright. Voiced by Kerry Washington.

title: Milo
text: Milo is Owner of Coolsville Comics & Toys, a rival comic shop to Comic Book Guy's Android's Dungeon. Milo is the friendly, fashionable owner of Coolsville Comics & Toys, a comic shop that opens across the street from Comic Book Guy's failing store. Unlike the stereotypical, grumpy comic fan image Comic Book Guy embodies, Milo is slim, trendy, and dating a girlfriend, which throws Comic Book Guy's attempts to discredit him into disarray. He wins over Springfield's kids with small kindnesses like handing out Japanese hard candy, playing fun music, and bringing in famous alternative comic creators for signings. Despite his laid-back, generous approach, he's deeply knowledgeable about comics and genuinely believes they should be read and enjoyed rather than hoarded for value. He treats customers' opinions with respect instead of lecturing them, marking a stark contrast to his rival's condescending style. Over time his relationship with girlfriend Strawberry develops into marriage and parenthood, cementing him as a recurring, good-natured fixture of Springfield's comic scene. Voiced by Jack Black, Maurice LaMarche. Notable quotes: Now I hope you all like Korean Pop Covers of Tom Jones songs, 'cause they're about to be blasted!
quotes: Now I hope you all like Korean Pop Covers of Tom Jones songs, 'cause they're about to be blasted!

title: César
text: César is A hostile French wine and leather maker who enslaved Bart during a French exchange trip; recurring minor antagonist. César is a gruff, exploitative French vintner who, alongside his nephew Ugolín, tricks Bart into forced labor under the guise of a foreign exchange program. He mistreats Bart badly, denying him proper food and shelter while making him test dangerously adulterated wine. Cunning but ultimately careless, his scheme collapses when Bart secretly learns French and exposes their crimes to the police. Despite being jailed, César resurfaces repeatedly across the series in various shady occupations, from a robber to a leather maker hunting an endangered snake. He and Ugolín share a recurring dynamic as a duo of small-time French criminals whose plans usually fail. Their names are a playful literary reference to characters from a classic French novel series. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Eddie
text: Eddie is One of the two police officers (alongside Lou) who assist Chief Wiggum on nearly every case in Springfield. Eddie is a background fixture of the Springfield Police Department, always trailing Chief Wiggum and Lou on their various bumbling investigations. He's portrayed as dim-witted, though not quite as clueless as Wiggum himself, and has grown quieter and less talkative over the years compared to his earlier appearances. Despite the low competence of the force, he takes genuine pride in his job, feeling it lets him "make a difference." He's occasionally given small moments of characterization, such as unwinding at Moe's Tavern with Lou or briefly getting promoted into Lou's role. There's a running undercurrent of ambiguity about his sexuality, with hints from his mannerisms and Wiggum's own remarks, complicated by a non-canon claim that he was involved with Lou's ex-wife. In noncanon material he's even been jokingly revealed as Ralph Wiggum's biological father due to their similar hair and non-sequiturs. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "It's a wonder why he can't get a girlfriend" - Chief Wiggum | "Why can't you be more like Eddie?" - Chief Wiggum | "He's right chief" - Eddie
quotes: "It's a wonder why he can't get a girlfriend" - Chief Wiggum
"Why can't you be more like Eddie?" - Chief Wiggum
"He's right chief" - Eddie

title: Bug Boy
text: Bug Boy is Comic-book superhero character; a member of the Superior Squadron and ally/friend of Radioactive Man. Bug Boy is an alien genius from the planet Kranium-4 who came to Earth after feeling out of place among his own hyper-intelligent species, despite having an IQ of 350. On Earth he built a public identity as Dr. Bix Bentley, Jr., working various odd jobs before joining the Superior Squadron as a costumed hero. He's resourceful and inventive, often devising gadgets and antidotes to solve the team's problems, and he possesses an unusual empathic link that lets him control insects. Despite his brilliance, he's shown to be business-savvy in a very mundane way, being the only squad member smart enough to secure merchandising rights to his own likeness. He serves as a loyal supporter of Radioactive Man through many of the hero's trials, including advising him during a dark turn as ruler of Zenith City. In one continuity he meets his end crushed by a defeated robot, only to be replaced by an alternate-reality counterpart.

title: Fidel Castro
text: Fidel Castro is Communist President of Cuba, appearing as a satirical caricature in various Simpsons episodes. This version of Fidel Castro is a shrewd and somewhat paranoid leader trying to keep his bankrupt nation afloat under Communist rule. He's willing to bend his principles for money, famously swindling Mr. Burns out of his trillion-dollar bill rather than letting him buy or settle on the island. Despite his tough exterior, he shows a petty, almost gossipy side, being oddly hurt to learn a street named after him caters to a gay clientele. He pops up repeatedly across the show's run in cameos, dream sequences, and background gags, often used as shorthand for old-school leftist dictators. He's also been linked romantically to Agnes Skinner and included on lists of famous leftists, adding a comedic touch to his historical infamy. Mr. Burns even lists him as one of the authority figures he enjoys dressing up as. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Jacques
text: Jacques is A French bowling instructor who once had an affair with Marge Simpson. Jacques is a smooth-talking bowling instructor whose real passion lies less in coaching and more in charming his female students. Speaking with an exaggerated French accent that oddly vanishes whenever he shouts, he embodies the classic seductive Casanova archetype. His most infamous storyline involves nearly winning over Marge Simpson, testing her marriage to Homer before she ultimately stays loyal. Despite this rejection, he never fully gives up on Marge, resurfacing years later to pursue her again while working as her instructor. He's a recurring background presence at Barney's Bowlarama and even competes on a team made up of other women linked romantically to Homer. Ultimately his womanizing catches up with him: after losing a decisive bowling match to Marge, he's arrested for having an expired visa. Voiced by Albert Brooks. Notable quotes: not quite breakfast, not quite lunch, but you get a slice of cantalope at the end
quotes: not quite breakfast, not quite lunch, but you get a slice of cantalope at the end

title: Funzo
text: Funzo is A malfunctioning must-have Christmas toy from Springfield's episode "Grift of the Magi", created by Kid First Industries. Funzo is a wildly popular robotic toy manufactured by the shady company Kid First Industries, which secretly used Springfield Elementary students to help design and name it. Beneath its cute exterior, Funzo is secretly programmed to violently destroy other children's toys, wiping out rivals like Bart's Krusty doll and Lisa's Malibu Stacy. Its limited vocabulary of creepy phrases hints at its sinister nature long before anyone realizes the danger. Once Bart and Lisa uncover the truth, they enlist Homer to pose as Santa and collect the toys from unsuspecting families for destruction. Even after seemingly all the dolls are burned in the Springfield Tire Fire, one Funzo survives and nearly attacks the Simpsons before being destroyed by Gary Coleman. The toy resurfaces in later episodes sitting harmlessly on shelves, a lingering reminder of its chaotic debut. Funzo serves as a not-so-subtle parody of the real-life Furby toy craze. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: I see you | give me a hug | I'm very mad at boo
quotes: I see you
give me a hug
I'm very mad at boo

title: Eddie Muntz
text: Eddie Muntz is Nelson Muntz's absent, largely deadbeat father. Eddie Muntz is the long-absent father of school bully Nelson, having walked out on his family under the classic excuse of 'going to get cigarettes' and never really returning. He once coached his son's soccer team and rides a motorbike, hinting at a rougher, biker-ish background. His disappearance became a running gag, with Nelson stubbornly clinging to the belief that his dad truly did just step out for smokes. When Bart eventually tracks him down, it's revealed that a chocolate bar with peanuts triggered a severe allergic reaction that left him disfigured and mute, after which an opportunistic circus manager caged him as a freak show exhibit, with gawking crowds throwing peanuts that kept him permanently swollen. Despite his squalid circumstances, he insists he never intended to abandon his family. He later reappears in a world's-tallest-human-pyramid stunt, and it's implied he and Nelson's mother eventually divorced for good when she remarries a clown. Voiced by Phil Hartman (first appearance); later Harry Shearer, Hank Azaria, and Earl Mann.

title: Larry Dalrymple
text: Larry Dalrymple is One of the two regular barflies at Moe's Tavern (alongside Sam), a minor recurring background character. Larry is a balding, tall barfly known for being quiet, dim-witted, and a bit odd, earning him the nickname 'the ear bender' despite rarely speaking. He's often seen among the men gawking at Marge Simpson while drinking at Moe's. Outside the bar, he apparently enjoyed fishing and was close to his mother, frequently telling her about his tavern friends. His most significant storyline comes after his death, when it's revealed he had been smuggling stolen sapphires for Fat Tony by concealing them in an unusual way, leading his fellow barflies on a chaotic road trip to scatter his ashes. The ashes-and-jewel caper results in mistaken identity, a mob hitman, and a car crash, ultimately revealing that Moe swindled everyone by keeping the gems for himself. Even in death, Larry's urn becomes a recurring prop and gag in later background appearances. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Hey, this stupid machine took my money!
quotes: Hey, this stupid machine took my money!

title: Gerald Samson
text: Gerald Samson is Baby rival of Maggie Simpson, known as "Baby Gerald" or "The Unibrow Baby". Gerald Samson is a recurring infant character best recognized for his single, thick unibrow and a curious blond curl atop his head. He and Maggie Simpson share an intense baby rivalry that seems to have started at birth, when a hospital mix-up left him wrapped in newspaper instead of a diaper, giving him a lasting rash. Unlike most babies who ignore Maggie, Gerald is fixated on her, often glaring at her from his stroller and even wielding a small mallet as a makeshift weapon. He's shown to be mobile and capable of walking, in contrast to Maggie who still crawls and stumbles, and like her he has never been heard to speak. Gerald can be sly and manipulative, once framing Maggie for his own messes while at Marge's daycare to earn rewards for himself. His antagonism reaches its peak in the short film where he and Maggie are wrongly placed among low-achieving toddlers, leading to a tense standoff over a butterfly chrysalis that Maggie ultimately outsmarts him over. In non-canon future depictions, the two rivals surprisingly grow up to fall in love and marry, complicating their otherwise adversarial dynamic. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "Baby Gerald, we can't help but wonder what mischief you'll get into next" - Mayor Quimby
quotes: "Baby Gerald, we can't help but wonder what mischief you'll get into next" - Mayor Quimby

title: Scratchy
text: Scratchy is Cartoon cat character from the fictional show-within-a-show 'The Itchy & Scratchy Show', a favorite cartoon of Bart and Lisa Simpson. Scratchy is the perpetual victim in the ultra-violent cartoon show that Bart and Lisa watch obsessively within the world of The Simpsons. Despite being portrayed as a kind, trusting, and gentle character, he exists solely to be tormented, maimed, and usually killed by his mouse nemesis Itchy in nearly every short. Unlike similar cat-and-mouse parodies, Scratchy rarely if ever fights back, making him a purely innocent and hapless figure rather than a rival trying to get revenge. His debut cartoon flopped commercially until he was paired with Itchy, after which the duo became wildly popular. Over the decades of the show's fictional history, he has gained a family including a wife and son, and even inspired a theme park, Itchy & Scratchy Land. Scratchy's design draws inspiration from classic cartoon cats like Tom from Tom and Jerry and Katnip from Herman and Katnip, but his character exaggerates their loser status into total helplessness. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Screamapillar
text: Screamapillar is An endangered animal that briefly lived in the Simpson family's backyard and became their forced responsibility. The Screamapillar is a bizarre, endangered red creature resembling a caterpillar, best known for its constant, piercing screaming, even while asleep. It is comically fragile in odd ways, being the favorite food of virtually everything, sexually attracted to fire, and dependent on emotional reassurance to survive, often needing to be burped like an infant. After it settled into the Simpsons' koi pond, the EPA forced the family to care for it under strange bureaucratic threat, leading to a series of misadventures including near-death experiences and a courtroom trial over its supposed demise. Despite the chaos it caused, the family—particularly Homer—ends up bizarrely devoted to its wellbeing, even as it later shows a darker, almost gleeful side by laughing at Homer's execution. The character serves as a vehicle for absurdist EPA-related satire and slapstick misfortune centered on Homer's incompetence and bad luck. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: You sure God doesn't want it to be dead?
quotes: You sure God doesn't want it to be dead?

title: Ian McKellen (character)
text: Ian McKellen (character) is Real-life celebrity guest character; English actor encountered by the Simpsons family during their trip to England. This version of Ian McKellen is a fictionalized cameo of the real actor, portrayed as deeply superstitious about the theatrical taboo surrounding the name "Macbeth." He crosses paths with the Simpsons outside a London theater where he is set to perform, and tries to warn them not to say the cursed name aloud. Ironically, his warnings only cause the family to repeat the word more, triggering a comedic chain of misfortunes—being drenched, hit by an anvil, and struck by lightning multiple times. His exasperation and old-world theatrical dignity clash humorously with the Simpsons' cluelessness. The segment plays entirely on real-world actor superstitions, including the belief that wishing someone luck before a show is itself bad luck. Beyond this appearance, he's noted as the star of the show-within-a-show "Cookie Castle," reinforcing his status as a working actor in the Simpsons universe. Voiced by Ian McKellen (himself). Notable quotes: Quiet, you blundering fool! You'll curse us all! | Macbeth!
quotes: Quiet, you blundering fool! You'll curse us all!
Macbeth!

title: Tito Puente (character)
text: Tito Puente (character) is Real-life Latin jazz musician who appears as a guest character, briefly hired as a music teacher and later a suspect in the Mr. Burns shooting. Tito Puente appears as himself, a celebrated Latin jazz bandleader who is almost hired to run a jazz program at Springfield Elementary after the school strikes oil. When Mr. Burns steals the oil out from under the school, the deal collapses and Puente's fury at losing the job makes him a suspect when Burns is later shot. He proves to be good-humored despite his anger, preferring artistic revenge to violence, and eagerly performs a mocking musical takedown of Burns for Chief Wiggum during the investigation. His club, Chez Guevara, and his Latin Jazz Ensemble reflect his professional musical background outside the show. Ultimately he's cleared as a suspect, charming even the police with his showmanship. He reappears only briefly afterward, mostly in photographs or archive footage referencing his one big episode. Voiced by Himself (Tito Puente). Notable quotes: "He robbed the school of Tito!" | I hope all our suspects are this much fun. | [setting Burns' soul afire with a slanderous mambo]
quotes: "He robbed the school of Tito!"
I hope all our suspects are this much fun.
[setting Burns' soul afire with a slanderous mambo]

title: Burns' alien
text: Burns' alien is Mr. Burns in a disoriented, glowing state after weekly medical treatments, mistaken for an alien by Homer. This isn't really an alien at all, but Mr. Burns after undergoing his secretive weekly regimen of life-extending medical procedures. The treatments leave him dazed, soft-spoken, and glowing faintly green, causing him to wander into the woods near Springfield in a stupor. Homer stumbles upon him during one of these wandering episodes and becomes convinced he's encountered extraterrestrial life, sparking a town-wide obsession and even drawing federal investigators to Springfield. The gag plays on X-Files-style alien mythology, with the 'alien' speaking in gentle, peaceful phrases before ultimately being revealed as the town's crotchety, misanthropic power plant owner. Once the effects of his treatment wear off via a booster shot from Dr. Nick, Burns snaps back to his usual venomous personality. The episode uses this dual identity to poke fun at both UFO paranoia and Burns' inhuman, otherworldly persona. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "Don't be afraid." | "I bring you peace." | "A lifetime of working in a nuclear power plant has given me a healthy green glow."
quotes: "Don't be afraid."
"I bring you peace."
"A lifetime of working in a nuclear power plant has given me a healthy green glow."

title: Roger Meyers, Jr.
text: Roger Meyers, Jr. is CEO of Itchy & Scratchy Studios, son of Roger Meyers, Sr.. Roger Meyers, Jr. runs the animation studio behind the violent Itchy & Scratchy cartoons that constantly draw the ire of concerned parents like Marge. He's portrayed as a cold, mercenary executive who views his young audience with disdain and only values people while they're useful to him. His short temper and cruelty surface repeatedly, from berating a fired writer to callously dismissing Otto after hiring him on the spot for a voice role. When the studio nearly collapses due to a lawsuit, he shows no gratitude toward Bart and Lisa for their late-arriving help, brushing them off with icy sarcasm. Desperate to boost sagging ratings, he greenlit the ill-fated character Poochie, only to have the experiment backfire spectacularly. Despite his unpleasant demeanor, he remains a recurring fixture tied to the show's satirical media empire. Voiced by Alex Rocco, Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Hey, great, mail it to last week—when I might've cared. I've got cartoons to make, kids.
quotes: Hey, great, mail it to last week—when I might've cared. I've got cartoons to make, kids.

title: Janey Powell
text: Janey Powell is A student at Springfield Elementary School and one of Lisa Simpson's classmates/friends. Janey is a young girl who attends Springfield Elementary alongside Lisa Simpson, often described as Lisa's 'fair-weather friend.' She drifts between genuine friendship and joining the other kids in teasing Lisa, showing a somewhat fickle loyalty. Unlike Lisa, she isn't particularly studious or intellectual, preferring simple pastimes like chewing gum over deep conversation. Despite the friction, she's spent time at the Simpson household and shares casual activities with Lisa, like reading together or watching cartoons. There are hints of a one-sided crush on Milhouse Van Houten, adding a bit of adolescent drama to her character. Oddly, her surname changes across different episodes, which the show later explained via her father's shady, ever-changing identity as a counterfeiter. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Abraham Lincoln
text: Abraham Lincoln is 16th President of the United States, appearing as a historical figure and recurring background character throughout the series. Abraham Lincoln appears in Springfield lore mostly as a historical icon rather than an active character, popping up as statues, animatronics, portraits, and coins throughout the town. He's affectionately nicknamed 'Honest Abe,' a trait played for a joke when he insults Mabel Simpson's disguise but insists on his own honesty. The show frequently references his assassination for dark comedy, whether in Homer's daydreams of rescuing him or Bart's mischievous school pageant reenactment. He's tied into Simpson family history through a legend that Abraham Simpson I was named after him. Lincoln also turns up in surreal cartoon-within-a-cartoon segments of Itchy & Scratchy, in Heaven in non-canon material, and even as a talking animatronic used for factory or customer service work. Overall he functions as a recurring cultural touchstone the show riffs on rather than a fleshed-out character with his own arc. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Harry Shearer, Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Hey, hey. Honest Abe.
quotes: Hey, hey. Honest Abe.

title: Juliet Hobbes
text: Juliet Hobbes is A girl who briefly became Lisa Simpson's best friend, sharing an obsessive imaginary world with her. Juliet is an imaginative, somewhat unstable girl who meets Lisa at an art class and quickly becomes her closest confidante. The two bond over a shared love of Josh Groban and later invent an elaborate fantasy kingdom called Equalia, which becomes an all-consuming obsession for Juliet. She has a strained relationship with her parents, who worry that her fixations, whether on Groban or Equalia, are unhealthy and excessive. Her devotion to fantasy over reality eventually leads her to run away from home, dragging Lisa along, and the pair end up in real danger when bullies capture them. Even after the ordeal, Juliet remains committed to her fantasy world, riding off alone while Lisa decides she's had enough. Her intense, escapist personality ultimately proves too much for Lisa's friendship to sustain. Voiced by Emily Blunt. Notable quotes: The real world is for people who can't imagine anything better.
quotes: The real world is for people who can't imagine anything better.

title: Rachel Jordan
text: Rachel Jordan is Christian rock singer and former love interest of Ned Flanders, first appearing after Maude Flanders' death. Rachel Jordan is a singer who once fronted the Christian rock band Kovenant before pursuing a solo career rooted in her faith. Her backstory reveals a troubled past involving alcohol, from which she was saved by finding religion. She crosses paths with Ned Flanders on multiple occasions, and the two share a tentative romantic connection, though it's repeatedly derailed by Ned's inability to move past his late wife Maude. Despite being deeply unsettled when Ned secretly cuts her hair to resemble Maude, Rachel proves remarkably forgiving, eventually reconciling with him. She's portrayed as steadfastly devout even as her old bandmates abandon Christian music for mainstream pop. Rachel later appears briefly among the angry Springfield mob during the events of the town being trapped under a dome. Voiced by Shawn Colvin.

title: Morty Szyslak
text: Morty Szyslak is Moe Szyslak's estranged, harsh father and former mattress store magnate. Morty Szyslak is a hardened, ruthless businessman who built a mattress empire called Mattress King through cutthroat and dishonest tactics, including sabotaging rivals with bed bugs. He raised Moe, Marv, and Minnie with cold discipline, favoring underhanded schemes over family loyalty, and disowned Moe when he refused to destroy a family-run competitor. Despite his gruff exterior, he eventually sought reconciliation with Moe upon retiring, though his true colors resurfaced when he later encouraged Moe to sabotage his own siblings rather than act with integrity. Morty's past includes a stint as a circus freak and heavy drinking with other troubled Springfield fathers, hinting at a rough, unstable upbringing that shaped Moe's own dysfunction. He's portrayed as manipulative and morally flexible, valuing profit and legacy over kindness. His reappearances tend to tie back to unresolved tension in the Szyslak family dynamic. Voiced by Ray Liotta.

title: Gil Gunderson
text: Gil Gunderson is A recurring minor character in Springfield, an unlucky, perpetually unemployed-or-nearly-so businessman who drifts through countless jobs and misfortunes. Gil is Springfield's poster child for bad luck and bad timing, having cycled through an absurd number of professions—from car salesman to Mall Santa to bank security guard—only to lose each one through misfortune or his own desperation. He habitually refers to himself in the third person and punctuates his speech with a nervous scat-like "ha-cha-cha," giving him a distinctly anxious, down-on-his-luck energy. Despite his constant failures, he remains a shameless moocher who can talk his way into staying with the Simpsons far longer than welcome. He's had a rocky romantic history, including multiple marriages and a memorably awkward stint dating and briefly wooing Elizabeth Hoover. Gil's health is as troubled as his career, plagued by ailments like bronchitis and a bad back, and he's even attempted suicide more than once, always surviving through dark comic circumstance. He's explicitly modeled after Jack Lemmon's desperate salesman character from Glengarry Glen Ross, embodying that same blend of pathetic charm and relentless hard luck. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: C'mon, help ol' Gil out here! | Those Cornell men at the head office are going to be doing the Saluki Strut tonight! | Welcome to the big league, Marge. There's over fifty years of experience right in this room! And forty-two of those years are Gil's!
quotes: C'mon, help ol' Gil out here!
Those Cornell men at the head office are going to be doing the Saluki Strut tonight!
Welcome to the big league, Marge. There's over fifty years of experience right in this room! And forty-two of those years are Gil's!

title: Hyman Krustofsky
text: Hyman Krustofsky is Rabbi and estranged father of Krusty the Clown; recurring figure in the Krustofsky family storyline. Hyman Krustofsky was a devout and strict rabbi in Springfield's Lower East Side who valued religious tradition above all else. His rigid expectations led him to disown his son Herschel after discovering he'd become a clown instead of following in his religious footsteps, creating a rift that lasted for years. He is portrayed as stubborn and hard to please, only reluctantly reconciling with Krusty after children intervened on his behalf, and he continued to hold his son to impossibly high standards even afterward. Despite his harshness, he showed moments of tenderness, such as playfully joining in on Krusty's comedy antics after their reunion. After his death, he continued to haunt Krusty's memory and conscience, appearing as an imagined voice, a ghost, and even a recorded message reminding his son of his perceived shortcomings. His disapproval became a recurring running gag representing Krusty's unresolved guilt and insecurity about pursuing his passion. Voiced by Jackie Mason, Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: You're still a disappointment | That was far enough
quotes: You're still a disappointment
That was far enough

title: Sadie Krustofsky
text: Sadie Krustofsky is Krusty the Clown's aunt and host of the TV show 'The Problem Is You'. Sadie Krustofsky was a blunt, no-nonsense older woman who wasn't afraid to call out bad behavior, especially her nephew Krusty's neglect of his own show's crew. Her sharp catchphrase-like insult became the spark for a whole reality TV career, turning her into a host who barged into families' lives to diagnose their dysfunction. She had a habit of oversimplifying complex family drama into a single culprit, which sometimes caused more conflict than it resolved, as seen when she blamed Marge for the Bouvier siblings' issues. Despite her confident, take-charge persona, she was ultimately undone by the very show she built her fame on, dying in a freak accident during a live reunion taping. Even after her death, she was remembered fondly enough to appear as an honored figure in a fantasy 'heaven' sequence for fighter pilots. Voiced by Susie Essman. Notable quotes: the problem is you. | Sadie declared that the problem was Marge, as she kept Homer and Patty and Selma apart rather than letting them work through their issues.
quotes: the problem is you.
Sadie declared that the problem was Marge, as she kept Homer and Patty and Selma apart rather than letting them work through their issues.

title: Hulk
text: Hulk is Marvel superhero (Bruce Banner) who appears as a comic-book/pop-culture reference and occasional costume/crossover character in the Simpsons universe. The Hulk is a green, super-strong alter ego of Bruce Banner who exists primarily as a piece of pop-culture lore that Springfield residents reference, dress up as, or collect merchandise of. He's often invoked as a comparison point, such as when a paint-covered, rampaging Homer is mistaken for him. Comic Book Guy is especially obsessed with Hulk memorabilia, from action figures and bookends to novelty hand and foot props, and even quotes Banner's famous anger line. Several characters, including Ralph Wiggum, Martin Prince, and Lenny Leonard, don Hulk costumes for various occasions like Halloween or superhero-themed adventures, sometimes even transforming into an actual raging Hulk when provoked. The character underscores the show's frequent parody of Marvel superhero culture, appearing more as a cultural touchstone than a fully developed character in his own right. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright, Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "I don't like me when I'm angry" — Comic Book Guy (paraphrasing Bruce Banner)
quotes: "I don't like me when I'm angry" — Comic Book Guy (paraphrasing Bruce Banner)

title: Joe Quimby, Sr.
text: Joe Quimby, Sr. is Deceased father of Mayor Joe Quimby and patriarch of the Quimby family. Joe Quimby, Sr. was an Irish immigrant born Joseph O'Shaughnessy who fled to Springfield after stealing a turnip from his own family's dinner. Despite facing prejudice for being Irish, he clawed his way to wealth and power by murdering a barrelworks owner and forging a will in his own favor, later founding a movie studio. Driven by political ambition he was denied due to his heritage, he pushed his son relentlessly into a political career, even encouraging him to keep mistresses to preserve a public image. Ruthless and image-obsessed, he was devastated when his son publicly abandoned that carefully built persona, suffering a fatal heart attack. On his deathbed he bitterly called his son a failure, pinning his last hopes on his grandson instead. Non-canon material paints him as an even shadier figure, running a bootlegging empire and fathering children outside his marriage before mysteriously vanishing, only to be found dead years later. Voiced by Brendan Gleeson, Domhnall Gleeson.

title: Martha Quimby
text: Martha Quimby is Wife of Mayor Joe Quimby and First Lady of Springfield. Martha Quimby is the dutiful, if weary, spouse of Springfield's philandering mayor. She's fully aware that her husband cheats on her but chooses to stay married to him largely for the status and perks of being the mayor's wife. Publicly she maintains a composed, dignified appearance, often dressed in a pink suit and pillbox hat reminiscent of Jacqueline Kennedy, and dutifully attends civic events like the Easter celebration at the mansion. Beneath that polished exterior, however, she occasionally lets her hurt and frustration show, such as breaking down in tears upon discovering her husband's secret bar/strip room. She socializes with the other wives and mothers of Springfield's prominent men, including Helen Lovejoy and Bernice Hibbert, fitting in as one of the more sane, low-key figures among them. Overall, she represents the archetype of the quiet, long-suffering housewife married to a corrupt or unfaithful husband. Voiced by Maggie Roswell, Tress MacNeille.

title: Jessica Lovejoy
text: Jessica Lovejoy is Daughter of Reverend and Helen Lovejoy; one of Bart Simpson's girlfriends. Jessica Lovejoy is a deceptively angelic-looking girl who hides a manipulative, troublemaking streak beneath her sweet exterior. She once dated Bart Simpson, and during their time together she proved to be even more reckless and devious than he was, egging him into dangerous stunts and pranks. Her rebellious behavior, including theft and vandalism, seems to stem from a deep desire to get attention from her emotionally distant father. She's intelligent but underachieving, uses her charm to manipulate boys, and has a habit of letting others take the blame for her misdeeds. Despite her troublemaking nature, she shares Bart's love of skateboarding and Krusty the Clown, and has popped up occasionally in later episodes and other media. Unlike his other exes, Bart notably never tried to win her back, though he kept a photo of their time together. Voiced by Meryl Streep. Notable quotes: Remember I'm the sweet, perfect minister's daughter and you're just yellow trash.
quotes: Remember I'm the sweet, perfect minister's daughter and you're just yellow trash.

title: Herman Hermann
text: Herman Hermann is One-armed owner of Herman's Military Antiques and recurring Springfield criminal/con artist. Herman is a one-armed military surplus dealer who dresses perpetually in fatigues and gives a different, often contradictory story about how he lost his arm each time he's asked. Despite being considered a bit unhinged by both Bart and Grampa Simpson, he's a shrewd tactical mind, once helping Bart win a water balloon war against Nelson. His moral compass is questionable at best, as he's dabbled in counterfeit jeans sales, hostage-taking, and even stood trial for a gruesome murder. He keeps odd company, from his mysterious friend Zed to membership in the Stonecutters and other secret Springfield societies, while also being a poker buddy of Homer's. His secret hobbies, like collecting Nazi underwear and taking rubber-ducky bubble baths, hint at a stranger side beneath the tough military exterior. Herman remains one of Springfield's shadier recurring background figures, popping up across decades of the show's run. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: The key to Springfield has always been Elm Street. The Greeks knew it. The Carthaginians knew it. Now you know it.
quotes: The key to Springfield has always been Elm Street. The Greeks knew it. The Carthaginians knew it. Now you know it.

title: Bill Clinton
text: Bill Clinton is Real-world U.S. President who appears as a recurring guest character interacting with the Simpson family. Bill Clinton appears in the show as a caricature of the real 42nd President, often popping up in odd, low-stakes situations involving the Simpsons. He's portrayed as good-natured but self-deprecating, willing to admit his own shortcomings, such as when he cheerfully agrees he's "a pretty lousy president" after overturning a school band contest for Lisa. He's shown answering Homer's random phone calls and getting caught up in Springfield's civic chaos, including being imprisoned alongside the Simpsons during an authoritarian crackdown. His association with the Lewinsky scandal is referenced humorously when Bart identifies him only as "sex guy." In non-canon material, he's abducted by aliens Kang and Kodos during a presidential election, and later revealed to have hidden a stash of pornographic videos at Camp David. Over the show's run, multiple actors have voiced him, reflecting his status as a recurring but minor real-world figure in the Simpsons universe. Voiced by Harry Shearer, Phil Hartman, Karl Wiedergott, Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Thank you, Lisa, for teaching kids everywhere a valuable lesson: If things don't go your way, just keep complaining until your dreams come true. | That's a pretty lousy lesson | Hey, I'm a pretty lousy president.
quotes: Thank you, Lisa, for teaching kids everywhere a valuable lesson: If things don't go your way, just keep complaining until your dreams come true.
That's a pretty lousy lesson
Hey, I'm a pretty lousy president.

title: Snowball I
text: Snowball I is Lisa Simpson's first pet cat, and the Simpson family's original pet before Snowball II and Santa's Little Helper. Snowball I was a white cat who belonged to Lisa and served as the Simpson family's very first pet. As a non-speaking character, his personality came through in small domestic moments, like unhappily fanning a block of ice with his tail during a heatwave before the family got an air conditioner. His death by being run over by a car became a recurring point of sentimental and dark humor throughout the series, referenced in Christmas letters, Lisa's poetry, and even a mournful song called 'My Kitty Died.' Despite a Sunday school teacher's claim that cats can't go to Heaven, Snowball is shown residing there happily, occasionally glimpsed by characters during near-death experiences. He's buried in Springfield's Pet Cemetery, and the show has had recurring gags about his afterlife, including him supposedly voting in a mayoral election. Non-canon material has expanded on his legacy in stranger ways, including a failed zombie resurrection attempt and his skeleton turning up inside a couch cushion. Many official Simpsons books have humorously dedicated themselves to his memory, cementing him as a beloved background figure in the show's mythology despite never appearing as a living character on-screen for long.

title: Sebastian Cobb
text: Sebastian Cobb is Scientist who built the ill-fated North Haverbrook monorail, later helps Marge and Homer with the Springfield monorail. Sebastian Cobb is the engineer originally commissioned by con man Lyle Lanley to construct North Haverbrook's monorail, a project undermined by Lanley's use of cheap materials. After the North Haverbrook monorail's disastrous debut ruined the town, Cobb lives on amid its ruins, willing to share the truth with anyone who asks, unlike the tight-lipped townsfolk. He proves crucial when Marge Simpson comes seeking answers, rushing back with her to Springfield to prevent history from repeating itself. His vanity gets the better of him, though, when a haircut delays their return just long enough for disaster to strike again. Despite this, his quick thinking over the radio saves the day, guiding Homer through an improvised fix to stop the runaway train. He resurfaces briefly during a Springfield mob scene and later meets a possibly fatal end when a revived monorail crushes him, leaving his fate ambiguous. His stern, foreign-tinged demeanor and passing resemblance to Dr. Strangelove add a distinct flavor to his brief but memorable appearances. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: You just better have a damn good conductor,
quotes: You just better have a damn good conductor,

title: Louie
text: Louie is A member of the Springfield Mafia, one of Fat Tony's henchmen. Louie is one of Fat Tony's loyal muscle men, usually paired with fellow enforcer Legs and occasionally Johnny Tightlips. He and Legs go way back with Fat Tony, having been the neighborhood's playground bullies together as kids. Eager to please his boss, Louie constantly looks for small ways to be useful, even down to offering ketchup packets, and he has no qualms about violence when ordered. Despite his tough exterior, he's plagued by anxiety about misinterpreting Fat Tony's cryptic instructions, worrying that a vague command to 'take care' of someone could just as easily apply to him. He's also shown to have quirky personal habits, like sneaking his own candy into movie theaters and owning a diva pop CD. His voice was modeled by Castellaneta after Joe Pesci's mobster performances, and the character later became the subject of a real-life lawsuit from actor Frank Sivero, who claimed Louie was based on his Goodfellas character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: You know how it is with us! Everything means 'kill!'.
quotes: You know how it is with us! Everything means 'kill!'.

title: Lionel Hutz
text: Lionel Hutz is Springfield's incompetent, ambulance-chasing lawyer frequently (and reluctantly) hired by the Simpson family. Lionel Hutz is a shady, perpetually broke attorney running his practice out of a shopping mall office called 'I Can't Believe It's a Law Firm!'. Despite claiming a law degree from a nonexistent Princeton law school (really acquired at a day-care garage sale), he is almost comically unqualified, relying on theatrical courtroom stunts, fake surprise witnesses, and outright bluffing rather than legal skill. He's also a barely-recovering alcoholic who name-drops his sponsor, keeps bourbon on hand, and jokes that the American Bar Association is a drinking club. Beyond law, he dabbles in real estate, acting, babysitting under fake aliases like Miguel Sanchez, and possibly even drug dealing. Despite his uselessness, he occasionally stumbles into wins for the Simpsons through luck or the family's own honesty rather than his legal prowess. He was briefly married to Selma Bouvier, and Marge openly distrusts him even while continuing to hire him. Following Phil Hartman's death, the character was retired from speaking roles, appearing only in archival clips and non-speaking cameos afterward. Voiced by Phil Hartman. Notable quotes: We really should stop hiring him. | brownest of the brown liquors | drug deal- errrrrr.... keeper awayer
quotes: We really should stop hiring him.
brownest of the brown liquors
drug deal- errrrrr.... keeper awayer

title: Loki (Marvel Comics)
text: Loki (Marvel Comics) is Marvel Comics crossover villain/god who appears in Simpsons specials, often bonding with and manipulating Bart. Loki is the mischievous, shape-shifting Asgardian god of trickery, adapted from Marvel Comics into the Simpsons universe. He's characterized by his cunning, dishonesty, and constant scheming, particularly his fondness for switching identities and impersonating others—especially Bart. Loki relates to Bart over their shared experience of having a distant father figure and a more favored sibling, which briefly earns him a place at the Simpson dinner table. Despite his god-like powers, he's frequently outwitted or humiliated, whether by Lisa wielding Thor's hammer, Ralph as the Hulk, or the bureaucratic Time Variance Authority. He's self-aware enough to break the fourth wall, acknowledging his status as a recurring crossover cameo tied to Disney's ownership of both franchises. Ultimately, Loki serves as a comedic, morally slippery outsider whose god-tier abilities are undercut by pettiness and bad luck. Voiced by Tom Hiddleston. Notable quotes: He then said his powers were no match for the accountants at Disney.
quotes: He then said his powers were no match for the accountants at Disney.

title: Cletus Spuckler
text: Cletus Spuckler is Recurring resident of Springfield; a stereotypical redneck farmer and family man, part of the extended Simpsons universe of townsfolk. Cletus Spuckler is the show's go-to caricature of a poor, uneducated hillbilly, living out on Rural Route 9 with his enormous, ever-multiplying brood of oddly named children. He's good-natured and easygoing, content with simple pleasures like whittling wooden 'piney babies,' scavenging roadkill, and running a moonshine operation, and he shows real affection for his mother 'Maw' and his animals. His relationship with wife (and possibly relative) Brandine is loving but chaotic, marked by jealousy, confusion over their actual family ties, and a never-ending stream of children of questionable parentage. Despite his low-brow habits and shaky grasp on modern technology, Cletus occasionally displays odd bursts of insight, such as predicting the future through his wood carvings. He and Brandine scrape together a living through dirt farming, moonshine, and a roadside vegetable stand, embodying the show's satire of both rural poverty and celebrity baby-naming trends. Introduced as a background yokel gawking at Bart's elephant, he grew into a beloved recurring joke machine used whenever the writers needed a quick laugh about backwoods life. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Oh my gosh, it's an outhouse sent from the future | Be quiet robo-potty! | I have sired a dumb-dumb, a mush-head, a whatsit, a dogboy, and something with a human face and fish body what we called Kevin. But my young'uns is not dirty players!
quotes: Oh my gosh, it's an outhouse sent from the future
Be quiet robo-potty!
