title: Sacagawea
text: Sacagawea is Native American guide from the Lewis and Clark expedition, portrayed as Lisa Simpson's historical counterpart in a non-canon segment. Sacagawea is depicted as a sharp, no-nonsense guide who quickly grows frustrated with the bumbling incompetence of Lewis and Clark during their expedition west. She's portrayed as the true brains of the operation, warning the group about dangers like poisonous berries and dangerous animals, though her advice is often ignored until it's too late. Her strained marriage to Toussaint Charbonneau is highlighted, including a darkly comic moment where she allows her brother to kill him. Despite her exasperation with the explorers' condescension, she ultimately softens when she sees they've actually learned from her teachings, sticking with them until they reach the Pacific. She's also referenced as a symbol of great historical women in Lisa's imagination, appearing on a wall of inspirational figures in her dream bedroom and as an element on Lisa's geeky periodic table. The character serves largely as a satirical, exasperated straight-woman figure poking fun at the incompetence of celebrated historical male explorers. Voiced by Yeardley Smith. Notable quotes: In our language, her name means "Little Know-It-All Who Won't Shut Her Maize Hole."
quotes: In our language, her name means "Little Know-It-All Who Won't Shut Her Maize Hole."

title: Beatrice Simmons
text: Beatrice Simmons is Grandpa Abraham Simpson's short-lived girlfriend at the Springfield Retirement Castle. Beatrice, nicknamed Bea, was an elderly resident of the Springfield Retirement Castle who struck up a whirlwind romance with Abraham Simpson after a medication mix-up brought them together. She was widowed, having once been married to a man named Charlie Simmons, and quietly dealt with health troubles including liver failure. Her storyline is tragic and darkly comic, as she dies of a literal broken heart after being stood up by Abraham on her birthday due to a family outing gone wrong. Even after death she remains a presence in Abraham's life, leaving him a sizable inheritance and later appearing as a ghost to offer him wisdom about mortality and reconciliation with his son Homer. Her legacy lives on through a memorial dining hall named after her at the retirement home, funded by Abraham using her money to help fellow seniors. Though her time on the show was brief, she left a lasting emotional mark on Abraham's character. Voiced by Audrey Meadows.

title: Sherri Mackleberry
text: Sherri Mackleberry is The elder of twin sisters (with Terri), classmate of Bart Simpson at Springfield Elementary School. Sherri is one half of an inseparable, mischievous twin duo who are both intelligent and unnervingly strange, even communicating in their own private language. Despite being clever, she and her sister channel their cunning into pranks and teasing rather than schoolwork, frequently targeting Bart, on whom she seems to have an unacknowledged reciprocal crush she'd rather deny. Her relationship with Lisa swings between rare moments of kindness and frequent scorn, hinting at a more personal rivalry than simple differences in personality. Though sometimes grouped with Springfield Elementary's popular clique, she and Terri are rarely treated as true equals to those girls, suggesting their social status is shakier than it appears. The twins are so close that separation frightens them, and they instinctively comfort each other by hugging when scared. Sherri is generally treated as the 'default' twin in the show's continuity, being the one named or favored when only one sister is referenced. Voiced by Russi Taylor (Season 1–30), Grey DeLisle (Season 31–present). Notable quotes: "Come play with us, Simpsons"
quotes: "Come play with us, Simpsons"

title: Gary (nerd)
text: Gary (nerd) is One of three college nerd friends Homer met at Springfield University. Gary is an African-American college student recognizable by his rectangular glasses, one of a trio of nerdy roommates who befriended Homer during his return to Springfield University. He and his friends get roped into Homer's schemes, from pranking a rival school to hacking grades, often suffering consequences like expulsion because of Homer's antics. Despite the trouble Homer causes them, Gary remains loyal, later helping build a rocket for Homer's model rocketry rivalry with Ned Flanders, which ends in disaster. He's also shown as a geek culture enthusiast, joining online discussions about the Radioactive Man movie casting. A minor running joke suggests he has ear troubles, referenced when he mentions spilling his ear medicine before a road trip. Visually, he's based on a caricature of animator Rich Moore, originally used with different skin tone in earlier background appearances. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Shary Bobbins
text: Shary Bobbins is A magical nanny hired by the Simpson family to help manage the household. Shary Bobbins is a magical, umbrella-flying nanny who arrives to help the Simpsons after Marge's stress causes her hair to fall out. She is warm, nurturing, and uses cheerful songs to motivate the family into better behavior, echoing classic movie-nanny charm. Despite her sunny disposition, she has a sterner side, threatening discipline when Bart misbehaves. Her defining arc shows that no matter how much good she does, the Simpsons inevitably relapse into their chaotic, lazy ways, eventually breaking her optimistic spirit to the point of drowning her sorrows with Barney. She's a clear parody of Mary Poppins, right down to her whimsical entrance and exit. Her story ends darkly and abruptly when she flies into a jet engine, though she reappears in later non-canon and dream sequences as a ghost or robot. Voiced by Maggie Roswell. Notable quotes: I'm an original creation, like Rickey Rouse and Monald Muck. Now, as your nanny, I'll do everything from telling stories to changing diapers.
quotes: I'm an original creation, like Rickey Rouse and Monald Muck. Now, as your nanny, I'll do everything from telling stories to changing diapers.

title: Eleanor Roosevelt
text: Eleanor Roosevelt is Real-life former First Lady of the United States, referenced and appearing in various Simpsons episodes as a historical figure and symbol of admirable womanhood. Eleanor Roosevelt exists in the Simpsons universe mainly as a historical touchstone rather than an active character, appearing as photos, posters, costumes, and imagined visions rather than through dialogue. She's frequently invoked as an ideal of intelligence and integrity, cited as inspiration for the empowering doll Lisa Lionheart and included among Lisa's pantheon of admired historical women in her dream house and bedroom fantasies. She has a knack for showing up in odd contexts, from being struck by a baseball hit by an elderly ex-player to having her image swapped in for a pinup girl by Mr. Burns during a WWII flashback. Chief Wiggum even dressed as her for a photo, adding a comedic touch to her legacy. Mr. Burns once cruelly joked about her kissing ability being as cold as bad weather, poking fun at her reputation. Despite her constant presence as a reference point, she never speaks on the show, existing purely as a symbol referenced by other characters.

title: Bumblebee Man
text: Bumblebee Man is Star of a Spanish-language slapstick sitcom on Channel Ocho, a recurring background character in Springfield's media landscape. Bumblebee Man, whose real name is said to be Pedro Chespirito, is a hapless TV comedian who dresses in a full bee costume for his low-budget slapstick show. He almost never removes the costume, even in private, and his clumsiness turns out to be genuine rather than a comedic act. His personal life is a mess—his parents died in a bizarre paintball accident, his own antics destroyed his house, and his wife eventually left him. He speaks in simple, deliberately mangled Spanish phrases and repeats a signature cry of distress as his catchphrase. Despite the show's fictional claims about his nationality shifting between Belgian, an unnamed immigrant, or even Norwegian in spin-off material, he's generally treated as a Hispanic television personality parodying a real-life Mexican comedy archetype. He briefly dated Edna Krabappel and became the subject of gossip when Bernice Hibbert took an unusual interest in his social media posts. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Ay, ay, ay!
quotes: Ay, ay, ay!

title: Evil House
text: Evil House is A haunted, malevolent house that the Simpson family briefly moved into, featured in the first "Treehouse of Horror" segment. This is a sprawling, suspiciously cheap house that Homer purchases without realizing—or caring—that it sits atop an ancient Indian burial ground. Once the family settles in, the house reveals itself to be sentient and hostile, manifesting through bleeding walls, flying objects, a dimensional vortex in the kitchen, and a chilling disembodied voice demanding they leave. It attempts to turn the family members against each other by whispering murderous suggestions to everyone except Marge. When confronted with the Simpsons' stubborn refusal to be scared off, the house ultimately gives up and self-destructs rather than continue living with them. Its design nods to horror classics, borrowing visual cues from Psycho and plot elements from The Amityville Horror and Poltergeist. Despite being a one-episode antagonist, it later got a spiritual successor in a similar-looking house owned by Great Uncle Boris. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "get out" | Marge told the house to get used to living with them.
quotes: "get out"
Marge told the house to get used to living with them.

title: Manacek
text: Manacek is A suave Polish-American freelance insurance investigator who investigated the theft of a painting from the Simpsons and other Springfield residents. Manacek is a smooth-talking, old-fashioned detective clearly modeled after 1970s TV sleuths, complete with an inflated sense of charm. He fancies himself irresistible to women and flirts relentlessly with nearly every female he encounters, brushing off rejection without missing a beat. His investigative method leans heavily on seduction, as he himself admits he solves tough cases best while wooing an attractive woman. Despite his overconfidence and chauvinism, he proves to be a sharp and persistent investigator, unraveling a complicated art theft involving forged paintings and multiple suspects. Beyond his central case, he pops up doing a bizarre range of activities around Springfield, from wrestling Cletus to attending a Sex Addicts Anonymous meeting, showing his role as a recurring oddball fixture in town life. He also has a habit of hitting on Marge specifically, only to be firmly rejected by her family. Voiced by Bill Hader. Notable quotes: Manacek told Marge that once he sent Homer to prison, she'd be kind of single. | He told Homer he knew he was innocent because Homer was too dumb to steal the painting.
quotes: Manacek told Marge that once he sent Homer to prison, she'd be kind of single.
He told Homer he knew he was innocent because Homer was too dumb to steal the painting.

title: Flanders the Devil
text: Flanders the Devil is Non-canon Treehouse of Horror version of the Devil, appearing in the form of Ned Flanders. This is a segment-specific incarnation of Satan who takes on Ned Flanders' friendly appearance to strike soul-selling bargains with unsuspecting Springfieldians, most famously Homer. He's outwardly polite and even folksy like the real Ned, but can snap into a monstrous, roaring true demonic form when angered or thwarted. He's legalistic and proud of his contracts, delights in ironic punishments in Hell, and is not above rigging a jury with history's worst villains to ensure a guilty verdict. Despite his menace, he's ultimately petty and can be outsmarted, losing his claim on Homer's soul through a legal technicality. The character recurs across multiple Treehouse of Horror installments and even ties into Ned's own occasional transformations into the Devil, including eventually replacing Satan as ruler of Hell in one non-canon story. He's a comedic blend of genuine cosmic evil and small-town neighborliness. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: It's always the one you least suspect! | You are NOT smarter than me! I'll see you in Hell yet! | Let that ill-gotten donut be forever on your head!
quotes: It's always the one you least suspect!
You are NOT smarter than me! I'll see you in Hell yet!
Let that ill-gotten donut be forever on your head!

title: Fred Kranepool
text: Fred Kranepool is Undercover persona created by Mr. Burns to spy on his Power Plant employees. Fred Kranepool is not a real person but an elaborate disguise Mr. Burns dons after discovering bathroom graffiti revealing how much his workers despise him. Wearing a high-tech suit with a voice modulator, he poses as an ordinary employee to learn the truth about his reputation. Fred quickly becomes genuine friends with Homer, Lenny, and Carl, and even experiences firsthand the cruelty of being chased by the hounds, which makes him sympathetic to the workers' plight. Through this friendship, Fred convinces Burns to make real improvements at the plant, temporarily transforming it into a happier workplace. The ruse falls apart when a jealous Smithers exposes Fred's true identity to Homer, leading to a falling out and a physical confrontation that destroys the suit. Despite being just a disguise, Fred is portrayed as representing the last remaining trace of goodness inside Mr. Burns. Voiced by David Harbour. Notable quotes: Fred told Burns that he was the last spark of goodness in Burns and couldn't be extinguished.
quotes: Fred told Burns that he was the last spark of goodness in Burns and couldn't be extinguished.

title: Adolf Hitler
text: Adolf Hitler is Real-world historical figure (Nazi dictator) referenced and parodied throughout the show. This version of Hitler is less a character than a running historical punching bag, popping up in flashbacks, fictional cartoons-within-the-show, and countless throwaway jokes. He's depicted as short-tempered, prone to fits of rage over minor annoyances like losing a race to Jesse Owens or missing a phone call from Bart. Several gags tie him to Mr. Burns' backstory, including a mix-up over Burns' beloved teddy bear Bobo. He's also a favorite target of the Itchy & Scratchy cartoons, repeatedly getting beaten up or humiliated in animated shorts within the show. Beyond his 'canonical' appearances, his name is constantly invoked as shorthand for evil, whether in insults, historical asides, or absurd comparisons. The show never portrays him as anything but a universally reviled cartoon villain used for quick historical or comedic effect. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Well, one in two million people has what we call the evil gene. Hitler had it. | Before I was a Nazi leader, I was a Nazi reader. | That was Hitler's car. What did he ever do to you?
quotes: Well, one in two million people has what we call the evil gene. Hitler had it.
Before I was a Nazi leader, I was a Nazi reader.
That was Hitler's car. What did he ever do to you?

title: Birch Barlow
text: Birch Barlow is Right-wing talk radio host on Springfield's KBBL station, later also a Fox News personality. Birch Barlow is a bombastic conservative radio and television personality who thrives on stirring up controversy to boost his ratings. He proudly boasts of his own outsized political importance, likening himself to a branch of government and even a whole state. Barlow has authored a bestselling book and appears on Fox News, cementing his status as a media provocateur. He's clearly modeled after real-world blowhard pundits, with his name nodding to a famous conservative political society. Beyond his radio work, he's been spotted at odd Springfield events like a giant human pyramid attempt and even among the customers at one of Marge's makeshift drug sales. His public persona is one of relentless self-righteous outrage, always looking to rally listeners against perceived liberal threats. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: the fourth branch of government | the fifty-first state
quotes: the fourth branch of government
the fifty-first state

title: Jesus Christ
text: Jesus Christ is The son of God who occasionally appears in visions, dreams, and background imagery throughout the show. Jesus Christ is depicted in the Simpsons universe as a divine figure, the son of God and cousin of John the Baptist, who rarely appears in person but is frequently referenced through pictures, statues, and religious commentary. When he does appear, he's often shown as somewhat weary or emotionally scarred by humanity's treatment of him, as seen when God reveals he's never been the same since visiting Earth. He sometimes shows up in surreal dream sequences or hallucinations, offering cryptic encouragement or judgment to characters like Bart and Homer. His image is a recurring visual gag, appearing as everything from a church statue to a bizarre 'Kool-Aid Jesus' museum piece. Despite his divine status, he's portrayed with a very human vulnerability, capable of grief, exasperation, and even physical retaliation (as in Bart's dream where he swats Bart with a sign). The character serves largely as a symbol for religious commentary and satire rather than a fully developed personality. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Nancy Cartwright, Dan Castellaneta.

title: Benjamin Franklin
text: Benjamin Franklin is Historical Founding Father and inventor who appears in dreams, fantasies, and hallucinations throughout the show. Benjamin Franklin pops up across the show not as a real character but as a recurring historical figure filtered through the Simpsons' imaginations and dreams. He's often portrayed with comic exaggeration, whether triumphantly battling a kite-eating tree in Bart's book report or facing off against Babe Ruth's ego at an animatronic display. His famous kite-and-key experiment and money-related legacy (via the hundred dollar bill) are frequently referenced as running gags. In one absurd twist, he's reimagined as a secret treasure-hunter who used the Treaty of Paris negotiations as a cover for stealing gold, aided by specially bred greyhounds. He also appears as a whimsical afterlife figure, playing air hockey with Jimi Hendrix in Heaven. Overall, Franklin serves as a flexible pop-culture icon the show uses for historical parody and absurdist humor rather than as a grounded character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Harry Shearer, Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Kite-eating tree, I'll see you in hell!!! | Early to bed, early to rise- | Bargain Basement Ben Franklin.
quotes: Kite-eating tree, I'll see you in hell!!!
Early to bed, early to rise-
Bargain Basement Ben Franklin.

title: Bernice Hibbert
text: Bernice Hibbert is Wife of Dr. Julius Hibbert and minor resident of Springfield. Bernice Hibbert is the housewife married to the town's affable physician, Dr. Julius Hibbert. She's a recovering alcoholic, a trait played for laughs, such as when she fainted alongside the other town drunks upon hearing about prohibition. Bernice tends to stay in the background of Springfield's social scene, popping up mostly as a background character at town gatherings and events. A running gag involving her social media habits once got her called out by Lenny for suspiciously liking Bumblebee Man's posts. Non-canon material hints she once had a past romance with Carl Carlson before marrying Julius. She's originally a Dupree by birth, making her the sister of Chester Dupree, and she and Julius have several children together. Voiced by Tress MacNeille, Dawnn Lewis.

title: Annette (therapist)
text: Annette (therapist) is A recurring therapist who treats various Simpsons characters, including Lisa, Homer, and Ralph, across different jobs and settings. Annette is a hardworking therapist who has held several different jobs over the years, from working at Springfield Community College to a therapy app called Nutz to the Children's Therapy Center and even a marriage counseling barn. She's generally warm and eager to help her patients, using creative methods like art therapy and go-kart racing to help Lisa work through her anxieties. Her career hit a rough patch after giving birth, when sleep deprivation turned her uncharacteristically snappish and unprofessional, even scaring off young Lisa during a session. She quickly bounced back to her kind and competent self once she recovered from new-parent exhaustion. Annette also seems to get little respect from her employers, having been fired from the therapy app for helping a client too efficiently. Despite the chaos of the families she treats, she remains a mostly steady, sympathetic presence in the lives of the Simpsons and their neighbors. Voiced by Rachel Bloom.

title: Santa's Little Helper
text: Santa's Little Helper is The Simpson family's pet greyhound dog. Santa's Little Helper is the Simpson family's loyal greyhound, originally a failed racing dog abandoned by his owner before Homer and Bart brought him home one Christmas. Despite rarely barking, he's portrayed as unusually intelligent for a dog, occasionally seeming to understand English and even performing improbable tricks like balancing a beer can or changing a diaper. He's prone to typical mischievous pet behavior, chewing furniture and digging holes, but has also shown surprising bravery, serving stints as a police dog and rescuing family members from danger. His history includes surviving a life-threatening stomach ailment, broken legs, temporary abandonment in favor of a 'better' dog named Laddie, and various adventures that test his bond with the Simpsons, especially Bart. He has fathered multiple litters of puppies and has a brother he was separated from as a puppy. Though mostly a background comic presence, he's a beloved fixture of the household whose loyalty ultimately always brings him back to the family. Voiced by Frank Welker, Dan Castellaneta, Hank Azaria.

title: Jonathan Frink
text: Jonathan Frink is Springfield's local mad scientist and college professor at Springfield University; a recurring figure who interacts with the Simpson family, especially Lisa. Professor Frink is Springfield's resident scientific genius, boasting an IQ of 197 and membership in Springfield Mensa, yet he's comically awkward in social situations. He speaks in bursts of nonsensical exclamations like 'Glaven!' when excited, a quirky vocal tic reminiscent of Jerry Lewis's comedic style, which the character was intentionally modeled after. Despite his brilliance, many of his inventions are wildly impractical or dangerous, ranging from hamburger earmuffs to a house that sprouts legs and catches fire. His personal life is a mess of failed relationships and a distant, complicated family history, including a strained bond with his own overbearing father. He maintains a special rapport with Lisa Simpson due to her shared passion for science, making him one of her most frequent adult allies outside her family. Over the years he's dabbled in inventions both benign and disastrous, briefly becoming Springfield's richest man through a cryptocurrency he created himself. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Glaven! | With the (random object) and the (other random object) and the hey hey hey | Well, we're up to fifteen!
quotes: Glaven!
With the (random object) and the (other random object) and the hey hey hey
Well, we're up to fifteen!

title: Gypsy
text: Gypsy is Non-canon fortuneteller from Ethnictown who appears in a Treehouse of Horror segment. The Gypsy runs a stereotypical fortunetelling shop in Ethnictown, complete with beaded curtains, a crystal ball, and Tarot cards. She's suspicious and street-smart, wary of cops and quick to sense trouble, which proves accurate when she distrusts Homer on sight. After Homer accidentally destroys her shop while fleeing in a panic, she retaliates by cursing him and his loved ones with grotesque misfortunes. Despite her vindictive side, she shows a hint of fairness, offering to lift the curse if Homer simply apologizes. Her story takes a comedic turn when a captured Leprechaun meant to break her curse instead falls in love with her, leading to their public wedding officiated by Yoda. The whole segment leans into exaggerated ethnic stereotypes and slapstick horror-comedy typical of the Treehouse of Horror episodes. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: You gotta tell me if you are. | You will bring bad luck to everyone you love! | She's not the boss of me.
quotes: You gotta tell me if you are.
You will bring bad luck to everyone you love!
She's not the boss of me.

title: Prince
text: Prince is Real-world musician who appears in cameo/non-canon roles within the Simpsons universe, notably as one of the online 'geeks' pestering Comic Book Guy for spoilers.. Prince exists in the Simpsons universe as a stylized version of the real-life musician, appearing mostly as a background or referenced figure rather than a fully developed character. He's depicted as a tech-savvy fan eagerly awaiting details about the Radioactive Man movie, tying him into the show's satire of obsessive comic and movie fandom. His famous real-world name change to the unpronounceable 'Love Symbol' becomes a running gag, referenced both through Homer's storytelling and through joke-naming of background characters like greyhound puppies. In non-canon Halloween specials, he's treated as fodder for dark comedic bits, appearing as a murder victim and as part of a macabre spelled-out title gag. He was also almost cast to voice a character in a planned sequel episode, but the deal fell through over script disagreements. Overall, Prince functions less as a personality-driven character and more as a pop-culture reference point and running joke tied to his real-life fame and quirks.

title: Miss Springfield
text: Miss Springfield is A recurring minor character in Springfield who serves as Mayor Quimby's longtime mistress and pageant-winning arm candy at town events.. Miss Springfield is best known as the secret (and not-so-secret) lover of Mayor Quimby, frequently caught with him in compromising situations despite his marriage to Martha. She's portrayed as sweet but not particularly bright, most notably revealed to be illiterate and unable to properly use a typewriter's space bar. Her relationship with Quimby is played for comedy, oscillating between passionate affair and public humiliation whenever her secret is exposed. Over time she's shown becoming a more visible fixture at Springfield functions, escorting the mayor to civic events rather than hiding their relationship. She has social ties to other town celebrities like Rainier Wolfcastle, Duffman, and Cookie Kwan, suggesting she's embedded in Springfield's minor celebrity circle. Her voice is a deliberate homage to Lina Lamont from Singin' in the Rain, giving her a breathy, dim-witted comedic delivery befitting her running gag as the mayor's not-too-clever companion. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Gareth Prince
text: Gareth Prince is Martin Prince's father, husband of Gloria Prince, and a minor recurring Springfield resident. Gareth Prince is the mild-mannered stock broker father of Martin Prince, who works in Springfield's financial world. He shares his son's nerdy demeanor, even speaking with a slight lisp reminiscent of Martin's own mannerisms. His most notable appearance came during a 'Bring Your Child to Work Day' outing, which ended disastrously when Martin's brief stock trading success evaporated almost entirely. He also joined the other Springfield fathers in a search party riding in Ned Flanders' RV to retrieve their sons from Shelbyville. For years his first name was never spoken on screen, with a script once referring to him only as 'Martin Prince, Sr.'—until the name Gareth was finally confirmed in a much later episode. Overall, he remains a background family figure rather than a prominent character in his own right. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Chris Edgerly, Hank Azaria.

title: Duffman
text: Duffman is Mascot and spokesman for Duff Beer, recurring character in Springfield. Duffman is the bombastic corporate face of Duff Beer, always clad in a skintight costume, cape, and a belt lined with beer cans. He's known for speaking about himself in the third person with theatrical pauses, punctuating every appearance with pelvic thrusts and his trademark exclamation. Despite being essentially a corporate puppet, the character is revealed to actually be portrayed by a rotating cast of different men, a running joke that lets the show kill off 'Duffman' repeatedly without consequence. Beneath the loud persona lies a surprisingly complicated personal life, including a daughter, an ex-wife, step-children, and various romantic entanglements with men and women alike. Some incarnations show flashes of conscience, occasionally clashing with Duff Beer's corporate interests. The role has become something of a Springfield institution, blending absurd bravado with surprisingly emotional or vulnerable moments. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Oh, yeah! | Duffman can never die! (Pause) Only the actors who play him! | New feelings brewing in Duffman! What would Jesus do?
quotes: Oh, yeah!
Duffman can never die! (Pause) Only the actors who play him!

title: Itchy
text: Itchy is Cartoon mouse star of the ultra-violent show-within-a-show "The Itchy & Scratchy Show," watched by Bart and Lisa Simpson. Itchy is the gleefully murderous mouse half of a classic cat-and-mouse cartoon duo, forever tormenting his co-star Scratchy with cartoonish, over-the-top violence. Unlike traditional trickster mice, Itchy isn't merely mischievous—he's portrayed as an outright sadistic psychopath who takes genuine pleasure in inflicting brutal harm. He almost always wins his conflicts with Scratchy, usually ending in the cat's gruesome demise, making their dynamic a dark parody of classic animated rivalries like Tom and Jerry. Itchy's in-universe history stretches back to early 20th-century animation, giving him a long, storied fictional legacy within the show's meta-narrative. He's rarely shown with family, though he was eventually given a son in one short. As a satire of sanitized children's cartoons, Itchy represents The Simpsons' commentary on media violence and its effects on young viewers like Bart and Lisa. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Oh Me, oh My!
quotes: Oh Me, oh My!

title: Sarah Wiggum
text: Sarah Wiggum is Wife of Police Chief Clancy Wiggum and mother of Ralph Wiggum; a recurring Springfield townsperson. Sarah Wiggum is a gentle, mild-mannered housewife who mostly appears in the background of Springfield's crowds and charity events organized by Marge. She's the devoted spouse of the bumbling police chief Clancy Wiggum and the mother of the oddball Ralph Wiggum, whose eccentric personality she may have unintentionally shaped by listening only to Mozart and Churchill speeches during pregnancy. Her backstory reveals a surprisingly colorful past as a jewel thief who fell for Clancy while trying to distract him during a heist, only to be betrayed by her criminal partner Lindsey Naegle. Clancy affectionately calls her by the pet name "Poppin Fresh," a nod to the Pillsbury Doughboy, highlighting the softer, comedic side of their marriage. In a non-canon spin-off scenario, their marriage falls apart, with Clancy gaining custody of Ralph and relocating to New Orleans. Overall, Sarah serves as a quiet, sweet-natured fixture of the show's ensemble rather than a driver of major plotlines. Voiced by Pamela Hayden (also Megan Mullally in "Uncut Femmes").

title: Fallout Boy
text: Fallout Boy is Fictional comic-book sidekick to Radioactive Man, a superhero franchise within the Simpsons universe. Fallout Boy is the plucky junior partner to the nuclear-powered hero Radioactive Man, gaining his own modest powers of flight and eye lasers after a freak accident links him to his mentor. In his comic-book origin he's really Rod Runtledge, an ordinary bookish teen who is thrust into superheroics almost by chance. Over the years he battles a rotating cast of costumed villains, endures kidnappings, temporarily loses and regains his powers, and even goes undercover with a gang to shed his sidekick image. He's loyal enough to mourn deeply when Radioactive Man appears to die, and resourceful enough to help save the day when his mentor turns evil. Within the show's real world, the role of Fallout Boy becomes a running joke thanks to Milhouse Van Houten being cast (and cracking under pressure) in a Radioactive Man movie. He's also noted as the inspiration for the real-world rock band's name, a fun meta nod included in the article. His exuberant catchphrase captures his earnest, boyish enthusiasm for heroics. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Pamela Hayden. Notable quotes: Jiminy jillickers!
quotes: Jiminy jillickers!

title: Bode Wright
text: Bode Wright is A charismatic youth minister who briefly replaces Reverend Lovejoy as Springfield's church leader. Bode Wright is an easygoing, progressive reverend who arrives in Springfield from Michigan after a scandal involving burning a Bible cost him his old job. Unlike the rigid, scripture-reciting Lovejoy, Bode preaches with humor, life lessons, and an inclusive message that everyone, regardless of religion, deserves a shot at heaven. His warmth and charisma quickly win over the congregation, sparking a bitter rivalry with the insecure Lovejoy and a doctrinal feud with Ned Flanders over who belongs in church. He bonds with Lisa over shared interests like jazz and science, and even becomes a drinking buddy confidant to Homer at Moe's Tavern. Despite reforming hardened sinners like Snake Jailbird and reviving the town's faith, his past catches up with him and he's ultimately driven out of Springfield. He's later reimagined in a non-canon fantasy sequence as an asylum inmate freed by chaotic allies. Voiced by Pete Holmes.

title: Mickey Rooney (character)
text: Mickey Rooney (character) is Real-life actor who appears as himself in a guest role, sent to persuade Milhouse to finish filming Radioactive Man. Mickey Rooney shows up in Springfield as a washed-up but still spirited former child star, hired by the movie studio to coax a burned-out Milhouse back onto the set of the Radioactive Man film. He tries heartfelt, old-Hollywood-style appeals, invoking loyalty to fans, foreign markets, and himself, but ultimately fails to change Milhouse's mind. Ever the trouper, he briefly attempts to take over the Fallout Boy role himself, complete with costume and catchphrase, before the production collapses for lack of funds. He then turns his charm into a scolding lecture aimed at the townspeople for bankrupting the film crew, revealing a flair for melodrama and self-importance. True to his restless show-business nature, he immediately drops the moment for another gig the second an opportunity arises. Beyond his main appearance, he's referenced in passing and shown in framed pictures elsewhere in the show, cementing his status as a recognizable but minor celebrity cameo. Voiced by Mickey Rooney (Himself). Notable quotes: Well, I hope you're all satisfied. You bankrupted a bunch of naive movie folks. | All right, I tried. | Fortunately, we have a perfectly good Fallout Boy right here.
quotes: Well, I hope you're all satisfied. You bankrupted a bunch of naive movie folks.
All right, I tried.

title: Sideshow Mel
text: Sideshow Mel is Krusty the Clown's current sideshow sidekick on the Krusty the Clown Show. Melvin Van Horne, better known as Sideshow Mel, took over as Krusty's sidekick after Sideshow Bob was sent to prison for framing Krusty. On camera he stays mute, wearing the traditional grass skirt and shark-tooth necklace and communicating only via a slide whistle, but off camera he speaks with an affected, grandiose Shakespearean accent. He's surprisingly cultured—an eloquent, poetic Cornell graduate and former award-winning actor—suggesting his real talents are wasted playing second banana to Krusty. His signature quirk is the bone permanently stuck in his curly green hair, which he claims lets him sense the weather. Mel's personal life is messy, including a troubled marriage to Barbara, an unnamed son, and various flings, plus quirks like lactose intolerance and possible recovering alcoholism. Despite his dignity, he's frequently the butt of Krusty's abuse and Springfield's general chaos. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Lisa, applause is an addiction, like heroin - or checking your e-mail.
quotes: Lisa, applause is an addiction, like heroin - or checking your e-mail.

title: Huckleberry Finn
text: Huckleberry Finn is Fictional 19th-century boy from Mark Twain's stories, appearing in a Simpsons tall tale and in Bart's daydream/play. Huckleberry Finn shows up in the Simpsons universe as a character from an in-episode retelling of Mark Twain's stories, narrated by a singing railroad hobo. Alongside his friend Tom Sawyer, he's depicted as a clever troublemaker who tricks other kids into doing chores and ends up fleeing an unwanted marriage by swapping himself for a pig. His adventures spiral into a life on the run, culminating in a darkly comic execution scene with Tom. In a separate appearance, he pops up in one of Bart's fantasy daydreams, acting as a laid-back voice of reason when historical figures intrude on the fantasy. He's also reimagined in a school play, with Milhouse taking on the role and battling an antagonist with a lightsaber. Overall, Huck functions as a recurring literary parody figure rather than a core cast member. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: "I dunno. It's your fantasy."
quotes: "I dunno. It's your fantasy."

title: Bear
text: Bear is Recurring wild animal seen throughout Springfield, often causing chaos for the Simpsons and other residents. Bears are a recurring presence in and around Springfield, usually emerging from the woods to disrupt daily life. They factor into Springfield's founding mythology through the legend of Jebediah Springfield supposedly fighting one off, though later evidence suggests the bear actually killed him. Bears have taken in Maggie as a surrogate family, mauled Bart, terrorized Ned Flanders, and even sparked the creation of the short-lived and costly Springfield Bear Patrol after a single bear sighting caused mass panic. Beyond real bears, the show also features fictional ones, including cartoon bears in Itchy & Scratchy, the fire-safety mascot Hosey the Bear, and Homer's dream alter-ego as Yogi Bear. Running gags include bears comically disrupting mundane situations, humans overreacting to their presence, and bears serving as unpredictable catalysts for Homer's misadventures. Overall, bears symbolize the chaotic, untamed edge of nature intruding on Springfield's suburban absurdity. Notable quotes: "There are no bad fathers in the wilderness." - Chalmers
quotes: "There are no bad fathers in the wilderness." - Chalmers

title: Bender Rodríguez
text: Bender Rodríguez is Crossover character from Futurama who appears in various non-canon Simpsons episodes and media. Bender is a wisecracking, hard-drinking robot from Futurama who repeatedly crosses over into the Simpsons universe in non-canon episodes and specials. He's portrayed as a comic anti-hero with a reputation for boozing, gambling, smoking, and general bad behavior, yet he shows surprising loyalty once he bonds with someone. In his biggest Simpsons appearance, he's sent back in time to eliminate Homer but instead becomes his drinking buddy at Moe's, ultimately refusing to kill his new friend even under pressure. He's shown to be resourceful and morally flexible, killing a losing racehorse in a fit of anger while babysitting Maggie, then generously splitting his gambling winnings with her. Bender's mechanical nature means he can simply power down for centuries when not needed, content to be refueled with beer. His name and personality nod to the character John Bender from The Breakfast Club, tying him thematically to Simpsons pop-culture references. Voiced by John DiMaggio. Notable quotes: All right! You guys are my new best friends. | You wish, loser! | Bite my shiny metal ass.

You wish, loser!
Bite my shiny metal ass.

title: Squeaky-Voiced Teen
text: Squeaky-Voiced Teen is Recurring minor character in Springfield, perpetually stuck working an endless string of dead-end teenage jobs. The Squeaky-Voiced Teen is a pimply, awkward adolescent whose voice constantly cracks between high and low registers, a running joke that defines his character. He seems doomed to bounce between an absurd number of minimum-wage jobs around Springfield, from Krusty Burger to a wax museum tour guide to a hardware store clerk, never holding one position for long. His real name is eventually revealed to be Andrew Teen, though various characters across the show mistakenly or jokingly call him by different names like Jeremy, Steve, or Mr. Freedman. Despite his meek voice and awkward demeanor, he has had a surprisingly active personal life, including a relationship with an older employee named Mom and a fling with Shauna. He briefly attempted suicide over the cancellation of Futurama, which comically backfired into a romantic encounter. He occasionally shows flashes of manliness, such as when he temporarily deepened his voice to prove a point to Lindsey Naegle. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Todd Flanders
text: Todd Flanders is Youngest son of Ned and Maude Flanders, and younger brother of Rod. Todd is the younger of the two Flanders boys, raised in a strictly religious and sheltered household by his father Ned. His extreme innocence makes him prone to overreacting whenever he encounters anything remotely inappropriate, whether it's mild profanity, loud yelling, or sugary contraband smuggled to him by Bart Simpson. Despite his gentle upbringing, these encounters occasionally cause him to snap and lash out with surprisingly harsh language, much to Bart's amusement. He's a talented musician who plays violin in the school band and is also skilled at miniature golf. Along with his brother Rod, he recites the moral rhymes Ned has taught them, reflecting his family's devout and old-fashioned values. His exact age relative to Rod has famously been depicted inconsistently across the show's history, becoming a long-running point of confusion among fans and even the show's own writers. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: Hell, no | I said I don't want any damn vegetables | Ow, my freaking ears!
quotes: Hell, no
I said I don't want any damn vegetables
Ow, my freaking ears!

title: The Beatles
text: The Beatles is Real-life British rock band who appear as themselves and are frequently referenced throughout the show's universe. The Beatles are depicted in the Simpsons universe much as they were in reality, a legendary rock group whose fame and influence ripple through Springfield's pop culture. They pop up in dream sequences, wax museum displays, and flashbacks, and are name-dropped constantly by characters ranging from Homer to Mr. Burns. Paul and Linda McCartney even befriend Apu, visiting his rooftop garden and offering Lisa encouragement when she becomes a vegetarian. Ned Flanders is shown to be an obsessive fan with a room full of memorabilia, while other characters reference their songs, breakup, and cultural legacy as running gags. Their popularity is treated as a kind of universal constant, invoked for jokes about fame, nostalgia, and even Springfield's own dubious claims to history. Notably, John Lennon has never appeared in the show, since the real Lennon died before the series began, while Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr have each voiced themselves in guest appearances.

title: Lindsey Naegle
text: Lindsey Naegle is Recurring Springfield businesswoman who seems to hold a different corporate job every time she appears. Lindsey Naegle is a slick, ever-shifting corporate executive who pops up in Springfield in an almost comical variety of professions, from network executive to financial planner to venture capitalist, so often that she just carries business cards reading "Does Everything." She embodies buzzword-driven upper management culture, constantly touting "synergy" no matter what field she's currently in. A defining trait is her blunt willingness to admit embarrassing or shocking truths about herself, such as being a registered sexual predator or unable to cry due to a botched face lift, without a hint of shame. She's also revealed to be an alcoholic who heads Springfield's Alcoholics Anonymous chapter, though she treats meetings as much as a networking opportunity as a support group. Fiercely childfree and something of a youth-hater, she once organized an anti-youth political movement to strip Springfield of child-friendly institutions. Her love life is a revolving door of Springfield men, having been linked to Ned Flanders, Moe Szyslak, Kent Brockman, Krusty the Clown, and several others. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: So we all know why we're here - to be sober .. and to network! | I'm a sexual predator.
quotes: So we all know why we're here - to be sober .. and to network!
I'm a sexual predator.

title: Doug (nerd)
text: Doug (nerd) is One of the three college nerds Homer Simpson befriended (and got expelled) at Springfield University. Doug is a heavyset, bespectacled college student known for his thick round glasses and ever-present cardigan, marking him as a stereotypical nerd. He and his roommates, Gary and Benjamin, become entangled in Homer's schemes after Homer talks them into pulling a prank on a rival school, which nearly costs them their education. Despite the trouble Homer causes them, the trio remains loyal, later helping him cheat on a exam and even building him a model rocket. Doug's nerdy enthusiasm extends beyond campus life, as he's shown participating in online fan discussions about a superhero movie production. He's remembered by fans largely for an offbeat comment about a 'magic xylophone,' which became something of a meme for calling out nerdy nitpicking. Overall, Doug serves as a background comedic figure representing academic geek culture within the show's universe. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Tabitha Vixx
text: Tabitha Vixx is Professional singer married to Springfield Isotopes baseball player Buck Mitchell, guest character in the Simpsons universe. Tabitha Vixx is a glamorous, provocative pop singer whose racy stage performances repeatedly cause friction in her marriage to baseball star Buck Mitchell. She turns a national anthem performance into a striptease-style number, embarrassing her husband and throwing off his game. When Homer and Marge step in as makeshift marriage counselors, Tabitha's flirtatious nature nearly derails things further after she comes on to Homer. Despite the chaos, she and Buck ultimately reconcile through a public gesture involving the Duff Blimp and a stadium attendance guessing game. Her defining trait is leaning heavily into her sex appeal both on stage and in personal interactions, prioritizing her singing career even when it clashes with her husband's wishes. Originally, the writers named her Fiona Vixx before changing it to avoid resemblance to musician Fiona Apple. Voiced by Mandy Moore.

title: Bartman
text: Bartman is Bart Simpson's superhero alter-ego, a parody of Batman. Bartman is the costumed persona Bart Simpson invents, complete with a mask, cape, and utility belt full of gadgets like grappling hooks and Bartarangs. He first dons the identity to sneak a discount at a comic book convention, only to find out the ploy doesn't actually work. The character became popular enough to spawn his own non-canon comic book series, in which he battles bullies and supervillains threatening Springfield. Beyond the comics, Bartman shows up as a playable form or costume in numerous Simpsons video games, granting Bart abilities like flight, gliding, laser vision, or slingshot attacks. The whole gimmick is a blatant homage to Batman, mirroring his name, gadgets, and general look. Despite being a joke identity born from a cheap convention scheme, Bartman has become one of Bart's most recurring and merchandised alter-egos. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: The Leader
text: The Leader is Mysterious cult leader of the Movementarians who briefly recruits the Simpson family in "The Joy of Sect". The Leader is the shadowy, rarely-seen figurehead of the Movementarian cult that sweeps through Springfield, promising followers a blissful new life on the fictional planet Blisstonia. He cultivates an air of mystique, appearing only briefly through the tinted window of his Rolls-Royce, never fully showing his face to the public. Behind the scenes, his supposed spiritual mission is really an elaborate con to bilk his followers of money, which he funnels into secretly building an escape vehicle hidden in the Forbidden Barn. When Homer breaks free of the cult's brainwashing and exposes the truth, The Leader's grand "flying saucer" is revealed to be nothing more than a bicycle rigged with bags of stolen cash. His scheme collapses in spectacular, humiliating fashion, crashing onto Cletus's farm. Clearly modeled after real-world cult leader L. Ron Hubbard (with a touch of Bhagwan Shree Rajneesh's Rolls-Royce obsession), he represents the show's satire of manipulative religious movements and gullible mass followings. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Herb Powell
text: Herb Powell is Homer Simpson's wealthy half-brother, illegitimate son of Abe Simpson, and former auto executive. Herb is the secret older half-brother of Homer, the result of a fling Abe Simpson had with a carnival worker decades earlier. Given up for adoption, he clawed his way through Harvard and built a successful car company, Powell Motors, before losing it all when he foolishly let Homer design a car. Despite his business savvy, he shares the family's poor judgment when it comes to trusting Homer's ideas. He's affectionate toward his newfound family, especially his niece Maggie, and prefers being called "Unky Herb" instead of uncle. After hitting rock bottom, he rebuilds his fortune by inventing a baby-language translator inspired by Maggie, and generously showers the Simpsons with gifts once he's rich again. Though he vanishes from the show for years afterward, later references suggest his fortunes fluctuate, and he measures wealth more in family and love than money. Voiced by Danny DeVito.

title: Ringo Starr (character)
text: Ringo Starr (character) is Real-life musician (drummer of The Beatles) who appears as a character in The Simpsons, notably tied to Marge's teenage crush and fan art. Ringo Starr appears as a fictionalized version of himself, best known for his connection to Marge's teenage art hobby and infatuation with him. He comes across as a good-natured celebrity who genuinely tries to respond to old fan mail, showing a thoughtful and humble side despite his fame. His belated reply to Marge's decades-old letter ends up rekindling her passion for painting at a crucial moment. Beyond this central story, he's referenced in passing as part of The Beatles' legacy, sometimes used as a punchline or comparison point for other characters like Sideshow Bob. He's also noted as an example of a "laudable lefty" and appears in flashbacks and dream sequences tied to Beatles lore in the show's universe. In a non-canon storyline, he even ends up married to Marge in Heaven. Voiced by Ringo Starr (himself); Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: P.S. Forgive the lateness of my reply. | we do have hamburgers and fries in England, but we call French fries 'chips'.
quotes: P.S. Forgive the lateness of my reply.
we do have hamburgers and fries in England, but we call French fries 'chips'.

title: Lunchlady Dora
text: Lunchlady Dora is Cafeteria chef (and part-time nurse) at Springfield Elementary School. Lunchlady Dora, formerly known as Lunchlady Doris, is the perpetually unenthusiastic cook who serves Springfield Elementary's students dubious meals made from questionable ingredients like beef hearts and even gym mats. Overweight, middle-aged, and famously laconic, she rarely shows much emotion or says much at all, embodying a jaded, worn-down attitude toward her thankless job. Due to budget cuts, she also serves as the school's nurse, further underscoring how underfunded and stretched-thin Springfield Elementary really is. Her personal life has included an on-and-off romance with Hans Moleman, a fling with Groundskeeper Willie that turned out to be a ploy to steal a key, and a mysterious past involving her possibly murdered ex-husband, Pete. After voice actress Doris Grau passed away, the character was retired for years before returning as a new, distinct character (implied to be Doris's sister) named Dora. She remains a recurring background fixture of the school staff, cementing her status as an ever-present, if underappreciated, cog in Springfield Elementary's machinery. Voiced by Doris Grau (1989-1997), Tress MacNeille (2006-present). Notable quotes: Whatever... —Lunchlady Dora
quotes: Whatever... —Lunchlady Dora

title: Frank Grimes
text: Frank Grimes is One-episode antagonist and self-declared enemy of Homer Simpson, a hardworking employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. Frank Grimes is a bitter, self-made man whose entire life has been a grinding struggle from an impoverished, loveless childhood to backbreaking work and night-school science studies. Hired at the power plant after Mr. Burns saw him profiled on a local news segment, Grimes is appalled to discover that Homer Simpson, a man he sees as lazy and incompetent, enjoys a life of comfort and unearned success. His resentment toward Homer curdles into obsession, especially after seeing the Simpsons' cozy home and hearing about Homer's absurd lucky breaks. Grimes is portrayed as a grounded, humorless stand-in for the audience, meant to expose how ridiculous and unfair Homer's charmed existence would seem to a real, hardworking person. His fixation on proving Homer a fraud ultimately drives him to a psychotic breakdown and his own accidental death by electrocution. Even after death, his legacy persists through his vengeful son, Frank Grimes Jr., who blames Homer for his father's demise. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: I'm saying you're what's wrong with America, Simpson. You coast through life, you do as little as possible, and you leech off of decent, hardworking people like me. | Heh, if you lived in any other country in the world, you'd have starved to death long ago. You're a fraud, a total fraud.
quotes: I'm saying you're what's wrong with America, Simpson. You coast through life, you do as little as possible, and you leech off of decent, hardworking people like me.
Heh, if you lived in any other country in the world, you'd have starved to death long ago. You're a fraud, a total fraud.

title: The Happy Little Elves
text: The Happy Little Elves is Fictional characters from a children's television show within the Simpsons universe, parodied as a merchandising-heavy kids' franchise. The Happy Little Elves are the cast of a saccharine, crudely animated children's show that exists within the Simpsons' world, living in the fictional Elf County. The group includes distinct members like the cane-carrying elder Moldy, buck-toothed Bubbles, the lone female elf Cheery, glasses-wearing Brainy, and the perpetually frowning Chilly, among others. Their franchise has spawned an absurd amount of merchandise, including lunchboxes, dolls, posters, and direct-to-video films, poking fun at real-world children's entertainment marketing. Bart Simpson despises the group, mockingly referring to them as "the crappy little elves." Interestingly, Lisa once points out that the self-loathing elf Gloomy bears a resemblance to Bart himself. The elves appear repeatedly throughout the show's run, often in the background as toys, pictures, or passing references rather than as active characters in the plot. Notable quotes: the crappy little elves
quotes: the crappy little elves

title: Stephen King (character)
text: Stephen King (character) is Real-world horror author who appears as himself in guest appearances on the show. Stephen King is depicted as a good-humored version of the famous horror novelist, popping up in Springfield at book signings and elsewhere. He often starts out sounding calm and normal but gradually slips into a dark, menacing tone whenever he starts describing something horrific, even mundane topics like a Benjamin Franklin biography. The show frequently references his real bibliography, turning titles like 'Under the Dome' and 'Misery' into running jokes and parodies within the Simpsons universe. He's shown as approachable enough for townsfolk like Lenny to bother him with fan fiction, though not always graciously received. In non-canon segments he's portrayed in more surreal or exaggerated ways, from cloning his 'Shining' typewriter scene to being chased by his own collected works. Overall he serves as a recurring celebrity cameo used for horror-genre gags and satire of his writing style. Voiced by Himself. Notable quotes: And that key he tied to a kite? It opened the gates of Hell! | Scary, good fun. | Thanks for many years of inspiration.
quotes: And that key he tied to a kite? It opened the gates of Hell!
Scary, good fun.
Thanks for many years of inspiration.

title: Bob Arnold
text: Bob Arnold is A corrupt former congressman for Springfield's state, first seen in "Mr. Lisa Goes to Washington". Bob Arnold is a smooth-talking politician who initially charms Lisa Simpson and the townsfolk with his warmth and political savvy. Beneath the friendly exterior, he's willing to accept bribes, agreeing to let a timber company clear-cut Springfield National Forest and later taking money to allow oil drilling on Mount Rushmore. His downfall comes when Lisa witnesses one of his bribery deals and exposes him in an essay, leading to his arrest and expulsion from Congress. Despite this scandal, he reappears in later episodes still involved in political proceedings, at one point trying to sneak funding for the "perverted arts" into an emergency evacuation bill. He's portrayed as something of a womanizer and a symbol of how easily politicians can manipulate public opinion through simple photo ops. After leaving office, he reportedly became a born-again Christian. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: let me put it this way: Timbeeeeerrrrrrr!! | Look, what a pooch
quotes: let me put it this way: Timbeeeeerrrrrrr!!

title: List of Showrunners
text:
The Simpsons has had a series of showrunners overseeing day-to-day production since its 1989 debut. Seasons 1-2 were run by the show's creators, James L. Brooks, Matt Groening, and Sam Simon. Al Jean and Mike Reiss took over for Seasons 3-4, then again briefly in Season 5 before David Mirkin led the show through Season 6 and into Season 7. Bill Oakley and Josh Weinstein ran Seasons 7-9, handing off to Mike Scully, who was showrunner through Season 12 and into Season 13. Al Jean then took over as primary showrunner partway through Season 13 and held that role continuously through Season 30, with Matt Selman periodically credited as co-showrunner starting around Season 23 and becoming his regular co-showrunner from Season 28 onward. During the 2021-2022 production stretch covering the back half of Season 33 into Season 34, Jean and Selman alternated as lead showrunner episode-by-episode, and Selman's episodes in that block additionally rotated through four co-showrunners: Rob LaZebnik, Carolyn Omine, Brian Kelley, and Tim Long. Starting in Season 34, Matt Selman became the primary showrunner, with additional co-showrunners credited on some episodes: Michael Price in Season 35 and Brian Kelley in Season 36. Season 37 (aired September 2025 - February 2026) was mostly showrun by Matt Selman; Al Jean showrunned at least the episode "Bad Boys... for Life?" (aired November 2, 2025) before stepping back from showrunning duties for the time being. No second showrunner name is documented for the remainder of Selman's Season 37 episodes.

Showrunner by season: S1-2: James L. Brooks, Matt Groening, Sam Simon. S3-4: Al Jean, Mike Reiss. S5: Al Jean/Mike Reiss, then David Mirkin. S6: David Mirkin. S7: David Mirkin, then Bill Oakley/Josh Weinstein. S8: Bill Oakley, Josh Weinstein. S9: Bill Oakley/Josh Weinstein, then Mike Scully. S10-12: Mike Scully. S13: Mike Scully, then Al Jean. S14-22: Al Jean. S23: Al Jean, with Matt Selman co-showrunner on some episodes. S24-27: Al Jean. S28: Al Jean, with Matt Selman co-showrunner on some episodes. S29: Matt Selman, Al Jean. S30: Al Jean. S31-32: Al Jean, with Matt Selman co-showrunner on some episodes. S33 (production season UABF): Al Jean and Matt Selman alternating, with Selman's episodes co-run by Rob LaZebnik, Carolyn Omine, Brian Kelley, or Tim Long depending on the episode. S34: Matt Selman primary (some early episodes still from the UABF production block above). S35: Matt Selman, with Michael Price co-showrunner on some episodes. S36: Matt Selman, with Brian Kelley co-showrunner on some episodes. S37: Matt Selman, with Al Jean showrunning at least one early episode before stepping back; no other co-showrunner name documented for this season.

title: Andre (Thank God It's Doomsday)
text: Andre (Thank God It's Doomsday) is An archangel who serves as a guide in Heaven, appearing in Homer's dream. Andre is a minor celestial character who works as an archangel concierge in Heaven. He appears in a dream sequence when Homer imagines himself in the afterlife, acting as a helpful and slightly quirky host. His guidance includes oddly specific suggestions, like recommending a nature walk and a pedicure, giving him a whimsical, customer-service personality despite his divine status. He also has a firm rule against using Leprechaun labor, hinting at some underlying bureaucratic or ethical structure in Heaven. Eventually, he escorts Homer to meet God himself, marking the peak of his role in the episode. Outside of the show, Andre also appears in a non-canon capacity within the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Jack Bauer
text: Jack Bauer is Crossover federal agent character from the TV series 24, who appears in special Simpsons episodes. Jack Bauer is a crossover character brought into The Simpsons universe from the real-world TV series 24, retaining his identity as an intense, no-nonsense CTU field agent. In his main appearance, he becomes obsessed with tracking down Bart Simpson after mistaking his prank call for a genuine threat, abandoning all other assignments and causing massive collateral damage in the process. This portrays him as comically overzealous, treating trivial situations with the same life-or-death urgency he'd apply to real terrorist threats. He's also used in a meta way, appearing to promote his own show '24' during a Treehouse of Horror special, only to be humorously shut down by Marge. Overall, Jack Bauer functions as a parody of his own dramatic, high-stakes television persona. Voiced by Kiefer Sutherland. Notable quotes: Bart Simpson, twelve minutes ago you made an annoying prank phone call to me. All units move in! I pulled every single field agent off all other cases to track you down and bring you to justice. It was a tough decision, but I think I made the right call.
quotes: Bart Simpson, twelve minutes ago you made an annoying prank phone call to me. All units move in! I pulled every single field agent off all other cases to track you down and bring you to justice. It was a tough decision, but I think I made the right call.

title: Russell Brand (character)
text: Russell Brand (character) is Real-life celebrity cameo appearance as himself in the Simpsons universe. Russell Brand appears as a fictionalized version of himself, the English comedian and actor, making a guest cameo in the Simpsons world. He is shown presenting the Golden Globe for best short film, only to have the podium hijacked by Homer before he can properly hand it over. During his brief moment in the spotlight, he reveals a bit of self-deprecating honesty about his past, joking that people he met in rehab weren't really his friends. Beyond this main appearance, he's treated as a minor pop-culture reference point, being name-dropped as one of Lisa's picks for cutest vegetarians on the family's food blog, and his picture decorates the walls of a bar called The Penny Loafer. His role is largely limited to celebrity cameo material rather than an integrated storyline character. Voiced by Russell Brand (Himself).

title: Becky (It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad Marge)
keys: becky (it's a mad, mad, mad, mad marge)
text: Becky (It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad Marge) is Otto's ex-fiancée who briefly became Marge's rival and helper in the Simpson household. Becky works the drive-thru at a German fast food joint in Springfield and becomes engaged to Otto, though she secretly can't stand heavy metal music. When her wedding plans fall through, she ends up staying with the Simpsons and proves to be a hardworking, likable houseguest who wins over Bart and Lisa. Despite her sweet demeanor, she has a darkly comic streak, twice contemplating murder but abandoning the idea purely due to trouble finding the right shovel. Her presence triggers Marge's paranoid jealousy, fueled by Patty and Selma, leading to a chaotic misunderstanding involving CPR mistaken for an affair. She's later seen among Springfield's angry mob in the Trappuccino incident, and ultimately reconciles with Otto. Her character is a comedic parody riff on a scheming nanny archetype from thriller films. Voiced by Parker Posey.

title: The Blue Man Group
text: The Blue Man Group is A recurring parody music/performance group referenced throughout the show, based on the real-life Blue Man Group. The Blue Man Group is a fictionalized version of the real avant-garde performance troupe, depicted as a band whose members paint their faces blue. They're mostly used as a punchline or offhand reference rather than an active presence in Springfield, popping up in drunken rants, morbid jokes about dead members, and even a barge of trash from Las Vegas. Homer has a running joke about claiming to be a secret member of the group, particularly the "fat guy." Chief Wiggum also darkly jokes about burying a blue-faced victim alongside deceased members of the group. The group is treated as a semi-real showbiz entity within the show's universe, existing mostly as pop-culture fodder for other characters' jokes. Notable quotes: Homer said that the Blue Man Group had total rip-off the Smurfs, and that the Smurfs suck. | Homer told his friends to tell Marge that he his the fat guy in The Blue Man Group. | Chief Wiggum said that she would be buried with the deceased members of The Blue Man Group.

Homer told his friends to tell Marge that he his the fat guy in The Blue Man Group.

title: Amphibian Man
text: Amphibian Man is A minor amphibian creature character, parodying a film monster, who appears briefly in the show. The Amphibian Man is a strange amphibious creature who exists as a parody of a well-known movie monster. He first appears hidden among the floorboards in a gag, oddly holding an Academy Award, hinting at his cinematic origins. In a non-canon Halloween segment, he ends up trapped in a tank alongside Kang, who mocks him as a freak before attempting to cook him. His storyline takes a darkly comedic turn when Selma interrupts to make out with Kang, leading the miserable Amphibian Man to beg to be killed instead of witnessing the moment. He has no dialogue-heavy role or deep characterization, functioning mostly as a one-off visual joke and horror-movie reference. His design and premise directly nod to the film he's based on rather than expanding into original Simpsons lore. Voiced by Chris Edgerly. Notable quotes: Kill me now, then. — Amphibian Man
quotes: Kill me now, then. — Amphibian Man

title: Busman
text: Busman is A fictional comic book superhero concept created by Otto Mann. Busman is not a real character within the show's universe, but rather a superhero concept dreamed up by Otto Mann. The idea combines the mundane with the fantastical: by day, Busman drives a city bus, and by night he transforms into a warrior who battles vampires in a desolate, post-apocalyptic wasteland. Otto pitches this concept at a comic book convention, hoping to impress a professional in the industry. The joke rests on the absurd contrast between Busman's ordinary day job and his over-the-top nocturnal heroics. Though his fate within the show remains ambiguous, the character found a life beyond the episode through a tie-in comic book published by Bongo Comics.

title: Wes Archer (character)
text: Wes Archer (character) is A real-world animator and director who appears as a recurring background cameo character in Springfield. Wes Archer is based on the real animator and director who worked on The Simpsons, appearing as a cameo character within the show itself. He's depicted popping up in various crowd scenes and background moments throughout Springfield's history, rather than having a distinct personality of his own. He attended rehearsals for the town's ill-fated musical production, delivered children's letters to Santa at the courthouse, and was among the unlucky citizens who tumbled off a malfunctioning escalator. He also showed up in a satirical campaign ad depicting escaped convicts. In a non-canon deleted scene, he's portrayed as the animator responsible for making Itchy and Scratchy's movements realistic by studying actual cats and mice.

title: The Burger King
text: The Burger King is Fictional mascot of the Burger King fast food chain, appearing in Homer's fantasies and dreams within the show. The Burger King is a fast-food mascot who exists mostly on the fringes of Homer's imagination rather than as a fully realized character. He first appears as a statue in Homer's daydream, imagined alongside other iconic fast food mascots atop a burger-themed version of Mount Rushmore. Later, he shows up in one of Homer's dreams, playfully sharing a see-saw with the Wendy's mascot. In non-canon material, he's portrayed more antagonistically, getting into a scuffle with Krusty over burger loyalty, and even turning out to be the true identity behind a masked king character in a Kang and Kodos scheme. He never speaks on screen, functioning purely as a visual gag and crossover figure representing corporate fast food culture.

title: Black Widow
text: Black Widow is Marvel superhero referenced in The Simpsons, appearing as a cardboard cutout and later as a costume worn by Agnes Skinner. Black Widow, whose real name is Natalia "Natasha" Romanova, is a Marvel superhero who makes only brief, non-speaking appearances in the Simpsons universe. She first shows up as a cardboard cutout of actress Scarlett Johansson in her Marvel Cinematic Universe costume, mentioned during Milo's song in "Married to the Blob." In a non-canon special, the character is referenced again when Agnes Skinner dresses up as Black Widow while participating in the Springfield Avengers. She has no powers listed and no dialogue, functioning purely as a pop-culture cameo tying the show to the broader Marvel franchise. Her presence highlights the show's frequent parody and homage to superhero media rather than serving any narrative role among the main cast.

title: Don Bookner
text: Don Bookner is Retired safety inspector at Springfield Nuclear Power Plant's Sector 7-G. Don Bookner is a minor character who worked as a safety inspector at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, quietly covering for Homer's mistakes for years without Homer ever realizing it. His retirement party serves as the catalyst for revealing just how much he had been compensating for Homer's incompetence on the job. Once he leaves, Homer is forced to handle his duties alone, exposing how reliant the plant had become on Bookner's diligence. He appears to be an unassuming, dutiful employee who worked behind the scenes rather than seeking recognition. Later, it's implied that Lenny and Carl manage to convince him to come out of retirement, suggesting he's not entirely resistant to persuasion despite his initial insistence that it was too late to stay. His return implies he resumes his role of covering for Homer's errors once again. Voiced by Stacy Keach.

title: Barry (Heartbreak Hotel)
text: Barry (Heartbreak Hotel) is Minor recurring character; husband of Grizzly Shawn and reality show contestant. Barry is a minor recurring character best known as the husband of Grizzly Shawn. The two competed as a team on the reality competition show The Amazing Place, ultimately triumphing in the final challenge to win the entire series. He later appeared as a guest at a tupperware party hosted by Julio, which Marge had arranged, where he and the other attendees mistakenly believed Marge was a drag queen. Barry is a non-speaking character, so his personality is conveyed mostly through his appearances rather than dialogue. His inclusion highlights Springfield's LGBT community, as he is noted as being in a same-sex marriage. Despite his limited screen time, he has appeared across several episodes as a background or supporting figure.

title: Charles Barkley (character)
text: Charles Barkley (character) is Real-world basketball player who appears as a guest character in Springfield. Charles Barkley is a fictionalized version of the real retired NBA star, appearing in a cameo capacity within the Simpsons universe. He is referenced by Nelson as an example of someone who was once tricked by his own mother, tying into a joke about Mrs. Muntz. He later appears in person when Mr. Burns pays a huge sum for a private basketball lesson with him, only for Burns to prove hopelessly bad at the sport. Barkley reacts with mild amusement rather than frustration, making a dry comparison to another famous athlete. His image also turns up as part of a barbershop poster celebrating bald black men, a nod to his real-life bald head. Overall, he's a minor recurring guest character used for quick celebrity cameo gags rather than a fully developed personality within the show. Voiced by Himself. Notable quotes: Barkley shrugged at this and remarked that Burns was still better than "Shaq".
quotes: Barkley shrugged at this and remarked that Burns was still better than "Shaq".

title: Black Voodoo
text: Black Voodoo is Superhero and member of the Vindicators team in the Simpsons universe. Black Voodoo is a member of the superhero team the Vindicators, wielding sharp metal claws and mystical voodoo powers. He is a clear parody of Marvel's Black Panther. He fought alongside his teammates against the villain Chinnos, and was temporarily turned to crystal during that battle. In a virtual reality simulation created for Bart, he sternly confronts Bart about the consequences of his selfish actions, showing a more serious and blunt side to his character. He holds the distinction of being Principal Skinner's favorite member of the Vindicators, and his popularity extends to fans within the show itself, such as cosplayers at Comicalooza and a figure owned by Comic Book Guy. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson. Notable quotes: you happened | son of a swamp witch
quotes: you happened
son of a swamp witch

title: Abel
text: Abel is Biblical figure appearing in a Ned Flanders-produced film within the show, son of Adam and Eve. Abel is a biblical character depicted as one of the sons of Adam and Eve, brother to Cain and to a middle sibling named Kevin. Within the show's universe, his story is dramatized by Ned Flanders in a home movie called The Passion of Cain and Abel, in which Todd Flanders plays the role of Abel. His famous conflict with his brother Cain is referenced humorously elsewhere in the show, such as when Todd threatens to "Cain and Abel" his brother Rod during a toy dispute. The family's saga is also used by Dr. Hibbert as a cautionary tale about middle-child syndrome, citing how the neglected middle brother Kevin framed Cain for murder. Abel himself has no direct dialogue or independent storyline, existing mainly as a mentioned or dramatized figure rather than an active character. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Stradivarius Cain
text: Stradivarius Cain is A suave spy character who appears in Homer's concussion-induced hallucination, resembling a movie action hero. Stradivarius Cain is a fictional secret agent that Homer imagines after suffering a concussion, styled like a classic movie spy hero. He's suave, resourceful, and unfazed by danger, appearing to emerge dramatically from unlikely places like the sea or even a football-playing robot. His main purpose in Homer's mind is to serve as a mentor, teaching Homer how to be a better husband to Marge by having him practice flirting with other women as a bizarre training exercise. Cain is unflappable even in absurd situations, such as squirting citrus in a jealous husband's eyes to escape trouble, and seems to genuinely enjoy the chaos he causes. He's flexible enough in Homer's imagination to transform into a woman when the lesson calls for it. Ultimately, his tutelage works, as Homer's antics convince Marge that her husband truly wants to please her. Voiced by Bryan Cranston.

title: Sergeant Activity
text: Sergeant Activity is An action figure toy belonging to Bart Simpson. Sergeant Activity is one of Bart's action figures, often paired with his other toy, Lieutenant Adventure. He served as a symbol of Bart's lingering childhood innocence, appearing during moments when Bart reflected on still being a kid at heart. In one storyline, Adventure comically tried to sell insurance to Activity, hinting at a strange imagined dynamic between the two toys. Sergeant Activity later appeared again when Bart played with him while hiding Mr. Burns in his closet. The toy also gained a bit of pop-culture status within the show's universe, appearing on the cover of a toy catalog. Overall, he's a minor but recurring prop that reinforces Bart's characterization as a kid who, despite his mischief, still enjoys imaginative play. Voiced by Terry Greene.

title: Canker
text: Canker is Non-canon supervillain and enemy of Bartman in the Bongo comics. Canker is a comic-book-only villain who plagues Springfield by sending henchmen to commit crimes and frame Bartman for them. He is ruthless toward his own men, lashing out violently when they question his schemes. He kidnaps Milhouse, mistaking him for Bartman due to a disguise mix-up, and later uses him as bait to lure the real hero into a trap. His hideout at the Laff 'Til It Hurtz Novelties Factory features a bizarre pit filled with giant novelty teeth, used to threaten captured heroes. The character turns out to be an elaborate disguise and robotic decoy, revealing a twist involving Mr. Burns and Smithers as fake identities. Ultimately, the true mastermind behind Canker is exposed to be Lenny, who was driven temporarily insane by nuclear waste exposure and sought to frame Mr. Burns using stolen android technology.

title: M.C. Birthday
text: M.C. Birthday is A minor recurring rapper character who performs at events in Springfield. M.C. Birthday is a novelty rapper who moonlights as an ice cream parlor employee at Phineas Q. Butterfat's, performing under the alias M.C. Safety when leading the safety-themed group M.C. Safety and the Caution Crew.
