He's the kind of over-the-top entertainer who shows up with a hype squad—the Goodtime Gang—to turn even mundane occasions like a senior citizen's birthday into a loud, flashy rap performance. His enthusiasm tends to backfire comedically, as his energetic routines end up frightening elderly bystanders rather than entertaining them. The character exists purely for quick comedic bits, using exaggerated rap braggadocio and cheesy rhymes as his defining trait. He has no deep backstory or relationships, functioning as a one-note gag character who pops up for surprise musical numbers. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: YO, YO, YO, Give it up for M.C Birthday | I said a Birth, a Day, A Birth of the Day | Now My good time gang are gonna' blow you away
quotes: YO, YO, YO, Give it up for M.C Birthday
I said a Birth, a Day, A Birth of the Day
Now My good time gang are gonna' blow you away

title: Björk
text: Björk is Real-world Icelandic singer-songwriter who appears as a minor character/cameo in the show. Björk appears as a background character based on the real-life musician, tied to Springfield's brief obsession with Iceland. A statue of her stands in the Icelandic Museum of National History, oddly depicted as capable of blinking. She also turns up in a crowd scene when Homer Simpson's plan to buy and rename Iceland falls through, appearing disappointed by the news. The character is a small nod to pop culture rather than a fleshed-out personality, existing mainly as an Easter egg for eagle-eyed viewers. A fun detail is that the statue's plaque incorrectly omits the umlaut from her name, and she's shown wearing her famous swan dress from the Oscars red carpet.

title: Pepita Bernstein
text: Pepita Bernstein is Extended family member; niece of Charles Montgomery Burns, appearing in a Simpsons family history book. Pepita Bernstein, nicknamed 'Squeaky,' is a minor figure from the extended Simpson/Burns family tree. She is the daughter of Sancho and Cornelia Hernandez, which makes her a niece of the wealthy Charles Montgomery Burns. She married Romeo Bernstein and the couple had five sons together. Pepita never actually speaks and exists only as a genealogical entry rather than an active character. Oddly, an altered version of her image was later reused to depict an unrelated ancestor of the Simpson family, even though she has no true connection to them. She is known only through her appearance in a spin-off book rather than the television series itself.

title: Ashley (black hair)
text: Ashley (black hair) is A minor recurring student character at Springfield Elementary School. Ashley is a background third-grader at Springfield Elementary, distinguished mainly by her black hair to differentiate her from other characters sharing the same name. She has no major storyline of her own and functions as part of the school's ensemble of students. She has been shown participating in town events, such as performing at a local pageant, and engaging in everyday childhood activities like shopping for popular toys. Her appearances are brief and scattered across a few episodes rather than any sustained arc. As a recurring but minor figure, she helps populate the world of Springfield Elementary without becoming a focal character. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Mike Benzie
text: Mike Benzie is A 5th grade teacher at Springfield Elementary School. Mike Benzie is a minor faculty member at Springfield Elementary School, responsible for teaching the 5th grade. He becomes entangled in an inter-grade conflict when a dodgeball game sparks a bitter rivalry between the 4th and 5th graders, leading to physical skirmishes among the students. His temper flares when he badmouths the 4th grade in the staff room, which escalates into a full-blown brawl involving fellow teacher Edna Krabappel. This incident showcases his short fuse and willingness to engage in petty, immature disputes despite being an authority figure. He later appears in a more lighthearted context, attending a karaoke fundraiser at the school. Overall, he's a background character used to illustrate the chaotic and sometimes childish dynamics among the school's staff. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Jar Jar Binks
text: Jar Jar Binks is A crossover character from the Star Wars film series referenced within The Simpsons universe. Jar Jar Binks is not an original character of The Simpsons but rather a pop-culture reference imported from the Star Wars franchise. Within the show, he mainly appears as a running gag tied to Comic Book Guy's obsessive fandom, most notably as a doll that Comic Book Guy sleeps with while murmuring affectionate nonsense to it. His presence is used to poke fun at the divisive reception the character received from Star Wars fans, with jokes implying that almost everyone dislikes him except die-hard collectors like Comic Book Guy. He shows up in various background references, from movie posters to nostalgic song lyrics, cementing his status as a piece of set dressing for satire rather than a full character. The show also created a parody version of him named Jim-Jam Bonks. His death in the Star Wars films was even referenced in a Simpsons episode dedication. Notable quotes: Oh Jar Jar, everyone hates you but me. - Comic Book Guy | And we had real heroes then, Like Jar Jar Binks and Qui-Gon Jinn. - Homer and Marge
quotes: Oh Jar Jar, everyone hates you but me. - Comic Book Guy
And we had real heroes then, Like Jar Jar Binks and Qui-Gon Jinn. - Homer and Marge

title: Aesop
text: Aesop is A historical/mythical figure appearing in Simpsons comics, depicted as the ancient Greek fabulist. Aesop is a non-canon character based on the real-world Greek storyteller, appearing in Simpsons comic stories. He is portrayed as a rival storyteller to Homer, competing for the attention of an ancient Greek audience with his famous fables. His storytelling is repeatedly disrupted by Homer, who barges in to spice up the tales for entertainment value. He also finds himself sidelined by modern show-business concerns, such as demographic targeting, which feels like a comedic anachronism given his ancient setting. Ultimately, he loses his platform entirely when Lindsey Naegle replaces his segment with an infomercial. The character serves as a vehicle for parody, blending classical mythology with modern media satire.

title: Bert (Muppet)
text: Bert (Muppet) is Crossover character from Sesame Street referenced/appearing occasionally in The Simpsons universe. Bert is a Muppet character borrowed from Sesame Street who pops up in various forms throughout the show, more as a running pop-culture reference than an actual character in Springfield. He's typically mentioned or seen alongside his companion Ernie, often as a symbol of wholesome, non-sexualized children's programming, as Marge points out when contrasting him to a raunchier parody show. Various Springfield residents have dressed as, hallucinated as, or displayed pictures of Bert and Ernie, showing how ingrained the duo is in the town's cultural consciousness. He even appears in a stage musical version of the Simpsons' world and in a tall tale involving a gambling bear. Overall, Bert functions purely as a nostalgic nod to Sesame Street rather than a developed character with his own arc. Notable quotes: Bert and Ernie left it to your imagination.
quotes: Bert and Ernie left it to your imagination.

title: Dante Calabresi, Sr.
text: Dante Calabresi, Sr. is Rival mob boss and father of Dante Calabresi, Jr., who clashed with Fat Tony's Springfield Mafia. Dante Calabresi, Sr. was the gray-haired patriarch of a rival Italian-American crime family that briefly warred with Fat Tony's organization. He led an attempt on Fat Tony's life after suspecting he had lost his edge, only to later smooth things over with a reconciliatory hug during a mafia sit-down. Despite the truce, his family still turned on Fat Tony violently, injuring him in a helicopter attack. He later showed a shrewd, almost mentoring side when negotiating with Michael D'Amico, bluntly telling him he lacked the killer instinct for mob life while suggesting young Bart Simpson might have a future in it instead. His story ends abruptly and darkly when he and his family are poisoned during a dinner meant to seal a territorial deal. Voiced by Joe Pantoliano.

title: 5th grade girl
text: 5th grade girl is A minor 5th grade student at Springfield Elementary, briefly interacting with Bart Simpson. The 5th grade girl is a minor background character attending Springfield Elementary alongside Bart Simpson and his classmates. She has brown hair and no notable job or defining personality trait beyond her few small appearances. Her most memorable moment comes when she asks Bart to dance with her at a school dance, and he agrees. She later appears again as a bystander on the school playground, present when Bart suffers an accident involving a tree. She has no recurring role beyond these two episodes, functioning mainly as part of the general student body of the school. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Chazz Busby
text: Chazz Busby is Owner of the Chazz Busby Ballet Academy and a recurring minor character in Springfield. Chazz Busby is a flamboyant, theatrical figure best known for running his own ballet academy, which he once accepted Lisa into after admiring her posture. He has a dramatic, self-important streak, seen in how he handled directing the Passion Play, sidelining Ned Flanders in favor of casting Homer as Jesus, then trying to spin an on-stage disaster to save face. He also dabbles in talent-scouting, showing up at events like the Hot Shot Tots contest with an oddly casual attitude toward his own health, treating a scheduled heart attack as just another item on his agenda. His character design and demeanor nod to real-life show business figures, giving him an exaggerated, showbiz-obsessed personality. Though not a major player in the main cast's lives, he pops up across many episodes and non-canon appearances as a quirky recurring presence tied to the arts and entertainment world of Springfield. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Richard Branson (character)
text: Richard Branson (character) is Real-world billionaire businessman who appears as himself in cameo roles in Springfield. Richard Branson appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, the real-life owner of Virgin. He's depicted rubbing elbows with other famous billionaires, showing up at exclusive gatherings like Billionaire Camp and entrepreneur expos. His appearances tend to poke fun at the eccentricities of the ultra-wealthy, such as engaging in archery at an exclusive retreat or getting into a playful shoulder fight with Mark Zuckerberg against Bill Gates and Nelson. He's also shown having odd personal connections, like being neighbors with Mr. Burns and hanging out on a satellite with Jeff Bezos. Mr. Burns even jokingly suggests he has enough wealth to hire Warren Buffett to hunt Branson for sport, highlighting the absurd rivalries among the show's billionaire characters. Overall, Branson serves as a satirical stand-in for real-world tycoon culture within the Simpsons universe. Voiced by Himself.

title: Pat Boone (character)
text: Pat Boone (character) is Real-world celebrity singer referenced and occasionally appearing in the Simpsons universe, associated with the Flanders family's wholesome image. Pat Boone is depicted as the epitome of squeaky-clean, conservative Christian entertainment, having moved from 1950s crooning to gospel and even a heavy metal phase. In the show's world he's most often invoked as a punchline for wholesome blandness, most notably when Lisa compares the Flanders' house to her own but with a 'creepy Pat Boone-ish quality.' His merchandise, like an album of Little Richard covers, turns up at a Flanders yard sale, reinforcing his tie to Ned's straight-laced sensibilities. Even Ned needs special permission from a ruling Waylon Smithers just to buy one of his CDs, poking fun at how tightly controlled and 'safe' Boone's image is. In a non-canon comic story, he takes on a heroic role, riding in on a motorcycle to save children from body-snatching monsters after Bart fails to stop them himself. He's also spotted in another non-canon appearance holding a pun-filled sign reading 'Hi-way to heaven,' cementing his role as a recurring, if minor, gag about religious wholesomeness. Notable quotes: Yeah, [Flanders house] seems like our house, but everything's got a creepy Pat Boone–ish quality to it.
quotes: Yeah, [Flanders house] seems like our house, but everything's got a creepy Pat Boone–ish quality to it.

title: Adam
text: Adam is The biblical first man, referenced/appearing in various Simpsons episodes and dream sequences. Adam is depicted as the first human being, created by God, and is the husband of Eve and father of Cain and Abel. He mostly appears as a background or referenced figure in the show, cropping up in jokes, children's drawings, comic mentions, and merchandise rather than as an active character. In one non-canon dream sequence, Marge imagines Adam living in the Garden of Eden, where he succumbs to the Temptation Serpent's offer of a forbidden apple and later shares it with Eve, leading to their expulsion from paradise. He is portrayed as somewhat foolish and easily tempted, though loyal enough to Eve that he later tries to sneak her back into Eden with help from a magical unicorn. Various Springfield residents reference Adam and Eve's story to make jokes about bookkeeping, procreation, and marital happiness. He has also appeared in mobile game tie-ins like The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: American spy
text: American spy is A minor recurring character; an American spy exchanged for the Albanian spy Adil Hoxha during Bart's student exchange storyline. This character is a covert American operative who becomes entangled in the Simpsons' storyline when Bart participates in an international student exchange program. He is captured while operating in Albania, mirroring the arrest of the Albanian spy who had posed as Bart's exchange partner. The two spies cross paths during a tense prisoner swap, sharing an oddly cordial moment despite being on opposing sides. Beyond this pivotal appearance, the character shows up briefly in a later episode, seen among the audience at one of Bart's mischievous ventures. He has little characterization beyond his profession and role in these two plot points, functioning mostly as a background or cameo figure tied to Cold War-style espionage humor. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Balthazar
text: Balthazar is Professor Frink's pet monkey, appearing in Simpsons comic book stories. Balthazar is an unusual pet belonging to Professor Frink, distinguished by his ability to both fly and talk, which sets him apart from an ordinary animal companion. As a non-canon character, he exists outside the main television continuity, appearing instead in the Bongo comic book line. His single documented appearance ties him to a comic story called The Time Bandit!, suggesting he plays a role in one of Frink's eccentric scientific adventures. Little else is detailed about his personality or behavior beyond his fantastical traits. His brown coloring and monkey species give him a simple, recognizable design typical of a scientist's quirky sidekick. Overall, Balthazar serves as a whimsical addition to Frink's world, reflecting the character's penchant for bizarre inventions and companions.

title: Black Panther
text: Black Panther is A Marvel superhero referenced in The Simpsons universe, appearing only as a poster and store standee. Black Panther is a crossover superhero character who exists only as a background reference rather than an active participant in Simpsons stories. He first appears as a movie poster glimpsed by Bart and Lisa at the Aztec Theater. Later, a standee of him shows up in the comic shop Zorbot the Geek, complete with a store sign written in Wakandan. Beyond these brief cameos, nothing is shown of his personality or actions within the show. His inclusion mostly serves as a nod to Marvel Comics and pop culture crossover humor.

title: Belle (Bart After Dark)
text: Belle (Bart After Dark) is Proprietress of the Springfield burlesque house La Maison Derrière, featured in "Bart After Dark". Belle is a savvy businesswoman who runs La Maison Derrière, a burlesque establishment that scandalizes much of Springfield's more conservative population. She comes from a long-established Springfield family and has spent her life in the city. When Bart accidentally damages her property, she puts him to work at her club as punishment, inadvertently exposing just how many of the town's men frequent the place. Her business becomes the target of a righteous mob, but Homer steps in to save it from destruction. Visually and thematically, she draws comparisons to the villainous Lady Tremaine from Disney's Cinderella, and is said to be loosely inspired by a real historical madam. Beyond her debut, she pops up in various crowd scenes and background appearances throughout the series' run. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Magnus Carlsen (character)
text: Magnus Carlsen (character) is Real-world chess champion who appears as himself, brought in to help Homer with his chess struggles. Magnus Carlsen is depicted as a good-natured real-life celebrity guest character who steps into Homer's life via a Skype call arranged by Marge. He offers earnest advice, encouraging Homer to resolve unfinished business with his father by finishing an old chess game. His involvement highlights his reputation as a serious, skilled world chess champion who takes an interest in helping an ordinary fan improve his mental state through chess. Beyond direct interaction, he later appears passively, watching Homer's chess match with Grampa remotely. His image is also used in a chess-themed captcha, showing his fame extends into pop-culture/tech references within the show. Overall, he functions as a cameo-style real-world figure rather than a fully developed sitcom character. Voiced by Magnus Carlsen (Himself).

title: Christine Baranski (character)
text: Christine Baranski (character) is Celebrity guest character appearing as herself, a real-life actress hired by Waylon Smithers. Christine Baranski appears in the show as a fictionalized version of herself, brought in by Waylon Smithers to add some star power to his vacation with Michael de Graaf. True to her real-life fame, she makes her entrance singing "Dancing Queen," a nod to her role as Tanya Chesham-Leigh in the Mamma Mia! films. Her cameo plays on the joke of celebrities being hired for surprisingly affordable fees for personal appearances. Beyond the musical gag, she is shown to have a kinder, more socially conscious side, traveling to Jacksonville to help a young teenager come out to his parents. Her appearance is brief but memorable, blending musical comedy with a warm, supportive moment. Voiced by Christine Baranski (herself).

title: Bully-Vern
text: Bully-Vern is An imaginary fused creature combining the show's three main bullies, appearing in a Homer hallucination. The Bully-Vern is a bizarre hallucinatory monster formed from the merged bodies of Kearney, Dolph, and Jimbo. It exists only as a vision conjured up by Homer and Yutaka Nakamura after the two get drunk on snake-rice wine. The creature has no dialogue and doesn't interact with the world in any normal way, fitting its status as a fictional, non-canon figure born purely from intoxicated imagination. Its fate is just as strange as its origin, as it ends up destroyed by a chick hatched from an equally imaginary swan version of Milhouse. Because of its odd, dreamlike nature, the Bully-Vern later resurfaces as a collectible creature in The Simpsons: Tapped Out during a Treehouse of Horror event. It stands out as one of the show's more surreal one-off monster mashups.

title: ALF
text: ALF is Crossover cameo character; a real-world alien TV celebrity referenced within the Simpsons universe rather than a member of the main cast. ALF, full name Gordon Shumway, is a furry alien best known from his own real-world television series who pops up repeatedly as a pop-culture reference in Springfield. He's never a true participant in the plot, instead appearing on magazine covers, TV Guides, and merchandise like pogs that Milhouse trades away. He's occasionally lumped in with other famous fictional aliens, such as during a police lineup Homer is asked to examine. His presence is treated as a nostalgic joke about 1980s celebrity culture rather than a character with any real personality on the show itself. In non-canon material, he even breaks the fourth wall a bit, chatting with Homer about the cancellation of his old series. Overall, ALF functions purely as a recurring visual gag and nostalgia nod rather than a developed character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta / Paul Fusco. Notable quotes: Homer told ALF that his show was canceled too soon, but ALF replied that it was canceled at the right time.
quotes: Homer told ALF that his show was canceled too soon, but ALF replied that it was canceled at the right time.

title: Rex Banner
text: Rex Banner is A U.S. Treasury officer temporarily sent to Springfield to replace Chief Wiggum and enforce Prohibition. Rex Banner is a stern, no-nonsense federal agent dispatched from Washington, D.C. to crack down on illegal alcohol in Springfield after Prohibition is reinstated. He temporarily takes over as Chief of Police, sidelining Clancy Wiggum, and becomes obsessed with catching the mysterious bootlegger known as the Beer Baron, unaware that it's actually Homer Simpson. His hyper-serious, by-the-book demeanor and old-fashioned law-enforcement style make him an outsider who clashes with Springfield's more relaxed approach to justice, including the town's bizarre catapult punishment for lawbreakers. Ultimately outmaneuvered when Wiggum solves the case himself, Banner is unceremoniously fired and disappears from town almost as abruptly as he arrived. He later resurfaces briefly as part of an angry mob confronting Homer. The character is a direct homage to Eliot Ness, both visually referencing Kevin Costner's film portrayal and vocally channeling Robert Stack's TV performance of the famous Prohibition agent. Voiced by Dave Thomas.

title: Mario Batali (character)
text: Mario Batali (character) is Celebrity chef who makes a cameo appearance in a Marge Simpson dream sequence. Mario Batali appears as a fictionalized version of himself, popping up in a surreal dream Marge Simpson has, where he's seen bouncing along on a space hopper while trailing after Homer. His appearance is brief and dreamlike, playing into the show's tradition of celebrity cameos in bizarre fantasy sequences. In a separate non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he takes on a much darker role, appearing as a figure Homer meets in therapy after Homer begins literally eating himself. In that segment, Batali reveals his own depression before gruesomely cooking Homer's head and body parts to serve as food. This split between a harmless dream cameo and a horrific Halloween-special role highlights the show's habit of using celebrity likenesses for both whimsical and macabre gags. Voiced by Himself.

title: Charles Bronson
text: Charles Bronson is Fictionalized version of the real actor, appearing as an in-universe celebrity in The Simpsons. This character is a comedic depiction of the real-life action star Charles Bronson, portrayed as a working actor within the Simpsons universe. He's shown starring in the fictional film Death Wish IX, which becomes a subject of review on a movie critique show that Marge watches while searching for a judge for the Springfield Film Festival. In another appearance, he's featured in a nostalgic clip show about celebrities' early careers, revealed to have briefly stood in for Andy Griffith on The Andy Griffith Show. His inclusion plays on the trope of blending real Hollywood figures into the show's satirical universe. He remains a minor, background-level recurring character rather than a fully developed personality. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Horatio Caine
text: Horatio Caine is Parody crossover character based on the CSI: Miami lead detective, appearing in Simpsons comic material. Horatio Caine is a comic-exclusive parody of the iconic CSI: Miami detective, brought into the Simpsons universe as a crossover gag. He's shown investigating a murder alongside his on-screen partner Frank Tripp, delivering a typically dramatic, over-the-top one-liner before dramatically putting on his sunglasses, a signature CSI: Miami running joke. His likeness also appears on a toy detective kit box, poking fun at his declining film career through a joke speech bubble. The character exists purely as a satirical nod to the CSI franchise rather than a true Simpsons cast member. His humor comes from exaggerating the seriousness and style of the live-action character in the show's cartoon world. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Help me find my dead movie career!
quotes: Help me find my dead movie career!

title: Bluella
text: Bluella is A blue whale that washed ashore in Springfield, becoming the focus of Lisa Simpson's environmental rescue efforts. Bluella is a female blue whale who becomes stranded on Springfield's beach after a windstorm, prompting Lisa Simpson to take on the role of her caretaker while Bart largely ignores the crisis. Lisa's deep emotional attachment to Bluella drives much of the story, as she spends hours comforting the whale and even reads to her, exhausting herself in the process. The episode plays on themes of environmental activism and the sometimes futile nature of good intentions, since despite the town's efforts to save her, Bluella ultimately dies. Her death leads to a secondary story involving her orphaned calves being threatened by sharks, which ties Lisa's compassion to a larger family drama in the ocean. Bluella herself doesn't speak or have distinct personality traits beyond being a passive, sympathetic creature in need of rescue. She later becomes a recurring reference point for Lisa's history of well-meaning but sometimes overly emotional environmental causes. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Raggedy Ann
text: Raggedy Ann is A rag doll toy appearing in the Simpsons universe, sister to Raggedy Andy. Raggedy Ann is a classic rag doll character with red yarn hair and a triangular nose, referenced as a toy within the Simpsons world rather than a living character. She notably appears as a prop when Moe uses one of her dolls to act out a character from The Godfather while entertaining baby Maggie, humorously renaming her 'Annie Hall.' Lisa is also shown to own a Raggedy Ann doll, hinting at the toy's presence in the Simpson household. As a recurring but minor crossover object rather than a sentient character, she has no personality of her own and exists mainly as a nostalgic pop-culture reference used by other characters for storytelling or play.

title: Beezee
text: Beezee is A minor student at Springfield Elementary School and one of Lisa Simpson's friends. Beezee is a minor recurring character who appears as one of Lisa Simpson's schoolmates. She's shown to be supportive of Lisa, complimenting her efforts on the school yearbook. Beezee is also involved in extracurricular activities, having been part of the Junior Achievers Club at Springfield Elementary. She doesn't have much of a defined personality beyond being a friendly classmate to Lisa, and her appearances in the show are limited to just a couple of episodes. She serves mainly as background support for Lisa's storylines rather than having significant plotlines of her own. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Camping man
text: Camping man is Minor recurring background character in Springfield, first seen camping with his family. The camping man is a minor Springfield resident who first appears taking his wife and young daughter on a camping trip to Springfield National Forest. He has a habit of joking around, such as pretending to attract bears despite there being none nearby, unaware that bears actually make off with his daughter's bottle. He pops up occasionally in crowd scenes throughout the town, including a picnic that goes wrong when Homer's homerun knocks him out, and a chaotic scramble for first-class upgrades during an overbooked flight. He's also seen reacting to major town events, like laughing nervously at the approaching comet during an emergency meeting, and attending a historical school field trip at Fort Springfield. Overall, he functions as one of the show's many recurring background townsfolk, appearing in small comedic or observational moments rather than taking a central role. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Ethan Ballantyne
text: Ethan Ballantyne is An artsy camp counselor in Sprooklyn who briefly captivates Lisa Simpson. Ethan Ballantyne is one of two bohemian counselors, along with his companion Kurt, who run the arts camp Expressions in the hipster enclave of Sprooklyn. He also works a day job at the sandwich shop Sprubway to make ends meet. Ethan and Kurt present themselves as free-spirited, artistic types who charm Lisa Simpson into believing Sprooklyn is a magical creative paradise. Their claims veer into the absurd, boasting of supposed magical artistic powers and even the ability to fly. When Lisa visits in person, she learns that the reality of Sprooklyn falls far short of their romanticized description, exposing them as exaggerators more interested in their artsy image than the truth. Despite this letdown, the pair part with Lisa on a sentimental note by painting a mural of her before she departs. Voiced by Jemaine Clement.

title: 50 Cent (character)
text: 50 Cent (character) is Real-life rapper and actor who appears as himself in a cameo encounter with Bart Simpson. 50 Cent appears as a guest celebrity cameo, portraying an exaggerated version of his real-life persona. He rolls up in a flashy golden limo and briefly imparts some earnest advice to Bart before undercutting the moment with a mundane, unglamorous task. This juxtaposition of celebrity swagger with an oddly humble chore is played for comedic effect. He's also referenced elsewhere as a piece of merchandise and shows up on a list of notable left-handed figures, suggesting his fame is used mostly as a cultural touchstone rather than a deep character. Overall, his role is brief and situational, existing mainly as a satirical nod to celebrity culture. Voiced by 50 Cent (Himself). Notable quotes: the more you know, the more you grow
quotes: the more you know, the more you grow

title: Bernie Ancheta
text: Bernie Ancheta is A snowboarder character appearing in Simpsons comic books. Bernie Ancheta is a minor comic-book character known primarily for his competitive snowboarding career. He has a mixed record in the Ultra-Extreme Mega-Downhill Snowboarding Competition, having both won and lost the event multiple times. Little else is known about his personality or background, as his appearances are limited to a couple of comic stories. He exists mainly as a side character tied to the extreme sports theme of those issues. There are no notable running gags or deep characterization associated with him beyond his athletic pursuits.

title: Bud Armstrong
text: Bud Armstrong is Commissioner of Pro Football, a recurring official who interacts with Homer and the Simpson family. Bud Armstrong is a gray-haired executive who oversees professional football and makes decisions that ripple into Homer's life. He first recruits Homer to design the Super Bowl half-time show after a viral video of over-the-top touchdown celebrations, leading to an ironic financial mix-up where Homer ends up paying to do a job he'd have done for free. He later brings the Springfield Meltdowns football team to town, a decision that causes Mayor Quimby to rename the town's streets with football themes. His attempt to attend the team's opening gets derailed by dead technology and outdated maps, landing him at the Simpson house in a bizarre, slapstick misunderstanding with Grandpa Abe. Bud comes across as a somewhat hapless authority figure who gets caught up in the chaos surrounding Springfield's eccentric residents. Ultimately, the mishap at the Simpson home leads him to cancel the Meltdowns altogether. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Eunice Bouvier
text: Eunice Bouvier is Marge Simpson's great half step-aunt, an elderly relative of the Bouvier family. Eunice Bouvier is an elderly relative of the Simpson family living in Gainesville, Florida, who is a great half step-aunt to Marge, Patty, and Selma. She first appears when she invites the Simpsons to celebrate her one hundredth birthday, only for the trip to go awry due to Homer's antics. Despite the chaos, she is shown as a somewhat lonely figure, singing to herself when no one else is around to celebrate with her. In a later appearance, she is believed to be on her deathbed, prompting Patty and Selma to greedily claim her belongings, only for Eunice to recover and confront them furiously about it. Her character serves as a source of dark comedy involving family greed and the absurdity of near-death scares. She is a minor but memorable recurring figure tied closely to the Bouvier family's eccentric lineage. Voiced by Julie Kavner.

title: Carol Berrera
text: Carol Berrera is Temporary substitute teacher at Springfield Elementary who briefly replaced Edna Krabappel. Carol Berrera stepped in as Bart's teacher following Edna Krabappel's death, bringing with her a background as an army servicewoman. Her arrival caused chaos when Bart, affected by hormone-laced milk, developed an early crush on her, while Principal Skinner also fell for her. She briefly dated Skinner, but the relationship ended abruptly once she encountered his overbearing mother Agnes, prompting her to end things and return to military service. A quirky detail about her is that she owns a cat with mismatched eye colors named Bowie. She later appeared symbolically in one of Bart's coma-induced dreams, listed among Ned Flanders' deceased wives, hinting at a strange alternate fate. Overall, she's a minor but memorable recurring character tied to a storyline blending romance, comedy, and Springfield Elementary's ever-changing staff. Voiced by Sofia Vergara (Tress MacNeille in-head).

title: Bongo (Life in Hell)
text: Bongo (Life in Hell) is A crossover cartoon character from Matt Groening's Life in Hell, referenced within The Simpsons universe. Bongo is a white rabbit character borrowed from Matt Groening's earlier comic strip, Life in Hell, and is the son of the character Binky. Within the world of The Simpsons, Bongo exists mainly as a piece of pop culture ephemera rather than a living character, appearing as merchandise and cultural references rather than in physical scenes. Maggie Simpson owns a stuffed Bongo doll that she is frequently seen playing with, showing his popularity as a children's toy. He also has his own in-universe comic book, underscoring his status as a beloved cartoon icon within the show's fictional media landscape. His likeness has even inspired costumes, as seen when Otto Mann dresses up as Bongo for a masquerade ball. Overall, Bongo serves as a fun nod to Groening's other work, woven subtly into the background of Springfield life.

title: Burpo
text: Burpo is Fictional comic book character who is Bart Simpson's favorite non-superhero comic book star. Burpo is the titular hero of a comic book series that Bart Simpson adores, ranking it just below his beloved superhero comics in popularity. He's portrayed as a boy who despises girls, making him relatable to young Bart. In one storyline, Burpo breaks his own rule and falls in love, which genuinely upsets Bart since it contradicts the character's established personality. Thankfully for Bart's peace of mind, the next issue resets things back to normal, restoring Burpo's girl-hating status quo. Beyond the comic itself, Burpo has a strange meta-existence in the Simpsons universe, appearing in a special dedication in one of the show's books. That dedication humorously reveals that Burpo died and ascended to a whimsical afterlife called Kitty Heaven, despite him being a human character rather than a cat.

title: Bubbles
text: Bubbles is A character from a fictional children's franchise called 'The Happy Little Elves,' referenced within the Simpsons universe. Bubbles is a minor fictional figure belonging to the in-universe franchise The Happy Little Elves, which appears throughout the show as merchandise and media Lisa and other characters interact with. His cheerful name hints at an upbeat, bubbly personality, fitting the wholesome tone of the elf franchise. He's best known for a storyline in which he helps save Christmas alongside his fellow elves. Beyond that small bit of backstory, Bubbles mostly appears as background material—dolls, pictures, and merchandise scattered throughout the Simpsons' world, including a picture hanging in Lisa's room alongside Curious Bear Cub. His presence is a running gag representing the franchise's saturation into pop culture, rather than an active character with dialogue or plot involvement. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: AT-AT
text: AT-AT is A minor robotic character appearing within the fictional Cosmic Wars: The Gathering Shadow film-within-the-show. AT-AT is a talking robotic vehicle featured in the parody film series Cosmic Wars, which spoofs Star Wars within The Simpsons universe. Its one notable moment involves barging into a galactic senate meeting to push for an amendment to a piece of legislation, only to be dismissed and told to wait its turn. Rather than protest, it calmly sits down and reads a newspaper, showing a mix of assertiveness and comic passivity. The joke rests on referencing the real-world Star Wars AT-AT walkers, which never spoke in the films, making this sentient version an amusing exaggeration. It's a background gag character rather than a recurring personality in the main Simpsons cast. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Antoine (Baby You Can't Drive My Car)
keys: antoine (baby you can't drive my car)
text: Antoine (Baby You Can't Drive My Car) is Co-founder of CarGo, a self-driving car company, who appears in the episode "Baby You Can't Drive My Car". Antoine is one of the two executives running CarGo, a company built around self-driving cars, working alongside his partner Zora. He and Zora show a shrewd, opportunistic side of the business world, valuing employees for exploitable traits like Homer's poor driving record and passive nature rather than genuine skill. Antoine is willing to bend ethics for profit, using in-car microphones to eavesdrop on customers' conversations in order to funnel them toward corporate sponsors, and hiding behind nondisclosure agreements when confronted. He shows little concern for privacy or consumer trust, later pushing an even more invasive plan to move listening devices into customers' key fobs. Despite his shady practices, he maintains a friendly, business-savvy demeanor, promoting employees like Homer and Marge when it benefits the company. His character serves as a satire of tech industry executives who mask invasive practices behind corporate-friendly language. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Race Banyon
text: Race Banyon is Astronaut who flew on a space shuttle mission with Buzz Aldrin and Homer Simpson. Race Banyon is a professional astronaut assigned to a NASA shuttle mission alongside Buzz Aldrin and, notably, an ordinary civilian, Homer Simpson. He comes across as impatient, condescending, and dismissive toward Homer, treating him as an unwelcome burden rather than a genuine crewmate. His attitude sours further when a life-threatening emergency strikes during the mission, revealing a darker, almost vindictive side to his character. He is essentially a parody of the heroic mentor figure Race Bannon from the classic cartoon Jonny Quest, subverting that archetype by making him petty and short-tempered instead of noble. Banyon's appearances are largely limited to his single major episode, though he shows up again in archive footage and a tribute segment years later. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Frodo Baggins
text: Frodo Baggins is A Lord of the Rings crossover character who appears in Simpsons hallucinations and comic book parodies. Frodo Baggins is the famous Hobbit ring-bearer from The Lord of the Rings, brought into the Simpsons universe as a crossover and parody character. He first appears as part of a drug-induced hallucination when Homer and Ned imagine themselves as Frodo and Samwise Gamgee after taking U-completeamine. In a non-canon comic story, the Simpson family is transported to Middle Earth, where they inadvertently cause the deaths of the rest of the Fellowship, leaving only Frodo and the Simpsons to continue the quest. When Frodo finally reaches Mordor to destroy the One Ring, he discovers that baby Maggie has taken it from him, adding a comedic twist to the epic tale. His character is used mostly for referential humor, tying into Bart's own quoting of Tolkien's work. Overall, Frodo functions as a pop-culture nod rather than a fully developed character within the show's canon. Notable quotes: You are a ring bearer, Frodo! To bear a Ring of Power is to be alone!
quotes: You are a ring bearer, Frodo! To bear a Ring of Power is to be alone!

title: Rick Blaine
text: Rick Blaine is Parody/crossover character based on the Casablanca protagonist, appearing in a Simpsons alternate-ending sketch. Rick Blaine is a version of the classic Casablanca character brought into the Simpsons universe as a crossover gag. He runs Rick's Café and is portrayed as a cynical American expatriate, mirroring Humphrey Bogart's original film role. In the show's alternate ending parody, he reconciles with Ilsa Lund after a series of absurd events involving Sam's piano and a hidden Hitler. The segment ends with Rick and Ilsa rekindling their romance and marrying, a comedic twist on the film's famously bittersweet conclusion. He's also referenced again as the subject of a school play and a movie poster, reinforcing his status as a background cultural nod rather than a core Simpsons character. Milhouse and Jack Deforest both take turns playing him in the Springfield Elementary production. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Amenhotep
text: Amenhotep is A non-canon monster character, an undead mummy Pharaoh appearing in Treehouse of Horror specials. Amenhotep is an ancient Egyptian Pharaoh who returned from the dead as a mummy, joining the ranks of Springfield's classic monster crew. He's often seen alongside Frankenstein's Monster, the Werewolf, and Count Dracula, treating Halloween like any other holiday complete with costume shopping. Despite being undead royalty, he has a mischievous, flirtatious streak, which gets him into trouble with his wife Womenhet. His name is a playful nod to Imhotep from The Mummy franchise, tying him into classic horror movie parody territory. He's a non-speaking, non-canon character who mostly appears in Halloween-themed content and spinoff media like The Simpsons: Tapped Out.

title: José Canseco (character)
text: José Canseco (character) is Real-life baseball player who appears as a celebrity guest on the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant softball team. José Canseco is a real-world celebrity athlete recruited by Waylon Smithers to bolster the power plant's softball team roster. Despite being handpicked by Ralph Wiggum, his heroic detour saving a woman's belongings from a house fire—escalating from her baby to her cat to increasingly random household items—causes him to miss the big game entirely. This gag pokes fun at his larger-than-life, distractible persona while showing off his athletic heroics in an absurd, over-the-top way. He later shows up as a background celebrity sighting in a laundrette, reinforcing his status as a recurring real-world cameo rather than a fully developed character. In non-canon material, he even appears as a fan attending a fictional premiere of the show itself, blurring the line between the show's universe and reality. Voiced by José Canseco (Himself).

title: Hank Azaria (character)
text: Hank Azaria (character) is In-universe fictionalized version of the real-life Simpsons voice actor, appearing as a picture/mentioned character within the show. This version of Hank Azaria exists as a meta, self-referential character rather than someone who actually interacts with the Springfield cast. He's depicted as a celebrity actor whose image and name pop up on posters and credits within the show's universe. He was slated to appear in a stage adaptation tied to Marshall Goldman, a character modeled after a real author, and his poster is spotted by Homer at Goldman's office. Comic Book Guy is shown owning a promotional poster for a fictional elf movie starring this Azaria, poking fun at his real-world film roles. In a non-canon special, he's acknowledged among the many behind-the-scenes contributors who make the show possible, highlighting the joke that one man can't run the whole series alone. Overall, he's a non-speaking, background nod rather than a fleshed-out character with personality traits of his own.

title: Mr. Boswell
text: Mr. Boswell is A famous fashion critic and recurring minor character who has judged pageants and commented on Springfield events. Mr. Boswell is a snide, waspish fashion critic best known for compiling scathing worst-dressed lists. He first appears as a judge on the Miss American Girl Pageant, where his cutting remarks delight the studio audience and amuse Bart at home. He later shows up at the reopening of a renovated version of Moe's Tavern, offering a colorfully worded compliment to its owners. In a non-canon dream sequence, he even hosts a surreal fashion show featuring donuts as models. His humor relies on delivering biting, high-society insults with theatrical flair, poking fun at real-world fashion critics of the era. Though he only appears sporadically, his sharp-tongued persona makes him memorable as a caricature of celebrity snobbery. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Memo to Goldie Hawn: Cheerleading tryouts were thirty years ago. Let's grow up, shall we? | Marge Simpson and Moe Szyslak, here's a mash note to your bangers: I wish you could live in me forever! | He's such a bitch!
quotes: Memo to Goldie Hawn: Cheerleading tryouts were thirty years ago. Let's grow up, shall we?
Marge Simpson and Moe Szyslak, here's a mash note to your bangers: I wish you could live in me forever!
He's such a bitch!

title: Beatrice (Dangerous Curves)
text: Beatrice (Dangerous Curves) is Girlfriend of the Squeaky-Voiced Teen, a minor character appearing in a single episode. Beatrice is a blonde teenage girl who briefly appears as the romantic interest of the Squeaky-Voiced Teen. She is a non-speaking character, so nothing is known about her personality through dialogue. Her only notable scene involves being dropped off with her boyfriend at Tongue-Kiss Point by Homer Simpson, who jokingly implies she's using the Squeaky-Voiced Teen for his money. Her suspicious reaction to Homer's comment is the only real hint of characterization given in the show. Beyond this cameo, she has no other canonical appearances, though she later shows up in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out.

title: Cadbury
text: Cadbury is Butler of Richie Rich, a minor crossover character appearing in the Simpsons universe. Cadbury is a mostly background character whose sole defined duty is serving Richie Rich as his loyal butler. His brief appearance ties into a comic story where Homer, Lenny, and Carl disrupt the peace of an upscale neighborhood with a paintball fight, prompting Richie Rich to have him contact a real estate agent about relocating. Beyond this, Cadbury seems to have some level of recognition or popularity, as evidenced by multiple people dressing up as him for a costume event on a cruise ship. He doesn't have an established voice actor, suggesting his role is minimal and largely visual. Cadbury represents one of the show's many small crossover nods to outside media, in this case referencing the Richie Rich franchise.

title: Aaron Burr
text: Aaron Burr is Historical figure (3rd U.S. Vice President) referenced/appearing as an animatronic in the Simpsons universe. Aaron Burr appears in the show primarily as a historical footnote rather than a living character, most notably as an animatronic figure in the Hall of Vice Presidents at a theme park. He's portrayed with a menacing edge, brandishing a gun toward Homer in a nod to his real-life fatal duel with Alexander Hamilton. Homer, having recently absorbed some pop culture knowledge from the Hamilton soundtrack, sums up Burr's reputation rather bluntly. Beyond the theme park gag, Burr's legacy also pops up in a more whimsical form as a fictional beer brand, Aaron Burr Pale Ale, glimpsed during one of Homer's beer-deprived nightmares. He has no voice actor and doesn't speak in his canonical appearance, existing mostly as a visual and historical gag tied to real-world American history. Notable quotes: "real jerk" - Homer, describing Aaron Burr
quotes: "real jerk" - Homer, describing Aaron Burr

title: Anderson (The Secret War of Lisa Simpson)
keys: anderson (the secret war of lisa simpson)
text: Anderson (The Secret War of Lisa Simpson) is A cadet at Rommelwood Military School who appears in "The Secret War of Lisa Simpson". Anderson is a minor cadet character at Rommelwood Military School, the setting where Bart and Lisa Simpson spend time in one episode. He's shown sneaking off campus with fellow cadets Larsen and Platt to grab some corn from town, showing a mischievous streak despite the school's strict discipline. Upon returning, he's the one who confronts Bart about lurking around, unaware Bart is actually hiding his sister Lisa up in a tree nearby. He also stands out as the first cadet brave or skilled enough to successfully defeat the school's tough obstacle challenge known as The Eliminator. As a bit of an inside joke, his character was designed and named after the episode's real-life director, Mike B. Anderson. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Bessie
text: Bessie is An elderly resident of the Springfield Retirement Castle and friend of Agnes Skinner. Bessie is one of the many senior citizens residing at the Springfield Retirement Castle. She comes across as a sweet, mild-mannered old woman, though she isn't above asking for small favors like having her support hose snapped to her girdle. Despite her gentle demeanor, she can be swept up in mischief, as seen when she joined a group escape from the retirement home orchestrated by Bart. She's sentimental, enjoying old films and romantic gestures like dancing on a tour boat, but she's also quick to assign blame when things go wrong. In another encounter, she proves an easy target for Bart's scams, falling for his fake grandson routine and handing over money for a supposed loose tooth. Overall, she represents the gullible but good-hearted elderly background characters who populate the retirement home setting. Voiced by Tress MacNeille, Yeardley Smith.

title: Larry Burns
text: Larry Burns is Long-lost son of Mr. Burns and a drinking buddy of Homer Simpson. Larry Burns is the estranged son of Mr. Burns, raised in an orphanage after being given up as a child. He eventually tracks down his wealthy father and lands a job at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. Crude, none-too-bright, and fond of drinking, Larry bonds instantly with Homer Simpson over their shared vices, much to Mr. Burns' disgust. His father ends up disowning him a second time after his behavior becomes too embarrassing. Larry is a family man with a wife and several children, though his impulsive nature once led him to disappear for a week without telling them where he went. He has since popped up around Springfield in mundane settings like the unemployment line and at local events. Voiced by Rodney Dangerfield.

title: Bashir bin Laden
text: Bashir bin Laden is Muslim student at Springfield Elementary School and friend of Bart Simpson. Bashir bin Laden is a young classmate of Bart's whose family relocated to Springfield from Jordan. He's portrayed as polite, gentle, and mannerly, always careful about how he behaves around others, though he harbors some insecurity about how people perceive him. His introduction sparked a subplot in which Homer, egged on by Lenny, Carl, and Moe, wrongly suspected Bashir's father of terrorism due to prejudice, leading to comedic fallout including a destroyed bridge to the Duff Brewery. Despite this rocky start, Bashir is well-liked by many of Bart's friends, including Milhouse, Richard, Ralph, Üter, Martin, Lewis, and Nelson, though Rod and Todd are oddly frightened of him, likely due to his religion. The character was notably well received by Muslim advocacy groups in both the US and UK. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Cable guy
text: Cable guy is Minor recurring character who operates a cherry picker and installs cable for Springfield Cable. The cable guy is a working-class tradesman who appears in a couple of episodes dealing with the Simpsons family. He's willing to bend the rules for profit, once trying to charge Ned Flanders for an illegal cable hookup before being turned away. When Homer flags him down instead, the cable guy happily installs free, stolen cable and even hands over a pamphlet explaining how to keep stealing it. He's shown to be pragmatic and easily persuaded by small bribes, later letting Homer borrow his cherry picker in exchange for balloons. Though not a major character, he represents the show's recurring gag about shady service workers and Homer's willingness to cut corners. Voiced by Phil Hartman, Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Well, I've already got some balloons, but... They're not this nice. Deal!
quotes: Well, I've already got some balloons, but... They're not this nice. Deal!

title: Dr. Bonebreak
text: Dr. Bonebreak is A minor professional wrestler character who appears in the episode "The Parent Rap". Dr. Bonebreak is a blond-haired professional wrestler known for his dramatic, televised exploits in the ring. He married fellow wrestler Rumbleina during a live broadcast, turning their wedding into a spectacle typical of pro wrestling showmanship. Unfortunately, their marriage quickly soured, and the two ended up brawling, with Dr. Bonebreak resorting to using a steel chair as a weapon against his new wife. His design and persona seem to draw inspiration from real-life wrestling icons, blending exaggerated machismo with theatrical flair. Despite his brief appearance in the show, he later resurfaces as a character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out video game.

title: Kim Basinger (character)
text: Kim Basinger (character) is A celebrity guest character in Springfield, based on real-life actress Kim Basinger. Kim Basinger appears as a fictionalized version of herself, a famous Hollywood actress seeking a temporary escape from the pressures of fame. She travels to Springfield alongside her husband Alec Baldwin and fellow celebrity Ron Howard, hoping to find some relief from their hectic acting careers. Her appearance ties into the show's tradition of having real-world celebrities play exaggerated versions of themselves interacting with the Simpsons universe. Little personality or running gag is developed for her beyond this brief celebrity cameo role. She is primarily remembered for her connection to the episode centered on Springfield's brush with Hollywood glamour. Voiced by Herself.

title: Yogi Bear
text: Yogi Bear is Crossover cartoon character (from Hanna-Barbera) who occasionally appears in Simpsons dreams, references, and gags. Yogi Bear is the classic Hanna-Barbera cartoon bear who lives in Jellystone Park, known for pestering Ranger Smith and swiping picnic baskets from unsuspecting campers. In the Simpsons universe he exists mainly as a pop-culture reference point, cited during a courtroom debate about how animation is built on borrowed ideas. His most memorable appearance comes in a surreal Homer dream sequence, where Homer imagines himself as "Homie Bear," Bart as his sidekick Boo-Boo, and Ned Flanders as the hapless Ranger Smith, complete with a savage mauling. He also shows up as a background gag, such as on a maze puzzle Homer carries during a Washington D.C. trip. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he even appears in a darkly comic scene carrying a severed head in a picnic basket. Overall, Yogi Bear functions as a nostalgic in-joke rather than a fully developed character within the show. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: I was having the most wonderful dream. I had a hat and a tie with no pants on.
quotes: I was having the most wonderful dream. I had a hat and a tie with no pants on.

title: Bono (character)
text: Bono (character) is Real-world celebrity guest character; Irish musician who appears in Springfield during a U2 concert. Bono appears as himself, the famous frontman of U2, when Homer interrupts one of the band's Springfield concerts to campaign for sanitation commissioner. He good-naturedly goes along with Homer's antics, even joining in singing about garbage collection and later helping out with a moving company. His fame is referenced elsewhere in the show, such as when a look-alike performer impersonates him during a charity song, and when Lisa mistakenly assumes a foreign classmate's musician father must be Bono due to his Irish accent. Lisa also cites him as one of her personal heroes, placing him alongside figures like Charles Darwin and Gwen Stefani. Overall, Bono serves as a real-world celebrity cameo rather than a recurring fictional character, used for comedic and pop-culture cachet. Voiced by Bono (Himself).

title: Artemis
text: Artemis is Bartender at The Confidential, a secret bar for bartenders, who interacts with Moe Szyslak. Artemis runs The Confidential, an exclusive speakeasy-like establishment where bartenders go to unload the secrets they've heard from their own customers. He is strict about enforcing the bar's one rule: that whatever is said there stays confidential. When Moe breaks this trust by gossiping about his patrons' secrets, Artemis retaliates by having Moe's customers 'cut off' from alcohol using a strange drug. He later rewards loyalty, offering an antidote to those who stick by Moe, showing he values discretion and loyalty above all else. His calm, commanding demeanor and mysterious operation make him a clear homage to a stylish criminal underworld figure. Artemis operates behind the scenes of Springfield's drinking culture, wielding surprising influence over its bartenders. Voiced by Ian McShane.

title: Anne of Cleves
text: Anne of Cleves is Historical figure (fourth wife of Henry VIII) portrayed in a Marge-told story and appearing as a ghost in a Homer dream sequence. Anne of Cleves is a real historical figure reimagined within the Simpsons universe, first depicted in a Marge-narrated retelling of English history where she is played by Agnes Skinner as an elderly widow married to Homer's version of Henry VIII. In that story she is portrayed as blunt and critical, even critiquing her own executioner's technique before her death. She later reappears as a ghost in one of Homer's dreams, offering him surprisingly sound parenting advice by warning him that doing all of Bart's schoolwork will stunt the boy's development. This ghostly version speaks with an English accent, despite the real Anne of Cleves being German and not originally an English speaker. The show plays loosely with history, having her executed in the sketch even though in reality she survived Henry VIII and was never beheaded. She serves mainly as a vehicle for historical parody and a bit of unexpected wisdom in Homer's subconscious. Voiced by Tress MacNeille, Pamela Hayden. Notable quotes: Anne of Cleves!?! | Homer Simpson
quotes: Anne of Cleves!?!
Homer Simpson

title: Barney the Dinosaur
text: Barney the Dinosaur is A parody of the real-life children's TV character, appearing occasionally within the Simpsons universe. Barney the Dinosaur is a fictional kids' show character that exists within the Simpsons' world, based on the real-life Barney & Friends franchise. Homer once watched him on TV with baby Maggie until Mr. Burns interrupted the broadcast. The character has also been referenced as a cultural touchstone, being compared to Itchy in terms of box-office fame. More sinisterly, the Movementarians used Barney to brainwash infants into following their cult leader. He's popped up elsewhere as background material, including a toy version carried by Milhouse and a sticker on Lisa's bedroom mirror. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, Maggie even transforms a giant monster into an oversized Barney. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Andy (Bart vs. Australia)
text: Andy (Bart vs. Australia) is Prime Minister of Australia who appears in the episode "Bart vs. Australia". Andy is the fictional Prime Minister of Australia who gets drawn into an international incident after Bart Simpson runs up a massive phone bill calling an Australian boy. Outraged citizens escalate the matter through their local MP until it reaches Andy himself, turning a childish prank into a diplomatic crisis. He insists on a bit of old-fashioned corporal punishment, agreeing to a formal one-kick booting of Bart as retribution. True to the show's satirical tone, the resolution is undercut when Bart dodges the kick entirely and moons the watching crowd, leaving Andy's attempt at justice foiled. His design and name are thought to be nods to real former Australian Prime Ministers, giving him a subtle satirical edge tied to actual politics. Aside from this single appearance, he shows up only in a background gag involving a Facebook-like feature in a non-canon future episode. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Carl's dad
text: Carl's dad is Fictional/possible father figure of Carl Carlson, mentioned only in a story told by Bart. Carl's dad is a shadowy, largely unconfirmed figure said to have discovered a set of caverns later named after him in 1956. His entire existence comes from a tale spun by Bart, which casts doubt on whether he or the caverns he supposedly found are real at all. This ambiguity is later reinforced when Carl's actual biological father, Wyatt, is revealed in a separate episode, further suggesting that Carl's dad may be nothing more than a fabricated character within Bart's story. In non-canon material, he's said to have vanished mysteriously inside the very caves that bear his name. He has no voice actor and never actually speaks on screen, appearing only in picture form. Despite his minimal presence, he holds a small place in Simpsons lore as a quirky, mysterious background character tied to the show's tradition of tall tales and unreliable narration.

title: Lynda Carter
text: Lynda Carter is Real-world actress and singer referenced/cameoed in the show, famous for playing Wonder Woman. Lynda Carter appears in the Simpsons universe as herself, the real actress renowned for her role as Wonder Woman. Her presence in the show is mostly through pop-culture references and fantasy sequences rather than direct interaction with the main cast. In one memorable moment, Marge imagines what a child between Carter and boxer George Foreman might look like after seeing them together in a fire extinguisher ad. She's also the object of Comic Book Guy's obsessive admiration, being humorously named as someone he has been legally warned to stay away from. In a non-canon holiday special, Comic Book Guy jokingly lists her, dressed as Wonder Woman, as an acceptable substitute for his real celebrity crush delivering his Christmas gifts. Overall, she serves as a recurring nostalgic and comedic reference point tied to Comic Book Guy's fandom. Notable quotes: "No" but her eyes said "yes" — as described by Comic Book Guy in "I Am Furious (Yellow)"
quotes: "No" but her eyes said "yes" — as described by Comic Book Guy in "I Am Furious (Yellow)"

title: Finn Bon Idée
text: Finn Bon Idée is CEO of GimmeChow, a food delivery app, and antagonist in a labor-dispute storyline involving the Simpsons. Finn Bon Idée is the greedy, image-conscious head of the food delivery company GimmeChow. He publicly claims his business is a small struggling startup to justify underpaying his workers, even as he secretly amasses billions in personal wealth. His hypocrisy is exposed on a financial TV show, sparking outrage that leads Marge to organize GimmeChow's employees into a union. Rather than negotiate fairly, he cynically hires Homer as a brand ambassador to try to manipulate Marge, and later attempts to crush a workers' strike by firing the entire staff and replacing them with automated kitchens and delivery drones. His scheme collapses when the drones are disabled, and he suffers a humiliating, almost cartoonish downfall as his company's stock crashes. Despite this defeat, he later reappears as an ordinary airline passenger, suggesting his corporate misadventures continue off-screen. Voiced by Jason Mantzoukas.

title: Connie Appleseed
text: Connie Appleseed is A character from a tall tale told by a singing railroad hobo, a female version of Johnny Appleseed, appearing in "Simpsons Tall Tales". Connie Appleseed is a fictional pioneer girl featured in a hobo's tall tale, cast as a Simpsons-universe stand-in for Johnny Appleseed. She's the compassionate daughter of buffalo-hunting parents, horrified by her family's slaughter of the animals for food and sport. Guided by a mysterious voice, she becomes devoted to apples instead, eventually abandoning her old surname to rename herself after her new mission. Left behind by her family's wagon train, she wanders the land planting apple trees wherever she goes. Her arc is one of quiet vindication, as her once-dismissive family is driven to the brink of starvation and cannibalism after wiping out the buffalo, only for Connie to arrive and save them with her apples. She embodies a moral about sustainability and kindness winning out over greed and destruction. Voiced by Yeardley Smith.

title: Cornelius Burns
text: Cornelius Burns is One of Mr. Burns's siblings, a minor member of the extended Burns family. Cornelius Burns is a background relative of Charles Montgomery Burns, appearing only in tie-in book material rather than the animated series itself. He is one of several children born to Daphne Burns, alongside Cornelia, George, Charles, and Zeph. As a non-speaking, picture-only character, nothing is known about his personality, appearance details, or personal history beyond his place in the Burns family tree. He exists mainly as trivia for fans piecing together the sprawling Burns lineage. His inclusion highlights just how large and obscure Mr. Burns's family is compared to the show's central characters.

title: David Byrne (character)
text: David Byrne (character) is Guest-starring real-life musician who appears as himself in a Simpsons episode involving Homer's brief music career. David Byrne appears as a fictionalized version of himself, drawn into the Simpsons' orbit after hearing Homer perform a song at Moe's Tavern. He's portrayed as an opportunistic but good-natured music producer, quick to sign talent and capitalize on a novelty hit, even producing a salsa remix of it. His pursuit of the Simpson family leads to a slapstick mishap where he ends up injured and then kidnapped by Moe, who forces him to produce music against his will. Outside of this main storyline, he's referenced as an example of a successful nerd, name-dropped alongside other notable figures. He's also noted as being politically left-leaning, appearing on a list of liberal celebrities. In a non-canon appearance, he shows up at a Hollywood premiere, reflecting his real-world celebrity status being folded into the show's universe. Voiced by David Byrne (Himself).

title: America's Most Armed and Dangerous presenter
keys: america's most armed and dangerous presenter
text: America's Most Armed and Dangerous presenter is TV presenter for the in-universe show America's Most Armed and Dangerous. This character is a minor recurring figure who hosts a fictional crime-themed television program within the Simpsons universe. He appears on screen reporting about various criminals, giving him a role similar to real-world tabloid crime show hosts. His most notable appearance involves reporting on both the Cueball Killer and the Babysitting Bandit when Bart happens to be watching. He later shows up again on television while discussing unrelated news, appearing in front of Springfield Elementary School during coverage related to the Radioactive Man film. He has no deep characterization beyond his role as a broadcast news figure, and he serves mainly as background television content referenced by other characters flipping through channels. He is also noted to be a smoker. Voiced by Christopher Collins.

title: Doreena Burns
text: Doreena Burns is Mr. Burns's aunt; daughter of Wainwright Montgomery Burns and Evelyn Graycomb, sister of Clifford Burns. Doreena Burns is a minor member of the extended Burns family, known only through print materials rather than the animated series itself. She has never appeared as a speaking character, existing solely as a picture in supplementary Simpsons books. Her family ties place her within the sprawling and often eccentric Burns lineage, being the daughter of Wainwright Montgomery Burns and Evelyn Graycomb, and sister to Clifford Burns. Because she has no dialogue or animated appearances, nothing is known about her personality, appearance details, or personal history beyond her family connections. She remains a trivia-level entry for dedicated fans exploring the Burns family tree.

title: Amid bin Laden
text: Amid bin Laden is Minor recurring character; father of Bashir bin Laden and husband of Mina bin Laden, mistaken by Homer for a terrorist. Amid bin Laden is a Springfield resident whose profession involves demolishing old, dilapidated buildings. His name and overheard phone conversation lead Homer to wrongly suspect him of being a terrorist, sparking a misunderstanding-driven plot. Amid takes pride in his work, insisting that his job is more difficult than people assume since he must carefully place explosives to bring down structures properly. His controlled demolition of the old Springfield Mall goes awry when Homer interferes, tossing the bomb into a river and accidentally destroying the bridge leading to the Duff Brewery instead. He is a family man, married to Mina and father to Bashir, and appears in a handful of episodes as a recurring but minor figure. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Chadlington
text: Chadlington is Golf caddie for Bildorf at the Springfield Junipers Golf Club. Chadlington is a minor character who works as the personal golf caddie for the wealthy Bildorf at the Springfield Junipers Golf Club. He briefly lost his job when Bart replaced him as caddie, but was reinstated once the golf club's closure plans fell through. Chadlington seems to find humor in the club's exclusivity, laughing when Bart insists he'll one day become a member. He's not particularly brave, fleeing in fear when Bart and his friends stage an ATV attack on the golf club. Overall, he's a background figure whose fortunes rise and fall based on Bildorf's whims and the ongoing conflict between Bart and the golf club. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Father Ben
text: Father Ben is Irish priest and exorcist who appears in a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment. Father Ben is an Irish priest called upon for his skills as an exorcist. He is brought in by Homer and Marge after Maggie becomes possessed by the demon Pazuzu. Methodical in his approach, he first tests the strength of the possessing spirit before proceeding with the ritual. His exorcism technique relies on repeating a specific phrase while brandishing a cross, showing a somewhat formulaic but effective method. Despite successfully driving Pazuzu out of Maggie, he reveals that the demon remains nearby, setting up further chaos as it moves to possess Bart. His appearance is limited to a single Treehouse of Horror segment, making him a minor but memorable non-canon character. Voiced by Ben Daniels. Notable quotes: By the power of Christ, may the Devil be out!
quotes: By the power of Christ, may the Devil be out!

title: Ariel
text: Ariel is A non-canon mermaid character based on Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tale, who appears in a Simpsons comic story as Homer's fantasy love interest. Ariel is a mermaid character borrowed from the classic fairy tale, appearing in a non-canon Simpsons comic story rather than the main show continuity. In her tale, she trades her fins for human legs after falling for a man she rescued, only to face the sea witch's curse that threatens to dissolve her into sea foam if her love marries another. Her story becomes intertwined with Homer, who proposes to her but ends up marrying someone else when she hesitates, triggering her transformation into foam. Fate intervenes when Homer later spots her in the foam of his beer, and their mutual declaration of love allows them to marry. She also makes a brief cameo appearance in human form waiting to visit a department-store Santa. As a crossover character, she blends Disney-style fairy tale elements with Simpsons humor.

title: Ken Burns (character)
text: Ken Burns (character) is Real-world documentary filmmaker who appears as a recurring character in Springfield, son of Manchester U. Burns and Zelda Stewart. Ken Burns is a fictionalized version of the real-life documentary filmmaker, appearing occasionally in Springfield-related media as the narrator or director of various documentaries. His works range from a documentary about Homer's life to one about cheese-making, construction of the Empire State Building, and even an exposé on the company LifeBoat that involved interviewing Mr. Burns himself. A recurring gag involves Grampa Simpson being so unbearably boring that he nearly drove Ken Burns out of the filmmaking business, leaving him traumatized and comparing Grampa's tedium to baseball. Lisa is a fan of his work, often referencing his documentary style and even wishing for niche films from him, like one about jazz musicians' ex-girlfriends. He also appears in a non-canon capacity attending a Simpsons season finale premiere, blurring the line between the show's universe and reality. Voiced by Ken Burns (Himself). Notable quotes: Grampa was more boring than baseball.
quotes: Grampa was more boring than baseball.

title: Bang Gang
text: Bang Gang is A motorcycle gang from the Radioactive Man comic universe, appearing in Simpsons comic stories. The Bang Gang is a rough-and-tumble motorcycle gang that rules the Nadir district of Zenith City, led by Isotope Rodriguez. Despite their tough biker image, they have an oddly specific fear: artists, whom they believe will gentrify their neighborhood and raise rent. Their path crosses with Fallout Boy, who joins the gang seeking a new image, and later with Radioactive Man, who recruits them as his personal bodyguards during his brief stint as a dictator ruling the city. Once Radioactive Man and his alter-ego Claude Kane III reconcile, Fallout Boy manages to reform the gang, steering them toward a more positive path. The Bang Gang's arc ends with them agreeing to a makeover, hiring Libby Biaz to overhaul their image. They exist purely within the comic book side of the Simpsons universe, tied closely to the Radioactive Man storyline.

title: Black-haired student
text: Black-haired student is A minor background student character at Springfield Elementary School. The black-haired student is a minor, non-speaking background character who attends Springfield Elementary School. He is identified mainly by his physical appearance, sporting black hair and a yellow polo shirt. He first appeared in the episode "Guess Who's Coming to Skinner" and has since made a handful of recurring background appearances in later seasons. As a non-speaking character, little is known about his personality or backstory beyond his visual design. He functions as one of the many faceless students populating the school scenes, occasionally reappearing to add to the crowd of Springfield Elementary pupils.

title: Señor Beaverotti
text: Señor Beaverotti is Robotic beaver conductor of the animatronic band at Wall-E-Weasel's pizza restaurant. Señor Beaverotti is a mechanical beaver who leads the animatronic house band at the children's pizza chain Wall-E-Weasel's, a clear parody of Chuck E. Cheese's. His main claim to fame within the show is conducting a birthday song for Bart during his party at the restaurant. Despite being a background novelty character, he's treated as having an actual musical career, having supposedly recorded a live album with jazz musician Bleeding Gums Murphy. The joke rests on the absurdity of a soulless robotic mascot being credited with genuine artistic collaboration. He never speaks or has personality traits beyond his role as a conductor, existing purely as a piece of restaurant animatronic scenery turned into a running gag prop. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Big Bird
text: Big Bird is A parody/crossover version of the Sesame Street character who occasionally appears in Springfield. Big Bird is a giant yellow bird character borrowed from Sesame Street who makes sporadic cameo appearances throughout the show's world. He first shows up as part of a mob of PBS characters chasing Homer down for dodging his pledge payment, squawking angrily like a real bird during the pursuit. Beyond that appearance, he mostly turns up as background media references, such as on TV, DVDs, banners, and even a disturbing sweater pattern knitted by Chief Wiggum. In one non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he's given a much darker fate, being bitten and drained of blood by Count von Count. Overall, Big Bird functions less as a developed character and more as a recurring pop-culture easter egg referencing his real-world Sesame Street counterpart.

title: Jason Bateman (character)
text: Jason Bateman (character) is Real-life celebrity who appears as himself in cameo roles in the show. Jason Bateman appears as a fictionalized version of himself within the Simpsons universe, popping up in celebrity-focused storylines. His first appearance has him on a reality-style show where his luxury car is torn apart in Beverly Hills, leaving him stranded and anxious about getting home. He's later referenced through his real film work, with Principal Skinner watching one of his movies and praising his charm, prompting Superintendent Chalmers to have an odd imagined conversation with the character Bateman played. He's also namechecked as part of a list of notable left-leaning celebrities compiled by Ned Flanders. Overall, his role is a brief celebrity cameo rather than a recurring storyline character, playing on his real-world persona and filmography for comedic effect. Voiced by Jason Bateman.

title: Angela (My Way or the Highway to Heaven)
keys: angela (my way or the highway to heaven)
text: Angela (My Way or the Highway to Heaven) is A minor angel character in Heaven, serving as an assistant to Jesus Christ, appearing in a non-canon episode and in a Simpsons mobile game. Angela is depicted as a functionary of Heaven, working directly under Jesus Christ in an administrative or assistant capacity.
