Her defining moment involves informing Jesus of a celebrity guest's arrival, which plays into the show's comedic take on the afterlife being populated by famous figures. She has white hair fitting her angelic appearance. As a non-canon character, she exists primarily within a single special episode and later appears as part of the Heaven-themed content in a mobile game tie-in. There isn't much depth to her personality shown beyond her role as a helpful, dutiful assistant figure in the divine hierarchy of the show's afterlife setting. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Amendment To Be
text: Amendment To Be is A satirical animated cartoon character appearing in a parody segment on The Simpsons. The Amendment To Be is a one-off parody character who appears in a fake Schoolhouse Rock!-style cartoon within the show. He is a right-wing proposed constitutional amendment, personified as a singing animated figure, mocking the educational tone of the original 'I'm Just a Bill' song. Despite his cheerful musical presentation, his actual content is disturbingly authoritarian, promoting police brutality against flag-burning liberals. He shows a menacing, bullying streak, threatening to crush political opposition and even out closeted figures who might resist him. The segment serves as biting satire on political propaganda disguised as children's entertainment, and it notably fails to entertain Bart and Lisa, who find it a poor replacement for their beloved Itchy & Scratchy. His voice actor, fittingly, is the same performer who originally voiced the real Schoolhouse Rock! shorts, adding an extra layer of parody. Voiced by Jack Sheldon.

title: Baal
text: Baal is Ancient pagan deity referenced in a Simpsons episode, unrelated to the main Simpson family. Baal is a minor, non-speaking figure based on the historical pagan god worshipped by various ancient cultures. Within the show's lore, he is tied to a joke origin story for April Fools' Day, supposedly stemming from an incident in the year 1022 when settlers disrupted a peaceful New Year celebration held in his honor. He appears only briefly, primarily as a visual reference rather than an active character with dialogue. Baal's inclusion leans into the show's tendency to poke fun at historical and religious lore with absurd, invented backstories. He has also shown up in non-canon material like The Simpsons: Tapped Out as a decorative item. Overall, he's a background curiosity rather than a character with any real personality or development.

title: Fatty Arbuckle
text: Fatty Arbuckle is Real-world silent film comedian referenced in The Simpsons, appearing on a postage stamp and mentioned in dialogue. Fatty Arbuckle is not an original Simpsons character but a reference to the real-life American silent film comedian and actor of the same name. In the show's canon, he appears only as an image on a 'Legends of Comedy' postage stamp that Krusty notices while at the post office, prompting Krusty to wonder what made Arbuckle more deserving of recognition than himself. In non-canon material, his name is used as a comparison for someone dressed in an unflattering suit, poking fun at his portly reputation. He's also woven into a whimsical, non-canon Grampa tale about the history of Christmas cookies, where he's cast as a spokesman for a fictional 'Cookie Initiative' that supposedly led to a 'Great Cookie Prohibition' in 1929. Since he never appears as an active character, he has no voice actor and no direct dialogue in the show itself.

title: Wade Boggs (character)
text: Wade Boggs (character) is Real-life baseball player who appeared as himself, playing for the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant softball team. Wade Boggs is a celebrity cameo character based on the real MLB Hall of Famer, recruited under false pretenses to work as a janitor at the power plant when he was actually meant to bolster the softball team. He's portrayed as intensely passionate about British history, particularly obsessed with debating who the greatest English Prime Minister was. This obsession proves to be his undoing, as a heated bar argument with Barney over Pitt the Elder versus Lord Palmerston ends with Barney knocking him unconscious, costing the team his services for the big game. He later resurfaces in a Christmas-themed episode as the star of two contrasting fantasy camp videos, one glorifying the Yankees and one mocking them. Boggs also appears in archive footage and picture cameos throughout later seasons, cementing his status as a recurring nod to the show's famous softball episode. Voiced by Wade Boggs (Himself).

title: Angela D'Amico
text: Angela D'Amico is Wife of mob boss Fat Tony, a recurring character in Springfield's criminal underworld. Angela D'Amico is a licensed real estate broker best known as the long-suffering wife of mafia boss Fat Tony. She's a sharp-tongued woman unafraid to confront confrontation head-on, especially when it comes to defending her marriage. Her most notable appearance revolves around discovering her husband's infidelity, leading to a fiery clash with his mistress. The character is designed as a parody of a similar figure from the film Married to the Mob. Though not a frequent presence on the show, she represents the domestic side of Fat Tony's otherwise criminal life. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: brutta puttana
quotes: brutta puttana

title: Clifford Burns
text: Clifford Burns is The biological father of Mr. Burns, appearing only in flashbacks. Clifford Burns was the natural father of Charles Montgomery Burns, remembered as an outwardly kind and affectionate man, though this image is complicated by his actual parenting choices. He once bought and shut down an entire comic book company simply to punish young Charles for reading comics instead of socializing, showing a controlling streak beneath his pleasant exterior. Despite knowing his own father Wainwright's cruelty, he was powerless to stop Wainwright from taking Charles away and molding him into the miserly man he became. Accounts of his death vary and are unreliable, including a claim that he was decapitated by a grain harvester. A conflicting flashback suggests he and his wife withheld affection from Charles his entire life, even sending him to boarding school on Christmas, though this account's accuracy is questionable since his wife Daphne is shown to still be alive elsewhere. He exists mostly as a shadowy, contradictory figure used to explain the origins of Mr. Burns' cold personality. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: John Adams
text: John Adams is Historical U.S. President referenced in a fantasy sequence and background appearances in The Simpsons. John Adams appears in the show as a historical figure rather than a regular character, representing the real second President of the United States. He first shows up in a fantasy imagined by Bart, tied to a whimsical moment involving John Hancock writing his name in the snow. Later, his image is glimpsed in a history book Superintendent Chalmers shows Bart, sparking Bart's brief obsession with Theodore Roosevelt instead. He also appears as an animatronic figure in a Hall of Vice Presidents exhibit at a theme park, referencing his earlier role as Vice President under George Washington. Adams isn't given much personality in the show, functioning mostly as a historical reference point and visual gag rather than an active character. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Bartina
text: Bartina is A female alter-ego/disguise imagined by Bart Simpson in a fantasy sequence. Bartina is not a separate character but a fantasy persona conjured up by Bart Simpson during a daydream. In this imagined scenario, Bart dresses up in a cocktail dress and curly wig to sneak into prison and rescue his mother Marge after she is arrested for shoplifting. As Bartina, Bart's plan involves seducing the prison warden before knocking him unconscious with a crowbar and stealing his keys to free Marge. The character only exists within this brief dream sequence, making her a one-off gag rather than a recurring figure in Bart's life. Bartina highlights Bart's mischievous, scheming nature and his willingness to go to absurd lengths, even in his imagination, to help his family. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Buck-toothed girl
text: Buck-toothed girl is A minor background student in Bart's class at Springfield Elementary. The buck-toothed girl is one of the many nameless background children who populate Bart's classroom and the halls of Springfield Elementary. Her most defining physical trait is a single prominent tooth jutting from her mouth, echoing the design of the similarly named Buck-toothed boy. She typically sports a light orange or light brown ponytail, though as a low-priority background character her hair color is inconsistent and shifts between episodes. She has no lines and has never been heard speaking in the series. Despite her obscurity, she appears repeatedly across many seasons, comics, and other media as part of the show's recurring crowd of schoolkids.

title: Nicolas Cage
text: Nicolas Cage is Real-world actor referenced/parodied within the Simpsons universe, related to Francis Ford Coppola and Sofia Coppola. Nicolas Cage appears in the Simpsons universe as a celebrity figure rather than a fully developed character, referenced through jokes and background details. He's the nephew of Francis Ford Coppola and cousin of Sofia Coppola, tying him into Hollywood royalty within the show's lore. His reputation for eccentric, over-the-top behavior is mocked through a Springfield-area statue depicting him attacking a mailman with a banana. He's also the butt of a joke about fans burning his DVDs at a sci-fi convention, poking fun at his mixed critical reputation. Homer once compared his own wig-wearing look to Cage, showing how the actor's image has become a pop-culture shorthand. Cage never speaks or physically appears as an active character, existing mainly as a running gag and pop-culture reference point.

title: Susan B. Anthony
text: Susan B. Anthony is Real-world historical civil rights leader referenced in the Simpsons universe. Susan B. Anthony appears in the show not as a living character but as a symbolic figure honored for her historical importance. Lisa Simpson includes her in a Thanksgiving centerpiece celebrating trailblazing women who shaped the United States, alongside Georgia O'Keeffe and Marjory Stoneman Douglas. She later shows up as a statue in another episode and as an element in one of Lisa's whimsical guides. In a non-canon comic book reference, a hero called Susan B. Anthony Man carries a shield bearing her image. She never speaks or interacts directly with the main cast, existing purely as a background nod to real-world history and feminism within the show's universe.

title: Annex administrator
text: Annex administrator is Minor recurring character who administers the Adult Education Annex. The Annex administrator is the gray-haired official in charge of signing people up to teach classes at the Adult Education Annex. He appears briefly to interview prospective instructors, most notably giving Homer a chance to teach despite Homer's utterly unconvincing qualifications. He seems willing to overlook weak credentials, ultimately allowing Homer to lead a course on marriage advice. Beyond his administrative role, he pops up in unrelated community activities in Springfield, such as singing hymns in church and joining in on a record-breaking group stunt. His appearances are brief and background-oriented, making him a minor recurring face rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Langdon Alger
text: Langdon Alger is A Springfield Elementary School student who briefly becomes romantically entangled with Lisa Simpson. Langdon Alger is a soft-spoken classmate of Lisa Simpson's who prefers puzzles to socializing. His main storyline involves a tangled romance where he dates Janey, breaks up with her, and then asks Lisa to the Spring Fling, all while secretly trying to make Janey jealous. Bart, suspicious of his motives, tries unsuccessfully to sabotage the budding relationship between Langdon and Lisa. Lisa eventually catches on to his scheme after witnessing him flirt with Janey, prompting her to reject him for the dance. The plan backfires further when his compliment to Lisa at the dance leads to Janey dumping punch on him out of jealousy. Outside of this romantic subplot, he's also mentioned by Lisa as a past crush she confided to Homer about.

title: Alec Baldwin (character)
text: Alec Baldwin (character) is Real-life actor who appears as himself, living secretly in Springfield and briefly entangled with the Simpsons family. Alec Baldwin is depicted as a celebrity residing incognito in Springfield alongside his wife Kim Basinger, with the pair counting Ron Howard among their close friends. His storyline centers on an unlikely bond formed with Homer after Homer literally crashes into his home, a friendship that sours once Homer exploits their acquaintance for a tasteless celebrity-mocking exhibit. Their falling out escalates into a chaotic high-speed pursuit, showcasing Baldwin's willingness to take physical risks, including a daring car-to-truck leap that even surprises himself. Beyond this main appearance, he's referenced humorously in political and cultural contexts, often tied to comparisons with his real-life brothers, especially Stephen Baldwin. He's also the subject of a joke about a Shakespeare performance derailed by a brawl with another famous family, and a satirical Twitter jab from Donald Trump about his hairpiece appears in a non-canon special. Overall, he functions as a guest-star cameo used for topical satire rather than a recurring dramatic role. Voiced by Alec Baldwin (Himself).

title: Jack Black (character)
text: Jack Black (character) is Real-world celebrity who appears as a fictionalized character/cameo in The Simpsons. This version of Jack Black is a fictionalized depiction of the real actor, comedian, and musician within the Simpsons universe. He's shown participating in a bizarre superhero-themed stunt, dressed as the Hulk alongside Ben Stiller as Iron Man, the two of them suspended on wires and dueling with light sabers to an unimpressed crowd. He's also referenced as having starred in a film called Kung Fu Person, cementing his in-universe status as a working actor. Adding to his legendary status, his picture hangs among great educators at a clown school, a nod to his broad, offbeat cultural influence. He never speaks in his appearances, functioning purely as a visual cameo/reference rather than a fleshed-out character.

title: Barry (The Marge-ian Chronicles)
text: Barry (The Marge-ian Chronicles) is Co-founder of Exploration Incorporated, a scientist involved in a fake Mars colony project. Barry is a scientist who, along with his partner Paul, co-founded Exploration Incorporated, a venture that claimed it would establish a human colony on Mars by 2026. When Lisa and Marge got approved for the program, Barry and Paul were forced to speed up their timeline due to a rival project nearing completion. Their scheme unraveled during the actual launch, when it was revealed the rocket was a fake, built only to inspire people rather than actually reach space. Adding to the embarrassment, they were unable to make a quick getaway because their car wouldn't start. Beyond this incident, Barry has been spotted attending live podcast recordings, showing he keeps a presence in Springfield's public events even after the scandal. Voiced by Jon Wurster.

title: Biclops
text: Biclops is A fictional comic book superhero referenced within the Simpsons universe, tied to the world of comic collecting that Bart and Milhouse frequent. Biclops is a comic-book superhero known primarily for his oddly thick eyeglasses, a visual gag that ties into his role as a parody of Marvel's Cyclops from the X-Men. His comics are published by the fictional in-universe tie-in to the real eyewear chain LensCrafters, poking fun at product placement and eyewear branding. He first appears in the episode "Worst Episode Ever," existing as one of the many comic-book properties referenced in the show's satire of nerd and collector culture. Beyond his debut, Biclops shows up repeatedly as background material in later seasons and Simpsons comic spin-offs, usually depicted in pictures, cut-outs, or figures rather than through spoken dialogue. He has no real personality traits explored on-screen, functioning mostly as a quick visual joke about superhero tropes and eyewear humor. His recurring cameo appearances suggest he's a minor but persistent piece of the show's fictional pop-culture landscape.

title: Billy the Kid
text: Billy the Kid is Historical Old West outlaw who appears as a zombie in a Simpsons Halloween episode. Billy the Kid is a real-life gunslinger from the Old West, depicted here as having died at age 21 and buried under his birth name, William H. Bonney. In the show's canon, he is grouped with other infamous figures who became celebrated in death. His main appearance comes in a non-canon Halloween story, where his grave is misread by Lisa, sparking a movement to ban guns in Springfield. This backfires spectacularly when he and other deceased criminals rise as gun-craving zombies, rampaging through town once firearms are removed. The joke hinges on grim irony: his tombstone's peaceful message about a gun-free world is used to horrific effect. Ultimately, it takes Homer traveling back in time to correct the mistake, ensuring the zombies—including Billy—are dealt with by force rather than pacifism. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: I dream of a world without guns
quotes: I dream of a world without guns

title: Mary Bailey
text: Mary Bailey is Governor of Springfield's state, occasional recurring political figure in the show. Mary Bailey is the elected governor overseeing Springfield's state, first introduced when she defeated Mr. Burns in a gubernatorial race. Her rise to power was aided by an infamous incident involving a mutated three-eyed fish that soured public opinion of her opponent. She's shown taking her civic duties seriously, whether judging a school flag design contest or ordering investigations into the town's nuclear power plant for pollution concerns. Bailey also demonstrated calm authority during a prison riot, managing to restore order and even grant pardons. Her political affiliation is never explicitly confirmed, though she's often assumed to lean opposite of the Republican Mr. Burns. Overall, she serves as a recurring authority figure representing state government in Springfield's satirical political landscape. Voiced by Maggie Roswell.

title: Nicky Bluepants Altosaxophony
text: Nicky Bluepants Altosaxophony is Undercover alias used by Homer Simpson while working as an FBI informant infiltrating Fat Tony's mob. Nicky Bluepants Altosaxophony is not a separate character but a disguise Homer Simpson adopts after being caught bribing a government official and offered a deal to work for the FBI. Wearing a gadget wig and given a new identity, he infiltrates Fat Tony's crime family from inside prison. He wins over Louie and Fat Tony by enduring punishment and showing more emotion than the other mobsters, which helps him break out of jail alongside them. To prove his loyalty to the family, he is ordered to burn down Moe's Tavern. The ruse falls apart when Fat Tony discovers he's a snitch, leading to a fatal heart attack. The name itself is a parody reference to the film Mickey Blue Eyes. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Butterfly
text: Butterfly is A recurring minor animal character/motif appearing in various Simpsons episodes and shorts. This is not a named character but a recurring butterfly that pops up across several Simpsons episodes as a small, wordless plot device. In one memorable instance, baby Maggie chases one across the roof of the house and tumbles off in pursuit of it. It also appears in Bart's musings about reincarnation, where he fantasizes about coming back as a butterfly so no one suspects him of mischief. In more surreal moments, a butterfly burrows into Homer's arm on a tropical island and later escapes his mouth after he accidentally swallows it as a caterpillar. As a non-speaking creature, the butterfly functions purely as a visual gag or symbolic touch rather than a fully developed character, showing up across the classic series and even later specials. Notable quotes: "nobody ever suspects the butterfly" - Bart
quotes: "nobody ever suspects the butterfly" - Bart

title: Blarg aliens
text: Blarg aliens is Non-canon alien race encountered by the Simpson family in a Treehouse of Horror-style segment. The Blarg aliens are a group of blue-haired extraterrestrials from a distant planet, appearing only in a non-canon Halloween-adjacent Thanksgiving special. They enter the story at a critical moment, arriving with bowls just as a dangerous jelly monster is about to attack the crash-landed Simpson family. Rather than being hostile, they use the bowls to contain the jelly monster, effectively neutralizing the threat. Their intervention turns a potential disaster into a peaceful resolution, leading to an unexpected shared Thanksgiving meal with the Simpsons. Beyond this single act, little else is revealed about their culture, personalities, or society, making them a minor but pivotal plot device in the episode. They later also make an appearance tied to a Thanksgiving-themed event in The Simpsons: Tapped Out game. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Dan Castellaneta, Chris Edgerly.

title: Billy (actor)
text: Billy (actor) is A recurring child actor in the Simpsons universe who appears in various in-universe films and TV shows. Billy is a young actor who appears in several fictional productions within the Simpsons world, most notably as a character on the show-within-a-show McGarnigale. In that role, he played a frightened witness who was pressured into revealing the truth about McGarnigale's innocence, only to meet a grisly end once he did. He has also starred in Troy McClure vehicles like Birds: Our Fine Feathered Colleagues and Someone's in the Kitchen with DNA!, showing he was a go-to child performer for schlocky in-universe media. Outside of acting, he's shown attending a Thanksgiving parade where he gets hit with fish guts thrown by a Santa-costumed Mr. Burns. Behind the scenes, his character's planned future appearances were cut short following the real-life death of Phil Hartman, who voiced his frequent co-star Troy McClure. He's a minor recurring background character rather than a fully developed personality. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Charcoal Briquette
text: Charcoal Briquette is A supervillain enemy of Radioactive Man, member of The Fossil Fuel Four. Charcoal Briquette is a fire-themed supervillain who battles Radioactive Man within the show's comic-book universe. She speaks with a distinct French accent, setting her apart from her teammates in the Fossil Fuel Four. Her power comes from a briquette perched on her head, which she can ignite to shoot flames at her enemies. She's shown to be tactically minded, mocking the weaknesses of opposing heroes during battle. Along with the rest of the Fossil Fuel Four, she plays a role in the defeat of Radioactive Man. Her name is a playful nod to the charcoal briquettes used to start fires, tying into her fiery abilities. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Brown-haired boy
text: Brown-haired boy is Background student in Bart Simpson's class at Springfield Elementary. The brown-haired boy is a minor, largely unnoticed member of Bart's class who has appeared in the background of countless episodes since the show's very first installment. He's a non-speaking character, defined mostly by his physical trait of brown hair and his habit of wearing shades. He doesn't have any notable storylines of his own, instead serving as one of the many nameless faces that populate Springfield Elementary. Despite his lack of dialogue or characterization, he has proven to be a remarkably persistent presence, showing up across decades of episodes, comics, and other Simpsons media. His mother is mentioned as unnamed in one episode, suggesting he has at least some family background acknowledged by the show. Overall, he exemplifies the show's tradition of recurring background characters who add texture to the world without ever taking center stage. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Aquaman
text: Aquaman is Comic book superhero from the DC Comics universe referenced within the Simpsons universe. Aquaman is not an original Simpsons character but a DC Comics superhero who pops up repeatedly as a piece of pop-culture flavor within the show. He appears in comic books read by Bart, such as titles found at the Android's Dungeon, and shows up as a costume at fan conventions like Bi-Mon-Sci-Fi-Con. Real-life actor Jason Momoa, known for playing Aquaman in films, even appears in character at a Springfield event, complete with trident and conch shell. Homer references Aquaman's fish-commanding abilities when trying to escape a whale, showing how the character is used as a running joke about his ocean-based powers. Comic Book Guy also references Aquaman lore, distinguishing between the 'Silver Age' and 'Golden Age' versions of the hero. Overall, Aquaman functions as a recurring nod to nerd culture and comic book fandom rather than a fully developed character in the show. Notable quotes: What would Aquaman do?
quotes: What would Aquaman do?

title: Jim-Jam Bonks
text: Jim-Jam Bonks is Fictional character within the show's universe, from the in-universe Cosmic Wars movie series (a parody franchise). Jim-Jam Bonks is a character from the Cosmic Wars films, existing within the Simpsons universe as a piece of pop culture satire. He's designed as a clear parody of Jar Jar Binks from Star Wars, right down to inspiring the same kind of backlash from fans. Both Bart and Lisa were immediately put off by him upon seeing his debut film, with Lisa and Luigi going further to call him out as a negative stereotype, mirroring real-world criticisms of his real-life counterpart. Despite the in-story disdain for the character, he's become a merchandising fixture, appearing as a mascot on theme park rides, novelty mugs, and even in a celebrity look-alike singing performance. He's a recurring background gag that pops up across many seasons rather than a character with real depth or dialogue of his own. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Ashley (male hacker)
text: Ashley (male hacker) is A non-canon male hacker who appears in a couch gag/short, working for Pseudo-nonymous. Ashley is a male hacker who, alongside a female hacker also named Ashley, breaks into Disney's servers to threaten the release of embarrassing, never-produced episode ideas for The Simpsons. During their scheme, the two hackers unexpectedly fall for each other. When the FBI catches up with them, they double down by threatening to delete other Disney projects entirely. Rather than being arrested, the pair are oddly let go, riding off together on a moped and kissing. As a non-canon character, Ashley exists purely for a gag rather than as part of the show's ongoing continuity. His brief appearance plays into a romantic, almost outlaw-couple dynamic between two people who share the same name. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Captain America
text: Captain America is Comic book superhero referenced within The Simpsons universe. Captain America is a fictional comic book hero that exists within the world of The Simpsons, appearing mostly as a reference point rather than a fully realized character. He's tied to the show's recurring gag about comic book culture, most notably through Comic Book Guy, who once displayed a Captain America poster in his shop. The character's mythos also plays into a joke about superhero traits being combined, as Everyman drew patriotic courage from a Captain America comic. In a non-canon special, Herman Hermann cosplays as Captain America while part of a parody superhero team called the Springfield Avengers. Overall, Captain America functions as background pop-culture flavor rather than an active participant in Simpsons stories.

title: Clyde Barrow
text: Clyde Barrow is A Simpsons parody version of the real-life outlaw Clyde Barrow, depicted in a story told by Marge as part of a Bonnie and Clyde retelling. Clyde Barrow is a Depression-era criminal from a story Marge tells, styled after the infamous real outlaw of the same name. He's portrayed as eager to prove himself "bad" to impress the object of his affection, Bonnie Parker, even going so far as to rob a feed store he actually co-owns himself. Together with Bonnie, he embarks on a crime spree robbing banks, relying on a hapless accomplice for getaways. His story ends in tragedy when their driver betrays them to the police, leading to a fatal shootout. Even in his final moments, he's a bit of a comic figure, as Bonnie casually tells him she wants to see other people because he isn't exciting enough. The character also appears among other historical figures who are honored in death, connecting him to a broader afterlife mythology in the show. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Army colonel
text: Army colonel is A military commander who appears in "G.I. (Annoyed Grunt)", leading a war-game exercise against Springfield residents. The Army Colonel is a hardened military officer who briefly commands Homer and other Springfield residents during a training exercise. When Homer's antics push him too far, he decides to treat the situation as an actual war game, ordering his troops to hunt down and eliminate the "too stupid" recruits, including Cletus. His stubborn refusal to back down escalates tensions with the townspeople, who eventually outsmart him by spiking the water supply with alcohol, leaving his entire army hungover and forced to surrender. Despite his tough exterior, he shows a comically weak spot when Lisa attempts to lecture him about the futility of occupying foreign nations, begging Homer to drown her out with a blowhorn rather than listen. This blend of authoritarian bravado and sudden vulnerability makes him a satirical stand-in for real-world military leadership. He remains a minor, one-episode character whose main function is to drive the plot's war-game conflict. Voiced by Kiefer Sutherland.

title: Baz
text: Baz is Ned Flanders' pet dog, a recurring animal character in the Simpsons universe. Baz, full name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, is the loyal white and brown dog belonging to Ned Flanders. She's a friendly and clever animal, known for performing tricks that impressed Lisa Simpson upon their first meeting. Baz develops an unexpected bond with Homer, which stirs jealousy in the Simpsons' own dog, Santa's Little Helper, leading to a tense rivalry between the two pets that eventually settles into peaceful coexistence. Despite Homer's fondness for her, Baz remains devoted to Ned, even when Flanders offers to give her away. She later gets caught up in a citywide dog-friendly initiative in Springfield, briefly running with a pack of feral dogs before being brought back home once Marge asserts dominance over the group. Baz also shows emotional sensitivity, comforting Ned during a dream involving his late wife Maude's ghost.

title: Nick Callahan
text: Nick Callahan is A realtor and former timeshare salesman who appears in dealings with Homer and Marge Simpson. Nick Callahan started out as a shady timeshare salesman, notably conning Homer and Marge into buying a timeshare at The Yellow Lotus a decade before his death. He later worked at Red Blazer Realty, where he was known for finally selling the Whitmans' house after Gil had failed to unload it for twenty-one years. Ever the skeptic of newcomers, he doubted Marge would last long in the real estate business when she joined the firm. In a twist, he eventually switched sides, taking a job that claimed to help people escape timeshare scams, though this too turned out to be a scam. His story ends abruptly and absurdly when he is killed by a drugged-up otter while swimming in the ocean, confronted shortly before by the very people he'd once deceived. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Lenora Carter
text: Lenora Carter is Special investigator from the attorney general's office who briefly takes over a police investigation in Springfield. Lenora Carter is a no-nonsense special investigator sent from the attorney general's office to handle a pickpocket case that Springfield's own police force couldn't solve. She wastes no time asserting authority over Chief Wiggum, openly mocking his competence in front of his own officers. Her methods are unconventional, choosing Homer as bait specifically because of his large backside, which she believes will attract the thief. Despite Marge's worries, the plan works, leading to a wallet being tracked to a warehouse full of stolen goods. She ultimately clashes with Wiggum's judgment, since he wrongly insists Fat Tony is innocent of the crime. Carter's tenure in Springfield is brief but memorable, defined by her sharp tongue and blunt dismissiveness toward local law enforcement. Voiced by Dawnn Lewis. Notable quotes: She then took over the investigation.
quotes: She then took over the investigation.

title: Trey Anastasio (character)
text: Trey Anastasio (character) is Real-world musician appearing as himself in guest appearances on The Simpsons. Trey Anastasio appears as a fictionalized version of himself, the real-life frontman of the band Phish. In his appearances, he's portrayed as a dedicated advocate for causes he believes in, taking part in a rally supporting medical marijuana. He also has a comedic run-in with Moe Szyslak, who recklessly drives on the sidewalk and crashes into signage, including one advertising Phish, before hitting Trey himself. This leads to a bit of irritation from Trey, since he and his associates had gone to the trouble of putting up that sign. His role is brief and cameo-based, mainly serving as a nod to fans of the band and a source of a quick comedic gag involving Moe's poor driving. Voiced by Trey Anastasio (Himself).

title: James L. Brooks (character)
text: James L. Brooks (character) is Real-world executive producer of The Simpsons who appears as himself in cameo roles within the show. James L. Brooks appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, the real executive producer and developer of The Simpsons. He shows up in celebrity-studded settings, such as an awards ceremony and a Hollywood restaurant alongside other famous names. In one gag, he's depicted offering Ned Flanders dessert before mocking Los Angeles's lack of a football team, giving him a mischievous, teasing edge. His appearances often play on his real-life role behind the show, blurring the line between the animated world and reality. In a non-canon segment, he's humorously portrayed surrounded by piles of money, evoking the image of a wealthy mogul. Overall, he serves as a meta, self-referential character rather than a traditional member of the cast. Voiced by Himself. Notable quotes: No!
quotes: No!

title: Canadian border security official
text: Canadian border security official is Minor unnamed official who checks travelers crossing from the USA into Canada. This character is a nameless border security officer stationed at the U.S.-Canada crossing, appearing only briefly in a single episode. He serves a simple functional role, greeting travelers and processing their entry into Canada. His most notable scene involves an unwitting mix-up when Homer and Grampa cross the border expecting to reach Mexico for cheap medication, only to realize their mistake upon his welcome. The character has no deep personality traits explored, existing mainly as a plot device for a joke about Homer's geographic confusion. He has since made a small non-canon cameo in a mobile game tie-in, where he is referred to as a Border Agent with a bit of added dialogue. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Bort (boy)
text: Bort (boy) is A minor recurring character; a boy encountered by Bart at Itchy & Scratchy Land who shares his name. Bort is a young boy who briefly crosses paths with Bart Simpson during a family trip to Itchy & Scratchy Land. He becomes notable purely because of his unusual name, which mirrors a running joke about personalized license plates. Bart is stunned to discover that despite thinking 'Bort' was a rare or nonsensical name, there are actually multiple people who share it, including this boy and an older man. Bort himself has little personality shown on screen, serving mainly as a punchline to the show's gag about novelty license plates never having the name you want. He appears alongside his unnamed mother at the theme park. Outside the main show, he has made small appearances in Simpsons-related video games. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Bella-Ella
text: Bella-Ella is A member of Addy's clique of wealthy young girls, and one of Lisa's tormentors during a sleepover. Bella-Ella is one of the snobbish girls who make up Addy's exclusive social circle. Due to her mother having too much Botox while pregnant with her, Bella-Ella is physically unable to laugh, which serves as a defining quirk of her character. Alongside Sloan and Tessa Rose, she is initially dismissive and cruel toward Lisa, mocking her riding skills and gift choices before joining in on bullying her throughout a sleepover, including posting embarrassing videos of her online. Her cruelty backfires when Lisa outsmarts the group using horse hoof hardener, leading to a chaotic horseback chase. Ironically, after Addy turns on the group and humiliates them, Bella-Ella and the others admire her meanness and want to befriend her even more. She later appears briefly in a crowd scene after a concert, showing she remains part of Addy's social world. Voiced by Lili Reinhart.

title: George Cauldron
text: George Cauldron is Minor non-canon character who appears seeking a date with Suzanne. George Cauldron is a fictional love interest invented as part of a joke within a Treehouse of Horror segment, existing only within the show's non-canon universe. He is described as strikingly good-looking, arriving eager to take Suzanne out on a date. His brief appearance plays on the classic sitcom trope of a made-up boyfriend, referencing a similar gag from a well-known American sitcom. He has little characterization beyond his charming looks and the joke of Suzanne's absence, being told she needs more time before she's ready. His inclusion is mostly a nod to television history rather than a fleshed-out role in the Simpsons universe. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Athena
text: Athena is Non-canon Greek mythology character appearing in Simpsons crossover content, goddess of wisdom. Athena is a depiction of the Greek goddess of wisdom, brought into the Simpsons universe as a non-canon crossover character. She is portrayed as a fair-minded arbiter, most notably serving as judge in a mythological dispute between Hades and Persephone. Her ruling shows a strict adherence to divine law even when it produces a somewhat unsatisfying compromise, acknowledging wrongdoing but still enforcing the letter of the rules. She comes from a famous divine lineage, being the daughter of Zeus and having numerous well-known siblings and relatives from Greek mythology. Athena's appearances in the show are brief and largely visual, such as a bust reference and a couch gag where Lisa dresses as her, rather than through extended storylines.

title: James Cagney
text: James Cagney is Real-world Hollywood actor depicted as a background character in Grampa's flashback. James Cagney appears in The Simpsons as a representation of the real-life American actor and dancer of the same name. He is depicted as one of several classic Hollywood stars, alongside figures like Jimmy Durante, W. C. Fields, Shirley Temple, Laurel and Hardy, and Boris Karloff's Frankenstein's Monster, seen departing a train in one of Grampa's nostalgic flashbacks. He does not speak in his appearance, functioning purely as a nostalgic cameo tied to Grampa's memories of old Hollywood. Interestingly, his likeness is later repurposed in a comic mash-up where Bart combines him with the Marvel villain Magneto to create a character called Cagneto. Beyond these brief nods, little personality or storyline is given to him within the show itself.

title: Bigfoot
text: Bigfoot is A mythical apelike cryptid figure referenced throughout the show's lore, most famously when Homer is mistaken for him. Bigfoot is the show's take on the classic cryptid legend, a large, hairy, human-like creature said to roam the forests and leave giant footprints. He rarely appears in person, functioning mostly as a running joke or urban legend referenced by tabloid TV and pop culture within Springfield. His most memorable moment comes when a mud-covered, clothesless Homer is captured by scientists who mistake him for the real thing. Other gags include a TV special faking Bigfoot footage with an actor in a suit, and Groundskeeper Willie's obsessive, decades-long hunt for him. When Bigfoot does appear as himself, he's surprisingly domestic, going home to a nagging wife and being asked to make his own dinner. Overall, he's treated as a recurring in-universe legend rather than a fully developed character. Notable quotes: This much I believe we can agree upon: this specimen is either a below-average human being or...a brilliant beast.|German scientist
quotes: This much I believe we can agree upon: this specimen is either a below-average human being or...a brilliant beast.|German scientist

title: Bill (Homie the Clown)
text: Bill (Homie the Clown) is Krusty the Clown's accountant. Bill is the numbers man tasked with keeping Krusty the Clown's chaotic finances in check. He's practical and blunt, unafraid to tell Krusty hard truths about his reckless spending habits. When Krusty's frivolous purchases threaten to bankrupt him, Bill comes up with the idea of founding a clown college as a new revenue stream. He also sticks around to oversee some of the college's classes, quietly tallying up the costs of Krusty's questionable teaching methods. Bill serves as a straight-man foil to Krusty's over-the-top antics, grounding the episode's comedy in mundane financial reality. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Blake (Three Dreams Denied)
text: Blake (Three Dreams Denied) is A student at Springfield Elementary School who briefly becomes Lisa Simpson's love interest and saxophone rival. Blake is a new student who catches Lisa's attention by sharing her love of the saxophone, though he turns out to be far less genuine than he first appears. He secretly wears blue contact lenses to hide his true red eyes and fakes being a vegetarian just to impress Lisa, tossing away the bacon from his own sandwich to keep up the ruse. Beneath his charming exterior, he's manipulative and competitive, going so far as to sabotage Lisa's saxophone reed with hot dog water to beat her in the first chair audition. Despite playing only slightly better than Lisa, he wins the position and gleefully rubs it in her face, showing a smug and self-satisfied streak. He also has a flair for self-promotion, later presenting himself as the coolest kid in school during a class project. Blake's arc pokes fun at teen crushes and the idea of a seemingly perfect love interest hiding ulterior motives. Voiced by Ben Platt. Notable quotes: Lisa, the 11th is the science fair.
quotes: Lisa, the 11th is the science fair.

title: Binky
text: Binky is A fictional cartoon rabbit character that appears as a toy/doll within the Simpsons universe, crossing over from Matt Groening's other comic strip, Life in Hell. Binky is a background cartoon rabbit whose likeness pops up repeatedly in the Simpsons household, most often as a stuffed toy or doll in Bart or Maggie's room. He's a crossover figure originally from Matt Groening's Life in Hell comic strip, where he is the father of Bongo. In the Simpsons universe he never speaks or acts on his own, existing purely as a recurring visual gag in the form of pictures, posters, keychains, and toys. Characters like Ralph and Ms. Botz are shown owning Binky merchandise, and even Otto hallucinates asking Binky for directions while driving the school bus. In the original Tracey Ullman shorts, Lisa was frequently depicted playing with either a Binky or Bongo toy, cementing his status as a minor recurring prop rather than an active character.

title: Tom Brokaw
text: Tom Brokaw is Recurring real-world journalist character who appears as a TV news reporter in Springfield. Tom Brokaw appears in the Simpsons universe as a caricature of the real-life news anchor, popping up periodically on television broadcasts throughout Springfield. He's shown covering a mix of serious and absurd stories, from the fall of the Berlin Wall to soccer moms who hate soccer, often revealing a vain and insecure side once the cameras stop rolling. He shares an odd rivalry and camaraderie with fellow anchors like Dan Rather and Kent Brockman, occasionally teasing or unsettling them. A recurring bit involves his surprising and slightly obsessive admiration for Lisa Simpson, whom he considers his idol, even owning her book and memorabilia. Despite being a real person, he never voiced himself on the show, with Harry Shearer performing an impression so convincing that Brokaw reportedly enjoyed it. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Candy Store bandit
text: Candy Store bandit is A minor criminal character who robs candy stores, briefly encountered by Bart Simpson. The Candy Store Bandit is a small-time crook whose criminal specialty is robbing candy stores. He is best known for his botched heist at Chupo's Candy Store, which was accidentally thwarted by Bart Simpson rather than through any heroic effort. This mishap led to Bart being offered a reward, which he cheekily requested in the form of candy bars, irritating Homer in the process. Beyond his main appearance, the character resurfaces in a couch gag, where he's shown stealing the Simpsons' couch alongside another accomplice. He's a fairly obscure, background-level character used mostly for quick comedic bits rather than any deep storyline. His presence highlights the show's tendency to recycle minor characters for gags across different episodes. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Billy (Krusty the Clown)
text: Billy (Krusty the Clown) is Fifth-grade student at Springfield Elementary who serves as news editor of the school's newspaper. Billy is a fast-talking, ambitious fifth-grader who takes over as editor of the Daily Fourth Gradian when it starts losing money. He wastes no time flexing his new authority, firing the previous editor and transforming the paper into a shallow, clickbait-driven online outlet, even at Lisa Simpson's expense by turning her into a TV recapper. His editorial priorities favor sensational, low-effort content over substantive journalism, as shown when he swaps out an important exposé for a story about scrambled eggs. Beyond his journalistic ambitions, Billy is also a devoted member of the Murmur Nation, the obsessive fanbase of pop star Ashlee Starling. His loyalty to the group leads him into a prank war against Homer and later against a rival fandom, though he eventually has a change of heart and calls off the attacks. Billy represents a satirical jab at modern clickbait media culture filtered through the eyes of an overconfident kid. Voiced by Billy Eichner.

title: Mina bin Laden
text: Mina bin Laden is Mother of Bashir bin Laden and wife of Amid bin Laden; a neighbor family who befriended the Simpsons. Mina bin Laden is a minor recurring character who is part of a Muslim family living near the Simpsons. She is introduced when Bart wanders into her backyard, drawn by the smell of a barbecue, and she responds warmly to his compliment. Later, she and her family are invited to dinner at the Simpsons' house, only to be unfairly suspected of terrorism by Homer because of their ethnicity, highlighting themes of prejudice and misunderstanding. Despite this treatment, she remains a background presence tied closely to her husband and son rather than having an extensive individual storyline. In a non-canon appearance, she is shown ending up in Heaven, implying she is regarded as a good person. Overall, her role centers on family and being a target of the show's satire on xenophobia. Voiced by Shohreh Aghdashloo.

title: Tom Brady (character)
text: Tom Brady (character) is Real-life NFL quarterback who appears as a guest-star character in The Simpsons universe. Tom Brady shows up as a celebrity athlete within the show's world, most notably when Homer is enlisted to teach him and other sports stars how to perform over-the-top victory celebrations. He's shown as somewhat image-conscious, carrying a flag proclaiming his own superiority and worrying about what Homer thinks of him after an awkward parking lot encounter. Beyond his main appearance, he's referenced multiple times in later episodes as a cultural touchstone for football greatness, virility, and even a controversial trade away from the Patriots. His character leans into his real-world fame and reputation rather than being a fully fleshed-out original personality. He mostly serves as a cameo/gag device tied to real NFL history and pop culture references. Voiced by Tom Brady (himself). Notable quotes: "everyone sucks but me"
quotes: "everyone sucks but me"

title: Aladdin
text: Aladdin is Non-canon character; a giant advertising mascot figure that comes to life in a Treehouse of Horror segment. This Aladdin is not the animated hero but a towering statue advertising Aladdin's Magic Carpets & Linoleum in Springfield. He springs to life alongside other giant mascots after a strange ionic disturbance animates the city's advertising figures. Riding his flying carpet, he joins the rampage of destruction sweeping through Springfield. Like the other mascots, he loses his power once the townspeople stop paying attention to him. His brief chaotic flight ends when he crashes into and demolishes a local landmark. He appears only in a Halloween special, marking him as a non-canon, one-off character used for comedic spectacle.

title: Archie Andrews
text: Archie Andrews is Crossover character from Archie Comics who has appeared in The Simpsons universe. Archie Andrews is a visiting character from the Archie Comics universe who occasionally crosses over into the world of The Simpsons. He first appears riding in his own jalopy alongside Homer after Bart is ejected from Sideshow Bob's limo. His fame is such that Milhouse later portrays him in a school play based on the Riverdale TV series. In another crossover story, the robot Plasmo escapes into the Archie Comics universe and tries to join Archie's gang, though they remain skeptical of his wild story. Archie functions mostly as a nod to comic-book fandom rather than a fully developed personality within the show. His recurring presence highlights the show's fondness for playful crossovers with other well-known franchises. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Cornelius Chapman
text: Cornelius Chapman is Springfield's oldest living resident, a minor recurring character known for his historic and comedic feats. Cornelius Chapman was a 108-year-old fixture of Springfield's history, credited with building the town's first log cabin and introducing the toothbrush to its citizens. For years he was the town's only professional basketball player, a fact that hurt his team's chances but still delighted audiences. He also had a dramatic streak of near-historical involvement, from assisting people during the 1929 stock market crash to accidentally taking a stray bullet meant for Huey Long. His long life came to an ironic end when a celebratory kiss from Britney Spears at an awards ceremony triggered a fatal heart attack. His death was treated with comic indifference by Kent Brockman, who simply shoved his body aside and passed his award on to the next-oldest resident, Mr. Burns. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: You're doing the right thing. Oh, oh, out you go!
quotes: You're doing the right thing. Oh, oh, out you go!

title: Blade
text: Blade is A superhero and vampire hunter costume/character appearing in non-canon segments of the show. Blade is a fictional superhero and vampire hunter referenced in a non-canon Simpsons segment. In the show's universe, Carl dresses up as Blade after Homer transforms and flees work during a Halloween-themed episode. While in costume, Carl decapitates Lenny before running off in pursuit of Homer, a darkly comic and violent gag typical of the Treehouse of Horror specials. The character also appears as a costume choice at a fan convention in a later episode, showing his status as a recognizable pop-culture figure within the show's world. Blade himself does not speak on screen and functions more as a costume or cultural reference than a fully realized character. His appearances are limited to non-canon storylines, emphasizing his role as a parody or homage to the Marvel vampire hunter rather than an original Simpsons creation.

title: Alex (I'm Spelling as Fast as I Can)
keys: alex (i'm spelling as fast as i can)
text: Alex (I'm Spelling as Fast as I Can) is A young student who competed against Lisa Simpson in the Spellympics. Alex is a bespectacled young boy known for his endearing speech quirk of swapping 'l' sounds for 'r's and 'w's. He rose to fame as a crowd favorite during the Spellympics, winning over audiences with his correct spelling of tricky words like "anthrax" and "rigged". His popularity was so strong that the competition's host tried to rig the contest in his favor by asking Lisa to intentionally lose. In the end, Alex won the Spellympics fairly after Lisa made a genuine mistake rather than a deliberate one. He's later spotted as a background character at a video game store, showing he remains part of Springfield's community of kids. Despite his brief appearances, Alex stands out for his charm and unusual pronunciation habit. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Ernest Borgnine (character)
text: Ernest Borgnine (character) is Celebrity guest character; a real-life actor who appears as a "celebrity dad" on a Junior Campers rafting trip. Ernest Borgnine appears as a fictionalized version of himself, volunteering as a celebrity father figure on a Junior Campers father-son rafting excursion. He is paired up with a boy named Warren for the trip, though things quickly go wrong when his raft group gets separated from Ned Flanders and Homer Simpson. Borgnine proves himself as a resourceful and protective figure, attempting to fend off a bear with his trusty Swiss Army knife, only to discover Homer had secretly swiped it to use as a gift for Bart. Despite this setback, he shows courage in the face of danger, guiding the stranded campers through a series of ominous woodland threats, including hillbillies and an unidentified stalking creature. His ultimate fate after taking shelter in an abandoned summer camp is left a mystery, adding a darkly comic, unresolved edge to his appearance. His role highlights the show's frequent use of real celebrities inserted into absurd, exaggerated Simpsons scenarios. Voiced by Ernest Borgnine (Himself).

title: Admiral Carstairs
text: Admiral Carstairs is A retired admiral and minor recurring character who appears at high-society Springfield events. Admiral Carstairs is an elderly, distinguished-looking retired naval officer who tends to show up wherever Springfield's elite gather. He first appears at Mr. Burns' party, where he's insulted by young Larry Burns, though he later surprises everyone with impressive break dancing skills at a street party despite his age. He later serves on the jury during the Simpsons' trial for the supposed murder of Captain Jack, and turns up at the presiding judge's party afterward. Like the Dowager, he seems to be a fixture of upscale social functions around town. In his later years he resides at the Springfield Retirement Castle, where he's part of a clique known as the preppies. In a non-canon storyline, it's revealed he secretly holds knowledge of who truly built the Egyptian pyramids, which Professor Frink's father attempts to steal from his mind. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: The Black Belch
text: The Black Belch is Non-canon superhero alter-ego of Barney Gumble, appearing in Simpsons comic stories. The Black Belch is a comic-exclusive persona taken on by Barney Gumble after he's exposed to a nuclear explosion that grants him strange powers. True to Barney's usual comedic identity, his newfound ability is a gross-out gag rather than a traditional heroic power, letting him unleash noxious belches as a weapon. The character exists purely within Bongo Comics' non-canon storylines, functioning as a parody of superhero origin tropes applied to one of Springfield's most disreputable barflies. He appears alongside other reimagined hero versions of Simpsons characters in a loosely connected superhero storyline. The joke relies on the contrast between grandiose superhero conventions and Barney's lowbrow, drunken persona. He has no impact on the show's main continuity and is strictly a comic book curiosity.

title: Steve Bannon
text: Steve Bannon is Non-canon character depicting White House Chief Strategist, appearing in Simpsons Trump-related specials. Steve Bannon is a non-canon, non-speaking character based on the real-life political strategist, appearing in satirical Simpsons specials about Donald Trump's presidency. He is depicted working within a chaotic White House alongside other real political figures like Jared Kushner and Kellyanne Conway. His brief appearances lean into dark, exaggerated humor typical of these topical specials, showing him in violent or bizarre situations rather than any characterized personality or dialogue. He never speaks on screen, making his presence purely visual and symbolic of the political satire being portrayed. Ultimately, his storyline ends in a grim, cartoonish fashion befitting the non-canon nature of these episodes.

title: Tucker Carlson
text: Tucker Carlson is Real-world television host and political commentator who appears as a caricature in Simpsons episodes. Tucker Carlson is depicted in the show as a version of his real-life persona, a conservative TV host known for stirring up controversy. He shows up on a Fox News-style segment discussing a local Springfield scandal involving Kirk and the collapse of a town landmark, reflecting how the show often satirizes real media figures weighing in on Springfield's absurd local news. In a non-canon appearance, he's used for a quick joke about political endorsements, poking fun at his on-air commentary style. His role is minor and largely functions as background satire of cable news culture rather than a fleshed-out character with personal traits. He has no family or personal history shown, staying purely in his public commentator role whenever he appears. Voiced by Chris Edgerly. Notable quotes: "Putin for President"
quotes: "Putin for President"

title: Hugs Bunny
text: Hugs Bunny is Referee at an Easter Egg hunt in Springfield. Hugs Bunny is a costumed rabbit character who serves as the referee for an Easter Egg hunt. Despite his friendly, huggable name and appearance, he awkwardly refuses physical contact, telling a child he's legally unable to hug him. His name is a punny nod to the classic Looney Tunes character Bugs Bunny. He ends up clashing with Homer Simpson after catching him cheating during the egg hunt on behalf of Maggie. This confrontation escalates into a physical fight, ending with Homer crashing through a window and tearing off one of Hugs Bunny's ears in the process. He's a minor, one-episode character whose main claim to fame is this brief but memorable scuffle with Homer. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Bao kid
text: Bao kid is Non-canon crossover character from the Pixar short film Bao, appearing in Disney+ Simpsons specials. The Bao kid is a crossover character brought into the Simpsons universe from the Pixar short film 'Bao,' appearing exclusively in special Disney+ promotional episodes rather than the main series. He is depicted as a non-speaking character, existing mostly in the background of larger celebratory events. He first shows up at Moe's Tavern during a party celebrating Disney+'s second anniversary. Later, he appears alongside his mother during a Mother's Day-themed excursion to a fictional attraction called Disney Playground Planet. Little is known about his personality since he never speaks, making him a purely visual cameo tying together Disney and Fox properties.

title: Camping woman
text: Camping woman is Minor recurring background character; a Springfield townsperson who first appeared camping with her family. The camping woman is a minor recurring background resident of Springfield, first seen on a camping trip with her husband and daughter. She's portrayed as fairly ordinary and easily frightened, notably being scared of bears during that outing. Over the years she's popped up at various town events and gatherings, from baseball picnics to mayoral debates to a TV taping, usually as part of the crowd rather than a central figure. She and her husband seem to share reactions to town happenings, such as laughing together at the approaching comet. She also took part in the chaotic rush for first-class seats during the Simpsons' oversold flight on Krazy Klown Airlines. Overall, she serves as a recognizable face in Springfield's ensemble of townsfolk, appearing across many different episodes and situations without ever taking on a major storyline of her own. Voiced by Maggie Roswell.

title: Jethro Bodine
text: Jethro Bodine is A crossover character from The Beverly Hillbillies who appears within Simpsons episodes as a show-within-a-show reference. Jethro Bodine is not an original Simpsons character but rather a character from the classic sitcom The Beverly Hillbillies, who appears in clips or references shown within The Simpsons universe. He's depicted as a somewhat dim-witted, rural character, consistent with his source material. In one referenced scene, he casually mentions going off to shoot Vietcong soldiers, prompting a humorously literal response from Granny about not wanting to cook them. In a non-canon deleted segment, his rustic simplicity again features when Granny delivers the odd news that Jethro ate her monkey. He also appears immortalized as a statue at a hillbilly-themed exhibit, cementing his fictional cultural status within the Simpsons world. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent parody and homage to classic television series. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Jethro ate her monkey.
quotes: Jethro ate her monkey.

title: Blitzen
text: Blitzen is One of Santa Claus's reindeer, appearing in Simpsons Christmas-themed episodes. Blitzen is a minor, non-speaking animal character who serves as one of Santa Claus's sleigh-pulling reindeer. He's mostly a background reference used for holiday gags rather than a fully developed character. His most memorable moment comes when Homer callously suggests Bart shoot him for sport while hunting, highlighting Homer's poor parenting instincts. He's also name-checked in a Christmas carol sung by the Simpson family and appears as a doll in an in-universe holiday special. In a non-canon segment, Blitzen is one of the reindeer that scatters after Mr. Burns mistakes Santa's sleigh for a German plane during World War II, adding him to a farcical wartime Christmas story involving Abe Simpson and Burns. Notable quotes: "be a sport man and kill Blitzen"
quotes: "be a sport man and kill Blitzen"

title: Fuzzy Bunny
text: Fuzzy Bunny is A cartoon rabbit character featured in the in-universe sex education film shown to students at Bart's school. Fuzzy Bunny is the animated protagonist of the educational film "Fuzzy Bunny's Guide to You Know What," which is shown to Springfield Elementary students to teach them about puberty and reproduction. His story follows a fairly innocent arc, going through the awkward changes of adolescence before falling for Fluffy Bunny. The two court each other through wholesome outings like trips to the park and an ice cream social, resisting their urges until marriage. Their eventual honeymoon leads to consummation and the birth of fourteen offspring, though only eight survive, giving the tale an oddly dark twist for a children's educational cartoon. As a non-speaking character, Fuzzy Bunny exists purely as a visual teaching tool within the show's universe rather than a fully developed personality. His brief appearance became memorable enough to be referenced again in a later clip show.

title: Dante Calabresi, Jr.
text: Dante Calabresi, Jr. is Rival mobster and son of Dante Calabresi, Sr., involved in conflicts with Fat Tony's Springfield Mafia. Dante Calabresi, Jr. is an Italian-American mob member belonging to the rival Calabresi crime family. He initially clashes with Fat Tony's outfit after his family attempts to have Fat Tony killed, but the two sides briefly reconcile during a sit-down. He shows a mix of dark humor and menace, joking about serving cold soup to Michael D'Amico after threatening to kill Fat Tony. Despite the truce, his family later ambushes Fat Tony in a helicopter attack. His story ends tragically when he and the rest of the Calabresis are poisoned during a dinner with the Simpsons, dying alongside his relatives. Even after his death, he oddly reappears as a background presence at a later wedding, hinting at the show's non-canon inconsistencies. His last wish, to be buried beside his late wife under a New Jersey bridge, gives him a strangely sentimental note amid his violent life. Voiced by Michael Imperioli. Notable quotes: Dante Jr. asked if Michael would serve their soup cold if they killed Fat Tony and then questioned if baby hot dogs were made that way or shrunk down.
quotes: Dante Jr. asked if Michael would serve their soup cold if they killed Fat Tony and then questioned if baby hot dogs were made that way or shrunk down.

title: Abra Ca-Debra
text: Abra Ca-Debra is A close-up magician hired for a party at the Springfield Power Plant. Abra Ca-Debra is a minor recurring character who works as a close-up magician. She was hired by Homer to entertain guests at Lenny's birthday party held at the Power Plant, where she performed tricks for the assembled employees. Her signature stage act involved a classic illusion of sawing Homer in half, a stunt that visibly disturbed onlooker Mike Wegman. She has no spoken lines in her appearances, existing purely as a background performer. Her only other connection to the show is a non-canon poster of her seen hanging in Werner Herzog's Magic Shop, suggesting she has some level of recognition as a professional magician in the Simpsons universe.

title: Ashley (female hacker)
text: Ashley (female hacker) is Non-canon hacker character who appeared in a special/short episode of The Simpsons. Ashley is a red-haired hacker working for a group called Pseudo-nonymous, appearing in a non-canon Simpsons segment. She teams up with a male hacker also named Ashley to break into Disney's servers, planning to leak unreleased and embarrassing episode concepts from the show. During their heist, the two hackers unexpectedly develop romantic feelings for each other. When the FBI catches up with them, she and her partner threaten to erase valuable Disney files unless they're allowed to leave. The authorities ultimately let the pair go, and the segment ends with the two riding off together on a moped, kissing. Her story is played mostly for comedic and romantic effect rather than serious characterization. Voiced by Anna Faris.

title: Jack Box
text: Jack Box is Mascot character representing the Jack in the Box fast food chain, appearing in Homer's fantasies. Jack Box is a fictional mascot based on the real-world Jack in the Box fast food chain. He appears as a non-speaking figure in Homer's imagination, first envisioned as a carved figure alongside other famous fast food mascots on a fantasy version of Mount Rushmore. He later shows up in one of Homer's dreams alongside other fast food icons. As a mascot character, he has no dialogue and exists purely as a visual gag tied to Homer's obsession with fast food branding. His inclusion highlights the show's tendency to satirize consumer culture and corporate mascots through surreal crossover cameos.

title: Angelica Button
text: Angelica Button is Fictional wizard character, the main character of the in-universe Angelica Button book/movie series parodied within The Simpsons. Angelica Button is a fictional young witch who serves as the central figure of a Harry Potter-style parody franchise referenced within the Simpsons universe. She is depicted as an 8-year-old wizard with brown hair, existing primarily as a pop-culture phenomenon that the Simpsons kids engage with, similar to real-world book and movie fandoms. In one of Bart's fantasies, she battles a rival wizard named Malicious Krubb using conjured boxing gloves, though she loses the fight. She's also been referenced as a category item in one of Lisa's quirky classification charts. Beyond the show itself, she's appeared as a costume, a mobile game character, and a comic book reference, reflecting her role as a recurring cultural touchstone rather than a fully fleshed-out personality. Notably, she's explicitly modeled after Lisa Simpson and designed as a female parody of Harry Potter. Voiced by Yeardley Smith.

title: Little Caesar
text: Little Caesar is Minor parody character based on the Little Caesars pizza mascot, appearing as a fast-food/historical mashup figure. Little Caesar is a comedic riff on both the Little Caesars pizza mascot and the Roman dictator Julius Caesar, blending fast-food branding with a mock-historical assassination scene. He shows up amid a dispute between two rival pizza makers, Famous Ray and Original Ray, and cheekily insists on being included in their argument. His nosiness backfires when he ends up stealing their pizzas, prompting both men to stab him repeatedly in a parody of Caesar's betrayal. The gag is topped off when a third mascot, Noid, joins in on the stabbing, leading to Little Caesar's dying pun referencing the famous "Et tu, Brute?" line. He later reappears briefly as part of a surreal lineup of fast-food mascots in one of Homer's dreams. Overall, he exists purely as a one-off visual/verbal pun rather than a developed character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Et tu, Noidus?
quotes: Et tu, Noidus?

title: Alice (Alice in Wonderland)
text: Alice (Alice in Wonderland) is Fictional character from Alice in Wonderland who appears in visions and book depictions within the Simpsons universe. Alice is the classic literary character from Alice in Wonderland, appearing in The Simpsons as a fantastical figure rather than a regular cast member. She first shows up in a vision experienced by Lisa, offering cryptic warnings about the dangers of trying to seem cool while a menacing Hatter menaces her with a gun. She later resurfaces when Lisa and Maggie flip through a pop-up storybook version of her tale, bringing the whimsical world to life. Her final appearance is a simple cover cameo on a copy of the original Alice in Wonderland book. Blonde-haired and status marked as fictional even within the show's own reality, she functions purely as a nod to the source material rather than a developed character with her own personality arc. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Azzlan
text: Azzlan is A non-canon lion character who appears in "The Serfsons" segment, parodying Aslan from The Chronicles of Narnia. Azzlan is a talking lion with a religious mission, going door to door in an attempt to convert people to Christianity. He's persistent and a bit oblivious to social cues, showing up unannounced and undeterred even after being physically thrown out of a house. His running gag involves popping up whenever someone happens to say "the word," mistaking casual phrases for an invitation to preach. Despite his failures, he seems to have some rapport with the Simpson family, who greet him with weary familiarity. He also exists as a recurring image within alternate reality or dream sequences, suggesting he's become a minor fixture of the show's more surreal, non-canon storytelling. Overall, he functions as a one-note parody character built entirely around religious zealotry and a Narnia reference. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson. Notable quotes: Hi, Azzlan.
quotes: Hi, Azzlan.

title: James Bont
text: James Bont is Secret agent and enemy of Hank Scorpio, killed during the episode "You Only Move Twice". James Bont is a clear parody of James Bond, evoking Sean Connery's take on the iconic spy. He appears as a determined agent working to bring down the villainous Hank Scorpio, CEO of Globex Corporation. Despite surviving traps like a slow-burning rope over an alligator pit and an attack by Scarface's giant weasel, his luck runs out when he's tackled by an unwitting Homer Simpson, who has no idea he's interfering with a real spy mission. Scorpio's guards promptly execute him, turning his death into a dark punchline once Homer proudly (and obliviously) reports catching a "loafer." His name gag—revealed as "James Bont"—plays into the show's love of subtle spoofs of famous franchises. Though a minor, one-off character, he's become a memorable piece of the beloved Scorpio storyline. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Stop him! He's supposed to die!
quotes: Stop him! He's supposed to die!

title: Uncle Ben (Death of a Salesman)
text: Uncle Ben (Death of a Salesman) is Fictional deceased uncle of Willy Loman in a play-within-the-show adaptation of "Death of a Salesman". Uncle Ben is a character who exists only within a stage adaptation of Death of a Salesman that appears in two separate Simpsons episodes. He's portrayed as a self-made rich man who tells a rags-to-riches story about venturing into the jungle as a young man and emerging wealthy years later. The character is notable for being recast in different productions with different actors playing him, first by a Chinese actor in a Chinese theater production, and later by Sideshow Mel in a local staging directed by Llewellyn Sinclair. In the second version, the jungle backstory is swapped out for a more modern twist involving getting rich by working for Amazon. Since he's a play character rather than a true Simpsons universe resident, his story details shift depending on which production is being shown. He never appears outside the context of these theatrical performances. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Bambi's mother
text: Bambi's mother is Non-canon crossover character from Disney's Bambi, appearing in Simpsons Treehouse of Horror and holiday specials. Bambi's mother is a borrowed Disney character who shows up in a few of the show's non-canon specials rather than the main Simpsons continuity. She is depicted as protective and fearful, especially of hunters, reflecting her original film's famous tragedy. In one appearance she panics when a car backfire is mistaken for gunfire, desperately offering herself in place of her son Bambi. In another, she and Bambi narrowly escape being shot by a hunter named Amos Slade, only saved when a buck intervenes. Her presence is largely a nostalgic nod to the classic Disney film, used for parody or crossover gags rather than deep characterization. She appears only briefly, often as a background or referenced figure, such as a joke tombstone in a Halloween special. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Blinky (Pac-Man)
text: Blinky (Pac-Man) is One of the ghost characters from the classic arcade game Pac-Man, appearing as a crossover/video-game reference in The Simpsons. Blinky is a non-speaking crossover character based on one of the ghosts from the arcade game Pac-Man. He shows up whenever the show references classic video games, appearing on screens being played by characters like Mr. Burns and Homer. He was even seen attending the in-universe wedding of Pac-Man and Ms. Pac-Man during a Super Bowl broadcast, dancing along with the other ghosts. Blinky also made a print appearance on the cover of a fictional album called Pacman Fever. He has no dialogue or real personality of his own, existing purely as a nostalgic nod to retro gaming culture within the Simpsons universe.

title: Blacula
text: Blacula is A vampire character appearing in a fictional film within the Simpsons universe, and later a Halloween costume worn by Carl. Blacula is a vampire character who exists within the Simpsons' fictional world as the star of a movie called Blacula Meets Black Dracula. In that film, he teams up with Black Dracula to menace a disco patron who dares to shut down the dance floor for a hockey rink. Outside of that in-universe film appearance, Blacula also exists as a Halloween costume, worn by Carl during a demon-infested Springfield Halloween. While wearing the costume, Carl actually transforms into Blacula and attacks his coworker Lenny. The character is a minor, mostly non-canon reference used for horror and Halloween-themed gags rather than a fleshed-out personality. Voiced by Karl Wiedergott.

title: El Bombastico
text: El Bombastico is A Mexican professional wrestler briefly sponsored by the Springfield Investorettes. El Bombastico is a Mexican professional wrestler who appears only briefly in the show's canon. He is notable for being sponsored by the Springfield Investorettes, a decision that Marge Simpson strongly opposed. Beyond this minor storyline, little else is revealed about his personality or background, as he is a picture-only, non-speaking character in the main series. He later gained a bit more presence in the non-canon mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, where he has dialogue. Overall, he functions as a minor recurring figure tied to Springfield's wrestling and investment subplots.

title: Curtis Armstrong
text: Curtis Armstrong is Real-life actor who appears as a fictionalized version of himself in the Simpsons universe. This character is a comedic self-parody version of actual actor Curtis Armstrong, referred to affectionately by the nickname 'Booger,' a nod to his famous role in Revenge of the Nerds. In the show's universe, he's depicted as a working actor who took on a role in the fictional film The Poke of Zorro, playing the Scarlet Pimpernel. He's also shown living the Hollywood lifestyle, dining at the upscale restaurant Morton's alongside real producer Jerry Bruckheimer. His appearances are brief and tied to the show's tradition of poking fun at celebrities by inserting them into Springfield's world. He doesn't have an established personality beyond these cameo-style appearances.

title: Bartzilla (character)
text: Bartzilla (character) is A fictional monster persona imagined by Bart Simpson, based on Godzilla. Bartzilla is a non-canon alter ego that exists only in Bart's imagination, appearing in a fantasy sequence where he envisions himself as a giant, city-smashing kaiju rampaging through Springfield. The character is a clear parody of Godzilla, complete with the destructive, oversized monster tropes associated with that franchise. Lisa joins in on the fun by playing along as her own monster persona, Robo-Sis, and the two engage in a mock battle until Marge intervenes to put a stop to their game.
