Bartzilla also shows up as one of the surreal dream levels in the video game The Simpsons: Bart's Nightmare, reflecting how deeply embedded the persona is in Bart's imaginative and mischievous psyche. As a non-canon character, Bartzilla serves purely as a whimsical, comedic device rather than a serious part of the show's ongoing storyline.

title: Cap Anson
text: Cap Anson is Real-world baseball legend referenced by Mr. Burns for the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant softball team. Cap Anson is based on the real historical baseball player who competed in the National League from 1871 to 1897. In the show, Mr. Burns wants to recruit him for the Plant's softball team in order to win a lucrative bet against Aristotle Amadopolis. However, Burns' plan hits a snag when Waylon Smithers has to inform him that Anson has long since passed away, making him unavailable for recruitment. He appears only as a picture, never speaking or physically interacting within the story. His inclusion is a nod to the episode's running joke of Burns hiring real, often deceased, baseball legends for the team.

title: Milford A. Alexander
text: Milford A. Alexander is Justice of the peace who officiated Homer and Marge's wedding. Milford A. Alexander is a justice of the peace working at Shotgun Pete's 24-Hour Wedding Chapel, assisted by Doris Troy. He is best known for having married Homer and Marge, though he rushed through their ceremony so quickly he barely acknowledged who they were. Just before performing that wedding, he also officiated the marriage of Cletus and Aline, showing how he treats matrimony as a fast, impersonal assembly-line process. His character underscores the show's comedic take on quickie chapel weddings, contrasting with the emotional weight of Homer and Marge's relationship. He appears mainly in flashback sequences recalling the couple's wedding day. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Betty Boop
text: Betty Boop is Famous cartoon character referenced within The Simpsons universe, not an original character. Betty Boop is a real-world cartoon icon who makes brief crossover appearances within the Simpsons universe rather than being an original character of the show. She appears as a photo stand-in prop at the Lazy I Ranch, where Bernice Hibbert dresses up as her alongside Julius Hibbert as Rambo. She also turns up as an image on a Cartoon Women's History poster hanging in Lisa's bedroom, underscoring her status as a celebrated figure in animation history. In another episode, an old Jewish man references her by name after watching an anti-union cartoon, showing her cultural association with classic animation. Betty Boop never speaks or acts independently in the show, existing only as a visual reference or verbal mention. Her presence functions as a nostalgic nod to golden-age cartoons rather than as a developed character.

title: Joe Biden
text: Joe Biden is Real-world political figure referenced in the show; the 47th Vice President of the United States. Joe Biden appears in The Simpsons primarily as a background reference to real-world politics rather than a fully developed character. He is mentioned by Homer as a target of potential lawsuits, invoked in typical Simpsons fashion as a punchline for litigious American culture. His most substantial in-universe appearance is as an animatronic figure in the Hall of Vice Presidents at a theme park, reflecting his historical role as Vice President rather than President. In a non-canon special, he appears in a comedic dance sequence with other 2020 presidential candidates, taunting Donald Trump after he falls. Despite winning the real 2020 election and becoming President during the show's run, the series curiously never references or parodies him in that presidential capacity, making him something of an anomaly among real-world leaders depicted in the show. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Biden asked him who the old man was now as he laughed at Trump.
quotes: Biden asked him who the old man was now as he laughed at Trump.

title: Blackbeard
text: Blackbeard is A historical pirate figure referenced in The Simpsons, appearing in a non-canon segment and mentioned elsewhere. Blackbeard, whose real name was Edward Teach, is depicted as a legendary pirate within the Simpsons universe. He is brought up when Bart tries to recall the name of the pirate from Treasure Island, though Bart ultimately answers incorrectly. In a non-canon appearance, Blackbeard serves as a member of the Jury of the Damned in a Halloween special, comically forced to sit in a high chair due to a lack of seating. His illiteracy becomes a running joke when he mistakes a wedding photo for a treasure map and is mocked by a fellow juror for not being able to read. He also appears as a criminal figure in a children's prayer about capture by the police, reinforcing his identity as an infamous outlaw. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Charlie Chaplin
text: Charlie Chaplin is Real-world silent film actor referenced and briefly depicted within the Simpsons universe. Charlie Chaplin appears in the show as a real historical figure rather than an original character, referenced through his famous 'Tramp' persona and iconic film moments. He's shown eating a shoe, a nod to The Gold Rush, and Grampa Simpson's potato-and-fork dance directly parodies another scene from that same film. His legacy pops up in background details like a poster of Legends of Comedy and a photo in Homer's hotel room. Mr. Burns even keeps the suit Chaplin was buried in as part of his eccentric estate. Grampa Simpson once mistakenly believes he's met the real Chaplin when he's actually talking to an impersonator. He's also listed among Ned Flanders' laudable lefties, tying into his real-life reputation as a left-handed icon.

title: Tattoo Annie
text: Tattoo Annie is A minor recurring inmate character who appears in the women's prison Marge is sent to. Tattoo Annie is a heavily tattooed prisoner who first appears when Marge is briefly incarcerated. She's a woman of few words, preferring to let the artwork covering her skin communicate for her, giving off an intense and unsettling vibe. Her most notable tattoo is a fold-up gag styled after a classic Mad magazine back cover, revealing an image of Alfred E. Neuman when folded correctly. She uses this tattoo to answer a rhetorical question Marge asks about the kind of man she married. Outside of prison, she has apparently kept up with modern life, picking up dating advice and even joining Facebook, where she's connected with Mark Zuckerberg. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Angry Dad (character)
text: Angry Dad (character) is Title character of Bart Simpson's cartoon series 'Angry Dad', a fictional creation within the show. Angry Dad is a cartoon character created by Bart Simpson, closely modeled after Homer's appearance and behavior, though Bart legally denies the resemblance. Bart draws inspiration for the comic by secretly observing and jotting down Homer's antics. The character's signature trait is exploding with rage over minor mishaps that are usually caused by his own foolishness, with his fury wildly disproportionate to the actual problem. When shown as a youth, the character is rebranded as Angry Kid instead of Angry Dad. The comic strip became a beloved hit among Bart's schoolmates, eventually spinning off into a short-lived animated webcomic through BetterThanTV.com before that company folded. Bart picked Dan Castellaneta to voice the animated version specifically because his voice was a dead ringer for Homer's, though ironically Homer himself ended up voicing Angry Dad in the later movie adaptation after Castellaneta lost his voice from shouting over a pay dispute. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Ben (Summer of 4 Ft. 2)
text: Ben (Summer of 4 Ft. 2) is One of the 'cool kids' Lisa befriends at the beach in the episode "Summer of 4 Ft. 2". Ben is a laid-back, easygoing beach kid Lisa meets under the pier in Little Pwagmattasquarmsettport during a family summer vacation. He and his friends welcome Lisa into their group, enjoying her company and her knowledge of sea life, unaware that back home she's seen as an unpopular nerd. When Bart exposes Lisa's true reputation, threatening to ruin her new friendships, Ben and the others prove surprisingly forgiving and kind-hearted. Rather than rejecting her, they show their affection by decorating the Simpsons' car with seashells as a parting gift. Ben leaves Lisa with a warm, reassuring sentiment about carrying good memories with her wherever she goes. He represents the fleeting but meaningful friendships of childhood summers, and the idea that true acceptance isn't bound by social status. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: "You could take the beach with you wherever you go."
quotes: "You could take the beach with you wherever you go."

title: Buzz Aldrin (character)
text: Buzz Aldrin (character) is Real-life astronaut who appears as a guest character, flying with Homer Simpson aboard the space shuttle. Buzz Aldrin appears as himself, the famed second man to walk on the Moon, brought in as a celebrity astronaut on a space shuttle mission alongside Homer Simpson. Unlike his more dismissive crewmate Race Banyon, Aldrin is polite and respectful toward Homer, even as he can't help being baffled by Homer's sheer incompetence and foolishness. During an onboard emergency, he serves as the calm, rational figure, trying to keep the crew focused despite distractions like James Taylor's ill-timed musical performance. Ultimately, he's gracious enough to credit Homer as the hero who saved the mission using a simple carbon rod. His appearance is largely a one-off cameo tied to a famous episode, though he's referenced again as a notable left-handed celebrity on one of Ned Flanders' lists. Overall, he embodies a good-natured, dignified real-world figure dropped into Homer's chaotic orbit. Voiced by Himself.

title: Baby Button-Eyes
text: Baby Button-Eyes is Fictional killer doll monster featured in a horror movie-within-the-show, seen at Springfield Googolplex Theatres. Baby Button-Eyes is a fictional horror movie villain within the Simpsons universe, appearing in the in-universe slasher film 'The Re-Deadening.' She is a possessed doll driven by murderous intent, killing anyone unlucky enough to cross her path, including a gardener character played by Lenny Leonard. Beyond her own violent rampage, she has the sinister ability to manipulate others into committing murder, as shown when she convinces a young girl to kill her own mother. A recurring gag surrounding her is her seeming indestructibility, appearing dead only to rise again and strike once more. She's clearly modeled after other iconic possessed-doll horror icons, drawing comparisons to both Dolly Dearest and Chucky. Baby Button-Eyes never appears outside of this movie-parody context and has no spoken dialogue herself. Notable quotes: "Well, what do you know? It's unkillable!" - Homer Simpson
quotes: "Well, what do you know? It's unkillable!" - Homer Simpson

title: The Aristocrat's bartender
text: The Aristocrat's bartender is Minor recurring character; bartender at a rundown bar called The Aristocrat. This gruff, balding barkeep runs a decidedly less friendly establishment than Moe's Tavern. He's quick to pull a massive shotgun on customers, showing just how little patience he has for newcomers like Homer. Despite his intimidating demeanor, he grudgingly complies with requests, though not without a healthy dose of sarcasm. His bar seems to struggle for business, leading him to attend gatherings with other bartenders to brainstorm ways to attract more customers. Overall, he represents the seedier, more dangerous side of Springfield's drinking establishments compared to the more familiar Moe's. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Your Majesty
quotes: Your Majesty

title: Tina Belcher
text: Tina Belcher is Crossover character from Bob's Burgers who appears in The Simpsons during special crossover segments. Tina Belcher is a member of the Belcher family from Bob's Burgers who crosses over into The Simpsons universe in a couch gag and a special appearance. She's shown observing Homer's antics with a dry, matter-of-fact curiosity, offering odd interpretations of what she witnesses. Her brief appearances place her alongside her parents Linda and Bob, and her siblings Gene and Louise, keeping the Belcher family unit intact even outside their own show. As a non-canon character, she exists purely for crossover fun rather than ongoing Simpsons continuity. Her commentary tends to be quirky and slightly awkward, fitting her known personality from her home series. Voiced by Dan Mintz. Notable quotes: She said that Bob Number 2 was thrown out some "major tootering".
quotes: She said that Bob Number 2 was thrown out some "major tootering".

title: Mama Celeste
text: Mama Celeste is Mascot of the fictional Mama Celeste Sausage Pizza brand, appearing on food packaging. Mama Celeste is a minor, cartoonish figure who exists solely as the smiling face on a pizza box label rather than a real character in Springfield. She becomes the object of Homer's brief, silly infatuation when he tries to match Marge's own fantasy about a towel-brand model, staring lustfully at the pizza label. True to her stern, matronly image, she snaps back at him with a threat involving her pizza cutter, showing she's not to be trifled with despite being a mere advertising illustration. The joke draws on the real-world history of the Celeste frozen pizza brand, which was named after an actual Italian immigrant restaurateur who became the face of her own product line. Beyond this one gag, Mama Celeste has no real presence in the show, appearing only as a background billboard image in a Simpsons video game. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: You touch-a me and I cut you. - Mama Celeste
quotes: You touch-a me and I cut you. - Mama Celeste

title: Bizarro
text: Bizarro is A fictional supervillain from the DC Comics universe, referenced within the Simpsons comic continuity. Bizarro is not an original Simpsons character but a nod to the classic DC Comics villain of the same name, existing only as a pop-culture reference within the show's universe. He never appears as a physical character in his own right; instead, he's invoked through the fandom of Comic Book Guy, who dresses as Bizarro for a costume contest at a comic convention. Homer also briefly imagines what Bizarro and Superman would do while struggling to control a runaway truck, showing how deeply comic book lore has seeped into Springfield's collective consciousness. As a crossover character, Bizarro exists purely as a background gag tying the show's comic-obsessed characters to real-world superhero mythology. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent parody of comic fandom rather than serving any plot-driving purpose.

title: Benjamin (Go Big or Go Homer)
text: Benjamin (Go Big or Go Homer) is An intern at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. Benjamin is a minor, largely background character who works as one of the interns at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. He's part of a group dynamic where he and his fellow interns get mocked and yelled at by their exasperated supervisor. He seems to go along with the crowd, laughing at Homer's expense alongside the other interns rather than standing out on his own. In a non-canon appearance, he shows a bit more initiative, agreeing to help Homer with a tedious task involving a spreadsheet. Overall, he functions as one of many faceless power plant employees rather than a fully fleshed-out character, appearing only briefly across two episodes. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Mel Brooks (character)
text: Mel Brooks (character) is Real-life celebrity guest character; American actor, comedian, and filmmaker who appears as himself in the Simpsons universe. Mel Brooks appears as a fictionalized version of himself within the Simpsons world, referenced first as one of several famous Jewish entertainers that surprises Homer. His most notable appearance comes when Homer, moonlighting as a limo driver to pay off a debt to Patty and Selma, picks him up as his very first fare. The encounter turns into a comedic bit where Homer begs Brooks to reenact a routine from his own life, revealing Homer's fanboyish love for his film work, especially Young Frankenstein. The scene escalates into slapstick chaos when Chief Wiggum arrests Homer for driving without a license and then tries to get in on the same bit with Brooks himself. Beyond this, he's mentioned in passing as an owner of a personal tennis court and shows up as a background picture during a musical number, underscoring his status as a recurring pop-culture reference rather than a fleshed-out character. Voiced by Mel Brooks (Himself).

title: Cayman Islands banker
text: Cayman Islands banker is Krusty the Clown's offshore banker in the Cayman Islands, appearing in a minor role in the episode "Bart the Fink". This gray-haired, balding banker manages a secret offshore account for Krusty at a Cayman Islands holding corporation. He becomes briefly relevant when Bart, trying to get Krusty's autograph, inadvertently uncovers evidence of the clown's illegal finances. When a Springfield bank teller calls to verify the account, the banker carelessly confirms its existence and hints at its illicit nature before catching himself and awkwardly trying to cover his slip. His flustered excuse of blaming the heat for his indiscretion gives him a comedic, bumbling quality despite his role in a serious financial subplot. Visually and thematically, he's designed as a nod to classic film archetypes, being modeled after Sydney Greenstreet's character in Casablanca. Though a minor character with only one canonical appearance, he later resurfaced in The Simpsons: Tapped Out as a business-owner character. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Bellboy
text: Bellboy is Minor recurring character; an unnamed bellboy at the Capital City Plaza Hotel who appears during Homer's stay. The Bellboy is a minor, comedic figure whose defining trait is his suggestive sound effects, which he uses to imply sexual activity whenever showing guests to their rooms. He assumes Homer is at the hotel for a tryst with Mindy Simmons and eagerly hints at this with his noises, only to be told plainly by Homer that the bed is for sleeping and eating, not that. His running gag continues later when he's spotted operating a floor buffer that eerily mimics Marge's disapproving groan. He can't seem to help himself, and later barges into Homer and Marge's room making the same suggestive noises again, which finally earns him a punch in the eye from an annoyed Homer. Despite this one-off appearance, he's remembered fondly enough to show up in a clip show flashback and a brief cameo in a later episode. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: TV's there, bathroom's there and there's your king-sized bed for (makes various sound effects)
quotes: TV's there, bathroom's there and there's your king-sized bed for (makes various sound effects)

title: Ms. Cantwell
text: Ms. Cantwell is A substitute teacher at Springfield Elementary who filled in for Elizabeth Hoover. Ms. Cantwell arrives at Springfield Elementary as a substitute while Miss Hoover is out with depression, initially impressing Lisa Simpson with her teaching. Her friendly facade quickly fades, and she begins targeting Lisa with unfair grading and bullying, seemingly just to assert power over her. When Lisa's parents try to intervene, school administrators dismiss their concerns, forcing Homer to enlist Edna Krabappel's help to drive Cantwell out. Her undoing comes courtesy of Bart, who wrecks her classroom and humiliates her, prompting her to flee the school entirely. In a rare moment of vulnerability, she admits to Lisa that her cruelty stemmed from jealousy over Lisa's looks and popularity. Despite the scandal, she later resurfaces attending a school fundraiser, showing no lasting consequences for her behavior. Voiced by Tina Fey.

title: Bearded lady (Krusty the Clown)
text: Bearded lady (Krusty the Clown) is A circus performer at Ding-A-Ling Bros. Circus and brief love interest of Krusty the Clown. The bearded lady is a minor circus act whose life briefly intersects with Krusty the Clown's when he goes undercover as a performer named Soggy the Clown. She falls for him after his act becomes a hit, forming a short-lived romance amid the circus's financial troubles. Her defining moment of vulnerability comes when she's about to shave off her signature beard out of desperation to save the failing circus, only for Krusty to intervene. His grand gesture of turning himself into the police to fund the circus doesn't quite earn him a storybook ending, though—she rewards him with a kiss followed swiftly by a knee to the gut. She's a one-episode character rather than a recurring fixture, existing mainly to add color to the circus subplot and to give Krusty a bittersweet romantic beat. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Bambi
text: Bambi is A baby deer referenced/used in a Simpsons courtroom scene, based on the Disney character. Bambi is a minor, non-speaking crossover character based on the classic Disney deer of the same name. In the show's canon, he is invoked during a courtroom scene where Wallace Brady uses the death of Bambi's mother to argue against evolution, blaming it for the forest fire that killed her. Beyond this brief mention, Bambi mostly appears in non-canon material, including a Christmas and Mother's Day special where he and his mother face danger from hunters. His running trait is essentially being a symbol of tragic loss, referencing the famous emotional scene from the original Disney film. He never speaks and functions purely as a background or referential character rather than a developed personality within the Simpsons universe.

title: Barbara Bush
text: Barbara Bush is Wife of former U.S. President George Bush, who briefly becomes the Simpsons' neighbor. Barbara Bush appears as a dignified but easily flustered First Lady during the Simpsons' visit to the White House. She is initially outraged when the family wanders into her private quarters and catches her in the bathtub, but she quickly composes herself upon learning they are VIP guests. Her demeanor is far warmer later on, when she and her husband end up living across the street from the Simpsons. In this later appearance, she bonds with Marge over their shared exasperation at their husbands' immature rivalry, showing a more relatable, down-to-earth side. Overall, she's portrayed as a patient, sensible counterpart to the more short-tempered George Bush. Voiced by Maggie Roswell.

title: BB-8
text: BB-8 is A Star Wars droid crossover character appearing in Simpsons Star Wars-themed episodes and shorts. BB-8 is a droid borrowed from the Star Wars universe, appearing in various Simpsons crossover segments. In canon, Bart and Lisa use BB-8-like droids as makeshift tools to carry Wakkety Yak out of J.J. Abrams Productions. In non-canon material, BB-8 forms a sweet bond with baby Maggie, first meeting her at Jabba's Hut Jedi Preschool where it helps retrieve her lost pacifier despite being attacked by other droids and even stabbed by Gerald dressed as Darth Maul. BB-8 continues to look out for Maggie across several specials, later finding her after an accident and journeying with her to a desert planet, and again turning up with a replacement pacifier from Grogu's pram. Another BB-8 droid meets a more explosive fate when Marge accidentally causes it to fly out of a window and blow up. Overall, BB-8 functions as a recurring, non-speaking crossover gag tied to the show's Star Wars parody specials.

title: Baby Bear
text: Baby Bear is Fictional baby bear character from the "Goldilocks and the Three Bears" story as retold/depicted within The Simpsons. Baby Bear is the young offspring of Papa Bear and Mama Bear, appearing in various Simpsons adaptations of the classic fairy tale Goldilocks and the Three Bears. He's first seen in a version of the story told by Bart to Maggie, where he delivers a cheeky line upon finding Goldilocks asleep in his bed before the family devours her. He also appears as an animatronic figure at a Bears' house attraction during a family outing, and in a darker, non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment where the bears violently attack Goldilocks. Baby Bear's characterization is minimal and largely serves as a vehicle for parody and dark humor rather than deep personality traits. His recurring gag involves twisted, exaggerated versions of the fairy tale ending, ranging from comedic to horrific. Voiced by Pamela Hayden, Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: Hey, look, man—breakfast in bed!
quotes: Hey, look, man—breakfast in bed!

title: Humphrey Bogart
text: Humphrey Bogart is Real-world actor referenced within the Simpsons universe, famous for his role in Casablanca. Humphrey Bogart appears in the show as a real-world Hollywood legend rather than a fictional Springfield resident. He's invoked by Homer as a historical precedent for minor mischief, since Bogart's own handprints marred a Hollywood sidewalk long ago. His most direct appearance comes through a treasure hunt involving a buried film canister containing an alternate ending to his classic movie Casablanca. Bogart's image and legacy pop up in odd places around Springfield, from a photo on a restaurant wall to a joke tombstone for a snake with a similar name. He's also humorously listed among a string of old Hollywood leading men rumored to have romanced Abe Simpson's wartime girlfriend. Overall, Bogart functions as a nostalgic pop-culture reference rather than a fleshed-out character. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Dr. Babcock
text: Dr. Babcock is NASA scientist involved in recruiting an 'everyman' astronaut, most notably in the episode "Deep Space Homer". Dr. Babcock is a cynical, ratings-obsessed NASA scientist who cares more about television viewership than actual space exploration. He hatches the plan to send an ordinary American into space to boost sagging ratings, deliberately dragging out the selection process to waste taxpayer money. He's shown to be impatient and quick to resort to violence, knocking out both Homer and Barney more than once during the course of the story. Despite overseeing serious astronaut training, his priorities remain shallow, caring only about broadcast numbers rather than the mission's success. He later resurfaces as part of a conspiracy to fake Mars rover footage and moon landings in the Springfield desert, revealing a willingness to deceive the public entirely for the sake of NASA's image. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Carl Carlson, Sr.
text: Carl Carlson, Sr. is Adoptive father of Carl Carlson, resident of Iceland. Carl Carlson, Sr. is an Icelandic man who, alongside his wife Sigrin, adopted Carl Carlson. His family, the Carlsons, carry a centuries-old shameful legacy as coastal watchmen who failed to stop an invasion of Iceland, a disgrace they long denied by insisting their ancestors fought bravely. Because of this dark family history, the Carlsons were treated as outcasts by their community for generations. When his son Carl returns to Iceland to buy back a missing page of the family saga in an attempt to clear their name, the truth turns out to be even worse than believed. Ultimately, it's not historical vindication but Carl's good deeds toward his friends that redeem the family's reputation, allowing Carl Sr. and Sigrin to finally be accepted by their neighbors. Beyond this storyline, little else is shown of him, though a photo of him and his wife is seen displayed in Carl's home. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Black teacher
text: Black teacher is An unnamed background teacher at Springfield Elementary School. This nameless faculty member is one of the many background teachers who populate Springfield Elementary School. He's shown as an engaged, if put-upon, member of the staff, joining his colleagues in griping about Principal Skinner's tight budget for school supplies and activities. He reacts with alarm when he learns that all the Teacher's Edition textbooks have gone missing, suggesting he relies heavily on them for his lessons. He's also present for major school-wide crises, such as the reveal that Springfield Elementary lost its oil money due to Mr. Burns' illegal drilling, and he later attends an emergency union meeting called by the teachers. Like many of Springfield Elementary's supporting teachers, he mostly exists to fill out crowd scenes during faculty disputes and announcements rather than to drive the plot himself. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Does anyone know the multiplication table?
quotes: Does anyone know the multiplication table?

title: Air Springfield flight attendant (2)
text: Air Springfield flight attendant (2) is A minor, unnamed flight attendant working for Air Springfield and Convenience Airways. This character is a background flight attendant who appears briefly in connection with Homer Simpson's air travel misadventures. She has black hair and works for both Air Springfield and Convenience Airways, suggesting she may be a recurring but unnamed staff member across different airline-related storylines. Her most notable moment involves chasing Homer down the aisle of a plane, acting under the direction of an air marshal to physically restrain him. She has no deep characterization beyond her professional role and this single dramatic incident. As a minor recurring character, she represents the show's tendency to populate its world with functional, nameless service workers who occasionally get pulled into the chaos surrounding the main cast. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Rhett Butler
text: Rhett Butler is Fictional character from Gone with the Wind who appears as a movie character within The Simpsons universe. Rhett Butler is not an original Simpsons character but rather a parody appearance of the classic Gone with the Wind film character, originally played by Clark Gable in the real-world movie. Within the show, he pops up in edited or referenced clips of the film, tying into different episode storylines rather than existing as a standalone personality with his own running gags. His most notable connection comes through a nostalgic tale from Abe Simpson, who recalls shining Clark Gable's shoes as a boy and even gifting him a copy of the Gone with the Wind novel. He also appears in a romantic movie montage juxtaposed with a CPR scene involving Bart, using his iconic on-screen romance with Scarlett O'Hara for comedic effect. Essentially, Rhett Butler functions as a crossover/cameo figure used to reference classic Hollywood cinema rather than a fully developed Springfield resident. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Caribbean outcast
text: Caribbean outcast is A minor recurring member of the Lost Souls, a group of drifters sailing the seas on the Ship of Lost Souls. The Caribbean outcast is a bald, world-weary wanderer who belongs to a mysterious crew of outcasts adrift at sea, each nursing untold personal tragedies. He keeps his own backstory a secret, never sharing it with anyone, including Homer. His one notable moment comes when he reacts with shock to Homer's confession about abandoning his father at the hospital instead of donating a kidney. That shocked reaction helps spur the group's decision to toss Homer overboard. He later appears briefly again when Homer nearly collides with the Ship of Lost Souls while piloting his own boat. Like the rest of the Lost Souls, he embodies a somber, mysterious archetype rather than a fully fleshed-out personality. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "good lord!"
quotes: "good lord!"

title: Ballet teacher
text: Ballet teacher is Minor recurring character; ballet instructor at Springfield Elementary School who teaches Bart Simpson. The ballet teacher is a minor, unnamed figure at Springfield Elementary School who is best known for discovering that Bart Simpson has a hidden talent for ballet. She appears only sporadically, popping up in scenes unrelated to dance, such as a record-breaking human pyramid attempt and a town meeting about lake pollution. Despite her limited screen time, she has recurring appearances across several episodes and even the movie, suggesting she's a recognizable part of Springfield's background community. Her character has no strong personality traits highlighted in canon beyond her profession, making her more of a functional cameo than a fleshed-out character. She's notable mainly for being voiced by a celebrity guest star, adding a bit of star power to an otherwise background role. Voiced by Susan Sarandon.

title: Bartron
text: Bartron is An imaginary alter-ego/alias of Bart Simpson, used during pretend play and pranks. Bartron is not a separate character but a make-believe persona Bart Simpson adopts during games and pranks. The identity originated when Lisa dubbed Bart 'Bartron, an evil robot from Mars gone berserk' while the siblings played 'Space Patrol' with saucepans and a vase on their heads. Bart later revived the alias for mischief, using it to prank Homer over the radio by claiming he'd eaten the president and planned to take over the world. He also used the name as a covert code when sneaking out with Milhouse to attend a comic expo. The character showcases Bart's playful, mischievous nature and his love of imaginative role-play and pranks. Bartron never appears as an independent entity, existing only as an extension of Bart's imagination and troublemaking antics. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: an evil robot from Mars gone berserk
quotes: an evil robot from Mars gone berserk

title: Gary Busey (character)
text: Gary Busey (character) is Celebrity guest character based on the real actor, appearing as himself in an episode about restraining orders. Gary Busey appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, best known for an odd instructional-style appearance explaining the ins and outs of restraining orders. He hosts a video guide on the subject and follows it with a second tape demonstrating how to obtain one, blurring the line between educational content and his own bizarre personal life. In a strange twist, he reveals he was actually a character in his own example video, having been the subject of a restraining order taken out by twelve different women and a film company because he is, in his own words, "too real." This self-referential, larger-than-life eccentricity is very much in keeping with the real Gary Busey's offbeat public persona. In a non-canon appearance, he's shown as an unprepared guest star on a fictional Simpsons variety show spin-off, arriving on a motorcycle without ever having seen a script or learned his lines, poking fun at chaotic behind-the-scenes show business mishaps. Voiced by Gary Busey (Himself). Notable quotes: Mary was 12 different women and a small film company, and they had gotten a restraining order against him as he's too real.
quotes: Mary was 12 different women and a small film company, and they had gotten a restraining order against him as he's too real.

title: Red Barclay
text: Red Barclay is A one-time trucker character who briefly crosses paths with Homer at a truck stop diner. Red Barclay is a burly trucker Homer encounters at The Slaughterhouse diner, where the two end up in a fierce eating contest over a massive steak called the Sir Loins-a-Lot. Red proves victorious, becoming only the second person ever to finish the dish within the time limit, but his triumph is short-lived as he immediately drops dead from beef poisoning. His death leaves behind an unfinished trucking job, which Homer inherits along with Red's distinctive red truck. Though he only appears briefly, Red's fate becomes something of a dark punchline, with a stranger later reacting to news of his demise as if it were an unsurprising, almost routine occurrence. He's remembered mainly as the guy whose sudden death kicks off Homer's cross-country trucking misadventure. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Sounds like ol' Red, all right.
quotes: Sounds like ol' Red, all right.

title: Louis Armstrong
text: Louis Armstrong is Fantasy/vision character based on the real-life jazz musician, appearing to Lisa Simpson. Louis Armstrong appears in Lisa's imagination as a wise, encouraging figure who helps her reconnect with her love of jazz and confidence as a musician. He first manifests as a statue that comes to life, offering Lisa advice about life and family before nearly performing his famous song for her and Homer. In a later dream sequence he returns as a sweaty, shirt-craving ghost who admits he'd love to be alive again. He resurfaces once more in one of Lisa's patriotic fantasies, showing a bit of exasperation at being repeatedly summoned into her thoughts. Even in the afterlife, he retains a laid-back, witty personality, including a joke about crossing into Canada for legalized cannabis. Overall, he serves as a recurring spiritual mentor figure who blends historical reverence with comedic, offbeat humor. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson. Notable quotes: your father knows best. | he was going to get cannabis as it was made legal.
quotes: your father knows best.
he was going to get cannabis as it was made legal.

title: Gene Belcher
text: Gene Belcher is Crossover character from Bob's Burgers who appears in a non-canon capacity in The Simpsons. Gene Belcher is one of the three Belcher children who crosses over from the animated series Bob's Burgers into a non-canon Simpsons appearance. He's shown as a curious, cheeky kid who isn't shy about speaking his mind, whether he's asking to keep a strange visitor or offering to clean up after him. His dialogue reflects a playful, slightly mischievous sense of humor typical of younger sibling characters, often chiming in with quick, offbeat remarks. Gene appears alongside his parents Bob and Linda and his sisters Tina and Louise, functioning as part of a family unit rather than a solo character. His inclusion is part of a broader gag involving Homer wandering into the Bob's Burgers restaurant, blending the two shows' universes for comedic effect. He also shows up in a later special tied to streaming service in-jokes, reinforcing his status as a guest/crossover character rather than a core Simpsons cast member. Voiced by Eugene Mirman. Notable quotes: "no way" - Gene Belcher
quotes: "no way" - Gene Belcher

title: Joe Camel
text: Joe Camel is A real-world advertising mascot for R. J. Reynolds Tobacco Company, referenced within the Simpsons universe rather than an original character. Joe Camel isn't a character created for the show but a famous cigarette-brand mascot who gets namechecked and briefly pictured within the Simpsons world. He's brought up by radio host Birch Barlow as an example of a public figure he believes was unfairly persecuted, lumped in with real political figures. Later, Barney recalls Joe Camel alongside the Frito Bandito as mascots who were pulled from advertising, drawing a parallel to Duffman's situation. In the non-canon Simpsons Animal Stories comic, he even shows up in person to visit Bart while Bart and Milhouse play a board game. His appearances are brief and mostly serve as topical, satirical references to real advertising controversies rather than establishing him as a recurring character with his own personality.

title: Blue
text: Blue is A dog belonging to an unnamed Springfield hobo, appearing occasionally in the background of episodes. Blue is a minor animal character in The Simpsons universe, notable mainly for his association with one of Springfield's homeless residents. He has popped up in a handful of episodes doing unremarkable dog things, like napping on Homer's work console or drinking water off a coworker's cleaning tool. A quirky running gag surrounding him is that his fur color inexplicably changes from appearance to appearance, despite always being called Blue. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, his barking incidentally saves his owner from being devoured alive by a monstrous blob version of Homer, giving him a rare moment of narrative importance. Overall, Blue functions as background texture for Springfield's homeless community rather than a fully developed character.

title: Angelo
text: Angelo is Minor recurring character, an employee at Luigi's and sub-contractor for J&J Construction. Angelo is a quirky background character who pops up in odd service roles around Springfield. At Luigi's restaurant, his peculiar job is to chew food for customers who can't or won't chew it themselves, which he seems oddly content doing. He later turns up as a sub-contractor helping build a kitchen for the Simpson family, where he reveals another unusual specialty: kissing on behalf of a contractor who identifies as gay. Both instances play into a running gag of Angelo having strange, hyper-specific personal services he performs for others without any apparent embarrassment. He's also glimpsed as a face in the crowd during a political rally, showing he exists as a recognizable Springfield townsperson beyond his odd jobs. Overall, Angelo is a one-note gag character defined by his bizarrely literal job descriptions. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: I like to chew. | I like to kiss.
quotes: I like to chew.
I like to kiss.

title: Jon Bon Jovi
text: Jon Bon Jovi is Real-world celebrity referenced in the show; musician whose likeness/work appears as background detail. Jon Bon Jovi appears in the Simpsons universe as himself, a real-world rock musician acknowledged rather than portrayed as an active character. A bust of him is seen displayed in Louie's home, hinting at the mobster's fandom. His album Christmas in the Stars is also noted as one of Comic Book Guy's favorite records, tying him into the show's pop-culture obsessed universe. Interestingly, Bon Jovi was originally approached to appear in a season 14 episode but declined, and the role ultimately went to fellow musician Jackson Browne instead. He never actually speaks or performs as a character on screen, existing only through these small references and cameo-like appearances.

title: Brenda (Brawl in the Family)
text: Brenda (Brawl in the Family) is A police-dispatched robot negotiator who appears in a Simpsons family domestic disturbance incident. Brenda is a robotic negotiator, or 'negotia-bot,' deployed by the police to defuse tense domestic situations. Her unconventional method of conflict resolution involves shooting taffy from a built-in tube, which she used to physically trap the entire Simpson family inside a giant sticky ball. After immobilizing the family this way, she dragged them out onto their front lawn for the authorities to handle. Chief Wiggum ultimately shut her down and took over the situation himself, suggesting her methods were seen as excessive or unnecessary once the family was subdued. Brenda's brief appearance highlights the show's penchant for absurd, over-the-top technology solutions to mundane problems. She later reappears in a non-canon capacity within The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Robert Chan
text: Robert Chan is CEO of Tianjin Mining and Smelting and Donuts and Tarps, a minor businessman character in the Simpsons universe. Robert Chan is a corporate executive whose company has an oddly broad portfolio spanning mining, smelting, donuts, and tarps. He is best known for presiding over the unveiling of the new Lard Lad Donuts statue, bringing in the original mascot inspiration, Laird Ladd, for the ceremony. Things go awry when sunlight reflects off the statue into a destructive beam that devastates Springfield, and in a bit of dark comedy, his own company is the one that supplies the tarp used to cover up the statue afterward. He mainly appears as a background/dialogue figure rather than a fully fleshed-out personality, functioning more as a punchline about corporate conglomerates than a deep character. Chan also appears in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out as part of the Battle of the Brands content. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Ant-Man
text: Ant-Man is Marvel Comics superhero who appears as a non-canon crossover character in The Simpsons specials. Ant-Man is a Marvel superhero who exists outside the show's normal continuity, appearing only in special crossover episodes. He is notably referenced through Ned Flanders, who dons an Ant-Man costume while acting as a member of the Springfield Avengers. In another special, Ant-Man appears alongside Jiminy Cricket in a near-miss incident involving Cinderella. He is a non-speaking character, existing mostly as a visual cameo or costume rather than a fleshed-out personality within the Simpsons universe. His appearances tie into the show's occasional forays into superhero parody and crossover events.

title: Rosa Barks
text: Rosa Barks is The Hibbert family's pet poodle, and mate of the Simpsons' dog Santa's Little Helper. Rosa Barks is a white poodle who belongs to the Hibbert family. She's best known for her fling with the Simpsons' dog, Santa's Little Helper, which Dr. Hibbert bluntly describes as a 'booty call.' That encounter results in a litter of eight Greyhound-Poodle mixed puppies, who end up being foster-dumped onto the Simpson family since Homer never got around to having Santa's Little Helper neutered. The puppies are eventually distributed to various Springfield residents, giving Rosa an indirect connection to several other side characters. She later reappears during Springfield's brief stint as a dog-friendly, dog-ruled town. As a non-speaking animal character, she has no personality quirks beyond being a pet and occasional plot device for canine chaos.

title: Libby Biaz
text: Libby Biaz is A publicist character appearing in Radioactive Man-related Bongo comics. Libby Biaz is a savvy publicist who specializes in image rehabilitation, capable of turning around sagging careers and arranging beneficial public appearances for her clients. She operates on a business model that includes taking a 20% commission for her services. Her most notable involvement was helping Fallout Boy, who came to her seeking a change of image after growing tired of being merely a sidekick. She devised a plan for him to infiltrate the Bang Gang undercover in order to dismantle it from within. When Fallout Boy succeeded in reforming the group into doing good deeds instead, the entire Bang Gang ended up signing on as her clients, showing her effectiveness at spinning even villains into positive public figures.

title: Wallace Brady
text: Wallace Brady is A southern lawyer who opposed Lisa Simpson in the courtroom battle of Lisa vs. God. Wallace Brady is a smooth-talking southern attorney who represents the opposition in Lisa's legal fight over the teaching of evolution versus creationism. He leans heavily on courtroom theatrics, bringing in a Christian scientist to bolster his case and dismissing evolution as nothing more than 'Hollywood hooey.' In a memorably manipulative move, he cradles a baby deer he calls Bambi on his lap while spinning a tearful story blaming evolution for a forest fire that supposedly killed the deer's mother. His folksy charm and emotional manipulation tactics make him a formidable, if morally questionable, opponent in the case. Brady appears only briefly in the show's run but leaves an impression as a slick manipulator of public sentiment. Voiced by Larry Hagman.

title: Beatrice (senior)
text: Beatrice (senior) is A minor resident of the Springfield Retirement Castle, briefly acquainted with Homer. Beatrice is an elderly woman living out her later years at the Springfield Retirement Castle. She's a background figure among the retirement home's residents, known to Homer through his time spent visiting the facility. She's often seen in the company of fellow seniors like Hattie and Asa, suggesting she's part of a small social circle within the home. As a non-speaking character, little is revealed about her personality or backstory beyond her presence in a couple of episodes. She represents one of the many elderly extras that populate the retirement castle setting used for storylines involving Abe Simpson and other seniors.

title: Alcatraaaz
text: Alcatraaaz is A famous gangster rapper favored by Bart Simpson. Alcatraaaz is a celebrity gangster rapper whose music and persona captivate Bart, prompting him to sneak out to attend one of his shows. He proves surprisingly friendly and accommodating, letting Bart join him onstage and even taking him for a ride in his lavish limo, complete with an odd wax museum. His mansion and entourage reflect an over-the-top hip-hop lifestyle, including armed gang members who are quick to react to disturbances. Despite his tough exterior, he shows a laid-back, welcoming side by throwing impromptu house parties and mingling with Springfield residents like Principal Skinner. He also has a habit of appearing at other celebrities' functions, showing he's a fixture in the wider entertainment world. His name is a playful nod to the infamous Alcatraz prison, fitting his gangster rap image. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "put it down unless he knew how to use it" | "a forty-something elementary school administrator"
quotes: "put it down unless he knew how to use it"
"a forty-something elementary school administrator"

title: Airshot
text: Airshot is A superhero member of the Vindicators team within the fictional Vindicators film franchise watched by Simpsons characters. Airshot is a fictional superhero who fights alongside the Vindicators, wielding a powerful air cannon as his signature weapon. He never speaks on screen, letting his explosive gunplay do the talking instead. In the films, he plays a key role in battling the villain Chinnos, at one point blasting the villain's head clean off before being turned to crystal like the rest of his team. His character is a clear parody of Hawkeye from the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Airshot's fictional death becomes a pivotal plot point in Bart's story when a spoiler ruins the emotional impact of his heroic final stand, teaching Bart a lesson about the dangers of spoiling media for others. Merchandise like figures and standees of Airshot appear in Comic Book Guy's collection, underscoring his status as a beloved figure within the show's superhero-fandom subplot.

title: Balrog
text: Balrog is Non-canon demonic creature encountered by the Fellowship of the Ring in a Simpsons comic parody. The Balrog is a massive, fearsome demonic monster that appears in a Lord of the Rings-themed Simpsons comic story. It emerges after the Fellowship of the Ring escapes through a crack in a wall, setting up a confrontation with Homer's group. True to the show's comedic style, the terrifying beast is defeated in an absurdly mundane way rather than through any epic battle. The character exists purely as a parody reference to Tolkien's mythology rather than a serious antagonist. It later gets a humorous nod in a video game poster, cementing its status as a one-off joke rather than a recurring threat. Overall, the Balrog serves as a quick gag tied to crossover parody content rather than a fleshed-out character. Notable quotes: Live nude Balrogs!!
quotes: Live nude Balrogs!!

title: Calvin (Step Brother from the Same Planet)
keys: calvin (step brother from the same planet)
text: Calvin (Step Brother from the Same Planet) is Adopted son of Blythe, Grampa's girlfriend, and a temporary rival/step-brother figure to Homer. Calvin is an eleven-year-old boy with an unusual passion for taxidermy, adopted by Blythe, who briefly dates Grampa Simpson. He becomes a source of jealousy for Homer, since Grampa dotes on Calvin in ways he never did for his own son, sparking a bitter prank war between the two when Homer is forced to stay in Calvin's room. Despite the initial animosity, Calvin proves surprisingly perceptive and kind-hearted, softening toward Homer once he understands the root of his resentment. He even gives Homer genuine advice about confronting Grampa honestly rather than resorting to petty revenge. Notably, Calvin holds the distinction of being the first male Simpsons character voiced by a female guest star. His story ends on a bittersweet note when Blythe leaves Grampa for another man who takes Calvin to Africa to study animals. Voiced by Melissa McCarthy.

title: Joan Bushwell
text: Joan Bushwell is A chimpanzee researcher the Simpsons encounter during their trip to Tanzania in "Simpson Safari". Joan Bushwell is a scientist devoted to studying chimpanzees, running a refuge that inspired Lisa's admiration for her work. She presents herself as a dedicated researcher who rises early and spends her days observing the animals in her care. However, her seemingly noble mission hides a dark secret: she has been exploiting the chimps as forced labor to mine diamonds hidden beneath her refuge. When Greenpeace activists show up to expose and stop her operation, she manages to buy the Simpsons' silence with diamonds rather than facing consequences. Her character serves as a satirical jab at the exploitation sometimes hidden behind environmental or scientific goodwill, and she is loosely modeled on real-life primatologist Jane Goodall. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Bartdog
text: Bartdog is Non-canon comic book character; the superhero alter-ego of Santa's Little Helper and sidekick to Bartman. Bartdog is the crime-fighting persona given to Santa's Little Helper after Bartman injures his ankle and needs a way to get around Springfield. Rigged to a skateboard, he becomes both a mode of transportation and a loyal fighting partner for Bartman. Despite being a dog, he shows surprising bravery, attacking the villain Canker and helping unmask him as Mr. Burns in disguise. He's easily distracted by simple canine temptations, as shown when Smithers manages to stop him with a squeaky hot dog toy. Bartdog plays a key role in leading the heroes to the true mastermind behind the comic's plot, and later becomes a bargaining chip when Patty and Selma capture him to negotiate with Kent Brockman. He only appears in this one non-canon comic story, making him a minor but memorable one-off character in the Bongo comics continuity.

title: Evelyn Burns
text: Evelyn Burns is Mr. Burns' paternal grandmother, a member of the extended Burns family. Evelyn Burns was born Evelyn Graycomb, the daughter of Otto and Lolly Graycomb, and sister to Axel and Amos. She married Wainwright Montgomery Burns and became part of the wealthy Burns lineage, giving birth to Clifford and Doreena Burns. As Mr. Burns' grandmother, she represents a small piece of the sprawling, aristocratic family tree that stretches back generations in the show's supplementary material. She is a non-speaking, picture-only character, existing mainly as a genealogical footnote rather than an active presence in any episode. Her inclusion highlights the show's penchant for building out elaborate, often satirical family histories for its wealthiest characters. She has since passed away, being listed among the deceased members of the Burns family.

title: Ernst Stavro Blofeld
text: Ernst Stavro Blofeld is A parody James Bond supervillain character appearing briefly in The Simpsons. Ernst Stavro Blofeld is a caricature of the classic James Bond villain, appearing in The Simpsons as a fantasy figure rather than a fully developed character. He surfaces in Homer's imagination alongside other Bond villains like Auric Goldfinger, Jaws, and Oddjob when picturing Marge as a Bond girl. In a non-canon deleted scene, he's shown playing poker at Mr. Burns' Casino with fellow villains, ganging up on James Bont after a rigged card game. His most recognizable trait, stroking a cat in classic villain fashion, has become a running gag referenced by other characters, including Mr. Burns during a date. Overall, Blofeld exists mostly as a nod to Bond film tropes rather than a character with his own storyline in the show. Voiced by Harry Shearer, Hank Azaria.

title: The California Raisins
text: The California Raisins is A crossover rhythm and blues band referencing the real-life California Raisins characters, appearing briefly in the Simpsons universe. The California Raisins are a novelty singing group based on the classic advertising mascots, appearing as a strange crossover element in the show. In canon, they exist merely as a reference through a lunchbox Homer purchased on eBay during one of his impulsive online shopping binges. In a non-canon Robot Chicken couch gag, they are portrayed performing a musical number when Homer wanders into their animated world while searching for another piece of pop culture memorabiliar. Homer's rude reaction to their singing sparks a chaotic brawl, during which he violently overpowers the group and even bites one of them. The scene ends on a dark comedic note as a fire breaks out and wipes out the entire band. Overall, the Raisins serve as a quick, absurd gag rather than a developed set of characters.

title: Bill (KBBL)
text: Bill (KBBL) is A radio DJ for KBBL, minor recurring background character in Springfield. Bill is one of the two on-air personalities at Springfield's KBBL radio station, working alongside his co-host Marty. Together they run contests and giveaways for listeners, most notably the promotion that led to Bart winning an elephant instead of the cash prize they expected him to pick. The duo also conducts interviews with celebrity guests who pass through Springfield, such as members of Spinal Tap. Bill mostly serves as a background functionary of the town's media landscape rather than a character with deep personal traits, appearing sporadically across many seasons and other Simpsons media like comics and games. His running gag is being paired inseparably with Marty as the station's broadcasting duo. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Cocoa Beanie
text: Cocoa Beanie is Mascot of the Ah, Fudge! Factory, appearing briefly in the Simpsons universe. Cocoa Beanie is an anthropomorphic cocoa bean who serves as the aging mascot for the Ah, Fudge! Factory. He's meant to embody joy and cocoa-related cheer, though his worn-down demeanor suggests years of thankless mascot duty have taken their toll. Due to a history of rough encounters with children, he now requires parents to sign a waiver promising their kids won't hit, kick, or spit on him before getting near him. He's a minor background character, mostly known for a brief appearance and a background sign cameo. His non-canon appearances extend into mobile game content as part of the mascot roster.

title: Mordecai Brown
text: Mordecai Brown is A real-life historical baseball player Mr. Burns tries to recruit for the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant softball team. Mordecai Brown, nicknamed "3-Finger," was a real Major League Baseball player who competed in the National League from 1903 to 1916. In the world of The Simpsons, Mr. Burns attempts to bring him onto the Power Plant's softball team as part of his scheme to win a large bet against Aristotle Amadopolis. Unfortunately for Burns, Waylon Smithers, Jr. has to inform him that Brown has long since passed away, making him unavailable for recruitment. He appears only briefly and silently, existing purely as a picture rather than a speaking character. His inclusion is a nod to real baseball history worked into the show's famous ringer-recruitment storyline.

title: Jeff Bezos (character)
text: Jeff Bezos (character) is Real-world billionaire businessman and Amazon founder, appearing as a caricatured guest character among Springfield's rich and powerful. Jeff Bezos appears in the show as a satirical version of himself, rubbing elbows with other ultra-wealthy figures like Mr. Burns and Elon Musk. He's portrayed as part of an elite billionaire social circle, attending exclusive events like Billionaire Camp and joining corporate boards alongside Springfield's wealthiest schemers. The show pokes fun at his massive influence and the public's mixed feelings toward Amazon, referencing his connection to the downfall of traditional retailers like Sears. He's depicted as somewhat thin-skinned or embarrassing, such as denying he wet his pants during a scary story. Bezos is treated as a running punchline for corporate excess and billionaire absurdity rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Himself.

title: Brittany Brockman
text: Brittany Brockman is Snobby daughter of news anchorman Kent Brockman; a recurring Springfield schoolkid. Brittany Brockman is a stuck-up, image-conscious student who attends Springfield Preparatory School and clearly takes after her famous father in both looks and attitude. She shares Kent Brockman's distinctive head shape and hairstyle, a trait she was drawn with much like Milhouse resembles his own parents. Brittany has shown herself to be easily swept up in trends and crushes, such as swooning over a popular boy named Cameron, and she's particular about details, once angrily correcting a sandwich order. She's part of Kent's blended family, with a step-mother and several unnamed siblings, and she enjoys pop culture pursuits like listening to podcasts at home. Though not a major player in most episodes, she pops up frequently as a background student and occasional plot device tied to her father's career. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: Fritz, you idiot! I didn't order a baloney sandwich! I ordered an abaloney sandwich!
quotes: Fritz, you idiot! I didn't order a baloney sandwich! I ordered an abaloney sandwich!

title: Jeb Bush
text: Jeb Bush is Real-world political figure appearing as a minor character; Governor of Florida and son/brother of U.S. Presidents. Jeb Bush appears as a minor, mostly background figure tied to his real-life political family, the Bushes. He is depicted as the Florida Governor and identified through his relation to his father and brother, both former Presidents. His main appearance comes as part of a prank Homer plays on George H. W. Bush, where cardboard cutouts of Jeb and his brother are used to trick their father into approaching a door. In a later non-canon segment, he appears in a fantastical, comedic vision of political unity, dancing alongside rival politicians and Donald Trump. His inclusion there ends on a comedic note when he kicks Trump in a sensitive area. Overall, Jeb Bush functions less as a developed character and more as a topical caricature used for political humor. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Ling Bouvier
text: Ling Bouvier is Adopted daughter of Selma Bouvier, cousin to Bart, Lisa, and Maggie Simpson. Ling is a young Chinese girl adopted by Selma Bouvier after Selma realized she had reached menopause and would never have a biological child. To satisfy Chinese adoption authorities, Selma falsely claimed to be married to Homer Simpson, giving Ling an unusual extended family that includes the Simpson children as cousins. As she has grown up on the show, Ling has become a notably talented kid, though much of that seems driven by Patty and Selma pushing her hard to excel. She's mostly a quiet background character, having spoken only a single word on screen, and otherwise communicates through baby giggles or simply staying silent. Interestingly, she's voiced by Nancy Cartwright, best known as Bart, making her the only female Bouvier not voiced by Julie Kavner. She's occasionally shown interacting with other Simpsons babies, like Maggie and Baby Gerald, at gatherings such as a baby club. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: Help me.|Ling Bouvier|The Changing of the Guardian
quotes: Help me.|Ling Bouvier|The Changing of the Guardian

title: Big Bad Wolf
text: Big Bad Wolf is Animatronic fairy-tale character featured as an attraction at Storytown Village, encountered by the Simpson family. The Big Bad Wolf is a mechanical, animatronic version of the classic fairy-tale villain, built as part of a nursery-rhyme themed attraction at Storytown Village. His act consists of repeatedly trying and failing to blow down the house of the Three Little Pigs, a performance so unimpressive that it entertains baby Maggie but earns mockery from Bart. After the park shuts down, his broken-down animatronic form is left standing amid the ruins, a decaying relic later swallowed up when the site becomes Praiseland. In a non-canon holiday special appearance, a more traditional version of the character actually succeeds in blowing down the Flanders family's house. Overall, he's less a personality-driven character and more a recurring visual gag tied to abandoned amusement park settings and fairy-tale parody. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Astrid
text: Astrid is A minor recurring character who co-hosts a MyTube gaming commentary series. Astrid is a young MyTube content creator who partners with French Fry to make videos about the online game Boblox. She's shown covering in-game drama, specifically the rivalry between Springfield Elementary and the Limitless Frontier Horizons school, breaking down the events for their viewers. Astrid comes across as the more grounded co-host, engaging directly with subscribers by inviting them to share their own theories. Her role in the show is largely tied to satirizing online gaming culture and kid-run internet content. She appears only briefly across a couple of episodes, functioning as a background/minor character rather than a major player in Springfield's world. Voiced by Montse Hernandez.

title: Brandon
text: Brandon is Talent agent for Duffman and Woketopus, minor recurring character. Brandon is a talent agent who represents both Duffman and his rival mascot Woketopus, putting him in an awkward position during their competition for the Duff Beer mascot poll. He's shown to be somewhat careless with phone etiquette, at one point failing to actually switch calls between his two clients, leading to an accidental mix-up. Despite representing two competitors, he tries to keep both informed and encourages Duffman to participate in industry events like the Corporate Spokescharacters Fan Convention. Brandon ultimately delivers good news to Duffman, informing him that a viral video helped him win the mascot poll thanks to an unexpected surge of support from K-pop fans. He comes across as a professional but slightly bumbling background figure in the world of corporate mascots. Voiced by Paul Brittain.

title: Baba Branka
text: Baba Branka is Moe Szyslak's deceased grandmother, briefly seen in flashbacks and a framed picture. Baba Branka is a minor, deceased relative of Moe Szyslak, implied to hail from North Macedonia. She appears only through a framed photograph and a flashback, giving a glimpse of a harsh and abusive family history that helps explain some of Moe's deep-seated insecurities. In the flashback, she is shown berating young Moe in Macedonian, calling him useless and a burden, and even putting cigarettes out on his neck. Her death is tied to a darkly comic detail involving water, referenced by Moe when Homer asks for a drink. Her portrait and death gag are a visual parody of the Wicked Witch of the West from The Wizard of Oz. Though never seen in a full scene, she adds a layer of grim backstory to Moe's troubled upbringing. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Barfly
text: Barfly is Superhero alter-ego of Moe Szyslak, appearing in Simpsons comic books. Barfly is the costumed identity adopted by bartender Moe Szyslak after a nuclear explosion grants him extraordinary powers. This non-canon persona exists only within the Bongo comic book continuity, separate from the mainstream television series. As Barfly, Moe joins a group of similarly transformed characters in superhero storylines that parody typical comic book tropes. The character's very name plays on Moe's everyday role as a bar owner, blending his mundane life with his new heroic identity. Barfly appears across a handful of comic issues that chronicle escalating superpowered conflicts. Overall, the character serves as a comedic twist on Moe's usual downtrodden persona, elevating him to unlikely hero status.

title: June Bellamy
text: June Bellamy is Voice actress for Itchy and Scratchy who befriended Homer during his Poochie role. June Bellamy is a veteran voice actress within the show's universe, best known for lending her talents to the animated stars Itchy and Scratchy. She's portrayed as loyal and supportive, quickly forming a bond with Homer when he joined the cast as Poochie's voice. She helps him navigate the odd world of fan conventions and explains industry quirks, like why cartoons aren't recorded live. When Homer's job is put in jeopardy, she loyally threatens to quit alongside him, though this ultimately doesn't save his role. Her career also boasts a claim to fame in classic animation, having voiced the Road Runner for Looney Tunes, though she jokes that she only recorded a single sound effect that was reused repeatedly. The character is a clear homage to real-life voice acting legend June Foray. Voiced by Tress MacNeille (normal voice); Dan Castellaneta (as Itchy); Harry Shearer (as Scratchy). Notable quotes: if he (Homer) goes, she goes
quotes: if he (Homer) goes, she goes

title: State Comptroller Atkins
text: State Comptroller Atkins is State comptroller for Springfield's state, occasionally interacting with Springfield Elementary and its staff. Atkins is a state-level bureaucrat responsible for overseeing school funding and academic standards for Springfield's schools. He first appears delivering a grant to Springfield Elementary after its GPA was fraudulently boosted, only to be duped for a time by Otto in a latex disguise. He later serves as a judge for a school band competition, showing he values fair play and integrity, and even threatens to withhold an award when he learns of cheating. His authority extends to hiring and firing school administrators, as seen when he dismisses and later reinstates Superintendent Chalmers depending on the circumstances. Despite his official, somewhat dry demeanor, he can be swayed by sentiment or absurd Simpsons-style chaos, such as being present during a bizarre school siege. Overall, he represents the recurring bureaucratic authority figures who intersect with the show's satire of institutional inefficiency and small-town politics. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: This grant ensures a light bulb in every classroom... and a high-definition TV for the teachers' lounge. | Now I'm just going to be sick.
quotes: This grant ensures a light bulb in every classroom... and a high-definition TV for the teachers' lounge.
Now I'm just going to be sick.

title: Albert (Walking Big & Tall)
text: Albert (Walking Big & Tall) is Founder of "Over-Feeders Anonymous", a minor recurring character who appears in one episode and later as a ghost. Albert was a passionate activist who ran a support group dedicated to helping overweight people embrace and take pride in their bodies rather than feel ashamed of them. He was confident and confrontational, unafraid to protest publicly against businesses he felt promoted unhealthy body standards, even getting arrested for his actions. Despite his advocacy for body positivity, his health ultimately failed him, as he suffered a fatal heart attack during one of his rallies while trying to stand up from his mobility scooter. Ironically, his name and appearance drew comparisons to the cartoon character Fat Albert. After his death, he made a brief symbolic reappearance as a ghost in Bart's coma dream, and his picture later showed up in a fictional afterlife-themed diner in one of Marge's imagined scenarios. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Kevin Burkhardt (character)
text: Kevin Burkhardt (character) is Real-life sportscaster appearing as himself in a Simpsons episode and a special, covering baseball news. Kevin Burkhardt appears as a fictionalized version of himself, playing the role of a baseball broadcaster reporting on events in the Simpsons universe. Alongside Kevin Millar, he covers the story of a player named Aeropos Walkov who is trying to move from Belarus to play in the American major leagues, detailing his backstory and the interest of major league clubs. He later reports on a gambling scandal, ultimately clearing Walkov of wrongdoing and pinning the blame on Moe. In a non-canon special, he hosts World Series coverage for MLB on Fox and jokingly settles for Milhouse as a celebrity guest after failing to secure Homer or Bart. His portrayal leans on his real-world persona as a professional, straightforward sports commentator, used mostly for comedic effect when paired with Simpsons characters. Voiced by Himself.

title: Fluffy Bunny
text: Fluffy Bunny is Animated rabbit character from the sex education film shown within an episode, wife of Fuzzy Bunny. Fluffy Bunny is a cartoon rabbit who appears in the fictional in-universe educational film Fuzzy Bunny's Guide to You Know What. Her story serves as a simplified, family-friendly allegory for puberty, dating, and reproduction, shown to Springfield Elementary students. She and Fuzzy Bunny go through a chaste courtship of wholesome outings before marrying and finally consummating their relationship on their honeymoon. Her tale ends with the birth of a large litter of offspring, though not all survive, adding a darkly comic twist to an otherwise saccharine cartoon. She has no spoken lines, functioning purely as a visual gag within the show's satire of outdated sex-ed materials.

title: Ben Carson
text: Ben Carson is Non-canon real-world political figure appearing in Simpsons specials. Ben Carson appears as a caricature of the real American politician in a couple of non-canon Simpsons specials. He first shows up in a fantasy sequence imagined by Marge, where politicians from both parties, along with Donald Trump, set aside their differences to sing and dance together. He later makes a brief cameo exiting the White House through a door labeled for recently fired staff, poking fun at the turnover in the Trump administration. He has no spoken lines in either appearance, functioning purely as a background political reference rather than a fleshed-out character. His inclusion reflects the show's tendency to satirize contemporary political figures in its special episodes.

title: Tony Bennett (character)
text: Tony Bennett (character) is Real-life singer who appears as himself in a cameo in the Simpsons universe. Tony Bennett appears in the show as a version of himself, the famous American crooner. His most notable moment comes when the Simpson family pulls their car up beside him on the street and he performs a song about Capital City. Beyond this brief musical cameo, his presence in the show is minimal, with a picture of him later appearing on the wall of a restaurant called The Pimento Grove. He's treated less as a developed character and more as a celebrity guest appearance, lending his real-world fame and singing talent to a quick gag. The wiki notes his real-life passing, tying the fictional cameo to his actual legacy as a legendary vocalist. Voiced by Tony Bennett (Himself).

title: Scotty Boom
text: Scotty Boom is A celebrity chef and TV host who appears in Springfield's culinary world, occasionally clashing with Homer. Scotty Boom is a professional chef who has built a television career hosting his own cooking program, Scotty Boom's Death-Row Bake-Off, on the Chew Network. He once found himself in a cook-off against Homer, expecting an easy win given his professional background. However, the contest took an unexpected turn when his own son secretly sabotaged his cooking. The sabotage wasn't out of malice but a desperate bid for attention, as the son hoped that ruining his father's dish would get him fired from television and free up time for their relationship. This family drama adds a surprisingly personal layer to what is otherwise a lighthearted culinary rivalry. Scotty also appears in non-canon material like The Simpsons: Tapped Out as part of the Foodie Fight content. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Don Castellaneta
text: Don Castellaneta is Rival Mafia boss who competes with Fat Tony for territory and respect in Springfield's criminal underworld. Don Castellaneta leads a rival crime family that stands in opposition to Fat Tony's organization. He is a shrewd and theatrical mob boss, willing to stage a fake mishap to defuse a tense standoff during a meeting at Luigi's. Despite the rivalry, he shows a surprising code of honor, valuing Fat Tony too much to actually want him dead even when other mafia members suspect Tony has gone soft. His name is a playful in-joke, since he shares the same name and voice as his real-life actor. He appears only briefly across two episodes, functioning mostly as a comedic foil within the show's recurring mafia storylines. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Clumsy me! I dropped my fork! Boys... | Clumsy us! We dropped our forks!
quotes: Clumsy me! I dropped my fork! Boys...
Clumsy us! We dropped our forks!

title: Eric Cartman
text: Eric Cartman is A crossover character from South Park who appears within the show-within-a-show that Bart and Milhouse watch on TV. Eric Cartman shows up in The Simpsons purely as a nod to South Park, appearing as a cartoon Bart and Milhouse are seen watching on television. In that clip, chaos breaks out at his school during a riot, and his severed head is shockingly shown on-screen, implying he's died in that continuity. He later gets referenced again when Nelson dresses up as him at a bus stop, and his silhouette briefly appears among a lineup of villains during a musical number performed by Mr. Burns. Within the actual South Park series, Cartman is one of the crude, scheming ringleaders of his friend group, but The Simpsons only uses him as a quick pop-culture cameo rather than fleshing out his personality. His appearances are non-speaking and largely played for cross-show fan recognition rather than characterization.

title: Sonny Bono
text: Sonny Bono is Real-world singer, producer, actor, and politician referenced/appearing as an image or mention in various Simpsons episodes. Sonny Bono is not really a character in the traditional sense but a real-world celebrity referenced throughout the show's run. He is best known in-universe for his musical partnership and marriage to Cher, which becomes a running point of comparison and jokes among Springfield residents. His likeness appears in background gags, such as on a kite Marge owns and as a mustache option in an app on Homer's tablet. Various characters bring him up in conversation, from Bart taunting Sideshow Bob to a man waking from a decades-long coma curious about his old talk show. He never appears as a fully voiced, physical character within the show, existing mostly as a pop-culture reference and visual cameo. Notable quotes: Bart said that he was just Sonny to his Cher.
quotes: Bart said that he was just Sonny to his Cher.

title: Ed Begley, Jr. (character)
text: Ed Begley, Jr. (character) is Real-life actor and environmentalist who appears as himself in guest cameos. Ed Begley, Jr. appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, playing up his real-world reputation as a devoted environmentalist. He's shown attending eco-friendly social gatherings and championing green inventions like solar-powered vehicles and pinwheel-spinning solar panels. His appearances tend to intersect with Homer's clumsiness, such as when Homer accidentally destroys a forest Begley was trying to protect.
