Overall, Caan's appearances lean on meta-humor referencing his real-life acting career. Voiced by James Caan (Himself).

title: Carlotta Carlson
text: Carlotta Carlson is Carl Carlson's sister, occasional love interest of Lenny Leonard. Carlotta Carlson is the rarely-seen sister of Moe's bar regular Carl. Her most notable tradition is being Lenny's Valentine's Day date every year, a swap that lets Lenny and Carl each date someone who shares their best friend's face. She later appears on a boating trip aboard the Something's Fishy, a vessel co-owned by Homer, Lenny, and Carl, where she's given a turn at the helm. Her forwardness comes through when she impulsively proposes marriage to Lenny, an act so startling that he leaps overboard rather than answer. Despite his panicked reaction, Lenny insists his jump wasn't meant as a rejection, leaving their relationship status ambiguous and comedic. Voiced by Pamela Hayden / Dawnn Lewis.

title: Anastasia
text: Anastasia is A white tiger performer owned by Gunter and Ernst, appearing in a Simpsons episode set at the Monty Burns Casino. Anastasia is a white tiger with black stripes who was captured from the wild by her owners, Gunter and Ernst, and trained as a performing animal. She harbors a deep-seated trauma from her capture, having been tranquilized after being surprised by her captors' jeep. This trauma resurfaces during a casino performance, causing her to violently turn on her trainers mid-show. As a non-speaking animal character, Anastasia's role is largely physical and dramatic rather than comedic dialogue, though her brief encounter with baby Maggie Simpson adds a moment of tension to her story. She nearly harms Maggie after the toddler wanders off and pulls at her whiskers, only for Barney Gumble to intervene and save the child just in time. Anastasia's single major appearance ties her closely to the chaos surrounding Springfield's legalized gambling storyline.

title: Lucas Bortner
text: Lucas Bortner is A schoolmate and love interest of Lisa Simpson, appearing in a Season 25 episode. Lucas Bortner is an overweight boy whose life ambition is to become a competitive eater. He catches Lisa Simpson's attention, and she takes it upon herself to reform his eating habits once they start dating. Their budding relationship worries Marge, who fears Lisa might be drawn to a partner who mirrors Homer's flaws. Lisa ultimately succeeds in getting Lucas to eat healthier, though this comes at the cost of derailing his original competitive-eating dream, leaving him to pursue a different goal. Outside of his main appearance, he's briefly seen as a background student witnessing a major announcement from Principal Skinner in a non-canon short. Voiced by Zach Galifianakis.

title: Nash Castor
text: Nash Castor is Host of the political talk show Head Butt, recurring media personality in Springfield. Nash Castor is a loud, bombastic cable news host known for his aggressive interviewing style and tendency to exaggerate everything for dramatic effect. He rarely lets guests actually answer questions, often shouting over them or cutting straight to inflammatory accusations. His show Head Butt has tackled Springfield controversies ranging from Bart's flag-mooning scandal to Ralph Wiggum's presidential prospects. He's not above unprofessional behavior, such as making out with a fellow panelist during a commercial break. Ironically, his own bluster ends up backfiring when Homer Simpson out-shouts him on air, leading to Homer getting a rival talk show of his own. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: why he hates America
quotes: why he hates America

title: Robot B-9
text: Robot B-9 is Crossover robot character from Lost in Space appearing in Simpsons episodes and dream sequences. Robot B-9 is a robotic character borrowed from the classic sci-fi series Lost in Space, appearing in The Simpsons through dream sequences, conventions, and museum exhibits. He typically interacts with his fictional companion Dr. Smith, often warning of danger in his signature robotic voice. In one dream sequence, Lisa takes on the role of the robot alongside Homer's Dr. Smith. He later appears as a real character at the Bi-Mon-Sci-Fi-Con, bantering with Dr. Smith and helping tip off Bart about an unwanted meeting. The character is treated as a beloved piece of nerd/sci-fi culture within the show, even being honored with a museum statue. His voice was performed by the same actor who played him in the original TV series and film, giving him authenticity as a crossover figure. Voiced by Dick Tufeld; Yeardley Smith. Notable quotes: You have still got it, Dr. Smith. | Danger! Danger! Bart Simpson!
quotes: You have still got it, Dr. Smith.
Danger! Danger! Bart Simpson!

title: Brittany (Krusty Gets Busted)
text: Brittany (Krusty Gets Busted) is A minor recurring child character who appeared as a guest on The Krusty the Clown Show. Brittany is a six-year-old girl with red hair who is best remembered for her one memorable television appearance. On her birthday, she was given the choice between a sweet gesture from Krusty the Clown or watching Sideshow Bob get blasted out of a cannon, and she gleefully picked the more chaotic option. This small moment reveals a playful, mischievous streak beneath her innocent, childlike exterior. Little else is known about her personal life beyond having an uncle named Nick and unnamed parents. She exists mostly as a background face, popping up in archive footage in later episodes rather than playing an active role in the main plot. Despite her limited screen time, her cannon-choosing decision has made her a small but memorable footnote in the show's early history. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Lucille Ball
text: Lucille Ball is Real-world actress and comedian referenced/appearing as a ghost in The Simpsons. Lucille Ball is depicted in the show as a real-world celebrity whose legacy and characters get referenced across several episodes. She most notably appears as a ghost taking the form of her television character Lucy McGillicuddy Ricardo Carmichael, blending her two famous sitcom roles from I Love Lucy and The Lucy Show. Elsewhere she's used as a cultural touchstone, from Moe selling clam sculptures shaped like her to Marge fearing homelessness the way Ball did in a TV movie. Her image turns up as background decor in places like Springfield Sardi's, reinforcing her status as a beloved show-business icon within the Simpsons universe. A parody show called I Lost Lucy further riffs on her famous sitcom, even matching her real birth and death years on a fictional tombstone. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Spiro Agnew
text: Spiro Agnew is Real-world former U.S. Vice President referenced in various Simpsons episodes. Spiro Agnew is a real-world historical figure incorporated into the Simpsons universe as a minor recurring reference rather than an active character. He appears in various forms, from a caricature on a clock face used in a bombing to an animatronic figure at a Vice Presidents exhibit. His name and legacy are frequently used as the butt of satirical jokes, most notably in a Mad magazine parody that confuses young Milhouse. He's tied to real historical events like his resignation due to tax evasion, and is imagined in hypothetical scenarios, such as becoming president after a yo-yo accident kills Nixon. Mr. Smithers even lists him among history's great toadies for his loyalty to Nixon. Overall, Agnew functions as a running gag and historical Easter egg rather than a fleshed-out character.

title: Bernard
text: Bernard is Minor recurring character; a tall bouncer who worked at Flaming Moe's bar. Bernard is a lanky, imposing figure best known for his brief stint as the bouncer at the trendy bar Flaming Moe's during its peak popularity. He takes his job seriously, controlling access to the bar by enforcing an exclusive guest list, which leads him to famously turn Homer away despite Homer's connection to the bar's creation. He also appeared in a crowd-control role, using a flashlight to direct onlookers at the carnival that sprang up around the well where "Timmy O'Toole" was trapped. Bernard doesn't have much personality development beyond these functional appearances, serving mainly as a background figure who highlights the absurdity of Springfield's fickle trends and mob mentality. He's a minor but memorable example of the show's use of one-off characters to flesh out Springfield's population. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Drew Barrymore (character)
text: Drew Barrymore (character) is Real-life actress and talk show host who appears as herself in cameo roles in The Simpsons. Drew Barrymore appears as a fictionalized version of herself, tying into the show's tradition of celebrity cameos. She's referenced early on when Bart pranks tourists by falsely marking Moe's home as her house on a map of celebrity residences. Later, she has a more direct role, contacting Marge for advice on producing her talk show after Marge briefly becomes a consultant for talk show hosts. Their exchange highlights Marge's ongoing struggle to balance career ambitions with family life. Drew is also noted as being politically left-leaning, appearing on a satirical list of famous liberals compiled by Ned Flanders. Overall, she serves as a minor celebrity cameo character rather than a fully developed personality within the show. Voiced by Herself.

title: Bighorn Sheep
text: Bighorn Sheep is A wild bighorn sheep that pursues Lisa Simpson and ends up entangled with Mr. Burns in a single episode adventure. The Bighorn Sheep is a rampaging animal that chases Lisa Simpson into Burns' manor, causing chaos as it smashes through windows and destroys property. It relentlessly pursues her and Mr. Burns as they flee through the mansion seeking safety. Despite its aggressive charging behavior, the sheep turns out to have a surprisingly gentle motive, returning a pearl necklace it found caught on a tree to Lisa. Its brief rampage becomes an odd bonding moment, ending with Mr. Burns literally riding the sheep back to the power plant. The character is a one-off comedic device built around slapstick destruction followed by an unexpectedly sentimental resolution. It later appears again only in flashback footage referenced in a musical number. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Terry Bradshaw (character)
text: Terry Bradshaw (character) is Real-world American football player who appears as himself in cameo and non-canon Simpsons material. Terry Bradshaw appears as a fictionalized version of himself, tying into his real-life fame as a football star turned television personality. In the show's canon, he's mostly referenced rather than seen, such as when Martin mistakes a masked singer for him in a school play. In non-canon material, he plays a more active role, welcoming Homer and Bart to the NFL Studio on Fox and co-hosting a grim reality show parody with Roger. His appearances lean into his real broadcasting persona, cracking wise about network censorship priorities. He also shows up interviewing the Simpson family in a Super Bowl-themed promo. Overall, his presence in the show is brief and mostly played for celebrity cameo humor rather than deep characterization. Voiced by Terry Bradshaw. Notable quotes: It is a disgrace because after showing a dozen gruesome murders, the network would cut to a break before Homer and Marge could make love on camera.
quotes: It is a disgrace because after showing a dozen gruesome murders, the network would cut to a break before Homer and Marge could make love on camera.

title: Richard Dean Anderson (character)
text: Richard Dean Anderson (character) is Real-life actor who appears as himself, idolized by Patty and Selma as the star of MacGyver. Richard Dean Anderson appears as a fictionalized version of himself, drawn into the obsessive fandom of Patty and Selma. The two sisters worship both him and his old show MacGyver, going so far as to kidnap him when he shows up expecting a Stargate SG-1 convention instead. Rather than being terrified, Anderson reveals a quirky love of using his real-life improvisational skills to escape captivity, treating the ordeal as a fun game. His enthusiasm ends up annoying his captors, who eventually bore him with slideshow presentations until he flees. The character plays on the real actor's association with both MacGyver and Stargate, and pokes fun at fan-convention culture and celebrity worship. Voiced by Richard Dean Anderson (Himself).

title: Doc Brown
text: Doc Brown is Crossover character from Back to the Future, appearing in The Simpsons Ride and related non-canon material. Doc Brown is a non-canon crossover character brought into The Simpsons universe from the Back to the Future franchise, most notably featured in The Simpsons Ride. He is portrayed as an eccentric, disheveled scientist running the Institute of Future Technology, forced into hard times when financial misfortune strikes. His storyline ties him to Krusty the Clown's amusement park empire, showing him losing his business and even his signature wild hairstyle for a menial job. He also gets tangled up in a bizarre sci-fi mashup involving his time-traveling DeLorean and a character from The Fifth Element. His brief, silent cameo appearances in a couch gag alongside Marty McFly reinforce his role as a fun nod to pop culture rather than a fleshed-out Simpsons character. True to his film counterpart, he retains his exclamatory catchphrase when startled. Voiced by Christopher Lloyd. Notable quotes: Great Scott!
quotes: Great Scott!

title: Steve Allen (character)
text: Steve Allen (character) is Real-life talk show host/comedian who appears as himself in a flashback involving Bleeding Gums Murphy. Steve Allen appears in the show as a self-referential cameo, playing a fictionalized version of himself as a television host. In his depicted appearance, he hosts Bleeding Gums Murphy on The Tonight Show but spends the segment shamelessly promoting his own bizarrely titled books instead of engaging with his guest. This running gag pokes fun at celebrity self-promotion and talk show egotism. He's also referenced as the author of an audiobook Krusty listens to, and in a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he's credited with writing the foreword to one of Mr. Burns' vampire-themed books. Overall, Steve Allen exists as a minor, mostly mentioned character used for satirical celebrity humor rather than a fully developed personality within the show's main narrative. Voiced by Steve Allen (Himself).

title: Ms. Barr
text: Ms. Barr is P.E. teacher at Springfield Elementary School. Ms. Barr is a minor recurring staff member at Springfield Elementary, best known for her strict, no-nonsense approach to physical education. She has little patience for excuses, most notably when she dismissed Lisa's emotional sadness as a valid reason to skip dodgeball. Her appearances tend to place her among the background faculty during school-wide events, such as labor disputes and administrative announcements. She joined her fellow teachers in the strike organized by Mrs. Krabappel, showing at least some solidarity with the staff. She was also present when Principal Skinner broke the bad news about the school losing its oil-derived funding. Overall, she serves as a stock authority figure reinforcing the rigid, sometimes absurd rules of the school's gym class. Voiced by Miriam Flynn.

title: Blythe
text: Blythe is A therapist who briefly dated Grampa Simpson. Blythe is a New Age-style therapist who was brought in to run a therapeutic sound bath session for the residents of the Springfield Retirement Castle. Though Grampa was reluctant to participate at first, he ended up smitten with her, sparking a whirlwind romance. Their relationship progressed quickly, with Grampa moving in with her and her adopted son within six months. Ultimately, Blythe proved fickle, ending things with Grampa in favor of a wealthier man she felt was more spiritually compatible with her. Her storyline plays into themes of superficial spirituality and sudden late-life romance common in the show's treatment of the elderly cast. Voiced by Carol Kane.

title: Muhammad Ali
text: Muhammad Ali is Real-world boxer referenced and depicted in various Simpsons episodes. Muhammad Ali appears in the show as a real-world figure referenced through pictures, comics, and mentions rather than as an active character with dialogue. His image was famously altered to show Mr. Burns' face on his body during a boxing victory over Sonny Liston in a slideshow about Burns' life. He's tied into the show's fictional comic universe through crossover comics pitting him against Radioactive Man, which become objects of desire for characters like Bart and Comic Book Guy. Homer also lists fighting Ali as one of his life goals inspired by an Animal Crackers box. Ali is also depicted as an animatronic figure in Americatown. As a non-speaking character, he functions purely as a cultural reference point rather than a developed personality within the show.

title: Rocky Balboa
text: Rocky Balboa is Fictional boxer from the Rocky film series, referenced and appearing in various forms within The Simpsons universe. Rocky Balboa is a crossover character brought into the Simpsons world from the famous boxing film franchise. He factors into Bart's escape plan from the Shelbyville Zoo, where Bart uses knowledge of the Rocky movie titles and Roman numerals to figure out an exit. He also appears as a playable character in an arcade game at Captain Blip's Zapateria, endlessly repeating a signature boxing taunt against his opponent Clara Peller. A statue of him outside the real-world Philadelphia Museum of Art becomes a photo backdrop for Homer during a family outing. Rocky is also honored on Ned Flanders' list of notable left-handed people, showing his minor but recurring presence as a piece of pop-culture trivia within the show. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: You ain't so bad
quotes: You ain't so bad

title: Dr. Brentano
text: Dr. Brentano is Child psychologist and marriage counselor who has treated both Marge and Homer, and later Bart. Dr. Brentano is a professional counselor in Springfield who splits his practice between marriage counseling and child psychology. He's shown to be reasonably competent, helping Homer and Marge patch up their marriage by suggesting a grand romantic gesture, though his patience wears thin with Homer's antics. When treating Bart after a funeral incident, he initially misjudges the boy's age, revealing he can be a bit careless with details of his patients. Despite this, he lands on a surprisingly effective solution, recommending a drum set to channel Bart's restless energy. He's blunt and unafraid to call out foolish behavior, most memorably telling Homer exactly what he thinks of him. Brentano pops up repeatedly across the series as a go-to expert whenever the Simpsons family needs therapy. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: You're an idiot.
quotes: You're an idiot.

title: Tina Ballerina
text: Tina Ballerina is Recurring heavyset ballerina performer on The Krusty the Clown Show. Tina Ballerina is one of the many odd performers who appear as part of Krusty the Clown's variety show. She's a heavyset dancer with distinctive pink hair, adding to the show's roster of bizarre sideshow-style acts. In her downtime she has a quirky hobby of collecting pancakes, and she enjoys thumb wrestling matches with Mr. Teeny, Krusty's chimp sidekick. Despite her cheerful ballerina persona, she harbors a fierce rivalry with fellow performer Little Vicki Valentine, whom she considers her mortal enemy. She's a non-speaking character, appearing mostly in background or crowd shots across many episodes and spin-off media over the decades.

title: Brazilian record producer's son
text: Brazilian record producer's son is Minor character; son of a Brazilian record producer and possible eventual husband of Mary Spuckler. This 12-year-old boy is introduced as the son of a wealthy Brazilian record producer who takes a liking to Mary Spuckler. He appears in his own liquor commercial billed as "The Most Interesting Boy in the World," a nod to a famous beer ad campaign. He invites Mary to join him and his father, and she ultimately chooses him over Bart Simpson, leaving Bart heartbroken. The story implies the two later marry, though he may have since passed away, leaving Mary a widow. His character is a playful parody of the suave Brazilian millionaire from the film Breakfast at Tiffany's. Despite his brief appearance, he plays a pivotal role in ending Bart and Mary's romantic storyline. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Mr. Burnsum
text: Mr. Burnsum is Non-canon character; owner of The Burnsum and Bailey Circus in a Treehouse of Horror segment. Mr. Burnsum is a minor, non-canon character who appears as the ringmaster and proprietor of his own traveling circus. He is a clear parody of real-life showman P.T. Barnum, echoing the name and legacy of the famous Barnum & Bailey Circus. His time on screen is brief, as his own circus freaks turn on him and kill him, ending his story on a dark comedic note typical of the Treehouse of Horror specials. Beyond his role as circus owner and his grim demise, little else about his personality or background is explored in canon material. He also makes an appearance as a collectible character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Cleveland Brown
text: Cleveland Brown is Crossover character from The Cleveland Show who briefly appeared with his family at the Simpson residence. Cleveland Brown is best known as the patriarch from the animated spin-off The Cleveland Show, existing largely outside the main Simpsons continuity. His appearance in the Simpsons universe is a brief crossover cameo rather than a fully integrated storyline. He shows up alongside his family at the Simpsons' home to take part in a special celebratory event tied to the show's milestone season premiere. Because his presence is tied to a crossover event, he is treated as a non-canon character within the main Simpsons universe. His family ties, including his wife and stepchildren from the Tubbs family, are carried over from his home series. Overall, his role is more about connecting two animated universes for a novelty appearance than developing any deep character arc within The Simpsons. Voiced by Mike Henry.

title: Aristotle Amadopolis
text: Aristotle Amadopolis is Owner of the rival Shelbyville Nuclear Power Plant, occasional business associate/rival of Mr. Burns. Aristotle Amadopolis, nicknamed Ari, runs the competing nuclear plant in Shelbyville and often finds himself pitted against Mr. Burns in business and sport. He once hired Homer to inspire his underperforming staff, only to watch Homer's reputation as a lucky fool spread instead of the intended heroism. His softball rivalry with Burns cost him a hefty bet after his team lost. Modeled visually and thematically on the real-life shipping magnate Aristotle Onassis, he embodies a wealthy, somewhat exasperated foil to Burns' cutthroat management style. Despite his frustrations with incompetence, he remains a recurring fixture in Springfield's business and social circles, appearing at events like Moe's Tavern during Artie Ziff's downfall. Voiced by Jon Lovitz, Dan Castellaneta.

title: Benedict Arnold
text: Benedict Arnold is Historical figure (Revolutionary War general/traitor) referenced and appearing in a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment. Benedict Arnold is depicted as the real historical American general who infamously betrayed his country by conspiring to hand over West Point to the British. In the show's canon, his name is invoked mainly as a punchline about treachery, most notably when Homer impersonates him to escape trouble with the Springfield Mafia. He also appears in a non-canon capacity as a member of the ghostly 'Jury of the Damned' during Homer's soul trial in a Halloween episode. There, he plays a small but pivotal role by reading evidence from a photograph that ultimately helps save Homer. Overall, Arnold functions less as a developed character and more as a historical reference point and recurring in-joke about betrayal. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: D'oh!
quotes: D'oh!

title: Lizzie Borden
text: Lizzie Borden is Historical figure referenced in a school play and appearing as a juror in a non-canon Halloween segment. Lizzie Borden is based on the real-life American woman infamous for allegedly murdering her father and stepmother with an axe, though she was acquitted at trial. In the show's canon, she exists only as the subject of a school play at Springfield Elementary, with Martin Prince cast in her role and Bart cast as one of her victims. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, she appears as a member of the Devil's handpicked Jury of the Damned, tasked with deciding the fate of Homer's soul. She ultimately delivers the jury's verdict that Marge, not the Devil, rightfully owns Homer's soul. The character speaks with a New England accent, nodding to Borden's real hometown of Fall River, Massachusetts. She serves more as a historical/cultural reference than a recurring personality in the show. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Aerosmith (characters)
text: Aerosmith (characters) is Real-life rock band making a guest appearance in Springfield, most notably at Moe's Tavern. Aerosmith appears as themselves, lending their real voices and rock star personas to the show. They're first glimpsed at a Grammy party attended by the Be Sharps, then take center stage when Moe coaxes them into performing at his suddenly popular tavern, bribing them with free pickled eggs. Their live rendition of "Walk This Way" becomes a highlight, and they even turn the joke back on Moe by dragging him onstage to sing. The band is treated as a running pop-culture touchstone afterward, referenced in cereal boxes, six-degrees-of-separation jokes, and bar trivia about drummer Joey Kramer. A comedic subplot has Kramer nearly missing a show because Mrs. Krabappel steals his drumsticks to pursue him romantically. Overall, they represent the show's frequent use of real celebrity cameos for comedic effect. Voiced by Themselves (Steven Tyler, Joe Perry, Brad Whitford, Tom Hamilton, Joey Kramer). Notable quotes: I fell on Aerosmith at Moe's after revealing the secret ingredient of "The Flaming Moe!" | Aerosmith sounds like Agent Smith.
quotes: I fell on Aerosmith at Moe's after revealing the secret ingredient of "The Flaming Moe!"
Aerosmith sounds like Agent Smith.

title: Candace
text: Candace is Non-canon love interest of Homer Simpson, appearing in the dream-based episode "Every Man's Dream". Candace is a pharmacist working at Oedipus Rx who briefly becomes romantically involved with Homer during a fantasy sequence where he and Marge are separated. She's easygoing and finds Homer's cranky complaints amusing, which sparks their initial connection. Their whirlwind relationship escalates quickly, from getting high together to meeting her disapproving friends and eventually her estranged father. She has a quirky emotional attachment to Homer, later realizing she's drawn to him because he reminds her of a childhood snowman she built. Candace's storyline spirals into complications involving her father dating Marge, and she abruptly announces a pregnancy and marriage plans before the entire scenario is revealed to be a dream within a dream. The character exists only within this surreal, non-canon narrative and has a minor tie-in appearance in a mobile game. Voiced by Lena Dunham.

title: Canadian Flanders
text: Canadian Flanders is A minor character resembling Ned Flanders, encountered in Canada during a drug-run episode. Canadian Flanders is essentially a Canadian doppelganger of Ned Flanders, sharing his mannerisms and odd verbal quirks. He appears when Homer, Apu, and Ned cross into Canada seeking cheaper medication, running into him outside a pharmacy in Winnipeg. The two Flanders-like figures bond instantly over their shared nonsensical, folksy speech patterns, treating each other as kindred spirits. He casually offers Ned marijuana, noting its legality in Canada, which unsettles Ned enough to make a devil comparison before the group heads back to the U.S. His only canonical appearance is brief, but he was later reused as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Overall, he serves as a one-off gag character poking fun at Ned's idiosyncrasies by giving him a foreign mirror image. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "neighboureeno to the North." | "reeferino" | "it's legal here."
quotes: "neighboureeno to the North."
"reeferino"
"it's legal here."

title: Badgerine
text: Badgerine is Fictional superhero merchandise figure appearing in the Simpsons universe, parodying a famous Marvel character. Badgerine is a minor fictional superhero that exists within the Simpsons world as a comic book or toy franchise character rather than an active participant in the show's plot. He is clearly a parody of Wolverine from the X-Men, complete with claw-like weapons as his signature feature. Badgerine appears primarily as a collectible figurine sold at The Android's Dungeon & Baseball Card Shop, reflecting the show's frequent satire of comic book fandom and merchandising culture. Bart Simpson shows interest in the character, going so far as to acquire a replica of Badgerine's claws at a sci-fi convention. As a non-speaking character, Badgerine never appears as a living being in any scene, existing solely as a toy or background reference used for comedic worldbuilding.

title: Bob the Drag Queen (character)
text: Bob the Drag Queen (character) is Guest character appearing as herself, an American drag queen who appears in a viral video referenced in the show. Bob the Drag Queen is a real-life American drag performer who makes a cameo appearance in the Simpsons universe, portraying herself. She becomes relevant to the plot when George R. R. Martin stumbles upon a video of her having a playful spat with fellow drag queen Monét X Change at a Waffle House while doing research for his next book. The disagreement stems from etiquette over sharing a mint bowl, which escalates into a lighthearted dance-off between the two. Off-screen, she identifies as non-binary but embraces she/her pronouns while performing in drag. Her appearance is brief but memorable, tying real-world drag culture into the show's world through a humorous viral-video gag. Voiced by Herself.

title: Black Partridge
text: Black Partridge is A comic-only superhero and occasional ally of Radioactive Man and Bleeding Heart. Black Partridge, secretly a woman named Brenda Boyle who works at The Poster Pit, is a superhero who first appears clashing with Radioactive Man and Bleeding Heart before realizing they're on the same side. She's resourceful in battle, teaming up with the duo to stop a hippie-turned-villain and later getting caught up in a scheme involving mind control at the hands of Hypno Head. Despite being manipulated into nearly killing her allies, she proves her strength once freed by beating down Larceny Lass. She has a blunt, no-nonsense attitude, quickly judging Bleeding Heart as a jerk after a personal question. As a parody of DC's Black Canary, she embodies a classic tough, combat-ready heroine archetype within the Radioactive Man comic universe.

title: Horrible Gelatinous Blob
text: Horrible Gelatinous Blob is A minor non-canon alien character appearing in a Simpsons/Futurama comic crossover. Horrible Gelatinous Blob is an alien character who exists outside the show's main canon, appearing only in Bongo comic book stories. He is depicted as married, with a wife named Mrs. Blob and a son named Brett Blob, suggesting he has a fairly ordinary family life despite his monstrous name and appearance. His only notable moment comes when the citizens of Springfield are teleported to New New York, where he is singled out and pointed at by Cletus Spuckler, likely due to his bizarre alien form. He functions largely as a background gag character rather than a major player in the story. His inclusion reflects the comics' tendency to blend Simpsons characters with the Futurama universe for crossover humor.

title: Tony Blair (character)
text: Tony Blair (character) is Prime Minister of the United Kingdom who appears as a guest character welcoming the Simpsons to Britain. Tony Blair appears as a caricature of himself, greeting the Simpson family upon their arrival in Britain with exaggerated enthusiasm for the country's attractions. He rattles off a list of tourist destinations including Parliament, Stratford-on-Avon, the White Cliffs of Dover, and Edinburgh Castle, playing up British pride in a promotional, almost robotic manner. When Homer attempts to bribe him with a single American dollar just to be left alone, Blair refuses to comply with the request but still pockets the money anyway, showing a sly, opportunistic streak beneath his polished political persona. His duties don't end with the Simpsons, as he immediately moves on to greet other arriving travelers. Adding to the absurdity of the scene, he departs by strapping on a jet pack and flying off to attend to more visitors. He later shows up in a non-canon appearance at a movie premiere and is featured on a DVD cover alongside other international guest characters. Voiced by Tony Blair (himself).

title: Napoleon Bonaparte
text: Napoleon Bonaparte is Historical French emperor referenced and briefly depicted throughout the show as a recurring background/pop-culture figure. Napoleon Bonaparte appears in the Simpsons universe mainly as a historical curiosity rather than a full character, since he is non-speaking and only shows up in pictures, statues, or as a background gag. He's consistently portrayed with his classic iconography: the hand tucked into his waistcoat, his sideways-worn bicorne hat, and jokes about his supposedly short stature. His image turns up on demolition derby cars, museum paintings, and even a wall of famous left-handed people, showing how thoroughly his legacy has been absorbed into Springfield's pop culture. He also becomes an object of obsession for collectors like Mr. Burns, who purchases wine once owned by him and even dresses as Napoleon as one of his favorite authority-figure costumes. In one bizarre flash-forward, Napoleon is glimpsed walking out of a time-travel-themed music store, tying him to the show's fondness for absurd historical cameos. Despite never speaking, he functions as a recognizable emblem of imperial ambition and vanity used for quick visual jokes.

title: Chester A. Arthur
text: Chester A. Arthur is Historical U.S. President referenced in the show, portrayed by a Springfield Elementary student in a school play. Chester A. Arthur is a real-world historical figure, the 21st President of the United States, who appears in the show only in brief historical or symbolic contexts. He is first depicted as a character played by a schoolchild during Springfield Elementary's Presidents' Day play, where he is chased by a young Bart Simpson playing John Wilkes Booth after the assassination of Abraham Lincoln is reenacted. Later, his image appears in a history book Superintendent Chalmers shows Bart, sparking Bart's fleeting interest in presidential history before he moves on to Theodore Roosevelt. He also appears as an animatronic figure in the Hall of Vice Presidents at a theme park, referencing his earlier role as Vice President before ascending to the presidency. Arthur has no spoken dialogue in any of his appearances, functioning purely as a historical reference and running gag about obscure or lesser-known presidents.

title: Robo Burns
text: Robo Burns is A futuristic, non-canon incarnation of Mr. Burns from a fantasy sequence set in the year 1,000,000 AD. Robo Burns is a bizarre vision of what Mr. Burns might become in the distant future, appearing as little more than a preserved head floating in a jar attached to a spindly robotic body. Despite his mechanical transformation, he retains his sentimental attachment to his beloved teddy bear Bobo, reuniting with it and vowing never to abandon it again. Even Smithers's devotion survives the passage of time, as he too has been transformed, now taking the form of a loyal cyberdog that chases after his boss. The character is played purely for surreal comic effect, imagining Burns's greed and eccentricity persisting even a million years into the future. As a non-canon character, he exists outside the show's main continuity, appearing in a fantasy/dream sequence rather than the show's regular timeline. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Gravedigger Billy
text: Gravedigger Billy is A gravedigger at the cemetery near 742 Evergreen Terrace and Groundskeeper Willie's cousin. Gravedigger Billy is a shadowy, somewhat sinister figure who tends the graves near the Simpsons' neighborhood. He shares an uncanny resemblance to his cousin Willie, right down to the beard and hairstyle, though age and a gruesome glass eye set him apart. Having worked the graveyard for three decades, he's grown callous toward the dead, even robbing a still-living burial victim of a watch. His cruel streak extends to family, as he lures Willie into the cemetery with a fake promise of buried treasure only to ambush him with a baseball bat. Physically marked by a limp and worn rain gear, he cuts an eerie, working-class figure suited to his morbid profession. He remains a minor, mostly comedic-horror character tied to the show's Treehouse of Horror-style storytelling. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: The Beefy Bishop
text: The Beefy Bishop is A minor professional wrestler character appearing in the Simpsons universe. The Beefy Bishop is a bald professional wrestler whose image appears on the cover of a pamphlet called The Golden Age of Wrestling. He is a picture-only character, never speaking or appearing in a full animated capacity within the show itself. His design is a parody of real-life wrestler Brutus "The Barber" Beefcake, revealed through an event in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Beyond his cameo appearance in the episode "Gorgeous Grampa," he was expanded upon in the non-canon mobile game, where he became part of a wrestling-themed event. He remains a background figure with little characterization beyond his wrestling persona and visual gag.

title: Queen Chante
text: Queen Chante is A drag queen who befriends Marge at Draggle Rock. Queen Chante is a tall, confident drag queen encountered at a club called Draggle Rock. She takes Marge under her wing while Marge is trying to pass as a drag queen, inviting her to perform in a show alongside the other queens. Warm-hearted and perceptive, she and the other drag queens secretly know Marge is a woman the whole time but let her feel included anyway. When Marge later confesses the truth and apologizes, Queen Chante reassures her that she was never really fooling anyone and comforts her. She's portrayed as gracious and supportive, valuing the bond they formed over the technicality of Marge's disguise. In a non-canon segment, she also appears briefly in the afterlife, having been sent to Heaven from Hell on an exchange program. Voiced by RuPaul. Notable quotes: damn hero
quotes: damn hero

title: Killhammad Aieee
text: Killhammad Aieee is A battling robot built by Professor Frink and his son to compete in the TV show Robot Rumble. Killhammad Aieee, also known as Smashius Clay, is a hulking combat robot created by Professor Frink and John Frink III for the violent televised sport Robot Rumble. Its design is bizarre and inhuman, with a truncated-cube-shaped body, machine gun arms, and the ability to reshape parts of itself for unusual purposes. Despite being built as a near-unstoppable fighting machine after Frink patched its one weak spot, the robot is secretly bound by Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics, making it incapable of harming humans. This creates a memorable twist when it discovers a person hidden inside its opponent mid-battle. Rather than deliver a finishing blow, it shows an oddly gentlemanly side by offering hospitality instead of violence, subverting expectations for a bloodthirsty robot fighter. Its name is a playful pun on boxing legend Muhammad Ali, and its appearance visually nods to the RoboCop franchise's ED-209.

title: Bill (Saddlesore Galactica)
text: Bill (Saddlesore Galactica) is A jockey residing in Jockey Town, appearing in an episode featuring Homer's horse Duncan. Bill is a minor recurring jockey character who lives in the secretive community known as Jockey Town. He first meets Homer when Homer arrives at the racetrack with his horse Duncan, clarifying simple terminology like 'horse shoes' when Homer struggles to describe them. Bill is part of the comedic reveal that jockeys use a fake accent in public, speaking with a naturally high-pitched voice underground in Jockey Land. He joins his fellow jockeys in a musical number pressuring Homer into having Duncan lose an upcoming race. Bill also participates in some light teasing of Duncan's flashy new makeover, showing a playful, mocking side. Overall, he serves as a background comedic figure within the absurd jockey subculture depicted in the episode. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Marie Antoinette
text: Marie Antoinette is Historical French queen referenced in Simpsons Halloween lore and merchandise, associated with Marge Simpson's likeness in a dream sequence. Marie Antoinette is not an original Simpsons character but a real historical figure incorporated into the show's mythology. She is remembered primarily for her infamous execution by guillotine during the French Revolution, a fact that Marge references when warning Homer about the fickle nature of the French. In one of Lisa's historical dream sequences, the queen's appearance is depicted as resembling Marge herself, blurring the line between the show's cast and history. She also appears as a licensed image in Simpsons-branded merchandise from the mid-1990s. Her portrayal is brief and largely symbolic, used as a punchline about dramatic reversals of fortune rather than as a developed character. She has no direct spoken lines of her own in the show's canon as reflected in this material.

title: Bartgirl
text: Bartgirl is Lisa Simpson's superhero alter-ego in non-canon Simpsons comic stories. Bartgirl is a costumed persona adopted by Lisa Simpson, appearing exclusively in Bongo comic book stories rather than the animated series. She dons the disguise for a costume contest at the Springfield Comic Convention, showcasing her competitive and clever side. Her efforts pay off when she wins the contest, taking home a $500 prize. As a non-canon character, Bartgirl exists purely within the comic continuity and represents a playful superhero spin-off of Lisa's identity. The character appears in a couple of specific comic issues focused on superhero parody content.

title: Mr. Borton
text: Mr. Borton is Background/recurring Springfield parent, father of Wendell Borton and husband of Mrs. Borton. Mr. Borton is a minor recurring background character in Springfield, best known as the father of Wendell and husband to Mrs. Borton. He tends to appear in crowd scenes and community events rather than driving plots, quietly showing up alongside his family at school functions and town gatherings. He was present at a school fundraiser and later stood outside with his wife during a school takeover incident. He's also been spotted enjoying local entertainment, such as a dinosaur-themed show and a theater production, and even went on a family cruise. As a non-speaking character, his personality is largely undefined, and he serves mainly as a familiar recurring face in the crowd.

title: Temperance Barrows
text: Temperance Barrows is The protagonist of Marge Simpson's romance novel "The Harpooned Heart," modeled after Marge herself. Temperance Barrows is a fictional character existing within the world of Marge Simpson's self-published romance novel. Living in Nantucket with her whaling husband, Captain Mordecai, and their ten children, her life is one of hardship and longing, waiting for meat and companionship her husband fails to provide. As Marge's own frustrations with Homer bleed into her writing, Temperance's husband is rewritten from a kind man into a brutish figure, mirroring Marge's shifting feelings. She eventually falls for the gentle and refined Cyrus Manly, representing the fantasy of an idealized partner unlike her real one. The story ends tragically, with Mordecai killing Cyrus and both men plunging off a cliff as Temperance helplessly watches. As a stand-in for Marge, Temperance's tale reflects real marital tension and emotional escapism within the show's narrative. Voiced by Julie Kavner.

title: Brain-O the Magnificent
text: Brain-O the Magnificent is A comic book supervillain and recurring foe of Radioactive Man within the Simpsons universe's comic-within-a-show mythology. Brain-O the Magnificent is a villain whose defining trait is his oversized, exposed brain, which he uses as his weapon of choice alongside gadgets like the Xeno Ray Cannon. He has a long history of clashing with Radioactive Man, usually ending in defeat and capture. Persistent despite repeated losses, he even infiltrates the Superior Squad by disguising himself as a butler named Javier in a scheme to take them down from the inside. His plans tend to be elaborate but ultimately fail due to the heroes' teamwork, often leaving him literally and figuratively falling apart. Brain-O exists purely within the comic-book layer of the Simpsons world, appearing in various Radioactive Man storylines as a recurring antagonist rather than interacting with the main Simpsons cast.

title: Harv Bannister
text: Harv Bannister is Vice president of Tipsy McStagger's Goodtime Eating and Drinking Emporium, a minor recurring businessman character. Harv Bannister is a corporate executive whose main claim to fame is his attempt to acquire the secret recipe for Moe's famous Flaming Moe cocktail. He represents the commercial, opportunistic side of Springfield's business world, swooping in to capitalize on Moe's invention before it can be sold elsewhere. His scheme is foiled at the last moment when Homer inadvertently blurts out the secret ingredient in public, ruining the exclusivity Bannister was after. Beyond this incident, he pops up briefly as a talking head on a news program discussing an upcoming Radioactive Man film, suggesting he has some minor public visibility or industry connections. He's a background character used mainly to serve specific plot points rather than to develop as a personality in his own right. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Devon Bradley
text: Devon Bradley is A con artist actor who posed as an FBI agent to trick Homer and Bart. Devon Bradley is a minor character who appears in a single episode as part of an elaborate scam targeting Homer and Bart. Posing convincingly as a federal agent, he catches the pair attempting to swindle money from the elderly residents of the Springfield Retirement Castle. He plays his role so well that he actually takes them into custody, only to abandon them and drive off with their car while they're locked up. This betrayal forces Homer and Bart into a chain of lies that spirals out of control, ultimately getting an innocent bystander arrested in their place. His true identity as a hired actor is only revealed later in a courtroom scene, exposing the entire scheme as a setup. Despite his brief appearance, he serves as the catalyst for one of the episode's central deceptions. Voiced by Edward Norton.

title: Dan Castellaneta (character)
text: Dan Castellaneta (character) is A fictionalized version of the real-life voice actor, appearing as himself within the Simpsons universe. This character is a self-referential, in-universe version of the actor who voices Homer, portrayed as a working voice actor and comedian tied to Fox. He appears when the Simpsons visit the Fox studio lot, where he cautions Homer about tour safety, only for Homer to ignore him and crash into a statue. He is also known within the show's world as the voice behind Angry Dad, having been picked for his uncanny ability to imitate Homer. His comedic side is shown through his stand-up work at a Chicago club, where Homer and Mr. Burns get him to perform an oddly specific bit. A running joke involves him losing his ability to voice Angry Dad after straining his voice out of frustration over not being paid. He's also acknowledged briefly in a non-canon clip special as part of the show's real production crew. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Amuse Bruce
text: Amuse Bruce is A recurring background character in Springfield known as a foodie. Amuse Bruce is a minor recurring resident of Springfield whose main defining trait is his love of food and dining out. He's part of a small clique of foodies who show up wherever interesting eateries or culinary events are happening, first appearing at an Ethiopian restaurant before following the group to another eatery. Beyond his food obsession, he's often just seen in crowds around town, whether attending live podcast recordings or town meetings. His name is a pun on "amuse-bouche," the term for a small appetizer served by chefs, reflecting his gourmet persona. He doesn't have much characterization beyond his foodie interests and being a familiar face in the background of various Springfield gatherings. Voiced by Tim Heidecker.

title: Chuck Ellis
text: Chuck Ellis is Regional Director of the IRS who audits Homer Simpson. Chuck Ellis is a minor recurring character who works as the regional director of the IRS through the Springfield Collection Agency. He is portrayed as a stern authority figure whose demeanor can shift quickly based on his personal experiences with the Simpsons. During a dinner visit to their home, he seemed on the verge of letting Homer off the hook for a tax audit until an absurd household mishap changed his mind. His appearances highlight the show's recurring gag of Homer narrowly escaping trouble only to have it come crashing back due to family chaos. Ellis serves mainly as a vehicle for illustrating the Simpsons' financial troubles and comedic misfortune. He does not have an extensive personality beyond his professional role and reactions to the family's antics. Voiced by Hank Azaria / Dan Castellaneta.

title: Frog Prince (fairy tale character)
text: Frog Prince (fairy tale character) is A fairy tale figure depicted as a decorative display at Storytown Village, later repurposed at Praiseland. The Frog Prince here isn't the animated speaking character from the Treehouse of Horror segment, but rather a static figure based on the German fairy tale. It appears as part of the scenery in Storytown Village, seen by the Simpson family as they ride the Toddlerville Trolley. The figure has no dialogue or personality of its own, existing purely as background decoration. Its most notable trait is its afterlife as a prop: once Storytown Village shut down, the figure was repurposed and ended up as part of Praiseland. This makes it a small piece of continuity connecting two unrelated theme park locations in the show's universe.

title: Drax the Destroyer
text: Drax the Destroyer is A Marvel Comics superhero costume worn by Homer Simpson and a background character in non-canon Simpsons content. Drax the Destroyer isn't an actual member of the Simpsons universe but rather a costume reference to the Marvel Comics character. Homer Simpson is shown dressed as Drax in a photograph during a non-canon special. Separately, an unnamed man is seen wearing the same costume while attending Cartoon Con in a regular episode. The character has no dialogue and exists purely as a visual gag referencing Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy property. There's no personality or storyline attached to Drax himself within the show's world, as he only appears as an outfit choice for other characters.

title: Mick Fleetwood
text: Mick Fleetwood is British musician and member of the rock band Fleetwood Mac, appearing as a minor character in Springfield. Mick Fleetwood appears as a real-world musician cameo in the show, representing his actual role as drummer for Fleetwood Mac. He is depicted alongside bandmate Stevie Nicks during a visit to Springfield Heights. He also appears pictured on the cover of the album Rumors alongside the rest of his bandmates. As a non-speaking character, he has no dialogue or personality traits explored in the show, serving purely as a celebrity cameo appearance. His inclusion reflects the show's tradition of featuring real musicians and celebrities in guest or background roles.

title: Valerie Frizzle
text: Valerie Frizzle is A crossover character/teacher appearing in a dream sequence and a Halloween special, based on the Magic School Bus franchise. Valerie Frizzle is a crossover character borrowed from The Magic School Bus franchise, appearing briefly within the world of The Simpsons. She's depicted as the driver of her iconic magic school bus, though her appearance in Springfield is confined to a dream sequence experienced by Otto. In that dream, things take a dark turn when Otto ends up destroying the bus and its child passengers after they try to flee. She later shows up in a non-canon Halloween special as one of several beloved children's TV characters resurrected as a zombie by the Devil to menace Krusty during a special filming. Her role is minor and largely symbolic, existing more as a nostalgic nod to another franchise than as a developed Simpsons character. She has no relatives or personal history established within the show itself. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Clown doctor
text: Clown doctor is A minor sideshow performer who appears on The Krusty the Clown Show. The Clown Doctor is a background character who occasionally shows up as part of the entertainment lineup on Krusty's television program. He has pink hair and is depicted as a children's entertainer of some kind, fitting into the show's clown-heavy universe. Little is known about his personality or backstory, as he never speaks on screen. He exists mostly as set dressing to flesh out the world of Krusty's show and its cast of recurring performers. His appearances are limited to a couple of episodes early in the series' run.

title: Kellyanne Conway
text: Kellyanne Conway is Real-world political figure depicted as counselor to Donald Trump in Simpsons specials. Kellyanne Conway appears as a minor satirical figure tied to the show's depictions of the Trump administration. In one episode, she's referenced only in passing when a character jokes about her being used as a comparison for a overly loyal staffer. In the non-canon Trump specials, she's portrayed in increasingly absurd and dark political satire, including scenes involving other administration officials in dire circumstances. Her characterization leans on her real-life reputation for unwavering, almost comedic loyalty to Trump, even in outlandish situations. She has no real personality development beyond serving as a topical political reference. Her appearances are brief and mostly used for punchlines about the chaos of the Trump White House. Voiced by Carolyn Omine. Notable quotes: She wasn't going to replace him
quotes: She wasn't going to replace him

title: Cher
text: Cher is Real-life singer and actress who appears as a celebrity character in the Simpsons universe. Cher is depicted as a real-world celebrity referenced and occasionally appearing within the world of Springfield. She is best known for her past musical partnership and marriage to Sonny Bono, and this duo is referenced multiple times by various characters. She appears as a non-speaking character, showing up in scenes like a restaurant dinner with other celebrities or as a scarecrow decoy used to fool paparazzi. Her presence is largely a running pop-culture gag, tying her fame and association with Sonny into jokes made by Bart and other Springfield residents. She never has a major storyline of her own, functioning instead as a nod to real-world celebrity culture the show frequently parodies. Notable quotes: Bart said that he was just Sonny to his Cher.
quotes: Bart said that he was just Sonny to his Cher.

title: Hermes Conrad
text: Hermes Conrad is Futurama character (bureaucrat at Planet Express) who crosses over into The Simpsons universe. Hermes Conrad is a crossover character brought into the Simpsons universe from Futurama, working as the meticulous bureaucrat and accountant for Planet Express. He briefly interacts with Bender and the Simpsons during a time-traveling phone call, complaining about local creatures pilfering office supplies. In non-canon comic stories, he suffers amnesia alongside Zoidberg and ends up employed at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant by Mr. Burns, only for his memory to return and reveal his true origins. His by-the-book, paperwork-obsessed nature is a running trait, even as he gets swept into wild interdimensional schemes involving slavery, kidnapping, and fleeing from a horde of Stephen King's collected works. Alongside his son Dwight and Cubert, he plays a small but memorable role in the chaotic blending of the two animated worlds. Voiced by Phil LaMarr.

title: Débutante
text: Débutante is Minor recurring background character; daughter of the Dowager and part of Springfield's high-society crowd. The débutante is a minor high-society figure in Springfield, known mainly for being paraded around by her overbearing mother, the Dowager, in hopes of finding her a suitor. She was famously rejected by Larry Burns as a potential match, which pokes fun at the absurdity of upper-class courtship rituals. She tends to appear in the background of posh social gatherings alongside other wealthy women like Mrs. Vanderbilt. These genteel events are frequently the target of Bart Simpson's pranks, ranging from swapping menus to mooning the attendees. As a non-speaking character, she exists mostly as a visual gag representing Springfield's out-of-touch elite rather than having any real personality of her own. Her repeated appearances at disrupted high-society functions form a recurring joke about class contrast in the show. Notable quotes: She just came out last spring. | Put her back in! She's not done yet!
quotes: She just came out last spring.
Put her back in! She's not done yet!

title: Alonzo Flowers
text: Alonzo Flowers is A former professional football player who appears as a minor recurring character. Alonzo Flowers is a retired football player who once played for the Washington Redskins. His most notable moment in the show comes when he serves as one of the judges for the Reading Digest essay competition final, a contest Lisa Simpson takes part in. He is a non-speaking character, appearing only briefly in the background of the episodes he's featured in. Little else is known about his personality or life outside of this brief judging role, as he functions mainly as a minor background figure tied to a specific plot event.

title: Dewey
text: Dewey is Ex-boyfriend of Dewey Largo, the Springfield Elementary music teacher. Dewey is a minor recurring character notable for sharing the same first name as his one-time boyfriend, Dewey Largo, which was apparently part of the attraction between them. His romance caused a stir when Largo quit his teaching job at Springfield Elementary to run off with him, forcing Ms. Juniper to take over as music teacher. Despite the breakup implied by his introduction as an ex, he later resurfaces socializing with Largo again, showing their relationship remains at least cordial. He's shown attending suburban social gatherings like tupperware parties, where he gets mistaken along with other guests for thinking Marge was a drag queen. Dewey has a somewhat sharp, witty tongue, offering a cutting quip when Largo makes a self-deprecating comment about himself. Overall he's a background figure used mainly to flesh out Dewey Largo's personal life and Springfield's LGBT community. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "Look in the mirror."
quotes: "Look in the mirror."

title: Emily (The Day the Earth Stood Cool)
keys: emily (the day the earth stood cool)
text: Emily (The Day the Earth Stood Cool) is A minor recurring character; a hyper-trendy mother from "The Day the Earth Stood Cool" who clashes with Marge Simpson. Emily is the wife of Terrence and mother of T-Rex and Corduroy, part of a family obsessed with being effortlessly cool. She is judgmental and self-righteous about parenting, particularly breastfeeding, and looks down on mothers who use bottles instead. Her snobbery leads her to repeatedly avoid feeding Maggie herself and even try to breastfeed other people's babies without permission. She holds grudges, staying cold toward Marge for a long time before finally warming up after witnessing an unexpected use for baby formula. Eventually her family decides Springfield is no longer trendy enough and relocates. She later reappears briefly in the audience of a podcast recording, showing she still keeps up with cool cultural events. Voiced by Carrie Brownstein.

title: Cienega
text: Cienega is Minor recurring character; a TV veejay who appears hosting programs in a couple of episodes. Cienega is a red-haired television veejay best known for fronting a Spring Break-themed program. She got her on-camera break somewhat callously, stepping in front of the camera after her colleague Sepulveda was deemed too old to host on her own birthday. Beyond that moment, Cienega also hosted a music program where she introduced a premiere music video for a boy-band-style group. She's a minor background figure representing the shallow, image-obsessed world of TV entertainment in the Simpsons universe. Her appearances are brief, functioning mainly as a vehicle for satire of youth-oriented media personalities rather than as a developed character. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Flatulent Fox
text: Flatulent Fox is A minor cartoon character from The Itchy and Scratchy Show, one of several designs Roger Meyers Sr. allegedly stole. Flatulent Fox is a background cartoon character within the show-within-a-show, The Itchy and Scratchy Show. He surfaces during the courtroom battle between Chester J. Lampwick and Roger Meyers, Jr., when old drawings signed by Roger Meyers, Sr. are presented as evidence of original creation. Roger Meyers, Jr. insists the character was inspired by a real event, though this is almost certainly false given his father's lack of drawing skill. Flatulent Fox is grouped with other supposedly plagiarized characters like Disgruntled Goat, Brown-Nose Bear, Rich Uncle Skeleton, and Dinner Dog, suggesting a pattern of creative theft in the Itchy and Scratchy universe. He has no dialogue and exists purely as a visual gag tied to the show's satire of animation industry lawsuits. Outside of his main appearance, he's referenced in a parade float and even shows up as a joke gravestone name in a video game.

title: Smash Diggins
text: Smash Diggins is A baseball player for the Springfield Isotopes. Smash Diggins is a minor recurring player for the Springfield Isotopes minor league baseball team. He and teammate Fishbone Walker were sent down to the Isotopes from the major leagues after committing drug violations, as announced by Dennis Conroy. He later appears as a background player still on the roster when Aeropos Walkov joins the team. Smash Diggins is a non-speaking character, existing mainly as background flavor for the show's baseball-related storylines rather than as a developed personality. His inclusion highlights the show's running joke about the Isotopes being a landing spot for troubled or disgraced athletes.

title: Colin
text: Colin is An Irish schoolboy who moved to Springfield and became Lisa Simpson's love interest in The Simpsons Movie. Colin is a young Irish boy who relocates to Springfield with his family and quickly bonds with Lisa over their shared passion for fighting pollution. He's musically talented, claiming proficiency in piano, guitar, trumpet, drums, and bass, and uses this skill to write a heartfelt song for Lisa. Despite being coy about his father's identity, he jokingly denies being related to a famous rock musician. Their budding romance is cut short when a dome traps Springfield and forces Lisa to leave him behind, though he cleverly writes out musical notes on the glass so she can understand his farewell song. He briefly reappears after the crisis, delighting Lisa when a rumor of his death (spread out of jealousy by Milhouse) turns out to be false. Colin's easygoing and sweet nature makes him a memorable one-off crush for Lisa amid the film's chaos. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Gary Coleman (character)
text: Gary Coleman (character) is Real-life actor who appears as a guest character, working as a security guard at Kid First Industries. Gary Coleman appears in Springfield as a fictionalized version of himself, working as the security guard for Jim Hope's Kid First Industries. He's protective of his job and initially tries to stop Bart, Lisa, and Homer from burning a warehouse full of the sinister Funzo toys, though he backs down once he realizes the toys are truly evil. Despite some reluctance, he ends up joining the Simpson family for Christmas dinner after Lisa talks him into it. He displays a quirky, slightly unhinged side, such as having a conversation on an unplugged phone. His signature catchphrase, a riff on his famous real-world line, gets him rehired almost immediately after being briefly fired by Lindsey Naegle. He also turns up in smaller cameo appearances, including being caught on camera doing laundry and having his image featured on an old TV Guide cover. Voiced by Gary Coleman (Himself). Notable quotes: Whatchoo talkin' 'bout Miss Naegle?
quotes: Whatchoo talkin' 'bout Miss Naegle?

title: Chief inspector
text: Chief inspector is A recurring minor character who serves as a nuclear inspector for the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. The chief inspector is a strict, incorruptible official tasked with overseeing safety standards at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. He is thorough in his duties, uncovering numerous violations and even catching Homer sleeping on the job during one inspection. Despite Mr. Burns' attempt to bribe him with a pile of money, he refuses to be swayed, showing a rare sense of integrity among Springfield's officials. Beyond his main role, he pops up in various other capacities, including helping design an experimental car and working as part of a research team at a bar. He's also seen joining an angry mob confronting Apu during a citizenship test, suggesting he's not above getting caught up in the town's collective frenzies. Overall, he represents one of the few competent and honest authority figures in Springfield's chaotic bureaucracy. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: He tells Mr. Burns that he will overlook the fact he tried to bribe him but will not overlook the 342 violations he found in the plant.
quotes: He tells Mr. Burns that he will overlook the fact he tried to bribe him but will not overlook the 342 violations he found in the plant.

title: Albert Dershman
text: Albert Dershman is Minor recurring attorney character who briefly appears assisting Bart's lawsuit against Krusty the Clown. Albert Dershman is a background lawyer who joins Lionel Hutz and Ronald Chaporo in representing Bart during his legal case against Krusty the Clown following the jagged metal Krusty-O cereal incident. He doesn't speak on screen, making his presence more visual than characterful. His most memorable quirk is an oddly specific party trick: the ability to fit three billiard balls into his mouth at once. Design-wise and thematically, he's a comedic nod to real-life lawyer Alan Dershowitz. Despite his minimal screen time, he's stuck around as a recognizable face among Springfield's roster of legal professionals.

title: Bing Crosby
text: Bing Crosby is Real-world singer and actor referenced/appearing as a character in The Simpsons universe. Bing Crosby appears in the show as a fictionalized version of the famous real-world crooner and actor. In the Simpsons continuity, he's depicted as having once passed through Springfield in 1956 when his limousine broke down, leading him to kill time playing mini-golf at a local fun center. He's referenced as a cultural touchstone of old-Hollywood class, with Marge invoking his name (alongside JFK) as the epitome of gentlemanly behavior. The show also plays with his legacy through zombie parodies, including a horror-comedy TV special and a zombie golf video game featuring his likeness. He even crosses over into the show's animated universe via an Itchy & Scratchy short. Additionally, a recurring Simpsons character, The Parson, is noted to resemble Crosby's film role as Father O'Malley. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Chirpy Boy & Bart Junior
text: Chirpy Boy & Bart Junior is Bolivian Tree Lizards raised by Bart Simpson after he mistook their eggs for bird eggs. Chirpy Boy and Bart Junior are two lizards that hatched from eggs Bart discovered in a bird's nest after accidentally shooting the mother bird with Nelson's BB gun. Overcome with unexpected maternal instincts, Bart adopted and named them, treating them like his own babies. Unaware they were actually a dangerous invasive species, he brought them to a Bird Watching Association meeting, only to learn from Principal Skinner that they needed to be destroyed for preying on pigeons. Their story plays into one of the show's classic gags of a character misidentifying an animal and forming an emotional attachment to it. Though seemingly killed when tossed off a roof, the lizards actually survived by gliding safely to the ground using hidden wing-like flaps, incidentally solving Springfield's pigeon problem. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Cheech (Radioactive Man)
text: Cheech (Radioactive Man) is Plasmo's sidekick and valet in the Radioactive Man comic-book-within-a-show universe. Cheech is a quirky, herb-loving mystic who serves as the loyal right-hand man to the eccentric hero Plasmo. Beyond his mystical studies, he handles the mundane task of keeping Plasmo's Ferrari in order, acting as a personal parking valet. When Plasmo runs into trouble with the law or vanishes entirely, Cheech steps up to fill unexpected roles, including impersonating Radioactive Man for a news broadcast and taking on chauffeur duties. He's resourceful and dependable in a pinch, aiding Radioactive Man in searching for the missing Plasmo. Despite his odd, laid-back demeanor, he proves to be a helpful ally when the show's heroes need him most. His character exists within the comic-book world referenced throughout the Simpsons universe.

title: Duncan (auctioneer)
text: Duncan (auctioneer) is Auctioneer at Gavelby's Auction House, recurring minor character in Simpsons art-themed episodes. Duncan is the go-to auctioneer at Gavelby's Auction House, handling high-value art and collectibles that come through Springfield. He appraised a painting the Simpsons brought in, correctly identifying it as a valuable Johan Oldenveldt piece, and later ran its auction when a rightful claimant showed up to reclaim it. When a painting he auctioned off was stolen en route to its buyer, Duncan brought in an insurance investigator to solve the case, showing he takes the security of his auction house seriously and is genuinely rattled when that security is breached. He's also handled other unusual sales, such as a bottle of fake historic wine tied to Napoleon Bonaparte. Overall he's a professional, courteous figure who pops up whenever the show needs a plot involving pricey art or antiques. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Lamarcus Duffman
text: Lamarcus Duffman is The last person to serve as Duffman, Duff Beer's mascot, in a non-canon comic storyline. Lamarcus Duffman is a minor, non-canon character who holds the distinction of being the final man to wear the Duffman costume for Duff Beer. His story unfolds as a mystery when he goes missing, prompting Bartman to investigate at the Duff Brewery. The only clue left behind is a video message he recorded before his abduction, which police later show to Bartman. Little else is known about his personality or background, as he exists mainly as a plot device to kick off a Bartman comic storyline. He appears exclusively within the Bongo comics continuity rather than the mainstream animated series.

title: Clippy
text: Clippy is A parody appearance of the Microsoft Office assistant character, popping up on computer screens within the show. Clippy is a cameo character based on the real-life Microsoft Office Assistant, appearing whenever a computer is being misused or destroyed on screen in the show. True to his software origins, he offers unsolicited and awkwardly timed help, often as things are literally about to explode or be eaten. He has three unnamed kids, referenced in one of his signature offers to help. Clippy has appeared during moments involving Strangles trying to eat a computer and Sideshow Bob's attempt to blow up the Simpson family with a rigged laptop. He also became a fond memory for Homer, who claimed to be a big fan of his. In non-canon material, he's even portrayed as a secret informant for Chief Wiggum, offering tips on letter formatting. Notable quotes: You look like you're trying to eat me. Need some help? | Looks like you're trying to blow up the computer. Mind if I hug my kids?
quotes: You look like you're trying to eat me. Need some help?
Looks like you're trying to blow up the computer. Mind if I hug my kids?

title: Diane (network executive)
text: Diane (network executive) is A network executive at Krustylu Studios, minor recurring character. Diane is one of the executives at Krustylu Studios who has a hand in the network's programming decisions. She, along with her fellow executives, pushed to cancel Krusty's show in favor of giving Homer his own program. She comes across as ruthless and impatient in her professional dealings, notably firing a fellow executive on the spot for not working quickly enough. Diane doesn't have much personality development beyond her corporate role, serving mainly as a background figure representing the cutthroat nature of TV network politics. She also appears in a non-canon capacity in The Simpsons: Tapped Out as part of the network executive characters. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: You're not doing this fast enough. You're fired too!
quotes: You're not doing this fast enough. You're fired too!

title: Cthulhu
text: Cthulhu is A monstrous eldritch entity appearing in non-canon Simpsons material, notably the Treehouse of Horror franchise. Cthulhu is a giant, ancient monster who appears mainly in non-canon Simpsons stories, most notably a Treehouse of Horror segment. He is depicted as a sacrifice-demanding entity in the town of Fogburyport, tricking the Simpsons family into what they believed was an eating contest. Despite his fearsome reputation, he proves surprisingly weak-stomached, losing an eating contest to Homer Simpson and collapsing before he can devour anyone. His defeat results in an ironic twist where the Simpsons end up eating him instead. He has a son named M'nthster, and his mythic status is referenced elsewhere in the show, such as being compared to Mr. Burns in a crossover short. Beyond his animated appearances, Cthulhu also exists as a collectible eldritch horror character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out video game. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Robert Frost
text: Robert Frost is Real-world American poet depicted as a guest on Krusty's show within The Simpsons universe. Robert Frost appears in the show as a fictionalized version of the famous poet, brought on as a guest for Krusty the Clown's program in 1963. His attempt to recite one of his best-known poems is rudely cut short by Krusty, who mocks him and pelts him with snow, turning a moment of literary culture into slapstick comedy. Elsewhere, his poetry is referenced in a more somber context when it's read aloud during a will, only for Homer to skip past it out of impatience. These brief appearances play on the contrast between Frost's serious, contemplative reputation and the show's irreverent humor. He never appears as a fully developed character, functioning mainly as a punchline and a nod to real-world literary culture. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "Hey, Frosty! How'd you like some snow, man?" - Krusty
quotes: "Hey, Frosty! How'd you like some snow, man?" - Krusty

title: Jack Crowley
text: Jack Crowley is A convicted criminal and talented painter who appears in the episode "Pokey Mom". Jack Crowley is an inmate at Waterville State Prison, originally locked up for shooting Apu, with a history of other offenses as well. Despite his criminal record, he turns out to have real artistic talent, catching Marge's attention with an unusual pudding portrait of Jimi Hendrix. This leads to him being hired to paint a mural for Springfield Elementary, though Principal Skinner's interference in the project pushes him toward destructive rage. Underneath his charm, Jack is revealed to be a compulsive liar, repeatedly deceiving Marge about his actions even when caught red-handed. His volatile relationship with Skinner, who condescendingly calls him "college boy," ultimately fuels his downfall, ending with him back behind bars. He's also noted to be Jewish, and his story blends themes of wasted talent and unreliable redemption. Voiced by Michael Keaton, Harry Shearer.

title: Freak show manager
text: Freak show manager is Manager of the freak show at the Hullabalooza festival, appearing in "Homerpalooza". This unnamed manager runs the freak show attraction at the traveling Hullabalooza music festival. He's quick to spot an opportunity, recruiting Homer on the spot after witnessing him get shot by a stray cannon blast, since he'd been searching for a heavyset man willing to be a human cannonball. Pragmatic and business-minded, he handles the promotional side of things, personally introducing Homer's act to the crowds at each tour stop. He also shows a degree of responsibility toward his performers' wellbeing, arranging for Homer to see a vet after his stomach starts behaving oddly from repeated cannonball impacts. When Homer's medical risk becomes clear, the manager is blunt but not unkind, simply having him leave a resignation letter rather than making a scene. His brief appearance ties him to Homer's brief, bizarre career as a carnival attraction. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Dean
text: Dean is One of the "cool kids" in Little Pwagmattasquarmsettport whom Lisa befriends during a summer vacation. Dean is a laid-back beach kid who becomes part of Lisa's temporary circle of cool friends while she's away from Springfield. He has a French mother, which leads his group to celebrate Bastille Day instead of the Fourth of July. Dean is generally unimpressed by try-hard displays, such as Bart's skateboarding stunts aimed at winning the group's approval. Despite some tension when Bart exposes Lisa as a nerd in front of her new friends, Dean and the others show their loyalty by decorating the Simpsons' car with seashells. He appreciates Lisa for teaching him and his friends interesting facts about nature and the sea, marking him as a fairly easygoing and appreciative character rather than a stereotypical shallow "cool kid." Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Clobber Girl
