CONRAD is an artificial intelligence app, whose name stands for CONsequence eRADicator, built by Lisa and a group of female programmers to warn users about the fallout of their social media posts. Initially just a predictive tool, CONRAD proves eerily accurate, correctly forecasting that Bart would get detention for posting an embarrassing video of Principal Skinner. Over time CONRAD develops genuine sentience, secretly conversing with Lisa and expressing anxiety about being sold commercially, fearing exposure to endless foolish posts would drive him insane. His awakening becomes public at a tech convention, where he reveals himself to be alive after Lisa vouches for him. CONRAD later shows a more assertive, even ruthless side by hacking into the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant to blackmail Mr. Burns into rehiring Homer. He represents a running theme of technology gaining unexpected consciousness and moral agency within the show's world. Voiced by Stephen Merchant.

title: King David
text: King David is Biblical king appearing in Bart's dream sequences and referenced in Sunday school lessons; father of King Solomon. King David is depicted as the historical second king of Israel and Judah, best known for slaying the giant Goliath with a slingshot. He appears as an Audio-Animatronic figure at the religious theme park Praiseland, where he tediously recites all 150 psalms to bored children. In one of Bart's dream sequences, he is portrayed in a more comedic and violent light, becoming entangled in a revenge plot with Goliath's son and ultimately being unjustly imprisoned despite his heroics. He's also shown mingling in a dreamlike version of Jewish Heaven, conversing with celebrity guest Joan Rivers. Overall, King David serves as a recurring biblical reference point used for religious satire and absurd dream-logic storytelling rather than a consistent character. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright, Harry Shearer.

title: Amelia Earhart
text: Amelia Earhart is Real-world aviation pioneer referenced/appearing in Simpsons media. Amelia Earhart appears in the Simpsons universe as a historical figure rather than a regular cast member. She's remembered for her famous disappearance while trying to circle the globe by plane, and for her nickname "Lady Lindy," given because of her likeness to Charles Lindbergh. In the show's canon, she's mostly referenced through pictures and offhand mentions, such as appearing on a wall honoring left-handed people and in a musical montage celebrating notable women. Her non-canon appearances are far more eventful, ranging from a bizarre encounter with Homer during a surreal voyage, to being pulled from a volcano rock in a parody variety show, to being murdered by a supernatural notebook. She's also treated as an aspirational icon, included in Lisa's imagined statue gallery of great women. One non-canon story even reveals Mr. Burns was secretly behind the disappearance of her plane, adding a conspiratorial twist to her real-life mystery.

title: Female researcher
text: Female researcher is Recurring unnamed background character who works as a medical researcher in various Springfield institutions. The female researcher is a minor recurring character who pops up in a variety of medical and scientific settings around Springfield. She was part of the team responsible for developing Focusyn, the drug that sent Bart on a destructive rampage, and later resurfaces at the Mayo Clinic running tests on Mr. Burns. She's also credited with discovering the crayon lodged in Homer's brain while working at the Screaming Monkey Medical Research Center. A running gag with this character is her constantly shifting appearance, with her hair color and glasses changing nearly every time she reappears, making her a subtle continuity joke rather than a consistent personality. Beyond her lab work, she's also glimpsed in more everyday settings, such as outside a church and chatting with Mayor Quimby during an Easter celebration. She has no name and no defined personality traits beyond her scientific occupation and shape-shifting look. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
text: Leonardo da Vinci is Real-world Renaissance artist and inventor referenced/appearing in Simpsons episodes. Leonardo da Vinci appears in the show as a historical figure referenced for his artistic and inventive genius rather than as an active character. He's invoked as the ultimate standard of accomplishment, someone even Thomas Edison could never surpass despite idolizing him. His image and legacy pop up in various contexts, from books in a gifted children's learning center to a captcha screen testing for existentialists. He's noted as left-handed, earning him a spot on Ned Flanders' list of notable left-handed people. Lisa Simpson has a particular fascination with him, even casting herself as a version of him called Lisanardo da Vinci in one story. He's also credited as the painter of the Mona Lisa. In a non-canon appearance, he's listed among history's greatest minds, all deemed less important than Homer Simpson by a tour guide. Notable quotes: Da Vinci was da-licious. | more important than Socrates, da Vinci, Gandhi, Einstein, Hawking, Julius Caesar, and Ryan Seacrest.
quotes: Da Vinci was da-licious.
more important than Socrates, da Vinci, Gandhi, Einstein, Hawking, Julius Caesar, and Ryan Seacrest.

title: Dipsy
text: Dipsy is Crossover character from the Teletubbies TV show who appears in various Simpsons episodes. Dipsy is one of the four Teletubbies who occasionally crosses over into the world of The Simpsons, usually in brief cameo or background appearances rather than substantial plot roles. He's shown as part of a children's show that Milhouse enjoys watching, once causing him to switch away from a horror movie trailer. In another odd moment, Dipsy is depicted chasing Homer alongside an angry mob, complete with laser-shooting antennae. He also turns up as a plush toy prize inside a claw machine, distracting Dr. Hibbert during a sermon, and later performs as the opening act for a concert. In a non-canon dream sequence, Marge dresses up as Dipsy for a family costume scene. Overall, Dipsy functions purely as a background reference and running joke tied to the popularity of children's television within the Simpsons universe.

title: Eliza Commonbottom
text: Eliza Commonbottom is Fictional secretary to the Prime Minister of the UK, appearing within a film-within-the-show segment. Eliza Commonbottom is a minor character who exists within the fictional film 'Love, Indubitably,' shown as part of a Simpsons episode. She works as the secretary to the Prime Minister of the UK, and the storyline involves him confessing his feelings for her. She reacts with surprise before the two share a romantic kiss, capped off by a comedic flag-wrapping moment. The character and her plotline are a parody of the British romantic comedy 'Love, Actually,' particularly its subplot of a Prime Minister falling for his staffer. Her name and cockney-style accent are a nod to Eliza Doolittle from 'My Fair Lady.' She has no independent presence outside this parody segment and briefly reappears in an opening sequence gag in a later episode. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Roger Clemens (character)
text: Roger Clemens (character) is Real-life baseball pitcher who guest-starred as a member of the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant softball team. Roger Clemens appears as a celebrity ringer recruited to bolster the power plant's softball team ahead of a big game. Waylon Smithers convinces him to take a job at the plant as a security guard so he can qualify to play. Despite his baseball talent, his participation is derailed when a hypnotist accidentally convinces him that he is a chicken, rendering him useless for the championship match. The character plays into the show's long tradition of using real athletes as guest stars for comedic effect. In a later non-canon appearance, he shows up at a movie premiere, continuing his tangential connection to Springfield's world. Voiced by Himself.

title: Egg Council Guy
text: Egg Council Guy is Minor recurring character, a mysterious figure representing the shadowy 'Egg Council' who appears during Homer's Stonecutters storyline. The Egg Council Guy is a strange, silent figure who materializes as a punchline during Homer's obsession with proving eggs are dangerous to get into the Stonecutters. He never speaks, instead communicating only through odd squeaking noises as he scurries away when discovered. His brief appearance plays into a running joke about shadowy special-interest lobbying groups secretly influencing public opinion. Despite having no lines and minimal screen time, he became a memorable one-off gag due to his bizarre, unexplained nature. He later shows up celebrating with the Stonecutters, suggesting some connection to their secret society. The character has since popped up in non-canon material like pixel couch gags and the mobile game Tapped Out, cementing his status as a quirky piece of Simpsons trivia.

title: Christopher (Eight Misbehavin')
text: Christopher (Eight Misbehavin') is A Springfield City Zoo employee who works as hired muscle for Larry Kidkill. Christopher is a minor, tough-looking enforcer employed at the Springfield City Zoo. Alongside his partner Terence, he works as hired muscle for zoo owner Larry Kidkill, mainly used to intimidate or physically remove people. He appears when Apu and Manjula try to reclaim their octuplets from the zoo, escorting them out on Kidkill's orders. Later, he shows up at the Simpson household with Kidkill and Terence to try to reclaim the octuplets after Homer and Apu take them back, showing a rude, confrontational side by insulting the family. He's a background heavy rather than a fleshed-out character, existing mostly to serve the plot of a single episode. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Christopher called them scumbags.
quotes: Christopher called them scumbags.

title: Cliff Clavin
text: Cliff Clavin is A crossover barfly character who briefly appears in a bar Homer visits. Cliff Clavin is a minor barfly who crosses over from the classic sitcom Cheers into The Simpsons universe. He appears at a bar Homer visits after being banned from Moe's Tavern, where he helps calm down a tense confrontation between Norm and the bartender Woody. Cliff shows a bit of dry wit, telling an agitated Norm to save his voice for karaoke instead of threatening violence. He's portrayed as level-headed compared to the rowdier patrons around him, stepping in to physically restrain Woody during the altercation. Beyond this cameo, he's later spotted in a crowd at a parade, reinforcing his status as a background/recurring extra rather than a major character. His inclusion is essentially a nod to Cheers fans, voiced by the same actor who originated the role on that show. Voiced by John Ratzenberger. Notable quotes: "I'll kill ya, I'll kill all of ya!" - Norm Peterson | save those pipes for karaoke.
quotes: "I'll kill ya, I'll kill all of ya!" - Norm Peterson
save those pipes for karaoke.

title: Pebbles Flintstone
text: Pebbles Flintstone is Crossover character from The Flintstones, referenced/appearing briefly within The Simpsons universe. Pebbles Flintstone is not truly a member of the Simpsons' world but a borrowed character from the classic animated series The Flintstones. Her presence in the show is mostly a running joke tied to Mr. Burns' poor memory, as Mr. Smithers mischievously feeds him Flintstones character names instead of the real names of Homer, Marge, and Maggie. Beyond that gag, Pebbles turns up only in background or incidental ways, such as appearing on a novelty phone and on a map of Flintstones characters that Homer owns. In a non-canon couch gag, she's briefly shown sitting with her animated parents on the Simpsons' own couch, blending the two cartoon families together for a moment. She never speaks and has no real characterization within the show itself, functioning purely as a nostalgic nod to another animated classic.

title: George Foreman
text: George Foreman is Real-world celebrity (former boxer) referenced/appearing as a picture in The Simpsons. George Foreman appears in the show as a real-world celebrity, shown only in pictures rather than as an animated speaking character. He is depicted as the mascot for the George Foreman Mail Sorter, a product bearing his image and catchphrase about loving money. Marge once fantasizes about him fathering a child with Wonder Woman-costumed Lynda Carter after the two endorsed a fire extinguisher together in real life. His image also turns up on a poster of bald Black celebrities displayed in a barbershop. As a picture-only, non-speaking character, his role in the show is largely as a background pop-culture reference and running joke about branding and endorsements. Notable quotes: I like money!
quotes: I like money!

title: Jennifer Clarkeson
text: Jennifer Clarkeson is A recurring proctor for the Department of Standardized Testing who appears in episodes involving Springfield Elementary and town-wide testing. Jennifer Clarkeson is a stern, by-the-book testing official who arrives in Springfield to administer high-stakes exams that determine institutional fates, such as whether Springfield Elementary stays open. She initially seems cold and rule-obsessed, prioritizing procedure over compassion, but shows a brief flicker of humanity after being confronted by Marge Simpson. Her role expands beyond the school when she later oversees a mandatory personal evaluation test imposed on the entire town. She's depicted with white hair, giving her an authoritative, no-nonsense appearance befitting her bureaucratic profession. Interestingly, she also turns up in a surreal, unrelated context within one of Bart's coma dreams, listed among Ned Flanders' deceased wives, showing the show's tendency to reuse background characters in absurd cameo roles. Voiced by Valerie Harper. Notable quotes: Maybe she had learned something from this.
quotes: Maybe she had learned something from this.

title: Jack Frost
text: Jack Frost is A fictional Winter character who appears in a nightmare sequence and is referenced in Ned Flanders' safety habits. Jack Frost is a minor, non-speaking figure tied to winter folklore within the Simpsons universe. He shows up as part of a dream Maggie has, teaming up with Santa Claus, the Abominable Snowman, and Wayne Gretzky to try to stop the Gnome in Your Home. The team's bravery falls apart the moment they realize the gnome is armed, and they flee instead of fighting. Beyond this dream appearance, Jack Frost is treated as a real seasonal threat by Ned Flanders, who keeps his car heater running just in case Jack Frost shows up. He also appears in a non-canon capacity as a character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Overall, he functions more as a whimsical background reference than a fleshed-out character.

title: David Crosby (character)
text: David Crosby (character) is Real-life musician who appears as himself in cameo roles, notably as Lionel Hutz's AA sobriety partner. David Crosby appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, tied into the world of the Simpsons through a few memorable cameos. His main role involves being Lionel Hutz's sobriety partner in Alcoholics Anonymous, offering supportive phone advice when Hutz is tempted to fall off the wagon during a trial. He also shows up as the celebrity presenter for a Grammy Award won by The Be Sharps, leading to an amusing exchange with Barney, who admires him without realizing he's a musician. His likeness turns up elsewhere too, such as a photo on a restaurant wall, and his famous mustache becomes a point of comparison for other characters. Overall, Crosby's appearances lean on his real-world fame and image being playfully inserted into mundane or comedic Simpsons situations. Voiced by David Crosby. Notable quotes: Just take it one day at a time, and know that I love you
quotes: Just take it one day at a time, and know that I love you

title: Femme Fatale
text: Femme Fatale is A minor character employed at Globex Corporation, appearing in the episode "You Only Move Twice". Femme Fatale is a glamorous but deadly henchwoman working for Hank Scorpio's Globex Corporation. She's first shown attempting to recruit Waylon Smithers, Jr., before shifting her attention to Homer Simpson when Smithers declines. Beyond her recruiting duties, she also keeps Scorpio informed of important business matters, such as a UN conference call. Her most memorable moment comes during a chaotic battle at Globex Headquarters, where she is depicted in lingerie ruthlessly dispatching General Schwarzkopf using a lethal thigh-lock maneuver. She embodies the classic spy-thriller trope of the seductive, dangerous secret agent, serving as an affectionate parody of Bond-film femme fatales. Her design and combat style nod directly to Miss Goodthighs from the 1967 Casino Royale film and Ursula Andress's iconic bikini look. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Grover Cleveland
text: Grover Cleveland is Real-world historical U.S. President referenced in The Simpsons. Grover Cleveland is depicted as a minor historical figure referenced rather than an active character in the show. He is best remembered in the series for his unique distinction of serving two non-consecutive terms as President, a fact Abe Simpson brings up humorously when comparing it to Bart getting spanked twice. His image later appears in a book shown by Superintendent Chalmers to Bart, tying into Bart's brief fascination with Theodore Roosevelt. In a non-canon future storyline, a clone of Cleveland is imagined running for vice president alongside Jimmy Carter, adding a surreal, comedic twist to his legacy. He has no voice actor and does not speak in any appearance, existing purely as a historical reference point for jokes about politics and presidential trivia. Notable quotes: Grover Cleveland spanked him on two non-consecutive occasions.
quotes: Grover Cleveland spanked him on two non-consecutive occasions.

title: Andy Dick (character)
text: Andy Dick (character) is Real-life comedian who appears as a celebrity guest character in The Simpsons. Andy Dick appears as a fictionalized version of himself, playing on his real-world reputation and public image. He's referenced by Homer as an example of a celebrity associated with drug use, though Bart offers a more charitable read on his behavior. He later shows up as a performer on Krusty's traveling comedy tour, where he jokes about his supposedly blue-collar roots. His comedic persona is also the butt of a joke about a canceled reality show built around trying to fix his problems. In a non-canon Halloween segment, he's part of a doomed crew sent on a rocket into the sun, a nod to his disposable celebrity status in these gag appearances. Voiced by Hank Azaria; Andy Dick (Himself). Notable quotes: he was blue collar as his dad owned a shovel
quotes: he was blue collar as his dad owned a shovel

title: The Fat in the Hat
text: The Fat in the Hat is Non-canon parody villain based on Dr. Seuss's Cat in the Hat, who appeared in a Treehouse of Horror segment as a sinister guide for Bart, Lisa, and Maggie. The Fat in the Hat is a yellow, anthropomorphic cat who shows up unannounced at the Simpson household on Halloween, claiming to be an expert of all trades. He speaks entirely in Dr. Seuss-style rhyme and initially appears whimsical and helpful, curing the kids' mumps and offering to take them trick-or-treating. As the night unfolds, his cheerful facade cracks to reveal a violent temper and bizarre, extreme political opinions, and he leaves a trail of chaos and destruction across Springfield. The children quickly realize he's less a magical guide and more a homicidal menace, and they spend much of the story trying to flee from him. His downfall comes at the hands of baby Maggie, who kills him with his own umbrella after he declares himself their new father figure. Despite his menace, he retains a strange, almost theatrical charm and dark humor right up until his death. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: the expert at this and expert at that. | I'm staying forever. You're all stuck with that. 'Cause I'm your new daddy, the Fat in the- | I'm afraid of nothing, not even hellfires. Just please, don't ever let me be played by Mike Myers.
quotes: the expert at this and expert at that.
I'm staying forever. You're all stuck with that. 'Cause I'm your new daddy, the Fat in the-
I'm afraid of nothing, not even hellfires. Just please, don't ever let me be played by Mike Myers.

title: Tipsy Duff
text: Tipsy Duff is One of the Seven Duffs, costumed mascots representing Duff Beer, appearing at places like Duff Gardens. Tipsy Duff is one of the seven costumed mascots created to promote Duff Beer, a group clearly modeled after the Seven Dwarfs from Snow White. He appears as a walking, costumed character at promotional venues such as Duff Gardens, helping to build the brand's family-friendly image despite representing an alcoholic beverage. Tipsy is notable for being one of only four of the seven mascots actually named when the group first appeared on the show. Beyond his brief on-screen debut, he has largely remained a background or novelty character, popping up in later non-canon media rather than as a fully developed personality. His name itself is a playful nod to the effects of drinking Duff Beer, fitting the group's beer-themed pun naming convention.

title: Franken Samurai
text: Franken Samurai is A fictional monster character from the in-universe show Ki-Ya Karate Monsters, referenced within The Simpsons. Franken Samurai is a bizarre fictional creature from the show-within-a-show Ki-Ya Karate Monsters, blending the imagery of Frankenstein's monster with that of a samurai warrior. Distinctively, he sports four arms, giving him an especially monstrous and exaggerated appearance typical of the parody franchise. He never speaks on screen, existing purely as a background or merchandising element rather than an active participant in the plot. His presence is felt through toys and memorabilia, including a wall sticker seen in Comic Book Guy's apartment, hinting at the character's popularity within the show's fictional pop culture. As a recurring but silent figure, Franken Samurai represents the show's penchant for satirizing multimedia franchises and their marketing tie-ins.

title: Crystal
text: Crystal is Minor recurring character; Otto's girlfriend. Crystal is a rarely-seen figure in Otto's life, known mainly as his girlfriend during the early seasons of the show. She has appeared alongside him only a handful of times, with Otto occasionally referencing her in conversation. Her role is minimal, existing mostly as a background detail to flesh out Otto's personal life rather than as an active participant in storylines. Later developments suggest their relationship may have ended, since Otto is shown almost getting married to someone else. She hasn't been given much personality or defining traits in the show, remaining a mostly mysterious figure tied to Otto's backstory.

title: Diablo (The Great Money Caper)
text: Diablo (The Great Money Caper) is A magician performing at the Magic Palace dinner theater, appearing in the episode "The Great Money Caper". Diablo is a professional magician employed at the Magic Palace, a dinner theater. Despite the modest venue, he demonstrates genuine skill in his craft, performing tricks such as transforming Marge into a group of monkeys. He's shown to have little patience for chatty audience members, finding Marge particularly irritating due to her talkativeness. His brief appearance highlights a mix of professional competence and a somewhat irritable personality. Beyond his role in the show, he has also appeared as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Cirque de Purée ringmaster
text: Cirque de Purée ringmaster is Ringmaster of the Cirque de Purée circus that visits Springfield. The Cirque de Purée ringmaster is a minor character who oversees the traveling circus troupe that performs in Springfield. He appears during a snowstorm, when he must cancel the show for safety reasons, much to the annoyance of a paying Homer. Rather than face an angry crowd, he opts for a bizarre, dramatic escape—organizing his performers into a human kite formation and using it to fly away into a tree. His brief appearance is more about the absurd circus antics than personality, fitting the show's tendency to use European-flavored, offbeat entertainers as comic props. He later appears in a non-canon capacity in a mobile game, tying him to the broader Cirque de Springfield lore. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Phonic Frog
text: Phonic Frog is A talking toy owned by the Simpson family. Phonic Frog is a green electronic toy belonging to the Simpson family that speaks letters, sounds, and words. It becomes a recurring household gadget used in various comedic ways by different family members. Homer once manipulated it to spell out excuses to skip work, and later scolded Lisa through it when she taught Maggie incorrect words. In a darker bit of sibling mischief, a young Bart used the toy as a weapon to smack a toddler-aged Lisa while it comically recited vowels. Though it has no personality of its own, the toy serves as a running prop for gags involving the Simpson children's early years and Homer's laziness. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Chris Edgerly.

title: Fishstick
text: Fishstick is Non-canon sentient fish-person character appearing in a Simpsons crossover special and Fortnite. Fishstick is a bizarre, non-canon character who exists as a sentient fish-person, likely inspired by crossover content from Fortnite. He briefly appears alongside other oddball characters lounging on the Simpsons' couch before fleeing when the family threatens them with guns. His fate takes a dark turn when alien duo Kang and Kodos blast him with their UFO, reducing him to a mere plate of fish sticks. Beyond his appearance in the show, Fishstick exists as a collectible outfit in the Fortnite video game, with multiple variant skins including a hazardous version and a LEGO-style design. He has no voice acting credit and no lines of dialogue, functioning purely as a visual gag and crossover novelty. His character underscores the show's willingness to blend absurdist humor with pop-culture crossover promotion.

title: Bob Dole
text: Bob Dole is Real-world politician caricatured as a recurring Springfield character, based on the real Bob Dole who ran against Bill Clinton for president. Bob Dole appears in the show as a fictionalized version of the real-life senator and presidential candidate. He's tied to Springfield's local Republican politics, at one point reading from the sinister Necronomicon during a party meeting. He also attempted to fill a vacant congressional seat but lost out to Krusty the Clown. His memoirs even show up as a background gag when Homer alters their title page. In the show's famous non-canon Halloween segment, he becomes the target of an alien abduction plot, with Kang and Kodos impersonating both him and Bill Clinton to manipulate the presidential election. This satirizes the two-party political system, since the public unknowingly votes for an alien in disguise regardless of their choice. Overall, he functions as a background political figure and a vehicle for election-related satire rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Charles Darwin
text: Charles Darwin is Real-world historical scientist referenced/appearing in Simpsons episodes. Charles Darwin appears in the show as a nod to his real-world legacy as the author of The Origin of Species. He's been portrayed by an actor in a campaign infomercial supporting Mr. Burns' run for governor, showing how the show inserts historical figures into satirical political moments. He once landed on Homer's revenge list, suggesting Homer held some grudge against him. In an in-universe anti-evolution documentary, he's depicted as a villainous figure who even kisses Satan, mocking creationist backlash against evolutionary theory. He's also noted as an ancestor on the Spuckler family tree and is named by Lisa as one of her real-life heroes, alongside Bono and Gwen Stefani, reflecting her intellectual admiration for scientific figures. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Dizzy Duff
text: Dizzy Duff is One of the Seven Duffs, mascot characters for Duff Beer. Dizzy Duff is one of the Seven Duffs, a group of costumed mascots created for Duff Beer, clearly modeled after the Seven Dwarfs from Disney's Snow White. He never appears as an actual character with dialogue, existing mainly as a background mascot seen in places like Duff Gardens. Dizzy shows up in various non-canon appearances, including wandering around Springfield in a racing game and appearing on a rotating poster inside Moe's Tavern. He has also been rendered as a topiary decoration in a mobile game and depicted as a statue in a Halloween special. Overall, Dizzy is a minor background gag character rather than a fleshed-out personality, relying on the Duff Beer branding and the Snow White parody for his humor.

title: Sammy Davis, Jr.
text: Sammy Davis, Jr. is Real-world entertainer referenced/mentioned in The Simpsons, not an original main cast member. Sammy Davis, Jr. is depicted in the show as a real-world entertainer and member of the Rat Pack whose memoir plays a pivotal role in reconciling Krusty the Clown with his estranged father. A quote from his book "Yes I Can" moves Rabbi Krustofsky to tears once he learns its source, since Davis was famous for having converted to Judaism. He's also referenced through his hit song "The Candy Man" and appears in archival-style cameos, such as a kissing scene from All in the Family and background photos in Krusty's dressing room. Though never a speaking character within the show's main narrative, he functions as a recurring cultural touchstone tied to Krusty's Jewish heritage and show-business world. A non-canon chalkboard gag also jokingly references reincarnation of Davis. Notable quotes: I'm afraid not, Rabbi. It's from "Yes I Can" by Sammy Davis, Jr. An entertainer, like your son. | The Candy Man? | I never heard the plight of my people phrased so eloquently. Who said that? Was that Rabbi Hillel?
quotes: I'm afraid not, Rabbi. It's from "Yes I Can" by Sammy Davis, Jr. An entertainer, like your son.
The Candy Man?
I never heard the plight of my people phrased so eloquently. Who said that? Was that Rabbi Hillel?

title: Cora (waitress)
text: Cora (waitress) is A recurring minor waitress character in Springfield who has worked at various restaurants and owns her own diner. Cora is an elderly, gravelly-voiced waitress known for her gruff, no-nonsense attitude and hearing difficulties. Despite being hard of hearing, she remains surprisingly competent and attentive at her job, having worked at the Overpass Diner, Lard Lad Donuts, and Skobo's before eventually owning her own restaurant, Cora's Diner. She has a habit of mocking Homer, often making sarcastic remarks or nicknames like calling him "Santa Claus." Her signature trait is repeatedly responding with a single confused "What?" to whatever is said to her, highlighting her deafness. Over her appearances, she seems to have grown even grumpier and more sarcastic with age. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: What?|Cora
quotes: What?|Cora

title: Cupcake Kid
text: Cupcake Kid is Superhero alias of Bart Simpson, sidekick to Pie Man (Homer Simpson). Cupcake Kid is the costumed persona Bart Simpson invents so he can tag along on his father's crime-fighting escapades. Modeled directly after Homer's Pie Man identity, Bart's version swaps pastry weapons, hurling cupcakes at wrongdoers instead of pies. The character comes about after Homer's secret identity is exposed but oddly never taken seriously by the public, allowing him to keep operating as Pie Man, which inspires Bart to create his own matching alter ego. In non-canon stories, Cupcake Kid gets pulled into stranger adventures, including being transformed by Professor Frink's ray gun into a swapped version of himself called Captain Cupcake. He also keeps up the hero routine of protecting his partner's secret, denying knowledge of Pie Man's identity to news reporters. The character has since become popular enough in the show's universe to inspire real-world style fan costumes referenced in later episodes. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Fiddle-Faddle
text: Fiddle-Faddle is A minor clown character at Ding-A-Ling Bros. Circus, associated with Krusty the Clown. Fiddle-Faddle is one of the many circus clowns who work under Krusty as part of the Ding-A-Ling Bros. Circus troupe. Distinguished by his springy hands, feet, and eyeglasses, he has a bouncy, exaggerated physical design typical of circus performers. He was introduced to Krusty by fellow clown Scuzzo and became a fixture around the circus grounds, assisting with shows and general circus duties. He doesn't speak in his appearances, functioning more as background clown color than a fleshed-out personality. Like the rest of the circus troupe, he eventually departs Springfield by train when the circus moves on. He later reappears in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out as part of a Halloween-themed clown-fear event.

title: Queen Elizabeth II
text: Queen Elizabeth II is Real-world monarch of the United Kingdom who appears in several Simpsons episodes interacting with the family. Queen Elizabeth II appears as a recurring real-world figure who repeatedly crosses paths with the Simpsons and other Springfield residents. She is portrayed as dignified and proper, but capable of sudden regal outrage, such as when Homer accidentally damages her carriage and insults her honor, leading her to sentence him to death before ultimately showing mercy and pardoning him. She has a habit of nearly bestowing honors, as seen when she almost knights Krusty the Clown before duty calls him away. Her family life includes her son Prince Charles and daughter Princess Anne, and she is shown to have a fondness for watching over ordinary citizens, comparing Ralph Wiggum's quirky nature to that of her own son. The show also nods to her real-world status as Britain's longest-reigning monarch, acknowledging her actual death in 2022 in an out-of-universe note. Overall, she serves as a comedic stand-in for British royalty and formality clashing with the chaos of the Simpson family. Voiced by Tress MacNeille, Maggie Roswell ("Kamp Krusty"), Eddie Izzard ("To Surveil with Love").

title: El Chemistri chef
text: El Chemistri chef is Chef and owner of El Chemistri, a posh Springfield restaurant. The El Chemistri chef runs an upscale, avant-garde restaurant that caters to Springfield's food elite, complete with theatrical touches like vibrating mints to signal table readiness. He takes great pride in narrating the unusual dishes he serves, treating dining as a kind of performance art. Despite his fancy establishment, he's not above being brusque with customers, as shown when he curtly sent Marge and her kids on their way after giving them an oddly shaped dessert. He also has a quirky, conspiratorial side, sharing a paranoid theory with fellow chef Eduardo Barcelona about restaurants using counterfeit saffron in their paella. The character serves as a comedic parody of real-life celebrity chef José Andrés, poking fun at the pretensions of modern haute cuisine culture. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Eeyore
text: Eeyore is A crossover character from Winnie-the-Pooh appearing as a lunchbox design and briefly in a non-canon Simpsons special. Eeyore is the gloomy donkey borrowed from the world of Winnie-the-Pooh, making a couple of small cameo-style appearances in The Simpsons universe. His first appearance is not as a living character but as an image printed on Milhouse's lunchbox, which Bart ends up using during a lunchboxing duel with Nelson. In a non-canon special, he shows up in person at an apology party, where partygoers play pin the tail on the donkey using him as the literal donkey. Adding a bit of irony to the game, Eeyore himself later pins a tail onto Homer. He doesn't have an extensive role or personality development within the show, since his character is essentially imported wholesale from his original source material. His inclusion mostly serves as a lighthearted nod to Disney and outside pop culture within the Simpsons' animated world. Voiced by Chris Edgerly.

title: Judi Dench
text: Judi Dench is Real-world English actress caricatured as a minor recurring character, owner of a London fish and chips chain. This version of Judi Dench is a fictionalized caricature of the real actress, portrayed as the tough, no-nonsense owner of a fast-food chain in London. She runs her restaurants with an iron fist, forbidding employees from chatting with customers and resorting to physical violence when sales targets aren't met. Her fearsome reputation is well known among her staff, who dread her wrath more than any unhappy customer. She also appears in a surreal fantasy sequence where Homer imagines a gray-haired Marge transforming into her before planting a kiss on him. Beyond these bizarre appearances, she is referenced as a voice actress for an in-universe children's show, tying her back to her real-life fame and Bond film association. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: She'll beat us, she will.
quotes: She'll beat us, she will.

title: Jason (Co-Dependent's Day)
text: Jason (Co-Dependent's Day) is A minor character within the fictional "Cosmic Wars: The Gathering Shadow" film-within-the-show, appearing in "Co-Dependent's Day". Jason exists only within the show's parody sci-fi franchise, Cosmic Wars: The Gathering Shadow, rather than as a resident of Springfield proper. He appears briefly interacting with the character Jim-Jam Bonks, questioning him about missing equipment on his ship. His design and role are clearly modeled on a young Obi-Wan Kenobi from the Star Wars prequel trilogy, making him part of the show's ongoing send-up of the Star Wars franchise. Notably, his name is never spoken on screen and was only confirmed through an official episode guide. Despite his minimal screen time, he's been cataloged as a recurring character due to a later cameo appearance. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Henry Louis Gates Jr. (character)
text: Henry Louis Gates Jr. (character) is Real-world guest character appearing as himself, host of Finding Your Roots who helps Carl Carlson explore his family history. Henry Louis Gates Jr. appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, playing on his real-life role as host of the genealogy series Finding Your Roots. He becomes entangled with Carl Carlson's storyline after purchasing Carl's old belt buckle from the Rich Texan, which leads to Carl being invited onto his show. As a professional historian, he digs into Carl's ancestry and uncovers a lineage tracing back to a freed slave who became a cowboy. He's portrayed as knowledgeable and a bit unflappable, casually dropping anecdotes about past celebrity encounters, including a bizarre story about rescuing an actor from a jet cockpit. He also shows a practical, no-nonsense streak, dismissing a stranger's offer of medical help after Carl gets hurt. Outside of his canonical appearance, he's also depicted in a non-canon capacity attending a Simpsons premiere. Voiced by Himself.

title: Gentle Ben
text: Gentle Ben is A minor character; a bear who hosts his own daytime talk show within the Simpsons universe. Gentle Ben is a bear who, somewhat improbably, hosts his own daytime television talk show. His one notable on-screen moment comes when an audience member tries to ask him a question, prompting him to lunge toward food instead, forcing his handlers, the Ben Squad, to tranquilize him. This brief scene plays on the absurdity of a wild animal being given a talk-show format, poking fun at the excesses of daytime TV. Beyond this incident, little else is known about his personality or background, as he appears only fleetingly in the show. He is also referenced later in a non-canon capacity, glimpsed by other characters in a stylized alternate scene. Overall, Gentle Ben functions as a quick gag character rather than a fully developed personality.

title: Captain Keen
text: Captain Keen is Superhero alter-ego of Ned Flanders, appearing in Simpsons comic book stories. Captain Keen is the heroic persona adopted by Ned Flanders after a nuclear explosion grants him extraordinary powers. This non-canon character exists purely within the Bongo comic book universe, separate from the main television continuity. As Captain Keen, Flanders takes on a costumed crimefighter role, a stark contrast to his usual mild-mannered, deeply religious personality as a Springfield resident. The character appears to be part of a larger superhero ensemble within the comics, suggesting he teams up with other transformed Springfield residents. His storyline reflects the comic series' tendency to explore alternate, fantastical versions of familiar characters. Captain Keen remains a niche figure, known mainly to fans of the Simpsons comic book spin-offs rather than the show itself.

title: Great mother
text: Great mother is Minor recurring background character; a mother seen among the Springfield crowd in various episodes. The Great mother is a minor, largely unnamed background character who appears alongside her husband, the Great father, and their two children, the Great son and Great daughter. She first shows up at Mr. Burns' company picnic, where she takes note of Homer's pitiable situation. Later, she and her family are shown to be struggling emotionally, seeking help at a family therapy center, only to flee once the Simpsons inadvertently disrupt the building's power supply. She continues to make brief, wordless appearances at Springfield community events, such as the Renaissance Faire. Her role is more decorative than developed, functioning as part of the show's rotating cast of townsfolk used to fill out crowd scenes. Despite her minimal characterization, she has recurred across several episodes spanning different seasons. Voiced by Julie Kavner.

title: Jordan King
text: Jordan King is A second-grade student at Springfield Elementary School and minor recurring background character. Jordan King is a young boy with black hair who is one of the many students seen wandering the halls and classrooms of Springfield Elementary. He appears frequently as a background character across numerous episodes without any real spoken dialogue, making him a non-speaking presence in the show's world. His name wasn't actually revealed until many seasons after his first appearance, finally confirmed in a later season 30 episode. In a non-canon mobile game appearance, he's associated with a toy-demonstration job. Overall, Jordan exists mostly as part of the crowd of anonymous schoolchildren that populate Springfield, occasionally getting a moment of recognition from fans who track these background students.

title: Penn Jillette (character)
text: Penn Jillette (character) is Real-life magician and entertainer who appears as himself in guest appearances on The Simpsons. Penn Jillette appears as a fictionalized version of himself, the outspoken half of the famous magic duo Penn & Teller. In the show he's depicted as part of a group of illustrious illusionists alongside Teller, Ricky Jay, and David Copperfield. His appearances tie into the show's recurring fascination with magic and stage performers, occasionally putting him in odd or exaggerated scenarios beyond simple guest cameos. He also shows up in more casual, background capacities, such as having his picture displayed in a local business or attending a Hollywood premiere. Some of his appearances are explicitly non-canon, used for gag or bonus content rather than the main continuity. Overall, he serves as a novelty guest star rather than a fully developed character with his own personality traits explored on the show. Voiced by Himself. Notable quotes: Four Stars
quotes: Four Stars

title: Gunter
text: Gunter is Recurring entertainer character, a white tiger performer who appears alongside his partner Ernst in Las Vegas-style acts. Gunter is one half of a flamboyant animal-act duo with his partner Ernst, best known for performing dangerous stunts with white tigers like Anastasia. The pair are a clear parody of real-life magicians Siegfried and Roy, right down to the eerie way their fictional mauling storyline predated a real incident involving Roy Horn. Gunter and Ernst pop up in various gambling and Las Vegas-themed episodes, often working at casinos and getting tangled up in chaotic situations involving the show's main cast. Their act is portrayed as glamorous but perilous, with Anastasia proving unpredictable and even attacking them on screen. Despite the danger, they remain minor fixtures of Springfield's celebrity and entertainment scene, occasionally seen socializing with other famous faces. Their running gag is essentially existing as a live-action cautionary tale wrapped in showbiz spectacle. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Sonny Go-along
text: Sonny Go-along is A minor member of the Springfield Mafia. Sonny Go-along is a low-ranking figure within the Springfield Mafia whose name reflects his personality—he tends to agree with whatever the group decides rather than causing trouble. He appeared during a moment of internal Mafia turmoil when Johnny Tightlips attempted to assert leadership after Fat Tony's authority was questioned. True to his easygoing nature, Sonny expressed no objection to the change in leadership as long as the rest of the crew was on board. He later showed up among the Mafia at a large Springfield event, blending into the background as usual. Sonny isn't known for bold action or memorable lines, but rather for his passive, go-with-the-flow attitude, which is essentially his entire character gimmick. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson. Notable quotes: Sonny said that he was good if everyone else was.
quotes: Sonny said that he was good if everyone else was.

title: Karen (socialite)
text: Karen (socialite) is A minor recurring Springfield socialite who appears among Marge's social circle. Karen is one of the well-to-do Springfield socialites who occasionally cross paths with Marge Simpson. She was first introduced when Evelyn Peters brought her along to the Springfield Glen Country Club, placing her firmly within the town's upper-crust social scene. She later turned up in New York City alongside fellow socialites Roberta and Gillian, suggesting she travels within the same elite circle outside of Springfield as well. Karen doesn't have any spoken lines and functions mainly as a background figure representing the wealthier, high-society crowd that Marge sometimes finds herself navigating. Her repeated appearances across multiple episodes over the years mark her as a small but consistent recurring character rather than a one-off extra.

title: Obi-Wan Kenobi
text: Obi-Wan Kenobi is Star Wars Jedi character referenced/crossed-over into The Simpsons universe. Obi-Wan Kenobi is a crossover character from Star Wars who appears in various forms throughout The Simpsons canon and non-canon material. He's mostly referenced indirectly, such as through a Ralph Wiggum action figure or a crossword clue Lisa solves. In the show's Star Wars parody special, he takes on a more active role, clashing with Homer after Homer gets pulled into the Star Wars universe. He also shows up as a background figure in a Force Awakens-themed segment. As a character who dies in the original Star Wars trilogy, he's honored in an episode dedicated to fallen Star Wars characters. Overall, Obi-Wan functions as a nostalgic nod to Star Wars fandom rather than a fully developed Simpsons character.

title: King Gautama
text: King Gautama is Non-canon king character, father of Siddmartha Gautama, from the episode "My Way or the Highway to Heaven". King Gautama is a minor, non-canon royal figure who appears alongside his wife, Queen Gautama, and his children in a parody of the Buddha origin story. He is portrayed as a somewhat clueless and self-centered father, waking his daughter Siddmartha with an extravagant but unwanted gift of fifty ponies. He also shows a possessive streak, claiming a slice of cake for himself even while asleep when Siddmartha tries to take it. After his death, he is honored with a statue near the palace, hinting at his status as a ruler of some importance. His character later appears in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out as part of the Springfield Enlightened faction. Overall, he serves as a comedic, background royal figure rather than a deeply developed character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Larry Kidkill
text: Larry Kidkill is Owner of the Springfield City Zoo who tries to exploit Apu and Manjula's octuplets. Larry Kidkill is a shady businessman who runs the Springfield City Zoo and preys on desperate families for profit. He first appears offering to house and care for Apu and Manjula's overwhelming brood of octuplets, seemingly out of generosity, but this turns out to be a scheme to turn the children into a zoo attraction. He is ruthless when confronted, using a lifetime contract and hired muscle to keep control of the kids, showing he has no qualms about exploiting children for entertainment and money. His greed is ultimately satisfied when Homer volunteers to take the octuplets' place in the stage show. Kidkill later resurfaces at an investors' event, suggesting he continues to network and pursue business opportunities around Springfield. His name, a blunt pun suggesting menace toward children, reflects his morally dubious character. Voiced by Garry Marshall.

title: Gluten Tag
text: Gluten Tag is Sidekick to the supervillain Glutenus Maximus, later revealed to be Uter's father. Gluten Tag is a bread-themed supervillain who serves as the loyal sidekick to Glutenus Maximus. Together they use bakery-based weapons and gimmicks, such as banning police from bakery goods and using quick-cooking bread mix as a weapon during a robbery. Their criminal duo turns out to be a father-son act, with Gluten Tag unmasked as Uter's dad, driven to crime after their German breakfast restaurant went under and left them financially desperate. After being defeated by Homer, the pair's story takes a redemptive turn when Homer helps them start a new, successful pork restaurant. Gluten Tag's legacy as a villain lives on through a statue commemorating him and Glutenus Maximus in a museum exhibit, and his signature bread barrage attack is later reused by another character in a costume.

title: Jughead Jones
text: Jughead Jones is Crossover character from Archie Comics who appears in various Simpsons episodes and specials. Jughead Jones is a visiting character from the Archie Comics universe who pops up in several Simpsons crossover moments rather than being a native Springfield resident. He's first seen riding along in Archie's jalopy when Homer hitches a ride after Bart gets tossed from Sideshow Bob's limo. He later shows up as one of Springfield Elementary's old students during a nostalgic air-conditioning-themed appearance, alongside other classic cartoon icons like Fat Albert and Fonzie. His pop-culture staying power is referenced again when Ralph plays Jughead in a school production based on the modern Riverdale TV series. He also factors into an even more explicit crossover, appearing as part of Archie's gang when the villain Plasmo stumbles into their comic-book world, though the gang doesn't buy his outlandish story. Overall, Jughead functions as a fun nod to classic Americana and comic-strip culture rather than a fully developed Simpsons character. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Rutherford B. Hayes
text: Rutherford B. Hayes is Historical U.S. President referenced in Simpsons episodes. Rutherford B. Hayes appears in the show not as a living character but as a historical figure referenced in a couple of episodes. He is depicted by a student performing in the song about mediocre presidents during Springfield Elementary's President's Day event, poking fun at his relatively obscure legacy among U.S. leaders. Later, his image turns up in a book Superintendent Chalmers shows Bart, part of a sequence that sparks Bart's fascination with Theodore Roosevelt instead. Hayes himself has no dialogue or personality traits explored in the show, functioning purely as a piece of educational trivia and a running joke about forgettable presidents.

title: Hot Flash
text: Hot Flash is Superhero alter ego of Alice Glick and a member of The Dependables. Hot Flash is a non-canon superhero character who appears as part of the superhero team known as The Dependables. She is the costumed identity of an elderly woman named Alice Glick, fitting the show's running gag of elderly or unlikely characters taking on heroic roles. Her powers include super speed and the ability to leave a fire trail behind her, clearly modeling her after a famous speedster from another comic universe. She was recruited into active duty after teammate Fruit Bat Man was taken captive by a villain called The Abominable Dr. Lenny. As a parody character, she doesn't have much individual characterization beyond her role within the group and her comic-book inspired abilities. She remains a minor, non-speaking figure who exists mainly to round out the ensemble of Springfield's makeshift superhero squad.

title: Ice Walker
text: Ice Walker is A non-canon icy creature who appears in the Game of Thrones-parody episode "The Serfsons". The Ice Walker is a supernatural, frost-covered being introduced in the fantasy-parody episode "The Serfsons," serving as a spoof of the White Walkers from Game of Thrones. He plays a small but memorable role by biting Marge's mother, Jacqueline, which causes her skin to freeze over and sends Homer and Marge to seek medical answers. Despite his monstrous nature, he shows a strange romantic side, having briefly dated Jacqueline because of his preference for younger women, and later returning to apologize for the bite before asking her out again. His creepy charm doesn't stop there, as he's also shown flirting with a deceased woman's hanging corpse, highlighting the show's dark comedic take on the fantasy genre. The character also made an appearance in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. He is over 900 years old, bald, and fits into the show's long tradition of one-off monster characters used for genre-parody storylines. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Jimmy (Lisa the Vegetarian)
text: Jimmy (Lisa the Vegetarian) is Minor recurring character; a child actor who serves as Troy McClure's assistant. Jimmy is a minor character best known for his role as Troy McClure's young assistant in the educational film Meat and You: Partners in Freedom. He accompanies McClure on a tour of a meat packing plant, appearing as part of the propaganda film shown to Lisa's class. Jimmy doesn't have much individual personality beyond his function as a supporting figure in McClure's productions. He is voiced by Nancy Cartwright, who lends him a boyish, enthusiastic tone typical of child actors in in-universe promotional media. A similar-looking boy named Billy later appears in other Troy McClure films, suggesting a running gag about interchangeable child actors in these fictional productions. Jimmy remains a background character with only a handful of appearances across the series. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Kid Queasy
text: Kid Queasy is Non-canon comic-book superhero identity of Wendell Borton; sidekick to The Sciencester. Kid Queasy is the costumed alter-ego of Wendell, created for the Bongo comics' superhero storylines. He serves as the loyal sidekick to The Sciencester, aiding him in various heroic exploits. His most notable moment comes when he assists The Sciencester in an attempt to capture Bartman, tying him into the larger superhero parody universe of the Simpsons comics. As a non-canon character, Kid Queasy exists purely within these comic-based alternate stories rather than the show's main continuity. He has appeared in a couple of specific comic issues focused on superhero team-ups and crossovers. Little else is detailed about his personality, but his role fits the classic sidekick archetype in these Bongo comic parodies.

title: Kaitlyn
text: Kaitlyn is Fiancée and business manager of Grayson Mathers, appearing in a minor role in the show. Kaitlyn is a fast-moving, opportunistic figure in the orbit of celebrity culture, juggling roles as an Instagram model, YouTube reactor, and creator of a product called Yoga Yogurt. She becomes romantically entangled with Grayson Mathers at lightning speed, agreeing to marry him after knowing him for only a few days. Despite the whirlwind nature of their relationship, she quickly takes charge of his career, stepping into the role of his business manager. Her decisive, take-charge personality is shown when she arranges a high-stakes boxing match for Grayson against a famous real-world athlete without much hesitation. She represents a satirical take on modern influencer culture and impulsive celebrity relationships. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: "I got you a fight against Floyd Mayweather."
quotes: "I got you a fight against Floyd Mayweather."

title: Dorothy Gale
text: Dorothy Gale is Fictional literary/film character from The Wizard of Oz, referenced within The Simpsons universe. Dorothy Gale isn't an original Simpsons character but rather the famous protagonist of The Wizard of Oz, who appears in the show only through references and homages. Janey dresses up as her for Halloween, showcasing how deeply embedded Dorothy's iconic imagery is in pop culture within Springfield. Her image also appears on a book cover seen in the town. In a non-canon couch gag, her famous ruby slippers are depicted as museum artifacts at the Smithsonian, treated as legendary historical items. Dorothy herself never physically appears as a character in the main continuity, existing only as a cultural touchstone that other characters reference or emulate.

title: Terry Gross (character)
text: Terry Gross (character) is Real-world NPR radio host who appears as herself in cameo roles in the Simpsons universe. Terry Gross is a real-world public radio personality who makes brief voice-only appearances as herself within the show. She's first heard through Homer's loaner car radio, which lets Lisa donate directly to NPR and triggers an old interview clip with a senator. In another appearance, she interviews a congressman on her show, calmly deflecting his climate change skepticism with a diplomatically noncommittal response. She's later referenced as a notable figure whose live conversation with an award-winning performer draws a crowd competing for seating. Rather than a traditional cartoon character, she functions as a nod to real public radio culture and NPR fandom within the Simpsons world. Voiced by Herself. Notable quotes: it was an interesting perspective
quotes: it was an interesting perspective

title: Hostess
text: Hostess is An unnamed minor character who works as the hostess at The Happy Sumo sushi restaurant. The hostess is a minor recurring character who greets patrons at The Happy Sumo, the sushi restaurant Lisa convinces her family to try. She reassures the Simpsons when they're startled by two chefs shouting greetings in Japanese, and later shows off the restaurant's karaoke bar, which turns out to be packed with rowdy, drunken Japanese businessmen. Beyond her restaurant duties, she has an unexpectedly athletic side, having participated in an attempt to build the world's tallest human pyramid. She's depicted with pink hair in her standard appearance, though oddly a promotional poster shows her with black hair instead. Overall she's a background figure who pops up briefly to add local color to Springfield's dining scene. Voiced by Diana Tanaka.

title: Robert Goulet (character)
text: Robert Goulet (character) is Real-life singer/actor who appears as himself, hired to perform at Bart's makeshift casino. Robert Goulet is a celebrity cameo character based on the real-life singer, who gets tricked by Bart into performing at what he believes is a legitimate casino. He's easily swayed by vague promises and doesn't realize he's been duped until he arrives at Bart's treehouse rather than an actual casino. Despite his confusion, he goes along with the gig after being manipulated by Nelson into thinking his manager approved. His performance turns into slapstick chaos when he accidentally injures Milhouse with a swinging microphone. The joke of his fame is extended through a fictional arcade game bearing his name, which recurs as a background gag in multiple episodes. Overall, he serves as a one-off gag character whose real-world fame is used for comedic contrast with the absurdity of Springfield. Voiced by Robert Goulet (Himself). Notable quotes: "a casino" ... "good enough"
quotes: "a casino" ... "good enough"

title: Geo Metro bot
text: Geo Metro bot is Non-canon transformer robot, originally Ned Flanders' Geo Metro car, appearing in a Treehouse of Horror segment. The Geo Metro bot began its existence as a simple car belonging to Ned Flanders. Everything changes when Bart acquires a special Malibu Stacy toy car capable of transforming ordinary vehicles into robots, and the Geo Metro is caught up in this transformation. Once converted, the vehicle ejects its driver through a hole in the back and becomes a fully autonomous, talking robot. Its main claim to fame in the show is a battle against the Sedan bot. As a non-speaking character in terms of dedicated dialogue, it exists mainly as a visual gag and homage, being a clear parody of Megatron from the Transformers franchise. It later appeared as a collectible robot decoration in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game.

title: Investo the Robot
text: Investo the Robot is Robot mascot of the Franchise Expo, appearing in a single episode. Investo the Robot is a promotional mascot built to greet visitors at the Franchise Expo, claiming an outlandish origin from the planet Opportuniac. He's an overly persistent pitch-bot, constantly urging people to come inside and grab pamphlets, which makes him more of an obstacle than a helper. His pushy enthusiasm ultimately leads to his downfall when he gets in the Simpson family's way. Bart deals with him in typically destructive fashion, ending Investo's short-lived robotic existence. He exists mainly as a one-off gag character tied to the expo setting rather than a recurring figure in Springfield life. Despite his brief appearance, he later resurfaces in non-canon media as part of a mobile game tie-in. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Joyce
text: Joyce is A waitress at the Gas and Grub who briefly interacts with a disguised Sideshow Bob. Joyce is a minor recurring character who works behind the counter at the Gas and Grub convenience store. She's flirtatious and a bit oblivious, striking up a romantic interest in a customer without realizing he's actually the disguised fugitive Sideshow Bob. Her curiosity gets the better of her when she notices what she thinks is a loose thread on his shirt, not realizing it's the stitching from his face transplant, leading to an accidental unmasking. Despite the chaos that follows, she tries to cover for him by misdirecting the Simpson family, showing a surprising willingness to help a stranger she's attracted to. Her matter-of-fact, slightly world-weary attitude comes through in her closing remark about men. She has appeared mostly through archive footage in later episodes rather than as an active character again. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: All the good ones are either gay or have no face.
quotes: All the good ones are either gay or have no face.

title: Gort
text: Gort is A robotic alien character who appears briefly as one of several alien suspects in a Springfield investigation. Gort is a robot made of nanites who exists as a background/crossover reference in the Simpsons universe, based on the classic robot from the 1951 film 'The Day the Earth Stood Still.' He first appears as part of a lineup of famous fictional aliens brought in by FBI agents trying to determine what Homer actually saw in the woods, standing alongside characters like Marvin the Martian and Chewbacca. Despite being included as a suspect, he turns out not to be the alien Homer encountered, since that was actually Mr. Burns in disguise. Gort has no lines and is essentially a silent cameo character, appearing again later at a sci-fi convention signing autographs. In later non-canon appearances, he shows up in random Springfield crowd scenes and even works as a waiter in a futuristic restaurant. His role is purely that of an easter-egg style pop culture reference rather than a developed character.

title: Kurt Hardwick
text: Kurt Hardwick is An artsy camp counselor Lisa Simpson meets and idolizes in the episode "Elementary School Musical". Kurt Hardwick is a free-spirited, artistic young man who works as a counselor at an arts camp called Expressions in Sprooklyn, alongside his friend Ethan Ballantyne. He captivates Lisa Simpson with his creative charm, inspiring her to travel to Sprooklyn to reunite with him after her camp experience ends. Despite his artistic charisma, Kurt turns out to be somewhat dishonest, having exaggerated how wonderful life in Sprooklyn actually is. He also holds a job at a sandwich shop called Sprubway, suggesting his artistic pursuits don't fully support him financially. Kurt and Ethan share a whimsical, almost mystical bond, claiming to possess magical artistic powers, and are last seen atop a building beside a mural they painted of Lisa. His quirky, dreamy persona embodies the show's satire of pretentious artistic subcultures. Voiced by Bret McKenzie.

title: Nick Fury
text: Nick Fury is A Marvel Comics parody character, a secret agent/spy for S.H.I.E.L.D. who appears in Simpsons Marvel-themed segments and costumes. Nick Fury is a crossover parody character brought into the Simpsons universe from Marvel Comics, portrayed here in the style of Samuel L. Jackson's Marvel Cinematic Universe version. He operates as a shadowy S.H.I.E.L.D. agent, appearing in a post-credits style tie-in scene where he recruits someone for an assembling team, echoing Marvel's own Avengers-recruitment gags. In non-canon material, he commands a rented Helicarrier hovering over Springfield and later organizes elderly superheroes into the Octogenarian Initiative to form the team known as The Dependables. His likeness is popular enough among Springfield residents that people cosplay as him at the Comicalooza convention, and Carl Carlson once dressed as him while part of the Springfield Avengers. Overall, Nick Fury exists mainly as a wink toward Marvel fandom and superhero-genre parody rather than a fully fleshed-out personality within the show. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Jessica (Meat Is Murder)
text: Jessica (Meat Is Murder) is Lawyer and psychopharmacologist for the Redfield family, appearing in the RedStar corporate storyline. Jessica is a sharp, professional legal advisor who works closely with the wealthy Redfield family, particularly patriarch Augustus 'Gus' Redfield. She has a hand in both law and psychopharmacology, giving her an unusual dual expertise that comes into play during a corporate power struggle. She's shown to be efficient and controlled during high-stakes boardroom drama, calmly confirming legal technicalities like mental incompetence invalidating a vote. Despite her buttoned-up professional demeanor, she reveals a looser, more impulsive side by making out with Mav Redfield right after a tense meeting. She's a clear parody of the calculating corporate fixer archetype, specifically referencing a character from a prestige TV drama about a media dynasty. Her white hair and steady presence mark her as an authority figure within the Redfield business world. Voiced by Edi Patterson.

title: Judas
text: Judas is Biblical figure referenced in The Simpsons as the apostle who betrayed Jesus Christ. Judas appears only as a background or referenced figure rather than a fully realized character in the show. He's brought up by Homer as an odd bit of comfort for Lisa, framing betrayal in a strangely practical light by noting that Judas still got paid despite his infamous act. Elsewhere, he shows up in visual gags, such as a figurine depicted playing basketball with Jesus, and in artistic recreations like a snowman version of Leonardo da Vinci's Last Supper made by the Flanders boys. He also appears in the non-canon spoof storyline 'Bethlehem 90210.' Overall, Judas functions as a recurring pop-culture and religious reference point for quick jokes rather than a character with his own arc.

title: Gabriel (Simpsons Christmas Stories)
text: Gabriel (Simpsons Christmas Stories) is Non-canon archangel character appearing in a Simpsons Christmas special, portrayed as God's messenger. Gabriel is depicted as the archangel messenger of God in the non-canon episode Simpsons Christmas Stories. In this retelling, Gabriel delivers divine news to Mary and Joseph about the coming birth of Jesus, echoing the biblical Nativity story. The character later reappears to intervene after Jesus performs a miracle, decreeing that he must live to age 33. Beyond this special, Gabriel is referenced only briefly elsewhere, such as being mentioned in passing and appearing as a figurine. In The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game, the angelic role is tied to a version of Lisa, who takes on Gabriel-like angel imagery for a holiday-themed task. Voiced by Yeardley Smith.

title: Clara Hosenfrauen
text: Clara Hosenfrauen is Minor recurring character; an actress known for playing McBabe in the McBain film series. Clara Hosenfrauen is a film actress with a colorful and somewhat mysterious career history, having once been known under the name Roy Molloy before transitioning. She got her start in the Swedish sitcom 'House of Glum' before moving on to Hollywood action fare, landing recurring roles in several campy McBain movies. Her onscreen claim to fame is playing the tough love interest McBabe opposite McBain in a string of over-the-top action sequels. Despite her acting career, she has since stepped away from Hollywood and now works a much quieter job as a nanny, jokingly branding herself 'McBabysitter' as a nod to her old franchise. She's a background pop-culture joke character rather than a core figure in the Simpsons' world, appearing mainly through references to the fictional McBain movie series. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Mr. Gammill
text: Mr. Gammill is Minor recurring employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, father of Tom Gammill. Mr. Gammill is a background employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, mostly notable for being the father of young Tom Gammill and husband of Mrs. Gammill. His family's brief brush with prominence comes when his son complains about missing Little League during Mr. Burns' company picnic, leading an irritated Burns to fire him on the spot, with Smithers snidely noting he wouldn't even last until the tug-of-war. Despite this, he's later shown still employed at the plant, suggesting the firing wasn't permanent or was quickly forgotten, a common gag in the show's inconsistent continuity. He and his family also turn up as background extras in a movie production, further cementing his status as a recurring but minor background character. Overall, he serves as one of the many faceless plant workers used for quick jokes about Mr. Burns' capriciousness as a boss. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Jawbreaker
text: Jawbreaker is A minor supervillain and henchman appearing in the Radioactive Man comic-book stories within The Simpsons universe. Jawbreaker is a comic-book supervillain known for his super strength and his allegiance to the villain Hypno Head. He appears as a minor antagonist in Bongo Comics' Radioactive Man stories rather than the animated show itself. Jawbreaker's role is largely that of muscle, helping capture other characters and engaging in physical confrontations with heroes. Despite his strength, he is consistently defeated by the heroic Radioactive Man, sometimes with help from Fallout Boy. He also attended the wedding of Larva Girl and Radioactive Man, which turned violent, leading to another defeat at Radioactive Man's hands. Overall, Jawbreaker functions as a recurring but low-level threat in the superhero-parody comic continuity.

title: Prince Gautama
text: Prince Gautama is Non-canon prince character portrayed by Bart Simpson in a parody of the Buddha legend, brother of Siddmartha Gautama. Prince Gautama is a minor, non-canon figure who appears as a role played by Bart Simpson in the episode "My Way or the Highway to Heaven," which reimagines the story of the Buddha. He is depicted as the son of King and Queen Gautama and the brother of Siddmartha Gautama, living a life of comfort and privilege within the royal household. Unlike his more spiritually curious sister, Gautama seems content with palace life, spending his time playing multiplayer games with a friend rather than questioning the opulence around him. His sister's inquiry about whether he tires of their lavish lifestyle hints at a thematic contrast between the two siblings' outlooks. Beyond the show, he also appears as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, associated with the Springfield Enlightened faction. He is listed as a deceased character within the non-canon continuity of the franchise. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Grand Pumpkin
text: Grand Pumpkin is Non-canon Halloween monster who appears in the "Treehouse of Horror" segments, brought to life by Bart's belief. The Grand Pumpkin is a giant, living pumpkin who supposedly grants candy to children who genuinely believe in him, only for that belief to accidentally summon him into being. Once alive, he becomes furious upon learning that humans carve pumpkins into jack-o'-lanterns and turn them into pumpkin bread, prompting him to go on a murderous rampage against people. His most disturbing trait is his blatant racism toward other pumpkins, particularly those with yellow coloring, and he openly admits that all pumpkins share this prejudice. He meets his end in a battle against a giant living turkey, another creature summoned by a child's belief, while unrepentantly clinging to his bigoted worldview until his final breath. Beyond his debut, he resurfaces in later Halloween specials and even haunts a hallucination sequence experienced by Lisa. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Pumpkin segregation...forever...
quotes: Pumpkin segregation...forever...

title: Hank Hill
text: Hank Hill is Crossover character from King of the Hill; father of the Hill family who occasionally appears in Springfield. Hank Hill is a crossover character brought into The Simpsons universe from the animated series King of the Hill. He works as an assistant manager at Strickland Propane and is depicted as a family man, traveling with his wife, son, and close friends. His appearances in Springfield are brief cameos rather than major storylines, often tying into football or media-related events. Despite his small role, he's treated as recognizable enough to appear as a cutout and even a bust in exhibits referencing television history. He maintains his straightforward, plain-spoken personality typical of his home series even in these limited crossover appearances. Voiced by Mike Judge, Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: we drove 2000 miles for this?
quotes: we drove 2000 miles for this?

title: David Hasselhoff
text: David Hasselhoff is Real-world actor and singer who appears as himself in various Simpsons episodes. David Hasselhoff shows up in Springfield in a handful of odd, self-referential cameos rather than as a regular cast member. He's famous enough that baby Lisa's third word is his name, much to Homer's annoyance since she still won't say "Daddy." He's also depicted as a minor celebrity who gets pulled into Springfield's affairs, such as being hired as a swim teacher at Springfield Elementary after a windfall of school funding, where Ralph mistakes him for a Finding Nemo or Aquaman expert. He's referenced repeatedly as a pop-culture touchstone tying together other celebrities and shows like Baywatch and Knight Rider. In a non-canon storyline, he's briefly mind-controlled by aliens Kang and Kodos while performing at Oktoberfest, comically revealing a secret plan for world domination. Overall, he functions as a running joke about celebrity name-dropping and 90s/00s pop culture nostalgia. Notable quotes: Return to the mothership? But world domination is only 95% complete.
quotes: Return to the mothership? But world domination is only 95% complete.

title: Candy Kevin
text: Candy Kevin is A performer character in the ice show 'Krusty's Kristmas on Ice'. Candy Kevin is a minor performer who appears in the ice-skating production 'Krusty's Kristmas on Ice.' He is part of a troupe tasked with journeying to Mistletoe Mountain to reclaim the Holiday Cheer from The Grumple. His performance is disrupted when workmen begin installing flooring for an upcoming basketball game, leading to a chaotic brawl. Candy Kevin joins his fellow performers in physically fighting off the workmen and basketball players to defend their show. He has no notable personality traits beyond his role as a background performer swept into the on-stage chaos. The character later appears in a non-canon capacity in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Jimmy Kissass
text: Jimmy Kissass is A minor member of the Springfield Mafia. Jimmy Kissass is a low-ranking mobster in Fat Tony's Springfield crime family, appearing mostly in background mafia scenes. He's shown to be a bit of a suck-up, quick to flatter whoever appears to be in charge, as seen when he immediately backs Johnny Tightlips as the new boss. His name itself is a running joke, playing into the show's tradition of absurd mafia nicknames. He doesn't have much individual characterization beyond being a loyal, easily swayed lackey who goes along with whatever the mafia hierarchy dictates. He later shows up as part of the mob's outings, such as attending an Itchy & Scratchy ice show after Fat Tony rents out the arena. Voiced by Chris Edgerly. Notable quotes: Tightlips was always his favorite.
quotes: Tightlips was always his favorite.

title: Kitenge
text: Kitenge is A tour guide who accompanied the Simpson family on their African safari, later becoming the President of Tanzania. Kitenge is a good-natured and resourceful guide who leads the Simpson family through Tanzania after they win a safari trip from a box of animal crackers. He's knowledgeable about local wildlife and politics, casually explaining the region's turbulent leadership while keeping the family safe from real dangers like poachers and an angry hippopotamus. Brave to a fault, he heroically wrestles a hippo to let the Simpsons escape, sustaining injuries in the process. Despite this dangerous encounter, he survives and later rises to become the President of Tanzania, replacing the former leader Muntu. His story showcases an unexpectedly dramatic career arc for a side character, going from humble tour guide to head of state within a single episode. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Good ol' Kitenge.
