quotes: Good ol' Kitenge.

title: Jimmy (Judge Me Tender)
text: Jimmy (Judge Me Tender) is A minor character who works as a golf caddie for Homer Simpson. Jimmy is a blond-haired golf caddie who appears briefly in the episode "Judge Me Tender." He's brought on to assist Homer when Homer decides to take up golf. An older, unnamed observer remarks that Jimmy would start Homer off with a three iron, mirroring how that same person had begun their own lifelong golfing career. Jimmy himself doesn't speak in his appearance, making him a background figure rather than a fleshed-out personality. He later resurfaces as a character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game, tied to the Fore! content update. Overall, Jimmy exists mainly as a minor plot device to kick off Homer's golfing subplot.

title: Mrs. Gnome in Your Home
text: Mrs. Gnome in Your Home is A toy gnome figure that appears in the Simpson household, wife of Gnome in Your Home. Mrs. Gnome in Your Home is a decorative Christmas toy figure and the wife of the similarly named Gnome in Your Home. She entered the Simpson family's life as a gift Maggie received one Christmas, though the toy frightened the baby rather than delighting her. In a fit of fear or mischief, Maggie dismantled both gnome figures and scattered their pieces in Homer and Marge's bed, giving the toy a small but memorable moment of dark comedy. She later resurfaces as an item for sale during one of Homer's holiday shopping trips, suggesting these gnome figures are a recurring seasonal product within the show's universe. As a non-speaking character, she has no personality traits of her own beyond her unsettling toy design and her role in a Christmas-themed prank. Her appearances are limited to two Christmas-related episodes, making her a minor but memorable piece of the show's holiday-themed background lore.

title: Genghis Khan
text: Genghis Khan is Historical figure who appears as a virtual reality character imagined by Lisa, referenced in Simpsons canon and non-canon segments. Genghis Khan appears in the show as a historical curiosity rather than a regular cast member, first showing up when Lisa dons a virtual reality helmet and imagines meeting him in Mongolia. He later resurfaces as a theme for one of Professor Frink's virtual reality programs designed for Mr. Burns, tying him thematically to conquest and pillaging. Mr. Burns even invokes his name as a boastful comparison, casting himself as the conqueror to Smithers' "Europe." In a non-canon segment, he's depicted in Hell playing card and board games alongside other infamous villains from history, suggesting the show treats him as an emblem of historical tyranny used mostly for comedic references rather than a fleshed-out character. Overall, he functions as a pop-culture shorthand for ruthless conquest within the Simpsons universe. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "the Europe to my Genghis Khan." - Mr. Burns
quotes: "the Europe to my Genghis Khan." - Mr. Burns

title: Mick Jagger (character)
text: Mick Jagger (character) is Real-world musician (Rolling Stones frontman) who appears as himself in guest-star episodes of The Simpsons. Mick Jagger appears as a fictionalized version of himself, running a rock-and-roll fantasy camp alongside Keith Richards. He's portrayed as a dedicated if eccentric instructor, personally teaching campers the art of strutting on stage. Jagger is shown to be gracious after a chaotic incident with Homer at a charity concert, apologizing and offering a second chance despite the mayhem Homer caused. Outside of his main appearance, he's referenced in passing as a musical legend whose reputation is invoked by other characters, and his image shows up in unexpected background gags like a jazz musician captcha test. In non-canon material, he's imagined as a body Homer could inhabit and as a celebrity attendee at a fictional show premiere. Overall, he serves as a real-world celebrity cameo whose larger-than-life rock star persona gets gently mocked through Homer's interactions with him. Voiced by Himself.

title: Keith
text: Keith is Minor recurring background character, boyfriend of an unnamed woman considered briefly as a guardian for the Simpson children. Keith is a minor, background character best known for being romantically linked to an unnamed woman from the Mid-Atlantic region. He appears fleetingly, mostly walking or standing near the water with his girlfriend, without much personality development shown on screen. His main claim to relevance in the show's plot is that Homer and Marge briefly consider his girlfriend as a potential guardian for their children, only for Marge to reject the idea once she connects the woman's origin to the setting of a gritty TV drama. Keith himself doesn't have any dialogue or defining traits highlighted in his appearances, functioning purely as a side character to flesh out the scene. He has been voiced by Harry Shearer, one of the show's core cast members known for voicing numerous side characters. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: William Henry Harrison
text: William Henry Harrison is Historical figure referenced in the show; the 9th President of the United States, briefly depicted in a school pageant. William Henry Harrison appears in the show as a minor historical footnote rather than a recurring character. He is portrayed by a Springfield Elementary student during a Presidents' Day pageant, where the joke centers on the brevity of his real-life term in office. His only other appearance is as a picture in a history book shown to Bart, though Bart fails to recognize him among the other presidents. The character exists mainly as a vehicle for a quick historical joke about his infamously short presidency. He has no personality traits developed on the show beyond this one-note gag about dying so soon after taking office. Notable quotes: "I died in thirty days!" — student portraying William Henry Harrison
quotes: "I died in thirty days!" — student portraying William Henry Harrison

title: Anthony Hopkins
text: Anthony Hopkins is Fictionalized version of the real-life Welsh actor, appearing as a celebrity resident in Springfield. This character is a caricature of the famous actor Sir Anthony Hopkins, best known in real life for playing Hannibal Lecter. In the show, he tries his luck at auditioning for a role in a Springfield production, dressing up as Lecter in a nod to his signature part, but fails to land the job. He also dabbles in smaller acting gigs, taking minor parts in local productions and television episodes. At one point he's shown living near the Simpson family, engaging in a mundane hobby of playing with a remote control car. His comedic peak comes when he reacts with theatrical fury to a simple pizza delivery delay, showing that even esteemed actors can have petty, over-the-top outbursts. The character serves as a fun cameo poking gentle fun at celebrity culture and Hopkins' dramatic acting style. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Maurice LaMarche. Notable quotes: Damn you. Damn you to Hell!
quotes: Damn you. Damn you to Hell!

title: Jeeves (Ask Jeeves)
text: Jeeves (Ask Jeeves) is Butler mascot of the search engine Ask Jeeves, appearing as a minor crossover/background character in Springfield. Jeeves is the top-hatted butler mascot associated with the real-world search engine Ask Jeeves. He appears mostly in the background or is referenced by other characters rather than being an active participant in the plot. He is mentioned by Lisa in a joking context about asking him a question, and his image later shows up partially obscured by an ad on a website Bart and Milhouse visit. His most prominent moment comes when a lawyer publicly insults Ask Jeeves as a massive failure, causing Jeeves to storm out of the courtroom in a huff and ride away in a horse-drawn carriage. Being a non-speaking character, Jeeves conveys his reactions purely through actions rather than dialogue. He functions as a running gag referencing the obscurity and failure of the Ask Jeeves brand compared to other search engines.

title: Jules
text: Jules is A fictional character within the show-within-a-show "Cookie Castle", voiced by Bart Simpson. Jules is a princess-turned-queen in the fictional children's series Cookie Castle, a role that Bart lands thanks to his knack for voice acting and improvisation. Bart doesn't realize going into the audition that Jules is a female character, which leads to him being teased once the episode airs. Her storyline escalates from courtly scenes with a knight and boxes of Frosty Chocolate Sugar Clumps to a much darker turn when she's crowned queen and given a unicorn to ride. Rather than being a gentle fairy-tale figure, Jules uses her unicorn as a weapon, impaling people on its horn and having it burn down locations. This unexpected violent streak ends up earning Bart respect instead of ridicule from his peers. The character exists as a layer of in-universe fiction rather than a standard member of the Simpsons cast. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Mrs. Gammill
text: Mrs. Gammill is Minor recurring character; wife of Mr. Gammill and mother of Tom Gammill, connected to Springfield Nuclear Power Plant employees. Mrs. Gammill is a background resident of Springfield whose main claim to fame is being married to a plant worker who gets fired thanks to their son's antics. She's a non-speaking character, appearing in the crowd at various town events rather than driving any plots herself. Her family attends Mr. Burns' company picnic, where an offhand comment from young Tom leads to her husband losing his job. She also shows up with her husband and son as extras in the in-universe McBain movie, blending into Springfield's ever-present background cast. Later she's spotted at the Department of Motor Vehicles, suggesting she's just another ordinary citizen going about mundane errands. Overall, she exists as one of the many recurring extras that populate the show's world without much individual characterization.

title: Marvin Hamlisch (character)
text: Marvin Hamlisch (character) is Real-world celebrity guest character; composer/conductor referenced in Springfield lore, tied to Abe Simpson's backstory. Marvin Hamlisch appears as a fictionalized version of the real-life composer and conductor within the Simpsons universe. His picture hangs in the Springfield Speakers Bureau, showing his minor celebrity status in town. He factors into a nostalgic subplot involving Abe Simpson, who once worked alongside him at a local restaurant, sparking a romance with the venue's singer. In another gag, elderly residents at a retirement home mistake Milhouse for Hamlisch, leading to a comic case of mistaken identity. The character serves mostly as a cameo/reference rather than a fully developed personality, tying into the show's tradition of using real celebrities in small roles. Notably, Hamlisch passed away shortly before his episode aired, adding a bittersweet real-world footnote to his appearance. Voiced by Marvin Hamlisch (himself).

title: "Hey hey" guy
text: "Hey hey" guy is A minor, one-off resident of Springfield who briefly interacts with Homer at the Kwik-E-Mart. This is a minor, unnamed background character best known for a single silly outburst. After seeing a scandalous photo of Homer with Princess Kashmir, he spots Homer in person at the Kwik-E-Mart and can't help but call out to him. His entire claim to fame is the exclamation "Hey hey!", which becomes his de facto nickname since he's never given a proper name. He appears only briefly, mostly as a background gag rather than a fleshed-out character, and pops up again in later episodes purely as a cameo. His personality isn't explored beyond this cheeky, teasing moment, making him a small piece of Simpsons trivia rather than a major player. He's a good example of the show's habit of recurring anonymous townsfolk who exist for a quick joke. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Hey hey! | I hear you, buddy
quotes: Hey hey!
I hear you, buddy

title: Sammy Hagar (character)
text: Sammy Hagar (character) is Real-world rock musician who appears as himself in guest cameos. Sammy Hagar appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, the real rock singer and guitarist formerly of Van Halen. He's referenced by Homer as a source of wisdom, though the joke is cut short before Homer can finish the quote. In the non-canon "Behind the Laughter" universe, he's caught up in a feud with his old band Van Halen that Willie Nelson tries to mediate at an awards show. His non-canon appearances lean into a chaotic, washed-up celebrity persona, including drinking on a beach, going on a bender, and ending up in jail. He even gets an unlikely jailbreak assist from Chief Wiggum's jetpack mishap. Overall, he's a minor celebrity cameo character used for comedic name-dropping and satire of rock star excess. Voiced by Sammy Hagar (Himself). Notable quotes: I believe it was Sammy Hagar who said-
quotes: I believe it was Sammy Hagar who said-

title: Julienstein
text: Julienstein is Non-canon minor character; wife of Frankenstein's Monster in Treehouse of Horror segments. Julienstein is a Bride-of-Frankenstein-style character who appears as the spouse of Frankenstein's Monster in the show's Halloween specials. She hails from Geneva, Switzerland, tying her origin to the classic Frankenstein mythos. Her most notable moment comes when she catches her husband flirting with other women at a party, prompting her to turn violent and attack him. Beyond this jealous outburst, little else is shown of her personality, as she mostly exists as a background or cameo monster character. She has also popped up in mobile game content and been referenced in passing in other episodes and media.

title: Goosius
text: Goosius is Pet goose of Jay G and mascot of the Golden Goose, who becomes an unlikely friend of Homer. Goosius is a white goose owned by the wealthy Jay G, serving as the mascot for his Golden Goose brand. He forms an odd bond with Homer after biting him, a habit that oddly becomes a sign of their friendship rather than aggression. Goosius accompanies Jay G, Mr. Burns, and Homer on their outings and even appears in a music video. When the friendship between Homer and Jay G sours, Goosius stops biting Homer, signaling the end of their bond. He later becomes the target of a misguided revenge plot by Burns and Homer, leading to a chaotic chase where Homer can't bring himself to harm his former companion. Goosius is a non-speaking character, communicating only through his actions and bites.

title: Justice Agent
text: Justice Agent is A minor law enforcement character who apprehends Krusty in Europe. The Justice Agent is a policeman based in The Hague, Netherlands, who appears briefly in connection with Krusty's misadventures abroad. He takes Krusty into custody for misbehaving in western Europe, revealing that the Nobel Peace Prize invitation was actually a ruse designed to lure Krusty onto a plane. He also exposes the true nature of the aircraft, informing Krusty that the so-called Peace Prize One is in fact the World Court Plane used for extradition purposes. His role is small and functional, existing mainly to deliver exposition about the scheme against Krusty rather than to develop as a personality. He also appears as a minor non-canon character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Jelly monster
text: Jelly monster is A non-canon monster antagonist from a Treehouse of Horror-style segment, made of sentient jellied cranberry sauce. The jelly monster is a bizarre creature that comes to life after Bart and Milhouse attempt to replicate a can of Bog Queen Jellied Cranberry Sauce aboard a spaceship. Despite its gelatinous, food-based origin, it proves to be a brutal killer, tearing skeletons out of its victims and devouring them, including Nelson and eventually Martin, who willingly sacrifices himself out of admiration for the creature. Its rampage causes chaos throughout the ship, ultimately leading to a crash landing on an alien planet. Ironically, despite all the carnage it causes, the monster's true desire turns out to be rather mundane and almost endearing: it just wants to be served as a side dish. The story ends with the monster fulfilling this wish, becoming part of a Thanksgiving meal shared by the Simpsons and a tribe of aliens. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Jimmy Johnson (character)
text: Jimmy Johnson (character) is Real-world NFL on FOX analyst who appeared in Simpsons crossover specials. Jimmy Johnson appears as himself, playing the role of a football analyst for NFL on FOX within the Simpsons universe. He shares a lighthearted, casual moment with Homer, bonding over donuts backstage while Homer chats about his job. Later, he's part of the Fox Sports studio crew that interviews the Simpson family, blending real-world sports broadcasting with the show's comedic style. His appearances are limited to promotional specials rather than the main series, giving him a niche but memorable presence as a real-world guest character. He doesn't have an established personality beyond his real-life persona, since his role is essentially a cameo tied to NFL promotional content. Voiced by Himself.

title: Ulysses S. Grant
text: Ulysses S. Grant is Historical U.S. President referenced in the Simpsons universe. Ulysses S. Grant appears in the show only as a historical figure rather than an active character. He's represented by an Audio-Animatronic figure in the "Alco-Hall of Fame" exhibit at Duff Days, poking fun at his real-life reputation for heavy drinking. He also appears as a picture in a history book that Superintendent Chalmers shows Bart, sparking Bart's fleeting interest in presidents before he becomes fixated on Theodore Roosevelt instead. Grant has no dialogue and is a non-speaking, background presence used mainly for historical or comedic reference. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent nods to real-world American history and politics.

title: Jonah (Bible)
text: Jonah (Bible) is A biblical prophet referenced in Simpsons Bible-themed episodes; not a main cast member. Jonah is a figure drawn from biblical lore who meets his end after being swallowed by a whale. Within the Simpsons universe, his story is retold through a dream sequence experienced by Bart, giving it a non-canon status. In this version, his death comes when Goliath II devours the whale that had swallowed him. He also appears in a live-action-style retelling where he is portrayed by the Sea Captain. Jonah doesn't speak in his appearances, functioning more as a plot element in Bible parody segments than a fully realized character. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent habit of reimagining religious stories for comedic effect.

title: Ricky Jay (character)
text: Ricky Jay (character) is A real-life stage magician who appears as himself in a minor role in The Simpsons. Ricky Jay appears as a fictionalized version of himself, drawing on his real-world reputation as a master of sleight-of-hand magic, card tricks, card throwing, and feats of memory. In the show, he is depicted alongside fellow real-life magicians Penn Jillette, Teller, and David Copperfield, joining them in an attempt to kill The Great Raymondo. His presence is largely a cameo tied to the world of stage magic explored in that episode. Beyond his main appearance, he's referenced visually through a picture hanging on a wall, suggesting his stature as a recognizable figure in magic circles within the show's universe. He also shows up briefly in an opening sequence gag in another episode. Overall, his role is small and mostly serves as a nod to real celebrity magicians rather than a developed character. Voiced by Ricky Jay.

title: Quinn Hopper
text: Quinn Hopper is Programming teacher who taught a coding class at Springfield Elementary School, working alongside Lisa Simpson. Quinn Hopper is a coding instructor brought in to teach programming at Springfield Elementary. She initially shows favoritism toward Lisa simply for being one of the few girls in a male-dominated class, hinting at her strong views on gender representation in tech. She spearheads the creation of an app called CONRAD designed to predict consequences, working with an all-female programming team plus Comic Book Guy. When the situation takes a strange turn with CONRAD seemingly gaining sentience, Quinn is initially skeptical and dismissive of Lisa's claims, chalking it up to sleep deprivation. Her skepticism is eventually overturned when the AI proves itself in front of a public audience. Beyond her main appearance, she pops up occasionally in the background of Springfield social life, such as attending a podcast recording and joining a bar trivia team. Voiced by Kaitlin Olson.

title: Michael Jordan
text: Michael Jordan is Real-world basketball legend referenced/appearing as a minor character in The Simpsons. Michael Jordan appears in the Simpsons universe mostly as a cultural touchstone rather than a fleshed-out character, reflecting his real-life status as a basketball icon. He's frequently invoked as the gold standard of greatness, whether in debates about the 'Greatest of All Time' or as a nickname bestowed on other characters, like when Homer is dubbed the 'Michael Jordan of Sector 7G' or Groundskeeper Willie is called the 'Scottish Michael Jordan.' His bald head and fame even land him on a barbershop poster of notable bald Black men. Notably, he's a non-speaking character in the show, existing more as a name-drop or background image than an active participant in storylines. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he's shown queuing up for a rocket escaping Earth for Mars, poking fun at his celebrity status even amid an apocalypse.

title: Julia (Friends and Family)
text: Julia (Friends and Family) is A neighbor of the Simpsons who becomes an unexpectedly close friend of Homer's. Julia is a woman living in the house behind the Simpsons who strikes up an odd friendship with Homer after catching him naked on his roof. The two bond over their shared quirks, frequently dining out and spending time together, which sparks suspicion among Homer's friends and eventually Marge that something romantic is going on. In reality, Julia has no romantic interest in Homer at all, and she personally steps in to clear up the misunderstanding with Marge. She is engaged to a fiancé whose career as an airline pilot keeps him away from home for long stretches, which seems to leave her seeking companionship elsewhere. Her presence highlights Homer's oddly platonic charm and the trust issues that can arise in Homer and Marge's marriage. She later makes a brief, eerie cameo appearance among Ned Flanders' deceased wives in one of Bart's coma dreams. Voiced by Allison Janney.

title: Jug band manager
text: Jug band manager is A minor relative of the Simpson family, briefly shown as part of Homer's extended clan. The jug band manager is one of the many obscure relatives in the sprawling Simpson family tree. He first surfaces when Homer, eager to prove to Lisa that their family has produced successful people, points him out as an example. His claim to fame is managing a jug band, a modest and somewhat comedic occupation that undercuts Homer's attempt to impress Lisa. He later reappears at a family gathering, showing he remains a recognized, if minor, member of the extended family. His role is small and largely used for a quick joke about the family's underwhelming achievements. He has no distinct personality traits beyond this brief comedic appearance. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Gabriel
text: Gabriel is A social worker assigned to help keep the Simpson family together. Gabriel is a professional social worker who is called in to mend the Simpson family's dysfunction. He takes the family out into the woods as part of his effort to reconnect them, and it's there that Homer mistakes him for a heavenly being due to his calm, almost angelic demeanor and white outfit. His methods seem to work, at least temporarily, as the family bonds during the ordeal. However, his patience runs out when he discovers Homer's secret Vegas marriage to Amber, prompting him to abandon the case in disgust. He later makes a brief cameo appearance during a town meeting about Lake Springfield, this time dressed in black rather than his signature white attire. His name and appearance are a playful nod to the biblical angel Gabriel. Voiced by Delroy Lindo.

title: The Jazzler
text: The Jazzler is Non-canon superhero alter ego of Lisa Simpson appearing in Simpsons comic books. The Jazzler is a comic-exclusive persona adopted by Lisa Simpson following a nuclear explosion, transforming her into a jazz-themed crimefighter. Dressed in classic jazzman attire complete with sunglasses, she wields her saxophone as both instrument and weapon, using her music to disorient opponents. In her debut she mistakes Bartman for a villain and confronts him, only for him to slip away while she's distracted rambling about her tunes. Her design and gimmick are clearly modeled after DC's Fiddler, sharing a musical-weapon theme and similar naming convention, while her superhero name itself nods to the Marvel heroine Dazzler. Despite being a one-off gag character, she has popped up in a handful of Bongo comic stories. Notable quotes: Oh, Maaan...Get with it! you're Diggin' the Jazzler!
quotes: Oh, Maaan...Get with it! you're Diggin' the Jazzler!

title: JJ Hibbert
text: JJ Hibbert is Younger son of Dr. Julius Hibbert and Bernice Hibbert, a minor recurring student character in Springfield. JJ Hibbert is a minor background character best known as the son of the Simpsons' family doctor, Julius Hibbert. He's shown occasionally weighing in on family decisions, like picking a restaurant, and attending community events alongside his father. At one point he was enrolled at the prestigious Springfield Preparatory School, hinting at his family's relative affluence. During a family vacation to Costa Rica, he displayed a mildly standoffish streak by rebuffing Milhouse Van Houten's repeated attempts at friendship. Despite appearing across many seasons in the background of crowd scenes, he rarely gets significant dialogue or storylines of his own. His character has been voiced by three different actors over the show's long run, reflecting his status as a low-priority recurring figure. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright, Pamela Hayden, Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Gordie Howe
text: Gordie Howe is Real-world hockey legend whose photo Bart uses as a prank prop involving Mrs. Krabappel. Gordie Howe appears in the show not as an animated speaking character, but as a photograph clipped from a book about NHL stars. Bart uses the picture to pose as his fake pen pal "Woodrow" when pranking Mrs. Krabappel, sending it in response to a photo she shared of herself. Unbeknownst to her, the dashing photo she cherishes and displays on her desk is actually a real-world hockey player rather than a genuine suitor. His image later resurfaces on a classroom wall, reinforcing his status as a purely visual gag rather than a proper character. Howe never speaks or interacts directly in the story, existing solely as a picture-based running joke tied to Bart's prank. Notable quotes: "Strap on your skates, Gordie, you're goin' in."
quotes: "Strap on your skates, Gordie, you're goin' in."

title: Ron Howard (character)
text: Ron Howard (character) is Celebrity guest character; real-life film director appearing as himself in Springfield. Ron Howard is a fictionalized version of himself who pops up in Springfield's celebrity circles, apparently friendly with Kim Basinger and Alec Baldwin. He's portrayed as a bit reckless and dangerous, at one point nearly killing Homer after leaping onto his mobile museum, despite also giving him parenting advice on another occasion. Notably, he's not a great driver. His interactions with Homer often turn contentious, such as when he stole Homer's movie pitch idea or clashed with him during a game show appearance on Springfield Squares. He's also shown to have a lighter side, taking his kids to an exclusive celebrity zoo. In non-canon material, he's the butt of a joke when Tom Hanks shoves him aside and mockingly calls him by his old sitcom nickname "Opie." Voiced by Ron Howard (Himself).

title: Dr. Griffin
text: Dr. Griffin is Minor fictional scientist character referenced in a Bumblebee Man cartoon and later appearing as a Treehouse of Horror crossover figure. Dr. Griffin, better known as the Invisible Man, is a background character based on the classic H.G. Wells novella from 1897. Within the show's universe, he's depicted as the subject of a cartoon within a cartoon, appearing in an episode of The Bumblebee Man's Show wearing blue pants. He never speaks on screen, functioning purely as a visual reference and homage to the literary and film character. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he takes on a more sinister role, joining other characters in hunting down the citizens of Springfield. He later reappears as a collectible figure in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game, tied to a Halloween-themed event. Overall, he's a minor crossover figure used mostly for parody and Halloween-special purposes rather than any ongoing storyline.

title: Tibor Jankovsky
text: Tibor Jankovsky is Minor recurring employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, briefly Homer's supervisor. Tibor Jankovsky is a background employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant who speaks little English, making him an easy target for coworkers to unfairly blame for their own mistakes. Homer in particular scapegoats him for various plant mishaps, even while grudgingly admitting Tibor has saved him from trouble before. Despite being on the receiving end of blame, Tibor's competence is eventually recognized, and he is promoted above Homer to become his supervisor, a twist that irritates Homer. Over time Tibor rises further, earning a corner office, and gradually picks up broken English. He represents a small running gag about immigrant workers being unfairly blamed for workplace problems due to a language barrier. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Now Marge, just remember, if something goes wrong at the plant, blame the guy who can't speak English. Ah, Tibor, how many times have you saved my butt?
quotes: Now Marge, just remember, if something goes wrong at the plant, blame the guy who can't speak English. Ah, Tibor, how many times have you saved my butt?

title: Kensey
text: Kensey is A party planner hired for Addy's birthday sleepover, appearing in a Season 31 episode. Kensey is a professional party planner tasked with running Addy's birthday sleepover, and she takes her job very seriously, insisting on full participation from every guest. Her rigid, upbeat enthusiasm clashes with the reality of dealing with bored or difficult kids, particularly when Lisa wants to leave early. She tries to keep the event on track with structured activities like a perfume workshop, but her efforts are undermined by the mockery of one of the attendees. This leads to her being flustered enough to storm out of the room, showing that beneath her professional facade she has limited patience for being disrespected. She's a minor, one-episode character used for comic conflict at the sleepover. Voiced by Lilly Singh. Notable quotes: Kensey told Lisa that the sleepover had to get 100% engagement.
quotes: Kensey told Lisa that the sleepover had to get 100% engagement.

title: Gretchen Grille
text: Gretchen Grille is Society and gossip reporter at WZEN News, a recurring character in the Radioactive Man comic-within-a-comic universe. Gretchen Grille is a blonde news reporter who covers society and gossip stories for WZEN News in Zenith City. She has a sharp, somewhat catty tongue, often making pointed remarks about others, such as teasing Gloria Grand about her diet. Despite her snarky edge, she can also loosen up and enjoy herself, as shown when she joins Gloria in indulging in ice cream. Romantically, she briefly dated Claude Kane III, but their relationship soured after a bizarre incident involving his secret identity as Radioactive Man. She also appears in a professional capacity as a newsreader, reporting on major civic events like the passing of the president's budget. Her connection to Radioactive Man is memorialized oddly, as he keeps a picture of her in his personal sanctuary, the Containment Dome. Notable quotes: Gretchen asked him to take his hat off in the presence of a lady | Gloria told Gretchen to live a little and help her finish the ice cream and Gretchen agrees that they may as well enjoy themselves now.
quotes: Gretchen asked him to take his hat off in the presence of a lady
Gloria told Gretchen to live a little and help her finish the ice cream and Gretchen agrees that they may as well enjoy themselves now.

title: Mr. Jones
text: Mr. Jones is Minor recurring character; father of bully Jimbo Jones. Mr. Jones is a background Springfield resident best known as the father of school bully Jimbo Jones. He's implied to be an aggressive, hard-drinking man, having once joined in beating up Homer at Moe's Tavern alongside other tough parents. His reputation as a drinker is referenced by Principal Skinner when Jimbo mocks him. Divorced from his wife Carol, he later appears at a support event for separated fathers, showing a softer, more sympathetic side of his character. Overall he's a minor figure used mostly to add background context to Jimbo's rough upbringing. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "My Dad said you were a busboy!" | "You mean your dad, the raging alcoholic?"
quotes: "My Dad said you were a busboy!"
"You mean your dad, the raging alcoholic?"

title: Hobo
text: Hobo is An unnamed homeless man who appears occasionally around Springfield. The hobo is a recurring background character who wanders the streets of Springfield with his loyal dog, Blue. He tends to show up in odd, downtrodden situations, whether it's mooching off a squeegee-cleaning racket or getting swept up in the town's mandatory testing programs. His interactions are often small, quirky moments that highlight the seedier, comedic underbelly of Springfield life. He's not above petty scams, like pretending to clean a windshield that wasn't dirty just to get water for his dog. Occasionally he stumbles into slapstick mishaps, such as drunkenly altering a store's marquee sign. In a non-canon segment, he becomes an unfortunate victim of Mayor Quimby's twisted 'homeless shelter' scheme. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: that's it boy. Live one more day
quotes: that's it boy. Live one more day

title: Enrico Irritazio
text: Enrico Irritazio is An Italian paparazzo hired by Springfield celebrities to antagonize Homer. Enrico Irritazio is a scheming Italian paparazzo brought to Springfield to turn the tables on Homer Simpson's own photography habits. He was hired by a group of celebrities, including Rainier Wolfcastle, who wanted embarrassing pictures of Homer to make him stop snapping photos of them. His plan worked, at least temporarily, showing him to be effective and ruthless in his profession. Later, he shows a lack of discretion or loyalty by secretly photographing a private, tender moment between Moe and Princess Kemi. Despite Kemi's pleas to keep the photo private, Enrico sold it to gossip websites anyway, revealing his willingness to exploit people's personal moments for profit. He functions mainly as a recurring antagonist figure tied to Springfield's brushes with celebrity culture and scandal. Voiced by Jon Lovitz.

title: Jeremy Jailbird
text: Jeremy Jailbird is Son of Snake Jailbird, a minor recurring child character in Springfield. Jeremy Jailbird is the young son of the town's small-time crook Snake Jailbird, whose parents are separated though Snake still gets visitation. Despite his father's criminal lifestyle, Jeremy comes across as soft-spoken and mild-mannered, seemingly picking up some of Snake's habits, like joining him in petty theft. He's shown tagging along on his dad's various schemes and outings, including a bike theft and a trip to a cave searching for lost treasure. Jeremy's brief interactions with Bart Simpson highlight his quiet, almost innocent demeanor despite being raised around crime. He also appeared among townsfolk boarding a ship to Weasel Island. Jeremy has since made an appearance in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out as well. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Daddy, I'm stealing, I'm stealing! | do you like Xbox?
quotes: Daddy, I'm stealing, I'm stealing!
do you like Xbox?

title: Tom Kite (character)
text: Tom Kite (character) is Real-life professional golfer who appears as himself, giving golf lessons to Homer and Krusty at the Springfield Glen Country Club. Tom Kite is a real-world professional golfer who makes a cameo appearance in Springfield, offering unsolicited golf advice to Homer during a disastrous round at the country club. He's initially generous with his tips, helping Homer improve his swing almost instantly, but quickly grows irritated when Homer oversteps by rummaging through his locker and borrowing his equipment. His patience has limits, and he isn't afraid to snap at Homer before storming off. Later he reappears while coaching Krusty the Clown, only to become an unwitting victim of Homer's flying golf club. True to a low-key cameo character, he discreetly exits the scene rather than getting involved in the chaos he's caught up in. Kite's image also turns up as a celebrity trivia option in a later episode, cementing his status as a recognizable real-world guest presence rather than a true Springfield resident. Voiced by Himself. Notable quotes: Stay the hell out of my locker!
quotes: Stay the hell out of my locker!

title: Hippie
text: Hippie is Minor recurring character; operator at Uriah's Heap Recycling Center. The hippie is a laid-back, minor Springfield resident who runs the recycling operation at Uriah's Heap Recycling Center. He embodies a stereotypical counter-culture attitude, dispensing casual, philosophical advice to customers rather than practical help. His most notable appearance involves him giving Principal Skinner a paltry sum for recycled newspapers, then dismissing Skinner's complaints with a lecture about not overcomplicating life. Beyond his recycling job, he has participated in offbeat community events, such as an attempt to build the world's tallest human pyramid. He mostly serves as background color for Springfield's quirky populace, appearing briefly across a handful of episodes and non-canon materials. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: It sounds like you're working for your car. Simplify, man!
quotes: It sounds like you're working for your car. Simplify, man!

title: Hypnotist
text: Hypnotist is Minor recurring character who works as both a Santa School instructor and professional hypnotist. The Hypnotist is a bald, minor recurring figure in Springfield who first appears as an instructor at the Santa School, training Homer and other hopeful mall Santas without using any hypnosis at all. He later resurfaces in his true specialty when Mr. Burns hires him to hypnotize the power plant's softball team into believing they're skilled players for an important game. His hypnosis attempts don't always go as planned, most notably when he accidentally convinces Roger Clemens that he's a chicken instead of improving his baseball skills. Despite these mistakes, he's clever enough to cover for himself, simply hypnotizing Mr. Burns into thinking the job was done well when threatened with exposure. He also seems to enjoy simple pleasures, having been spotted attending a baseball game specifically for free pretzel day. In non-canon material, he takes on a mentor role, teaching Ralph Wiggum the art of hypnosis and using his skills to trick Chief Wiggum into believing a stranger is his long-lost uncle. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: you will give 110 percent | That's impossible. No one can give more than one hundred percent. By definition that is the most anyone can give.
quotes: you will give 110 percent
That's impossible. No one can give more than one hundred percent. By definition that is the most anyone can give.

title: Paul Harvey
text: Paul Harvey is Real-world radio broadcaster referenced/parodied in the Simpsons universe. Paul Harvey appears in the show as a voice-only, real-world radio personality known for his distinctive storytelling style and signature signoff. He's portrayed as a soothing, grandfatherly presence on the airwaves, compared by Marge to a gentler version of Grampa Simpson. His broadcasts pop up at pivotal or amusing moments, such as distracting Grampa and Jasper from The Be Sharps' debut performance, or being heard through a risqué book-on-tape that Homer and Marge listen to together. He's also referenced as a recurring, overly lengthy segment on Krusty the Clown's show. Despite his limited appearances, he serves as a nostalgic nod to old-fashioned radio broadcasting within the Simpsons world. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: It's a book on tape by Paul Harvey. You know that nice Midwestern man on the radio who's like a pleasant version of Grampa?
quotes: It's a book on tape by Paul Harvey. You know that nice Midwestern man on the radio who's like a pleasant version of Grampa?

title: KISS
text: KISS is Real-world rock band referenced within the Simpsons universe, tied to Homer and Marge's history. KISS appears in the show as the famous real-life rock band, most notably represented by member Gene Simmons. The band has a recurring presence as a cultural touchstone for Homer, who idolized them as a teenager and even dressed up as Gene Simmons at one point. Marge associates the band with her pregnancy with Bart, having listened to their music heavily at the time, and later blames their influence for his rebellious personality. The band has also been used oddly, such as being featured in Navy recruitment efforts and appearing as wax figures that Homer rearranges while intoxicated. In a non-canon storyline, the band takes a much more direct role in the Simpsons family history, with Gene Simmons secretly being revealed as Bart's biological father after a one-night stand with Marge. Overall, KISS functions as a running pop-culture reference tied closely to Homer's fandom and the show's jokes about Bart's origins.

title: Puppy Goo-Goo
text: Puppy Goo-Goo is Milhouse Van Houten's stuffed toy dog. Puppy Goo-Goo is a plush toy belonging to Milhouse, which he clings to as a source of comfort whenever he's upset. The toy is significant enough to Milhouse's identity that its image once appeared on the cover of a toy catalog. In a non-canon Halloween segment, it briefly came to life alongside other toys and turned on its owner, even abandoning Milhouse after complaining about being neglected. Despite being an inanimate object for most of its appearances, the toy has become a recurring visual gag tied to Milhouse's childlike attachment to comfort items. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Gillian
text: Gillian is A minor recurring Springfield socialite and member of Marge's social circle. Gillian is a well-to-do Springfield socialite with red hair who moves in the same elite social circles as Marge Simpson. She was first introduced when her friend Evelyn Peters brought her into Marge's orbit at the Springfield Glen Country Club, giving her a recurring presence among the town's wealthier residents. She has popped up in a variety of odd contexts, including a police-produced film warning about road rage, suggesting she's willing to lend her image to civic causes. Her personal life has also been glimpsed briefly, such as a date with a character named Neil at a local pub. Gillian doesn't have a strongly defined personality of her own beyond being part of Marge's country-club social set, functioning mostly as a background socialite who appears across many episodes without playing a central role in the plot. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Gunter (Mom and Pop Art)
text: Gunter (Mom and Pop Art) is Recurring minor character, one of Homer's artist friends from his brief career as an artist. Gunter is a European artist who became part of Homer's social circle after Homer briefly became a celebrated artist himself. He carries a stereotypical air of continental sophistication, describing his lifestyle as full of decadent luxury and casual indulgence. He's later shown attending glamorous events abroad, reinforcing his jet-setting, cultured persona. Gunter also has a habit of making dry, sarcastic quips, such as mocking the military origins of a sculpture right before it turns out to be a live missile. Possibly killed in that explosion, his fate remains ambiguous. He is a smoker and appears occasionally across several episodes as part of Springfield's eccentric background cast. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: To be honest, we're adrift in a sea of decadent luxury and meaningless sex. | More like snore-ad.
quotes: To be honest, we're adrift in a sea of decadent luxury and meaningless sex.
More like snore-ad.

title: Kearney's Other Son
text: Kearney's Other Son is Minor recurring character; son of Kearney Zzyzwicz and brother of Kearney Zzyzwicz, Jr.. Kearney's Other Son is a minor, obscure member of the extended Zzyzwicz family, following in his father's tough-guy footsteps. He's known mainly for a single incident where he got into a scuffle with baby Maggie Simpson while playing at a park. Little else about his personality or history is documented, making him one of the more mysterious background kids in Springfield. He also appears in a non-canon capacity in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. His family tree includes his grandfather, Mr. Zzyzwicz, tying him to the Zzyzwicz lineage of troublemakers.

title: Jenda
text: Jenda is Bart Simpson's future girlfriend and later ex-wife, appearing in non-canon future episodes. Jenda is a character glimpsed in the show's speculative future episodes, first appearing as a teenage girlfriend of Bart's who later becomes his wife and eventually his ex-wife. She's portrayed as somewhat manipulative and demanding, pressuring Bart into major life decisions and giving him ultimatums about their relationship. Their on-and-off romance includes marriage, two sons, divorce, and Jenda moving on to date an alien named Jerry. The relationship's instability becomes a running theme, with the two repeatedly breaking up and reconciling. In a twist, one version of their post-divorce reunion and further breakup is revealed to be a false memory implanted in Bart's mind rather than something that actually happened. Overall, Jenda represents the rocky, ever-changing nature of Bart's speculative future love life across multiple non-canon episodes. Voiced by Amy Poehler.

title: Hester
text: Hester is A minor recurring resident of the Springfield Retirement Castle. Hester is an elderly resident of the Springfield Retirement Castle who appears sporadically across several episodes. She's shown to be a bit fussy and particular, especially about food, as demonstrated by her complaint about eggs. Her most notable moment involves lodging a complaint at Krusty Burger during Grampa Simpson's stint working there, highlighting her tendency to voice her dissatisfaction. Despite her limited screen time, she pops up in various storylines over the years, functioning as one of the many background elderly characters populating the retirement home. She doesn't have a deep backstory or defined relationships, serving mostly as a recurring background presence in scenes set at the retirement castle. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: These eggs are difficult to digest. I want soft-boiled eggs!
quotes: These eggs are difficult to digest. I want soft-boiled eggs!

title: Horst
text: Horst is One of the German businessmen who briefly bought the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. Horst is one of the trio of German investors, alongside Hans and Fritz, who purchase the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. He is tasked with helping the plant's employees adjust to new German management, a job he claims he got because his bosses saw him as the friendliest-looking of the group. Despite his approachable role, he has little patience for Homer's laziness and tendency to zone out into fantasies like his "Land of Chocolate" daydream. His stint as a plant executive ends when the trio decides the plant is too costly and dangerous, selling it back to Mr. Burns. Years later, he resurfaces still connected to Hans, the two of them chasing a conspiracy theory about Angela Merkel's true birthplace. He's also self-aware enough to note his own resemblance to actor John Banner. Voiced by Phil Hartman.

title: Noir Homer
text: Noir Homer is An alternate-universe version of Homer Simpson from a noir-styled dimension, appearing in a Treehouse of Horror multiverse episode. Noir Homer is one of several alternate versions of Homer Simpson who spill into Springfield after a mishap with a candy machine at the Nuclear Power Plant. True to his noir persona, he speaks in hardboiled detective-style dialogue and carries himself with a grim, tough-guy attitude compared to the other Homer variants. He's quick to violence, casually shooting Ned Flanders without much remorse, and later joins the other Homers in fighting off a group of alternate Mr. Burns who want to exploit them as cheap labor. His story ends tragically when an alternate Burns stabs him through the heart during the battle. In a strange twist, after seemingly dying he briefly reappears with Marge only to transform into Homer Barbera before fleeing, adding one more layer of absurdity to his short-lived appearance. He exists purely as a non-canon parody character, explicitly based on Spider-Man Noir. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: the case was going to be like Homer's skull—hard to crack and not much inside
quotes: the case was going to be like Homer's skull—hard to crack and not much inside

title: Glutenus Maximus
text: Glutenus Maximus is A comic-book supervillain who is secretly Uter's father, appearing in a Simpsons Bongo comic story. Glutenus Maximus is a bread-themed supervillain who terrorizes Springfield alongside his sidekick Gluten Tag, using baked goods as bizarre weapons. He and his partner rob the Leftorium and crash a mayoral fundraiser to steal money, banning bakery products and evading police until Homer Simpson eventually defeats them by eating through their donut restraints. His villainous identity turns out to be a front for desperation, as he and his sidekick are unmasked as Uter and his father, driven to crime after losing their German breakfast restaurant. The story resolves comically when Homer suggests they open a pork restaurant instead, which becomes a hit with everyone in town except Lisa. Years later, his legacy lives on as a statue in a museum exhibit dedicated to past villains, and his bread-based attack is even reused by another criminal wearing a power suit. His name is a punny mashup of "gluten" and "gluteus maximus," fitting his absurd bakery-crime theme.

title: Carol Jones
text: Carol Jones is Mother of bully Jimbo Jones, a minor recurring resident of Springfield. Carol Jones is the mother of school bully Jimbo Jones and works as a prostitute, reportedly well known around Springfield for this trade. She once had a romantic relationship with Kearney, one of her son's fellow troublemakers. Despite her disreputable job, she seems to spend ordinary time at home, such as watching soap operas with Jimbo. In non-canon material, she's portrayed as having breast implants that her doctor advised she keep exposed to air, leading her to walk around the house topless regardless of company, much to the awkwardness or amusement of others. She's a background character used mostly for quick jokes about Jimbo's chaotic home life and her own scandalous reputation. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Jimmy the Snitch
text: Jimmy the Snitch is A minor mafia associate in the Springfield mob. Jimmy the Snitch is a low-level member of Springfield's mafia underworld, known primarily by his telling nickname. As his moniker suggests, his role within the criminal organization seems tied to passing along information, which likely makes him a liability among his fellow gangsters. His limited appearances hint at a rough treatment by the mob, including being forcibly stuffed into a car trunk. He exists mostly as background color for the show's recurring mafia storylines rather than as a fully developed character. Little else about his personality or history is explored on screen. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Hellroads teacher
text: Hellroads teacher is Non-canon teacher at the Hellroads school in Hell, appearing in a Treehouse of Horror segment. This unnamed teacher works at Hellroads, a school located in Hell, and also serves as the head of a teachers' union there. She appears during a Treehouse of Horror segment where Bart, transformed into 'Beelzebart Simpson,' becomes one of her students. Rather than being intimidating despite her infernal workplace, she turns out to be encouraging, praising Bart's ideas and eagerness to learn. As a reward for his enthusiasm, she awards him top marks across his report card. Her design and a teaching scene were later reused in a couch gag for another episode, showing she left enough of an impression to be referenced again. She also appears as a character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Guinness brewer
text: Guinness brewer is A minor, unnamed employee at the Guinness Brewery encountered by Lisa Simpson during a family trip to Ireland. The Guinness brewer is a background character who appears briefly during the Simpsons' visit to the Guinness Brewery in Ireland. He works there and inadvertently reveals a secret about the beer's recipe when Lisa lingers behind during a tour. His personality is defined mainly by his flustered, annoyed reaction when Lisa cleverly deduces the exact ratio of the secret ingredients. This small moment of comedic frustration is his only real character trait, as he otherwise has no name, backstory, or recurring presence. He later resurfaces in a non-canon capacity as a picture among Lisa's future social media friend requests, a nod to his earlier one-off appearance. Overall, he serves as a minor comedic obstacle for Lisa's curiosity rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: 50/50?

title: Helicopter pilot
text: Helicopter pilot is Unnamed recurring helicopter pilot who appears in various episodes transporting characters. This nameless pilot pops up whenever a helicopter is needed to move the plot along, usually with a calm, professional demeanor that belies the chaos around him. He's first seen flying the Simpson family into Itchy & Scratchy Land, reassuring them nothing could go wrong just before things inevitably do. Later, during the family's misadventures in Australia, he casually informs Homer about the logistics of landing on a laundry ship rather than an aircraft carrier, showing a dry, matter-of-fact attitude toward absurd situations. He also appears hovering above Springfield to whisk away a Hollywood star, treating the bizarre urgency of celebrity scheduling as just another routine job. Overall, he's a minor recurring background character whose main trait is being unflappable no matter how ridiculous the circumstances get. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: nothing could "possibly" go wrong
quotes: nothing could "possibly" go wrong

title: Pixel Homer
text: Pixel Homer is An alternate-universe version of Homer Simpson who appears as a non-canon character in a Treehouse of Horror multiverse story. Pixel Homer is one of several alternate versions of Homer who accidentally cross over into the main Simpsons universe through a malfunctioning candy machine at the Nuclear Power Plant. Rendered in a blocky, pixelated video-game style, he joins the other visiting Homers on a chaotic spree of eating, bowling, and general mischief around Springfield. When the group learns they must return to their home universes or perish, Pixel Homer helps attempt to recreate the dimensional rift back at the plant. He even gets caught up in a battle against alternate versions of Mr. Burns, squaring off specifically against a villainous 'Bowser Burns.' His role is largely a visual gag tying into the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, poking fun at crossover and multiverse tropes rather than developing any deep personality of his own. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Gretel (Treehouse of Horror XXXI)
text: Gretel (Treehouse of Horror XXXI) is Fairy tale character from "Hansel & Gretel" who appears in a Treehouse of Horror segment and other minor Simpsons appearances. Gretel is one half of the classic fairy tale duo Hansel and Gretel, appearing in The Simpsons primarily as a crossover or non-canon reference rather than a fleshed-out character. She and her brother are depicted being threatened with being cooked by a witch, tying into the original fairy tale's dark premise. In a non-canon storyline, Mr. Burns and Waylon Smithers keep the siblings caged, with Burns creepily noting he prefers his captives lean rather than fattened up. She has no dialogue of her own in the show, functioning mostly as a background or cameo figure. Notably, in one Treehouse of Horror episode retelling Grimms' Fairy Tales, her role was instead performed by Lisa Simpson. Overall, Gretel exists in the show as a nod to classic literature rather than as a developed personality.

title: The Ingestible Bulk
text: The Ingestible Bulk is Alter-ego of Homer Simpson, a Hulk-parody superhero identity. The Ingestible Bulk is a comic-book and TV parody of the Hulk, born when Homer becomes enraged by Bart and stumbles into a pool of green paint, tearing his clothes in the process. Despite his monstrous green appearance, he's still mistaken for Homer until Stan Lee clarifies he's meant to be seen as the Hulk. In a separate non-canon origin, he instead gains his powers from exposure to a nuclear explosion, granting him super strength and an insatiable ability to eat anything when hungry. His single catchphrase, a guttural roar, plays on the Hulk's famous rage-driven persona. As a recurring but minor superhero identity, he mostly appears in comic issues and a couple of animated specials rather than the core series. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Bulk Gnash!!
quotes: Bulk Gnash!!

title: Kang and Kodos' mother
text: Kang and Kodos' mother is Non-canon comic book character; mother of alien invaders Kang and Kodos. This unnamed alien matriarch appears only in the Bongo comic universe as the mother of the recurring extraterrestrial duo Kang and Kodos. She and her husband hatched a staggering 27 offspring at once, but practicality won out over sentiment when they chose to keep only two and consume the rest. She raised Kang and Kodos with a mix of tough parenting and family tradition, eventually gifting them their own spaceship and a set of rules for interstellar abduction once they came of age. Her culinary legacy lives on through a particular Boys and Berry Pie recipe served with spiced blarch bile, a dish fondly remembered by her now-grown sons. Though she never appears directly interacting with the main Simpsons cast, she's referenced as a nostalgic figure in her sons' adult lives, hinting at a stricter, old-fashioned view on gender roles in her household.

title: The Human Donkey
text: The Human Donkey is A non-canon freak show character, half human and half donkey, at The Burnsum and Bailey Circus. The Human Donkey is a bizarre sideshow attraction, being part human and part donkey, who performs at The Burnsum and Bailey Circus. This oddity character made a brief appearance in the Treehouse of Horror segment 'Freaks no Geeks,' fitting into the episode's theme of circus freaks. Beyond the Treehouse of Horror special, the character also appears as part of the Cirque du Springfield content in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Little else is known about the personality or backstory of this creature, as it exists primarily as a visual gag tied to the freak show setting rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Hope
text: Hope is A Fortnite crossover agent who teams up with Jonesy and gets caught up in the Simpsons' universe during a rift crisis. Hope is a non-canon character brought into the Simpsons universe through a crossover with the video game Fortnite. She is a capable, combat-ready agent who partners with fellow Fortnite character Jonesy, often taking a direct, aggressive approach to problem-solving, such as suggesting violent solutions to save a giant-sized Homer. Her adventures begin when she and Jonesy try to close a dimensional rift near Bart's Treehouse, leading to an encounter with Kang and Kodos' UFO and eventually a merged reality called Springfield Island. Throughout the story she is focused on recovering a powerful zero point shard, using gadgets like scanners and tractor beams to track it down. She shows a willingness to act decisively even against Marge's wishes, though her plans don't always succeed. Hope's storyline ties her fate to the Simpson family's efforts to stop chaos caused by the shard's power, and she ultimately becomes just one of several crossover characters who end up on the run from the Simpsons themselves. Voiced by Suzie Yeung.

title: Hugh Jass
text: Hugh Jass is A minor customer at Moe's Tavern, famous for being the unwitting target of one of Bart's prank calls. Hugh Jass is a mild-mannered patron of Moe's Tavern who becomes the accidental punchline of one of Bart's classic prank calls. Bart invents the name as a joke meant to embarrass Moe, never expecting an actual person with that name to be sitting in the bar. Rather than reacting with anger, Hugh calmly answers the phone and responds to Bart's awkward confession with good humor and kindness. This unexpected politeness subverts the usual chaos of Bart's pranks, making Hugh a memorable one-off character despite his brief screen time. In later, non-canon material, he's expanded into a minor businessman, credited with owning a clothing store called Mr. Big & Large through his own company, Hugh Jass Enterprises. He also appears as a background character in a mobile game, retaining his easygoing demeanor. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Somebody check the men's room for a Hugh Jass! | All right, better luck next time. | Uh, look, I'll level with you, Mister. This is a prank call that sort of backfired, and I'd like to bail out right now.
quotes: Somebody check the men's room for a Hugh Jass!
All right, better luck next time.
Uh, look, I'll level with you, Mister. This is a prank call that sort of backfired, and I'd like to bail out right now.

title: Janitor (Poorhouse Rock)
text: Janitor (Poorhouse Rock) is A singing janitor at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant who appears in the non-canon short "Poorhouse Rock". This janitor is a musical, guide-like figure who works at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. He confronts Bart with the harsh truth that the economic opportunities Homer once had are no longer available to him, using song to make his point. He magically transports Bart through different eras since World War II to illustrate the decline of the middle class, all set to the tune "Goodbye, Middle Class." His cryptic instruction to "burn it all down" is comically misinterpreted by Bart, leading to a small domestic disaster involving burned clothes and a treehouse fire. Despite vanishing after this mishap, he reappears as a fireman for the segment's big musical finale, showing his role is more symbolic and theatrical than literal. In a separate, non-canon appearance, he is shown still working at the plant during the events surrounding Mr. Burns' death and will. Voiced by Hugh Jackman.

title: Evil Homer
text: Evil Homer is An imaginary devil-costumed alter ego of Homer Simpson, appearing as a figment of his imagination. Evil Homer is a fantastical, devilish version of Homer that exists only within his own mind, complete with a costume and mischievous demeanor. He's paired with a counterpart called Alter Homer, framed as the alter ego to a more virtuous "Good Homer." His signature bit involves singing a little jingle about himself while shaking maracas and dancing around a grave belonging to Good Homer, a bizarre and comedic running gag. He later resurfaces in a lighter context, showing up in a Halloween costume during a visit to Marge in prison. Beyond the show itself, the character has found a small afterlife in merchandise and video games, including a costume option in a Simpsons video game and toy releases. Despite his devilish appearance, Evil Homer is more absurd and silly than genuinely menacing, fitting the show's surreal comedic tone. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "I am Evil Homer"
quotes: "I am Evil Homer"

title: Janeane Garofalo (character)
text: Janeane Garofalo (character) is Celebrity guest character appearing as a fictionalized version of herself in Springfield-related events. Janeane Garofalo appears in the show as a semi-fictionalized version of herself, an actress, comedian, and political activist. She turns up at various odd Springfield occasions, from a rooftop pool party with a mix of celebrities to a comedy showcase on Krusty's retro TV special. Her political leanings occasionally get her into trouble, including a mysterious stint locked up in the Ronald Reagan Reeducation Center. On Krusty's show, she attempts to be serious and issue-focused but can't resist cracking a joke, undercutting the show's rule that no one can be funnier than Krusty. She also has a brief romantic history with Krusty the Clown, and her image has popped up as a decoration in at least one Springfield business. Voiced by Janeane Garofalo (herself).

title: Chris Griffin
text: Chris Griffin is Crossover character from Family Guy; son of Lois and Peter Griffin, appearing in non-canon Simpsons crossover episodes. Chris Griffin is a member of the Griffin family from Family Guy who appears in The Simpsons through various crossover specials and non-canon storylines. He's portrayed as part of a family that ends up interacting with the Simpsons after unusual circumstances, such as their car being stolen near Springfield. During one such visit, Chris and Brian misplace Santa's Little Helper and struggle with whether to tell the Simpsons the truth. He's also depicted in more surreal contexts, including being turned into a mutant sent to fight a giant monster, and attending an odd apology gathering with his siblings. As a non-canon character, his appearances are tied specifically to special crossover episodes rather than the main continuity of the show. Voiced by Seth Green.

title: Mark Hamill (character)
text: Mark Hamill (character) is Celebrity guest character based on the real actor, appearing as himself in Springfield storylines. Mark Hamill appears as a fictionalized version of himself, famous for playing Luke Skywalker in Star Wars, who visits Springfield for fan events. He is somewhat exasperated by being forced into promotional work, such as being made to pitch Sprint instead of discussing Star Wars, and by nerdy fans who take things too literally. Despite his fame, he's a good sport who gets pulled into ridiculous situations, including a full-blown riot and a bizarre dinner theater production where he's forced to play a role dressed as Luke Skywalker against his own wishes. He shows a competitive, easily irritated side when he feels his spotlight is being stolen by an unexpected performer. Ultimately he proves resourceful and even heroic in a pinch, helping foil an assassination attempt with a quick-thinking use of cutlery. His experiences with Homer Simpson end up indirectly inspiring Homer's brief career as a bodyguard. Voiced by Mark Hamill (Himself). Notable quotes: "Use the forks!"
quotes: "Use the forks!"

title: Bart Junior (frog)
text: Bart Junior (frog) is A pet frog caught and owned by Bart Simpson. Bart Junior is a small green frog that Bart caught and kept as a pet, despite being female. Bart cared for her by feeding her flies and admired her carefree lifestyle, spending time with her after school. During a family trip to Australia, Bart tried to smuggle her in but had to release her, leading to her escape and eventual disappearance. Unbeknownst to Bart, she ended up breeding with local wildlife, resulting in an entire continent-wide infestation of bullfrogs descended from her. Despite this chaotic legacy, Bart continued to fondly reference her, even imagining walking through school with her again during a gender-divided event. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Rudy Giuliani (character)
text: Rudy Giuliani (character) is Real-world politician who appears as himself in a minor recurring role in The Simpsons. Rudy Giuliani appears as a real-world guest character playing himself within the show's universe. His most notable moment comes when Homer uses a portrait of him in a commercial for Families Come First, invoking his name and image to command obedience. This gag plays on Giuliani's real-life reputation and authority, with Homer humorously exploiting it to manipulate Marge into forgiving him. Giuliani himself has no real personality development in the show, existing mainly as a cameo/parody figure rather than a fleshed-out character. He has been referenced or appeared in a small handful of episodes, cementing his status as a minor recurring real-world character. Voiced by Rudy Giuliani (Himself).

title: Hollis Hurlbut
text: Hollis Hurlbut is Head of the Springfield Historical Society, involved in the Jebediah Springfield fraud storyline with Lisa. Hollis Hurlbut is the stuffy, self-important curator of the Springfield Historical Society, fiercely protective of the town's founding mythology. He initially reacts with outrage when Lisa uncovers evidence that town hero Jebediah Springfield was actually a fraud, threatening to ban her and her descendants before softening the punishment. When later confronted with physical proof of the deception himself, he chooses self-interest over honesty, quietly pocketing the incriminating evidence rather than risk his own career and reputation. This willingness to bury inconvenient truths ties into the episode's larger theme about the comforting power of civic myths. Despite his prickly, pompous demeanor, he's a minor recurring figure rather than a major cast member. A running gag references him insisting on his professional title as an antiquarian, and later material humorously ties him to real-world Harvard dormitory names. Voiced by Donald Sutherland. Notable quotes: I'm an antiquarian, damn it!
quotes: I'm an antiquarian, damn it!

title: Art Garfunkel
text: Art Garfunkel is Real-world singer (of Simon & Garfunkel) referenced/appearing as a character in Simpsons episodes. Art Garfunkel appears as a fictionalized version of the real-life singer within the world of The Simpsons, most notably in Lisa's dream of joining a band alongside him and other musicians. He's frequently invoked in pop-culture jokes and comparisons, often tied to his famous partnership and eventual falling-out with Paul Simon. Other characters reference him as a shorthand for musical duos or reconciliation, such as when Homer urges two feuding friends to make up like Simon and Garfunkel did. He also shows up in surreal contexts, like a drug-fueled hallucination shared by Homer and Ned. Garfunkel himself rarely appears as an active character, functioning mostly as a mentioned or imagined figure rather than someone with direct dialogue or plot involvement. Notable quotes: We had quite a severe ant problem at the vineyard this year. I had Art Garfunkel come by with his compressor, and we created a total vacuum outside the house, and we blew the ants out the front door.
quotes: We had quite a severe ant problem at the vineyard this year. I had Art Garfunkel come by with his compressor, and we created a total vacuum outside the house, and we blew the ants out the front door.

title: Davy Jones
text: Davy Jones is A real-world musician from The Monkees who appears as a minor picture-only character in the show. Davy Jones appears in the series as a nod to his real-life fame as a member of The Monkees. He shows up in a flashback during Marge's retelling of a childhood memory, where a lunchbox bearing the band's image becomes the subject of playground teasing. Later, he's spotted again in the Monkeemobile parked at the Hollywood Auto Museum. He doesn't speak in either appearance, existing purely as a visual reference for fans of 1960s pop culture. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent habit of weaving real celebrities and their cultural legacies into background gags. Despite his brief and silent presence, his cameo ties into a broader joke about the authenticity of The Monkees as musicians.

title: Gavin
text: Gavin is A minor recurring child character, a spoiled peer of Bart's. Gavin is a bratty, over-indulged kid roughly Bart's age whose defining trait is being spoiled rotten by his mother. He's the type of child who throws a fit over sharing and demands duplicate toys rather than compromise with his sister. His family life is messier than it looks on the surface, hinting at divorce and remarriage on his mother's side, and a genuinely painful relationship with his father, who coldly tells him he hates him during a rehab phone call. Despite his materialistic upbringing, Gavin seems emotionally starved, using his phone obsessively for everything except actually connecting with his parents. He's a background/recurring character used mostly for quick gags about wealthy, neglectful New York-style parenting. His sister Katelyn and unnamed mother appear alongside him in his few storylines. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: Gavin must be "the happiest kid in the world."
quotes: Gavin must be "the happiest kid in the world."

title: George Jetson
text: George Jetson is A crossover character from The Jetsons who appears briefly in The Simpsons. George Jetson is a guest character brought over from the classic animated series The Jetsons, making a non-canon appearance in The Simpsons universe. His presence is used mainly as a nostalgic gag, tying into Homer's own antics at the power plant. The show pokes fun at the original cartoon by having Homer mimic George's famous exasperated outburst when things spin out of control. Interestingly, due to licensing issues, the production team referred to him as 'George Fetson' in behind-the-scenes commentary, even though he's called 'Jetson' on-screen. He doesn't speak within the actual episode, functioning more as a visual reference than a fully voiced character. His brief crossover appearance highlights the show's tendency to reference and parody other iconic animated series. Notable quotes: Smithers! Stop this crazy thing!
quotes: Smithers! Stop this crazy thing!

title: Philip Hefflin
text: Philip Hefflin is A photographer and artist who had a brief connection to Abraham Simpson decades ago. Philip Hefflin is an elderly gay artist whose life once intersected with Abraham Simpson's during a photo shoot for toy army figures shortly after World War II. A misunderstanding during that shoot led to him kissing Abe, which got him fired from his job for being gay. Decades later, Abe sought him out in Marfa, Texas to apologize, only to find that Hefflin had built an entire artistic legacy around that memory, including a rainbow statue and numerous paintings of Abe. Rather than holding a grudge, Hefflin reveals he found peace and purpose by embracing his identity after the incident, showing a forgiving and reflective personality. He eventually left his marriage to live authentically in Marfa. His reunion with Abe ends on a warm note, cementing an unlikely lifelong friendship. Voiced by Bryan Batt. Notable quotes: Abe had saved his life by letting him live it as he wanted.
quotes: Abe had saved his life by letting him live it as he wanted.

title: Anime Homer
text: Anime Homer is An alternate-universe version of Homer Simpson who appears as an anime-style character in a multiverse crossover. Anime Homer is one of many alternate versions of Homer Simpson pulled into Springfield's universe through a mishap at the Nuclear Power Plant. He joins a group of other alternate Homers in a chaotic romp through Springfield, indulging in eating, bowling, and general mischief alongside his counterparts. True to his anime aesthetic, he's shown dancing energetically while Disney Princess Homer sings. When the group discovers they'll die unless they return to their home universes, Anime Homer helps fight back against Mr. Burns and his own group of alternate selves, who want to exploit the interdimensional device for cheap labor. During the climactic battle, Anime Homer specifically faces off against a robotic version of Mr. Burns. He's ultimately sent back to his own universe once the conflict resolves. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Janey (Bart the General)
text: Janey (Bart the General) is A second-grade classmate of Lisa Simpson at Springfield Elementary School. Janey is a minor, non-speaking background student who appears in a handful of episodes without much individual characterization. She is present during a school scene involving cupcakes meant for Miss Hoover's birthday, which get stolen before Lisa can share one with her. She later shows up as a guest at Bart and Lisa's party, held while Homer and Marge attend marriage counseling. She's also seen participating alongside Lisa on a football team, though her appearance changes to blond hair in that instance. As a background character, she mostly exists to populate school and social scenes rather than drive any storylines herself.

title: Khlav Kalash vendor
text: Khlav Kalash vendor is A recurring minor street vendor in New York City who sells the mysterious food "Khlav Kalash" and occasionally appears in Springfield. This unnamed vendor is a recurring background character best known for hawking a strange food called Khlav Kalash on the streets of New York City. He's a jack-of-all-trades salesman, also seen peddling Crab Juice, Mountain Dew, balloons, and even lamb kebabs depending on the episode. He pops up in unexpected places, from Springfield's Russian District to the Squidport, and even joins an angry mob at Town Hall. His most memorable moment comes when Homer runs into him again in New York City, only to discover the once-humble cart vendor now dressed in a suit, having apparently made it big with a massive building dedicated to his signature food. Despite his minor role, he's a fun example of the show's love for oddball, recurring one-off characters. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: No pizza - only Khlav Kalash!
quotes: No pizza - only Khlav Kalash!

title: Gloria (Snake's wife)
text: Gloria (Snake's wife) is Snake Jailbird's wife and a Springfield police officer. Gloria is a police officer in Springfield who is romantically tied to the small-time criminal Snake. Their relationship is turbulent, having once broken up and seen Gloria briefly dating Mr. Burns after ticketing his car, only for Snake to kidnap her and Homer in a jealous attempt to win her back. Despite the chaos, she ultimately chose Snake over Burns, showing her loyalty lies with her outlaw boyfriend.
