title: Robin Hood
text: Robin Hood is Fictional English folklore outlaw referenced briefly within the Simpsons universe. Robin Hood is not an original Simpsons character but a figure from English folklore who occasionally appears or is referenced within the show's world. He first surfaces as an image Dr. Hibbert shows Homer during a hallucination test, briefly making Homer wonder if the legendary hero is real. In another instance, Marge dresses the family pets and baby Maggie as Robin Hood-themed characters to amuse Moe, showing how the legend has been absorbed into pop culture within the show. A non-canon alternate timeline also features Homer cosplaying as Robin Hood. Overall, Robin Hood functions as a minor pop-culture reference and costume motif rather than a developed character, appearing mostly in cameo or non-speaking roles across various episodes and spin-off media.

title: Jimmy the Scumbag
text: Jimmy the Scumbag is A minor recurring criminal and small-time crook in Springfield. Jimmy the Scumbag is one of Springfield's many low-level criminals, often popping up in the background of the town's shadier happenings. He's a registered sex offender with a rap sheet that includes illegal telemarketing and bank robbery, frequently getting mixed up with other petty criminals like Snake. Despite his lawless lifestyle, he's shown a strange knack for show business, landing an acting gig in a local pudding commercial. He's easily duped, falling for a police scam involving free boats, showing he's not the sharpest crook in town. His travels have taken him as far as the slums of Brazil before returning to America, where he's been spotted among gun enthusiasts and mourning the closure of Moe's Tavern. Overall, Jimmy serves as a recurring background gag representing Springfield's colorful underbelly of small-time hoodlums. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Goofy
text: Goofy is Crossover Disney character occasionally appearing in Simpsons episodes and shorts. Goofy is the classic Walt Disney cartoon dog who makes occasional cameo appearances in the Simpsons universe rather than being a core cast member. He's referenced through old family photographs, offhand mentions, and even a bootleg costume worn by a street performer in Capital City. In non-canon material, he shows a friendly, somewhat lonely side, showing up to a party without a date and quickly bonding with Homer over drinks. His running gag in these appearances is being treated as a genuine celebrity within the Simpsons world, drawing crowds and mingling with other famous cartoon icons like Shrek and Pikachu. He's also shown to have a caring side, attempting to rescue Homer when he gets tangled in Christmas lights, and enjoying family-friendly outings like a Mother's Day trip with his own mother. Despite his brief screen time, he's treated as an established part of the show's broader pop-culture universe. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Chris Edgerly.

title: Jer
text: Jer is Employee (and later manager) at King Toot's Music Store, occasionally interacting with the Simpson family. Jer is a blue-haired store clerk who works at King Toot's Music Store, the shop where the Simpsons often go for musical instruments and supplies. He's shown as a stickler for closing times, refusing to reopen the store for Homer until reminded of a personal debt he owed to Moe. Despite this rigid streak, he proves capable of compassion when persuaded, ultimately helping Homer get Lisa a reed for her saxophone. He later plays a small role in the show's saxophone shop storyline, offering an inscription option on Lisa's new instrument. As a boss, he's shown firing an incompetent Dewey Largo and hiring Lisa in his place, though he leaves her alone to handle demanding customers on her first day. Jer is a minor recurring character whose appearances tie him closely to King Toot's and its ongoing role in Lisa's musical life. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Igner
text: Igner is Non-canon comic book character; one of Mom's sons from Futurama who crosses over into a Simpsons/Futurama comic story. Igner is a minor crossover character appearing in Simpsons/Futurama comic book stories, identified as one of the sons of the ruthless businesswoman Mom from Futurama. He shares family ties with his half-brothers Walt and Larry, and his father is revealed to be Professor Farnsworth. Igner's appearances are mostly comedic and humiliating, as he is shown being bullied by Dolph after the Springfield residents are teleported to New New York. He also suffers physical abuse from both his mother Mom and Mr. Burns during a corporate takeover subplot involving MomCorp. As a non-canon character, Igner exists purely within the pages of Bongo comics rather than the television series itself.

title: Jake
text: Jake is Elderly barber who owns Jake's Unisex Barbershop, a minor recurring Springfield character. Jake is the aging, none-too-skilled proprietor of Jake's Unisex Barbershop, a shop once known as Snippy Longstockings Barbershop. His eyesight seems to be failing him, which leads to some notably botched haircuts, including one he gave Bart that was cut far too short. He isn't entirely inept, however, as he managed to competently fix Lisa's hair after Bart ruined it with gum. Adding to his eccentric reputation, Jake reportedly pays his employees in hair rather than money, hinting at a loose grip on sound business practices or sanity. He has appeared sporadically across many seasons of the show, spanning from the Tracey Ullman shorts all the way to later seasons, showing his status as a long-running but minor background character. His voice was inspired by comedian Bob Elliott. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Stu Grimson (character)
text: Stu Grimson (character) is Real-life hockey player who appears as a coach at Top Goon Academy in The Simpsons. Stu Grimson, nicknamed "The Grim Reaper" from his hockey career, appears as himself in a guest role teaching at Top Goon Academy. He's introduced by the academy's head coach as someone with a deceptively calm appearance masking a fiercer nature. In his brief appearance, he takes on the role of an instructor, mentoring students such as Nelson Muntz in the ways of being a hockey enforcer. As a real-world figure voicing himself, he adds authenticity and a bit of novelty to the episode's sports-comedy premise. He's a minor, one-episode character whose entire purpose ties into the show's satire of hockey goon culture. Voiced by Himself.

title: Dr. Hillbilly
text: Dr. Hillbilly is A minor professional wrestler character who appears in a Texas Death Match in Springfield. Dr. Hillbilly is a masked professional wrestler who competes in a brutal Texas Death Match at the Springfield Grapplarium, facing off against his rival, The Iron Yuppie. The stakes of their bout are unusually high, with the losing wrestler set to be unmasked and killed inside the ring. He never speaks on screen, leaving his personality and motivations a mystery to viewers. It's left ambiguous whether he is meant to be seen as a hero or a villain in the match. Homer, watching the fight, roots against Dr. Hillbilly's opponent, hinting at some level of audience sympathy for him. Despite his brief appearance, he has become a memorable piece of Springfield's bizarre wrestling scene.

title: Chuck Garabedian
text: Chuck Garabedian is Minor recurring character; a savings seminar host who Homer and Marge sought financial advice from. Chuck Garabedian is a smooth-talking financial guru who runs a Mega-Savings Seminar promising to reveal secrets Wall Street doesn't want people to know. He boasts about acquiring absurdly overpriced or bizarre items for pennies, using dubious bargain-hunting logic as proof of his methods' success. His claims are exaggerated and comedic, poking fun at get-rich-quick seminar culture. Homer and Marge attend one of his seminars while trying to get their finances in order. Beyond his one seminar appearance, his image later shows up as part of the Springfield Speakers Bureau, suggesting he's a recognized (if questionable) public speaker in town. He's a minor one-off character used mainly for a satirical gag about financial self-help hucksters. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "12 savings secrets Wall Street won't tell you" | "squeeze every penny"
quotes: "12 savings secrets Wall Street won't tell you"
"squeeze every penny"

title: Saddam Hussein
text: Saddam Hussein is Real-world Iraqi leader depicted as a minor recurring character targeted for assassination in the show's storyline. Saddam Hussein appears in the show as a fictionalized version of the real-world Iraqi dictator, mostly referenced during Gulf War-era storylines. His most notable role comes when Erin, a soldier, is sent on a mission to assassinate him, only to be sidetracked by a romantic encounter with Krusty the Clown. When Krusty later discovers Erin aiming a rocket launcher at Saddam, he intervenes to save him, absurdly citing Saddam's importance to his own comedy act. Beyond this storyline, he's mentioned in passing through song lyrics, magazine headlines, and a non-canon Halloween special where superheroes beat him up. He never speaks in the show, functioning as a background historical figure and running punchline tied to real-world events rather than a fleshed-out character.

title: Angelina Jolie
text: Angelina Jolie is Real-world celebrity referenced/appearing as herself in Simpsons episodes. Angelina Jolie appears as a fictionalized version of the real-life actress and director within the Simpsons universe. She is mostly referenced in connection with her real-world ex-husband Brad Pitt, with the show repeatedly joking about their famous relationship, dubbed "Brangelina". She physically appears in "Homer the Whopper" and is trained by the character Lyle McCarthy alongside Pitt. In one of Bart's surreal coma dreams, she is imagined marrying Mr. Burns, a twist gruesome enough to send Waylon Smithers leaping into the power plant's cooling towers. She's also listed among Ned Flanders' roster of politically liberal celebrities, poking fun at her real-world reputation for humanitarian activism. In non-canon material, she shows up in a comic-style fantasy involving Lenny and other actresses.

title: Jericho
text: Jericho is A minor criminal character who ran a counterfeit jeans operation out of the Simpsons' garage. Jericho is a shady criminal figure best known for orchestrating a counterfeit jeans operation, partnering with Herman Hermann and using the Simpsons' garage as a front since it seemed like the last place police would look. His scheme fell apart when Marge, working as a police officer at the time, discovered and arrested him along with his men. He has a distinctive look, wearing a large fishing hat that hides his hair entirely, sunglasses, and a dark shirt similar to Grampa's style. He's rarely seen without a cigarette and is typically flanked by two guards, giving him an air of low-level menace. Despite his criminal downfall, he later resurfaced in a much more lighthearted context, participating in an attempt to build the world's tallest human pyramid. He hasn't been seen since his brief appearances tied to these two storylines. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Joe Gardner
text: Joe Gardner is Crossover character from Pixar's Soul, appearing in non-canon Simpsons specials. Joe Gardner is a crossover character brought into the Simpsons universe from the Pixar film Soul, marking him as non-canon to the main series continuity. He is a jazz pianist by profession, reflecting his defining trait from his original film. In his Simpsons appearances he acts mainly as a background or cameo figure rather than a driver of plot, appearing without any spoken dialogue. He shows up at a celebratory gathering at Moe's Tavern and later takes part in a family outing with his mother, Libba Gardner. His inclusion highlights the Simpsons' tendency to use special episodes for playful crossovers with other animated properties. Overall, he functions more as an easter egg for fans of Soul than as a developed character within the show.

title: Howard, Jr.
text: Howard, Jr. is Minor recurring character; owner of a Springfield flower shop. Howard, Jr. is a minor Springfield resident known for running a local flower shop and sporting distinctive half-moon glasses. He first appears in a wedding-themed episode, fitting his profession as a florist into the town's everyday commerce. In a non-canon appearance, he's shown as part of a shadowy board at the Springfield Retirement Castle that seems to have dark intentions toward the elderly residents. He reacts with disbelief when he learns that two ten-year-old kids built a robotic seal toy, only to be corrected that just one of them actually did the work. His role is small, functioning mostly as background texture for Springfield's cast of quirky business owners and townsfolk. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Hawkman
text: Hawkman is A DC Comics superhero referenced within the Simpsons universe, appearing in comics and as a costume, rather than a core cast member. Hawkman is not an original Simpsons character but a nod to the real-world DC Comics superhero of the same name, incorporated into the show's universe. He never physically appears as an active character in Springfield's storylines, instead surfacing as a pop-culture reference. He's mentioned by Ned Flanders as an alternative to Shiva when Apu panics during a chaotic car ride, showing how the show weaves comic book lore into everyday absurd situations. His image also appears on comic book covers within the show, tying into Springfield's fictional comics industry. Additionally, fans at the Comicalooza convention are shown dressed as Hawkman, reflecting the franchise's popularity among Springfield's nerd culture. Overall, Hawkman serves as a background easter egg rather than a fleshed-out character with his own personality or arc.

title: James Joyce
text: James Joyce is Real-world Irish novelist referenced/depicted in Springfield media and history. James Joyce appears in the show not as a character with dialogue but as a cultural reference woven into Springfield's world. A poster of him hangs in the Bookaccino's coffee shop, and a balloon in his likeness is featured in Capital City's Highbrow Artists Parade. His novel Ulysses is shown being read by locals during a Simpson family trip to Dublin, and Lisa at one point plans to explore his writing at the Springfield Public Library. In a flashback set a century earlier, he is depicted as part of a mob chasing a young turnip thief. He's also invoked by Kent Brockman in a news report comparing a refurbished Irish-themed district to the world of Finnegans Wake. As a non-speaking figure, his presence is purely symbolic, representing highbrow literary culture within the show's universe.

title: Harry Houdini
text: Harry Houdini is Real-world historical magician/escape artist referenced and briefly appearing in Simpsons canon and comics. Harry Houdini is depicted as the legendary real-world escape artist whose legacy echoes throughout Springfield lore. He is credited with teaching The Great Raymondo his signature milkcan escape trick, and his ghost later helps another magician, Cregg Demon, learn the same feat in a dream. His name has become a shorthand for slipping out of restraints, as seen when a sheriff jokes about baby Maggie freeing herself from handcuffs. In a non-canon comic story, he is brought back from the dead during a séance, hoping to share secrets of the afterlife, only to be dragged back to Heaven by fantastical flying animals. Another non-canon tale lists him among victims of a mysterious cursed black notebook. Though never voiced or given personality traits directly on the show, he functions as a recurring cultural reference tied to escape artistry and mystery. Notable quotes: "It looks like we got a teeny Houdini here."
quotes: "It looks like we got a teeny Houdini here."

title: Jim Jarmusch (character)
text: Jim Jarmusch (character) is Real-life filmmaker who appears as himself at the Sundance Film Festival in an episode of The Simpsons. Jim Jarmusch is portrayed as an independent film director attending the Sundance Film Festival. He boasts about being able to eat a whole onion without crying, though he actually cannot pull it off. He's shown to be working on an absurd sequel project, Cheaper by the Dozen 3, poking fun at his indie credentials by attaching him to a mainstream franchise. Despite his quirky bravado, he shows kindness by comforting Lisa after her film is poorly received by festival attendees. His appearance is a brief celebrity cameo tied to the show's satire of the indie film scene. Voiced by Jim Jarmusch.

title: Great son
text: Great son is Minor recurring background character; a young boy seen at Mr. Burns' company picnic. The great son is an unnamed child belonging to a background family that appears at Mr. Burns' company picnic in the show's early days. He's shown alongside his father, mother, and sister as a seemingly ordinary, well-adjusted family unit, which makes him take pity on Homer's chaotic life when he witnesses it firsthand. Despite looking put-together on the outside, his family later turns out to be dysfunctional themselves, seeking help at a family therapy center. He and his family panic and flee when the Simpsons inadvertently draw all the power from the therapy building. As a character, he exists mainly as a one-off visual gag family used to contrast with or mirror the Simpsons' own troubles, and he has made brief, wordless appearances in a handful of other early episodes. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Lois Griffin
text: Lois Griffin is Crossover character from Family Guy; wife of Peter Griffin, appearing in non-canon Simpsons crossover episodes. Lois Griffin is the matriarch of the Griffin family from Family Guy, brought into the Simpsons universe through a series of non-canon crossover appearances. She is depicted as a devoted wife to Peter and mother to Stewie, Chris, and Meg. In her appearances with the Simpsons, she ends up bonding with Marge after the Griffins' car is stolen near Springfield, showing her ability to connect with other put-upon sitcom moms. She's also been reimagined in stranger contexts, including as a mutant unleashed in a battle against a giant creature called The Glavin. Because these appearances exist outside the show's main continuity, Lois functions more as a novelty crossover figure than a regular part of the Simpsons cast. Her presence usually signals a special event episode or meta celebration of the show's history. Voiced by Alex Borstein.

title: Al Gumble
text: Al Gumble is Owner of Barney's Bowlarama and uncle of Barney Gumble. Al Gumble is a minor recurring character best known as the proprietor of Barney's Bowlarama, the bowling alley frequented by Homer and his league teammates. He briefly employed Homer during a period when Homer had quit the Power Plant, giving him a temporary job away from the plant. As a boss, he comes across as stingy, notably overcharging his employees for beer and forcing them to comically pour spilled beer back into bottles rather than waste it. Family ties run through the business, since he is the brother of the late Arnie Gumble and thus the uncle of the perpetually thirsty Barney Gumble. He mostly appears in flashbacks and background material rather than as an active present-day character, cementing his status as a peripheral figure tied to the bowling alley setting. His gray hair and general demeanor mark him as an older, no-nonsense small business owner in Springfield. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: beer "costs six dollars a bottle"
quotes: beer "costs six dollars a bottle"

title: Hera
text: Hera is Greek goddess of women and marriage, appearing in a non-canon Simpsons comic story, portrayed by Marge. Hera appears in the non-canon comic story 'Greek to Me' as the long-suffering wife of Zeus, frustrated by his habitual philandering and nights out at singles bars. When Zeus' illegitimate son Hercules arrives, she assigns him twelve labors as a form of punishment, though he only manages to complete ten. She later attempts to hand over the running of Olympus to Hercules, but quickly reverts to acting like a strict parent, imposing homework, chores, and curfews on him. This gives her a comedic role as a nagging, authority-figure type of goddess rather than a purely mythological one. In the show's tradition of mapping its cast onto other roles, Hera is portrayed by Marge Simpson.

title: Joey Joe
text: Joey Joe is A minor background character; a teenage entertainer featured in the Simpsons universe's media. Joey Joe is a minor, non-speaking character who exists only as a picture within the show's fictional world. He is depicted as a teenage entertainer whose popularity with girls is highlighted through his appearance on the cover of Non-Threatening Boys Magazine. His hair color is inconsistent between his two appearances, being blue in one and brown in the other, a small continuity quirk. Joey Joe never speaks or interacts directly with the main cast, existing purely as a background visual gag referencing teen idol culture. He represents the show's tendency to parody celebrity culture through fictional in-universe media. Despite his limited presence, he is recognized as a recurring picture-only character across multiple episodes.

title: Captain Hook
text: Captain Hook is Pirate captain villain from Peter Pan, referenced/crossover character in The Simpsons. Captain Hook is the famous pirate villain from Peter Pan, brought into the Simpsons universe mainly through crossover appearances rather than the main storylines. He first comes up as a name Bart considers, but ultimately gets wrong, when trying to recall the pirate from Treasure Island. He later appears in a non-canon context as a guest among Disney characters, showing up at Moe's Tavern for a Disney+ anniversary celebration. In the darker, villain-centric special featuring Disney Villain Land, he plays a genuinely menacing role, using his iconic hook to threaten Prince Charming and ultimately maiming him. He also joins a chorus of other Disney villains in a holiday-themed musical number. Overall, his role in the show is that of a recognizable pop-culture villain used for cameo and crossover humor rather than a developed character. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Jack (Bart's Dog Gets an "F")
text: Jack (Bart's Dog Gets an "F") is A fictional character within the show-within-a-show soap opera 'Search for the Sun', watched by various Simpsons characters. Jack is a melodramatic soap opera character from the fictional daytime drama Search for the Sun, a show frequently watched by residents of Springfield. His storyline revolves around a tangled romance with his lover Margarita, including a paternity dilemma and an attempted seduction despite her marriage. The show's absurd plotting often includes wild twists, such as a supposedly dead character named Father McGrath reappearing at a dramatic moment. Jack himself never appears as a 'real' figure in Springfield, existing only within the world of the TV screen the townspeople watch. Interestingly, the actor who portrays Jack crosses over into the real world of the show by joining other celebrities in a charity song. This blurring of fictional and 'real' Simpsons universe is part of the running gag around soap operas in the series. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Goobie-Woo
text: Goobie-Woo is A Happy Little Elves doll owned by Maggie Simpson, appearing as an imagined character in one of Homer's fantasy sequences. Goobie-Woo is a toy doll belonging to baby Maggie that comes to life only in Homer's imagination during a wild, slow-motion car crash. As Homer flies through the air after hitting a fire hydrant, the doll acts as a guide through his memories, helping him work through his anger and understand Marge's side of things. She accidentally reveals a bit too much family history, letting slip that Marge's late father disliked Homer and left Marge money specifically so she could leave him if needed. Despite this awkward slip, Homer ends up genuinely thankful to the doll once he lands. Goobie-Woo has a quirky, whimsical habit of narrating or singing about the story itself, even announcing the end of the episode. She later reappears briefly as a visual gag when Homer crashes his car again in a later episode. Voiced by Lizzo.

title: Jeff Goldblum (character)
text: Jeff Goldblum (character) is Non-canon parody character based on real-life actor Jeff Goldblum, appearing as a baby version of himself within a fictional in-universe TV show. This character is a whimsical, non-canon take on actor Jeff Goldblum, reimagined as an infant starring in his own Disney television series called The World According to Baby Jeff Goldblum. He exists mainly as a background joke rather than a fully developed character, appearing briefly in the show's universe as a piece of media Lisa or other characters might watch. His fame is referenced elsewhere in a gag where a sign at Geriatric Park humorously declares the area 'Now Goldblum-Free,' poking fun at the real actor's frequent appearances in blockbuster films. The character has no established personality traits beyond being a baby version of a recognizable celebrity, making him purely a satirical cameo. He has been dubbed by different voice actors internationally, suggesting the joke was considered notable enough to localize. Overall, he serves as a quick, absurdist nod to pop culture rather than a substantive figure in Springfield's world. Voiced by Matthew Friend.

title: Agatha Harkness
text: Agatha Harkness is Non-canon Marvel Comics crossover character/costume worn by Selma Bouvier as part of the Springfield Avengers. Agatha Harkness is a non-canon crossover character borrowed from Marvel Comics, appearing in Simpsons specials as a costume Selma Bouvier wears while part of the Springfield Avengers superhero group. She has no spoken lines in her appearances, functioning purely as a visual gag and pop-culture reference. In one special she's shown flying around Springfield Town Square alongside Patty and Selma, only to later be attacked by them with magic. Her portrayal nods to her comic and TV counterpart's dual nature as both hero and villain, referencing her role in WandaVision and the Agatha All Along miniseries. As a non-speaking, adult character, she exists mainly as an Easter egg for Marvel fans within the Simpsons universe.

title: Planet Jackson
text: Planet Jackson is Fictional character from the in-universe TV show "Planet Jackson and the Earth Brigade", appearing as a toy in the actual Simpsons universe. Planet Jackson isn't a real character in Springfield but rather the star of a cartoon show within the Simpsons universe, marketed heavily through action figures and merchandise. He first turns up as a talking doll that gets activated when Maggie tosses it across a pile of toys. The character is clearly modeled after Captain Planet, poking fun at eco-hero cartoons and their tie-in merchandising. His presence in the show is limited to brief toy appearances rather than any real screen time as an actual character. Homer even picks up a Planet Jackson toy for Milhouse during a shopping trip, showing how pervasive the toy line is in Springfield. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Planet power!
quotes: Planet power!

title: Andrew Johnson
text: Andrew Johnson is Real-life 17th President of the United States, referenced briefly in the show. Andrew Johnson appears in the Simpsons universe as a historical footnote rather than a fleshed-out character. He is depicted as the 17th U.S. President who took office after Abraham Lincoln's assassination. His only on-screen presence is a picture shown to Bart in a history book, before Bart's attention shifts to Theodore Roosevelt. He later appears again as an animatronic figure in a Hall of Vice Presidents at a theme park. He has no dialogue and functions purely as a background historical reference in the show.

title: Hercules (Greek mythology)
text: Hercules (Greek mythology) is Greek mythological hero, son of Zeus, referenced in various Simpsons stories and parodies. Hercules is a legendary figure from Greek mythology who appears in the show mainly through stories, films, and parodies created by the Simpsons characters rather than as a consistent character himself. He's depicted as immensely strong, most famously in Homer's retelling of the tale where he pulls a thorn from a lion's paw and is rewarded with riches. He's also the subject of a fictional in-universe film, 'The Erotic Adventures of Hercules,' starring Troy McClure, and is portrayed by Ned Flanders in a homemade movie about the ancient Olympics. In a non-canon storyline, he undertakes clever, comedic shortcuts to complete his twelve labors for Hera, such as tricking a rich Greek into valuing dung over gold and outsourcing the capture of dangerous creatures to an animal control agency. His mythological role as Zeus's illegitimate son and his complicated relationship with Hera are played for comedic effect in these parodies. Overall, Hercules functions less as a recurring character and more as a flexible mythological reference used for various jokes and homages throughout the series. Voiced by Phil Hartman.

title: Orion Hughes
text: Orion Hughes is Owner of the Slipreme clothing brand and cloned son of celebrity Darius Hughes; became a friend of Bart's. Orion Hughes is a young actor, singer, producer, and fashion mogul who runs the trendy clothing brand Slipreme. He was secretly created as a clone from his father Darius Hughes's blood, a fact Darius hid from him until well into their relationship. Despite owning a skateboarding-themed brand, Orion is oddly unskilled at skateboarding himself, which becomes a bonding point when Bart teaches him. He's image-conscious and easily rattled, suffering an anxious breakdown when his brand risks becoming uncool by attracting middle-aged dads instead of kids. Orion is generally kind-hearted, apologizing sincerely to Bart after his employees mistreated him and going on to design a sneaker collaboration with him. His storyline touches on themes of celebrity cloning and the fragile, image-driven nature of youth culture branding. Voiced by The Weeknd.

title: Increase
text: Increase is A minor recurring elderly resident of the Retirement Castle. Increase is an elderly background character who lives out his days at the Retirement Castle alongside other seniors like Jasper and Hans Moleman. He's mostly seen napping or shuffling about, embodying the stereotype of the sleepy, cranky old man. His most notable moment comes when he joins a group of fed-up seniors who successfully push for a citywide curfew to stop noisy kids and adults from disturbing their rest. Ironically, this backfires on him personally when his pill can ends up kicked into the street, leaving him to chase after it. He has almost no dialogue in the show itself, existing mainly as a face in the retirement home crowd. Notably, his voice is identical to that of the Old Jewish Man, both performed by Hank Azaria. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Agent Johnson
text: Agent Johnson is An FBI agent who appears in the episode "The Trouble with Trillions". Agent Johnson is a federal agent working for the FBI, first appearing during an episode centered on tax evasion and espionage antics. Alongside his partner, Agent Miller, he recruits Homer Simpson to help carry out a covert assignment, using the threat of prison time for tax evasion as leverage. His role is largely functional, representing government authority within the show's satire of bureaucracy and law enforcement. Beyond his one canonical appearance, he has shown up in non-canon material, including dialogue roles in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. He isn't fleshed out with much personal history or distinct comedic quirks, serving mainly as a plot device to push Homer into an unusual mission. His presence highlights the show's recurring theme of ordinary citizens being roped into absurd governmental schemes. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: International Olympic Committee chairman
text: International Olympic Committee chairman is Chairman of the International Olympic Committee who briefly awards Springfield the right to host the Olympics. This gruff, authoritative official presides over the International Olympic Committee's deliberations on which city should host the games. He is swayed by a heartfelt letter from a Springfield girl and unilaterally overrules the objecting representatives to award the town the Olympics, showing he answers to no one but himself. During his inspection visit, he is notably impressed by Springfield's sewer system, a small comedic detail highlighting his oddly specific priorities. However, his goodwill evaporates after Bart's offensive comedy routine insults the visiting dignitaries, leading him to pull the Olympics from Springfield entirely. He appears only in one episode, making him a minor but memorable one-off authority figure whose decisions have outsized consequences for the town. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Jack the Ripper
text: Jack the Ripper is Historical real-world serial killer referenced in The Simpsons universe, not an original character. Jack the Ripper is the infamous unidentified murderer who terrorized Whitechapel, London in 1888, and he appears in the show only as a reference point rather than a fleshed-out character. His legend surfaces during a Victorian-era fantasy sequence involving Bart, Lisa, Maggie, and Shary Bobbins, where a newsboy hawks papers about his latest crime. He's also brought up as a trivia question at Moe's Tavern, prompting Homer to confidently but dubiously name a suspect. In another episode, he's listed among historical figures rumored to have known the mysterious entity called The Answer. Beyond these brief mentions, he also appears in a non-canon capacity in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out as a villain character. Overall, he functions as a piece of dark historical trivia woven into the show's satirical and whimsical storytelling. Notable quotes: Extra! Extra! Ripper strikes in Whitechapel! | The Queen's private surgeon.
quotes: Extra! Extra! Ripper strikes in Whitechapel!
The Queen's private surgeon.

title: Reverend Kartawijaya
text: Reverend Kartawijaya is A minor recurring character; a Protestant minister from Indonesia who once spoke at the First Church of Springfield. Reverend Kartawijaya is a minister hailing from Indonesia who converted to Protestant Christianity after having been raised Islamic. His main claim to fame within the show is a guest appearance at Springfield's First Church, where he shared a parable-like story with the congregation about a village boy named Sumadi who refused to attend church. Little else is known about his personality or daily life, as he appears only briefly and is not a regular fixture in Springfield. His inclusion highlights the show's occasional forays into showcasing diverse, international religious figures. He is a minor character who has made only a couple of appearances in the series. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Cliff Huxtable
text: Cliff Huxtable is Crossover character from The Cosby Show, appearing on TV screens within The Simpsons. Cliff Huxtable is a parody appearance of the beloved sitcom father from The Cosby Show, popping up as a show-within-a-show reference for the Simpson family. He first appears on the Simpsons' television during the final broadcast of his own series, prompting Homer and Bart to reflect on when a show should end. Later, he shows up in a flashback tied to Bleeding Gums Murphy's backstory, where he introduces the jazz musician to his TV children as a random 'grandpa' figure. In that scene, he dominates the conversation with a rambling monologue comparing jazz to popular products like Jell-O Pudding Pops and New Coke, while his children remain bored and dismissive. The joke plays on his reputation as an overly preachy, product-endorsing father figure, all while Murphy stands silently in the background. He never interacts directly with any Simpsons characters, existing purely as a TV-within-TV gag. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: King of Sweden
text: King of Sweden is Minor character; the king of Sweden who appears in a Homer-imagined fantasy sequence and is later tied to Waylon Smithers, Jr. in a non-canon storyline. The King of Sweden is a minor figure who exists mostly within a fantasy sequence imagined by Homer, where he presents an adult Lisa with a Nobel Prize for kickboxing, only to be knocked out by her front kick. His reign is said to have ended in chaos, as having no heirs led to lawlessness and rebellion after his death. In a non-canon storyline, it's revealed he may have fathered an illegitimate son, leading Waylon Smithers, Jr. to briefly believe he could become the future king of Sweden. A DNA test later disproves this claim, though it's implied Smithers actually is the king's secret heir who chooses to keep the truth hidden. Overall, the character serves as a comedic device tied to royal absurdity and mistaken identity rather than a fully developed personality.

title: Giuseppe Granfinali
text: Giuseppe Granfinali is Retired Italian fireworks pyrotechnic that Homer idolized. Giuseppe Granfinali is an elderly Italian man known for his past career as a skilled fireworks pyrotechnic. Homer admired him and his dazzling firework displays, especially after Mona Simpson left. When Springfield's official fireworks show got cancelled due to budget issues, Homer sought out Giuseppe to put on a replacement display, hoping to recapture that childhood wonder. Unfortunately, the resulting show didn't go as planned, leading to chaos. Giuseppe also appears as a collectible character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, tied to its 4th of July content. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Mother Gothel
text: Mother Gothel is Non-canon Disney crossover character appearing in Simpsons specials. Mother Gothel is a Disney villain character from the Tangled franchise who makes a crossover appearance in The Simpsons universe. She is depicted as the adoptive mother of Rapunzel, maintaining her original Disney lore within this non-canon context. Her appearances are brief and non-speaking, fitting into larger ensemble scenes involving other Disney characters. She joins a Mother's Day-themed outing to a Disney-branded amusement location alongside her adoptive daughter. She also appears among a gathering of Disney villains performing a holiday song. As a non-canon figure, she exists purely for crossover and novelty purposes rather than as part of the core Simpsons cast.

title: Geoffrey
text: Geoffrey is Boyfriend of school music teacher Dewey Largo. Geoffrey is a grey-haired, older gentleman who is in a long-term relationship with Springfield Elementary's music teacher, Dewey Largo. He tends to be a bit dismissive or teasing toward Dewey, such as mocking him for having recurring nightmares, yet he also supports him through important moments like the school concert. He's shown to have modern hobbies like browsing Pinterest and enjoys leisure activities such as cruises and podcast recordings. Their relationship has had rocky moments, including a scene where Dewey threatens to kick him out over their dog's name, though they clearly remain devoted to one another. Geoffrey appears mostly in a domestic, supportive role, popping up in the background of various Simpsons-related events tied to Dewey's life. He represents one of the show's recurring same-sex couples. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Jack (The Wife Aquatic)
text: Jack (The Wife Aquatic) is Captain of the Rotting Pelican and resident of Barnacle Bay, featured in the episode "The Wife Aquatic". Jack is a weathered sea captain who leads a crew fishing for the once-plentiful Yum-Yum Fish out of the fading tourist town of Barnacle Bay. He's practical and a bit gruff, willing to put newcomers like Homer to work aboard his ship to pay off debts. He has an odd physical quirk where his trick knee acts up as a sign of impending danger, which proves accurate during a violent storm. Despite the perilous nature of his job, he shows a rough sense of mercy, planning to spare a stowaway from a slow drowning death. After his ship sinks and he's presumed dead, he survives and is rescued, only to return home and pivot the town's economy toward deforestation instead of fishing, seemingly ignoring warnings about overfishing. His arc highlights a cycle of environmental exploitation without much reflection on the consequences. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Homer's kidnappers
text: Homer's kidnappers is Minor antagonists who kidnapped Homer during the Simpson family's trip to Brazil. This pair of kidnappers snatched Homer off the street in Brazil, holding him for ransom while his family scrambled to come up with the money. One of them held Homer at gunpoint in a taxi before Bart managed to escape, leading the criminals to haul Homer via boat through the Amazon Rainforest to a remote hideaway. There, Homer was strapped to a table, and in a running gag typical of the show's absurdist humor, he ended up eating food worth more than the ransom the family had raised. The situation was resolved when the family secured funds from Ronaldo and made a dramatic cable car exchange atop Sugarloaf Mountain. Interestingly, one of the kidnappers who drove the taxi seems to have relocated afterward, later popping up working as a taxi driver in Springfield itself, suggesting an odd continuity where former criminals casually reappear in mundane roles. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Mr. Incredible
text: Mr. Incredible is A superhero from The Incredibles film franchise, referenced in the Simpsons comics as a costume worn by Comic Book Guy. Mr. Incredible isn't a native Simpsons character but rather a crossover figure from the Pixar film series The Incredibles. In the world of the Simpsons comics, he appears only as a costume that Comic Book Guy wears to a science-fiction convention. He has no dialogue or independent storyline within this universe, existing purely as a nod to the popular animated superhero franchise. His family from the source material, including his wife Helen and children Violet, Dash, and Jack-Jack, is listed as background context rather than actively featured. As a non-speaking character, his inclusion is more of an easter egg or pop-culture reference than a fleshed-out character in the Simpsons canon.

title: Impervo the Painless
text: Impervo the Painless is A minor carnival freak performer who appears at Hullabalooza and later joins a traveling carnival. Impervo the Painless is a sideshow performer whose claim to fame is hammering nails up his nose without apparent pain, at least in theory. Despite his stage name, he's not actually invulnerable, as shown by a couple of unfortunate on-the-job injuries. He first appears as a novelty act at the Hullabalooza festival, where he introduces the band Cypress Hill after a mishap with his own routine. He later resurfaces working for a different, more low-rent traveling carnival, where he becomes an incidental victim of Bart's carelessness. His brief appearances make him a minor running gag about carnival acts not living up to their tough-guy names. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Guy Incognito
text: Guy Incognito is A minor one-time character who is Homer Simpson's exact double, appearing in the episode "Fear of Flying". Guy Incognito is a mysterious stranger who happens to be identical to Homer Simpson in every way except for a mustache, a British accent, and sharper fashion sense. His unlucky resemblance to Homer causes him to be mistaken for the troublesome barfly the moment he steps into Moe's Tavern. Despite his polite manner and clear attempt to distinguish himself by name, no one believes he isn't Homer in disguise, leading to a comedic case of mistaken identity. The joke of his name is that "Guy Incognito" essentially just means "unknown person in disguise," which ironically convinces Moe that it's proof he's really Homer. He gets beaten up and thrown out of the bar as a result of the confusion, never getting the chance to clear his name. Homer himself briefly glimpses his uncanny double on the street but is quickly distracted before he can process the encounter. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Homer? Who is Homer? My name is Guy Incognito. | Get out of here, Homer.
quotes: Homer? Who is Homer? My name is Guy Incognito.
Get out of here, Homer.

title: Henry (Smart and Smarter)
text: Henry (Smart and Smarter) is Interviewer and gatekeeper for Miss Wickerbottom's Pre-Nursery School, appearing in a Season 15 episode. Henry is the stern gatekeeper who decides which babies are worthy of admission into an elite pre-nursery school, testing them for intelligence before letting them in. He initially rejects Maggie for being unable to speak, only to later reverse course when Lisa proves her baby sister is remarkably smart. His strict, judgmental demeanor mirrors that of his real-life inspiration, and he shows no hesitation in revoking Maggie's acceptance once he suspects the test results were rigged. Henry is largely humorless and businesslike, treating infant admissions with the same harsh scrutiny of a talent show judge. His visual design and personality were intentionally modeled after Simon Cowell, who also voices him. The character exists mainly as a one-episode parody figure rather than a recurring presence in the Simpson family's world. Voiced by Simon Cowell.

title: Harper Jambowski
text: Harper Jambowski is A wealthy student at Springfield Elementary and a brief friend of Lisa Simpson. Harper Jambowski is a rich, generous-seeming girl who joins Lisa's Magic Club and quickly develops an intense friendship with her. She has a habit of showering Lisa with expensive gifts, but she does this less out of true kindness and more out of a need to control the relationship, never letting Lisa make her own choices. Her overbearing generosity becomes suffocating, and the friendship falls apart when Lisa refuses one gift too many. Harper's family wealth and private island lifestyle set her apart from the other kids at school, and her father's own entanglement with the Simpsons mirrors her clingy dynamic with Lisa. She largely disappears from the show after this arc, only reappearing in an archival capacity. Voiced by Kristen Bell.

title: Gary the Unicorn
text: Gary the Unicorn is A minor non-canon character appearing in Marge's dream during a Garden of Eden segment. Gary the Unicorn is a fantastical creature who exists within a dream sequence imagined by Marge, set in the Garden of Eden. He assists Adam in digging a tunnel meant to help Eve sneak back into the garden, showing a helpful and loyal nature. Tragically, his heroics come at a cost, as he dies right after completing the tunnel, making him something of a sacrificial figure in the story. His death inadvertently causes God's wrath to fall upon Adam and Eve, adding a darkly comic twist to the biblical parody. Gary later reappears in a non-canon capacity within The Simpsons: Tapped Out video game, tied to a heaven-themed storyline. Overall, he's a small but memorable piece of the show's surreal humor and biblical satire. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Gummy Joe
text: Gummy Joe is A minor worker at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. Gummy Joe is an elderly, background employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, notable mainly for his lack of teeth. He has lost every tooth except one, which he affectionately calls 'Chomper,' and he uses it as a makeshift tool to open cans. That single remaining tooth is only preserved thanks to the plant's dental plan, a small joke about the low quality of Mr. Burns' employee benefits. He briefly gained a bit of odd celebrity by appearing on a bubble gum package under the ironic nickname 'Toothless Joe.' Though he's a very minor character, he's popped up in supplementary media like The Simpsons: Tapped Out and been referenced in fan letters imagining bigger comedic roles for him. Overall, he's a small recurring gag character defined almost entirely by his dental situation. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Joey (mafia)
text: Joey (mafia) is A mobster working for Fat Tony in the Springfield Mafia. Joey is a low-level Springfield mobster identifiable by a distinctive scar on his cheek. He works under Fat Tony at the Legitimate Businessman's Social Club alongside fellow goons Legs and Louie. He's been present for several key mafia moments, including Bart's stint as an underage bartender at the club. Beyond typical criminal duties, Joey has shown up in unexpected contexts, such as teaching a class at Krusty's Clown College where he encouraged students to rob children after shows. He's a durable background character who has survived explosions and shifting mafia allegiances, at one point defecting to the rival Calabresi family before returning to Fat Tony's fold. Despite his criminal profession, he participates in oddly wholesome community events like a record-setting human pyramid attempt. Voiced by Phil Hartman ("Bart the Murderer"); Dan Castellaneta ("Homie the Clown").

title: Andy Hamilton
text: Andy Hamilton is Former Springfield Elementary prankster turned writer for Krusty the Clown. Andy Hamilton is a onetime legendary prankster from Springfield Elementary School whose infamous stunt against Principal Skinner became local lore. After leaving school, he fell into a slump, becoming unemployed and stuck living with his mother, losing his old mischievous spark. Bart Simpson takes an interest in reviving Andy's confidence, helping him land a job working for Krusty the Clown. Andy struggles at first, quitting after being pushed around by his demanding boss, but eventually returns and finds his footing as a writer. His subplot doubles as a coming-of-age moment, with Bart urging him to mature rather than cling to his prankster glory days. Andy's personal life includes a girlfriend in the studio's makeup department, adding a lighthearted romantic note to his otherwise awkward, arrested-development characterization. Voiced by Jonah Hill.

title: Hoppy
text: Hoppy is A fictional cartoon animal from The Flintstones that appears as a crossover reference in The Simpsons. Hoppy is a green pet 'hopparoo' belonging to Barney Rubble within the fictional universe of The Flintstones, a show that exists within The Simpsons' world. He never actually appears as a living character in Springfield, but rather shows up as an image, referenced on merchandise-like items within episodes. His presence is purely a nod to crossover fandom, appearing on a toy phone and later on a map, without any dialogue or personality development. As a non-speaking, picture-only character, Hoppy exists solely as a background easter egg for fans of both animated franchises. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent parody and homage to other classic cartoons.

title: Lady Justice
text: Lady Justice is A statue personifying justice, located at the Springfield County Courthouse. Lady Justice is not a living character but a statue representing the abstract concept of justice, standing outside the Springfield County Courthouse. She becomes part of a minor scandal when Mr. Burns, after being fined for illegally dumping nuclear waste in Springfield Park, uses his connections to have the statue removed and taken as a kind of trophy or bribe-related favor. The incident is memorialized in a photo in the Springfield Shopper showing Smithers hauling the statue away. As a non-speaking, inanimate object, she has no personality of her own, but her removal serves as a running visual gag about corruption and the misuse of civic authority in Springfield. She later reappears as a purchasable decoration in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out.

title: Jaws
text: Jaws is A James Bond villain henchman character imagined/referenced within The Simpsons. Jaws is a non-canon crossover character based on the iconic James Bond henchman from the film franchise. In the Simpsons universe, he appears mainly as a figment of imagination or in archive/deleted material rather than as a fully integrated part of the show's world. He's depicted alongside fellow Bond villains Ernst Stavro Blofeld and Oddjob, reinforcing his role as a stock villain archetype. In one non-canon appearance, he's shown participating in a poker game at Mr. Burns' Casino with other supervillains, ganging up on a cheated gambler. Jaws himself is a silent, non-speaking presence in the show, existing purely as a nod to Bond film lore rather than developing any personality of his own. His inclusion is largely played for reference humor rather than serving any real narrative purpose in Springfield.

title: Melody Juniper
text: Melody Juniper is Minor character; daughter of substitute music teacher Calliope Juniper, briefly a love interest of Bart Simpson. Melody Juniper is a nine-year-old student at Springfield Elementary School who briefly becomes entangled in her mother's romantic pursuits when Principal Skinner arranges for Bart to date her. She quickly grows fond of Bart, going so far as to sketch drawings of the two of them together, showing a sweet, earnest, and somewhat naive personality. Unfortunately for her, Bart doesn't share her feelings and eventually tells her he isn't interested in a relationship. This rejection devastates Melody emotionally, leading her and her mother to leave Springfield altogether. Her brief appearance ties her fate directly to Bart's often awkward and reluctant romantic entanglements, a recurring theme for his character. Voiced by Alyson Hannigan.

title: Green Lantern
text: Green Lantern is A DC Comics superhero referenced within the Simpsons universe, mainly through Comic Book Guy's fandom and costumes. Green Lantern is not an original Simpsons character but a real-world DC superhero who pops up as a pop-culture reference throughout the show. He's most closely associated with Comic Book Guy, who owns Green Lantern merchandise and once dressed as him for Halloween. The character also briefly crosses Bart's mind when he's brainstorming his own superhero identity, only for Bart to realize Green Lantern is already taken. Green Lantern's name gets used for a joke about the sound effect of him being thrown into acid by his nemesis Sinestro. In non-canon material, Ralph Wiggum also cosplays as the character for Halloween. Overall, he functions as a running nerd-culture gag rather than a fleshed-out character in the show.

title: Houseboy
text: Houseboy is Milhouse Van Houten's comic-book superhero alter-ego, serving as sidekick to Bartman. Houseboy is a noncanonical superhero identity adopted by Milhouse within the Simpsons comic book universe, existing as the loyal sidekick to Bartman. True to Milhouse's character, Houseboy plays a supporting role rather than taking center stage, backing up his more famous partner in various heroic exploits. He has helped thwart the schemes of the Brotherhood of the Bullies alongside Bartman, showing that even in costume, the duo faces familiar Springfield threats. In a larger team-up, Houseboy joined forces with Bartman, Shelbyville's Fighting Owl, and Four-Eyes to take down the villainous Squirrel Girl. As a comic-exclusive character, Houseboy appears across numerous Simpsons Comics, Bartman, Bart Simpson, and Simpsons Super Spectacular issues, cementing his place as a recurring but minor fixture of the franchise's print media side stories.

title: Mr. Johnson
text: Mr. Johnson is Physical Education (gym) teacher at Springfield Elementary School. Mr. Johnson is a minor recurring faculty member at Springfield Elementary, known specifically for teaching gym class. He seems to take his rope-climbing curriculum quite seriously, insisting it has real-world value even when his students clearly disagree. His class is dreaded enough that students compare it unfavorably to actual hardship and peril. Despite his stern insistence on the usefulness of his lessons, the kids remain unconvinced, poking fun at his teaching in a mild running joke. He appears only briefly across a few episodes, mostly as background faculty, but also shows up socially outside school, attending a student's birthday party. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: In the real world, rope-climbing skills are vital.
quotes: In the real world, rope-climbing skills are vital.

title: Homer's clones
text: Homer's clones is Non-canon duplicates of Homer Simpson created via a magic hammock in a Treehouse of Horror segment. These clones came into existence after Homer bought a magical hammock that could duplicate whoever slept in it. True to his lazy nature, Homer churned out an army of copies of himself to handle his chores instead of doing them himself. When he grew tired of them, he tossed the clones and the hammock into a cornfield, only for them to keep multiplying on their own and eventually spiral out of control, consuming resources across Springfield. The army had to intervene, using a clever trick involving giant doughnuts to lure the clones off a cliff to their doom. The twist ending reveals that the real Homer was accidentally caught up in the destruction, leaving one of the clones to take his place unnoticed. As an Easter egg, the crowd of clones includes a visual nod to Homer's original crude design from the Ullman shorts, plus a cameo appearance by Peter Griffin from Family Guy. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Goose Gladwell
text: Goose Gladwell is Owner of Goose's Gags and Gifts, a joke shop chain, and business associate of Bart Simpson. Goose Gladwell is a quirky novelty store owner who first crosses paths with Bart when he accidentally runs him over with his car at a novelty expo, then decides to sell Bart's T-shirt designs in his stores. Despite his goofy, magician-like persona, he turns out to be a shrewd businessman, using legal tricks to cut Bart out of profits when he sells the shirt line to Disney. His eccentric habits include sneaking around unnoticed, pulling props like confetti and flowers seemingly from nowhere, and vanishing through a hidden trapdoor in his shop. He claims a dark past as a Green Beret who served in Vietnam, hinting that his wartime experiences left him a bit unhinged. He's clearly modeled after Willy Wonka, blending whimsy with a hidden ruthless streak. He later appears among the townsfolk at a pollution meeting and as a member of a local bowling team, showing he's a recurring fixture of Springfield life. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Disney Princess Homer
text: Disney Princess Homer is An alternate-universe, female version of Homer Simpson, styled as a Disney princess. Disney Princess Homer is one of many alternate versions of Homer pulled into the main Simpsons universe through a multiverse mishap at the Nuclear Power Plant. She appears as a whimsical mashup of classic Disney princesses, complete with a blue gown, a pumpkin carriage, and a fairy godmother wand. Despite her elegant appearance, she joins the other Homers in classic Homer-style chaos, gorging on non-salad food and wrecking a bowling alley alongside her counterparts. She's shown to have a musical streak, breaking into song to explain the group's bizarre predicament. When the alternate Homers must return to their home universes or perish, she ends up in a magical battle against an evil counterpart of Mr. Burns known as Maleficent Burns, ultimately succumbing to a poisoned drink and falling into a fairy-tale-style sleeping death. She serves as a parody blending Cinderella and Snow White into the Homer mold. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Ricky Gervais (character)
text: Ricky Gervais (character) is Real-life celebrity guest character appearing as himself in The Simpsons. This character is a self-parody of comedian Ricky Gervais, who appears as a guest character playing himself. He is shown attending the Golden Globes, where he pulls a small prank involving a tip for a bartender, sneaking the money back after the bartender isn't looking. In another scene, he mistakenly believes he is networking with director Ridley Scott, becoming overly emotional in hopes of landing a film role, only to grow annoyed upon learning the man is merely a seat filler. He is also referenced through a promo for his real-life mockumentary series, rendered in that show's distinctive animation style. Overall, the character serves as a comedic cameo poking fun at celebrity self-importance and awkward Hollywood social situations. Voiced by Ricky Gervais (Himself).

title: Steve Johnson
text: Steve Johnson is A Shinigami (god of death) who appears to Lisa Simpson in a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, parodying Death Note. Steve Johnson is a death god who unleashes the Death Tome, a supernatural book capable of killing anyone whose name is written in it, upon the world. He becomes visible only to Lisa Simpson after she gains possession of the book, acting as her guide and commentator as she experiments with its deadly power. Though initially bemused by how quickly Lisa embraces killing, he offers matter-of-fact advice, such as needing a person's full name for the tome to work. His presence highlights Lisa's gradual corruption, as he calmly observes her escalating body count without much moral objection. Ultimately, his role ends when Lisa, realizing the book has twisted her, kills him with space junk to break free of the tome's influence. Ironically, his death only transforms Lisa into the new Shinigami, continuing the cycle. The character is a clear parody of Ryuk from the anime/manga Death Note. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Ice Bishop of Beverly Hills
text: Ice Bishop of Beverly Hills is A fictional character within the show-within-a-show 'Ice World: Los Angeles', appearing on TV in the Simpsons universe. The Ice Bishop of Beverly Hills is a minor fictional figure who exists inside a movie or program called Ice World: Los Angeles, watched by characters within The Simpsons itself. He is depicted delivering a lengthy, self-important speech to his people in Los Angeles, suggesting a pompous or ceremonial personality typical of a religious or civic leader. His speech is cut short when another character, portrayed by guest star Tom Skerritt, interrupts him, implying his role is more comedic filler than significant plot. He later resurfaces in a non-canon capacity as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, categorized among its Dystopian Fighters. His icy blue hair ties into his 'Ice Bishop' title and the frosty, dystopian aesthetic of that game content. Overall, he's a background gag character rather than a core member of the Simpsons cast. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: King Homer (character)
text: King Homer (character) is A giant-ape parody version of Homer Simpson, appearing in Grampa's King Kong-style story during a Treehouse of Horror segment. King Homer is a non-canon, larger-than-life version of Homer Simpson reimagined as a giant black ape in the style of King Kong. He appears within a story Grampa tells during a Halloween gathering at the Simpson family home, casting Homer in the role of the legendary movie monster. The character is a direct parody of the classic 1933 King Kong film, complete with black-and-white styled scenes to match that era's aesthetic. Despite his brief appearance, King Homer became memorable enough to be turned into a physical action figure as part of a Simpsons toy line. He has also popped up in later years as a recurring visual gag, showing up in title screen gags and merchandise, and even inspiring fan costumes at conventions. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: The Human Fly
text: The Human Fly is Minor recurring Springfield resident known for climbing skyscrapers in a fly costume to attract attention. The Human Fly is the alter ego of Jerry Patton, a disgruntled postal worker who tries to gain fame by donning a fly costume and scaling the tallest building in Springfield. His stunt goes completely unnoticed, leaving him bitter and disillusioned, which causes him to abandon his mail route and start burying letters in his backyard instead of delivering them. He resurfaces during a Be Sharps reunion performance, once again scaling a skyscraper while everyone's attention is fixated elsewhere. He's a small, quirky example of the show's background gag characters who never quite achieve the recognition they crave. In non-canon comic material, he continues his climbing routine, quipping sarcastically at a flying Bart Simpson. He also has a bit of trivia tying him to Bumblebee Man, having unsuccessfully auditioned for that role. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Hellooo, Human Fly here. Come on, I spent all night dying my underwear! | Sheesh! Why not use the elevator, kid?
quotes: Hellooo, Human Fly here. Come on, I spent all night dying my underwear!
Sheesh! Why not use the elevator, kid?

title: Mike Jambowski
text: Mike Jambowski is Wealthy businessman, CEO of J-Cloud Digital Storage Solutions and owner of Springfield Sports Arena; briefly a friend of Homer's. Mike Jambowski is a rich entrepreneur who briefly enters the Simpsons' orbit due to his wealth and status. He first appears inviting Lisa and Homer to a concert at his own Springfield Sports Arena, alongside his daughter Harper. Homer quickly latches onto him as a friend, seemingly drawn more to his money than his personality, and the two families end up vacationing together on the Jambowskis' private island. That friendship falls apart after Lisa becomes upset over how Harper mistreats her pets, causing a rift between Homer and Mike. Despite the falling out, Mike continues to appear in Springfield's upper-crust social scene, showing up at a charity event and a high-end auction house bidding on rare wine once owned by Napoleon Bonaparte. He functions mainly as a symbol of shallow wealth and status-driven friendships within the show's satire of the rich. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: German scientist
text: German scientist is Minor recurring background character, an unnamed German scientist who appears in various expert or professional roles. This nameless German scientist is a minor recurring figure who pops up in a handful of expert or authority roles throughout the series. He first appears as part of a scientific team, alongside Marvin Monroe and a French scientist, sent to investigate a supposed Bigfoot sighting, and he can't quite decide if the creature is a lowly human or a magnificent beast. He later resurfaces in a completely different profession as the head doctor at the mental institution New Bedlam, showing the show's tendency to recycle background character designs for various unrelated jobs. He also makes an appearance during a record-breaking attempt to build the world's tallest human pyramid. Consistent with many of Springfield's incidental characters, he has no real personality arc or defining traits beyond his German accent and scientific/professional demeanor, existing mainly as background flavor voiced by Harry Shearer. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Hedonismbot
text: Hedonismbot is A crossover robot character from Futurama's New New York who appears in The Simpsons universe. Hedonismbot is a robot crossover character originally from Futurama's New New York, brought into The Simpsons universe through a crossover episode. True to his name, he embraces indulgence and excess, famously choosing to stay and enjoy decadence even when the world seems to be ending. He values pleasure and debauchery above self-preservation, treating catastrophe as just another occasion for indulgence. Beyond his brief appearance in the crossover episode, he becomes a piece of pop-culture trivia within Springfield, referenced in a science museum exhibit about Futurama. He also inspires fan cosplay, showing his status as a recognizable icon even among ordinary Springfield citizens. In non-canon material, he appears in a bizarre alternate world dominated by sentient couches, reinforcing his role as a surreal, over-the-top character used mostly for comedic cameo appearances. Voiced by Maurice LaMarche. Notable quotes: "...as there was no debauchery like end-of-the-world debauchery."
quotes: "...as there was no debauchery like end-of-the-world debauchery."

title: Hawkeye
text: Hawkeye is A Marvel Comics superhero referenced within The Simpsons universe, used as a costume rather than an actual character. Hawkeye isn't a true Simpsons character but rather a Marvel superhero identity that gets borrowed by other characters for dress-up purposes. Comic Book Guy notably wears a Hawkeye costume during an attempt to break a world record for the most fictional deaths performed in one minute. In a non-canon storyline, Milhouse Van Houten also takes on the Hawkeye persona while serving as part of the Springfield Avengers team. Since the character never appears as himself, there's no personality or voice actor associated with him, and he functions purely as a costume gag referencing the real Marvel hero Clint Barton. His appearances are brief and tied entirely to other characters' cosplay rather than his own storyline.

title: Hypnotic Head
text: Hypnotic Head is A villain from the Radioactive Man comic books (a fictional comic series within The Simpsons universe), known as a master of mind control. Hypnotic Head, sometimes called Hypno Head, is a bald supervillain who specializes in mind control within the Radioactive Man comic book world. He often works through henchmen and disguises, at one point posing as a peace-gathering reverend to lure victims into his control. His schemes typically target Radioactive Man and his allies, using mind-controlled pawns and rigged weapons to try to destroy his enemies. Despite his elaborate plots, he is consistently thwarted by heroes like Fallout Boy, Bleeding Heart, and Purple Badge of Courage. He commands other villains such as Larceny Lass and Jawbreaker, showing he holds some standing within the supervillain community. His recurring appearances and mentions across multiple comic issues establish him as a persistent, if often defeated, threat in the Radioactive Man universe.

title: Ashley Grant
text: Ashley Grant is A grad student and babysitter who briefly babysits the Simpson kids and accuses Homer of harassment. Ashley Grant is a graduate student at Springfield University who works as a babysitter, likely to help fund her studies. She's a self-described feminist who takes her convictions seriously, sometimes to a fault, as shown when she jumps to conclusions about Homer's behavior. Despite the rocky start, she proves fair-minded, willing to admit when she's wrong once shown clear evidence. She has a good rapport with the Simpson kids, especially Lisa, who looks up to her feminist ideals. She also shows a clever, manipulative streak, using a video game to trick Bart into doing chores. Beyond her babysitting gig, she pops up in various Springfield settings, from a record store to Krusty's retirement special to a town hall meeting about local pollution. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Goodbye Yellow Brick Road
text: Goodbye Yellow Brick Road is A band hired by Artie Ziff to perform at his second senior prom for Marge. Goodbye Yellow Brick Road is a minor fictional band within the Simpsons universe, brought in by the lovestruck Artie Ziff to provide live music for an elaborate do-over prom he throws for Marge. The joke surrounding the band is that they are washed up, having not performed since the wrap party of an obscure television show decades earlier, and are rumored to be cursed. Their name is a nod to the real Elton John song of the same title, tying into the show's frequent musical references. Beyond their appearance at Artie's prom, the band shows up briefly elsewhere, with only a guitarist glimpsed in a later opening sequence gag. They function purely as background texture for Artie's over-the-top romantic gesture rather than as characters with personalities of their own.

title: Alfred Hitchcock
text: Alfred Hitchcock is Real-world film director referenced/depicted as a minor recurring pop-culture figure in the Simpsons universe. Alfred Hitchcock appears in the show mostly as a background reference or photograph rather than a speaking character. He is shown having once posed for a picture with Krusty the Clown, swapping director chairs with him, and his image later hangs in Krusty's office alongside photos with the Beatles and the Incredible Hulk. He's invoked by Kent Brockman as one of the classic examples of a jolly, fat public figure, and a deranged street person accuses him of stealing all his ideas. His likeness also shows up in unexpected modern contexts, like a celebrity-chef verification captcha on a fictional website and a poster during a musical number. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he appears as a mischievous figure who sics birds on Mrs. Krabappel, a nod to his own famous film. Overall, he functions as a recurring visual easter egg rather than an active character with dialogue.

title: Agent J
text: Agent J is A minor crossover character based on the Men in Black film franchise, appearing within a movie Bart watches. Agent J is a parody character lifted straight from the Men in Black movies, appearing on screen during a film Bart is shown watching. He's depicted as a tough, wisecracking alien hunter alongside his partner Agent K, blasting extraterrestrial threats without hesitation. His brief appearance leans on the audience's familiarity with the real Will Smith role, played here for a quick nod to the source material rather than deep characterization. He later shows up again in a stage musical parody, further playing into the show's love of referencing pop culture franchises. Agent J doesn't have any real interaction with the Simpsons family beyond being viewed as entertainment. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "raggedy maggots" - Agent J
quotes: "raggedy maggots" - Agent J

title: Mama Jugs
text: Mama Jugs is A minor recurring background character; a prostitute working in Springfield. Mama Jugs is a blonde-haired sex worker who operates in various seedy spots around Springfield, including the waterfront, a skid row street corner, and the Sleep-Eazy Motel. She's a minor background figure rather than a fully developed character, appearing briefly across a handful of episodes. In a non-canon deleted scene, she has an awkward encounter with Homer that plays on her profession for comic effect, including a joke about her refusing to do certain tasks "by mouth." She's associated with smoking and criminal activity, fitting into the show's background cast of Springfield's less reputable citizens. Her name is more of a moniker than an official identity, and she has no confirmed voice actor credited. Notable quotes: Looking for a good time, sailor?
quotes: Looking for a good time, sailor?

title: Tom Jones (character)
text: Tom Jones (character) is Celebrity singer who makes guest appearances in Springfield, notably held captive by Mr. Burns. Tom Jones appears as a fictionalized version of himself, a famous crooner known for his hit songs. In one memorable encounter, Mr. Burns forces him at gunpoint to serenade Marge and Homer with his song, an ordeal Jones endures rather than being helped by the oblivious couple. His fame is referenced by Bart and Lisa as proof that some celebrities never fade from the spotlight, putting him alongside legends like Bob Hope, Frank Sinatra, and Dean Martin. His music also gets a comedic afterlife when a comic shop owner plays Korean pop covers of his songs in his store. Jones is later depicted in a risqué album cover gag, shown covered in women's underwear, poking fun at his ladies'-man reputation. Overall, he functions as a running pop-culture cameo rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Tom Jones (Himself).

title: Jesse Grass
text: Jesse Grass is Teenage environmental activist and leader of the Dirt First club, first appearing in "Lisa the Tree Hugger". Jesse Grass is a dedicated teenage activist who heads Dirt First, a group devoted to opposing anything he views as environmentally destructive, from fast food chains to logging. He takes his principles to an extreme degree, following a strict vegan diet so rigorous that he won't eat food that casts a shadow. His passion for causes has repeatedly landed him in legal trouble, including multiple arrests tied to his protests, one of which caused major damage to Springfield's business district. Despite his troublemaking tendencies, he remains a recognizable fixture at environmental and cultural events around town, and even took part in a daring effort to rescue a captive orca. Lisa Simpson views him as the embodiment of unwavering idealism, using him as an example in one of her personality classifications of schoolmates. His name is a nod to the real-life brother of a Simpsons writer, who once played in a band called Grass. Voiced by Joshua Jackson.

title: Tony Hawk (character)
text: Tony Hawk (character) is Guest-star celebrity character; professional skateboarder who becomes Bart's neighbor and idol. Tony Hawk appears as a fictionalized version of himself, playing the cool, effortlessly talented skateboarder who moves in above Bart after Bart gets his own apartment. His constant parties, often joined by the band Blink-182, and his skateboarding prowess make him an instant hero to Bart, which drives a wedge between father and son. Homer, jealous of the attention Bart gives Hawk, tries to outdo him in a skate-off using a rigged, super-powered skateboard, leading to a comedic clash of egos. Despite the friction he unintentionally causes, Hawk ultimately plays a positive role in helping Homer and Bart reconcile. Outside the main canon, he's also depicted attending a season finale premiere, poking fun at his real-life celebrity status. Overall, he serves as a lighthearted symbol of extreme-sports coolness that highlights the generational gap between Homer and Bart. Voiced by Tony Hawk (Himself).

title: Herod the Great
text: Herod the Great is Historical/biblical figure parodied in Simpsons Christmas specials, portrayed as a villainous Roman client king of Judea. Herod the Great is a non-canon depiction of the historical Judean king, appearing in the show's holiday-themed specials and games. In the Christmas story parody, he is portrayed as greedy and paranoid, initially assuming gifts meant for the baby Jesus were intended for him. When corrected, he flies into a rage and vows to have the child killed, leading soldiers on a hunt that is ultimately foiled by a clever ruse involving a duck wearing Jesus' halo. His pursuit ends in comedic failure when he and his soldiers become tangled in a falling pine tree, transforming into unwitting Christmas ornaments. He also appears as a video game villain in 'Frosty the Hit Man,' where he meets his end at the hands of Frosty. Overall, Herod serves as a recurring holiday-special antagonist used for comedic and satirical religious parody. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Jamie Hyneman (character)
text: Jamie Hyneman (character) is Real-world special effects expert and TV host appearing as himself in a guest role on The Simpsons. Jamie Hyneman appears in the show as a version of his real-life self, known for co-hosting the myth-testing television series MythCrackers alongside Adam Savage.
