In his appearance, he's shown conducting an eccentric experiment involving firing a stuffed bear from a cannon to study a myth about falling animals, only to lose track of the original point of the test. His antics end up inspiring Bart and Milhouse to start their own amateur myth-testing endeavors. Beyond this direct appearance, his image also turns up as a piece of décor in a local hangout, showing his minor but recognizable presence in the show's world. He's portrayed as a curious, slightly scattered but dedicated scientific tinkerer, true to his real-world reputation. Voiced by Himself.

title: Hades (Disney)
text: Hades (Disney) is Non-canon Disney crossover character, god of the underworld from Hercules, appearing in Simpsons specials tied to Disney+. Hades is a crossover character brought into The Simpsons universe from Disney's Hercules as part of Disney+ promotional specials. He appears as one of several Disney villains integrated into the show's world, first showing up at Moe's Tavern during a Disney+ anniversary celebration. He later turns up at Disney Villain Land, where Lisa brings him to school, leading to a chaotic volcanic eruption in her classroom. He also joins a large ensemble of Disney villains performing a holiday-themed song. As a non-speaking character in these appearances, his role is largely visual and tied to spectacle rather than dialogue or characterization.

title: Ham
text: Ham is A minor Springfield Elementary student and member of the Superfriends club. Ham is a background student character at Springfield Elementary, best known as one of the geeky Superfriends alongside Database, Cosine, E-mail, Report Card, and Lisa Simpson. He's depicted as a short, heavyset kid with suspenders, a bow-tie, and glasses, giving him a distinctly nerdy look. True to the group's quirky tradition of assigning nicknames, his own name playfully references his love of ham radio operating. His main claim to fame in the show's continuity comes from the episode where Bart Simpson discovers a comet, during which Ham helps welcome Bart into the club and takes part in dubbing him "Cosmos." He also plays a small part in the tense sequence where the Superfriends realize the comet is on a collision course with Earth and rush to warn the observatory. Beyond this storyline, Ham mostly appears as a recurring background character across many later seasons and Simpsons comic books. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Samwise Gamgee
text: Samwise Gamgee is A Lord of the Rings parody character who appears as a hallucination/crossover figure in Simpsons media. Samwise Gamgee is a Hobbit companion from the Fellowship of the Ring who crosses over into the Simpsons universe in a couple of tie-in appearances. He first shows up as part of a drug-induced fantasy when Homer and Ned imagine themselves as Frodo Baggins and Samwise Gamgee after taking a strange substance. In a separate, non-canon comic story, he actually teams up with the Simpson family alongside the rest of the Fellowship. Unfortunately for him, that team-up ends badly when Homer accidentally knocks him and fellow Hobbits Merry and Pippin off a cliff into a pack of hungry wolves. He doesn't have much characterization beyond his source material, functioning mainly as a nod to Tolkien fans. His appearances are brief and largely played for slapstick comedy rather than deep characterization.

title: Kermit
text: Kermit is Muppet character (crossover celebrity) who appears in cameo roles within The Simpsons. Kermit is the famous frog puppet from The Muppets, best known as the host and master of ceremonies of The Muppet Show. Within the Simpsons universe he shows up as a celebrity cameo, often interacting with other real-world guest stars like Lurleen Lumpkin and Troy McClure. His long-running romantic pairing with Miss Piggy is treated as running gag material, including a moment where she jealously attacks him on stage. One appearance humorously breaks the fourth wall by revealing Jim Henson and another puppeteer operating him after a swarm of frogs knocks him off a rock. He's also referenced as a notable figure on Ned Flanders' list of admirable liberals, cementing his status as a beloved pop-culture icon rather than a true series regular. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: J. Edgar Hoover
text: J. Edgar Hoover is Real-world historical figure (first FBI director) referenced in Simpsons canon. J. Edgar Hoover appears in the show only as a background reference rather than a fully realized character. He's brought up in a Grampa Simpson story explaining why Mr. Burns was demoted in the army, having obstructed one of Hoover's investigations. A framed picture of Hoover, oddly depicted in a dress, hangs in the FBI office of Dana Scully and Fox Mulder during their crossover appearance. He's also listed among the notable left-handed people on Ned Flanders' list of famous lefties. Hoover never physically appears or speaks in any canonical episode, existing purely as a historical footnote and running joke tying real-world figures into Springfield lore. In non-canon material, he appears as a playable character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out, including an 'Undercover Hoover' variant.

title: Jazzy James
text: Jazzy James is Former rapper/songwriter turned stall owner, tied to the storyline about rapper Jay G. Jazzy James is a one-time member of the rap group The Five Boyfriends, for whom he wrote all the songs, though he has since moved on to running the Elite Candles stall. He's shown as someone who tries to profit off any interaction, initially refusing to help Bart unless he first bought an overpriced candle. When enlisted by Bart, Homer, and Mr. Burns to take down the powerful producer Jay G, he struggles creatively, having seemingly lost his rapping talent, and only manages to write something worthwhile after being literally hung out a window under pressure. His comeback track brings in famous real-life rappers to help finish the job, but the whole scheme backfires when it's revealed Jay G had already bought the rights to the song from everyone involved, including James. Despite this setback, he continues to make minor appearances around Springfield, such as attending a podcast taping. Voiced by Keegan-Michael Key.

title: Agent K (Men in Black)
text: Agent K (Men in Black) is Fictional MIB agent appearing in a Men in Black film watched by Bart, partnered with Agent J. Agent K is a minor fictional character based on the Men in Black movie franchise, appearing within a film-within-the-show that Bart watches. He is depicted as a stern, alien-hunting government agent alongside his partner Agent J, mirroring the real-world Men in Black films. His appearances are brief cameos rather than fully developed roles, existing mainly as a nod to the popular sci-fi comedy series. He later shows up again in a musical parody segment, continuing the show's tradition of referencing pop culture through fictional media within episodes. Agent K has no dialogue and is categorized as a non-speaking character. The role is a clear homage to actor Tommy Lee Jones, who portrayed the character in the actual Men in Black films.

title: Jeremy (network executive)
text: Jeremy (network executive) is A network executive at FOX who works alongside Lindsey Naegle and other executives. Jeremy is one of the interchangeable, faceless network executives who torment Krusty the Clown until he retires out of sheer annoyance. He and his fellow executives are eventually revealed to be liquid metal androids, surviving an explosion caused by Mr. Teeny's bomb. Despite this near-indestructibility, Jeremy is ultimately fired by fellow executive Diane for not firing Krusty quickly enough. He has a habit of parroting the phrase "I was just thinking that," reflecting his lack of original ideas and yes-man nature typical of network suits. His android nature and eventual dismissal poke fun at the corporate, disposable culture of television executives. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: You can kill me but two more will take my place!
quotes: You can kill me but two more will take my place!

title: Jesus fish
text: Jesus fish is Fish bred and owned by Ned Flanders, shown at the Springfield Pet Fair. The Jesus fish are a curious breed of fish raised by Ned Flanders, showcased proudly at the Springfield Pet Fair. Ned claims their unusual appearance comes from selectively breeding fish that God made to resemble what he wanted, a process Lisa cheekily points out sounds just like natural selection. The exchange highlights the show's recurring gag of poking fun at the tension between Ned's devout faith and scientific reasoning. In a strange and comedic twist, one of the fish begins evolving before their eyes, growing legs and breathing air, forcing Ned to hastily shove it back into the tank and seal it shut. The fish serve mainly as a one-off joke about creationism versus evolution rather than as significant recurring characters. They later reappear as a decorative item in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Notable quotes: so naturally [he] selected those for further breeding. | so that "natural selection" was the origin of this species?
quotes: so naturally [he] selected those for further breeding.
so that "natural selection" was the origin of this species?

title: Jessica (The Canine Mutiny)
text: Jessica (The Canine Mutiny) is A collie owned by Kent Brockman, appearing as a minor animal character in the Simpsons universe. Jessica is a brown and white collie belonging to news anchor Kent Brockman. She first appears at the Springfield Dog Park, where the Simpsons bring their own dog Laddie. Though Homer hopes for puppies between the two dogs, it's revealed Jessica has already been spayed and simply craves affection. As a non-speaking animal character, Jessica doesn't have much personality development beyond her role as Brockman's pet. She later resurfaces during a chaotic period when Springfield becomes dog-friendly, and like many other dogs in town, she succumbs to sudden aggressive behavior. Jessica's appearances are brief and largely background, making her a minor recurring figure tied to the show's various dog-centric storylines.

title: Miss Grant
text: Miss Grant is Secretary to Kent Brockman, appearing in the Bartman comic book series (non-canon). Miss Grant is a minor comic-book character who works as Kent Brockman's secretary. She is sharp-eyed and not afraid to needle her boss, noticing the suspicious timing of Bartman's rising fame alongside Brockman's anti-Bartman campaign. Her comments hint that she suspects Brockman is secretly orchestrating the whole Bartman story for ratings, which visibly rattles him. Despite her insight, she remains a background figure mostly used to deliver news updates and carry out Brockman's orders, including calling security when Bartman confronts him directly. She has red hair and exists only within the non-canon Bartman comic continuity. Notable quotes: if she didn't know any better, she'd say that Brockman was masterminding the whole story himself
quotes: if she didn't know any better, she'd say that Brockman was masterminding the whole story himself

title: Calliope Juniper
text: Calliope Juniper is Substitute music teacher at Springfield Elementary School, love interest of Principal Skinner. Calliope Juniper stepped in to teach music at Springfield Elementary after Mr. Largo fled his post. She quickly became the object of Principal Skinner's affection, which led to an odd scheme involving her daughter Melody and Bart. Calliope seems open to spontaneity and romance, as shown by her impromptu getaway proposal to Skinner. That escape turned out to be far longer than Skinner realized, hinting at a somewhat carefree or mysterious streak in her personality. She's since made minor appearances around Springfield, including attending a local podcast recording. As a divorced single mother, she brings a bit of domestic complexity to her otherwise brief but memorable role in the show. Voiced by Kristen Wiig.

title: Steve Guttenberg
text: Steve Guttenberg is Minor recurring character based on real-life actor Steve Guttenberg, depicted as a former member of the Stonecutters secret society. This version of Steve Guttenberg is a fictionalized, non-speaking cameo character who belongs to the secretive Stonecutters organization. He's shown singing along with his fellow members during their ritual song, which credits the group for his fame and stardom. In a later, more bizarre appearance, he's depicted appearing on South Park and playing in a band alongside an unlikely pair of bandmates, Farty the Crippled Robot and Calista Flockhart. His fictional storyline takes a dark comedic turn when he meets his end at the hands of O.J. Simpson. Despite his brief and strange appearances, he remains a fun piece of celebrity-cameo trivia within the show's universe. As a non-speaking character, he never delivers any memorable dialogue of his own.

title: Jonesy
text: Jonesy is Non-canon crossover character from Fortnite who appears in Simpsons crossover specials. Jonesy, full name John "Jonesy" Jones, is an agent originally from the video game Fortnite who crosses over into the Simpsons universe during a rift-related crisis. He teams up with fellow Fortnite character Hope to battle a demon and retrieve a zero point shard, getting swept into a merged reality called Springfield Island alongside Kang and Kodos. Practical and a bit impulsive, he's shown getting into a slap fight with Kang and casually snacking on a self-feeding pretzel powered by strange magic. He also lends a hand to the Simpson family when Homer is enlarged to giant size, offering suggestions when other plans fail. Later he's seen lounging on the Simpsons' couch with other Fortnite characters before being chased off at gunpoint. As a non-canon character, his role is purely tied to the show's Fortnite crossover specials rather than the main continuity. Voiced by Troy Baker.

title: Juggler
text: Juggler is A boardwalk performer at the Springfield Squidport who briefly interacts with the Simpson family. The juggler is a minor performer working the boardwalk at Springfield Squidport, entertaining crowds with his juggling act. His notable appearance comes when Homer, watching him work, decides to test his skills by tossing his own children into the mix. Rather than being a fully developed character, he mostly serves as an exasperated straight man to Homer's escalating antics, reacting with alarm as more people get added to his juggling routine. Eventually, the situation spirals out of his control entirely, ending with everyone collapsing on top of him. He also appears in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out as an unlockable boardwalk performer character. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: The juggler calls Homer insane
quotes: The juggler calls Homer insane

title: Peggy Hill
text: Peggy Hill is Crossover character from King of the Hill; wife of Hank Hill and mother of Bobby Hill, appearing briefly in The Simpsons. Peggy Hill is a guest character brought over from the animated series King of the Hill, appearing in The Simpsons as part of a crossover. She is depicted simply as a member of the Hill family, attending a pee-wee football game alongside her husband Hank and son Bobby. Peggy does not have any spoken lines in her canonical appearance, making her a non-speaking character in the show. She later shows up in non-canon specials, including an anniversary celebration and a Disney+/Hulu-themed party segment. Her presence mainly serves as a nod to fans of King of the Hill rather than to develop her own personality within the Simpsons universe. As a recurring but minor crossover figure, she represents the show's tendency to reference other animated series created by the same production circles.

title: Lillian Gish
text: Lillian Gish is Real-world actress referenced within the Simpsons universe, appearing as a poster image and a mistaken date for Mr. Burns. Lillian Gish is not really a character in the traditional sense but a nod to the real-life silent film actress of the same name. Her presence in the show is limited to a picture of her from the play Broken Blossoms, which Grampa Simpson hangs up after moving in with the Simpson family. She later becomes the subject of a comedic mix-up when Mr. Burns believes he has a date with her, only to discover that Smithers has disguised himself as her in a dress and wig. Gish never appears as a living, speaking character, and her role is purely a background reference and running joke tied to Mr. Burns' old-fashioned tastes. She symbolizes the show's frequent use of classic Hollywood references for humor.

title: Goliath
text: Goliath is Biblical giant referenced in Simpsons lore, defeated by King David. Goliath is a figure from biblical legend within the Simpsons universe, known for being the giant slain by King David using a slingshot. He is mentioned in a Sunday school lesson taught by Ms. Albright, where a replica of the fateful slingshot is passed around the class. In a non-canon dream sequence appearance, Goliath is portrayed by Nelson and is depicted as the father of Goliath II, who later seeks revenge for his death. This dream-world version ties him into a larger comedic retelling of biblical history featuring the Simpsons cast. Goliath himself does not speak and appears mostly as a legendary or background figure rather than an active character. His story serves as a springboard for jokes about size, strength, and vengeance in the show's parody of Bible stories.

title: Ken Griffey, Jr. (character)
text: Ken Griffey, Jr. (character) is Real-life baseball player recruited to play on the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant softball team. Ken Griffey, Jr. appears as a guest celebrity athlete recruited by Waylon Smithers, Jr. to work at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant so he could bolster its softball team against Shelbyville. He's given a mundane job as the plant's lunchroom cashier despite his sports fame, a classic gag in the episode about ringers hired for the big game. His storyline takes a bizarre turn when he becomes addicted to Brain & Nerve Tonic, leading to an overdose that causes gigantism and forces him to miss the crucial final game. Griffey is later referenced as one of the notable left-handed people on Ned Flanders' list of laudable lefties. In non-canon material, footage of his gigantism episode resurfaces, and he's shown attending a premiere for a Simpsons season finale in Los Angeles. His character blends real-world celebrity cameo humor with the show's tendency to give sports stars absurd, exaggerated fates. Voiced by Ken Griffey Jr..

title: Janitor (Burns, Baby Burns)
text: Janitor (Burns, Baby Burns) is A minor, unnamed background character who works as a janitor at the Peabody Museum of Natural History. This nameless janitor is a minor background figure whose only claim to fame is stumbling upon Mr. Burns in a compromising situation. While going about his duties at the Peabody Museum of Natural History, he unexpectedly witnesses Mr. Burns and Lily Bancroft in an intimate encounter near an Eskimo sculpture. He has no dialogue or characterization beyond this brief, awkward moment. In a non-canon appearance, he is glimpsed again, this time standing in a line to pay respects to an alligator accidentally killed by Homer in Florida. The character exists purely as a background gag rather than a developed personality, and his fate is unknown, with the wiki noting he is possibly deceased. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Meg Griffin
text: Meg Griffin is Crossover character from Family Guy; daughter of Lois and Peter Griffin, appearing in Simpsons crossover episodes. Meg Griffin is a member of the Griffin family from Family Guy who crosses over into the Simpsons universe in non-canon material. She's frequently the butt of jokes, as referenced by the 'Dump On Meg' attraction at Family Guy World, continuing her role as the perpetually mistreated teenager of her own show. In the crossover story, she and her family end up in Springfield after their car is stolen, leading to an unlikely friendship between her and Lisa Simpson. Lisa discovers that Meg has a hidden talent for playing the saxophone and tries to encourage her by gifting her own instrument, but Peter callously throws it away, underscoring the running gag of Meg's family disrespecting her. She later appears among the Griffins at a gathering tied to a Disney+/Hulu-themed event. Overall, Meg serves as a vehicle for crossover humor and a poignant contrast to Lisa's supportive family dynamic. Voiced by Mila Kunis.

title: Guy with big hand
text: Guy with big hand is Minor recurring background employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, known for his unusually large hand. This nameless plant worker is defined entirely by his oversized hand, which has made him the target of endless workplace teasing. Sensitive about the mockery, he once tried to explain the origin of his condition by writing a message on his hand, only to be cut off mid-story. He claims the enlargement resulted from radiation exposure in the reactor core, and he even encouraged Homer to expose a donut to the same radiation in hopes of enlarging it. Despite the hand being his most obvious trait, he oddly seems to forget which hand is the big one, leading to moments of surprise and even losing his balance from its weight. He's shown as a fairly ordinary, somewhat grumpy coworker otherwise, telling other employees to pipe down when they complain about changes at the plant. In non-canon material, he's also present when Mr. Burns dies and leaves his fortune to the plant's employees. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: I am tired of these jokes about my giant hand. The first such incident occurred in 1956 when...
quotes: I am tired of these jokes about my giant hand. The first such incident occurred in 1956 when...

title: Julius Hibbert's oldest son
text: Julius Hibbert's oldest son is Minor recurring character; oldest son of Dr. Julius Hibbert and Bernice Hibbert. Julius Hibbert's oldest son is a minor background character belonging to the Hibbert family, appearing occasionally throughout the show's long run without ever being given his own name. He has black hair and is depicted as a teenager. His one notable moment involves a family outing where he weighs in on where to eat, suggesting a themed restaurant before the family ends up briefly stopping at Moe's Tavern. Beyond that scene, he mostly appears as a background presence in crowd or family scenes across many seasons. He has an older brother, JJ Hibbert, and an unnamed sister, rounding out the Hibbert household. Despite his lack of characterization, he has shown up sporadically in episodes spanning from season 7 all the way into the 30s, making him a long-running if obscure fixture of Springfield. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Prince Hamlet
text: Prince Hamlet is Bart Simpson's role as Prince Hamlet of Denmark in the 'Do the Bard, Man' segment, a parody retelling of Shakespeare's Hamlet. Prince Hamlet is the tragic hero of the Springfield adaptation of Shakespeare's classic play, featured in the anthology episode 'Tales from the Public Domain.' After his father's ghost reveals that his uncle Claudius murdered him to seize the throne and marry his mother Gertrude, Hamlet is driven to seek vengeance. He enlists a clown's help to expose Claudius's guilt through a staged play, leading to a chain of accidental deaths, duels, and betrayals typical of the source material's dark comedy. True to the original story's tragic irony, Hamlet finally kills Claudius but dies almost immediately afterward in a slapstick twist, slipping on blood right after his triumph. The character is later invoked outside his own story as a benchmark for tragic figures, humorously contrasted with the far less noble Principal Skinner. Overall, he represents the show's playful, irreverent take on classic literature. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Gavin's mother
text: Gavin's mother is Minor recurring character; mother of the spoiled boy Gavin, occasionally seen in Springfield background scenes. Gavin's mother, sometimes jokingly called the Range Rover mom, is a minor Springfield resident best known for indulging her demanding son Gavin. She's often shown running errands like shopping or grocery store trips, only to be rudely dismissed or criticized by her ungrateful child. There's a streak of dramatic irony to her appearances, as she tends to judge other parents' failures just before her own son embarrases her. Beyond her role as Gavin's exasperated caretaker, she has popped up in various unrelated contexts, such as a marketing focus group and an airplane flight, suggesting she's a fairly ordinary background fixture of the town. She also has an ex-husband or husbands, hinted at by Gavin's offhand remark about wanting to live with 'one of his dads.' Voiced by Maggie Roswell. Notable quotes: Bart's parents went wrong in raising him.
quotes: Bart's parents went wrong in raising him.

title: Lyndon B. Johnson
text: Lyndon B. Johnson is Real-world 36th President of the United States, referenced and appearing briefly in various Simpsons episodes. Lyndon B. Johnson appears in the Simpsons universe as a historical figure rather than a regular character, popping up mostly through archival footage, mentions, and a theme park animatronic. He's depicted in a disturbing training video shown to Santa's Little Helper, where he's seen lifting a dog by its ears, a nod to a real-life controversy involving the president. He's also the subject of a tabloid TV hoax claiming he voiced Yosemite Sam, later retracted. Marge references her own grief over his death when comforting Bart, giving him an odd emotional touchstone in the show's world. Homer even uses Johnson's later years as an unflattering comparison for Bart's erratic behavior. Overall, Johnson functions as a recurring bit of historical trivia and running gag fodder rather than an active character. Notable quotes: "LBJ, y'know towards the end."
quotes: "LBJ, y'know towards the end."

title: Howard, Sr.
text: Howard, Sr. is A minor recurring character who owned Howard's Flowers, a florist shop in Springfield. Howard, Sr. was a florist and small business owner who ran Howard's Flowers with dedication, working hard to support his wife and son. He appeared briefly in the show's history, once selling Homer a single long-stem rose, and was later spotted waiting in line for a water ride at Mt. Splashmore. Not much else is known about his personality, as he was largely a background character used for quick gags rather than deep storylines. After his death, his son, Howard, Jr., took over the family flower business, continuing his father's legacy. His passing was only mentioned rather than shown on screen. Voiced by Paul Willson.

title: The Human Lawn Dart
text: The Human Lawn Dart is A comic-book supervillain and member of the Threatening Threesome, enemy of Radioactive Man. The Human Lawn Dart is a minor villain existing within the fictional Radioactive Man comic book universe featured in The Simpsons. As part of the group known as the Threatening Threesome, he stands as one of many foes that the superhero Radioactive Man has battled over the years. His defeats are treated as fairly unremarkable, appearing mostly as background material in Radioactive Man's storied history. He shows up in person at a wedding, only to be swiftly taken down by another hero rather than Radioactive Man himself. Later, he resurfaces not as a physical threat but as a hologram used to unsettle Radioactive Man, showing how his legacy persists even without direct confrontation. Overall, he functions as a small piece of the larger comic-within-a-show mythology rather than a fully developed character.

title: Ted Kennedy
text: Ted Kennedy is Real-world U.S. Senator who appears as a recurring background/reference character in Springfield's world, younger brother of President John F. Kennedy. Ted Kennedy is depicted as the real-life younger brother of John F. Kennedy and Bobby Kennedy, occasionally popping up in Springfield-related events and pop culture references. He's shown attending Lisa's essay competition, being romantically linked to Vanna White by a psychic llama-reading incident, and getting bitten by a llama much to another character's delight. Several episodes reference him through news headlines, radio commentary, crossword clues, and even a surreal Kennedy-family boating daydream involving Homer. He's mostly used as a running gag or cutaway reference rather than a fully developed character, often tied to jokes about his family's political legacy and personal reputation. In non-canon material, he's even imagined as having once been President before Lisa took office. The show also credits him as inspiration for Mayor Quimby, tying his real-world persona into Springfield's fictional political satire. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "I'll make Ted Kennedy pay - if he fights back, I'll say that he's gay."
quotes: "I'll make Ted Kennedy pay - if he fights back, I'll say that he's gay."

title: Hermann Göring
text: Hermann Göring is Historical Nazi Party figure referenced in flashbacks involving Abe Simpson. Hermann Göring appears in The Simpsons as a real-world historical figure tied to a tall tale told by Abe Simpson. According to Abe's story, Göring was present alongside Hitler and Mussolini watching him perform as a German cabaret singer, one of Grampa's many dubious wartime anecdotes. In another account, Abe claims he spared Göring's life during World War II and was rewarded with a priceless watch, adding a layer of absurdity to Abe's unreliable narration. The character is also said to have escaped to Argentina after the war, adopting the alias Señor Hermann Gomez. He exists purely as a background element in Grampa's exaggerated war stories rather than as an active character in the show's present-day storyline. A non-canon comic story further references Göring when Grampa recalls a trick he once used on him during the war.

title: Hippie teacher
text: Hippie teacher is A minor recurring substitute teacher at Springfield Elementary School. The hippie teacher is a background staff member at Springfield Elementary School who occasionally fills in for regular teachers. True to his name, he's fond of reminiscing about the 1960s, once trying to keep a class entertained with stories from that era after the actual textbooks went missing. He tends to show up during school-wide events and controversies, such as joining the crowd that trails Homer during a public scandal, attending an emergency union meeting during a snowstorm crisis, and taking part in a teachers' strike organized by Mrs. Krabappel. He was also present when the school's funding crisis was revealed after Mr. Burns' illegal oil drilling was exposed. He remains a minor, rarely named character who appears mostly in group or crowd scenes of school staff. Voiced by Harry Shearer, Hank Azaria.

title: Sven Golly
text: Sven Golly is A criminal hypnotist who briefly menaces Springfield, notably hypnotizing Homer and Chief Wiggum. Sven Golly is a traveling circus performer whose real talent for hypnosis doubles as a tool for crime and mischief. He first appears using his powers to trick Homer into believing he's a ten-year-old boy, turning a simple act into a chaotic scenario for the Simpson family. When Chief Wiggum tries to arrest him, Golly turns the tables by hypnotizing the police chief into stripping down, allowing himself to escape custody. Eventually captured, he's forced to undo his hypnosis on Homer before being locked away in a special plastic holding cell. Even in prison, he can't resist using his gift for manipulation, hypnotizing Wiggum yet again during a chess game to escape once more. His name is a playful nod to Svengali, the classic manipulative hypnotist of literature, tying his gimmick directly into his identity. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Moe Howard
text: Moe Howard is Real-world comedian character based on the leader of the Three Stooges, appearing in cameo roles within The Simpsons universe. Moe Howard is a fictionalized version of the real-life Three Stooges star, appearing sporadically throughout the show as a background or novelty reference rather than a core character. He's depicted in the classic slapstick style of the Three Stooges, engaging in his signature rough physical comedy with his fellow Stooges. In one referenced episode, he pokes Curly in the eyes fatally, slaps Larry on both cheeks to compensate for one being paralyzed, and struggles with forgetting his usual insults. His appearances in the Simpsons universe are brief and unconventional, ranging from just his face appearing in the sky to his skeleton or brain being shown. He embodies the classic comedic violence and gruff persona associated with the real Moe Howard. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Iron Foot
text: Iron Foot is Lenny Leonard's superhero alter ego in a comic-book-within-the-show, non-canon parody character. Iron Foot is the superhero persona of Lenny Leonard, gained after years of exposing his propped-up foot to radiation from late-night kung fu movies on TV. His right foot transforms into a heavy iron-like substance, granting him powerful kicks but also making it very difficult for him to walk normally. He partners with Nuclear Power Man in a comic book that spoofs classic Marvel superhero team-ups, most notably Power Man and Iron Fist. His clumsy mobility becomes a running joke, culminating in an incident where he accidentally kicks Linus Van Pelt instead of the villain he was aiming for. Despite his good intentions, Iron Foot is portrayed as a bit slow and prone to comedic mishaps due to his unwieldy power. He's ultimately a well-meaning if bumbling hero who values camaraderie, as shown by his participation in the group's Christmas dinner. Notable quotes: My foot's as heavy as a substance like unto iron! | You've got a kick like a guy with a foot made out of a substance like unto iron!
quotes: My foot's as heavy as a substance like unto iron!
You've got a kick like a guy with a foot made out of a substance like unto iron!

title: Andrew Jackson
text: Andrew Jackson is The real 7th President of the United States, appearing as a minor recurring figure in the Simpsons universe, usually depicted via currency or historical imagery. Andrew Jackson shows up in the show mostly as an image rather than a fleshed-out character, most notably as the face on the twenty dollar bill. In one episode, his printed likeness on currency comes to life just enough to talk Homer into spending money Marge had secretly saved. He also appears as a picture in a history book Superintendent Chalmers shows Bart, sparking a brief tangent before Bart's attention shifts to Theodore Roosevelt instead. Beyond these appearances, he's referenced or seen in passing across several other episodes, usually just as currency in the background. He has no real personality development, existing mainly as a historical cameo and running visual gag tied to money. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Hendrix
text: Hendrix is Homer Simpson's dog from his childhood, later renamed and living with Miss Viola. Hendrix, originally named Bongo, was the devoted dog Homer grew up with as a child. He had a special bond with Homer, able to comfort him and stop him from crying even as a baby. Their relationship was disrupted after Bongo bit Mr. Burns while defending Homer from an unwanted gift, leading Springfield Animal Control to hunt the dog down. To keep him safe, Bongo was given away to live with Miss Viola on her farm and took on a new name and life, seemingly forgetting his old owner. Despite the sad separation, a heartwarming detail years later reveals the dog secretly still remembers Homer, sleeping on the sweatshirt Homer once gave him. His story is a bittersweet subplot about loyalty, loss, and quiet remembrance. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Ishmael
text: Ishmael is Minor recurring student character at Springfield Elementary School (and later Springfield Christian School). Ishmael is a background fourth-grader at Springfield Elementary whose religious upbringing sets him apart from his classmates. He and his classmate Ezekiel are excused from watching a sex-ed film because of their parents' wishes, allowing them to leave class and pray instead. He later reappears at Springfield Christian School, where he ends up in the same class as Bart Simpson after Bart's expulsion from Springfield Elementary. Ishmael is a non-speaking character, existing mostly as a quiet fixture in the background of school scenes. His defining trait is his devout, sheltered nature, which is used as a mild running joke about strict religious parenting. He has no notable personality traits beyond this and never plays an active role in the plot.

title: Great Maggeena
text: Great Maggeena is Non-canon superhero alter-ego of baby Maggie Simpson, sidekick to Bartman and Lisa the Conjuror in the Bongo comics. Great Maggeena is the secret superhero identity of infant Maggie Simpson, created for the Bartman comic storylines. As a baby, she can't speak, which conveniently keeps her superhero identity safe from outsiders. Too small to actually fight crime, her main contributions to the Bart Alliance involve sitting quietly in the Bartcave and swiping cupcakes for Houseboy. Despite her limitations, she proves surprisingly resourceful in a pinch, using her rattle to save herself and Lisa from a trap filled with giant novelty teeth. She later teams up with her sister, operating as Lisa the Conjuror, to fight crime across Springfield and helps uncover the true villain behind Canker's schemes. The character is a comic-only creation and has no role in the animated series.

title: Joe (Lemon of Troy)
text: Joe (Lemon of Troy) is Shelbyville counterpart of Moe Szyslak, owner of Joe's Tavern. Joe is essentially a mirror-image version of Moe Szyslak, existing in the rival town of Shelbyville. As the proprietor of Joe's Tavern, he serves the same function in Shelbyville that Moe does back in Springfield, reinforcing the episode's theme of the two towns being strange reflections of each other. He appears briefly and silently, standing outside his bar during the chaos of Bart's skateboard chase through town. Joe doesn't get any lines and is mostly a visual gag highlighting the parallel structure between Springfield and Shelbyville. He later shows up again in a non-canon appearance tied to a fictional in-universe cartoon about the two towns. Overall, he's a minor background character defined entirely by his resemblance to Moe.

title: Inspector Baboon
text: Inspector Baboon is Minor comic-book character; a baboon superhero belonging to The Secret Society of Super-Simians in the Radioactive Man comics. Inspector Baboon is a comic-relief superhero from the Radioactive Man comic-book universe within The Simpsons franchise. Styled after a detective, he is part of a super-simian team alongside characters like Radioactive Ape. He's shown to be a bit competitive and impatient, growing annoyed when a teammate hogs the spotlight by retelling his own origin story. Despite his minor role, he pops up alongside Radioactive Ape during team gatherings and incidents involving other superheroes. The character appears to be a comedic riff on DC Comics' Detective Chimp, poking fun at obscure animal-themed superheroes. He has only appeared in a couple of comic issues, making him a rare and niche background figure in the extended Simpsons universe.

title: Kim
text: Kim is Marge's old high school friend and minor recurring background character in Springfield. Kim is a minor character best known as one of Marge's old high school friends, first appearing in a flashback about the women's rights movement. She shared Marge's activist spirit, joining her in campaigning for women's rights and even witnessing Marge's dramatic bra-burning moment. Beyond that early flashback, Kim mostly pops up as a familiar face in the background of Springfield life, showing up at civic and community events like Mt. Splashmore, the Do What You Feel Festival, and the Springfield Mall. She was also swept up in the mob mentality of the town, following Homer around after his harassment scandal. Kim's appearances tend to place her as an observer of the show's larger comedic chaos rather than a driver of the plot herself, cementing her role as a recognizable recurring extra tied to Marge's past. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Jenny (What to Expect When Bart's Expecting)
keys: jenny (what to expect when bart's expecting)
text: Jenny (What to Expect When Bart's Expecting) is A minor character who sought Bart's help to get pregnant. Jenny is a woman desperate to have a child but unable to conceive on her own. When she hears about Bart's accidental voodoo-induced pregnancy of his art teacher, she seeks him out for help, bringing along her skeptical husband. She pays Bart a small fee to perform the same ritual in his treehouse, showing her willingness to try unconventional methods out of desperation. Weeks later, she returns overjoyed to announce that the ritual worked and she is finally pregnant. Grateful for his help, she and her husband plan to spread the word to friends facing similar fertility struggles, hinting that Bart's makeshift services might see more use. She appears only briefly in the show, functioning mainly as part of a subplot about Bart's unexpected foray into fertility magic. Voiced by Tavi Gevinson.

title: Henry Kissinger
text: Henry Kissinger is Real-world diplomat and political scientist who appears as a minor character in Springfield. Henry Kissinger is a caricature of the real-life diplomat who pops up occasionally in Springfield's orbit. In his main appearance, he visits the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant and ends up losing his glasses, which Homer picks up and wears, leading to a mishap where Kissinger walks into a wall and is hospitalized. He's also referenced by Grampa and Homer as the undeserving recipient of a Nobel Peace Prize, a jab at his real-world reputation. In a non-canon comic story, he becomes entangled in a geek-versus-nerd conflict in Springfield, fighting on the geek side dressed as a Cylon. He also makes a non-canon guest appearance alongside Yoko Ono on a fictional talk show. Overall, he's used mostly as a topical, satirical cameo rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Ian (Bart the Genius)
text: Ian (Bart the Genius) is A minor recurring student character attending the Enriched Learning Center for Gifted Children alongside Bart. Ian is a young student at the Enriched Learning Center for Gifted Children, one of many background kids who occasionally interact with Bart Simpson. He's shown to be intellectually inclined, taking part in classroom debates about abstract topics like free will and paradoxes. Despite his academic setting, he also tries his hand at typical schoolyard trading, attempting to swap lunch snacks with Bart, only to be turned down since Bart had already been swindled by other kids. He's also been seen participating in neighborhood mischief, joining a large snowball fight with other local children. Beyond his on-screen appearances, Ian has a small musical claim to fame, serving as one of the backing singers in the song "Do the Bartman." Overall, he's a minor recurring character who adds background texture to Bart's school and neighborhood life rather than driving any major storylines. Voiced by Russi Taylor.

title: Joey (And Maggie Makes Three)
text: Joey (And Maggie Makes Three) is Minor recurring character; a shoe-shine boy who works at Barney's Bowlarama. Joey is a young, sickly-sounding boy employed as a shoe-shine boy at Barney's Bowlarama. He appears briefly during an emotional moment when Homer is forced to leave his job and says goodbye to his coworkers and acquaintances. Joey's defining trait is his persistent cough, which punctuates his brief dialogue and reinforces his portrayal as an unwell child. Despite his rough circumstances, he responds to Homer with a cheerful, almost resigned optimism about the future. He is a minor background character, later appearing only in a photograph within the bowling alley alongside another minor character, Al Gumble. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: sure we will, Mr. Homer, sure we will
quotes: sure we will, Mr. Homer, sure we will

title: Gretchen (Go Big or Go Homer)
text: Gretchen (Go Big or Go Homer) is An intern at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant supervised by Homer. Gretchen is a minor character who appears as one of the power plant interns placed under Homer's supervision after his demotion. She comes across as a bit condescending, joining her fellow interns in mocking Homer when he fails to answer their technical questions. Her curiosity about workplace jargon like contamination versus irradiation gets her drawn into an awkward confrontation. She also has an odd habit of drinking coffee creamer straight from the bottle, which becomes the target of a coworker's frustrated outburst. Ultimately she walks out with the other interns rather than stick around for the drama. In non-canon material, she's shown continuing her intern duties and even present for a major workplace event involving Mr. Burns' fortune. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Peter Griffin
text: Peter Griffin is Crossover character from Family Guy; father of the Griffin family who appears in The Simpsons universe. Peter Griffin is the Family Guy patriarch who occasionally crosses over into the world of The Simpsons. He's depicted as a somewhat bumbling figure, at one point being listed in a criminal book as an accused plagiarist alongside Stan Smith, poking fun at the long-running joke that Family Guy copies The Simpsons. In the non-canon crossover film, he and Homer Simpson become rivals after a heated dispute over whose beer is superior, leading to a lawsuit that shuts down his hometown brewery in Quahog. Their rivalry escalates into a physical fight, but the two eventually reconcile, agreeing to keep a safe distance from one another. He's also shown as one of Homer's many mutated clones in a Halloween special, and in another non-canon story his mutant counterpart is used in a failed attempt to defeat a powerful entity called The Glavin. Overall, Peter serves as a comedic nod to the crossover between the two long-running animated sitcoms. Voiced by Seth MacFarlane.

title: Sarah Michelle Gellar (character)
text: Sarah Michelle Gellar (character) is Real-life celebrity referenced in Simpsons media, appearing as herself in a comic book story. Sarah Michelle Gellar appears in the Simpsons universe as a nod to her real-world fame as an actress, best known for playing Buffy the Vampire Slayer. In the comic 'Springfield's Letters to Santa', Comic Book Guy specifically requests that she personally deliver his complete collection of Buffy action figures, highlighting his obsessive fandom. She doesn't have an active role or dialogue of her own, existing more as an object of Comic Book Guy's devotion. In a non-canon appearance, Comic Book Guy is shown owning a life-size figure of her, humorously imbued with a fanboy's disdainful expression. Overall, her presence in the show is a brief celebrity cameo tied to geek culture references rather than a fully developed character.

title: Invisible Woman
text: Invisible Woman is Marvel superhero (Fantastic Four member) referenced in a Simpsons comic-book parody and Halloween segment. Invisible Woman, whose real name is Susan Storm, is a member of the Fantastic Four and the wife of Mr. Fantastic. She exists in the Simpsons universe mainly as a piece of pop-culture reference rather than an active character, appearing briefly in a comic book excerpt within an episode. Her only real interaction with the main cast comes when Lenny dons an Invisible Woman costume for a superhero-themed pub crawl, played strictly for comedic effect. In a non-canon Halloween segment, baby Maggie is magically transformed into a version of Invisible Woman when Lisa messes around with a mystical stopwatch that turns the family into the Fantastic Four. She has no spoken lines and functions purely as a costume or transformation gag rather than a developed personality within the show.

title: The Human Torque
text: The Human Torque is Non-canon superhero alter-ego of Otto Mann, appearing in Simpsons comic books. The Human Torque is the superhero identity taken on by Otto Mann after he gains powers from exposure to a nuclear explosion. His name and concept are a playful parody of Marvel's Human Torch, fitting the comic's tendency to riff on classic superhero tropes. As a non-canon character, he exists only within the pages of Bongo Comics rather than the animated series itself. His appearances are limited to a specific comic storyline involving other transformed heroes. The character represents a comedic, over-the-top take on Otto's usual slacker persona, reimagined as a costumed crimefighter. He's part of a broader group of makeshift superheroes featured in the same storyline.

title: Humongo
text: Humongo is Fictional comic-book superhero, a gorilla member of The Secret Society of Super-Simians in the Radioactive Man comics. Humongo is a massive, grey-furred gorilla who fights crime as part of a superhero team called The Secret Society of Super-Simians. He appears within the Radioactive Man comic-book universe that exists inside the world of The Simpsons, rather than as a mainstream television character. His few appearances show him attending team meetings and casually spending time with fellow ape hero Radioactive Ape. In one instance he's depicted simply reading a book while Fallout Boy tries to track down Radioactive Man by phone. Despite his imposing size and superhero status, he's portrayed as low-key and unassuming in his limited scenes. He exists mainly as a background member of the super-simian roster rather than a prominent, developed character.

title: Queen Helvetica
text: Queen Helvetica is A fictional queen of Equalia, an imaginary kingdom created by Lisa Simpson in the episode "Lisa the Drama Queen". Queen Helvetica is one of the two co-rulers of the imaginary land of Equalia, sharing her throne with Queen Valedictoria. She exists primarily within the fantasy world that Lisa conjures up during the episode "Lisa the Drama Queen," making her more of a whimsical, storybook figure than a fully fleshed-out character. Being a product of childlike imagination, she has a fairy-tale queenly persona fitting the fantastical, princess-like setting of Equalia. She later reappears as a collectible outfit/skin in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, extending her presence beyond the original episode into non-canon material. Despite her regal title, little else is explored about her personality or backstory in the source material. Voiced by Yeardley Smith.

title: Iron Man
text: Iron Man is Marvel superhero referenced/appearing in Simpsons episodes as a comic book and pop-culture figure. Iron Man is the real-world Marvel superhero, secretly the inventor Tony Stark, who exists as a piece of pop culture within the Simpsons universe rather than a true member of the main cast. He shows up mostly as a picture, costume, or prop rather than a fully speaking character, reflecting how Springfield residents reference and dress up as famous superheroes. Ben Stiller once donned his armor for a lightsaber battle against a Hulk-costumed Jack Black, and Barney Gumble later wore an Iron Man costume as part of the non-canon Springfield Avengers. His armor has even been auctioned off as movie memorabilia, and Chief Wiggum name-drops Tony Stark when wishing for experimental gadgets. The show also has several in-universe parody characters, like Iron Lung and Iron Frink, clearly modeled after him. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "So-called 'Iron Man' may contain trace elements of Tungsten."
quotes: "So-called 'Iron Man' may contain trace elements of Tungsten."

title: Jafar
text: Jafar is Crossover Disney villain character appearing in non-canon Simpsons specials. Jafar is the classic villain from Disney's Aladdin, brought into the Simpsons universe as a non-canon crossover character. He appears in specials tied to Disney+ promotions, mingling with other Disney villains rather than the show's regular cast. His presence is largely background and non-speaking, fitting his role as a recognizable Disney icon rather than a developed Simpsons character. He's shown attending festive or celebratory events alongside fellow villains, reinforcing his sinister reputation through small mischievous acts. Notably, he uses his sorcery to transform the Sultan into a frog during a group musical number. Overall, he serves as a nostalgic nod to Disney fans within the Simpsons' special crossover episodes.

title: Great father
text: Great father is A minor recurring character who works at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, appearing as part of a seemingly perfect family contrasted with the Simpsons. The Great Dad is a background employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, best known for representing an idealized, put-together family unit that stands in stark contrast to the dysfunctional Simpsons. He appears with his wife and two children as a seemingly happy household, first showing up at a picnic hosted by Mr. Burns, where he looks down on Homer's chaotic home life. Despite his outwardly composed appearance, his family later turns out to have hidden troubles of its own, seeking help at a family therapy center. His family's storyline ends abruptly when the Simpsons' antics cause a citywide blackout, forcing them to flee. He has made a handful of other minor appearances across early seasons, always in the background as a plant employee. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Hazel
text: Hazel is Minor recurring elderly Springfield resident, often seen at the Retirement Castle. Hazel is an elderly woman living in Springfield who spends much of her time at the Retirement Castle and appears to be deaf. She's shown as part of a group of older women who pressure Mayor Quimby into enforcing prohibition, inadvertently causing Chief Wiggum to lose his job temporarily. She later becomes a background fixture at the retirement home, where Homer gets to know her during one of his many visits there. Hazel has also popped up in ensemble roles, such as performing in a Broadway musical parody. In non-canon material, she offers a dryly humorous comment about Orson Welles during the Bart's Comet incident, showing a bit of wit beneath her frail exterior. Overall, she's a background character used mostly for crowd scenes involving Springfield's senior citizens. Voiced by Maggie Roswell / Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: That young man had a lot of potential.
quotes: That young man had a lot of potential.

title: Galactus
text: Galactus is A Marvel Comics supervillain referenced within the Simpsons universe, appearing mainly as a costume, statue, or pop-culture reference rather than a true character. Galactus is not an original Simpsons character but a real Marvel Comics villain who pops up in the show as a running pop-culture nod. He's most often seen as a costume worn by anonymous fans, such as at a superhero pub crawl and at the convention Comicalooza. Comic Book Guy references his galaxy-devouring appetite when boasting about his own eating skills at a pie contest. Mr. Burns lists Galactus among the intimidating authority figures he enjoys dressing as, tying him into Burns' obsession with dominance and costumes. He also appears in a joke mash-up with Peanut Allergy Guy created by Bart, forming the character Anaphylactus, and shows up on a cereal box parody. Overall, Galactus functions purely as a background gag and Easter egg for comic fans rather than a speaking or story-driving character.

title: Sherlock Holmes
text: Sherlock Holmes is Fictional detective referenced and occasionally appearing as a pop-culture allusion in Simpsons canon. Sherlock Holmes is the famous literary detective who exists in the Simpsons universe mostly as a cultural touchstone rather than a recurring character. He's frequently invoked as a comparison point for cleverness, suspicion, or nemesis-style rivalries, such as being likened to Skinner's role as Bart's foil or Marge and Homer's pursuit of their kids. Homer has a personal fixation on him, having once owned a deerstalker hat and even briefly run his own detective agency in tribute. Ned Flanders has to remind Homer that Holmes is fictional, which Homer promptly misunderstands in his usual dim-witted way. Beyond the show proper, Holmes turns up in tie-in material like a British romcom parody, a crime-novel reading list, and Lisa's geeky trivia chart, and in a non-canon comic he's one of many literary figures freed into reality by a book-tearing machine.

title: Geoff Jenkins
text: Geoff Jenkins is Cartoonist and creator of the Danger Dog cartoon series who visits Springfield Elementary. Geoff Jenkins is a professional cartoonist and animator best known as the creator of Danger Dog, a popular cartoon among Springfield's kids. He is invited to speak at Springfield Elementary after Kirk Van Houten's disastrous assembly speech, and turns out to be a charismatic and engaging presenter who captivates the students. He wins over the crowd by sharing behind-the-scenes trivia about his show, including a gross-out in-joke about drawing crew members' faces into vomit gags. His visit inspires a wave of imitation cartoons among the kids, most notably leading Bart to create his own creation, Angry Dad. Later, Jenkins continues his career in animation, working on the film adaptation of Angry Dad. He's portrayed as talented and likable, a stark contrast to the awkward guest speaker who preceded him. Voiced by Hank Azaria / Harry Shearer.

title: Godzilla (character)
text: Godzilla (character) is A giant movie monster referenced and briefly appearing in The Simpsons universe. Godzilla appears in the show as a nod to the famous Japanese movie monster franchise rather than as a fully developed character. He shows up in various forms, from a news graphic illustrating the Osaka flu outbreak to an action figure sold at Cockamamie's. He makes a more active appearance attacking the Simpsons' plane alongside other classic kaiju like Mothra, Rodan, and Gamera during their trip from Tokyo. He's also seen at a sci-fi convention and gets mentioned by celebrities and directors as a beloved pop-culture icon. Godzilla has family ties within the show's mythology, being cousin to Sheldon Godzilla and uncle to Godzooky. He never speaks, functioning purely as a background reference or visual gag tied to his real-world film legacy.

title: Gladys (Gladys the Groovy Mule)
text: Gladys (Gladys the Groovy Mule) is A talking mule mascot who appears in the fictional film-within-a-comic "Gladys the Groovy Mule". Gladys is a jazzy, talking mule who serves as the mascot for a high school football team in the movie parody featured in a Simpsons comic. She takes on the role of mentor, teaching an awkward student named Peter Lewis how to be cool and confident. Her adventures with Peter include run-ins with Soviet agents at a jazz club and a triumphant appearance on the football field that helps win a big game. Gladys is a supporting yet pivotal character in this send-up of mid-20th-century Americana, blending Cold War satire with sports-movie tropes. She's loyal to Peter throughout his journey, ultimately being honored by him after his recruitment to Los Alamos.

title: Tom Hanks (character)
text: Tom Hanks (character) is Real-world celebrity who appears as himself in cameo roles throughout the show, most notably in The Simpsons Movie. Tom Hanks plays a fictionalized version of himself who pops up in various Springfield-related media rather than as a regular cast member. His biggest role comes in The Simpsons Movie, where he lends his celebrity credibility to a government commercial announcing a new Grand Canyon over Springfield, later begging fans in the credits to leave him alone if they spot him in public. He's frequently referenced by other characters as a benchmark for respectable, likable acting, such as when Marge cites him as an example of a comedian who became a serious actor, or when Lenny wishes a real-life romance played out like a Tom Hanks movie. His picture turns up as set dressing in places like Springfield Sardi's and during a musical number. In non-canon material, he shows a more irritable side, getting annoyed over a rented tuxedo and mocking Ron Howard with the nickname "Opie." Voiced by Himself. Notable quotes: If you see me in person, please, leave me be. | How many captains can one guy play?
quotes: If you see me in person, please, leave me be.
How many captains can one guy play?

title: Human Torch
text: Human Torch is Marvel superhero (Fantastic Four member) referenced in The Simpsons, occasionally parodied via costumes and transformations. The Human Torch, secretly Johnny Storm, is a fiery Marvel superhero and part of the Fantastic Four whose brief presence in The Simpsons universe is mostly through homage and costume gags rather than direct appearances. He's referenced as the brother of the Invisible Woman, tying him to the broader Marvel mythos the show occasionally nods to. In one instance, Barney dons a Human Torch costume during a superhero-themed pub crawl, showing how the character exists as pop-culture shorthand within Springfield. In a non-canon Halloween special, Marge is magically transformed into the Human Torch, letting the show play with the family taking on iconic superhero identities. Overall, the character functions less as an active personality in the show and more as a recognizable comic-book reference used for sight gags and parody.

title: Che Guevara
text: Che Guevara is Real-world Argentine Marxist revolutionary depicted in mural/poster form within the Simpsons universe. Che Guevara appears in the show not as a living character but as an image or reference tied to his real-world legacy as a Cuban Revolution figure. He's depicted as a mural in Havana, humorously holding a can of Duff Beer, poking fun at commercialism overtaking revolutionary iconography. He's also mentioned in the afterlife, revealed by Mona Simpson to be one of the notable left-wing radicals residing in Hell rather than a more traditional heaven. In a non-canon appearance, his image shows up as a poster near Jesus Christ. Guevara never speaks or acts directly in any episode, existing purely as a background or symbolic reference rather than an active character.

title: Fois Garth
text: Fois Garth is A minor recurring background character in Springfield known as a foodie. Fois Garth is a minor Springfield resident whose defining trait is his passion for food, appearing among the city's foodie crowd. He was present at Haile Delicious Ethiopian Food when Marge, Bart, and Lisa dined there, and later joined fellow foodies at El Chemistri. Beyond food events, he's shown to be a fan of podcasts, turning up in the audience for live recordings of both Tabitha Shingle's and Kent Brockman's shows. He also has an interest outside of dining, having attended a taxidermy convention at the Shelbyville Inn. As a background character voiced by a guest star, he doesn't have an extensive personal history but pops up repeatedly in crowd scenes tied to Springfield's various niche hobbies and events. Voiced by Eric Wareheim.

title: Joe (Zip Boys)
text: Joe (Zip Boys) is One of three giant advertising mascots for the Zip Boys, appearing mainly as background signage in Springfield. Joe is a non-speaking, picture-only character who exists mainly as part of Springfield's advertising landscape, appearing alongside fellow mascots Mack and Manny as the faces of the Zip Boys brand. His likeness shows up on signs and billboards scattered around town, including one sponsoring the First Church of Springfield and another near a bridge Homer and Bart visit. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, Joe's giant rooftop statue comes to life along with other oversized ads after a strange ionic disturbance, leading to a city-wide rampage of animated mascots. The chaos only ends once Springfield's citizens stop paying attention to the mascots, draining their power and causing them to collapse. As a character, Joe has no dialogue and functions purely as a visual gag and parody figure, based on Maurice 'Moe' Strauss, co-founder of the real-world Pep Boys auto parts chain.

title: Neil Gaiman (character)
text: Neil Gaiman (character) is Guest-starring celebrity character; a fictionalized version of author Neil Gaiman who assists Homer and friends in writing a children's book. This version of Neil Gaiman is a good-natured but eccentric celebrity author who inserts himself into Homer's group's attempt to write a children's fantasy novel. He proves helpful during the writing process, keeping the team focused and even handing out drinks, though he memorably tasers Moe instead of serving him one. Despite claiming credit for helping finish the book, he later admits he spent the whole time making tuna salad rather than actually writing. His helpfulness turns out to be a front, as he secretly betrays the group by taking credit on the back flap of their book once it's published by TweenLit Inc. He shows a laid-back, mischievous side when confronted, casually lounging on a beach and joking about his own illiteracy. He also pops up in unrelated cameos around Springfield, showing a warm nostalgia for comic books and geek culture. Voiced by Neil Gaiman (Himself).

title: Mad Doctor Itchy
text: Mad Doctor Itchy is Alter ego of Itchy from The Itchy & Scratchy Show, cast as a Frankenstein-style mad scientist. Mad Doctor Itchy is a cartoon-within-a-cartoon persona taken on by Itchy in an episode of The Itchy & Scratchy Show, casting him as a twisted version of Dr. Frankenstein. In this role he builds his own monstrous creation, Frankenscratchy, purely so he can use it as a target for sadistic experiments. His personality is identical to Itchy's normal violent streak, just dressed up in mad-scientist trappings, reveling in cruelty and suffering. The character's big moment directly spoofs the famous 1931 Frankenstein film scene where the monster is brought to life with lightning. Beyond his single canonical appearance, he later resurfaced in a non-canon capacity within The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Overall he's a minor parody figure used to lampoon classic horror movie tropes within the show's ultra-violent cartoon-within-a-cartoon format. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Nancy Kerrigan
text: Nancy Kerrigan is Real-world Olympic figure skater who appears as a minor character in Simpsons media, notably in a fictional TV role opposite Dr. Hibbert. Nancy Kerrigan appears as a fictionalized version of herself, the real-life American Olympic figure skater. In one story, she portrays a nurse in a television show alongside Dr. Hibbert and propositions him to leave his wife for her, only to be rebuffed. She is also referenced in a clip shown by Professor Frink depicting the infamous real-world attack by rival skater Tonya Harding. Her appearances lean on her real-life fame and the well-known Harding scandal rather than establishing her as an original character with her own personality traits within the Simpsons universe. She serves mainly as a cameo tied to actual events from her skating career. Notable quotes: Hibbert told her that he was too much man for her to handle.
quotes: Hibbert told her that he was too much man for her to handle.

title: Brian Grazer (character)
text: Brian Grazer (character) is A real-life film producer who appears as a celebrity guest character in Springfield-related storylines. Brian Grazer is depicted as a version of himself, a Hollywood film producer who occasionally interacts with the citizens of Springfield. He first becomes involved with the town when Ron Howard brings him a script that Homer had written, hoping to get it produced. Later, he pops up again discussing casting news with Denis Leary, mentioning that Leary landed a role in a film called Everybody Poops, shot in Tunisia. As a guest-star cameo character, he doesn't have much depth beyond representing the real-world entertainment industry poking fun at itself. His appearances are brief and tied directly to specific episode plots involving show business satire. He serves more as a running joke about celebrity culture than as a fully developed character. Voiced by Brian Grazer (Himself).

title: Cecil Hampstead
text: Cecil Hampstead is An artist in Springfield who briefly became friends with Homer during his art career. Cecil Hampstead-on-Cecil Cecil is a minor character from Springfield's art scene who takes a liking to Homer's work when Homer briefly pursues a career as an artist. He is part of a small circle of eccentric art-world acquaintances that Homer falls in with, alongside characters like Kyoto and Gunter. His unusually elaborate, repetitive name is itself a small running joke, hinting at the pretentious nature of the art community he belongs to. Beyond his admiration for Homer's art, little else is revealed about his personality or background. He appears only briefly across a couple of episodes, functioning mainly as color for the satire of the art world rather than as a developed character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Richard Gere (character)
text: Richard Gere (character) is Celebrity guest character who appears as himself, notably introducing Lisa Simpson to Buddhism. Richard Gere appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, an actor and devoted Buddhist. He first shows up on screen starring in a film that a temporarily super-intelligent Homer criticizes for being predictable. His more meaningful role comes when Lisa, disillusioned with Christianity, wanders into the Springfield Buddhist Temple and finds Gere meditating alongside Lenny and Carl. He patiently mentors Lisa on Buddhist philosophy, later reassuring her that Buddhism allows respect for other faiths and holidays, which helps her reconcile her new beliefs with her family's Christmas traditions. He's portrayed as calm, spiritual, and generous with his time despite his celebrity status. Outside canon, he's referenced humorously as a heartthrob figure Bart jokes about kissing Groundskeeper Willie as. Voiced by Himself.

title: Jamaican musician
text: Jamaican musician is Minor recurring background character, an unnamed Jamaican musician seen in New York City. This character is a nameless Jamaican drummer who pops up briefly in a couple of episodes set around New York City. His main claim to fame is bossing around other drummers, urging them to play louder and more obnoxiously. He later resurfaces as part of a drum circle at a Blazing Guy event, suggesting a fondness for group drumming and street performance culture. Little else is known about his personality or background, as he functions mostly as a one-off comedic bit player rather than a developed character. His appearances are brief but memorable enough to warrant a page in the show's extensive catalog of background New Yorkers. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Siddmartha Gautama
text: Siddmartha Gautama is Non-canon Buddhist princess character resembling Lisa Simpson, appearing in a Simpsons episode and mobile game. Siddmartha Gautama is a non-canon character clearly modeled after Gautama Buddha, sharing an uncanny resemblance to Lisa Simpson. She begins as a pampered, dissatisfied princess who feels something is missing despite her wealth and privilege. A visit to a scientist exposes her to impoverished children who seem genuinely happy, prompting her to question the value of material riches. This realization pushes her to abandon palace life in search of true knowledge and wisdom. Her quest for scholarly enlightenment takes an ironic turn when the university she seeks out turns out to be more of a party school than a place of learning. Undeterred, she turns to solitary meditation under a tree, eventually attaining enlightenment through perseverance rather than formal education. Her story serves as a lighthearted parody of the Buddha's spiritual journey within the show's non-canon universe. Voiced by Yeardley Smith.

title: Professor Huntington
text: Professor Huntington is A professor at Swigmore University and former mentor to Moe Szyslak. Professor Huntington is an elderly academic at Swigmore University who serves as a mentor figure to Moe when the bartender loses his passion for the job. He's warm and affectionate toward his former student, using the fond nickname "Old Glasswipe" for him, and insists that bartending is Moe's true calling. He convinces Moe to renovate his rundown bar as a way to reignite his enthusiasm. Tragically, Huntington reveals he is terminally ill with cancer, and rather than let the disease take him, he chooses to end his life by walking into a pond. Even after death, he doesn't fully disappear from Moe's life, returning as a ghost to guilt him into repairing his neglected friendships. His brief but memorable appearance ties into themes of mortality, mentorship, and redemption. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Beautify your hole, and you'll beautify your soul.
quotes: Beautify your hole, and you'll beautify your soul.

title: Captain Haddock
text: Captain Haddock is Fictional character from the Tintin comics who appears as a crossover reference in The Simpsons. Captain Haddock is not an original Simpsons character but a crossover figure borrowed from the famous Tintin comic book series by Hergé. Within the show's universe, he exists as a fictional sea captain who lives in Paris alongside his friend Tintin and Tintin's dog Snowy. He appears as an in-universe comic book character that Bart Simpson enjoys reading, specifically appearing on the cover of a comic Bart owns. He also shows up in a background cameo, seated in an audience in Paris. As a non-speaking character, Haddock never interacts directly with the main cast or has dialogue of his own. His inclusion is purely a nod to fans of the classic European comic series.

title: Adil Hoxha
text: Adil Hoxha is Albanian foreign exchange student who stayed with the Simpsons and turned out to be a communist spy. Adil Hoxha was a polite, well-mannered ten-year-old sent to live with the Simpson family through a foreign exchange program while Bart stayed in France. He quickly won over the household, particularly Homer, by showing genuine interest in his work at the power plant. This charm turned out to be a cover, since Adil was secretly gathering intelligence and photographs to send back to Albania under the code name Sparrow. He rigged up surveillance and communication equipment in Bart's treehouse to transmit the stolen information. Once his espionage was uncovered, a SWAT team stormed the neighborhood to capture him, but rather than face punishment, he was simply deported and swapped for an American child spy held in Albania. Despite the betrayal, the Simpsons genuinely missed him after he left, showing how likable he had been during his stay. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Mrs. Simpson, you have been oppressed enough today. I will clear the dishes. | Sparrow to Nest. Sparrow to Nest. Stand by for transmission.
quotes: Mrs. Simpson, you have been oppressed enough today. I will clear the dishes.
Sparrow to Nest. Sparrow to Nest. Stand by for transmission.

title: Billie Holiday (character)
text: Billie Holiday (character) is Real-world jazz singer referenced in the Simpsons universe, connected to Bleeding Gums Murphy. Billie Holiday is depicted as the famous American jazz singer and songwriter from real life, incorporated into the Simpsons universe as a deceased figure of legend. She's mentioned in connection with Bleeding Gums Murphy, Lisa's saxophone-playing mentor, tying her into the show's jazz mythology. In one storyline, Murphy is unable to reunite with Lisa musically because he supposedly has a date with Holiday, adding a whimsical afterlife twist to the show's treatment of deceased jazz legends. She also appears in a non-canon comic story where Lisa purchases one of her albums from a record store. Her presence in the show is minor and mostly symbolic, representing the jazz tradition that inspired Lisa's own musical passions.

title: Brian Griffin
text: Brian Griffin is Crossover character; the anthropomorphic dog of the Griffin family from Family Guy who appears in Simpsons crossover episodes. Brian Griffin is a talking dog and member of the Griffin family, brought into the Simpsons universe through crossover episodes with Family Guy. He is depicted as intelligent and personable, able to interact with the Simpson family as a peer rather than a typical pet. During a visit to Springfield, his family's car is stolen, leading to an encounter and eventual friendship with the Simpsons. He and Chris Griffin get into a bit of a comedic mishap when they lose track of Santa's Little Helper while walking him, forcing Brian to cover for the mistake. His appearances are non-canon, existing purely as fun crossover cameos rather than part of the show's main continuity. Despite being a dog, Brian carries himself with a dry, self-aware demeanor typical of his Family Guy characterization. Voiced by Seth MacFarlane.

title: Michael Jackson (character)
text: Michael Jackson (character) is Real-world musician referenced and depicted in cameo/mentions throughout The Simpsons. Michael Jackson appears as a fictionalized version of the famous pop star within the Simpsons universe, though the real Jackson himself notably voiced a character named John Jay Smith in "Stark Raving Dad" rather than playing himself outright. He's referenced repeatedly across the series, from Bart owning his Thriller album to waxworks, look-alikes, and street names bearing his name. In one episode he even shows up in person at the Springfield Squidport, showing sympathy for Bart and giving him money, leaving Homer confused about which version of Jackson was real. His pop-culture status is often used as a punchline or reference point, such as Bart comparing him to the Boogeyman. Despite rarely being seen directly, his legacy and image loom large over Springfield as a symbol of celebrity culture. Voiced by Karl Wiedergott. Notable quotes: [souls are] just something they made up to scare kids, like the Boogeyman or Michael Jackson
quotes: [souls are] just something they made up to scare kids, like the Boogeyman or Michael Jackson

title: Brad Goodman
text: Brad Goodman is A recurring self-help psychiatrist and television personality who appears in Springfield media. Brad Goodman is a laid-back, relaxed psychiatrist who preaches a philosophy of self-acceptance and letting go of inhibitions. His most notable moment comes when he encourages the citizens of Springfield to embrace their inner impulses and be more like Bart, an experiment that quickly spirals into citywide chaos. Beyond that appearance, he pops up as a minor television personality, seen discussing pop culture topics like the Radioactive Man film, and his image later turns up decorating the walls of local businesses. In non-canon media, he even has his own self-help video dealing with pain. The character is essentially a parody vehicle for his voice actor Albert Brooks, both visually and vocally modeled after him.
