Despite his limited screen time, he became memorable enough to warrant his own action figure in a Simpsons collectible line. Voiced by Albert Brooks.

title: Charlton Heston
text: Charlton Heston is Fictionalized version of the real-life American film actor, appearing as a guest character in The Simpsons universe. Charlton Heston appears in the show as a caricature of the real-world Hollywood legend, known for his commanding, larger-than-life screen presence. He's referenced most for his role as Taylor in Planet of the Apes, an association that recurs throughout multiple episodes. In one storyline he takes on the part of Judah Ben-Hur for a Springfield production, poking fun at his classic epic film roles. Other characters, like Principal Skinner, invoke his name as a symbol of dignified, authoritative wisdom. Even after his real-life death, the show continued referencing him, including a posthumous digital cameo in a commercial and a joking comparison drawn by Grampa Simpson during a monkey attack. Different voice actors have portrayed him across his various appearances, reflecting his recurring but non-central role in the show's universe. Voiced by Phil Hartman. Notable quotes: If Chuck Heston can whip your butts, so can I! (Abraham Simpson, referencing Heston)
quotes: If Chuck Heston can whip your butts, so can I! (Abraham Simpson, referencing Heston)

title: Tonya Harding
text: Tonya Harding is Real-world figure skater referenced as a minor character in the Simpsons universe. Tonya Harding appears in the show as a caricature of her real-life notoriety rather than as a developed character. She is mentioned by Krusty the Clown, who is accused of marketing videos of her wedding night during a scandal-plagued press conference. In another episode, Professor Frink shows a clip of her infamous attack on fellow skater Nancy Kerrigan with a pipe while skating, directly referencing the real-world scandal that made her famous. She also makes a brief non-canon appearance in a Treehouse of Horror segment, seen aboard a rocket headed into the sun as part of a mass suicide gag. Harding never speaks in any of her appearances, functioning purely as a pop-culture reference point for the writers. Her presence in the show is tied entirely to her real-life reputation rather than any original characterization.

title: John (Cockamamie's)
text: John (Cockamamie's) is Owner of Cockamamie's Collectibles Shop, a minor recurring character who befriends the Simpson family. John runs a quirky antique and novelty shop stuffed with kitschy 'camp' collectibles in Springfield. He's openly gay and quickly becomes friendly with the Simpsons after appraising an item in their home, even taking them on a tour of the town. Homer initially enjoys his company but turns cold once he realizes John is homosexual, worrying his influence might be rubbing off on Bart. Their friction resolves after John heroically rescues Homer from an attack by wild reindeer during an ill-advised hunting trip, using a novelty robot Santa to scare them away. Afterward he is shown wearing one of Homer's old bowling shirts, apparently given away by Marge. He resurfaces in later appearances tied to LGBT storylines, including hints of a relationship with Waylon Smithers and use of a gay dating app. Voiced by John Waters.

title: Aunt June
text: Aunt June is Aunt and guardian of Rod Runtledge (Fallout Boy) in the Radioactive Man comic-book series. Aunt June is a minor character who appears only within the pages of the in-universe Radioactive Man comics. She lives next door to Gloria Grand while raising her nephew Rod, keeping a watchful and somewhat scolding eye on his comings and goings. Her health is fragile, and she suffers from recurring 'brain fevers' that eventually force her into a nursing home, leaving Rod without a guardian. This plot point conveniently sets up Rod's move into the household of Claude Kane III. She's a clear parody of Aunt May from the Spider-Man comics, mirroring the trope of the elderly, caretaking aunt to a young superhero sidekick. Aunt June never appears in the actual Springfield-based storylines, existing solely as a piece of the comic-within-a-comic lore.

title: Howie
text: Howie is Minor recurring character, a kid who frequents Noiseland Video Arcade. Howie is a self-styled cool kid known for wearing sunglasses and spending his time at Noiseland Video Arcade. He appears confident and skilled at video games, positioning himself as someone with expertise to share. In his most notable appearance, he takes on the role of mentor, teaching Homer strategies to beat Bart at a video-game boxing match. His moment of coaching authority is cut short when his mother shows up and pulls him away, revealing he's still just a kid despite his cool demeanor. This leads to an awkward moment where his mother chastises Homer for playing games with children. Howie mostly serves as a background character populating the world of Springfield Elementary students and arcade regulars. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Gregory House
text: Gregory House is Crossover character from the TV series House, appearing briefly in The Simpsons. Gregory House is not a native Simpsons character but a crossover figure from the medical drama House, where he is portrayed by Hugh Laurie. Within the Simpsons universe, he appears mainly as a reference point when Lisa watches an episode of his show. His main trait carried over is his tendency toward misdiagnosis, which is referenced when Bart gets distracted from a chore during one of his incorrect diagnoses on screen. In a non-canon Halloween segment, he shows up in a more exaggerated, comedic fashion, attempting to promote his TV show at an inopportune moment. That cameo ends badly for him, played for slapstick horror-comedy effect. He has no dialogue in his Simpsons appearances, making him a silent, background pop-culture nod rather than a fully developed character.

title: Mother Goose
text: Mother Goose is A minor background character depicted as a statue at Storytown Village, a nursery-rhyme themed amusement park in Springfield. Mother Goose exists in the show mostly as an inanimate figure rather than a living character, appearing as a statue among other nursery rhyme attractions at Storytown Village. Her most memorable moment comes when Bart Simpson's trolley ride crashes into the Paul Bunyan statue, sending the lumberjack's axe flying into her, decapitating the figure in a darkly comic bit of park mayhem. The broken statue is left standing as junky scenery even after the park shuts down and gets rebranded into the religious-themed Praiseland. Beyond her physical appearances, she's also referenced in a lullaby Marge sings to Bart, tying her to the show's recurring theme of children's stories and nursery rhyme nostalgia. She has no real personality of her own, functioning purely as set dressing and a punchline prop rather than an active character. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: The Hounds
text: The Hounds is Mr. Burns' pack of guard dogs, used to attack unwanted visitors on his property. The Hounds are a group of cropped-eared Dobermans owned by Mr. Burns, kept specifically to menace or attack anyone he doesn't want trespassing on his estate. Despite being called hounds, they're technically pinschers, a fact tied into a running joke about Mr. Burns' outdated, old-fashioned vocabulary. Several individual dogs have been identified as part of the pack over the years, including some former members who no longer serve in the role. In a softer twist on their usual menacing purpose, a group known as the Therapy Hounds were once sent by Burns to comfort Homer after a humiliating public speech. The command to unleash them has become one of Mr. Burns' most memorable and chilling catchphrases. Overall, the Hounds function as a recurring symbol of Burns' cold, aristocratic cruelty toward the working class of Springfield. Voiced by Frank Welker. Notable quotes: Release the hounds.
quotes: Release the hounds.

title: Julie
text: Julie is A recurring Springfield Court judge who presides over several notable cases involving the Simpson family. Julie is one of Springfield's judges, known for handling a variety of legal matters involving the Simpsons and other townsfolk. She is the one who stripped Homer of his driver's license following a DUI incident, showing her willingness to enforce the law strictly. She also presided over a notable civil case between Freddy Quimby and Mr. Lacoste, and later ordered Homer and Marge to attend a parenting class after their children were removed by social services. Beyond the courtroom, Julie expanded her career into television, hosting her own court show, blending her judicial authority with a media presence. Her career took an unexpected turn when she was arrested alongside Krusty the Clown while vacationing, adding a comedic twist to her otherwise serious profession. Overall, she serves as a recurring authority figure whose rulings often intersect with the chaotic lives of Springfield's residents. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Arnie Gumble
text: Arnie Gumble is Barney Gumble's deceased father and a World War II veteran of the Flying Hellfish unit. Arnie Gumble served as a Private Fifth Class in the Flying Hellfish, the same World War II unit led by Grampa Simpson, where his job was watching his fellow soldiers' backs from inside a tank. He joined his unit's infamous tontine, an agreement that whoever outlived the rest would inherit a stash of looted paintings, reportedly hoping the wealth would elevate him into high society. His life ended in 1979 when he was one of five tontine members killed together in a bizarre parade float accident. As Barney's father, his relationship with his son seems to have been distant or strained, hinted at through an odd remark Barney makes about him during a near-death experience. Arnie appears only briefly in flashbacks and mentions, making him a minor but historically important figure tied to the show's WWII backstory. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "my loved ones, my dad, and that plant I never watered"
quotes: "my loved ones, my dad, and that plant I never watered"

title: J. Jonah Jameson
text: J. Jonah Jameson is A poetry publisher who appears in a crossover cameo with Moe Szyslak, based on the Spider-Man character. J. Jonah Jameson is a fast-talking, hot-tempered publisher who crosses over into the Simpsons universe when he agrees to print Moe's poem. True to his comic-book and film persona, he flies into erratic rages, hiring and firing the same employee within seconds while somehow becoming and un-becoming friends with him in the same breath. Despite the chaos he creates, he cheerfully declares his love for his job, showing he thrives on the stress. He also has a recurring interest in Spider-Man, requesting photos and poems about the superhero. In a non-canon appearance, his obsession with Spider-Man photos leads him into a deal with Peter Griffin. The role is a nod to actor J. K. Simmons' famous portrayal of the same character in the Spider-Man film franchise. Voiced by J. K. Simmons. Notable quotes: He then says that he loves his job.
quotes: He then says that he loves his job.

title: George Harrison (character)
text: George Harrison (character) is Real-world musician (member of The Beatles) who appears as a guest character in The Simpsons. George Harrison appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, tied to his real-life fame as a Beatles guitarist. He crosses paths with Krusty the Clown and later with Homer Simpson at a Grammy after-party, where Homer's obsession with brownies leaves Harrison bemused rather than offended. He later reappears during a Be Sharps reunion, dismissing their rooftop performance as unoriginal since the Beatles already did it. The character is used mostly for comedic cameos referencing real Beatles history, such as their famous rooftop concert. He also turns up in archive footage and one comic strip continuity involving a young Homer and Abe Simpson being mistaken for the band. Voiced by Himself / Chris Edgerly. Notable quotes: Oh my God, Oh my God. Where did you get that brownie? | Wow, what a nice fellow. | It's been done.
quotes: Oh my God, Oh my God. Where did you get that brownie?
Wow, what a nice fellow.
It's been done.

title: Randy Jackson (character)
text: Randy Jackson (character) is Real-life celebrity guest character who appears as an American Idol judge in Springfield. Randy Jackson is a fictionalized version of the real musician and television personality, appearing in the show in his familiar role as an American Idol judge. He shows up when Moe Szyslak improbably becomes a fellow judge on the panel, and his critique of a contestant is so vague that nobody can tell if he means it as praise or criticism. This ambiguity becomes a bit of a running joke, with Ryan Seacrest having to ask viewers to interpret the response themselves. Beyond his judging duties, he's shown mingling in Springfield's celebrity social scene, attending a charity event. As a guest-starring cameo character, he doesn't have much personality development beyond playing off his real-world persona as an enigmatic, catchphrase-prone judge. Voiced by Randy Jackson (Himself).

title: Wolfguy Jack
text: Wolfguy Jack is Owner of Greaser's Cafe, a minor character who appeared in the biker episode featuring Homer. Wolfguy Jack is a gruff, gravelly-voiced biker cafe owner who serves as an obvious parody of the real-life radio DJ Wolfman Jack. True to his name, he has a habit of howling, though he claims his throat doctor has warned him to cut back on it. He ran Greaser's Cafe, a biker hangout that eventually went out of business. Within the show's continuity, he hosted a dance competition at his establishment and was the one who gave Homer his Harley-Davidson motorcycle. Beyond his single major appearance, he's remained a minor recurring figure, popping up in archive footage and later in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Mr. Glasscock
text: Mr. Glasscock is A supply teacher at Springfield Elementary who briefly appears in the series. Mr. Glasscock is a minor, largely forgettable substitute teacher at Springfield Elementary whose unfortunate surname becomes the source of constant classroom ridicule. His tenure is short-lived, as relentless teasing from students eventually drives him to quit the job. Bart and Principal Skinner attempt to curb the mockery, but it isn't enough to keep him around once Lisa's scheme to hide all the Teacher's Edition books adds to the chaos. Despite Skinner's efforts to talk him out of resigning, Glasscock leaves the school for good. He later resurfaces briefly as a background character near Ned Flanders' storm-wrecked house, showing he still lives in Springfield even after his teaching days ended. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Ash Ketchum
text: Ash Ketchum is Crossover character from the Pokémon franchise appearing within a Simpsons episode. Ash Ketchum is a guest crossover character brought into the Simpsons universe from the Pokémon TV series. He shows up as a character within a show-within-a-show that Bart watches, interacting with his partner Pikachu in a typical adventure moment. He later becomes fodder for a drug-fueled hallucination when Homer and Ned imagine themselves as a parody version of Ash and Pikachu. In a non-canon Halloween story, his likeness inspires Milhouse's costume, leading to a punny exchange with Lenny about the horror character Ash Williams. Ash himself doesn't have an original personality within the Simpsons universe since he is simply borrowed from his source material for parody and reference gags. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: "My Ash can kick your Ash's... um... Ash!"
quotes: "My Ash can kick your Ash's... um... Ash!"

title: Irish policeman
text: Irish policeman is A minor recurring Springfield police officer who appears in various episodes. The Irish policeman is a background member of the Springfield Police Force, distinguished mainly by his orange hair and Irish accent. He's shown leading the officers during the St. Patrick's Day parade, giving him a bit of thematic significance tied to his heritage. He also handled the arrest of L.T. Smash, showing he takes part in more serious police duties beyond ceremonial ones. His personality comes through in a comedic moment where he teases Ned Flanders about his date, sarcastically claiming he himself was off to go apple picking with Scooby-Doo. He's a minor but recurring face on the force, later appearing with gray hair in a flashback, suggesting he's been part of the Springfield PD for a long time. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: He was going apple picking with Scooby-Doo.
quotes: He was going apple picking with Scooby-Doo.

title: Julius Hibbert's daughter
text: Julius Hibbert's daughter is Minor recurring character; unnamed daughter of Dr. Julius and Bernice Hibbert, sister to JJ Hibbert and an unnamed older brother. This character is the unnamed daughter of Springfield's Dr. Hibbert and his wife Bernice, rounding out the Hibbert family alongside her brothers JJ and an unnamed older sibling. She appears as a background child in Springfield, attending Springfield Preparatory School rather than the usual elementary school. In one of her more notable appearances, she weighs in on where the family should eat before they end up at Moe's Tavern, and she isn't shy about voicing her opinion on the place's unpleasant smell. She also shows a curious streak, questioning her father about the town's odd enthusiasm for the return of the Stinging Red Jellyfish. Though she has appeared across many episodes over the show's run, she remains a minor, largely background figure without a defined personality beyond these small moments. Voiced by Russi Taylor / Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: The daughter said the place smelled like tinkle.
quotes: The daughter said the place smelled like tinkle.

title: Hydrangea
text: Hydrangea is A superhero member of the Vindicators who appears in the Simpsons universe's superhero franchise. Hydrangea is a plant-themed superhero who fights alongside her fellow Vindicators against the villain Chinnos. She has a romantic connection with fellow hero Moby Man, sharing a poignant moment with him as they are both turned to crystal during battle. Her design and powers seem to blend traits of Black Widow and Poison Ivy, giving her a mix of stealthy heroism and plant-based abilities. She later plays a mentor-like role for Bart Simpson, pulling him into a virtual reality world to teach him that superheroes are real and that piracy has real consequences within their fictional universe. Despite being a relatively minor character, she has proven popular enough to inspire cosplay and merchandise like figures within the show's world. Voiced by Cobie Smulders. Notable quotes: "I'll take that dance now." - Hydrangea, to Moby Man | "Don't pirate movies. It hurts everyone." - Hydrangea, to Bart
quotes: "I'll take that dance now." - Hydrangea, to Moby Man
"Don't pirate movies. It hurts everyone." - Hydrangea, to Bart

title: Park Ranger Johnson
text: Park Ranger Johnson is A park ranger stationed at the Springfield Glacier, appearing in a minor role in the Simpsons universe. Park Ranger Johnson oversees the Springfield Glacier and represents a satirical jab at government denial of environmental issues. When confronted with evidence that the glacier is melting, he dismisses the concern by parroting an official stance that climate change isn't real. He also displays a quirky, dry sense of humor about his personal life, joking about being 'married' to the glacier itself. His deadpan delivery and absurd devotion to his post make him a brief but memorable comedic figure. Johnson's appearance ties into the show's recurring commentary on real-world political and environmental topics. He later reappears in a non-canon capacity within the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Johnson told her that he was married to the glacier, but it was an open marriage.
quotes: Johnson told her that he was married to the glacier, but it was an open marriage.

title: Kako
text: Kako is Barney Gumble's girlfriend during his time in the Be-Sharps. Kako is a minor character best known as a clear parody of Yoko Ono, mirroring her role of disrupting a famous band's harmony. She became involved with Barney Gumble while he was a member of the barbershop quartet Be-Sharps, and the two are credited with creating the song 'Number 8' together. Her presence coincides with tension in the group, echoing the real-life dynamic often attributed to Ono and the Beatles. Interestingly, she also appears in a completely unrelated context, taking a citizenship test alongside Apu, Luigi, and Moe. Her name was never actually spoken on screen, only later confirmed in an official episode guide, adding a layer of trivia to her otherwise brief appearances. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Homer II
text: Homer II is A non-canon half-human, half-plant creature created by Lisa, appearing in Simpsons comic books. Homer II is a monstrous plant-human hybrid born from one of Lisa's scientific experiments gone awry, combining plant DNA with Homer's own. After dying and mysteriously reviving, it develops an insatiable hunger for donuts, growing to an enormous and dangerous size. Its rampage escalates when it devours both Mr. Burns and Smithers, who had come to try to purchase it. Homer ultimately seems to destroy the creature by setting it ablaze, though unsettling hints suggest a piece of it survives, still reaching for donuts, and another fragment turns up preserved in a jar in Dr. Nick's office. The character is a clear comic-book parody of Audrey II from Little Shop of Horrors, right down to the title of the story it appears in.

title: Jim Hope
text: Jim Hope is Former teacher and president of Kid First Industries, a toy company that took over Springfield Elementary School. Jim Hope runs Kid First Industries, the corporation that buys out and privatizes a bankrupted Springfield Elementary School. Under the guise of education, his company secretly spies on students through hidden cameras and two-way blackboards to gather ideas for a new toy. He comes across as a friendly, business-savvy executive, even personally handing out a free sample of the resulting toy, Funzo, to the Simpson kids. Despite his polished exterior, his operation reveals a willingness to exploit children for corporate profit, forming the central conflict Lisa uncovers in her investigation. He later appears among a mob of angry townspeople demanding Homer's death after an environmental disaster at Lake Springfield. His role highlights the show's recurring satire of corporate greed and marketing schemes targeting children. Voiced by Tim Robbins.

title: Leslie Hapablap
text: Leslie Hapablap is An Air Force colonel and minor recurring character in Springfield. Colonel Leslie "Hap" Hapablap is a gruff military officer known for his short temper and foul mouth, especially when things don't go his way. His tendency to cuss out fellow soldiers over minor annoyances, like someone using his restroom, once created a security loophole that Sideshow Bob exploited to sneak into a nuclear warhead storage facility. Despite his hard-edged demeanor, he's shown popping up in everyday Springfield life, even offering advice to Lisa about getting gum out of her hair. He mostly appears as a background or one-off character rather than a central figure. His military bearing and irritable nature are his defining comedic traits. Voiced by R. Lee Ermey.

title: Judo Mummy
text: Judo Mummy is A fictional character within the show's fictional media franchise Ki-Ya Karate Monsters, not a member of the main Simpsons cast. Judo Mummy is a minor character who exists only within the show-within-a-show franchise Ki-Ya Karate Monsters. As his name suggests, he is an undead mummy warrior whose specialty is judo, blending classic monster-movie imagery with martial arts action. He has no spoken lines in the actual episodes of The Simpsons, appearing instead as background merchandise, such as a wall sticker seen in Comic Book Guy's apartment. This placement reinforces Comic Book Guy's obsessive fandom for niche pop-culture properties. Judo Mummy's presence is largely a visual gag and world-building detail rather than a character with personality traits shown on screen. He remains a recurring but silent piece of set dressing tied to the fictional franchise's aesthetic.

title: Jakob
text: Jakob is Israeli tour guide who leads the Simpson family's tour of Israel. Jakob is a brash, hand-gesturing tour guide who escorts the Simpsons around Israel, leaning heavily into an exaggerated, stereotypical Israeli persona. He's blunt to the point of rudeness, repeatedly telling his tour group to shut up and shut their faces, seemingly unaware or unbothered that this comes across as offensive to English speakers. He works alongside his niece Dorit, who assists him on the tour. Adding a darker edge to his tough-guy image, he hints that he participated in the real-world 1976 Entebbe hostage rescue, claiming to have killed three Ugandans during the operation. Beyond his one canonical appearance, he shows up briefly in a non-canon future vision as a Facebook friend request on Lisa's futuristic social network. Voiced by Sacha Baron Cohen. Notable quotes: Yalla, b'seder, you can shut up now!
quotes: Yalla, b'seder, you can shut up now!

title: Kathy
text: Kathy is Minor recurring character; a personnel worker at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. Kathy is a background employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, working in the personnel department. She's mostly known through a brief, awkward encounter involving Homer and Mr. Burns, where her personality became an unwitting punchline. She appears calm and professional when addressed by Burns, giving a simple, upbeat response despite the tense situation around her. Kathy has since made minor appearances in other episodes and in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, where she appears as a non-canon character. She has grey hair, suggesting she's an older employee, and doesn't have any notable relatives or deep backstory revealed. Overall, she serves as a minor recurring face among the Power Plant's staff. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: "excellent."
quotes: "excellent."

title: Princess Kemi
text: Princess Kemi is A Nigerian princess who visits Springfield and becomes involved with Homer and Moe. Princess Kemi is the daughter of a Nigerian king who comes to Springfield while her father negotiates a uranium deal with Mr. Burns. Homer is tasked with watching over her, but her heritage sparks suspicion from Moe, who fears she might be tied to a scam after his own past experience with a Nigerian prince hoax. Despite his initial wariness, Moe warms up to Kemi and ends up showing her around Springfield, leading to an unexpected romantic connection between them. Her story introduces a mix of culture clash, comic misunderstanding, and a surprisingly tender relationship with Moe. She's depicted as adventurous and curious about American life, willing to explore beyond the confines of her hotel and royal duties. Ultimately, her brief romance with Moe has real consequences, nearly derailing her father's business deal with Burns. Voiced by Yaya DaCosta.

title: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
text: Ruth Bader Ginsburg is Real-world Supreme Court Justice referenced and briefly depicted in various Simpsons media. Ruth Bader Ginsburg appears in the Simpsons universe mostly as a real-world reference rather than a fully developed character. She's brought up in conversation, shown in pictures, and listed among notable progressive figures on Ned Flanders' list of admirable liberals. Her name gets played with for jokes, such as being confused with poet Allen Ginsberg or mashed up with Darth Vader by Bart to create the character Darth Vader Ginsburg. In a non-canon storyline, she's depicted being forcibly removed from the Supreme Court and replaced by Ivanka Trump, leading to a chaotic confrontation with security. Overall, she serves as a cultural touchstone used for quick references and satirical jabs rather than a recurring personality within the show's main narrative. Voiced by Carolyn Omine.

title: Jeremy Irons (character)
text: Jeremy Irons (character) is Real-world English actor referenced within the show's fictional universe (not the guest-starring version). This version of Jeremy Irons exists only as a cultural reference within the Simpsons universe rather than an actual appearing character. His likeness appears on a Brideshead Revisited lunchbox owned by a gifted student named Tanya. He's also referenced when Lisa plays an anagram game with Allison Taylor, cleverly rearranging his name into "Jeremy's iron." Despite her cleverness, the joke falls flat with Allison's father, showing how her intellectual humor often goes over people's heads. Irons himself never physically appears as a character, only existing through these brief pop-culture nods. Notable quotes: "Jeremy's iron"
quotes: "Jeremy's iron"

title: Mugger
text: Mugger is An unnamed criminal who mugs Marge Simpson, sparking her journey into bodybuilding. This nameless mugger is a minor but memorable antagonist defined by his trenchcoat and Goofy-branded hat. He robs Marge of her necklace during a nighttime encounter, leaving her traumatized and afraid to leave the house afterward. His attack indirectly kickstarts one of Marge's most notable character arcs, as she takes up weightlifting to rebuild her confidence. Fittingly, he becomes the instrument of her triumphant redemption when their paths cross again and she overpowers him in a public beatdown. Outside of this storyline, he later appears as a background townsperson during the Springfield dome crisis. He's a one-note but pivotal figure whose brief menace triggers real character growth for Marge. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Whatcha been up to? Livin' in fear?
quotes: Whatcha been up to? Livin' in fear?

title: Yao Ming (character)
text: Yao Ming (character) is Real-world basketball star who appears as a guest character in The Simpsons. Yao Ming appears as a fictionalized version of himself who gets roped into Homer Simpson's Showboating Academy, a class meant to teach athletes how to perform obnoxious victory celebrations. He shows a mischievous streak by pretending not to understand English when Marge asks for help cleaning up after dinner, only to be caught out by Lisa, who knows he speaks it fluently. Rather than admit it, he bluntly tells her to back off since his ruse was working out well for him. Despite his tough front, he's later seen doing more humble tasks like ironing clothes around the Simpsons' house. He also takes part in the chaotic finale of Homer's Super Bowl halftime show alongside the other athletes. In a non-canon appearance, he shows up as a celebrity attendee at a Simpsons season finale premiere. Voiced by Himself. Notable quotes: Ming then told Lisa to shut up as he had a good thing going on here.
quotes: Ming then told Lisa to shut up as he had a good thing going on here.

title: Magneto
text: Magneto is Marvel Comics supervillain who appears as a minor pop-culture reference/cameo in The Simpsons universe. Magneto, whose real name is Erik Lehnsherr, is a Marvel Comics villain referenced a handful of times within the Simpsons franchise rather than being a true recurring cast member. He first shows up as a character played by a child in a stage production about the Royalty Valhalla, where he insists that humans must be ruled. His likeness also turns up as a costume worn by fans at the Comicalooza convention, showing his status as a recognizable pop-culture icon within the show's world. Milhouse compares the intensity of certain hatred to that of Magneto and Emperor Palpatine, using him as a shorthand for dramatic villainy. In a playful mash-up created by Bart, Magneto is combined with actor James Cagney to form the hybrid character Cagneto. Overall, Magneto functions less as an active character and more as a running cultural reference used for humor and homage. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: The kind of hate only found in Magnetos, Emperors Palpatine and little girls! - Milhouse
quotes: The kind of hate only found in Magnetos, Emperors Palpatine and little girls! - Milhouse

title: Eugene Levy
text: Eugene Levy is Real-world Canadian actor/writer who appears as a minor reference within the show. Eugene Levy is depicted in the show as a fictionalized version of the real Canadian actor and writer, appearing only briefly and without any spoken dialogue. His main claim to fame within the Simpsons universe is playing the king in a movie called Princess Rock Star, which Homer attempts to watch with Lisa in an effort to bond with her. Later, he becomes the subject of an odd bit of Springfield civic history when a statue originally made from melted-down cannonballs and modeled after Joe Paterno is altered to resemble him instead. He functions purely as a background gag and pop-culture cameo rather than a developed character, never speaking on screen. His inclusion highlights the show's habit of referencing real celebrities in absurd, tangential ways.

title: Larva Girl
text: Larva Girl is A supervillain from the in-universe "Radioactive Man" comic book series, serving as a recurring antagonist to the superhero Radioactive Man.. Larva Girl is a green-haired villainess who appears exclusively within the fictional comic books read by Bart and his friends. Her defining scheme involves manipulating Radioactive Man into falling in love with her and agreeing to marry her, using his altered molecular structure and exposure to an alien sun to control his emotions. She kidnaps Fallout Boy as leverage, forcing Radioactive Man to travel to a distant planet to retrieve a ransom of rare gems. Her wedding plot is ultimately foiled when another character interferes with an antidote hidden in lipstick, breaking the spell she cast over her intended husband. Even after being defeated, she resurfaces in later comic appearances, sometimes as a hologram or in unrelated fights, showing she remains a persistent fixture of the Radioactive Man mythology. As a comic-book creation, she never interacts directly with the main Simpsons cast, existing only within the pages the characters read.

title: Yo-Yo Ma (character)
text: Yo-Yo Ma (character) is A celebrity guest character based on the real-life cellist Yo-Yo Ma, who appears occasionally in Springfield. Yo-Yo Ma is a fictionalized version of the famous real-world cellist, appearing as a recurring celebrity cameo in the show. He's shown to be part of a mob of PBS personalities chasing down Homer, tying into the show's habit of lampooning public broadcasting figures. He's also brought in for high-society occasions, such as playing cello at Jacqueline Bouvier's 80th birthday party at the request of Mr. Burns. In a lighter, more mundane moment, he's seen reading a diet book while Patty and Selma pester him with pictures. His name is even used as a punchline by Principal Skinner when comparing success and failure, and he's referenced again by Dewey Largo alongside real conductor Gustavo Dudamel. Overall, Yo-Yo Ma exists in the show as a nod to real-world classical music culture rather than as a fully developed character. Voiced by Hank Azaria / Yo-Yo Ma (Himself).

title: Rhoda Morgenstern
text: Rhoda Morgenstern is A minor crossover/reference character based on the TV show Rhoda, appearing only as a picture in The Simpsons. Rhoda Morgenstern is not an original Simpsons character but a reference to the title character of the 1970s sitcom Rhoda. She appears only visually, never speaking, first shown on a poster advertising her own show within a fictional TV listing. She later resurfaces in a comic book crossover with Batman, playing on the absurdity of unrelated franchises colliding. Her inclusion is purely a nostalgic nod for fans familiar with classic television, tying into actress Valerie Harper's real-life connection to The Simpsons as a recurring guest star. She has no personality or dialogue established within the show itself, existing solely as a background gag and pop-culture reference.

title: Angela Merkel
text: Angela Merkel is Real-world political figure (former German Chancellor) who appears as a character in the show. Angela Merkel is depicted as a retired German politician and scientist who once led the country as chancellor. In her appearance on the show, she attends a RedStar board meeting where she gets into an amusing exchange with Charli D'Amelio about how she 'monetizes' being a voice of reason in Europe. She also plays a small role in the political drama surrounding Augustus Redfield, casting a vote against his removal. In a later episode, she becomes the subject of a silly conspiracy theory investigated by Hans and Horst, who believe she was actually born in Brazil. Overall, she's used as a cameo-style real-world figure inserted into absurd Simpsons scenarios rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: "I am often the only voice of reason in all of Europe." - Angela Merkel
quotes: "I am often the only voice of reason in all of Europe." - Angela Merkel

title: Alfred Nobel
text: Alfred Nobel is Historical figure referenced in the show; Swedish chemist and creator of the Nobel Prize, appearing in cameo/parody form. Alfred Nobel appears in the show as a real-world historical figure rather than a regular cast member, honored for inventing dynamite and establishing the Nobel Prize. His likeness turns up in odd, comedic contexts, such as a picture used in a fantasy sequence and an ice sculpture at a fictional afterparty. In one memorable gag, Al Gore treats his own Nobel Prize medal as if it could speak, impersonating Nobel's voice while venting about a stolen election. The character functions less as a personality and more as a running visual/verbal joke tied to the prestige of the award bearing his name. His portrait, always shown facing left, is noted as appearing on every medal awarded in his honor. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Linguo
text: Linguo is A grammar-correcting robot built by Lisa Simpson for a school science fair. Linguo is a small robotic invention created by Lisa Simpson to automatically correct people's grammatical mistakes. Its defining trait is an obsessive, almost comedic devotion to proper grammar, correcting anyone within earshot whenever they misspeak. This quirk leads to its downfall, as it overheats and explodes after being overwhelmed by a barrage of grammatical errors from the Springfield Mafia. Even in its final moment, Linguo's programming compels it to correct Homer's grammar before dying, blending tragedy with dry humor. The robot also appears in various non-canon material, including video games and comic tie-ins, often used for comedic or gameplay purposes. Overall, Linguo represents Lisa's intellectual creativity as well as the show's love of grammar-based jokes. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Linguo is dead
quotes: Linguo is dead

title: Hettie Mae Boggs
text: Hettie Mae Boggs is A homeless folk singer whom Bart and Lisa encounter and briefly take in. Hettie Mae Boggs is a homeless woman originally from Lickskillet, Kentucky, whom Bart meets after her shopping cart ends up stuck beneath a lake. She ends up living temporarily in the closets of Bart and Lisa's rooms. Despite her rough circumstances, she turns out to have a remarkable talent for folk singing, which impresses Lisa enough to try to arrange a concert for her. True to her skittish nature, Hettie flees to Cletus's farm rather than face the spotlight, and only performs once nearly everyone else has left the venue. Her gentle, wandering spirit is underscored by Lisa's kindness in offering her a place to sleep after hearing her sing. She also appears in a surreal, imagined story from Marge's mind, where she's locked away in an asylum and later rescued by fictional alter-egos of the family. Voiced by Kate McKinnon (Natalie Maines for singing).

title: Methuselah
text: Methuselah is Minor biblical figure referenced in a Simpsons trading card and appearing in Bart's dream sequence. Methuselah is a background biblical character loosely woven into the show's parody of scripture. He's depicted as King David's oldest friend, giving him a personal connection to one of the Bible's most famous figures. His main claim to fame within the show is being killed by Goliath II, the vengeful son of the giant David slew with a slingshot. This act of revenge is what spurs David to hunt down and kill Goliath II in turn, making Methuselah's death a minor plot catalyst in a dream sequence. Outside of that non-canon appearance, he exists in the Simpsons universe merely as an image printed on a religious-themed trading card handed out by Ned Flanders. He has no real personality of his own, functioning purely as a reference point for the show's biblical satire. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Don Mattingly (character)
text: Don Mattingly (character) is Real-life baseball player recruited by Mr. Burns to play on the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant softball team in "Homer at the Bat". Don Mattingly appears as a fictionalized version of himself, brought in by Waylon Smithers to bolster the power plant's softball roster ahead of a big game against Shelbyville. He comes across as good-natured and easygoing, welcoming Smithers into his home without hesitation. His storyline becomes a running gag about Mr. Burns' ignorance, as Burns fixates on Mattingly's "sideburns" without understanding what they actually are. Despite trying to comply by shaving the sides of his head, Mattingly is unfairly kicked off the team by an irrationally angry Burns. He takes the dismissal in stride, even managing a dry joke comparing Burns favorably to another famously demanding boss. The character is a one-off celebrity cameo tied specifically to the softball episode, though later referenced in archive footage and other media. Voiced by Don Mattingly (Himself). Notable quotes: I still like him better than Steinbrenner.
quotes: I still like him better than Steinbrenner.

title: Moby Dick (character)
text: Moby Dick (character) is Fictional giant sperm whale from Herman Melville's novel, referenced within The Simpsons universe. Moby Dick is a legendary white sperm whale, best known as the antagonist of the classic novel by Herman Melville. Within the Simpsons universe, he appears as a background or referenced figure rather than a fully developed character, tying into the show's fondness for literary crossovers. According to family lore recounted by Abraham Simpson, one of Homer's ancestors served on a whaling ship that crossed paths with the massive creature. That ancestor's obsession with whale meat led to a bizarre and fatal encounter, linking Moby Dick to the Simpson family's strange history. He is depicted as non-canon and non-speaking, appearing mostly in picture cameos rather than active scenes. His notability comes largely from serving as a nod to classic literature within the show's comedic framework.

title: Meth lab owner
text: Meth lab owner is Minor recurring character; a criminal owner of a meth lab mistaken by Homer for a restaurant. The meth lab owner is a bald, mustached criminal who runs an illicit drug operation out of 1501 East Oak Street. He becomes unexpectedly involved with the Simpsons family when Homer wanders into his lab, mistaking it for a restaurant called El Chemistri. Despite his dangerous profession, he almost casually offers Homer crystal meth before chaos erupts when police storm the building. His downfall comes courtesy of Marge, who uses a bizarre and comedic method involving apple pie to subdue him, exploiting a deep-seated nostalgic weakness for his mother's cooking. He appears only briefly, serving as a one-off gag character rather than a developed personality. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Morton Mankiewicz
text: Morton Mankiewicz is Elderly creator of the Radioactive Man comic book character, appearing in Simpsons Comics/Bongo stories. Morton Mankiewicz, better known by his pen name Morty Mann, is the original artist and creator behind the Radioactive Man comic franchise. Now an elderly resident of the Springfield Retirement Castle, he represents the classic trope of the artist who was cheated out of the rights to his own creation, having sold them off for a mere $250. Despite his advanced age, he remains connected to his legacy character, stepping back into action when that legacy is threatened. His storyline highlights themes of exploitation in the comic book industry and generational nostalgia. He forms an unlikely alliance with Bart Simpson to protect Radioactive Man from being killed off by the publisher, showing that beneath his frail exterior he still cares deeply about his creation.

title: Marcus Le Marquez
text: Marcus Le Marquez is A jazz musician who recruits Bart into his band as a drummer. Marcus "Marbles" Le Marquez is a bass-playing jazz musician who, alongside his bandmate Defonzo "Skinny" Palmer, discovers Bart's talent for drumming and invites him to join their group under the nickname "Tick-Tock." He treats Bart as a genuine member of the band rather than a novelty, even organizing a benefit concert to pay for surgery after Bart injures his arm. Marbles has a tragic personal history, having been married to Skinny's sister until her death. He appears sporadically across the series' timeline, showing up at events like the Trappuccino gathering and the burying of Springfield's time capsule, often performing music alongside Lisa and Defonzo. In non-canon material, he continues his musical partnership with Defonzo in bizarre Treehouse of Horror scenarios and mobile game content. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Arnold Leach
text: Arnold Leach is Editor and CPO of Boffo Comics, publisher of the Radioactive Man comic. Arnold Leach is a comic book industry executive who oversees the publication of Radioactive Man for Boffo Comics. He's portrayed as a cynical, dismissive figure toward fans, at one point openly insulting his own readership as "moronic little fanboy geeks." Despite being honored for his lifetime contributions to comics with a Good Guy award, he was willing to kill off a beloved character until confronted by Bart in his Bartman persona. He is later implicated in a bigger scandal involving stealing a fan-created comic concept, leading to his arrest alongside other Boffo Comics staff. His arc shows him as a corrupt corporate figure more concerned with profit and reputation than integrity or fan loyalty. Notable quotes: "moronic little fanboy geeks" - Arnold Leach
quotes: "moronic little fanboy geeks" - Arnold Leach

title: McCrary twins
text: McCrary twins is Minor recurring characters; a pair of professional wrestlers who appear briefly in the Simpsons universe. The McCrary twins are a duo of American professional wrestlers known for their shared love of riding motorcycles. They first appear as mannequins in a store window at The Vast Waistband, spotted by Homer while he shops for new clothes after gaining weight. Later, they show up in person as surprise courtroom witnesses during a lawsuit involving Chester J. Lampwick and Itchy & Scratchy Studios, called upon by the eccentric lawyer Lionel Hutz. True to form, they make their courtroom entrance riding motorcycles rather than simply walking in. They are non-speaking characters, existing mostly as a visual gag tied to their signature motorcycle riding. Despite their brief and odd appearances, they remain a recognizable pair among the show's many background character groups.

title: Luci
text: Luci is A crossover character/personal demon appearing as a figure and hallucination in The Simpsons, originally from Matt Groening's Disenchantment. Luci is a personal demon character who originates from Matt Groening's animated series Disenchantment, making a crossover appearance in The Simpsons universe. He is mostly seen as a small collectible figure, appearing alongside statues or figurines of Princess Bean and Elfo in Comic Book Guy's apartment. In a non-canon segment, Luci appears in a Treehouse of Horror hallucination experienced by Lisa, depicted casually sitting on a wall while smoking. He doesn't speak in any of his appearances, functioning more as a background reference and nod to Groening's other show rather than an active participant in Simpsons stories. His inclusion highlights the show's tendency to reference other works by the same creator.

title: Mailman
text: Mailman is An unnamed recurring mailman who delivers mail in Springfield. The mailman is a minor recurring background character in Springfield who seems to have remarkably bad luck on the job. He was once run over by Marge and pinned under her car, yet remained calm and even good-humored about the incident, insisting it was just part of the job. While waiting for help, he casually passed the time reading a magazine, only to be dismayed when he discovered his glasses had broken. Years later, he suffered further misfortune when Elon Musk crash-landed in the Simpsons' backyard, crushing him and breaking his leg. Despite the pain, his first instinct was to call his wife to explain what had happened. He's never given a name, but his unlucky encounters with the Simpson family have made him a small but memorable fixture of the show. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Mini-Me
text: Mini-Me is Costume/character referenced when Comic Book Guy dresses up as Austin Powers villain duo Dr. Evil and Mini-Me. Mini-Me is not an original Simpsons character but a crossover reference to the Austin Powers film franchise. In the Simpsons universe, the character appears only as a costume worn by Comic Book Guy, who dressed up as both Dr. Evil and his diminutive clone Mini-Me for a Bond Parody Con in 2003. Since Mini-Me exists purely as a costume gag rather than an active participant in any storyline, the character has no dialogue or personality traits established within the show. This makes Mini-Me a non-speaking, background reference that appeals to fans of both franchises rather than a fleshed-out Simpsons character. The joke relies entirely on Comic Book Guy's penchant for elaborate pop-culture cosplay.

title: Michael Moore (character)
text: Michael Moore (character) is Real-world filmmaker and political commentator who appears as a guest character supporting Lisa's causes. This character is a fictionalized version of the real documentary filmmaker Michael Moore, appearing in Springfield as a champion of liberal causes. He backs Lisa when she organizes a student strike at her school, offering an oddly specific and unsourced statistic about unemployment among students who skip arts education. When pressed on where he got his facts, he deflects with a flippant, nonsensical answer rather than any real evidence, playing into his real-life reputation for provocative claims. Later he turns up as an unjustly detained prisoner at a reeducation camp, suggesting the show imagines a more authoritarian future where dissenting voices like his are silenced. He's also referenced by Ned Flanders, who likens his own amateur political filmmaking to Moore's work. Overall, he functions as a satirical cameo poking fun at both his documentary style and his polarizing public persona. Voiced by Michael Moore (Himself). Notable quotes: "your mother"
quotes: "your mother"

title: Molly (My Octopus and a Teacher)
text: Molly (My Octopus and a Teacher) is An octopus rescued and temporarily kept as a pet by Lisa Simpson. Molly is a purple octopus that Lisa encounters and rescues while filming an underwater documentary for a school project. After a shark bites off one of her tentacles, Lisa secretly saves her, though the film ends with a staged depiction of her death to comply with non-interference rules. Molly proves mischievous once brought home, repeatedly escaping her tank and roaming through the house's pipes, even turning up in the family dog's bowl. She becomes an unpredictable classroom companion, causing a chaotic incident during Lisa's school presentation when she latches onto Bart's face. Ultimately Lisa learns to let go of things she loves but can't keep, releasing Molly back into the ocean and protecting her one last time from the same shark. Molly never speaks, existing purely as a physical presence whose antics drive the episode's plot and themes.

title: Clubber Lang
text: Clubber Lang is A crossover character referenced in The Simpsons, from the Rocky film franchise. Clubber Lang is not an original Simpsons character but a fictional boxer borrowed from the Rocky movie franchise. His only presence in the show is through a statue outside the Philadelphia Museum of Art, which Homer stops to take a selfie with during a family trip. In a non-canon appearance, a Rocky III poster featuring Clubber Lang decorates the wall of the apartment Homer once shared with Barney. He has no lines and never appears as a living character within the show's universe, functioning purely as a nostalgic pop-culture reference. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent habit of nodding to famous films and franchises.

title: Munchie
text: Munchie is One of Homer's hippie friends and co-owner of the Groovy Grove Juice Corporation. Munchie is a laid-back, aging hippie who has been friends with Homer since the 1960s, when he also knew Mona Simpson. Alongside his fellow hippie Seth, he co-owns the Groovy Grove Juice Corporation and later runs an organic vegetable patch. He tends to be the more spontaneous and easygoing of the pair, often the first to embrace a wild idea. Over the years he and Seth appear together at major life events tied to the Simpson family, including Mona's funeral, showing their long history with Homer. He remains politically active as a member of the Springfield Democratic Party, and his name itself is a nod to the classic stoner slang for food cravings. Voiced by George Carlin.

title: Nikki McKenna
text: Nikki McKenna is A fourth-grade student at Springfield Elementary School and one of Bart Simpson's on-and-off girlfriends. Nikki McKenna is a spirited, skateboard-loving classmate of Bart's known for her unpredictable, mood-swinging personality, often described as 'Hot then Cold.' She initially resists Bart's flirtatious advances but eventually warms up to him, sharing a rooftop moment watching Michelle Obama before their relationship implodes after Bart's clumsy accident and her panicked reaction. Despite her rebellious streak and love of skateboarding, she maintains a better reputation than Bart. Her volatile temperament resurfaces in a later encounter, where she flips between affection and hostility within moments, ultimately branding Bart a stalker. Nikki's romance with Bart also triggers a schoolwide 'Hands-Off Policy' after her parents intervene with Homer and Marge. She remains a recurring, non-canon presence in spin-off media like The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Sarah Silverman. Notable quotes: "save me!"
quotes: "save me!"

title: George Meany
text: George Meany is Real-world American labor leader who appeared as a guest on Krusty the Clown's TV show within the show-within-a-show. George Meany is a fictionalized version of the real-life labor leader who makes a brief appearance as a guest on Krusty the Clown's show. He is invited on to discuss collective bargaining agreements, giving a characteristically dry, evasive answer when pressed about a labor crisis in America. His appearance is part of an old rerun episode that Krusty is forced to air during a slow summer, one that bores a bedridden Bart nearly to tears. The bit works mostly as a gag about the tedium of old, low-energy talk-show television being repeated ad nauseam. He later shows up again briefly in archive footage during the finale of Krusty's show. Otherwise, little is known about his personality beyond his measured, wonkish way of speaking. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Well, that depends what you mean by 'crisis'
quotes: Well, that depends what you mean by 'crisis'

title: Charles Manson
text: Charles Manson is Real-world criminal and cult leader referenced within the Simpsons universe. Charles Manson appears in the world of The Simpsons mostly as a historical or pop-culture reference rather than a fleshed-out character. He's briefly brought up by Homer, who oddly notes that Manson once aspired to be a musician, poking fun at the strange footnotes of infamous criminals. In a non-canon appearance, a statue of Manson alongside two of his cult followers turns up as a macabre exhibit in a haunted attraction called Captain Krusty's Museum of Monsters-Madmen. This nod plays into the show's tendency to use dark historical figures as background jokes or set dressing. He has no real personality or dialogue of his own within the show's canon, existing purely as a punchline or visual gag tied to true-crime infamy.

title: Matt Lauer
text: Matt Lauer is Real-world television journalist who appears as a minor recurring character in The Simpsons. Matt Lauer is depicted as a version of the real-life news anchor, popping up in the show's world as a media figure connected to various Springfield happenings. He's shown hosting a talk show clip that becomes crucial evidence when Bart and Homer search for dirt to free Krusty from an international tribunal. Later he's referenced as having been fired from his talk show job, a nod to his real-world career downfall. He also turns up as a baseball correspondent for a sports website, where he's easily duped by a mistranslated interview and gets flustered trying to keep Grampa Simpson out of a press-only area. His attempt at asserting authority is undercut when Grampa mockingly nicknames him, a jab referencing real allegations of misconduct against him. Overall, he serves as a topical, satirical cameo rather than a core character. Voiced by Chris Edgerly. Notable quotes: "Skinny Weinstein." - Grampa (about Matt Lauer)
quotes: "Skinny Weinstein." - Grampa (about Matt Lauer)

title: Mojo
text: Mojo is Homer Simpson's trained helper monkey, briefly appearing as a pet/servant. Mojo is a highly trained monkey originally intended to serve as a helper for the disabled, but ends up assigned to Homer through a bit of deception. Homer sees Mojo less as a genuine aid and more as free labor to make his own life lazier, but Mojo quickly picks up on Homer's slothful habits and adopts them himself. He develops a taste for junk food, mocking Homer at one point by taking a bite out of a donut before offering it to him. Over time this lifestyle wrecks Mojo's health, leaving him bloated, exhausted, and unable to perform even simple tricks. When Marge grows upset over the monkey's condition, Homer abandons Mojo back at the lab rather than deal with the consequences. The running gag of the episode is Mojo's rapid transformation from an agile professional animal into a couch-potato mirror of Homer himself, capped by his desperate typed plea for help. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Pray... For... Mojo... | Pray... For... Mojo!
quotes: Pray... For... Mojo...
Pray... For... Mojo!

title: Nana Sophie Mussolini
text: Nana Sophie Mussolini is Milhouse Van Houten's Italian grandmother. Nana Sophie Mussolini is a fiery Tuscan grandmother who harbors a deep resentment toward the English language, a grudge rooted in being left pregnant by an American G.I. during World War II. Milhouse used to spend part of his summers with her in Italy, where she enforced strict Italian-only speech by whipping him whenever he slipped into English. This unusual upbringing left Milhouse fluent in Italian, a skill he later passed on to Lisa. Despite her harsh methods, she remains a recurring figure tied to the Van Houten family tree, appearing mostly through mentions and flashbacks rather than direct involvement in Springfield life. Her strict, old-world temperament and short temper are best summed up by her signature outburst of frustration. Voiced by Maggie Roswell. Notable quotes: Idiota!
quotes: Idiota!

title: Slow Leonard
text: Slow Leonard is A tortoise residing at Springfield Zoo whose disappearance sparks a conspiracy theory subplot involving Homer. Slow Leonard is a green tortoise kept at Springfield Zoo, known to Homer from past visits. His mysterious disappearance from his enclosure sets off a chain of events where Homer becomes convinced of foul play, eventually joining an online conspiracy group to investigate. Theories about his fate range from wild kidnapping plots to more absurd notions like drug smuggling and being used to breed slow horses. Despite being a non-speaking animal character, Slow Leonard becomes the unwitting center of an escalating conspiracy narrative, even being accused by the group of secretly being a robotic spy. Ultimately, he is found safe by Homer down a rabbit hole at the zoo, though his rescue nearly causes a rift between Homer and his newfound conspiracy-theorist friends.

title: Vladimir Lenin
text: Vladimir Lenin is Historical figure referenced/depicted in the show; the real-world founder of the Soviet Union appears as a minor figure in Simpsons lore. Vladimir Lenin appears in the Simpsons universe as a historical footnote rather than a recurring character with his own personality. He is depicted in artwork, most notably in Diego Rivera's mural, which stirs controversy with Rockefeller. Patty and Selma take a trip to see his preserved body at his tomb in Moscow, treating it as a tourist attraction. In a more absurd twist, his corpse is shown reanimating to defend communism when the Soviet Union is restored, playing into the show's penchant for surreal, exaggerated takes on history. Overall, Lenin functions as a symbol of communism and Cold War-era references used for background jokes and cultural gags rather than a fleshed-out character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: George R. R. Martin
text: George R. R. Martin is Real-world author who appears as a caricature character in The Simpsons. George R. R. Martin appears as a fictionalized version of the real fantasy author known for the A Song of Ice and Fire novels. In his show appearances, he's often shown procrastinating or getting distracted from his writing duties, such as when he ends up watching unrelated YouTube videos instead of working on his next book. He's also depicted attending fan conventions where admirers plead with him to keep writing, poking fun at his real-life reputation for slow output. In a non-canon segment, he's seen wandering near Moe's wearing a sign referencing his famously unfinished book series. Overall, the character serves as a satirical nod to fan frustration over the delayed completion of his novels and their television adaptation. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: the end is not nigh. I'll tell you when it's nigh.
quotes: the end is not nigh. I'll tell you when it's nigh.

title: Kung Fu Werewolf
text: Kung Fu Werewolf is Fictional character from the in-universe show Ki-Ya Karate Monsters. Kung Fu Werewolf is a minor fictional character within the Simpsons universe, existing as part of the show-within-a-show Ki-Ya Karate Monsters. As his name suggests, he's a werewolf who practices kung fu, blending horror and martial arts tropes into a single novelty character. He has gray hair and is depicted as a non-speaking figure, appearing mostly as background material rather than an active participant in any storyline. His most notable real-world appearance is as a wall sticker decoration in Comic Book Guy's apartment, underscoring his status as pop-culture merchandise beloved by fans of geek culture. He also appears as a collectible character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, tied to a Treehouse of Horror event. Overall, he's more of an easter-egg reference than a fleshed-out character.

title: Jack Marley
text: Jack Marley is Elderly former worker at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, occasional background character in Springfield. Jack Marley is an aging plant worker whose forced retirement kicks off Marge's brief career at the power plant. Despite loving his job and resisting the change, he's pushed out, seemingly so Mr. Burns has an excuse to throw a party. Even after retiring, he doesn't disappear from town life, continuing to pop up as a recognizable elderly extra in Springfield. He's shown serving civic duty on a jury during Marge's shoplifting trial, and he joins the crowd at a town meeting concerning one of Mr. Burns' schemes. As a minor recurring character, he mostly exists in the background of countless episodes rather than driving plots himself. His gray hair (occasionally depicted as black) and frail, senior citizen presence mark him as one of Springfield's many elderly residents. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Mechanical Ants
text: Mechanical Ants is A group of giant robotic ants that exist only in Bart Simpson's imagination, appearing in "Marge vs. the Monorail". The Mechanical Ants are a fantastical creation dreamed up by Bart after Mr. Burns is fined for illegally dumping nuclear waste in Springfield Park. In Bart's daydream, the fine money is used to build four giant robotic ants instead of anything sensible. These imaginary machines go on a destructive rampage, tearing through Springfield Elementary and even cutting Principal Skinner in half. Since they exist purely as a comedic aside in Bart's head, they never actually interact with the real world of Springfield. The gag highlights Bart's mischievous, chaotic imagination and his love of destruction and revenge fantasies aimed at authority figures like Skinner. In later non-canon material from The Simpsons: Tapped Out, the four ants were given individual names—Chompy, Daffodil, Killer, and Nippy.

title: Ranger McFadden
text: Ranger McFadden is Park ranger at Mt. Useful, appearing as a minor recurring character. Ranger McFadden is a minor park ranger stationed at Mt. Useful, working out of the Ranger Lookout Post. He is best known for his appearance during a chaotic scene involving a crowd of people and a fellow ranger searching for him, only to discover he was hidden among the group the whole time. His job involves monitoring the mountain for dangers, including avalanches that threatened to bury the Mt. Useful cabin. Beyond his ranger duties, he also participated in a record-breaking attempt to build the world's tallest human pyramid, showing a willingness to get involved in unusual community events. He's a background character used mostly for brief comic moments rather than deep characterization. His appearances are sparse, mostly limited to a couple of episodes plus a brief flashback cameo. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Captain Mordecai
text: Captain Mordecai is Fictional antagonist within Marge's romantic novel "The Harpooned Heart," modeled after Homer Simpson. Captain Mordecai is a character invented by Marge as the villain of her own novel, a fisherman whose personality shifts to mirror her frustrations with Homer. Initially written as a devoted husband and skilled whaler, he's rewritten into a lazy, selfish oaf once Homer's real-life behavior irritates Marge. His transformation serves as a clever narrative device showing how Marge channels her marital annoyances into fiction. Mordecai's story ends violently, as he becomes tangled in his own harpoon rope after killing a rival named Cyrus Manly, leading to his fall off a cliff and subsequent drowning. Though never a physical presence in Springfield, he later reappears as a character within the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. His entire existence is tied directly to the theme of art imitating life, particularly Marge's own domestic struggles. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Cho Lum Kin
text: Cho Lum Kin is Minor recurring background character in Springfield. Cho Lum Kin is a minor, rarely-seen Springfield resident of Asian or Pacific Islander descent. He first appears when Marge approaches him while searching for Lurleen Lumpkin's biological father, mistakenly asking if he could be the man. Though he denies any connection to Lurleen, he politely wishes Marge luck in her search, showing a friendly and helpful demeanor despite the odd request. He later shows up in an entirely different context, attending a crossword tournament at a bar, hinting that he may have an interest in word games or trivia. Beyond these two brief appearances, little else is known about his life, job, or relationships, making him one of the show's many background townsfolk used to populate crowd or minor plot scenes. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Lem
text: Lem is A minor recurring character, a retail clerk who occasionally gets involved in criminal schemes around Springfield. Lem is a low-level retail worker who first appears working at a Halloween pop-up shop with his friends Dickie and an unnamed pal. After being fired by Apu at Homer's urging, he and his friends plot petty revenge, only to be caught by Chief Wiggum. His antagonistic streak resurfaces later when he participates in a bank robbery, disguising himself in a clown mask alongside his usual crew. Despite his criminal tendencies, he manages to evade real consequences more than once, thanks to distractions and mishaps involving the Springfield police. Lem also shows up in more mundane contexts, such as attending a live podcast recording, showing he's a fairly ordinary background fixture in town. In an alternate fantasy sequence imagined by Marge, he even appears as an asylum inmate freed by exaggerated caricatures of Homer and Marge, hinting at his role as a stock 'shady townsperson' type used for comic effect. Voiced by Nick Kroll.

title: Todd Linux
text: Todd Linux is Former executive of the internet company BetterThanTV.com, briefly involved with Bart's Angry Dad cartoon. Todd Linux is a minor businessman who ran the website company BetterThanTV.com. He saw commercial potential in Bart's comic strip Angry Dad and hired Bart to help turn it into an online cartoon, bringing Lisa on board as well. Rather than paying them in cash, he compensated them with company stock, a decision that later proved disastrous. When BetterThanTV.com collapsed, the stock became worthless, leaving Bart and Lisa with nothing. In a fittingly shady exit, Linux was last seen stripping copper wire out of the office walls before abandoning the failed business. He's a small but memorable example of the show's satire of dot-com era business schemes and exploitative executives. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Mall Santa boy
text: Mall Santa boy is A minor, unnamed child character who briefly interacts with Homer while visiting the Springfield Mall Santa. This character is a small, spoiled boy who appears fleetingly in the show's very first episode. He's shown enjoying a donut before being brought to the mall to sit on Santa's lap and list off his Christmas wishes. His demands come across as oddly specific and a bit whimsical, hinting at a materialistic streak typical of a pampered child. The moment becomes memorable mainly because of Homer's reaction, as he can't resist stealing a bite of the boy's donut. Despite his minimal screen time, he has stuck around in Simpsons trivia thanks to a later archive footage cameo. He has no known name, family, or ongoing storyline, existing purely as a one-off gag character. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: He asked Homer for Robotoids and a Goop Monster
quotes: He asked Homer for Robotoids and a Goop Monster

title: Klu Klux Clam
text: Klu Klux Clam is A minor character doll from the fictional Itchy & Scratchy and Friends Hour, sold as merchandise at Itchy & Scratchy Land. Klu Klux Clam is a strange, short-lived cartoon character invented for the failed spin-off show Itchy & Scratchy and Friends Hour. He's a non-speaking character whose entire existence is a dark joke, with a name and design that overtly parodies the white supremacist group the Ku Klux Klan. Alongside similarly odd creations like Disgruntled Goat and Uncle Ant, he represents the show-within-a-show's desperate and unfunny attempt to expand its cast of characters. His only real appearance is as a doll in a gift shop at Itchy & Scratchy Land, where even Lisa fails to recognize him, prompting Bart to explain his obscure origins. The joke rests entirely on the absurdity and poor taste of his concept rather than any actions he takes, since he never speaks or does anything on-screen.

title: Stephen Merchant (character)
text: Stephen Merchant (character) is Real-world English comedian who appeared as an animated cameo in a Simpsons episode parody of The Ricky Gervais Show. Stephen Merchant appears as a fictionalized, animated version of himself within the Simpsons universe, depicted in the visual style of The Ricky Gervais Show. His cameo comes in the form of a promo shown on the fictional network HBOWTIME, tying into his real-world career as a writer, director, and performer. He's also referenced by Lisa, who associates him with British culture alongside Shakespeare, tea, and scones. As a real-world figure rather than a traditional Springfield resident, his role is brief and largely a nod to fans of his actual work with Ricky Gervais. He has no defined personality traits within the show beyond this cameo appearance and passing mention.

title: Lisa, Jr.
text: Lisa, Jr. is A young girl from the island of Microatia who resembles Lisa Simpson, met by Homer during his time as a missionary. Oovilu-Eeoo-Kitana-Wanjay is an island girl whose uncanny resemblance to Lisa Simpson, in both looks and voice, quickly earns her a much simpler nickname from Homer. Unable to wrap his tongue around her real name, he dubs her "Lisa, Jr." for convenience. Her brief appearance ties into a chaotic episode where Homer's missionary work leads to unintended disaster. She and Homer end up in mortal danger together when their enthusiastic bell-ringing accidentally triggers a volcanic eruption. Despite the peril, the encounter highlights the show's recurring gag of strange doppelgangers popping up in Homer's misadventures. She remains a minor, one-off character tied to a single, memorable escapade. Voiced by Yeardley Smith.

title: Max (Ice Cream of Margie (with the Light Blue Hair))
keys: max (ice cream of margie (with the light blue hair))
text: Max (Ice Cream of Margie (with the Light Blue Hair)) is An ice cream truck vendor whose frequent customer was Homer Simpson. Max was a minor character who ran an ice cream van and counted Homer among his most loyal patrons. His time on the show was brief but pivotal, as his sudden death while serving Homer led directly to Homer taking over his ice cream business. Following his passing, Max's widow handed the truck over to Homer, setting up that episode's plot. He later resurfaced as a ghostly figure in one of Bart's dream sequences, appearing among other deceased characters trying to guide Bart toward the afterlife. Beyond these two appearances, little else is known about his personality or backstory, as he functions mainly as a catalyst for other characters' storylines. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Mopey Mary
text: Mopey Mary is A vengeful ghost girl who appears in a Treehouse of Horror segment, haunting Lisa and Bart after they watch a cursed video. Mopey Mary is a tragic, ghostly figure whose sorrow curdled into vengeance after a cruel prank drove her to end her own life in an old school well back in 1932. Ignored for days by an indifferent Groundskeeper Willie, she resurfaced as a supernatural killer, targeting anyone who watched a cursed video exactly seven days after viewing it. Her story surfaces again in the present when a viral TikTok trend spreads the video among Springfield Elementary students, drawing the attention of Lisa and Bart. Unlike typical horror antagonists, Mopey Mary shows a softer, more emotionally complex side when Lisa reaches out to her with kindness instead of fear. The two form an unlikely bond, but Mary's deep-seated insecurity and inability to trust quick affection ultimately drive her back to the well she never truly escaped. She serves as a clear parody of horror icons Sadako Yamamura and Samara Morgan, blending genuine pathos with the show's signature Halloween-episode dark comedy. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Larceny Lass
text: Larceny Lass is Comic-book supervillain from the Radioactive Man comics-within-the-show, a recurring foe of Radioactive Man and Fallout Boy. Larceny Lass is a green-haired supervillainess who operates within the fictional Radioactive Man comic series read by Bart and other characters. True to her name, she is a thief obsessed with stealing valuables, but her real fixation is winning the affection of Radioactive Man, whom she pursues romantically despite his repeated rejections. She commands a group of henchmen and isn't above using advanced weaponry, like a solar ray, to incapacitate her heroic crush and gain the upper hand. She has also allied herself with other villains such as Hypno Head and Jawbreaker, showing she's willing to work within a larger criminal network rather than act alone. Ultimately she tends to be foiled and captured by the combined efforts of Radioactive Man and his sidekick Fallout Boy. Despite being her enemy, Radioactive Man keeps a picture of her, hinting at a complicated history between them.

title: Marty
text: Marty is Radio DJ for KBBL, recurring minor character partnered with Bill. Marty is one half of the duo of KBBL radio hosts, working alongside his partner Bill on various on-air segments and contests. He's known for engaging the people of Springfield through giveaways, most notably the contest that resulted in Bart winning his pet elephant, Stampy. Marty and Bill also conduct celebrity interviews on their show, once hosting the band Spinal Tap. In a non-canon deleted scene, Marty is shown to be a bit gullible and anxious, falling for an April Fools prank from Bill and worrying aloud about having to return to Kentucky. Overall he serves as a background fixture of Springfield's media landscape rather than a deeply characterized figure. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: I can't go back to Kentucky.
quotes: I can't go back to Kentucky.

title: Klaunax
text: Klaunax is A non-canon elder Rigellian alien from Rigel 7, appearing in a Treehouse of Horror-style segment. Klaunax is an aged member of the Rigellian species, the recurring alien race from Rigel 7 that has crossed paths with the Simpsons family in various non-canon segments. He holds a position of some esteem among his people, evidenced by being given the honor of taking the first ceremonial bite of Homer Simpson. His appearance ties into the show's tradition of using alien invaders as a vehicle for dark comedy involving the Simpsons being threatened or consumed. As an elder, Klaunax likely carries authority or ritual significance within Rigellian culture, though little else about his personality is detailed. His brief role centers entirely around this one dinner ceremony. He exists as a minor but memorable figure within the show's non-canon alien mythology. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Mervin Monroe
text: Mervin Monroe is Tattoo artist who runs The Happy Sailor Tattoo Parlor in Springfield Mall, and younger brother of Dr. Marvin Monroe. Mervin Monroe is a minor recurring character best known as the inker behind Springfield Mall's tattoo shop.
