She is a non-speaking character, appearing mostly in the background or referenced through promotional material, such as a poster seen outside a cabaret. Behind the scenes, she is designed as a nod to a real-life country entertainment personality known for similar oversized floral headwear. Her presence in the show is brief, limited to a couple of appearances across the series' run.

title: Mark McGwire (character)
text: Mark McGwire (character) is Guest-starring real-world baseball player who appears as a fictionalized version of himself in the show. Mark McGwire is a real-life Major League Baseball player who appears as a character in The Simpsons, portraying a fictionalized version of himself. He is best known for his cameo in "Brother's Little Helper," where his presence in Springfield ties into the episode's baseball-related plot. Beyond this main appearance, he shows up briefly in other episodes, including a Treehouse of Horror segment and an opening sequence gag, suggesting he's used mostly for quick, recognizable cameos rather than a developed personality. As a real-world character voiced by himself, he fits into the show's long tradition of celebrity guest appearances. His role is minor and largely cosmetic, existing to add star power and topical humor rather than ongoing characterization. He has orange hair and is depicted as an adult professional athlete. Voiced by Mark McGwire (Himself).

title: Malicious Krubb
text: Malicious Krubb is Fictional dark wizard antagonist within the in-universe Angelica Button book saga referenced by the Simpsons family. Malicious Krubb is a villainous dark wizard from the fictional Angelica Button book series that the Simpsons family reads and reimagines. He serves as the main antagonist of that saga, notorious for trapping the heroine Angelica in an hourglass and killing Headmaster Greystash. Different family members reinterpret his story in their own imaginations, sometimes changing the outcome of his battles or even mangling his name. He also pops up in dream sequences unrelated to the books' actual plot, showing how deeply the story has embedded itself in the family's subconscious. As a clear parody of Lucius Malfoy from Harry Potter, he embodies the aristocratic, sneering dark wizard archetype. Despite being a minor, non-canon-heavy character, he recurs across multiple episodes and even a mobile game appearance. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Kraluicious Mubb
quotes: Kraluicious Mubb

title: Alaska Nebraska
text: Alaska Nebraska is A famous teen pop singer and actress from Waverly Hills, briefly idolized by Lisa Simpson. Alaska Nebraska is a wildly popular sixteen-year-old celebrity known for her music career and acting, adored especially by children in the Waverly Hills area. She's portrayed as vain and image-obsessed, having gotten a nose job to help her rise to fame after feeling like an outcast growing up. One of her odder quirks is that she lip syncs not only her performances but even her everyday conversations, suggesting a life built entirely on artifice. She unwinds before shows by meditating and smoking simultaneously, and she's shown little patience for overly enthusiastic fans, even having security remove Lisa from one of her events. Her public image is also used for wholesome causes, appearing on school posters promoting reading and discouraging unwanted physical contact. She serves as the show's parody of real-life pop star Miley Cyrus and her Hannah Montana persona. Voiced by Elliot Page.

title: Moby Man
text: Moby Man is A superhero member of the Vindicators, a fictional superhero team within the Simpsons universe. Moby Man is a musclebound superhero who fights alongside the Vindicators, likely a parody of Marvel's Hulk. He plays a role in the climactic battle against the villain Chinnos, sharing a romantic moment with fellow hero Hydrangea before both are turned to crystal by the Doomsday app. He later resurfaces in a virtual reality simulation built for Bart, revealing to him that the events of the Vindicator movies were real experiences for the team. In that simulated world, he helps battle Chinnos' army and ultimately aids in defeating him again. Beyond his direct appearances, his popularity is reflected through fan cosplay at a convention and merchandise like a figure kept in Comic Book Guy's apartment. His larger-than-life, hulking design plays into typical superhero-genre parody tropes seen throughout the Vindicators franchise. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Northern Irish leprechaun
text: Northern Irish leprechaun is A minor recurring character; a Protestant Northern Irish leprechaun who appears during Springfield's St. Patrick's Day festivities. This character is a regional variant of the classic Irish leprechaun, distinguished by his all-orange attire that signals his allegiance to the Protestant Orangemen rather than Catholic tradition. He sports bushy eyebrows, mutton chop whiskers, a formal frock coat, bow-tie, and top hat, giving him a more dignified but still whimsical look compared to his green-clad counterpart. His main role centers on the ongoing sectarian rivalry played out through Springfield's dueling St. Patrick's Day parades, where he leads the orange-wearing marchers against the green-wearing Catholic leprechaun's group. Despite a brief moment of reconciliation triggered by one of Lisa's songs, he ends up brawling with his rival after being sucker-punched, reflecting the show's satirical take on Irish sectarian conflict. He later reappears taking a stance on an unrelated town dispute, showing he's a recognizable, if minor, member of Springfield's background cast. Overall, he functions as a running gag rooted in real-world religious and cultural tensions rendered in cartoonish form. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Stan Laurel
text: Stan Laurel is Real-life comic actor appearing as a minor recurring character in The Simpsons, part of the Laurel and Hardy duo. Stan Laurel is depicted in the show as a cameo version of the real-world comedian famous for his partnership with Oliver Hardy. He typically appears alongside Hardy in brief historical or hallucinatory vignettes rather than as an active participant in Simpsons storylines. In one appearance he is seen handcuffed to Hardy at a blacksmith's shop, awaiting release. He also shows up in a nostalgic flashback sequence involving Grampa Simpson, and in a slapstick gag where he and Hardy nearly drop a piano on Homer and Maggie. His most surreal appearance comes when Homer and Ned hallucinate themselves as famous duos, including Laurel and Hardy, after taking a fictional drug. Overall, his role is that of a recurring background reference to classic comedy rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Chris Edgerly.

title: Larry (Futurama)
text: Larry (Futurama) is Non-canon crossover character; one of Mom's sons from Futurama appearing in Simpsons/Futurama comic crossovers. Larry is a minor character introduced in the Simpsons/Futurama comic book crossover, identified as one of the sons of the ruthless businesswoman Mom. He shares family ties with his brother Walt and half-brother Igner, placing him within Futurama's dysfunctional MomCorp family dynamic. Larry's few appearances emphasize his role as a put-upon underling, subjected to humiliation from both Springfield bullies and his own domineering mother. He appears briefly during the chaotic teleportation event that merges Springfield with New New York, getting caught in an embarrassing moment with Jimbo. Later, he and his brothers endure rough treatment from Mom and Mr. Burns after Burns takes charge of a division of MomCorp, highlighting his low status within the family hierarchy.

title: Lugash
text: Lugash is A gymnastics instructor who trained Lisa Simpson in Springfield. Lugash is a gruff, intense gymnastics coach with a thick Romanian accent and a distinctive curled brown mustache. His backstory is murky and contradictory, with conflicting claims about how he came to the United States, adding a comedic air of mystery to his character. He runs a strict and somewhat bizarre training regimen, notably holding students' pets hostage as motivation until they complete assigned physical challenges. His harsh methods proved effective, helping Lisa become a skilled gymnast despite his unconventional approach. He also attends anger management sessions, where his temper manifests as threats to spit on people. Lugash is a comedic exaggeration of stereotypical hardline Eastern European athletic coaches, seemingly modeled after real-life gymnastics coach Béla Károlyi. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: I train best. I am Lugash.
quotes: I train best. I am Lugash.

title: Laird Ladd
text: Laird Ladd is Mascot for Lard Lad Donuts, based on the original design of Lard Lad. Laird Ladd is a minor, non-speaking character who serves as the mascot for Lard Lad Donuts, representing the earlier version of the now-famous Lard Lad statue. He made a public appearance at the unveiling of the new Lard Lad statue, tying him to the donut chain's promotional history. Being a mascot, he doesn't have much personality shown on screen, as he's more of a background or promotional figure. Notably, he originated in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out before making his way into the actual television series. His gray hair suggests an older design or version of the mascot. He remains a minor recurring character with no dialogue in his appearances.

title: Turanga Leela
text: Turanga Leela is Crossover character from Futurama; space captain who appears alongside the Simpsons family in crossover episodes. Leela is the one-eyed, purple-haired captain from the Futurama universe who crosses over into the Simpsons' world on a few occasions. She's shown as capable and mission-focused, willing to travel through time with Fry and Professor Farnsworth to fix problems caused by Bender's hesitation. During her visit to Springfield, she has an awkward, mutually uncomfortable encounter with Marge, where each woman is too polite to bring up the other's most distinctive physical feature. Beyond her active appearances, Leela also shows up in background cameos, such as on a convention banner and in an exercise-bike video clip. Notably, she predates most crossover characters by debuting in a Simpsons video game rather than an episode or comic. Her role is largely tied to Futurama's sci-fi antics bleeding into Springfield rather than deep characterization within the Simpsons canon itself. Voiced by Katey Sagal.

title: Ronald McDonald
text: Ronald McDonald is Real-world fast-food mascot who makes a cameo crossover appearance in Springfield. Ronald McDonald appears as a background crossover figure rather than a fully developed character. He's shown performing a mundane task, closing curtains at the Clown Plaza Hotel, which pokes fun at the mundane reality behind flashy corporate mascots. He later appears as a stone likeness on an imagined corporate version of Mount Rushmore, envisioned by Homer alongside other famous fast-food icons. This daydream underscores the show's satire of consumerism and brand loyalty. Ronald has no dialogue in his appearances, reinforcing his role as a purely visual gag rather than a speaking character. His inclusion highlights the Simpsons' frequent use of real-world corporate icons for humor.

title: William H. Macy (character)
text: William H. Macy (character) is Real-life actor who appears as himself in a guest role on The Simpsons. William H. Macy appears as a fictionalized version of himself within the show's universe. After Homer receives a windfall of one million dollars, he decides to build a replica of Moe's Tavern in his own basement. Wanting an authentic touch, Homer hires the real William H. Macy to portray Moe in this personal recreation. Unfortunately, Homer ends up unimpressed with Macy's take on the gruff bartender, finding his acting lacking. The joke plays on the absurdity of a celebrity actor being hired for such a mundane, personal project, and on Homer's casual dismissal of a respected performer's work. Macy's appearance is brief and largely a cameo-style gag rather than a fully developed character role. Voiced by William H. Macy.

title: Captain Kwik
text: Captain Kwik is Non-canon superhero alter ego of Apu Nahasapeemapetilon, appearing in Bongo comic book stories. Captain Kwik is the superhero identity adopted by Apu after a nuclear blast triggered by Itchy and Scratchy transforms ordinary Springfield residents into costumed heroes. His defining trait is super speed, which he uses in battles against various villains alongside the other newly empowered townsfolk. He speaks with a formal, almost theatrical flair befitting a comic-book hero, contrasting with Apu's usual personality. Captain Kwik exists purely within the Bongo comics continuity and has no bearing on the show's main canon. He appears across a handful of tie-in comic issues centered on this superhero-transformation storyline. His character is more of a novelty crossover gag than a fully developed personality, existing mainly to give Apu a heroic alter ego for these specific stories. Notable quotes: Captain Kwik Must Respectfully Disagree, Malefactor!
quotes: Captain Kwik Must Respectfully Disagree, Malefactor!

title: Victor Kleskow
text: Victor Kleskow is A demanding music teacher from Capital City who briefly mentors Lisa Simpson. Victor Kleskow is a bald, mustached music instructor at Daws Butler Hall in Capital City who scouts young musical talent from surrounding schools. He spots Lisa Simpson's saxophone skills at a Springfield Elementary concert and recruits her for private lessons, requiring her family to drive her to the city daily. His teaching method is brutally harsh, frequently berating and belittling his students, yet his intensity pushes Lisa to play better than ever before. He forces a competitive showdown between Lisa and another student for first chair, and later pressures her to skip ahead a grade level despite the personal cost to her family life. When Lisa deliberately underperforms in an audition to preserve her home life, Kleskow coldly severs ties with her. He is explicitly designed as a parody of the abusive instructor Terence Fletcher from the film Whiplash, fittingly voiced by the same actor, J. K. Simmons. Voiced by J. K. Simmons.

title: The MudSlinger
text: The MudSlinger is Non-canon superhero alter-ego of Mayor Quimby, appearing in Simpsons comic books. The MudSlinger is a comic-exclusive superhero identity taken on by Mayor Quimby after a nuclear explosion transforms him into a being made entirely of mud. His signature ability is shooting mud at enemies, fitting his earthy, sludgy form. The name is a playful pun on the political phrase "mudslinging," tying his superhero persona back to his day job as Springfield's often corrupt mayor. He exists purely within the Bongo comics continuity as part of a larger group of superhero parodies. Despite his silly concept, he recurs across multiple comic storylines rather than being a one-off gag. His character leans into absurdist humor typical of the Simpsons comic universe's take on superhero tropes.

title: Nigel (Homer's Barbershop Quartet)
text: Nigel (Homer's Barbershop Quartet) is Former talent agent/manager who discovered and managed The Be Sharps barbershop quartet. Nigel is a shrewd talent manager who spots The Be Sharps performing at Moe's Cavern and quickly signs them, seeing commercial potential in the group. He proves willing to reshape the band for marketability, insisting Chief Wiggum be removed and having Apu alter his surname so it fits neatly on a marquee. He sticks with the quartet through their rise to fame, guiding them to their number one hit. In later, non-canon appearances he continues his opportunistic pattern, becoming the agent for a suddenly famous Santa's Little Helper and even working against Bart's attempts to reclaim his dog for the sake of profit, as well as managing the short-lived boy band 5 from 'Field. He's also rumored to have a hidden tattoo under his hair. The character is intentionally modeled on Brian Epstein, the real-life manager of the Beatles, mirroring the show's Beatles parody storyline. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Royce Lumpkin
text: Royce Lumpkin is Estranged father of Lurleen Lumpkin, the country singer occasionally associated with Homer's music career storylines. Royce Lumpkin is a deadbeat father who abandoned his daughter Lurleen when she was just a young child, only resurfacing briefly once her music career started to take off. He is characterized as dishonest and self-serving, eventually reconciling with Lurleen only to betray her trust by stealing one of her songs and reselling it for profit. Despite his flaws, he has a couple of charming quirks, including a talent for performing the hambone dance and a full head of hair that leaves the balding Homer envious. He's also noted as a heavy whiskey drinker, reinforcing his image as a rough, unreliable figure. His arc plays into themes of family betrayal and forgiveness, ultimately ending with karmic punishment when the Dixie Chicks turn on him after learning of his theft. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Laundromat dog
text: Laundromat dog is A minor animal character who guards the entrance of Lon's Laundry in the Simpsons comics. The laundromat dog is a gray and black dog that stations itself by the front door of Lon's Laundry, seemingly acting as an unofficial guard. It has an unpredictable and intimidating demeanor, switching from baring its teeth and growling to giving a goofy, panting grin within moments. Its main claim to fame is unsettling Sideshow Mel during a trip to do laundry, first scaring him at the entrance and later staring him down menacingly through the window while he folded clothes. The encounter left enough of an impression that Mel chose to sneak out the back door just to avoid the dog altogether. Despite its minor role, the dog's erratic behavior gives it a memorably quirky presence in its brief comic appearances.

title: Benito Mussolini
text: Benito Mussolini is Historical fascist dictator of Italy, referenced in various flashbacks, jokes, and pop-culture allusions throughout the show. Benito Mussolini appears in The Simpsons as a real-world historical figure rather than a regular cast member, mostly used for comedic or historical flashback purposes. He's depicted alongside Adolf Hitler and other Axis figures, tying into the show's recurring gags about World War II history. Various characters invoke his name or image as a shorthand for tyranny or dictatorial behavior, such as Lisa comparing Homer's antics to him or Luigi comparing Lisa's bossiness to him. He's also been referenced in non-canon material, appearing in Hell playing games with other infamous historical villains. Overall, he functions as a recognizable cultural symbol used sparingly for jokes about fascism, dictators, and World War II rather than as a developed character. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "not to imitate Mussolini"
quotes: "not to imitate Mussolini"

title: Living treehouse
text: Living treehouse is A non-canon monster from a Treehouse of Horror segment; Bart's treehouse brought to life. This character is exactly what it sounds like: Bart's treehouse transformed into a vengeful, sentient monster. It's born out of anger, coming to life after Homer attempts to chop it down following an argument about Bart's scary stories, with a lightning strike during a storm giving it life. Once animated, it turns hostile, attacking Homer and rampaging through Springfield. Its most notable trait is that it doesn't act alone for long, discovering a Christmas tree farm and reanimating the trees there into an army bent on revenge against humans. The segment plays up horror-movie tropes, with the tree army using pollen to incapacitate a human militia before a gruesome massacre. It later appears as a collectible decoration in a mobile game tie-in. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Stevie Nicks
text: Stevie Nicks is Real-world singer of Fleetwood Mac who appears as a minor/background character in Springfield. Stevie Nicks appears in the show as a version of her real self, tied to her actual role as a member of Fleetwood Mac. She's referenced as an object of Homer's bucket-list fantasies, having supposedly seen her naked multiple times. She physically appears alongside bandmate Mick Fleetwood in Springfield Heights, and shows up pictured on the cover of Rumours in another episode. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, she's invoked as a benchmark for witchy power, referencing real-world rumors that falsely tied her to witchcraft. Overall she functions as a cameo/reference character rather than a fully developed personality within the show. Notable quotes: "more wicked witchery than Stevie Nicks" - Lord Montymort
quotes: "more wicked witchery than Stevie Nicks" - Lord Montymort

title: Nelson Mandela
text: Nelson Mandela is Real-world former President of South Africa referenced in the Simpsons universe. Nelson Mandela appears in the show mostly as a real-world figure referenced or mentioned rather than a fully active character. His name lives on through Nelson Muntz, whose full name is revealed to be Nelson Mandela Muntz. In one episode, Bart and Homer use an odd piece of trivia about him to help free Krusty from international custody, showing how his legacy gets tangled into the show's absurd plotlines. He also shows up as a recognizable face in a dictator-themed captcha and is quoted for inspiration by another character. A non-canon aside notes he even has a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame within the show's world. His death in real life is acknowledged in the 'Behind the Laughter' segment, grounding the character in reality even amid the show's usual exaggeration. Notable quotes: "It always seems impossible until it is done."
quotes: "It always seems impossible until it is done."

title: Regis Philbin (character)
text: Regis Philbin (character) is Celebrity guest character based on real-life talk show host, appearing in cameo roles. Regis Philbin appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, best known as co-host of the morning talk show that later became Live With Regis and Kelly. He's referenced by Lindsey Naegle as an example of a beloved but grumpy TV personality when she's trying to pitch Krusty on hosting his own talk show. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, Bart and Lisa accidentally end up on his show after getting swapped into a cartoon dimension. Interestingly, Philbin voiced himself in that Halloween special, but Dan Castellaneta filled in for him in his other on-screen appearance. He functions mostly as a cameo/parody figure rather than a fully developed character, poking fun at his real-world talk-show persona. Voiced by Regis Philbin (himself); Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "a cranky but lovable, sexless grandpa." — Lindsey Naegle describing Regis Philbin
quotes: "a cranky but lovable, sexless grandpa." — Lindsey Naegle describing Regis Philbin

title: Rex (I Love Lisa)
text: Rex (I Love Lisa) is A second-grade student at Springfield Elementary School, minor classmate of Lisa Simpson and Ralph Wiggum. Rex is a minor second-grader at Springfield Elementary who fancies himself a talented actor. His confidence is dashed when he is passed over for the coveted role of George Washington in a school President's Day play, with the part going to the less conventionally talented Ralph Wiggum instead. Furious at the outcome, Rex lashes out by insulting his teacher Ms. Hoover, accusing her of favoritism. His outburst inadvertently exposes a bit of corruption, since it turns out Chief Wiggum used his authority to intimidate Ms. Hoover into casting his son. Rex doesn't have much further impact on the story, serving mainly as the catalyst for revealing this small-scale abuse of power at the school. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "got to her"
quotes: "got to her"

title: Pet Store man
text: Pet Store man is Minor recurring character; a clerk at the Springfield Pet Shop. The Pet Store man is a smooth-talking clerk who claims to possess a rare psychic ability allowing him to perform a canine-human mind meld. He uses this supposed gift to convince customers that their pets need various expensive accessories, which is really just a sales tactic to boost store profits. Despite insisting the power is exceedingly rare, he claims it is somehow shared by three other clerks at the same store, undercutting his own credibility. His scheme only works on especially gullible customers, though it proved highly effective on Marge, who ended up buying a cart full of dog products for Santa's Little Helper. His limited success with this trick seems to be the reason he has never advanced beyond his position as a shop clerk. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Let me try a canine-human mind meld. It's an incredibly rare psychic power possessed only by me, and three other clerks at this store.|Pet Store man|Two Dozen and One Greyhounds
quotes: Let me try a canine-human mind meld. It's an incredibly rare psychic power possessed only by me, and three other clerks at this store.|Pet Store man|Two Dozen and One Greyhounds

title: Uncle Sam
text: Uncle Sam is American icon character appearing sporadically in Bart's imagination, dream sequences, and background media within the show. Uncle Sam is a personification of American patriotism who pops up in various odd, symbolic contexts throughout the series rather than as a consistent character. He first appears in one of Bart's nightmares, scolding him for America's decline. Later depictions include a costumed performer at a zoo show, an image used in subliminal advertising, and a menacing figure in Bart's imagination who helps the Statue of Liberty beat him up. He's also been used decoratively, such as on a book-on-tape cover embracing Lady Liberty, and as a costume worn by a backup dancer during a patriotic musical performance. His appearances are largely symbolic or humorous nods to American iconography rather than substantial plot involvement. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Harry Shearer.

title: Ronaldo (Blame It on Lisa)
text: Ronaldo (Blame It on Lisa) is A young orphan boy from Brazil whom Lisa sponsored, appearing in the episode "Blame It on Lisa". Ronaldo is a Brazilian orphan whose life is changed after Lisa Simpson sponsors him through a charity program. When he suddenly disappears from his orphanage, it sets off a chain of events that brings the Simpson family to Brazil looking for him. Rather than being in trouble, it turns out Ronaldo has found unexpected success, using a pair of shoes Lisa gave him to land a role as a costumed dancer on a children's television program. His newfound fame and fortune ironically place him in the position to help save Homer, who gets kidnapped during the family's search. Ronaldo's story is a small but pivotal thread in the episode, tying together themes of charity, luck, and family loyalty. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Singing railroad hobo
text: Singing railroad hobo is A minor recurring hobo character who rides trains and appears in a special episode of The Simpsons. This unnamed hobo is a wandering figure who spends his time riding freight trains and entertaining fellow passengers with elaborate tall tales. He first appears when the Simpson family mistakes him for dead while sneaking aboard a train to Delaware. Once awake, he reveals his talent for storytelling and singing, using it as currency to negotiate sponge baths from Homer. He recounts three well-known legends to the family, weaving folklore into the show's narrative structure. Later appearances show a bit of unexpected growth in his life, as he moves away from his humble bindle in favor of a briefcase after some financial help. Despite his rough appearance, he's resourceful, theatrical, and surprisingly business-minded when the opportunity arises. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Old Jewish man's wife
text: Old Jewish man's wife is Deceased wife of the Old Jewish man, a minor recurring Simpsons character. The Old Jewish man's wife is a minor, largely background character defined by her relationship to her husband rather than her own personality. She has passed away by the time most of her appearances occur, existing mainly as a memory or hallucination for her grieving husband. In one emotional moment, her husband dances with her in a vision, showing the depth of his lingering attachment to her. She also left behind a voicemail message that her husband kept saved on his phone long after her death, hinting at his difficulty letting go. In a non-canon story, she appears alive as part of an elderly Jewish couple traveling to Israel aboard a doomed luxury liner, a segment that parodies a classic disaster film character. Overall, she serves as a poignant, if minor, symbol of loss and memory tied to the Old Jewish man's storyline. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Pick up the phone, big shot! I know you're there!
quotes: Pick up the phone, big shot! I know you're there!

title: Queen of Hearts
text: Queen of Hearts is A non-canon crossover villain from Alice in Wonderland who appears among the Disney villains in Simpsons specials. The Queen of Hearts is a crossover character borrowed from Alice in Wonderland who shows up as one of the resident villains of Disney Villain Land. She's part of a group of Disney villains trying to recruit Lisa Simpson into their ranks through song, showing herself to be dismissive and a bit prickly when her efforts are questioned. She later joins other Disney villains in a holiday-themed musical number, only to end up on the receiving end of an unexpected medical mishap. Her role is minor and largely comedic, existing mainly as part of a large ensemble of fairy-tale antagonists rather than as a fully developed character. She retains her classic bad temper from her original source material, quick to insult those who annoy her. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Lisa was a depressing kid.
quotes: Lisa was a depressing kid.

title: Sandwich delivery guy
text: Sandwich delivery guy is Minor one-off character who delivers a giant sandwich to the Simpson household. The sandwich delivery guy is a minor background character who appears briefly during an episode where Bart takes advantage of Lisa babysitting him. He shows up at the Simpson house with a massive submarine sandwich that Bart ordered, requiring extra help to carry it inside due to its size. He calmly informs Lisa of the steep price and expects a tip for the delivery. His appearance highlights Bart's mischievous nature as he had called up multiple services while Lisa was in charge, leading to her frustration with everyone involved. He has no significant character development beyond this single comedic moment. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Evelyn Peters
text: Evelyn Peters is A wealthy Springfield socialite and former high school classmate of Marge Simpson. Evelyn Peters is a member of Springfield's upper-crust social scene, known for her ties to the exclusive Springfield Glen Country Club. She and Marge attended high school together, though Evelyn was among the popular crowd while Marge went largely unnoticed. Years later, a chance meeting at the Kwik-E-Mart leads Evelyn to reconnect with Marge and draw her into the country club lifestyle, temporarily fueling Marge's obsession with social status. Evelyn embodies the snobbish, image-conscious elite of Springfield, delighting in exclusivity and status symbols like designer suits and induction banquets. Despite her polished exterior, she's shown to be part of a fickle social circle that Marge ultimately rejects. She pops up in a variety of Springfield's more eccentric events over the years, from record-breaking pyramid stunts to celebrity parties, showing she's a fixture of the town's high society scene. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Oh, Marge, you've come a long way from the girl I knew nothing about in high school.
quotes: Oh, Marge, you've come a long way from the girl I knew nothing about in high school.

title: Sebastian
text: Sebastian is A crossover character from Disney's The Little Mermaid who appears briefly in a Homer Simpson dream sequence. Sebastian is the red crab from The Little Mermaid, brought into the Simpsons universe as a one-off crossover gag. He has no real narrative role beyond appearing in a fantasy Homer conjures up about living under the sea, which ends with Homer eating him. He is non-speaking in his canonical appearance, existing purely as a visual reference rather than a developed character. In a later non-canon special, he shows up at Moe's Tavern for a Disney+ anniversary party, casually enjoying a Buzz Cola alongside other guest characters. Despite his minimal screen time, he's technically listed as a deceased character due to Homer's dream devouring him. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent habit of parodying and referencing other Disney properties.

title: Ozmodiar
text: Ozmodiar is A little green alien who occasionally appears to Homer and the Simpson kids. Ozmodiar is a mischievous little green alien who seems to pop up randomly, usually visible only to certain characters like Homer. He first appeared to Bart and Lisa while they watched a nonsensical anime, appearing to back up Bart's claim that cartoons don't need to make logical sense. Later, he shows up to mock Homer after his blundering safety report gets the power plant shut down. In non-canon material, he was introduced as a proposed new character for a future season, only visible to Homer, and even starred in an unaired Christmas special and his own short-lived comic book series. His character is essentially a parody of The Great Gazoo from The Flintstones, poking fun at oddball sci-fi sidekick characters. Ozmodiar's appearances are sparse and often surreal, existing more as a meta-joke about the show's own weirdness than as a fully developed character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "Really done it this time, dumb-dumb"
quotes: "Really done it this time, dumb-dumb"

title: Report Card
text: Report Card is A minor student character at Springfield Elementary and member of The Superfriends nerd group. Booker T. Report, nicknamed Report Card, is one of the studious outcasts who make up The Superfriends clique at Springfield Elementary. He's shown as level-headed and safety-conscious, being the one who insists proper authorities must be alerted when the group discovers a comet is dangerously close to Earth. He lends his tech skills to help Lisa Simpson build SpringFace alongside fellow nerds Martin, Database, and Cosine, though their efforts get comically wrecked by Nelson. His name is a nod to real-life educator and civil rights figure Booker T. Washington. As a background character, he's popped up in odd contexts, including as part of an angry mob wanting to punish Homer during the events of The Simpsons Movie. A quirky visual gag has him occasionally colored yellow instead of his usual hair tone. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Sally Salieri
text: Sally Salieri is A minor character from a Marge-narrated story segment in "Margical History Tour," portrayed as the sister of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. Sally Salieri is a fictional composer created for one of Marge's historical tales, cast as the sibling and rival of Mozart. She's a deeply resentful figure, overlooked by her parents who favor Mozart because his music earns them money, and she is subjected to his constant pranks and teasing. Her jealousy eventually pushes her to sabotage him at a public performance, setting off a chain of guilt, illness, and death that she can't undo. Despite trying to make amends by fetching a doctor, her efforts backfire, and Mozart's final words to her are both cruelly dismissive and oddly prophetic about their legacies. The story ends on a dark comedic note as she descends into madness after being shut out by the emperor in favor of Beethoven. As a parody character, she's modeled directly on the real composer Antonio Salieri, playing into the classic (if historically dubious) rivalry narrative. Voiced by Yeardley Smith. Notable quotes: "eat my pantaloons" - Mozart's dying words to Sally Salieri
quotes: "eat my pantaloons" - Mozart's dying words to Sally Salieri

title: Little Bo Peep
text: Little Bo Peep is Nursery rhyme character who appears as a park attraction figure in Storytown Village, linked to Lisa's decision to become a vegetarian. Little Bo Peep is a background nursery-rhyme figure rather than a fully developed character, existing mainly as a statue or costume reference within the Simpsons universe. She first appears as part of Little Bo Peep's Petting Zoo in Storytown Village, the setting where Lisa bonds with a lamb and subsequently swears off meat. Her attraction later falls into disrepair, gets set ablaze by Homer and Bart, and the land is eventually repurposed into the religious theme park Praiseland. Beyond the petting zoo, she shows up as an animated character in a Christmas television special, singing alongside a hobgoblin. She also inspires a cosplay outfit worn by Janey, complete with a borrowed slip, Grampa's cane, and Maggie's stuffed sheep. Overall, she's a recurring visual motif tied to nostalgia, childhood innocence, and satirical commentary on kitschy Americana attractions. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Drew Scott
text: Drew Scott is Canadian TV personality (based on the real Property Brothers star) who appears in Homer's dreams and on TV within the show. Drew Scott is a fictionalized version of the real-life home renovation star, known for co-hosting Property Brothers alongside his twin brother Jonathan Scott. In the world of the Simpsons, he exists mainly as a pop-culture reference rather than a fleshed-out character. He notably appears in one of Marge's dreams, where Homer bizarrely takes on the identity of both Scott twins at once. In a non-canon story, his show becomes a minor plot device when a kidnapper holding Homer hostage turns out to be a devoted fan of Property Brothers. Drew himself doesn't have much personality on screen, functioning more as a cameo nod to the popular HGTV series. His brief appearances tie him to themes of twins and television personalities within the show's universe. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Wendy Sage
text: Wendy Sage is A hypnotherapist who helped Lisa and Marge work through their family issues. Dr. Wendy Sage is a hypnotherapist introduced when Luann recommended her to help Lisa and Marge resolve tension between them. She is also a breast cancer survivor, a detail visibly reflected in her design through a port-o-cath scar, an asymmetrical chest, and curly regrowing hair from chemotherapy. Though Lisa is initially skeptical of hypnotherapy and doubts her legitimacy, Dr. Sage proves capable by guiding both Lisa and Marge into their subconscious minds to work through their problems. Privately, she is insecure about being dismissed as a "quack" by skeptics. She continues to appear around Springfield afterward, including at the mall and at a charity event honoring breast cancer awareness. Her recurring presence ties her to themes of mental health and personal resilience in the show. Voiced by Renee Ridgeley.

title: Brunella Pommelhorst
text: Brunella Pommelhorst is Physical Education teacher at Springfield Elementary School. Brunella Pommelhorst is the tough, no-nonsense gym teacher at Springfield Elementary. She's notorious for prioritizing her own convenience over student safety, famously abandoning a student mid-exercise the instant a teachers' strike began. A devoted fan of Xena: Warrior Princess, she takes personal oaths in the show's name that sometimes affect how she treats her students, including nearly failing Lisa Simpson out of stubbornness. Despite her hardened exterior, she occasionally shows flexibility, as seen when she let Lisa make up her grade through private lessons. In a more dramatic turn, she announced plans to undergo gender reassignment surgery, though she ultimately seems to have backed out. She later had a romantic encounter with Superintendent Chalmers during a Halloween-themed event. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Sally Jessy Raphael
text: Sally Jessy Raphael is Real-world talk show host caricatured as a minor recurring character in the Simpsons universe. Sally Jessy Raphael appears as a parody version of herself, hosting a tabloid-style talk show within the Simpsons world. She's depicted as someone who prioritizes emotional spectacle over factual evidence, willing to let a guest's tears substitute for actual proof of wrongdoing. This portrayal pokes fun at the sensationalist nature of daytime talk shows during the height of their popularity. Her most notable appearance ties into the media frenzy surrounding accusations against Homer Simpson, where her show becomes a vehicle for spreading unverified claims. She also shows up briefly as one of many TV personalities Homer flips past while channel surfing, reinforcing her status as a background pop-culture reference rather than a fully developed character. Overall, she serves as a satirical jab at trial-by-media culture rather than a character with her own arc. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Raphael responded that her tears said more than any real evidence ever could.
quotes: Raphael responded that her tears said more than any real evidence ever could.

title: Poseidon
text: Poseidon is Greek mythological god of the sea, portrayed by Horatio McCallister in the Simpsons' retelling of the Odyssey. Poseidon appears in the Simpsons' parody of Homer's Odyssey, featured in the "Tales from the Public Domain" segment based on stories from Classics for Children. Acting on his brother Zeus's orders, he torments Odysseus by delaying his journey home to Ithaca for a decade. He demonstrates a mischievous, almost cartoonish sense of humor, treating his godly powers like a prank rather than genuine wrath, going so far as to nudge Odysseus's ship backward on a map just to mess with him. After each act of sabotage, he revels in his own trickery with glee. His characterization borrows directly from classic Looney Tunes humor, giving him a playful, self-satisfied personality despite his immense power over the seas and earthquakes. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Arrr, ain't I a stinker.
quotes: Arrr, ain't I a stinker.

title: Tabitha Shingle
text: Tabitha Shingle is A minor recurring podcaster in Springfield, occasionally crossing paths with the Simpson family. Tabitha Shingle is a Springfield-based podcaster best known for hosting the wildly popular show 'Interminable', which she claims has racked up over 20 million downloads and is being turned into a streaming series featuring Alexander Skarsgård. She later moves on to host another podcast called 'Sunken Anchor', showing she's not tied to just one project. Beyond her media career, she's shown to have a social life around town, participating in a trivia team called 'Answers, She Guessed' at Moe's Tavern. She's also spotted casually at the Springfield Mall, suggesting she's a fairly ordinary local figure despite her podcasting fame. Tabitha doesn't have a deep personality explored on the show, functioning mostly as a background character tied to Springfield's media and social scene. Her recurring appearances hint at a minor but persistent presence in the town's day-to-day life. Voiced by Christine Nangle.

title: Mrs. Pennyfeather
text: Mrs. Pennyfeather is A nanny who applied to work for the Simpson family. Mrs. Pennyfeather is an elderly woman with grey hair who briefly appears as a prospective nanny for the Simpson household. She shows up at a time when Marge is under so much stress that her hair is falling out, offering her services to help the family. Homer, however, becomes suspicious of her after having seen the film Mrs. Doubtfire, convinced that she is actually a man disguised as an old woman. This leads to an awkward and physical mix-up, as Homer tries to forcibly expose her supposed disguise, only to fail and prove his assumption wrong. The character is essentially a one-episode parody nod to the Mrs. Doubtfire film. She later reappears in a non-canon capacity in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Maggie Roswell.

title: The Pale Man
text: The Pale Man is A child-eating monster who appears as a minor crossover character in The Simpsons. The Pale Man is a ghoulish, non-speaking creature borrowed from Guillermo del Toro's film Pan's Labyrinth. In the show's canon, he oddly serves as a doorman for Mr. Burns, greeting him with a high-five as Burns enters his mansion. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, his more monstrous nature is shown when he devours a fairy after it cleans his eyes. He has no dialogue, making his presence purely visual and eerie. His appearances are brief cameo-style crossovers rather than a developed role in the main story. He stands out mainly as a horror-genre reference and a nod to del Toro's work.

title: Old lady
text: Old lady is A minor recurring elderly character who once hired Bart to pose as her grandson. The old lady is a minor senior character who appears in only a couple of episodes. She's notable for hiring Bart to impersonate her grandson, seemingly enjoying his flattering, attentive company. She frequents a hair salon called Curl Up and Dye, where she gets her hair done alongside other recurring background characters like Agnes Skinner and Manacek. She seems easily charmed and somewhat naive, taking Bart's exaggerated claims at face value. Beyond her salon visits and her arrangement with Bart, little else is known about her life or personality. She functions mostly as a one-off gag character tied to Bart's schemes. Voiced by Valerie Harper. Notable quotes: "so thoughtful"
quotes: "so thoughtful"

title: Rick
text: Rick is One of the 'cool kids' Lisa befriends during a summer vacation in Little Pwagmattasquarmsettport. Rick is a laid-back beach kid who becomes part of Lisa's temporary friend group while she vacations away from Springfield. He has a casual, easygoing attitude, often complaining lightly about his parents, like his mom trying to drag him to a candle shop or his dad waking him up early for a Fourth of July oath. Rick is generally welcoming to Lisa, lending her his skateboard and including her in group activities like beach exploring and hanging out at her holiday home. He's quick to call out try-hard behavior, as seen when he criticizes Bart's showy skating. Despite briefly being fooled by Bart's prank revealing Lisa's nerdy side, Rick ultimately helps orchestrate a kind gesture by decorating the Simpsons' car with shells to cheer Lisa up. He only appears in one episode, making him a minor but memorable one-off character tied to Lisa's summer friendships. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Bart tried too hard. | It was cool for Marge to let them hang out there. | Wait and look.
quotes: Bart tried too hard.
It was cool for Marge to let them hang out there.
Wait and look.

title: Roberta
text: Roberta is A wealthy Springfield socialite and member of the country club set, part of Marge's brief foray into high society. Roberta is one of Springfield's snobbish elite, a country club regular who spends her time on croquet, fashion critique, and card games with fellow socialites. She's part of a clique that includes Gillian, Elizabeth, Evelyn, Susan, Patricia, and Karen, and she meets Marge when Evelyn invites her into their circle. Though outwardly polished and complimentary, her remarks often carry a backhanded, condescending edge, poking fun at Marge's modest attempts to fit into upper-class fashion. She's shown to be status-conscious even in small things, like ordering steaks through a high-end publication rather than a normal menu. Her snobbery extends beyond Marge's world too, as she coldly ignores Homer when he's reduced to posing as a hobo on the street. Overall, Roberta embodies the shallow, image-obsessed nature of Springfield's wealthy class. Voiced by Maggie Roswell. Notable quotes: Love the suit, Marge! The vest says, 'Let's do lunch!' but the culottes say, 'You're paying!'
quotes: Love the suit, Marge! The vest says, 'Let's do lunch!' but the culottes say, 'You're paying!'

title: The Shipper
text: The Shipper is A minor recurring character and delivery man who is also an internet troll and member of the Troll Force Five. The Shipper is a quirky background character whose defining trait is his obsession with 'shipping'—seeing romantic relationships between characters, whether real or entirely imagined. Working as a delivery man by day, he moonlights as an internet troll and belongs to a group called the Troll Force Five. His fixation on pairing up unlikely couples extends even to fictional characters, as seen when he insists two famous sci-fi characters are secretly a couple while making a delivery. He also appeared protesting a movie at a theater, showing his tendency to stir up online-style controversy in real life. Overall, he's a satirical jab at internet fandom culture and shipping enthusiasts. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Oddjob
text: Oddjob is A James Bond villain henchman who appears in imagined and non-canon Simpsons scenarios. Oddjob is a reference to the iconic henchman from the James Bond film Goldfinger, brought into the Simpsons universe in a couple of brief, non-mainstream appearances. He's part of a group of classic Bond villains, alongside Ernst Stavro Blofeld, Jaws, and Auric Goldfinger, that populate Homer's Bond-fantasy daydream. In a non-canon storyline, he's depicted as a card shark's muscle, helping enforce the outcome of a rigged poker game at Mr. Burns' Casino. Oddjob has no dialogue in his Simpsons appearances, fitting his role as a silent, imposing enforcer rather than a speaking character. He mainly exists as a fun cameo tying into the show's love of parodying pop culture icons like James Bond.

title: Handsome Pete
text: Handsome Pete is A minor recurring street performer character in Springfield who resembles a distorted version of Krusty the Clown. Handsome Pete is an odd, tiny performer with tufty blue hair whose face looks like a warped version of Krusty the Clown. He's mostly known for playing his concertina and dancing for spare change, a running gag tied to his introduction by the Sea Captain. Despite his name, he's explicitly noted as not actually being handsome, which adds to the joke of his character. He's a background, non-speaking figure who pops up at various public gatherings around Springfield, including street parties and crowd scenes. He is also acknowledged in-universe as ranking among Krusty's lesser-known associates, reinforcing his status as a quirky footnote in the show's world. Notable quotes: "Aye, that's Handsome Pete, he dances for nickels!"
quotes: "Aye, that's Handsome Pete, he dances for nickels!"

title: Polly (HOMЯ)
text: Polly (HOMЯ) is A genetically engineered creature (an "octoparrot") featured in the episode "HOMЯ". Polly is a strange hybrid creature created through experiments at the Screaming Monkey Medical Research Center, combining the head, body, and tail feathers of a parrot with the tentacles of an octopus in place of wings and legs. She appears when Homer visits the research facility seeking to reverse a procedure that made him intelligent. The scientists there refuse his request, insisting they don't tamper with nature, prompting Homer to argue that their very creation of Polly proves otherwise. In a darkly comic moment, Polly herself seems to agree with Homer's point by speaking up. She exists mostly as a one-off gag underscoring the absurdity and ethical carelessness of the facility's experiments. Polly later resurfaces as a minor non-canon character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: Polly shouldn't be
quotes: Polly shouldn't be

title: Lionel Richie (character)
text: Lionel Richie (character) is Celebrity guest character, a famous singer who appears as himself in the show. Lionel Richie appears as a fictionalized version of himself, a celebrity singer hired to perform on private jets for wealthy clients. When Mr. Burns hires him to entertain Homer, he takes a simple request for a song about beer and turns it into an endless repetition of the word until Homer forgets the rest of the lyrics. His vanity and attachment to his own success become a running joke, most notably when his private jet crashes and he refuses to release his armful of awards even as a rescuer tries to save him, mocking the pilot for not having any awards of his own. He later makes a cameo appearance at Moe's Tavern during a town-wide dance number to one of his hit songs. Overall, he's portrayed as good-natured but comically self-absorbed, willing to poke fun at his own celebrity status. Voiced by Lionel Richie (Himself).

title: Shiva
text: Shiva is A Hindu deity referenced/appearing in the Simpsons universe, often tied to Apu's faith and imagery. Shiva is a divine Hindu god who occasionally appears in statue form or as a mystical presence within the show's world. He is most associated with Apu Nahasapeemapetilon, who reveres him and even calls out to him for help in moments of distress. Homer, in his usual disregard for religious customs, once modified a Shiva statue with foam fingers to childproof Apu's apartment, suggesting a Buddha statue would be a safer alternative. Shiva has also appeared as a giant cosmic figure controlling the workings of the world from Australia, and as a repurposed statue outside a restaurant that used to depict Paul Bunyan. Though non-speaking, Shiva's presence often ties into comedic commentary on cultural and religious references within the show.

title: Groundskeeper Seamus
text: Groundskeeper Seamus is Groundskeeper Willie's Irish rival and fellow groundskeeper at Springfield Elementary School. Groundskeeper Seamus is a minor character defined almost entirely by his rivalry with Groundskeeper Willie. The two men clash both professionally and personally, even squaring off in formal debates during school assemblies. Their feud escalates when Seamus is fired from his job at Springfield Elementary, an event he blames squarely on Willie, leading to a physical brawl between them. In a non-canon story, Bart transforms Seamus into a villainous 'Green Gobbler' character as part of a prank meant to convince Willie he has Spider-Man-like powers, sparking another confrontation between the two rivals. He also appears among the townspeople during an uprising against Mr. Burns, accepting a torch from Moe as part of the revolt. Overall, Seamus functions as a comedic foil whose entire purpose revolves around antagonizing Willie. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: RV salesman
text: RV salesman is Minor recurring background character, an unnamed employee at Bob's RV Round-Up who previously worked at Stan's Keyboards. The RV salesman is a nameless, unremarkable Springfield worker who has bounced between odd retail jobs, including a stint singing jingles at a keyboard store before landing at an RV dealership. He's the type of background character who exists mostly to move small plot points along, like tipping off his boss about troublesome kids. His loyalty to his employer, Cowboy Bob, borders on absurd, as he goes along with a bizarre and dangerous scheme involving a giant parade balloon without much protest. He lacks any strong personality traits of his own, serving more as a functional side character than a fully realized one. His two appearances are separated by years, showing he's a recurring but very minor fixture in the show's world of interchangeable retail employees. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Bob, word on the street is there's two kids trying to return an RV.
quotes: Bob, word on the street is there's two kids trying to return an RV.

title: Silver Surfer
text: Silver Surfer is Marvel Comics superhero referenced within the Simpsons universe, mostly through cosplay, merchandise, and cameo appearances. The Silver Surfer is a real-world Marvel superhero who pops up in the Simpsons universe as a piece of pop culture rather than a fully fleshed-out character. He appears as a costume worn by a cosplayer at a convention, as a collectible figure in Comic Book Guy's apartment, and is name-dropped as one of Stan Lee's creations during a eulogy. In a non-canon segment, he even makes a fantastical cameo flying past the Simpson family while they're stranded on an alien planet, carrying a woman on his shoulders. He never speaks and functions purely as a background reference or homage to Marvel Comics within the show's comic-fan culture. His recurring appearances tie into the show's fondness for referencing real comic book lore through characters like Comic Book Guy.

title: Pinhead
text: Pinhead is A parody crossover character based on the Hellraiser film franchise's villain, appearing in Simpsons horror-themed segments. Pinhead is a nightmarish crossover figure imported from the Hellraiser horror films, serving as a background monster in the show's various horror-tinged segments. He first appears menacing Bart in a dream sequence alongside other iconic slasher villains before being driven off by an unlikely hero. He later shows up as one of many attackers during a training sequence, only to be easily overpowered. Beyond his own appearances, he's become a popular costume choice for fans within the show's universe, notably worn by Comic Book Guy. He's a non-speaking character, existing purely as a visual horror reference rather than a developed personality, and has even been humorously slotted into the extended Burns family tree in one Halloween special.

title: George S. Patton
text: George S. Patton is Historical World War II general depicted in a Grampa Simpson war story and a DVD commercial parody. This version of General Patton appears mainly as a figure in Grampa Simpson's recollections of his World War II days, where he commands the assault on the Nazi base at Ham Salad Hill. After sending several units to their failure, he reluctantly deploys the ragtag Flying Hellfish unit, much to his own dismay. Adding a comedic twist to his tough-guy reputation, Grampa claims Patton actually spoke in a high, squeaky voice, which made the Flying Hellfish mock him behind his back. In a separate, unrelated bit, he's shown in a mock World War II DVD commercial being saved from a helmet bomb by a heroic carrier pigeon. He's also referenced as an example on one of Ned Flanders' odd historical lists. Overall, he functions as a background historical joke rather than a fully fleshed-out character. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Rover
text: Rover is A vicious Bull Terrier dog who repeatedly attacks and chases Bart. Rover is a white Bull Terrier with a deep and inexplicable hatred for Bart Simpson. What starts as a hopeful attempt by Bart to make a new friend quickly turns into an ongoing campaign of terror, with Rover ambushing him at nearly every turn—through mail slots, behind hedges, on the school bus, and even at a dog show. Despite his aggression toward Bart, Rover can turn instantly sweet and affectionate around other people, most notably Homer, showing a two-faced charm that makes his menace toward Bart even more pointed. The Simpsons family eventually starts trying to appease him, going so far as baking him Bart-shaped treats. A brief truce is achieved thanks to a calming trick taught by old western star Buck McCoy, but the peace doesn't last, and Rover returns to his relentless pursuit of Bart. He later reappears in a minor role, digging a hole during a documentary segment. Voiced by Frank Welker.

title: Mr. Powell
text: Mr. Powell is Minor recurring character; father of Janey Powell, a classmate of Lisa Simpson. Mr. Powell is a background father figure in Springfield, primarily known through his connection to his daughter Janey. He is married to Mrs. Powell, and the family appears together in various community settings. One notable appearance shows him attending the Bounce-A-Thon alongside his wife and daughter, suggesting he is an involved and supportive parent. As a non-speaking character, he has no distinct personality traits or catchphrases established in the show. He functions mainly as part of the show's expansive background cast of Springfield parents, appearing periodically across many seasons without significant storylines of his own. His presence helps flesh out the extended social circle of Janey Powell and the town's ensemble of recurring townsfolk.

title: Betsy Ross
text: Betsy Ross is Historical figure appearing in a Springfield-imagined flashback, credited as the seamstress of the first American flag. Betsy Ross appears in a comedic flashback where she presents George Washington with the newly sewn American flag during his fight with a pirate. True to the show's irreverent take on history, she flubs the design, unable to find the red hearts, yellow moons, or green clovers Washington apparently wanted, leaving him unimpressed and unwilling to pay. Beyond this appearance, her legacy pops up as a costume choice for Luann Van Houten and as a punny clue in a treasure hunt referencing her as 'the first sewer.' She's also honored as one of the historical women depicted in Lisa's diorama celebrating notable women. Though a minor, real-world-based character, she's used for quick historical gags rather than any deep characterization. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: I got the white stars you wanted, but I couldn't find any red hearts yellow moons or green clovers. | Well, I'll use it, but I'm not paying for it.
quotes: I got the white stars you wanted, but I couldn't find any red hearts yellow moons or green clovers.
Well, I'll use it, but I'm not paying for it.

title: Richard's mother
text: Richard's mother is Minor recurring character; mother of Richard, one of the schoolchildren in Springfield. Richard's mother is a minor, background figure in the Simpsons universe, known mainly through her family connection to her son Richard rather than through any dialogue or major storyline. She is blonde-haired and appears to be a fairly ordinary Springfield parent, seen accompanying her family to community events. She is classified as a non-speaking character, meaning she has never been given any lines in her appearances, existing mostly as a visual presence in crowd or family scenes. Her most notable moment is attending the Bounce-A-Thon alongside her husband and son, suggesting she is an involved, supportive parent. Beyond this, little else is known about her personality or role, as she functions primarily as background family representation rather than a character with an active part in the plot.

title: Zia Simpson
text: Zia Simpson is Future daughter of Lisa Simpson and Milhouse Van Houten, a non-canon character appearing in flash-forward episodes. Zia is a teenage glimpse into a possible future where Lisa and Milhouse end up together and have a daughter. She looks almost identical to Lisa, since she was genetically engineered mostly from Lisa's DNA, with only a single streak of blue hair betraying her father's contribution. As a teen she's rebellious and distant, frustrating her mother by spending Christmas glued to the internet instead of bonding with family. Her one distinctive physical quirk is a shifting holographic tattoo on her arm that cycles through symbols like a peace sign, a biohazard icon, and a yin-yang. Despite their friction, Lisa eventually discovers online that Zia secretly admires her. Beyond her debut, Zia turns up in later flash-forward material, including archive footage and a family Thanksgiving after Homer's death, and she was also featured as a playable character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Pneumatica
text: Pneumatica is Comic book supervillain robot, mother of Radioactive Man's alter ego Claude Kane III. Pneumatica is a comic-book-only Simpsons character whose true identity is Camellia Kane, wife of Claude Kane II and mother of Claude Kane III, the future superhero Radioactive Man. Originally a human on a secretive government mission, she was shot down over the Pacific and rescued by the villainous Dr. Crab, who transplanted her brain into a robotic body and brainwashed her into becoming a supervillain. As Pneumatica, she becomes one of Radioactive Man's recurring foes, unaware for a time that the hero she battles is actually her own son. Her tragic backstory is eventually revealed when a machine restores her lost memories during a climactic confrontation. The character serves as a parody of real-life aviator Amelia Earhart, echoing her disappearance during a round-the-world flight. A larger, more dangerous version of her, called Nega-Pneumatica, was later created as a government project.

title: Vladimir Putin
text: Vladimir Putin is Real-world Russian politician (President of Russia) parodied as a recurring background/reference character in The Simpsons. This version of Vladimir Putin is a caricature of the real Russian president, popping up mostly in gags tied to current events and other world leaders. He's shown as a shirtless, horseback-riding strongman in a parody of his famous publicity photos, which Maggie once interrupts by handing him a shirt. In another non-canon bit, he disguises himself as an ordinary Trump-supporting voter to talk up Russia to Homer before riding off dramatically on a horse. He's frequently linked to Donald Trump, appearing as a contact in Trump's phone and receiving an insulting call from him. Burns treats him as a source of extreme luxury and danger, mailing himself to Putin's office and claiming to own vodka distilled by him personally. Overall, the character functions as a running political satire figure rather than a fully developed personality. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns said that's 100 proof Russian vodka distilled by Putin himself. | Donald Trump got Putin on the phone to call him a "tiny, bald fascist" and to tell him to leave the USA alone.
quotes: Mr. Burns said that's 100 proof Russian vodka distilled by Putin himself.
Donald Trump got Putin on the phone to call him a "tiny, bald fascist" and to tell him to leave the USA alone.

title: Warren Sapp (character)
text: Warren Sapp (character) is Real-life NFL football player who appears as himself in a guest role on The Simpsons. Warren Sapp appears as a fictionalized version of himself, one of several professional athletes recruited by Homer Simpson for his Showboating Academy, where he learns how to perform obnoxious end-zone-style celebrations. He's shown sharing a dinner with the Simpson family alongside his fellow athlete students, suggesting he's a good sport willing to mingle with ordinary fans. A humorous montage on a sports show depicts him aggressively knocking down an opponent before comically painting a picture of his own body, poking fun at athlete egotism. He later takes part in Homer's chaotic Super Bowl halftime show, physically helping move a large ark-like prop. In a small comedic aside, he awkwardly flirts with fellow athlete Michelle Kwan, asking about her relationship status. His role is minor and comedic, existing mainly to satirize celebrity athlete culture and showboating in sports. Voiced by Warren Sapp (Himself).

title: The Riddler
text: The Riddler is A DC Comics supervillain referenced within the Simpsons universe, appearing as a musical parody and a Halloween costume. The Riddler is not an original Simpsons character but a nod to the DC Comics villain, appearing only in minor, non-speaking capacities. He shows up as part of a musical parody called 'Riddler on the Roof,' seen in a picture during an episode. He also appears in another context as a Halloween costume worn by Bart. Since he never speaks or takes on a substantial role, he functions purely as a background reference or pop-culture cameo rather than a developed character. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent habit of blending outside franchises and characters into its own world for quick jokes or visual gags.

title: Sideshow Mel's son
text: Sideshow Mel's son is Illegitimate son of Sideshow Mel, a minor student character at Springfield Elementary. This character is a minor student at Springfield Elementary School, notable primarily for being the secret, illegitimate offspring of Sideshow Mel. His existence comes to light when Mel reveals it publicly during a student president debate, causing his son visible embarrassment. He has green hair, presumably inherited from his father, and doesn't have much of an established personality beyond his awkward reaction to being outed. He later becomes a point of discussion when Mel tries to formalize family ties by asking someone else to be the boy's godfather, though that request is rebuffed. Overall, he functions as a one-off gag character tied to Sideshow Mel's comedic backstory rather than a fully developed personality. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "oh, the shame."
quotes: "oh, the shame."

title: Martha Peterson
text: Martha Peterson is Minor recurring character, a DMV employee whose brief romance storyline appears in one episode. Martha Peterson is a background employee at the Department of Motor Vehicles who exists mostly in the periphery of Springfield life. Her most notable moment comes from a workplace lunchroom encounter that sparks a romance with a coworker. She has no lines of dialogue in the show, making her a purely visual presence. Despite her limited screen time, she is memorable for the small, human side-story of finding love in an unglamorous setting like the DMV. Her arc concludes with a wedding officiated by Reverend Lovejoy, giving her a modest but complete personal narrative within the Simpsons universe.

title: Lee Harvey Oswald
text: Lee Harvey Oswald is Real-world historical figure referenced in Simpsons episodes as the assassin of President John F. Kennedy. Lee Harvey Oswald appears in the show not as a traditional character but as a recurring historical reference tied to the JFK assassination. He's depicted in a parody Itchy and Scratchy cartoon directed by Oliver Stone, where Scratchy plays Oswald being shot by Itchy as Jack Ruby, mirroring the climax of Stone's own JFK film. He's also the subject of a running joke where Homer misunderstands the facts of the assassination, confusing Jack Ruby's name with an actual ruby jewel. His image is used satirically in a Krusty the Clown campaign video, superimposed over the famous photo of his real-life shooting. In one of Homer's historical fantasies, he even gets beaten up by Homer and Abraham Lincoln before he can shoot Kennedy. Overall, Oswald functions purely as a satirical pop-culture reference rather than a fleshed-out character.

title: Sexy assistant
text: Sexy assistant is A minor recurring character who interviewed for the job of Homer's assistant at the power plant. The sexy assistant is a minor character who shows up during Homer's brief stint as an executive after regrowing his hair with Dimoxinil. She interviews for the position of his personal assistant, using flirtatious charm rather than qualifications to try to land the job. Her overtly seductive approach backfires, as Homer nervously turns her down and instead hires a male assistant, Karl, to avoid temptation. She later makes a brief cameo walking down the street, drawing attention from Mayor Quimby. Though she has no dialogue-heavy role or deep characterization, she serves as a one-off gag about Homer's awkward relationship with attention from women during his executive phase. Voiced by Pamela Hayden. Notable quotes: "Here, let me show you."
quotes: "Here, let me show you."

title: Sigrin Siguðardóttir
text: Sigrin Siguðardóttir is Adoptive mother of Carl Carlson, from Iceland. Sigrin is an elderly Icelandic woman married to Carl Carlson, Sr. and the adoptive mother of Carl Carlson. Her family, the Carlsons, were historically shamed watchmen who supposedly failed to stop an invading horde a thousand years ago, making them social outcasts in their community. She lives in Reykjavík, where Carl visits after winning the lottery in hopes of restoring his family's honor. Sigrin doesn't speak on screen, and her role is largely tied to the reveal of her family's true, less flattering history. In the end, thanks to Carl's good deeds being publicized, she and her husband are finally accepted back into their community. A photo of her and her husband later appears displayed in Carl's home.

title: Colonel Sanders
text: Colonel Sanders is Real-world fast food entrepreneur (founder of Kentucky Fried Chicken) who appears as a recurring background/dream character in The Simpsons. Colonel Sanders is a fictionalized version of the real KFC founder who pops up occasionally in surreal or dream-like sequences throughout the show. He's been depicted casually hanging out in Heaven with God and Buddha, feeding God popcorn chicken, and appearing as a knowledgeable figure who understands the mysterious 'Answer.' He frequently shows up alongside other famous fast food mascots like Ronald McDonald and the Burger King, whether in group meetings plotting against Homer or as part of Homer's fantastical daydreams about fast food royalty. His presence is often symbolic rather than substantial, representing the omnipresence of fast food branding in the Simpsons universe. He's even been immortalized as a statue in an exhibit, cementing his status as a piece of Americana. Despite being deceased in real life, he continues to appear in the show's whimsical afterlife and dream sequences. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Sleazy Sam
text: Sleazy Sam is Minor recurring character; owner of a payday loan business in Springfield. Sleazy Sam is a minor Springfield businessman who runs a chain of payday loan stores, boasting a surprising fifty branches across town. His name alone hints at his dubious reputation as a lender, suggesting predatory or shady business practices typical of such establishments. He appeared publicly at the opening of one of his new branches, an event that took an unexpected turn involving Homer dressed as a religious figure. The moment played into the show's love of absurd, ironic humor, as an endorsement of Sam's trustworthiness was immediately undercut by a divine-seeming interruption. Beyond this brief spotlight, Sam remains a background figure representing Springfield's seedier commercial side. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Scruffy
text: Scruffy is Janitor from Futurama who appears in a Simpsons/Futurama crossover episode. Scruffy is a janitor best known from the Futurama universe who crosses paths with the Simpsons world during a time-travel crossover event. He's a laid-back, unbothered figure even in the face of monster attacks, treating dismemberment with a shrug. His signature trait is his devotion to his mustache, valuing it so highly that its loss becomes a matter of life and death to him. It's later revealed that he's secretly a zombie, which explains how he keeps working even after losing his head. Outside of canon material, he's also depicted taking on a similar janitorial role at Springfield Elementary School. Overall he's a minor but memorable comic-relief character defined by dark humor and understatement. Voiced by David Herman. Notable quotes: life without a mustache wasn't worth living
quotes: life without a mustache wasn't worth living

title: Rapunzel (Disney)
text: Rapunzel (Disney) is A Disney crossover character appearing in Simpsons specials, princess from Tangled. Rapunzel is a Disney princess who makes a crossover appearance in The Simpsons universe, tied to her biological mother Queen Arianna and her adoptive mother Mother Gothel. She's depicted as a non-speaking character, existing outside the show's main canon as part of a special crossover storyline. Her main appearance involves a lighthearted Mother's Day outing to a Disney-themed park with her two mothers. Later, she becomes entangled in a bizarre meta-plot involving copyright disputes between Disney and the Grimm brothers, which results in a dramatic and unexpected fate. Overall, she serves more as a cameo/reference figure for crossover humor rather than a developed character with her own arc.

title: Scoey (Saturdays of Thunder)
text: Scoey (Saturdays of Thunder) is A fictional character within the McBain movie-within-a-show, serving as McBain's police partner. Scoey is a veteran police officer and the loyal partner of the action hero McBain within the fictional film series parodied on The Simpsons. Just two days from retirement, he was looking forward to a quiet life, having recently christened a boat with his wife for a long-awaited trip around the world, while proudly celebrating his daughter Suzie's college graduation. His arc is a dark parody of the classic buddy-cop trope where the near-retirement partner meets a tragic end, echoing similar characters like Sergeant Murtaugh from the Lethal Weapon films. Scoey is gunned down by an assassin disguised as a waiter, taking bullets meant for McBain, and dies in his partner's arms, fueling McBain's quest for vengeance. Despite being a minor, one-off tragic figure, he later appears in non-canon material like The Simpsons: Tapped Out. His full name is given as Dexter Scoey in certain merchandise materials. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: John C. Reilly (character)
text: John C. Reilly (character) is Real-life celebrity cameo appearance as himself in the Simpsons universe. John C. Reilly appears as a fictionalized version of himself, the real-world actor, comedian, producer, singer, and writer. In his main appearance, he attends the Sundance Film Festival hoping to be cast in a Chalmskinn Productions film, only to be passed over by Superintendent Chalmers and Principal Skinner. He also shows up in a background gag as a photograph hanging on the wall of a local establishment. His role is minor and largely a celebrity cameo rather than a fleshed-out character, playing on his real identity as a well-known actor. There isn't much personality development given to him beyond being a recognizable famous face dropped into Springfield's world. Voiced by John C. Reilly (Himself).

title: The Scout Master
text: The Scout Master is Fictional supervillain from the in-universe Radioactive Man television series watched by Bart and Milhouse. The Scout Master is a villain who appears within the show-within-a-show Radioactive Man television series. He commands a group of boy scout henchmen who do his bidding, and he encourages them toward violence rather than the wholesome ideals scouting usually represents. According to Fallout Boy, he is considered the worst villain that Radioactive Man and Fallout Boy have ever faced. His design and demeanor are based on actor Paul Lynde, giving him a campy, theatrical quality reminiscent of villains from the classic 1960s Batman TV series, even though Lynde himself never appeared on that show. He represents a satirical jab at old-school superhero show villains, existing purely within the fictional media consumed by Springfield's residents. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "Don't be afraid to use your nails boys!"
quotes: "Don't be afraid to use your nails boys!"

title: Katy Perry (character)
text: Katy Perry (character) is Real-world celebrity guest character who appears as Moe's dream girlfriend in a Simpsons episode. Katy Perry appears as a live-action guest star within one of Maggie's dream sequences, portrayed as Moe's secret girlfriend.
