Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "Oh, do your research, Shutton!" - Kent Brockman
quotes: "Oh, do your research, Shutton!" - Kent Brockman

title: Tupac Shakur
text: Tupac Shakur is Real-world rapper/actor referenced and appearing as a hologram in the Simpsons universe. Tupac Shakur appears in the show as a deceased real-world celebrity, referenced in various episodes rather than as a regular character. He's imagined as one of Heaven's eligible bachelors alongside figures like John Wayne and Sherlock Holmes. His most notable appearance is as a hologram entertainer, once dancing to a song by Princess Diana at the Simpsons' home, and later appearing in a bizarre wedding invitation hologram where he raps and expresses a wish to be freed from his digital resurrection. In non-canon material, he's depicted competing against Ludwig van Beethoven in a heavenly rap contest. His likeness has also been used in smaller gags, such as a photo on a website's musician-identifying captcha test. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson. Notable quotes: god bless you
quotes: god bless you

title: Pokey
text: Pokey is Lisa Simpson's pet guinea pig. Pokey is a small, light brown guinea pig belonging to Lisa Simpson. He's a minor, non-speaking pet character whose main claim to fame is causing a bit of household chaos by destroying the Simpsons' living room art. Unlike many other Simpsons pets, Pokey originated outside the show, first appearing in a content update for the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out tied to the episode "The War of Art" before later making an appearance in the actual TV series. He holds the distinction of being the second character to be introduced this way, following Kumiko and preceding several others like Freedom and the Mutant Rabbit. As a guinea pig, Pokey doesn't have much personality shown beyond being a mischievous little pet.

title: Julius Pringles
text: Julius Pringles is A minor recurring parody character based on the Pringles mascot, appearing occasionally in Springfield-related fantasies and media. Julius Pringles is a comedic stand-in for the real-world Pringles brand mascot, popping up in odd, surreal contexts throughout the show. He first appears in a fantasy sequence involving Homer, reacting with deadpan shock after a mishap involving another character. His likeness later shows up as a mustache option on a Homer's tablet app, prompting an unexpectedly complimentary remark from Marge about his eyes. He's also used as a promotional mascot for a fictional novelty product, tying his brand-parody nature into the show's love of consumer culture jokes. Julius doesn't have much personality of his own beyond his role as a background gag, but his recurring cameo appearances make him a fun bit of trivia for eagle-eyed fans. He's more of a running visual joke than a fully developed character. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "you killed him"
quotes: "you killed him"

title: Rodan
text: Rodan is A fictional Japanese movie monster that appears as a background/cameo creature in Simpsons episodes referencing Godzilla-style films. Rodan is a giant irradiated pteranodon monster borrowed from the world of Japanese kaiju films, appearing in The Simpsons purely as a visual gag and pop-culture reference. He first shows up in Lisa's anxious daydream about being exiled to a monster-infested island as punishment for failing gym class, alongside other famous movie monsters. Later, he makes a more active appearance attacking the Simpson family's plane as they leave Tokyo, teaming up with Godzilla, Mothra, and Gamera. He also turns up in a retelling of the Paul Bunyan legend, where he battles Paul Bunyan and Babe the Blue Ox. Notably, in that tall tale appearance he is given Godzilla's roar instead of his own. Rodan never speaks and functions as a non-speaking, recurring background monster rather than a developed character.

title: Michelle Obama
text: Michelle Obama is First Lady of the United States and wife of President Barack Obama, appearing as a real-world guest character. Michelle Obama appears as a supportive, encouraging figure who takes a personal interest in Lisa Simpson's life outside the White House. She secretly follows Lisa's organic gardening blog under the anonymous username "FLOTUS1," leaving supportive comments without revealing her identity at first. When Lisa is bullied by classmates for being an overachiever, Michelle dramatically intervenes, landing at Springfield Elementary in a helicopter with Marines and Secret Service agents in tow. She delivers a heartfelt speech urging students to respect academically gifted peers like Lisa, Martin Prince, and Allison Taylor. Her reveal as FLOTUS1 ties into a running gag involving Ralph Wiggum, who had already claimed the username "FLOTUS" for himself with a nonsensical comment. She is portrayed as warm, principled, and genuinely invested in children's education and self-esteem. Voiced by Angela Bassett. Notable quotes: "[swam] with his flotuses on." (Ralph Wiggum, referenced in context of Michelle Obama's username story)
quotes: "[swam] with his flotuses on." (Ralph Wiggum, referenced in context of Michelle Obama's username story)

title: Rosie O'Donnell
text: Rosie O'Donnell is Celebrity guest character based on the real-life comedian, appearing in cameo and Halloween episode roles. Rosie O'Donnell appears in the show as a fictionalized version of the real-life comedian and talk show host. In canon, she is briefly seen among a group of celebrities who fall from the Duff blimp during a mishap. Her more memorable moments come in the non-canon Treehouse of Horror segments, where she is depicted aboard a rocket heading into the sun, cheerfully telling everyone to stay positive before breaking into song, an act so unbearable it pushes Homer and Bart to hasten their own demise. She's also referenced through a fictional stage musical based on her life, which Ned Flanders predicts will be a quick flop. Later, she's mentioned again in a phone call from Donald Trump, who praises her performance in a Flintstones movie. Overall, she serves as a running pop-culture gag rather than a fleshed-out character. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Rod Serling
text: Rod Serling is Non-canon real-world character (based on the actual TV writer/narrator) who appears briefly in Simpsons media. This is a non-canon depiction of the real-life American screenwriter, playwright, television producer, and narrator Rod Serling, best known for hosting anthology shows in the style of The Twilight Zone. In the Simpsons universe he shows up as a background or framing figure rather than a fully developed character. He was spotted around Springfield during a Halloween special, and later served as a narrator figure introducing a segment where Bart falls asleep after drinking a bad Squishee. He's also referenced in a comic mash-up, where Bart combines him with the character Gorilla Grodd to create the punny hybrid figure Grodd Serling. Being non-canon and drawn from a real person, he doesn't have an established personality or recurring gags within the show itself, functioning more as a pop-culture cameo.

title: Scarlet tanager
text: Scarlet tanager is A minor recurring animal character, a songbird that inadvertently gets caught up in Bart's schemes. The scarlet tanager is a small, colorful songbird that appears in a couple of episodes as an unwitting participant in Bart's antics. In one instance, Bart ties a tracking chip to the bird's leg, causing his family to mistakenly follow the tanager all the way to Machu Picchu, believing it to be him. In another appearance, the bird disrupts one of Bart's pranks by pecking at the buttons of a laptop being used to fool Principal Skinner with a recording of Barack Obama's voice. The tanager has no dialogue and functions purely as a comedic plot device rather than a character with personality of its own. Despite its minor role, it has become a memorable one-off gag creature within the show's long history of odd animal appearances.

title: Scratchy, Jr.
text: Scratchy, Jr. is Cartoon character; son of Scratchy the Cat in the show-within-a-show The Itchy & Scratchy Show. Scratchy, Jr. is a minor cartoon character who exists within the violent world of The Itchy & Scratchy Show, following in his father's unfortunate footsteps as a victim of Itchy's schemes. Like most characters in this parody cartoon, he suffers gruesome, slapstick fates alongside his father, Scratchy the Cat. His appearances are brief but memorable, often showing him witnessing or sharing in his father's misfortune. He has no real personality of his own beyond being a helpless bystander in the chaotic cat-and-mouse violence that defines the show. His recurring role highlights the exaggerated, dark humor of the Itchy & Scratchy cartoons that The Simpsons uses to satirize classic animated shorts. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Hiram Simpson
text: Hiram Simpson is An ancestor of the Simpson family, a sharecropper appearing in the flashback episode "The Color Yellow". Hiram Simpson was a sharecropper living in Springfield during the antebellum period, toiling under the plantation owner Colonel Burns. He was married to Mabel Simpson and was the father of Eliza Simpson, making him an early link in the Simpson family line. Though he grudgingly agreed to shelter an escaped slave named Virgil after being won over by his cooking, Hiram's loyalty proved shallow, as he betrayed Virgil's hiding spot the moment Colonel Burns offered him a bribe. His greed and weakness led directly to the collapse of his marriage, since Mabel left him for Virgil after their escape to Canada. The divorce left him humiliated, forced to surrender one of the very shoes he'd been bribed with, though he pettily held onto the laces. Overall, Hiram is portrayed as a morally compromised, self-interested figure whose small betrayal has lasting personal consequences. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Gary Price
text: Gary Price is A minor recurring Springfield resident who works as a realtor (and apparently also runs a beauty salon). Gary Price is a background Springfield character best known for his brief but memorable appearance trying to sell 742 Evergreen Terrace after the Winfields moved out. His sales pitch collapses the moment prospective buyers hear Homer splashing around in his kiddie pool, leading to an exasperated reaction from Gary. He seems to have more than one profession, later shown running a beauty salon where a loud barber chair noise startles Officer Marge into pulling her gun. He also turns up unexpectedly at a resort during Smithers' vacation, blending into a crowd scene involving a conga line. Gary doesn't have a strong personality of his own, functioning mostly as a recurring extra who pops up in unrelated professions and situations across several episodes. Voiced by Harry Shearer, Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Sigh!
quotes: Sigh!

title: Ebenezer Scrooge
text: Ebenezer Scrooge is A crossover/fictional-within-fiction character referencing Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol, appearing briefly in the Simpsons universe. Ebenezer Scrooge is a reference to the classic Charles Dickens character, appearing in the Simpsons universe as a nod to the famous holiday tale. In this incarnation, he shows up as a character within a video game called Frosty the Hit Man, where his story takes a dark turn when he is killed by Frosty. In a non-canon appearance, his presence is hinted at through a gravestone bearing his name, spotted by Homer in a graveyard-themed room. His inclusion serves mostly as a pop-culture easter egg rather than a fully developed character, playing on audience familiarity with the original Dickens tale. He has no dialogue or defined personality traits within the show itself, functioning purely as a background reference and crossover gag.

title: Miguel Rivera
text: Miguel Rivera is Crossover character from Pixar's Coco, appearing in non-canon Simpsons specials. Miguel Rivera is a crossover character brought into the Simpsons universe from the Pixar film Coco. He appears as part of special, non-canon episodes celebrating Disney+ milestones, reflecting the studio's crossover promotional content. Miguel is depicted alongside his mother, Luisa Rivera, suggesting a close family bond carried over from his original film appearance. He doesn't have an established personality within the Simpsons canon beyond his brief guest appearances. His inclusion mainly serves as a nod to Disney's ownership of both Pixar and The Simpsons franchises. He is featured attending festive, celebratory events like a tavern party and a family trip rather than engaging in typical Simpsons storylines.

title: Asa Phelps
text: Asa Phelps is A member of the Flying Hellfish, Grampa Simpson's World War II unit. Asa Phelps was one of the soldiers who served alongside Grampa Simpson in the Flying Hellfish during World War II. He participated in the unit's tontine, a pact in which the last surviving member would inherit a cache of paintings the group had liberated during the war. Outside of his brief military service and a single high school day trip, Asa spent his entire life in Springfield. He worked as a molder at the United Strut and Bracing Works until he was replaced by an automated Molder-Matic machine, after which he died. He was the seventh member of the Hellfish to pass away, as recounted in a eulogy by Reverend Lovejoy. Asa never speaks on screen, appearing only as a background figure tied to the show's ongoing WWII tontine storyline.

title: Ryan Seacrest (character)
text: Ryan Seacrest (character) is Real-life celebrity guest character; TV host who appears in Springfield-related media, notably as host of American Idol during Moe Szyslak's stint as a judge. This character is a fictionalized version of the real Ryan Seacrest, playing himself as the smooth, camera-savvy host of American Idol. He's shown keeping the show running professionally even amid chaos, such as calmly directing Moe Szyslak to angle a broken bottle label toward the camera during an on-air altercation. His presence in Springfield extends beyond the show itself, appearing as a framed picture in a local business and popping up in non-canon material tied to real-world events like New Year's Eve broadcasts and movie premieres. He functions mostly as a cameo/guest personality rather than a fully developed character, existing to add star-powered authenticity to Simpsons parodies of pop culture and reality TV. His interactions are brief but memorable, emphasizing his role as an unflappable TV professional. Voiced by Ryan Seacrest.

title: Phoebe Pratt
text: Phoebe Pratt is Elderly retired nature photographer whom Bart befriends at Sunnyday Nursing Home. Phoebe Pratt is a former nature photographer living out her later years in a nursing home, still yearning for the freedom of the outdoors. She cleverly hires Bart to pose as her grandson so she can be signed out to photograph the woods, and the two form a genuine bond over their shared excursions. Beneath her adventurous spirit lies a darker struggle, as she secretly uses Bart's help to slip away alone while contemplating suicide. Her story takes a hopeful turn when nature itself renews her will to live, showing a resilient, introspective side to her character. She's also notable as a rare case of a Simpsons character modeled directly on a real person, Jane Goodall. Despite the heavy subject matter, her friendship with Bart remains warm, and she continues to appear in Springfield afterward, including a cameo in a coma dream and a later sighting at the Leftorium. Voiced by Jennifer Saunders.

title: The Sequelizer
text: The Sequelizer is Non-canon superhero alter-ego of Troy McClure, appearing in Simpsons comic stories. The Sequelizer is a comic-book-only persona adopted by Troy McClure after he's caught in an explosion that grants him superpowers. His signature ability is splitting himself into multiple copies, though each successive duplicate is noticeably weaker than the last. He's shown battling The Black Belch, a superhero identity taken on by Barney, in a rooftop confrontation. The character is essentially a comedic riff on Marvel's Multiple Man, poking fun at superhero-comic tropes within the Simpsons universe. As a non-canon figure, he exists purely within the Bongo comics rather than the show's main continuity, appearing across a couple of related issues. Notable quotes: I, the Sequelizer can create an infinite number of copies of myself although each is only 50% as Powerful as the one before
quotes: I, the Sequelizer can create an infinite number of copies of myself although each is only 50% as Powerful as the one before

title: Number Six (The Prisoner)
text: Number Six (The Prisoner) is A fictional character from the TV series The Prisoner, referenced in The Simpsons as a costume worn by Comic Book Guy. Number Six isn't actually a Simpsons character in his own right, but rather the protagonist of the classic British series The Prisoner, whom Comic Book Guy chooses to emulate through cosplay. This nod appears as part of a crossover reference, showing Comic Book Guy's dedication to pop culture fandom by dressing as the iconic secret agent for a convention. The character has no dialogue or independent presence in The Simpsons universe, existing solely as a costume choice. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent habit of referencing other well-known television properties through its background characters. Number Six himself displays no personality traits within the Simpsons continuity since he's purely a visual homage rather than an active participant in the story.

title: Scarecrow
text: Scarecrow is The Scarecrow from The Wizard of Oz, appearing as a crossover/reference character in The Simpsons. Scarecrow is not an original Simpsons character but a recurring reference to the classic Wizard of Oz figure, appearing in various forms throughout the show. He shows up as an image in a book, a costume worn by Bart for a school play, a picture on a book cover, and even as a costume in a Treehouse of Horror segment. He is non-speaking in the show and mostly exists as a visual gag or pop-culture allusion rather than a fleshed-out character. In one notable scene, Homer, Ned, and Carl banter about the traits of the Scarecrow, Tin Man, and Cowardly Lion, using them as metaphors for lacking courage, a heart, or intelligence. In a non-canon future segment, someone dressed as the Scarecrow auditions for a college theater production of The Wizard of Oz. Overall, the character functions as a nostalgic nod to the famous film rather than a developed personality within the Simpsons universe.

title: Paul Rudd (character)
text: Paul Rudd (character) is Real-life actor who appears as a celebrity guest character in The Simpsons universe. Paul Rudd appears as a fictionalized version of himself, drawn into Springfield's chaotic pop-culture antics. His film work becomes the center of a legal dispute after Homer illegally downloads and screens one of his movies for the town, leading to a courtroom showdown. In a dramatized movie version of these events, he's portrayed as filmmaker Judd Apatow, adding a layer of meta humor. Later, he's shown attending a Comic-Con-style event called Comicalooza, where he has an awkward, self-deprecating encounter with Comic Book Guy. He reveals he's insecure about his likable, approachable image, poking fun at his real-world reputation. When pressed with an odd hypothetical about erasing an embarrassing film role from his past, he dodges the question and retreats to a VIP area, reinforcing his light comedic role as a good-natured but evasive celebrity cameo. Voiced by Paul Rudd (Himself).

title: Phillips
text: Phillips is Minor recurring character; Marge's cellmate during her stint in prison. Phillips is a tough convict who shares a cell with Marge Simpson during her brief incarceration. Her name comes from the grim detail that she murdered her husband using a Phillips-head screwdriver, giving her a darkly comedic backstory typical of the show's prison characters. After her appearance in prison, she goes on to date Barney Gumble, who deceives her by pretending to be named Homer and claiming to work at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. She appears only briefly in the series, mainly as a background element of Marge's prison arc, and later gets a non-canon cameo in a couch gag alongside other minor Springfield characters like Fat Tony and Lurleen Lumpkin. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Jim Reardon (character)
text: Jim Reardon (character) is A background/cameo character depicting a real-world animator who appears briefly in crowd scenes in Springfield. Jim Reardon is a non-speaking background character based on a real animator who worked on The Simpsons. He appears fleetingly in a handful of episodes, blending into crowds rather than taking part in the main action. He's seen at Springfield Station during Lisa's attempt to stop Mr. Bergstrom from leaving, among the group welcoming Marge home from Rancho Relaxo, and walking behind Mr. Burns and Smithers during their trip to New Haven for a football game. In a non-canon deleted scene, he's portrayed as the animator responsible for Itchy and Scratchy, going so far as to study real cats and mice to make the cartoon violence look authentic. As a real-world/staff cameo character, he exists more as an in-joke nod to the show's production team than as a developed personality within the Simpsons universe.

title: Orville Redenbacher
text: Orville Redenbacher is Former Stonecutters world council member and council member of The Ancient Mystic Society of No Homers, based on the real popcorn magnate. Orville Redenbacher is a parody of the real-life popcorn businessman who appears as an animated council member within the secretive Stonecutters organization. He is cited by Lisa as an example of a nerd who accomplished great things, alongside figures like David Byrne and David Souter, in an attempt to make Homer more tolerant of nerdy people. Despite this reputation for accomplishment, his in-show characterization leans toward the sinister side of the secret society trope, as he turns against Homer once Homer begins doing good deeds as the chosen one. His appearances are brief but tie him firmly into the show's satire of shadowy fraternal organizations. He later shows up as part of a background gag in a later episode's couch gag sequence. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Mrs. Rhenquist
text: Mrs. Rhenquist is Mother of school bully Francine Rhenquist, minor recurring character. Mrs. Rhenquist is a minor character best known as the mother of the notorious bully Francine Rhenquist. She appeared alongside her husband helping to contain their daughter, going so far as to assist in caging her for a public science presentation. Her calm, almost nonchalant attitude toward Francine's violent outbursts suggests she's used to her daughter's aggressive behavior. When Francine attacked an audience of scientists, Mrs. Rhenquist showed little alarm, simply predicting the girl would eventually tire herself out. This blasé parenting response is her main character trait, hinting at a household desensitized to Francine's temper. She has made only sporadic appearances since her debut, functioning mostly as background family context for Francine. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Father Sean
text: Father Sean is Roman Catholic priest at St. Jerome's Catholic School who briefly draws Bart and Homer into Catholicism. Father Sean is a warm, persuasive priest who teaches at St. Jerome's Catholic School, where Bart ends up after being wrongly expelled from Springfield Elementary. He has a dramatic backstory involving a drunken brawl with his own father, after which St. Peter appeared to him and set him on the path to the priesthood. He uses that story, along with gifts like a saints' comic book, to spark Bart's interest in the faith, and later charms Homer with the appeal of confession and church social events like pancake dinners and bingo nights. His efforts spark a small religious tug-of-war with Marge, Reverend Lovejoy, and Ned Flanders, culminating in a comedic standoff between the two faiths. Despite his kindly demeanor, he shows a surprisingly combative streak, riding in on a motorcycle and getting into a paintball-fueled confrontation to reclaim Bart. He's also shown to have some judgmental views, criticizing both gay people and Buddhism in the process. Voiced by Liam Neeson.

title: Johnny Rotten
text: Johnny Rotten is Parody character based on the real Sex Pistols singer, appearing in a Bart-narrated story. Johnny Rotten is a fictionalized version of the Sex Pistols frontman, appearing within a tale narrated by Bart Simpson. He's depicted as the frustrated leader of the band, growing increasingly irritated with bandmate Sid Vicious as Sid's chocolate addiction and infatuation with Nancy Spungen wreck his musical performance. His anger boils over when Sid shows up to a gig completely unable to play, prompting Johnny to lash out about the future of their partnership. Beyond this main storyline, he later shows up as part of a British invasion force that briefly conquers Springfield, and is also referenced as being featured on a list of notable left-leaning figures. As a character, he mainly serves as a punk-rock caricature rather than a fully fleshed-out personality, existing mostly to riff on real-world rock history within Simpsons-style parody. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright. Notable quotes: Johnny got angry at Sid about this, saying that he thought they would have a thirty-three-year business relationship.
quotes: Johnny got angry at Sid about this, saying that he thought they would have a thirty-three-year business relationship.

title: Bonestorm Santa
text: Bonestorm Santa is A Santa Claus mascot used in television commercials advertising the video game Bonestorm. Bonestorm Santa is a promotional character featured in an outlandish TV advertisement for the violent video game Bonestorm. Instead of delivering gifts in a traditional way, he bursts through the wall of a house belonging to two unimpressed kids and fires a copy of the game into their console using a bazooka. His aggressive sales pitch culminates in a threatening ultimatum aimed straight at the audience, urging children to pressure their parents into buying the game. The character is a parody of over-the-top, aggressive advertising aimed at children, blending the wholesome image of Santa with violent, hard-sell marketing tactics. Though only appearing briefly within the show as an in-universe commercial, he later resurfaced as a collectible character in a Simpsons mobile game. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: So tell your folks: Buy me "Bonestorm" or go to hell!
quotes: So tell your folks: Buy me "Bonestorm" or go to hell!

title: Petroleus Rex
text: Petroleus Rex is Supervillain enemy of Radioactive Man and member of The Fossil Fuel Four. Petroleus Rex is a comic-book supervillain who began his life as an environmental scientist named Rex Bernstein before turning to a life of crime. He joins forces with the other members of The Fossil Fuel Four to attack the Zenith City nuclear power plant, ultimately helping to defeat and kill the hero Radioactive Man. His signature ability is shooting gas from pump-like devices built into his arms, tying his powers directly to his fossil-fuel theme. His name is a punning combination of petroleum and Tyrannosaurus Rex, reflecting his oil-and-dinosaur inspired villain persona. Though primarily a background antagonist within the show's fictional comic-book universe, he also appears as a playable character in a Simpsons mobile game. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Peta
text: Peta is A minor, non-canon character who appeared briefly in a Treehouse of Horror segment parodying The Hunger Games. Peta is a young boy who takes part in a deadly battle dome competition in a dystopian parody segment. Alongside his companion Pita, he meets Lisa and quickly forms a friendly connection with her, with Lisa taking a liking to the pair almost instantly. Unfortunately, his story is cut tragically short when Homish falls from the sky and crushes both him and Pita to death. He exists primarily as a spoof of Peeta Mellark from The Hunger Games franchise, fitting into the segment's satirical take on dystopian young-adult fiction. Peta also made an appearance as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out as part of the Dystopian Fighters set. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Adam Savage (character)
text: Adam Savage (character) is Guest real-world character; co-host of MythCrackers who inspires Bart and Milhouse. Adam Savage appears as a fictionalized version of himself, a special effects expert and television personality known for co-hosting MythCrackers with Jamie Hyneman. In his appearance, he and Jamie conduct a chaotic experiment to test whether cats always land on their feet, but instead of using an actual cat they use a stuffed bear fired from a cannon. The pair get so caught up in the spectacle of the experiment that they lose track of what they were originally trying to prove, poking fun at the show-first, science-second nature of their real-life program. Their antics end up inspiring Bart and Milhouse to start their own amateur myth-testing hobby. Adam Savage functions as a brief cameo/guest character rather than a recurring fixture in Springfield. Voiced by Himself.

title: Shrek
text: Shrek is A crossover character (fictional ogre from the Shrek franchise) who appears in various background gags and references throughout The Simpsons. Shrek is not a true member of the Simpsons universe but a recurring pop-culture reference borrowed from the famous animated film franchise. He tends to pop up in the background of episodes—printed on merchandise like shirts and Squishee cups, worn as a Halloween mask, sold as a talking doll, or portrayed by someone in a costume. Homer seems particularly fond of referencing him, whether recounting the plot of a Shrek sequel to fellow captives or using his likeness as a disguise. Other characters occasionally invoke him too, such as Marge comparing two swamp-dwelling characters to him or Kirk using a Shrek costume photo on a dating profile. His presence is purely a running visual gag rather than a storyline, emphasizing the show's habit of nodding to outside franchises. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "Donkey!" - Shrek doll
quotes: "Donkey!" - Shrek doll

title: Burger Reynolds
text: Burger Reynolds is A Krustyland mascot character appearing in the background of the Simpsons universe. Burger Reynolds is one of the costumed mascot characters found at Krustyland, existing as a minor piece of the show's theme park scenery. He first appeared as a background figure at Krusty Fest, silently participating in the park's festivities. His most notable moment came when Krusty brought him along with Princess Fry to the Simpson house to comfort Marge after Homer was declared legally dead, as part of an offer for free food from Krusty Burger's Widow's Club. Burger Reynolds never speaks and functions purely as a visual gag character. His name and design serve as a pun-based parody of actor Burt Reynolds. As a non-speaking, picture-only character, he appears sparingly but is technically classified as a recurring figure in the Simpsons universe.

title: Pinky
text: Pinky is A ghost character from the classic arcade game Pac-Man, appearing as a crossover cameo in The Simpsons. Pinky is one of the four ghosts from the video game Pac-Man, appearing as a non-speaking crossover character within the show. First glimpsed on a screen while Mr. Burns played Ms. Pac-Man in his office, Pinky later shows up alongside the other ghosts at a televised wedding between Pac-Man and Ms. Pac-Man. The character also appears in a video game sequence displayed after Homer disrupts a competition by cutting the power. Pinky has no dialogue and exists purely as a background nod to classic gaming culture. Despite being fictional even within the show's universe, Pinky is treated as a deceased character in the wiki's continuity for tracking purposes.

title: Jeff Ross (character)
text: Jeff Ross (character) is Real-life comedian who appears as himself, serving as roastmaster at Krusty the Clown's roast. Jeff Ross is a guest-star cameo character based on the real-life American insult comic and stand-up comedian of the same name. In the show, he works as a roastmaster for The Comedy Cable Channel, a job that fits his real-world reputation for biting celebrity roasts. His main appearance comes when he hosts the Roast of Krusty the Clown, cracking jokes at Krusty's expense alongside other comedians like Sarah Silverman and Carrot Top. Beyond that event, his presence in the show is minimal, reduced to a background photo hanging on a wall in a later episode. As with many celebrity cameo characters on the show, he isn't given much personality beyond his real-life persona as a roast comic. Voiced by Jeff Ross (Himself).

title: Annie Oakley
text: Annie Oakley is Real-world historical figure referenced in The Simpsons; American sharpshooter and folk heroine. Annie Oakley is not an original character but a real-world historical figure incorporated into the show's universe as a piece of Americana. She appears as an image on the Bouvier family quilt, linking the Simpsons' extended family to a broader tapestry of American history and folklore. Later, her legacy resurfaces when Lisa dresses up as Annie Oakley during a Western-themed craze at Springfield Elementary. She has no spoken lines or active role in the plot, existing purely as a visual reference and costume inspiration. Her inclusion reflects the show's tendency to weave real historical and cultural icons into its background details.

title: Rocket Raccoon
text: Rocket Raccoon is Marvel superhero character referenced within the Simpsons universe, appearing as a costume/cameo rather than an actual character interacting with the main cast. Rocket Raccoon is a non-speaking cameo character based on the Marvel superhero of the same name, appearing only in brief references rather than as a fully developed part of the Simpsons cast. He first shows up as a costume worn by a raccoon being walked alongside a person dressed as Groot at a convention. In non-canon material, Santa's Little Helper is shown dressed up as Rocket Raccoon in a picture, and the character also appears animated on Groot's shoulder wielding a gun during a drive-in movie screening of a Guardians of the Galaxy film. Since he never speaks or interacts directly with the Simpsons characters, his role is essentially that of a pop-culture cameo and visual gag referencing the broader Marvel franchise. He has no defined personality traits within the show, functioning purely as an easter egg for fans of Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy.

title: Seth
text: Seth is One of Homer's old hippie friends and co-owner of the Groovy Grove Juice Corporation. Seth is a graying, laid-back hippie who has been part of Homer's life since Homer's youth alongside Mona Simpson. He runs a juice company and later an organic vegetable patch with his partner Munchie, and tends to be the more responsible, business-minded of the pair. Despite his practical streak, he still gets pulled into countercountercultural antics with Homer and Munchie, like freaking out squares in town. He shows loyalty and sentimentality, appearing at Mona Simpson's funeral and later at community events like Lisa's town meeting. Seth and Munchie also share a fondness for concerts and pop culture nostalgia, popping up at shows featuring Cheech and Chong-style acts. His firing of Gil Gunderson for stealing vegetables shows he has limits even in his easygoing business dealings. Voiced by Martin Mull.

title: Joe Perry (character)
text: Joe Perry (character) is Real-world guest character; lead guitarist of Aerosmith who appears in Springfield. Joe Perry is depicted as himself, the real lead guitarist of the rock band Aerosmith, making a guest appearance in Springfield. He and his bandmates perform at Moe's Tavern, giving Moe's bar an unexpected brush with rock stardom. He is also shown among celebrities attending a Grammy Awards party alongside the Be Sharps. Notably, he is listed as a left-handed person on Ned Flanders' list of notable lefties, tying him into the show's running gag about famous left-handers. As a real-world musician cameo, Perry doesn't have an extensive personality arc, but his presence adds star power and musical authenticity to the episodes he appears in. Voiced by Himself.

title: Shoshanna
text: Shoshanna is A minor Springfield resident known for going on a date with Snake. Shoshanna is a background character in Springfield whose most notable appearance involves a dinner date with the town's resident criminal, Snake. During their meal at Uncle Moe's Family Feedbag, she unwittingly benefits from Snake exploiting a promotional deal, getting a free meal out of Moe's inability to smile. She's a non-speaking character, appearing mostly as a face in the crowd rather than a fleshed-out personality. Her only other notable appearance is answering her door when Lisa canvasses the neighborhood about Lake Springfield. She has black hair and no other defining physical or personal traits are given. Overall, she serves as a minor recurring extra rather than a fully developed character.

title: Princess
text: Princess is A pony briefly owned by Lisa Simpson. Princess is a brown pony that Homer impulsively bought for Lisa, using money meant for a saxophone reed after stopping for a drink at Moe's. Her upkeep quickly proved too costly for the family, causing financial strain on Homer and Marge. Realizing the burden she placed on her family, Lisa made the difficult decision to give Princess up after only a short time together. Despite this, Lisa retained a fondness for the pony, later expressing that she missed her even though she'd only had her for a week. Princess has also appeared in non-canon material such as The Simpsons: Tapped Out, where she exists as a decoration with accompanying dialogue. Voiced by Frank Welker.

title: R2-D2
text: R2-D2 is Crossover cameo character from Star Wars appearing in various Simpsons episodes and merchandise. R2-D2 is a non-speaking droid crossover character from the Star Wars franchise who pops up repeatedly throughout The Simpsons as a background gag or collectible item. He's been featured in a Bi-Mon-Sci-Fi-Con commercial wrestling alongside C-3PO against Cylons from Battlestar Galactica, and shows up as a statue, figure, or prop in Comic Book Guy's shop and apartment as well as at a memorabilia auction. He also appeared on a movie poster parody and in one of Bart's fantasy daydreams playing bass guitar. In non-canon Treehouse of Horror and Star Wars parody segments, he's been reimagined in odder forms, including having Homer's head mounted on a similar robot and being the site of an Itchy & Scratchy gag. As a recurring but silent robotic character, R2-D2 mostly serves as an easter egg for fans of both franchises rather than a character with personality or dialogue.

title: Paul (The Marge-ian Chronicles)
text: Paul (The Marge-ian Chronicles) is Co-founder of Exploration Incorporated, a Mars colonization project featured in a Simpsons episode. Paul is a scientist who, along with his partner Barry, runs Exploration Incorporated, a company claiming it will establish a human colony on Mars by 2026. When rivals threaten to beat them to the launch, Paul and Barry rush their own rocket into action despite it not actually being functional. It's eventually revealed that the rocket was a fake, staged purely to inspire public interest in space exploration rather than to actually go anywhere. Ironically, their scheme nearly falls apart not because of the hoax being discovered, but because their getaway car fails to start. Beyond this main appearance, Paul pops up as a background audience member at live podcast recordings hosted by other Springfield characters, suggesting he's a minor recurring figure interested in local media events. His characterization leans toward the comedic archetype of an overambitious, slightly dishonest showman-scientist. Voiced by Tom Scharpling.

title: Roscoe
text: Roscoe is Minor recurring character; manager of the Ajax Steel Mill and worker at the Play-Doh Factory. Roscoe is an openly gay man who oversees operations at the Ajax Steel Mill, where he leads a workforce made up entirely of gay employees. He first appears when Homer brings Bart to the mill in a misguided attempt to toughen him up, only to be startled when a break-time dance party with a disco ball reveals the true nature of the workplace. Beyond his steel mill duties, Roscoe pops up in various odd jobs around Springfield, including work at the Play-Doh Factory and a stint helping tear down the Paradise Pear building. He later appears again working construction for Mr. Burns' basketball stadium, following orders that range from mundane to bizarre. Roscoe serves mostly as a background gag character tied to the show's recurring exploration of LGBT themes, appearing sporadically across several seasons. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Pharm team male researcher
text: Pharm team male researcher is A recurring minor character who works as a pharmaceutical researcher and later appears as a teacher at Springfield Elementary. This gray-haired background character first appears as part of the research team responsible for developing the dangerous drug Focusyn, which famously sent Bart on a destructive rampage. He later resurfaces in a medical capacity, working at the Screaming Monkey Medical Research Center, where he helps discover and remove the crayon lodged in Homer's brain. Despite his scientific background, he's shown living an ordinary Springfield life, attending a Green Day concert, going to church, and participating in town meetings about local environmental issues. His career eventually shifts entirely, as he's later seen working as a teacher at Springfield Elementary School, even joining in a group song with fellow faculty members. Though he never gets a name, he pops up across a surprising number of episodes and eras of the show, suggesting he's one of Springfield's many recognizable recurring faces despite his low profile. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Mrs. Risotto
text: Mrs. Risotto is Mother of Luigi Risotto, owner/matriarch tied to Luigi's restaurant, grandmother to several Risotto granddaughters. Mrs. Risotto is an elderly Italian-American woman who serves as the formidable mother of Luigi, the owner of Luigi's restaurant. She's fiercely protective of her son's business, becoming visibly upset when Homer's excessive eating threatens to bankrupt the restaurant, and she's not above stepping in personally to handle problem customers. Outside the restaurant, she moonlights as a fortune teller and tarot card reader, once ominously warning a room full of people that someone would die. Her personal life includes a complicated relationship with her own sexuality; she initially disapproved of Waylon Smithers' relationship with Michael de Graaf, but later confided in Luigi that she is a lesbian and had struggled with self-hatred over it, finding acceptance from her son. She's also depicted in non-canon material as an unlikely legal crusader, starring in a fictional show where she attends Harvard Law School to defend Luigi from smuggling charges. Overall, she's a colorful, strong-willed side character whose family devotion and hidden depths occasionally surface amid the show's comedic plots involving the Risotto family. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Edgar Allan Poe (character)
text: Edgar Allan Poe (character) is Real-world American author and poet referenced multiple times in the Simpsons universe. Edgar Allan Poe appears in the show not as a living character but as a historical and cultural reference point. His tombstone was famously used by Dr. Nick to demonstrate the cleaning product Spiffy, cementing him as a recurring punchline. Lisa Simpson is shown to be a fan of his work, keeping his poetry alongside other literary greats on her bookshelf. His famous story 'The Tell-Tale Heart' inspired a school diorama project, and his poem 'The Raven' is referenced through the naming of the Baltimore Ravens football team, which Moe mocks in a joking insult. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, a bust of Poe appears in a nightmarish setting tied to his poem 'The Raven,' further cementing his ties to the show's horror parodies. Overall, Poe functions as a recurring literary and cultural allusion rather than an active character. Notable quotes: Troy, I brought with me the gravestone of author and troubled soul, Edgar Allan Poe. | One of our best writers.
quotes: Troy, I brought with me the gravestone of author and troubled soul, Edgar Allan Poe.
One of our best writers.

title: She Biscuit
text: She Biscuit is Mother of Santa's Little Helper, the Simpson family's dog. She Biscuit is a light brown greyhound who was originally bred and owned by Les Moore for racing purposes. She was separated from her son Santa's Little Helper when he was taken away young to be trained as a racer, but the two shared a strong bond as puppy and mother. Years later she was joyfully reunited with him when the Simpson family visited Les Moore's home. Afterward she went to live elsewhere but still visits the Simpsons occasionally, such as for a Mother's Day get-together where she and her son bonded over a dog-themed streaming show and a rather gross gift of a dead bird. She is a non-speaking character whose appearances are brief but emotionally tied to Santa's Little Helper's backstory.

title: Mr. Seckofsky
text: Mr. Seckofsky is Shop teacher at Springfield High School during Homer and Marge's student years. Mr. Seckofsky is a minor background figure from Homer and Marge's high school days, remembered mainly for his role in disciplinary mishaps rather than any strong personality traits shown on screen. He taught shop class, and his most notable moment involved catching Homer and Barney skipping class to smoke in the bathroom, which led to their detention under Principal Dondelinger. Marge also sought him out for a character reference, suggesting he was viewed as a reasonably trustworthy authority figure at the school. In a later non-canon appearance, he's shown giving safety instructions about handling wood-cutting boards, hinting at a dry, procedural teaching style. He's something of a trivia footnote in the show's history, holding the record for the longest real-world gap between appearances of any recurring character. Overall, he's a lightly sketched nostalgia-era character tied to the Simpsons' flashback continuity rather than a fully developed personality. Voiced by Jon Lovitz, Hank Azaria.

title: Randy (Burns, Baby Burns)
text: Randy (Burns, Baby Burns) is Minor character; tour guide at Mt. Swartzwelder Historic Cider Mill who appears in the episode "Burns, Baby Burns". Randy is a blond-haired tour guide employed at the Mt. Swartzwelder Historic Cider Mill in Springfield. His main claim to fame in the show is leading the Simpson family around the mill, giving them the full rundown of its history and workings. Beyond his job, he's later spotted enjoying himself at a party somewhere in town, suggesting he has a life outside of work. He's a fairly minor, one-episode character with little development beyond his occupation. Randy later resurfaces in a non-canon capacity within the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Will Shortz (character)
text: Will Shortz (character) is Real-world puzzle editor who appears as a guest character helping Homer reconcile with Lisa. Will Shortz appears as a fictionalized version of himself, the real-life crossword editor, drawn into the Simpsons' family drama. He is recruited by Homer, along with crossword constructor Merl Reagle, to help craft a secret message hidden within a New York Times crossword puzzle. His role is brief but pivotal, acting as a behind-the-scenes figure who helps mend the rift between Homer and Lisa after a betting incident during a crossword championship. Shortz is portrayed as no-nonsense and focused on his craft, ultimately telling Reagle to get back to work once the plan succeeds. His cameo ties into the episode's celebration of crossword culture and wordplay. Despite his minimal screen time, his presence lends real-world authenticity to the episode's puzzle-solving plot. Voiced by Will Shortz (Himself).

title: Jerry Rude
text: Jerry Rude is Shock jock radio host who hosts "Jerry Rude and the Bathroom Bunch", appeared when Mr. Burns went on his show. Jerry Rude is a crude, brash radio personality whose show thrives on crass bathroom humor and invasive personal questions, making him a clear parody of Howard Stern. His rudeness is baked into his very name, and he seems to delight in embarrassing his guests with vulgar and probing inquiries. When Mr. Burns appears on his program seeking attention, Jerry pushes him with humiliating questions and mocking sound effects until Burns suffers a heart attack live on air. Despite the chaos he causes, Jerry doesn't seem to hold any real malice, casually moving on to chat with lesbian gladiators after the incident. He also has a habit of interviewing bizarre guests, as shown by his earlier interview with Knick-Knack and Paddy-Whack. Overall, he represents the shock-jock archetype of talk radio taken to an absurd, Simpsons-style extreme. Voiced by Michael McKean.

title: Secretariat
text: Secretariat is A background/mentioned character in The Simpsons universe, based on the real-life racehorse. Secretariat is a recurring but non-speaking reference in the show, based on the famous real-world Thoroughbred racehorse of the same name. Rather than appearing as a proper character, the name pops up as a running joke or offhand cultural reference in various episodes. At one point, a baseball supposedly made from the horse is sold at a store, poking fun at bizarre memorabilia culture. Another gag involves a fictional boxing match between Secretariat and Mike Tyson, referenced via a poster. The character is also invoked as a symbol of class and prestige when compared to other iconic figures. Overall, Secretariat functions purely as a humorous nod to the real racehorse rather than an active participant in the show's plots.

title: Robby the Automaton
text: Robby the Automaton is A robot advertiser for the Springfield Knowledgeum, appearing in a few Simpsons episodes. Robby the Automaton is a promotional robot created to drum up interest in the Springfield Knowledgeum. He speaks in a stiff, mechanical greeting style and is used to pitch quirky trivia to schoolchildren, like facts about touching stars or the brain weights of the Three Stooges. His behavior is entirely dependent on a hidden human controller, and when that link is severed, he defaults to a violent "crush, kill, destroy" mode, turning from a friendly mascot into a menace. This mishap leads him to attack Principal Skinner, played for dark comic irony as the students cheer rather than help. Robby also briefly questioned his own programming when a fire broke out at the Springfield Robotics Laboratory, wondering why he was made to feel pain. He's a clear homage to the classic sci-fi robot Robby the Robot from Forbidden Planet, and he reappears in non-canon material as "Floyd the Scrubbing Robot." Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Greetings, Earth children.
quotes: Greetings, Earth children.

title: Powder Puff
text: Powder Puff is A cat belonging to Lil' Vicki, appearing in a film watched by Lisa. Powder Puff is a small white cat that appears in a movie-within-the-show viewed by Lisa. He belongs to a sad little girl named Lil' Vicki, who fears he might die. The tomcat's story is resolved when Bojangles, a tap dancer, comforts Vicki by showing her that dancing can lift one's spirits. Powder Puff watches the impromptu dance lesson with wide-eyed surprise before his mood brightens and he joins in the dancing himself. He has no spoken lines, fitting his role as a background animal character used for a heartwarming, whimsical moment. Powder Puff later shows up in a non-canon capacity in The Simpsons: Tapped Out video game.

title: Sir Oinks-A-Lot
text: Sir Oinks-A-Lot is Pig mascot of Springfield A&M, rival school to Springfield University, appearing in "Homer Goes to College". Sir Oinks-A-Lot is the beloved pig mascot representing Springfield A&M, a school with a storied rivalry against Springfield University. Despite being a non-speaking animal character, he holds surprising influence and prestige, having once conferred an honorary degree on Richard Nixon and presiding over the school's annual Homecoming Dance. His most notable moment comes when Homer and his nerdy college friends kidnap him as a prank and get him drunk on malt liquor, leading to disastrous consequences for the students involved. The incident highlights how much clout the pig commands, since his powerful connections force the dean to expel the pranksters. Ultimately he is returned home safely to Springfield A&M via helicopter, restoring order. He later makes a brief non-canon cameo in a couch gag, wandering through Springfield itself.

title: Danica Patrick (character)
text: Danica Patrick (character) is A celebrity guest character, a race car driver who appears in Homer's imagination. Danica Patrick is a fictionalized version of the real-life race car driver who appears as a figment of Homer's imagination. In her one major scene, she tries to convince Homer to enter Raymond Bird into the Annual Springfield to Shelbyville Birditeron. Things get complicated when Marge intrudes on the same fantasy, leading the two women to argue and then team up to physically attack Homer, who bizarrely admits he's enjoying it. She's also referenced outside of her direct appearance, used by Homer as a nickname for Lisa during her stint as a go-kart racer, showing her name has become shorthand for female racing skill in the Simpsons universe. Beyond these brief moments, little else is established about her personality, since she functions more as a celebrity cameo than a fully developed character. Voiced by Danica Patrick (herself).

title: Thomas Pynchon (character)
text: Thomas Pynchon (character) is Real-life author who appears as himself in cameo roles in Springfield. Thomas Pynchon is a reclusive, famously private novelist who makes several self-parodying cameo appearances in Springfield. He's known for hiding his identity with a paper bag over his head, poking fun at his own reputation for anonymity by hawking autographs and photo ops on the street. His humor tends to be dry and self-deprecating, as seen when he sarcastically reviews Marge's book by comparing his love for it to his love of cameras, despite his supposed camera-shy persona. He occasionally pops up in Springfield's cultural scene, sampling Marge's cooking and attending literary gatherings. In one non-canon appearance, his dense writing style becomes the punchline when a novel of his is used as a boring bedtime story. He also seemingly attends a Simpsons-related premiere in a later non-canon appearance. Voiced by Himself.

title: Glenn Quagmire
text: Glenn Quagmire is A Family Guy character (Peter Griffin's friend and neighbor) who crossed over into a non-canon Simpsons appearance. Glenn Quagmire is a character imported from Family Guy who shows up in the crossover special where the two shows collide. True to his Family Guy characterization, his brief interactions with the Simpsons cast focus on his fixation with sex, which comes up when he's compared to Lenny. He's shown mingling with Peter Griffin's world, offering creative input on Peter's comic strip, and attending a satirical beer-rivalry event held at the Springfield Court House. As a non-canon figure, he exists mainly for gag purposes rather than as a true part of Springfield continuity. He's also referenced in park attraction lore tying the two franchises together. Voiced by Seth MacFarlane.

title: Stanley Peterson
text: Stanley Peterson is Minor recurring character; a security guard at the Springfield DMV who marries Martha Peterson. Stanley Peterson is a background employee at the Springfield DMV, identifiable as a security officer by his uniform. His most notable moment comes when he inadvertently becomes part of a romantic subplot involving Patty and Selma Bouvier. After declining to let Selma sit beside him in the lunch canteen, he ends up meeting Martha, who would become his wife, when Patty interrupts the encounter. Reverend Lovejoy later officiates their wedding, giving Stanley a small but memorable place in Springfield's web of minor romances. He has no significant characterization beyond this storyline, appearing only briefly in a couple of episodes. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Count Orlok
text: Count Orlok is A vampire character referenced and briefly appearing in The Simpsons universe, based on the classic film character Nosferatu. Count Orlok is a non-canon vampire figure inspired by the iconic silent film character of the same name. He was mentioned as a favorite monster by Guillermo del Toro in a short film segment, and later appeared briefly in Springfield during a Treehouse of Horror opening sequence. In The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game, he goes by the name Nosferatu, likely to avoid copyright issues tied to the original film's title. He is a non-speaking character with no defined personality traits shown on screen, existing mostly as a nod to classic horror cinema. His inclusion reflects the show's frequent habit of referencing famous horror icons during Halloween-themed content.

title: Princess Opal
text: Princess Opal is A minor recurring fortune-telling gypsy character who appears in Springfield. Princess Opal is a fortune teller who runs her own storefront business in Springfield. She's occasionally consulted by locals, including the police, for guidance on missing persons or personal matters, though her predictions can be a mixed bag of accuracy. She once assisted the police in trying to locate a missing Principal Skinner, offering up unrelated celebrity gossip predictions instead. Her business also caters to lovelorn customers like Selma, selling dubious potions with questionable ingredients. She accidentally reveals the truth about her own products after unknowingly ingesting a truth serum, showing a comedic vulnerability beneath her mystical persona. Overall, she serves as a source of quirky humor tied to fortune-telling and small-time con artistry. Voiced by Jo Ann Harris, Pamela Hayden. Notable quotes: it was mostly corn syrup and a little rubbing alcohol, and she would be lucky if it didn't make her hair fall out
quotes: it was mostly corn syrup and a little rubbing alcohol, and she would be lucky if it didn't make her hair fall out

title: Spiro Papadapaconstantikasgianopolopodopotopolis
text: Spiro Papadapaconstantikasgianopolopodopotopolis is Greek restaurant owner who once employed Abe Simpson as a waiter. Spiro is a minor Greek character best known for owning the restaurant Spiro's, where Abe Simpson once worked as a waiter. He appears when Marge and Homer track down clues about Abe's past, leading them to Spiro's establishment. His backstory reveals he fired Abe after catching him goofing off, writing songs and playing piano with Rita LaFleur, instead of doing his job. Despite the falling out, Spiro expresses genuine regret for losing touch with both Abe and Rita. A recurring joke surrounding him is his absurdly long surname, which both Homer and Marge somehow pronounce flawlessly, contrasted humorously with Homer's inability to remember the much simpler name "Rita LaFleur." He later appears in a non-canon capacity in The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Quilloughby (real)
text: Quilloughby (real) is Lead singer of the band The Snuffs, briefly Lisa Simpson's musical idol. Quilloughby is the frontman of the band The Snuffs, a musician modeled after real-world singer Morrissey. Lisa Simpson discovers him through a Slapify subscription and becomes enamored with his political views and vegetarian ideals, even conjuring an imaginary version of him after a moment of guilt over eating bacon. The real Quilloughby turns out to be a huge disappointment in person, having let fame and fortune change him for the worse. He's depicted as having grown overweight, bigoted, and hypocritical, abandoning his old principles by eating meat and suing critics regardless of their point. His disastrous live appearance at a festival, complete with hurling sausages at the audience, causes him to be run off stage by an angry mob. His fictional, idealized counterpart even warns Lisa against becoming like him, highlighting the show's commentary on fallen idols and disillusionment. Voiced by Benedict Cumberbatch.

title: Vincent Price
text: Vincent Price is Real-world horror actor referenced and appearing as a character in The Simpsons universe. Vincent Price is a fictionalized version of the real-life horror film actor, appearing sporadically as a novelty figure within the Simpsons world. He's portrayed as being possibly deceased, yet still active enough to answer customer service calls and drive buses, playing on the absurdity of celebrity endorsements outliving the celebrities themselves. His humor stems from a deadpan acceptance of his own uncertain mortality, casually referencing his grave and crypt as if they were just another part of his daily routine. He's tied to a joke product called Vincent Price's Egg Magic, cementing his role as a parody of celebrities lending their names to gimmicky merchandise. In non-canon material, he appears in horror-themed gags, fitting his classic association with campy scary movie roles. His grandson Jody Price is his only established family connection in the show. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Maurice LaMarche. Notable quotes: the grave could never tame him | poor old Vincent Price floating around in a toilet keg telling me about the horrors of an unfresh bowl
quotes: the grave could never tame him
poor old Vincent Price floating around in a toilet keg telling me about the horrors of an unfresh bowl

title: Parasite
text: Parasite is A cartoon mouse character from the show-within-a-show "The Worker & Parasite Show", which briefly replaced Itchy and Scratchy on Krusty's show. Parasite is an animated mouse who stars alongside a character named Worker in a bizarre, foreign cartoon that Krusty airs after losing the rights to Itchy and Scratchy. Unlike the typical violent cat-and-mouse antics fans expect, Parasite's only real action is aimlessly bouncing around to music, making the short seem strange and unsatisfying to audiences. The cartoon is presented as an import from Eastern Europe, playing into a joke about odd, low-budget foreign animation. Parasite himself has no real personality beyond his repetitive bouncing motion, serving mainly as a parody device rather than a fleshed-out character. Despite his minimal role, he has become memorable enough to appear later as a costume reference at a fan convention. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Barney Rubble
text: Barney Rubble is Crossover cartoon character from The Flintstones, appearing only as a picture within The Simpsons. Barney Rubble is not an original Simpsons character but a crossover figure from the classic animated series The Flintstones, brought into the show's universe as a background reference rather than an active participant. He never speaks or physically appears in animated form; instead, his likeness shows up on objects like a novelty phone and a map, functioning purely as an Easter egg for fans of both shows. His family ties—husband to Betty Rubble and father to Bamm-Bamm Rubble—are acknowledged even though none of them actually interact with the Simpsons cast. Interestingly, the show's own perpetually tipsy neighbor, Barney Gumble, was named as a playful homage to this character. The joke comes full circle when Gumble himself dresses up as Barney Rubble in a later episode, blurring the line between homage and cameo. Overall, Barney Rubble exists in the Simpsons universe as a nostalgic nod rather than a fleshed-out character.

title: Captain Quisp
text: Captain Quisp is Mascot character for the fictional Quisp cereal brand, appearing in a Homer daydream sequence. Captain Quisp is a minor, non-speaking novelty character tied to the Quisp cereal brand within the show's universe. He appears in a fantasy sequence when Homer imagines an idyllic scenario after receiving his first kiss from Marge, in which Homer greedily devours an entire box of Quisp cereal aboard a spaceship before eating the Captain himself. This bizarre and exaggerated moment plays into the show's frequent use of surreal dream logic and cereal-mascot parody. He later reappears only as an image on a cereal box during an unrelated storyline involving Homer's voting habits. As a background gag character, he has no dialogue and exists purely as a visual reference rather than a fleshed-out personality.

title: Norm Peterson
text: Norm Peterson is A crossover bar patron from the sitcom Cheers who appears in a bar Homer visits after being banned from Moe's. Norm Peterson is a beer-loving barfly transplanted from the world of Cheers into a Simpsons bar scene. He's shown sitting with two buddies, eager for a drink, and quickly becomes irate when the bartender refuses to serve him. His anger flares into an over-the-top threat before comically dissolving into a tearful, sentimental moment where he professes love for his friends. This emotional whiplash—from menacing to weepy—plays on his easygoing, drink-dependent barfly persona. He also shows up briefly in a crowd scene at a parade, reinforcing his role as a background nod to Cheers fans. Overall, he functions as a one-off crossover cameo rather than a recurring, developed character. Voiced by George Wendt.

title: Clay Roberts
text: Clay Roberts is A minor recurring character and coach who briefly moved into the Simpsons' old neighborhood. Clay Roberts is a minor character who works as a coach and briefly became a resident of 744 Evergreen Terrace after Ned Flanders relocated to Humbleton, Pennsylvania. His time in Springfield's most famous house didn't last, and he later reappeared living in far less impressive circumstances—a run-down house that hinted at a decline in his fortunes. His most memorable moment comes from a botched arrest attempt, when Ned and Homer try to bring him in for skipping bail, only for the mission to end in slapstick failure. He doesn't have much personality development beyond these brief appearances, functioning mainly as a plot device tied to Ned's temporary absence from Springfield. Despite his small role, he's notable for being one of the few characters to occupy the iconic Simpson family home. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Shadow Knight
text: Shadow Knight is Bart Simpson's evil knight character in the online game "Earthland Realms", featured in the episode "Marge Gamer". The Shadow Knight is the most fearsome and destructive avatar in the fictional MMORPG Earthland Realms, secretly controlled by Bart Simpson. He terrorizes other players, slaughtering villagers and even killing Skinner's in-game character with a flaming sword. Living lavishly in his own castle with Lady Milhouse as his servant, he delights in cruel and darkly comic demands, such as ordering a drink made from a pixie's blood or forcing Moe's character to flagellate himself. His identity is uncovered by Marge, who is initially shocked but ends up feeling oddly proud of her son's virtual villainy. Ultimately his own reckless act of kindness, reviving Marge's character at great personal cost, leaves him vulnerable, and the townspeople take their revenge by killing him gruesomely and celebrating his death. Voiced by Hank Azaria (Knight's voice), Nancy Cartwright (Bart's voice). Notable quotes: The Shadow Knight? He's the most evil, destructive player in this game. - Moe Szyslak
quotes: The Shadow Knight? He's the most evil, destructive player in this game. - Moe Szyslak

title: Mike Reiss (character)
text: Mike Reiss (character) is A writer for The Itchy & Scratchy Show under Roger Meyers, Jr., appearing as a fictionalized version of the real Simpsons writer/producer. Mike Reiss is depicted as one of the many writers employed by Roger Meyers, Jr. to write The Itchy & Scratchy Show. He loses his job when Meyers fires all his writers after bringing on Abraham Simpson instead. He is married to Denise Reiss, with whom he later attends a timeshare presentation. In a running gag typical of the show's use of real names, Kent Brockman lists him among people rumored to be gay. He also shows up at the Annual Cartoon Awards held at the Springfield Civic Center. In a non-canon special, his name is honored among the many real-life staffers who help make The Simpsons possible.

title: Ron Rabinowitz
text: Ron Rabinowitz is Agent and friend of Krusty the Clown. Ron Rabinowitz, also known as Max, works as a talent agent representing Krusty the Clown, along with other performers like Gabbo and Arnie Pye. He shows a cold, self-serving side when convenient for his career, most notably abandoning Krusty as a friend in order to justify dropping him as a client after Krusty lost his show on Channel 6. His callousness is emphasized by small cruel acts, like deleting Krusty from his phone contacts and literally shutting a door on him. Despite this, he still occasionally helps Krusty in dangerous situations, such as pulling him out of the path of a runaway chili dog trailer. He is portrayed as an older, gray-haired Jewish businessman who balances loyalty and self-interest depending on the situation. He has also appeared in non-canon media like The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Mario Risotto
text: Mario Risotto is Minor comic-book character; a truck driver and brother of Luigi Risotto. Mario Risotto is a background character who appears in the Simpsons comic book stories rather than the animated show. Unlike his brother Luigi, he speaks without any accent, setting the two apart despite their shared name reference to famous video game siblings. He works as a truck driver and gets called on for odd jobs, such as helping with leaf removal using his truck. His appearances tend to involve small comedic mishaps, including nearly causing an explosion after swerving to avoid a turtle in the road. Mario is depicted as a family man eager to get home to his loved one making dinner. The character is essentially a parody nod to the video game character Mario, mirroring the naming convention of his brother Luigi's game counterpart.

title: The Sciencester
text: The Sciencester is Non-canon superhero alter-ego of Martin Prince, appearing in Simpsons comic books. The Sciencester is a comic-book-only superhero persona adopted by Martin Prince. He operates with a sidekick named Kid Queasy, suggesting a partnership similar to classic superhero duos. His main claim to fame in the Bongo comics is attempting to capture Bartman, placing him in opposition to Bart's own superhero alter-ego. As a non-canon character, he exists purely within the comic continuity rather than the television series. The character reflects Martin's nerdy, science-oriented personality translated into a costumed hero role. He appears in a couple of specific comic issues focused on superhero crossover storylines.

title: Rosa
text: Rosa is Minor recurring character; wife of Nigel. Rosa is a minor character best known as Nigel's wife, appearing briefly in the show's later seasons. She's shown accompanying her husband on everyday errands, such as touring the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant and picking up a lip tint from the pharmacy, before the two attend Moe's new bar venture. Her most notable, if odd, appearance is a cameo in a surreal dream sequence, where she's depicted among Ned Flanders' deceased wives on his wall. Rosa doesn't have much of a defined personality on screen, functioning mostly as a background figure tied to Nigel's storylines. She also has a small presence in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, again linked to Nigel's in-game activities. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Dana Scully
text: Dana Scully is FBI Special Agent who guest-starred in a crossover episode, partnered with Fox Mulder while investigating Homer's alien sighting. Dana Scully is a crossover character from The X-Files who appears in Springfield as part of an FBI investigation alongside her partner Fox Mulder. She serves as the rational skeptic of the duo, relying on scientific evidence rather than belief in the paranormal, which contrasts with Mulder's more credulous nature. Her visit to Springfield to investigate Homer's supposed alien encounter leads to some dry, deadpan humor as she subjects Homer to bizarre tests and dismisses his story as ridiculous. Despite her skepticism, she eventually gets swept up in the town's eccentric antics, appearing in a goofy T-shirt and singing with the townspeople. Beyond her main appearance, she's referenced or depicted in passing throughout the show's history, including as a phone operator, a picture on a wall, and an entry in one of Lisa's fictional guides. Her presence highlights the show's fondness for parodying and crossing over with other popular series. Voiced by Gillian Anderson. Notable quotes: I just thought he could stand to lose a little weight. | It's like a lava lamp. | the worst assignment we've ever had
quotes: I just thought he could stand to lose a little weight.
It's like a lava lamp.
the worst assignment we've ever had

title: Yuma Simpson
text: Yuma Simpson is Homer Simpson's great-grandmother, a minor ancestral member of the Simpson family. Yuma Hickman Simpson is a deceased figure from the far reaches of the Simpson family tree, hailing from a vaguely defined ancestral homeland resembling Ireland or Scotland. She married Orville J. Simpson and became the mother of several sons, including Abraham Simpson, who later became Homer's father. According to family lore, she and her husband once lived inside the Statue of Liberty with their children until the head became too cluttered with garbage to inhabit. This tale, however, is treated with skepticism since it originates from one of Grampa Simpson's rambling, senility-tinged stories. Yuma exists mostly as a background footnote in Simpson family history, appearing only briefly in flashback and print materials rather than as an active character. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Janet Reno (character)
text: Janet Reno (character) is Real-life former U.S. Attorney General who appears as a guest character, most notably presiding as judge over Bart's youth court trial. Janet Reno appears as a version of her real-world self, brought into Bart's world thanks to Grampa's unlikely long-distance chess friendship with her. She takes her judicial duties seriously, patiently listening to a parade of testimonies from people who dislike Bart before delivering a fair verdict once the truth comes out. Outside her main appearance, she's mostly referenced in passing, whether as a punchline on a church marquee about "evil women" or as a fact-check correction on a satirical news show. She even shows up as a recognizable face in a chess-themed captcha in a later episode. Due to her real-life battle with Parkinson's disease, her dialogue was split between her own voice and that of her sister, reflecting the show's grounding of the character in reality even in animated form. Voiced by Herself; Maggy Reno Hurchalla.

title: The Great Raymondo
text: The Great Raymondo is An aging professional magician who becomes Lisa Simpson's mentor in magic. Harvey Raymondo, known professionally as The Great Raymondo, is a once-famous stage magician living a quiet life until Lisa Simpson stumbles into his home while fleeing a raccoon. Initially gruff and secretive, he warms to Lisa after witnessing her natural talent, taking her on as a protégé and sharing his prized trick, an escape routine passed down from Houdini himself. He is deeply protective of his craft's secrets, growing furious when Lisa's carelessness allows a rival to steal his signature illusion. Despite his temper, he proves forgiving and even heroic, risking his own safety to rescue the man who wronged him during a climactic magic show. Raymondo represents the old-school magician archetype, valuing tradition, mystery, and mentorship over fame. He also appears briefly as a victim of one of Homer's get-rich-quick schemes, showing he's not immune to being duped himself. Voiced by Martin Landau.

title: Sardonicus
text: Sardonicus is A recurring prisoner character at Waterville Prison and later Springfield Penitentiary in The Simpsons. Sardonicus is a minor inmate character who appears in a handful of prison-related episodes. He's shown taking part in an art class run by Marge, revealing an oddly violent artistic streak by painting a scene of a judge being stabbed. Also known by the alias Terrance, a name used by fellow inmate Snake, he later turns up at Springfield Penitentiary during an incident involving Artie Ziff. His look is inconsistent between appearances, with one episode mistakenly coloring his hair grey instead of red. Overall, he functions as background color for the show's recurring prison settings rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Raiders dad
text: Raiders dad is Minor recurring background resident of Springfield. The Raiders dad is a minor Springfield resident identifiable by his Las Vegas Raiders branded hat and shirt and his brown mustache. He's a non-speaking background character who tends to pop up in crowd scenes rather than driving any plots himself. At one point he served as one of the crossing guards at Springfield Elementary School under Homer's supervision. He was also among the group of Hispanic townsfolk who found Bumblebee Man's physical comedy routines funny while Homer worked as his stuntman. Beyond these brief appearances, little else is known about his personality or life, as he exists mainly as a recognizable recurring extra.

title: Sexy pirate
text: Sexy pirate is Fictional romantic pirate character from a novel Marge reads, appearing in her fantasy sequence. The sexy pirate is a fictional character who exists only within the pages of the steamy novel Love in the Time of Scurvy and, subsequently, within Marge's imagination. Described as tanned and muscular with blonde hair and an earring, he embodies a swashbuckling romantic archetype, all smooth talk and flirtation aboard his ship. He appears when Marge becomes absorbed in reading the novel and daydreams herself into the story as his love interest. His entire existence in the show is confined to this one fantasy sequence, which is comically interrupted by real-world noise. Despite his brief appearance, he later resurfaces as a collectible character type in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Well, no more than your bountiful bosom, milady. | Ah, the seas have quieted. And only in the sweet embrace of quietude can two lovers truly be - | Ooh, such noise! Well, I'm done for the evening
