title: Pikachu
text: Pikachu is Crossover cameo character from the Pokémon franchise appearing in various Simpsons episodes. Pikachu is a guest crossover character brought into the Simpsons universe from the Pokémon franchise, usually appearing in brief, absurd cameos rather than as a true part of the cast. The character shows up in hallucination sequences, background gags, and parody scenarios, such as when Bart imagines a classmate transforming into Pikachu during a televised meltdown, or when Homer and Ned trip on drugs and envision themselves as a twisted version of Pikachu and its trainer. Pikachu's appearances lean heavily on recognizable Pokémon lore, like referencing its bond with Ash Ketchum, while also being repurposed for adult humor, such as being used as a bong. It also turns up in mundane real-world parody moments, like a shabby bootleg costume posing for photos with tourists alongside other beloved characters. Overall, Pikachu functions as a pop-culture reference point the show uses for quick sight gags and satire rather than a character with its own ongoing storyline. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Professor Pocket Pool
text: Professor Pocket Pool is A minor recurring professor character in Springfield, mentioned as an example of someone defined by an odd personal trait. Professor Pocket Pool is a background Springfield resident whose entire identity seems to revolve around his unfortunate, suggestive name. He's brought up by Marge as a cautionary example of what Bart might become if he continues to be known by 'his thing' instead of his actual name. Despite the awkward moniker, he holds a respectable academic position with lifetime tenure, a detail Homer finds oddly reassuring. He later turns up as a fellow airline passenger, revealing a habit of forming impromptu book clubs with other questionable Springfield figures during flights. His brief appearances lean into absurdist humor typical of the show's background characters, using his name as the main running joke. Voiced by Chris Edgerly.

title: MacArthur Parker
text: MacArthur Parker is Talent agent representing Troy McClure. MacArthur Parker is the shrewd, career-obsessed agent who represents washed-up actor Troy McClure. He goes silent on his client for years, only to resurface the moment Troy generates tabloid buzz by dating Selma Bouvier, seeing an opportunity to relaunch Troy's career through good publicity. His advice is coldly pragmatic, treating Troy's personal relationships as little more than career strategy, even pushing for Troy and Selma to have a baby just to land a film role. Parker's manipulative, image-driven approach ultimately backfires when it costs Troy his relationship with Selma. He later makes a minor background appearance in a completely different context, showing up as one of the townspeople in Springfield during a crisis. His name is a playful nod to the classic song "MacArthur Park." Voiced by Jeff Goldblum.

title: Bill Oakley (character)
text: Bill Oakley (character) is A minor background character depicted as a writer and producer within the Springfield universe. Bill Oakley is a minor, mostly background character who appears sporadically across several episodes rather than playing any central role in the show's plots. He's briefly named on Kent Brockman's rumored list of gay Springfield residents, and he's seen among the crowd mocking Nelson after an embarrassing incident. He has a boxing match with Moe at one point, and he's shown working as part of the writing staff for the in-universe cartoon The Itchy & Scratchy Show. Fittingly, his character seems to be a nod to the real-life Simpsons writer and producer of the same name, blurring the line between the show's creative team and its fictional world. He also gets a non-canon nod in a clip-show special that credits the many people behind the show's production. Overall, he's a subtle in-joke rather than a fleshed-out personality.

title: Rey
text: Rey is Non-canon Star Wars character referenced in Simpsons crossover specials. Rey is a non-canon character borrowed from the Star Wars franchise for use in Simpsons crossover material. She doesn't exist as an original Simpsons creation but appears through Lisa's cosplay portrayal during a special segment. In that appearance, Lisa dresses as Rey and battles Marge, who is costumed as Kylo Ren. Rey also shows up briefly in the background during a Star Wars-themed short. She has no speaking lines and functions purely as a visual reference/cameo rather than a developed character. Her inclusion reflects the show's tendency to parody or homage popular franchises through its characters.

title: The Secret Society of Super-Simians
text: The Secret Society of Super-Simians is A fictional superhero team from the Radioactive Man comic-within-a-show, based in Simian City. This group is a comic-book construct within the Simpsons universe, a band of ape and monkey superheroes led by Radioactive Ape. They're depicted holding monthly meetings at their leader's house, where serious talk of city safety devolves into getting drunk on banana daiquiris, a nod to superhero-team tropes played for comedy. The team includes other simian-themed heroes like Combo-Rilla, Humongo, Inspector Baboon, and Flash Gibbon, each presumably with their own powers befitting a pulpy comic parody. They appear tied closely to the Radioactive Man comic lore, surfacing again when Fallout Boy phones Radioactive Ape looking for the missing hero. As a group, they exist purely within the fictional comic pages referenced in the show rather than as characters who interact directly with the Simpsons family.

title: Cecile Shapiro
text: Cecile Shapiro is A minor recurring student character at the Enriched Learning Center for Gifted Children, occasionally appearing alongside Bart and Lisa. Cecile Shapiro is a young student who attends the Enriched Learning Center for Gifted Children, the same institution Bart briefly joins after an IQ test mishap. She's a minor background character who pops up in several episodes over the years, often in scenes involving school activities or academic competitions. Notably, she is one of the children who submits an essay in a nationwide contest, showing she has some academic ambition or talent. Cecile doesn't have a strongly defined personality in the show, functioning mostly as a recognizable face among the gifted-program kids. Her orange hair helps her stand out visually among the sea of Simpsons background characters. She has made numerous cameo-level appearances across the series' run without ever becoming a major storyline character. Voiced by Yeardley Smith.

title: Seth Rogen (character)
text: Seth Rogen (character) is Real-life celebrity who appears as himself in cameo roles within The Simpsons universe. Seth Rogen appears as a fictionalized version of himself, popping up in various media-related storylines in Springfield. He's shown following celebrity gossip and legal drama, such as watching the Hollywood versus Homer Simpson court case, and he's tied to the entertainment industry through his roles in in-universe films and appearances at podcast recordings and premieres. He shares screen time with fellow celebrity guest star Jonah Hill as co-leads in a movie, reinforcing his presence in the show's world of parody films. In a non-canon appearance, he's depicted as a mildly obnoxious presence at a Simpsons premiere, irritating another celebrity with his laughter. Overall, his character functions as a running gag device for inserting real Hollywood personalities into the show's universe rather than as a fully developed character with his own arc. Voiced by Seth Rogen (Himself).

title: Radioactive Worm
text: Radioactive Worm is A supervillain worm and enemy of Radioactive Man in the Bongo comics. Radioactive Worm is a minor but memorable villain from the Radioactive Man comic book series. He gained his mind-control abilities from the very same nuclear explosion that transformed Claude Kane III into the superhero Radioactive Man, making the two foes linked from their origins. He operates behind the scenes, manipulating other villains like Dr. Crab and Pneumatica as pawns in his schemes. His signature plot involves reverting Radioactive Man back into his weaker Radio Man form so he can control his mind, showing him to be a calculating and manipulative schemer rather than a brute-force fighter. Ultimately his plan is undone by sheer accident when Radio Man stumbles and breaks the machine meant to be used against him. Trying to escape after his defeat, Radioactive Worm meets an ironic end by frying himself on an exposed electrical wire, cementing his fate as a deceased character.

title: Old Tree Spirit
text: Old Tree Spirit is A magical talking tree in the Simpsons' backyard, appearing in a non-canon future episode. The Old Tree Spirit is a sentient, talking tree found in the backyard of 742 Evergreen Terrace, notable for its resemblance to the Ents from The Lord of the Rings in both look and voice. It reveals that trees have secretly possessed the abilities to move and speak for millennia, a secret nearly kept intact until one careless fir tree exposed it. When asked by Bart, it obligingly lowers Bart's treehouse to the ground by bending its trunk. Despite its helpfulness, it comes across as somewhat grumpy about the breach of ancient tree secrecy. As a non-canon character, it exists only within a flash-forward vision of the future rather than the show's main continuity. It later appears as a purchasable decoration in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Phillie Phanatic
text: Phillie Phanatic is Real-life mascot of the Philadelphia Phillies baseball team, appearing as a crossover character in The Simpsons. The Phillie Phanatic is a green, non-speaking mascot who appears as a crossover character rather than an original Simpsons creation. He briefly interacts with the show's cast during their travels to Philadelphia, first appearing to greet nuns who have just landed in the city. Later, he shows a more aggressive side when he attacks Homer during an outing with the H.O.A.G.I.E. Men. As a licensed mascot rather than a fictional Simpsons character, he has no dialogue and serves mainly as a comedic, real-world cameo tied to the city of Philadelphia. His appearances are brief and limited to just two episodes.

title: She-Hulk
text: She-Hulk is A Marvel comic book character referenced within the Simpsons universe, tied to Comic Book Guy's merchandise. She-Hulk isn't an actual character who appears in the Simpsons world, but rather a comic book property that exists within it, tied to the infamous flop title 'She-Hulk vs. Leon Spinks.' Comic Book Guy owns a large unsold stock of these comics, considering the crossover a total failure, and tries to keep neighborhood kids from getting their hands on them when he tosses them out. A She-Hulk poster also plays a small but memorable role in exposing one of Comic Book Guy's hidden secrets when it gets destroyed during a scuffle. Outside of canon, the character has inspired at least one Springfield resident to dress up as her for a superhero-themed event. She never speaks or acts on her own in the show, existing purely as background material tied to comic culture and fandom jokes.

title: Polystar executive
text: Polystar executive is Minor character; a film executive at Polystar Pictures who deals with Krusty the Clown. This executive represents the corporate side of the movie business within the Simpsons universe, specifically working for Polystar Pictures. He is portrayed as a shrewd businessman who wants to capitalize on Krusty's fame by continuing a successful franchise rather than taking creative risks. When Krusty refuses to make a sequel and insists on adapting a notoriously difficult book instead, the executive reluctantly agrees but does so with minimal investment, essentially setting the project up to fail. His actions reveal a cynical, pragmatic approach to filmmaking, prioritizing profit and control over artistic ambition. He appears only briefly in the show's canon but also exists as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Roy (The Itchy & Scratchy & Poochie Show)
text: Roy (The Itchy & Scratchy & Poochie Show) is A college-aged guy who temporarily moved in with the Simpson family. Roy is a laid-back, self-assured young man who ends up crashing at the Simpsons' house for a stretch of time before moving out to live with two women he describes as sexy. He was created as a satirical jab at network executives who wanted a hip new character added to shake up the show's format, and his design and attitude deliberately echo both Poochie and Fonzie from Happy Days. Despite his brief stay, he pops up again later attempting to help set a world record for the tallest human pyramid. In non-canon material, he's depicted as a member of a short-lived boy band, though he was too talentless to actually sing his own parts. He also has a strange, dreamlike run-in with an amnesiac Leela from Futurama, who swipes his sunglasses. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Photo girl
text: Photo girl is A minor recurring student in Bart's fourth grade class at Springfield Elementary School. The photo girl is a minor background character who appears sporadically throughout the series as one of Bart's classmates. She's shown participating in school activities, such as singing in the Christmas pageant and joining a field trip to the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. She's also a member of the Future Photographers of America club, showing an interest in photography as a hobby. In one notable moment, she unsuccessfully asks Bart to give her a copy of an embarrassing photo he took of Homer. Visually, she's noted to resemble another minor Simpsons character, Violet Bazaar. Overall, she serves as one of the many recognizable but rarely spotlighted faces filling out Bart's classroom scenes. Voiced by Russi Taylor.

title: Old King Coal
text: Old King Coal is Comic-book supervillain enemy of Radioactive Man and member of The Fossil Fuel Four. Old King Coal is a fictional supervillain who exists within the comic-book universe of Radioactive Man, a superhero followed by Bart and Milhouse. He operates as part of a group called The Fossil Fuel Four, a team of villains themed around fossil fuels. His signature power involves shooting coal projectiles from a scepter he carries, tying into his coal-themed persona. He and his teammates once attacked a nuclear power plant and succeeded in killing Radioactive Man, marking a significant, dark moment in the in-universe comic lore. His design draws visual inspiration from Marvel's The Thing, giving him a rocky, hulking appearance, while his name is a playful nod to the British nursery rhyme character Old King Cole. Beyond his comic appearances, a collectible figure of him has shown up in Comic Book Guy's collection, underscoring his status as niche pop-culture memorabilia within the show's world.

title: Security guard
text: Security guard is A minor recurring background character who works as a security guard at various Springfield locations. This unnamed security guard is a minor recurring figure who has held jobs at both the Springfield Grocery Store and the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. He isn't portrayed as particularly diligent, as shown by his tendency to get distracted from his duties. At the grocery store, he did manage to catch Bart Simpson attempting to shoplift chocolate bars. However, at the power plant, he was caught slacking off watching television instead of watching over the premises, which allowed a group of schoolchildren to sneak past the car barrier unnoticed. His characterization leans into the running gag of incompetent or easily distracted authority figures in Springfield. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Yosemite Sam
text: Yosemite Sam is A crossover Looney Tunes character referenced within The Simpsons universe, rather than an original character. Yosemite Sam is not a native Simpsons character but a borrowed Looney Tunes cowboy famous as one of Bugs Bunny's rivals. Within the world of The Simpsons, he exists mainly as a piece of pop culture trivia and background imagery rather than an active participant in the plot. He's been referenced as part of a fictional family tree, appeared as a picture used to test whether viewers are cartoon characters, and even been immortalized as a statue in a hillbilly-themed exhibit. A recurring joke ties him to a real-world figure, clarifying that a former U.S. president did not actually voice him. Despite his minor, mostly non-speaking presence, his inclusion highlights the show's fondness for referencing classic animation icons.

title: Pepi
text: Pepi is A poor boy who was matched with Homer as a 'little brother' through the Bigger Brothers Agency, and later became a recurring friend of Bart's. Pepi is a young boy from Springfield who first appears as Homer's assigned 'little brother' in a program meant to mirror Bart's own mentorship with Tom. Despite Homer feeding him dubious facts, Pepi is polite and easily impressed, and the two form a quick bond. When Homer is injured, Bart selflessly pairs Pepi with Tom instead, recognizing Pepi deserves a better mentor. Later, Pepi resurfaces as a student at East Springfield Elementary, living with Bumblebee Man in an unclear guardian arrangement, and reconnects with Bart after a bizarre accident leaves Bart speaking only Spanish. He's a good-natured, trusting kid who tends to get swept up in the odd adventures of the adults around him, including a lucha libre outing with Bumblebee Man. Behind the scenes, his character is a nod to the classic comic strip character Dondi. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: mi papa nuevo
quotes: mi papa nuevo

title: Peely
text: Peely is A non-canon sentient banana character who appears alongside other Fortnite crossover characters in Simpsons episodes. Peely is a living, walking banana who crossed over into the Simpsons universe from the video game Fortnite. He first appears helping Hope and Jonesy assist the Simpson family in finding a way to restore Homer to his normal size after he grows to enormous proportions. During that encounter, a powerful burp from Homer accidentally knocks Peely's peel clean off. He later resurfaces lounging on the Simpsons' couch with fellow Fortnite characters Jonesy, Hope, Meowscles, and Fishstick, only for the group to be confronted at gunpoint by the family. Unlike his companions, Peely fails to escape and ends up passing out, leading to the rather grim fate of being turned into a banana split and eaten by the Simpsons. Beyond his appearances in the show, Peely also exists as a cosmetic outfit in the Fortnite video game, complete with both a standard Fortnite style and a LEGO-themed variant. He is a non-speaking character throughout his appearances, existing purely as a visual gag tied to the Fortnite crossover.

title: Miss Piggy
text: Miss Piggy is Muppet character who crosses over into The Simpsons universe, appearing in Muppet-themed sketches within the show. Miss Piggy is a pink pig Muppet best known as a co-star and love interest of Kermit the Frog on The Muppet Show. She's portrayed as fiercely jealous and protective of her relationship with Kermit, willing to resort to violence when she feels threatened by rivals. Her appearances in The Simpsons universe are tied to Muppet parody segments rather than the main Springfield storylines, often alongside celebrity guest stars. She also starred in a Muppet film alongside Kermit and Troy McClure. Despite her comedic diva persona, she's a recognizable pop-culture figure referenced by Simpsons characters as an example of a famous on-screen romance. She functions as a non-speaking, recurring crossover character within the show's universe.

title: Toucan Sam
text: Toucan Sam is A cereal mascot character who appears in a Homer fantasy sequence. Toucan Sam is a blue-feathered toucan who serves as a cereal mascot, based on the real-world Froot Loops advertising character. Within the show, he exists as a fictional figure who shows up in one of Homer's food-related fantasies, blending real-world advertising icons into the Simpsons universe. He also makes an appearance in the in-universe video game Cereal Killer, suggesting he has some pop-culture presence beyond just cereal boxes. Despite his brief and minor role, he's notable enough to be catalogued among the show's recurring and deceased fictional characters. His character leans entirely on his real-world branding rather than any original personality traits developed by the show. Voiced by Maurice LaMarche.

title: Mrs. Powell
text: Mrs. Powell is Mother of Janey Powell, one of Lisa Simpson's friends, and a minor recurring Springfield resident. Mrs. Powell is a background resident of Springfield known mainly as the mother of Janey, Lisa Simpson's close friend. She is a non-speaking character, appearing quietly in the background of various scenes rather than taking part in dialogue. Her most notable appearance came when Lisa visited the Powell household to watch a banned episode of The Itchy and Scratchy Show after Marge forbade it. She has also been seen attending a town meeting concerning Mr. Burns' scheme to block out the sun. Beyond these brief moments, she functions as one of many recurring extras populating the town, with little defined personality shown on screen.

title: Plato
text: Plato is Historical Athenian philosopher referenced in the Simpsons universe, appearing via a book and as a casino mascot. Plato is not a regular character but a historical figure incorporated into the Simpsons world in small, humorous ways. His writings appear as a book in the collection at the Enriched Learning Center for Gifted Children, hinting at the intellectual pretensions of that institution. More prominently, an actor dressed as Plato works for Plato's Republic Casino, greeting visitors including residents of the Springfield Retirement Castle. This casino-employee version blends the gravity of classical philosophy with the show's love of absurd, low-brow business branding. Plato himself never appears as a living, speaking character in the main story, but his name and image are used as background gags and signage throughout Springfield. He represents the show's recurring habit of dropping historical and literary references into mundane settings for comedic effect. Voiced by Phil Hartman.

title: Scene Blow
text: Scene Blow is A minor clown character at Ding-A-Ling Bros. Circus. Scene Blow is a green-haired clown who works at Ding-A-Ling Bros. Circus. He was introduced to Krusty by Scuzzo, and greeted him with a classic clown prank by spraying him with water instead of a proper introduction. He's a background presence around the circus, helping with performances and general activities. His most memorable gag involves chasing after the departing circus train on a handcar after giving Krusty one last spray of water. He's a non-speaking character, letting his physical comedy do the talking. He later shows up as part of a trivia team at Moe's Tavern, suggesting he has a life outside the circus.

title: Pigeon-Rat
text: Pigeon-Rat is A hybrid creature created by Hugo Simpson, Bart's evil conjoined twin brother, in a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment. The Pigeon-Rat is a bizarre creation stitched together by Hugo Simpson as a way to hone his surgical skills before attempting to reattach himself to Bart. Made by sewing a pigeon and a rat back-to-back, the creature is comically dysfunctional, unable to fly or scurry into small spaces due to its awkward combined form. It never speaks and exists mainly as a visual gag illustrating Hugo's twisted experimentation. The creature later made a small appearance in The Simpsons: Tapped Out as part of Hugo-related content. It stands as one of the show's many non-canon Halloween special oddities, more of a prop than a character with personality.

title: Linda Ronstadt (character)
text: Linda Ronstadt (character) is Guest celebrity character; a real-life singer who appears in a Springfield commercial. Linda Ronstadt appears as a fictionalized version of herself, brought in by Barney Gumble to lend star power to his Plow King commercial. She performs the Plow King jingle in English and later mentions to Barney that she is developing a Spanish-language version, singing a bit of it for him. Her willingness to collaborate with Barney puzzles Moe, who questions how such an arrangement came about. Beyond her singing cameo, her likeness resurfaces in a non-canon context, appearing on a T-shirt worn by an unrelated background character. She functions primarily as a one-episode celebrity guest rather than a recurring personality with defined traits. Voiced by Herself.

title: George Plimpton (character)
text: George Plimpton (character) is Real-life journalist and writer who appeared as himself, hosting the Spellympics spelling competition. George Plimpton is a guest-starring version of the real-life journalist and Paris Review founder, appearing in the show as the host of the Spellympics competition. He proves to be manipulative behind the scenes, secretly pressuring Lisa Simpson to intentionally lose the contest in exchange for a guaranteed spot at a prestigious college. When she refuses and calls him out publicly, he vindictively ensures she gets nothing after her loss, revealing a petty and corrupt side beneath his polished public persona. He's also shown to have a side career in acting, having played a villainous dean in a fictional film called Boner Academy. His appearance ties into the show's tradition of having real celebrities voice comedic, occasionally unflattering versions of themselves. Voiced by George Plimpton (Himself). Notable quotes: I'm George Plimpton, founder of the Paris Review. I also played the evil dean in "Boner Academy". | He replaced my tennis racket with a rubber phallus. | You monster! Why did you expel Boogerman?
quotes: I'm George Plimpton, founder of the Paris Review. I also played the evil dean in "Boner Academy".
He replaced my tennis racket with a rubber phallus.

title: Mike Pence
text: Mike Pence is Real-world political figure (former U.S. Vice President) who appears as a minor/background character in Simpsons specials and mentions. Mike Pence appears in the show as a caricature of the real former Vice President of the United States, mostly in non-canon holiday specials tied to the Trump administration. He's portrayed as a quiet, somewhat eerie background presence, best known in-universe for unsettling Lisa with his unblinking stare. In one special he's shown scheming at his desk, altering his nameplate from "Vice President" to "President Pence," hinting at ambition beneath his calm exterior. In another, he acts as a moral compass for Trump, and is even comically produced in miniature form from Trump's pocket. His appearances lean heavily on political satire rather than deep characterization, using his real-life persona for topical humor. He remains a minor, mostly non-speaking figure rather than a fleshed-out character in the show's core canon. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: the "cold dead eyes of Mike Pence" were bothering her
quotes: the "cold dead eyes of Mike Pence" were bothering her

title: Robot Santa
text: Robot Santa is Non-canon crossover character from Futurama; a robotic version of Santa Claus who appears in Simpsons comic books. Robot Santa is a mechanical stand-in for Santa Claus, originally created for the show Futurama before crossing over into Simpsons comic book stories. He appears in bizarre, non-canon scenarios such as when Springfield residents are teleported to a futuristic city, where Ralph is seen sitting on his lap. Elsewhere, one of Santa's own elves builds a miniature model of him for the unusual purpose of punishing children. He even shows up as an imagined figure in Comic Book Guy's holiday-themed dream about becoming Santa himself. Robot Santa exists purely within whimsical, fantastical storylines rather than the show's normal continuity, reflecting the series' willingness to borrow characters from its sister show for comic relief.

title: Allan Sherman
text: Allan Sherman is Real-world comedy writer/singer referenced in The Simpsons, not a speaking character in the show. Allan Sherman is a real-life American comedy writer, television producer, singer, and actor whose work is referenced within the Simpsons universe rather than portrayed as an active character. His presence in the show is limited to background gags and pictures rather than dialogue, making him a non-speaking, picture-only figure. He is most notably tied to his song 'Hello Muddah, Hello Fadduh (A Letter from Camp)', which Bart uses to prank the family by swapping it in for the answering machine tape. His name is also invoked by Homer as a comparison point for 'Weird Al' Yankovic, suggesting a similar niche in musical comedy. Additionally, one of his albums appears as a background reference in another episode. Overall, Sherman exists in the show as an homage to real-world comedic music history rather than as a developed character.

title: Praline
text: Praline is Minor recurring character; ex-wife of Jay G, seeking revenge against him. Praline is a minor character defined largely by her bitter split from her ex-husband Jay G, who she claims took everything from her. She enlists Mr. Burns, Homer, Bart, and Jazzy James to help her get back at Jay G through a recording studio scheme, bringing in RZA, Snoop Dogg, and Common to assist. She has a change of heart later, appearing as a hologram to admit she no longer hates Jay G. Praline has a checkered past, having spent time in prison at some point. She also has a personal assistant named Miata and participates in a trivia team at Moe's Tavern. The character is a parody of Cookie Lyon from the TV drama Empire, fittingly voiced by the same actress who played that role, Taraji P. Henson. Voiced by Taraji P. Henson.

title: Professor Rubber-Mouth
text: Professor Rubber-Mouth is A minor Springfield celebrity known for a unique mouth-based talent. Professor Rubber-Mouth is a barely-there Springfield celebrity whose sole claim to fame is his oddball party trick of stuffing multiple billiard balls into his mouth. He's shown briefly in a segment of News on Parade Corporation News, existing as one of the town's many strange, minor local personalities. He never actually speaks on screen, fitting the show's tradition of introducing bizarre one-off background characters purely for a quick visual gag. His appearance is tied to a flashback sequence rather than any ongoing storyline, underscoring his status as a fleeting curiosity rather than a developed character.

title: Russian businessman
text: Russian businessman is Minor recurring character, a member of the International Brotherhood of Evil. The Russian businessman is a shadowy figure tied to the villainous International Brotherhood of Evil, appearing briefly in a Simpsons spy parody episode. He is defined mainly by a single dramatic action rather than an ongoing personality trait: leaping out of a cake to gun down General Stradivarius Cain. This surprise attack came after his unnamed mistress falsely claimed to have already killed Cain herself, adding a twist of betrayal and deception to the scene. He has gray hair and no other physical or background details are given, keeping him a mysterious, almost cartoonishly sinister spy-thriller stock character. His appearance is limited to a single episode, with a later cameo only via archive footage. Overall he exists as a quick, comedic nod to Bond-villain tropes rather than a deeply developed character. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Pharaoh
text: Pharaoh is The King of Egypt, appearing in Lisa's dream sequence based on the story of Exodus. Pharaoh is a minor, non-canon figure who appears in Lisa's imagined retelling of the biblical Exodus story, where he is portrayed by Principal Skinner. In this dream, he stubbornly refuses to free the Israelites, played by Lisa and Moses, despite facing a string of comedic plagues. He eventually loses his prisoners after they escape a pyramid and cross a dried seabed created by flushing all of Egypt's toilets at once. His pursuit ends in disaster when the sea rushes back and washes him and his guards away. Outside of this dream sequence, he is only briefly mentioned in another story as a joking reference point for royalty. He later appears as a mobile game character based on his Skinner-as-Pharaoh design. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Tom O'Flanagan
text: Tom O'Flanagan is Former bartender and owner of O'Flanagan's Pub in Ireland, sold to Homer and Grampa Simpson. Tom O'Flanagan is an aging Irish publican whose once-thriving business fell victim to Ireland's modernization, leaving him with a nearly empty bar. Rather than adapting or fighting to keep his pub alive, he resigned himself to a quiet, nostalgic decline, spending his days watching old horse race videos instead of tending to customers. His fortunes changed when Homer and Grampa Simpson stumbled into his establishment while drunk and impulsively bought it from him. Tom seemed relieved rather than sentimental about letting go, suggesting a weary acceptance of his fading livelihood. He's a minor but memorable figure representing old-world Irish charm giving way to new ownership and change. Voiced by Colm Meaney.

title: Jiff Simpson
text: Jiff Simpson is Future son of Bart Simpson, grandson of Homer and Marge, appearing in flash-forward episodes. Jiff Simpson, also referred to as Kirk Simpson, is depicted as the younger child of a future version of Bart Simpson and his ex-wife Jenda. He initially seems reluctant to spend the holidays with his father, gravitating instead toward his grandfather Homer. His storyline highlights Bart's struggles and growth as a parent, with Homer stepping in to reassure the kids that their father, though imperfect, loves them. Jiff shares a playful bond with his brother Skippy, seen chasing Homer's consciousness through family photos in a lighthearted game. The two brothers are named as an homage to Star Trek captains Kirk and Picard, reflecting the show's penchant for pop-culture nods even in its non-canon future timelines. He continues to appear in later flash-forward-related episodes, including family gatherings after Homer's death. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Oscar the Grouch
text: Oscar the Grouch is A crossover Muppet character from Sesame Street who occasionally appears or is referenced in The Simpsons. Oscar the Grouch is a guest character borrowed from Sesame Street who makes sporadic cameo appearances in Springfield rather than being a true Simpsons original. He's most associated with garbage and trash cans, fittingly popping out of one while Homer sings about garbage men, and later joining a chase of Homer alongside other PBS characters. His grouchy, trash-dwelling nature has become a running comparison point, with characters like Homer and Ralph likening smelly or dumpster-dwelling people to him. He's also referenced in dialogue and even appears on a promotional banner for a fictional ice show. Despite his limited screen time, his presence highlights the show's fondness for pop-culture crossovers and parody of children's television icons. Due to legal considerations, he was jokingly referred to by an alternate name in a DVD commentary. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Dodd Runtledge
text: Dodd Runtledge is Twin brother of Rod Runtledge, a minor character in the Radioactive Man comic book series within the Simpsons universe. Dodd Runtledge is a comic-book character believed dead by his twin brother Rod after a plane crash in a South American jungle. He turns up alive years later, discovered by Rod (secretly the superhero Fallout Boy) via a photo from an Armed Forces Day barbecue. Dodd is found at a hippie peace gathering under the mind-control influence of the villain Hypno-Head, and is freed after Radioactive Man and Fallout Boy defeat the villain. Suffering from amnesia that erased his memories after the crash, he's sent off to military school by Radioactive Man to help him readjust. Eventually he reunites with his brother Rod and goes to live with him. His story is a small side-plot within the larger Radioactive Man comic mythology rather than a major recurring presence.

title: Safety Salamander
text: Safety Salamander is A safety mascot costume/persona for Springfield Elementary School, adopted by Homer Simpson. The Safety Salamander is an orange salamander mascot costume that Homer Simpson wears after Principal Skinner suggests it as a way to become a positive role model for Lisa. His early attempts at the role are disastrous, including a botched bus safety demonstration and an accidental gymnasium fire during a school presentation. Despite these failures, he becomes a genuine town hero after rescuing people from a multi-car pileup, leading to unexpected fame and a key to the city. This popularity inspires Lisa to push Homer into running for mayor as the Safety Salamander, and the costume briefly becomes a symbol of civic trust. The gag largely revolves around the absurd contrast between Homer's incompetence and the costume's earnest, heroic image, culminating in the suit literally falling apart at a crucial debate. The character underscores recurring themes of Homer's bumbling nature clashing with moments of accidental heroism. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Pie Man
text: Pie Man is A homemade superhero alter-ego of Homer Simpson. Pie Man is a makeshift vigilante identity invented by Homer during a county fair after his rage at The Rich Texan for ruining Lisa's contest entry got the better of him. To avoid another assault charge, he disguised himself with a quilt cape and a pie tin mask, choosing to humiliate wrongdoers with pies to the face instead of violence. His secret identity doesn't stay secret for long, as both Lisa and later Mr. Burns figure out he's really Homer, with Burns even blackmailing him into targeting his personal enemies. Chief Wiggum treats the vigilante as a genuine threat, at one point shooting him during an attempt to unmask him. Despite eventually revealing the truth himself during a visit from the Dalai Lama, nobody but Marge believes that mild-mannered Homer is actually Pie Man. Bart later joins in on the act as his sidekick, dubbed Cupcake Kid. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Gordon Ramsay (character)
text: Gordon Ramsay (character) is Real-world celebrity chef who appears as himself in cameo roles in the Simpsons universe. Gordon Ramsay is a real celebrity chef who makes several cameo appearances throughout the show, often playing on his real-life persona as a culinary personality. He first shows up in a surreal dream sequence experienced by Marge, where he offers her guidance about a fancy restaurant reservation before claiming the dream was actually his own. Beyond that appearance, he mostly exists as a background reference, with his image turning up on a restaurant wall and even as part of an online captcha test for identifying celebrity chefs. He is also depicted hosting his own television cooking competition show, tying into the franchise's frequent parodies of reality TV culinary programs. His fame is such that even background characters mention watching his show casually. Overall, Ramsay serves as a fun cameo/reference gag rather than a fleshed-out character with personality traits explored in depth. Voiced by Gordon Ramsay.

title: Stanley Roper
text: Stanley Roper is A background reference/crossover character representing the landlord from the sitcoms Three's Company and The Ropers, appearing as a statue/poster within the Simpsons universe. Stanley Roper isn't an original Simpsons creation but rather a nod to the character played by Norman Fell in Three's Company and its spin-off The Ropers. Within the show's world, he exists only as a statue and a poster displayed at the Museum of TV and Television, making him a non-speaking background reference rather than an active participant in any storyline. He's also referenced in a non-canon story told by Homer, where he's mentioned as the landlord of Jack, Janet, and Chrissy. His inclusion serves as a playful homage to classic sitcom history rather than developing him as a character in his own right. He has no dialogue or direct interaction with the main Simpsons cast.

title: Jonathan Scott
text: Jonathan Scott is Fictionalized version of the real-life Property Brothers TV personality, appearing in cameo-style roles in The Simpsons. Jonathan Scott is a parody of the real Canadian TV personality known for co-hosting the home renovation show Property Brothers alongside his twin brother Drew. In the world of the Simpsons, he appears mostly in brief or surreal contexts rather than as a fully developed character. He once showed up in one of Marge's dreams, where Homer bizarrely took on the identity of both Property Brothers at once. His other appearance is non-canon, tied to a storyline where Homer is held hostage and forced to watch Property Brothers because his captor is a fan of the show. As a character, Jonathan doesn't have much personality development in the show itself—he mainly exists as a nod to real-world pop culture and reality TV tropes. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Gloria S.
text: Gloria S. is Minor recurring character; wife of John S., attended Reverend Lovejoy's marriage counseling retreat. Gloria S. is a minor Springfield resident whose marriage was on the rocks until Reverend Lovejoy intervened during a counseling retreat. She and her husband John rediscovered their affection for each other simply by locking eyes, leaving the retreat as a happy couple. The pair later appear enjoying a night out at a club, watching a performance by baseball player Steve Sax. Little else is known about Gloria's personality or life outside of her relationship with John. Behind the scenes, the couple is intended as a nod to Martha and George, the battling spouses from the play Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?. She remains a background character who has made only a handful of brief appearances. Voiced by Julie Kavner.

title: Doctor Octopus
text: Doctor Octopus is Marvel comic-book supervillain (Spider-Man enemy) referenced within the Simpsons universe, often via costumes and cameos. Doctor Octopus, real name Otto Octavius, is a fictional Marvel villain who exists as a pop-culture reference within the Simpsons world rather than an original character. He's most often seen as a costume choice for background characters like Comic Book Guy at various comic conventions, or as a party entertainer hired for Nelson's birthday. His signature four extra mechanical arms are a recurring visual gag, notably used by Dr. Nick when he humorously imitates the villain in a cemetery. The character also appears in in-universe comic book covers, including one depicting his wedding to Mary Jane Watson. A trivial continuity nod points out that his hair color changes between appearances, being blond in one comic depiction despite traditionally having brown hair. Overall, he functions as a recurring nerd-culture easter egg rather than a fleshed-out character in the show. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: I'm not Dr. Nick, I am Dr. Octopus!
quotes: I'm not Dr. Nick, I am Dr. Octopus!

title: Dirk Richter
text: Dirk Richter is Deceased actor within the Simpsons universe who played Radioactive Man in the TV series. Dirk Richter was a fictional actor best known for portraying the superhero Radioactive Man on television. His later years were marked by scandal, and his life ended violently when he was found shot to death in a bordello. There are hints of an unusual personal relationship between him and Buddy Hodges, the actor who played his sidekick Fallout Boy. Despite being long dead, his name was still floated as a potential casting choice for a Radioactive Man film, only for the idea to be dismissed due to his age and, more obviously, his death. He also had a stage career, having starred in a musical adaptation of the Radioactive Man story. A non-canon detail humorously notes that a romance novelist shares his exact name, leading to a mix-up involving Bart and Milhouse. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Richter was "73 years old and dead."
quotes: Richter was "73 years old and dead."

title: Ashley Olsen (character)
text: Ashley Olsen (character) is Real-life celebrity guest character; twin sister of Mary-Kate Olsen, appearing as herself in a cameo. Ashley Olsen appears as a fictionalized version of herself within the Simpsons universe, representing the real-life actress and one half of the famous Olsen twins. She's depicted alongside her sister Mary-Kate, with the two working together seamlessly, finishing each other's sentences and passing off narration duties to one another. Her main claim to fame in the show is co-narrating an audiobook and having written a series of books that a young fan, Milhouse, is obsessed with. She comes across as a bit detached from history and everyday sadness, offering an innocent, almost naive comment about the past. Ashley's presence is brief but memorable, tying into the show's tradition of using real celebrities as themselves in cameo roles. Voiced by Herself. Notable quotes: I didn't know people were sad in the past.
quotes: I didn't know people were sad in the past.

title: Rottweiler
text: Rottweiler is A bounty hunter and former love interest of Nelson Muntz, appearing in a non-canon future storyline. Rott is a tough, no-nonsense bounty hunter who first crosses paths with Nelson Muntz over something as trivial as an overdue library book, sparking an unlikely romance. The two become a formidable duo, teaming up on odd jobs like busting Principal Skinner for a minor mattress tag violation, and later working together to thwart a train robbery attempt by Jeremy Jailbird. During that same train encounter, she strikes up an easy rapport with Lisa Simpson, sharing a drink with her. Despite her chemistry with Nelson, her secretive involvement in a fight club ultimately drives a wedge between them, leading to their breakup. She embodies a rugged, independent personality fitting her bounty-hunter profession, existing within the non-canon future timeline explored in "When Nelson Met Lisa." Rott also appears as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Bernie Sanders
text: Bernie Sanders is Real-world American politician who appears as a caricature in The Simpsons universe. Bernie Sanders appears in the show as a fictionalized version of the real senator, often used for topical political humor. He's referenced as a notable figure whose identity is teased when Grampa wakes from a coma unaware of current events. A flashback imagines him as a socialist baby prophesied by Frida Kahlo to one day take down capitalists, complete with tough infant enforcers called the Bernie babies. In non-canon material, he's shown getting along with rival politicians like Donald Trump and Hillary Clinton, even being comically strangled by Clinton's necklace, and later appears dancing in a can-can line with other presidential candidates. The character leans into his real-life reputation as a fiery, idealistic socialist figure. He's also noted to have attended a real-world Simpsons Movie premiere alongside a Vermont politician, blending the show's fictional and real-world connections. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, Chris Edgerly. Notable quotes: it's not Bernie? | getting a cootie shot should not cost your lunch money | if they didn't listen to him, they should listen to the Bernie babies
quotes: it's not Bernie?
getting a cootie shot should not cost your lunch money
if they didn't listen to him, they should listen to the Bernie babies

title: Butch Patrick (character)
text: Butch Patrick (character) is Real-life actor (famous for playing Eddie Munster) who appears as himself in a Simpsons episode. Butch Patrick appears as a fictionalized version of himself, lending his real-world fame as the actor behind Eddie Munster to a Springfield storyline. He shows up when Apu is weighing whether to place his octuplets in the city zoo, offering reassurance that childhood stardom didn't damage him. In a humorous aside, he can't quite explain the biological logic of his own famous character, agreeing with Apu that a werewolf son of a vampire and a Frankenstein doesn't add up. Beyond his cameo, he's shown to have an odd side job as a notary, formally stamping Apu's contract. He later takes part in a bizarre stunt performance, riding atop Homer's shoulders on a tiny bicycle while dodging cobras. In a non-canon nod, he's also referenced as one of the trendy guest stars brought on to boost ratings. Voiced by Butch Patrick (Himself).

title: Freddy Quimby
text: Freddy Quimby is Nephew of Mayor Quimby, and later his press secretary. Freddy Quimby is a recurring member of Springfield's corrupt Quimby political dynasty, first appearing as a wealthy young man on trial for savagely beating a French waiter. He narrowly escapes conviction thanks to Bart Simpson's testimony, highlighting the family's knack for dodging accountability. Later gags reveal a darker side to his past, including being listed among sex offenders required to register in town. Over time his character softens somewhat, changing his look and voice as he matures into a more responsible role serving as his uncle's press secretary. Despite his checkered history, he eventually shows a flash of integrity by being willing to publicly criticize his uncle's administration during a contentious town hall meeting. In non-canon material, he's shown briefly running a fish stick factory before being fired by his own uncle. His character is a satirical nod to the Kennedy family, complete with a recurring joke about his love of chowder. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Pikkanoze
text: Pikkanoze is Non-canon manga/comic character; a Pokémon-parody creature featured in Simpsons comic book stories. Pikkanoze is a fictional creature from the in-universe manga Porkeymen, a parody of the Pokémon franchise and specifically Pikachu. He first appears alongside similarly parodic characters Sailor Moose and Dragonbrawler X. His notable trait is a hypnotic ability, which he uses on Maggie Simpson, causing her to become fixated on caring for him. This gag continues when the Simpson family visits Springfield Wild Animal Park, where Maggie escapes to look after Pikkanoze again. As a non-canon comic-exclusive character, he exists purely within the world of Bongo Comics stories rather than the show's main continuity.

title: Brad Pitt
text: Brad Pitt is Real-life celebrity actor referenced/appearing as himself in The Simpsons. Brad Pitt appears in the show as a version of his real-world celebrity persona, most notably known for his high-profile romance with Angelina Jolie, often dubbed 'Brangelina.' Characters in Springfield frequently bring up his relationship with Jolie as a reference point for celebrity romance and gossip. He is trained by local personal trainer Lyle McCarthy, tying him briefly into the town's storyline. In a non-canon twist, a version of him is depicted as a doctor who gets arrested, showing the show's playful, exaggerated use of celebrity cameos. He also shows up in a non-canon Oscar Selfie special. Overall, Pitt functions less as a developed character and more as a running pop-culture reference point for the show's satire of celebrity culture.

title: Scrat
text: Scrat is A crossover character appearing briefly in The Simpsons, based on the Ice Age franchise character. Scrat is a saber-toothed squirrel-rat who crosses over into The Simpsons universe from the Ice Age film franchise. He appears in a brief comedic scene where Willie kicks him for stealing an acorn, only to be swarmed by more of Scrat's kind in retaliation. His inclusion is a nod to the popular animated movie series, serving as a fun cameo rather than a fully developed character within the show. Scrat has no dialogue and communicates through physical comedy, consistent with his portrayal in Ice Age. He also appears in non-canon media such as The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Overall, his role is minor and largely serves as an easter egg for fans of both franchises. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta / Chris Wedge.

title: Popeye
text: Popeye is Crossover character from the Popeye comic strip/cartoons referenced within the Simpsons universe. Popeye is not an original Simpsons character but a crossover figure borrowed from the classic comic strip and cartoon franchise of the same name. Within the show, he exists mostly as a background reference or pop-culture nod rather than an active participant in the plot. He's cited by Comic Book Guy as the source of one of the greatest quotes of all time, and his image has shown up on fast food packaging parodying the real-world restaurant chain that shares his name. He also appears as a fantastical figure in one of Bart's nightmares, tending a spinach farm on the site of his former school. Fittingly for a character so tied to his signature girlfriend, he's shown attending a party alongside Olive Oyl, and the couple's iconic look has even inspired a couples' costume for Cletus and Brandine Spuckler. Overall, Popeye functions as a fun cameo/reference rather than a developed character in the show. Notable quotes: "I yam what I yam" by Popeye
quotes: "I yam what I yam" by Popeye

title: Steve Sax (character)
text: Steve Sax (character) is Real-life baseball player recruited as a guest star to play for the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant softball team. Steve Sax appears as a fictionalized version of himself, recruited by Waylon Smithers to bolster the power plant's softball roster ahead of a big game against Shelbyville. Like the other real-life ballplayers brought in for the episode, his cameo pokes fun at celebrity guest appearances and the absurd lengths Mr. Burns and Smithers go to in order to win. His storyline takes a darkly comic turn when he is mistakenly pulled over by local police and connected to a string of unsolved murders in New York City, threatening him with multiple life sentences. This bizarre subplot is left unresolved, adding to the episode's satirical tone about celebrity scandal and small-town paranoia. Outside of the main show continuity, he also reportedly turns up at a non-canon event tied to a Simpsons season finale premiere. Voiced by Steve Sax (Himself).

title: Sailor boy
text: Sailor boy is A minor recurring background character and student at Springfield Elementary, briefly allied with Bart. Sailor Boy is a minor, non-speaking background kid seen occasionally around Bart and the Springfield Elementary crowd. His most memorable moment comes when he joins Bart's makeshift army in the fight against Nelson, and after their victory he impulsively kisses Lisa in a nod to the iconic World War II victory photograph. Lisa is unimpressed, shoving him away and slapping him for the unwanted kiss. Beyond that comedic cameo, he pops up in a few other episodes as just another face in the crowd, such as sneaking into an adult movie screening at the Simpsons' house. He has no dialogue and no defined personality beyond that single gag, existing mainly as a visual joke and recurring extra.

title: Peter Pan (character)
text: Peter Pan (character) is Fictional storybook character referenced in The Simpsons, based on the classic Peter Pan tale. Peter Pan appears in The Simpsons universe mainly as a literary and costume reference rather than a fully developed character. He's depicted as the eternally young boy who refuses to grow up, staying true to his classic origins. In one storybook reading, Marge reads Lisa a passage he reportedly disliked, involving a comment about needing a mother's love. He also appears as a costume choice for Captain McCallister at a masquerade event. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he's humorously treated as a real criminal, arrested by Scotland Yard on suspicion of child abduction, staying defiant about never growing up even under interrogation. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: He will never grow up.
quotes: He will never grow up.

title: Montaigne Prince
text: Montaigne Prince is Younger brother of Martin Prince and a student at Springfield High School. Montaigne Prince is a minor recurring character best known as the sibling of the brainy Martin Prince. He briefly competes for a spot as lead drummer in the Springfield High School band, only to be upstaged when Shauna commandeers his drum kit for her own audition. Outside of school activities, he shows a normal teenage social life, attending a classmate's party where he manages to make out with a girl. He's also depicted spending time with his family, visiting the public library and joining his parents and brother at a town Bounce-A-Thon event. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he meets a grim fate at the hands of Lisa Simpson's murderous alter ego, ending up transformed into a clock. Overall, Montaigne serves as an extension of the Prince family dynamic rather than a character with a defined personality of his own. Voiced by Grey DeLisle.

title: Quetzelica
text: Quetzelica is Fictional superhero and member of the Vindicators team within the Simpsons universe. Quetzelica is a superhero belonging to the Vindicators, a fictional superhero team referenced within the show's universe. She is depicted as a magical weapon-wielding fighter with purple hair. Her most notable appearance involves the climactic battle against the villain Chinnos, during which she and her teammates were turned to crystal by his Doomsday app. She later resurfaces in a virtual reality simulation built for Bart, where she again battles Chinnos' forces before ultimately helping defeat him. Beyond her combat appearances, she has also shown up as background pop-culture ephemera, such as a costume worn by convention-goers and a collectible figure owned by Comic Book Guy. Design-wise, she serves as an in-universe parody of Thor from the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

title: Richie Rich
text: Richie Rich is A crossover comic-book character (from Harvey Comics) appearing within the Simpsons universe, both as a comic Bart and Lisa read and as an in-universe figure. Richie Rich is a wealthy cartoon boy borrowed from the Harvey Comics universe who occasionally pops up in the world of The Simpsons. He's first noticed by Bart and Lisa while reading a comic book, sparking their theory that Casper the Friendly Ghost is actually his deceased spirit. Beyond the comic-book page, he's depicted as an extremely rich figure with his own butler, Cadbury, whom he orders around when trouble arises near his estate. He even shows up in the non-canon world of Springfield as a stand-in actor for Bart during a rehab storyline, though his episodes weren't well received. His recurring appearances as a comic book, background gag, or costume highlight his role as a nostalgic pop-culture reference rather than a fully fleshed-out character. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Red Queen
text: Red Queen is A fictional character from Alice in Wonderland who appears in a pop-up book Lisa reads to Maggie. The Red Queen is a storybook character originating from Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, brought into the Simpsons universe when Lisa reads a pop-up edition of Alice in Wonderland to Maggie, voicing the character herself. She has black hair and holds the title of Queen within the story. Her depiction in a later special draws directly from her literary description rather than Disney's film versions. In a non-canon holiday special, she is depicted as one of the many characters who gets snapped out of existence by Thanos, referencing the Marvel villain. She has no independent personality development in the show beyond her brief appearances tied to the storybook framing device. Voiced by Yeardley Smith.

title: Park engineer
text: Park engineer is An engineer working at Itchy & Scratchy Land theme park. The park engineer is a minor employee of Itchy & Scratchy Land who oversees the technical operation of the park's animatronic attractions. He first appears when the Simpson family visits the Tavern on the Scream ride, attempting to reassure a nervous Marge about the safety of the robotic animatronics. However, his confidence seems shaky, as he quickly leaves the scene when Marge presses him with doubts. Despite this, he later returns to insist the animatronics would never harm anyone, showing a somewhat unconvincing but persistent effort to maintain the park's safety image. He also takes a moment to warn Cletus against using flash photography near the robots, hinting at some technical sensitivity in the animatronics' systems. Overall, he serves as a background character emphasizing the recurring theme of Itchy & Scratchy Land's questionable safety standards. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer (character)
text: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer (character) is Santa Claus's reindeer, appearing in various Christmas-themed episodes of The Simpsons. Rudolph is the famous red-nosed reindeer belonging to Santa Claus, referenced throughout the show's various Christmas specials. He rarely appears as a fully active character, showing up more often as a mentioned figure, statue, or costume rather than in person. In one particularly dark gag, Santa Claus reveals he was forced to eat Rudolph out of desperation, displaying a grim stew made from the beloved reindeer. He's also been imagined by Homer as morphing into a strange baboon, and Ralph Wiggum once dressed up as him for Halloween, using a glowing red nose to guide lost kids home through the fog. In a non-canon segment, Rudolph meets an even stranger fate, being devoured by a giant snake on a deserted island. Overall, Rudolph serves as a recurring holiday reference point and source of dark humor rather than a fleshed-out character.

title: Charlie Sheen
text: Charlie Sheen is Real-life actor who appears as a celebrity cameo character in Springfield, part of the Sheen-Estevez clan. Charlie Sheen appears as a fictionalized version of himself within the Simpsons universe, tied to his real family through the Sheen-Estevez clan alongside his father Martin Sheen and brother Emilio Estevez. He is depicted as a spectator at high-profile events, such as attending the boxing match between Drederick Tatum and Homer Simpson. His clan has a reputation for getting into altercations, notably a feud with the Baldwin brothers that derailed his planned appearance in a Shakespeare in the Park production of Romeo and Juliet. As a non-speaking character, he never delivers memorable dialogue, functioning more as a background celebrity cameo than a character with dialogue-driven personality. His presence reflects the show's frequent habit of poking fun at real Hollywood figures and their public personas. Voiced by Maurice LaMarche.

title: Paul Revere
text: Paul Revere is Historical American patriot referenced/depicted in Springfield settings, not a main cast member. Paul Revere appears in the show as a historical figure rather than a fleshed-out character, showing up mostly as costumes, statues, or imagined apparitions. A child dressed as him while being scolded by his father over a school essay, tying him to a moment of civic-minded satire. He later turns up as a background figure during a tour of a historical theme park, and even appears as an imagined talking statue in Bart's mind, humorously voiced as if it were Lisa. His ghost also makes an appearance at a parade, blending real American history with the show's surreal humor. Overall, he functions as a recurring visual gag and symbol of patriotic Americana rather than an active participant in the plot.

title: Calypso Self-Knowledge
text: Calypso Self-Knowledge is A minor character who attended the Blazing Guy festival and briefly interacted with Marge and Homer. Calypso Self-Knowledge is a mysterious, free-spirited woman encountered at the Blazing Guy festival. She has a calming, almost otherworldly presence, offering Marge a soothing tea when she seemed stressed. Her name itself hints at a New Age, festival-going persona, fitting for the eccentric crowd at Blazing Guy. Oddly, she possesses actual butterfly wings, which allow her to fly away after her brief exchange with Marge. These wings later become crucial when Homer takes them to rescue Bart from Jack Lassen, giving her a small but pivotal role in the episode's events. Beyond this appearance, little else is known about her background or life. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: "Does that look like something I'd do?"
quotes: "Does that look like something I'd do?"

title: Mrs. Scratchy
text: Mrs. Scratchy is Cartoon cat character; wife of Scratchy and mother of Scratchy, Jr. in the show-within-a-show The Itchy & Scratchy Show. Mrs. Scratchy is a minor cartoon character who exists within the fictional Itchy & Scratchy Show watched by the Simpsons family. She appears alongside her husband Scratchy and their son as part of the doomed Scratchy family unit. True to the violent slapstick nature of the cartoon, she is almost always brutally killed off by the sadistic mouse Itchy in whatever scenario she appears. For a long time her design and appearance were inconsistent across episodes until they were seemingly standardized in a later installment. Despite her recurring status, she has no formal name of her own and is simply identified through her relation to Scratchy. She has also made a cameo appearance in mobile game media outside the core show. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Robert Reich (character)
text: Robert Reich (character) is Real-world guest character; American professor, author, lawyer, and political commentator who appeared in a non-canon segment. Robert Reich appears as a version of himself in a musical segment of the show, lending his real-life expertise on economics and class issues to the story. He is depicted discussing the fading feasibility of the traditional 'American Dream' for ordinary people. In a whimsical touch typical of the show's guest cameos, he also dons a fireman's costume during the musical number. His appearance is brief and largely serves as a satirical, informative aside rather than a recurring plot element. As a non-canon character, he exists outside the main continuity of the Simpsons universe, appearing mainly for topical commentary and humor. Voiced by Himself.

title: Rosa Parks
text: Rosa Parks is Real-world historical figure referenced in the Simpsons universe. Rosa Parks appears in the show not as a fully realized character but as a reference to the real-life civil rights icon. She is depicted in a picture shown during a musical number performed by the Kneesock Dolls, appearing alongside other notable women. She is also mentioned in dialogue when Homer compares the treatment of celebrities to her legacy. Her presence in the show is brief and non-speaking, existing mainly as a nod to American history rather than a developed character. Interestingly, her name is also echoed in a minor joke involving Dr. Hibbert's poodle, Rosa Barks. Notable quotes: Well, then I guess I'll be riding the bus. | That's right. Like rock stars and Rosa Parks.
quotes: Well, then I guess I'll be riding the bus.
That's right. Like rock stars and Rosa Parks.

title: Mr. Pinchy
text: Mr. Pinchy is Homer Simpson's pet lobster, briefly featured in a season 10 episode. Mr. Pinchy was a lobster Homer originally bought from a grocery store intending to fatten up and eat, but he quickly grew fond of the creature and adopted him as a pet instead. Homer housed him first in a fish tank and later in an indoor wading pool, viewing him as an innocent little companion despite Marge's insistence that he was just an ordinary, vicious crustacean. The running joke centers on Homer's blind sentimentality toward an animal everyone else sees as unremarkable. Tragically, Pinchy's story ends in dark comic irony when Homer accidentally boils him alive after placing him in a hot bath to clean him off. The episode closes with a heartbroken Homer unknowingly eating his own pet at the dinner table. In non-canon material like The Simpsons: Tapped Out, Pinchy is resurrected as a cloned boss villain before being defeated and eaten by Homer once again.

title: Keith Richards (character)
text: Keith Richards (character) is Real-world musician (Rolling Stones guitarist) who appears as himself in guest episodes of The Simpsons. Keith Richards appears as a fictionalized version of himself, running a rock-and-roll fantasy camp alongside his bandmate Mick Jagger. He's portrayed as a laid-back, somewhat eccentric rock legend who takes camp administration seriously enough to teach a class on escaping via limousine. When Homer joins him onstage for a charity concert, things go awry and a fire breaks out, but Richards proves gracious enough to apologize afterward and even invites Homer to perform again. Outside of his main appearance, he's referenced through a look-alike in a music video and shows up in a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment as one of the bodies Homer considers taking over. His mundane final scene, putting up storm windows on his house, plays against his rock star image for comic effect. Voiced by Himself.

title: Angry Ricky
text: Angry Ricky is An intern at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. Angry Ricky is a lower-level intern working under Mr. Burns at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, whose name suggests a short temper and combative attitude. He's shown to be willing to carry out physical dirty work for Burns, once being sent to rough up Homer when the usual thugs weren't available. Ricky also has a mocking streak, needling Homer over his confusion during a plant safety exercise and getting the other interns to laugh along. He isn't universally respected, though, as fellow intern Mike Wegman quickly turns the joke back on him over his use of a stand-up desk. Ricky's behavior with coworkers Lenny and Carl even threatened his internship and course credit at one point, hinting he sometimes oversteps professional boundaries. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: James Patterson (character)
text: James Patterson (character) is Real-world author who appears as a non-canon character in Marge's dream and on a book cover. James Patterson is a fictionalized version of the real-life bestselling author who pops up in Marge Simpson's imagination and in the background of her reading material. In her dream, he's portrayed as a suave, slightly self-absorbed figure riding a horse on a beach, more interested in flirting with Marge than in literary craft. He asks her to help brainstorm nursery-rhyme-inspired titles for his thriller novels, poking fun at his real-world habit of prolific, formulaic book titling. The joke culminates in an innuendo-laden line that gets cut off by Marge's alarm clock, keeping the gag family-friendly. He later resurfaces indirectly when Marge is seen reading one of his novels in prison, with his face printed on the back cover. Overall, his role is a brief celebrity cameo used for a satirical jab at his novel-writing empire rather than a fleshed-out character. Voiced by James Patterson (Himself). Notable quotes: Marge, the real mystery is why we're still talking when I could be kissing your...
quotes: Marge, the real mystery is why we're still talking when I could be kissing your...

title: Lois Pennycandy
text: Lois Pennycandy is Executive assistant to Krusty the Clown. Lois Pennycandy is Krusty the Clown's devoted and long-suffering personal assistant, handling both his professional and emotional affairs. She has played a quiet but pivotal role in several key moments of Krusty's life, from encouraging him to reconcile with Bart to standing by him during his reunion with his estranged father. Her loyalty to Krusty borders on personal infatuation, as hinted by her wistful conversation with Marge about why people stay devoted to those who hurt them. She's shown to be a good sport in Springfield's quirkier social events, participating in a charity bachelor auction and a record-setting human pyramid attempt. Pennycandy is a clear parody of Miss Moneypenny from the James Bond franchise, both in her role as a devoted secretary and in her namesake nod to actress Lois Maxwell. Despite her minor role, she's a recurring fixture in Krusty-centric storylines throughout the series. Voiced by Pamela Hayden. Notable quotes: Oh, Mrs. Simpson, I've wasted my womanhood asking that same question
quotes: Oh, Mrs. Simpson, I've wasted my womanhood asking that same question

title: Miss Phipps
text: Miss Phipps is School nurse at Springfield Elementary School. Miss Phipps is one of the two nurses at Springfield Elementary, sharing duties with Lunchlady Dora. She's quick to diagnose students with exaggerated or made-up ailments, as shown when she took Bart's faked illness at face value and declared he had amoria phlebitis. Outside of the nurse's office, she socializes with the school's staff, having joined Principal Skinner, Edna Krabappel, Dr. Pryor, and Moe Szyslak for a game of hockey during a snow day. She also showed some solidarity with her coworkers by joining the teachers' strike organized by Mrs. Krabappel. Interestingly, her name has been inconsistent across appearances, being called Nurse Farrell in one episode and Miss Phipps in another, suggesting the writers weren't overly concerned with keeping her identity consistent. She remains a minor but recurring background character in the Springfield Elementary staff. Voiced by Russi Taylor.

title: Ms. Sinclair
text: Ms. Sinclair is Strict owner and operator of the Ayn Rand School for Tots, a daycare attended by Maggie Simpson. Ms. Sinclair is the stern proprietor of a daycare center built entirely around the philosophy of Ayn Rand, emphasizing self-reliance over comfort or coddling. She decorates her nursery with objectivist slogans and firmly bans pacifiers, believing infants should develop independence rather than rely on soothing objects. This rigid policy famously backfires when Maggie and the other babies orchestrate an elaborate escape to reclaim their pacifiers. She is the sister of theater director Llewellyn Sinclair, though the two seem to run in very different professional circles. In later appearances, she continues to oversee daycare operations with the same no-nonsense, ideology-driven approach. Non-canon material expands her role, tying her to a babysitting union owned by Mr. Burns and forcing her through babysitter retraining after that business collapses. Voiced by Jon Lovitz.

title: Big Rhonda
text: Big Rhonda is A minor child actress in the Simpsons universe, appearing only as a picture reference. Big Rhonda is a background child actress who exists mostly as a piece of Simpsons trivia rather than a fleshed-out character. She's known for starring alongside Lil' Vicki in the fictional film 'Little Vicki vs. Big Rhonda,' a title that plays on typical rivalry-themed movie tropes. She has no spoken lines in the show, appearing only in picture form during a brief reference. Her presence is largely a background gag tied to the world of child stardom that the show occasionally parodies. Little else is known about her personality or background, as she has not been given significant screen time or development.

title: Dr. Olberman
text: Dr. Olberman is A scientist working for Mr. Burns at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, appearing only in Simpsons comic book stories. Dr. Olberman is a non-canon comic-book character who serves as the resident mad-scientist figure at the Nuclear Power Plant. He is best known for inventing an experimental ray gun that was meant to reverse aging but instead grew or shrank whatever it touched, leading to several bizarre mishaps involving Homer. His inventions tend to spiral out of control, whether it's turning Homer into a giant, shrinking him to cure Mr. Burns' indigestion, or creating an addictive donut that left plant employees too obese to work. He's also been caught up in larger schemes involving Mr. Burns, including a giant robotic ant and stolen android duplicates of Burns and Smithers from his own lab. Despite the chaos his experiments cause, he continues working loyally for Burns across multiple comic stories, reflecting the recurring gag of unchecked, reckless science at the plant.

title: Dolly Parton (character)
text: Dolly Parton (character) is Real-life celebrity singer/actress who appears as herself in the Simpsons universe. Dolly Parton appears as a fictionalized version of herself within the Simpsons world, occasionally popping up in Springfield-related events. She's portrayed as a well-known and admired celebrity, being the object of Krusty the Clown's crush and a friend of Wally Kogen. Her fame is referenced through jokes, such as Bart Hope's comment about looking at her dress in heaven, and Mr. Burns dismissing another celebrity as being 'too Dollywood' in comparison to her. She even indirectly inspires a moment where Bart dresses baby Maggie up like her to entertain elderly guests. Parton's cultural presence is treated as universally recognized, with even elderly strangers assuming Bart might know her personally. Overall, she serves as a running pop-culture reference rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Herself.

title: Opal
text: Opal is Talk show host in Springfield, parody of a famous real-world media personality. Opal hosts her own talk show, aptly titled The Opal Show, which has become a fixture of Springfield's celebrity culture. She's clearly modeled after a real-world daytime television icon, right down to giving away extravagant gifts to her studio audience. A recurring bit involves her long-term, commitment-shy boyfriend Straightman, whose reluctance to propose becomes an amusing running joke whenever she's put on the spot about it. When cornered with awkward personal questions, she tends to deflect by showering her audience with prizes instead. Various Springfield residents, including members of the Simpson family, have appeared as guests on her show over the years. She's popular enough to show up in music videos alongside other Springfield celebrities and has become part of the town's broader media landscape. Voiced by Tress MacNeille, Dawnn Lewis.

title: Amber Simpson
text: Amber Simpson is Homer's accidental "Vegas wife" from a drunken marriage, later Grampa's wife. Amber was a cocktail waitress at Nero's Palace casino in Las Vegas who briefly became entangled with the Simpson family after a drunken wedding to Homer. She and her friend Ginger tracked down their husbands, Homer and Ned Flanders, and moved in with them, threatening to destabilize both marriages. Homer's attempt to have the marriage annulled failed since it was legally binding, forcing the family to scheme their way out of the situation. In a clever twist, the Simpsons tricked Amber into marrying Grampa instead, which legally nullified her marriage to Homer. She later appeared as a ghost in one of Bart's coma dreams, and it's implied she may have also worked at a rival casino. Her story ends tragically with a fatal overdose on a rollercoaster in a theme park, ignoring a posted safety warning. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Darryl Peyton
text: Darryl Peyton is Oboist in the Springfield Symphony Orchestra and husband of Bart's teacher Ms. Rayshelle Peyton. Darryl Peyton is a minor recurring character best known as the devoted husband of Bart's teacher, Rayshelle Peyton.
