He relocated to Springfield from Ghana after failing to make the cut for Ghana's own orchestra, eventually finding a spot playing oboe for the Springfield Symphony Orchestra. His storyline is mostly tied to his wife's arc, most notably a romantic moment where he brings her flowers just as Bart is about to confess a secret to her, complicating Bart's feelings for his teacher. He's shown supporting his wife at community events like a school project presentation and outings at the Springfield Mall. The couple's struggle to conceive a child is later revealed by Rayshelle to her class. As a non-speaking character, Darryl exists mostly in the background, defined by his loyalty to his wife and his musical profession.

title: Pa
text: Pa is Minor recurring elderly farmer character in Springfield. Pa is a background elderly farmer character who appears only briefly in a couple of episodes. He's depicted as part of a group of old-timers who experience a strange incident involving their eyes falling out, suggesting he's used for a bit of odd, cartoonish physical comedy typical of the show's treatment of minor senior characters. Later he appears alongside a character named Mother, where the two of them sense a tremor caused by a passing train. Pa doesn't have much individual characterization beyond his age and occupation as a farmer, functioning mainly as background flavor for rural or old-timer gags rather than a fleshed-out personality. He has no known relatives listed and no distinguishing quotes attributed to him. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Julia Roberts
text: Julia Roberts is Real-world actress referenced/appearing in a movie-within-the-show that Homer watches. Julia Roberts is depicted in the Simpsons universe as the famous actress she is in real life, appearing as a bride in the fictional film Love is Nice, which a newly intelligent Homer watches and critiques. She becomes the subject of a running joke about celebrity gossip and mistaken identity, as Homer, Dr. Hibbert, and the Sea Captain argue over who she'll end up marrying and mix up actors like Richard Gere, Bill Paxton, and Bill Pullman. She's later referenced in a news context when a reporter's boss claims to be covering her haircut instead of a natural disaster, poking fun at trivial celebrity news coverage. She's also listed among notable liberal celebrities on Ned Flanders' list. In non-canon material, she appears in a selfie-themed short and is mentioned as a hypothetical kissing target in a Groundskeeper Willie storyline.

title: Dr. Simpson
text: Dr. Simpson is A distant relative of Homer Simpson's, appearing as a successful doctor in the extended Simpson family. Dr. Simpson is a successful physician who serves as chief of complicated surgeries at an invasive care clinic, making her a rare example of accomplishment among the extended Simpson family. She is called upon by Homer during a moment of crisis, when he desperately searches for proof that not all Simpson men are doomed to intellectual decline. Her medical expertise proves useful in explaining the hereditary science behind the family's flaws, giving her a brief but meaningful role in clarifying the Simpson family's genetic quirks. She also appears in a family gathering, showing she maintains ties with relatives outside of Homer's immediate household. Though not a major recurring character, she represents the more capable, professional side of the sprawling Simpson family tree. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo
text: Cristiano Ronaldo is Non-canon celebrity cameo appearance; real-world Portuguese soccer player who appears in a Nike ad crossover. Cristiano Ronaldo appears as a non-canon, real-world cameo in The Simpsons universe, representing his actual identity as a famous Portuguese soccer star. In his brief appearance, he visits Homer at his home and kicks a soccer ball at him, prompting Homer's classic exclamation. The scene also references his signature on-field wink, a gesture he became known for during a real 2006 World Cup match against England. As a non-speaking character, his role is purely visual and comedic, relying on recognition of his real-life fame and mannerisms rather than dialogue. He exists outside the show's main continuity, appearing only in a promotional crossover context. Notable quotes: "Ronal", Cristiano Ronaldo
quotes: "Ronal", Cristiano Ronaldo

title: Portia
text: Portia is Environmental lawyer chosen by Homer and Marge to be the guardian of Bart, Lisa, and Maggie. Portia is a recurring character who works as an environmental lawyer. Along with her husband Mav, she was selected by Homer and Marge to serve as the potential guardian of their three children in case anything ever happened to them. Little is detailed about her personality in the show, as her main role centers around this guardianship arrangement. She is notable for being a minor but distinct addition to the extended cast of adults surrounding the Simpson family. Her introduction ties her closely to the theme of parental responsibility and planning for the unexpected. Voiced by Rashida Jones.

title: Grizzly Shawn
text: Grizzly Shawn is Recurring gay resident of Springfield, part of the LGBT community subplots in later seasons. Grizzly Shawn is a bald, openly gay Springfield local first seen frequenting Moe's bar, where he repeatedly tried and failed to woo an oblivious Moe. He pops up in various LGBT-themed storylines around town, from crashing a diaper-clad exit at Julio and Grady's apartment to using the dating app Grinder with a lumberjack-themed profile picture. He's sociable and eager to help friends, once attending a party at the Simpson house specifically to find Waylon Smithers a boyfriend. His biggest claim to fame is marrying a man named Barry and the two competing on and winning the reality show The Amazing Place. He also gets swept up in one of Marge's schemes, mistakenly believing she's a drag queen during a Tupperware party. Overall he serves as a recurring background character used for comic bits tied to Springfield's gay community. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Ms. Pac-Man
text: Ms. Pac-Man is Arcade game character who appears as the wife of Pac-Man in Simpsons universe references. Ms. Pac-Man is a crossover video game character referenced a handful of times throughout the show, tied to her fictional marriage to Pac-Man. She first appears as a game Mr. Burns is playing in his office, showing up as a background gag rather than an active character. Later episodes build on the joke of her marriage, including a mock news broadcast covering her wedding to Pac-Man, complete with the ghosts dancing along. Marge even credits her with striking a blow for women's rights back in 1983, treating the arcade character as a minor pop-culture icon. She's non-speaking and exists purely as a nostalgic nod to classic gaming culture rather than a true character with personality or dialogue.

title: Mr. Roman
text: Mr. Roman is A minor recurring character; a ghostwriter hired by Mr. Burns to write his life story. Mr. Roman is a professional ghostwriter with a reputation as one of the best in his field, recommended by Smithers to help Mr. Burns tell the tale of his blood transfusion ordeal. He has a distinctive shock of green hair and a knack for turning real events into published books. His working relationship with Burns sours quickly once he starts pushing for embellishments or inappropriate content that Burns finds unacceptable, leading to his dismissal from the project. Despite this brief and rocky gig, he's apparently a prolific author, credited with several oddly titled novels. He later shows up again with a minor injury, receiving treatment at Springfield General Hospital. Overall, he's a peripheral figure whose main claim to fame in Springfield lore is his short, contentious stint ghostwriting for one of the town's most powerful men. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: The Rolling Stones
text: The Rolling Stones is Real-world English rock band that appears/is referenced as a musical group within the Simpsons universe. The Rolling Stones are depicted as a famous rock band whose members Mick Jagger and Keith Richards occasionally interact with the citizens of Springfield. In one storyline, Mr. Burns mistakenly orders their assassination after confusing them with another band that insulted him at his birthday party. Jagger and Richards later run a rock star camp attended by several Springfield residents. The band is also tied to Homer and Marge's nostalgic memories, having been the act at the first concert they attended together back in 1989. They're referenced humorously elsewhere, such as being mocked for their name by a talking Krusty Doll. In non-canon material, the band is shown still touring decades later under a joke name playing on their age, and even appear as a possible body option in a body-swapping Halloween segment. Notable quotes: Where do kids today get these band names? The Kinks? The Stones? Sounds like my last physical.
quotes: Where do kids today get these band names? The Kinks? The Stones? Sounds like my last physical.

title: Long John Silver
text: Long John Silver is Fictional pirate character from Robert Louis Stevenson's Treasure Island, referenced within The Simpsons. Long John Silver isn't a Simpsons original character but a literary pirate from Treasure Island who gets referenced in the show, particularly tied to Bart's chronic inability to do his schoolwork. He appears as a picture on the book's cover when Bart is supposed to give a book report but hasn't actually read it. Bart's ignorance of the character becomes a running joke, even carrying into a fantasy sequence about his future where his own son knows the answer he doesn't. The character also gets a silly pun treatment when Lisa disguises herself as "Long John Seltzer" during one of Krusty's sketches. Overall, Silver functions less as a character in his own right within the show and more as a recurring literary reference and punchline. Notable quotes: Pirates with green birds on their shoulders and shiny gold teeth
quotes: Pirates with green birds on their shoulders and shiny gold teeth

title: Mr. Roarke
text: Mr. Roarke is Fictional TV character from Fantasy Island who appears within the Simpsons universe (crossover character). Mr. Roarke is not an original Simpsons character but a reference to the host of the television series Fantasy Island, originally portrayed by Ricardo Montalbán. Within the show, he exists only as a figure seen on TV or imagined by other characters, never appearing as a fully developed presence. He is a non-speaking character, underscoring his role as background pop-culture flavor rather than a participant in the plot. His appearances tie into Homer's fondness for television and the show's habit of referencing classic pop culture. He also shows up during a surreal hallucination sequence, further cementing his role as a whimsical, dreamlike crossover figure rather than a grounded Simpsons character. Overall, Mr. Roarke serves as a nostalgic nod for viewers familiar with 1970s-80s television.

title: Rowena
text: Rowena is A minor recurring character who serves as a contest judge, unrelated to the main Simpson family. Rowena is a professional skin-care consultant who occasionally appears as a contest judge in Springfield. She notably served on the judging panel for the Patriots of Tomorrow essay contest sponsored by Reading Digest, an event Lisa Simpson entered. She later reappears as one of the judges for the Miss American Girl pageant, which the Simpson family watches on television. Rowena is a background figure with no dialogue, existing mostly as a visual presence rather than a developed personality. Interestingly, her design bears a resemblance to an unnamed executive character from the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, suggesting reused animation models. She also makes a brief cameo appearance in a later episode, cementing her status as a recurring but minor face in the show's expansive universe.

title: William Shatner
text: William Shatner is Real-world actor/musician (Star Trek's Captain Kirk) who appears as a celebrity character in Springfield. William Shatner is depicted as a fictionalized version of the real Canadian actor and musician famous for playing Captain Kirk in Star Trek. He's portrayed as a minor celebrity figure in Springfield's world, cited by Lisa as one of many Jewish entertainers despite the show's real-world Shatner not necessarily fitting that trait for the joke. He auditions unsuccessfully for the role of Mr. Burns in a fictional biopic, showing the show's love of poking fun at Hollywood casting quirks. Shatner is also mocked for his questionable music career, releasing a cover song and other albums that other characters find irritating enough to want stopped by any means, including a non-canon joke involving a phaser. His fame is used as a running gag reference point, appearing in stage productions, geography jokes about Canada, and pop-culture asides rather than as a fully fleshed-out recurring character. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Judith Underdunk
text: Judith Underdunk is Wife of Dr. Robert Terwilliger Sr. and mother of Sideshow Bob and Cecil Terwilliger. Judith Underdunk is a retired, highly acclaimed Shakespearean stage actress who carries herself with the dignified air of British nobility, fitting her honorary title of Dame. She bears a strong family resemblance to her son Sideshow Bob, right down to a gray-haired version of his distinctive hairstyle. Fiercely loyal to her family, she appears at Sideshow Bob's murder trial to support him during his darkest hour. Her prestigious acting career is well-regarded even by Springfield residents, with Lisa Simpson citing her as the greatest classical actress of her generation. She shows genuine maternal grief, breaking down in tears when she believes her son has died. Beyond the main show, she also appears as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Springfield Nuclear Power Plant employee (Some Enchanted Evening)
keys: springfield nuclear power plant employee (some enchanted evening)
text: Springfield Nuclear Power Plant employee (Some Enchanted Evening) is Minor background employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, working in Sector 7G alongside Homer Simpson. This nameless plant worker is one of Homer's colleagues in Sector 7G, appearing briefly in the show's first season. He initially comes across as a workplace acquaintance or even friend to Homer, but his loyalty proves shallow. When Marge unwittingly insults Homer by calling him a pig during a radio broadcast, this coworker finds the moment amusing rather than sympathetic, laughing at Homer's expense. His fleeting appearances place him among the many faceless plant employees who populate the background of Homer's work life. He has no defining personality traits beyond this single moment of mockery, making him a minor footnote in the power plant's cast of characters. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Terence
text: Terence is Minor character; an employee at Springfield City Zoo who works as hired muscle. Terence is a blond-haired zoo worker who appears in only one episode of the show. He serves as muscle for the unscrupulous zoo owner Larry Kidkill, alongside his partner Christopher. His main function in the story is to physically enforce Kidkill's business dealings, including confronting the Simpson and Nahasapeemapetilon families. He has no lines of dialogue, making him a background enforcer rather than a fleshed-out character. Terence's role highlights the shady, exploitative nature of the zoo's management during the octuplet storyline. Outside the show itself, he also appears in a mobile game tie-in performing a similar henchman-type task for Kidkill.

title: Lucy Van Pelt
text: Lucy Van Pelt is Crossover character from Peanuts who appears in The Simpsons via hallucination and Halloween costume references. Lucy Van Pelt is borrowed from the classic Peanuts comic strip and pops up in The Simpsons as a nod to that beloved franchise rather than as an original creation. She's best known for her cranky, bossy demeanor, famously earning the nickname 'fussbudget' from her fellow Peanuts characters. In one Simpsons episode, Homer hallucinates himself as Lucy after taking a strange drug, pulling a football away from Ned (playing Charlie Brown) in a classic gag from the source material. Her likeness even inspired a Junior Camper merit badge called 'Fussbudgeting,' complete with her signature outraged expression. In a non-canon Halloween special, Lisa dresses up as Lucy while Bart takes on the role of Charlie Brown. She never actually speaks in these Simpsons appearances, existing purely as a visual or conceptual reference rather than a fleshed-out character.

title: Sungazer
text: Sungazer is A fictional 1980s hard rock band that recruits Apu Nahasapeemapetilon as its lead singer. Sungazer is a once-famous hard rock band whose glory days trace back to the 1980s, best known for their hit song "Hopin' for a Dream." After the tragic death of their original singer Grant LeDavid from erotic asphyxiation, the band finds themselves in need of a new frontman. They discover Apu among the crowd during a Covercraft performance and pressure him into joining for what turns out to be a grueling three-year tour, revealing the band's more manipulative side beneath their rock star image. Ironically, karma catches up with the band when they all fall ill from food poisoning after eating tainted hot dogs from the Kwik-E-Mart—except for Apu, who is spared. The group's lineup includes Freddy Freeman, Shredder Stevens, Nick Delacourt, and Peter D'Abbruzio. In a bit of non-canon trivia, even the sinister cult leader of the Movementarians is revealed to be a secret fan, wearing a Sungazer t-shirt under his robes.

title: Martha Stewart (character)
text: Martha Stewart (character) is Real-life celebrity guest character appearing in dream sequences and cameos in The Simpsons. Martha Stewart appears as a fantastical, almost magical version of her real-world persona within the Simpsons universe. In one memorable dream sequence, she responds to a letter from Marge by transforming the Simpson household into an elaborate, over-the-top holiday display, complete with homemade furniture, spray-painted snowflakes, and family members turned into living decorations. She's portrayed as having an almost supernatural level of domestic skill, able to conjure changes with a wave of her wand, though her efforts ultimately clash with what Marge actually wants for her family. Outside of this fantasy element, she is referenced as a cultural touchstone for perfectionist homemaking, with Marge being compared favorably to her (minus any implied "evil"). She also shows up in smaller cameo capacities, such as an image used in an online chess captcha test. In non-canon material, she's depicted attending Simpsons-related events and being read about in hellish demon magazines, reinforcing her status as an instantly recognizable real-world icon within the show's satirical universe. Voiced by Herself.

title: Springfield's oldest man
text: Springfield's oldest man is Minor recurring background character known for being the oldest man in Springfield. This unnamed elderly resident of Springfield holds the distinction of being the town's oldest living man. He gained a small moment of local fame when he was featured on the news program Eye on Springfield, appearing alongside Springfield's fattest man. He is a non-speaking character who mostly appears in crowd scenes, such as being present in the town square during Otto Mann's infamous school bus crash. There's some ambiguity about his fate, as it's suggested he may have died before Cornelius Chapman later received the town's oldest man award at the Springfield Pride Awards. Despite his minimal screen time, he represents the show's tendency to create quirky, hyper-specific local celebrities and titles for background characters.

title: Truckasaurus
text: Truckasaurus is A giant mechanical car-crushing truck/dinosaur robot that appears at demolition-style events in Springfield. Truckasaurus is a massive, fire-breathing robotic hybrid of a truck and a dinosaur, built by an inventor named Leo G. Clark and later reimagined by Professor Frink in one continuity. Standing four stories tall and weighing twenty tons, it exists purely to smash and crunch cars for crowds of spectators, embodying over-the-top demolition-derby spectacle rather than any real personality. It poses a genuine danger to onlookers, having once nearly crushed the Simpson family's car with them inside. The robot has appeared under different names and voices across the show's continuity, including a movie version dubbed by a famous actor, and has spawned a short-lived sequel machine that was destroyed almost instantly. It's also been merchandised as a toy and reworked in video games, cementing its status as a recurring piece of Simpsons pop-culture background lore. Ultimately, Truckasaurus is less a character with feelings and more a running gag about spectacle, danger, and over-engineered entertainment gone wrong.

title: Train engineer
text: Train engineer is Minor recurring background character who operates a train in Springfield. The train engineer is a minor character seen driving a train through Springfield on at least two occasions. He's shown to be somewhat easily flustered, as in one instance he crashed his train into a ship after being distracted by the chaos surrounding Homer's kidnapping, then dashed off mid-journey just to buy a camera battery before resuming his route. Despite these mishaps, he takes his job seriously, later complaining that the track manufacturers should have made the rails resistant to Homer's earthquake-inducing catchphrase. He doesn't have much personality development beyond these brief comedic appearances, functioning mainly as a background gag character. His scenes tend to highlight the absurd, disaster-prone nature of Springfield's infrastructure rather than his own traits. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Harry S. Truman
text: Harry S. Truman is Historical U.S. President appearing in cameo/historical references in The Simpsons. Harry S. Truman is depicted in the show as the real-world 33rd President of the United States, referenced in a few episodes for historical flavor or comedic effect. He is shown printing a one trillion-dollar bill intended for post-war European reconstruction, which famously never reaches its destination due to Mr. Burns' interference. Truman also appears in a documentary Lisa and Homer watch, tying into a bet about the 1948 presidential election. His likeness later shows up as an animatronic figure and even replaces Thomas Jefferson on an altered Mount Rushmore in a non-canon appearance. He's also listed among notable historical liberal figures on a satirical list. Overall, Truman functions more as a historical prop for jokes about American politics and Europe's grudges than as a fleshed-out character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Three-eyed crow
text: Three-eyed crow is A recurring background animal/mutated crow that frequently appears in the show's title screen gags. The three-eyed crow is a minor recurring visual gag rather than a speaking character, first appearing in the title screen for "Take My Life, Please." Its extra eye is presumed to be a mutation similar to Blinky the three-eyed fish, hinting that it too may have been affected by radiation from the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. The crow can often be heard cawing during wide establishing shots of the power plant, reinforcing this connection. Over the years it became one of the most frequently used title card images, even being the sole title screen gag throughout an entire season. It has been depicted in a variety of humorous scenarios, such as carrying a rat, clutching Blinky, getting snatched by King Homer, flying past Martin Prince, being struck by lightning, and even appearing pixelated. Despite having no dialogue or defined personality, it has become a beloved piece of recurring visual trivia for attentive fans.

title: Unnamed news reporter
text: Unnamed news reporter is A minor recurring news reporter appearing in early episodes of the show. This nameless reporter is a background media figure used to deliver news updates within the show's fictional world. He first appears covering the frenzy around a supposed Bigfoot sighting, later reporting on how that mystery is resolved. He resurfaces covering a more scandalous story, interviewing Krusty the Clown after his arrest for armed robbery. He has no defined personality traits beyond his professional role as a newsman, existing mainly as a narrative device to relay information to the town and viewers. With gray hair and no other distinguishing features, he blends into the world of Springfield's local news media. His appearances are brief and functional rather than comedic or character-driven. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Doris Troy
text: Doris Troy is Minor recurring character; clerk at Shotgun Pete's 24-Hour Wedding Chapel where Homer and Marge got married. Doris Troy works behind the counter at Shotgun Pete's 24-Hour Wedding Chapel, handling the paperwork and logistics for the establishment's quickie weddings. She's the one who processed Homer and Marge's marriage license, even offering them a loyalty punch card for repeat business, a joke about how disposable the chapel's ceremonies are treated. She finds Homer's earnest declaration that his marriage would last forever amusing, hinting at a cynical, world-weary attitude from having seen countless hasty weddings. Beyond her clerical duties, she doubles as the chapel's musician, playing the wedding march on a synthesizer for couples too impatient to arrange a real procession. She's a background fixture of the franchise's world rather than a fully developed character, appearing mostly in flashback and reference. Voiced by Doris Grau.

title: John Steed
text: John Steed is A fictional British secret agent who appears as part of a British invasion storyline in a Simpsons comic. John Steed is a crossover character based on the classic British spy from the television series The Avengers, portrayed by Patrick Macnee. In his Simpsons appearance, he shows up as part of a British invasion of Springfield, which occurs after Lisa's meddling with the constitution leads to a ban on guns and Springfield falling under British rule. He takes part in the occupying force alongside other British characters during the town's brief transformation into a British city. The storyline plays on culture-clash humor, including the British throwing hot chips as a form of retaliation during the New Revolutionary War. Steed himself is more of a background figure representing the British occupation rather than a character with distinct personal traits explored in the story. His inclusion is a nod to British pop culture and secret agent tropes rather than an original Simpsons creation. Voiced by Chris Edgerly.

title: Ivanka Trump
text: Ivanka Trump is Non-canon real-world character; daughter of Donald Trump who appears in Simpsons specials. Ivanka Trump is depicted in the show as a non-canon, real-world figure tied to satirical Simpsons specials lampooning her father's presidency. She's referenced as one of Donald Trump's smartphone contacts and later shown taking on an oddly powerful role, replacing Ruth Bader Ginsburg as Supreme Justice while flaunting a robe and cheap, Russian-sourced jewelry. A future gag shows Homer wearing a badge supporting an imagined 'Ivanka 2028' political campaign, poking fun at dynastic political ambitions. Another appearance hints at strain in her marriage to Jared Kushner, with a newspaper suggesting he'd lost access to her. Overall, she functions less as a fleshed-out character and more as a satirical prop used to mock real-world politics and the Trump family's public image.

title: Thelonious
text: Thelonious is A student at West Springfield Elementary School whom Lisa briefly meets. Thelonious is a young student who appears at a rival elementary school in Springfield. He crosses paths with Lisa Simpson only because of a bizarre chain of mishaps involving a missing bike, Homer's severed thumb, and a mistaken ride from Krusty the Clown's chauffeur. Despite the brief encounter, he and Lisa instantly bond over feeling like outsiders with no real friends, sharing a dance together before she has to rush off. Their connection is fleeting but memorable enough that Lisa later categorizes him as a kindred spirit type in her own personal taxonomy of elementary school archetypes. He never appears again after this one encounter, making him a minor but emotionally significant one-off character in Lisa's life. Voiced by Frankie Muniz.

title: Queen Victoria
text: Queen Victoria is Historical British monarch referenced/appearing in Simpsons media. Queen Victoria is depicted in the Simpsons universe as a real historical figure rather than a regular cast member, referenced across episodes, comics, and games. She's shown appearing on book covers, in pictures, and even a snowglobe, often as a background nod to her historical significance. One recurring gag ties her to a list of famous left-handed people compiled by Ned Flanders. Her appearances are largely non-speaking cameos or mentions, emphasizing her role as a cultural icon rather than an active character in the show's plot. A non-canon appearance in a video game adds a cheeky, irreverent joke about her royal image. Overall, she serves as a brief historical easter egg rather than a developed character.

title: Jean-Claude Van Damme
text: Jean-Claude Van Damme is Real-world Belgian martial artist and actor referenced/appearing in the Simpsons universe. Jean-Claude Van Damme appears in the Simpsons universe as a version of his real-life self, known for his martial arts prowess. He's cited by Bart as an example of a top-tier action star alongside Schwarzenegger and Stallone, showing his status as a pop-culture action icon. In one appearance, he participates in a reality-style show called Celebrity Bear Fights, taking on bears in physical combat. In a non-canon Belgian comic parody, he has a lighthearted encounter involving waffles, a collapsing porch, and an awkward flirtation. He's mostly a background pop-culture reference rather than a fleshed-out recurring character, often used for comedic cameo purposes.

title: Adam West (character)
text: Adam West (character) is Real-life actor famous for playing Batman, appearing as himself in guest spots on The Simpsons. Adam West appears as a fictionalized version of himself, best known in-universe for his role as Batman in the 1960s TV series. He briefly gets involved in Springfield life when he helps Homer with his snow plowing business, eventually handing the enterprise over to Barney once he surpasses Homer's skills. His fame as Batman is referenced multiple times, including when Bart and Milhouse watch old Batman episodes and later imitate a stunt from the show. He's treated as a nostalgic pop-culture icon, cropping up in photos, comic book references, and offhand mentions around town. In a non-canon crossover appearance, a version of him even shows up as the mayor of Quahog, mingling with Mayor Quimby. Overall, he's a lighthearted celebrity cameo character rather than a fully developed personality within the show. Voiced by Adam West / Hank Azaria.

title: Yoda parody
text: Yoda parody is A minor character appearing within the fictional in-universe film "Cosmic Wars: The Gathering Shadow", parodying Star Wars' Yoda. This character is a purple-colored spoof of the iconic Star Wars figure Yoda, existing only within the movie-within-the-show "Cosmic Wars: The Gathering Shadow." His main function in the plot is presiding over a galactic senate scene, where he formally closes a session. He then undercuts his own authority by second-guessing his ruling right after making it, playing on Yoda's distinctive inverted speech pattern for comedic effect. The joke relies on the audience's familiarity with the real Yoda's calm, wise demeanor, subverted here by sudden indecision. He has no independent role outside this parody film appearance. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: The decision is final. Tabled, this motion is. Or is it?
quotes: The decision is final. Tabled, this motion is. Or is it?

title: Dr. Thurston
text: Dr. Thurston is A child and animal psychiatrist who occasionally treats members of the Simpson family. Dr. Thurston is a psychiatrist in Springfield who specializes in treating both children and animals. She first appears when Bart is brought to her office after becoming despondent over the loss of a pet bird, using Santa's Little Helper's destructive behavior in her office as evidence to reach her professional conclusion. In non-canon material, she is shown handling stranger cases, such as counseling a bickering Bart and Lisa after a bizarre body-swapping incident, encouraging them to resolve conflict through simple compliments. She also appears as a medical professional overseeing Homer's care during a coma in an alternate continuity. Across her appearances, she comes across as calm, procedural, and no-nonsense, unfazed by the chaos and absurdity often surrounding the Simpson family. Her role is largely functional, providing exposition or resolution during emotionally or physically strange predicaments involving the family. Voiced by Rachel Weisz, Tress MacNeille.

title: Yendor
text: Yendor is One of The Happy Little Elves, a fictional children's show character within the Simpsons universe. Yendor is one of the three main characters from the fictional cartoon show The Happy Little Elves, which airs within the world of The Simpsons. He appears alongside fellow elves Bubbles and Cheery as part of this show-within-a-show that Lisa and other characters watch. Yendor's main claim to fame in the Simpson household is as a piece of merchandise, most often appearing as a doll on Lisa's bookshelf rather than through direct dialogue or action. His presence recurs mostly through background appearances, pictures, and toy versions rather than substantial on-screen plot involvement. Despite this limited direct characterization, Yendor has become a persistent visual gag, popping up in dozens of episodes across many seasons as a nod to the merchandising of children's entertainment. Voiced by June Foray.

title: Vitruvian Man
text: Vitruvian Man is An animated parody of Leonardo da Vinci's famous drawing, appearing as a living character in Homer's dream and in Lisa's imagined storybook. The Vitruvian Man is a surreal, fourth-wall-breaking take on the iconic anatomical sketch, brought to life first as a nightmarish figure attacking Homer and later as a mischievous character imagined by Lisa (as "Lisanardo da Vinci") in one of her fantasy sequences. In this second appearance he acts as a sinister advisor, urging Lisa to violently punish anyone who angers her and to channel her intelligence into inventing weapons of war. He also has a comedic, whimsical side, boasting that he intends to invent the Charleston dance and breaking into a jig. His antics are cut short when Lisa slams her book shut on him, painfully trapping his limbs. Beyond these appearances, the character serves as a recurring visual gag, having been parodied multiple times throughout the series' run. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Smothers Brothers (characters)
text: Smothers Brothers (characters) is A minor band appearing in a Bart dream sequence and a comic story, based on the real-life comedy duo. The Smothers Brothers are a fictional variety act appearing in The Simpsons, modeled after the real-life comedic duo Tom and Dick Smothers. They first appear performing a song within one of Bart's dreams, where their playful bickering over being fired leads to a chaotic yo-yo mishap that brings down the Wright Flyer. In another story, they get mistakenly targeted by Homer and Mr. Burns, who believe them to be brothers worth fighting, only to be soundly beaten before heading into the Springfield Music Hall. Their humor largely stems from sibling-style bantering and slapstick mishaps rather than deep characterization. As a guest-star voiced act, they exist mostly as a novelty cameo rather than recurring cast members.

title: Yale man
text: Yale man is Minor recurring character; a Yale University administrator who occasionally appears in Springfield. The Yale man is a minor recurring figure representing Yale University's administration, first appearing when Mr. Burns tries to secure his son Larry's admission. He's portrayed as a somewhat stuffy academic official who gets mocked for his weight by Larry Burns during their meeting. Despite being brushed off by Mr. Burns when the school seeks a donation, he later turns up in unexpected, comedic contexts around Springfield, such as dancing outside a theater. He also serves a civic function in the town, appearing as a juror in both a real courtroom case and an elaborate prank trial designed to fool Homer and Bart. Overall, he functions as a background gag character tied to the recurring Yale University joke in the series. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Tessa Rose
text: Tessa Rose is A member of Addy's clique and a minor antagonist to Lisa Simpson. Tessa Rose is one of the stuck-up girls who rides in Addy's social circle, known primarily as a self-proclaimed beauty icon. She and her friends Bella-Ella and Sloan initially come across as cliquey and cold toward outsiders like Lisa. Their treatment of Lisa escalates from mockery into outright cruelty, including stealing her phone and posting humiliating videos online during a sleepover. When Lisa retaliates with a prank involving horse hoof hardener, Tessa Rose's hair breaks off, fueling her anger and a horseback chase after Lisa and Bart. Ultimately, she and her friends have a change of heart after witnessing Addy's mean streak, deciding they actually want to befriend her. She later reappears simply as a background attendee at a Kneesock Dolls concert. Voiced by Camila Mendes.

title: Tiana
text: Tiana is Crossover Disney princess character appearing in non-canon Simpsons specials. Tiana is a guest character brought into the Simpsons universe from Disney's The Princess and the Frog as part of various crossover specials. She appears in non-speaking cameo roles, often alongside other Disney princesses, highlighting the show's tendency to mix in outside franchises for anniversary and holiday specials. Her appearances include attending a party at Moe's Tavern and being depicted as a statue at a princess-themed castle Lisa visits. She's also shown spending time with her mother Eudora during a family-oriented outing to a Disney-themed park. In one special, she's involved in a comedic mix-up where a frog she kisses unexpectedly transforms into an unrelated character. Overall, she serves as a light novelty reference rather than a fully developed personality within the show.

title: Heather Spuckler
text: Heather Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children, a minor recurring background character. Heather Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of the backwoods Spuckler family, rarely given individual attention beyond being one of the many kids Cletus and Brandine keep track of. She's been present during family moments, such as when Cletus invited his children to a pretzel-fueled dinner and when Brandine rallied the kids to sing in an effort to win Cletus back home. Musically inclined in her own small way, Heather contributes to the family's makeshift ensemble by playing the rainstick in the Spuckler Family Band. Like most of her siblings, she is a non-speaking character who exists mostly as background filler for jokes about the Spucklers' chaotic, oversized household. She has no distinct personality traits highlighted in the show, serving instead as one face among the sprawling brood.

title: Birthday Spuckler
text: Birthday Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children, a minor recurring member of the Spuckler clan. Birthday Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, identifiable by the potato sack he wears in place of proper clothing. Like his siblings, he received tutoring from Lisa Simpson, which led to an odd brush with fame when Krusty overheard the children singing and recruited them for his show. His time in showbiz was short-lived, as his mother put a stop to the family's planned appearance on Krusty's comedy tour. Musically inclined despite his rough upbringing, Birthday plays kazoo alongside fellow Spuckler kids Jitney, Taylor, and Cody as part of the so-called Fabulous Skunk Holler Horn Section. He's also been shown attending family outings like the Springfield Demolition Derby, reflecting the Spucklers' close-knit, backwoods lifestyle. Overall, he serves as background color for the show's recurring jokes about the sprawling, impoverished Spuckler family. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Strawberry
text: Strawberry is Wife of Milo, owner of Coolsville Comics & Toys, and minor recurring Springfield resident. Strawberry is a minor character best known as the girlfriend, and later wife, of comic shop owner Milo. She first appears when Comic Book Guy tries to use her relationship with Milo as ammunition to discredit him as a true comic fan, though the scheme fails to win back customers for The Android's Dungeon. Over time she and Milo's relationship deepens, culminating in marriage and a child, and the couple remain on friendly terms with Comic Book Guy despite his earlier jabs. She's depicted as somewhat quirky, notably carrying a Malibu Stacy lunchbox as a purse, but is otherwise warm and easygoing with everyone she meets, including her husband's customers. She's made a handful of background appearances over the years, including a surreal cameo among Ned Flanders' deceased wives in one of Bart's coma dreams. Strawberry also appears as a character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Voiced by Maggie Roswell. Notable quotes: This man is not one of us! He has a girlfriend!
quotes: This man is not one of us! He has a girlfriend!

title: Worker
text: Worker is Fictional cartoon cat character within the show, part of a parody cartoon-within-the-show on The Simpsons. Worker is a cartoon cat who stars alongside his partner Parasite in a bizarre Eastern European cat-and-mouse cartoon that Krusty the Clown airs after losing the rights to Itchy and Scratchy. Unlike traditional cartoon rivals, Worker doesn't really do much of anything meaningful in his own show—he simply bounces around aimlessly to the background music. The cartoon itself is presented as a strange, low-budget substitute that audiences find baffling compared to the violent slapstick of Itchy and Scratchy. Worker's simplicity and lack of any real characterization is part of the joke, poking fun at foreign or oddly translated animation. The character has made minor appearances beyond his debut, including as a costume seen at a fan convention. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Jason Voorhees
text: Jason Voorhees is Crossover horror-movie villain from the Friday the 13th franchise who appears as a background antagonist in Simpsons Halloween/horror-themed episodes. Jason Voorhees is the mute, hockey-masked killer borrowed from the Friday the 13th film series who pops up repeatedly in The Simpsons' horror-parody segments. He's typically shown as one of several classic monsters and slashers lumped together, alongside figures like Pinhead, Dracula, the Mummy, the Wolfman, and Freddy Krueger. In one Bart daydream he menaces the boy before being thwarted by a RoboCop-styled Santa's Little Helper. In the non-canon Treehouse of Horror universe, he's unleashed from Homer's cellar as part of a demonic horde, and later waits on a couch with Freddy Krueger for the Simpson family. He even gets a bizarrely tame cameo as a church choir singer in a re-edited, family-friendly parody film shown at the Flanders house. True to his source material, he never speaks, existing purely as a visual gag and horror reference rather than a fleshed-out character.

title: Luke Skywalker
text: Luke Skywalker is Star Wars character referenced and parodied throughout The Simpsons; a crossover figure rather than a core cast member. Luke Skywalker exists in the Simpsons universe purely as a piece of pop culture from the Star Wars franchise, referenced through merchandise, costumes, and pop-culture gags rather than as an active character. Mark Hamill, who played Luke in the original trilogy, has appeared in the show dressed as the character. The show frequently jokes about the famous twist involving his father, Darth Vader, including Homer spoiling the reveal for a line of moviegoers. Darth Vader even makes a surreal cameo interrupting a heavenly conversation between Lisa and Bleeding Gums Murphy to deliver the iconic line about being Luke's father. Various characters, including Comic Book Guy, Reverend and Helen Lovejoy, and Scratchy from Itchy & Scratchy, reference Luke through costumes, action figures, or statues. He also appears in non-canon material like Star Wars-themed episodes and comics, cementing his status as a recurring cultural touchstone rather than a true Simpsons character.

title: Stan (salesman)
text: Stan (salesman) is A recurring car sales manager who appears at various dealerships in Springfield. Stan is a slick, dishonest car salesman who pops up at different dealerships throughout the series, always ready to squeeze extra money out of customers. He first appears selling Homer a Canyonero along with a pile of unnecessary add-ons, showing his knack for upselling. Later, he tries to overcharge Marge once he realizes she's shopping alone, and he lies repeatedly about his job title and personal life to manipulate her sympathy. His lies are comically exposed when Marge points out his own Facebook page contradicts his sob story about having children. He even claims to own two Yorkies in a further attempt to seem relatable and trustworthy. His storyline pokes fun at pushy sales tactics and the way salespeople exploit personal information for profit. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: the dealership websites are taking food out of his children's mouthes
quotes: the dealership websites are taking food out of his children's mouthes

title: Stacey Swanson
text: Stacey Swanson is Child psychologist who treats Bart Simpson for his behavioral issues. Dr. Stacey Swanson is a Ph.D.-holding child psychologist who takes on Bart as a patient after he causes trouble at school with a scary story about Dark Stanley. She initially wins Bart over by playing a video game with him, and the two form a genuine bond over several sessions as she helps him open up about his problems. When their sessions end, Bart becomes fixated on her and starts following her around town, unable to let go of their connection. It's later revealed she has her own hidden trauma, having lost a son who was killed by Dark Stanley, which may explain why she became so attached to Bart. She struggles to confront this painful connection when questioned by another psychologist, showing a more vulnerable and fearful side beneath her professional exterior. Voiced by Meg Ryan.

title: Dr. Smith
text: Dr. Smith is A fictional character from the show-within-a-show "Lost in Space", appearing in Marge's dream and at a fan convention in Springfield. Dr. Smith is a parody of the classic sci-fi character from Lost in Space, appearing in two separate contexts within The Simpsons universe. In one instance, he shows up in a shared dream Marge and Homer have, where Homer plays the grumbling, put-upon Smith complaining about being stranded on a desolate planet. He has a testy, sarcastic relationship with his robotic companion, Robot B-9, often hurling insults at it when annoyed. In another appearance, an actor portraying Dr. Smith works a booth at the Bi-Mon-Sci-Fi-Con, delivering dramatic, over-the-top lines when questioned by a skeptical Bart. This actor is easily offended when fans don't recognize his authenticity, especially when compared to the movie version of the character. Overall, Dr. Smith serves as a comedic nod to classic television nostalgia and fandom culture within the show. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "why, you clattering clank of cogs" | "Oh, the pain, the pain ... the pain of it all!" | "Silence, you nickel-plated nitwit!"
quotes: "why, you clattering clank of cogs"
"Oh, the pain, the pain ... the pain of it all!"
"Silence, you nickel-plated nitwit!"

title: Mrs. Smithers
text: Mrs. Smithers is Mother of Waylon Smithers, Jr., a minor recurring character in the Simpsons universe. Mrs. Smithers is the elderly mother of Mr. Burns' loyal assistant, Waylon Smithers, Jr. She is 81 years old, with gray hair, and is a widow following the death of her husband, Waylon Smithers, Sr. Her presence in her son's life is a source of mild comedic tension, as she makes requests of him that clearly cause him discomfort, such as asking him to visit a certain risqué establishment. She is largely a background figure, mentioned more often than actually seen, and does not speak in her appearances. Despite being peripheral to the main plot, she highlights Smithers' filial devotion, as seen when he ultimately gives her a birthday gift of earrings after a brief detour involving a bet with Homer.

title: Xoxchitla
text: Xoxchitla is A minor recurring character; a Brazilian actress and children's TV show host who appears in Simpsons episodes set in or referencing Brazil. Xoxchitla is a blonde-haired Brazilian celebrity known for hosting a children's educational program and appearing in various television specials. She's a parody of the real-life Brazilian TV personality Xuxa, poking fun at her wholesome image and international fame. Krusty struggles to pronounce her name, calling her a 'South American sensation' despite the mangled attempt. Interestingly, despite appearing on screen multiple times, she has never actually spoken a line of dialogue, only appearing silently or as part of a group singing. She pops up in unrelated contexts throughout the show's run, from Christmas specials to carnival scenes to soccer broadcasts, always tied to her home country of Brazil. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: George Takei (character)
text: George Takei (character) is Guest character based on real-life actor George Takei, appearing at a party meant to find Waylon Smithers a boyfriend. This version of George Takei is a fictionalized cameo appearance by the real actor, playing into his public persona as a witty, openly gay celebrity. He shows up at a party arranged by Homer, who found him through the app Grinder while trying to set Smithers up with a date. At the gathering, Takei engages in some dry, teasing banter with Tom Collins, referencing his Star Trek co-star William Shatner in a joking way. His humor leans on sly innuendo and pop-culture self-awareness, poking fun at Star Trek fandom terminology. Later, he's mentioned again as being managed by the same shady talent manager who represents the group United Parasites, suggesting he's a working actor navigating Springfield's entertainment world. Overall, his role is brief but memorable, played for celebrity-cameo comedic effect rather than deep characterization. Voiced by George Takei (Himself). Notable quotes: Click me and we will boldly go to yoga class. But, be warned, I don't care for people who Klingon.
quotes: Click me and we will boldly go to yoga class. But, be warned, I don't care for people who Klingon.

title: Stavros
text: Stavros is Minor recurring character; a Greek chef who works with Homer at Skobo's and later Odyssey Diner. Stavros is a hardworking Greek chef known for his thick accent and short temper when it comes to customers skipping out on their bills. He first appears at Skobo's, where he mistakenly believes Homer is trying to dine and dash after Bart pulls a prank, leading to a comedic confrontation involving a frying pan. Despite this rocky start, he later turns up working alongside Homer at the Odyssey Diner, showing he's willing to take on various kitchen jobs around Springfield. He's not shown to hold a grudge, treating his diner mishaps—like dropping a band-aid into the hash browns—with the same casual attitude as his earlier outburst. Stavros functions mainly as a one-off gag character whose brief appearances tie into Homer and Bart's misadventures rather than having a larger storyline of his own. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: What?! No one dashy-dine on Stavros!
quotes: What?! No one dashy-dine on Stavros!

title: Yellow weasel
text: Yellow weasel is One of Nelson Muntz's two bully sidekicks at Springfield (later Shelbyville) Elementary School. The Yellow Weasel is a minor recurring student who runs with Nelson Muntz's small gang of bullies, nearly indistinguishable from his companion the Black Weasel aside from skin color. He rarely gets individual lines or storylines, mostly appearing as background muscle whenever Nelson needs backup. After Bart bests Nelson, the weasels are shown loosely drifting away from their leader, only occasionally still hanging around him. Later continuity moves him to Shelbyville Elementary, where he crosses paths with Nelson again at a gathering of bullies. His role is largely visual and comedic, reinforcing Nelson's status as a bully with a small crew rather than acting as a fleshed-out character in his own right. Voiced by Susan Blu, Nancy Cartwright.

title: Willie Whatever
text: Willie Whatever is A minor member of the Springfield Mafia. Willie Whatever is a low-level associate of the Springfield Mafia, known mostly for his laid-back, indifferent attitude. His defining trait is his signature response of "whatever" to nearly any question, which also serves as the joke behind his name. He was present during a tense moment when Fat Tony wore a wire to expose a pickpocket within the crew, and later when Johnny Tightlips claimed leadership of the Mafia. He also took part in mafia gatherings involving Don Castellaneta discussing plans against Fat Tony, and turned up at a Springfield Sports Arena event rented out by Fat Tony. Overall, he's a background wiseguy defined by apathy rather than ambition. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "whatever"
quotes: "whatever"

title: Woman in wedding dress
text: Woman in wedding dress is Minor character, a member of the Lost Souls who sail aboard The Ship of Lost Souls. The Woman in wedding dress is one of the eccentric, world-weary Lost Souls who drift the seas hoping to leave their painful histories behind them. She has a habit of drawing out her storytelling, even pausing to make sure her audience has taken a bathroom break before she begins. Her tragic backstory involves growing up in extreme poverty, stealing bread, and freezing it solid so she could use it as a makeshift weapon to rob a bank. She reacts with shock and moral outrage to Homer's confession about abandoning his father, prompting the group to toss him off the ship. The character is a comedic riff on the literary figure Miss Havisham from Charles Dickens' Great Expectations, fitting her jilted-bride aesthetic and melancholic demeanor. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: oh, how could you?
quotes: oh, how could you?

title: Professor Taylor
text: Professor Taylor is Father of Allison Taylor, a minor recurring background character in Springfield. Professor Taylor is a minor character best known as the father of Allison Taylor, Lisa Simpson's academic rival. He first appears when Lisa visits Allison's home, revealing his fondness for anagrams as a hobby. He's a low-key presence who mostly shows up in the background of Springfield life, such as attending a Springfield Wildcats game with his daughter. He also appears wandering around town during the events surrounding Trappuccino in The Simpsons Movie, where his hairstyle is noted to be slightly lighter than in his television appearances. In that film he's also dressed similarly to another background character, J. Loren Pryor, a small in-universe detail fans have pointed out. Overall, he functions as a recurring but largely non-speaking or minor background figure rather than a character with a defined personality arc. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Shaun White
text: Shaun White is Real-world celebrity athlete referenced/appearing in cameo form in The Simpsons. Shaun White appears in the show as a version of himself, the famous American snowboarder and skateboarder. His fictionalized counterpart shows up in exaggerated media forms, such as a time-traveling snowboarder character and a snow vampire seen in a book display. He's also referenced by Principal Skinner as an example of someone skilled at their craft, contrasted humorously with unrelated people who share his name. Bart also invokes White's snowboarding fame when dreaming up a get-rich-quick scheme involving a snow half-pipe. White himself has no spoken lines in the show and functions mainly as a background or mentioned celebrity reference rather than an active character.

title: Stan Smith
text: Stan Smith is Crossover character from American Dad! who appears briefly in The Simpsons. Stan Smith is the CIA agent protagonist of American Dad! who makes a few cameo crossover appearances in The Simpsons universe. He's depicted as a criminal in an in-universe book alongside Family Guy's Peter Griffin, accused of a joke crime tied to accusations that American Dad! itself is a copycat show. His image is later used as a punchline about corny "dad jokes" at a gathering called Man Camp. Rather than having an active speaking role, Stan functions mostly as a visual gag and meta-reference to the perceived lineage of animated sitcoms following The Simpsons. His inclusion pokes fun at the shared creative DNA and rivalry between the three long-running adult animated comedies.

title: Hayley Smith
text: Hayley Smith is Crossover character from American Dad!, daughter of Stan Smith, who made a brief non-speaking cameo appearance in The Simpsons. Hayley Smith is not originally a Simpsons character but a member of the Smith family from the animated series American Dad!. In her only real connection to The Simpsons universe, a picture of her appeared as an example of a corny 'dad joke' shown by Greg during a segment at Man Camp. She also appeared, in a non-canon capacity, alongside her family at 742 Evergreen Terrace during a celebration for the premiere of the show's twenty-fifth season. She has no spoken lines in her Simpsons appearances, existing purely as a visual crossover cameo. Her characterization and personality are not explored within this context, as she functions solely as a nod to American Dad! rather than a developed presence in the Simpsons world.

title: Amy Tan (character)
text: Amy Tan (character) is Real-world author who appears as herself in a guest cameo, meeting Lisa at a book festival. Amy Tan is a real-world novelist who appears as a fictionalized version of herself in the show. She's depicted as a guest panelist at a book festival discussing 'The Future of Reading' alongside other famous authors. When Lisa approaches her as an enthusiastic fan, Tan comes across as curt and dismissive rather than warm, correcting Lisa's interpretation of her novel bluntly. This brief but memorable interaction plays on the comedic trope of a beloved celebrity turning out to be less friendly than their fans imagine. Ironically, according to the show's own behind-the-scenes note, Lisa's original reading of the book was actually correct, making Tan's harsh correction unwarranted. Her appearance is minor, limited mostly to this one scene and a cameo in an opening sequence gag. Voiced by Herself.

title: Trucker 2
text: Trucker 2 is A minor recurring truck driver character who appears in the episode "Maximum Homerdrive". This gray-haired trucker is one of several drivers who cross paths with Homer during his ill-fated journey to deliver Red Barclay's shipment to Atlanta. He's part of a secretive brotherhood of truckers who know about the Navitron Autodrive Systems that let trucks drive themselves, and he's not above threats to keep that secret safe. When Homer breaks his promise of silence, this trucker joins a group chase and blockade to stop him, though Homer ultimately escapes. He shows a practical, scheme-oriented mindset, quickly shifting from worrying about exposure to plotting a new smuggling scam involving Beanie Babies. Outside of his trucking exploits, he's noted to have had some kind of romantic relationship with Mrs. Muntz. He appears in a handful of episodes, mostly as a background or cameo character. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Fontanelle Spuckler
text: Fontanelle Spuckler is One of the many Spuckler children, daughter of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler. Fontanelle Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of the backwoods couple Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, blending into the large, chaotic brood of siblings that make up the Spuckler family. She's shown picking up shift work at Mother Hubbard's Sandwich Cupboard Express, apparently filling in for family members who work nights. Fontanelle has also appeared at a family dinner attended by Homer Simpson, giving a glimpse of the Spucklers' unconventional home life. In another appearance, she is enlisted by her mother to help sing in an effort to lure Cletus back to the family. As a non-speaking recurring character, Fontanelle doesn't have much individual personality on display, functioning mostly as background family filler typical of the sprawling Spuckler clan.

title: Carla Tortelli
text: Carla Tortelli is Crossover bar employee who appears briefly in Springfield-set episodes. Carla Tortelli is a minor crossover character brought into The Simpsons universe, working as a cleaner at a bar. She has a no-nonsense, gossipy demeanor, seen chatting with patrons about their complicated personal lives. Her appearance ties into the show's tradition of referencing other sitcoms, as she originates from outside the core Simpsons cast. She plays a small but memorable role advising a bar patron on the risks of his romantic scheming. Beyond her brief scenes, she also shows up as a background figure in a civic parade, reinforcing her status as a recurring but minor presence rather than a central character. Voiced by Rhea Perlman.

title: Jitney Spuckler
text: Jitney Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children, part of the extended Spuckler clan. Jitney Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of Cletus and Brandine, growing up in the rough-and-tumble backwoods world of the Spuckler family. She was among the siblings tutored by Lisa Simpson, an experience that led to an unlikely brush with show business when Krusty discovered the children's singing talents. Like much of her family, Jitney's storylines often revolve around chaotic, low-income rural life, including brushes with the law and family drama. She's also musically inclined within the family unit, playing kazoo as part of the informal Spuckler Family Band. Jitney tends to appear as part of a group rather than as an individual character with distinct personality traits, reflecting the show's use of the Spuckler children as a collective comedic device. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Ursula
text: Ursula is Crossover Disney villain character (from The Little Mermaid) appearing in Simpsons crossover specials. Ursula is a non-canon crossover character brought into the Simpsons universe from Disney's The Little Mermaid, appearing primarily in specials that mash up Disney villains with the Simpsons cast. She's depicted as part of a larger group of Disney villains, socializing and performing musical numbers alongside them, including a memorable drag-show-favorite tune. Her sea-witch nature comes through in her physical menace, as she uses her tentacles to threaten other characters. She has a chaotic, danger-prone presence, at one point driving a car off a cliff with Lisa inside. Ultimately, her fate takes a grim turn when she ends up eaten by other characters while they search for food. Overall, she serves as a fun cameo tying Disney villain lore into the show's crossover specials rather than a fully developed recurring character. Voiced by Dawnn Lewis.

title: Tinky Winky
text: Tinky Winky is A crossover character from the children's show Teletubbies who appears within The Simpsons universe. Tinky Winky is the purple, antenna-headed Teletubby who occasionally pops up on screens and in scenes throughout Springfield. He's usually seen alongside his fellow Teletubbies as background entertainment that the Simpson kids watch on TV. In one memorable and bizarre appearance, he joins an angry mob chasing Homer and shoots lasers from his head antenna after Homer fails to pay money he'd pledged. He and the other Teletubbies also turn up as the opening act for a concert by the character Roofi. In a non-canon moment, the Simpson family dresses up as the Teletubbies for a costume gag, with Homer taking on the role of Tinky Winky himself. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Stewart
text: Stewart is A duck employed at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, owned by Mr. Burns. Stewart is a minor, non-speaking animal character who oddly holds a job at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. He is depicted wearing a hard hat and hauling a wagon of nuclear waste, treated by Mr. Burns as just another employee despite being a duck. His brief appearance highlights the absurdity and lax standards of Burns' hiring practices, especially in contrast to Burns' reluctant compliance with labor regulations. Stewart shows a bit of mischievous behavior, pecking at a co-worker's head. He has since appeared in various non-canon spin-off media like The Simpsons: Tapped Out, comics, and books, cementing his status as a recurring background gag character. Notable quotes: Get back to work, Stewart!
quotes: Get back to work, Stewart!

title: Pat Summerall (character)
text: Pat Summerall (character) is Real-world football commentator who appears as himself in a Simpsons episode covering the Super Bowl. Pat Summerall appears as a fictionalized version of himself, the real former football player turned television sportscaster. In the show he teams up with fellow commentator John Madden to call the action during a Super Bowl broadcast. Their commentary shifts between analyzing the game itself and weighing in on the personal drama unfolding among the Simpson family back at home. He later shows up again in a brief cameo, pictured on the cover of a fictional book. As a real-world guest character, he doesn't have much personality development beyond his role as a broadcaster lending authenticity to the show's sports satire. Voiced by Pat Summerall.

title: Southern Cracker manager
text: Southern Cracker manager is Manager of the Southern Cracker factory who fired Kirk Van Houten. The Southern Cracker manager is a minor executive figure at the Southern Cracker company, a business that prides itself on being family-oriented. His most notable action is firing Kirk Van Houten after Kirk's divorce from Luann, citing the company's family-focused values as justification. He comes across as rigid and dismissive of single people, treating marital status as a professional qualification. Though he only appears briefly on screen, he plays a key role in kickstarting Kirk's financial and personal decline in the episode. He later shows up in non-canon material, including a SIMPFLIX parody show and a background cameo. His character has also been adapted into a dialogue-driven role in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Kirk, crackers are a family food, happy families. Maybe single people eat crackers, we don't know. Frankly, we don't want to know.
quotes: Kirk, crackers are a family food, happy families. Maybe single people eat crackers, we don't know. Frankly, we don't want to know.

title: Tortoise
text: Tortoise is A hallucinated guide figure that appears to Homer during his chili-induced vision quest. This tortoise is not a real animal but a bizarre hallucination born from Homer's spicy chili-fueled trip. It first appears as a rock that mysteriously crawls away from a distress message Homer spelled out, revealing itself as a slow-moving tortoise with a cryptic message written in the sand. Despite its role as a guide meant to lead Homer toward enlightenment, Homer's impatience gets the better of him, resulting in a comedic act of violence against the poor creature. The tortoise seems to have a bit of supernatural power, as its silent nod of confirmation causes a pyramid to instantly grow after Homer kicks it. Ultimately its purpose is fulfilled, as it directs Homer toward the pyramid where he finally encounters his spirit guide. It never speaks, communicating only through gestures and written messages in the sand. Notable quotes: Follow the tortoise.
quotes: Follow the tortoise.

title: Sun Tzu
text: Sun Tzu is Historical Chinese military strategist who appears as an imagined/hallucinated advisor figure to Bart and Homer. Sun Tzu is depicted as the real-world author of The Art of War, who materializes in Bart's imagination after he buys a copy of the book from a Springfield shop. He acts as a whispering strategic advisor, urging Bart to use cunning tactics against both a bully and his own father. When Homer later reads the same book, Sun Tzu offers him philosophical wisdom about deception in warfare, only to be dismissed and literally thrown away. He is treated as a legendary, almost mythic figure whose teachings ripple into other characters' lives, such as Lisa applying his strategies to win a ring hockey game. In a non-canon gag, he even shows up outside the Flanders house, silently waving at the camera. Overall, he functions as a recurring device for exaggerated internal monologue and comedic strategic scheming rather than a fully fleshed-out character. Voiced by Jimmy O. Yang. Notable quotes: if Bart used the book, his father would lie shattered before the gates of Bart's palace | all warfare is deception
quotes: if Bart used the book, his father would lie shattered before the gates of Bart's palace
all warfare is deception

title: Witch (Treehouse of Horror XVI)
text: Witch (Treehouse of Horror XVI) is A one-off supernatural character who appears in a Treehouse of Horror Halloween segment. This witch shows up in Springfield during a Halloween costume contest, blending in enough to enter and actually win. When she reveals that her witchy appearance isn't a costume at all, the judges strip her of the prize, which sets her off. She retaliates by magically transforming everyone into the literal characters they were dressed as, then makes her escape on a broomstick. A small recurring visual gag involves her glass eye popping loose from her face at random moments. Being a non-canon Halloween-special character, she has no deeper backstory or connection to the main Simpsons family beyond this single act of magical revenge. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Mary Sue
text: Mary Sue is Minor recurring character; an Internet troll and member of the Troll Force Five. Mary Sue is a minor troll character defined largely by her online persona and love of self-insert fanfiction. She was among the protesters at the Aztec Theater rallying against Agents of P.I.Z.Z.A., showing her tendency to stir up controversy as part of the Troll Force Five. Her defining trait is writing fanfiction starring an idealized version of herself, even inserting her fictional counterpart into a Harry Potter story where the famous wizard thanks her for resurrecting Dumbledore. Her name is a direct nod to the well-known "Mary Sue" trope, describing overly perfect, flawless characters that fanfiction writers create as stand-ins for themselves. She also appears in a smaller cameo near Homer's car during the incident involving Santa's Little Helper being trapped inside. Overall, she serves as a satirical jab at fandom culture and self-indulgent fan fiction tropes. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Kirkedemious Van Houten
text: Kirkedemious Van Houten is A deceased, distant ancestor of the Van Houten family, seen only in a portrait. Kirkedemious Van Houten is a minor, non-speaking historical figure belonging to the extended Van Houten family. He was once an explorer who ventured to Costa Rica on behalf of a Dutch cracker-trading company, helping settle the area. His legacy lives on through a villa he had built there, which remains in the family's possession generations later. A portrait of him hangs on the wall of that villa, serving as the only glimpse fans get of him. Notably, his descendants Kirk and Luann seem a bit embarrassed or indifferent about him, choosing to cover his picture with a Costa Rican flag when guests visit. He exists purely as a background reference to flesh out the Van Houten family's history rather than as an active character in the show.

title: Dubya Spuckler
text: Dubya Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's children, a recurring member of the Spuckler family. Dubya is one of the many Spuckler children raised in the backwoods of Springfield, notable for identifying with they/them pronouns after absorbing a twin in the womb. They briefly found fame singing self-deprecating songs on Krusty's show after being discovered by Lisa during a tutoring session. Dubya is often swept up in the chaotic, impoverished, and eccentric antics of their family, from meth lab raids to demolition derbies. They played a key role in helping Bart track down their runaway sister Mary by giving him her address in New York City. Dubya also contributes to the family's makeshift musical talents, playing a comb wrapped in wax paper in the Spuckler Family Band. Despite occasional mishaps, like tumbling into a lake inside a truck, they always seem to bounce back unharmed. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: The Snuffs
text: The Snuffs is A fictional English rock band that Lisa Simpson is a fan of, fronted by Quilloughby. The Snuffs are a fictional rock band that Lisa discovers through the streaming service Slapify, leading her to fill her room with their merchandise. Fronted by Quilloughby, the band represents Lisa's idealized image of youthful rebellion and artistic authenticity. That illusion crumbles when she and an imagined younger version of Quilloughby attend their performance at the Bummershoot Festival, only to witness the real, present-day Quilloughby revealed as a bitter and unpleasant person. He ends up chased offstage, and the band never actually performs the set. Their catalog includes the album Hamburger Is Homicide, featuring the song Hamburger Homicide, reflecting an animal-rights, vegetarian-themed edge to their music. The band's poster also turns up as decor in Shauna's bedroom, showing their reach among younger fans in Springfield. Overall, they exist as a clear parody of the real-life band The Smiths.

title: Oprah Winfrey (character)
text: Oprah Winfrey (character) is Real-world celebrity talk show host who appears as herself in cameo and mentioned roles in The Simpsons. Oprah Winfrey appears in the show as a fictionalized version of the real-life talk show icon, often referenced rather than seen in person. She's treated as a cultural touchstone, invoked by characters like Patty as someone credible enough to swear an oath on, and used as a benchmark of media excellence by characters like Lindsey Naegle. Her fame extends into odd corners of Springfield, from sponsoring a section at Isotope Stadium to being memorialized on a wall of famous left-handed people. In one canonical story she plays a surprisingly active role, personally visiting the Simpson household to help turn baby Maggie's courtroom drama into a published book. Non-canon material expands on her presence further, including an in-universe interview with Matt Groening and the Simpson family, and offhand references to her influence during Homer and Lisa's personal crises. Overall, she functions as a real-world guest character whose brand recognition adds humor and cultural commentary to the show. Voiced by Herself.

title: John Swartzwelder (character)
text: John Swartzwelder (character) is A recurring background character, depicted as a former writer for The Itchy & Scratchy Show, named after real-life Simpsons writer John Swartzwelder. John Swartzwelder is a minor recurring in-universe character who appears as a cartoonist and author connected to the world of The Itchy & Scratchy Show. He authored a book called How to Get Rich Writing Cartoons and was among the writers dismissed by Roger Meyers Jr. after Abraham Simpson was hired. His life takes some odd turns, including being called as a surprise witness by Lionel Hutz, attending Krusty's funeral alongside Kermit the Frog, visiting the scandalous Maison Derriere, and even being committed to Calmwood Mental Hospital. Despite this troubled stretch, he's honored around Springfield with a statue outside the Courthouse and a plaque on the Springfield Wall of Fame. He also turns up in unexpected places like Krusty's ill-fated blimp. The character serves largely as an inside joke referencing the real Simpsons writer of the same name, appearing sporadically across many episodes in background or cameo roles.

title: Two-nicorn
text: Two-nicorn is A fictional two-horned unicorn appearing in the imaginary fantasy world of Equalia, created within Lisa's story. The two-nicorn is a whimsical creature dreamed up by Lisa Simpson and her friend Juliet Hobbes as part of the fantasy world they invent together in their shared story. He exists only within the imaginative narrative the girls construct, appearing as a magical unicorn with two horns instead of one. His most memorable trait is an odd and surprising ability: when given a sugar cube by Queen Valedictoria, he vomits up a rainbow, seemingly surprising even himself. This gag highlights the offbeat, silly logic of the fantasy world Lisa and Juliet create. Beyond this single moment, little else is established about his personality, since he is a minor figure invented for a specific scene in their story. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "I didn't know I could do that."
quotes: "I didn't know I could do that."

title: Annika Van Houten
text: Annika Van Houten is Milhouse Van Houten's Dutch cousin who briefly appears in Springfield. Annika is a teenage relative of the Van Houten family who hails from the Netherlands and visits Springfield for a family gathering. She's introduced smoking e-cigarettes at Rod's birthday party, which catches Bart's attention and sparks a short-lived crush. In response, Bart starts smoking e-cigarettes himself just to impress her, showing how easily he can be swayed by infatuation. Aside from this brief appearance, she's mostly remembered through a family photo displayed in the Van Houten house. She hasn't had much further development beyond this one episode, making her a minor but memorable one-off character tied to the show's exploration of vaping culture. Voiced by Carice van Houten.

title: Greta Wolfcastle
text: Greta Wolfcastle is Daughter of actor Rainier Wolfcastle and one of Bart Simpson's romantic interests. Greta Wolfcastle is the young daughter of the action-movie star Rainier Wolfcastle, making her something of a minor celebrity by association at Springfield Preparatory School.
