She briefly became Bart's girlfriend after he rescued her from a group of bullies, but the relationship soured when he found her too clingy and ended things. In a fit of spite, Greta then dated Milhouse, sparking a jealous rivalry between the two boys that escalated into an international chase and a curling-rink brawl in Canada. Ultimately she rejected both suitors, choosing instead to focus on her career by producing her father's films rather than dating. She reappears occasionally in later episodes, including a cameo waiting in line for ice cream with her dad, showing she remains tied to her father's storylines even after her romantic subplot ends. Voiced by Reese Witherspoon ("The Bart Wants What It Wants"); Tress MacNeille ("Treehouse of Horror XXXII").

title: International Harvester Spuckler
text: International Harvester Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children, a minor recurring member of the Spuckler family. International Harvester Spuckler is one of the countless offspring of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, distinguished mainly by his unusual name among his many siblings. He briefly found himself in the spotlight when Lisa's tutoring led to a singing performance that caught Krusty's attention, landing the Spuckler children a spot on Krusty's show performing self-deprecating songs. He was nearly sent on tour with Krusty before his mother intervened to stop it. Like the rest of his family, he tends to appear in group scenes reflecting the Spucklers' rural, chaotic lifestyle, such as standing outside a raided meth lab looking disappointed. He also took part in a musical effort to convince his father Cletus to return home to the family, and plays noisemakers in the family's makeshift band during New Year's celebrations. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Tom Skerritt
text: Tom Skerritt is A fictionalized version of real-life actor Tom Skerritt who appears as a minor celebrity character in the show. This character is a cartoon depiction of the real actor Tom Skerritt, appearing briefly in the Simpsons universe rather than as a regular cast member. His main claim to fame within the show is a role in the film Ice World: Los Angeles, where he played a character reminiscing about a hot homeland where ice only came from refrigerators. He's portrayed as an elderly gray-haired man, fitting his real-world status as a senior actor. Beyond this small acting cameo, he doesn't have an established personality or recurring role, functioning mainly as a celebrity cameo for humor. His appearances are limited, marking him as a minor recurring figure rather than a core character. Voiced by Maurice LaMarche.

title: Xylem
text: Xylem is Non-canon alien antagonist who appears in a Treehouse of Horror segment. Xylem is an extraterrestrial who takes part in an invasion of Earth alongside his companion Phloem, using plant pods to absorb humanity's consciousnesses. He presents himself as a benevolent savior rather than a conqueror, insisting that he and his kind rescued people rather than harmed them. His stated motivation is oddly moralistic, claiming humanity needed saving because everyone had become too addicted to phones and devices. This justification falls apart comically when the people he 'saved' are suddenly given phones anyway, leaving him visibly caught off guard. Xylem's calm, reassuring demeanor toward Lisa contrasts with the unsettling nature of his actions, giving him a darkly comedic edge typical of Treehouse of Horror segments. He exists purely within this non-canon Halloween story and the Tapped Out game tie-in. Voiced by Chris Edgerly.

title: Herb Tannenbaum
text: Herb Tannenbaum is A sentient Christmas tree who appears as a gift-giver in a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment. Herb Tannenbaum is a bizarre, non-canon character who is literally a living, talking Christmas tree. He shows up in a segment of Treehouse of Horror XXIX where Bart and the townspeople have been transformed into an odd utopian setting involving beings named Phloem and Xylem. When those two notice everyone carrying cell phones, Bart explains that the gadgets were found wrapped beneath Herb himself, prompting Herb to cheerfully introduce himself as the one responsible for handing out the gifts. His whole purpose seems tied to the holiday spirit, embodying the classic image of presents appearing under a Christmas tree taken to a literal, talking extreme. Beyond this brief but memorable appearance, he later shows up as a character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. He's a lighthearted, silly addition to the show's long history of surreal Halloween-special creatures. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Vampiredna
text: Vampiredna is Non-canon comic book superhero alter ego of Edna Krabappel. Vampiredna is the superhero identity Edna Krabappel takes on after being exposed to a nuclear explosion in the Bongo comics. Styled as a parody of the classic vampire heroine Vampirella, she boasts a menacing, seductive persona typical of that genre. As a superhero she gets involved in battles against other costumed characters, including a clash with Radioactive Man. She appears exclusively in non-canon comic storylines rather than the television series. Her look and powers play into vampire tropes, fitting her name and visual design. She's part of a broader cast of parody superheroes that populate the Bongo comic universe. Notable quotes: Do not struggle, mortal! You cannot resist Vampiredna
quotes: Do not struggle, mortal! You cannot resist Vampiredna

title: Voodoo queen
text: Voodoo queen is A minor character who sells voodoo supplies, encountered by Bart Simpson. The Voodoo queen is a shadowy figure who deals in voodoo equipment and supplies. She appears only briefly when Bart Simpson, egged on by Shauna's suggestion to use voodoo against his teacher Evelyn Trunch, visits her shop. Her intimidating presence is enough to unsettle Bart, who is visibly frightened during their encounter. After bagging up his purchased supplies, Bart hastily snatches the bag and flees rather than sticking around. She has no deep backstory or recurring role, existing mainly as a one-off source of comedic tension in Bart's misguided scheme. Her design and character later resurfaced in a non-canon capacity within The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: WALL-E
text: WALL-E is A crossover trash-compacting robot from Pixar's WALL-E who makes cameo appearances in The Simpsons. WALL-E is a small trash-compacting robot brought over from the Disney/Pixar film of the same name to make cameo appearances in The Simpsons universe. He first appears in Homer's imagination as part of a bleak vision of a honey-less Earth that mirrors the desolate world of his own movie. He shows up again in a background montage moment, sharing an affectionate kiss with EVE while chaos unfolds around Bart. In a more bizarre and comedic turn, he later menaces Lisa with a gun before a Golden Globe awards ceremony, a surreal gag rather than an in-character motivation. Outside of canon episodes, he also appears at Moe's Tavern during a Disney+ anniversary special, reinforcing his role as a crossover character used mainly for fan-service cameos. He doesn't have an established personality within the show itself, functioning more as a nostalgic nod to the source film than a fully developed character. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Grandma Van Houten
text: Grandma Van Houten is Milhouse Van Houten's paternal grandmother. Grandma Van Houten is a minor recurring figure in the extended Van Houten family, known mainly through brief appearances rather than a well-developed personality. She lives on 257th Street and once hosted Milhouse and his parents at her apartment while their home was being treated for pests. Her marriage to Grandpa Van Houten ended in divorce, leaving her as a single elderly relative in Milhouse's life. She has a quirky claim to fame, having participated in an attempt to build the world's tallest human pyramid, hinting at a spirited streak beneath her grandmotherly exterior. Overall, she serves as a background character who fills out the Van Houten family tree rather than driving storylines herself. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Dermott Spuckler
text: Dermott Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's numerous children. Dermott Spuckler is one of the many offspring of the eccentric hillbilly couple Cletus and Brandine Spuckler. Like most of the Spuckler children, he is a minor background character who rarely speaks and is mostly notable for simply being part of the sprawling Spuckler brood. He has appeared alongside his siblings in family gatherings, such as being called in for dinner and being taken on a family outing to a local museum. As a non-speaking character, little is known about his individual personality, and he exists mainly as part of the running gag of the Spucklers having an uncountable number of similarly named or unnamed children. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he meets a gruesome fate at the hands of a murderous alter-ego of Lisa Simpson.

title: Peter Tork
text: Peter Tork is Real-world musician referenced in The Simpsons as a former member of The Monkees. Peter Tork appears in the show as a real-world reference rather than an active character, tied to Marge Simpson's childhood memories. He is depicted as part of The Monkees, a band whose legitimacy was questioned by other kids because of claims they didn't write their own songs or play their own instruments. His image appears on a lunchbox that Marge carried on her first day of school, which became a source of childhood embarrassment. He also appears visually in connection with the Monkeemobile at a car museum. Tork himself doesn't speak or interact with the main cast, existing purely as a pop-culture nod. His presence in the show is brief and non-speaking, serving as a nostalgic touchstone rather than a fully developed character.

title: Oscar Wilde
text: Oscar Wilde is Real-world Irish writer who appears as a historical/ghostly figure in various Simpsons episodes. Oscar Wilde appears in the Simpsons universe as a real historical figure rather than a regular cast member, showing up in flashbacks, dreams, and tall tales told by other characters. He's depicted as a witty ghost whose famous quips get recycled by other characters, often to comedic or annoying effect, such as when his ghost lectures Homer during a dream about parenting advice. His legacy as a legendary wit is played for laughs, with his sayings being quoted by everyone from angels to mechanics. He's also woven into Springfield's Irish-American folklore, appearing in a St. Patrick's Day parade float and in Grampa's nostalgic memories of an Irish pub. In one absurd anecdote, Homer claims Edna Krabappel almost married Wilde during one of his book tours. Even his death isn't the end of his presence, as his ghost reportedly haunts a legendary tank in a non-canon story. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Tattoo
text: Tattoo is Crossover character from the TV series Fantasy Island who appears briefly within The Simpsons. Tattoo is not an original Simpsons character but a borrowed figure from the classic show Fantasy Island, originally portrayed by Hervé Villechaize. He shows up in the Simpsons universe only in the background, first glimpsed on a television screen that Homer is watching while reviewing an old home video of Lisa's first steps. His only other appearance is as part of a drug-induced hallucination, when Homer and Ned Flanders imagine themselves as famous duos after taking a strange substance, casting themselves as Tattoo and his boss Mr. Roarke. Because he never actually speaks or interacts directly with the Simpsons cast, Tattoo functions purely as a nostalgic pop-culture nod rather than a developed character. He has no personality traits established within the show itself, since his role is limited to a cameo and a fantasy sequence.

title: Poor Violet
text: Poor Violet is A minor recurring orphan character in Springfield, sister of Patches. Poor Violet is one of Springfield's orphans, often paired with her brother Patches in scenes highlighting the town's poorer, overlooked residents. She's portrayed as a pitiable figure, prone to a chronic cough she attributes to years of unexpressed depression, and she has expressed a wish to be able to kiss people despite claiming to be very sick. In one notable moment, she selflessly gave her only dollar of vitamin money to Bart, only for him to waste it thoughtlessly. She and Patches also became briefly entangled in the drama surrounding Ned Flanders and Homer's short-lived Bible-themed amusement park, when townsfolk suggested its profits should go to the orphanage—though the park's closure meant the orphanage never saw a cent. Poor Violet mostly appears in background or minor plot roles, reinforcing recurring jokes about neglected orphans in Springfield. She has also appeared in non-canon material like The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Hank Williams, Jr. (character)
text: Hank Williams, Jr. (character) is Real-world musician who appears as a caricature character in The Simpsons. Hank Williams, Jr. is a fictionalized version of the real country musician, appearing briefly in the show's world of advertising parody. His main claim to fame in the series is a bizarre soccer-themed commercial where he aggressively barbecues and stabs a soccer ball while shouting for viewers to open wide for soccer, poking fun at over-the-top celebrity endorsements. He's a minor, one-off gag character rather than a recurring presence in Springfield life. His appearance ties into the show's love of skewering advertising culture through absurd celebrity cameos. Beyond his commercial bit, he's also referenced in a background gag and mentioned in a Simpsons book, cementing his status as a background pop-culture nod rather than a developed character. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Tom (Brother from the Same Planet)
text: Tom (Brother from the Same Planet) is Bart's "Bigger Brother" from the Bigger Brothers Agency, appearing in "Brother from the Same Planet". Tom is a confident Navy F-14 pilot who rides a motorcycle and briefly becomes a mentor figure to Bart after he signs up with the Bigger Brothers Agency following a rift with Homer. He quickly wins Bart over with cool activities like baseball games, workouts, and watching cartoons together, filling the fatherly void Bart claims to feel. Tom's temper flares when he hears exaggerated stories about Homer being a deadbeat drunk, leading him to threaten violence against a man he's never met. This culminates in an all-out brawl with Homer at a Bigger Brothers event, which Tom wins decisively. Despite his tough exterior, the story ends with Bart playing matchmaker, pairing Tom off with Pepi. Notably, the character was originally written as a vehicle for a guest appearance by Tom Cruise, packed with references to the actor and his films, though Cruise ultimately declined and Phil Hartman took over the role. Voiced by Phil Hartman.

title: Suzanne
text: Suzanne is A witch character appearing in a Treehouse of Horror segment parodying Hansel and Gretel. Suzanne is a witch living in a gingerbread house in the woods, embodying a classic fairy-tale villain archetype. She lures in Bart and Lisa when they're abandoned in the forest, treating them as prisoners rather than guests. Her methods are cruelly practical: fattening up Bart for eating and forcing Lisa into domestic labor. She has a romantic side, mentioning a date with a suitor named George Cauldron, though this becomes her undoing when the children mock her for it. Her cruelty and short temper lead to her own demise, as she is thrown into her own oven by Homer during a magical confrontation. The segment ends on a dark comedic note, with her unaware suitor still expecting to see her. As a non-canon Halloween character, she exists solely within this one Treehouse of Horror story and later material. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Mrs. Spencer
text: Mrs. Spencer is Minor recurring elderly resident of the Springfield Retirement Castle. Mrs. Spencer is a gray-haired senior citizen who resides at the Springfield Retirement Castle, appearing as one of the many background elderly characters populating Springfield. She has a habit of turning up in crowds and public gatherings, such as juries, town meetings, and studio audiences, without ever taking center stage. Her family, like many others, failed to visit her on Thanksgiving, hinting at the theme of neglected elderly relatives common among the retirement home's residents. She served civic duty as a juror in a notable court case involving Marge Simpson, showing she's an active, if unremarkable, member of the community. She's also been spotted outside Springfield, once waiting in line at the World Trade Center in New York City. Overall, she functions as a recurring extra rather than a character with a distinct personality or catchphrase. Voiced by Maggie Roswell.

title: John Travolta
text: John Travolta is Real-life actor referenced/parodied in various Simpsons episodes, occasionally appearing as a bartender lookalike or in dream sequences. John Travolta appears in the Simpsons universe mostly as a celebrity reference rather than a fully developed character. His most direct appearance is as a bartender at Itchy's 70's Disco who bears an uncanny resemblance to the real actor, though he never confirms his identity. Elsewhere he's invoked in dreams, jokes, and background pictures, showing how deeply his celebrity persona has permeated Springfield culture. He's tied into a running gag involving Mel Gibson, who prioritizes helping Homer over keeping a promise to Travolta. He also shows up symbolically in items like a Travolta-shaped potato chip and a nostalgic photo used to date a keychain. Overall, he functions as a recurring pop-culture punchline rather than a character with his own arc. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: yeah... looks like... | Like by switching faces with John Travolta?

Like by switching faces with John Travolta?

title: Q-Bert Spuckler
text: Q-Bert Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children, and a minor recurring member of the Spuckler family. Q-Bert Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, the Simpsons' backwoods neighbors. He briefly became romantically involved with Lisa Simpson after the Spuckler family moved next door, though the relationship ended once their parents disapproved and Lisa discovered they were actually related, a detail Q-Bert himself didn't seem bothered by. He contributes to the family's musical side by playing maracas in the Spuckler Family Band. As a non-speaking character, Q-Bert doesn't have much individual personality shown on screen, existing mostly as part of the large, chaotic Spuckler brood. His name is likely a nod to the classic 1980s arcade game Q*bert.

title: Tintin
text: Tintin is Fictional comic-book reporter/adventurer who appears as a crossover character in The Simpsons universe. Tintin is a reference to the famous Belgian comic-book hero, appearing within the Simpsons universe as a character whose adventures exist in printed comic form. He's shown alongside Captain Haddock in a Paris scene, tying him to the classic Hergé stories. His comics are popular among Springfield residents, with Lisa Simpson picking up a copy at Coolsville Comics & Toys and Bart Simpson being enough of a fan to own multiple volumes and treasure them deeply. The character's presence highlights the show's fondness for referencing real-world pop culture and literary icons. Even minor characters like Comic Book Guy pay homage to Tintin by dressing as him for Halloween. Tintin himself doesn't have an extensive personality within the show, functioning mainly as an homage/crossover figure rather than an active participant in Springfield's storylines. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: John Wick
text: John Wick is Fictional hitman and vigilante character appearing in a movie Bart watches, based on the real John Wick film franchise. John Wick is a crossover character who appears within a movie that Bart is seen watching in the episode "Iron Marge." He is depicted as a lethal, no-nonsense hitman who visits an ice cream shop called Assassins Only Frozen Treats, only to end up in a violent confrontation with an antagonist there. His brief scene plays on the seriousness and stoicism of the real John Wick film franchise, contrasted with the silly setting of a dessert shop. The character is a direct parody/homage to the Keanu Reeves-led John Wick movies. Despite his minimal appearance, he made enough of an impact to later be referenced in a Fortnite crossover as a stylistic skin variant. His humor comes largely from deadpan violence delivered over a trivial semantic dispute about gelato versus ice cream. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: It's gelato.
quotes: It's gelato.

title: Carl Yastrzemski
text: Carl Yastrzemski is Real-life baseball player referenced in the show, primarily via a collectible baseball card that becomes a source of conflict among Bart, Martin, and Milhouse. Carl Yastrzemski isn't a character who appears in person on the show, but rather a real-world baseball legend whose 1973 trading card, notable for his big sideburns, becomes an object of desire for Milhouse. The card first surfaces at The Android's Dungeon & Baseball Card Shop, where Milhouse tries to buy it for $30 while Bart and Martin are after a valuable Radioactive Man comic. When the boys end up fighting over the comic instead, Milhouse insists all he ever really wanted was the Yastrzemski card. The card resurfaces later as a bargaining chip when Bart trades his headless Omar Vizquel card for it, hoping to help Milhouse in his pursuit of Samantha. As a real-world figure rather than an animated speaking character, Yastrzemski exists purely as a running gag tied to childhood nostalgia and the absurd value kids place on collectibles.

title: Severus Snape
text: Severus Snape is Fictional Potions teacher at Hogwarts, a crossover character appearing in a Harry Potter-themed parody within The Simpsons. Severus Snape is a crossover character brought into The Simpsons universe from the Harry Potter franchise, appearing as the Potions teacher at Hogwarts. He shows up in a parody film called Love, Indubitably, where he delivers a surprisingly sentimental line about love overpowering magic. He's also referenced by Sideshow Bob, who compares his own murderous scheming against Bart to Snape's infamous killing of Dumbledore. The character serves as a nod to fans of the Harry Potter series, playing on Snape's dark, mysterious reputation while giving him an uncharacteristically tender moment. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent habit of parodying and referencing popular film franchises. Despite his minimal appearances, he's treated as a recurring character within the show's expansive crossover universe. Voiced by Benedict Cumberbatch. Notable quotes: Love is more powerful than all my magic.
quotes: Love is more powerful than all my magic.

title: Alex Whitney
text: Alex Whitney is A classmate of Lisa Simpson at Springfield Elementary, known for acting older than her age. Alex Whitney is a precocious eight-year-old girl in Lisa Simpson's class who behaves far beyond her years. She carries a mobile phone, purse, and credit cards, and treats shopping and dating like a grown woman. Her signature quirk is piercing her friends' ears using thumb tacks and paper towels, showing her reckless approach to trendy behavior. She flaunts her family's wealth and always keeps lip gloss, perfume, and spare platform shoes in her backpack. Alex represents a satirical archetype Lisa dubs "The Blasé Sophisticate," poking fun at kids who try to seem sophisticated beyond their age. She later appears taking dance classes, continuing her image as a fashionable, image-conscious pre-teen. Voiced by Lisa Kudrow. Notable quotes: not be such a Phoebe.
quotes: not be such a Phoebe.

title: King Winter
text: King Winter is Fictional king and main character of an in-universe Christmas special watched by the Simpsons. King Winter is a menacing, larger-than-life figure who appears as the villain of a holiday-themed special within the Simpsons universe. He rules over a frozen domain and is depicted as a monstrous, icy figure who terrorizes children by devouring them in his cave. His dialogue is theatrical and villainous, mixing dark humor with maniacal laughter to unsettle both his victims and the audience watching the special. He taunts his captives with grim promises of gruesome fates, waiting mockingly for a rescuer named Princess Summer. The character exists purely within a show-within-a-show format, making him a meta-fictional creation rather than a resident of Springfield. He later appears in a non-canon capacity in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out during a Winter 2014 content update. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: By the time Princess Summer comes to save you, you'll all be blood in my beard | Your own Fathers beard!
quotes: By the time Princess Summer comes to save you, you'll all be blood in my beard
Your own Fathers beard!

title: Springfield Nuclear Power Plant employee (Life on the Fast Lane)
keys: springfield nuclear power plant employee (life on the fast lane)
text: Springfield Nuclear Power Plant employee (Life on the Fast Lane) is A minor employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant who briefly interacts with Homer Simpson. This character is a background worker at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, appearing only briefly in the series. He is best known for a small interaction with Homer Simpson, asking him what to tell Mr. Burns when Homer leaves work early with Marge. Little else is known about his personality or background, as he serves mainly as a minor plot device rather than a fully developed character. He has brown hair and is depicted wearing a hard hat, fitting his role as a plant employee. His appearance is limited to a single episode, with a later cameo in archival footage during a clip show. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Sheriff Woody
text: Sheriff Woody is Crossover character from Toy Story who appears briefly in The Simpsons universe. Sheriff Woody is a guest character imported from Pixar's Toy Story franchise rather than an original Simpsons creation. His main appearance comes when Homer and Ned take a hallucinogenic substance called U-completeamine and imagine themselves as famous duos, briefly picturing themselves as Buzz Lightyear and Woody. In a non-canon special, he shows up at Moe's Tavern celebrating Disney+'s two-year anniversary, watching Buzz Lightyear arm wrestle The Mandalorian. He does not speak in his Simpsons appearances, functioning purely as a visual cameo and nod to Disney's ownership of both properties. His role is minor and tied entirely to crossover gags rather than any developed personality within the show.

title: Susan (socialite)
text: Susan (socialite) is Wealthy Springfield socialite and member of the country club set. Susan is one of Springfield's snobbish, upper-crust socialites who spends her time at the exclusive Springfield Glen Country Club with a circle of similarly wealthy friends. She is catty and condescending, especially toward outsiders like Marge who try to break into her social circle. Susan delights in subtly mocking Marge's fashion choices and social missteps, showing a sharp, sarcastic wit beneath a veneer of high-society politeness. She is petty about small things, like her suspicion that two different clothing brands are scamming her with identical products. Her character is reportedly based on the acerbic wit of American poet Dorothy Parker. Despite her cruelty, she maintains a facade of concern, feigning worry after driving Marge away from the club. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: I thought that perhaps changing suits had gone out of fashion, eh Marge? | Where exactly will you be attaching them to that mangled Chanel suit? | I hope she didn't take my attempt to destroy her too seriously.
quotes: I thought that perhaps changing suits had gone out of fashion, eh Marge?
Where exactly will you be attaching them to that mangled Chanel suit?
I hope she didn't take my attempt to destroy her too seriously.

title: Steven Wright (character)
text: Steven Wright (character) is Real-world comedian who appears as himself in guest appearances on the show. Steven Wright is a real-life stand-up comedian who makes cameo appearances as a version of himself within the Simpsons universe. His most memorable moment comes when Homer is comically attacked by a bobblehead figure made in his likeness, poking fun at the strange collectible culture surrounding celebrities. He later shows up as a face in the crowd during a parade for the Boston Americans, reinforcing his role as a background celebrity cameo rather than a recurring personality. Wright doesn't have an established personality within the show since his appearances are brief and cameo-based, relying on his real-world persona as a deadpan comedian. He represents the show's recurring gag of incorporating real celebrities into bizarre, often self-referential scenarios. His presence is minimal but memorable due to the odd nature of the bobblehead gag. Voiced by Steven Wright (Himself).

title: Veterinarian
text: Veterinarian is Unnamed veterinarian who treats the pets and animals of Springfield, including Santa's Little Helper. This nameless vet is a recurring background character who provides medical care to Springfield's animals, most notably the Simpson family's dog, Santa's Little Helper. Having flunked out of dental school, he ended up treating pets instead, working at locations like The Veterinarian and later the Springfield Pet Hospital. He's shown performing serious procedures, like fixing Santa's Little Helper's twisted stomach and mending a broken leg, but also delivers his diagnoses with a dry, understated humor. He even joined in on a record-breaking human pyramid stunt for the Duff Book of World Records, showing he's game for silly town-wide antics. During a Career Day visit from Lisa Simpson, he candidly shared his blunt opinions on animal patients, such as calling Mr. Hoots the owl a jerk. His design and voice are a deliberate homage to the 1960s TV doctor character Ben Casey. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Your dog's condition has been upgraded from stable to frisky.|The Veterinarian
quotes: Your dog's condition has been upgraded from stable to frisky.|The Veterinarian

title: Zoe Spuckler
text: Zoe Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children, a minor recurring background character. Zoe Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of the rural Spuckler family, headed by Cletus and Brandine. She is a background character with no distinct personality traits explored on screen, largely defined by being part of the sprawling and chaotic Spuckler brood. Zoe appears briefly when her father calls the children in for dinner after a windfall of pretzel tokens from Marge. As a non-speaking character, she has no memorable lines or individual storylines of her own. Her presence mainly serves to emphasize the running joke about the sheer size and disorganization of the Spuckler family.

title: Helen Thomas
text: Helen Thomas is Reporter character based on real-life White House correspondent Helen Thomas, appearing in a flashback and a non-canon future episode. Helen Thomas is depicted as a veteran White House press corps journalist, mirroring her real-world namesake and career. In a flashback recalled by Homer, she appears at a press conference asking President Kennedy a question that he dodges with a joke, drawing amused laughter from her fellow reporters. In a non-canon future vision, she resurfaces to question Lisa after Lisa becomes President of the United States, engaging in a small, slightly odd exchange about whether she was wearing a hat. Her role is minor and mostly functions as a nod to real-world journalism history within the show's universe. She's portrayed as persistent and professional, fitting the archetype of a hardened press reporter. The character serves more as a historical/pop-culture cameo than a fully developed personality within the show. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: If I, uh, may Helen, I'd like to respond to that question with yet another flip remark.
quotes: If I, uh, may Helen, I'd like to respond to that question with yet another flip remark.

title: Willy Gilligan
text: Willy Gilligan is A crossover/guest character based on Gilligan from Gilligan's Island, referenced and briefly appearing in Simpsons episodes. Willy Gilligan is essentially a fictionalized version of the famous castaway from Gilligan's Island, brought into the Simpsons universe as a pop-culture reference. He's mentioned in a flashback involving Chief Wiggum's jealousy over being replaced, and later appears in the real world when Homer and Marge attend a Naval Reserve show featuring the real Bob Denver. The joke revolves around fans annoying Denver by calling him "Little Buddy" and hitting him with a hat, a gag Homer eagerly wants to reenact. In a non-canon Halloween episode, he shows up as one of several celebrities abducted by an alien Collector. Overall, his role is minor and comedic, existing mainly as an homage to the classic sitcom rather than a fully developed character within the Simpsons continuity. Voiced by Bob Denver. Notable quotes: Hey, Little Buddy
quotes: Hey, Little Buddy

title: Jimmy Stewart (character)
text: Jimmy Stewart (character) is Real-world actor referenced/appearing as a character in The Simpsons, tied to Homer's movie escapades. This version of Jimmy Stewart pays homage to the classic Hollywood star known for his everyman roles in films like It's a Wonderful Life and Mr. Smith Goes to Washington. In the show's universe, his legacy becomes a punchline when Homer Simpson helps remake one of his famous films, dismissing the iconic filibuster scene as outdated for modern action-hungry audiences. His granddaughter later confronts Homer and Mel Gibson in anger over the disrespectful adaptation. Stewart also appears posthumously as the voice of Mr. Mailman in a low-budget puppet special, prompting Homer to change the channel out of sheer discomfort. In a non-canon Halloween story, he even tries heroically to intervene when Homer is being hunted by vengeful dead celebrities, only to be trampled for his trouble. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Wolf the Bounty Hunter
text: Wolf the Bounty Hunter is A minor bounty hunter character who inspires Homer's brief career as a bounty hunter. Wolf is a tough, intimidating bounty hunter hired by Lucky Jim to hunt down people who skip bail. He's known for roughing up his targets, including Gil Gunderson, and keeping grisly trophies like a tooth necklace made from his victims. His rugged, no-nonsense persona is what inspires Homer to try his hand at bounty hunting, leading Homer to unexpected success in the field. Wolf himself is clearly a parody of the reality TV personality Dog the Bounty Hunter, right down to his blond hair and gruff demeanor. He appears only briefly in the show's canon but resurfaces in non-canon material like The Simpsons: Tapped Out video game. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: William Sullivan
text: William Sullivan is A fictional character (General) played by Treat Williams within the movie 'Pandora Strain' shown in a Simpsons episode. General William Sullivan is a character who exists within the fictional movie 'Pandora Strain,' which is featured in an episode of The Simpsons. He appears as an authority figure who delivers grim news about a deadly virus outbreak, ordering ships to stay at sea as a containment measure. As a movie-within-the-show character, he has a meta layer of humor since he's played by the same actor both in the in-universe film and in real life. His appearances are largely limited to a single episode, though he's referenced again in later episodes through recycled footage or gag sequences. He represents the show's frequent parody of disaster films and their overly serious military or government officials. Voiced by Treat Williams.

title: White Dragon
text: White Dragon is A large white dragon that appears in a hallucination Homer has during a flight to China. The White Dragon is a fantastical, imaginary creature born from Homer's drug-and-alcohol-induced hallucination while flying to China. He speaks in a formal, oddly dramatic manner, and appears to have his own sense of etiquette when it comes to sharing snacks. When Homer fails to give him enough peanuts, the dragon reacts with theatrical hurt feelings rather than anger, flying off to tattle to his fellow dragons. His brief appearance plays into the episode's absurd, dreamlike tone, existing purely as a comedic figment rather than a real entity in Springfield's world. Despite being non-canon in later appearances, he has become a minor pop-culture reference within the show's mobile game tie-ins. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Ooh you are a very greedy man the other dragon shall hear of this

title: John Tyler
text: John Tyler is Historical U.S. President referenced in the show, portrayed by a Springfield Elementary student in a school play. John Tyler is depicted in the Simpsons universe as the real 10th President of the United States, who took office after William Henry Harrison's untimely death. His only real presence in the show comes through a Springfield Elementary Presidents' Day play, where a young student plays his role. He also appears as a background image in a book Superintendent Chalmers shows Bart, tying him briefly into Bart's fleeting historical interests. Tyler has no spoken lines and functions purely as a piece of educational trivia and background reference rather than an active character. His inclusion reflects the show's frequent use of real historical figures for educational or comedic classroom settings.

title: Baron Von Kiss-A-Lot
text: Baron Von Kiss-A-Lot is Minor recurring character, a baron mistakenly billed for Marge's taxi ride. Baron Von Kiss-A-Lot is a minor, one-off style character whose name becomes the punchline of a misunderstanding involving Marge Simpson. When Marge sarcastically tells a cab driver to bill Artie Ziff using the nickname "Baron Von Kiss-A-Lot," the joke backfires when it turns out a real baron with that exact title exists. He is left utterly baffled when a servant hands him a bill for a taxi ride he never took. Based on his title, clothing, castle residence, and accent, he is presumed to be German. Despite his odd introduction, he later resurfaces as a member of the bowling team the One and Dones, giving him a small recurring presence in the show's background gags. Voiced by Karl Wiedergott.

title: Rip Taylor
text: Rip Taylor is Real-life actor and comedian who appears as a minor/non-canon character in The Simpsons. Rip Taylor is depicted as a version of the real American actor and comedian, referenced a couple of times in passing dialogue before making an actual appearance in a Treehouse of Horror segment. He's mentioned as having performed in Las Vegas, and is even used as a comedic point of comparison by Homer regarding a certain kind of tingly excitement. His non-canon appearance leans into a wacky, over-the-top persona, complete with glitter-throwing antics and skipping while singing after confronting Comic Book Guy. This portrayal plays up his real-life reputation for flamboyant, silly comedy bits involving confetti and glitter. He's a minor gag character rather than a fixture of the main cast, appearing mostly for quick jokes and cameo references. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Rip Taylor, you're not even dead. | Someone needs to check my apartment.
quotes: Rip Taylor, you're not even dead.
Someone needs to check my apartment.

title: The Warden
text: The Warden is Warden of Waterville Prison, a minor recurring character in the show's prison-related storylines. The Warden oversees Waterville Prison and appears mainly in episodes involving Homer's brushes with incarceration. He seems to take a gleeful, almost sadistic pleasure in the suffering of inmates, particularly during the prison rodeo where he enjoys watching criminals get hurt. Despite his rough exterior, he shows a bit of concern for animal welfare, reassuring Delbert that the animals aren't being slaughtered during the rodeo. He is dismissive of complaints, brushing off Homer's grievances about pain without sympathy. Overall, he serves as a gruff, unsympathetic authority figure typical of the show's exaggerated bureaucratic and institutional characters. Voiced by Charles Napier, Hank Azaria.

title: George Wilson
text: George Wilson is A minor neighbor of the Simpson family, married to Martha Wilson. George is an elderly resident living in the same neighborhood as the Simpsons, married to his wife Martha. His most notable moment comes when Homer accidentally strikes him with a stick after losing his driver's license, sparking George's anger and a threat of divorce that oddly delights Martha. He later appears as part of the town's chaos during the events of The Simpsons Movie, attending a Green Day concert, standing outside Krusty Burger when the dome descends, and joining the angry mob that storms the Simpson household. George is designed as a parody of the character George Wilson from the 1993 film Dennis the Menace, originally portrayed by Walter Matthau. He remains a background, recurring figure rather than a central character, mostly used for quick comedic or crowd-related scenes. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Barry White (character)
text: Barry White (character) is Real-life soul singer who appears as himself in guest spots on the show, most notably helping save Springfield's snakes on Whacking Day. Barry White appears as a fictionalized version of himself, brought to Springfield to serve as the honorary Grand Marshal for Whacking Day. He starts out offended by the town's mispronunciation of his name and horrified to learn the tradition involves clubbing snakes to death, but his outrage is comically ignored by the cheering crowd. He proves surprisingly kind and helpful, agreeing to assist Lisa and Bart's scheme to lure the snakes to safety using the deep bass of his voice and music. Beyond that starring moment, he pops up as a recurring bit of Simpsons lore: a game-show guest during a beach-set taping that gets hit by a tsunami, a photo on a restaurant wall, a clip in a nostalgia special, and even the imagined narrator of a novelty spoken-word album Moe owns. His signature trait is his smooth, deep singing voice, which becomes the literal plot device that saves the town's snake population. Voiced by Barry White (Himself). Notable quotes: You people make me sick! | Anything for a lady. | I love the sexy slither of a lady snake.
quotes: You people make me sick!
Anything for a lady.

title: Mary Worth (character)
text: Mary Worth (character) is Fictional comic strip character referenced within The Simpsons universe, not an actual member of the main cast. Mary Worth is a real-world newspaper comic strip character who occasionally gets referenced or parodied within The Simpsons. She never appears as a living character in the show itself, but rather as a running joke tied to a Mary Worth-branded telephone that circulates among various Springfield residents. Comic Book Guy is particularly fond of Mary Worth memorabilia, at one point trading a Mary Worth telephone for one of Bart's prized possessions and later showing off a rare strip with a darkly comic plot twist. The strip's low popularity among Springfield's citizens is also mocked during a tour of the local newspaper. Overall, Mary Worth functions less as a character in her own right within the show and more as a recurring background gag about a mostly-forgotten comic strip.

title: King Toot
text: King Toot is Owner of King Toot's Music Store and recurring rival of Moe. King Toot is a Springfield shopkeeper who runs a music store and has a long-running feud with Moe over petty disputes, including a memorable brawl involving a dumpster that ended with both of them being arrested. He's shown to be somewhat morally flexible in business, letting Lisa test out a saxophone for hours before selling it to Krusty instead. He also has a personal life outside the store, attending Alcoholics Anonymous meetings at the First Church of Springfield. His competitive streak extends to coaching a youth hockey team, the Li'l Tooters, which previously triumphed over Moe's rival team. Unfortunately, his finances aren't in the best shape, as he owes money to the Springfield Mafia, leading to a kidnapping threat against him. Overall, King Toot is a minor but recurring background character defined by his rivalry with Moe and his shady business dealings. Voiced by Will Forte.

title: Brittany Spuckler
text: Brittany Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children. Brittany Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring belonging to the backwoods Spuckler family. She appears as a minor background presence in episodes centered on her parents, rarely if ever speaking on her own. Her role tends to involve being called upon by her father Cletus for family matters, such as being told about dinner plans, or joining her siblings in a group effort orchestrated by her mother Brandine. Like many of the other Spuckler children, she blends into the large, chaotic brood and isn't distinguished by a strong individual personality. Her appearances are brief and largely supportive of storylines focused on Cletus and Brandine's relationship.

title: Han Solo
text: Han Solo is Star Wars character who crosses over into the Simpsons universe in various references and cameos. Han Solo is a crossover character from Star Wars who appears in The Simpsons through toys, hallucinations, and pop-culture references rather than as a full storyline character. He shows up as a Blocko figure, in comic strip dialogue, and in background cameos like the Star Wars Rules segment. In one memorable moment, Homer and Ned hallucinate themselves as Han Solo and Chewbacca after taking a strange substance. Comic Book Guy also cites one of Han's classic lines among the greatest quotes of all time, showing his status as a beloved pop-culture icon within the show's universe. Since he never actually speaks on screen in the show itself, Han functions purely as a nostalgic nod to Star Wars fandom. Notable quotes: I've got a bad feeling about this.
quotes: I've got a bad feeling about this.

title: Serena Williams (character)
text: Serena Williams (character) is Real-life tennis star who appears as herself in a guest role, sister of Venus Williams. Serena Williams appears as a celebrity guest character based on her real-life persona as a professional tennis champion. In the show, she gets pulled into a charity tennis event alongside her sister Venus, initially being asked to step in for Lisa before Homer opts for Venus instead. When Marge later objects to the arrangement, Serena ends up playing against Bart, and she brings in fellow tennis star Pete Sampras to replace Marge. Her appearance is brief and functional, mainly serving to drive the tennis-themed plot of the episode she's featured in. She's also glimpsed in a musical montage and referenced in non-canon material as attending a premiere event. As with many celebrity cameos on the show, she plays a lightly fictionalized version of herself rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Herself.

title: Wiggles (clown)
text: Wiggles (clown) is A minor clown character at Ding-A-Ling Bros. Circus, associated with Krusty the Clown. Wiggles is a background clown performer with pink hair who works as part of the Ding-A-Ling Bros. Circus troupe. He was introduced to Krusty by Scuzzo along with a group of other clowns, and he took part in various circus performances around Springfield. His signature bit is juggling pins as part of his act. He eventually moved on when the circus left town by train. Later, he resurfaces as an instructor or staff member at a clowning school, where he shows a helpful and playful side by giving Milhouse a pair of joke glasses after he lost his own. Wiggles is a non-speaking character, existing mostly as a recurring visual gag rather than a fleshed-out personality.

title: Sloan
text: Sloan is One of Addy's clique of wealthy young friends who briefly torments Lisa. Sloan is a British girl and one of the stuck-up but ultimately good-natured friends in Addy's social circle. Along with Bella-Ella and Tessa Rose, she initially teases Lisa Simpson for not fitting into their wealthy, horse-riding lifestyle. During a sleepover, Sloan participates in mocking Lisa and posting embarrassing videos of her online, showing a mean-girl side typical of the clique. Her cruelty backfires when Lisa applies horse hoof hardener to her hair, causing it to break off, leading to a chaotic horseback chase. Despite her initial nastiness, the story suggests she and her friends have a softer side once you get past their cliquish exterior, especially after witnessing Addy's tougher side firsthand. Voiced by Madelaine Petsch.

title: Mr. Snookums
text: Mr. Snookums is Moe Szyslak's pet cat. Mr. Snookums is a minor, mostly off-screen character who belongs to Moe Szyslak. He briefly appears as a source of comic relief, showing that even the gruff bartender has a softer side when it comes to his pet. His only real interaction involves Moe seeking advice from Reverend Lovejoy about the cat, only to get flustered when Marge answers the phone instead. Later, during a near-death moment aboard a naval submarine, Moe's thoughts turn to Mr. Snookums, hinting at a sentimental attachment beneath his tough exterior. The character never appears fully on-screen, existing mostly as a name and a meow rather than a visual presence. Despite his limited screen time, he adds a small quirky detail to Moe's characterization. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: What you lookin' at?!
quotes: What you lookin' at?!

title: Fishbone Walker
text: Fishbone Walker is A minor recurring player for the Springfield Isotopes baseball team. Fishbone Walker is a background athlete tied to Springfield's minor-league baseball team, the Isotopes. He's introduced as one of two players demoted from the majors due to drug violations, alongside teammate Smash Diggins. Despite this rocky start, he sticks around on the roster long enough to still be playing when another new player joins the team later on. He's a non-speaking character, existing mainly as set dressing for Isotopes-related storylines rather than having any real personality traits explored. His brown hair is about the only distinguishing physical detail given. He mostly pops up in cameo appearances rather than driving any plot himself.

title: Teletubbies (characters)
text: Teletubbies (characters) is Crossover characters from the real-life children's show, appearing occasionally within the Simpsons universe. The Teletubbies are parody crossover characters brought into the Simpsons world from their own famous children's television program. They first appear when Milhouse is caught watching them instead of a movie trailer Bart wants to discuss, highlighting their status as a beloved kids' show within the show. In another appearance, they take on a surprisingly aggressive role, joining an angry mob chasing Homer and even firing lasers from the antennae on their heads. They later show up again on a children's program alongside another character named Roofi. Their inclusion is largely played for comedic effect, poking fun at their odd, colorful design and universal recognizability among young audiences. Merchandise based on them, such as toys and costumes, has also appeared throughout the show's run.

title: Titania
text: Titania is A minor recurring character who works as a bartender at Juggernauts and Knockers, known for competing in a Duff Days beer-tending contest. Titania is a buxom bartender who has worked the taps at both Juggernauts and Knockers, two establishments where her physical assets are as much a draw as her drink-pouring skills. Her defining moment comes during the "Beer-Tender of the Year" contest at Duff Days, where she shamelessly leans into her looks rather than actual bartending talent to get ahead. She's shown to be clever in a scrappy way, bluffing through a trivia question and physically distracting judges and rivals alike. Her contest run ends in humiliation and anger when Duffman, with whom she'd previously had a relationship, reneges on a promise and forces her to compete in a round she wanted no part of. Beyond the contest, she pops up in various Duff-related advertisements and Springfield events, and she later assists Homer during his brief stint as Duffman. In non-canon material, she even dabbles in amateur detective work alongside Baby Gerald. Voiced by Pamela Hayden. Notable quotes: Goat! | Duffman says a lot of things.
quotes: Goat!
Duffman says a lot of things.

title: Sheldon Skinner
text: Sheldon Skinner is Father of Principal Seymour Skinner and husband of Agnes Skinner; a deceased World War II veteran. Sheldon Skinner served as the radio operator in Grampa Simpson's WWII unit, the Flying Hellfish, where he was frequently the target of his fellow soldiers' pranks and teasing. Despite the harassment, he stuck with the group and later became invested in the unit's tontine scheme, even fantasizing about eating chicken dinners as a reward. He went on to fight in the Korean War, leaving behind his pregnant wife Agnes, who would give birth to their son Seymour. After returning home, he settled into civilian life with Agnes, at one point watching a young Krusty the Clown perform. His life ended tragically in a 1979 parade float accident that also killed several of his fellow Flying Hellfish members, and his grave has since become a target for local troublemakers like Nelson. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: "didn't join the unit to make friends"
quotes: "didn't join the unit to make friends"

title: Space Coyote
text: Space Coyote is Homer Simpson's hallucinatory spirit guide, a talking coyote. The Space Coyote is a mystical, orange-colored talking coyote who first appeared to Homer during a chili pepper-induced vision quest. He serves as a spirit guide figure, appearing atop a towering pyramid formed in Homer's hallucination to deliver cryptic wisdom about finding one's soul mate. Despite his mystical presentation, he later admits he's nothing more than a manifestation of Homer's own memory, unable to offer any real new insight. The character recurs as a general symbol of chili-induced hallucinations throughout the series, showing up in visions experienced by other characters like Chief Wiggum and Marge. He has a surprisingly casual, almost workaday attitude toward his supernatural role, at one point complaining with another spirit guide about the lack of benefits like a dental plan. His most bizarre appearance finds him nonchalantly eating the Road Runner in a shared fantasy between Homer and Marge. Voiced by Johnny Cash. Notable quotes: some dumb fat guy
quotes: some dumb fat guy

title: Viktor
text: Viktor is A Ukrainian mob boss and antagonist who serves as an enemy of Wayne Slater in a one-episode storyline. Viktor is a gray-haired Ukrainian crime boss from Kiev who becomes locked in a deadly feud with the action-hero-like Wayne Slater. Tragedy strikes his family when his wife is accidentally killed by Wayne during a terrorist attack at a party, setting the stage for his quest for revenge. He tracks Wayne down after seeing an online video of him attacking Mr. Burns, leading him to interrogate Homer Simpson in Springfield about Wayne's whereabouts and any friends he might have. His mobsters kidnap Homer as bait to lure Wayne into a trap at an ice rink. The storyline is a clear parody of the TV series 24, mirroring the relationship between Jack Bauer and Victor Drazen. Ultimately, Viktor meets a grisly end at Wayne's hands after a failed confrontation involving a well-placed icicle. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Supporting guy
text: Supporting guy is Minor unnamed Springfield resident who briefly appeared supporting Homer. The Supporting guy is a minor, unnamed background character in Springfield. He first appears speaking up in favor of Homer during a rally outside the power plant, where Homer was protesting unsafe working conditions. His supportive words highlight the community backing Homer briefly received during his safety crusade. Later, he shows up again as an apparent parent affiliated with the PTA, seen around Springfield Elementary School. This suggests he has children attending the school, though no further details about his family or personal life are given. He has no distinct personality traits beyond his role as a supportive townsperson, and he functions mainly as background flavor in crowd scenes. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Mr. Vanderbilt
text: Mr. Vanderbilt is Minor recurring character; wealthy husband of Mrs. Vanderbilt, occasionally seen in upper-class Springfield settings. Mr. Vanderbilt is a wealthy, upper-crust gentleman known for his monocle and easily-startled demeanor. He shares his wife's snobbish sensibilities and tendency to be scandalized by the crude realities of Springfield life. Rather than fainting like his wife, his signature comedic reaction to shock is having his monocle pop out of his eye. He first appeared attending a horse race, where he was appalled by both the state of a broken-down horse and Bart's rude language. He later turned up as a potential investor at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, continuing his role as a background figure representing Springfield's elite social class. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Jack Tate
text: Jack Tate is A comic book artist who appeared at a comic book convention in Springfield. "Jolly" Jack Tate is a minor character who set up shop at a comic convention, offering to evaluate the work of aspiring comic artists at his table. He comes across as a tough critic, shown rejecting a couple of hopefuls who approached him. Despite the rejections, a long line of fans and creators still waited for his feedback, including Otto, who showed off his self-made superhero Busman. His gray hair and gruff professionalism give him the air of a seasoned industry veteran. The character is designed as a nod to legendary comic artist Jack Kirby, tying him to real-world comic book history. Jack Tate only appears in one episode but has been referenced in a couple of Simpsons comic-related tie-in books. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Stephen Sondheim (character)
text: Stephen Sondheim (character) is Real-world composer/lyricist who appears as himself, hired by Krusty the Clown to write songs. This character is a fictionalized version of the real Stephen Sondheim, appearing as a guest voice playing himself. He is brought in by Krusty the Clown to compose material for the Spuckler children's act, showcasing his reputation for sophisticated, layered songwriting. His refined style clashes comically with Krusty's demand for something simpler and more commercial, highlighting the gap between high art and lowbrow entertainment. When pressed to imitate the style of Cats, he is quick to clarify he had no involvement with that musical. Ultimately he pivots his talents toward writing a simple advertising jingle, poking fun at how even celebrated artists can be reduced to commercial work. He's later referenced admiringly in a song by another character, cementing his portrayal as a respected, if put-upon, figure in the show's world of entertainment. Voiced by Stephen Sondheim (Himself).

title: Eustace Van Houten
text: Eustace Van Houten is A former Mayor of Springfield and the great-grandfather of Kirk Van Houten. Eustace Van Houten was a long-ago mayor of Springfield whose legacy is defined by one disastrous public works project. He championed the construction of the Great Springfield Gazebo, a structure that ultimately collapsed due to faulty bracing, turning him into a town-wide laughingstock and pariah. His downfall became such a notable piece of local history that it was later taught as a lesson in Springfield Elementary School, and even inspired a book dedicated to chronicling his humiliating failure. He is remembered by his descendants, including great-grandson Kirk Van Houten and great-great-grandson Milhouse Van Houten, as an ancestor associated with embarrassment rather than pride. Fittingly, his final words reflected a nonchalant, almost comedic acceptance of his blunder. Eustace serves as a bit of Simpsons-style historical trivia, illustrating the show's tendency to give even minor background characters an absurd, tragicomic backstory. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: His dying words were "my bad".
quotes: His dying words were "my bad".

title: U2 (characters)
text: U2 (characters) is Real-world Irish rock band that appears in cameo roles within the Simpsons universe. U2 exist in the Simpsons world much as they do in reality, appearing as themselves rather than as scripted characters with personalities. Their most notable in-universe moment comes when Homer barges onto their concert stage to campaign for Springfield Sanitation Commissioner, prompting the band to launch into a snippet of "The Garbage Man." Beyond that cameo, the show plays with their real-world image through sight gags, such as a billboard for a moving company called U2 Moving Crew that puns on their song title. They're also referenced as a point of Irish pride, and even become a link in one of Homer's absurd six-degrees-of-separation chains connecting him to a monkey named Marcel. Largely a running pop-culture cameo rather than a developed character, U2 functions as a nod to the band's real fame and Irish origins. Notable quotes: We move in mysterious ways
quotes: We move in mysterious ways

title: Normal Head Joe Spuckler
text: Normal Head Joe Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children. Normal Head Joe Spuckler is one of the countless offspring of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, distinguished by an unfortunate physical mishap. Despite his name suggesting normalcy, he was afflicted by a tick infestation shortly after birth that caused his head to swell dramatically, creating an ironic contrast to his name. He is a non-speaking background character, largely notable as a running gag about the Spuckler family's chaotic and rural lifestyle. His swollen head became a point of comparison when Bart and Lisa Simpson were out hunting for truffles. He later appeared as one of the many children Brandine used to help win Cletus back to the family. As a baby with no dialogue, he exists mostly as visual comic relief tied to the larger Spuckler family jokes.

title: T-Rex
text: T-Rex is A hipster child from a 'cool' family who briefly becomes friends with Bart and Lisa. T-Rex is the son of Terrence and Emily and brother of Corduroy, part of an eccentric family obsessed with being cool and avant-garde. He befriends Bart and Lisa after they're invited into his oddly furnished, TV-less room, but the friendship sours when he mocks a homemade gift from Homer during his birthday party, prompting Bart to fight him in defense of his father. Despite this falling-out, the two boys eventually reconcile, though a mishap involving unattended compost catches a donut truck on fire and leads to his family's departure from Springfield. He's shown to have a sharp, occasionally cruel tongue when interacting with friends, but is capable of admitting fault and letting go of grudges quickly. He's made brief background appearances since leaving, including at a podcast recording and in a line for a water park ride. Voiced by Patton Oswalt.

title: Yale woman
text: Yale woman is A minor recurring character who works as an administrator at Yale University. The Yale woman is a minor background character depicted as a university official tasked with handling admissions and donor relations. She appears alongside a male colleague when Mr. Burns attempts to use his wealth to get his son Larry into Yale. Rather than accepting a lavish donation of an international airport, Burns dismisses her and her colleague from his office, showing little patience for their fundraising pitch. Outside of her administrative duties, she has a creative side, having performed in a stage play about the Betty Ford Center. She has only made brief appearances in the series, functioning mainly as a plot device to highlight Mr. Burns's arrogance and wealth. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Swimming pool lifeguard
text: Swimming pool lifeguard is Minor recurring background character; the unnamed lifeguard who oversees the Springfield Swimming Pool. This nameless lifeguard is a stickler for the rules at the Springfield Swimming Pool, constantly trying to enforce a strict no-horseplay, no-running policy despite the chaos around him. He's easily outmaneuvered by clever loophole-finding troublemakers like Jimbo, Kearney, and Dolph, and gets exasperated by residents he dubs "swimming pool lawyers" who argue technicalities to skirt his rules. Despite his frustrations, he takes his job seriously enough to save Homer's life during a bowling-ball mishap in the pool. He also gets pulled into unrelated town disputes, showing up at an intersection standoff, and later leads a group of fellow lifeguards and pool-goers to reclaim the pool from Homer and Grampa's makeshift Noodleball court. Ultimately he's a mild-mannered but persistent enforcer of pool safety in a town that rarely respects rules. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: no horseplay | swimming pool lawyers
quotes: no horseplay
swimming pool lawyers

title: David St. Hubbins
text: David St. Hubbins is Member of the fictional rock band Spinal Tap who appears as a guest character in The Simpsons. David St. Hubbins is a musician and singer who fronts the band Spinal Tap, appearing as a guest celebrity character in the series. He is depicted performing live in Springfield during a world tour, giving fans a glimpse of the band interacting with the town's residents. He also turns up at a Grammy party attended by the Be Sharps, tying him into the show's barbershop quartet storyline. His appearances are brief and largely cameo-based, referencing the real-life mockumentary band Spinal Tap from the film 'This Is Spinal Tap'. St. Hubbins doesn't have an extensive personal storyline within the show, functioning mainly as a nod to rock music culture and satire. His presence highlights the show's frequent use of celebrity and pop-culture crossovers. Voiced by Michael McKean.

title: Jordan Spuckler
text: Jordan Spuckler is One of the many children of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, part of the extended Spuckler clan of minor recurring characters. Jordan Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, the eccentric backwoods couple known for their sprawling brood of children. Like most of the Spuckler kids, Jordan is a background character who rarely gets individual attention or dialogue, blending into the large family unit. Jordan appears in a scene where Cletus calls his children in for dinner after receiving free pretzel tokens from Marge Simpson. Jordan is also among the children Brandine enlists to sing a song aimed at convincing Cletus to come back home to the family. As a non-speaking character, Jordan's role is largely to add to the comedic chaos and sheer size of the Spuckler household rather than to drive any plot independently.

title: Sonic the Hedgehog
text: Sonic the Hedgehog is Crossover video game character appearing in cameo roles within The Simpsons. Sonic the Hedgehog is a guest character borrowed from Sega's famous game franchise, popping up occasionally as a nod to gaming culture. He's first seen as one of the video game characters egging Bart on to steal a copy of Bonestorm from a store. Later he's referenced on a billboard promoting abstinence, humorously paired with Amy Rose. He also becomes the subject of a joke about internet fan backlash when Comic Book Guy cites Sonic's movie redesign controversy as an example of troll behavior. In non-canon material, an aged version of Sonic shows up among a crowd of video game parodies and even becomes an enemy sent by God. He's more of a running pop-culture reference than a fully developed character within the show. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Tiago
text: Tiago is A samba dance teacher in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, who briefly interacts with Marge and Lisa Simpson during their trips to the country. Tiago runs a samba school in Brazil where he teaches dance moves that are noted for their overtly sensual style. He comes across as blunt and easily irritated, especially when dealing with tourists who don't follow his instructions the way he expects. His most memorable trait is his repeated rudeness toward Marge, whom he insults on two separate occasions when the Simpson family visits Brazil. Despite being a minor character who appears only twice in the show's run, he leaves an impression through his short temper and dismissive attitude. He later reappears as a collectible character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, listed among the game's foreign characters. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Seymour Skinner (The Principal and the Pauper)
keys: seymour skinner (the principal and the pauper)
text: Seymour Skinner (The Principal and the Pauper) is The original Seymour Skinner, a Vietnam War veteran whose identity was later assumed by Armin Tamzarian, the man fans know as Principal Skinner. This is the real Walter Seymour Skinner, the man whose name and life were quietly taken over by the character known throughout most of the series as Principal Skinner. A U.S. Army sergeant during the Vietnam War, he spent years as a prisoner of war before being sold into forced labor at a Chinese shoe factory, only returning to Springfield after the United Nations intervened. His backstory reveals that he mentored a troubled young soldier named Armin Tamzarian, whom he shaped into a responsible adult, and that when he was presumed dead, Tamzarian took his identity to spare his grieving mother pain. When the real Skinner unexpectedly returned, the town of Springfield literally ran him out on a rail rather than give up the impostor they'd grown to love as their principal. Afterward, the entire incident became a forbidden topic, treated almost like an in-universe secret never to be spoken of again. He makes a brief later appearance reconciling with his mother, Agnes, during the show's series finale. Voiced by Martin Sheen.

title: Fit Tony
text: Fit Tony is Fat Tony's cousin who takes over the Springfield Mafia after Fat Tony's death. Fit Tony starts out as a health-conscious gym owner, quite different from his infamous mobster cousin, Fat Tony. When Fat Tony dies, Fit Tony steps up to lead the Springfield Mafia as its new caporegime. The pressures of running a criminal organization take a toll on him, and over time he piles on weight and even begins to sound just like his late cousin. Eventually he becomes so similar to Fat Tony in appearance and voice that he essentially becomes a second version of him, leading to the nickname Fit-Fat Tony. His transformation serves as a darkly comedic commentary on how the stresses of a mob boss lifestyle can physically reshape a person. He appears primarily in the non-canon storyline of the episode 'Donnie Fatso' and in The Simpsons: Tapped Out game. Voiced by Joe Mantegna.

title: Knifey Spooney
text: Knifey Spooney is Minor recurring Australian character who appears in a bar scene with Bart. Knifey Spooney is a blond Australian man who briefly crosses paths with Bart in a bar. He's known for his odd insistence that a spoon can be considered a knife, playing on a twist of the famous 'that's not a knife' line. His name is a pun referencing this bizarre exchange and the game he references, 'knifey-spoony.' He later shows up laughing at a bartender who falls victim to one of Bart's prank calls, suggesting he has a mischievous or easily amused streak. Beyond these brief appearances, little else is known about his life or background. He also appears as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: You call that a knife? This is a knife!
quotes: You call that a knife? This is a knife!

title: Tom Wolfe (character)
text: Tom Wolfe (character) is Real-world author appearing as a guest character in Springfield literary events. Tom Wolfe appears as a fictionalized version of himself, a celebrated author who turns up at literary gatherings in Springfield. He's known for his flashy, exclamation-mark-heavy writing style, which he proudly owns when called out on it. During one memorable mishap, he gets messily smeared with dessert but reveals he was prepared with a spare suit underneath. He's shown to be generous and encouraging toward amateur writers, praising Moe Szyslak's surprisingly poetic work at a literary conference. He also has a quirky fondness for mashed potatoes, making a point to ask for the leftovers at a convention dinner. Overall, he's portrayed as an eccentric but good-natured literary celebrity who occasionally crosses paths with Springfield's residents. Voiced by Tom Wolfe (Himself). Notable quotes: It's true!
quotes: It's true!

title: The Mysterious Waylon
text: The Mysterious Waylon is Drag queen alter ego of Waylon Smithers, appearing at Draggle Rock. The Mysterious Waylon is a secret persona adopted by Waylon Smithers, revealed during a visit to a drag club called Draggle Rock. This character exists to help Marge practice blending in as a drag queen alongside other performers. The Mysterious Waylon joins in a group song and dance number on stage with Marge and the other queens. Despite the disguise, the character and fellow drag queens are perceptive enough to see through Marge's own attempt at disguise, showing they were never truly fooled. The character is non-speaking, adding to the mysterious quality suggested by the name. Overall, The Mysterious Waylon serves as a fun, one-off glimpse into a hidden side of Smithers within the show's drag-themed storyline.

title: The Strong Man
text: The Strong Man is A non-canon alter-ego of Homer Simpson, appearing as a circus strong man in a Treehouse of Horror segment and as an outfit in The Simpsons: Tapped Out. This character is essentially Homer Simpson recast as a circus strong man working for The Burnsum and Bailey Circus. In his segment, he's revealed to be conniving and greedy, scheming to obtain Moe's prized emerald ring through a convoluted plot involving marriage and murder. He manipulates Moe's fiancée Marguerite into marrying Moe quickly, intending to poison Moe and then marry the grieving widow to claim the ring. His plan unravels when Marguerite discovers his true intentions and throws him out. The segment ends with poetic justice as the circus freaks, having murdered the abusive Mr. Burnsum, capture Homer and transform him into a duck-themed freak show attraction. The character also exists as a purely cosmetic skin for Homer in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: "One of us! One of us!"
quotes: "One of us! One of us!"

title: Tin Man
text: Tin Man is Character from The Wizard of Oz referenced in The Simpsons universe. The Tin Man is a fictional character borrowed from The Wizard of Oz who occasionally pops up in Springfield-related media rather than being an original Simpsons character. He's referenced in conversation when Homer and Ned Flanders debate the traits of various Oz characters, showing how deeply embedded Oz lore is in the show's cultural references. His image has appeared on book covers and as a costume choice for background characters, including at a Wizard of Oz audition in a flash-forward episode. He doesn't speak or act independently in canon appearances, functioning more as a pop-culture touchstone than a developed character. His most memorable use is as a punchline in a mixed-up discussion about who lacks what body part or quality among the Oz characters. Notable quotes: Just like the Cowardly Lion.
quotes: Just like the Cowardly Lion.

title: Vincent van Gogh
text: Vincent van Gogh is Historical Dutch painter referenced within the Simpsons universe, not a main cast member. Vincent van Gogh appears in the show as a real-world historical figure rather than a recurring character in Springfield itself. He's depicted in a fictional TV documentary that the Simpson family watches, which offers a comedic alternate explanation for his famously missing ear—here shown as the result of a barber's mistake rather than self-mutilation. His artwork also surfaces in the show's world, including a traveling exhibit that gets caught up in a riot, and one of his paintings being purchased by Lisa during a bankruptcy sale. He's treated more as a piece of cultural trivia and a punchline vehicle than as an active character with personality traits. The show plays on the real historical mystery surrounding his ear injury for comedic effect. He has no dialogue or voice actor credited, appearing only in visual or referenced form.

title: Roger Smith
text: Roger Smith is Crossover character from American Dad!, appearing as a non-canon alien guest in The Simpsons. Roger Smith is a grey alien best known from the animated series American Dad!, who makes a non-canon crossover appearance in The Simpsons universe. He turns up during a chaotic scene where Homer Simpson and Peter Griffin are fighting, siding with fellow aliens Kang and Kodos in their cynical view of humanity. He casually reveals a shared history with the two aliens, claiming they all attended summer camp together, adding a strange sense of camaraderie to the encounter. When the fight escalates and the UFO gets crashed through, Roger makes a quick and cheerful exit, unbothered by the destruction around him. His brief appearance plays on his known personality from American Dad! as a sarcastic, self-interested alien who treats bizarre situations with nonchalance. As a non-canon character, his role is purely for crossover fun rather than any lasting impact on Simpsons continuity. Voiced by Seth MacFarlane. Notable quotes: Bye, thanks for having me.
quotes: Bye, thanks for having me.

title: J.T. Winchester
text: J.T. Winchester is A judge in Conklin who presides over a trial involving Superintendent Chalmers and Principal Skinner. J.T. Winchester is an elderly, no-nonsense judge presiding over cases in Conklin County Courthouse. She's easily irritated when her personal time is interrupted, particularly her beloved Lifetime Movies. Despite her stern exterior, she proves susceptible to flattery and pampering, as seen when Principal Skinner charms her with a manicure using the same tactics he uses on his own mother. She has a strained relationship with her son Fennimore, whom she blames for booking her with an incompetent manicurist and subsequently orders to do menial chores as punishment. Her willingness to bend courtroom rules after being buttered up shows a comedic vulnerability beneath her judicial authority. She later appears as a character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Ozzie Smith (character)
text: Ozzie Smith (character) is Real-life baseball star recruited by Waylon Smithers to play on the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant softball team.
