Ozzie Smith appears as a fictionalized version of himself, brought into the Simpsons universe when Smithers spots him at an Elvis Presley museum and convinces him to take a job at the power plant just so he can bolster the softball roster. Like several other real-world athletes recruited for the big game against Shelbyville, his involvement is brief and oddly mysterious. Right before the crucial match, he wanders off to the Springfield Mystery Spot and simply vanishes, never to be seen or heard from again. This bizarre, unexplained disappearance becomes his defining trait, played as an absurd throwaway gag rather than a real plot point. Outside of this canonical appearance, he shows up only as a background photograph in later non-canon material. Voiced by Himself.

title: Linda van Schoonhoven
text: Linda van Schoonhoven is Newsreader for Channel √2 News, appearing in a Futurama crossover episode. Linda van Schoonhoven is a minor character who co-anchors the news alongside Morbo, appearing in the Simpsons/Futurama crossover. She's shown reporting on a crisis involving monstrous creatures overtaking New New York. Her defining moment is oddly comedic: she laughs at grim news before meeting a gruesome end herself. This dark, absurdist humor mirrors the tone of Futurama, the franchise she originates from. She has no deep characterization beyond this single crossover appearance, existing mainly as a one-off gag character. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Skeletor
text: Skeletor is Referenced villain from Masters of the Universe, He-Man's archnemesis, used as a recurring pop-culture reference in The Simpsons. Skeletor is not an original Simpsons character but a crossover reference to the villain from Masters of the Universe. He appears mostly as a mentioned figure or visual gag rather than a fully realized character in the show. Mr. Burns is repeatedly compared to or nicknamed after him by other characters, reflecting Burns' villainous reputation. He also appears as a shadow during a musical number listing famous evildoers, and as a hallucination when Homer and Ned imagine themselves as He-Man and Skeletor after taking a drug. Burns even lists Skeletor among the authority figures he enjoys dressing up as, tying the character into Burns' obsession with domination and costumes.

title: Springfield Mall security guard
text: Springfield Mall security guard is Minor recurring security guard employed at Springfield Mall. This unnamed guard patrols Springfield Mall, occasionally popping up in other security-related jobs around the world. He's most notable for taking Bart Simpson into custody after Bart falsely claimed responsibility for stealing perfume, showing he takes his job seriously even when the culprit is a kid covering for someone else. His duties aren't limited to the mall, as he's also shown working airport security at LaGuardia Airport in New York City. During that gig, he's seen listening in on a conversation involving another security official during the chaos of Lady Gaga missing her flight. Despite his brief, background-level appearances, he's recurred across several episodes spanning multiple seasons, making him a small but consistent piece of Springfield's world. He has brown hair and no other distinguishing personality traits are given beyond his occupational role. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Shirley Temple
text: Shirley Temple is Real-life American actress referenced/parodied in The Simpsons, appearing briefly in a flashback and a Treehouse of Horror segment. Shirley Temple appears as a fictionalized version of the real Hollywood child star within the Simpsons universe. She's glimpsed among a group of classic Hollywood celebrities, including Jimmy Durante, W.C. Fields, James Cagney, and Laurel and Hardy, disembarking from a train during one of Grampa's nostalgic flashbacks. In a non-canon Halloween segment, she's portrayed performing her famous song on stage, only to become an unfortunate victim of a giant monster attack. Her presence is brief and largely cameo-based, serving as a nod to old Hollywood rather than a developed character. The show later references her again through a parody character in a different episode, showing her lasting cultural influence on the series' humor. Voiced by Russi Taylor.

title: Robert Terwilliger, Sr.
text: Robert Terwilliger, Sr. is Father of Sideshow Bob and Cecil Terwilliger, doctor. Robert Terwilliger, Sr. is the elderly patriarch of the Terwilliger family and a doctor by profession, best known for aiding his son Sideshow Bob in an elaborate murder scheme against Bart Simpson. He testified at Bob's trial, claiming his son suffered from a mysterious illness tied to his obsession with killing Bart, which added a layer of sympathy to Bob's defense. In truth, he secretly injected Bob with a drug to fake his death, allowing the family to carry out a twisted plot to trap and cremate Bart. His willingness to manipulate medical ethics for his son's criminal ambitions shows a family loyalty that crosses into complicity in crime. Like the rest of his scheming relatives, he ultimately ends up imprisoned for his role in the plan. His casting carries a fun bit of behind-the-scenes trivia, as his voice actor also played the father of two brothers in another famous sitcom, mirroring his on-screen role as father to two sons. Voiced by John Mahoney.

title: Becky Thatcher
text: Becky Thatcher is A minor character appearing in a story told by a singing railroad hobo, based on the Tom Sawyer/Huckleberry Finn tales, portrayed within the Simpsons universe by Lisa Simpson's counterpart in the fictional retelling. Becky Thatcher is a character who exists within a fictional tall tale narrated by a singing hobo, drawing on Mark Twain's classic stories. In this version of events, her father Judge Thatcher discovers her holding hands with Huckleberry Finn and forces the two into marriage as punishment. Huck manages to escape the wedding by swapping himself out for a pig, leaving Becky as part of a comedic mishap rather than a fully fleshed-out character. She also appears in a school play adaptation, where she is kidnapped and must be rescued by Huck and Tom in a scene that humorously features lightsabers. Since she is a character-within-a-character, her role is largely functional, existing to drive the plot of the tall tale rather than to showcase deep personality traits. Voiced by Yeardley Smith.

title: Tweedledum and Tweedledee
text: Tweedledum and Tweedledee is Non-canon crossover twin characters from Alice in Wonderland who appear in various Simpsons comics and specials. Tweedledum and Tweedledee are the classic literary twins from Alice in Wonderland, imported into the Simpsons universe as non-canon crossover characters. They first appear waking up after Bender tears open a literary reality machine, spilling fictional characters into the New New York Public Library. Beyond that comic-book origin, they turn up in odd cameo roles, such as dancing alongside Patty and Selma and joining a Mother's Day outing to a Disney-themed amusement planet. In a darker crossover moment, one of the pair is erased from existence by Thanos' universe-halving snap. As background or gag characters, they don't have much individual personality beyond their shared identity as an inseparable literary duo, and their appearances are scattered across specials, comics, and even a Treehouse of Horror costume reference.

title: Xena
text: Xena is Fictional superhero from a real-world TV series referenced within The Simpsons universe. Xena is a reference to the real-world television heroine Xena, Warrior Princess, who exists within the Simpsons universe as a pop-culture icon rather than a true member of the main cast. She's the kind of character fans and geeks in Springfield admire, cropping up as a costume choice, a poster, a standee, and even a mentioned figure of worship. Comic Book Guy in particular is fond of her, owning memorabilia and requesting a Xena-costumed delivery in a letter to Santa. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, the actress who portrayed her, Lucy Lawless, gets mistaken for the real Xena by a villain, though the mix-up is cleared up when Lawless displays powers Xena doesn't have. She also appears in international Simpsons comic spin-offs, humorously placed as one of Superman's wives alongside other famous fictional women. Voiced by Lucy Lawless.

title: Unnamed financial planner
text: Unnamed financial planner is A minor recurring character who works as a financial planner at Let's Get Fiscal, meeting with Chief Wiggum and his wife. This gray-haired financial advisor appears briefly to handle the retirement planning of Clancy and Sarah Wiggum. He comes across as blunt and tactless, pointing out the couple's lack of savings in an accusatory manner rather than offering helpful advice. His insensitive follow-up question about Clancy's morbid retirement joke ends up upsetting Sarah to the point of tears, showcasing his lack of social grace. Despite his small role, he later shows up as part of the angry mob chasing Homer during the Trappuccino incident in the movie, suggesting he's a background Springfield resident who can be swept up in town hysteria. He has no known name, family, or backstory beyond these two appearances. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: You haven't set anything aside for the future. | What if you don't get shot?
quotes: You haven't set anything aside for the future.
What if you don't get shot?

title: Wilbur Wright
text: Wilbur Wright is Historical aviator who appears as a dream character in a Bart Simpson dream sequence. Wilbur Wright is depicted in the show as a fictionalized version of the real-life aviation pioneer who, alongside his brother Orville, built the first airplane. He appears only within a dream sequence experienced by Bart, where the historical duo's famous invention becomes a source of comedic sibling rivalry. In this dream, Wilbur is stuck pedaling a penny farthing bicycle behind Orville, who gets to actually fly the Wright Flyer. The scene plays on Wilbur's frustration at being left out of the fun, turning a moment of aviation history into a petty brotherly squabble. He has no other appearances or characterization beyond this single dream cameo. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Spider-Man
text: Spider-Man is Marvel superhero referenced/appearing in various Simpsons episodes and comics. Spider-Man exists as a real-world superhero franchise within the Simpsons universe, referenced through parodies, merchandise, and costumes rather than as a recurring character with his own storyline. He appears in visual gags, such as a parody of his Amazing Fantasy origin story and a kiss montage alongside Mary Jane Watson. Various characters, including Bart, Carl, and criminals in New York, dress up as or reference him for costumes and disguises. He's also tied into jokes about corporate ownership, with Bart mistakenly claiming Disney created him. In non-canon material, his origin gets tangled up with other cartoon universes, such as an alternate version where the radioactive spider that bites him was originally meant for a Simpsons character. Overall, Spider-Man functions as a pop-culture reference point rather than a fully developed character in the show. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Superior Squadron
text: Superior Squadron is A team of superheroes led by Radioactive Man, appearing in Simpsons comic books. The Superior Squadron is a comic-book-only super team built around Radioactive Man, joined by a colorful roster of heroes including Bloody Heart, Bug Boy, Fallout Boy, Lure Lass, Plasmo, Captain Squid, and Weasel Woman, with Purple Haze and Black Angus as former members. They band together to protect Zenith City from villains like Hypno Head and Dr. Crab, often teaming up for large-scale battles against robotic or monstrous threats. The group isn't always harmonious, as seen when Radioactive Man's apparent death sparks an internal power struggle over who should lead. Their loyalty is tested further when a resurrected, evil version of their leader turns on them and defeats them in battle. Ultimately it's Fallout Boy's quick thinking that saves the day, restoring Radioactive Man's heroism. The team exists purely within the non-canon comic universe of the show, appearing across multiple Simpsons comic series.

title: Emily Winthrop
text: Emily Winthrop is Minor recurring character; British dog trainer who runs a canine obedience school seen in Springfield. Emily Winthrop is a stern, no-nonsense British dog trainer who founded and runs Emily Winthrop's Canine College. Her devotion to dog training stems from childhood tragedy, having lost her beloved dog Lord Smiley when she was young, which inspired her to dedicate her life to canine education. She employs harsh, choke-chain based discipline methods, believing strict control is essential, and isn't afraid to publicly shame owners of poorly behaved dogs while praising those who succeed. Beyond dogs, she extended her strict training philosophy to a ballroom dancing school, drawing criticism for using the same severe techniques on human students. She takes pride in her professional accomplishments, including a record-setting choreographed parade of dachshunds. She has made minor appearances across several episodes and non-canon media, typically tied to Springfield's pet-related storylines. Voiced by Tracey Ullman.

title: Baron von Wörtzenburger
text: Baron von Wörtzenburger is Wealthy German heir connected to art stolen by the Flying Hellfish during World War II. Baron von Wörtzenburger is a young, affluent German who arrives with U.S. State Department agents to reclaim artwork that had been looted from his family during World War II and later found by Grampa and Mr. Burns. He shows little genuine concern for the stolen art itself, seeming far more preoccupied with getting to a Kraftwerk concert on time. His privileged upbringing shows through in his impatience and disdain for those around him, including snapping at police over his car's CD changer and brushing off apologies from the agents. He also seems baffled or indifferent to warm family bonds, awkwardly telling Bart and Grampa to "get a room" after they reconcile. In a non-canon appearance, he shows up on Krusty's show as a favor tied to an old debt, only to find the experience less enjoyable than expected—especially after Krusty humiliates him on air. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: get a room.
quotes: get a room.

title: Miss Wyoming
text: Miss Wyoming is A recurring super model character romantically linked to Jonathan Frink, Jr.. Miss Wyoming is a glamorous super model whose main claim to fame in the show is her on-and-off romance with Jonathan Frink, Jr. She appears devoted to him, pining for his affection despite the rocky nature of their relationship. In one storyline, a Valentine's Day date takes an odd turn when Frink gets distracted by a centrifuge request from Marge, leading to an awkward moment where Miss Wyoming is seen with someone else. In a non-canon appearance, she's left heartbroken when Frink cancels their date to help Bart and Martin with a Robopet problem, prompting her to cry out in despair. Her characterization leans on comedic melodrama, portraying her as emotionally invested in a partner who's easily sidetracked by science and other obligations. She's a minor but memorable figure tied closely to Frink's storylines rather than having independent plots of her own. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Why won't he love me?
quotes: Why won't he love me?

title: Count von Count
text: Count von Count is A vampire character from Sesame Street who appears as a crossover/parody character on The Simpsons. Count von Count is a crossover character borrowed from Sesame Street who pops up in a handful of Simpsons episodes, usually as something Maggie or Homer happens to be watching or encountering. True to his source material, his defining trait is an obsessive love of counting, accompanied by gleeful laughter, ominous thunderclaps, and eerie music after every number. His appearance is inconsistent across appearances, sporting black hair and lavender skin with a unibrow on TV, but blue hair and skin with distinct eyebrows and an elongated head in a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment. In one memorable moment, Marge reacts with hostility to him simply because his laughter seemed sinister rather than jolly. In a non-canonical Halloween story, he menacingly feeds on Big Bird before nonchalantly helping Homer and Count Dracula by counting the kisses shared between their runaway children. He's also referenced elsewhere as pop-culture shorthand for "that vampire from Sesame Street." Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: Go back to your own country!
quotes: Go back to your own country!

title: Truth-Anne
text: Truth-Anne is A student who secretly runs the Limitless Frontier Horizons school, appearing in a feud with Springfield Elementary. Truth-Anne is a young student who turns out to be the true power behind Limitless Frontier Horizons, despite Sandra officially holding the title of principal. She has an unshakeable belief in her school's ability to succeed at anything, which gives her and her classmates a commanding edge in disputes with Springfield Elementary. Though composed and confident, she's genuinely rattled when Skinner resorts to extreme measures like driving a bulldozer into her school. She's ruthless in her authority, firing Sandra the moment she oversteps. Outside of school conflicts, she's shown to be an animal lover, keeping an emotional support chicken named Gwyneth Poultry that she brings with her to public spaces and even on flights. Her father's background as a director for a prestigious TV drama hints at a privileged home life that may explain her outsized influence at school. Voiced by Jenny Yokobori.

title: Willie's father
text: Willie's father is Groundskeeper Willie's unnamed father, a minor recurring character from Scotland. Willie's father is a gruff, unnamed Scotsman who owns a small bar in Kirkwall, Orkney. He was portrayed as harsh and emotionally distant, particularly during a flashback to Willie's birth where he showed little affection or hope for his son's future. Over the years, conflicting stories about his fate have circulated, including claims that he was hanged for stealing a pig, though he later appears alive and well, contradicting Willie's earlier tales. Despite their rocky relationship, he later reappears at meaningful family moments, including visiting Willie at Loch Ness and attending Willie's wedding to Maisie MacWeldon. In non-canon material, he even provides Willie with his groundskeeping tools, hinting at a softer, more supportive side to their relationship. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: He said that Willie wouldn't amount to anything, and that he'd be lucky if he grew up to be "garbage."
quotes: He said that Willie wouldn't amount to anything, and that he'd be lucky if he grew up to be "garbage."

title: Stretch Dude
text: Stretch Dude is Bart Simpson's superhero alter-ego, gained from a freak accident. Stretch Dude is the non-canon superhero identity Bart Simpson adopts after a mishap with a portable X-ray machine grants him elastic stretching powers. Paired with his sister Lisa, who becomes the super-strong Clobber Girl, he fights an assortment of villains ranging from bank robbers to Nazi Zeppelins, though he can't resist using his powers for mischief as well as heroics. His greatest foe is The Collector, the villainous alter-ego of Comic Book Guy, who kidnaps actress Lucy Lawless in a memorable Halloween special adventure. Despite his good intentions, Stretch Dude is more of a comic bumbler than a true action hero, getting knocked out and nearly melted alongside Clobber Girl before the damsel in distress ends up saving them instead. The character has persisted as a piece of Simpsons pop-culture ephemera, showing up in comics, games, and even real-world costume references. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Tootso
text: Tootso is A clown who works at the Ding-A-Ling Bros. Circus and has a recurring, secretive romantic interest in Krusty the Clown. Tootso is a minor circus clown whose main claim to fame is a flirtatious and rather secretive history with Krusty the Clown. She communicates largely through honking her horn rather than speaking, using it early on to bluntly tell Krusty he was a terrible performer. Despite Krusty publicly being with the bearded lady, Tootso still pursues him, and the two arrange a secret rendezvous behind the seal tank, hinting at an on-the-side relationship. She eventually moves on with the circus when it leaves Springfield, but resurfaces later in Krusty's life, joining him for a night cruise and even competing on a trivia team at Moe's Tavern. Her image also appears among a wall of retired television clowns, suggesting she eventually stepped away from performing. Tootso is a non-speaking background character, appearing mostly for quick comedic or nostalgic beats tied to Krusty's past.

title: Taquito
text: Taquito is Milhouse Van Houten's pet Chihuahua. Taquito is a small brown Chihuahua belonging to the Van Houten family, given to Milhouse as a reward for not wetting the bed for a week. Despite his tiny size, he surprisingly proved to be the alpha dog when leading a pack of canines in an attack on Springfield, forcing Marge to kick him away to end the chaos. He's appeared in the background of several Springfield locations, including tagging along with Bart during his attempt to land the role of Fallout Boy, and hanging around Bumblebee Man's house. In a darkly comic twist, Taquito later strikes up a friendship with the elderly Gil, though his motives are less than noble since he plans to eat Gil's corpse once he passes away. He is a non-speaking character who mostly serves as a recurring background gag.

title: Unnamed carnival woman
text: Unnamed carnival woman is Biological mother of Herbert Powell, Homer's half-brother, and a one-time fling of Abe Simpson. This unnamed woman worked a Dunk Tank booth at a traveling carnival and had a brief paid encounter with a young Abe Simpson while he was still courting Mona. The tryst resulted in a son, whom she gave birth to roughly a year later when the carnival returned to town. Ashamed of the situation and unmarried, she and Abe made the difficult decision to give the baby up, leaving him at the Shelbyville Orphanage. That child was later adopted and renamed Herbert Powell, eventually becoming a successful auto executive in Detroit. Nothing else is known about her fate after the adoption, making her a minor but pivotal figure in the Simpson family's hidden history. Voiced by Julie Kavner.

title: Sydney Swift
text: Sydney Swift is A minor recurring student at the Enriched Learning Center for Gifted Children, appearing alongside Bart in early episodes. Sydney Swift is one of the gifted-program classmates Bart briefly mingles with after being mistakenly placed in advanced classes. He's introduced greeting Bart with a quirky backwards-phonetics style of speech, hinting at the eccentric, overly clever nature of the gifted kids. He's part of a small clique with Ian, Ethan, and Calvin who take advantage of Bart's naivety by swapping his snacks for lesser items, showing a mildly manipulative streak common among the ELCFGC students. Beyond this, he pops up in background capacity, such as attending a party at Bart's house and receiving mail while away at Kamp Krusty. He doesn't have much individual personality development beyond these appearances, functioning mostly as set dressing for Bart's academic and social world. Interestingly, his character design was later recycled for another minor character, Truong Van Dinh. Voiced by Russi Taylor.

title: Tyler Winklevoss
text: Tyler Winklevoss is Olympic athlete and twin brother of Cameron Winklevoss, a minor recurring character based on the real-life Winklevoss twins. Tyler Winklevoss is depicted as an Olympic rower alongside his identical twin brother Cameron, mirroring the real-life Winklevoss twins famous for their Facebook lawsuit. In his appearance in Springfield lore, he competes in a rowing event at the London 2012 Olympics but is embarrassingly defeated by Patty and Selma, despite the sisters being out of shape, smokers, and barely trained. The loss is attributed to the brothers being distracted by thoughts of their massive Facebook settlement money. After the race, the two brothers share an intimate moment together, adding a comedic hint at their relationship. He later makes a brief background appearance in a crowd scene during a parade. Overall, Tyler exists mostly as a parody figure poking fun at the real Winklevoss twins' public image and legal history with Facebook. Voiced by Armie Hammer.

title: The Three Musketeers
text: The Three Musketeers is Fictional French heroes who appear within the movie-within-the-show "The Poke of Zorro". The Three Musketeers are a trio of French swordsmen who exist within the fictional film 'The Poke of Zorro,' a movie watched by the Simpsons family. They serve as swashbuckling heroes who cross paths with the masked hero Zorro, only to meet a swift and dramatic end at his blade. Their appearance is brief, existing mainly as a plot device to showcase Zorro's signature fighting move before he moves on to his true rival. Despite their minor role, they're notable for a memorably dramatic death line delivered in classic melodramatic fashion. Interestingly, the characters and the actors who portray them go uncredited within the movie itself, adding a layer of meta-humor about low-budget film productions. They later show up again in Treehouse of Horror-style cameo material as costumes. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Sacre bleu! The deadly poke of zorro!
quotes: Sacre bleu! The deadly poke of zorro!

title: Stan (Moaning Lisa)
text: Stan (Moaning Lisa) is A minor student at Springfield Elementary School, classmate of Lisa Simpson. Stan is a young student at Springfield Elementary who plays in the school band alongside Lisa. He's shown to be somewhat shallow in his social judgments, having previously dismissed Lisa as odd because of her visible sadness. When Lisa fakes happiness on Marge's advice, Stan quickly warms to her and invites her to do homework together, showing how easily his approval can be won or lost based on surface appearances. This brief interaction becomes a turning point in the episode, prompting Marge to reconsider her advice to Lisa about hiding emotions. Beyond this moment, Stan remains a background character, appearing in a handful of episodes mostly as part of the general student body. He doesn't have much individual characterization outside of this single formative scene. Voiced by Susan Blu.

title: Zachary Vaughn
text: Zachary Vaughn is Fourth grade teacher at Springfield Elementary School who briefly replaced Edna Krabappel. Zachary Vaughn is a young, tech-savvy teacher who takes over Edna Krabappel's fourth grade class after she's fired due to a prank orchestrated by Bart and his classmates. Fresh out of a Master's program at Tufts, he initially wins over the students by embracing social media and modern technology instead of traditional teaching methods, and he takes an unusually relaxed approach with parents, reassuring them rather than raising concerns. However, his laid-back persona hides a serious drinking problem, as he's caught spiking his energy drink with vodka on a regular basis. His unraveling culminates in a drunken tirade about the misery of bureaucracy and life itself, leading to his removal from the school. Despite this scandal, he continues to appear around Springfield afterward, including at social gatherings and public events, showing he remains part of the community even after losing his teaching job. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: it's always the good ones that go crazy the fastest
quotes: it's always the good ones that go crazy the fastest

title: Biff Westwood
text: Biff Westwood is A young rock star who bears a striking resemblance to Bart Simpson, appearing in Simpsons comics. Biff Westwood is a teen pop idol whose uncanny likeness to Bart Simpson drives the plot of a couple of comic-book stories. His fame causes chaos when adoring fans mob the mall waiting for him, leading Bart to impersonate him just to escape a crowd, only for the ruse to accidentally help Westwood's actual manager. In a later story, the two doppelgangers deliberately swap identities, with Biff doing Bart's homework and fooling Marge and Principal Skinner, while Bart prepares to take Biff's place on stage. The mix-up nearly unravels when Lisa figures out the switch, forcing Biff and Lisa to scramble to keep the secret from being exposed on live television. Ultimately the two look-alikes cooperate, with Biff singing off-camera while Bart mimes the performance. Biff's main traits are his celebrity status, his physical identical appearance to Bart, and his role as a catalyst for mistaken-identity hijinks.

title: L'il Squiddie
text: L'il Squiddie is Comic-book superhero sidekick to Captain Squid, within the Radioactive Man comic universe. L'il Squiddie is a minor superhero character who exists within the fictional comic book world of the Simpsons universe, serving as the junior partner to the hero Captain Squid. As a sidekick character, he embodies the classic comic-book trope of the plucky young helper standing alongside a more established costumed crimefighter. His appearances are limited to Bongo Comics tie-in material rather than the animated series itself, making him a niche piece of the show's expansive comic-book-within-a-show mythology. He was notably present at a significant social event in the superhero community, attending the wedding of two other established heroic characters. Beyond his role as a sidekick, little else is detailed about his personality or abilities, keeping him a background figure in the broader Radioactive Man comic continuity.

title: Temptation Serpent
text: Temptation Serpent is A minor biblical/fictional character representing the Devil, appearing in a Marge-imagined retelling of the Garden of Eden story. The Temptation Serpent is a mythical snake creature who appears within a dream sequence imagined by Marge, casting him in the role of the Bible's classic tempter. Colored in green and black, he serves as an embodiment of The Devil, using cunning persuasion to lead Adam astray in the Garden of Eden. His actions set off a chain reaction, as Adam then convinces Eve to also eat the forbidden fruit, resulting in humanity's expulsion from paradise. Though a minor and non-canon figure, he plays a pivotal narrative role in this parody of the biblical creation story. The character later resurfaced in mobile game form, extending his presence beyond the original television appearance. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Tad Winslow's actor
text: Tad Winslow's actor is Minor recurring character; an actor who played Dr. Tad Winslow on the soap opera It Never Ends, both before and after Moe Szyslak took over the role. This unnamed actor originated the role of Dr. Tad Winslow on the fictional soap opera It Never Ends. He briefly lost the part to Moe Szyslak after Moe got plastic surgery and impressed the show's producer, forcing him to hand over his character's eye patch in a moment of quiet defeat. Despite this setback, he later reclaimed the role once Moe was fired from the show. His story ties into Moe's ongoing quest for validation and highlights the fickle, appearance-obsessed nature of the entertainment industry within the Simpsons universe. He has no depth beyond his connection to the soap opera plot, serving mainly as a minor obstacle and later a quiet beneficiary in Moe's storyline. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: The Thung
text: The Thung is A minor comic-book-universe superhero character within the Simpsons franchise. The Thung is a fictional superhero existing within the comic book lore referenced in the Simpsons universe. He is a clear parody of Marvel's The Thing, sharing an orange, rocky appearance and a similar name pattern. His feats of strength are debated by fans within the show, such as comparisons to giving a piggyback ride to an entire football team. He later appears embroiled in a politically charged conflict, fighting against another hero due to his skin color aligning him with a particular faction. The character never speaks on screen, existing mostly as a background reference or discussion topic for other characters like Bart and Milo. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent habit of satirizing mainstream comic book tropes and superhero rivalries.

title: The Who (characters)
text: The Who (characters) is Guest-starring rock band who appear as themselves in a Simpsons episode. The Who are a real-world English rock band who make a special guest appearance in Springfield after the town splits into New Springfield and Olde Springfield. Homer mistakenly believes he's won concert tickets and ends up convincing the band to perform in New Springfield instead of Olde Springfield. True to their reputation, they're initially thrown off by the small crowd, and end up humoring Homer by covering Grand Funk Railroad songs and even letting him join in on a rendition of Pac-Man Fever. When tensions rise between the two rival towns, the band steps in as peacemakers, using their music to literally help tear down the wall dividing Springfield. Their drummer is drawn as a non-speaking tribute to the real Keith Moon. The band's likenesses have also turned up in look-alike form and in archival concert footage elsewhere in the show.

title: Little Miss Springfield
text: Little Miss Springfield is A children's beauty pageant title briefly held by Lisa Simpson. Little Miss Springfield is the title given to the winner of a local children's beauty pageant. Homer entered Lisa into the competition, where she initially placed second behind Amber Dempsey. After Amber suffered an accident, Lisa was bumped up to the winning title and took on the Little Miss Springfield role. Lisa used her newfound platform to speak out, which put her at odds with the pageant's sponsor, Laramie Cigarettes. The sponsor then sought ways to strip her of the title due to her outspokenness. The character also appears as a cosmetic skin for Lisa in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Lona Williams, Yeardley Smith.

title: Milford Van Houten
text: Milford Van Houten is Milhouse Van Houten's ancestor, a historical figure married to Eliza Simpson. Milford Van Houten is a distant ancestor of Milhouse, appearing in a flashback episode set during America's slavery era. He's depicted as a passive observer who witnesses a morally troubling moment between Hiram Simpson, Eliza Simpson, and Colonel Burns regarding a runaway slave named Virgil. His silence and inaction during this event haunt him, leaving him unable to look Eliza in the eye afterward. Despite this lingering resentment and low opinion of her, he eventually marries Eliza anyway. Adding to his misfortunes, he goes blind after drinking contaminated well water. He's portrayed as bookish, having been introduced reading a book about Thomas Jefferson's inventions under a tree. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Groundskeeper Wilma
text: Groundskeeper Wilma is Groundskeeper at Shelbyville Elementary School, the Shelbyville counterpart to Groundskeeper Willie. Groundskeeper Wilma, also known as Katie MacLoughlan, is Shelbyville's answer to Springfield's own Groundskeeper Willie, right down to sharing his gruff demeanor and appearance. She's first glimpsed hollering at Bart and Shelby as they race past Shelbyville Elementary during their chase through town. In a later non-canon appearance, it's revealed she belongs to the MacLoughlan clan, longtime rivals of Willie's Tullabardine clan, which sparks a physical confrontation between the two groundskeepers that Willie ultimately wins. Lisa, unaware of this bitter feud, had innocently mentioned Willie to her at the library, inadvertently setting the clash into motion. Wilma's shouted threats and thick brogue-style insults mirror Willie's own comedic bluster, reinforcing the running gag that Shelbyville is an eerie mirror image of Springfield. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Slow down, ya sidewalk-surfin' cube gleamers!
quotes: Slow down, ya sidewalk-surfin' cube gleamers!

title: Amelia Vanderbuckle
text: Amelia Vanderbuckle is A historical 19th-century Springfield scientist and inventor who appeared in a period-set segment. Amelia Vanderbuckle was a pioneering female inventor living in Springfield during the 1800s, notable for being the first woman to graduate from Springfield Tech. Her early life was marked by tragedy, coming from a huge family decimated by mundane hazards like drafty windows, and having a father who worked in dangerous poison mines. Despite her genius, she was institutionalized by a medical board that absurdly diagnosed her ambition as a mental illness, reflecting the era's dismissive attitude toward capable women. Even confined to an asylum, she continued her inventive work, creating devices like a steam-powered barber chair and an early computational loom. She reportedly had a romantic history with Nikola Tesla, though the relationship ended. Her story serves as a darkly comic commentary on historical sexism toward brilliant women. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Mac Tonight
text: Mac Tonight is Fictional fast food mascot for McDonald's who appears as a recurring gag/dream figure in the show. Mac Tonight is a crossover-style mascot character based on McDonald's real 1980s advertising figure, reimagined here as a singer and pianist. He first shows up as a cardboard cutout that Homer uses to trick his family into obeying its instructions while he's away. Later, he becomes a recurring presence in Homer's dreams, crooning original songs that push Homer toward specific actions in waking life. His musical numbers act as a manipulative but comedic device, essentially functioning as an advertisement come to life inside Homer's subconscious. Through these dream sequences, he manages to influence Homer into publicly denouncing a rival burger chain. The character leans into corporate satire, poking fun at brand mascots and their subtle persuasive power. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Meryl Streep (character)
text: Meryl Streep (character) is Real-life actress who appears as a minor/non-speaking character and recurring pop-culture reference in the Simpsons universe. Meryl Streep exists in the Simpsons world as a version of the famous real actress, though she rarely appears on-screen in a speaking capacity. Within the show's fictional history, she once played the Stupid Nun in the fictional film The Poke of Zorro. Her fame is used as a running gag, with her name being dropped by other characters in odd contexts, such as Homer jokingly calling himself by her name and her husband's, or Lenny mistakenly using her name as a trivia answer about beer ingredients. She's also referenced through Simpsons-universe merchandise, like an award-collection DVD spotted at a yard sale. In a non-canon segment, Lisa recalls a bizarre incident of Streep spitting on her after the Oscars, which is depicted in a surreal, exaggerated flashback. She also made a cameo in the meta short Oscar Selfie. Overall, she functions more as a celebrity in-joke than a fully developed character.

title: Treestache
text: Treestache is A minor non-canon character; a sentient tree appearing in a Simpsons video game tie-in. Treestache is a talking tree who exists outside the show's main canon, appearing only in a special game-based storyline. He and his fellow trees attempted to help the trapped citizens of Springfieldia escape by tearing down the wall that confined them. Tragically, the townspeople repaid this act of kindness by chopping the trees down and repurposing their wood into ladders. Treestache doesn't speak in his appearances, giving him a silent, tragic quality typical of background fantasy creatures. His design and concept are clearly modeled after a famous literary character, giving him a bit of a parody role rather than an original creation. Ultimately, his story is a small, dark joke about sacrifice and ingratitude within a lighthearted fantasy parody setting.

title: Unnamed surfing rabbi
text: Unnamed surfing rabbi is A minor background character; a rabbi who authored a book that Marge buys. This unnamed rabbi is best known not for anything he says or does on screen, but for having written a book titled 'When Bad Things Happen To Cute Children.' He is depicted with brown hair and appears to have a surfing theme associated with his image, though the show never elaborates on this connection. Marge is shown purchasing his book, suggesting it holds some appeal to worried or overprotective parents in Springfield. He never speaks in his appearances, existing purely as a visual gag on a book cover and later as a picture in a side character's office. Despite his brief and silent presence, he has become a small piece of Simpsons trivia due to his oddly specific occupation and the whimsical title of his work.

title: Woodrow Wilson
text: Woodrow Wilson is Real-world 28th President of the United States, referenced as a picture/historical figure in Springfield. Woodrow Wilson appears in the show only as a historical figure, depicted through pictures rather than as an active character. Bart Simpson borrows his first name as a fake alias to keep up a prank romance with Mrs. Krabappel through a personals ad. His portrait later becomes the target of a childish prank when Milhouse doodles a mustache on it during the kids' takeover of Springfield Elementary. He's also used as a benchmark for Bart's poor grasp of American history, since Bart fails to recognize him among a lineup of presidents. Wilson never speaks or acts in the show himself, existing purely as a background reference tied to real-world history and gags about the Simpsons kids' antics. Notable quotes: Dear Woodrow, I must admit I'm intrigued. You're not like the other men I've met. | Yeah, I'm the 28th President of the United States.
quotes: Dear Woodrow, I must admit I'm intrigued. You're not like the other men I've met.
Yeah, I'm the 28th President of the United States.

title: Snowball III
text: Snowball III is The third pet cat adopted by Lisa Simpson for the Simpson family. Snowball III was a short-lived brown cat with light green eyes, adopted by Lisa after the death of Snowball II. Lisa carefully picked him from an animal shelter, passing over several other animals before choosing him. Tragically, his time with the Simpsons was cut short almost immediately after arriving at their home. While Lisa was preparing his first meal, he attempted to catch a goldfish in the family's aquarium and drowned in the process. His death is played as a dark, quick running gag typical of the show's treatment of pet cats. He later made a brief cameo as a ghost in one of Bart's dream sequences.

title: Mr. Wong
text: Mr. Wong is Minor recurring background character; father of Hubert Wong and husband of Mrs. Wong. Mr. Wong is a minor, non-speaking figure in Springfield's background crowd, most notable for being the father of Hubert Wong and husband to Mrs. Wong. He first appeared bringing cupcakes with his wife to Hubert's first-grade class birthday celebration, showing him as an involved and supportive parent. He has since popped up in various crowd scenes, including as an audience member for podcast recordings by Tabitha Shingle and Kent Brockman. He also attended a community event, the Bounce-A-Thon, alongside his wife and son, reinforcing his role as a background family man. As a non-speaking character, he has no distinct personality traits explored on screen, but his consistent appearances alongside his family suggest a stable, ordinary household within the town. He functions mainly as set dressing to populate Springfield's many public gatherings.

title: Paris Texan
text: Paris Texan is The Rich Texan's socialite daughter, a minor recurring character. Paris Texan is the pampered, celebrity-obsessed daughter of the Rich Texan, clearly modeled on real-world tabloid fixture Paris Hilton. She's the kind of over-the-top socialite who carries a tiny dog in her purse, which itself carries an even tinier dog in its own purse. Her first appearance has her getting riled up by Bart at Homer's instigation, leading to an attack that turns into a kiss, all captured on camera and sold by Homer to the press. She's also shown to be a bit fickle in her affections, later caught making out with Milhouse. Beyond her direct interactions with the Simpsons kids, she pops up as a fixture of Springfield's celebrity scene, attending high-profile awards shows. Her whole character leans into satire of vapid celebrity culture and paparazzi obsession. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Hubert Wong
text: Hubert Wong is A minor recurring student at Springfield Elementary School and classmate of Lisa Simpson. Hubert Wong is a young student at Springfield Elementary who mostly appears in the background of classroom scenes. He's rarely given major storylines, typically shown sitting near Lisa Simpson during class. In a non-canon Halloween segment, he's picked over Lisa for a special reading assignment, hinting at a rivalry between the two. A separate speculative future-set episode imagines him growing up to run a tech company and dating Lisa Simpson, though their relationship goes through a breakup and later reconciliation before ultimately falling apart again. His design and name are a playful nod to two characters from Matt Groening's other show, Futurama. Overall, he functions as one of Springfield Elementary's many recognizable but lightly developed background kids. Voiced by Tress MacNeille (season 21-34); Simu Liu; Rosalie Chiang (season 35 onward).

title: Norbert Van Houten
text: Norbert Van Houten is Milhouse Van Houten's adventurous Danish uncle and Kirk Van Houten's brother. Norbert, who prefers to be called 'Zack,' is Milhouse's dashing and adventurous uncle who swoops into Springfield by piloting his own biplane. His arrival instantly boosts Milhouse's social standing at school, giving the usually unpopular kid a taste of coolness by association. He's bold and daring, whisking Milhouse (and an uninvited Bart) off on a hot air balloon trip around the world. Norbert displays a fierce pride in his Danish heritage, getting into a heated conflict with his brother Kirk after being called a 'Damn Dutchman.' This leads to a physical scuffle where he mocks Kirk's fighting ability. He's clearly modeled after a swashbuckling adventurer archetype, drawing comparisons to Indiana Jones. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Damn Dutchman! | You grapple like a girl.
quotes: Damn Dutchman!
You grapple like a girl.

title: Tiffany Spuckler
text: Tiffany Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children. Tiffany Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of the rural, backwoods couple Cletus and Brandine Spuckler. Like many of her siblings, she is a minor background character who appears without dialogue, contributing to the running joke of the Spucklers' enormous, chaotic brood of children. She has been shown participating in ordinary family activities, such as being called to dinner and being taken on a family outing to a museum. Tiffany doesn't have a distinct personality of her own within the show, since her role is largely to exist as part of the sprawling Spuckler family gag. She has appeared in a handful of episodes over the years, usually in passing background moments rather than as a focus of the story.

title: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
text: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn is Real-world Russian author referenced/pictured in the show, unrelated to the main cast directly but tied to Sam Monroe's family library. Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn appears in the show purely as a picture-only, non-speaking reference to the real historical novelist and historian. His likeness shows up as part of a collection of Russian authors owned by Sam Monroe's family, tying him briefly to the show's world. He later appears again as one of four Nobel laureates featured in the 'LV U 4 Ever' music video. He has no dialogue or active role in any storyline, functioning solely as a background cultural reference. Because he never speaks or interacts with characters, his presence is essentially an Easter egg nod to real-world literary history. He is classified among the show's recurring but silent background depictions of real deceased public figures.

title: Trucker 1
text: Trucker 1 is Minor recurring character; a truck driver and friend of Red Barclay who appears at The Slaughterhouse. This unnamed trucker is a minor background character tied to the trucking world featured in one of Homer's odder adventures. He's shown as a loyal friend, standing by Red Barclay's side at The Slaughterhouse and sharing in the camaraderie of the road. When Red dies suddenly after winning an eating contest against Homer, the trucker is genuinely mournful, reflecting on his friend's impressive delivery record. His brief appearance highlights the tight-knit, almost old-fashioned honor code among truckers, since he seems more concerned with Red's unbroken shipment streak than anything else. He ultimately fades into the background once Homer takes it upon himself to finish Red's final delivery. Despite his minimal screen time, he represents the show's knack for giving even one-scene characters a bit of personality and pathos. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: I guess this is one delivery old Red won't be making
quotes: I guess this is one delivery old Red won't be making

title: Theo
text: Theo is One-episode character; owner of The Institute, an organization that helps rehabilitate the reputations of social pariahs, including Homer. Theo runs The Institute, a mysterious organization devoted to restoring the public image of disgraced individuals. He recruits Homer after Homer accidentally shoves Reverend Lovejoy out a window, grouping him with other local outcasts for a series of goodwill projects like beach cleanups and tree planting. When those efforts fail to sway public opinion, Theo reveals a much riskier scheme involving hacking into ChumNet to erase incriminating footage of the group from the internet. He proves to be a persuasive and somewhat manipulative leader, framing the group's charity work as covert training for the real mission. Ultimately his plan collapses when Homer sabotages the operation, and Theo is left to face unspecified but ominous consequences from his superiors, comparing his fate to what was done to democracy. Voiced by Kumail Nanjiani.

title: Bourbon Verlander
text: Bourbon Verlander is A billionaire businessman and antagonist who scams the education system in a Simpsons episode. Bourbon Verlander is a wealthy, unscrupulous businessman who owns hundreds of college campuses and built his fortune through exploiting the for-profit education system. He manipulates Mr. Burns into founding a for-profit college, then swoops in to acquire it once he recognizes Homer's surprising talent as a teacher. His scheme involves using Homer to train robotic students who can pass as human, enroll at Yale, and fraudulently siphon taxpayer-funded student loans on a massive scale. Verlander's greed and corporate cunning make him a formidable foe, commanding an army of nearly-perfect robot pupils. Ultimately his plan collapses when the robots, designed to be flawless, are so offended by Homer's crude parody of them that they self-destruct. He represents a satirical jab at predatory for-profit colleges and corporate greed in the education industry. Voiced by Jason Alexander.

title: Barbra Streisand
text: Barbra Streisand is Real-life celebrity referenced within the Simpsons universe; a recurring pop-culture punchline rather than an active character. Barbra Streisand appears in the show only as a cultural touchstone, referenced repeatedly by the Simpsons and Springfield residents rather than as a fleshed-out character. She's brought up in jokes about celebrity culture, movies, and music, often used by Homer as a punching bag for his cynical views on fame. Her autobiography and songs are referenced by other characters, showing her presence in the show's fictional media landscape. She even appears as a look-alike performer during a musical number in one episode. A deleted, non-canon scene once placed her working at the Kwik-E-Mart, stealing hairspray. Overall, she functions as a running gag anchor for jokes about Hollywood and celebrity worship rather than a character with her own storyline. Notable quotes: at least she's not singing Barbra Streisand
quotes: at least she's not singing Barbra Streisand

title: Mr. Winfield
text: Mr. Winfield is Former neighbor of the Simpson family, husband of Sylvia Winfield. Mr. Winfield was an elderly resident of Springfield who, along with his wife Sylvia, lived next door to the Simpsons before growing tired of them and relocating to Florida. His disdain for the family was strong enough to drive them out of town entirely, making way for Ruth and Laura Powers to move into their old house. Despite leaving Springfield behind, he and Sylvia couldn't resist returning for the town's bicentennial parade, showing a lingering connection to the community. He also popped up in the background at a baseball game, suggesting he still had ties to the area even after moving away. For many years, he was a recognizable face in the show's opening sequence, cementing him as a minor but familiar part of Springfield's background cast. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Michael Stipe (character)
text: Michael Stipe (character) is Guest character based on real-life musician; appears as himself, lead singer of R.E.M., in episodes involving Homer and Moe's Tavern. Michael Stipe appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, portrayed as an earnest and environmentally conscious musician who is easily manipulated by Homer's schemes. He agrees to have R.E.M. perform at Moe's Tavern after being tricked into believing it's a benefit concert for the rainforest. When he discovers the deception, he briefly turns violent but quickly reverts to his eco-friendly ways by recycling the broken glass he used as a weapon. Later, he shows a gentler, comforting side when he consoles a distraught Kirk Van Houten. His appearances highlight a running gag of celebrities being duped by Homer while maintaining an exaggerated version of their real-life public persona. Voiced by Michael Stipe (Himself). Notable quotes: Much on, Kirk.
quotes: Much on, Kirk.

title: Strangles
text: Strangles is A pet python briefly owned by Bart Simpson, later adopted by Groundskeeper Willie. Strangles is a green pet python that Bart bought to fill the void left when Santa's Little Helper joined the police force. His time as Bart's pet is short-lived and chaotic, culminating in an accident at school during show and tell that creates a dangerous toxic cloud. Though not a major character, Strangles plays a pivotal role in a dramatic rescue scene where both he and Santa's Little Helper try to save an unconscious Bart. Ultimately, Bart's loyalty remains with his dog, leading to Strangles being given up. He finds a new home with Groundskeeper Willie, who keeps him as an unusual pet in a fire hose cabinet at the school. As a non-speaking animal character, Strangles never has dialogue but serves as a memorable one-episode plot device.

title: John Wayne
text: John Wayne is Real-world actor referenced/appearing as a character in Simpsons canon, notably in the afterlife/heaven and hell settings. John Wayne is depicted as a deceased celebrity who pops up in the show's various afterlife-related storylines rather than as a regular cast member. He is namedropped by Homer as one of the eligible bachelors in Heaven, alongside other deceased icons like Tupac Shakur and the fictional Sherlock Holmes. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he appears in Hell, being woken up by Satan's noogie-induced shouting match with Homer. He later shows up in Celebrity Heaven, unhappy about his likeness being exploited for advertising after death. Wayne is also mentioned in old wartime correspondence and in Krusty's photo collection, reinforcing his status as a legendary star name-dropped for humor and nostalgia rather than an active participant in the show's plots. Voiced by Karl Wiedergott.

title: Skeleton judge
text: Skeleton judge is A non-canon judge from Hell who presides over Homer Simpson's trial in a Treehouse of Horror segment. The skeleton judge is a spooky, otherworldly figure who serves as the presiding authority in a courtroom located in Hell. He appears bald and skeletal, fitting the macabre, comedic horror tone of the segment he's featured in. His role is largely procedural, opening and overseeing the court session with a stern, judicial demeanor. Despite the absurdity of the trial's premise, he takes his duties seriously, nearly ruling against Homer before being interrupted by new evidence. He represents a classic parody of courtroom drama, transplanted into a devilish, otherworldly setting for comedic effect. As a non-canon character, he exists only within this special Halloween-themed story. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Fernando Vidal
text: Fernando Vidal is A hired assassin brought in by Mr. Burns to kill Abe Simpson. Fernando Vidal is a self-proclaimed master assassin hired by C. Montgomery Burns to eliminate Abe Simpson so Burns could claim sole ownership of the Flying Hellfish fortune. Despite his reputation as the world's most devious killer, his attempts on Abe's life are comically inept, ranging from poisoning dentures to a poorly executed disguise as Homer. His grand finale, storming a retirement home with a machine gun, ends in embarrassing failure when an elderly nurse scares him off with a shotgun. Vidal's character plays on the trope of the deadly professional who is ultimately undone by absurd circumstances, adding dark comedy to the episode's crime caper plot. He later appears as a villain character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Stogie
text: Stogie is Pianist and singer who works at MoHo House, appearing in a minor role connected to Moe. Stogie is a musician employed at MoHo House, where he plays piano and sings for patrons. He's shown to be accommodating, willing to take requests like playing 'Moonglow' for Moe, though he initially misunderstands whether Moe means the song or the drug of the same name. Beyond simple requests, he also crafts a more personal, commentary-driven song for Moe that reflects on his life situation. He later provides romantic musical accompaniment for Homer and Marge as they dance. His character is a clear homage to Sam, the piano player from the classic film Casablanca, fitting the moody, lounge-like atmosphere of MoHo House. Stogie remains a background figure whose main function is to underscore emotional moments for other characters through his music. Voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.

title: Dr. Velimirovic
text: Dr. Velimirovic is A plastic surgeon at the Stomach Staples Center who has treated several members of the Simpson family and Moe. Dr. Velimirovic is a recurring plastic surgeon in Springfield known for handling both cosmetic and medical procedures. He speaks with a thick Eastern European accent and has a habit of exclaiming references to Nicolae Ceaușescu, hinting that he may hail from Romania. His practice sees him working on Moe's disastrous face reconstruction, Marge's liposuction gone wrong, and Homer's stomach stapling surgery. Despite occasional mix-ups in his operating room, such as accidentally giving Marge breast implants meant for someone else, he remains a trusted, if slightly quirky, medical professional in town. He's also shown to be somewhat community-minded, attending events like a funeral and a town meeting about Lake Springfield. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Great Ceaușescu's ghost!
quotes: Great Ceaușescu's ghost!

title: Waldo
text: Waldo is A minor Springfield resident based on the 'Where's Waldo?' book character, appearing briefly in various episodes. Waldo is a background character in Springfield who is essentially a cameo appearance of the famous 'Where's Waldo?' book character. He rarely speaks or interacts directly with the main cast, instead popping up in the background of scenes, much like his book counterpart hides in busy illustrations. He's referenced when Otto asks Marge if she owns any of his books, and he's later spotted in Ned Flanders' bomb shelter during a citywide emergency, as well as walking past the Simpsons' kitchen window. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, Bart flips through a Waldo book and jokes about Waldo's lack of effort in hiding. Overall, Waldo functions as a fun crossover easter egg rather than a fully developed character. Notable quotes: He's just not trying anymore.
quotes: He's just not trying anymore.

title: Denzel Washington
text: Denzel Washington is Real-world actor referenced in the show via a poster and a fictional monument; not an actual character with dialogue. Denzel Washington appears in the Simpsons universe only as a background reference rather than an active character. He is depicted through a brochure for a tourist attraction called The Denzel Washington Monument, one of the vacation options considered by the Simpson family. He also shows up as a photo on a poster of notable black men displayed inside a barber shop, which inspires Carl to get a haircut styled after him. Since he never speaks or interacts with the main cast, he functions purely as a visual gag and pop-culture nod. There are no notable personality traits or running gags attached to him within the show itself, as he remains a non-speaking, picture-only presence.

title: Hikaru Sulu
text: Hikaru Sulu is Star Trek character parodied in Simpsons crossover parody segments. Hikaru Sulu is a parody appearance of the famous Star Trek helmsman, appearing in animated spoof segments within The Simpsons. He is depicted as an elderly, cane-using crew member aboard the Enterprise, poking fun at the aging original cast of the Original Series films. In one segment he calmly reports a Klingon threat to a bored, complaining Captain Kirk, highlighting the joke that the crew has grown old and weary of their duties. In another appearance, within a Christmas Carol-themed parody, he serves as Kirk's dutiful officer, reporting ghostly happenings and following orders even as chaos ensues aboard the ship. Sulu's role is largely comedic and background, existing to reinforce jokes about the tired, aging Star Trek universe rather than to develop as an independent character within the Simpsons universe. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: there are Klingons on the starboard bow
quotes: there are Klingons on the starboard bow

title: Gogo Yubari
text: Gogo Yubari is An assassin who appears in a flashback attacking Wayne Slater during his CIA training. Gogo Yubari is a minor, non-speaking character who appears only in a brief flashback sequence tied to Wayne Slater's past as a CIA operative. She is depicted as a skilled and dangerous assassin, wielding a large meteor hammer as her weapon of choice. Her attack ultimately backfires when Slater kicks the weapon back at her, causing its chain to wrap around her own neck and strangle her. The character is a direct crossover reference, borrowed from the Kill Bill film series rather than being an original Simpsons creation. She has also appeared in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out under a different guise as a secret villain.

title: Cassidy Spuckler
text: Cassidy Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's numerous children. Cassidy Spuckler is one of the many offspring of the notoriously unkempt hillbilly couple Cletus and Brandine. She's a background member of the sprawling Spuckler brood, rarely singled out for individual storylines but occasionally appearing in family scenes. She was present when Cletus rounded up his kids after receiving a stack of free pretzel tokens from Marge, and later tagged along on a family outing to the Springfield Air & Space Museum. At one point she joined her siblings in singing to help persuade Cletus to come back home to the family. As a non-speaking character, Cassidy exists mostly as visual filler representing the chaotic size of the Spuckler clan, and even her apparent height has been noted to change inconsistently between appearances.

title: Starla (A Milhouse Divided)
text: Starla (A Milhouse Divided) is A minor character who briefly dated Kirk Van Houten after his divorce from Luann. Starla is a rough-around-the-edges woman who briefly became romantically involved with Kirk Van Houten during his post-divorce rebound phase. She has a hard-living, disreputable air about her, marked by heavy smoking and drinking, and wears wigs to hide her gray hair. Claiming to work as a temp at a local radio station, she supposedly promised to help jump-start Kirk's stalled music career, though nothing seems to have come of it. Adding to her unsavory reputation, she ends up stealing Kirk's car, showing her willingness to use and discard the people around her. Despite her brief appearance, she represents one of the low points in Kirk's string of bad luck after his marriage falls apart. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Walt (Futurama)
text: Walt (Futurama) is Non-canon comic-book character, one of Mom's sons from Futurama who appears in a Simpsons/Futurama crossover story. Walt is one of the sons of the ruthless businesswoman Mom from Futurama, making him part of a family dynamic built on intimidation and subservience. He shares a brother, Larry, and a half-brother, Igner, both of whom mirror his role as a put-upon underling. When the citizens of Springfield are transported to New New York in a crossover story, Walt finds himself on the receiving end of a wedgie from Springfield bully Kearney, showing he's not immune to humiliation even in his own city. He and his brothers are also shown being physically pushed around by both his mother and Mr. Burns, once Burns is placed in charge of MomCorp's western division. This suggests Walt occupies a fairly powerless position within his family's corporate empire, often serving as comic relief through being bullied by more dominant figures. As a non-canon character, his appearances are limited strictly to Bongo Comics crossover issues rather than the television series.

title: Betty White (character)
text: Betty White (character) is Real-life celebrity guest character who appears as herself in cameo roles within the Simpsons universe. Betty White appears in the show as a fictionalized version of herself, playing off her real-world fame from The Golden Girls. She's shown as fiercely committed to public broadcasting, going so far as to shame viewers into donating and even organizing a mob of PBS characters to hunt down a deadbeat pledger. Despite this intense side, she's also portrayed as unexpectedly warm and down-to-earth, treating an awkward paparazzo with kindness rather than the diva behavior he expected from celebrities. Her appearances are brief but memorable, blending her wholesome public image with a comedic edge tied to PBS fundraising culture. She mostly exists as a one-off gag character who pops up in a couple of episodes and gets referenced elsewhere. Voiced by Herself. Notable quotes: If you watch even one second of PBS and don't contribute, you're a thief. A common thief!
quotes: If you watch even one second of PBS and don't contribute, you're a thief. A common thief!

title: Trucker 4
text: Trucker 4 is A minor truck driver character who appears in the episode 'Maximum Homerdrive'. This trucker is one of several anonymous truck drivers who share a secret about the Navitron Autodrive System, a technology that lets their trucks drive themselves. He spots Homer atop his truck's hood while bragging about the secret to a busload of tourists, and quickly alerts his fellow truckers to stop him before he exposes their scam. Along with his companions, he takes part in a tense highway chase, forming a blockade to try to stop Homer from reaching Atlanta. Despite their efforts, Homer escapes, and the truckers decide to move on to a new scheme involving smuggling Beanie Babies. He later makes a brief cameo appearance as one of the many faces on a wall of people who have abandoned Nelson. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Steve Urkel
text: Steve Urkel is A crossover/reference character from the sitcom Family Matters who appears or is mentioned in several Simpsons episodes. Steve Urkel is not an original Simpsons character but a real sitcom figure from Family Matters who pops up repeatedly as a pop-culture reference within the show. He's treated as a famous, somewhat iconic TV personality in the Simpsons universe, referenced by name-brand cereal, magazine covers, and even a stage production of Othello. His fame is so pervasive that his likeness alone can incite a mob when a fan is mistaken for him. He briefly appears in person during a meeting about the fate of television broadcasting, standing alongside other TV figures like Krusty the Clown and Bumblebee Man. Homer even compares an alien's voice and schedule to Urkel's, showing just how ingrained the character is in Springfield's cultural consciousness. Overall, Urkel serves as a running gag and nostalgic nod to 90s television rather than a fleshed-out character within the show itself.

title: Mrs. Wong
text: Mrs. Wong is Minor recurring character; mother of Hubert Wong and wife of Mr. Wong. Mrs. Wong is a background parent figure in Springfield, most notable for being Hubert Wong's mother. She's shown participating in ordinary school and community activities, such as bringing cupcakes to her son's first-grade class for his birthday. She also appears as an audience member at live podcast recordings hosted by local figures like Tabitha Shingle and Kent Brockman. As a family, the Wongs are depicted attending community events together, including a Bounce-A-Thon. She doesn't have a strong individual personality showcased in the show, functioning mainly as part of the extended cast of Springfield parents. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Rubella Scabies Spuckler
text: Rubella Scabies Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children, a minor recurring baby character. Rubella Scabies Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring belonging to the Spuckler family, known for their rural, chaotic household. Her unusual middle name came about when her father Cletus asked Lisa to spell the word 'Scabies' while Lisa was practicing for a spelling bee. She first appeared under odd circumstances, discovered by Homer when he unwrapped what he thought was a bag of sugar, only to find her inside instead. As a non-speaking character, Rubella has no dialogue and mostly exists as background detail emphasizing the sprawling and disorganized nature of the Spuckler clan. She has made brief appearances since her introduction, including in a group family photo. Her character is less about individual traits and more about contributing to the running joke of the Spucklers having an ever-growing, hard-to-track number of children.

title: Mark Twain
text: Mark Twain is Real-world American author referenced within the Simpsons universe, mostly via a nude photo in Mr. Burns' collection. Mark Twain, born Samuel Clemens, appears in the Simpsons universe as a historical figure rather than an active character. He is best known in the show for the bizarre detail that Mr. Burns owns the only existing nude photograph of him, kept alongside other absurd treasures like Excalibur and the Venus de Milo in his mansion's basement. Twain's legacy is also honored by Springfield's schoolchildren, who put on a play based on his stories for Mark Twain Day. In non-canon material, he becomes a bit of a running joke, including a local theater billboard claiming Duffman portrayed him, and an appearance in a Treehouse of Horror-themed mobile game update. Overall, Twain functions as a real-world literary reference used for humor rather than a fleshed-out character with personality traits of his own within the show.

title: Yahweh
text: Yahweh is The Jewish god, appearing alongside other deities in a minor role. Yahweh is a divine figure representing the Jewish faith who appears briefly in the show's exploration of world religions. He is depicted arguing with the Christian God over the religious status of Krusty, showing a somewhat bickering, all-too-human dynamic between the deities. When the disagreement escalates, he suggests consulting Mazda for a resolution, only for God to dismiss the idea due to Mazda's drunkenness. This mirrors the episode's comedic take on interfaith debates by portraying gods as squabbling like ordinary people. Yahweh's appearance is brief but memorable, fitting into the show's tradition of irreverently blending religious commentary with humor. He also appears in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out as part of a holiday-themed event. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Taekwon Dracula
text: Taekwon Dracula is A fictional character within the show's fictional franchise Ki-Ya Karate Monsters, referenced as a toy/collectible in the Simpsons universe. Taekwon Dracula is a fictional monster character existing within the show-within-a-show franchise Ki-Ya Karate Monsters, blending the classic vampire mythology of Count Dracula with the martial art of Taekwondo. He doesn't appear as an active character interacting with the main cast, but rather exists as merchandise within the Simpsons universe, notably as a wall sticker decorating Comic Book Guy's apartment. This nods to the show's frequent parody of collectible franchises and geek culture ephemera. As a non-speaking character, he has no dialogue or personality traits displayed on screen. His most substantial appearance comes in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, where he was featured during a Treehouse of Horror-themed event. The character represents the show's tendency to create elaborate fictional media properties that exist only in the background of Springfield.

title: King Snorky
text: King Snorky is Non-canon villainous dolphin antagonist from a Treehouse of Horror segment. King Snorky is a dolphin that Lisa frees from captivity at Marine World, only for the creature to turn on humanity. Once liberated, he reveals a surprising ability to speak English and rallies a dolphin army to violently drive the citizens of Springfield off dry land and into the sea. He becomes a direct enemy of the Simpson family, who are forced to battle his forces before defeating him by knocking him into a tank of electric eels. Beyond his original Treehouse of Horror appearance, he resurfaces as a video game villain, appearing as one of God's enemies in a rhythm-based sequence and later in mobile game content. He represents a classic Simpsons parody of nature-turns-on-humanity horror tropes, elevated by the absurdity of a talking, army-leading dolphin king. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Bruce Vilanch (character)
text: Bruce Vilanch (character) is Real-life comedy writer who appears as himself in a minor role, providing a joke for Principal Skinner. Bruce Vilanch appears as a fictionalized version of himself, a comedy writer known for penning material for celebrities like Whoopi Goldberg. In his sole appearance, he supplies Principal Skinner with a pun-based joke to use during a school mural dedication, which falls flat with the audience. Rather than acknowledging that the joke itself was weak, Vilanch smugly assumes the failure was due to Skinner's delivery rather than his writing. He's shown as somewhat out of touch, casually dressed in a Fred Flintstone T-shirt while watching the disastrous speech unfold. The joke serves as a running gag about awkward silence and public humiliation, with Skinner sarcastically thanking Vilanch afterward. His brief cameo pokes fun at behind-the-scenes Hollywood comedy writers and their inflated sense of their own material's quality. Voiced by Bruce Vilanch (Himself). Notable quotes: Well, thank you, Bruce Vilanch. | Whoopi would've made it work.
quotes: Well, thank you, Bruce Vilanch.
Whoopi would've made it work.

title: Yupprechaun (2)
text: Yupprechaun (2) is Minor background character; a modernized leprechaun seen in Ireland during the Simpsons family's visit. The Yupprechaun is a bizarre hybrid character encountered by the Simpson family while traveling through the once-quaint town of Dunkilderry, which has since become unexpectedly modernized. Grampa Simpson coins the term to describe the strange creatures, blending the traditional image of a leprechaun with the trendy, self-important demeanor of a yuppie. Rather than speaking in coherent sentences, the Yupprechauns are shown babbling nonsensical phrases and random words as they walk down the street. Later, they appear in a bar setting where their odd, whimsical behavior continues, including a playful and intimate moment between two of them. The character serves mostly as a one-off visual gag poking fun at cultural modernization clashing with old-world folklore. It has no formal name, family, or occupation, existing purely as a comedic curiosity within the episode's Irish setting. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Stan Taylor
text: Stan Taylor is A football player for the Springfield Atoms, appearing briefly in the show. Stan Taylor, nicknamed 'The Boy,' is a member of the Springfield Atoms football team who competes against the Shelbyville Sharks in the Pigskin Classic. He's introduced as a hard-partying celebrity type, known for lingerie models and wild nights, embodying the excesses of fame. His life takes a turn when Ned Flanders convinces him that there's more to life than his hedonistic lifestyle, leading him to become a devoted Christian. He has an adoring group of fangirls who chant his name in support during games. Later, he makes a brief cameo appearance in stock footage, seen relaxing in a pool with his teammates during a bye week in a Super Bowl commercial. Overall, Stan serves as a minor but memorable side character tied to Springfield's football culture and Ned Flanders' influence. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Stan, Stan, he's our boy, if he can't do it, no one... will.
quotes: Stan, Stan, he's our boy, if he can't do it, no one... will.

title: Steven Spielberg
text: Steven Spielberg is Real-world film director referenced and occasionally appearing as a background/look-alike character in the show. Steven Spielberg appears in The Simpsons mostly as a celebrity reference rather than a fully realized character. He is famously the director Mr. Burns wanted for his vanity biopic, but since the real Spielberg was unavailable, Burns settled for a cheap impersonator instead. Beyond that gag, Spielberg is mentioned as the owner of a fancy car and is said to be beloved even by a dying robotic dinosaur attraction. A look-alike of him shows up singing in a crowd of celebrity doubles, and he's later spotted dining among other Hollywood figures at a trendy restaurant. He never has any real speaking role, functioning purely as a punchline or cameo nod to his real-world fame.

title: St. Sebastian
