text: St. Sebastian is Historical/religious figure referenced in Springfield lore; early Christian saint and martyr appearing in comics, dreams, and parades. St. Sebastian is a real-world Christian martyr who appears in The Simpsons through various in-universe references rather than as a living character on the show. He's depicted as a pious Roman soldier who was executed with a hail of arrows for spreading Christianity under Emperor Diocletian. His legacy shows up in odd ways in Springfield, from a school named after him to Ned Flanders cosplaying as him for a religious parade. He even makes a nightmarish appearance in one of Ned's visions of hell, where the Devil literally consumes and regurgitates him. In a non-canon afterlife gag, he's shown still riddled with arrows while waiting impatiently in Heaven's lobby. His image was also parodied in a Simpsons calendar spoofing famous Renaissance artwork of the saint. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: St. Sebastian was a pious Roman soldier. For preaching Christianity to the Romans, the Emperor Diocletian sentenced him to death by hail of arrows. | Hey man, I've been waiting here a long time.
quotes: St. Sebastian was a pious Roman soldier. For preaching Christianity to the Romans, the Emperor Diocletian sentenced him to death by hail of arrows.
Hey man, I've been waiting here a long time.

title: Yoda
text: Yoda is Star Wars character who crosses over into The Simpsons universe in various references and cameos. Yoda is the diminutive, wise Jedi Master from Star Wars who appears in the Simpsons universe mostly as merchandise, background references, and crossover gags rather than a fully developed character. He shows up as a bust and Magic 8 Ball figure in Comic Book Guy's shop, a LEGO figure on a toy catalog cover, and a statue in Professor Frink's dorm room. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he takes on the role of a wedding officiant, marrying two unlikely fantastical characters. Other gags include a child dressed as him at a fan convention and Bart mistakenly calling another wizard-like character by his name. Overall, Yoda's presence in the show is a running series of nods to Star Wars fandom rather than a storyline of his own. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Husband and wife I pronounce you now.
quotes: Husband and wife I pronounce you now.

title: Tanya
text: Tanya is One of Lisa Simpson's friends and a fellow attendee of the Enriched Learning Center for Gifted Children. Tanya is a minor recurring background character best known as one of Lisa's childhood friends, frequently seen alongside her and Janey. She enjoys simple, gentle activities like picking flowers and crafting, fitting her role as a quiet, gifted schoolchild rather than a fleshed-out personality. As a student at the Enriched Learning Center for Gifted Children, she was present in Bart's class during the infamous test-swapping incident with Martin Prince. Although she was planned to be a more prominent character in early Simpsons tie-in fun books, complete with her own cut-out theater figure, she never gained a substantial role in the actual show and remains a non-speaking character. Despite this, she holds the distinction of being the most frequently appearing of the gifted classmates introduced in "Bart the Genius."

title: Wesley Spuckler
text: Wesley Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children. Wesley Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring belonging to the backwoods couple Cletus and Brandine Spuckler. Like many of his siblings, he exists mostly in the background of the Spuckler family's chaotic household scenes, rarely if ever speaking on screen. His most notable moment comes when his father calls him along with the other children to announce dinner after receiving free pretzel tokens from Marge. Wesley embodies the running gag of the Spuckler family having an overwhelming and often uncountable number of children. He has appeared in a handful of episodes, typically as part of a background gag rather than in a speaking role.

title: Uncle Ant
text: Uncle Ant is A minor cartoon character within the show-within-a-show Itchy & Scratchy franchise, appearing as merchandise in the actual Simpsons universe. Uncle Ant is a background character invented for the fictional spin-off program Itchy & Scratchy and Friends Hour, existing in the Simpsons world mainly as licensed merchandise rather than an active character with dialogue. He is depicted as an orange ant and appeared alongside other short-lived spin-off creations like Disgruntled Goat and Klu Klux Clam. His main claim to fame is being sold as a doll at Itchy & Scratchy Land and later as a plush toy during the franchise's 75th anniversary celebration at Comic Book Guy's shop. The joke surrounding him is that he's an obscure, forgettable addition to the Itchy & Scratchy universe, unrecognized even by devoted fans like Lisa. He never speaks or takes independent action in the show, existing purely as a piece of in-universe merchandise and trivia.

title: Clancy Wiggins
text: Clancy Wiggins is An army brigadier general in Springfield, minor recurring character. Clancy Wiggins is a high-ranking military officer stationed in Springfield, holding the rank of brigadier general. His main claim to fame in the show comes from a mix-up involving a jet pack he ordered, which ended up being mistakenly sent to Chief Wiggum instead of him. This error led to a chaotic chase as Wiggum tried to evade Wiggins and his soldiers, culminating in the destruction of the First Church of Springfield. Beyond this incident, he has also made a brief appearance at a pee-wee football game, suggesting some involvement in community events despite his military role. Wiggins shares a similar last name with Chief Wiggum, which seems to be the source of the delivery confusion. He's a minor character whose presence highlights the show's penchant for absurd bureaucratic errors and small-town chaos. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Springfield Super Squadron
text: Springfield Super Squadron is A comic-book-only superhero team composed of alter egos of many Springfield residents. The Springfield Super Squadron is a parody superhero team that exists only in the Simpsons comic book spin-offs, poking fun at classic superhero team tropes. Nearly every notable resident of Springfield gets a costumed alter ego, from Homer's Ingestible Bulk to Bart's Bartman to Marge's Entangler. The joke lies in how mundane character traits are exaggerated into ridiculous superpowers, such as Barney's Black Belch or Otto's Human Torque. Even background characters like Wendell and the Van Houten kid get in on the action with names like Kid Queasy and The Scarlet Whimpernel. The team has appeared across a handful of comic storylines, always played for laughs rather than serious continuity. As a non-canon group, it never factors into the show's actual televised universe.

title: Jack Sparrow
text: Jack Sparrow is A crossover/parody reference to the Pirates of the Caribbean character, appearing only as an image or costume in the Simpsons universe. Jack Sparrow isn't an actual character in the Simpsons universe but rather a recurring visual reference to the famous pirate captain from the Pirates of the Caribbean films. He first appears as artwork on a DVD cover that Bart accidentally creates out of manure, and later resurfaces as a design inspiration for a Transformer parody and as a costume worn by other characters. Krusty dons a Jack Sparrow costume for a comedy sketch, while in a non-canon Halloween special, a Mummy character dresses up as him. Since he never physically appears as an active participant in any story, he has no dialogue and functions purely as a background gag or pop-culture nod. His inclusion highlights the show's frequent parody of popular film franchises.

title: Francine Smith
text: Francine Smith is Crossover character from American Dad!, appearing briefly in The Simpsons. Francine Smith is the wife of Stan Smith, imported into The Simpsons universe as a crossover reference to American Dad!. She appears without any dialogue, existing mainly as a visual cameo rather than an active participant in the story. In one instance, her image is used as an example of "dad jokes" shown to attendees at Man Camp. In a non-canon appearance, she and her family attend a celebration at 742 Evergreen Terrace marking the premiere of the show's twenty-fifth season. Beyond these brief nods, little is explored about her personality or role within the Simpsons continuity, as she functions purely as an Easter-egg style crossover character.

title: Addem-up Spuckler
text: Addem-up Spuckler is One of the many Spuckler children, part of the extended redneck family in Springfield. Addem-up Spuckler, also called Taylor, is one of the numerous offspring of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler. Like his siblings, he blends into the large, chaotic Spuckler brood and is rarely singled out for individual attention. He has worked at Mother Hubbard's Sandwich Cupboard Express, sometimes covering shifts for his nocturnal siblings. He also contributes musically to the family by playing kazoo in the Spuckler Family Band, as part of a group nicknamed 'The Fabulous Skunk Holler Horn Section.' He was among the children who joined in singing to help convince Cletus to return home to the family. As a non-speaking recurring character, his presence mostly reflects the sprawling, disorganized nature of the Spuckler household.

title: Slava
text: Slava is Minor recurring character; a Russian taxi driver and father of Zhenya, Bart's piano teacher. Slava is a Russian immigrant who becomes a taxi driver in Springfield after learning to drive later in life. He's Zhenya's father, and his connection to the family comes through Bart's infatuation with his daughter, which led Bart to take piano lessons just to be near her. Marge actually taught Slava to drive so he could earn money to cover the cost of those piano lessons, showing a somewhat unconventional and resourceful side to how he entered the workforce. His path to becoming a licensed driver wasn't entirely by the book, as he secured his license through a bribe involving new pants for Patty and Selma. Slava is a minor, comedic side character whose presence ties into the show's exploration of Bart's awkward childhood crushes and the lengths people go to for family. Voiced by Bill Hader.

title: Dylan Spuckler
text: Dylan Spuckler is One of the many children of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, part of the extended Spuckler family in Springfield. Dylan Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of the backwoods couple Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, blending into the large, chaotic brood of siblings collectively known as the Spuckler children. Dylan appears in various family scenes, from being called to dinner to joining a family outing at the Springfield Air & Space Museum. Like other Spuckler kids, Dylan has been used by Brandine as part of efforts to keep the family together, including singing to lure Cletus back home. Dylan also shows a musical side, contributing beatboxing to the Spuckler Family Band. Overall, Dylan exists mostly as a background member of the sprawling Spuckler clan, appearing in family-oriented storylines rather than having an independent arc. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Truckasaurus II
text: Truckasaurus II is A robotic dinosaur attraction featured at the Springfield Demolition Derby, sequel to the original Truckasaurus. Truckasaurus II was built as a scientifically updated version of the original Truckasaurus, designed to reflect newer paleontology theories about dinosaur appearance. Unfortunately for the robot, its debut did not go well, as the crowd at the Springfield Demolition Derby reacted with hostility, booing it and hurling objects until it collapsed. In a strangely humanizing moment, the broken machine expressed its admiration for filmmaker Steven Spielberg as it fell. Despite this inauspicious end, it was memorialized afterward in an 'In Memoriam' segment, only to be booed once again by the unforgiving crowd. Its brief existence plays into the show's recurring gag of over-the-top, poorly received spectacle attractions in Springfield. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Derek Smalls
text: Derek Smalls is Bassist of the fictional rock band Spinal Tap, a minor real-world musician character appearing in Springfield. Derek Smalls is a musician who plays bass for the band Spinal Tap. He appears in Springfield when the band performs a stop of their world tour there. He's also glimpsed at a Grammy party attended by the Be Sharps, suggesting he mingles in the same music industry circles as Springfield's own celebrities. As a real-world crossover character, he doesn't have much depth beyond his connection to Spinal Tap's antics. His appearances are brief, mostly cameo-like, reinforcing the show's habit of blending real bands and personas into its universe. He remains a recurring but minor presence rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Elizabeth Warren
text: Elizabeth Warren is Real-world American politician and US senator referenced/depicted in cameo appearances within the Simpsons universe. Elizabeth Warren appears in the show not as a fleshed-out character but as a real-world political figure referenced through pictures and mentions. Homer keeps a poster of her in his workplace office, treating it with an oddly affectionate gesture. She's also glimpsed in a crowd scene and is credited as the narrator of an audiobook that Bart gives to Lisa as an apology gift. In non-canon material, her image even shows up as a dartboard target inside a Trump-themed hotel, playing into the show's satirical political humor. Overall, she functions as a topical cameo rather than a fully developed character, appearing mostly through pictures and brief mentions across a handful of episodes.

title: Robert Wagner (character)
text: Robert Wagner (character) is Real-life actor who appears as himself in a menopause instructional video shown to Selma Bouvier. This entry features actor Robert Wagner playing a fictionalized version of himself within the show's world. He appears hosting an educational video about menopause that Dr. Hibbert has Selma watch, delivering awkward, overly cheerful commentary on the subject. His attempt at a punny sign-off backfires comically when he refuses to say the line but it airs anyway, poking fun at scripted, corny educational media. Beyond this cameo, his fame is referenced humorously in another episode, where a bank associate is excited about his supposed visit. The character is a one-off gag relying on the absurdity of a respected actor being attached to such an embarrassing project. Voiced by Robert Wagner (Himself). Notable quotes: What do you know? She's out of eggs. And if you're watching this, so are you. | So let's all give menopause a round of men-applause.
quotes: What do you know? She's out of eggs. And if you're watching this, so are you.
So let's all give menopause a round of men-applause.

title: Channing Tatum (character)
text: Channing Tatum (character) is Real-life actor who appears as himself in a Simpsons episode, cast to portray Homer Simpson in a movie. Channing Tatum appears as a fictionalized version of himself, playing the role of Homer Simpson in a movie called Streaming Valor. He gets the part after Homer strikes a deal with movie producers, promising film rights to his life story to whoever could convince Tatum to gain enough weight to resemble him. A producer succeeds in this odd task, leading to Tatum's involvement in the project. Beyond this storyline, he also makes a non-canon cameo appearance in a special segment called Oscar Selfie. His character is largely a celebrity cameo used for comedic effect rather than a deeply developed personality within the show's main narrative. Voiced by Channing Tatum.

title: Troubled son
text: Troubled son is A minor child-actor character who appeared in a fictional TV commercial for Dr. Monroe's Family Therapy Center. The troubled son is a fictional child actor who appears in a satirical television advertisement for a family therapy center. In the ad, he walks in on his squabbling parents and delivers a line telling them both to be quiet, shifting from a soft tone to an angry shout for comedic effect. Beyond this brief acting gig, he also had a small extra role in the first McBain movie, appearing just after McBain's Captain falls into a fountain. He doesn't have much characterization outside of these two appearances, functioning mainly as a one-off gag character used to poke fun at overly dramatic self-help commercials. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Why don't you both shut up!
quotes: Why don't you both shut up!

title: David Spade
text: David Spade is Real-world actor and comedian referenced within the Simpsons universe. David Spade appears in the show as a cultural reference rather than a fully developed character. He's mentioned as a comedic point of comparison, notably when Homer likens himself to Spade minus Chris Farley during a moment of marital insecurity. His fictional show 'Jody's World' is glimpsed on a sign at the FOX studio lot, poking fun at the real-world FOX network's programming. In a non-canon Treehouse of Horror segment, he appears alongside Farley in a slapstick movie watched by Homer as the last man on Earth. Spade doesn't speak or interact directly with the Simpsons family, functioning purely as a background pop-culture nod tied to comedy and FOX-related humor.

title: Kevin Smith (character)
text: Kevin Smith (character) is Real-life filmmaker who appears as himself in cameo roles in The Simpsons. Kevin Smith appears as a fictionalized version of himself, the real-world actor, director, and comic book writer. In the show, he becomes unwittingly entangled with Homer, who had lied his way into an event by pretending to be Smith's father. When Homer's carelessness leads to a building burning down, Smith is left confused and asks his supposed father what happened. He is also referenced as having released an album that ranks among Comic Book Guy's favorite records, tying him into the show's pop-culture-obsessed side characters. In a non-canon appearance, he shows up at a glitzy movie premiere, fitting his real-life persona as a film industry figure. Overall, Smith serves as one of many celebrity cameos used by the show to blend real-world personalities with Simpsons-style absurdity.

title: Miss Viola
text: Miss Viola is A minor recurring character who took in the Simpsons' dog Bongo (renamed Hendrix) to protect him from Mr. Burns. Miss Viola is a countryside woman living just outside Springfield who ends up caring for the Simpsons' dog after he's threatened by Mr. Burns. She's shown to be a devoted pet owner, quickly renaming and settling the dog into a happy new life on her property. She lives with her wife, though this leads to an awkward moment when Abe mistakenly assumes her wife is a husband, causing offense to both women. Miss Viola later reaches out to the Simpson family with a thoughtful gesture, sending a Christmas card featuring the dog resting on Homer's old sweatshirt. Though she only appears in one episode plus a brief cameo, she represents a warm, responsible presence outside the main cast's chaotic world. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Zack (The Old Man and the Key)
keys: zack (the old man and the key)
text: Zack (The Old Man and the Key) is A resident senior at the Springfield Retirement Castle, minor recurring character. Zack is an elderly ladies' man living at the Springfield Retirement Castle who enjoys charming the female residents. His main claim to fame among the seniors is stealing Zelda away from Abraham Simpson, largely thanks to his minivan equipped with a wheelchair ramp, which made him more appealing than his rival. He later appears among a group of retirees heading off on a bus trip to Atlanta. Zack doesn't have much depth beyond his role as a rival to Grampa Simpson and a stereotype of a smooth-talking senior citizen. He appears only briefly across a couple of episodes and a spin-off book. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Malibu Stacy (character)
text: Malibu Stacy (character) is Fictional character who is the basis for a popular line of dolls owned by Lisa Simpson and other children in Springfield. Malibu Stacy is a doll character within the Simpsons universe, essentially a parody of Barbie, whose merchandise is beloved by kids like Lisa. She has appeared as a stage character in a musical, portrayed by an unnamed actress. In one imaginative sequence, Lisa envisions her own Malibu Stacy dolls coming to life during a town-wide lockdown, showing how deeply the toy is woven into childhood fantasy in Springfield. In a non-canon storyline, a Malibu Stacy doll ventures out from Malibu Stacy Land searching for the fan who loves her most, only to be met with hostility as the recipient tries to maintain a tough exterior. The character mostly exists as a symbol of idealized girlhood and consumer culture rather than having a personality of her own across canon appearances. Voiced by Tress MacNeille, Yeardley Smith, Grey DeLisle.

title: Tom Turkey
text: Tom Turkey is A non-canon imaginary turkey creature that appears in a Treehouse of Horror segment. Tom Turkey is a bizarre, non-canon creature who exists only within the fictional world of a Treehouse of Horror Halloween special. He is summoned to life after Milhouse prays for a savior to save him from the villainous Grand Pumpkin. Initially intended to be a helpful, friendly holiday figure representing Thanksgiving, his purpose twists into something sinister once Bart explains the holiday's tradition of eating turkey. This revelation triggers a violent turn, and Tom begins attacking and devouring people instead of helping them. His brief appearance plays into the show's tradition of dark comedic horror parodies. Outside of his Halloween debut, he also shows up in a title screen gag and as a collectible decoration in a mobile game spin-off. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Venus Williams (character)
text: Venus Williams (character) is Real-life tennis player who appears as a guest character, sister of Serena Williams. Venus Williams appears as a fictionalized version of herself in the Simpsons universe, brought in as a real professional athlete for a comedic sports storyline. She's recruited by Homer to fill in for Lisa during a charity tennis match, showing a willingness to go along with the show's absurd celebrity cameo premise. Her participation leads to a slapstick moment involving Marge's hair, tying her briefly into the family's chaotic antics. Beyond this appearance, she's referenced as attending a premiere event in a non-canon story, reinforcing her status as a celebrity figure within the show's world. Her role is minor and largely functions as a guest-star cameo rather than a developed character. Voiced by Herself.

title: Wayne Slater
text: Wayne Slater is Former CIA agent who became a Springfield Nuclear Power Plant security guard and later a DMV employee, befriending Homer. Wayne Slater is a stoic, guarded man who hides a violent past as a CIA agent behind the mundane job of a security guard. He is reluctant to form close relationships, preferring solitude and distance from co-workers, but ends up unwillingly bonding with Homer after a chance encounter in the rain. His skilled, lethal combat abilities are revealed when he single-handedly stops Snake from robbing Moe's Tavern. Beneath his tough exterior, he carries deep trauma from his past missions, suffering flashbacks tied to a deadly rivalry with a man named Viktor. Despite his cold demeanor, he grows close to the Simpson family, even teaching them self-defense moves. When Homer is kidnapped, Wayne's history catches up with him, culminating in a violent rescue that finally allows him to retire from his secretive life. On Marge's advice, he settles into a quieter existence working at the Springfield DMV. Voiced by Kiefer Sutherland. Notable quotes: I prefer not to have social interaction with co-workers.|Wayne Slater
quotes: I prefer not to have social interaction with co-workers.|Wayne Slater

title: Marv Szyslak
text: Marv Szyslak is Moe Szyslak's brother, part of the Szyslak family involved in the Mattress King business. Marv is one of Moe Szyslak's siblings, raised in the family business of selling mattresses under the Mattress King brand. As a child, he appeared alongside his family in commercials for the store. He has a contentious relationship with Moe, often siding with his sister Minnie against their brother, especially after their father Morty divided the family business among his children. Marv is shown to be somewhat hot-headed and eager to provoke Moe, willingly participating in sabotage against his store. Despite this rivalry, there are hints of underlying family bonds, as seen when an old commercial briefly reminds the siblings of their shared history. He later appears in the audience for a couple of in-universe podcast recordings, suggesting he remains a minor recurring presence in Moe's orbit. Voiced by Chris Edgerly.

title: Minimum Wade Spuckler
text: Minimum Wade Spuckler is One of the many Spuckler children, part of Cletus and Brandine's extended family. Minimum Wade Spuckler is one of the countless offspring of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, blending into the sprawling and chaotic Spuckler brood. Like his many siblings, he's rarely distinguished as an individual, often appearing as part of a group rather than having a unique personality showcased on screen. He has taken shifts working at Mother Hubbard's Sandwich Cupboard Express, stepping in for his more nocturnal siblings when needed. He was also among the Spuckler children enlisted by his mother Brandine to sing in an effort to lure Cletus back home to the family. As a non-speaking character, Minimum Wade exists mostly as background family filler, contributing to the running gag of the Spucklers having an overwhelming and hard-to-track number of children.

title: Nigel Tufnel
text: Nigel Tufnel is Lead guitarist of the band Spinal Tap, a minor real-world celebrity character who appears in Springfield. Nigel Tufnel is a fictionalized version of the mockumentary rock star, brought into the Simpsons universe as the guitarist of Spinal Tap. He shows up in Springfield while on tour with his bandmates, giving fans of the band a crossover cameo. He's later glimpsed at a Grammy party attended by the Be Sharps, suggesting he moves in the same celebrity music circles as Springfield's own barbershop quartet. His appearances are brief and largely non-speaking, functioning more as a nostalgic nod to Spinal Tap fans than a fleshed-out character. He has no family or personal history explored within the show. His role is essentially a background cameo rather than a recurring storyline character. Voiced by Christopher Guest.

title: Werewolf
text: Werewolf is A non-canon monster character appearing primarily in Halloween specials, married to She-Wolf. The Werewolf is a minor monster character who exists in the non-canon Halloween universe of the show. He socializes with other classic monsters like Frankenstein's Monster, Count Dracula, and Amenhotep, notably joining them on a shopping trip for Halloween costumes. His attempt at a costume disguise as Harry Potter leads to a comedic domestic dispute when his wife, She-Wolf, catches him flirting with other women at a party and attacks him. Beyond his brief appearance in the Treehouse of Horror franchise, he's referenced only in passing in a couple of regular episodes. The character also appears in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, expanding his presence into that spin-off universe. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Britney Spears (character)
text: Britney Spears (character) is Real-world celebrity guest character; pop singer who appears in Springfield as herself. Britney Spears appears as a fictionalized version of herself, brought into Springfield's world as a celebrity guest star. She's portrayed as wildly popular with the public, easily overshadowing local news anchor Kent Brockman during a shared hosting gig. Her signature bit involves an oddly dangerous kiss of congratulations that inadvertently causes the death of an elderly award recipient, played for dark comedic effect. She's referenced elsewhere in pop-culture-savvy jokes, including being name-checked by other characters as a symbol of contemporary celebrity culture and tabloid fame. Even a background character imitates her gap-toothed grin as a marker of trendiness. Her presence in the show reflects the series' recurring use of real celebrities to satirize fame and pop culture. Voiced by Herself. Notable quotes: Look! A people tooth! | Now I's jes' like Britney Spears.
quotes: Look! A people tooth!
Now I's jes' like Britney Spears.

title: Grandpa Van Houten
text: Grandpa Van Houten is Kirk Van Houten's father and Milhouse's grandfather, a minor recurring character. Grandpa Van Houten is an elderly member of the Van Houten family, having divorced his first wife before remarrying and taking to the open road. He and his second wife spent their retirement traveling the country in an RV, chasing adventure wherever they could find it, including a memorable win at a chili cook-off in Beaumont, Texas. Despite his rambling lifestyle, he still makes time for family, showing up to support his grandson Milhouse at Springfield Elementary's grandparents day events. He's a background figure in the Van Houten family tree, rarely central to the plot but appearing as a nod to the extended, quirky relatives that populate Springfield. His character underscores the show's running theme of the Van Houtens as an eccentric, often troubled family line. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Toadstool jockey
text: Toadstool jockey is A minor jockey character residing in Jockey Town, appearing in a Simpsons episode about horse racing. The toadstool jockey is a small, background resident of Jockey Town, a community of tiny jockeys who befriend Homer after he takes up horse racing. He joins his fellow jockeys in a group musical number aimed at pressuring Homer into throwing a race. Notably, he's the one who directly instructs Homer to intentionally lose an upcoming race, making him a small but functional plot device in the episode's storyline. Like many one-off Simpsons characters, he has no deep characterization beyond his brief appearance and role in the jockey subplot. He later shows up again only through reused archive footage in a later episode. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Francesca Terwilliger
text: Francesca Terwilliger is Sideshow Bob's second ex-wife, an Italian woman who joined the Terwilliger family's criminal schemes against the Simpsons. Francesca Terwilliger is introduced as the Italian second wife of Sideshow Bob, with whom she shares a son named Gino. Like the rest of the Terwilliger clan, she is drawn into the family's twisted vendetta against the Simpson family, conspiring alongside Bob, his parents, and their son to exact revenge on Bart. Her involvement in this plot lands her in prison along with the rest of the family, marking her as a willing accomplice rather than an innocent bystander. After this, her marriage to Bob seems to quietly dissolve, as he is later shown living alone and eventually moving on to other relationships. She largely exists as a supporting piece of the larger Terwilliger family lore, appearing mostly in connection to Bob's criminal schemes and family ties rather than as an independent character with her own storyline. Outside of the show's canon, she has also appeared in tie-in media like The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Maria Grazia Cucinotta.

title: Steven Tyler (character)
text: Steven Tyler (character) is Real-world celebrity cameo appearance; lead singer of Aerosmith who appears as himself in Springfield. Steven Tyler appears in the show as a real-world celebrity guest, portraying himself alongside his bandmates from Aerosmith. He's depicted performing live music at Moe's Tavern, showing the band's willingness to lend their star power to Springfield's oddball locals. He also turns up as part of the crowd at industry events like the Grammy Awards, brushing shoulders with Springfield's own musical group, the Be Sharps. Later, he's spotted among the crowd at a parade for the Boston Americans, showing his continued presence in the town's background events. As a real-world character voiced by a guest star, Tyler doesn't have an extensive personality arc in the show but instead serves as a fun cameo tying Springfield to real celebrity culture. Voiced by Steven Tyler (Himself).

title: Tribal Chief
text: Tribal Chief is Manager of Caesar's Pow-Wow Casino, briefly encountered by Bart Simpson. The Tribal Chief runs the day-to-day operations of Caesar's Pow-Wow Casino with meticulous attention to detail, keeping tabs on everything from the laundry to gamblers' losses. He moonlights as a shaman-like mystic figure, offering visions of the future to those who toss a treasured item into a ceremonial fire. Despite his stern and businesslike demeanor, he shows a softer side when discussing his brother, Crazy Talk, revealing genuine family concern beneath his mystical persona. He's easily annoyed by disruptions to his ritual, particularly explosive ones, but maintains a dry, coy wit when questioned about his supernatural abilities. His role ties him to a broader web of reservation characters and casino lore introduced during Bart's misadventure. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: Who says I'm not? | That's crazy talk! | That's my brother, Crazy Talk. We're all a little worried about him.
quotes: Who says I'm not?
That's crazy talk!
That's my brother, Crazy Talk. We're all a little worried about him.

title: Dr. Zaius
text: Dr. Zaius is Fictional ape doctor character from the musical Stop the Planet of the Apes I Want to Get Off, a parody of Planet of the Apes. Dr. Zaius is a parody character based on the Planet of the Apes franchise, appearing within the show-within-a-show musical starring Troy McClure. He serves as a comedic riff on the classic sci-fi character, existing mainly as a stage role rather than a fully fleshed-out Simpsons character. His most notable moment involves interacting with Troy McClure's character and offering him the chance to play piano during a musical number. Beyond the musical itself, Dr. Zaius has become a popular costume choice among Springfield's fandom culture, appearing at sci-fi conventions like Bi-Mon-Sci-Fi-Con and Ape-Con. Comic Book Guy notably dressed as him for one of his convention costumes, cementing the character's status as a niche pop-culture reference within the show. He doesn't have an ongoing personality of his own beyond this satirical, theatrical context. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Thad
text: Thad is Minor recurring character in Springfield, former husband of Julio Franco. Thad is a minor character best known for his brief marriage to Julio Franco, officiated by Homer Simpson. He is a non-speaking character, which means the show never gives him dialogue to establish much personality. His relationship with Julio dissolves at some point, as Julio is later shown reconciled with his old partner Grady, implying a breakup between Thad and Julio. Despite this, Thad and Julio are later seen together again at a wedding, leaving their exact status ambiguous. His storyline reflects the show's ongoing inclusion of LGBT characters and relationships in later seasons. Overall, Thad exists mostly as a background figure tied to Julio's romantic history.

title: Springfield University student
text: Springfield University student is An unnamed minor student attending Springfield University, appearing briefly in a few episodes. This character is a nameless background student at Springfield University who pops up in a handful of unrelated scenes across the series. He's most memorable for his role at a college party where Homer Simpson, posing as a student, spikes the punch bowl. After drinking some, he oddly announces to the other partygoers that their parents will be arriving soon to pick them up, a strange and comedic non-sequitur reaction to the spiked drink. Beyond that odd moment, he has no real personality traits explored, serving purely as a background gag character. He later resurfaces as a face in the crowd at a Krusty the Clown special and again as an attendee of the Springfield Cabbage Festival. His hair color is noted to change from blond to brown between appearances, though this is never explained. He remains an anonymous fixture of Springfield's collegiate and community life. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Iggy Wiggum
text: Iggy Wiggum is Deceased father of Chief Clancy Wiggum and grandfather of Ralph Wiggum. Iggy Wiggum was a World War Two veteran who served in the Flying Hellfish squad alongside Abraham Simpson and a young C. Montgomery Burns. He shared his son Clancy's bumbling, absent-minded nature, notably once leaving an unpinned grenade loose in his own backpack. Despite his clumsiness, he held himself to a stricter moral code than some of his comrades, objecting when Burns tried to loot paintings from a captured castle. Before the war, he had a poverty-stricken youth in Slobtown, scavenging horse dung for coins and buttons with a young Joe Quimby Sr. He met an unfortunate end in 1979, dying alongside four fellow Hellfish members in a parade float accident, and was laid to rest at the Flying Hellfish memorial in Springfield Cemetery. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Tumi
text: Tumi is A second-grade classmate of Lisa Simpson at Springfield Elementary School. Tumi is a young girl who briefly becomes Lisa's close companion after stepping in as her square dancing partner in gym class. She shares Lisa's interests, joining her for record shopping, listening to NPR, and drinking veggie smoothies, which makes their friendship seem like a perfect match. However, it's later revealed that Tumi was actually paid by Marge to befriend Lisa, only intending the arrangement to last until she could afford a nice belt. Despite this mercenary start, she admits to genuinely growing fond of Lisa. Tumi also has a quirky, somewhat blunt personality, casually mentioning her fondness for horse meat and questioning Lisa's vegetarian assumptions about her, which ultimately drives Lisa away. She is later shown to be intellectually gifted, attending advanced classes at Springfield STEM Academy. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Swamp Hag
text: Swamp Hag is A villain character from the fictional Radioactive Man comic books referenced within The Simpsons universe. Swamp Hag is a comic-book supervillain who exists within the world of Radioactive Man, the fictional superhero comic that Bart and his friends read. She appears as the antagonist in the issue Radioactive Man vs. Swamp Hag, which Bart owns a copy of. As a non-speaking character, she has no dialogue or developed personality shown on screen, functioning more as a background reference to deepen the show's parody of comic book culture. In a non-canon video game tie-in, she takes on a more active role as the very first boss enemy players must defeat. Her design and role tie into the show's larger fictional Radioactive Man mythology, which spoofs classic superhero comic tropes. She remains a minor, largely obscure figure within the Simpsons universe.

title: Monét X Change (character)
text: Monét X Change (character) is Guest character appearing as herself, a real-life drag queen featured in a Simpsons episode. Monét X Change appears in the show as a version of herself, the real American drag queen. Her storyline involves a bizarre incident referenced by George R. R. Martin's research, where she's seen in a viral video having a comedic altercation with fellow drag queen Bob the Drag Queen at a Waffle House. The dispute is famously trivial, centering on proper spoon etiquette for a mint bowl, and it escalates into a spontaneous dance-off rather than real conflict. Off-camera lore notes that while Monét identifies as non-binary, she uses she/her pronouns while performing in drag. She's a minor recurring guest character rather than a core cast member, appearing briefly across a couple of episodes. Voiced by Herself.

title: Wayne the Grip
text: Wayne the Grip is A grip working on Krusty the Clown's TV show, part of his behind-the-scenes crew. Wayne is a long-serving but largely unnoticed member of Krusty's production crew, having worked on the show since its earliest days without Krusty ever knowing his name. He's a working-class guy juggling family troubles, including bailing out his stepson's illegal street racing hobby, which makes him anxious about job security. When Krusty suddenly tries to bond with him, Wayne responds with genuine hospitality, inviting him to a crawfish boil, though the gathering quickly turns disastrous. Despite his friendly gesture, Wayne turns out to be quietly cynical about Krusty, seeing through his sudden interest as fake. His arc highlights the show's recurring theme of Krusty's disconnect from the people who work for him. In a non-canon Halloween story, Wayne is shown to carry a gun and uses it to kill a demon-possessed Mr. Teeny. Voiced by Ike Barinholtz. Notable quotes: Krusty didn't know any of his "work family" and had never attended any events with them.
quotes: Krusty didn't know any of his "work family" and had never attended any events with them.

title: White chocolate rabbit
text: White chocolate rabbit is A minor non-canon character appearing in The Simpsons Game, encountered in Homer's dream of The Land of Chocolate. This character is a rabbit sculpted entirely from white chocolate, existing only within a fantastical dream sequence conjured by Homer's imagination. It appears in The Land of Chocolate, a candy-themed dreamscape that represents pure indulgence and excess. The rabbit taunts Homer by claiming he's devouring its territory, sparking a comedic chase across the sugary landscape. The gag culminates in Homer catching and eating the rabbit atop an enormous cake, embodying the show's classic humor about Homer's gluttony. Beyond the game, the character also makes a cameo appearance as an image on a coin used in a football-themed spin-off, adding a small extra layer to its brief but memorable existence. Its non-canon status keeps it firmly in the realm of parody and dream logic rather than the show's main continuity. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Thanos
text: Thanos is Crossover supervillain from Marvel Comics who appears in non-canon segments and gag references on The Simpsons. Thanos is the imposing, purple-skinned Marvel villain best known for his quest to collect the Infinity Stones and wipe out half of all life in the universe. In his Simpsons appearances he mostly shows up as a joke or cameo rather than a fully developed character, fitting into the show's various crossover specials and gag segments. In one non-canon bit, he mistakes Maggie's pacifier for the final Infinity Stone and uses it to turn most of the Simpson family to dust. He's also referenced as a betting subject on a fictional gambling website and listed among suspects in a lighthearted mystery about Lisa's missing college fund. Comic Book Guy is even shown cosplaying as him during a parody of Avengers-style events. In another gag, Thanos is shown snapping away not just half of Earth's population but also a handful of Disney princesses and fairy tale characters, poking fun at Disney's ownership of both Marvel and those properties. Voiced by Maurice LaMarche.

title: Slavedriver Willie
text: Slavedriver Willie is A non-canon alternate version of Groundskeeper Willie, appearing as a slavedriver for the Pharaoh in a Bart-imagined biblical dream sequence. Slavedriver Willie is a fantastical, non-canon incarnation of the show's usual groundskeeper, reimagined as a taskmaster overseeing pyramid construction in ancient Egypt. He enforces discipline among the enslaved workers with a whip, showing little patience for anyone who slacks off during their labor. His role escalates when Bart, in the dream, disrespects the Pharaoh's sarcophagus, prompting Willie to switch from a lenient whip to a harsher one to punish everyone. The character is a one-off gag appearance rather than a fixture of the main continuity, existing only within a dream sequence framing device. He later resurfaced as a collectible character skin in a mobile game tie-in, further cementing his status as a whimsical, non-canonical variant. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Pediculus Spuckler
text: Pediculus Spuckler is One of the numerous Spuckler children, part of Cletus and Brandine's extended family. Pediculus Spuckler is one of the many offspring belonging to Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, fitting into the show's running gag of the family having an overwhelming and ever-expanding brood of kids. He's shown to be a working member of the family, pitching in at Mother Hubbard's Sandwich Cupboard Express when needed. Like most of his siblings, he doesn't have a distinct personality of his own in the show, instead existing as part of the collective Spuckler children gag. He appeared at a family dinner that Homer attended, blending into the chaotic Spuckler household dynamic. He was also among the siblings enlisted by Brandine to sing in an effort to lure Cletus back to the family. As a non-speaking character, he remains largely in the background of the episodes he appears in.

title: Kate Spayed
text: Kate Spayed is A doberman puppy who becomes the pet of Waylon Smithers, Jr.. Kate Spayed is a doberman puppy born into a litter descended from the original Dobermann breeding line, initially raised under Mr. Burns' orders and trained by Smithers using Homer as a practice dummy. Deemed too gentle-natured to be given away as a bribe gift, she was instead adopted by Michael de Graaf, Smithers' boyfriend at the time. She unwittingly becomes a turning point in their relationship when Michael reacts cruelly after she accidentally spills his wine, prompting Smithers to end things with him and keep her for himself. Since then, she has remained Smithers' loyal companion, even accompanying him on outings like a visit to Little Vest Park. Her name is a playful nod to real-world fashion designer Kate Spade, and it was revealed by the show's writing staff rather than stated on-screen.

title: Cody Spuckler
text: Cody Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children. Cody Spuckler is a member of the sprawling, backwoods Spuckler family, one of the many children belonging to Cletus and Brandine. He is a non-speaking character, existing mostly in the background of the show's redneck family gags rather than as an individual personality. Cody's one notable trait is his musical contribution to the family: he plays kazoo in the Spuckler Family Band. Alongside siblings Birthday, Jitney, and Taylor, he forms part of a quartet jokingly dubbed the horn section of the group. Beyond this, little else distinguishes him from his numerous brothers and sisters, reflecting the show's running joke about the Spucklers having an uncountable number of children with unusual names.

title: US marine
text: US marine is Minor recurring character; a U.S. marine stationed at American embassies who briefly interacts with the Simpson family. This unnamed marine serves as a stern guardian of U.S. government property abroad, first appearing at the American Embassy in Australia and later at the embassy in Tokyo. He's a no-nonsense figure who takes his duty seriously, explaining diplomatic technicalities to Bart and not hesitating to use force against Homer when provoked. His role is largely functional, representing the intersection of the Simpsons' misadventures with official bureaucracy and international law. Despite his minimal screen time, he leaves an impression through his physical response to Homer's antics and his role in turning the family away when they seek help in Japan. He embodies a rigid, by-the-book military demeanor typical of background authority figures in the show. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Snitchy the Weasel
text: Snitchy the Weasel is A minor character who appears as an alter-ego on the dark web, encountered by Bart, Nelson, and Milhouse. Snitchy the Weasel is a strange digital figure tied to the shady corners of the internet, functioning as a snitch who threatens to report wrongdoers to the FBI. He emerges from Hacky, a helpful dark web guide, transforming into this weasel persona whenever someone attempts illicit activity online. His role is brief but memorable, serving as a comedic warning system for kids dabbling in things they shouldn't. Snitchy embodies a satirical jab at online privacy concerns and the murky, untrustworthy nature of internet dealings. Despite his menacing threat of exposure, he still nudges characters along to accept the very terms that could get them in trouble, adding an ironic twist to his role. Voiced by Jon Lovitz.

title: Alex Trebek (character)
text: Alex Trebek (character) is Real-life game show host who appears as himself in cameo references throughout the series. Alex Trebek is portrayed in the show as the famous host of Jeopardy!, appearing mostly through references, mentions, and brief cameos rather than substantial storylines. He's referenced when Homer jokes about making him answer questions instead of ask them, playing on the show's trivia format. His image and persona pop up in the background of Springfield life, from a TV airing at Moe's Tavern to a photo hanging in a local restaurant. In a non-canon Halloween segment, his name is humorously invoked as part of a nonsensical incantation meant to raise the dead, lumped in with department store names. Overall, he serves as a pop-culture cameo character rather than a fully developed personality within the show. Voiced by Himself.

title: Shredder Stevens
text: Shredder Stevens is Guitarist for the band Sungazer, who recruited Apu as their lead singer. Shredder Stevens is a grizzled, gray-haired rocker who plays guitar for the band Sungazer. He and his bandmates recruited Apu Nahasapeemapetilon to become their new lead singer after the death of their previous frontman, Grant LeDavid. Shredder comes across as someone who makes promises he doesn't always keep, telling Apu he could have time off after a Springfield gig while admitting he'd also once promised to quit heroin. This suggests a somewhat unreliable, rock-and-roll lifestyle typical of an aging musician. He appears primarily as a minor figure tied to Apu's brief foray into the music world. Beyond his connection to Sungazer, little else is known about his personal life or history. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Ahsoka Tano
text: Ahsoka Tano is Non-canon Star Wars crossover character employed at Jabba's Hut Jedi Preschool in Simpsons/Disney+ specials. Ahsoka Tano is a crossover character brought into the Simpsons universe from Star Wars, working as a preschool employee with a rather unconventional disciplinary style. She has no qualms about freezing misbehaving children in carbonite and hanging them on a time-out wall, blending Star Wars imagery with mundane childcare duties for comedic effect. Beyond her preschool job, she pops up at various Disney+ promotional gatherings, showing she's as much a part of the Disney synergy machine as an actual character in the Simpsons world. She's also seen chauffeuring kids and parents around in her own vehicle to special events. As a non-speaking character, her humor comes entirely from visual gags and the absurdity of her role rather than dialogue. She represents the show's frequent parody of Disney's ownership and crossover branding.

title: Tammy (The Last of the Red Hat Mamas)
keys: tammy (the last of the red hat mamas)
text: Tammy (The Last of the Red Hat Mamas) is Leader of the Cheery Red Tomatoes, a women's society appearing in The Last of the Red Hat Mamas. Tammy is a minor recurring character who leads the Cheery Red Tomatoes, a social club for women. She is married to a man named Stanley. One of her defining traits is a strong personal dislike for Mr. Burns. Her orange hair is noted as being dyed, suggesting a flashy, image-conscious personality typical of social club leaders. She has appeared briefly across a handful of episodes and print materials rather than being a major storyline character. Voiced by guest star Lily Tomlin, she represents one of the many one-off adult female characters populating Springfield's social scene. Voiced by Lily Tomlin.

title: Slick
text: Slick is A publisher for TweenLit Inc. who appears in "The Book Job". Slick is the shady publishing executive that Homer's group turns to when trying to sell their ghost-written young-adult novel. He agrees to publish the book but insists on installing a fake author, leading to Lisa being chosen as the public face of the project. His true colors show when he unilaterally rewrites the book into a totally different story without the group's consent, then claims ownership over it, leaving them with no legal recourse. This betrayal sets off a heist-style plot as the group tries to reclaim their original manuscript. Ultimately, he is outmaneuvered when Lisa, motivated by a desire for fame, tips him off about the plan too late to stop the original book from being printed. He represents the exploitative, profit-driven side of the publishing industry in this storyline. Voiced by Andy García.

title: Troll (Treehouse of Horror XI)
text: Troll (Treehouse of Horror XI) is A minor non-canon creature appearing in a Treehouse of Horror segment, resembling Moe Szyslak. This Troll dwells beneath a bridge and, despite his gruff and unsettling appearance, genuinely just wants companionship. Unfortunately, his eagerness to connect with others tends to be off-putting, causing people to flee rather than befriend him. His look, voice, and demeanor closely mirror those of Moe Szyslak, making him something of a monstrous parody of the bartender. He appears in the segment "Scary Tales Can Come True" from Treehouse of Horror XI, existing outside the show's main canon. He later resurfaced as a character in The Simpsons: Tapped Out mobile game, referred to there as Bridge Troll Moe. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Dr. Steve (Pokey Mom)
text: Dr. Steve (Pokey Mom) is A chiropractor recommended to Homer Simpson by Dr. Hibbert. Dr. Steve is a minor recurring character who runs his own chiropractic clinic and briefly treats Homer Simpson for back pain. He's portrayed as a fairly ordinary, no-nonsense professional who tries to get through his sessions despite Homer's antics, including Homer falling asleep mid-treatment. When Homer later decides to set himself up as a rival, unlicensed chiropractor, Dr. Steve reacts with anger, calling him out for stealing his patients and resorting to physical violence. He's ultimately sidelined when other chiropractors steal Homer's invention before he can get to it himself. Despite his small role, he represents the legitimate, licensed side of the medical profession that Homer often clashes with in his get-rich-quick schemes. Voiced by Harry Shearer.

title: Chrissy Teigen (character)
text: Chrissy Teigen (character) is Real-life model and TV personality who appears as herself in a guest role helping Marge with a Springfield cause. Chrissy Teigen appears as a fictionalized version of herself, drawn into Springfield's affairs when Marge asks for her help. She's portrayed as an obliging celebrity who enjoys doing favors for her social media followers, agreeing to help persuade her husband John Legend to perform for the town. Despite her fame, she's shown handling mundane domestic matters, like reminding John to charge their kids' iPads. She also has a habit of capturing moments with fans through selfies, reflecting her real-world image as a social media personality. Her appearances are brief and tied to celebrity cameo humor rather than an ongoing storyline. Voiced by Herself.

title: Kurt Vonnegut
text: Kurt Vonnegut is Real-world author referenced/appearing in cameo form within The Simpsons universe. Kurt Vonnegut appears in the show as a nod to his real-world literary fame, mostly through references to his books rather than as a fully active character. Lisa is shown to be a devoted fan, packing multiple of his novels for a trip, including Timequake, and defending their necessity by claiming they self-reference one another. His works also show up on other characters' bookshelves, underscoring his status as a respected author within the Simpsons world. In a fantasy sequence imagined by Marge, he appears as a guest on Krusty the Clown's talk show, engaging in a brief discussion about the deeper meaning behind Slaughterhouse-Five. He's also listed among Ned Flanders' notable left-leaning figures, hinting at a political dimension to how the show portrays him. Overall, Vonnegut functions as a literary cameo, appearing mostly as a picture or mention rather than a speaking role. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Evelyn Trunch
text: Evelyn Trunch is Art teacher at Springfield Elementary School. Evelyn Trunch teaches art to the students of Springfield Elementary, including Bart Simpson's class. She is overly warm and encouraging, praising even the most half-hearted or bizarre student work, which grates on Bart, who has no interest in art. Her relentless positivity became the catalyst for one of Bart's stranger schemes, when he attempted to use voodoo to get her out of school and instead accidentally caused her to become pregnant, leading to town-wide gossip. She also appears as a stern quiz-giver, unwilling to tolerate students' nitpicky questions during class. Overall, she's a minor but memorable recurring background teacher known for her chipper, if oblivious, classroom demeanor. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Mrs. Trunch then told him to shut up and fill in the bubbles.
quotes: Mrs. Trunch then told him to shut up and fill in the bubbles.

title: Amy Wong
text: Amy Wong is A Futurama character (intern at Planet Express) who crosses over into The Simpsons universe via a special episode. Amy Wong is a human character from Mars who works as an intern at the Planet Express Delivery Company in the Futurama universe. She appears in The Simpsons through a crossover episode, bridging the two animated worlds. In her appearance, she plays a role in a time-travel related emergency, contacting her Futurama colleagues to warn them about a monster attack back at their headquarters. Her personality traits mostly stem from her established Futurama character rather than any deep development within The Simpsons canon. She serves as a fun nod to fans of both shows, existing primarily within comic book crossover stories aside from her animated debut. Her presence highlights the show's willingness to blend continuities for a lighthearted mash-up. Voiced by Lauren Tom.

title: Yo Yo
text: Yo Yo is Minor fictional character appearing in a children's TV show-within-the-show and in The Simpsons: Tapped Out game. Yo Yo is a minor character who first appears in the fictional cartoon 'Yo Yo and the Cloud Palace,' shown within an episode of The Simpsons. She is depicted riding a kangaroo, giving her an adventurous, whimsical air typical of a children's show protagonist. Little is revealed about her personality or backstory beyond this brief appearance. She later resurfaces as a collectible character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, tied to the Moe's Ark content. Her role is largely a background gag referencing the show's tendency to parody other children's media rather than a fully developed character. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Maw Spuckler
text: Maw Spuckler is Mother of Cletus Spuckler, elder member of the Spuckler family. Maw Spuckler is the matriarch of the sprawling, backwoods Spuckler clan and the mother of Cletus Spuckler. She's an elderly, gray-haired woman who appears only briefly in the show's canon, most notably on a family outing to a theme park. She's also referenced during one of Cletus's typically absurd mishaps, when he ends up stuck on a phone pole and calls out to her for help getting off a roof. Like much of the extended Spuckler family, she embodies the show's exaggerated hillbilly humor, existing mostly as background color for Cletus's chaotic home life. She has no lines of dialogue in her canonical appearances, making her a non-speaking character. Outside the main show, she also shows up as a collectible character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out.

title: Jennifer Tilly (character)
text: Jennifer Tilly (character) is Real-life celebrity guest character who appears in a poker instructional video watched by Lisa. Jennifer Tilly appears in the show as a version of herself, drawing on her real-world reputation as an actress and skilled poker player. Her main contribution to the Simpsons universe comes through an instructional video she made on how to play poker, which Lisa watches in hopes of boosting her college fund through winnings. Beyond this, her presence in the show is fairly minor, showing up as a background photo hanging in a local business and briefly in an opening sequence gag. She doesn't have an extensive personality or storyline within the show, functioning more as a nod to her real fame in both Hollywood and the poker world. Voiced by Herself.

title: The Tramp

title: Chloe Talbot

His signature bit involves emerging from Krusty's absurdly small clown car, only to get comically stuck while trying to climb out. The joke culminates in the reveal that his supposedly large rear end is actually just an inflated balloon, which deflates or is otherwise exposed as fake during his struggle. He has no deep backstory or personality beyond this single physical comedy routine, functioning purely as a background gag character in Krusty's circus-style performances. Despite his brief appearances, he has shown up more than once in the series as part of the recurring troupe of clowns. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Ali Rudy Vallée
text: Ali Rudy Vallée is A musical automaton owned by The Great Raymondo, appearing in the Simpsons universe. Ali Rudy Vallée is a robotic musical performer belonging to The Great Raymondo, designed to play songs as part of an act. Its brief appearance shows a bit of mechanical unreliability, as it stops playing partway through a performance, hinting at glitches typical of automaton characters in the show. The character's name is a playful nod to real-life singer and saxophonist Rudy Vallée, tying its identity to a bit of showbiz history parody common in The Simpsons' humor. Beyond its single canonical appearance, the automaton also exists in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out as a magic-themed decoration. It has no deep personality of its own, functioning more as a novelty background gag than a fully developed character. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Crystal Meth Spuckler
text: Crystal Meth Spuckler is One of the many children of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler. Crystal Meth Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of the hillbilly couple Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, and like her siblings, she's often swept up in the family's chaotic and impoverished antics. She briefly found herself in the spotlight when Krusty the Clown discovered her singing talent and put her and her siblings on his show performing crude songs about themselves. She's shown to have some musical ability, playing the didgeridoo in the Spuckler Family Band. Crystal Meth also appears to have a soft spot for dancing, stepping in to partner with Ralph when Lisa needed a partner during a school dance lesson. Her storylines mostly revolve around family loyalty, such as singing to help convince her father Cletus to return home, and enduring the general poverty and misfortune that surrounds the Spuckler household. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Snowy
text: Snowy is Fictional dog from the Tintin comic book series, referenced within the Simpsons universe. Snowy is a white wire fox terrier belonging to the comic book adventurer Tintin, existing as a fictional character within a comic series that Simpsons characters read. He resides in Paris alongside Tintin and Captain Haddock, having accompanied them on numerous adventures chronicled in the Tintin comic books. Within the show's universe, Snowy appears as artwork on comic covers rather than as a living, speaking character, making him a non-speaking crossover figure. Lisa is shown reading a Tintin comic featuring him at the Coolsville comic shop, and Bart owns a copy of another comic depicting Snowy on its cover. As a nod to the source material, the writers noted that although Snowy isn't shown on-screen during a particular musical scene, it's reasonable to assume he'd be present given how closely he sticks to Tintin in the original comics.

title: Smug girl
text: Smug girl is A minor background student in Bart Simpson's class at Springfield Elementary. The smug girl is a recurring but unnamed background character who appears throughout Bart's classroom scenes and around Springfield Elementary. She is instantly recognizable for the persistent smirk on her face, which gives her a perpetually self-satisfied or condescending look. As a minor character, her design isn't strictly consistent, and her hair color shifts between episodes, most often appearing brown or red, though other shades have appeared over the years. She has never been given a single line of dialogue in the entire run of the show, making her a purely visual fixture of the classroom crowd. Despite her silence and lack of development, she has shown up in an enormous number of episodes spanning decades, as well as in comics and other Simpsons media, cementing her as a beloved piece of background scenery for attentive fans.

title: Squawky
text: Squawky is A bald eagle briefly adopted as a pet by the Simpson family. Squawky was a wild bald eagle that first appeared as a threat, snatching small birds and even attempting to carry off baby Maggie before Homer intervened. After causing chaos around the Simpson household, including stealing a toy mouse from Bart's room, the eagle was captured by Homer using a broom and a plastic bag. Lisa convinced the family to nurse the injured bird back to health, and Bart gave it the name Squawky. Despite their efforts, the eagle's freedom was short-lived, meeting a sudden and unfortunate end after being released. Squawky never speaks, fitting the show's pattern of animal characters who exist mainly for physical comedy and brief emotional beats. The character also appears as a non-canon figure in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out.

title: Vivienne St. Charmaine
text: Vivienne St. Charmaine is Grampa Simpson's girlfriend and a former actress, introduced in "Podcast News". Vivienne St. Charmaine is a retired actress living at the Retirement Castle who becomes romantically involved with Abraham Simpson. She once starred in the TV show Falcon Landing and claims that dating Abe finally gave her something different from the string of younger men she used to pursue. Her relationship with Grampa gets caught up in a bizarre scheme involving a faked death, an insurance scam, and a murder investigation sparked by Kent Brockman's podcast. It turns out she and Grampa had planned the whole scheme together so they could collect insurance money and retire together in Mexico, though Grampa's memory problems complicate things. Despite the chaos, she ultimately returns to Springfield and settles down with Grampa in the Retirement Castle. She also appears in a non-canon musical number about the struggles of the elderly. Voiced by Morgan Fairchild.

title: Dr. Wolfe
text: Dr. Wolfe is The dentist who owns Painless Dentistry, treating Lisa's teeth in Springfield. Dr. Wolfe is a minor recurring dentist character best known for his role in Lisa's braces saga. He first appears telling Marge that Lisa needs braces at the worst possible time, since Mr. Burns had just revoked Homer's dental plan. Forced to work with a limited budget, he outfits Lisa with an embarrassingly outdated set of braces before she eventually gets a modern, invisible pair once the family's insurance is restored. Years later it's revealed he was actually an unlicensed, rogue periodontist all along, forcing Lisa to go through the ordeal of braces yet again. The character has an odd bit of trivia behind him, as the show originally tried to cast several notable actors for the role before settling on Hank Azaria. Overall, he's a background figure used mainly to drive Lisa's dental-related storylines. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Jon Stewart (character)
text: Jon Stewart (character) is Guest character based on the real-life comedian/actor, appearing during a Springfield presidential primary storyline. Jon Stewart appears as a fictionalized version of himself when Springfield becomes the site of the first presidential primaries in the country. During his visit, Krusty the Clown attempts to secretly steal jokes from him, leading to an awkward confrontation once Stewart notices. He reacts with irritation, expressing disappointment in how far Krusty has fallen as a comedian. Beyond his direct appearance, Stewart is referenced elsewhere in the show as a cultural touchstone, invoked in comparisons about public disdain and political fundraising. His image also shows up as background decor in at least one Springfield establishment. Overall, he serves as a topical guest-star cameo tied to real-world political and comedic commentary. Voiced by Jon Stewart.

title: Ernest P. Worrell
text: Ernest P. Worrell is A fictional movie character within the Simpsons universe, parody of the real-life Ernest franchise, referenced through films, posters, and a statue seen around Springfield. Ernest P. Worrell is a parody character existing within the show's fictional world, based on the real low-budget comedy film series starring Jim Varney. He never truly interacts with the main cast but appears as a recurring pop-culture reference through movie titles, posters, and memorabilia scattered across Springfield. His films have absurd titles that spoof the actual Ernest movies, showing up on theater marquees and even inspiring a stage play in New York City. A statue of him is later found in a hillbilly-themed museum exhibit, cementing his place as a running joke about lowbrow entertainment. Despite his frequent mentions, he is mostly a background gag rather than an active participant in the show's plots. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Lucius Sweet
text: Lucius Sweet is Boxing manager of Drederick Tatum and former manager of Moe Szyslak. Lucius Sweet is a flashy, wealthy boxing promoter modeled directly on real-life boxing figure Don King, right down to his signature look and larger-than-life persona. He first appears when he recognizes Homer's unexpected boxing talent and arranges for him to face his star fighter, Drederick Tatum. Before that, he had managed Moe Szyslak's own boxing career. He's shown moving in elite circles, attending Krusty's funeral, and later getting swept up in trouble alongside Gil and Homer over unpaid taxes. A minor running gag ties him to modern celebrity culture, noting he's Facebook friends with Mark Zuckerberg. Despite his limited screentime, his connection to Springfield's boxing world and his Don King parody status make him a memorable recurring figure. Voiced by Paul Winfield.

title: Tinker Bell
text: Tinker Bell is A Disney crossover character referenced in Simpsons media, inspiring one of Lisa's cosplay costumes. Tinker Bell is the classic fairy from the Peter Pan stories, appearing in the Simpsons universe mainly as a pop-culture reference rather than an active character. Lisa cosplays as her using household items, cleverly repurposing her mom's dress, her dad's belt, cotton balls on ballet slippers, and paper plates fashioned into wings. In a non-canon appearance, Tinker Bell shows up as an actual guest at a Disney+ anniversary party held at Moe's Tavern, arriving with a date. She has no spoken lines in either appearance, functioning purely as a visual cameo and nod to Disney's ownership of Fox properties. Her presence highlights the show's frequent habit of blending in outside franchises for comedic crossover effect.

title: Wind Lad
text: Wind Lad is Minor superhero character, sidekick to Citizen Solar and ally of Radioactive Man. Wind Lad is a lesser-known superhero within the Radioactive Man comic universe, serving as the sidekick to Citizen Solar. He appears alongside other heroes when Radioactive Man needs backup, though his powers seem underwhelming compared to his peers. A running joke about him involves the noise he generates, which apparently annoys people around him rather than impressing them. Charcoal Briquette notably calls out both him and Citizen Solar for lacking real energy or power. Despite his minor status, he's popular enough in Simpsons merchandising lore to appear as an action figure collected by fans like Comic Book Guy. He also exists as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Walter White
text: Walter White is Crossover character from Breaking Bad who appears briefly in The Simpsons via hallucination and a couch gag. Walter White is not truly a Simpsons character but a crossover figure borrowed from Breaking Bad. He appears in the show when Homer and Ned, under the influence of the drug U-completeamine, hallucinate themselves as the infamous meth-making duo of Walter White and Jesse Pinkman. In a separate, non-canon couch gag segment, he's shown sitting with Jesse Pinkman watching an episode of The Simpsons, played in live-action by Bryan Cranston, reprising his famous role. Notably, he has no dialogue in this appearance, making him a silent cameo rather than a fully voiced character. His inclusion is purely a pop-culture reference and homage to Breaking Bad rather than a meaningful addition to Simpsons canon.

title: Embry Joe Spuckler
text: Embry Joe Spuckler is One of the many Spuckler children, offspring of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler. Embry Joe Spuckler is one of the numerous children born to the backwoods couple Cletus and Brandine Spuckler. His most distinctive trait is that he remains attached to his mother by an umbilical cord well after birth, a running gag that highlights the family's exaggeratedly rustic and neglectful lifestyle. His name is a pun on the word 'embryo,' referencing the early developmental stage of a human being. Embry Joe doesn't have much individual personality shown, as he is largely a background gag character used to illustrate the chaotic and unconventional nature of the Spuckler household. He briefly appears when Cletus finally manages to find something to cut his umbilical cord, only for Brandine to nonchalantly feed him by drinking chocolate milk herself first. Voiced by Pamela Hayden.

title: Elizabeth Taylor (character)
text: Elizabeth Taylor (character) is Real-life celebrity who appears as herself in a guest role on The Simpsons. Elizabeth Taylor appears as a fictionalized version of herself within the Simpsons universe, portrayed as a genuine Hollywood star sought after for prestigious appearances. She is approached by Bart and Lisa to join the Krusty Comeback Special, but her overly protective agent initially blocks the request. Once she witnesses the special's triumphant success, she reacts by firing that agent, showing she values good judgment over blind loyalty from her staff. There's a touch of melancholy to her character, as she is shown wistfully looking in on the celebration afterward, seemingly left out. Beyond her main appearance, her image turns up as a background decoration and in a clip show about celebrities before they were famous, reinforcing her status as an iconic figure referenced throughout the series. Voiced by Herself.

title: Incest Spuckler
text: Incest Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children, a member of the Spuckler clan. Incest Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, part of the sprawling hillbilly family that recurs throughout the show. He was among the Spuckler children tutored by Lisa Simpson, and he gained a brief taste of fame when Krusty the Clown discovered the kids singing and put them on his show performing crude songs about themselves. That fame nearly led to a spot on Krusty's comedy tour before his mother intervened. Incest also has a musical side, playing the jug in the Spuckler Family Band. Like the rest of his family, he's associated with the Spucklers' impoverished, rural, and slightly lawless lifestyle, including being present when a meth lab connected to the family was raided by police. He appears mostly as a background or minor character rather than a focus of storylines. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Philippa Wickerbottom
text: Philippa Wickerbottom is A teacher at Miss Wickerbottom's Pre-Nursery School, involved in identifying Maggie Simpson's high IQ. Philippa Wickerbottom is a minor recurring character connected to the prestigious pre-nursery school that bears a similar name. She works alongside Henry, and together they discover that baby Maggie Simpson possesses an unusually high IQ of 167. Rather than nurturing this discovery, the school ultimately expels Maggie, with Philippa accompanying Henry to deliver the news at the Simpson household. She appears only briefly across a handful of episodes and the Simpsons Movie, functioning mostly as a background figure tied to the running gag of Maggie's secret genius. Little is revealed about her personal life or personality beyond her professional role in early childhood education. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Stan (Do PizzaBots Dream of Electric Guitars?)
keys: stan (do pizzabots dream of electric guitars?)
text: Stan (Do PizzaBots Dream of Electric Guitars?) is Minor recurring character; an internet troll and member of the Troll Force Five. Stan is a minor background character known primarily as an internet troll who runs with a group called the Troll Force Five. He has a knack for ruining things by loving them excessively, as shown when he dressed as Groot and blocked other moviegoers' view in a crowded theater. He was also spotted protesting outside the Aztec Theater against a film called Agents of P.I.Z.Z.A. Stan is a non-speaking character, appearing only briefly in a couple of episodes without dialogue. His personality is conveyed mostly through his obsessive fan behavior and troll-like antics rather than any spoken lines.

title: Darryl Strawberry (character)
text: Darryl Strawberry (character) is Real-life baseball player who appeared as a guest star, recruited to play for the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant softball team. Darryl Strawberry is a real-world baseball celebrity who was brought into the Simpsons universe when Mr. Burns had Smithers recruit top players for the power plant's softball team. He was hired to take Homer's roster spot, and notably was the only recruited ringer who avoided the bizarre string of misfortunes that befell the other star players. Despite his skill, Burns ultimately benched him in favor of Homer for the final crucial moment of the championship game, reasoning that both Strawberry and the opposing pitcher were left-handed. He's later referenced as being included on a list of notable left-handed people. In a non-canon appearance, he's shown attending a Simpsons season finale premiere event.
