Overall, his role is a brief but memorable cameo tied to one of the show's famous celebrity-athlete episodes. Voiced by Darryl Strawberry.

title: Orville Wright
text: Orville Wright is Historical figure (aviation pioneer) appearing in a Bart dream sequence on The Simpsons. Orville Wright is depicted as a non-canon, real-world historical character based on the actual American aviation pioneer who co-invented the airplane with his brother Wilbur. In the show, he appears only within a dream sequence experienced by Bart, where he is shown flying the Wright Flyer while Wilbur struggles to keep up on a bicycle. The scene plays on the sibling rivalry between the two brothers, with Wilbur frustrated at not getting a turn to fly. Orville's role is brief and comedic, existing purely as part of a fantastical dream rather than the show's main continuity. He has made only a couple of appearances in the series, mostly tied to this single dream concept. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Willie's mother
text: Willie's mother is Unnamed mother of Groundskeeper Willie. Willie's mother is a minor, unnamed background character tied to the Groundskeeper Willie mythos. She lives in Scotland where she runs a small bar, giving a glimpse into Willie's working-class Scottish roots. She appeared briefly when Willie visited her at Loch Ness, and later attended his wedding to Maisie MacWeldon, showing she remains a supportive presence in his life. In non-canonical material, her fate takes a darker comedic turn, as Willie claims she died in a haggis eating contest, which he references while competing in a Duff Eating Challenge in her memory. She's also mentioned in connection with Willie's brother Angus MacMoran and the World Groundskeeping Cup, tying her into the larger extended MacDougal family lore. Overall, she serves as a small piece of world-building that fleshes out Willie's family background rather than a fully developed character in her own right. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Adriatica Vel Johnson
text: Adriatica Vel Johnson is Minor recurring character; a political news reporter and ex-wife of Julio Franco. Adriatica Vel Johnson is a politically active news reporter and prominent member of the Democratic party in Springfield. She was once married to Julio, but their marriage ended after he came out and moved in with his partner Grady Little. She's shown covering a Springfield primary election, indicating her role as a media and political figure. On a talk show called Head Butt, she displayed a flirtatious and opportunistic side, making out with fellow guest Nash Castor and admitting she was looking for a wealthy husband. She's a clear parody of real-world political commentator Arianna Huffington, right down to a divorce storyline mirroring Huffington's own ex-husband's public coming out. Her surname is a nod to actor Reginald VelJohnson. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: she wanted a rich husband
quotes: she wanted a rich husband

title: Wyatt
text: Wyatt is Biological father of Carl Carlson and Carlotta Carlson, appearing in a flashback/family history episode. Wyatt is a minor character revealed to be Carl Carlson's birth father, discovered through a genealogy investigation on a parody of Finding Your Roots. He comes from a line of cowboys, descended from a former slave turned cowboy named Ellis, and Wyatt himself carried on that legacy as a bull rider. His claim to fame is surviving a full 20-second ride at the Okmulgee Oklahoma Rodeo, an accomplishment significant enough to earn him a commemorative belt buckle. That buckle becomes a meaningful heirloom, eventually passed down to Carl. Despite his rodeo achievements, Wyatt's personal life took a hard turn, as he gave up both Carl and Carlotta for adoption, leaving their later fate murky. He appears only briefly, mostly through historical narration rather than direct interaction with the main cast. Voiced by Alex Désert.

title: Gummy Sue Spuckler
text: Gummy Sue Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children, a minor recurring member of the Spuckler clan. Gummy Sue Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of Cletus and Brandine, embodying the same rustic, backwoods charm as the rest of her family. She first appears missing most of her teeth, delighted when her father hands her a stray tooth caught at a hockey game to fill the gap. Like her siblings, she's often seen as part of a background crowd of Spuckler children rather than getting much individual focus, appearing in family photos, at demolition derbies, and gathering gas cans with her dad. She also contributes musically to the family's unconventional band, playing the drum machine. Overall, she represents the comically large and chaotic Spuckler brood, popping up occasionally in family-centric storylines. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: Now I's jes' like Britney Spears!
quotes: Now I's jes' like Britney Spears!

title: Mr. Thai
text: Mr. Thai is Owner of the Thai restaurant You Thai Now in downtown Springfield, briefly employed Bart as a menu boy. Mr. Thai is a small business owner striving to keep his restaurant profitable enough to fund his daughters' college educations. He's resourceful and enterprising, going as far as heavily distributing menus across Springfield to drum up business. When he hires Bart as a menu distributor, he shows a patient, mentoring side, coaching the initially inept boy until he becomes surprisingly skilled at the job. His ambition sometimes veers into the ethically questionable, as seen when he attempts to purchase Springfield's oldest redwood tree just to turn it into more advertising menus. Overall, he's a minor recurring figure whose storyline intersects mainly with Bart's brief entrepreneurial adventures. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Springy
text: Springy is Mascot created by Homer Simpson for the Springfield Olympic Games. Springy is a spring-shaped mascot invented by Homer as a backup idea after his first attempt, Abby the Olympic Tabby, was rejected by his family. Made simply from a large coiled spring, Springy proved surprisingly popular and ended up winning a mascot contest sponsored by Channel 6, beating out Patty and Selma's competing entry, Ciggy. Despite the win, Springfield ultimately lost its bid to host the Olympics, rendering the mascot pointless. Left with a large shipment of unused springs, Homer comically tried offloading them onto others before eventually dumping them into the ocean. Springy is a non-speaking character and stands as one of Homer's many short-lived, half-baked inventions. The character later appeared in a minor capacity in other Simpsons media, including a mobile game.

title: Telephone operator
text: Telephone operator is An unnamed, recurring automated/voice-only telephone operator who appears in various phone-related mishaps involving Homer. This character is never given a name or physical appearance, existing only as a voice heard through the phone during moments of Homer's frustration. She typically delivers automated or bureaucratic messages, such as informing callers that a number can no longer be reached or explaining odd technical instructions. Her interactions with Homer often highlight his comedic misfortune, whether it's being unable to reach his kids, dealing with a malfunctioning dialing system due to his weight gain, or being denied help while trying to retrieve his car in New York City. She serves a functional, almost mechanical role in the show, appearing only when the plot requires a disembodied voice to deliver information or complications. Despite her minimal characterization, she recurs across several episodes, making her a small but memorable background presence tied to Homer's chaotic phone calls. Voiced by Joan Kenley.

title: Wink
text: Wink is Japanese game show host who appears in the Simpsons' Tokyo episode. Wink is the flamboyant and manipulative host of the deadly Japanese game show "Happy Smile Super Challenge Family Wish Show," which the Simpson family is forced to compete in to earn tickets home. He delights in devising absurd and dangerous challenges, including turning Homer into a human pinata and lightning rod, showing a gleeful disregard for contestant safety in pursuit of entertainment. Behind his cheerful on-air persona, he secretly berates his stagehands in Japanese when things don't go as planned. His sadistic streak is further shown when he later traps a couple with scorpions purely for a laugh. Despite his menace, Homer eventually manages to teach him and the audience a lesson about fairness in game shows. He later resurfaces hosting a separate show involving Santa's Little Helper's love interest, Suds McDuff. Voiced by George Takei.

title: Johnny Unitas (character)
text: Johnny Unitas (character) is Real-world football legend who appears as himself in a cameo role on the show. Johnny Unitas appears as a fictionalized version of himself, the famous American football player, making a brief guest appearance in the Simpsons universe. His main claim to fame in the show is hosting an infomercial for Lady Krusty's Moustache Removal System, where he interacts with a model testing the product. He comes across as terse and matter-of-fact, offering blunt responses rather than warmth or humor. He is also referenced by Grampa Simpson in a flashback, where his neat, timeless haircut is used as a point of comparison against fellow football star Joe Namath's more flamboyant look. Overall, Unitas serves as a minor real-world cameo character rather than a fully developed personality within the show. Voiced by Himself. Notable quotes: Probably.
quotes: Probably.

title: Muhammad Yunus (character)
text: Muhammad Yunus (character) is Real-world guest character; Bangladeshi banker who appears in a Lisa Simpson storyline. Muhammad Yunus appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, the real-life Bangladeshi banker famous for founding the Grameen Bank and winning the Nobel Peace Prize. His role in the series is tied to an educational internet presentation about micro financing, which Lisa Simpson watches while deciding how to help a struggling entrepreneur. In a lighthearted gag, his animated nose becomes an interactive, moving target that Lisa must click on with her cursor, turning a serious economic lesson into a bit of playful comedy. He doesn't have an extensive personality within the show beyond this cameo, since his purpose is largely educational and promotional, reflecting real-world humanitarian and economic themes. His appearance underscores the episode's charitable, microloan-focused plot rather than serving as a recurring comedic character. Voiced by Muhammad Yunus (Himself).

title: Joseph Stalin
text: Joseph Stalin is Real-world Soviet dictator referenced/mentioned in the Simpsons universe, occasionally appearing in pictures or the afterlife. Joseph Stalin appears in the show mostly as a historical name-drop rather than an active character, cited as an example of a horrible tyrant or communist figure. He's invoked in jokes ranging from Homer listing dead celebrities to Abe naming him during a Communist-hunting HUAC parody. Several townsfolk have personal, exaggerated connections to him, like Lenny claiming Stalin imprisoned his grandmother, or Agnes admitting her lifelong dream was to marry and then murder him. Mr. Burns has also referenced Stalin in villain-themed contexts, even claiming to have once met and sketched him. In non-canon material, Stalin turns up in the afterlife, playing poker and other games with fellow infamous historical villains. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta. Notable quotes: Don't worry, son. I'm sure he's up in Heaven right now laughing it up with all the other celebrities: John Dillinger, Ty Cobb, Joseph Stalin,... - Homer Simpson
quotes: Don't worry, son. I'm sure he's up in Heaven right now laughing it up with all the other celebrities: John Dillinger, Ty Cobb, Joseph Stalin,... - Homer Simpson

title: William Howard Taft
text: William Howard Taft is Real-world 27th President of the United States, referenced/appearing in the Simpsons universe. William Howard Taft appears in the show as a historical figure woven into Springfield's lore rather than a regular character. His most notable connection is a scandalous rumor that he once had an affair with Mr. Burns' mother, a fact Burns refuses to discuss and never forgave her for. He's also the subject of a running gag involving his portrait at Springfield Elementary, which already sports a moustache, foiling Milhouse's vandalism plans. Taft's image pops up elsewhere too, such as in a history book Superintendent Chalmers shows Bart. In a more bizarre twist, an animatronic version of Taft is used to help automate the Duff Brewery when Homer takes it over. Overall, he's treated as a piece of trivia and background reference rather than an active character in the story. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns can't stand talking to his mother. He never forgave her for having that affair with President Taft. | Taft, you old dog.
quotes: Mr. Burns can't stand talking to his mother. He never forgave her for having that affair with President Taft.
Taft, you old dog.

title: Teller (character)
text: Teller (character) is Real-life magician and comedian who appears as himself in guest cameo roles in The Simpsons. Teller is depicted in the show much as he is in real life: the quiet, non-speaking half of the magic duo Penn & Teller, standing alongside his partner Penn Jillette. His silent persona is played up as a running gag, most notably when he is quoted as saying essentially nothing at all about a rival magician's shop. In one storyline, he joins fellow illusionists Ricky Jay, Penn Jillette, and David Copperfield in a scheme against The Great Raymondo, hinting at a mysterious rivalry within the show's magician community. Outside of that darker plot point, his other appearances are brief cameos, including attending a red carpet event in Los Angeles. Overall, Teller functions as a novelty guest character whose humor comes from his real-world reputation for silence rather than dialogue-driven jokes. Voiced by Himself.

title: Slithers
text: Slithers is Non-canon character; loyal snake assistant to Lord Montymort in a Harry Potter-parody segment of Treehouse of Horror XII. Slithers is a green and yellow snake who serves as the devoted assistant to the villainous wizard Lord Montymort, a parody character clearly modeled on Voldemort's pet snake Nagini from Harry Potter. Despite his sinister master's schemes, Slithers shows genuine emotional attachment, offering practical advice like using Satan as a go-between to help capture Lisa Simpson. When Montymort is killed by Bart, Slithers reacts with overwhelming grief, weeping as he performs the grim snake instinct of swallowing his master's body whole. His mournful declaration of eternal devotion, delivered while consuming his master's corpse, blends dark comedy with a strange sincerity. Beyond his Harry Potter parody roots, Slithers doubles as a pun-based parody of Waylon Smithers, Jr., tying his loyal-assistant role to a familiar Simpsons dynamic. He remains a one-off Halloween special character who later appeared in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: In death, we shall be together always.|Slithers|Treehouse of Horror XII
quotes: In death, we shall be together always.|Slithers|Treehouse of Horror XII

title: Wiggle Puppy
text: Wiggle Puppy is Imaginary friend of Ralph Wiggum, a flying dog character that appears in his drawings and imagination. Wiggle Puppy is a whimsical creature born from Ralph Wiggum's imagination, depicted as a cream and brown dog who flies by spinning its tail. Ralph is known to act out being Wiggle Puppy, running around in circles, and even keeps a drawing of the creature in his bedroom. The character later takes on a surreal role when Chief Wiggum hallucinates Wiggle Puppy as a spirit guide after eating an extremely spicy pepper. In non-canon material, Wiggle Puppy is portrayed with a darker comedic twist, supposedly helping people in need but actually making their situations worse. The character has no spoken dialogue, existing purely as a visual and conceptual gag tied to Ralph's odd, childlike worldview.

title: Patrick Star
text: Patrick Star is Crossover character from SpongeBob SquarePants making brief cameo appearances in The Simpsons. Patrick Star is a starfish character borrowed from the animated series SpongeBob SquarePants who shows up only in fleeting, non-speaking cameos within The Simpsons universe. He first turns up as part of a museum exhibit photo display, appearing among a set of mollusc images rather than as an active participant in the story. Later he resurfaces as one of the images used in a captcha test designed to screen out overly intelligent cartoon characters online, though Lisa passes over his picture without clicking it. He's also referenced through a costume worn in a bonus segment, showing his presence extends slightly beyond simple images. Patrick never speaks or interacts directly with the Simpsons cast, existing purely as a visual nod to the crossover with Nickelodeon's undersea cartoon. His inclusion is a playful easter egg for fans of both shows rather than a meaningful narrative role.

title: Springfield Flight School employee
text: Springfield Flight School employee is Minor recurring character who works as an instructor at the Springfield Flight School. This gray-haired employee runs helicopter lessons at the Springfield Flight School and typically appears in only brief, functional scenes. He's shown to be a bit rule-bound at first, initially refusing service until proof or payment is provided. His most memorable moment comes when Barney Gumble, freshly sober, redeems a coupon for a free flight lesson, prompting the employee to relent and teach him to fly. Beyond this, he's a background utility character, later glimpsed piloting Arnie Pie's news helicopter. He doesn't have much personality development beyond being a practical, slightly gruff professional who does his job when properly incentivized. Voiced by Hank Azaria. Notable quotes: "hop in"
quotes: "hop in"

title: "Weird Al" Yankovic (character)
text: "Weird Al" Yankovic (character) is Celebrity guest character; real-life parody singer who appears in Springfield as himself. "Weird Al" Yankovic appears in the show as a fictionalized version of himself, continuing his real-world reputation as a parody musician. He's shown writing and performing comedic song parodies, including one that helps mend Homer and Marge's relationship after a rough patch. Homer is famously not a fan of his music at first, though he's later cited as beloved enough that Lisa includes him on a list of favorite vegetarians. He pops up in various background and cameo roles throughout the series, often just as a picture or brief mention rather than a major plot presence. In non-canon material, he's depicted as friendly and eager to spend time with the Simpsons, even asking to stay for dinner. Overall, he functions as a lighthearted celebrity cameo tied to his real talent for musical comedy. Voiced by "Weird Al" Yankovic. Notable quotes: He who is tired of Weird Al is tired of life.
quotes: He who is tired of Weird Al is tired of life.

title: Whitney Spuckler
text: Whitney Spuckler is One of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler's many children, part of the Spuckler family. Whitney Spuckler is one of the numerous offspring of Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, growing up in the family's rural, impoverished household. She briefly had a taste of show business when Krusty discovered her and her siblings singing and put them on his program, though a planned tour was cut short by her mother's intervention. Whitney is often shown participating in family activities, from standing outside a raided meth lab to attending the Springfield Demolition Derby. She also contributes musically to the family's makeshift band, playing the Jew's harp. Her father affectionately calls her by the nickname "Peaches" during at least one public interview. Like many of her siblings, she embodies the show's exaggerated, comedic take on rural poverty and large families. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Slarg Fish
text: Slarg Fish is A species of fish found near Barnacle Bay, featured in a single episode. Slarg Fish are a green-colored species that live in the waters around Barnacle Bay. They're notorious for their foul taste, a fact confirmed firsthand by both Jack and Homer when they sampled one during a fishing trip. Despite being inedible, the fish do serve a practical purpose, since their oil is apparently useful for polishing stripper poles. They have no known individual personality, being purely a background element of the show's marine wildlife. Beyond their appearance in "The Wife Aquatic," they also popped up in a non-canon capacity as event currency in a mobile game tie-in.

title: Ray Stantz
text: Ray Stantz is A Ghostbusters franchise character referenced in The Simpsons comics, portrayed via a costume worn by Comic Book Guy. Ray Stantz is not actually an original Simpsons character but a crossover reference to the Ghostbusters franchise. In the world of the Simpsons comics, he exists only as a costume that the collectibles-obsessed superfan Comic Book Guy wore to a fan convention. This appearance highlights Comic Book Guy's obsessive devotion to pop culture memorabilia and cosplay, as he dresses up as various iconic characters from movies and franchises he admires. Ray Stantz himself has no dialogue or independent action in the Simpsons universe, existing purely as a costume choice rather than a fully realized character. His inclusion is a nod to fans of both franchises, blending Simpsons humor with Ghostbusters nostalgia.

title: Spinal Tap (characters)
text: Spinal Tap (characters) is A fictional heavy metal band that performs in Springfield, appearing as guest characters in a few episodes. Spinal Tap is a rock band made up of David St. Hubbins, Nigel Tufnel, Derek Smalls, and two unnamed musicians on keyboards and drums. Their Springfield concert turns chaotic when a riot breaks out, yet the show still leaves a strong impression on Bart, inspiring him to pick up the guitar. Their tour bus later meets a disastrous end after Otto, distracted by his own impromptu performance, crashes into it while driving recklessly. The band's appearances tend to be brief and often played for comedic misfortune rather than musical spotlight. They later turn up again as fellow attendees at a Grammy party alongside the Be Sharps, showing they occupy the same show-business world as Springfield's own celebrities. Their name is also the basis for a non-canon joke involving Homer undergoing a real medical spinal tap procedure. Voiced by Michael McKean, Christopher Guest and Harry Shearer.

title: Springfield Elementary School therapist
text: Springfield Elementary School therapist is A minor recurring character who worked as a therapist at Springfield Elementary School and is married to the sushi chef. This brown-haired therapist briefly counseled students at Springfield Elementary, offering Milhouse support when he grew confused about Lisa's affections for him. She seems caring on the surface, promising to be there for students as long as needed, but she's abruptly let go from her job mid-session, revealing the fragile and underfunded nature of the school's counseling services. Her firing leads to a darkly comic moment where she tells Milhouse to stop being himself, since being himself clearly isn't working. Outside of school, she's revealed to be married to the town's sushi chef, and their relationship has its own tension, particularly around her desire to have a baby rather than pursue further education. She appears only briefly in the show but adds a touch of quirky, offbeat humor typical of one-off Simpsons side characters. Voiced by Wanda Sykes. Notable quotes: I'm here for you, for as long as it takes. | Don't be yourself. Being yourself isn't working.
quotes: I'm here for you, for as long as it takes.
Don't be yourself. Being yourself isn't working.

title: Melania Trump
text: Melania Trump is First Lady of the United States and wife of Donald Trump, appearing in non-canon Simpsons specials. Melania Trump is a minor, non-canon character depicted as the wife of Donald Trump in special Simpsons shorts satirizing his presidency. She is a largely silent figure, appearing more as a visual gag than a fully developed character. In one instance, a risqué picture of her is shown hanging in the White House. In a dream sequence, she is shown reading and editing books related to Trump's controversies, suggesting a subtly skeptical or guarded attitude toward her husband's public image. Overall, she serves as a background presence used to comment on the Trump household through irony and visual humor rather than dialogue or action.

title: Minnie Szyslak
text: Minnie Szyslak is Moe Szyslak's sister and daughter of Morty Szyslak, working as a mattress saleswoman. Minnie is a member of the Szyslak family, best known for her rocky relationship with her brother Moe. As a child she appeared alongside her family in commercials for the family business, Mattress King. She has a combative streak, often clashing with Moe rather than reconciling with him, and she isn't above sabotaging his business ventures. When their father retired and split the family store among his children, Minnie teamed up with her brother Marv to undermine Moe's shop, sparking a bitter sibling rivalry. Despite the family's dysfunction, a shared nostalgic moment over an old commercial briefly reminded them they were still family. She's also been spotted attending live podcast recordings around Springfield, showing she keeps a foot in the town's social scene. Voiced by Debi Mazar.

title: Uhura
text: Uhura is A Star Trek character who appears as a crossover figure in The Simpsons universe. Uhura is a lieutenant from the Star Trek universe who makes crossover appearances in The Simpsons, tying into the show's frequent parodies of the sci-fi franchise. She becomes part of a hallucinated fantasy sequence involving Comic Book Guy, who imagines himself as Spock and directs his romantic attention toward her along with other pop-culture female icons. She also appears briefly in a comedic dream-like montage of famous kisses. As a character, Uhura herself has little independent personality within the show, instead functioning as a nostalgic nod to the original Star Trek series for fans. Her inclusion highlights the show's love of parodying classic sci-fi tropes and its willingness to blend fictional universes for comedic effect. Notably, the character's original live-action portrayer, Nichelle Nichols, also appeared as herself in an episode of The Simpsons. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Samantha Stanky
text: Samantha Stanky is A former Springfield Elementary student who became Milhouse's love interest in the episode "Bart's Friend Falls in Love". Samantha Stanky is a brief but memorable love interest for Milhouse, arriving as a new student who instantly wins his heart after an accidental collision on the playground. Her budding romance with Milhouse causes Bart to feel excluded and ultimately leads him to betray their secret, resulting in her strict father discovering the two kissing in the treehouse. As punishment, her overprotective father yanks her from Springfield Elementary and enrolls her in a strict Catholic school for girls run by French-Canadian nuns. Despite the harsh transfer, Samantha adapts well, enjoys her new school, and forgives Bart for his role in exposing her romance. She's portrayed as a good, well-behaved student who enjoys girly comic books and once struggled with bed-wetting as a younger child. Her story is a small but poignant subplot about first love, friendship, and the awkwardness of growing up. Voiced by Kimmy Robertson.

title: Robin Williams
text: Robin Williams is Real-life actor and comedian who appears as a caricature/reference in a few Simpsons episodes. Robin Williams appears in the show mostly as a pop-culture reference rather than a fully developed character. His famously hairy image is used as the measuring stick for a hazardous ozone-hole warning in Springfield, where a 'class 9' or 'Robin Williams' level of body hair is treated as the maximum protective covering. He's also brought up in conversation at Moe's Tavern, with Lenny noting that Williams was dining out with his kids but failing to make them laugh, a nod to the pressure of always being expected to be funny. In another episode, he shows up inside one of Homer's dreams, claiming that director Stanley Kubrick wanted him to star in The Shining. These appearances play on his real-world reputation for manic energy, hairiness, and comedic talent. The article also notes his real-life death by suicide in 2014. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Leslie Swisher
text: Leslie Swisher is A pro-golfer who disguised himself as a woman to compete in an LPGA tournament and briefly became Patty Bouvier's fiancé. Leslie Swisher is a professional golfer known for masquerading as a female golfer named Veronica in order to enter a women's tournament. His deception leads to an unlikely romance when Patty Bouvier falls for 'Veronica' after being knocked out and revived by him. When Leslie reveals himself to Patty following the legalization of same-sex marriage, she initially doesn't realize he's a man, and their relationship almost leads to marriage. His disguise unravels comically when Marge notices small giveaways, like the toilet seat left up, and finally exposes his Adam's apple at the wedding ceremony. Despite being exposed, he still offers to marry Patty for real, though she chooses to continue living as a lesbian. The character is notably one of the few adult male Simpsons characters voiced by a woman, adding to the show's running gag of gender-bending voice casting. His look was said to be partly inspired by tennis legend Billie Jean King. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Sparky
text: Sparky is A dog belonging to the fire department, briefly borrowed by a young Krusty in a Bongo comic story. Sparky is a minor comic-book-only character who serves as a firehouse dog. He becomes part of a young Krusty's antics when Krusty borrows him to use in a homemade circus-style act. The trick involves having Sparky jump through a ring, but things go wrong when Krusty sets the ring on fire, causing the frightened dog to flee. Sparky is eventually rescued by the fireman who arrives to put out the blaze Krusty accidentally started. His role is brief and largely functions as a vehicle for a young Krusty's mischief-making backstory. Sparky doesn't have an established personality beyond being a loyal, if unlucky, animal caught up in Krusty's schemes.

title: Brad Whitford (character)
text: Brad Whitford (character) is Real-world musician (guitarist of Aerosmith) who appeared as himself in a guest role on The Simpsons. This character is a self-parody appearance by Brad Whitford, guitarist of the rock band Aerosmith, voicing himself on the show. He appears alongside his bandmates rather than as a fictional Springfield resident, blurring the line between the show's universe and real-world celebrity cameos. His main claim to fame within the series is performing music at Moe's Tavern, giving Moe an unexpected brush with rock stardom. He and the rest of Aerosmith are also glimpsed among the crowd at a Grammy Awards party attended by the Be Sharps, tying him into one of the show's beloved flashback storylines. He has no distinct personality traits developed in the show beyond being himself, the musician, since his role is essentially a cameo rather than a scripted character arc. Voiced by Brad Whitford (Himself).

title: Sylvia Winfield
text: Sylvia Winfield is Former next-door neighbor of the Simpson family. Sylvia Winfield was one half of an elderly couple who lived beside the Simpsons before relocating to Florida. She and her husband reportedly grew so tired of the family's antics that they packed up and left Springfield entirely, though they still found their way back for the town's bicentennial parade. She isn't uniformly hostile toward the Simpsons, since she's shown being friendly enough to greet Lisa at the library. Sylvia and her husband also make a recurring cameo appearance in the show's opening credits sequence, spotted by Marge and Maggie during their drive home. Her design was memorable enough to be repurposed as multiple pedestrian character models in a Simpsons video game. Voiced by Tracey Ullman, Maggie Roswell.

title: Winnie-the-Pooh
text: Winnie-the-Pooh is Crossover character/imagined figure appearing in The Simpsons, based on the classic Disney bear. Winnie-the-Pooh is a version of the beloved storybook bear who pops up in The Simpsons universe as a hallucination, toy, and guest character. He first appears as one of several imaginary bears marching toward a traumatized Homer after a real bear attack at the dump. Later, a Pooh toy is spotted in the Simpsons' home, tying him to the family's everyday life. In a more elaborate encounter, Homer inserts himself into a bedtime reading of the Pooh books, rescuing Pooh from a honey pot stuck on his head, only to strangle him afterward in a dark comedic twist. In non-canon material, he shows up at a Disney+ anniversary party at Moe's Tavern, humorously getting into the bar without pants while Homer is left outside complaining. Across his appearances, he retains his gentle, honey-loving persona but is repeatedly used for absurdist or satirical gags. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Vindicators
text: Vindicators is A fictional team of superheroes from the in-universe film franchise "Vindicators," featured in a virtual reality world Bart visits. The Vindicators are a superhero team parodying the Avengers, existing within the Simpsons universe as characters from a blockbuster movie franchise. Their adventures center on battling the villain Chinnos, first in Vindicators: Crystal War and later in its sequel, Crystal War 2: Resurgence. Through a virtual reality experience created by Marble Studios, the team members insist to Bart that the events of their films are genuinely real to them, blurring the line between fiction and reality. The group faces real consequences when Bart's spoilers about the sequel to Comic Book Guy allow the villains to alter the story's outcome, resulting in the death of teammate Airshot. Despite this loss, the remaining Vindicators unite their powers to defeat Chinnos and his army. The team includes Magnesium Man, Airshot, Hydrangea, Black Voodoo, Moby Man, and Quetzelica.

title: Waylon Smithers, Sr.
text: Waylon Smithers, Sr. is Father of Waylon Smithers, Jr. and former assistant to Mr. Burns at the Nuclear Power Plant. Waylon Smithers, Sr. was a loyal plant worker who died a heroic death, sacrificing himself to stop a reactor meltdown and save Springfield, including his own son. Mr. Burns callously disposed of his body in a drainage pipe rather than reveal the truth, later fabricating a story that he'd been killed by Amazon women to spare his son's feelings. His skeleton resurfaces decades later when a young Homer discovers it while swimming, an experience that haunts him well into adulthood. The mystery is eventually solved by the Simpson family, leading to Mr. Burns finally revealing the truth of his heroic sacrifice to Smithers Jr. He also appears in flashbacks tied to Mr. Burns' public relations efforts and even shows up as a ghost in one of Bart's dream sequences, guiding lost souls toward the afterlife. Despite his limited screen time, his tragic backstory adds depth to both Mr. Burns' cold pragmatism and Smithers Jr.'s devotion to his employer. Voiced by Hank Azaria, Harry Shearer.

title: The Stickler
text: The Stickler is Superhero alter-ego of Principal Seymour Skinner, appearing in Simpsons comic books. The Stickler is the costumed persona adopted by Springfield Elementary's stern principal, Seymour Skinner, after a nuclear explosion unexpectedly grants him extraordinary abilities. True to his by-the-book nature, he brings the same rigid discipline and rule-following mindset to his superhero exploits as he does to running his school. This non-canon identity exists purely within the Bongo comic book continuity, separate from the main television series. His name plays on Skinner's well-known reputation as an inflexible enforcer of order, now literalized into a crime-fighting gimmick. He appears in a couple of comic storylines that pit him against other threats in a superhero-parody setting alongside Springfield's other transformed residents.

title: Tiger Woods
text: Tiger Woods is Real-world celebrity golfer who appears as a minor character/reference in The Simpsons. Tiger Woods is depicted in the show as the famous real-life professional golfer, son of Earl Woods. He occasionally shows up on the in-universe sports program Jock Center and is referenced by various characters as a symbol of excellence in golf. His fame is used as a comedic yardstick, such as when Homer boasts about his own prowess by comparing himself to Woods, or when Marge dresses as a female equivalent from an earlier era. He's largely a background or mentioned figure rather than a fully developed character, appearing more in references and cameos than in extended storylines. Notably, he is a non-speaking character throughout his appearances. His connection to his father Earl is also referenced through the book "Training a Tiger" and a dream sequence involving a trophy.

title: Honus Wagner
text: Honus Wagner is Real-life historical baseball player referenced in the Simpsons universe, considered for Mr. Burns's softball team. Honus Wagner is depicted as a legendary baseball player who competed in the National League from 1897 to 1917. In the show's continuity, Mr. Burns wanted to recruit him for the power plant's softball team to help win a lucrative bet, only to be informed by Waylon Smithers that Wagner had already passed away. He appears only in picture or mentioned form, never as a speaking character, reflecting his status as a historical figure rather than an active participant in the story. A box of his baseball cards later turns up in the Simpsons' attic, referencing the real-world value and rarity of Wagner memorabilia. In a non-canon appearance, one of his cards is used by Mr. Burns as packaging material to disguise a valuable Tiffany lamp. His inclusion largely serves as a nod to baseball history and card-collecting culture rather than an active role in the plot.

title: The Thing
text: The Thing is Marvel superhero (member of the Fantastic Four) referenced within the Simpsons universe as a comic book/pop-culture figure. The Thing, whose real identity is Ben Grimm, is a rock-skinned superhero from the Fantastic Four who exists as a piece of comic book lore within the Simpsons world rather than an active character in the show. He mostly turns up as merchandise, costumes, and references tied to Springfield's nerd culture, particularly through Comic Book Guy, who owns Thing-themed bookends and once sent Bart shopping for Thing action figure parts. Homer has dressed up as The Thing for a superhero-themed pub crawl, and in a non-canon Halloween segment he was magically transformed into the character alongside his family as the Fantastic Four. The character is treated as a beloved but somewhat gimmicky classic, referenced through toys, comics, and catchphrases rather than given any personality of his own on the show. He never speaks or appears as a live character, existing purely as an in-universe pop culture artifact. Notable quotes: It's clobberin' time!
quotes: It's clobberin' time!

title: Crazy Vaclav
text: Crazy Vaclav is Owner and salesman of a shady used car dealership; minor recurring character in the Springfield universe. Crazy Vaclav is a sketchy used-car dealer of apparent Eastern European origin who runs his own lot, Crazy Vaclav's Place of Automobiles. He speaks with a heavy, thick accent and has a habit of making outlandish, nonsensical claims about his vehicles' performance. His salesmanship is built on bravado and misdirection, especially when questioned about the shady origins of his cars. He appears only briefly in the show's canon, capitalizing on Homer's desperation after a car accident to unload a dubious vehicle on him. Despite his limited screen time, he's become a memorable one-off character due to his absurd sales pitch and mysterious backstory. He later reappears in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Voiced by Harry Shearer. Notable quotes: will get three hundred hectares on a single tank of kerosene. | the country no longer exists
quotes: will get three hundred hectares on a single tank of kerosene.
the country no longer exists

title: Womenhet
text: Womenhet is Non-canon minor character, wife of Amenhotep, appearing in a Treehouse of Horror segment. Womenhet is a minor, non-canon character introduced in the Treehouse of Horror XX Halloween special. She is depicted as the wife of the mummy Amenhotep, and her main claim to fame is catching her husband flirting with other women at a party. Enraged by his behavior, she confronts and attacks him, showing herself to be a jealous and vengeful spouse rather than a passive figure. Beyond this brief appearance, she later shows up as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, categorized among the mummy-themed characters. She has no other significant history or personality traits explored in the show itself. Voiced by Tress MacNeille.

title: Space Marshmallow
text: Space Marshmallow is Non-canon alien creature from a Treehouse of Horror segment that causes Homer to transform into a monster. The Space Marshmallow, also called The Blob, is an extraterrestrial creature that crash-lands in Springfield inside a meteor during a Treehouse of Horror parody of the classic monster film. After Homer impulsively eats the strange lifeform, he becomes insatiably hungry and gradually mutates into a giant green blob himself, consuming pets, townsfolk, and even a celebrity guest star along the way. The segment plays as a dark comedic riff on monster-movie tropes, with Homer's gluttony literalized into a body-horror transformation. Despite the chaos he causes, Homer tries to spin his condition into something beneficial for the community, leading to a darkly ironic twist involving a fake homeless shelter. The character has since made small non-canon appearances in other Simpsons media, including a mobile game and a printed guide book.

title: Gina Vendetti
text: Gina Vendetti is A juvenile delinquent girl and one of Bart Simpson's love interests, met while both were incarcerated. Gina Vendetti is a tough, volatile girl serving time in a juvenile correctional facility after shoving a Snow White performer at Disneyland. She first meets Bart when he's placed in the neighboring boys' facility, and their initial hostility turns into an unlikely spark during a forced dance-class pairing. When Gina spots a chance to escape, she drags Bart along, and the two bond during their time on the run before ultimately being caught. Despite her rough exterior, she shows a surprising streak of loyalty, taking the blame for the escape so Bart won't face harsher punishment. Underneath her tough act, she hides a lonely truth—she has no family waiting for her outside prison. Later encounters show her relationship with Bart soured, hinting at her volatile and unpredictable nature. She's also been reimagined in alternate, non-canon universes, including as a supervillain-adjacent character in one of Marge's imagined scenarios. Voiced by Sarah Michelle Gellar. Notable quotes: eat fist jerk!
quotes: eat fist jerk!

title: Cameron Winklevoss
text: Cameron Winklevoss is Olympic rower and twin brother of Tyler Winklevoss, a minor recurring parody character. Cameron Winklevoss is one half of a pair of twin Olympic rowers, clearly modeled after the real-life Winklevoss twins. He and his brother Tyler compete in the rowing event at the London 2012 Olympics, only to be humiliated by losing to Patty and Selma despite the sisters being out of shape, chain-smokers, and barely trained. Their embarrassing defeat is blamed on the twins being distracted by thoughts of their massive Facebook lawsuit settlement. Adding to the joke about their close, competitive bond, the two brothers end up making out with each other after the race. Cameron makes a brief later appearance in a crowd scene during a parade for the Boston Americans. He's largely a one-note gag character built around parody of real-world figures and Olympic sports satire. Voiced by Armie Hammer.

title: Barbara Van Horne
text: Barbara Van Horne is Wife (now separated) of Sideshow Mel, a minor recurring resident of Springfield. Barbara Van Horne is a minor, largely silent character best known as the estranged wife of Sideshow Mel. Her marriage to Mel was troubled, marked by his complaints that she didn't respect his French artistic sensibilities and by a secret affair she carried on with Krusty the Clown for over a decade. Eventually their relationship fell apart entirely, with Barbara leaving Mel a note to announce she was leaving him for good. She shares Mel's distinctive green hair color, though hers is styled normally rather than in his exaggerated fashion. Despite appearing in several episodes, she is notable for almost never speaking on screen, making her a quiet background presence rather than an active participant in the show's comedy.

title: Tiger Williams (character)
text: Tiger Williams (character) is A former hockey player who works as a coach at Top Goon Academy, appearing in an episode about Nelson Muntz's training as an enforcer. Tiger Williams is a minor, real-world-inspired character based on the actual retired NHL enforcer of the same name, voiced by himself. In the show, he serves as an instructor at Top Goon Academy, a school dedicated to training hockey goons. His curriculum oddly blends physical brutality with literary study, as he teaches both basic pummeling techniques and a course on American novels from 1930 onward, notably assigning Toni Morrison's Beloved. He is one of the mentors responsible for training Nelson Muntz during his time at the academy. As a guest-starring real-life athlete, his role leans into the show's tradition of poking fun at sports culture and academic tropes simultaneously. Voiced by Stu Grimson.

title: Dr. Zander
text: Dr. Zander is Director of a fathering enrichment class attended by Homer, appearing in one episode. Dr. Zander runs a fathering enrichment class at the Community Centre, which Homer is forced to attend after making Bart wet his pants on live stadium TV. He comes across as stern and moralistic, especially once he learns Homer once strangled his son, reacting with genuine horror. To teach Homer a pointed lesson, he manipulates the class by excusing every other father so Homer is left alone to face consequences. His unlikely friendship with basketball legend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar adds a comedic layer, as the two are shown to socialize over weekend basketball games. Dr. Zander uses this connection to further shame Homer, bringing Kareem in to express his own disturbed reaction to Homer's parenting story. The basketball anecdote about points scored also serves as a light, absurd aside amid the otherwise serious tone of the confrontation. Voiced by Paul Rudd.

title: Mark Zuckerberg (character)
text: Mark Zuckerberg (character) is Real-world tech billionaire (Facebook co-founder) who appears as a caricature in Springfield, occasionally interacting with Lisa and other characters. This character is a fictionalized version of the real Facebook co-founder, portrayed as obsessively tied to his own social network and oddly detached in his reactions to real-world events. He first turns up at an entrepreneur expo, where he brags about dropping out of Harvard and getting rich anyway, and later gets knocked over at a rollerskating rink by Lisa and Nelson. A recurring gag is his habit of updating his Facebook status to describe whatever is happening to him, no matter how mundane or painful. In another appearance he creeps out a country club manager by reciting personal details he found through her online profile, only to be comically attacked by a bear moments later. He's also referenced as an object of scorn by other characters, including Mr. Burns and Professor Frink, suggesting a reputation as either overly powerful or personally disliked. Despite his fame and wealth, the show frames him as socially awkward and a bit clueless about boundaries. Voiced by Mark Zuckerberg (himself); Chris Edgerly. Notable quotes: take that, Founder of Facebook | is in intense pain | Haw Haw!
quotes: take that, Founder of Facebook
is in intense pain
Haw Haw!

title: Marge Ziff
text: Marge Ziff is Alternate-universe version of Marge Simpson who married Artie Ziff instead of Homer, appearing in non-canon stories. Marge Ziff is a non-canon alternate-reality counterpart of Marge Simpson, born from a timeline where Bart's meddling kept Marge and Homer apart. In one version of events, she ends up married to Artie Ziff and has a son named Barty, but grows disillusioned with her choice after witnessing Artie and Barty's bad behavior, eventually falling for a version of Homer instead. In another depiction, she serves as the Mayor of Springfield in an alternate world created by Professor Frink, still married to Artie Ziff and raising a mischievous daughter named Lisa. This version of Marge finds herself drawn to an alternate Homer Simpson who had been married to Mindy Simmons. She also appears as a character in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out. Overall, she exists as a glimpse into a 'what if' scenario exploring what Marge's life might look like without Homer. Voiced by Julie Kavner.

title: Zhenya
text: Zhenya is Bart's piano teacher and one of his crushes/girlfriends. Zhenya is a piano teacher hired by Marge to give Bart lessons, and Bart quickly develops a crush on her. Her father Slava strikes a deal allowing the arrangement, trading piano lessons for driving lessons from Marge. Zhenya turns out to be more focused on her father's needs than actually teaching Bart, revealing she only takes on students so her father can get driving instruction. Distracted by his infatuation, Bart fails to progress musically and ends up cheating by hiding a CD inside the piano to fake his talent. As his fraudulent fame grows, Zhenya gains a surge of new students but has less time to genuinely teach Bart. The whole scheme unravels publicly at a talent show, though Slava intervenes to smooth things over with an angry Marge. Voiced by Jane Krakowski.

title: Mrs. Zörker
text: Mrs. Zörker is Mother of Üter Zörker, the German exchange student at Springfield Elementary School. Mrs. Zörker is a minor, non-speaking background character known primarily as Üter's mom. She's distinguished visually by her blonde hair styled in a traditional crown braid, giving her a stereotypically German appearance fitting her family's background. She appeared alongside her husband and son at the Bounce-A-Thon, showing her as a supportive family figure who participates in town events. Beyond this brief family outing, little else is known about her personality or history, as she has never been given lines of dialogue. She remains a recurring but low-profile presence in the extended Springfield community.

title: Zelda
text: Zelda is Former resident of Springfield Retirement Castle and ex-girlfriend of Abraham Simpson. Zelda is an elderly woman who briefly dated Grandpa Simpson after he regained his driver's license. She's portrayed as manipulative and shallow, using Abe purely for his ability to drive her around rather than any genuine affection. Despite warnings from Abe's family that she was only interested in his car privileges, he pursued her anyway, only to be dumped the moment he lost his license in a car accident. She quickly moved on to another resident with a wheelchair-accessible van, leading to a dramatic and humiliating public confrontation when Abe tracked her down in Branson. Her flirtatious, opportunistic nature is played for comedy, culminating in her being publicly shamed on stage. She later resurfaces on a cruise ship, seemingly unbothered by the earlier incident. Voiced by Olympia Dukakis. Notable quotes: Who's that tall drink of Maalox? | Drive me!
quotes: Who's that tall drink of Maalox?
Drive me!

title: Uncle Zio
text: Uncle Zio is Fat Tony's uncle, a minor mafia-connected relative who appears from Sicily. Uncle Zio is an elderly relative of mob boss Fat Tony, hailing from Sicily. He is flown to America by Johnny Tightlips with the intention of celebrating a festival together with his nephew, but plans change when Fat Tony shows little interest and instead the two end up at Burning Man. Despite the rocky start, uncle and nephew use the trip as an opportunity to reconnect and bond. Unfortunately, his visit takes a turn for the worse when he accompanies Fat Tony to an abandoned warehouse, where Fat Tony ends up getting arrested. He is a widower, having lost his unnamed wife before the events of the show. Uncle Zio is a minor, one-off character whose main narrative purpose is to add a bit of family background and comic mishap to Fat Tony's storyline. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Zorro
text: Zorro is A superhero swordsman character who appears in a fictional segment within The Simpsons, later becoming King of England. Zorro is a masked swashbuckler who shows up in a Simpsons fantasy sequence as a dashing hero skilled with a rapier. He makes short work of the Three Musketeers with his signature deadly poke and later duels the Man in the Iron Mask, declaring his intent to restore King Arthur to the throne. His storyline takes a romantic turn when he discovers his girlfriend has been wooed by the cowardly Scarlet Pimpernel, prompting him to challenge his rival to a duel at an opera house. Since the Pimpernel flees rather than fight, Zorro is rewarded by King Arthur, who tosses him the crown, which Zorro dramatically catches on the tip of his sword to become King of England. He's also referenced as appearing in an in-universe film called Zorro Joins the Navy. Outside of animation, he was portrayed by John Byner in a live-action segment called The Poke of Zorro. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Dr. Zweig
text: Dr. Zweig is Psychiatrist who treated Marge Simpson for her fear of flying. Dr. Zweig is a psychologist Marge consults after developing a fear of flying, charging her thirty dollars an hour for sessions. She digs into Marge's psyche and traces the phobia back to an odd family detail involving her father, though Homer's anxious interruptions complicate the therapy. Generally composed, she has occasional bursts of passion, particularly when discussing the Monkees or when she learns a payment has bounced. Despite the depth of their sessions, Marge can never quite remember her name correctly, mistakenly calling her "Lowenstein." She has made small recurring appearances since her debut, including a cameo in a hairdressing-themed episode and in one of Bart's dream sequences. Voiced by Anne Bancroft. Notable quotes: Yes, yes, it's all a rich tapestry! - Dr. Zweig
quotes: Yes, yes, it's all a rich tapestry! - Dr. Zweig

title: Mr. Zzyzwicz
text: Mr. Zzyzwicz is Father of Kearney, one of the school bullies at Springfield Elementary. Mr. Zzyzwicz is a minor recurring character defined mostly by his rough, unpleasant demeanor and his resemblance to his son Kearney, though he's rougher-looking and sports a beard. He's portrayed as a deadbeat and irresponsible parent, joked about by his own son as being more afraid of paying child support than facing any real danger. His temper is on full display when he violently confronts Homer at Moe's Tavern over a dispute involving their sons, resulting in a moment of comic violence that ties into Homer's later boxing career. Despite his brutish qualities, he's shown participating in more ordinary family activities, such as taking his son and grandson to a baseball game. He fits into the show's pattern of bullies coming from troubled, similarly rough family backgrounds. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Mr. Zörker
text: Mr. Zörker is Father of Üter, a minor recurring character. Mr. Zörker is a minor character best known as the anxious father of exchange student Üter. He appears primarily in situations tied to his son's wellbeing, such as when Üter goes missing on a school trip. He is depicted attending family events alongside his wife, showing him to be an involved, if infrequently seen, parent. Little is revealed about his personality beyond his concern for Üter, and he functions mostly as background family for the Zörker household. His appearances are sporadic, spanning many seasons of the show as a recurring but rarely featured figure. Voiced by Hank Azaria.

title: Empress Zimzam
text: Empress Zimzam is A minor non-canon future character who appears only as a picture; a poster idol of Zia Simpson and a romantic conquest listed in Bart's little black eBook. Empress Zimzam is a background, non-canon figure glimpsed only in future-themed flash-forward episodes of the show. She never appears in person or speaks, existing solely as an image—first as a poster on the wall of Lisa's rebellious future daughter Zia, and later as a photo in adult Bart's little black eBook, hinting he once had a romantic fling with her. Her design is a clear visual homage to Queen Amidala from the Star Wars prequels, right down to her elaborate headdress. Because she's picture-only and non-speaking, she has no personality traits or dialogue established, functioning purely as a pop-culture easter egg and a running joke about Bart's womanizing future. Her title 'Empress' suggests she holds some kind of royal or imperial status in this speculative future world, though no further backstory is given.

title: Kearney Zzyzwicz, Jr.
text: Kearney Zzyzwicz, Jr. is Son of Kearney, a minor recurring child character from Springfield. Kearney Zzyzwicz, Jr. is the young son of school bully Kearney and his unseen ex-wife. He's a minor background character who has appeared in numerous episodes over the show's run without much development. One notable detail about him is that he coped with his parents' divorce in an unusual way, by sleeping in a drawer at night instead of a bed. He also showed up sitting on Gil's lap during a holiday scene when Gil was dressed as Santa Claus. In a non-canon mobile game appearance, he's oddly referred to by a different name, Jason, and described as being around Bart's age. Overall, he exists mostly as a nod to Kearney's family life rather than a fully fleshed-out character. Voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Irving Zitsofsky
text: Irving Zitsofsky is A minor recurring dermatologist in Springfield who treats various family members. Dr. Irving Zitsofsky is the owner and lead physician of his own dermatology clinic in Springfield. He's best known for treating Bart after a botched tattoo incident, charging Marge a steep fee to laser it off. He also pops up in other medical contexts, such as giving Sideshow Bob an injection after his Emmy win. As a background character, he doesn't have much of a defined personality beyond being a competent, if pricey, medical professional. His recurring presence across several episodes and even a shorts appearance suggests he's one of Springfield's go-to specialists whenever skin-related mishaps occur. Voiced by Harry Shearer, Dan Castellaneta.

title: Klaus Ziegler
text: Klaus Ziegler is An art forger living on Isla Verde who becomes entangled with Homer and Kirk's family troubles. Klaus Ziegler is an elderly, gray-haired forger whose skill is so refined that his fake paintings can pass for genuine works by famous artists. He struggles with alcoholism, specifically an addiction to the beverage Strupo, which drives much of his behavior. Desperate to pay off a bar tab, he once handed over a forged painting to a cafe, setting off a chain of events involving Kirk Van Houten and Homer Simpson. After Homer uncovered the truth about the painting's origins, Klaus was recruited to produce more forged art to help both men smooth things over with their wives. True to his vice, he accepted payment for this work in the form of more Strupo rather than money. Voiced by Max von Sydow.

title: Mao Zedong
text: Mao Zedong is Real-world Chinese Communist revolutionary who appears as a hallucination, corpse, and image in the Simpsons universe. Mao Zedong appears in the show not as a living character but through brief, surreal cameos rooted in real history. He first shows up as one of several historical figures Mr. Burns hallucinates while lost and starving in the mountains. Later, the Simpson family encounters his preserved corpse on a trip to China, where Homer mistakes the embalmed body for a sleeping baby and coos over him despite acknowledging his brutal death toll. He's also referenced as one of history's great monsters who never got a valentine, placing him alongside other infamous tyrants. Finally, his image resurfaces as one of several 20th-century dictators used in a CAPTCHA test on a fictional website, which Lisa ends up clicking. Across these appearances, Mao is treated as a darkly comic historical footnote rather than a fleshed-out character.

title: John A. Zoidberg
text: John A. Zoidberg is Crossover character from Futurama; a lobster-like alien doctor who appears in Simpsons crossover episodes and games. Dr. Zoidberg is a crustacean-like alien physician from the Futurama universe who occasionally crosses paths with the Simpsons cast. He tends to make odd, tangential remarks that miss the point of conversations, as shown when he awkwardly joins a phone call meant for Bender. In video game appearances, he serves as a strange, mouth-shooting enemy, once drawn into existence by Matt Groening himself to torment Bart and Homer. He also turns up as a foe summoned by God in a Dance Dance Revolution-style level, and even appears as an ordinary lobster deep in the ocean in one Simpsons episode. His humor often relies on absurd non-sequiturs and callbacks to his home series, Futurama, including a joke referencing Fry's long cryogenic freeze. Despite his minor role in the Simpsons universe, he remains a recognizable oddball figure tied to the show's occasional crossovers with Futurama. Voiced by Billy West. Notable quotes: I'll digest you in my eggs for a thousand years
quotes: I'll digest you in my eggs for a thousand years

title: Zutroy
text: Zutroy is Minor recurring employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, briefly Charlie's replacement as dangerous emissions supervisor. Zutroy is a minor background worker at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant who briefly took over the dangerous emissions supervisor role from Charlie. His storyline highlights Mr. Burns' exploitative treatment of workers, as Burns tries to underpay him with a mere shiny penny instead of real wages. His time on the job is cut short when immigration authorities raid the plant and deport him for being in the country illegally, despite his competence at the dangerous job. He later resurfaces as a participant in one of Smithers' bizarre employee competitions. Eventually, he appears to have legally become an American citizen and returned to work at the plant. Though he's a very minor character, his brief arc serves as a satirical jab at labor exploitation and immigration issues. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Zora
text: Zora is Co-founder of CarGo, a self-driving car company that hires Homer and Marge. Zora is a tech executive who, along with her business partner Antoine, runs the self-driving car startup CarGo. She has a knack for exploiting employees' quirks, hiring Homer specifically because of his terrible driving and passive nature, which makes him a perfect fit for their unconventional application process. Zora is shown to be shrewd and somewhat sinister in her business practices, using surveillance in the company's vehicles under the guise of a friendly-sounding customer program. She's also quick to reward employees who bring positive energy to the workplace, promoting Homer and hiring Marge after they lifted staff morale. Despite her corporate charm, Zora reveals an unsettling side when discussing the lengths CarGo goes to for consumer data collection, including cross-breeding lawyers with wolves and eavesdropping through key fobs and tattoos. Voiced by Tress MacNeille. Notable quotes: She told Homer and Marge that they had lawyers that were cross-bred with wolves.
quotes: She told Homer and Marge that they had lawyers that were cross-bred with wolves.

title: Yodelin' Zeke
text: Yodelin' Zeke is A minor country-western performer who appears at The Beer -N- Brawl and on the show Ya Hoo!. Yodelin' Zeke is a country-western entertainer whose whole act revolves around yodeling over twangy backing music. His performances don't always go over well with rowdy crowds, leading to a memorable incident where an unappreciative bar patron knocked him out mid-song with a chair. Despite this, he's treated as a regular fixture at The Beer -N- Brawl, with the announcer implying such attacks are a recurring hazard of his career. He also holds a steady gig as a cast member on the cheesy variety program Ya Hoo!, appearing there still bandaged up after his on-stage injury. Zeke's presence highlights the show's fondness for parodying earnest, low-rent country entertainment and the rough crowds that don't always appreciate it. Voiced by Dan Castellaneta.

title: Jasper Johns (character)
text: Jasper Johns (character) is One-time guest character; an American contemporary artist who appears at an art convention Homer attends. Jasper Johns is depicted as a real-world contemporary artist making a comedic guest appearance in Springfield. He's portrayed as sneaky and opportunistic, using his trench coat to pilfer free food and even a light bulb at an art convention. His criminal streak escalates when he steals Astrid Weller's boat during a flood and later swipes Marge's artwork right off the roof. Despite his fame as an artist, his defining trait in the show is petty theft, often executed with a casual, unbothered attitude. He also briefly threatens Homer, showing a willingness to intimidate to keep his thefts secret. Overall, he's a quick comedic cameo built around the running gag of him constantly stealing things. Voiced by Jasper Johns (Himself). Notable quotes: yoink!
quotes: yoink!

title: Frinkenstein (Treehouse of Horror XIV segment)
text: "Frinkenstein" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XIV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 14"), which aired as Season 15, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. Homer excitedly believes he's won the Nobel Prize, only for Lisa to reveal the honor actually belongs to Professor Frink. Overjoyed, Frink decides to reanimate his long-dead father so he can witness the achievement at the ceremony. The reanimated Frink Sr. proves monstrous, tearing organs from Springfield residents to rebuild his own decaying body, taking Ned Flanders' heart, Principal Skinner's spine, and Sideshow Mel's hair. At the Nobel ceremony in Stockholm, Frink Sr. briefly reconciles with his son before losing control again, rampaging through the crowd of scientists and absorbing their brains to become ever more intelligent. Frink Jr. finally subdues his father with a swift kick to the groin. In the end, Frink Jr. keeps what remains of his father's soul contained in a small box, where it can still speak to him. Notable quotes: Lisa: Did a shark do that? | Jonathan Frink, Jr: Yes. He was testing out a new blood-based sun-tan lotion. | Professor Frink, Sr.: I'm getting me a real spleen and then I'm gonna vent it on you boy chick. | Agnes Skinner: Lost your spine, huh? You just keep finding new ways to disappoint me.
quotes: Lisa: Did a shark do that?
Jonathan Frink, Jr: Yes. He was testing out a new blood-based sun-tan lotion.
Professor Frink, Sr.: I'm getting me a real spleen and then I'm gonna vent it on you boy chick.
Agnes Skinner: Lost your spine, huh? You just keep finding new ways to disappoint me.

title: Into the Homer-verse (Treehouse of Horror XXXI segment)
text: "Into the Homer-verse" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 31"), which aired as Season 32, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. On Halloween night, Homer eats all the candy meant for trick-or-treaters and sneaks into a restricted room at the Power Plant looking for more. There he finds a mysterious machine, and when it refuses his quarter, he smashes it open, unleashing multiple alternate-universe versions of himself into Springfield, including a noir detective Homer and a Hanna-Barbera cartoon Homer. Kent Brockman reports the citywide chaos on the news as the Homers wreak havoc, while Marge tries luring them home with a can of Duff beer. Lisa figures out that her father's tampering ripped open the space-time continuum, and warns that unless the Homers return to the plant to recreate the explosion, they'll be trapped repeating deadly loops forever. Mr. Burns interferes, wanting to exploit the duplicate Homers as free labor, and summons alternate versions of himself and Smithers, sparking a chaotic battle that kills off most of the Homers. After Burns learns his noir counterpart is subordinate to Smithers in that universe, he banishes the remaining doubles back through the machine. Marge is finally left with the sole Homer she actually wanted, Noir Homer, but he then morphs into a bizarre Green Cat Homer and flees. Notable quotes: Homer: Listen, machine, there's no evidence that you contain any candy or take any money. But desperate times call for something something. | Homer: Who the heck are you? | Homer Barbera: I'm Homer Barbera, a-smarter than the average Homer. | Noir Homer: This case is gonna be like Homer's skull: hard to crack and not much inside.
quotes: Homer: Listen, machine, there's no evidence that you contain any candy or take any money. But desperate times call for something something.
Homer: Who the heck are you?
Homer Barbera: I'm Homer Barbera, a-smarter than the average Homer.
Noir Homer: This case is gonna be like Homer's skull: hard to crack and not much inside.

title: Barti (Treehouse of Horror XXXII segment)
text: "Barti" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 32"), which aired as Season 33, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. This segment spoofs Disney's Bambi, casting young deer Barti and his mother fleeing through the forest from a trigger-happy hunter, Mr. Burns. After a frantic chase, Barti takes shelter in a cave, only to discover his mother is missing and feared dead. Venturing back out into the woods alone, he encounters Mr. Burns and desperately demands to know his mother's fate. Just as things look grim, his mother reappears alive and well, explaining that Barti's father intervened to save her. The father deer then violently stabs Mr. Burns using Lenny (apparently transformed into a weapon or accomplice), turning the tables on the hunter. The segment ends with the deer family gruesomely feasting on Mr. Burns' body, flipping the predator-prey dynamic of the original Bambi story. Notable quotes: Homer: Time for a little "stag party." | Mr. Burns: Thank God you're herbivores. | Homer: That's right. And today your name is "Herb."
quotes: Homer: Time for a little "stag party."
Mr. Burns: Thank God you're herbivores.
Homer: That's right. And today your name is "Herb."

title: Easy-Bake Coven (Treehouse of Horror VIII segment)
text: "Easy-Bake Coven" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror VIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 8"), which aired as Season 9, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. In 1649 Sprynge-Fielde, the townsfolk hold a chaotic witch trial after a string of burnings, with neighbors wildly accusing one another until Marge steps in to calm them, only to be denounced as a witch herself by Moe. Mayor Quimby explains the 'fair' test: she'll be pushed off a cliff on a broomstick, surviving only if she's truly a witch, in which case she must return for execution. Despite Lisa's pleading, Marge is shoved off the cliff and reappears flying, revealing she really is a green-skinned witch, and she swears revenge on the town. She reunites with her sisters Patty and Selma in their mountain lair, and the trio fly off to torment the townspeople, targeting the Flanders family first. When Maude Flanders cleverly offers gingerbread men instead of her children, the witches take the treat and spare the kids, inspiring them to go house to house trading candy for spared children. Narrator Horatio McCallister explains this is how Halloween and trick-or-treating began. The segment ends the following Halloween with Homer accidentally revealing his own house went candy-less, then hypocritically accusing Lisa of witchcraft, sparking a comedic mob chase. Notable quotes: Witch Marge: That's right, I'm a witch! And I'm the one who whithered your livestock, soured your sheep's milk, and made your shirt itchy! | 1649 Chief Wiggum: Well, hear me out, if you're innocent, you will fall to an honorable Christian death. | 1649 Ralph: Bye, witches, thanks for not eating me! | 1649 Mayor Quimby: Everyone, let us not turn into an angry mob! Goodie-Simpson is entitled to due process!
quotes: Witch Marge: That's right, I'm a witch! And I'm the one who whithered your livestock, soured your sheep's milk, and made your shirt itchy!
1649 Chief Wiggum: Well, hear me out, if you're innocent, you will fall to an honorable Christian death.
1649 Ralph: Bye, witches, thanks for not eating me!
1649 Mayor Quimby: Everyone, let us not turn into an angry mob! Goodie-Simpson is entitled to due process!

title: Homerzilla (Treehouse of Horror XXVI segment)
text: "Homerzilla" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXVI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 26"), which aired as Season 27, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. This segment opens as a parody of Godzilla, set in a fictionalized Springfield, Japan. Grampa Simpson, portrayed as an elderly local mocked by the townsfolk, performs a daily ritual of dropping a perfect donut into the ocean, accompanied by his skeptical grandchildren Bart and Lisa. He explains that the offering keeps a slumbering sea monster from waking and destroying the city, but Bart and Lisa dismiss him as foolish rather than believing his warning. Tragedy strikes when Grampa accidentally chokes on donut toppings while preparing the sacred offering and dies. With the ritual broken, the sea monster, revealed to be a giant Homer Simpson called Homerzilla, awakens and rampages through the city. The segment then jumps to modern-day movie executives watching the disastrous 'Homerzilla' film, mocking its quality and deciding it warrants a remake. Two years later their reboot, titled 'Zilla', flops just as badly, so they dump all the unsold merchandise into the ocean. This dumping accidentally reawakens the real Homerzilla, and a closing title card ominously warns that he will return once the public has forgotten about him again. Notable quotes: Lisa: Grampa, everyone in town thinks you are foolish. | Grampa Simp-san: Who is more foolish - the fool, or the fool who thinks the fool a fool? | Bart: What the hell does that mean, Grampa-san? | Grampa Simp-san: For centuries, our family has made a daily offering of a special donut to a slumbering underwater sea creature, so that he does not rise and destroy us all.
quotes: Lisa: Grampa, everyone in town thinks you are foolish.
Grampa Simp-san: Who is more foolish - the fool, or the fool who thinks the fool a fool?
Bart: What the hell does that mean, Grampa-san?
Grampa Simp-san: For centuries, our family has made a daily offering of a special donut to a slumbering underwater sea creature, so that he does not rise and destroy us all.

title: Four Beheadings and a Funeral (Treehouse of Horror XV segment)
text: "Four Beheadings and a Funeral" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 15"), which aired as Season 16, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. Set in Victorian London, this segment parodies Sherlock Holmes and Jack the Ripper mysteries. A serial killer known as the Mutton Chop Murderer stalks the city, prompting Inspector Wiggum to hastily arrest Apu despite no evidence. Amateur sleuths Eliza Simpson and her bumbling companion Dr. Bartley launch their own investigation, tracing the murder weapon—one of the Swords of Osiris—through Comic Book Guy's shop (where he is killed before revealing much) and then to C. Montgomery Scrooge/Burns, who sold the swords for opium money. Their trail leads to an opium den where Homer is wrongly implicated and nearly executed as the killer. Just before Homer's public hanging, Simpson and Bartley expose the truth: Inspector Wiggum himself is the murderer, revealed by the smell of eel pie on the weapon and mutton chops hidden under Lou's hat. Wiggum flees via hot air balloon but is struck down by a UFO piloted by Kang and Kodos, and the segment closes with a surreal dream-within-a-dream twist involving Ralph and Wiggum flying off on a bed. Notable quotes: Inspector Wiggum: Well, well, well, look who's here. Master detective Eliza Simpson and her easily amazed sidekick, Dr. Bartley. | Dr. Bartley: What's this? A doorknob! Good show! | C. Ebenezer Burns: The sword of Osiris! I once possessed the entire collection. Then I sold them all for opium. | Inspector Wiggum: Why can't you be more like Eddie? He never says a word against me.
quotes: Inspector Wiggum: Well, well, well, look who's here. Master detective Eliza Simpson and her easily amazed sidekick, Dr. Bartley.
Dr. Bartley: What's this? A doorknob! Good show!
C. Ebenezer Burns: The sword of Osiris! I once possessed the entire collection. Then I sold them all for opium.
Inspector Wiggum: Why can't you be more like Eddie? He never says a word against me.

title: I've Grown a Costume on Your Face (Treehouse of Horror XVI segment)
keys: i've grown a costume on your face
text: "I've Grown a Costume on Your Face" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XVI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 16"), which aired as Season 17, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Springfield holds a Halloween costume contest, and a genuine witch enters disguised as a costume and wins first prize. When the judges discover she's an actual witch and not just dressed as one, they strip her of the trophy, prompting her to cast a furious revenge spell. The curse transforms every citizen into the literal creature or character their costume represented, causing chaotic side effects: Homer's head detaches, Marge becomes a skeleton with her own head still attached, Bart turns into a real werewolf, Lisa becomes Albert Einstein, and baby Maggie is turned into an actual witch. As townspeople flood the Simpson house demanding to be changed back (while others enjoy their new forms), Lisa realizes that Maggie, now possessing real magic, might be able to reverse everything. Overwhelmed by the competing demands, Maggie instead impulsively zaps the entire crowd into giant pacifiers that retain their normal heads before flying off on a broomstick. The segment closes with a meta gag as Moe addresses the audience directly, followed by a Dennis Rodman cameo, before Maggie returns to cast one more spell as the credits roll, implying she finally undoes the chaos.

title: Scary Tales Can Come True (Treehouse of Horror XI segment)
