text: "Scary Tales Can Come True" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 11"), which aired as Season 12, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. In this fairy-tale parody, the Simpsons live as poor peasants in a pumpkin cottage, and after Homer loses his job, he decides the only way to keep everyone fed is to abandon Bart and Lisa in the woods. The kids discover the skeletal remains of an earlier son and daughter Homer discarded, and Lisa uses her book of Grimm's fairy tales to navigate dangers like a bridge troll and the Three Bears. Meanwhile, Marge forces Homer to go find the children, leading him to Rapunzel's tower, where his attempt to climb her hair ends in gruesome disaster when her hair rips free from her scalp. Bart and Lisa eventually stumble into a gingerbread house belonging to a witch who enslaves Lisa and begins fattening Bart up for dinner. Homer smashes into the house to save them, gets magically transformed into a chicken-fish hybrid by the witch, but manages to shove her into her own oven, killing her. Just after Homer reverts to normal, the witch's unaware suitor George Cauldron arrives for their date, confused to find her gone. The segment ends with the family sitting down to a meal, Marge noting that thanks to Homer's new chicken half laying eggs, they'll never go hungry again. Notable quotes: Suzanne: That was a load bearing candy cane, you clumsy oaf! | Marge: Husband, without your weekly penitence, how shall we feed our children? | Homer: So long, kids! Enjoy your new home. Say hi to your other brother and sister. | Lisa: Face it, they're not great parents.
quotes: Suzanne: That was a load bearing candy cane, you clumsy oaf!
Marge: Husband, without your weekly penitence, how shall we feed our children?
Homer: So long, kids! Enjoy your new home. Say hi to your other brother and sister.
Lisa: Face it, they're not great parents.

title: Master and Cadaver (Treehouse of Horror XXI segment)
text: "Master and Cadaver" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 21"), which aired as Season 22, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Homer and Marge set out on a romantic second honeymoon cruise aboard a yacht, only to be interrupted when they rescue a shipwrecked castaway named Roger. Roger claims he was the chef aboard the ill-fated Albatross and was knocked unconscious while trying to stop an attempted mass poisoning of the passengers. When Homer and Marge spot a dead shark with a freshly baked pie pan in its mouth, they become convinced that Roger himself is the poisoner and decide to take justice into their own hands, seemingly killing him and dumping his body overboard. Sailing on, they discover the wreck of the Albatross and realize with horror that Roger had actually been telling the truth all along. Roger then reappears very much alive, prompting Homer to kill him for real, along with the surviving bankers he finds aboard. Marge, horrified by Homer's violence, unwittingly eats a slice of the actual poisoned pie. The entire twisted tale is ultimately revealed to have just been a story imagined by baby Maggie. Notable quotes: Homer: They should call this one recipe for murder. | Marge: What do you mean "this one?" | Homer: Nevermind.
quotes: Homer: They should call this one recipe for murder.
Marge: What do you mean "this one?"
Homer: Nevermind.

title: Act III: Homer's nightmare (Treehouse of Horror II segment)
text: "Act III: Homer's nightmare" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror II" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 2"), which aired as Season 3, Episode 7 of The Simpsons. Frightened by his own nightmare, Bart runs with Lisa to Homer and Marge's room, and Homer grumbles about having to wake for work soon, setting up his own dream sequence. In it, Homer has been fired and taken a job as a cemetery gravedigger, where he dozes off inside an open grave. Mr. Burns and Smithers, scouring the graveyard for a fresh brain to power their prototype worker robot, mistake the sleeping Homer for a corpse and harvest his brain for the machine. The robot, now running on Homer's mind, proves just as lazy and clumsy as the real Homer, infuriating Mr. Burns, so Smithers has the brain put back—only for the robot to topple onto Burns and crush him. Homer wakes from the dream to discover, in a final twist, that Mr. Burns' severed head has actually been grafted onto his own body. The segment closes the next morning with the two-headed Homer squabbling over conflicting evening plans—Lisa's school spaghetti dinner versus a royal reception for Queen Beatrix—leaving Homer lamenting the burden of having two heads. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: Perhaps you are curious as to why you have two heads. Well, my body was crushed, so I had my head grafted onto your, shall we say, ample frame. | Homer: I can wake up. title: Wraparound part 2 (Treehouse of Horror IV segment)
text: "Wraparound part 2" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror IV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 4"), which aired as Season 5, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. This brief wraparound segment bridges the anthology's second and third stories. Bart returns to introduce the final and supposedly most terrifying painting of the night, the famous image of dogs playing poker. Homer stares at it and dissolves into crazed laughter, seemingly driven mad by the image, mirroring the show's earlier gags about horrifying paintings. Bart explains to the audience that the writers originally had a full story to accompany this painting, but it was deemed too twisted and disturbing to air. Instead, he says they hastily assembled a substitute tale involving vampires. This sets up the next segment, effectively excusing away the unseen "real" story with a meta joke about censorship and improvisation. title: How to Get Ahead in Dead-Vertising (Treehouse of Horror XIX segment)

text: "How to Get Ahead in Dead-Vertising" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XIX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 19"), which aired as Season 20, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Homer and Marge enroll Maggie at a daycare center, where she feels isolated until she bonds with a mural of Krusty the Clown's face. When the real Krusty shows up and angrily paints over his own image, calling it unlicensed use, Homer retaliates for upsetting Maggie by shoving him into a chain of mishaps ending with Krusty being shredded in a wood chipper. Businessmen soon approach Homer, revealing that dead celebrities' likenesses can be used in commercials for free since they can't refuse endorsements. They recruit Homer to start killing celebrities like George Clooney, Emma Bunton, Prince, and Neil Armstrong for advertising purposes. In Heaven, the murdered celebrities, joined by John Lennon, are furious and, led by Krusty, descend to earth for revenge, with Krusty shooting Homer dead. Abraham Lincoln, however, enjoys his own posthumous ad (kissing George Washington), angering Washington. When the vengeful celebrities try to return to Heaven, Homer—now a ghost—locks them out in retaliation and ends up befriending Abraham Lincoln.

title: The Terror of Tiny Toon (Treehouse of Horror IX segment)
text: "The Terror of Tiny Toon" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror IX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 9"), which aired as Season 10, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. After Marge bans Bart and Lisa from watching the Itchy and Scratchy Halloween special and disables the remote, Bart rigs it with a stray chunk of plutonium from Homer's toolbox. The jury-rigged remote sucks Bart and Lisa into the cartoon world itself, where they watch Itchy decapitate Scratchy and use his head as a jack-o-lantern. When Scratchy's severed head realizes the kids are laughing at his suffering, he reattaches himself and teams up with Itchy to get revenge on them. The cartoon duo chase Bart and Lisa with lethal props, running over the despised character Poochie along the way, and the kids briefly get flung into a pot of soup on a live talk show before landing back in the cartoon house. Lisa manages to use the remote's exit button to pull them out of the TV, though Bart emerges as a piranha-stripped skeleton until Lisa rewinds him back to normal. Unfortunately, Itchy and Scratchy escape into the real world too, with Homer adopting Itchy as a pet and Snowball II falling for Scratchy, only for Marge to plan to neuter him. title: Lout Break (Treehouse of Horror XXXIV segment)

At the Power Plant, Homer sneaks donuts despite Smithers' warnings and rants about living in a "nanny state." When a donut rolls away, he chases it through the plant, and it becomes coated in radioactive waste before he eats it anyway. That night the tainted donut begins mutating his DNA, and by morning he passes the effect to Ned via a burp, turning Ned into a Homer clone. Ned then infects the entire congregation at church, and the burp-borne virus spreads across Springfield, making everyone lazy and dim-witted like Homer. Because Bart, Lisa, and Maggie share Homer's genes, they're immune, and Professor Frink recruits them to track down their father for a cure. They eventually find him hiding in a car wash toilet, where Homer explains he loves this new dumbed-down world and sees no reason to fix it, especially now that an infected Marge seems more appealing to him than ever. When Homer accidentally punctures Frink's protective suit, the professor is infected too, and the outbreak spreads worldwide as newly minted Homers everywhere celebrate their "me-topia," ending with Earth shown engulfed in green mutant clouds from space. Notable quotes: Homer: Pfft. The nanny state wins again. No tanning in the reactor core, no texting while driving and eating ribs. | Homer: Wait. Hold on. Why would I want that? Finally, everyone thinks the way I do. | Professor Frink: Uh, children, your father's less than stellar genetic code is spreading through burp-borne transmission. | Ned-Homer: I've been neighborino'd into Home-diddly-omer. Homer, dismissive of the threat, heads to a military surplus store to buy a real bomb shelter and is inside one when France actually launches a neutron bomb, wiping out the town. Emerging unharmed, Homer initially doesn't notice everyone is dead, casually going about his day until he realizes he's the town's sole survivor. He briefly enjoys his newfound freedom, dancing nude in the church, before encountering a group of mutated townsfolk who call themselves 'freaks' and want to eliminate anyone tied to the old, flawed world—including Homer. He escapes back home, only to find his family alive, protected by the many layers of lead paint in their house. Just as Ned Flanders proposes peace between mutants and normal humans, Marge and the kids reveal hidden shotguns and gun down all the mutants. title: Heck House (Treehouse of Horror XVIII segment)
text: "Heck House" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XVIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 18"), which aired as Season 19, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. On Halloween, Bart, Lisa, Milhouse and Nelson grow annoyed when neighbors refuse to hand out candy, so they escalate from harmless pranks to outright vandalism across Springfield. Ned Flanders steps in, offering to set them straight by converting the church into a haunted 'Heck House' meant to scare them away from sin. His clumsy live reenactments of sinful consequences only make the kids laugh, so he prays for real power and is transformed into the Devil himself, dragging them down to Hell. There, using a giant crystal ball, he shows them graphic visions of Springfield residents being punished for the Seven Deadly Sins—Homer turned into pasta for gluttony, Groundskeeper Willie decapitated by his tractor for wrath, Doctor Hibbert crushed between vehicles for pride, Homer chopped up in a hammock for sloth, and Moe suffering for lust, greed, and envy involving a stripper. Thoroughly terrified, the kids admit they've learned their lesson, and Ned returns them to the surface, reverting to his normal form. The segment closes with Ned breaking the fourth wall to warn viewers that watching Fox will also send them to Hell. Initially horrified at his own transformation into a walrus, Homer quickly embraces his new bestial lifestyle of eating, sleeping, mating, and wallowing in filth, deciding it suits him perfectly. text: "The Thing and I" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror VII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 7"), which aired as Season 8, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. Bart and Lisa become curious after hearing mysterious noises coming from the attic at night, but Homer and Marge refuse to explain and forbid them from going up there. As the family and Dr. Hibbert search the neighborhood for the escaped Hugo, Bart is left alone, and Hugo reveals he never actually left the house. Dr. Hibbert arrives just in time to knock Hugo unconscious, but then makes a shocking discovery: the scar's positioning proves Hugo was actually the good twin all along, meaning Bart is the true evil one. The segment ends with Bart banished to the attic in chains while Hugo takes his place as part of the family. Notable quotes: Marge: You went into the attic? title: Title Cards (Treehouse of Horror X segment)
text: "Title Cards" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror X" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 10"), which aired as Season 11, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. This brief segment consists solely of the traditional title cards that introduce each of the episode's three stories, a recurring gimmick in the Treehoues of Horror series. The first card, 'I Know What You Diddly-Iddly-Did,' is a pun combining the slasher film 'I Know What You Did Last Summer' with Ned Flanders' catchphrase. The second, 'Desperately Xeeking Xena,' riffs on the movie 'Desperately Seeking Susan' while referencing the TV show 'Xena: Warrior Princess.' The third, 'Life's a Glitch, Then You Die,' plays on the phrase 'life's a bitch, then you die' with a tech/computer twist. Each card visually sets up the tone and parody target of its respective segment before the actual story begins. No dialogue or action occurs during this purely text-based interstitial segment.

title: Clown Night with the Devil (Treehouse of Horror XXXVI segment)
text: "Clown Night with the Devil" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXVI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 36"), which aired as Season 37, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. The segment takes us back to 1995's Krusty Halloween Special, where Krusty, desperate to save his declining show, agrees to a devil's bargain for better ratings. During a sketch called "The Yuk-sorcist," Mr. Teeny becomes possessed and violently mauls Sideshow Mel on live TV, and the shocking spectacle actually boosts home viewership. Later, during the costume contest, Ralph is turned inside out as the real Devil emerges and begins killing people, revealing he's come to collect on Bart's deal to keep Krusty's show on top by canceling the competition. The Devil seizes Krusty to drag him to his infernal workshop, summoning ghosts of canceled TV characters to help, but Bart nobly offers himself instead and gets dragged down in Krusty's place. The story jumps forward to the present day, where Krusty tries to sell the horrifying old tape exclusively to Netflix, joking that not even the Devil can save a TV show now that streaming has taken over. The Devil, still hanging around, agrees with him about the sorry state of the industry, and the two end up fielding awkward questions about how this all makes sense in the modern era. [laughs] Now that's fresh! | Devil: I am Satan, and I have come for you. | Krusty: I've never shown anyone this horrific tape... until today. title: Dry Hard (Treehouse of Horror XXVII segment)
text: "Dry Hard" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXVII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 27"), which aired as Season 28, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. In a parched, post-apocalyptic Springfield, Mr. Burns has seized total control of the town's water supply, forcing residents to pay dearly for every drop while he hoards the reservoir. To settle disputes and entertain himself, Burns forces the town's children into a brutal 'Battle Dome' death match, promising the winner a day of unlimited water access. Lisa is chosen to represent Nevergreen Terrace and is paired with a grizzled mentor named Homish, in a clear riff on Mad Max: Fury Road and Hunger Games-style survival arenas. Ralph is eliminated almost immediately, blown up by a landmine before the fighting even begins. As the battle rages, two boys try to charm and manipulate Lisa but are dispatched by Homish, who then gets trapped himself and surrounded by the remaining kids. Rather than let the slaughter continue, Lisa delivers a rousing speech convincing the children to unite against Burns instead of each other. The freed kids and townspeople storm the reservoir and destroy it, but the sudden release of all that water triggers catastrophic rains, flooding, and ultimately plunges Springfield into a new ice age.

Marge hires bumbling lawyer Lionel Hutz to defend Homer before a jury of infamous villains chosen by the Devil, but Hutz inadvertently sabotages the case and flees. At the last moment, Marge produces an old photo revealing Homer had already pledged his soul to her on their wedding day, nullifying the Devil's contract. Enraged at losing, the Devil transforms Homer's head into a donut, leaving him to be devoured by the eager Springfield police the next morning. Homer forgets to buy Bart a birthday present and rushes to a strange shop called House of Evil, where he picks up a talking Krusty the Clown doll despite the store owner's ominous warnings. Homer stuffs the doll into a bag of dirty socks, locks it in a suitcase, and dumps it in a bottomless pit, only to find it has somehow followed him home anyway. As the doll tries to strangle him again, Marge calls the KrustyCo company for help, and a repairman discovers the doll's switch had simply been flipped from 'Good' to 'Evil.' Once flipped back, the now-friendly doll becomes Homer's obedient servant, forced into humiliating chores. title: Morf Transers, Trans Morfers, Snort Farmers, Untitled Robot Parody (Treehouse of Horror XIX segment)

text: "Morf Transers, Trans Morfers, Snort Farmers, Untitled Robot Parody" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XIX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 19"), which aired as Season 20, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. On Christmas Eve, Bart searches a dollar store for a last-minute gift for Lisa and dismisses a shape-shifting toy truck until it morphs into a pink Ferrari, which he decides is 'perfect.' The toy turns out to be a secretly sinister Transformer, spoofing the Transformers franchise, and it begins performing small mischievous acts around the Simpson house, from torching the tree-topper angel to comforting Maggie and menacing Lisa's doll. Overnight it summons a group of fellow 'Posibots,' each transformed from household items like an alarm clock, lamp, and boom-box, revealing an entire secret robot society hiding in plain sight. The chaos spreads the next morning as the Simpsons' appliances and even Homer's car transform into robots, while across Springfield other machines awaken and clash, including one incorporating Ned Flanders. Two giant leader robots, 'Carnage Destructicus' and 'Bestimus Mucho,' prepare for an epic battle in the town square, but Marge intervenes and gets them to stop fighting. Realizing they have no real reason to fight each other, the robots unite instead to enslave humanity, forcing Springfield's citizens into servitude as living foosball players for their amusement. Notable quotes: Moe Szyslak: Okay, who's the idiot who taught them what foosball was? | Homer: I thought they might enjoy it.
quotes: Moe Szyslak: Okay, who's the idiot who taught them what foosball was?
Homer: I thought they might enjoy it.

title: Danger Things (Treehouse of Horror XXX segment)
text: "Danger Things" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 30"), which aired as Season 31, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Set in the 1980s, Bart and his friends are playing arcade games in his treehouse when they split up to bike home, and Milhouse vanishes after being attacked in the woods. The segment parodies Stranger Things, with Kirk and Luann searching for their missing son using a wall of letters to communicate across dimensions, all while Luann's affair with Disco Stu comes to light. Meanwhile, Lisa realizes Milhouse is trapped in an alternate dimension called the Over Under after receiving a strange call from him, and she rallies Bart, Martin, and Nelson to help using Professor Frink's sensory deprivation tank. Venturing into the parallel Springfield, Lisa finds Milhouse just as flesh-eating Demogorgons attack, biting off his leg when he won't stop rambling. The kids try to flee through a monster-ravaged town until Homer bursts in with a flamethrower, revealing that Mr. Burns opened the interdimensional portal as part of a secret government experiment. Trapped together in the alternate dimension, the group settles onto a couch just before encountering—and torching—a monstrous doppelganger of Ned Flanders. Notable quotes: Chief Wiggum: Your friend's bike crashed here. We found his inhaler here. And over here is his final pee stain. | Lisa: I'd better use my psychic powers. | Homer: Mr. Burns opened a portal to another dimension that released a lot of monsters. | Milhouse: What was he looking for?
quotes: Chief Wiggum: Your friend's bike crashed here. We found his inhaler here. And over here is his final pee stain.
Lisa: I'd better use my psychic powers.
Homer: Mr. Burns opened a portal to another dimension that released a lot of monsters.
Milhouse: What was he looking for?

title: Reaper Madness (Treehouse of Horror XIV segment)
text: "Reaper Madness" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XIV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 14"), which aired as Season 15, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. Death arrives at the Simpson house to collect Bart, sparking a frantic Benny Hill-style chase through the rooms before he finally pins Bart's shirt to the wall with his scythe. Just as Death is about to deliver an eternity of torment, Homer smashes him with a bowling ball, accidentally killing the Grim Reaper himself. This sets off chaos, since with Death gone no one in the world can actually die, leading to grim but comedic scenes like a mobster being shot repeatedly without dying and Moe failing to successfully hang himself. When Marge insists Homer haul the dead Reaper's body out with the trash, he tries on the robe and instantly becomes the new Grim Reaper, forced to harvest souls from God's list. Things get personal when God orders him to kill Marge, and Homer desperately tries to negotiate his way out of the job. In a moment of dark cleverness, Homer swaps Marge's body for her sister Patty's to fulfill the quota. An enraged God attempts to smite Homer with a lethal sunbeam, but Homer escapes on a motorcycle, leaving God to grumble about being too old for this nonsense. The segment ends back home with Marge rewarding Homer with an extra pork chop, unaware of what he did. Notable quotes: Homer: Death! Death! We miss you so much! You were a busboy in the restaurant of life. | Lisa: Dad! You've become the new Grim Reaper! | Homer: No way, forget it. I might occasionally kill out of anger, or to illustrate a point. But I am not a Grim Reaper! | Moe: If I knew this would take so long I'd put out a TV.
quotes: Homer: Death! Death! We miss you so much! You were a busboy in the restaurant of life.
Lisa: Dad! You've become the new Grim Reaper!
Homer: No way, forget it. I might occasionally kill out of anger, or to illustrate a point. But I am not a Grim Reaper!
Moe: If I knew this would take so long I'd put out a TV.

title: B.I.: Bartificial Intelligence (Treehouse of Horror XVI segment)
text: "B.I.: Bartificial Intelligence" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XVI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 16"), which aired as Season 17, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. After Bart falls attempting a rooftop stunt and lapses into a coma, the grief-stricken Simpsons adopt a robotic replacement son named David, spoofing sci-fi tales of artificial children. David proves eerily obedient and superior, quickly winning over the family, which upsets Bart when he unexpectedly wakes up and returns home. The two boys become bitter rivals for the family's affection, and Marge worries about the tension escalating. Rather than resolve things sensibly, Homer decides to secretly dump Bart in the woods, where Bart scavenges parts from a group of derelict robots and rebuilds himself into a vengeful cyborg. He storms home to attack David, slicing through both David and Homer in the process, leaving Homer legless until he's grafted with David's robotic legs. The entire nightmarish scenario turns out to be a hallucination brought on by Homer being possessed by a demon, spoofing 'The Exorcist,' complete with a priest's exorcism, Homer's head spinning around, and him crawling on the ceiling before collapsing contentedly on the bed. Notable quotes: Homer: WHY YOU METAL!! [begins strangling David] Wow! The windpipe is so responsive! | David: Bart, we can be friends. | Bart: Eat my shorts! | Homer: This stinks! I've got stubby little robot legs and an ass that's not equipped for an adult diet!
quotes: Homer: WHY YOU METAL!! [begins strangling David] Wow! The windpipe is so responsive!
David: Bart, we can be friends.
Bart: Eat my shorts!
Homer: This stinks! I've got stubby little robot legs and an ass that's not equipped for an adult diet!

title: Wild Barts Can't Be Token (Treehouse of Horror XXXIV segment)
text: "Wild Barts Can't Be Token" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXIV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 34"), which aired as Season 35, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. The segment opens with Mayor Quimby announcing that Springfield's art museum will close permanently, with its collection digitized into NFTs. Homer and Bart sneak into the museum, and Bart cheekily decides to turn his own mooning image into an NFT using the E-Z Funge Art Digitizer, unaware the machine actually destroys what it scans. Bart's physical body is obliterated and his essence sent into the blockchain, horrifying Marge when Homer breaks the news. Celebrities Kylie Jenner, Rob Gronkowski, and Jimmy Fallon appear to explain that Marge must enter the blockchain herself to rescue him. Inside, Marge finds herself trapped in a train of worthless NFTs, and discovers that killing other NFTs raises her value, letting her advance car by car toward the front. Meanwhile in the real world, Kirk and Chief Wiggum greedily digitize Milhouse and Ralph, who emerge fused together in the blockchain, only for Marge to destroy them too. Reaching the front, Marge finds Bart living a life of NFT luxury and tries to convince him to leave, while Mr. Burns tempts Homer into selling Bart; Homer instead accidentally sells himself as an NFT while Marge and Bart escape. Homer briefly enjoys his own luxurious blockchain life until the NFT market crashes, and his enormous shout of "D'oh!" triggers an avalanche that buries him and all the NFTs forever. Notable quotes: Mayor Quimby: Art lovers of Springfield, good news. The art museum is closed forever! Instead, our entire collection will be digitized and sold for a fortune on the blockchain as non-fungible tokens, or NFTs. | Homer: Honey? Remember how we're always saying we wish Bart was less fungible? | Marge: [gasps] My baby is an app! | Chief Wiggum: No one is putting another child into that scanner... before mine.
quotes: Mayor Quimby: Art lovers of Springfield, good news. The art museum is closed forever! Instead, our entire collection will be digitized and sold for a fortune on the blockchain as non-fungible tokens, or NFTs.
Homer: Honey? Remember how we're always saying we wish Bart was less fungible?
Marge: [gasps] My baby is an app!
Chief Wiggum: No one is putting another child into that scanner... before mine.

title: Terror at 5 1/2 Feet (Treehouse of Horror IV segment)
text: "Terror at 5 1/2 Feet" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror IV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 4"), which aired as Season 5, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. Bart wakes from a nightmare about a bus crash and boards the school bus in a paranoid, jittery mood, only to be mocked by his classmates after Lisa's attempt to defend him backfires. During the ride he keeps spotting a mysterious Gremlin tearing at the bus's exterior, but every time he alerts someone, the creature vanishes before they can see it, making him look increasingly unhinged. In a parody of the classic 'Nightmare at 20,000 Feet' Twilight Zone segment, no one believes him, including Principal Skinner, who scolds him for using his imagination, and Milhouse, who abandons him for fear of looking weird by association. Meanwhile a cutaway reveals aliens Kang and Kodos mocking humans for imagining monsters, right before the Gremlin destroys their own ship. Desperate, Bart grabs a flare and hurls it out the window at the creature while being restrained by Willie and Skinner, successfully knocking the Gremlin off the bus and into the path of Ned Flanders' car. The bus limps into school wrecked, proving Bart right, but as punishment for his 'disruptive' behavior he's sent away to a mental institution anyway. The segment closes with the Gremlin, having taken up residence with Ned, attacking the ambulance carrying Bart while clutching Ned's severed head. Notable quotes: Bart: Eyahh! Everybody! There's a monster on the side of the bus! | Skinner: The only monster on this bus is a lack of proper respect for the rules. | Bart: Look at the bus! I was right, I tell ya! I was right! | Skinner: Right or wrong, your behavior was still disruptive, young man. Perhaps spending the remainder of your life in a madhouse will teach you some manners.
quotes: Bart: Eyahh! Everybody! There's a monster on the side of the bus!
Skinner: The only monster on this bus is a lack of proper respect for the rules.
Bart: Look at the bus! I was right, I tell ya! I was right!
Skinner: Right or wrong, your behavior was still disruptive, young man. Perhaps spending the remainder of your life in a madhouse will teach you some manners.

title: America the Beautiful (Treehouse of Horror XXXVI segment)
text: "America the Beautiful" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXVI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 36"), which aired as Season 37, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. The episode opens with a Simpson-like family enjoying Halloween outside their home when a sudden storm interrupts the festivities. Three ominous figures approach: a werewolf symbolizing global trade wars, Frankenstein's Monster representing debates over gender pronouns, and Death himself embodying the real-world measles outbreak. Terrified, the family flees indoors, treating network television as their only refuge from these looming societal horrors. They turn on the TV to watch "The Simpsons" itself, seeking comfort in the show as chaos looms outside. Meanwhile, outside their window, series creator Matt Groening looks on approvingly, wearing a shirt that mocks or references devoted fans of the show. The bit serves as a satirical framing device, blending real-world anxieties with Halloween imagery before the episode's actual segments begin.

title: UNnormal Activity (Treehouse of Horror XXIII segment)
text: "UNnormal Activity" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 23"), which aired as Season 24, Episode 2 of The Simpsons. Spoofing the Paranormal Activity franchise, Homer sets up a camcorder to document strange nocturnal events plaguing the house. That first night an unseen force strips off the covers and beats Homer with a golf club before wrecking the living room downstairs. Homer installs more cameras, and later footage shows Marge eerily standing over sleeping Homer and even watching him in the bathroom. Chief Wiggum investigates hellfire damage and declares someone made a pact with the devil, then is promptly eaten by the unseen demon. When the entity tries to snatch baby Maggie, Marge intervenes, and Bart exposes the invisible creature as a Moe-lookalike Satan using talcum powder. Marge confesses she struck a deal years earlier with the devil to save Patty and Selma from a summoning gone wrong, promising to sacrifice her favorite child in return. Homer tries to renegotiate the deal, leading to an awkward proposed three-way with the devil and another demon, which ends with Homer doing something so objectionable that the devil frantically repeats his own safe word. Notable quotes: Homer: We've bought this camera because strange things have been going on at our house in the dead of night. And if anyone finds this footage after we're all missing or dead, remember me as a hero. | Homer: Oh, sweetie, sometimes a mysterious, invisible being from hell waits for a family to go to sleep then kills them. Now go to bed. | Homer: Now, before we start what's the safe word? | Moe-looking Satan: Cinnamon! Cinnamon! Cinnamon!
quotes: Homer: We've bought this camera because strange things have been going on at our house in the dead of night. And if anyone finds this footage after we're all missing or dead, remember me as a hero.
Homer: Oh, sweetie, sometimes a mysterious, invisible being from hell waits for a family to go to sleep then kills them. Now go to bed.
Homer: Now, before we start what's the safe word?
Moe-looking Satan: Cinnamon! Cinnamon! Cinnamon!

title: Act I: Lisa's nightmare (Treehouse of Horror II segment)
text: "Act I: Lisa's nightmare" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror II" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 2"), which aired as Season 3, Episode 7 of The Simpsons. After gorging on Halloween candy despite Marge's warning, the Simpsons drift into nightmares, starting with Lisa's. While vacationing in Morocco, Homer purchases a cursed monkey's paw from a mysterious merchant, ignoring warnings that it grants wishes with terrible consequences. Back home, each family member makes a wish: Maggie's request for a golden pacifier goes fine, but Bart's wish for wealth and fame turns the family into overexposed celebrities plastered on tacky ads. Lisa's wish for world peace backfires spectacularly when aliens Kang and Kodos invade the now-defenseless Earth and enslave humanity. Homer, trying to outsmart the curse, wishes for a plain turkey sandwich, only to be enraged over a piece of slightly dry turkey, prompting him to hurl the paw away. Ned Flanders picks it up and inadvertently becomes a hero by wishing away the alien invaders, then wishes his house into a castle, leaving a jealous, fuming Homer to declare he wishes he had a monkey's paw of his own. Notable quotes: Marge: Homer, where'd you get the monkey's paw? | Homer: I got it from the stand... over... there. | Merchant: You will be sorry. | Kodos: They constructed a board with a nail in it, but they won't stop there.
quotes: Marge: Homer, where'd you get the monkey's paw?
Homer: I got it from the stand... over... there.
Merchant: You will be sorry.
Kodos: They constructed a board with a nail in it, but they won't stop there.

title: I Know What You Diddily-Iddily-Did (Treehouse of Horror X segment)
text: "I Know What You Diddily-Iddily-Did" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror X" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 10"), which aired as Season 11, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. During a foggy, moonlit drive, Marge accidentally runs over Ned Flanders, killing him instantly. Homer and the family panic and decide to cover up the death, with Homer even puppeteering Ned's corpse to convince Maude he's fine before secretly dumping the body. After a hasty funeral, Homer gloats about getting away with murder, but the family soon finds the ominous message "I know what you did" scrawled on their door, then covering the interior of their house and car, echoing the slasher-parody premise of 'I Know What You Did Last Summer.' A creepy phone call turns out to be a wrong number from Moe trying to reach Maude, ratcheting up the tension before a hook-wielding, cloaked figure chases the family from their home. Homer sends everyone to separately hide in horror-movie clichés like an abandoned amusement park and a pet cemetery, but the stalker catches up regardless. The figure is revealed to be Ned himself, who survived the crash only because he'd been bitten by a werewolf moments earlier. As the family laughs off the reveal, the moonlight triggers Ned's transformation into a werewolf, and he mauls Homer to death while the rest of the family flees. Notable quotes: Homer: Hello? | Mysterious Voice: I know you're alone! | Moe: Oh! Hey Homer, it's Moe! I must have dialed the wrong number.
quotes: Homer: Hello?
Mysterious Voice: I know you're alone!
Moe: Oh! Hey Homer, it's Moe! I must have dialed the wrong number.

title: Heaven Swipes Right (Treehouse of Horror XXX segment)
text: "Heaven Swipes Right" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 30"), which aired as Season 31, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. At a football game, Homer chokes to death on a hot dog while the crowd chants "choke." In Heaven, he's greeted by St. Greeter, whose pun on his own name so annoys Homer that the greeter is damned to Hell on the spot. Homer learns that God has sold Heaven to Google and that he died before his allotted time, but his own decaying body is no longer usable. As compensation, he's allowed to inhabit the body of someone else fated to die that day, and he picks star quarterback Case Diggs, delighting Marge with his new physique. Homer quickly ruins the body through gluttony, prompting Bart and Marge to push him into trying Superintendent Chalmers next. Using Chalmers' authority, Homer forces Skinner to give Bart perfect grades and torment himself with an ever-deepening "purple nurple," but abandons that body upon discovering Chalmers' meager salary. After hopping bodies again, an exasperated Marge finally gets Homer to settle down—he chooses to possess Moe, the man who loves her almost as much as he does—but the swap goes wrong, leaving Moe's consciousness stuck in baby Maggie's body, announcing that he's thirsty. Notable quotes: St. Greeter: No, I'm St. Greeter, if you'll forgive the pun. | Homer: I don't forgive it. | Homer: Give yourself a purple nurple. Purpler. Purpler. | Homer: Because I know something about you that no one else knows.
quotes: St. Greeter: No, I'm St. Greeter, if you'll forgive the pun.
Homer: I don't forgive it.
Homer: Give yourself a purple nurple. Purpler. Purpler.
Homer: Because I know something about you that no one else knows.

title: The Pookadook (Treehouse of Horror XXXIII segment)
text: "The Pookadook" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 33"), which aired as Season 34, Episode 6 of The Simpsons. Marge searches her bookshelf for a bedtime story and keeps finding a mysterious book called The Pookadook, which she doesn't remember owning. She reluctantly reads it to Maggie, but it terrifies them both, so she puts it away. That night Maggie is found screaming with the book somehow back in her crib, prompting Marge to destroy it and toss it in the trash. The next morning the repaired book reappears on the doorstep, and when Marge burns it on the barbecue, a page reveals the book wanted to be burned all along—releasing a monstrous entity called The Pookadook, which possesses Marge. Now controlling Marge's body, The Pookadook sends the rest of the family off on an aquarium sleepover so it can hunt down Maggie alone. Maggie flees to the basement and rigs a trap using recalled baby products, battling the creature with a flaming doll and a crayon gun before it's finally knocked out by tripping on a crayon. After being tied up and breaking free again, The Pookadook nearly overpowers Maggie, but a tender touch from Maggie breaks through to the real Marge, who coughs up the entity and vacuums it away with her birthday present, an outdoor vacuum. The segment ends with Marge and Maggie reconciling as the rest of the family returns home sick from their aquarium trip. Notable quotes: Marge: When Pookie gets a hold of you, you'll change for the worse, eliminate those nuisances... the littlest one first. | The Pookadook: The family's getting in the way of Maggie-Mommy time. I'll make them sleep with the fishes. | The Pookadook: Look what else my loving family got me for my birthday. A vacuum that cleans the outside. | Marge: Oh, Maggie, I'm so sorry I got possessed and almost chopped you up into little pieces. Oh, but I'm here now. Mommy's here.

The Pookadook: The family's getting in the way of Maggie-Mommy time. I'll make them sleep with the fishes.

title: Wraparound part 1 (Treehouse of Horror IV segment)
text: "Wraparound part 1" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror IV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 4"), which aired as Season 5, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. In a parody of Rod Serling's Night Gallery, Bart walks through a dark gallery of eerie paintings, introducing the night's Halloween anthology segments. He begins his ominous narration about paintings coming to life as portals to horror, but before he can finish, Marge interrupts. She insists Bart warn viewers that the episode is very frightening, suggesting nervous audience members might prefer listening to an old radio broadcast instead. Maggie is also present during this brief exchange, though she doesn't speak. Bart reluctantly agrees to his mother's request rather than argue. The wraparound then transitions directly into the episode's first horror segment. Notable quotes: Bart: Paintings. Lifeless images rendered in colorful goop. But at night, they take on a life of their own. | Marge: Bart! You should warn people this episode is very frightening and maybe they'd rather listen to that old 1938 radio drama broadcast on NPR, Hmmm? | Bart: Yes, mother.
quotes: Bart: Paintings. Lifeless images rendered in colorful goop. But at night, they take on a life of their own.
Marge: Bart! You should warn people this episode is very frightening and maybe they'd rather listen to that old 1938 radio drama broadcast on NPR, Hmmm?
Bart: Yes, mother.

title: Coralisa (Treehouse of Horror XXVIII segment)
text: "Coralisa" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXVIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 28"), which aired as Season 29, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Still queasy after her ordeal with the demon Pazuzu, Maggie vomits at the dinner table while Lisa retreats to her room, where Snowball II suddenly reveals he can talk and leads her through a hidden tunnel. On the other side she discovers an alternate version of her family, all with buttons sewn over their eyes, who eat vegetables and play jazz—everything Lisa wishes her real family would do. The other-Homer offers to let her stay permanently if she lets them sew buttons over her eyes, and though she initially flees home in terror, a chance encounter with a snake and her saxophone changes her mind, and she returns to accept the buttons. Days later her real family barely mourns her disappearance, casually redistributing her room and belongings, and Bart sneaks through the tunnel to join the button-eyed world himself. Marge follows to retrieve her children but gets seduced into staying by the alternate Homer's total lack of flatulence. Snowball then lures the real Homer through the tunnel, where he violently decapitates the other Bart and accidentally causes the other Homer's death by impaling him on a sewing needle, provoking the alternate Marge to sprout extra grotesque limbs in rage. The segment ends with the real Homer and Marge exploiting their captured other-world duplicates for chores and parent-teacher conferences. Notable quotes: Lisa: Whoa! For a Halloween show middle segment, this is amazing!
quotes: Lisa: Whoa! For a Halloween show middle segment, this is amazing!

title: In the Belly of the Boss (Treehouse of Horror XV segment)
keys: in the belly of the boss
text: "In the Belly of the Boss" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 15"), which aired as Season 16, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. At an invention expo, Professor Frink unveils a shrink ray combined with a giant medicine capsule, and baby Maggie sneaks into the capsule thinking it holds toys just before Frink shrinks it. Mr. Burns swallows the tiny pill without noticing Maggie inside, and Marge realizes what happened when she hears her daughter's voice coming from within him. Frink shrinks the rest of the Simpsons and sends them into Burns aboard a miniature "Bionaut" ship to retrieve her, spoofing Fantastic Voyage. Homer's reckless piloting sends the ship crashing into Burns' heart and later causes an internal explosion after he mashes every button on the console. The family eventually rescues Maggie, but her added weight overloads the ship, forcing Homer to stay behind inside Burns while the others escape. Before Frink can plan a rescue, Homer grows back to full size inside Burns, bursting partway through his skin. The segment ends with the enlarged Homer and Burns dining together at The Gilded Truffle, then bursting into a rendition of "I've Got You Under My Skin" as characters from the episode's other segments join in dancing. Notable quotes: Professor Frink: Bio-nauts assemble! | Homer: Captain! | Marge: Why is my swimsuit so revealing? | Marge: Bart, what are you doing?

Homer: Captain!

title: Ei8ht (Treehouse of Horror XXXIV segment)
text: "Ei8ht" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXIV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 34"), which aired as Season 35, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. This segment is a horror-mystery parody blending "Cape Feare" with the film Se7en. It opens with an alternate ending where Sideshow Bob catches on to Bart's stalling tactic and kills him with a machete while Lisa watches in horror. Decades later, Lisa is a criminal psychology professor recruited by Officer Nelson Muntz to solve a string of murders, each victim marked with the cryptic phrase "[Name] is the first," including Rod Flanders, Martin's brother Montaigne, Dermott Spuckler, and Sherri. Stumped, Lisa turns to imprisoned Sideshow Bob, who refuses direct help but taunts her with riddles, anagrams, and a grisly limerick about Bart's death. After learning from Terri that Sherri was actually the older twin, Lisa deduces the victims are all first-born children and that Bob's "anagram" comment points to Ana Gram's Spooky Abandoned Slaughterhouse. There, Nelson is killed, and Lisa discovers a lair resembling her own bedroom along with footage proving she herself is the murderer. In the final twist, it's revealed Lisa has a split personality, with her security-guard sister Maggie aiding her killer alter ego, and the segment ends with Lisa murdering Sideshow Bob in his cell while dancing to "He Is an Englishman." Notable quotes: Sideshow Bob: Wait. Did you only ask me to sing to forestall your gruesome end? | Lisa: Our killer took his time. Had fun with it. Enjoyed a game of Solitaire. Red King on a Red Queen? This psycho doesn't play by the rules. | Sideshow Bob: Really, Professor Simpson, am I meant to spoon-feed you all the answers? Speak in riddles or drop a clue in a clever anagram hidden in something I've just said right now. | Lisa: You're gonna die in that cell, Bob. And when that happens, wherever I am, I'll be dancing.
quotes: Sideshow Bob: Wait. Did you only ask me to sing to forestall your gruesome end?
Lisa: Our killer took his time. Had fun with it. Enjoyed a game of Solitaire. Red King on a Red Queen? This psycho doesn't play by the rules.
Sideshow Bob: Really, Professor Simpson, am I meant to spoon-feed you all the answers? Speak in riddles or drop a clue in a clever anagram hidden in something I've just said right now.
Lisa: You're gonna die in that cell, Bob. And when that happens, wherever I am, I'll be dancing.

title: Tweenlight (Treehouse of Horror XXI segment)
text: "Tweenlight" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 21"), which aired as Season 22, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Lisa falls for Edmund, a brooding vampire boy, in a clear parody of the Twilight romance saga. When he confesses what he is, Lisa brings him home for a family dinner that Homer and the ever-present Count Dracula turn into a mortifying spectacle, driving the embarrassed teens to flee together to the fantastical realm of Dracula-la Land. Homer and Dracula track them down, and Dracula and Edmund attempt to force Lisa into becoming a vampire against her will. Homer intervenes to protect his daughter, and in the struggle the vampires bite him, only to discover his blood is dangerously high in cholesterol, which poisons and kills them both. Triumphant but transformed, Homer then finds himself turned into an obese bat. He tries to fly off to safety but, weighed down by his own fatness, plummets to his death instead. Notable quotes: Homer: They should call this one recipe for murder. | Count Dracula: His blood! It's full of cholesterol! | Homer: And not the good kind. | Edmund: Let's move between the trees the way a bat does: by jumping!
quotes: Homer: They should call this one recipe for murder.
Count Dracula: His blood! It's full of cholesterol!
Homer: And not the good kind.
Edmund: Let's move between the trees the way a bat does: by jumping!

title: Closing (Treehouse of Horror XXVI segment)
text: "Closing" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXVI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 26"), which aired as Season 27, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. In this brief closing segment, aliens Kang and Kodos appear once more to bookend the episode. They grumble to each other that despite being fan-favorite characters, they have once again been relegated to a mere cameo appearance rather than getting a full segment of their own. Their brief bit serves as a meta, self-aware joke about the show's tendency to use them only for quick gags in the Treehouse of Horror specials. The two aliens express frustration at being underused, breaking the fourth wall to comment on their own minor role. There's no plot beyond this short comedic exchange, and the episode ends immediately after their complaint, closing out the anthology on a humorous, self-referential note. Notable quotes: Kang: Just 'cause it looks like season four doesn't make it season four!
quotes: Kang: Just 'cause it looks like season four doesn't make it season four!

title: The Diving Bell and Butterball (Treehouse of Horror XXII segment)
text: "The Diving Bell and Butterball" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 22"), which aired as Season 23, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. A real spider gets tangled among the Halloween decorations and bites Homer, leaving him completely paralyzed, unable to move or speak, in a parody of "The Diving Bell and the Butterfly." Lisa tries to keep him entertained by reading aloud from Dostoevsky's The Brothers Karamazov, which horrifies the trapped and conscious Homer. Unable to protest verbally, Homer discovers he can still fart, and uses these flatulent outbursts as a makeshift Morse code to communicate his displeasure. Lisa cleverly deciphers his gaseous signals and relays his wishes to Marge, restoring some quality of life to him. Later, Homer is bitten by yet another spider, but this time the bite grants him superpowers instead of paralysis. He becomes a flatulent version of Spider-Man, swinging around the city on a hand truck cable, blasting web-like farts to catch criminals. The segment ends with Homer and Marge swinging off together back toward home, fully embracing his new powers.

title: In the Na'vi (Treehouse of Horror XXII segment)
text: "In the Na'vi" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 22"), which aired as Season 23, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. On the distant planet Rigel 7, human forces scheme to harvest hillarium, a rare liquid that makes everything seem hilarious, intended as a gift for Krusty the Clown. Bart Simpson and Milhouse are transferred into blue avatar bodies, à la the film Avatar, and sent to infiltrate the native Rigellian population and locate the hillarium source. While undercover, Bart falls for a Rigellian named Kamala, and their relationship results in her becoming pregnant. Milhouse learns that the hillarium is actually secreted by the Rigellian queen, and reports this back to the human command, triggering an all-out war between humanity and the Rigellians backed by their planet's hostile nature. Despite the humans' assault, the Rigellians triumph, and Bart personally defeats the human commander Gary Chalmers in combat. In the aftermath, Kamala reveals the bitter irony that the Rigellians would have willingly handed over the hillarium if the humans had simply asked instead of attacking. Notable quotes: Bart: Where am I?
quotes: Bart: Where am I?

title: Send in the Clones (Treehouse of Horror XIII segment)
text: "Send in the Clones" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 13"), which aired as Season 14, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. Homer's hammock collapses, so he buys a replacement from a shady vendor who cryptically warns it's cursed. He soon discovers the hammock clones anyone who lies on it, and the copies lack belly buttons and are noticeably dumber than the original. Homer exploits an army of clones to handle his chores and family duties, but chaos ensues when one clone misinterprets a request from Ned Flanders and returns with his severed head instead of his chainsaw. Panicked, Homer loads the clones into a truck and dumps them in a remote cornfield, shooting the ones dumb enough to ask for directions home before abandoning the rest with the hammock. The remaining clones use the hammock to multiply into a massive army, including bizarre 'mutant' variants like Tracy Ullman-era Homer and Family Guy's Peter Griffin, and they rampage through Springfield destroying everything except Moe's Tavern. In a war room parody of Apocalypse Now, Lisa devises a plan using donut-laden helicopters to lure the donut-obsessed clones off a cliff into a gorge, wiping them out one by one with echoing 'D'oh!' cries. That night, Marge realizes the Homer beside her in bed is actually a clone (no belly button) who reveals the real Homer died first in the gorge, but she's soon comforted by his offer of a back rub. Notable quotes: Homer clone: First over cliff. | Marge: My homie's dead?! How will I go on? | Homer clone: You like backrub? | Homer: Now there's four of me. I think this might be a magic hammock.

Marge: My homie's dead?! How will I go on?
Homer clone: You like backrub?
Homer: Now there's four of me. I think this might be a magic hammock.

title: Mr. and Mrs. Simpson (Treehouse of Horror XVIII segment)
text: "Mr. and Mrs. Simpson" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XVIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 18"), which aired as Season 19, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. Homer and Marge sit in what appears to be a marriage counselor's office, recounting a recent incident to explain their tension. In flashback, Homer sneaks off to a hidden television hidden in the bathroom, revealing he's a secret assassin working for Mr. Burns, tasked with killing news anchor Kent Brockman. Both spouses lie to each other about their evening plans before heading out. At Brockman's rooftop party, a mysterious blonde-wigged woman stabs Brockman before Homer can shoot him, and after a chaotic shootout that claims several bystanders, Homer shoots off her wig to reveal it's Marge, also a professional killer. The couple's mutual distrust erupts into a violent standoff with grenades, rifles, and a minigun, but after accidentally teaming up to kill Chief Wiggum with a crossbow, they realize the thrill of killing together reignites their passion, leading to a tryst over Wiggum's body. The story loops back to reveal the 'counselor' was actually Principal Skinner discussing Bart's misbehavior, and the couple, uninterested in disciplining their son, simply shoot Skinner together instead.

title: Citizen Kang (Treehouse of Horror VII segment)
text: "Citizen Kang" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror VII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 7"), which aired as Season 8, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. While fishing, Homer is abducted by aliens Kang and Kodos, who demand to meet Earth's leader. Homer explains the upcoming presidential election, prompting the aliens to kidnap candidates Bill Clinton and Bob Dole, sealing them in tubes aboard the ship and impersonating them. To discredit Homer as a witness, they douse him in rum before dumping him back on Earth, ensuring his family and everyone else dismiss his story as drunken rambling. Disguised as Clinton and Dole, Kang and Kodos run a bizarre, contradiction-filled campaign, spouting nonsensical policies and behaving oddly in public, all while the media and public remain oblivious. On election night, Homer stumbles onto the parked UFO and frees the real Clinton and Dole, but accidentally launches the ship into space and ejects them, killing both candidates. He crash-lands the UFO into the U.S. Capitol and exposes Kang and Kodos on live television, proving his earlier claims true. Unfazed, the aliens simply remind the shocked crowd that America's two-party system means they must vote for one of them anyway. Kang wins the election, and the aliens begin enslaving humanity as the segment ends.

title: Dial "Z" for Zombies (Treehouse of Horror III segment)
text: "Dial "Z" for Zombies" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror III" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 3"), which aired as Season 4, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. Bart searches the school library for material for a book report and stumbles upon a book of occult magic. Wanting to cheer up Lisa, he attempts to use it to resurrect their late cat, Snowball I, but instead accidentally raises hundreds of corpses from the Springfield Cemetery. The reanimated dead swarm the town, forcing Homer to grab a shotgun and lead Bart and Lisa back to the school library to find the counter-spell. Along the way, a zombified Ned Flanders threatens to eat Homer's ear, prompting Homer to shoot him dead without realizing he was undead. Bart finds a spell, but casts it incorrectly, turning Lisa into a snail without her noticing; he awkwardly covers by complimenting her instead of explaining. He then finds the correct incantation and reverses the zombie plague, sending the reanimated corpses back to their graves and dropping the infected dead in the streets, while also restoring Lisa to normal. The segment, a parody of Alfred Hitchcock's "Dial M for Murder," ends with the family safely back home watching TV. Notable quotes: Lisa: Dad, we did something very bad! | Homer: Did you wreck the car? | Ned: Hey, Simpson. I'm feeling a mite peckish. Mind if I chew your ear!? | Bart: Dad, you killed the zombie Flanders!

Homer: Did you wreck the car?

title: Be Nine, Rewind (Treehouse of Horror XXXI segment)
text: "Be Nine, Rewind" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 31"), which aired as Season 32, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. On her ninth birthday, Lisa comes downstairs only to have Sherri and Terri mock her party as a gathering for losers, prompting her to wish for death—which she gets when a car crashes through the window. She wakes up back at the start of the day, trapped in a Groundhog Day-style time loop, and begins experimenting with changing events, including shoving Milhouse in front of the same car driven by a test-taking Gil with Patty as his instructor. Each reset ends in another absurd death, from a collapsing treehouse to a falling mirror, birthday candle burns, a stabbing, and a crushing air conditioner. She eventually discovers Nelson is also aware of the loop, and after he dies in a woodchipper, Lisa sacrifices herself to save him, though he reveals too late that there was another solution. Consulting Comic Book Guy for genre expertise on breaking temporal loops, the pair conclude the key is stopping Gil's car before it ever crashes into the house. They successfully throw a brick at Gil's car, ending the loop, and Lisa finally gets to enjoy her birthday party in peace, aside from Ralph's head being twisted backward as a lingering side effect. Notable quotes: Sherri: Nice party, Lisa. Didn't realize the theme was being a loser. | Lisa: My party is not full of losers. | Ralph Wiggum: I can burp magic. | Nelson: Or we could just kill Gil.
quotes: Sherri: Nice party, Lisa. Didn't realize the theme was being a loser.
Lisa: My party is not full of losers.

title: There's No Business Like Moe Business (Treehouse of Horror XX segment)
keys: there's no business like moe business
text: "There's No Business Like Moe Business" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 20"), which aired as Season 21, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. This segment parodies the backstage/stage-musical genre by staging Moe's life as a musical number set in Moe's Tavern. When a tap breaks, Moe heads to the basement to fix it just as Homer leaps over the bar for a free drink and falls through a trap door, becoming grotesquely impaled on machinery below. Rather than helping his friend, Moe seizes the chance to pursue Marge, lying that Homer abandoned her because he no longer loves her. He serves Marge a drink secretly mixed with Homer's blood, which sparks her romantic feelings for Moe. A week later, Moe fabricates a letter claiming Homer left because he realized he was gay, then sneaks back downstairs to "restock" more of Homer's blood for another drink. Just as Moe and Marge begin a romantic duet, Homer reappears—still skewered on the machine—exposes Moe's scheme, and beats him up. Homer asks if Marge could love a man who's essentially half beer, and she tearfully affirms she always has, leading into a full-cast musical finale.

title: The Shinning (Treehouse of Horror V segment)
text: "The Shinning" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror V" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 5"), which aired as Season 6, Episode 6 of The Simpsons. The Simpsons drive off to spend the winter as caretakers of a remote hotel owned by Mr. Burns, a clear parody of The Shining, with repeated comic delays as they forget to lock doors and even leave Grampa behind. Once they arrive, Bart discovers he has "the shinning" after reading Groundskeeper Willie's mind in the hedge maze, and Willie warns him to call for help if Homer ever goes crazy. Mr. Burns has Smithers cut the cable and remove all the beer, and deprived of television and alcohol, Homer quickly descends into madness, scrawling deranged messages on the walls. The ghost of Moe appears in the bar and urges Homer to murder his family in exchange for a beer, pushing him further over the edge. Homer knocks himself out, is locked in the pantry, but is freed by Moe's ghostly cronies and goes on a rampage with an axe, chasing his family through the hotel. Marge's call for help is misunderstood by Chief Wiggum, so Bart uses his psychic link to summon Willie, who rushes to help but is axed to death by Homer upon arrival. The family escapes into the snow, and Lisa calms Homer by showing him Willie's dropped portable TV, but they end up frozen solid around it, horrified that they can't change the channel when the Tony Awards come on. Notable quotes: Marge: Homer, did you remember to lock the front door of the house? | Willie: [gasps] Boy, you read my thoughts! You've got the "shinning." | Moe: See? Now waste your family and I'll give you a beer! | Marge: [over radio] Hello, police? This is Marge Simpson. My husband is on a murderous rampage. Over.

Willie: [gasps] Boy, you read my thoughts! You've got the "shinning."
Moe: See? Now waste your family and I'll give you a beer!

title: Dial D for Diddily (Treehouse of Horror XXII segment)
text: "Dial D for Diddily" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 22"), which aired as Season 23, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. Ned Flanders is shown driving around a rundown part of Springfield, performing small acts of kindness before shockingly disposing of a corpse in a lake. Mr. Burns arrives to illegally dump nuclear waste at the same spot, and a booming voice Ned believes is God commands him to kill Burns, which he obediently does. Returning home, Ned continues to receive what he thinks are divine orders, murdering Sideshow Bob, Patty, and Selma one by one. When Ned discovers that the voice guiding him is actually Homer pretending to be God, he sets out to kill Homer in retaliation. Homer desperately burns Ned's Bible to stop the killings, but the real God then appears and strangles Homer to death himself. Marge walks in on the aftermath, and God pins the blame on Ned instead of Homer or himself. When Marge begs God to fix everything, he claims the Devil wouldn't approve, and the Devil then appears asking God to bring him tea, while Maude Flanders shows up asking the Devil to return to bed, much to Ned's horror and confusion.

title: The Exor-Sis (Treehouse of Horror XXVIII segment)
text: "The Exor-Sis" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXVIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 28"), which aired as Season 29, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. An ancient Pazuzu statue is unearthed in Iraq and shipped via Amazon to the Simpson household, where it briefly possesses Homer before he places it in Maggie's crib. Downstairs, the Simpsons are hosting a cocktail party, unaware that Maggie has become possessed and is now floating menacingly down the stairs. The demonic baby kills Helen Lovejoy for complaining, seals the house shut, and exposes Dr. Hibbert's infidelity before murdering him as well. Ned Flanders insists an exorcism is needed, but is killed before help arrives. Father Ben finally performs the ritual, successfully driving the demon out of Maggie—only for it to leap into Bart without anyone noticing. Bart uses Pazuzu's power to sprout small horns, and when Homer teases him about them, he angrily grows them to enormous antler size, impaling Homer through the nose. The segment ends with Homer forced to attend jury duty with a giant antler still lodged in his head. Notable quotes: Marge: Maggie, sweetie. You should be in bed. | Pazuzu: No one leaves alive! | Pazuzu: I used to be very important. Google it. | Priest: If you can't trust a Catholic priest with a child, who can you trust?

Pazuzu: No one leaves alive!

title: Intrusion of the Pod-Y Switchers (Treehouse of Horror XXIX segment)
text: "Intrusion of the Pod-Y Switchers" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXIX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 29"), which aired as Season 30, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. In Mapple's underwater lair, aging CEO Steve Mobbs unveils his replacement along with the new MyPhone Ultima, but his chosen successor is secretly an alien scout preparing an invasion of Earth. Alien spores rain down on Springfield, silently duplicating townspeople like Comic Book Guy, Marge, and Chief Wiggum with emotionless pod-people copies, a clear riff on Invasion of the Body Snatchers. Bart and Lisa realize what's happening and try to flee town with Lou in a police cruiser, but their escape attempt fails. Lisa is abducted and taken to the aliens' home world in the Crab Nebula, which at first appears to be a shining utopian society. There she's greeted warmly by two alien beings named Xylem and Phloem. The twist ending reveals that even this seemingly perfect alien civilization isn't immune to modern annoyances, as huckster Herb Tannenbaum shows up peddling phones to the aliens just as he would on Earth.

title: Denim (Treehouse of Horror XXXV segment)
text: "Denim" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 35"), which aired as Season 36, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. Homer and Barney go pants shopping so Homer can impress Marge, a waitress he's smitten with, though Homer doubts any jeans can help his luck. A strange electrical rift suddenly tears open in the store and spits out a sentient pair of jeans called Denim, which fits Homer perfectly and hitches a ride with him to the diner. Denim reveals itself as an alien "bio-adaptive symbiote" fleeing its dying home planet, and it needs a human host to survive, taking control of Homer's body to fend off a robbery by Snake and later to woo Marge with slick dance moves. Their romance blossoms with Denim's coaching, but the jeans refuse to be removed even during an intimate hotel night, and Homer starts to feel trapped by his clingy new pants. Desperate to break free, Homer gets Denim drunk so Marge can wash it, but the jeans become enraged and attack her, forcing Homer to blind it with a lemon and stab it, wounding his own leg in the process. The wounded Denim detaches and hops between hosts until it possesses Marge, dragging her to a rooftop, where Homer is forced to choose between saving her and keeping Denim. Denim ultimately lets Marge live since its species needs many hosts to survive, and the segment ends with a massive rift opening in the sky, raining down countless more Denim-jeans onto Earth. Notable quotes: Denim: I'm magical pants, okay? | Denim: To survive on your planet, our species requires a human host. And my host is you. | Homer: Run, Marge, run! Run from my pants! | Denim: No, no, no. Homer, don't break up with me. No one will ever flatter your ass like I do.

title: Opening segment (Treehouse of Horror III segment)
text: "Opening segment" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror III" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 3"), which aired as Season 4, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. The episode opens with a parody of Alfred Hitchcock's classic silhouette introduction, but Homer takes the place of the famous director. He warns the audience that the upcoming stories might be too frightening, joking that this especially applies to Christian viewers, and playfully dares them to turn off their television while doing a chicken impression. As the screen goes dark, Homer and Marge's voices continue to be heard even though nothing is visible. The scene then transitions through a spooky graveyard before settling on the Simpson house, where the family performs their traditional couch gag as animated skeletons. It's revealed that the Simpsons are hosting a Halloween costume party, and the assembled guests are exchanging scary stories, setting up the anthology format for the episode. The partygoers are dressed in a variety of costumes, including Homer as Julius Caesar, Marge as Cleopatra, Bart as a droog from A Clockwork Orange, and Lisa as the Statue of Liberty, along with several of Bart's and Lisa's costumed friends.

title: Starship Poopers (Treehouse of Horror IX segment)
text: "Starship Poopers" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror IX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 9"), which aired as Season 10, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Marge notices baby Maggie's tooth is oddly sharp, and soon Maggie sprouts tentacles instead of legs. A panicked trip to Dr. Hibbert proves useless after Maggie destroys his equipment, so the family discovers she can summon someone by sucking rapidly on her pacifier. This turns out to be a signal to Kang and Kodos, who arrive claiming Maggie as their own — Marge then reveals that Kang is actually Maggie's biological father, having abducted and impregnated her years earlier using a mind-control trick and an insemination ray. When Homer and Kang begin fighting over custody, Bart proposes settling it on The Jerry Springer Show, parodying the trashy talk show format. There, Kang casually vaporizes a heckling audience member, and Maggie suddenly attacks and kills Jerry Springer himself during his closing remarks. Kang and Kodos then threaten to assassinate every American politician unless Maggie is handed over, but the Simpsons goad them into believing it's an impossible task, so the aliens fly off to attempt it, with Bart reminding them not to forget Ken Starr. Just before departure, Maggie eerily speaks in Kang's voice, declares she'll drive, and menacingly states she needs children's blood as the segment ends.

title: The Screaming Woman (Treehouse of Horror Presents: Simpsons Wicked This Way Comes segment)
keys: treehouse of horror presents: simpsons wicked this way comes
text: "The Screaming Woman" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror Presents: Simpsons Wicked This Way Comes", which aired as Season 36, Episode 7 of The Simpsons. While wandering through the woods, Bart hears a woman's screams coming from underground, but when he runs home to tell his parents, Homer and Marge brush him off as another one of his lies, recalling a previous false story about a wolf. Milhouse also refuses to help, being stuck at his grandmother's, so Bart investigates alone. He visits the Van Houten house, where Luann feeds him milk that seems designed to make him drowsy, but he stays alert and returns to the grave in the woods where he again hears the woman singing. Homer recognizes the tune as one belonging to Kirk Van Houten, and together they dig up the grave to find Kirk alive but buried. Kirk explains that Luann buried him after he was seen by Miss Hoover buying her hair dye, which humiliated her. Chief Wiggum decides not to arrest Luann, reasoning that in the 1950s murder was more socially acceptable than divorce. Marge promises Bart they'll trust him from now on, but Bart immediately abuses that trust by falsely accusing Lisa of being a communist, leading Wiggum to haul her away. Notable quotes: Marge: I think we all know this is another one of your famous fibs. | Homer: Yeah, like that time you said there was a boy in the woods crying wolf, and when we got there, there was no boy at all. Just a fat wolf. | Bart: You can't be dead. You can't. I'm sorry, lady. I tried. The one time I'm not lying to make other people look stupid for believing me, and no one will believe me. | Chief Wiggum: Uh, she's got a point. Here in the 1950s, murder is much more socially acceptable than, uh, you know, divorce. You're free to go.

title: Poetic Interlude (Treehouse of Horror XXXII segment)
text: "Poetic Interlude" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 32"), which aired as Season 33, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. This short interstitial segment is narrated by Vincent Price reciting a rhyming poem titled "The Telltale Bart" to a listening Maggie, chronicling Bart's escalating misdeeds month by month throughout the year. Each stanza pairs a calendar month with an outrageous prank, from putting worms in Homer's waffles in January to catfishing Mrs. Krabappel on Tinder in February, vandalizing the school playground, and photocopying nude photos of himself. The rhymes continue through summer and fall, covering him stealing Skinner's car, drinking his first beer, mutilating Lisa's Malibu Stacy dolls, torturing a turtle, serving detention for a month, gorging on Halloween candy, and beheading his family at the Thanksgiving table. Just as the narration is about to reveal what horrific act Bart commits in December, Maggie—apparently the true audience for this bedtime poem—reaches up and strangles Bart to death mid-sentence. Satisfied, Maggie then climbs into her bed and goes to sleep, ending the segment on a darkly comic note. Notable quotes: Vincent Price: In January, Bart was awful, put earthworms in his father's waffle. | Homer: Oh, how many months are there?! | Vincent Price: Then, worst of all, in cold December... [choking sounds] | Phonic Frog: R. I. P.

title: The Ned Zone (Treehouse of Horror XV segment)
text: "The Ned Zone" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 15"), which aired as Season 16, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. This segment parodies The Dead Zone, opening with Homer accidentally knocking out Ned Flanders with a stray bowling ball while trying to retrieve a Frisbee from the roof. At the hospital, Dr. Hibbert reveals the blow actually dislodged a fatal brain tumor, but when the two shake hands, Ned gains psychic visions of people's deaths, starting with Hibbert's own fatal fall from a window. Panicked, Ned begins seeing more visions, including Moleman being devoured by sewer alligators, which he inadvertently causes by dropping him after saving him. When Homer demands a vision of his own fate, Ned sees himself shooting Homer, prompting Ned to try to move away and later destroy a gun to avoid the outcome. Undeterred, Homer provokes Ned into a confrontation at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, where Ned's attempt to stop a nuclear meltdown backfires spectacularly when Homer's flailing body still manages to hit the detonation button with his tongue. The plant explodes, sending both Homer and Ned to Heaven, where Homer is reunited with his Frisbee by God himself before heading off to the buffet. Notable quotes: Dr. Hibbert: Ned, you nearly died... of a brain tumor. Thank goodness that bowling ball knocked it out of your head. | Ned: Homer, please, don't tempt the gods. I-I mean God! There's-there's one God! Only one! Well, sometimes there's three. | Homer: Oh, I'm so scared. Ned Flanders is pointing a gun at me. You couldn't even shoot me by accident, even if I whacked the barrel like this. | Ned: Homer, stay away from the nuclear plant.

title: Desperately Xeeking Xena (Treehouse of Horror X segment)
text: "Desperately Xeeking Xena" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror X" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 10"), which aired as Season 11, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. At Springfield Elementary, Chief Wiggum is X-raying kids' Halloween candy for hidden dangers when Nelson's overstuffed bag causes the machine to explode, blasting radiation onto Bart and Lisa. The blast gives Lisa super-strength and Bart the ability to stretch, and the siblings become costumed heroes "Stretch Dude" and "Clobber Girl," complete with their own in-universe TV show. In their debut adventure, Comic Book Guy, posing as supervillain "The Collector," uses a magnet to kidnap Lucy Lawless (playing herself, mistaken for Xena) from a sci-fi convention and stashes her with other captured celebrities in his lair. Stretch Dude and Clobber Girl attack, but The Collector knocks them both out with a rare phaser and prepares to lower them into a vat of liquid Lucite. Lawless tricks him with a fake seduction, beats him up, and when he brandishes a mint-condition Phantom Menace lightsaber, she points out he's ruined its collectible value by opening it, sending him fleeing into the vat where he hardens into a statue. Lawless then flies the two heroes home, clarifying to a confused Clobber Girl that she isn't actually Xena, just Lucy Lawless. Notable quotes: Lucy Lawless: Must... remove... breast plate! | The Collector: Goodnight Retch Dude & Slobber Girl. Sweet screams!
