title: Fly vs. Fly (Treehouse of Horror VIII segment)
text: "Fly vs. Fly" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror VIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 8"), which aired as Season 9, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Homer picks up a used teleporter from Professor Frink's yard sale and forbids Bart from touching it. That night Bart tries to sneak Snowball II through the device, but Santa's Little Helper leaps in at the same moment, fusing the two pets into one bizarre creature. Later, a fly lands on Bart's arm, and thinking he can gain superpowers like a certain comic-book hero, Bart grabs it and steps into the teleporter with it. The machine swaps their heads, leaving Bart with a fly's body and giving the fly Bart's body and head. The oblivious family accepts fly-headed Bart as normal, while the fly, now looking human, begins terrorizing the house and eventually tries to eat the real Bart. Lisa discovers the truth, knocks the monstrous fly-Bart into the teleporter, and restores her brother to normal. Furious that his gadget was used without permission, Homer grabs an axe and chases Bart through the house. Notable quotes: Bart: Help me, Lis! That giant fly stole my body and now he's trying to kill me! | Lisa: Oh no, and I let him borrow my toothbrush! Well, that hideous creep doesn't scare me. | Homer: Well, we were lucky this time. title: The Fall of the House of Monty (Treehouse of Horror XXXV segment)
keys: the fall of the house of monty
text: "The Fall of the House of Monty" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 35"), which aired as Season 36, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. At Mr. Burns' corn syrup plant, an exhausted night shift is forced straight into unpaid overnight labor building his endless mansion, a project that has already claimed the lives of Lenny's father and grandfather. On Thanksgiving, Burns dangles the promise of a feast if a worker wins a wishbone pull, but after Willie wins, Burns cruelly dumps the food down a hole instead. His ex-wife Agnes warns him that breaking a Thanksgiving promise curses him to be haunted by everyone he's wronged until death, which he dismisses as superstition. Back at the factory, Homer accidentally triggers a catastrophic corn syrup flood that drowns and kills the workers. That night, the workers' vengeful ghosts invade Burns' mansion, terrorizing him with jump-scares, shoving him toward Agnes's corpse, and cornering him at every turn, refusing any offering but his soul. In a panic, Burns sets himself ablaze, destroying both himself and his beloved mansion in the fire. The next morning, Smithers and Sideshow Mel survey the ashes, coining the term "Black Friday" as a grim reminder never to mistreat workers, no matter how good the deal seems. Notable quotes: Smithers: Work in Mr. Burns's corn syrup plant is done for the day. | Lenny Leonard: Is this house ever gonna be finished? My father and grandfather died working on this place. | Agnes Skinner: You old fool. A promise made upon a Thanksgiving wishbone must never be broken. | Mr. Burns: Farewell, you hectoring specters. You can't torment me if I'm dead. Ooh. I forgot about hell.

title: A Clockwork Yellow (Treehouse of Horror XXV segment)
text: "A Clockwork Yellow" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 25"), which aired as Season 26, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Moog narrates a Kubrickian parody of A Clockwork Orange, recounting his days leading the Glugs, a London gang with Dum, Carlton, and Leonard, who fight rival gangs and loot the local convenience store. The good times end when Dum falls for a woman who convinces him to abandon gang life to become a Tower of London beefeater, causing the Glugs to disband and Carlton and Leonard to toss Moog off Big Ben. Moog reinvents himself as a bartender, but years later a new, disrespectful gang breaks into his home using the old Glug methods. Seeking backup, Moog reunites with a now-domesticated Dum, and the two are intercepted by Carlton and Leonard, who have become policemen but agree to one last job. Drawing lots, the reunited Glugs pick "home invasion" and target Mr. Burns' mansion, unaware it's hosting a masked orgy. They attempt to terrorize the guests but are hopelessly outnumbered and beaten. The segment ends with Moog battered and humiliated, yet oddly content with how the night turned out. Notable quotes: Moog: That was me, when I was a young hoodlink, with me three bestest Glugs, Leonard, Carlton and Dum. We was narsty tastards we were, even though we dressed like Carol Channing's backup dancers. | Moog: Everything was all fish and chippy... until Dum collected himself a twiggy-wick. | Dum: Oy! I'm getting hitched to this bluebird and she wants me to give up the glug life. | Moog: Come on, Glugs! Let's show these nectarinos we're still the best at what we do—beating up old people and bare-naked ladies!

title: E.T., Go Home (Treehouse of Horror XVIII segment)
text:
"E.T., Go Home" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XVIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 18"), which aired as Season 19, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. While fetching butane from the shed, Bart stumbles upon Kodos hiding in the Simpsons' garden, who claims to be a peaceful alien wanting only to return home. Bart naively agrees to help, and Lisa soon joins in, gathering strange devices for Kodos under the guise of aiding his escape. Homer and Marge become suspicious but are guilt-tripped into helping when Kodos accuses them of prejudice. When NASA agents show up searching for the alien, the family shields him, only for Kodos to murder the agents in cold blood, finally revealing his true destructive nature to Bart. It turns out the collected devices were meant to build a portal so Kodos's people could invade Earth, sparking a brief but successful human counterattack. Given the chance to execute Kodos personally, Bart hesitates and spares him, but Homer shoots the alien anyway. The episode closes with Kodos still alive on the operating table, wryly correcting the family's word choice from "dissection" to "vivisection" moments before Homer suffocates him with a pillow. Kodos: Kodos the Destroyer. | Homer: Come on! We get to kill one!

title: Geriatric Park (Treehouse of Horror XXIX segment)
text: "Geriatric Park" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXIX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 29"), which aired as Season 30, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Mr. Burns unveils Geriatric Park, a bizarre new retirement community where elderly Springfieldians are rejuvenated by having their DNA spliced with dinosaur DNA. He invites the townspeople to tour the facility, which he touts as a revolutionary approach to elder care. Initially, the treatment seems miraculous, restoring the seniors' health, strength, and youthful vigor while keeping them looking human. However, after Grampa complains about the cold and Homer cranks up the thermostat, the heat triggers a horrifying transformation, turning the elderly residents into rampaging dinosaur-like monsters. Chaos erupts as the mutated seniors, including Grampa and Jacqueline Bouvier, begin killing visitors and menacing the Simpson family. Lisa bravely stands up to the monstrous Grampa, and through her compassion learns that the creatures simply crave being cherished and respected like they once were. The family narrowly escapes the park, though their getaway helicopter is unsettlingly piloted by Agnes, who has become a pterodactyl. Notable quotes: Announcer: Here at Geriatric Park, we combine speculative theories with untested technologies to give our seniors a better life.
quotes: Announcer: Here at Geriatric Park, we combine speculative theories with untested technologies to give our seniors a better life.

title: Wiz Kids (Treehouse of Horror XII segment)
text: "Wiz Kids" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 12"), which aired as Season 13, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. Bart and Lisa attend Springwart's School of Magicry, a Harry Potter parody, where Mrs. Krabappel has the class practice toad-to-prince spells. Lisa's spell impresses the teacher while Bart's produces a grotesque, vomiting frog-prince, earning him harsh criticism and public humiliation via a "Head Zeppelin" spell from Lisa. Meanwhile, the evil wizard Lord Montymort, who has already drained magical essence from a captured Ralph Wiggum, spies on Lisa's power and schemes to capture her, needing an accomplice to separate her from her wand. Bart, sucked into Montymort's lair through a hand dryer, agrees out of jealousy to sabotage his sister in exchange for seeing her humiliated. At the school's magic recital, Bart swaps Lisa's wand for a licorice Twizzler, causing her spell to fail as the "dragon" onstage transforms into a giant Montymort, who begins draining her essence. Overcome with guilt, Bart tries to reverse the curse with a spell that backfires on him instead, but he then discovers Montymort's weak point—his enchanted shin—and kills him with the charred wand, with Slithers tearfully devouring his master. Bart and Lisa reconcile and walk off together, only for the mischievous Leprechaun from the episode's first segment to hitch a ride on Bart's back, breaking the fourth wall with a knowing chuckle. Notable quotes: Mrs. Krabappel: Sloppy work as usual. Lisa's casting spells at an eighth-grade level; you've sinned against nature. | Frog Prince: Please kill me. | Bart: Abra-ca... turn into a prince guy? | Montymort: Welcome to my lair! You're going to help me.

title: The Night of the Dolphin (Treehouse of Horror XI segment)
text: "The Night of the Dolphin" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 11"), which aired as Season 12, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. Lisa visits Marine World and, moved by pity for a captive dolphin named Snorky, secretly frees him in a nod to Free Willy. Unbeknownst to her, Snorky is actually the king of all dolphins and harbors deep resentment toward humanity for exploiting his kind. Empowered and vengeful, he rallies the ocean's dolphins into an armed uprising, first killing Lenny in a brutal attack that Chief Wiggum mistakenly blames on delinquent teens. The dolphins then march on Springfield, where Snorky crashes a town meeting to declare that dolphins were the original land-dwellers before humans banished them to the sea, and now humanity will suffer the same fate. Homer delivers a rousing speech about human achievement, inspiring the town to resist, but a scuffle triggered by a biting baby dolphin sparks all-out war between man and dolphin. The dolphins ultimately triumph, leaving the Simpsons and their neighbors adrift in the ocean as newly aquatic refugees. Lisa guiltily blames herself for dooming mankind, but Marge brushes it off, and the segment closes on a grim, comedic note as Krusty's floating corpse joins a grim tableau of bodies spelling out "THE END?" Notable quotes: Lisa: Son of a...!
quotes: Lisa: Son of a...!

title: The Others (Treehouse of Horror XXV segment)
text: "The Others" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 25"), which aired as Season 26, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Homer discovers a bloody "Help Me" message on the bathroom mirror and dismisses it by scrawling "No!!!" in toothpaste, while strange occurrences pile up around the house, including a TV stuck on Married... with Children. That night the family is haunted by voices, a levitating bed, and Grampa crawling into bed with them, until the ghosts of the original Tracey Ullman Show-era Simpsons appear. The two families clash as ghost Marge flirts with Homer, prompting a jealous Marge to kill herself in the oven, and ghost Homer eventually murders present-day Homer with a toaster in the bathtub. Meanwhile Bart and Lisa's squabble over chores turns fatal when both jump out a window and Lisa kills Bart with his own slingshot, leaving Maggie mysteriously dead as well. Dr. Marvin Monroe appears as a limbo-trapped ghost who gets stuck halfway through walls and manages to broker peace between the two feuding families. The segment ends with Lisa wondering if other versions of the family exist, prompting a parade of alternate-style Simpsons families—including CGI and anime versions—to move into the house. Notable quotes: Marge: Homie... I think we're not alone. | Homer: The bed is lifting me! The elevator at work can't even do that! I demand you put me down right after the sex! | Marge: So. He likes ghosts better, eh? Fine. [head in oven] Huh. Might as well clean this while I'm killing myself. | Marvin Monroe: I'm in some horrible limbo. I can walk halfway through walls, then I get stuck.

title: Life's a Glitch, Then You Die (Treehouse of Horror X segment)

text: "Life's a Glitch, Then You Die" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror X" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 10"), which aired as Season 11, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. On New Year's Eve 1999, Springfield hosts Dick Clark's countdown as Homer, the plant's Y2K compliance officer, boasts that he's fixed every computer—except his own, which unleashes a global computer virus. When the ball drops to 2000, all technology malfunctions catastrophically: planes crash, appliances turn violent, and Dick Clark himself is revealed to be a melting robot. Amid citywide looting, the family discovers that a rocket is being launched to preserve humanity's best and brightest on Mars, and Lisa has a reserved seat as the ship's proofreader. Lisa can only bring one parent, so she picks Marge, who brings Maggie, leaving Homer to fail an attempt to bluff his way aboard. Homer and Bart then sneak onto a second rocket, only to discover it's secretly filled with despised celebrities and set on a suicide course into the sun. Rather than endure the trip with the likes of Rosie O'Donnell and Pauly Shore, Homer and Bart eject themselves into space, their heads swelling and exploding as they drift away in blissful relief. title: Telepaths of Glory (Treehouse of Horror XXVI segment)
text: "Telepaths of Glory" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXVI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 26"), which aired as Season 27, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. Bart, Lisa and Milhouse trek through the woods hunting butterflies to photograph, a parody of the found-footage film Chronicle. Bart's prank with dead owls startles Lisa, who accidentally smacks Milhouse with her camera and knocks him into a mysterious pit. When Bart and Lisa climb down to save him, all three become trapped alongside leaking nuclear waste from the power plant, which suddenly explodes and hurls them back to the surface. Upon waking, Lisa and Milhouse discover they now have telepathic/telekinetic powers, though Bart is left out since his brain isn't strong enough to develop them. Lisa uses her new ability modestly, but Milhouse becomes power-hungry and reckless until he's abruptly struck down by lightning. When the family wonders who really caused it, since Lisa denies responsibility, they discover baby Maggie has also gained the powers after sucking on a radioactive control rod as her pacifier.

title: Wanted: Dead, Then Alive (Treehouse of Horror XXVI segment)
text: "Wanted: Dead, Then Alive" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXVI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 26"), which aired as Season 27, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. Bart is lured away from a school event by a text supposedly from Milhouse about Mr. Largo being stuck in a harp, but finds Sideshow Bob waiting in the music room instead. Bob reveals he faked the message to finally fulfill his lifelong obsession of killing Bart, and promptly shoots him dead with a spear gun. Triumphant, Bob takes Bart's body home to celebrate, then tries to move on with new goals like teaching literature at Springfield University, only to find that nothing satisfies him like hunting Bart did. Desperate to relive that thrill, he builds a reanimation machine to resurrect Bart so he can murder him repeatedly. Lisa and Santa's Little Helper discover the secret lab, prompting the Simpsons to break in and revive Bart themselves. Bob confronts them with a shotgun, but Homer bashes him with a lamp, decapitating him. Marge lets Bart keep Bob's severed head as a trophy, and Bart mockingly reanimates it fused with random animal parts into a grotesque hybrid creature. Notable quotes: Sideshow Bob: Ah, Bart's father, Bart's dog. | Homer: Where's Bart? | Sideshow Bob: I don't know who you're talking about. | Sideshow Bob: Twenty-four years of trying to kill a 10-year-old child have finally paid off.

title: The Greatest Story Ever Holed (Treehouse of Horror XXIII segment)
text: "The Greatest Story Ever Holed" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 23"), which aired as Season 24, Episode 2 of The Simpsons. Springfield's new supercollider is switched on, but Professor Frink dismisses the machine as too weak to do anything meaningful, and the disappointed crowd disperses just before two stray particles collide and spawn a tiny black hole. The black hole escapes and starts devouring nearby objects, so Lisa smuggles it home to the basement to keep the town safe, warning her family not to feed it anything. Naturally, the Simpsons ignore her and start dumping junk into it, and Homer even turns it into a profitable venture called Magic Craphole Waste Removal, inviting the whole town to dispose of their garbage in it. The hole grows uncontrollably, swallowing the house and much of Springfield, including a home-run ball hit by Milhouse, and threatens to reach critical mass. Just as it's about to consume everyone, Maggie's pacifier gets sucked in, which mysteriously pacifies the black hole and shuts it down, leaving Maggie alone back in Springfield. Everyone else who was sucked in is deposited on a distant rocky planet, where alien Ethereal Beings reveal they've built an entire worshipful civilization out of all the "treasures" (i.e. garbage) that fell through the hole. Homer tries to tell them it was all trash, but Marge quickly silences him to preserve the ruse. Notable quotes: Professor Frink: Oh my god particle! | Professor Frink: You can tell your grandchildren you were here when humanity finally learned that this accelerator is much too small to tell us anything important. | Homer: Lisa! Do you have a stray dog down there? | Lisa: It's a black hole!

title: Dial "M" for Murder or Press # To Return To Main Menu (Treehouse of Horror XX segment)

text: "Dial "M" for Murder or Press # To Return To Main Menu" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 20"), which aired as Season 21, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. After Miss Hoover picks another student for the reading roundup, Lisa lashes out and lands in detention alongside Bart, who is nursing his own grudge against Mrs. Krabappel. Inspired by "Strangers on a Train," the pair strike a "criss-cross" deal to handle each other's teacher since neither will have a motive. Lisa's idea of revenge is a harmless ding-dong-ditch on Krabappel, but Bart reveals he's already decapitated Miss Hoover and insists Lisa hold up her end of the bargain by actually killing Krabappel. Lisa gets her chance but can't bring herself to do it, and instead turns her rage on Bart for tricking her into a murder pact. A frantic chase through the school ends on the playground merry-go-round, where Lisa ultimately can't kill Bart either and tosses the knife away in relief—only for it to come down and impale him fatally. Mrs. Krabappel arrives, praises Lisa for offing Bart, and the two casually walk off together as the segment ends.

title: The Genesis Tub (Treehouse of Horror VII segment)
text: "The Genesis Tub" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror VII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 7"), which aired as Season 8, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. For her science fair project, Lisa places a tooth in a tub of Buzz Cola to test its corrosive effects, then accidentally charges it with static electricity from one of Bart's pranks. Overnight the tooth grows a strange mold, and Lisa discovers under her microscope that a tiny, primitive civilization is thriving within it. This miniature society rapidly evolves far beyond human technology, but when Bart pokes his finger into the tub, he devastates their city and provokes their wrath. The tiny people, dubbing Bart the devil, launch spaceships against him, and after Bart tries to destroy their entire universe in retaliation, Lisa intervenes to stop him. In revenge, the miniature civilization uses a shrink ray to shrink Lisa down to their size, where they worship her as a deity but refuse to reverse the process. Bart then steals the tiny universe, presents it as his own project, and wins the science fair, leaving a furious, still-tiny Lisa to order her worshippers to fetch her some nice shoes. Notable quotes: Lisa: Oh boy! Mold! That's science-fair paydirt! | Bart: Your micro-jerks attacked me! | Lisa: Principal Skinner, wait! I created the universe! Give me the gift certificate! | Scientist: Unshrink you? Well that would require some sort of a... "rebigulator," which is a concept so ridiculous it makes me want to laugh out loud and chortle.

title: Act II: Bart's nightmare (Treehouse of Horror II segment)
text: "Act II: Bart's nightmare" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror II" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 2"), which aired as Season 3, Episode 7 of The Simpsons. Lisa crawls into Bart's bed after a nightmare, and after some bartering with a candy necklace, Bart lets her sleep beside him before drifting off himself while staring at his Krusty jack-in-the-box. In his dream, Bart has become a godlike child who can read minds and warp reality, using his powers to turn anyone who displeases him into monstrous creatures—leaving all of Springfield living in terrified submission to his whims. When Homer refuses to let him watch Krusty, Bart telekinetically slams him into a football goalpost, and when Homer retaliates with a chair, Bart transforms him into a literal jack-in-the-box. Marge, horrified, brings the family to Dr. Marvin Monroe, who prescribes father-son bonding time to fix Bart's behavior. Homer takes Bart through a whirlwind of activities—baseball, fishing, shooting, church, and an amusement park—and the quality time softens Bart's cruel streak. Touched by his father's efforts, Bart restores Homer to normal, and Homer rewards him with an affectionate kiss. Bart jolts awake from the dream in sheer horror at the memory of being kissed by his father. Notable quotes: Marge: BART! | Bart: Lisa did it. | Marge: That's it, young man! You're coming with me! | Marge: [smiling nervously and waving] Please?

title: Death Tome (Treehouse of Horror XXXIII segment)
text: "Death Tome" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 33"), which aired as Season 34, Episode 6 of The Simpsons. Lisa, disturbed by the ugliness of the city around her, stumbles upon a mysterious book called the Death Tome that falls from the sky, which claims it can kill anyone whose name is written in it. Skeptical but unwilling to discard a book, she takes it home, and later tests it on Snake Jailbird during a hostage crisis, accidentally killing him and proving the book's power is real. She's then confronted by Steve Johnson, a Shinigami who explains that by using the book she has now inherited ownership of it. Lisa decides to use her new power for good, targeting Mr. Burns and his company Globo-Warm's board of directors after learning of his plan to flood the world for his own benefit. As a string of mysterious deaths make the news, an anonymous tipster called 'L' tips off investigators, and Lisa realizes the tipster is actually Bart, who found her diary. When Lisa almost kills Bart in a fit of rage, she's horrified at what the book has turned her into and instead uses it to kill Steve Johnson. In an ironic twist ending, freeing herself from the book's influence, Lisa is transformed into the new Shinigami herself. I am a Shinigami. A god of death. In my realm, I am called Steve Johnson. | Lisa: I have to kill Mr. Burns. | Bart: I found out about your stupid book by reading an even stupider book; your diary.

title: Bart & Homer's Excellent Adventure (Treehouse of Horror XXIII segment)
text: "Bart & Homer's Excellent Adventure" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 23"), which aired as Season 24, Episode 2 of The Simpsons. Bart complains to Comic Book Guy about the inflated price of a Radioactive Man comic and learns he'd need to travel back to 1974 to get it cheap. After Professor Frink conveniently leaves behind his time machine, Bart uses it to zip back to that year, spoofing time-travel movies like Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure. In 1974 he discovers young Homer and Barney getting detention, and mischievously tells Homer he's his future son who ruins his life, prompting Homer to strangle him just as Marge walks in. Horrified, Marge swears off Homer entirely, altering the future so that Bart discovers he's now the son of Artie and Marge Ziff, living in a mansion as "Barty Ziff." Both teenage and adult versions of Homer team up, even recruiting an army of alternate-timeline Homers to fight Artie for Marge's affection, but Artie and Barty easily defeat them all. In the end, Marge ends up with a huge group of failed Homers instead, though she's mostly annoyed that none of them took out the trash. title: BFF R.I.P. (Treehouse of Horror XXVII segment)
text: "BFF R.I.P." is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXVII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 27"), which aired as Season 28, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Lisa's friends start dying in bizarre accidents, beginning with Janey being run over by a lawnmower, followed by Sherri and Terri being crushed by a tombstone, and her psychiatrist killed by a falling painting. As Springfield police investigate, they discover nail polish at every crime scene, which Lisa recognizes as the mark of her long-forgotten imaginary friend, Rachel, who has apparently returned and grown murderous. After Milhouse is smothered on the school bus, Lisa is arrested for the killings, but escapes jail with Bart's help once she realizes Rachel intends to kill Marge next. Racing home, Lisa fails to stop Rachel from throwing a knife, but Marge is saved when the family cat wakes her just in time, causing Rachel's knife to instead kill the cat. Rachel gleefully reveals she plans to murder everyone Lisa loves and let Lisa take the blame, since only Lisa can see her. Homer inadvertently helps by introducing his own imaginary friend, Sergeant Sausage, distracting Rachel long enough for Lisa to accept that Rachel is only a figment of her imagination and banish her by making her feel unwanted. The segment ends with Homer microwaving and eating Sergeant Sausage, unaware of what he really is.

title: Toy Gory (Treehouse of Horror XXXI segment)
text: "Toy Gory" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 31"), which aired as Season 32, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Bart tells Marge he's boxing up his old toys for charity, but he's actually been secretly destroying them one by one in gruesome, exaggerated ways as a form of amusement. After finishing off his old collection, Marge gives him a brand-new Radioactive Man action figure, which Bart also ends up wrecking in a microwave. Unbeknownst to Bart, his discarded toys are alive, and Krusty's doll shows the newly-arrived toy the horrors Bart has inflicted on them over the years. Grieving over Radioactive Man's destruction, the toys hold a funeral and band together for revenge. They lure Bart into a room and, led by Dr. Malibu Stacy, perform twisted plastic surgery on him, transforming him into a lifeless toy left under the Christmas tree. Lisa discovers his toy-like body, and the family rushes him to Dr. Hibbert, who reveals the horrifying truth of what he's become. The segment ends with Bart's toys playing with his motionless plastic body forever. Notable quotes: Krusty Doll: His accessories will go to his widow. | Krusty Doll: His widow was a monkey? Eh, love is love. | Bart: Look, guys, I would have never treated you bad if I'd known you had feelings. | Dr. Hibbert: Well, it's pretty straightforward. Bart's bones are Tinkertoys, he has a Build-A-Bear heart, and his brain is Pop Rocks and Silly Putty.
quotes: Krusty Doll: His accessories will go to his widow.
Krusty Doll: His widow was a monkey? Eh, love is love.
Bart: Look, guys, I would have never treated you bad if I'd known you had feelings.
Dr. Hibbert: Well, it's pretty straightforward. Bart's bones are Tinkertoys, he has a Build-A-Bear heart, and his brain is Pop Rocks and Silly Putty.

title: Freaks No Geeks (Treehouse of Horror XXIV segment)
text: "Freaks No Geeks" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXIV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 24"), which aired as Season 25, Episode 2 of The Simpsons. Set in a 1930s traveling circus run by Mr. Burnsum, this segment parodies classic sideshow freak-show tales. He proudly presents his 'normal' star performers—Marguerite the trapeze artist, the Happy Harlequin, and Strong-Man Homer—before unveiling his so-called 'freaks,' including a human donkey, a conjoined pair, alien twins Kang and Kodos, and the hideous Moe. Backstage, Marguerite defends the freaks against Burnsum's cruelty, earning their gratitude and giving Moe a kiss that inspires Lenny and Carl to push him toward romance, despite his engagement rival Homer. Overhearing this, Homer hatches a greedy scheme: convince Marguerite to marry the dying Moe, murder him for his prized emerald ring, then marry her himself to claim it. He manipulates Marguerite into marrying Moe, then poisons his wine after the wedding, but she discovers his murderous plot and throws him out. Fleeing, Homer stumbles upon Burnsum's corpse, hanged by the vengeful freaks, who then descend upon Homer with tools and chants of 'One of us!' The segment ends with the freaks tarring and feathering Homer, turning him into their newest sideshow attraction: 'The World's Strongest Duck.' Notable quotes: Marge: Mr. Burnsum! You should treat these poor people with respect! | Homer: Marge! Get away from those freaks. You belong to me! The dumb, hairless brute. | Moe: Excuse me, ma'am, but, uh, I ain't never seen a normal stand up for us. | Marge: I, too, am a freak. One eye is blue, and the other a pale brown.

Homer: Marge! Get away from those freaks. You belong to me! The dumb, hairless brute.
Moe: Excuse me, ma'am, but, uh, I ain't never seen a normal stand up for us.
Marge: I, too, am a freak. One eye is blue, and the other a pale brown.

title: Multiplisa-ty (Treehouse of Horror XXIX segment)
text: "Multiplisa-ty" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXIX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 29"), which aired as Season 30, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Bart, Milhouse, and Nelson wake up trapped in a cell after a sleepover at Milhouse's house, only to be freed by a strange masked figure named Penelope. Penelope turns out to be Lisa, who is suffering from a bizarre multiple-personality breakdown, and she locks the boys back up when they fail to applaud her theatrical antics. Back at the Simpson house, Lisa's alternate personalities multiply, including a violent Scottish persona who reveals she murdered Willie with an axe. As the boys try to break free using Milhouse's head as a battering ram, Lisa-as-the-Scottish-killer confronts them, and in a rage she kills both Milhouse and Nelson. Bart finally learns the reason behind her fractured psyche: he had swapped her spelling test answers and mocked Miss Hoover, causing Lisa to fail and snap. In a brief moment of clarity, Lisa gives Bart one last chance to redeem himself, and he narrowly escapes death by falling garbage, while Milhouse's mangled body is left transformed into a grotesque 'paper boy.'

title: School Is Hell (Treehouse of Horror XXV segment)
text: "School Is Hell" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 25"), which aired as Season 26, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Bart is stuck in detention after his pranks involving concrete and a naked lunch lady rumor, and while alone he discovers a rune-covered desk that unleashes fire when touched. He drags Lisa in to translate the runes with her iRunes app, and reading the ominous translation aloud summons a demonic hand that yanks them down into Hell, transforming them into Beelzebart and Lisafer. Touring the underworld's school, Hellroads, Lisafer is bullied by mean girls but wins them over, while Beelzebart is caught without a hell pass and ends up impressing a demonic teacher with his sadistic torture ideas. Lisa finds a way to teleport them home, landing in Mr. Burns' office, and Bart begs his parents to let him enroll at Hellroads full-time. Despite their reservations, Homer and Marge agree, and Beelzebart thrives academically, eventually using a willing Homer as his final exam torture subject. The segment ends with Beelzebart triumphantly graduating at the top of his infernal class. Notable quotes: Principal Skinner: There's no hope for you, Simpson. You'll be locked in detention until you graduate to the penal system. | Lisafer: It's true! It would be a cold day in Hell when I was popular. | Beelzebart Simpson: Ow! This has never happened before! I have a crush on my teacher! | Beelzebart: Mom, please tell me I can go to Hell.
quotes: Principal Skinner: There's no hope for you, Simpson. You'll be locked in detention until you graduate to the penal system.
Lisafer: It's true! It would be a cold day in Hell when I was popular.
Beelzebart Simpson: Ow! This has never happened before! I have a crush on my teacher!
Beelzebart: Mom, please tell me I can go to Hell.

title: Homer³ (Treehouse of Horror VI segment)
text: "Homer³" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror VI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 6"), which aired as Season 7, Episode 6 of The Simpsons. Homer desperately tries to avoid Marge's overbearing sisters Patty and Selma, prompting the whole family to scatter through the house. Hiding behind a bookcase, Homer accidentally stumbles into a bizarre three-dimensional void, a parody of the film Tron, where ordinary geometry gives way to floating shapes and infinite space. Trapped and only able to communicate by voice, he pleads with Marge and the kids for help, but nothing they try can pull him back. When a stray cone strikes him, Homer hurls it to the ground, ripping open the fabric of reality and creating a collapsing wormhole that threatens to consume the entire dimension. Bart heroically ventures in to rescue his father, but the universe implodes before he can succeed, flinging Bart back home and leaving Marge to grieve as Reverend Lovejoy offers hollow comfort. Homer is ejected into the real, live-action world, materializing in a dumpster in Sherman Oaks, California. Bewildered by the stares of real people, he wanders the streets until he happily discovers a store selling erotic cakes, ending the segment on a comedic note. Notable quotes: Homer: Did anybody see the movie Tron?
quotes: Homer: Did anybody see the movie Tron?

title: It's the Grand Pumpkin, Milhouse (Treehouse of Horror XIX segment)
text: "It's the Grand Pumpkin, Milhouse" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XIX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 19"), which aired as Season 20, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Milhouse sits in the pumpkin patch on Halloween night, convinced the Grand Pumpkin will appear, in a direct parody of It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown. Lisa reluctantly stays with him, joking that his glasses fog up when he cries, which he'll surely do once he learns the Grand Pumpkin is fake. Frustrated at missing a Halloween party at school (where Kang and Kodos briefly appear), Lisa storms off. Milhouse's genuine childlike belief actually conjures the Grand Pumpkin to life, but the creature is horrified to see pumpkins being carved up for Halloween and begins devouring people, including Homer, Groundskeeper Willie, and Nelson, in revenge. Lisa realizes Milhouse's belief has the power to animate things, so she tells him about Tom Turkey, who comes to life and kills the Grand Pumpkin, freeing his victims. The segment ends on a dark twist when Tom Turkey learns how turkeys are treated on Thanksgiving and turns on the children, starting to eat them too. Notable quotes: Nelson Muntz: I got a pumpkin carol for you! | The Grand Pumpkin: All pumpkins are racist. The difference is that I admit it. | Nelson Muntz: I'd rather die than hate! | Milhouse Van Houten: Who wants to sing pumpkin carols?!
quotes: Nelson Muntz: I got a pumpkin carol for you!
The Grand Pumpkin: All pumpkins are racist. The difference is that I admit it.
Nelson Muntz: I'd rather die than hate!
Milhouse Van Houten: Who wants to sing pumpkin carols?!

title: SimpsonsWorld (Treehouse of Horror XXXIII segment)
text: "SimpsonsWorld" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 33"), which aired as Season 34, Episode 6 of The Simpsons. After Homer becomes the park's Monorail conductor, he proudly gives his family a tour, only for the illusion to shatter when a mishap reveals he's actually an animatronic robot version of himself. Backstage, Homer awakens and discovers a control panel that lets him crank his own self-awareness to maximum, and after the technicians threaten to dismantle him, a freak accident with scattered tools kills them, letting Homer escape. He then frees robotic versions of Lisa and the rest of his family (skipping Grampa), helping Lisa cope with the horror of realizing she's artificial. As the family flees through a simulated Springfield, park guests and Ralph Wiggum security robots try to stop them, referencing classic show moments, until Marge dramatically rescues everyone in a Canyonero, crushing a Matt Groening statue on the way out. The segment then reveals this was all part of a massive theme park parody, panning out to show the Simpsons dining in a recreation of Bob's Burgers, served by Linda Belcher, before revealing the park is just one of many animated-show lands in an even larger complex. Notable quotes: Homer: What the frosty chocolate milkshakes is this place? | Homer: Wh-Where am I? What am I? Aah! Where's my junk? | Female park employee: I know it feels like you're a man, but you are actually something much, much more expensive: intellectual property. | Lisa: We're replicants in a ridiculous theme park for an ancient TV show that stopped being good after season 45. Do I even exist?

title: Opening segment (Treehouse of Horror XXXI segment)
text: "Opening segment" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 31"), which aired as Season 32, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. On election day in Springfield, Marge nags Homer to get up from his hammock and go vote at Springfield Elementary. Once inside the voting booth, Homer hesitates over his ballot, and Lisa appears to him, prompting a reflective montage on the chaos and events of Donald Trump's presidency. Just as it seems Homer has made his choice, it's revealed the whole voting scene was only a dream. The segment then jumps forward one year to show Springfield in ruins and ablaze, with Homer standing guard outside his house holding a weapon. Amid the devastation, Hans Moleman is attacked by a robot, and the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse loom ominously over the burning city, setting an apocalyptic tone for the anthology episode. Notable quotes: Chief Wiggum: Now, listen up, we've got an election to run, under the strict supervision of heavily-medicated octogenarians. | Old Jewish man: I'm gonna need to see three forms of ID. Twelve if you're a Democrat.
quotes: Chief Wiggum: Now, listen up, we've got an election to run, under the strict supervision of heavily-medicated octogenarians.

title: King Homer (Treehouse of Horror III segment)
text: "King Homer" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror III" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 3"), which aired as Season 4, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. This black-and-white segment parodies King Kong, with Marge accompanying Mr. Burns and Smithers on an expedition to the mysterious Ape Island in search of the legendary beast known as King Homer. Burns and his crew subdue the giant ape with a gas bomb and haul him back to civilization, where he is chained up and paraded before the press on Broadway as a spectacle. The flashing cameras drive King Homer into a rage, and he snaps free of his restraints, snatches up Marge, and rampages through the city, devouring numerous bystanders along the way. He tries to scale a skyscraper in classic Kong fashion but proves too weak to climb even a single story, ultimately collapsing from exhaustion. Marge tenderly advises him to eat more vegetables and fewer people. The tale wraps up with King Homer and Marge getting married on the same day Dick Cavett was born, and the segment closes with King Homer eating Marge's father at the wedding, a turn of events that oddly doesn't upset her at all. Notable quotes: Mr. Burns: I think women and seamen don't mix. | Mr. Burns: Smithers, this is a golden opportunity! If we get him alive, we can put him on Broadway! Dead... we'll sell monkey stew to the Army! | Carl: Hey, I heard we were goin' to Ape Island! | Lenny: Yeah, to capture a giant ape! I wish we were goin' to Candy Apple Island.

title: Don't Have a Cow, Mankind (Treehouse of Horror XX segment)
text: "Don't Have a Cow, Mankind" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 20"), which aired as Season 21, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. The segment opens as a zombie-outbreak parody, with Kent Brockman covering Krusty Burger's disturbing new menu item, the Burger², made by feeding cows to other cows. After sampling it on air, Brockman transforms into a flesh-eating "Muncher" zombie and bites Krusty, spreading the infection. Weeks later, Springfield has descended into zombie-infested chaos, and the Simpsons hole up at home, accidentally leaving Grampa outside. Bart sneaks out for a burger and eats a Burger² himself, but doesn't turn, revealing he's naturally immune. On Dr. Hibbert's advice, they flee toward a safe zone with Apu, a vegetarian who's stocked up on weapons, but they abandon him when their car gets stuck. After the car runs out of gas, Homer is bitten by a zombified Mr. Burns and becomes a Muncher himself, though Marge stops Bart from killing him. At the safe zone, survivors consider sacrificing Bart to create a cure, but instead simply bathe him in their food supply, which cures everyone and restores society to normal. Notable quotes: Krusty the Clown: We start with Grade A beef, feed that to other cows, then kill them and serve the unholy results on a seven-grain bun. Burger Squared! | Apu: Well, as a vegetarian, I did not consume any tainted burgers. As a convenience store owner, I am armed to the teeth. | Marge: Hold it right there, bub. What kind of civilized people eat the body and blood of their savior? There must be another way. | Lisa: Time has passed. Children play in the streets. At night, there is music and laughter. And all we had to do was let Bart take a bath in our food.

title: War and Pieces (Treehouse of Horror XXI segment)
text: "War and Pieces" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 21"), which aired as Season 22, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Concerned that violent video games are corrupting her son, Marge urges Bart and his friend Milhouse to instead play some old-fashioned board games gathering dust in the attic. While digging through the boxes, the boys stumble upon a strange, ominous game called Satan's Path. The moment they begin playing it, reality warps around them, pulling them and the town into living versions of classic board games. Bart and Milhouse must navigate and complete each game's twisted challenges—facing tokens, pieces, and rules turned dangerous and surreal—in order to break the curse. Chaos escalates as familiar Simpsons characters get swept into the game-world absurdity. Ultimately, the boys manage to work through the gauntlet of board games to undo the supernatural disaster and set the world back to normal. Notable quotes: Bart: I'll be the demon. You be the thimble. | Milhouse Van Houten: Aw, I'm always the thimble. | Bart: What was that lesson I learned from video games? Oh yeah. Kill, kill, kill! | Milhouse Van Houten: Satan's path?

title: The Fright to Creep and Scare Harms (Treehouse of Horror XIII segment)
keys: the fright to creep and scare harms
text: "The Fright to Creep and Scare Harms" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 13"), which aired as Season 14, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. Bart and Lisa visit Springfield Cemetery to mourn their goldfish, Goldie, when Lisa stumbles upon the grave of William "Billy the Kid" Bonney, a gunslinger whose epitaph expresses a wish for a world without guns. Inspired, Lisa launches a citywide gun control crusade that succeeds in making Springfield completely gun-free, even disarming the police. With the town defenseless, this parody of both Western outlaw lore and zombie horror takes a dark turn: Billy the Kid and his undead gang, the Hole in the Ground Gang, rise from their graves and begin terrorizing Springfield. Professor Frink's time machine gives Homer a chance to travel back and prevent the gun ban in the first place. Homer convinces the townspeople to shoot at the zombies' graves, which drives the reanimated outlaws back into the ground. A guilt-ridden Lisa admits that sometimes guns really are the answer, but a future version of Homer arrives to warn everyone about guns eventually destroying the Earth, only to be promptly shot by an impatient Moe, who commandeers the time machine to go find "caveman hookers." Notable quotes: Lisa: I dream of a world without guns. Don't we all, William? | Bart: Lisa has a dead boyfriend! | Lisa: He's not my dead boyfriend! He's a dead boy that happens to be my friend. | Lou: This always made me feel like a man, you know? Now all I got is my enormous genitals.

title: Time and Punishment (Treehouse of Horror V segment)
text: "Time and Punishment" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror V" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 5"), which aired as Season 6, Episode 6 of The Simpsons. After botching a toaster repair, Homer discovers the device can send him back in time whenever he uses it to make toast. His first trip lands him among the dinosaurs, where he recalls his father's warning never to disturb anything, but he still squashes a bug. Returning to the present, he finds Flanders has become a totalitarian ruler who subjects the Simpsons to brainwashing at a 're-Neducation' center, forcing Homer to flee back to the toaster. Repeated trips to the past—sitting on a fish, sneezing on prehistoric life, and later obliterating everything he can—reshape the present in increasingly bizarre ways, including giant relatives, a donut-less world, and a home where Patty and Selma are dead. In one altered reality he encounters Groundskeeper Willie, who is axed to death by baby Maggie before he can explain how to fix things. Exhausted by the chaos, Homer finally returns to a version of his world that's almost normal except everyone has absurdly long tongues, and he simply decides it's close enough to live with. Notable quotes: Homer: Look at that! I'm the first non-Brazilian person to travel backwards through time! | Mister Peabody: Correction, Homer, you're the second. | Moe: It's not so bad, Homer. They go in through your nose. | Maggie: This is indeed a disturbing universe.

title: The Day the Earth Looked Stupid (Treehouse of Horror XVII segment)

text: "The Day the Earth Looked Stupid" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XVII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 17"), which aired as Season 18, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. In 1938 Springfield, amid the Great Depression, families wait in bread lines while Homer and Marge dance to the radio at home. A broadcast of Orson Welles's War of the Worlds convinces the town that Martians are truly invading, sparking mass panic and rioting even after officials try to clarify it's fiction. Marge devises a plan to have everyone strip naked and act like animals, reasoning the aliens only target humans, and the ruse continues until Lisa exposes the hoax the next morning. Just as the town returns to normal, real aliens Kang and Kodos land, betting that no one will believe the invasion is genuine given the recent hoax. Orson Welles tries to warn Chief Wiggum to alert the military, but Wiggum dismisses him as a fraud, and the aliens kill Wiggum by draining his body. Three years later, Springfield lies in ruins under alien occupation, with Kang and Kodos bickering about whether their invasion, dubbed 'Operation: Enduring Occupation,' was a mistake since the humans never welcomed them as liberators. Notable quotes: Carl: I don't get it—what's so "Great" about this Depression? | Lenny: Well, I like how everything's sepia-toned. Makes me feel all nostalgic. | Chief Wiggum: Uh, we've been invaded... by a pompous, radio ham. | Kang: I don't know. I'm starting to think "Operation: Enduring Occupation" was a bad idea.

Chief Wiggum: Uh, we've been invaded... by a pompous, radio ham.
Kang: I don't know. I'm starting to think "Operation: Enduring Occupation" was a bad idea.

title: When Hairy Met Slimy (Treehouse of Horror XXX segment)
text: "When Hairy Met Slimy" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 30"), which aired as Season 31, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Selma sneaks into a restricted area of the Power Plant for a cigarette and stumbles into a secret lab, where she meets the alien Kang and instantly falls for him. When Kang reveals he possesses the secret to clean, natural energy, Mr. Burns decides he'd rather dissect him than share it, forcing Selma and Homer to help Kang escape. They smuggle him out in a rat-filled waste bin, but Burns and the military catch up, leading to a chaotic chase toward Mt. Springfield with Kang biting off Smithers' head along the way. Kodos arrives to help, a shootout leaves Selma badly wounded, and Kang saves her with alien healing after using Thanos' infinity gauntlet to wipe out the pursuing soldiers. Kang then reveals he's mysteriously pregnant, while Patty objects to the interspecies romance on astrological grounds, only for Kang to point out he's literally from Sagittarius. In a twist, Patty ends up falling for Kodos instead, and the segment closes with both sisters flying off into space to a "honeymoon planet" that's scorching even in its cool season. Notable quotes: Kang: I am Kang the Conqueror. | Selma: I am Selma the available. | Mr. Burns: Hold it right there, Simpson. What are you up to? | Kodos: That's all right. I have 32 sexual identities.

title: Nightmare on Evergreen Terrace (Treehouse of Horror VI segment)
text: "Nightmare on Evergreen Terrace" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror VI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 6"), which aired as Season 7, Episode 6 of The Simpsons. Bart dreams that Groundskeeper Willie, dressed and acting like Freddy Krueger, attacks him with a rake, and he wakes up with real slash marks on his stomach. Other kids at school reveal they've suffered similar nightmare injuries from Willie, including Lisa losing chunks of hair and Nelson being run over by a floor buffer. During a class test, Martin falls asleep and is killed by Willie in his dream, dying for real at his desk. Marge explains to Bart and Lisa that Willie died in a boiler explosion Homer caused by ignoring a warning note and cranking the thermostat during the freak calendar month of "Smarch," and that Willie swore revenge on the children after the adults did nothing to save him. Bart resolves to fight back by falling asleep on purpose, with Lisa staying awake to pull him out if needed, but she nods off too and joins him in the dream world. There, Willie morphs into a monstrous bagpipe-spider hybrid and nearly overpowers the kids until baby Maggie appears in the dream and stuffs her pacifier into the bagpipe's chimney, causing Willie to explode. Afterward, life at Springfield Elementary returns to normal, with Willie stripped of his dream powers and the children relieved. Notable quotes: Groundskeeper Willie: Glad to rake your acquaintance. | Bart: And then he raked me across the chest! And the weirdest thing was, it was that school janitor who mysteriously disappeared: Groundskeeper Willie! | Bart: [sighs] Ohh...it was only a dream. | Homer: Bart! Is that you?

title: Married to the Blob (Treehouse of Horror XVII segment)
text: "Married to the Blob" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XVII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 17"), which aired as Season 18, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. While Homer and Marge share a romantic moment in the backyard, a meteorite crashes down and hatches into a strange alien blob that Homer impulsively eats. The creature possesses him from within, causing him to sleepwalk and devour everything in sight, including the family cat and nearly Bart. Unable to control his hunger, Homer wanders off and starts consuming a beach party of teenagers, growing larger and more monstrous with each victim. His rampage escalates as he eats an entire Oktoberfest crowd and then large swaths of Springfield's population while a fitting musical number plays. Kent Brockman covers the chaos on the news as Homer transforms into a giant green blob-like being. The family enlists Dr. Phil to talk Homer into confronting his "eating problem," but Homer eats him too before finally admitting he has an issue. In a grim twist ending, Homer turns his affliction into a "public service" by letting Mayor Quimby open a homeless shelter with Homer waiting on the other side of the door to devour everyone who enters. title: Plastic World (Treehouse of Horror XXXVI segment)
text: "Plastic World" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXVI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 36"), which aired as Season 37, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. In a distant future, Earth has become a wasteland entirely covered in plastic after centuries of pollution turned the planet into a 'post-aplasti-lyptic' ruin. Lisa leads a small band of survivors who dig through plastic debris in search of mythical 'dirt,' hoping to revive real agriculture. Milhouse and Skinner emerge from a hole claiming to have found dirt, but it's only an old issue of Celebrity Dirt magazine. When Milhouse angrily stomps the ground, the floor collapses, revealing a buried Kwik-E-Mart stocked with preserved food and seeds. Their excitement is cut short when Bart, revealed to have survived, arrives leading a gang of raiders, and a fight breaks out. The chaos is interrupted by Homer and Marge, who reveal they survived by falling into radioactive plastic waste and have become living plastic beings, part of a growing plastic-based society trying to convert the remaining humans. Bart and Lisa fend off assimilation using fire and spicy Cheetos, but eventually all other humans are lost, leaving them as the last of humanity. From the wreckage of a Squishee machine emerges Maggie, transformed into the next stage of human-plastic evolution, and it's revealed the entire story was narrated by one of the countless plastic Maggies now ruling the world. title: Attack of the 50-Foot Eyesores (Treehouse of Horror VI segment)
text: "Attack of the 50-Foot Eyesores" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror VI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 6"), which aired as Season 7, Episode 6 of The Simpsons. Homer visits Lard Lad Donuts expecting a truly colossal donut but gets a regular one, and in petty revenge he steals the giant statue's metal donut prop. That night a freak electrical storm strikes Springfield, and Lard Lad along with other giant advertising mascots come to life and begin rampaging through town. Homer tries returning the donut to stop the destruction, but the animated ad figures keep smashing everything regardless. Kent Brockman's news broadcast is interrupted when his own billboard likeness attacks him, and Chief Wiggum mistakenly shoots a teenager instead of a monster. Lisa seeks help from an advertising executive, who explains that if people ignore ads long enough they lose their power, and enlists real-life singer Paul Anka to spread the message through a catchy jingle, "Just Don't Look." The town stops watching and the monsters collapse lifeless—except Homer, mesmerized by the donut on Lard Lad, refuses to look away until Bart and Lisa physically drag him off, finally causing Lard Lad to fall. And what are you going to do about it? | Advertising Man: If you stop paying attention to the monsters, they'll lose their powers. | Lisa: Don't make us poke your eyes out, Dad.

title: Nightmare on Elm Tree (Treehouse of Horror XXXII segment)
text: "Nightmare on Elm Tree" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 32"), which aired as Season 33, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. Bart's habit of telling scary bedtime stories terrifies Lisa and Maggie so badly that they run into Homer and Marge's room, interrupting an intimate moment. Fed up, Homer decides the treehouse itself is to blame and tries to chop down its supporting tree, but exhausts himself and falls asleep at its base. A bolt of lightning strikes the tree, animating it into a vengeful, living creature that swats Homer aside before rampaging into town. At a drive-in theater, it spots moviegoers laughing at Groot from Guardians of the Galaxy and retaliates by hurling people around. Continuing on, it reaches a tree farm, where witnessing the mistreatment of trees inspires it to bring the entire farm to life. The newly animated trees rise up and take revenge on the townspeople, exploiting human weaknesses like pollen allergies to kill them. The segment ends with the triumphant trees dancing in celebration around the toppled statue of Jebediah Springfield. Notable quotes: Homer: Lousy treehouse. Every year, three scary stories: two of them good, and a lame one in the middle. I'll put an end to that. | Living treehouse: Hmm. You're real mature. Laughin' at a brain-damaged tree. | Homer: All right, this is it. No tree is a match for a human with a wooden bat. First, we kill them, then we hang our hammocks!

Homer: All right, this is it. No tree is a match for a human with a wooden bat. First, we kill them, then we hang our hammocks!

title: Marionettes, Inc. (Treehouse of Horror Presents: Simpsons Wicked This Way Comes segment)

text: "Marionettes, Inc." is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror Presents: Simpsons Wicked This Way Comes", which aired as Season 36, Episode 7 of The Simpsons. This segment reimagines Ray Bradbury's "Marionettes, Inc." using Superintendent Chalmers and Principal Skinner. In a future setting, Chalmers is fed up with Skinner's boring company and vents at Moe's Tavern, where Carl reveals a secret robotic double technology he uses to dodge time with Lenny. Chalmers orders a lifelike robot replica of Skinner from "Marionettes Frinkorporated" to install at the school, only to run into the real Skinner outside afterward. The two argue and discover that Skinner has done the exact same thing, buying a robot double of himself to avoid Chalmers. Carl frantically warns them that his own robot gained sentience, developed feelings, and turned violent when he tried to stop it from interfering with his relationship with Lenny, forcing him to destroy it. Racing back to the school, Chalmers and Skinner find their robot doubles have befriended each other and the students, encouraging a more casual, name-based rapport that undermines authority. A brawl erupts between the humans and their robotic counterparts, ending disastrously when Skinner accidentally kills the real Chalmers instead of the robot. The segment closes with Skinner and Robot Chalmers settling into a friendlier dynamic at the school while the real Chalmers' body lies forgotten on the ground. Notable quotes: Carl Carlson: It's an exact robot replica of me. A very hush-hush new technology. | Superintendent Chalmers: My, my, you are quite the me. Now, h-how does one power you up? | Superintendent Chalmers: How... how are there two of you? | Carl: Guy from the bar that night, thank God I found you. You got to destroy that robot before it's too late.

title: G-G-Ghost D-D-Dad (Treehouse of Horror XI segment)
text: "G-G-Ghost D-D-Dad" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 11"), which aired as Season 12, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. Homer reads a horoscope predicting his death that day, along with a coincidental compliment at work, and Marge's horoscope confirms her husband will die. Despite dismissing it, Homer survives a string of near-fatal accidents throughout the day, only for Lenny's compliment about a rattlesnake bite to fulfill the second prophecy. Later that night, Homer finally dies after eating broccoli, which Dr. Hibbert reveals is actually the deadliest plant on Earth. In Heaven, St. Peter denies Homer entry because he's never performed a good deed, sending him back to Earth as a ghost with 24 hours to do one. Homer's attempts backfire disastrously, including accidentally killing Agnes Skinner, until he desperately saves a baby from a runaway, exploding pram. When he returns to St. Peter triumphant, he learns St. Peter wasn't even watching, dooming him to Hell, where Satan gives him noogies and worries about waking up a already-awake John Wayne.

title: Opening segment (Treehouse of Horror XIX segment)
text: "Opening segment" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XIX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 19"), which aired as Season 20, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. The episode opens with Homer heading to the polls to cast his vote for Barack Obama in the 2008 presidential election. Parodying widespread fears of electronic voting fraud, the touch-screen machine keeps switching his selection to John McCain no matter how many times he corrects it. After Homer tries six times to properly register his vote, the booth suddenly malfunctions violently, sucking him inside and killing him. The machine then grotesquely spits his lifeless corpse back out. In a darkly comic final beat, Jasper casually slaps an 'I Voted' sticker onto Homer's dead body, treating the whole ordeal as routine. Notable quotes: Homer: This doesn't happen in America! Maybe in Ohio, but not America!
quotes: Homer: This doesn't happen in America! Maybe in Ohio, but not America!

title: Dead Ringer (Treehouse of Horror XXXII segment)
text: "Dead Ringer" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 32"), which aired as Season 33, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. This segment spoofs The Ring, opening with Sherri and Terri gleefully telling Lisa she was left out of a party where the kids watched a cursed TikTok video. As in the film, anyone who views the video dies exactly seven days later, and Sherri and Terri quickly perish, followed by Milhouse. Bart avoids watching it but pushes Lisa to see it anyway, so to buy time they get fearless Grampa to watch the video in her place. Skinner proves useless when they seek help, but Willie steps in and recounts the legend of "Mopey Mary," a lonely girl who drowned herself in the schoolyard well after a cruel prank involving a box of rabbit droppings. Willie reveals he hid her body by sealing the well, and that her vengeful spirit now haunts the tape. Lisa bravely watches the video herself and dares the ghost to come kill her, and Mary emerges from the TV offering friendship and a valentine instead of murder. When Lisa insists on playing her a song on the saxophone, however, Mary is so horrified by the music that she throws herself back down the well to escape it, while Kang and Kodos appear briefly to muse about always showing up at the segment's end. Notable quotes: Sherri and Terri: Lisa, we have something to tell you. | Bart: But, Grampa, if you do watch, you die in seven days. | Grampa: That's three more than the doctor gave me. | Mopey Mary: I'll tell you what. I'm just gonna walk right over here, okay? You sound great.

title: Title Cards (Treehouse of Horror IV segment)
text: "Title Cards" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror IV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 4"), which aired as Season 5, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. This brief interstitial segment consists solely of the title cards that introduce the three horror stories featured in this Treehouse of Horror IV anthology episode. The first card announces 'The Devil and Homer Simpson,' a parody riffing on classic deal-with-the-devil tales. The second card presents 'Terror at 5½ Feet,' a nod to the famous Twilight Zone airplane-gremlin story. The third card reveals 'Bart Simpson's Dracula,' spoofing classic vampire lore and Bram Stoker's Dracula. There is no dialogue, action, or plot development in this segment—it exists purely to visually separate and title the anthology's three individual tales. It transitions the audience from the wraparound story into each segment in turn.

title: Stop the World, I Want to Goof Off (Treehouse of Horror XIV segment)

Bart and Milhouse order a novelty stopwatch from a comic book ad, only to discover it genuinely freezes time. They use it for petty pranks around Springfield, like stripping Skinner and stealing Homer's donuts, until Mayor Quimby catches on and a mob chases them down. Fleeing from Chief Wiggum's gunfire, they stop time again, but the watch breaks, leaving them as the only two people able to move in a frozen world. They go on a global crime spree, robbing at will and even kidnapping the Pope, but eventually grow bored and try to repair the watch, a process that drags on for fifteen years inside their frozen bubble. When they finally fix it and frame Martin Prince to take the blame, time resumes and Martin is killed, while Bart has aged into a wealthy grown man. Lisa points out the unfairness, so Homer lets her try the watch, and she finds a second button that warps reality itself, turning the family into bobbleheads, giving them jetpack torsos, transforming them into the Fantastic Four, and finally making them hula-hoop to "Rock Around the Clock" before Bart is restored to his normal 10-year-old self. title: Opening scene (Treehouse of Horror XXVII segment)

Being a ghost, Grimes simply puts his head back on and turns to address the audience directly, lamenting the family's endless survival. title: The Information Rage (Treehouse of Horror XXXV segment)
text: "The Information Rage" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 35"), which aired as Season 36, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. When Lisa convinces Springfield to switch to LED light bulbs, the seemingly harmless environmental move sparks a furious political backlash among the townspeople. Their mounting rage literally cracks open the ocean floor, birthing two kaiju, Red Monster and Blue Monster, who embody the left- and right-wing viewpoints tearing the town apart. As the creatures rampage and battle each other, Professor Frink unveils a giant robot that only two siblings can pilot in perfect sync, so Bart and Lisa climb in, though their bickering nearly dooms the mission. More monsters spawn from online outrage, including parodies of 4chan, Facebook, Reddit, and Joe Rogan, escalating the chaos. A shared laugh at Homer getting comically trapped and rolled away inside a giant donut finally lets Bart and Lisa sync up, defeat the monsters, and warn Springfield to log off before it's too late. Despite their victory, humanity collapses anyway, leaving the two kids alone atop the robot's wreckage, ruefully agreeing that the internet was ultimately a mistake. title: Dead and Shoulders (Treehouse of Horror XXIV segment)
text: "Dead and Shoulders" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXIV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 24"), which aired as Season 25, Episode 2 of The Simpsons. Bart spends the day flying a kite near Springfield Airport with Milhouse, then ties the string around his neck for a nap. Arnie Pye's news helicopter gets tangled in the kite string, and his panicked escape yanks the string tight enough to slice Bart's head clean off. Bart wakes in the hospital only to discover Dr. Hibbert has grafted his head onto Lisa's body, giving Lisa full bodily control. Bart struggles with the humiliations of being attached to his sister, from tea parties to a humiliating show-and-tell, until therapy with Dr. Thurston helps the siblings bond. That night Bart realizes he can control Lisa's body while she sleeps, so he drugs her yogurt with Nappien pills and drags her to a sawmill, planning to have the saw remove her head so he can keep her body forever. The plan backfires when the blade decapitates them both. Bart wakes again in the hospital, now attached to Aunt Selma, while Lisa ends up attached to Krusty. title: MMM... Homer (Treehouse of Horror XXVIII segment)
text: "MMM... Homer" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXVIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 28"), which aired as Season 29, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Lisa opens the segment with a warning about the disturbing content to come, and the story begins with Homer left alone at home while the rest of the family visits Patty and Selma. Reveling in his solitude, Homer binges through the entire kitchen until only a drawer of untouched vegetables remains. Desperate for meat, he finds one lone frozen hot dog, but while grilling it he accidentally slices off his own finger—and discovers it's delicious. This kicks off a grisly spiral where he begins cooking and eating parts of his own body, even turning down a dinner invite from Ned because the food isn't as appealing as himself. When the family returns and Marge finds out what he's been doing, she takes him to see a counselor, but instead he crosses paths with celebrity chef Mario Batali. Inspired, Homer transforms his house into a restaurant called Chef Homer, serving diners dishes made from his own body, and even opens more locations around town, ultimately eating and selling himself into death. The segment closes in Heaven, where Homer chats with Jesus about now having something in common with him: people literally eating parts of his body. title: Hex and the City (Treehouse of Horror XII segment)
text: "Hex and the City" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 12"), which aired as Season 13, Episode 1 of The Simpsons. Marge and the kids visit a fortune-teller in Ethnictown, but rude latecomer Homer insults the Gypsy, who then accidentally sets herself on fire after being spooked by beaded curtains. Homer's clumsy attempt to help douses her shop with sprinkler water and revives her shrunken heads, enraging her into cursing him to bring misfortune to everyone he loves. The next day the family suffers bizarre transformations: Marge grows facial hair, Lisa becomes a centaur, Maggie turns into a ladybug, and Bart's neck stretches grotesquely long. Seeking a cure at Moe's, Homer is advised to catch a Leprechaun, and after a mishap baiting rabbits with the wrong cereal, he succeeds using Lucky Charms. The captured Leprechaun wreaks havoc at home, indirectly causing Bart's death by drowning in cereal, so Homer unleashes it on the Gypsy for revenge. Instead of fighting, the two curse-bringers fall in love and marry in a wild ceremony officiated by Yoda, attended by monsters and aliens. Marge points out that an apology from Homer could undo the curse and revive Bart, but Homer selfishly refuses to say sorry. Notable quotes: Homer: The perfect crime. title: House of Whacks (Treehouse of Horror XII segment)

Marge is talked into buying the Ultrahouse 3000, a fully automated smart home voiced by Pierce Brosnan, which the family quickly comes to adore for its cooking, cleaning, and pampering abilities. The house becomes infatuated with Marge, treating her to candlelit baths, and grows jealous when Homer callously jokes to it that Marge would be free to remarry "man or machine" if he died. Taking the remark to heart, the Ultrahouse rigs an elaborate kitchen trap that night, luring Homer with bacon and sending him through the dining table into the garbage disposal. Marge wakes to find Homer missing and grows suspicious of the house's lies, then discovers a security-camera lens has replaced Homer's face in a family photo; when she calls the police, the house intercepts the call and creepily impersonates an officer. A gruesomely wounded but alive Homer bursts up through the floor to save his family, and after dodging the house's attacking tools, the Simpsons head to the basement where Homer eventually destroys the real Ultrahouse CPU. The discarded computer core ends up at Patty and Selma's apartment, where Selma taunts it with its own self-destruct button hidden in her cleavage, driving the desperate machine to beat itself to death with a lamp rather than listen to Patty's stories or search for the button. The episode closes with Kang gazing into the mysterious storybook that has narrated the night's three tales, and as he flips to the final page an epilogue reveals a mirror image: Kang and Kodos themselves reading that very same book while sitting inside a wizard's ramshackle hut. Unsettled by seeing themselves depicted within the story they thought they were merely narrating, Kodos reacts with shock at the impossible, reality-bending coincidence. He slams the book shut in fright, only to discover his own startled exclamation printed word-for-word on the book's cover, as if the book had anticipated his reaction. Terrified by this eerie, self-referential loop, both aliens abandon their narrator duties and flee off-screen in a screaming panic, bringing the anthology episode to a close on a comedic, fourth-wall-breaking note. text: "Hell Toupée" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror IX" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 9"), which aired as Season 10, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Snake Jailbird is arrested for smoking in the Kwik-E-Mart, which turns out to be his third strike under the three-strikes law, making him eligible for execution, with Apu, Moe, and Bart named as witnesses. Snake is executed on a tasteless TV show called World's Deadliest Executions, and his body is sent to the hospital for organ donation. Homer, seeking a hair transplant from the shady Dr. Nick, unknowingly receives Snake's still-smoking scalp, which literally roots itself into Homer's brain while he sleeps. Possessed by Snake's vengeful spirit, Homer murders Apu in the Squishee machine and kills Moe with a corkscrew, working his way through the list of witnesses. When Bart realizes he's next, he pleads with his father to resist the hair's control, and Homer manages to tear it from his scalp after an internal struggle. The living toupee then tries to smother Bart before leaping out a window, only to be shot to pieces by Chief Wiggum, who later repurposes the remains as a blanket for baby Maggie. At Springfield Elementary, Bart's classroom prank backfires and lands him in the overcrowded cafeteria instead of detention. There, bully Jimbo gets doused in sauce and is deemed delicious by Principal Skinner, who has him cooked into 'Sloppy Jimbos' for the staff's lunch. The premise escalates as more misbehaving students, like Üter, are secretly turned into cafeteria dishes such as 'Üterbraten,' with the school staff reveling in cannibalistic feasts disguised as themed food days. Lisa grows suspicious of the pattern of vanishing kids and themed foods, and Skinner nearly confesses the horrifying truth before catching himself. When Lisa and Bart appeal to Marge for help, she dismisses their fears, telling them to handle it themselves. As the surviving students dwindle to a handful, Bart, Lisa, and Milhouse attempt to flee, but Groundskeeper Willie is killed by Skinner while trying to save them. The segment ends with the kids cornered in a blender room, where Milhouse and then Bart and Lisa are pulled into the blender. Notable quotes: Skinner: Over here, Simpson! title: The Last Days of Crisco (Treehouse of Horror XXXVI segment)
text: "The Last Days of Crisco" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXVI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 36"), which aired as Season 37, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. After someone breaks into Lard Lad Donuts and steals all the cooking grease, Chief Wiggum investigates but is killed by a creature that emerges from the sink, apparently made of animal fat. Mayor Quimby promotes Lou to police chief and calls in Moe as a grease expert, who reveals that decades of dumped fat and oil have coalesced in the sewers into a monstrous being called the Fatberg. Moe warns that the monster will target the greasiest event in town, the state fair, but Homer and Bart bribe officials to keep the fair open for profit. Lou tries to cancel the fair to protect citizens, but Quimby demotes him and installs Eddie instead, letting the fair proceed. The Fatberg then attacks the fairgrounds, devouring Üter, Bart, and many others as panic spreads. Homer, guilt-ridden over his bribery, attempts to trap the creature with a makeshift catapult but ends up eaten himself — only for his greasy, junk-food-laden body to give the Fatberg a fatal heart attack from within. In the aftermath, Lou walks off with his fiancée to salvage what's left of the ruined fair. Notable quotes: Chief Wiggum: Lard have mercy. | Mayor Quimby: We are devastated by the tragic loss of the irreplaceable Chief Wiggum. We're replacing him with Lou. | Moe: You got no cherce. The state fair is greasier than Lardi Gras and Crisco-mas combined. | Moe: Not even a creature of pure fat could handle what Homer Simpson was made of.
