title: Survival of the Fattest (Treehouse of Horror XVI segment)
text: "Survival of the Fattest" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XVI" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 16"), which aired as Season 17, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. Mr. Burns invites Homer and the rest of Springfield's citizens to his mansion, ostensibly for a hunting party, though the fine print reveals he actually intends to hunt them himself. Despite warnings from Lisa about the cruelty of the trip, Homer goes anyway, and Burns soon reveals his true intentions, gunning down victims like Comic Book Guy and even his own lawyer after using them to legally justify his actions. As the massacre unfolds, it becomes a televised spectacle called "The World Series of Manslaughter," watched in horror by Marge and Lisa at home. One by one, the citizens are killed in absurd ways, including being catapulted from trees, eaten by Homer, or gunned down by Burns' helicopter, leaving only a handful of survivors. Homer manages to endure the night by disguising Barney's corpse as himself, fooling Burns long enough to avoid being shot. Just as Burns takes final aim at Homer, Marge arrives and knocks out both Burns and Smithers with a frying pan, then smacks Homer for staying away from home without calling. The segment closes with two news reporters awkwardly reporting in front of Homer and Marge, who begin making love behind them. Notable quotes: Lisa: Don't accept this invitation dad. Hunting is cruel! | Homer: Lisa, animals don't feel death. That was proven by the scientists at Black Angus! | Burns: Now, since I am so kind, I will give you a five minutes' head-start. You may commence running! | Comic Book Guy: Five minutes of running? Just shoot me now!
quotes: Lisa: Don't accept this invitation dad. Hunting is cruel!
Homer: Lisa, animals don't feel death. That was proven by the scientists at Black Angus!
Burns: Now, since I am so kind, I will give you a five minutes' head-start. You may commence running!
Comic Book Guy: Five minutes of running? Just shoot me now!

title: Bart Simpson's Dracula (Treehouse of Horror IV segment)
text: "Bart Simpson's Dracula" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror IV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 4"), which aired as Season 5, Episode 5 of The Simpsons. After a series of vampire attacks plague Springfield, Mr. Burns invites the Simpsons to a strange midnight dinner at his Pennsylvania mansion, and Lisa quickly suspects he's a vampire, though no one believes her. Bart and Lisa sneak into Burns's secret lair and find a book proving vampires are real, but Bart gets trapped by a hidden slide and is captured and turned into a vampire by Count Burns. The family dismisses Lisa's warnings until Bart himself, now undead, attacks Lisa at home alongside several vampiric classmates, finally convincing everyone she was right. Following Lisa's advice, the family drives back to Pennsylvania and Homer stakes Count Burns through the heart, believing this cures Bart and ends the vampire threat, though it costs Homer his job. The next morning, however, Lisa discovers the rest of her family has become vampires too, revealing that Marge—not Burns—was secretly the true head vampire all along. Just as the vampire family closes in on Lisa, the segment breaks off into a cheerful faux-"Peanuts" musical closing number wishing everyone a Happy Halloween. Notable quotes: Marge: No, I'm the head vampire! [maniacal laughing] | Marge: Well, I do have a life outside this house, you know. | Homer: Correction. Free blood. | Bart: Hello, Mother. Hello, Father. I missed you during my uneventful absence.
quotes: Marge: No, I'm the head vampire! [maniacal laughing]
Marge: Well, I do have a life outside this house, you know.
Homer: Correction. Free blood.
Bart: Hello, Mother. Hello, Father. I missed you during my uneventful absence.

title: Bong Joon Ho's This Side of Parasite (Treehouse of Horror XXXII segment)

text: "Bong Joon Ho's This Side of Parasite" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXXII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 32"), which aired as Season 33, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. The Simpsons are reimagined as a poor family living in a flooded, pizza-box-littered basement apartment, mirroring the setup of the film Parasite. Their fortunes change when Bart lands a job tutoring Greta Wolfcastle, daughter of wealthy action star Rainer Wolfcastle, though he spends more time watching Itchy & Scratchy than actually teaching her math. Bart schemes to get his whole family hired by the Wolfcastles, conveniently pushing out the previous employee, Kirk Van Houten, just as Wolfcastle departs on vacation. The Simpsons quickly settle into a life of luxury in the mansion, but their scheme unravels when a desperate, soaked Kirk returns begging to be let inside. Once let in by Marge, Kirk reveals a secret door leading to a hidden basement where his own family has been squatting all along. This discovery sparks a chaotic, violent brawl between the Simpsons, Kirk's family, and other impoverished Springfielders also hiding in the house. By the end of the fight almost everyone is killed, but the Simpsons emerge victorious and remain comfortably ensconced in their newly claimed mansion. Notable quotes: Bart: Family, I have excellent news. I got a job as a tutor in a nice, rich home. | Bart: Okay, here's a math problem. How long can the two of us watch your hundred-inch TV before anyone gets wise? | Kirk Van Houten: Please let me in. My jeans are wet. And they're my only pair of pants. | Lisa: Wait! If we all work together, regardless of class, we could finally change everything for the better.

title: Oh, the Places You'll D'oh! (Treehouse of Horror XXIV segment)
text: "Oh, the Places You'll D'oh!" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXIV" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 24"), which aired as Season 25, Episode 2 of The Simpsons. In a Dr. Seuss-style rhyming Springfield, Bart, Lisa and Maggie are stuck home sick with the mumps on Halloween while Marge heads off to a costume party, leaving them just one candy each. Bored and craving trick-or-treating, they're visited by the mysterious Fat in the Hat, a self-proclaimed jack-of-all-trades who cures their mumps and whisks them away on his cycle after knocking out Grampa. As he leads them through town, his cheerful demeanor curdles into violent chaos, robbing Apu, blowing up Mr. Burns' mansion and Town Hall, killing Moe, and unleashing the zoo animals. Terrified, the kids flee across town on a series of Seussian versions of familiar Springfield faces, including Barney and a decapitated Krusty, before flying home on Bumblebee Man. To their horror, the Fat in the Hat is waiting for them at home, declaring himself their new father, but Maggie stabs him with his own umbrella before he can finish his sentence. He dies with a strange final wish about never being played by Mike Myers, and the kids turn his body into a rug, calmly eating candy on top of him until Marge returns none the wiser. Notable quotes: Marge: Now, I'm off to a party, my outfit is chic. It's a Catwoman costume, I'm sure is unique. | Grampa: You should not be here when their mother's away! | Moe Szyslak: I ain't got no candy, I only serve beer. And who said that you could bring minors in here? | Lisa: We thought we escaped from our psychotic guide, but when we got home he was waiting inside!

Lisa: We thought we escaped from our psychotic guide, but when we got home he was waiting inside!

title: Lisa's nightmare (Treehouse of Horror II segment)
text: "Lisa's nightmare" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror II" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 2"), which aired as Season 3, Episode 7 of The Simpsons. After gorging on Halloween candy despite Marge's warning, the kids and Homer drift into disturbing dreams. In Lisa's nightmare, the family is vacationing in Morocco when Homer purchases a cursed monkey's paw that grants wishes but always with a terrible price. Back home, each family member makes a wish: Maggie's golden pacifier seems harmless, but Bart's wish for wealth and fame turns the Simpsons into unwilling celebrities plastered across embarrassing advertisements. Lisa's wish for world peace backfires spectacularly when the aliens Kang and Kodos exploit humanity's disarmed state to invade and enslave Earth. Homer, trying to make a foolproof wish, asks for a turkey sandwich without surprises, only to be enraged that the turkey is slightly dry. Furious, he discards the paw, which Ned Flanders picks up and uses to free humanity from alien rule, becoming a hero. The nightmare ends with Flanders wishing for a castle while a jealous, embittered Homer looks on. Notable quotes: Marge: Homer, where'd you get the monkey's paw? | Homer: I got it from the stand... over... there. | Merchant: You will be sorry. | Kodos: They constructed a board with a nail in it, but they won't stop there.

Homer: I got it from the stand... over... there.
Merchant: You will be sorry.
Kodos: They constructed a board with a nail in it, but they won't stop there.

title: Bart's nightmare (Treehouse of Horror II segment)
text: "Bart's nightmare" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror II" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 2"), which aired as Season 3, Episode 7 of The Simpsons. As Bart drifts off to sleep after letting Lisa join him in bed, his dream begins as a parody of the Twilight Zone episode "It's a Good Life." In the dream, Bart possesses godlike mental powers, able to read minds and transform anyone who displeases him into monstrous or absurd forms, leaving all of Springfield terrified and forced to indulge his every whim. When Homer refuses to let him watch Krusty the Clown, Bart magically swaps a football player on TV for Homer's head, then turns Homer into a Jack-in-the-box after Homer tries to attack him with a chair. Marge, horrified, brings the family to psychiatrist Dr. Marvin Monroe, who advises Homer and Bart to bond through father-son activities like baseball, fishing, and church outings. The quality time softens Bart's tyrannical behavior, and out of newfound affection he restores Homer to normal. The segment ends with Homer giving Bart a loving kiss, at which point Bart wakes up in genuine horror at the sentimental moment. Notable quotes: Marge: BART! | Bart: Lisa did it. | Marge: That's it, young man! You're coming with me! | Marge: [smiling nervously and waving] Please?

title: The Sweets Hereafter (Treehouse of Horror XXVIII segment)
text: "The Sweets Hereafter" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror XXVIII" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 28"), which aired as Season 29, Episode 4 of The Simpsons. The Simpson family finds themselves reincarnated as Halloween candy sitting on a plate for trick-or-treaters. Bart, now a Butterfinger, worries about never being chosen, while Marge reassures him with dark humor about being perpetually overlooked. Other candies are quickly grabbed, and Lisa, transformed into a candy apple, laments that no one wants her for fear of hidden razor blades, prompting an unsettling joke from Marge about caramel dipping. Shauna eventually eats Grampa, who has become Senior Mints, right after Homer nudges him forward. The next night, the unclaimed Simpson candies are shelved with the Halloween decorations and discover a living chocolate Easter bunny warning them they'll all be forgotten there. Disturbed by the bunny's suffering, Homer begins eating it despite Marge's protests, insisting chocolate can't feel pain, and the rest of the family joins in once he silences its screaming mouth. The scene closes with chocolate splattering over a wall that reads 'The Simpsons Easter Special,' the mess reforming into the title 'Treehouse of Horror XXVIII.' Notable quotes: Lisa: No one ever wants the apple. They must be afraid there's a razor blade in me. | Bart: Yeah, THAT'S the reason. | Lisa: Daaaad! I can't listen to this horror! | Homer: Okay, I'm onto it.

title: Hungry are the Damned (Treehouse of Horror segment)
text: "Hungry are the Damned" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 1"), which aired as Season 2, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. After a backyard cookout, the Simpson family is suddenly beamed aboard a UFO run by two familiar aliens, Kang and Kodos, along with an alien butler named Serak the Preparer. Playing on classic alien-abduction lore and 'To Serve Man'-style sci-fi tropes, the aliens shower the family with luxury, endless food, and promises of a glorious life on their home planet, Rigel IV. Lisa grows suspicious of their true intentions and sneaks into the ship's kitchen at night, where she finds a book titled 'How to Cook for Forty Humans.' Misreading it as 'How to Cook Humans,' she panics and accuses the aliens of planning to eat her family. The Rigellians are offended and hurt by the false accusation, revealing that they had genuinely intended to treat the Simpsons like gods. Disgusted by the family's paranoia, they return the Simpsons to Earth to resume their ordinary lives, lamenting the paradise they've lost. As the family blames Lisa for ruining their chance at a perfect existence, Lisa muses that maybe humans are the real monsters after all. Notable quotes: Kang: Greetings Earthlings, I am Kang. Do not be frightened. We mean you no harm. | Serak the Preparer: Here you go, earthlings. Take all you want. Eat all you take. | Homer: Listen, you big stupid space creature. Nobody, but nobody eats the Simpsons. | Kang: We offered you paradise. You would have experienced emotions a hundred times greater than what you call love.

title: The Raven (Treehouse of Horror segment)
text: "The Raven" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 1"), which aired as Season 2, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. Lisa reads Bart Edgar Allan Poe's classic poem "The Raven" as their Halloween story, and the tale plays out with Homer cast as the grief-stricken narrator mourning his lost love Lenore. Alone at night with an old book of forgotten lore, Homer is startled by a tapping at his chamber door, and upon opening it finds only darkness. Moments later a tapping comes from the window, and a talking raven flies in to perch atop a bust of Pallas above the door. Homer tries desperately to converse with the bird, but it only ever answers "Nevermore," driving him into a rage. He chases the raven wildly around the room, smashing furniture and knocking books off shelves, even beaning himself in the head with a thrown plant pot, causing him to hallucinate tiny chanting ravens. The chaos ends with the raven serenely back on its perch while Homer sits amid the wreckage, mentally unraveled, as the narration closes with Poe's famous final stanza about the soul being lifted "nevermore." Back in the present, Bart shrugs off the story as not scary, unaware that Homer found it thoroughly terrifying, and the family heads to bed for the night. Notable quotes: Homer: Sir, or Madam, truly your forgiveness I implore; But the fact is I was napping, and so gently you came rapping, And so faintly you came tapping, tapping at my chamber door, That I scarce was sure I heard you. | The Raven narrator: Here I opened wide the door; -- | Bart: You know what would have been scarier than nothing? | Lisa: Bart! Stop it. He says "nevermore". That's all he'll ever say.

title: Bad Dream House (Treehouse of Horror segment)
text: "Bad Dream House" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 1"), which aired as Season 2, Episode 3 of The Simpsons. Marge opens the anthology by warning parents that tonight's episode may be too scary for children, but the warning is ignored. The segment then follows the Simpsons as they move into a suspiciously cheap new house that turns out to be alive and malevolent, featuring a swirling vortex in the kitchen and a menacing voice demanding they leave. The house's hostility escalates from strangling Bart with a lamp cord to hurling the family against the ceiling and finally brainwashing them into attacking one another. Marge, immune to the brainwashing, snaps the family out of it and furiously confronts the house, refusing to be intimidated by its threats of gruesome death. Standing her ground, she insists that since they now live there, the house will simply have to accept them. Given a moment to think it over, the house decides it would rather cease to exist than live with the Simpsons, and dramatically implodes into nothing, ending the haunting for good. Notable quotes: Evil House: Get out! | Marge: This family has had its differences, and we've squabbled, but we never had knife fights before... and I blame this house. | Evil House: You will die, you will die slowly. Your stomach will swell, your intestines will writhe and boil... | Lisa: It chose to destroy itself rather than live with us. You can't help but feel a little rejected.

title: Homer's nightmare (Treehouse of Horror II segment)
text: "Homer's nightmare" is a segment from "Treehouse of Horror II" (also called "Treehouse of Horror 2"), which aired as Season 3, Episode 7 of The Simpsons. After Bart's nightmare, the kids pile into Homer and Marge's bed, and Homer grumbles about having only two hours before work, setting up his own dream. In it, Homer has been fired and taken a job as a cemetery gravedigger, where he dozes off inside a freshly dug grave. Meanwhile, Mr. Burns and Smithers are scouring the town for a fresh brain to install in a robotic worker they hope will be the perfect, tireless employee. Mistaking the sleeping Homer for a corpse, they harvest his brain and place it into their robot, but the machine turns out just as clumsy and lazy as Homer, infuriating Burns. Smithers persuades Burns to return the brain to Homer's body, but as they do so the robot topples over and crushes Mr. Burns, fatally injuring him. Homer wakes from the nightmare only to discover, in a final twist, that Mr. Burns's severed head has actually been grafted onto his own body. The segment closes the next morning with the family at breakfast, where Homer is dismayed to find he still has two heads and must choose between a school spaghetti dinner and a royal reception with Queen Beatrix. It's all a dream. It's just a dream. | Mr. Burns: Oh, that's right. It's all a dream... Or is it? | Homer: Oh, I hate having two heads.
